**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract slice of RWB-E4-006, the baseline that the payoff and range calculation of rwb-valuation builds against on Day 1. The baseline fixes the calculation elements of `POST /cases/{caseId}/route` (API-S1-001) on `/api/recovery/valuation/v1` (DP-13) — the payoff, `payoff_as_at`, `settlement_range_low`, `settlement_range_high`, `floor_price`, the rule id and version and the calculation state — the five consumed rows of rwb-source-data, rwb-decision, rwb-case and rwb-access (DP-05), the decision-record element and the library that carries it (DP-03), the elements of `RouteDecisionWorkflow` and its two activities, the rights, the error envelope and the fakes; it publishes no event, because the ownership rows give S1 none. No source publishes the operation names of the consumed rows or the element name of the payoff amount (GAP-2616 and -6; ASM-4318 and -6), gives S1 a table for the payoff, the range or the floor (GAP-2615; ASM-4317) or fixes the freshness limit and the floor method (GAP-2618; ASM-4320). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead of rwb-valuation**, I want **the published contract baseline of the payoff and range calculation of rwb-valuation — its calculation elements in the route answer, its consumed rows, its decision-record element, its workflow elements, its rights, its error envelope and its fakes — fixed and tagged before the build starts**, so that **the application story, the wave 3 harness and the four owners it consumes can build and test on Day 1 against one versioned surface instead of guessing the shape of a neighbour's answer**.

This is the contract slice of legacy RWB-E4-006. It owns:

- the document that fixes the calculation elements of `POST /cases/{caseId}/route` (API-S1-001) on base `/api/recovery/valuation/v1`: `RouteRequest` in, `Approval` out, the payoff, `payoff_as_at`, `settlement_range_low`, `settlement_range_high`, `floor_price`, the rule id, the rule version and the calculation state as declared elements, the `Idempotency-Key` header, the rights and the error set (DP-13);
- the five consumed rows: the account and balance read and the freshness read of rwb-source-data, the rule-set-in-force and decision-log read of rwb-decision, the case and account-set read of rwb-case, and the authorise operation of rwb-access, each with its owner, its use and a placeholder where the name is not published (DP-05);
- the decision-record element, the library that carries it and the shared topic it reaches (DP-03);
- the elements of `RouteDecisionWorkflow` and its two activities on task queue `rwb-valuation`;
- the calculation elements of SCR-13 Route decision, one hop through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19);
- the fakes and their documented answers;
- the naming and boundary rule of the baseline: one base, one topic, one queue, one login, no foreign schema, no monolith base, no balance copy.

It does not own: the calculation itself, its freshness gate, its exception handling and the screen behaviour, which are RWB-S1-E4006-APP; the recommendation and its reasons, which are FEAT-VAL-07; the approval and the case move, which are the route-decision submission slice of RWB-E4-005 and rwb-case (P3); the ACE balances and their batch date, which are rwb-source-data's (P1); the rule set, the range bounds, the floor and the central ledger, which are rwb-decision's (P7); the roles and scopes, which are rwb-access's (P4); the treatment record and the offer, which are rwb-treatment's (S2); the composite route and the screen field list, which are RWB-PLT-N001-CON; and the deployment, which is the operations story of this legacy key.

##### 2. Business rationale

A contract baseline is what lets several teams start together. Legacy RWB-E4-006 asks for a payoff worked out from balances the Workbench does not own and a range the bank governs, recorded with its rule version before the route is chosen. That means the step reads two contracts and writes one record in a third, and without a tagged baseline each of those shapes would be discovered at the first integration instead of at the review.

The three rules the baseline applies:

- **the owner publishes, the consumer adapts.** Every consumed row names its owner, its use and its 2 s budget, and every row whose name is not published carries the placeholder and its gap (GAP-2616; ASM-4318).
- **one hop, one budget.** Each consumed row is a single hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker; a balance is never read from a table of this service and never chained through a second service (DP-05, ADR-020).
- **additive only.** A new optional element is a minor version; a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version and a new document (s9).

The business outcome the baseline protects is the one FEAT-VAL-06 and REQ-S1-004 of FSD S1 state: the payoff and the range are calculated by rule from current balances, with the floor applied. The baseline states no outcome and no business value of its own, and no criterion here asserts a particular payoff amount.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The Ownership Map rows for S1 are in force: `POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations`, `POST /assets/{assetKey}/valuations` and `POST /cases/{caseId}/route`; no table, no event, no job, and one workflow, `RouteDecisionWorkflow`. The two valuation paths belong to the appraisal-intake baseline and are not declared here.
- The service naming is fixed: schema `rwb_valuation`, one login of its own, base `/api/recovery/valuation/v1`, topic `rwb.valuation.events.v1` with `.retry` and `.dlt`, task queue `rwb-valuation` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.valuation`.
- TSD S1 is the shape of record for the service: T-A.1 gives API-S1-001 with right Treatment and offer U; T-A.2 gives `RouteRequest` in, `Approval` out, errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 and the `Idempotency-Key`; T6.1 gives the capability area and its rights.
- The platform CON stories are published: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for the decision record (DP-03) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the composite route (DP-19). A CON story has no build dependency (R5.7 rule 1), so both sit in the preconditions and not in the H row.
- The range bounds, the floor and the freshness limit are values of the settlement route set in force and are referenced with their identifier and version; no source publishes their numeric values and none is declared here (GAP-2618; ASM-4320).
- No approval is needed to publish a Draft baseline; the document is baselined by its own review and the build waits only for its tag (ASM-4323).

##### 4. Flow

1. The author drafts the baseline from the Ownership Map rows of the context pack, TSD S1 T-A.1, T-A.2 and T6.1, the FSD S1 A2.6 rules and the DP table.
2. Every provided element is declared with its method, path, type, nullability, source, rights and error set.
3. Every consumed row is declared with its owner, its use, its budget and a placeholder where the name is not published.
4. The decision-record element is declared with the library of DP-03, the shared topic and the transaction it joins.
5. The workflow and its two activities are declared with their input, their signals and their outcome elements.
6. The closed lists are referenced with their identifier and their version and are never enumerated in code; the range bounds, the floor and the freshness limit are referenced with their rule id.
7. The fakes are declared with their documented answers, one per consumed row and one for the composite route.
8. The compatibility check runs on the draft against the previous tag: a breaking change fails it.
9. The document goes to review as Draft; the reviewers are the owners of the five consumed rows and the tech lead of the service.
10. On the review's close the document is tagged; the application story and the wave 3 harness start against the tag and the fakes, and the code never moves ahead of the document.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A consumer asks for a shape the sources do not publish | The element or row carries the placeholder and its gap; no name, value or path is invented | C3, C4 |
| X2 | A change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element | The compatibility check fails and the document needs a new major version | C1 |
| X3 | A declared element or operation reaches another service's data, base or table | The review refuses the baseline and the boundary test fails the build | C7 |
| X4 | A consumed row has no fake, or its fake has no documented answer | The baseline is not tagged and the application story cannot start | C6 |
| X5 | The rights of an operation are not a row of the access matrix | The operation is not declared and the error set stays incomplete | C5 |
| X6 | An owner changes its documented answer after the tag | The owner publishes a version, this document follows in a minor or major version, and the fake is updated | X2, s9 |
| X7 | Two documents claim the same base, topic, queue or element name | The owner named in the Ownership Map keeps it and the other document changes | C7 |

X1 to X3 are the paths of an incomplete source, X4 to X6 the paths of a baseline moving under a build, and X7 the naming boundary.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs no build, no live service and no approval; starts on Day 1 and is finished before the application story's first line |
| Negotiable | The wording, the section order and the fake data are this story's choice; the operation, the request, the answer, the rights and the error set are fixed by TSD S1 |
| Valuable | Four teams build at once against one tagged surface, and the first integration finds behaviour, not shape |
| Estimable | One document, one provided operation with eight declared elements, five consumed rows, one decision-record element, one workflow with two activities, one screen subject and eight fakes |
| Small | Finished inside a week; the review is the only gate |
| Testable | Every criterion is a document check that runs in the contract test suite, plus the compatibility check on the published schema |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the payoff and range calculation

  Scenario: C1 The baseline validates and only additive changes pass (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published schema, the element list and the closed lists of the baseline
    When a change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element
    Then the compatibility check fails and the change needs a new major version
    And a change that adds an optional element passes as a minor version

  Scenario: C2 The calculation elements of the route answer are published as declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the element table of the baseline
    When POST /cases/{caseId}/route on /api/recovery/valuation/v1 is read
    Then it names RouteRequest in, Approval out, the Idempotency-Key header and the scope rule of T-A.2
    And the answer declares the payoff, payoff_as_at, settlement_range_low, settlement_range_high, floor_price, the rule id, the rule version and the calculation state, each with its type, its nullability and its source

  Scenario: C3 The five consumed rows carry their owners, their budgets and their placeholders (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed operation table of the baseline
    When the rows of rwb-source-data, rwb-decision, rwb-case and rwb-access are read
    Then each row names its owner, its use, one hop and a 2 s budget
    And where the operation name is not published the row carries the placeholder and the gap identifier and no path

  Scenario: C4 The consumed rows are declared as reads and no balance or rule table is declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed table and the table-ownership table of the baseline
    When the balance, the freshness and the rule-set rows are read
    Then each is declared as a consumed read of its owner and never as a table of this service
    And no v_ace_* copy, no foreign schema, no payoff table and no foreign key is declared

  Scenario: C5 The rights and the error envelope are declared for the operation (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operation the baseline provides
    When the rights and the error set are read
    Then it names the capability area Treatment and offer and the right U of the access matrix
    And the error set names 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503 in one problem envelope

  Scenario: C6 The decision-record element, the workflow elements and the fakes are declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the baseline document
    When the decision-record element, the workflow table and the fake table are read
    Then the element names RWB-PLT-E1027-CON as its library, the shared topic and the transaction it joins
    And RouteDecisionWorkflow and its two activities name their input, their signals and their task queue
    And every consumed row has a fake with a documented answer, including the stopped decision-record stub

  Scenario: C7 The naming, the publication and the boundary of the baseline hold (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the base, the topic, the queue, the schema and the outbox of the baseline
    When the document is checked against the naming rule, the ownership rows and the event list
    Then one base, one topic, one queue and one login are declared and no monolith base and no foreign topic appear
    And no event is published, because the ownership rows give S1 none, and no Schedule is declared
```

The seven criteria are new to this run and are tagged as such. They test the contract deliverable only: the schema, the elements, the lists, the consumed rows, the rights, the envelope, the decision-record element, the workflow, the fakes and the boundary. No criterion states a business outcome of the application story, and none asserts a payoff amount, a range value or a floor value.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One owner per operation, row, element and table: the baseline declares the route operation that the Ownership Map gives S1 and names every other row with its owner | Ownership Map rows of S1; TSD S1 T-A.1 |
| BR2 | A consumed row with no published operation name carries the placeholder and its gap and never an invented path, an invented parameter or an invented transport | Template and Rules v1 §R9; GAP-2616 |
| BR3 | The baseline is additive: a new optional element is a minor version, and a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version | ADR-020; s9 |
| BR4 | Every consumed row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and no chain; a balance arrives on the rwb-source-data data product or on this service's own SELECT-only view and is never copied | DP-05; ADR-020; D-RCV-35 U1 |
| BR5 | The range bounds, the floor and the freshness limit are referenced by rule id and version and are never declared as a literal, a default or a fixture value | BR-S1-006; R-SET-01, R-SET-03, R-SET-05 |
| BR6 | No event is published by this baseline: the ownership rows give S1 no event, and the decision record reaches the ledger on the shared topic through the library of DP-03 | DP-03; context pack S1 ownership rows |
| BR7 | The decision record is written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the caller's transaction before the answer is composed, and its element is declared once for the service | DP-03 |
| BR8 | The baseline declares no payoff, range or floor table: the ownership rows give S1 no table and TSD S1 T3.1 declares only `valuation` and `score` | GAP-2615; ASM-4317 |
| BR9 | No personal data in any element, fake, example or log of the baseline | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR10 | The baseline never declares another service's table, operation or topic as its own, and a check fails the build where one names it | DP-01, DP-13, DP-14 |

##### 9. State transitions

The object of this section is the document, not a case: the lifecycle of the contract baseline.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | The draft is complete | Every element, row, fake and error is declared | Draft |
| Draft | The review is opened | The owners of the five consumed rows are named as reviewers | In review |
| In review | The review closes with no open comment | The compatibility check passes | Baselined, tagged for the application story and the harness |
| In review | A comment needs a shape change | The change is applied to the draft | Draft |
| Baselined | An additive change is approved | A new optional element only, and the check passes | Baselined, new minor version |
| Baselined | A breaking change is approved | A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element | Draft of a new major version, and the consumers are notified |
| Baselined | An owner changes its answer | X6 | Draft of a new minor or major version, and the fake is updated |

| Step | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Being authored | A consumed row has no published name | X1 | The row carries the placeholder and the gap, and the draft continues |
| In review | An element or a row reaches a foreign schema, base or topic | X3, X7 | The baseline is refused |
| Ready to tag | A consumed row has no fake | X4 | Not tagged, and the review reopens |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| Tech lead of rwb-valuation | Authors the baseline, resolves the calculation elements, the workflow elements and the decision-record element, and signs the tag |
| Owner of rwb-source-data (P1) | Reviews the account, balance and freshness rows, and publishes the operation names when they exist |
| Owner of rwb-decision (P7) | Reviews the rule-set row and the decision-record element with the platform library |
| Owner of rwb-case (P3) | Reviews the case and account-set row and the case element of the answer |
| Owner of rwb-access (P4) | Reviews the authorise row and the capability area and right of the declaration |
| Platform library owner (RWB-PLT-E1027, RWB-PLT-N001) | Publishes the decision-record element and the composite route the baseline references |
| Reviewer of the access matrix | Confirms the capability area and the right of the declared operation |
| Any team | Reads the baseline and its fakes from Day 1; no team may change a declared shape outside the lifecycle of s9 |

No person is named anywhere in this document; the roles above are the roles of the run.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-valuation (S1); base `/api/recovery/valuation/v1` (DP-13). This is the operation the legacy story names in its Endpoints table, and the only one this baseline declares.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/route` | `RouteRequest` in and `Approval` out (API-S1-001); the answer declares the payoff, `payoff_as_at`, `settlement_range_low`, `settlement_range_high`, `floor_price`, the rule id, the rule version and the calculation state | Treatment and offer, right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header; the stored answer is returned on a repeat |
| None | A calculation or range operation of its own | No source publishes a second operation for the calculation, so no path is declared and the calculation rides the route answer | Not applicable | Not applicable |

The element name of the payoff amount itself is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2620; ASM-4322); the other seven element names are the names the routing workbook uses (Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, R-SET-02, R-SET-04 and R-SET-05). The two valuation operations of the map are S1's and are the appraisal-intake slice, not this baseline's.

The error envelope of the declared operation: 400 for a malformed request, 401 for an unauthenticated call, 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope case, 409 on a second submission under a new key, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for an invalid element, and 503 when the decision library or a consumed contract does not answer, in one problem document with a code, a message ID and a correlation reference.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Document.** `04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-S1 rwb-valuation (Valuation and route)/RWB S1 E4006 CON Calculate the payoff and settlement range - contract v1.md`, with the schema and the examples in the service contract folder of RWB-S1-E4006.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Sections and owners of the review.** The document is written in nine parts: the provided operation and its eight calculation elements, the five consumed rows, the empty publication, the workflow and its activities, the tables, the fakes, the call-type summary, the data elements and the lifecycle. Each part is reviewed by the owner of the rows it names, and the tag waits for every reviewer.

**Compatibility check.** The schema is published as JSON Schema with `additionalProperties: false` on the closed objects, and the check runs on three inputs: the previous tag, the new draft and a corpus of recorded answers from the fakes. A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element fails the check and forces a new major version (C1, BR3).

**Fakes.** One per consumed row plus the composite route, each built from the document and not from the real service, so that a fake can be published before its owner's build finishes (C6).

**Done when.** The seven criteria pass, the five reviewer roles have closed their comments, the compatibility check passes on the tag, the eight fakes are published with their documented answers, and RWB-S1-E4006-APP and the wave 3 harness can start against the tag with no open shape question.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the baseline: the range bounds, the floor, the freshness limit and the closed lists are referenced with their identifier, list or version, never enumerated as a constant or a default.
- No personal data in any element, fake, example or log: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the service's own view: the baseline declares no `v_ace_*` copy and no ACE table, and the balances appear only as the rwb-source-data data product (DP-05).
- The case stays with rwb-case, the rule set and the ledger with rwb-decision, and the treatment record with rwb-treatment: none is declared as this service's own.
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; no document, module or test names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no monolith base `/api/recovery/v1`, no account copy table, no shared job table, no Quartz row, no Schedule, no foreign schema and no event published by this baseline.
- Additive only: a breaking change needs a new major version and a re-tag, and the code never moves ahead of the document (BR3).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the application slice of RWB-E4-006 split out for rwb-valuation. The two legacy criteria this story owns are copied word for word with their origin tag. The payoff is read from the ACE balances of the account on the rwb-source-data contract or on this service's own SELECT-only view (DP-05) and is not copied anywhere; the settlement range and the floor come from the rule set in force at its version; the result is written to the local decision record with the rule id and version before the answer leaves (DP-03); the answer travels on `POST /cases/{caseId}/route` on base `/api/recovery/valuation/v1` (DP-13) and reaches SCR-13 Route decision through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). No source gives S1 a table for the payoff, the range or the floor (GAP-2615; ASM-4317), publishes the names of the two reads (GAP-2616; ASM-4318), fixes the source of the balances or the composition of the payoff (GAP-2617; ASM-4319) or fixes the freshness limit and the floor method (GAP-2618; ASM-4320); the trigger set is FSD wording with no event and no job behind it (GAP-2619; ASM-4321). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner**, I want **the Workbench to work out the payoff from the balances ACE holds for the account and the settlement range from the rules, with the floor applied**, so that **the route is chosen on expected return with reasons**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E4-006. It owns:

- the legacy criteria AC1 and AC2 of the key, copied verbatim, and the rules, messages, screens and tests they carry;
- the calculation step inside `RouteDecisionWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-valuation`: the payoff at the ACE batch date and the settlement range with the floor applied, computed per assessment, never stored as a constant;
- the read of `total_balance`, `past_due_amount` and `collections_fee` of each account of the case from the ACE account data product, one hop, 2 s, read only, with no `v_ace_*` copy and no balance of this service (DP-05);
- the read of the settlement route set in force, with the range bounds, the floor and the rule id and version (DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015, owner P7);
- the local decision record of the step, written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the caller's transaction before the answer is composed (DP-03);
- the calculation elements of the answer of `POST /cases/{caseId}/route` on `/api/recovery/valuation/v1`, whose shape is baselined by RWB-S1-E4006-CON (DP-13);
- the states of SCR-13 Route decision that the calculation produces, reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

It does not own: the route recommendation and its reasons, which are FEAT-VAL-07 and its story; the approval and the case move, which are the route-decision submission slice of RWB-E4-005 (RWB-S1-E4005-APP) and rwb-case; the offer built inside the range, which is rwb-treatment's (S2) on R-SET-04 and the settlement stories; the ACE balances and their freshness, which are rwb-source-data's (P1); the rule package, its approval and the central ledger, which are rwb-decision's (P7); the roles and scopes behind the right, which are rwb-access's (P4); the composite route and the screen field list, which are RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the fresh-payoff request to EAPI and the interfaces behind it, which are rwb-integration's (P2).

##### 2. Business rationale

The route of a case is a decision about money, and it can only be taken on expected return if two numbers are on the table: what the bank will collect if it calls the account now, and how far it may go in a settlement without breaching the floor. Today both numbers sit in an officer's account plan, read from ALS through the Workbench's own copies of the account, and the range is looked up by hand. D-RCV-60 puts the balances where they already are — ACE, through the contract of rwb-source-data or this service's own SELECT-only view (DP-05) — and puts the range and the floor where the bank governs them: in the rule set in force, read with its version.

The three things the target changes, and nothing else:

- **the balances are read, not held.** This service keeps no loan account copy and no balance (ADR-010, D-RCV-35 U1); the payoff is computed from `total_balance`, `past_due_amount` and `collections_fee` at the ACE batch date and is not persisted as a second fact.
- **the range is governed data.** The bounds and the floor are values in force with a version, referenced by identifier and never written in code (BR-S1-006); a change of limit is a release of the rule set, not a build.
- **the decision is on record.** The payoff, its as-at date, the range and the floor are recorded with the rule id and version in the caller's transaction, and a calculation that cannot be recorded does not proceed (DP-03).

Two boundaries are recorded rather than assumed. No source gives S1 a table for the payoff, the range or the floor: the ownership rows give S1 no table, TSD S1 T3.1 declares only `valuation` and `score`, and the legacy data table names `v_ace_account`, `treatment`, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row`, none of which is this service's (GAP-2615; ASM-4317). And the FSD's phrase "payoff from ALS" and the legacy story's "from v_ace_account" are the same read after the ACE re-base, while the composition of the payoff out of the three balances is published by no source (GAP-2617; ASM-4319).

Serves the route decision of EP04 in wave 3 on release 28 February 2027 (tentative). No business value is invented: the amounts of AC1, the messages and the rights are the values the legacy story and the FSD already carry.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S1-E4006-CON is published: base `/api/recovery/valuation/v1`, the calculation elements of `POST /cases/{caseId}/route`, the error set, the `Idempotency-Key` header and the fakes. This story builds against that baseline and never against a sibling service.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the decision-record writer with `@Transactional(propagation = MANDATORY)`, its refusal and failure messages, and the `decision_record` DDL template applied in `rwb_valuation` (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the composite route that serves SCR-13 from the case read and this service's answer, one hop each, read only (DP-19).
- The `rwb_valuation` schema and its login exist from the platform database story; SELECT on the ACE account data product — the rwb-source-data contract or `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_batch_status` — is granted and on nothing else (ASM-4318, ASM-4319).
- The settlement route set — R-SET-01, R-SET-02, R-SET-03, R-SET-04 and R-SET-05 — is in force with its rule id and version for the business date, and the range bounds and the floor are values of that set (Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; GAP-2618; ASM-4320).
- The freshness limit of `payoff_as_at` and the batch-date rule of the ACE data product are reference values in force for the business date; they are read, never constant (VR-S1-006-1; BR-S1-006).
- FSD S1 and TSD S1 carry status "In review" and no approval is needed to build against a Draft baseline; the split proceeds at status Draft (ASM-4323).
- The story has only CON build dependencies, so it is Day 1 by rule (§R5.7 rule 8).

##### 4. Flow

1. The case owner opens SCR-13 Route decision for a case and prepares the route decision; the browser calls `POST /cases/{caseId}/route` on the service base through gateway-bff (DP-13, DP-19).
2. The guard resolves right U in the capability area Treatment and offer from the contract's `security` declaration and applies the scope (TSD S1 T6.1).
3. The freshness gate runs: VR-S1-006-1 reads `v_ace_batch_status` for the account product and, when the product is from an earlier date, the step stops with MSG-P1-001 and writes nothing.
4. The service resolves the accounts of the case and reads `account_key`, `account_code`, `account_status`, `total_balance`, `past_due_amount` and `collections_fee` for each account at the ACE batch date through the rwb-source-data contract (DP-05).
5. The payoff is computed by the calculation in force from those three balances; the formula, the fee inclusion and the rounding are governed values read with their version and are not written in code (BR-S1-006; GAP-2617; ASM-4319).
6. `payoff_as_at` is stamped from the ACE batch date of the data product. When it is older than the freshness limit, R-SET-03 blocks the step and a fresh payoff is requested through rwb-integration (P2); this service writes nothing on that path.
7. The settlement route set in force is read with its rule id and version, and the range bounds and the floor are taken from it; the floor is applied to the range so that no offered amount below it leaves this step unflagged (R-SET-01, R-SET-05).
8. One transaction opens: the local `decision_record` is written with the rule id, the rule version, the payoff, `payoff_as_at`, the range bounds, the floor and the facts reference, and the request's idempotency row is written in the same transaction (DP-03).
9. The transaction commits and the answer to the caller carries the payoff, its as-at date, the two range bounds, the floor, the rule version and the state; a missing payoff or a missing floor holds the calculation as UNMATCHED_EXCEPTION, names the missing field and raises a task for the case owner (R-SET-25).
10. A repeated request with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the first answer and writes no second record.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A role without right U in Treatment and offer, or a case outside the scope | 403 before any read; the refusal is the guard library's answer and the log carries the role and the operation, never a personal field | MSG-P4-002 | Section 10; TC-E4-006-03 |
| X2 | The account data product is stale for the business date | The step stops before a balance is used: nothing is calculated, nothing is written | MSG-P1-001 | TC-S1-E4006-APP-02 |
| X3 | The decision record cannot be written | The transaction rolls back: no record, no idempotency row, no answer; the caller may retry with the same key | MSG-P7-003 | AC2; TC-E4-006-02, TC-E4-006-04 |
| X4 | The account of the case has no row in the ACE account product | No payoff is computed, the range is not offered, and the screen states that no balance is held; nothing is invented | None | R-SET-25; TC-S1-E4006-APP-01 |
| X5 | `payoff_as_at` is older than the freshness limit | R-SET-03 blocks the calculation at PAYOFF_AND_RANGE_SET and a fresh payoff is requested through rwb-integration; this service writes nothing | None | TC-S1-E4006-APP-02 |
| X6 | The rule set in force carries no floor, or no range for the route set | The calculation holds as UNMATCHED_EXCEPTION, names the missing value and raises a task for the case owner (R-SET-25) | MSG-GEN-001 | TC-S1-E4006-APP-01 |
| X7 | A required element of the request is absent or outside its list | 422 with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field; the transaction never opens | MSG-GEN-001 | Section 12.1 |
| X8 | The rwb-source-data read or the rule read does not answer inside 2 s | 503 with the platform problem body; nothing is written and the workflow retries on its own schedule | None | Section 12.2 |

X1 to X3 are the legacy paths carried onto the split: X1 is the permission check of the legacy story, X2 the freshness rule the FSD gives the feature, X3 legacy AC2. X4 to X8 are the paths the read of two contracts adds. A refusal under X1, X2 or X7 writes nothing, because the guard, the gate and the validator run before the transaction opens.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on Day 1 against the RWB-S1-E4006-CON fake, the decision-record writer fake and the composite-route fake, with a balance fixture and a rule-set fixture; needs no live ACE, rwb-decision or rwb-case |
| Negotiable | The component names, the internal method boundary and the shape of the calculation object are this story's choice; the operation, the element names of the routing workbook, the messages and the rights are fixed |
| Valuable | The officer sees the payoff and the range with the floor before choosing a route, and the bank can prove which rule version produced them |
| Estimable | One calculation, two reads, one library adapter, one transaction, one answer and one freshness gate |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion and each exception path is one automated test on fixtures and fakes; the two reads are contract-level |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Calculate the payoff and settlement range

  Background:
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns the settlement route set in force with its rule id and rule version
    Given account "A-0001" belongs to case "RC-2026-000401" and the ACE account data product is fresh at the business date

  Scenario: AC1 Calculate the payoff and settlement range (legacy RWB-E4-006 AC1)
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns total balance 1240000, past due amount 86000 and collections fee 4500 for account "A-0001" at the ACE batch date 2026-12-14
    Given v_ace_account holds total balance 1240000, past due amount 86000 and collections fee 4500 for account "A-0001" at the ACE batch date 2026-12-14
    When the case owner prepares the route decision
    Then the Workbench works out the payoff from the balances in v_ace_account and the settlement range from the rules, with the floor applied
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E4-006 AC2)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

**Target reading.** Both criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E4-006 word for word, with their origin tag added and nothing else changed: the repeated `Then`, `v_ace_account`, `the case owner prepares the route decision` and `the action is taken` all stand. The cross-service part of AC1 is mocked, so AC1 carries one `Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns <x>` line holding the legacy amounts unchanged, and that added line is the only addition to the criterion. AC2 needs none, because the decision-record library is local. What the legacy lines describe happens in four places in the target: the balances are ACE's and arrive on the rwb-source-data contract or this service's own view, read only (DP-05); the range and the floor are the settlement route set at its version (R-SET-01, R-SET-05); "the decision log" is the local `decision_record` written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the same transaction (DP-03), with the central `decision_log_entry` ledger of rwb-decision behind it; and the answer is served on `POST /cases/{caseId}/route` on `/api/recovery/valuation/v1` (DP-13), composed into SCR-13 by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The word "system" in AC1 is kept: the calculation is unattended, as FSD S1 A2.6.3.3 states.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The payoff is computed from the balances ACE holds for the account and is never read from a copy, a staging table or a balance of this service | legacy RWB-E4-006 story; D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010; DP-05 |
| BR2 | The three balances used are `total_balance`, `past_due_amount` and `collections_fee` at the ACE batch date; no other balance is added and no balance is stored | legacy RWB-E4-006 AC1; Physical Schema v6 DF-ACE-020, DF-ACE-022 and DF-ACE-024 |
| BR3 | The settlement range and the floor are values of the rule set in force, read with the rule id and version; the floor is applied to the range and no amount below it leaves unflagged | legacy RWB-E4-006 AC1; R-SET-01, R-SET-05; BR-S1-006 |
| BR4 | A stale account data product stops the step with MSG-P1-001 and nothing is calculated | VR-S1-006-1; FSD S1 A2.6.3.1 |
| BR5 | `payoff_as_at` older than the freshness limit blocks the calculation and a fresh payoff is requested through rwb-integration | R-SET-02, R-SET-03 |
| BR6 | A missing payoff or a missing floor holds the calculation as UNMATCHED_EXCEPTION, names the missing field and raises a task for the case owner | R-SET-25 |
| BR7 | The result is recorded in the local decision record with the rule id and version before the answer is composed, and a result that cannot be recorded does not proceed | legacy RWB-E4-006 AC1, AC2; DP-03; REQ-S1-004 |
| BR8 | No value a business person may change is written in code: the formula, the range bounds, the floor, the freshness limit and the lists are values in force read with their version | BR-S1-006; FSD S1 A2.6.3.1 |
| BR9 | The step needs right U in the capability area Treatment and offer; the check is the platform guard library's and no role list is written here | TSD S1 T6.1; legacy permission checks |
| BR10 | This service writes no case table, no treatment row and no rule row, and reads no table of another service | DP-01; GAP-2615 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 and BR2 are the `AccountBalanceReadClient` and the absence of any account repository. BR3, BR5 and BR6 are the rule-set adapter and the three named conditions of the settlement route set. BR4 is the freshness gate in front of the read. BR7 is the `DecisionRecordAdapter` and the one transaction. BR8 is the reference-data reads and the Drools runtime of the service template. BR9 is the contract's `security` section and the guard library. BR10 is the schema boundary and the absence of a cross-schema key.

##### 9. State transitions

No case status is owned here; the case and its route state are moved by `CaseWorkflow` on rwb-case and by the route-decision submission slice of RWB-E4-005. The only lifecycle this story writes is the calculation and its record.

| Object | From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Calculation | absent | the route decision is prepared | the account product is fresh and the rule set is in force | payoff and range calculated, `payoff_as_at` stamped |
| Calculation | calculated | the result is recorded | the decision record is written in the same transaction | recorded with the rule id and version, and answered |
| Calculation | calculated | the record cannot be written | X3 | nothing written, the transaction rolled back, MSG-P7-003 |
| Calculation | absent | the account product is stale | X2 | stays absent with MSG-P1-001 |
| Calculation | calculated | `payoff_as_at` is older than the freshness limit | R-SET-03 | blocked at PAYOFF_AND_RANGE_SET, no range offered, a fresh payoff requested |
| Calculation | calculated | the payoff or the floor is missing | R-SET-25 | UNMATCHED_EXCEPTION with the missing field named and a task raised |
| Calculation | recorded | the route is approved as settlement and the offer is prepared | R-SET-04, R-SET-05 | re-read for the offer step; the re-read is rwb-treatment's call and not this story's write |

The calculation carries no `state` of its own beyond the standard record lifecycle of the decision record (TSD S1 T3.0). It has no workflow state machine: it either commits its one transaction or writes nothing.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The rwb-valuation squad, service identity of `rwb_valuation` | Runs the calculation on the case's behalf; holds SELECT on the ACE account product only |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner (right U) | Prepares the route decision of a case in scope and thereby triggers the calculation |
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer; RW-SPECIAL, hardship and vulnerability specialist; RW-GUARANT, guarantee officer (right U) | The same right in the same capability area, on the cases in scope |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-CREDCOMM, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL, RW-CONDUCT, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE (right R) | Read the payoff, the range and the floor on SCR-13; they trigger nothing here |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-AGENT | Read as service identities through the same checks |
| rwb-source-data (P1) | Owns the ACE account data product, its freshness and the `v_ace_*` views it grants |
| rwb-decision (P7) | Owns the settlement route set, its approval, its version and the central ledger |
| rwb-access (P4) | Owns the roles, the rights and the scope data the guard answers with |
| rwb-integration (P2) | Owns the fresh-payoff request to EAPI that R-SET-03 asks for |
| No delegation of authority level applies | The story calculates and records; it approves nothing and moves no case |

No credential and no personal name appears in the request, the record, the workflow input or the logs. The account is held as its ACE business key and never as a customer identifier.

| DF-ACE-020, DF-ACE-022, DF-ACE-024 | `recovery.v_ace_account` | total_balance, past_due_amount, collections_fee | Read only: the three balances of the payoff |

| `v_ace_batch_status` (no DF id in the legacy story) | `recovery.v_ace_batch_status` (view owned by rwb-source-data) | the product and its date | Read only: the freshness gate VR-S1-006-1 and the `payoff_as_at` stamp |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | `rule_row` (`rwb_decision`, owner P7) | rule_id, rule_version, route_set, from_state, event_code and 11 more | Not read directly: the evaluated package returns the rule id, the version, the range bounds and the floor |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | `decision_record` (local, in `rwb_valuation`) and `decision_log_entry` (`rwb_decision`, owner P7) | all fields of the record | Write the local record through the library in the same transaction; the central ledger is sealed by P7 |

The payoff, the range and the floor are held in this story only as the outcome of the local decision record and as elements of the answer; no table of this service holds them, because the ownership rows give S1 no table and TSD S1 T3.1 declares no payoff, range or floor table (GAP-2615; ASM-4317). No foreign key points into a view, no column of another service's table is joined, and no balance is copied into `rwb_valuation` (DP-01). **No personal data** appears in the record, the answer or the logs.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-valuation (S1); base `/api/recovery/valuation/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the calculation part of the route answer; the published shape, the error set and the fakes are declared by RWB-S1-E4006-CON.

| Method | Path | Request and response | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/route` | `RouteRequest` in, `Approval` out (TSD S1 T-A.2); the answer carries the payoff, `payoff_as_at`, `settlement_range_low`, `settlement_range_high`, `floor_price`, the rule id, the rule version and the calculation state | Treatment and offer U, scope applied, through the guard library | `Idempotency-Key` header required |

The element names of the range, the floor and the as-at date are the names the routing workbook uses; the element name of the payoff amount itself is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2620; ASM-4322). No second operation is claimed: the FSD lists one endpoint for the feature and it is the route operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The account and balance data-product read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2616; ASM-4318)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | `total_balance`, `past_due_amount` and `collections_fee` of each account of the case at the ACE batch date, with the product date; faked |
| The freshness read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2616; ASM-4318)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The account product and its batch date for VR-S1-006-1; faked |
| The rule-set-in-force read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2616; ASM-4318)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The settlement route set at its version, with the range bounds, the floor and the rule id; faked |
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case and its account set, to resolve the accounts to read; faked |
| `POST /authorise` | `/api/recovery/access/v1` | P4 rwb-access | The capability area, the right and the scope of the caller; faked |

Each row is one hop, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). This story has no C dependency, so every row is built against its fake.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The ownership rows give rwb-valuation no event: the topic `rwb.valuation.events.v1` exists with its `.retry` and `.dlt` under the naming rule, but this story declares no event, no event name and no outbox row on it. The only publication of the step is the decision record, which the library of DP-03 sends to `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and that is the library's publication and not an event of this service.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. FSD S1 A2.6.2 step 1 names the trigger set as "a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer" and no source publishes an event name for any of them; the ownership rows give S1 no job and no event, so the calculation runs inside the route-decision command and its freshness is proved by VR-S1-006-1 (GAP-2619; ASM-4321).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RouteDecisionWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per assessment, continues-as-new | `rwb-valuation` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the account set and the rule set in force; signals: the freshness answer of the account product and the rule version |
| `calculatePayoffAndRange` | Activity | `rwb-valuation` | The account set and the business date in; the payoff, `payoff_as_at`, the range bounds, the floor, the rule id and version and the decision record out, in one transaction |
| `readAccountBalances` | Activity | `rwb-valuation` | The account keys in; the three balances and the product date out; no write |

The activity names are a design choice of this story; the baseline RWB-S1-E4006-CON carries them so that the workflow history stays stable across the two documents.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The ownership rows give S1 no job, and this story declares no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job. The phrase "a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer" would be a Schedule of this service if a source named one, and none does (GAP-2619; ASM-4321).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| None | S1 declares no payoff, range or floor table | The ownership rows give S1 no table and TSD S1 T3.1 declares only `valuation` and `score`; the outcome lives in the decision record (GAP-2615; ASM-4317) |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_valuation` | The local decision record of DP-03, declared through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_valuation` | The key of the repeated command and the answer it holds |

No migration, index or column is added by this story, and no table of another owner is declared: `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_batch_status` (P1), `rule_row`, `decision_log_entry` and `approval` (P7), `treatment` (S2) and `recovery_case` and `timer` (P3) are named by their owners.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Build steps.**

1. `PayoffCalculator`: the payoff from `total_balance`, `past_due_amount` and `collections_fee` by the calculation in force, with the formula, the inclusion and the rounding read from governed values (BR2, BR8).
2. `RangeResolver`: the settlement route set in force, the range bounds, the floor and the rule id and version; a missing floor or range raises UNMATCHED_EXCEPTION (BR3, BR6).
3. `FreshnessGate`: VR-S1-006-1 on the account product and the `payoff_as_at` limit of R-SET-03 (BR4, BR5).
4. `AccountBalanceReadClient`, `RuleSetClient` and the rwb-case and rwb-access clients on the contract and its fake (section 12.2).
5. `DecisionRecordAdapter` on RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the same transaction as the answer (BR7).
6. `calculatePayoffAndRange` and `readAccountBalances` as activities of `RouteDecisionWorkflow` (section 12.5).
7. The calculation elements of the answer and their state, and SCR-13 through the composite route fake (section 12.1).
8. The idempotency row and the repeat answer (section 9).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Done when.** AC1 and AC2 pass on the fakes, the boundary and freshness tests pass, the record carries the rule id and version, and the answer holds the payoff, its as-of date, the two range bounds and the floor with no constant in code.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Treatment and offer right calls the operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required element of `RouteRequest` is absent or invalid, or a governed value the calculation needs is missing | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE account data product is stale after a late or failed batch (VR-S1-006-1) | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The four message IDs are those of the legacy story and of FSD S1 A2.6.3.1, copied unchanged. No message text is written in this story beyond these rows.

##### 15. Screens and states

The calculation feeds SCR-13 Route decision through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

| Screen | States | What the screen shows from this step |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-13 Route decision | Loading; recommendation; overridden; submitted | The payoff and its as-at date, the range bounds, the floor, the rule version, and the calculation state: calculated, blocked on a stale product, or an unmatched exception naming the missing value |

No screen is built here: the field list, the merge order and the states of the composite route are RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the recommendation and override elements are the sibling stories'.

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID; the `-ITG` copies belong to the wave 3 harness.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the formula, the range bounds, the floor, the freshness limit and the lists are read with their version and never written as a constant, a default or a fixture in production code (BR-S1-006).
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs or logs: the account is an ACE business key, and the payoff, the range and the floor are amounts and codes only.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the service's own `v_ace_*` view, SELECT only, with no copy and no cross-schema key (DP-05, DP-01).
- The case stays with rwb-case, the rule set and the ledger with rwb-decision, and the treatment record with rwb-treatment: none is declared here.
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; no document or test names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element returns: no monolith base `/api/recovery/v1`, no account copy table, no Quartz row, no Schedule and no data-lake extract (DP-17).
- A calculation that cannot be recorded does not proceed (BR7).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract slice of RWB-E4-007, the baseline the route-scoring and recommendation step of rwb-valuation builds against on Day 1. The baseline declares the recommendation elements of the route-decision operation `POST /cases/{caseId}/route` (API-S1-001) on `/api/recovery/valuation/v1` as an additive slice of the operation RWB-S1-E4001-CON baselines (DP-13), the five consumed rows of rwb-source-data, rwb-agent, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access (DP-05), the recommendation element and the decision-record library that carries it (DP-03), the elements of `RouteDecisionWorkflow` and its two activities, the rights, the error envelope and the fakes; it publishes no event, because the ownership rows give S1 none. The operation names of the five consumed rows are not published (GAP-2621; ASM-4324); the recommendation element set, the reasons and the alternatives are not published and the operation already carries another slice of this service (GAP-2622; ASM-4325); no S1 route-decision rule package, decision code, confidence threshold or route-code mapping is in force (GAP-2623; ASM-4326); the agent client of DP-20 and its C row are outside this key's pattern set (GAP-2625; ASM-4328); no source fixes the store of the recommendation (GAP-2626; ASM-4329); the mapping of `LOV-ROUTE` onto the eight routes is not published (GAP-2628; ASM-4331). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead of rwb-valuation**, I want **the published contract baseline of the route-scoring and recommendation step of rwb-valuation, being its recommendation elements on the route operation, its five consumed rows, its decision-record element, its workflow elements, its rights, its error envelope and its fakes, fixed and tagged before the build starts**, so that **the application story and the five owners it consumes can build and test on Day 1 against one versioned surface instead of guessing the shape of a neighbour's answer or of the agent's recommendation**.

This is the contract slice of legacy RWB-E4-007. It owns:

- the document that fixes the recommendation elements of `POST /cases/{caseId}/route` (API-S1-001) on base `/api/recovery/valuation/v1`: the recommended route code, the expected return of each route, the reasons, the alternatives, the confidence, the model codes and versions, the rule version, the `Idempotency-Key` header and the scope rule (DP-13);
- the five consumed rows: the COLLINS score data product of rwb-source-data, the route-agent call of rwb-agent, the case state and open route set of rwb-case, the rule-in-force and decision-log read of rwb-decision, and the authorise operation of rwb-access, each with its owner, its use, its budget and a placeholder where the name is not published (DP-05);
- the recommendation element and the decision-record element, the library that carries it and the shared topic it reaches (DP-03);
- the elements of `RouteDecisionWorkflow` and its two activities on task queue `rwb-valuation`;
- the subject of SCR-13 Route decision, one hop through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19);
- the fakes and their documented answers, including the low-confidence, out-of-set and no-answer answers of the agent;
- the naming, versioning and boundary rule of the baseline: one base, one topic, one queue, one login, no foreign schema, no monolith base, additive only.

It does not own: the scoring, the ranking, the recommendation, the decision records and the screen behaviour, which are RWB-S1-E4007-APP; the appraisal slice of the same operation, which is RWB-S1-E4001-CON; the COLLINS call and the return it records per route, which are RWB-S1-E4005-CON; the payoff and the settlement range, which are RWB-S1-E4006-CON; the approval elements of the operation, which are RWB-S1-E4008-CON and its siblings; the agent runtime, its models and its autonomy, which are rwb-agent's (P10) and its own baseline; the ACE score, collateral and account facts, which are rwb-source-data's (P1); the case of record and its route states, which are rwb-case's (P3); the rule rows and the central ledger, which are rwb-decision's (P7); the roles and scopes, which are rwb-access's (P4); the composite route and the screen field list, which are RWB-PLT-N001-CON; and the deployment, which is the operations story of this legacy key.

##### 2. Business rationale

A contract baseline is what lets two teams and five owners start together. Legacy RWB-E4-007 asks for a recommendation with its reasons and its alternatives, recorded with the rule version, so the step reads a score per route from one service, calls an agent in another, checks the case in a third, reads the rule version in a fourth and writes one record. Without a tagged baseline each of those shapes would be discovered at the first integration instead of at the review.

The three rules the baseline applies:

- **the owner publishes, the consumer adapts.** Every consumed row names its owner, its use and its 2 s budget, and every row whose name is not published carries the placeholder and its gap (GAP-2621; ASM-4324).
- **one hop, one budget, one check.** Each consumed row is a single hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker, the score is never read from a table, and no chain runs through a second service (DP-05, ADR-020). The agent answer is declared with the schema check and the confidence element the caller applies, so the shape of a refusal is part of the surface (NFR-055).
- **additive only.** A new optional element is a minor version; a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version and a new document. The recommendation elements are added to the operation another baseline declares as exactly such a minor version, and no path, no base and no queue changes (GAP-2622).

The business outcome the baseline protects is the one FEAT-VAL-07 states: the route agent recommends a route and states the reasons and the alternatives. The baseline states no outcome and no business value of its own, and no criterion here asserts that a route is recommended.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The Ownership Map rows for S1 are in force: `POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations`, `POST /assets/{assetKey}/valuations` and `POST /cases/{caseId}/route`; no table, no event, no job, and one workflow, `RouteDecisionWorkflow`. This baseline declares the third operation only, and only its recommendation slice.
- The service naming is fixed: schema `rwb_valuation`, one login of its own, base `/api/recovery/valuation/v1`, topic `rwb.valuation.events.v1` with `.retry` and `.dlt`, task queue `rwb-valuation` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.valuation`.
- TSD S1 is the shape of record for the service: T-A.1 gives API-S1-001 with right Treatment and offer U; T-A.2 gives `RouteRequest` in, `Approval` out, errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 and the `Idempotency-Key`; T3.1 gives `score` as REUSE ACE with DF-DEC-019 to DF-DEC-027; T3.2 gives `LOV-ROUTE`; T6.1 gives the capability area and its rights.
- The platform CON stories are published: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for the decision record (DP-03) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the composite route (DP-19). A CON story has no build dependency (R5.7 rule 1), so both sit in the preconditions of this baseline and not in its H row.
- RWB-S1-E4001-CON has baselined the same operation with the appraisal and approval elements; this baseline adds the recommendation elements to it in a minor version and declares no second path (GAP-2622; ASM-4325).
- The agent row names rwb-agent as its owner, the route agent as its subject and D6.3 as the sub-decision it serves; its client contract of DP-20, `RWB-P10-TE013-CON`, is not in this key's pattern set, so the row is declared with the placeholder and the gap (GAP-2625; ASM-4328).
- No S1 route-decision rule package, decision code or confidence threshold is in force, and the mapping of `LOV-ROUTE` onto the eight routes is not published; the baseline references each with its identifier and asserts none (GAP-2623, GAP-2628; ASM-4326, ASM-4331).
- No approval is needed to publish a Draft baseline; the document is baselined by its own review and the build waits only for its tag.

##### 4. Flow

1. The author drafts the baseline from the Ownership Map rows of the context pack, TSD S1 T-A.1, T-A.2, T3.1, T3.2 and T6.1, the FSD S1 A2.7 rules, the Agent Catalog row of the route agent and the DP table.
2. The recommendation elements are declared against the operation RWB-S1-E4001-CON already publishes, as an additive minor version of it.
3. Every consumed row is declared with its owner, its use, its budget and a placeholder where the name is not published.
4. The agent row is declared with the sub-decision it serves, the check the caller applies to its answer and the refusal shapes the caller must recognise.
5. The decision-record element is declared with the library of DP-03, the shared topic and the transaction it joins.
6. The workflow and its two activities are declared with their input, their signals and their outcome elements.
7. The schema, the open lists and the closed lists are published; a closed list is referenced with its identifier and its version and is never enumerated in code.
8. The fakes are declared with their documented answers, one per consumed row, one per agent refusal shape and one for the composite route.
9. The compatibility check runs on the draft against the previous tag of the operation: a breaking change fails it, and the additive slice passes.
10. The document goes to review as Draft; the reviewers are the owners of the five consumed rows, the tech lead of the service and the reviewer of the access matrix.
11. On the review's close the document is tagged; the application story starts against the tag and the fakes, and the code never moves ahead of the document.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A consumer asks for a shape the sources do not publish | The row carries the placeholder and its gap; no path, no element and no model code is invented | C3, C4 |
| X2 | A change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element of the operation | The compatibility check fails and the document needs a new major version | C1 |
| X3 | The recommendation slice is declared as a second operation, a second path or a second base | The review refuses the baseline: one operation, one base, additive only | C2, C7 |
| X4 | A consumed row has no fake, or its fake has no documented answer | The baseline is not tagged and the application story cannot start | C6 |
| X5 | The rights of the operation are not a row of the access matrix | The recommendation elements are not declared and the error set stays incomplete | C5 |
| X6 | An owner changes its documented answer after the tag | The owner publishes a version, this document follows in a minor or major version, and the fake is updated | X2 |
| X7 | A row declares a model code, a threshold, a weight, a return or a route mapping the sources do not publish | The element is declared as a reference with its identifier and its version, and never as a literal | C4, C5 |

X1 to X3 are the paths of an incomplete or misplaced slice, X4 to X6 the paths of a baseline moving under a build, and X7 the no-invented-value rule.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs no build, no live service and no approval; starts on Day 1 and is finished before the application story's first line |
| Negotiable | The wording, the section order and the fake data are this story's choice; the path, the request, the answer, the rights and the error set are fixed by TSD S1 |
| Valuable | Two teams and five owners build at once against one tagged surface, and the first integration finds behaviour, not shape |
| Estimable | One document, one provided operation and one additive element group, five consumed rows, one decision-record element, one workflow with two activities, one subject of SCR-13 and seven fakes |
| Small | Finished inside a week; the review is the only gate |
| Testable | Every criterion is a document check that runs in the contract test suite, plus the compatibility check on the published schema |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the route-scoring and recommendation step

  Scenario: C1 The baseline validates and only additive changes pass (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published schema, the element list and the closed lists of the baseline
    When a change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element
    Then the compatibility check fails and the change needs a new major version
    And a change that adds an optional element passes as a minor version

  Scenario: C2 The recommendation elements are published as an additive slice of the route operation (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operation table of the baseline
    When POST /cases/{caseId}/route on /api/recovery/valuation/v1 is read
    Then it names RouteRequest in, Approval out, the recommendation elements, the Idempotency-Key header and the scope rule of T-A.2
    And it declares no second path, no second base and no second operation

  Scenario: C3 The five consumed rows carry their owners, their budgets and their placeholders (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed operation table of the baseline
    When the rows of rwb-source-data, rwb-agent, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access are read
    Then each row names its owner, its use, one hop and a 2 s budget
    And where the operation name is not published the row carries the placeholder and the gap identifier and no path

  Scenario: C4 The recommendation, the alternatives and the reasons are declared as elements with their sources (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the recommendation elements and the data-element table of the baseline
    When the recommended route, the return of each route, the reasons, the alternatives, the confidence and the versions are read
    Then each element carries its type, its nullability and its source
    And the route code references LOV-ROUTE and no model code, return, weight or threshold is declared as a literal

  Scenario: C5 The rights, the error envelope and the refusal shapes of the agent are declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operations and the consumed rows the baseline provides
    When the rights, the error set and the agent refusal shapes are read
    Then the operation names the capability area Treatment and offer and the right of the access matrix
    And the error set names 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503 in one problem envelope
    And the agent row names the schema check, the confidence element and the fallback the caller applies

  Scenario: C6 The decision-record element, the workflow elements and the fakes are declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the baseline document
    When the decision-record element, the workflow table and the fake table are read
    Then the element names RWB-PLT-E1027-CON as its library, the shared topic and the transaction it joins
    And RouteDecisionWorkflow and its two activities name their input, their signals and their task queue
    And every consumed row has a fake with a documented answer, including the low-confidence, out-of-set and no-answer answers of the agent and the stopped decision-record stub

  Scenario: C7 The naming, the publication and the boundary of the baseline hold (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the base, the topic, the queue, the schema and the outbox of the baseline
    When the document is checked against the naming rule, the ownership rows and the event list
    Then one base, one topic, one queue and one login are declared and no monolith base and no foreign topic appear
    And no event is published, because the ownership rows give S1 none, and no Schedule is declared
```

The seven criteria are new to this run and are tagged as such. They test the contract deliverable only: the schema, the elements, the lists, the consumed rows, the rights, the envelope, the agent refusal shapes, the decision-record element, the workflow, the fakes and the boundary. No criterion states a business outcome of the application story, and none asserts that a route is scored, that a recommendation is made or that a rule fires.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One owner per operation, row, element and table: the baseline declares the recommendation slice of the route operation that the Ownership Map gives S1 and names every other row with its owner | Ownership Map rows of S1; TSD S1 T-A.1 |
| BR2 | A consumed row with no published operation name carries the placeholder and its gap and never an invented path, an invented parameter or an invented model code | Template and Rules v1 §R9; GAP-2621 |
| BR3 | The baseline is additive and sits on one operation: a new optional element is a minor version, and a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version | ADR-020; GAP-2622 |
| BR4 | Every consumed row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and no chain; ACE facts arrive on the rwb-source-data data product and never on a view of this service | DP-05; ADR-020 |
| BR5 | No event is published by this baseline: the ownership rows give S1 no event, and the decision record reaches the ledger on the shared topic through the library of DP-03 | DP-03; context pack S1 ownership rows |
| BR6 | The decision record is written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the caller's transaction before any change, and its element is declared once for the service | DP-03 |
| BR7 | No business value is declared in the baseline: the route codes, the returns, the weights, the confidence threshold and the open route set are referenced with their identifier, their list or their version | TSD S1 T3.2; FSD S1 A2.7.3.1 BR-S1-007 |
| BR8 | The agent row declares what the caller checks and never what the agent decides: the schema check, the confidence element and the fallback are part of the surface, and the autonomy level is the agent's own | NFR-051, NFR-055; Agent Catalog, Route agent |
| BR9 | No personal data in any element, fake, example, prompt or log of the baseline | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17); NFR-052 |
| BR10 | The baseline never declares another service's table, operation or topic as its own, and a check fails the build where one names it | DP-01, DP-13, DP-14 |

##### 9. State transitions

The object of this section is the document, not a case: the lifecycle of the contract baseline.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | The draft is complete | Every operation, row, element, fake and error is declared | Draft |
| Draft | The review is opened | The owners of the five consumed rows are named as reviewers | In review |
| In review | The review closes with no open comment | The compatibility check passes on the previous tag of the operation | Baselined, tagged for the application story |
| In review | A comment needs a shape change | The change is applied to the draft | Draft |
| Baselined | An additive change is approved | A new optional element only, and the check passes | Baselined, new minor version |
| Baselined | A breaking change is approved | A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element | Draft of a new major version, and the consumers are notified |
| Baselined | An owner changes its answer | X6 | Draft of a new minor or major version, and the fake is updated |

| Step | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Being authored | A consumed row has no published name | X1 | The row carries the placeholder and the gap, and the draft continues |
| Being authored | A row declares a model code, a threshold or a route mapping | X7 | The value is replaced by a reference with its identifier and its version |
| In review | The slice is declared as a second operation or path | X3 | The baseline is refused and the elements move into the operation that exists |
| Ready to tag | A consumed row has no fake | X4 | Not tagged, and the review reopens |

| Owner of rwb-agent (P10) | Reviews the route-agent row, its model codes, its confidence element and its refusal shapes, and publishes the operation name and the autonomy level when they exist |

| Owner of RWB-S1-E4001-CON | Confirms that the recommendation elements are an additive slice of the operation it declared |
| Any team | Reads the baseline and its fakes from Day 1; no team may change a declared shape outside the lifecycle of section 9 |

No person is named anywhere in this document; the roles above are the roles of the run.
