##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.treatment`, modules `deed-in-lieu` and `treatment`, with the published types in `...treatment.api`. Service base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1`, schema `rwb_treatment`, topic `rwb.treatment.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | ACE data read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views; here the facts arrive on the case signal and no view is named | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the record of each step inside the same transaction; DP-05 is the customer and NPA-asset read that comes to this stage as facts, because the connection matrix gives rwb-treatment no call to rwb-source-data and the views are granted to rwb-source-data alone (ASM-4389); DP-13 fixes the service base on which the sibling operations answer; DP-19 is the route by which SCR-14 and SCR-16 reach this service. The ownership rule of DP-01 is applied in prose and in the SQL: `recovery_case`, `asset`, `document` and the two views are never named in a statement of this service.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `TreatmentWorkflow` (deed-in-lieu stage) | Workflow | The offer release, the inspection, the unlock, the transfer, the outcome report and the record |
| `generateOfferDocuments` | Activity | The document and notice requests, the validity date and the offer timer |
| `scheduleInspection`, `recordInspection` | Activities | The inspection need, the checklist fact and the treatment's inspection outcome |
| `decideAssetUnlock` | Activity | The unlock rule and the `ApprovalWorkflow` child for the exception |
| `completeTransfer` | Activity | The asset, AMIS, settlement and registration requests and the facts that return |
| `recordAndApply` | Activity | The five treatment columns, the decision record and the outbox row in one transaction |
| `publishApproved` | Activity | The `TreatmentApproved` outbox row |
| `DeedInLieuHandler` | Handler | The stage entry from the case signal: the price, the state and the facts mapped onto the stage input |
| `TreatmentRepository` | Repository | The update of `treatment` by ID, with the optimistic-lock version of the row |

**Database.** `treatment` already holds DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033. This story adds `transferPrice`, `inspectionOutcome`, `unlockDecision`, `assetRef` and `transferredAt` on the service's own migration sequence and creates no table: the inspection and the transfer have none of their own (GAP-2672; ASM-4393). `decision_record` is the library object of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the same schema.

**Configuration and reference data.** The product conditions of R-DIL-18 and R-DIL-28, the unlock thresholds, the offer and title clocks, the state names and the reason codes `offer_expired`, `unlock_refused` and `title_not_clean` are values in force of their owners and are read, never set here (BR6). The package version arrives through `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1`. The capability area and the rights are the guard library's data.

**Build steps**

1. The migration that adds the five deed-in-lieu columns to `treatment` on the service sequence, with no new table.
2. `generateOfferDocuments` against the document, notice and envelope fakes, with the validity date and the offer timer (AC1, AC3).
3. `scheduleInspection` and `recordInspection` against the inspection fixtures, complete and incomplete (AC1).
4. `decideAssetUnlock` against the unlock fixture and the `ApprovalWorkflow` fake, with the pass, the release, the refusal, HELD_NO_LIMIT and the timeout (AC1).
5. `completeTransfer` against the asset and integration answers, with the accepted transfer, the title hold, the unknown registry and the timeout (AC2).
6. `recordAndApply` with the treatment update, the decision record through the fake and the outbox row, and the rollback on MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P7-009 (AC4).
7. The stage entry and the guard, with the case signal, a role without right U and a role without RA (AC1, TC-E3-012-05).
8. The outcome report to the parent and the two mocked case statuses (AC2, AC3).
9. Tests for AC1 to AC4 against the fakes and the fixtures.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.treatment.deed-in-lieu`.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, a synthetic deed in lieu walks from TRANSFER_PRICE_SET to ASSET_ON_BOOKS in SIT with the document set, the inspection, the unlock and the transfer facts recorded on the treatment, `TreatmentApproved` appears on `rwb.treatment.events.v1` once at the offer release and not on a refusal, a forced record failure leaves the treatment unchanged with MSG-P7-003, and SCR-16 shows the stage, the inspection outcome and the asset reference through the gateway-bff route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S2-001 | The transfer price is below the floor of its case and has been routed for approval | The offer is below the floor of {floor}. It has been sent for approval. |
| MSG-S2-002 | The payoff or the figure behind the offer is older than the freshness limit | The payoff is from {date}. A new figure has been requested. |
| MSG-S2-003 | The offer to the customer carries its end date | The offer to the customer ends on {date}. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of the inspection or the transfer is missing | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role does not hold the right the action needs in "Treatment and offer" | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written and the action is not taken | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P7-009 | The record is refused for a missing or invalid field (service log and incident, not shown to the customer) | The decision record was refused: {field} is missing or not valid. |

The six legacy texts are carried unchanged; MSG-P7-009 comes with the decision-record contract of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON. MSG-S2-001 and MSG-S2-002 are raised by the branch of RWB-S2-E3003-APP and are listed because the legacy story carried them. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-16 Deed in lieu: states Checks, appraisal, approved, transferred; this story owns the step from approved to transferred — the offer release, the inspection outcome, the unlock answer and the asset reference — and shows the deed-in-lieu facts of section 12.1. SCR-14 Treatment record (states Draft, submitted, approved, booked, broken) shows the treatment and its outcome. Both reach this service through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls rwb-treatment and the screen's other owners in parallel, one hop each; the officer's action on SCR-16 is an update of the treatment through the surface of RWB-S2-E3002-CON, and the stage learns it on the case signal. The screen field list and the composite route specification belong to the platform edge story and the screen owners; this story fixes the service side only.

The `-ITG` copies belong to the wave 2 integration harness, RWB-ITG-W2, and are not listed here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the product conditions, the unlock thresholds, the clocks, the state names and the reason codes are values in force of their owners, read with their version, never constants (BR6).
- No personal data in logs, events, workflow inputs or the fixture: the stage carries treatment and case identifiers, codes, amounts, versions and timestamps; test data is synthetic and no customer field is copied.
- No read of another service's table and no read of an ACE view: the case and asset facts arrive on the case signal, the asset record and the documents are requested, and no `v_ace_*` view is named in a statement of this service (DP-01; DP-05; ASM-4389).
- No write outside the transaction that records the change: the treatment update, the decision record and the outbox row commit together or not at all (DP-03; BR8).
- The decision is written before the change takes effect, and a refused or unavailable record leaves the case exactly as it was, which is what R-UNI-39 and Principle 5 require.
- The rule version and the approver level are written with every answer, so an auditor can see why an asset was released or held.
- No case status and no case task is written: the parent moves the status and raises the task on the stage outcome (ASM-4388).
- One event only, and no event on a refusal or a hold: rwb-comms and rwb-payment hear only of an approved deed in lieu (EV-10).
- No credential, no secret and no document content appears in code, configuration, a prompt or an event payload.

##### 19. Out of scope

- The published element set, the event reference, the compatibility rule and the fakes: RWB-S2-E3012-CON.
- The treatment record, its creation, its fields DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 and its own migration: RWB-S2-E3001-APP and RWB-S2-E3001-CON.
- The offer surface `POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/offer`, the draft-terms change and the settlement range: RWB-S2-E3002-APP and RWB-S2-E3002-CON.
- The below-floor second signature and the transfer price comparison against the floor: RWB-S2-E3003-APP and RWB-S2-E3003-CON.
- The encumbrance and eligibility check before negotiation, the early valuation and the appraisal order: FEAT-TRT-13 and the sibling stories of this service.
- The document templates, the document hub, the e-signature and the customer notice: rwb-document, rwb-comms and FEAT-TRT-18.
- The asset record, the asset list, the AMIS interface, the core-bank settlement, the registration release in SCIS and the Land Office path: rwb-asset and rwb-integration, through their own contracts.
- The buy-back rental, the auto-debit and the arrears follow-up of FEAT-TRT-16: the sibling stories of this service and rwb-payment.
- The case status, the case table, the task of the inspector and the task of the approver: rwb-case, RWB-P3-E1018 and its contract; the status reaches this service on the case signal only.
- The `approval` record, the `ApprovalWorkflow` and the rule package registry: rwb-decision.
- The topic, its ACLs, the retry topics and the dead-letter topic: the event platform and the platform infrastructure stories.
- The deployment, the flag, the dashboards and the alerts of this build: this legacy key's DevOps story.
- The real cross-service proof against the live rwb-case, rwb-asset, rwb-document and rwb-integration: the wave 2 integration harness.

##### 1. Story

As a **contract owner for rwb-treatment**, I want **the published contract of the encumbrance and eligibility check — the `readiness` section of the treatment answer with the encumbrance, registration and title-set facts and the rule version that decided them, the title-set task request the stage reports to the parent, the read-only column contract of the three ACE views the facts come from, the error set, the compatibility rule and the fakes — instead of the monolith's one `recovery` schema and one in-process check**, so that **the application slice, the gateway route, rwb-case's parent workflow and the wave 2 harness all build against one frozen readiness surface from Day 1, and no consumer invents a column or a task that the source never gave**.

This story owns:

- the `readiness` section of the treatment answer: its name, its properties, which of them are stored and which are computed per request, and the statement that it is an optional addition to the treatment resource of RWB-S2-E3001-CON;
- the read operation entry the section is served through, on base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1`, with the access right, the error set and the note that it declares no write operation (DP-13);
- the `TitleSetTaskRequest` element the stage outcome carries, with the rule ID, the package version, the clock and the references, and the statement that the task itself is rwb-case's;
- the read-only column contract of `v_ace_collateral`, `v_ace_collateral_detail` and `v_ace_npa_asset`, with the statement that the encumbrance and title statuses are columns of that read and are never derived in code (DP-05);
- the compatibility rule, the pinning rule and the drift test, and the fake set every consumer uses.

It does not own: the behaviour behind the section, which is RWB-S2-E3013-APP; the treatment resource, its create, its read and its element, which are RWB-S2-E3001-CON; the settlement and deed-in-lieu offer surfaces, which are RWB-S2-E3002-CON and RWB-S2-E3012-CON; the case status, the task and the timers, which are rwb-case's; the decision-record library, which is RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; the gateway-bff composite route, which is RWB-PLT-N001-CON; and the ACE views themselves, their grant and their ingestion, which are P1's and the ACE DB stories'.

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E3-013 had no contract to publish: the encumbrance and title facts were columns read in the same process, the task was a row in a table of the same schema, and the decision log was a row beside them. The microservice split removes that option. The facts now come from ACE views read by rwb-treatment, the status they lead to is moved by rwb-case, the answer is served by the gateway route, and the harness proves the path across services, so four consumers need the same answer to the same questions before any of them writes code.

**The division of the legacy key is fixed.** The legacy acceptance criteria **AC1 to AC4 stay with RWB-S2-E3013-APP**; every criterion in section 7 is new and tests only the contract deliverable in this title. The treatment resource and its read are RWB-S2-E3001-CON's, the offer surfaces are the siblings' of the same legacy key group, and nothing of either is restated here.

The contract has to exist first for three reasons. The **result has no field anywhere**: TSD S2 T3.1 gives `treatment` DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 and none of them is an encumbrance, a registration or a title-set status, the functional specification's A2.13 has no field catalog at all, and the legacy data table names the fields of the three views only as ranges, so without a published section one consumer reads a status from a table that will never hold it and another computes it from `lien_rank` in code (GAP-2675; ASM-4395, ASM-4396). The **task is not the service's**: R-SET-22 says "raise a task" and the connection matrix of Architecture v5 slide 13 gives rwb-treatment no call to rwb-case, so the request has to be published as an element the parent turns into a task, not as a write of this service (ASM-4394). And the **ACE read is a dependency with no publication**: DP-05 allows either the service's own views or the contract read of rwb-source-data, and the choice belongs in one document, not in four consumers' heads (ASM-4395).

The contract also fixes what it does not do: it declares no business table, adds no column, publishes no event of its own, declares no workflow and no Schedule, and publishes no write operation, because the officer takes no action in this step.

The fake is the Day-1 unblocker: the application slice, the gateway route, the parent workflow's title-set path and the harness can build the clear, blocked, resumed and missing-title answers before the live views, the live case workflow and the live rule packages exist (Template and Rules §R5.4 class C).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service identity is fixed by Template and Rules §R4 and the context pack: schema `rwb_treatment`, base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1`, topic `rwb.treatment.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-13).
- The readiness section has no source shape: TSD S2 T3.1 carries no readiness field, FSD S2 A2.13 has no field catalog, and the legacy story names the view fields only as ranges DF-ACE-091 to DF-ACE-098, DF-ACE-196 to DF-ACE-207 and DF-ACE-208 to DF-ACE-219, so the section and its properties are the working read of ASM-4396 (GAP-2675).
- The encumbrance condition of R-DIL-02 and R-DIL-04 is `encumbrance_status`, and no named view field carries it; the contract therefore states that it is a column of the ACE read and not a derived value, and the column name is the working read of ASM-4395 (GAP-2675).
- The read of the three views is fixed as DP-05's own-view form, which adds no dependency; the alternative, the contract read of rwb-source-data, would be a C dependency and is named as the fallback in section 19 (ASM-4395).
- The target state of the task is fixed: the stage reports an outcome, the parent `CaseWorkflow` raises the task on the 5 working-day clock of R-SET-22 and moves the case status, so the contract publishes a request element and no task write (ASM-4394).
- The capability area "Treatment and offer" and right R are the access declaration of TSD S2 T6.1 and the legacy permission table; the check is the guard library's and the contract declares the right only (ASM-4398).
- RWB-S2-E3001-CON is named and not restated: the readiness section is declared as an optional addition to the treatment element of that contract, at the same major version, so its consumers see a compatible change.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON are published, so the contract can name the record write and the composite route without redeclaring either (DP-03; DP-19).
- The validation messages keep their legacy identifiers and texts, and no published catalogue defines their entry format, so the entry format is the working read.
- No build dependency and no approval stop: a CON story is Day 1 by rule (§R5.7), sits in contract group `CG-W2`, and is published at status Draft (realignment v1).

##### 4. Flow

1. The contract author fixes the `readiness` section: its name, its properties, the stored and the computed ones, and its place in the treatment answer of RWB-S2-E3001-CON.
2. The author records the one read operation entry the section is served through, its access right, its errors and the statement that no write operation is published.
3. The author fixes the `TitleSetTaskRequest` element the stage outcome carries: the rule ID and package version, the case and treatment references, the clock and the reason code.
4. The author fixes the read-only column contract of the three views: the field identifiers, the column names the source gives and the two statuses it does not.
5. The author fixes the error set: the status codes, the message identifiers and the texts, and the note that no idempotency key applies because nothing is written.
6. The author writes the compatibility rule — an optional section may be added at the same major version and a breaking change raises major version 2 — and the pinning rule for the consumers.
7. The author writes the negative rules: no table, no column for a status, no derivation of a status in code, no case write, no task write and no ACE write.
8. The lint and schema steps run: the operation entry compared against TSD S2 T-A.1, the section and the request validated against the OpenAPI document, the examples scanned for personal data, and the error table checked against the message identifiers.
9. The fake set is generated from the document: the clear, blocked, resumed, missing-title and no-collateral answers, the refusal answer and the failed record answer.
10. The contract test runs the fakes against the document on every change and fails the build on any drift; the document and the fakes are published at v1 and the consumers pin the version.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The section is published as required, or without a version tag on the treatment answer | The schema validation fails the build; the section is optional on the answer of RWB-S2-E3001-CON | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A status is published as a column of `rwb_treatment`, or the document says a status is derived from `lien_rank` | The schema and lint steps fail the build; the statuses stay properties of the read | None | AC1, AC5 |
| X3 | The task is published as a write of this service, or the request carries no clock and no rule version | The lint fails the build; the request is an element of the stage outcome and its consumer is rwb-case | None | AC2 |
| X4 | An error answer is published without a message identifier, or with a code the legacy story does not carry | The error-table check fails the build; every code is mapped to its identifier and its text | None | AC3 |
| X5 | A breaking change is made to a path, a property or the answer | The change raises major version 2; v1 is never edited in place and stays readable | None | AC4 |
| X6 | A consumer ships without the drift test, or its code drifts from the published schemas | The registry refuses the change and the drift test fails that consumer's build | None | AC5 |
| X7 | A value a consumer needs is named by no source — the section name, a property name, the encumbrance column or the task reason code | The value is published as the working read of the assumption and the gap stays open | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2675; ASM-4396) | Section 3 |

X1 and X5 are contract-governance paths, X2, X3 and X4 are the paths an invented column, task or error adds, X6 is the drift rule of class C, and X7 is the reason the section and the request are published as a working read.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Publishes a document and fakes; builds against nothing but the two named contracts, reads no business data and starts on Day 1 |
| Negotiable | The property names, the example values and the fixture set are open until v1 is frozen; the one operation entry, the request element, the error set and the compatibility rule are fixed |
| Valuable | Unblocks the application slice, the gateway route, the parent workflow's title-set path and the wave 2 harness on Day 1 and keeps the statuses out of the schema |
| Estimable | One section, one request element, one operation entry, four errors, two rules and six fakes |
| Small | One sprint for the document, the schemas, the fakes and the lint rules |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one document, schema or fake assertion in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: encumbrance and eligibility readiness contract

  Background:

    Then the document states that encumbranceStatus, registrationStatus and titleSetStatus are values of the ACE read and are never derived in code from lien_rank or register_date
    Then the document states that the section is an additive, backward-compatible change at major version 1 and that RWB-S2-E3001-CON owns the operation entry
    Then the document declares no table and no column for a status, a hold date or a check time
    Then an example carries a status, a rule version and a date and no national identifier, account number or name

  Scenario: AC2 The title-set task request is an element of the stage outcome, not a write of this service (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then the document states that rwb-case raises the task and the service reports the request, so no task row, no timer row and no case row is declared here

    Given the operation section of the document
    When it is validated against TSD S2 T-A.1 API-S2-002 and the legacy permission table
    Then exactly one operation entry is published, the read of the treatment answer at GET /treatments/{treatmentId}, under capability area Treatment and offer with right R
    Then no write operation is published, because the check is started by rule R-DIL-01 on the case signal and the officer takes no action in it
    Then the entry declares 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 and 503, and declares no idempotency key because no state changes
    Then the document maps MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P7-009 to the answers that carry them and adds no message identifier

    Then adding an optional property or an optional section keeps major version 1 and is accepted by the registry in BACKWARD mode
    Then a breaking change to the operation entry, a required property, an error code or the answer raises major version 2 and v1 is never edited in place
    Then each consumer pins a published version and raises a change request rather than a private variant

  Scenario: AC5 The view column contract is read only, and no status is derived or stored (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then the document lists v_ace_collateral with DF-ACE-091 to DF-ACE-098, v_ace_collateral_detail with DF-ACE-196 to DF-ACE-207 and v_ace_npa_asset with DF-ACE-208 to DF-ACE-219, each marked read only
    Then the document states that the check holds SELECT on the three views and writes no ACE object
    Then the document states that the encumbrance and title-set statuses are columns of that read whose names no source fixes, so the names are the working read
    Then the lint fails the build if the document declares a write, a table copy or a derivation of a status in code
    Then no property of the section carries a personal field

  Scenario: AC6 The fake answers the document and every consumer runs the drift test (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fake set generated from the document

    Then the readiness fake answers a clear mortgage, an unresolved mortgage with a hold date, an HP asset clear in SCIS, a collateral-release case with title documents missing and a case with no collateral row
    Then the error fake answers 403, 404 and 503 with their message identifiers and no personal data

```

These criteria are new and test only the contract deliverable: no legacy acceptance criterion is repeated here, because **AC1 to AC4 of RWB-E3-013 are owned by RWB-S2-E3013-APP**, and every identifier, rule, message and field range is taken from the legacy story, the TSD appendix or the rule set character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The readiness answer is one optional section of the treatment answer of RWB-S2-E3001-CON, at the same major version, and no consumer carries a private copy of it | GAP-2675; ASM-4396 |
| BR2 | The encumbrance, registration and title-set statuses are values of the ACE read and are never derived in code and never stored in this schema | R-DIL-02, R-DIL-04, R-SET-22; DP-05; ASM-4395 |
| BR3 | The title-set task is rwb-case's: the stage reports a request with the rule, the version and the clock, and no task, timer or case write is declared | R-SET-22; ASM-4394 |
| BR4 | One read operation is published under right R with its error set, and no write operation, because the check is started by rule and ends in a report | R-DIL-01; TSD S2 T-A.1 API-S2-002 |
| BR5 | The three views are read with SELECT only under DP-05; no ACE object is written and no view is copied into `rwb_treatment` | DP-05; DP-01 |
| BR6 | The contract declares the access right only; the check is the guard library's on capability area "Treatment and offer" | TSD S2 T6.1; ASM-4398 |
| BR7 | A published version is never edited: a compatible addition stays in major version 1 and a breaking change raises major version 2 | Template and Rules §R7.2; §R5.4 class C |
| BR8 | No value a business person may change is enumerated in the contract: the statuses, the hold limit and the clocks are values in force, and the only values in the document are examples | BR-S2-013 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 is the section table and the note on the operation entry. BR2 is the stored-versus-read column of every property and the lint rule of X2, and it is the reason the section exists at all rather than a set of columns. BR3 is the request table and the lint rule of X3. BR4 and BR6 are the operation table with its access column and the error table. BR5 is the view contract and the lint rule of AC5. BR7 is the compatibility section and the pinning rule. BR8 keeps every status an example and never an enumeration.

##### 9. State transitions

None at run time: a document and a schema have no state. Two vocabularies are fixed here, and the runtime transitions behind them are specified by RWB-S2-E3013-APP section 9.

| Object | State | Meaning in the contract |
|---|---|---|
| Readiness answer | Clear | The encumbrance or registration status of the read is clear and the title set is present |
| Readiness answer | Blocked | The status is unresolved and the answer carries a hold date |
| Readiness answer | Title set missing | The title documents are absent and the answer carries the task request |
| Readiness answer | Undetermined | No collateral row is found for the case; the answer carries the unmatched outcome |
| Task request | Reported | The stage outcome carries the request; rwb-case raises the task |
| Contract version | v1 | The published version every consumer pins |
| Contract version | v2 | Raised by a breaking change; v1 stays readable and is never edited in place |

The case states ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL, EARLY_READINESS_CHECK, ENCUMBRANCE_BLOCKED, VALUATION_ORDERED and COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED are rwb-case's and are named in the request only as the reason they lead to.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The contract author (any team, per U3) | Writes and versions the document, the section and request schemas, the error table and the fakes |
| The service team of rwb-treatment | Consumes the contract, pins the version and raises a change request rather than a private variant |
| The rwb-treatment tech lead | Confirms that the one operation entry and the request element are the ones the application slice fills |
| The rwb-case owner (P3) | Confirms that the task is raised by the parent workflow on the request and that no case write is declared |
| The P1 rwb-source-data owner | Confirms the read-only view contract and the fallback to its own contract read |
| The platform edge owner | Confirms the composite route the two screens use, which this contract names and does not declare |
| The wave 2 integration harness owner | Confirms the fake set is enough to prove the cross-service path |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A service contract is a technical artefact, not a credit decision |

No personal name, no email address and no credential appears in the document, an example or a fake. Where a caller must be named, the example uses a role code or a user identifier only.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Business data published | None. The document publishes one operation entry, two schemas, codes, message identifiers and three examples; no customer, account or case value appears |
| Stored fields referenced | DF-TRT-003 `decision_log_id`, DF-TRT-013 `outcome` and DF-TRT-014 `outcome_at` of `treatment`, referenced through the section and declared by RWB-S2-E3001-CON, not redefined here |
| Read fields referenced | DF-ACE-091 to DF-ACE-098 of `v_ace_collateral`, DF-ACE-196 to DF-ACE-207 of `v_ace_collateral_detail` and DF-ACE-208 to DF-ACE-219 of `v_ace_npa_asset`, each read only |
| Personal data | None. The examples carry a status, a rule version, a date and a business key, and the actor and trace references are identifiers, never names |
| Tables published | None. The contract declares no table and no column; `treatment` is the application slice's and `decision_record` is the library's (DP-01; DP-03) |
| Field identifiers | The stored fields and the view fields carry the identifiers above; the section's own properties carry none, because no source gives them one (GAP-2675; ASM-4396) |

The one place where the contract could leak a value is the status: the document therefore fixes that `encumbranceStatus`, `registrationStatus` and `titleSetStatus` are values of the read, that they are never an enumeration of this contract and never a default, and that no example value is presented as the value of the rule set in force.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-treatment (S2); base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` (DP-13). The contract declares the readiness section and names the one operation it is served through; the operation entry belongs to RWB-S2-E3001-CON and this contract adds an optional section to its answer at major version 1.

| Method | Path | Answer | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/treatments/{treatmentId}` | The treatment element of RWB-S2-E3001-CON with the optional `readiness` section: `checkType`, `encumbranceStatus`, `registrationStatus`, `titleSetStatus`, `checkedAt`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion`, `holdUntil`, `collateralNo` and `assetKey` | Treatment and offer, right R | Not applicable; the read changes no state |

No write operation is published. R-DIL-01 starts the check on the case signal, the check reports its outcome to the parent `CaseWorkflow`, and the officer takes no action in this step, so there is nothing to post or patch; the legacy endpoint table of RWB-E3-013 names the treatment read only, which is consistent with this surface (GAP-2675; ASM-4394, ASM-4396). The errors are 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 and 503. The reasons the section has no source shape, and whether the bank ever intended a separate readiness operation, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2675; ASM-4396).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The contract declares the surface and calls no service: the route, the product group and the collateral keys arrive on the signal the parent forwards, the statuses are read from the three views, and the decision record is an in-process call of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (DP-03; DP-05; ASM-4394). This is why the Work Package records no C dependency for the pair.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic of the service is `rwb.treatment.events.v1` with event names `rwb.treatment.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and its events `TreatmentApproved` and `TreatmentClosed` belong to other stories. This contract publishes no event schema and declares no outbox row.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The contract declares no subscription; the two events the application slice consumes — `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` (EV-30) and `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` (EV-06) — belong to P7 and S8 and are named in section 19, and the case status is a workflow signal and not an event of this contract (ASM-4394).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The contract declares no workflow and no activity. It states only that the section is filled inside an activity on the owner's own task queue and that the decision record is called from that activity, so a replay reuses the recorded decision; the workflow itself is RWB-S2-E3013-APP's readiness branch of `TreatmentWorkflow` on `rwb-treatment` (DP-12).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The contract declares no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job. The 2 working-day lead clock, the 10 working-day hold and the 5 working-day title-set clock are durable timers inside the workflow and values in force in the rule set, not part of the published surface.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The contract declares no table, no column and no key, and the negative rule is the deliverable: no encumbrance, registration, title-set or hold column exists in `rwb_treatment`, because no source gives one and a column would freeze a status that the rule set owns (GAP-2675; ASM-4396; DP-01). `treatment` is RWB-S2-E3001-APP's business table, `decision_record` is the library object of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, `decision_log_entry` is P7's ledger, and the case, the task and the timer are rwb-case's; all are named here only.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| Readiness fake | The `readiness` section on `GET /treatments/{treatmentId}` | A clear mortgage, an unresolved mortgage with a hold date, an HP asset clear in SCIS, a collateral-release case with title documents missing and a case with no collateral row |
| Task-request fake | The stage outcome element | A `TitleSetTaskRequest` with rule R-SET-22, its version, the 5 working-day clock and the reason code; a request with no clock refused as invalid |
| Error fake | The error table | 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 and 503, each with its identifier, its merge fields and a trace identifier |
| Treatment resource fake | The answer the section extends | The treatment element of RWB-S2-E3001-CON, referenced and not restated |
| Composite route fake | The gateway-bff composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON | One hop for SCR-16, joining the treatment read with its readiness section; a refused route for a role without right R |
| Decision-record fake | The library write the application slice makes | An accepted record with an entry reference; a refusal with MSG-P7-009 and the field; a failed write with MSG-P7-003 |

The fakes answer from the same example set as the document, so a change to the contract shows up as a contract-test failure in a consumer rather than as a surprise at run time. The treatment resource fake and the decision-record fake are the published contracts of their stories and are referenced here, not redeclared.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 operation entry, extended | 0 | OpenAPI 3.1 fragment; one hop to the service, 2 s timeout |
| Kafka | 0 event schemas | 0 | The service topic is named; this contract declares no event |
| SQL view | 3 read-only views referenced | 3 | SELECT only under DP-05; no write to any ACE object |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 | The contract states the section is filled in an activity and declares no workflow |
| File, Nexus | 0 | 0 | No file and no Nexus operation crosses the contract |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Contract artefact of rwb-treatment: the OpenAPI fragment and the two element schemas in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.treatment.api`, the error table and the compatibility note in the contract document, and the fake set as a test asset. Service base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1`, schema `rwb_treatment`, topic `rwb.treatment.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`. The artefact coordinates and the publication channel are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2675; ASM-4396).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 enters the contract as one statement — the section is written with a record in the caller's transaction — and the H dependency sits on the application slice, which calls the library. DP-05 is the read-only column contract of the three views and the reason the statuses are published as read values. DP-13 is the base of the operation entry and the reason the legacy base appears nowhere in the document. DP-19 is the route the two screens use, named here so that the composite route fake has an owner.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `TreatmentReadOpenApi` | OpenAPI 3.1 fragment | The one operation entry, its parameter, its errors, its access declaration and the note that it extends RWB-S2-E3001-CON |
| `ReadinessSectionSchema` | Answer schema | The ten properties of the section and the stored, read and computed note on each |
| `TitleSetTaskRequestSchema` | Stage-outcome schema | The request the parent turns into a task, with the rule, the version, the clock and the reason code |
| `AceViewContract` | Document table | The three views, their field identifiers, their read-only mark and the two statuses whose column names no source fixes |
| `ErrorCatalogue` | Document table | The status codes, the message identifiers, the legacy texts and the merge fields |
| `CompatibilityNote` | Document section | The additive-versus-breaking rule, the pinning rule and the negative rules |
| `ReadinessFakeSet` | Test asset | The six fakes of section 12.8 and the drift test every consumer runs |

**Database.** None. The contract creates no table, adds no column and declares no key; the negative rules of section 12.7 and of AC5 are the deliverable, and a review that finds an encumbrance, registration, title-set or hold column in `rwb_treatment` fails this story.

**Configuration and reference data.** The contract fixes no business value. The statuses, the hold limit and the three clocks are values in force in the rule set; the only values in the document are the example values, and they are marked as examples. Capability area "Treatment and offer" and right R are read from rwb-access through the guard library, which the application slice calls (ASM-4398). The grant on the three views is a DB story's (DP-05; ASM-4395).

**Build steps**

1. Write the one operation entry, its access right and its errors, and lint that no write operation and no second form appear (AC3).
2. Write the `readiness` section, its ten properties and the stored, read and computed note on each (AC1).
3. Write `TitleSetTaskRequest` and the lint that refuses a task, timer or case write (AC2).
4. Write the `AceViewContract` table with the three field ranges and the two statuses, and the lint that refuses a derivation in code (AC5).
5. Write the error table with the four identifiers and their legacy texts, and validate one answer per code (AC3).
6. Write the compatibility note, the pinning rule and the negative rules (AC4).
7. Generate the six fakes and the drift test; wire the drift test into the build of RWB-S2-E3013-APP, the gateway route, the parent workflow's title-set path and the wave 2 harness (AC6).
8. Publish v1 and record the pinned version of each consumer.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.treatment.readiness-contract`.

**Done when.** The document and the two schemas validate, the operation lint passes with one read entry and no write, the error table matches the four legacy identifiers and texts, the six fakes answer every example including the blocked answer and the missing title set, the drift test is green on the build of this story and on the build of the application slice, and v1 is published with the pinned versions recorded.

No screen in this story, and the contract declares none. The screen states of SCR-16 — Checks, appraisal, approved, transferred — are the runtime states of the application slice and are named in section 9 only to keep the vocabulary apart.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the statuses, the hold limit and the three clocks are values in force in the rule set, and the only values in the document are examples, marked as examples.
- No personal data in a schema, an example, a fake or a log: the examples carry a status, a rule version, a date and a business key, and the scan fails the build otherwise.
- No table, no column and no key in the contract: the statuses, the hold date and the check time stay out of `rwb_treatment` (DP-01; GAP-2675; ASM-4396).
- No status derived in code: the lint of AC5 fails any document or consumer that computes an encumbrance or title status from `lien_rank` or `register_date` (ASM-4395).
- No write operation and no task write: the check is started by rule and ends in a report, and the task is rwb-case's (ASM-4394).
- No event and no outbox row of the contract's own: the service topic is named and its events belong to other stories.
- ACE data only through the read-only views or the owner's contract: the view contract declares SELECT and no write, and no ACE object is copied (DP-05).
- A published version is never edited in place: a breaking change raises major version 2 with a migration note and a superseded marking.

##### 1. Story

As a **restructuring officer (FCR)**, I want **the Workbench to run the encumbrance and title checks on a deed-in-lieu candidate as soon as the route is approved, to block the route and raise the title-set task where the asset cannot transfer, and to record every check with the rule version that decided it**, so that **a deed in lieu is not negotiated on an asset that cannot transfer and the deed-in-lieu path reaches its 12-day target instead of the 26 days it takes today**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E3-013. It owns:

- all four legacy acceptance criteria of the story, copied verbatim with their origin tag, and the rules, messages, screens and data rows they depend on;
- the deed-in-lieu readiness step of `TreatmentWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, as the stage child of `CaseWorkflow` owned by rwb-case, with the activities `readEncumbrance`, `evaluateReadiness` and `recordAndApply`;
- the read of the ACE collateral, collateral-detail and NPA-asset views under DP-05, and the encumbrance, registration and title-set facts they carry;
- the rules R-DIL-01 to R-DIL-06 of the DEEDINLIEU package and R-SET-22 of the SETTLEMENT package, with the 2, 10 and 5 working-day clocks read from the rule set in force;
- the local decision record of each check, written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the same transaction as the `treatment` row (DP-03);
- the readiness outcome of the `treatment` row in schema `rwb_treatment`, and the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` uses to move the case status and raise the title-set task.

It does not own: the published shape of the readiness section, of the title-set task request and of the error set, which are RWB-S2-E3013-CON; the deed-in-lieu offer, price, floor and second signature, which are RWB-S2-E3012-APP and its siblings; the treatment record and the treatment read, which are RWB-S2-E3001-APP and RWB-S2-E3001-CON; the case, its status, its tasks and its timers, which are rwb-case's; the valuation order that follows a clear asset, which is S1 rwb-valuation and S5 rwb-asset; the asset unlock that follows the inspection, which is RWB-S2-E3014-APP; and the deployment of this build, which is the wave 2 integration harness and the platform DevOps stories.

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E3-013 existed because a deed in lieu negotiated on an asset that cannot transfer loses the negotiation, the appraisal fee and weeks of the case clock. The functional specification keeps the objective unchanged — the encumbrance and title checks run early, so a deed in lieu is not negotiated on an asset that cannot transfer — and the program keeps the requirement: REQ-S2-005 states that deed-in-lieu readiness, including the encumbrance check and an early valuation, is established before negotiation starts, and the program metric for the deed-in-lieu path is 12 days against 26 today.

What D-RCV-60 changes is where the check runs, what it reads and what it writes. In the monolith the check was a method in the same process as the case row, the collateral rows and the decision log. In the target:

- the readiness step runs inside `TreatmentWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, as the stage child of `CaseWorkflow`, so the check happens where the DEEDINLIEU and SETTLEMENT rules live and the case keeps one parent workflow from entry to closure (DP-12; Architecture v5 slides 5 and 11);
- the collateral, registration and NPA facts are read from the ACE views this service is granted, read only, and never from another service's table (DP-05; DP-01);
- the check answer and the outcome are written to `treatment` in `rwb_treatment`, and the decision goes to the local decision record in the same transaction (DP-03);
- the case status, the tasks and the clocks they run on stay rwb-case's: the stage reports an outcome and the parent moves the status and raises the title-set task (ASM-4394);
- the officer reads the answer through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, on SCR-16 (DP-19; DP-13).

No business value moves. The 2 working days of R-DIL-01, the 10 working days of R-DIL-04 and the 5 working days of R-SET-22 are values in force in the rule set, read with the rule version and never written in code (BR-S2-013).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S2-E3013-CON is published: the `readiness` section of the treatment answer, its properties, the title-set task request element, the error set, the compatibility rule and the fakes are baselined and handed to this story. The section and the task request have no source shape and are published as the working read (GAP-2674; ASM-4396).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: `DecisionRecordWriter.record(DecisionRecord)` runs with `@Transactional(propagation = MANDATORY)`, refuses with MSG-P7-009 and fails with MSG-P7-003, so the check and its record commit together or not at all (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-16 and SCR-14 reach this service through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop each, and no screen calls a service directly (DP-19).
- The three ACE views are readable by the login of rwb-treatment with SELECT only, and they carry the encumbrance, registration and title-set facts under DP-05. The named fields are DF-ACE-091 to DF-ACE-098, DF-ACE-196 to DF-ACE-207 and DF-ACE-208 to DF-ACE-219; the column that carries `encumbrance_status` of R-DIL-02 and R-DIL-04 is not among the names in the source and is the working read of ASM-4395 (GAP-2674).
- The route decision signal is available: the parent `CaseWorkflow` forwards the case status change to the running stage, and the signal that starts the deed-in-lieu stage carries the route R3, the product group and the collateral business keys. Where the rwb-case contract fixes field names, they are copied from it; no source fixes them here (GAP-2674; ASM-4394).
- The embedded Drools runtime and the DEEDINLIEU and SETTLEMENT packages are the service template's wave-0 capability, and the package version in force arrives on `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1`; this story names the packages and their versions and adds no build dependency of its own (ASM-4397).
- The access guard, the outbox and inbox library and the workflow kit are service-template capabilities; this story declares the capability area "Treatment and offer", the right R and the call types and adds no build dependency of its own (ASM-4398).
- The per-service Flyway sequence of rwb-treatment carries `treatment` with DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 and the library object `decision_record`; this story adds no table, no column and never edits an applied migration.
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-S2-E3013-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-case's `CaseWorkflow` receives the case status change and forwards it to the running `TreatmentWorkflow` child on queue `rwb-treatment` as a signal; the stage never calls rwb-case (ASM-4394).
2. R-DIL-01 starts the readiness step: the lead is prioritised and the early readiness checks begin, on the 2 working-day clock of the rule set. The route is R3, the route state ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL, the target state EARLY_READINESS_CHECK.
3. `readEncumbrance` reads `v_ace_collateral`, `v_ace_collateral_detail` and `v_ace_npa_asset` for the collateral of the case by `collateral_no` and `asset_key`, read only and with no write to any ACE object (DP-05).
4. The read returns the encumbrance fact for a mortgage (`encumbrance_status` clear or unresolved), the registration fact for hire purchase (registration clear in SCIS) and the title-set fact (the title document numbers of the collateral detail are present or missing).
5. `evaluateReadiness` evaluates the DEEDINLIEU package in the version in force: R-DIL-02 or R-DIL-03 sends a clear asset to VALUATION_ORDERED, R-DIL-04 blocks an unresolved mortgage in ENCUMBRANCE_BLOCKED with the 10 working-day hold, R-DIL-05 resumes on a cleared status and R-DIL-06 returns the case to the route decision when the hold expires.
6. The same activity evaluates R-SET-22 of the SETTLEMENT package for the settlement-side title set: a case at COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED with title documents missing raises the title-set request and stays at COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED, on the 5 working-day clock.
7. `recordAndApply` assembles the `DecisionRecord` — the decision code of the readiness event, the case, the rule ID with the package version, the recommendation, the final call and the actor — and writes it through `DecisionRecordWriter.record` in the caller's transaction, then writes the readiness outcome and the decision reference to the `treatment` row in the same transaction (DP-03).
8. The stage publishes nothing: it reports the outcome to the parent `CaseWorkflow`, which moves the case status and, on the title-set outcome, raises the task to re-create the title set with its 5 working-day clock (ASM-4394).
9. The officer reads the answer on SCR-16 Deed in lieu through the treatment read, one hop through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19): the encumbrance status, the title-set status, the hold date, the rule ID and version, and the check time.
10. While the route is blocked nothing is negotiated: the case owner sees the hold and its review date, and the resume or the return is decided by R-DIL-05 and R-DIL-06 on the fact that arrives.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The role does not hold right R on "Treatment and offer" | 403 before any read; the refusal is the guard library's and is logged by it | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, TC-E3-013-05 |
| X2 | The decision record cannot be written | `recordAndApply` throws before the `treatment` row is written and the transaction rolls back; nothing changes | MSG-P7-003 | AC4, TC-E3-013-06 |
| X3 | The decision record is refused for a missing or invalid field | Nothing is written and the field is named in the service log and the incident | MSG-P7-009 | AC4 |
| X4 | The mortgage encumbrance is unresolved | The route is blocked and held for the 10 working-day limit; the stage reports ENCUMBRANCE_BLOCKED to the parent | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2674; ASM-4394) | AC1, AC3 |
| X5 | The title documents are missing on a collateral-release case | The title-set request is reported to the parent, which raises the task on the 5 working-day clock, and the case stays where it is | None in the source | AC2 |
| X6 | No collateral row is found for the case's `asset_key` | The check cannot decide: the stage reports an unmatched readiness outcome and raises a task for the case owner; nothing is blocked or cleared | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X7 | The hold expires with the encumbrance still unresolved | R-DIL-06 reports the return to the route decision with reason `encumbrance_unresolved`; the parent moves the case | None in the source | AC3 |
| X8 | The rule package in force is not the one the step started on | The step re-evaluates against the package named on `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` and records the version it used | None | AC1 |

X1, X2 and X3 are the exception paths of RWB-E3-013 carried onto the split, X4 to X7 are the readiness paths the rule set adds, and X8 belongs to the parent-and-child workflow model of the target. The 10-day hold and the 5-day clock are values in force, so neither is a constant of this story.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the published readiness contract, the decision-record library and the gateway route with their fakes, on its own schema and its own ACE views, and needs no live rwb-case, no live rwb-valuation and no live rwb-decision to start |
| Negotiable | The activity names, the decision code per readiness event and the shape of the stage outcome are this story's choice; the rules, the messages, the screens and the seven view tables are fixed |
| Valuable | A deed-in-lieu candidate is blocked or cleared in days instead of after negotiation, and every check carries the rule version that decided it |
| Estimable | One workflow branch, three activities, one view read set, one repository and one record write |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes and the view fixture |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on synthetic treatments and collateral facts through the fake and the view fixture, plus the two component cases of the access answer and the failed record write |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Check encumbrance and eligibility before negotiation

  Scenario: AC1 Check encumbrance and eligibility before negotiation (legacy RWB-E3-013 AC1)
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When its trigger arrives
    Then runs the encumbrance and title checks early, so a deed in lieu is not negotiated on an asset that cannot transfer
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Rule R-SET-22 (legacy RWB-E3-013 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns case status COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED
    Given a case in state COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED
    When title documents missing
    Then raise a task to re-create the title set before release
    Then the case moves to COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED

  Scenario: AC3 Rule R-DIL-01 (legacy RWB-E3-013 AC3)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns case status ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL
    Given a case in state ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL
    When route approved
    Then prioritize the lead and start the early readiness checks
    Then the case moves to EARLY_READINESS_CHECK

  Scenario: AC4 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E3-013 AC4)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

**Target reading.** Every line and every value above is the legacy line and the legacy value, unchanged, including the repetition of `Then` and the legacy wording `the action is taken` and `the decision log cannot be written`; what changes is where it runs, what produces the fact and how it is reached. The one added line is the mock Given of AC2 and AC3, which stands in for the case status that rwb-case owns, so the stage can be tested before the live case workflow exists (ASM-4394). The check runs on the deed-in-lieu readiness step of `TreatmentWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, with the activities `readEncumbrance`, `evaluateReadiness` and `recordAndApply` (Architecture v5 slides 5 and 11; DP-12). The facts of AC1 are read from `v_ace_collateral`, `v_ace_collateral_detail` and `v_ace_npa_asset` under DP-05, read only, and the encumbrance and title statuses are values of that read and never derived in code (GAP-2674; ASM-4395). "The decision log" of AC1 and AC4 is the local decision record of `decision_record` in `rwb_treatment`, written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON with `@Transactional(propagation = MANDATORY)` in the same transaction as the `treatment` row; `decision_log_entry` is P7's ledger and is neither written nor read here (DP-03). The states of AC2 and AC3 — COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED, ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL and EARLY_READINESS_CHECK — are case statuses of rwb-case: the stage reports the outcome and the parent moves the status, so the transition is proved against the mock and not by a write of this service (ASM-4394). R-SET-22 is carried by this story because the title set is the same readiness fact on the settlement side; its self-loop keeps the case where it is and the task is the only move. The answer the officer reads, its property names and the title-set request are published by RWB-S2-E3013-CON as the working read (ASM-4396).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | An approved deed-in-lieu route starts the early readiness checks at once: the lead is prioritised and the encumbrance and title facts are read before any negotiation | R-DIL-01; REQ-S2-005 |
| BR2 | A mortgage whose encumbrance is clear, and a hire-purchase asset whose registration is clear in SCIS, order the valuation and leave the readiness state | R-DIL-02, R-DIL-03 |
| BR3 | An unresolved mortgage encumbrance blocks the route and holds the case for the hold limit, resumes on a cleared status and returns to the route decision when the hold expires | R-DIL-04, R-DIL-05, R-DIL-06 |
| BR4 | Title documents that cannot be found raise a task to re-create the title set before release, and the case stays where it is until the set exists | R-SET-22 |
| BR5 | The decision is recorded with the rule version before or with the change; if it cannot be recorded, nothing changes | REQ-DRI-005; DP-03; MSG-P7-003 |
| BR6 | No value a business person may change is written in code: the encumbrance and title statuses, the hold limit and the three clocks are values in force, read with their version | BR-S2-013 |
| BR7 | The case status, the task and its clock are not this service's: the stage reports and the parent moves and raises | DP-01; ASM-4394 |
| BR8 | ACE data is read only, through this service's own views, and never written and never copied into another service's table | DP-05; DP-01; ASM-4395 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 is the start signal and the first step of the branch. BR2, BR3 and BR4 are `evaluateReadiness` against the DEEDINLIEU and SETTLEMENT packages, with the statuses taken from the view read and no threshold in code. BR5 is the `MANDATORY` transaction of the library, so the `treatment` row and the `decision_record` row commit together or not at all. BR6 is the reason the hold limit and the three clocks are read from the rule set with the package version and not configured here. BR7 is the reason the stage outcome carries the request and the parent raises the task. BR8 is the reason the read is a SELECT against the views and no ACE object is written.

##### 9. State transitions

The case status is rwb-case's and is not changed by this story: the readiness step reports an outcome and the parent `CaseWorkflow` moves the case (ASM-4394). The transitions below are the rule set's, and each row is one outcome this story reports.

| From | Event | Condition | To (rule) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL | ROUTE_APPROVED | decision.approved and route = R3 | EARLY_READINESS_CHECK (R-DIL-01) |
| EARLY_READINESS_CHECK | ENCUMBRANCE_CLEAR | product = MTG and encumbrance_status = clear | VALUATION_ORDERED (R-DIL-02) |
| EARLY_READINESS_CHECK | REGISTRATION_CHECK_PASSED | product = HP and registration clear in SCIS | VALUATION_ORDERED (R-DIL-03) |
| EARLY_READINESS_CHECK | ENCUMBRANCE_UNRESOLVED | product = MTG and encumbrance_status = unresolved | ENCUMBRANCE_BLOCKED (R-DIL-04) |
| ENCUMBRANCE_BLOCKED | ENCUMBRANCE_CLEARED | encumbrance_status = clear | VALUATION_ORDERED (R-DIL-05) |
| ENCUMBRANCE_BLOCKED | HOLD_EXPIRED | still unresolved at the hold limit | RETURNED_TO_ROUTE_DIL (R-DIL-06) |
| COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED | TITLE_DOCUMENTS_MISSING | title documents not found | COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED (R-SET-22) |

| `treatment.state` | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | readiness outcome reported | `treatment_type` is DEED_IN_LIEU or SETTLEMENT | Draft, with `outcome` and `outcome_at` written |
| Draft | decision record refused or failed | X2, X3 | Draft, unchanged |

The readiness step moves from running to waiting on each signal and ends when the parent closes the stage. No readiness state is stored as a lifecycle of its own: the answer is the outcome columns, the hold date and the decision record, and the case states above stay the parent's.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The recovery squad (RW-TRIBE) | Writes the readiness branch, the three activities, the view read and the repository |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the answer, holds the case while the route is blocked and receives the title-set task; holds CRU |
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer (FCR) | Reads the answer and acts on the resumed route; holds CRUA |
| RW-SPECIAL, RW-GUARANT | Read the answer; hold CRU |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL, RW-CONDUCT, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-BIANAL | Read the answer; right R only |
| RW-PRODHEAD, RW-CREDCOMM | Read the answer; right RA, and no approval is made in this story |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-AGENT | Read as service identities, subject to the same checks |
| The case status, the task and its clock | Not this story: rwb-case owns them and the parent moves and raises (ASM-4394) |
| The valuation order, the price, the floor and the second signature | Not this story: S1 rwb-valuation and the deed-in-lieu offer stories hold them |

The rights above are those of TSD S2 T6.1 for the capability area "Treatment and offer", and the check itself is the platform guard library's: this story declares the area and the right R and calls the guard, and it owns no check of its own. No delegation of authority level applies, because a readiness check is not a credit decision. No credential and no personal name appears in the request, the payloads or the logs, which carry case and treatment identifiers, collateral and asset keys, statuses, dates and rule versions only.

`treatment` is the only business table this story writes, in schema `rwb_treatment` and through this service's own login (DP-01). The three views are read with SELECT only under DP-05 and no ACE object is written; the `decision_record` row is a library object of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON written in the caller's transaction, and `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision` is P7's and is named here only. The encumbrance status, the title-set status and the hold date are not columns of `rwb_treatment`: no source gives them one, and TSD S2 T3.1 carries no such field, so they travel in the answer and in the decision record (GAP-2674; ASM-4396).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-treatment (S2); base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` (DP-13). None of its own. The readiness answer is served as the optional `readiness` section of the treatment read `GET /treatments/{treatmentId}`, whose operation entry belongs to RWB-S2-E3001-CON and whose section is declared by RWB-S2-E3013-CON as a compatible addition at major version 1. This story fills that section and publishes no operation entry of its own: the check is started by R-DIL-01 on the case signal and the officer takes no action in it, so there is no write operation to publish, and the legacy endpoint table of RWB-E3-013 names only the treatment read that already exists (GAP-2674; ASM-4396).

The section carries the check type, the encumbrance status, the title-set status, the checked time, the rule ID and version, the hold date and the references by business key — the property names are the working read of the contract story and are not restated here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The route, the product group and the collateral keys arrive on the signal the parent forwards, the collateral facts are read from this service's own views, and the decision record is called in process inside the caller's transaction (DP-03; DP-05; ASM-4394). This is why the Work Package records no C dependency for this story.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic of the service is `rwb.treatment.events.v1` with event names `rwb.treatment.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and its events `TreatmentApproved` and `TreatmentClosed` belong to the approval and closure stories. This story writes no outbox row of its own and reports its outcome to the parent as a stage outcome.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` (EV-30) | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The DEEDINLIEU and SETTLEMENT package versions in force, so each check is evaluated and recorded with the version it used |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` (EV-06) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | A deviation raised on the case, so the stage holds while the case clock is paused |

Both events arrive through the inbox of the outbox library, deduplicated by cloud event id, so a redelivery changes nothing. The case status change is not an event of this table: it arrives as the signal the parent forwards (ASM-4394).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TreatmentWorkflow` (deed-in-lieu readiness branch) | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, the child of `CaseWorkflow` | `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the route R3, the product group and the collateral keys; signals: the case status forwarded by the parent, the rule package in force and the deviation |
| `readEncumbrance` | Activity | `rwb-treatment` | The collateral and asset keys in; the encumbrance, registration and title-set facts of the three views out, read only |
| `evaluateReadiness` | Activity | `rwb-treatment` | The facts in; the outcome of R-DIL-01 to R-DIL-06 and R-SET-22 with the hold date and the rule version out |
| `recordAndApply` | Activity | `rwb-treatment` | The `DecisionRecord` and the `treatment` row written in one transaction through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, and the stage outcome for the parent |

The stage is the deed-in-lieu branch of the one `TreatmentWorkflow` the service owns, and the parent-and-child model with the steps of receive, ask, record and apply, wait is the one of the target design (DP-12; Architecture v5 slides 5 and 11). The activity names are a design choice of this story and are fixed by no source document. A workflow class never calls the decision-record library directly: the call is made inside `recordAndApply`, so a replay reuses the recorded decision.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step runs from the signal the parent forwards, and the 2 working-day lead clock, the 10 working-day hold and the 5 working-day title-set clock are durable timers inside the workflow, not Temporal Schedules. The service has no legacy Quartz job in this legacy key.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `treatment` | `rwb_treatment` | S2 rwb-treatment | Written for `decision_log_id`, `outcome`, `outcome_at` and the standard record columns; created by the per-service Flyway sequence and never re-created here |
| `decision_record` | `rwb_treatment` | PLT, library object | Not written directly: the row is written by RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the caller's transaction (DP-03) |
| `v_ace_collateral`, `v_ace_collateral_detail`, `v_ace_npa_asset` | `recovery` (read-only views) | ACE, read through DP-05 | Read only; never written and never owned |

No table of another service is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01). The case, the task and the timer are rwb-case's and are not read here (ASM-4394). No encumbrance, title-set or hold column is added to `treatment`, because no source gives one (GAP-2674; ASM-4396).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| RWB-S2-E3013-CON readiness fake | The `readiness` section, the title-set task request and the error set | A clear mortgage; an unresolved mortgage with a hold date; an HP asset with clearance in SCIS; a collateral-release case with title documents missing; a case with no collateral row |
| RWB-PLT-E1027-CON writer fake | The decision record | An accepted record with chain sequence and entry hash; a refusal with MSG-P7-009 and the field; a failed write raising MSG-P7-003 |
| RWB-PLT-N001-CON route fake | The gateway-bff composite route | A composite answer for SCR-16 that joins the treatment read and its readiness section; a refused route for a role without right R |
| rwb-case case-status mock | The signal the parent forwards, used by AC2 and AC3 | A case at COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED and a case at ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL; a case status the readiness step does not accept. Test-only, adds no contract dependency (ASM-4394) |
| ACE view fixture | The read of the three views | A mortgage collateral with a clear registration and present title documents; one with an unresolved encumbrance; one with the title document numbers absent; one HP asset with a clear SCIS registration |

The readiness fake is the published contract of RWB-S2-E3013-CON; the case-status mock and the view fixture stand in for the signal of the parent and for the ACE read, which have no published shape of their own here (GAP-2674; ASM-4394, ASM-4395).

| REST | 0 operations of its own | 0 | The readiness section is served inside the treatment read of RWB-S2-E3001-CON |

| Temporal | 0 | `TreatmentWorkflow` readiness branch and 3 activities on `rwb-treatment` | Namespace `rwb-recovery`; stage child of `CaseWorkflow`; no Schedule |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.treatment`, modules `readiness` and `web`, with the published types in `...treatment.api`. Service base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1`, schema `rwb_treatment`, topic `rwb.treatment.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the transaction rule of the check: the record and the `treatment` row commit together, and a failed record leaves nothing behind. DP-05 is the read of the three views, taken as this service's own read-only views, which is the form that adds no dependency; the alternative, the contract read of rwb-source-data, would be a C dependency and is not taken here (ASM-4395). DP-13 moves the base of the operations the screens use and nothing else. DP-19 is how SCR-16 and SCR-14 reach this service, one hop through the gateway, so no screen reads a view or a table.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `TreatmentWorkflow` readiness branch | Workflow | One execution per case per stage; the route facts, the collateral keys, the package in force and the stage outcome |
| `readEncumbrance` | Activity | The read of the three views and the encumbrance, registration and title-set facts |
| `evaluateReadiness` | Activity | The DEEDINLIEU and SETTLEMENT evaluation, the outcome, the hold date and the rule version |
| `recordAndApply` | Activity | The `DecisionRecord` and the `treatment` row in one transaction through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| `ReadinessRepository` | Repository | The readiness columns of `treatment` in `rwb_treatment`, with the optimistic lock of `version` |
| `AceViewReader` | Repository, read only | The SELECT against the three views by `collateral_no` and `asset_key` |
| `StageOutcomeReporter` | Signal reporter | The outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` uses to move the case and raise the title-set task; it reports, it never changes a case row |

**Database.** `treatment` holds the readiness columns of DF-TRT-003, DF-TRT-013 and DF-TRT-014 and the standard record columns of T3.0, with the optimistic lock on `version`. No new table and no new column: the encumbrance status, the title-set status and the hold date have no field in the source and stay in the answer and the decision record (GAP-2674; ASM-4396). `decision_record` is the library object applied by the per-service Flyway sequence, written only through the library.

**Configuration and reference data.** The capability area "Treatment and offer" and right R are access rows of rwb-access, read through its guard. The three clocks and the hold limit are values in force in the rule set, read with the package version and never written in code (BR-S2-013). The grant on the three views is a DB story's, not this one's: this story reads them under the login it is given (DP-05; ASM-4395).

**Build steps**

1. The readiness branch of `TreatmentWorkflow` and its input record, registered on `rwb-treatment` as the stage child of `CaseWorkflow`, with the case signal and the route facts (AC3).
2. `AceViewReader` and `readEncumbrance` against the view fixture, read only (AC1).
3. `evaluateReadiness` against the DEEDINLIEU and SETTLEMENT packages, with the clear, blocked, resumed and returned outcomes and the title-set request (AC1, AC2, AC3).
4. `recordAndApply` with the `DecisionRecord`, the `MANDATORY` transaction and the `treatment` row, plus the failed-write path (AC4).
5. The readiness section of the answer with the guard check on right R and the error mapping of section 12.1 (AC1).
6. `StageOutcomeReporter` and the parent signal, with the two rule outcomes of AC2 and AC3 and the title-set request.
7. Tests for AC1 to AC4 against the fakes and the view fixture, plus the two component cases of section 16.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.treatment.readiness-check`.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the step runs from a synthetic case signal in SIT, a clear mortgage orders the valuation, an unresolved mortgage blocks with its hold date, a missing title set reports the request the parent turns into a task, a repeated `asset_key` read returns the same answer, the decision record and the `treatment` row commit or roll back together, and SCR-16 answers through the gateway-bff composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is absent or invalid, or no collateral row is found for the case | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role does not hold right R on the capability area | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P7-009 | The decision record is refused for a field | The decision record was refused: {field} is missing or not valid. |

MSG-S2-001, MSG-S2-002 and MSG-S2-003 are the offer messages of the same module and belong to RWB-S2-E3002-APP and RWB-S2-E3003-APP; the readiness check raises none of them. The message shown when the route is blocked and held has no text in any source and is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2674; ASM-4394). The four texts above are carried unchanged from the legacy story, and no message identifier is added or renamed. MSG-P4-002 is the access answer of the guard library, and MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P7-009 are raised by RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and shown here. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-16 Deed in lieu (Checks; appraisal; approved; transferred) and SCR-14 Treatment record (Draft; submitted; approved; booked; broken) are the two legacy screens of this story and keep their state lists unchanged. The "Checks" state of SCR-16 is where the officer reads the encumbrance status, the title-set status, the hold date, the rule ID and version and the check time; the blocked state shows the hold and its review date and nothing is negotiated while it lasts. Both screens reach the service through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop each (DP-19); the screen field list and the composite route specification belong to the platform edge story and the screen owners, and this story fixes the service side of the answer only.
