| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-E3-013-01 | AC1 | End to end | Check encumbrance and eligibility before negotiation |
| TC-E3-013-02 | AC2 | End to end | Rule R-SET-22 |
| TC-E3-013-03 | AC3 | End to end | Rule R-DIL-01 |
| TC-E3-013-04 | AC4 | End to end | Not recorded |
| TC-E3-013-05 | Access | Component | A role without the right is refused with MSG-P4-002 |
| TC-E3-013-06 | Principle 5 | Component | A forced decision log write failure stops the action with MSG-P7-003 |

The six legacy test case IDs, their Covers and their Data are kept in order and character for character; the legacy level "System" maps to "End to end" and "Access" and "Principle 5" map to "Component", as in the other stories of this run. The readiness fake, the decision-record writer fake, the route fake and the ACE view fixture of section 12.8 stand behind every case, and the case-status mock supplies the two statuses of AC2 and AC3. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in the legacy test document under the same test case ID. The `-ITG` copies of these cases belong to the wave 2 integration harness and are not listed here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No value that a business person may change is written in code: the encumbrance and title statuses, the hold limit and the three clocks are values in force in the rule set, read with the package version (BR-S2-013).
- No personal data in logs, events, workflow inputs, prompts or the fixture: the rows carry case and treatment identifiers, collateral and asset keys, statuses, dates and rule versions only, and the test data is synthetic.
- No read of another service's table and no write to an ACE object: the collateral facts come from the three read-only views and the case rows are never touched (DP-01; DP-05).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views, and here only through the views, with SELECT granted to this service's login and no derivation of a status in code (ASM-4395).
- No encumbrance, title-set or hold column in `rwb_treatment`; a schema change that adds one fails the guardrail test (GAP-2674; ASM-4396).
- No event of this story and no outbox row: the outcome is reported to the parent, so a replay of the stage produces no second message.
- The decision record and the `treatment` row commit in one transaction through the `MANDATORY` rule of the library; an action that commits without its record is a build failure, not a defect (DP-03).
- An applied migration is never edited: any correction to the `treatment` table is a new version on the service sequence.
- No screen calls a service directly and no screen reads a view: SCR-14 and SCR-16 go through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E3-013 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **restructuring officer (RW-RESTRUCT)**, I want **the encumbrance and eligibility answer of a deed-in-lieu check applied to my case by the case workflow — the case moved to EARLY_READINESS_CHECK or held in COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED, the early-readiness or title task raised with its due date from the rule's timer spec, and one decision record naming the rule and the package version written in the same transaction** so that **a deed in lieu is never negotiated on an asset that cannot transfer, and the case itself shows why it moved and when the next step is due**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A deed in lieu transfers an asset, so the encumbrance and title position has to be known before the offer is negotiated. The legacy story ran the encumbrance and title checks early in the deed-in-lieu route, so that a sale officer does not negotiate a release on an asset that cannot transfer, and it recorded the result with its rule version. When the title documents are missing, the legacy story raises a task to re-create the title set before release and keeps the case where it is; when the route is approved, it prioritises the lead and starts the early readiness checks.

In the target the same journey is cut across services. rwb-treatment (S2) owns the treatment, the deed-in-lieu agreement and the check itself: it reads the collateral, the collateral detail and the non-performing-asset data it needs and evaluates the SET and DIL rule packages in its own service, so the check answer is produced where the treatment lives. rwb-case (P3) owns the case of record: the case state, the task, its due date and the local decision record. This story is the case side of that split. It receives the RuleResult of R-DIL-01 or R-SET-22 through the contract of RWB-S2-E3013-CON, applies the outcome as a state move and a task, holds the due date as a durable timer of `CaseWorkflow`, writes the decision record with the rule ID and the package version in the same `rwb_case` transaction, and publishes CaseStateChanged. It reads no treatment row, no collateral view and no ACE data itself: the check belongs to S2 and the ACE collateral views belong to P1 rwb-source-data.

What the case keeps is small on purpose. The answer is not copied into `rwb_case`: only the outcome code, the check reference and the decision record ID of the record written with the move are stored, so a later reader can find the evidence in the ledger without a second copy of the check in a second schema. That boundary is DP-01 (never read another service's tables) and DP-05 (ACE data only through the owner's contract or the service's own views) applied to a service that owns neither the check nor the collateral.

The realignment work is therefore: the monolith's in-process call from the deed-in-lieu flow to the encumbrance and title check and to the case state move becomes a contract (DP-13 renames the base to `/api/recovery/case/v1` and the S2 contract carries the answer), the state move becomes one `rwb_case` transaction with its outbox rows and its decision record, the due date becomes a durable timer instead of a scheduler row, and the check state becomes a read-only part of the case record composed at the edge by gateway-bff (DP-19) rather than a second screen reading a second database.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S2-E3013-CON is published: the check-answer resource of rwb-treatment (S2) with its rule ID, its package version, its outcome code, its check reference and its task instruction, its error envelope and its contract fake. The method, the path and the field names of that operation are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0736; ASM-1316); the S2 contract story fixes them, and this story builds against that contract and its fake and never against rwb-treatment, the treatment tables or an ACE view.
- The `rwb_case` schema baseline and the case of record exist from the Epic 1 case story (RWB-P3-E1018-APP): `recovery_case`, `task`, `timer`, `assignment`, `queue`, `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key`.
- `CaseWorkflow` (parent, workflow ID = case ID, one per case) runs on task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` from the reference workflow story (RWB-P3-E2043-APP), with the workflow kit of the platform contract stories.
- The local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` are published by the platform contract story of DP-03, and the library writes the record in the caller's transaction.
- The case can already hold the deed-in-lieu route: the route decision moved the case to ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL, and the release request moved it to COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED, by the route and treatment stories of this epic.
- Packages SET and DIL are in force for the business date with rows R-SET-22 and R-DIL-01, each row carrying its action text, its owner role and its timer spec; the version in force per environment is the version the answer carries.
- The properties of the check, its batch size and its timeout are the business of rwb-treatment; the only local parameter this story would need is the name of the timeout of the call, and that name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0736; ASM-1319), so the platform contract default of one hop and 2 s is used.

##### 4. Flow

1. The deed-in-lieu route reaches the point where the encumbrance and eligibility check decides the next step: R-DIL-01 on an approved route, R-SET-22 on a release request.
2. The case router of rwb-case signals `CaseWorkflow` (workflow ID = case ID) for the case; the parent workflow already holds the case from entry to closure and starts the treatment stage as a child on queue `rwb-treatment`.
3. `CaseWorkflow` runs its `EvaluateAndApply` step for the case. The step calls the rwb-treatment check-answer operation of RWB-S2-E3013-CON for the case: one hop, 2 s, breaker; the call is recorded in the workflow history, so a replay reuses the same answer and never asks twice.
4. The answer names the rule ID (R-DIL-01 or R-SET-22), the package version, the outcome code, the check reference and the task instruction. An answer that names neither rule is rejected as not this story's answer and no state, task or record is written.
5. R-DIL-01 on a case in ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL: the case moves to EARLY_READINESS_CHECK, and the early-readiness task is raised for role RW-RESTRUCT with its `due_at` from the timer spec of the rule row that fired.
6. R-SET-22 on a case in COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED with the title documents missing: a task is raised to re-create the title set before release, and the case stays in COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED.
7. `EvaluateAndApply` writes, in one `rwb_case` transaction: the case state and `rule_version`, the task row with its `task_code` and `due_at`, the `timer` projection row of that due date, the three check columns (outcome code, check reference, decision record ID) and the local decision record naming the rule ID and the package version, hash-linked to the previous record; and it inserts CaseStateChanged and DecisionRecorded in the outbox.
8. A failed write rolls the whole transaction back, so the state does not move, no task exists and no decision record exists: the user sees MSG-P7-003 and the step is retried with the same answer.
9. `CaseWorkflow` holds the due date of the raised task as a durable timer of the workflow kit and raises TimerBreached through its own state when the timer passes; no Quartz row and no five-minute timer check is involved.
10. A repeated answer for the case — the same check reference with the same outcome code — is absorbed by the inbox row and the idempotency key: no second state change, no second task, no second decision record and no second event.
11. `NoPackageInForce` in the answer is a refusal, never a default move: MSG-P3-027 names the package and the business date, the case keeps its state and no task is raised.
12. The case owner and the restructuring officer see the check state on SCR-16 and SCR-14 through the gateway-bff composite route, which composes it from the existing case read and the treatment stage answer in one hop each, read only (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The answer names no rule ID, or names a rule other than R-DIL-01 or R-SET-22 | The answer is not applied; no state, task, record or event is written; the step fails with the contract error and the case keeps its state | MSG-GEN-001 | AC3 |
| X2 | The rwb-treatment operation does not answer within 2 seconds or is unavailable | No state change and no task; the step is retried with the same answer on the workflow retry policy; the case keeps its state | MSG-GEN-001 | AC3 |
| X3 | The answer carries the same check reference and outcome code twice | The inbox row and the idempotency key absorb the repeat; no second state change, task, record or event | None | AC4 |
| X4 | No SET or DIL version is in force for the business date | `NoPackageInForce`; MSG-P3-027 names the package and the business date; the case keeps its state and no task is raised | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X5 | The local decision-record write fails during the apply | The transaction rolls back: the state, the check columns, the task and the timer do not move; the user sees MSG-P7-003 | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X6 | A role without Treatment and offer R reads the check state | Refused; nothing is returned and nothing is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC7 |
| X7 | A user reads the check state of a case outside their scope | Refused with 404; nothing is returned and nothing is written | MSG-P4-003 | AC7 |
| X8 | `CaseWorkflow` is replayed after a worker restart | The recorded answer is reused; no second call to rwb-treatment and no second write | None | AC4 |

The retry policy of a failed step is the platform policy (1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts), and `NoPackageInForce` is non-retryable. A rejection under X1 or X2 is a contract failure between two services and is counted in the step metrics of rwb-case; the check itself and its data quality remain the exception of rwb-treatment, which owns the treatment and the collateral read.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on Day 1 against the RWB-S2-E3013-CON contract fake and the platform workflow and decision-record kits; no work order sits inside another team's lane |
| Negotiable | The rule rows, the timer specs, the package versions and the outcome codes are data of the packages and of the S2 contract; the story fixes the case-side behaviour only |
| Valuable | A deed in lieu is not negotiated on an asset that cannot transfer, and the early-readiness work is on the right desk with a due date the case holds |
| Estimable | One step of one workflow, one client, one comparator, one apply service, one migration, one read-only screen field |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each of the eight criteria of section 7 is one automated test; the cross-service answer is stubbed in the rwb-treatment contract fake |

AC1 to AC8 are new for the rwb-case slice: the four legacy criteria of RWB-E3-013 are proved end to end by RWB-ITG-E3013-ITG and by the S2 slice RWB-S2-E3013-APP, so this story owns no legacy criterion and copies none. The package version labels "DIL-2026.12" and "SET-2026.12", the check reference "CHK-SYN-0313", the outcome code "ELIGIBLE" and the case ID are synthetic test fixtures of the same kind as the legacy "SYN" values; the version in force, the outcome code and the check reference of a real case come from the S2 answer and the rwb-decision registry (GAP-0736; ASM-1321).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The encumbrance and eligibility check is run before a deed in lieu is negotiated, so that a release is not negotiated on an asset that cannot transfer | FEAT-TRT-13; legacy RWB-E3-013 AC1 |
| BR2 | An approved deed-in-lieu route prioritises the lead and starts the early readiness checks | R-DIL-01; legacy RWB-E3-013 AC3 |
| BR3 | When the title documents are missing, a task is raised to re-create the title set before release and the case stays in COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED | R-SET-22; legacy RWB-E3-013 AC2 |
| BR4 | The check answer is applied by the case workflow that owns the case state; rwb-treatment owns the check, its data and its rule evaluation | RWB-S2-E3013-CON; DP-05; ASM-1316 |
| BR5 | The result is written to the decision record with the rule ID and the rule version | legacy RWB-E3-013 AC1; DP-03 |
| BR6 | A decision that cannot be recorded does not proceed: the record, the state move, the task and the outbox row are one transaction, and the user sees MSG-P7-003 | Principle 5; legacy RWB-E3-013 AC4; DP-03 |
| BR7 | `NoPackageInForce` is a refusal, never a default move: no state change, no task, MSG-P3-027 | legacy RWB-E3-013 AC1, AC3 read with the platform rule refusal |
| BR8 | A repeated answer for the same check reference changes nothing and raises no second event | legacy RWB-E3-013 AC1; inbox and idempotency key |
| BR9 | The answer is not copied into `rwb_case`: only the outcome code, the check reference and the decision record ID are stored, and collateral and title fields are never read from the treatment tables or from an ACE view | DP-01, DP-05 |
| BR10 | The task due date is the timer spec of the rule row that fired, held as a durable timer of `CaseWorkflow`, not as a scheduler row | R-DIL-01, R-SET-22 timer spec; ASM-1318; platform workflow kit |
| BR11 | Reading the check state requires Treatment and offer R and the caller's scope; a read writes nothing | legacy RWB-E3-013 permission check; MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 |
| BR12 | The case state values of this story are ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL, EARLY_READINESS_CHECK and COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED, as named by R-DIL-01 and R-SET-22; no code invents a further state | legacy RWB-E3-013 AC2, AC3 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL | EARLY_READINESS_CHECK | R-DIL-01 fires on the approved route of the deed in lieu | EARLY_READINESS_CHECK |
| COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED | TITLE_SET_RECREATE | R-SET-22 fires and the title documents are missing | COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED (no change; task and timer raised) |
| ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL | NoPackageInForce | no SET or DIL version is in force | ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL (no change) |
| Any of the above | apply failed | the decision record cannot be written | unchanged (the whole transaction rolls back) |

These are the case states named by R-DIL-01 and R-SET-22 in the legacy story; on `recovery_case` the state is held in `route_state` (DF-CAS-007) as the sibling rwb-case stories hold it. The case status stays "In progress", and the story writes no stage code and no closure. The legacy AC2 wording — "the case moves to COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED" from a case already in COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED — is read as the case staying in that state with a task raised, which is the only reading that keeps the release from proceeding on a missing title set.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-case service identity (its own login, one per service) | Runs the `EvaluateAndApply` step, writes the case state, the task, the timer, the check columns and the decision record |
| rwb-treatment service identity (S2) | Owns the check, reads the collateral data it is entitled to, evaluates SET and DIL, and answers the check result through its contract; never writes the case state |
| CaseWorkflow | Holds the durable timer of the task due date and raises TimerBreached through its own state; moves no state by itself |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the local decision record and its outbox row in the caller's transaction (DP-03) |
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer | Receives the early-readiness task and reads the check state on cases in scope (Treatment and offer R) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the check state on cases in scope and sees the task and its due date (Treatment and offer R) |
| RW-LEGAL, legal officer | Reads the check state on the deed-in-lieu cases in scope (Treatment and offer R) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reassigns a task of the check and reads the cases of the team (Treatment and offer R) |
| RW-REFADM, reference-data administrator | Holds no Treatment and offer R; refused on the read with MSG-P4-002 |

The check is not re-run from the case side by any role: a person who needs a new check asks rwb-treatment, which owns the treatment and the check reference.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity in rwb_case | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case | id, case_no, product_group, primary_person_key, status, stage_code and 17 more; `route_state` (DF-CAS-007) carries the state this story moves | Read; `route_state` and `rule_version` written |
| DF-CAS-007 | recovery_case | route_state (the case state of section 9) | Write |
| DF-CAS-021 | recovery_case | rule_version (the package version that fired) | Write |
| DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-026 | task | id, case_id, task_code, element_type, discretion, status and 4 more; the task of AC1 and AC2 with its `due_at` | Write |
| DF-WRK-009 to DF-WRK-016 | assignment | id, case_id, task_id, assignee_user_id, assigned_at, ended_at and 2 more; the placement of the raised task | Write |
| DF-WRK-030, DF-WRK-031, DF-WRK-035 | timer | timer_type, started_at, status; the screen projection of the due date behind the timers read | Write |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_record (local, in rwb_case) and decision_log_entry (rwb_decision) | all fields | Write locally in the same transaction; the central entry is sealed by rwb-decision |
| DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-014 | treatment (rwb_treatment, owner S2) | the treatment and deed-in-lieu agreement of the case | Not read and not written: the check answer is a contract field, and the treatment belongs to S2 (DP-01) |
| DF-ACE-091 to DF-ACE-098 | v_ace_collateral (read by S2/P1, not by rwb-case) | collateral_no, asset_key, account_key, collateral_value, collateral_type, register_date and 2 more | Not read: ACE data reaches the case only through rwb-treatment's answer or the P1 contract (DP-05) |
| DF-ACE-196 to DF-ACE-207 | v_ace_collateral_detail (read by S2/P1, not by rwb-case) | asset_key, title_doc_no, plot_no, area_text, province, lien_rank and 6 more | Not read; the missing-title outcome arrives as the R-SET-22 answer |
| DF-ACE-208 to DF-ACE-219 | v_ace_npa_asset (read by S2/P1, not by rwb-case) | asset_ref, asset_key, asset_code, transfer_in_type, from_segment, book_value and 6 more | Not read |

Three columns are added to `recovery_case` for the case-side record of the check (`check_ref`, `check_outcome_code`, `decision_record_id`); their field IDs in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0736; ASM-1320), so the table above cites the existing entity range and the three columns by name.

The answer fields themselves — the rule ID, the package version, the outcome code, the check reference and the task instruction — are read from the rwb-treatment contract and are stored only as the outcome code, the check reference and the decision record ID. No collateral row, title document row, plot row or asset row is written into `rwb_case`, and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This story adds no person-facing operation and no new path: the check state is shown on SCR-16 and SCR-14 from the existing case read `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` of rwb-case, composed by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and the state move writes nothing that a caller posts. The legacy deed-in-lieu read of the treatment record on the old base becomes rwb-treatment's `GET /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` (DP-13), owned by S2 and not by this story.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0736; ASM-1316) | rwb-treatment (S2) | The encumbrance and eligibility check answer of RWB-S2-E3013-CON for the case: the rule ID (R-DIL-01 or R-SET-22), the package version, the outcome code, the check reference and the task instruction; built against the contract and its fake | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | rwb-access (P4) | The Treatment and offer R right, the Case record right and the scope before a person read, cached by the guard library | One hop, 2 s |

The check-answer operation is the only service call of this story; its method, its path and its field names are fixed by RWB-S2-E3013-CON, and rwb-case makes no call to rwb-source-data, to an ACE view or to rwb-decision for this check.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId | caseId, fromRouteState, toRouteState, ruleId (R-DIL-01 or R-SET-22), packageVersion, taskCode |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 owns the type and the central ledger; every service writes its own record | caseId | decision record reference, rule ID, package version, business date |

Both are written to the outbox in the same `rwb_case` transaction as the state move and relayed with the CloudEvents envelope; no personal data is carried and the account number is not in any payload.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The check answer arrives by a REST call inside the workflow step (12.2), so this story consumes no event and opens no consumer of its own; the inbox row is used only to deduplicate a repeated answer (AC4).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow (parent, one per case, workflow ID = case ID) | `rwb-case` | Holds the case from entry to closure, runs the step for the check answer, and waits on the durable timer of the task due date |
| EvaluateAndApply | Step of CaseWorkflow (in-workflow, no separate activity) | `rwb-case` | Calls the S2 check-answer operation, rejects an answer that names neither rule, applies the state move or the hold, and writes the task, the timer, the check columns, the decision record and the outbox rows in one transaction |
| durable timer | Timer of CaseWorkflow | `rwb-case` | Holds the due date of the early-readiness task or of the title task and raises TimerBreached through the workflow state |

No other activity is added. The rule evaluation is not done here: it is S2's, and this story only applies the answer it receives.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step is started by the case workflow on the deed-in-lieu route, not by a Schedule, and no Quartz row and no timer check job is created.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | P3 (rwb_case) | The story adds `check_ref`, `check_outcome_code` and `decision_record_id`, and writes `route_state`, `rule_version` and the status of the case |
| task | P3 (rwb_case) | The early-readiness task of R-DIL-01 and the title task of R-SET-22, with `task_code` and `due_at` |
| timer | P3 (rwb_case) | The screen projection of the due date; the clock itself is the durable timer of CaseWorkflow |
| outbox_event | PLT library, created in rwb_case | The published events of 12.3, written in the same transaction |
| processed_event | PLT library, created in rwb_case | The inbox row that absorbs a repeated answer |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_case | The key of the answer: case ID, check reference and outcome code |
| decision_record | P3 (rwb_case) | The local decision record of the move or hold, hash-linked, written in the same transaction (DP-03) |

Treatment rows are S2's and the collateral, collateral-detail and NPA rows are ACE's, read by S2 and by P1: rwb-case holds no copy, no foreign key and no cross-schema join (DP-01).

| rwb-treatment WireMock | The S2 contract of RWB-S2-E3013-CON | The R-DIL-01 answer with package version "DIL-2026.12"; the R-SET-22 missing-title answer with package version "SET-2026.12"; a delayed answer beyond 2 s; the `NoPackageInForce` answer; an unreadable answer (no rule ID) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `encumbrance`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.encumbrance`; front end `src/modules/recovery/case/EncumbranceCheckState.tsx`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/<service>` base of the monolith | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 is the schema rule behind the store boundary of 12.7 and AC3 (no read of another service's table); it adds no dependency and is not a pattern change of this story. DP-05 resolves to no ACE view and no rwb-source-data call here: rwb-case reads no collateral, no collateral detail and no NPA row, because the check and its data belong to rwb-treatment and the ACE views belong to rwb-source-data. The H and C dependencies this table adds are held by the platform contract stories and are not repeated in the metadata rows, which carry only the contract dependency of the legacy read: RWB-S2-E3013-CON (ASM-1317).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CheckAnswerClient | Client | Calls the rwb-treatment check-answer operation with one hop, the 2 s timeout and a breaker; rejects an answer that names neither R-DIL-01 nor R-SET-22 |
| CheckAnswerComparator | Service | Builds the idempotency key from case ID, check reference and outcome code and reports a repeat so nothing is written twice |
| CheckOutcomeApplier | Service | Maps the answer to the case-side outcome: the move to EARLY_READINESS_CHECK by R-DIL-01, the hold in COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED with the title task by R-SET-22, and the refusal on `NoPackageInForce` |
| CaseCheckRepository | Repository | Writes `route_state`, `rule_version`, `check_ref`, `check_outcome_code` and `decision_record_id` in schema `rwb_case` only |
| TaskTimerWriter | Service | Writes the task row with its `task_code` and `due_at` from the rule's timer spec, the assignment and the `timer` projection, and signals the due date to CaseWorkflow |
| DecisionRecordWriter | Library adapter | Writes the local decision record with the rule ID and the package version, hash-linked, in the same transaction (DP-03) |
| CaseCheckEventPublisher | Outbox adapter | Inserts CaseStateChanged and DecisionRecorded in the outbox in the same transaction |
| EncumbranceCheckState | React component | Shows the check state, the outcome code and the task due date on SCR-16 and SCR-14, read only |

**Database and migrations**

- Migration `V3013_1__encumbrance_check.sql` adds `check_ref` varchar(40), `check_outcome_code` varchar(20) and `decision_record_id` uuid to `recovery_case`, nullable, with no database constraint on the outcome code (the list is validated by the contract of S2).
- No new table: the task, the timer, the assignment, the outbox, the inbox, the idempotency and the decision-record tables already exist in `rwb_case`.
- One index for the read of a case by its check reference: `ix_recovery_case_check_ref ON recovery_case (check_ref) WHERE check_ref IS NOT NULL`.
- The migration runs in the rwb-case Flyway sequence of the service's own schema; no other schema is touched.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The rule rows R-DIL-01 and R-SET-22, their action text, their owner role and their timer spec are the data of packages DIL and SET and are owned by rwb-decision with RW-COE as their author; this story reads none of them directly and receives the timer spec in the answer (ASM-1316).
- No parameter and no list of values is added by this story; the check's own parameters belong to rwb-treatment.
- The role that holds the early-readiness task is the owner role the rule row names, RW-RESTRUCT for R-DIL-01.

**Build steps**

1. `CheckAnswerClient` against the RWB-S2-E3013-CON fake, with the 2 s timeout, the breaker and the rejection of an answer that names neither rule; tests for AC3 and AC1.
2. `CheckAnswerComparator` and the idempotency key; test for AC4.
3. `CheckOutcomeApplier` with the two outcomes and the refusal; tests for AC1, AC2 and AC5.
4. `CaseCheckRepository` and `DecisionRecordWriter` in one transaction with the outbox rows; test for AC6.
5. `TaskTimerWriter` with the due date from the timer spec, the assignment and the signal to CaseWorkflow; tests for AC1 and AC2.
6. Register `EvaluateAndApply` into CaseWorkflow for the deed-in-lieu route and run a replay test, so the recorded answer is reused; test for AC4.
7. The access check and the scope on the read path, with the existing case read; test for AC7.
8. `EncumbranceCheckState` and the composite-route contract test; test for AC8.

**Feature switch.** None is named in the legacy story. The step is reached only when the case is on the deed-in-lieu route and the S2 check answer exists for the case, so the route itself is the switch; a check that has not been run raises no task and moves no state.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the RWB-S2-E3013-CON contract tests stay green, every apply of this story leaves one decision record naming its rule ID and its package version, and no case in the SIT run is released on an asset whose title answer said the documents are missing.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S2-002 | The payoff shown on the deed-in-lieu screen is from an earlier date | The payoff is from {date}. A new figure has been requested. |
| MSG-S2-001 | An offer below the floor is submitted | The offer is below the floor of {floor}. It has been sent for approval. |
| MSG-S2-003 | An offer with an end date is shown | The offer to the customer ends on {date}. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is missing, or the check answer cannot be used | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No SET or DIL version is in force | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Treatment and offer R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A case outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

MSG-S2-001, MSG-S2-002 and MSG-S2-003 are the messages of the S2 check and offer screens and are listed here because the legacy story carries them; the case side renders none of them, and the check state is read only on the case screens. For MSG-P3-027 in this story, {check} is "no package in force" and {detail} names the package code "DIL" or "SET" and the business date only, never a case fact. MSG-GEN-001 is used on the contract path only where the answer is unusable; the case screens add no field of their own.

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | States shown for this story |
|---|---|
| SCR-16 Deed in lieu | The check state and the outcome code of the case, and the due date of the early-readiness task, read only; the screen keeps its own states Checks, appraisal, approved and transferred from S2 |
| SCR-14 Treatment record | The same check state on the case record of the deed in lieu, read only; the screen keeps its own states Draft, submitted, approved, booked and broken from S2 |

Both screens are served by the gateway-bff composite route, which composes the case read of rwb-case with the treatment read of rwb-treatment, one hop each, read only (DP-19); the browser calls no owner service directly. The screen writes nothing: a person who needs the check repeated asks rwb-treatment, and a person who needs the task closed does it on the task, not on the check state. The full read-only case record view, the timer section and the deviation flag remain with RWB-P3-E1023-APP.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the rule IDs, the package versions, the outcome codes, the timer specs, the states and the owner role are data of the packages and of the S2 contract, not constants.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts: logs hold case IDs, check references and rule IDs, never account numbers, names or identity numbers; the workflow payloads pass the payload codec.
- No read of another service's tables and no ACE view: the check answer comes from the rwb-treatment contract, the rights from rwb-access, and `rwb_case` holds no foreign key into another schema (DP-01, DP-05).
- One owner of the check: the encumbrance and title check is run only by rwb-treatment; rwb-case applies the answer and never re-evaluates a rule or re-reads collateral for it.
- A read of the check state writes nothing and raises no event.
- The decision record is written in the same transaction as the state move; a failed write rolls the whole apply back (MSG-P7-003).
- `NoPackageInForce` is never caught and turned into a default move.
- Every outbound event is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the state change and carries IDs and facts only.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E3-013 for the wave 2 integration harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As the **integration and QA harness**, I want **one repeatable cross-service harness that proves the encumbrance and title checks run early, that a missing title document raises the task that re-creates the title set before release, and that the case reaches EARLY_READINESS_CHECK with one decision record naming the rule and its version — across rwb-treatment, rwb-case, the ACE collateral views read through rwb-source-data, and rwb-decision**, so that **a deed in lieu is never negotiated on an asset that cannot transfer, and every early readiness check is proven with the rule and the rule version that decided it**.

The harness builds no production operation, no table, no workflow, no schedule and no screen. RWB-S2-E3013-APP owns the encumbrance and title check inside rwb-treatment, the R-DIL-01 and R-SET-22 rules and the deed-in-lieu treatment; RWB-P3-E3013-APP owns the case move, the task that re-creates the title set and its assignment. This story drives those two services' published contracts, reads the ACE collateral, title and non-performing asset facts through the rwb-source-data products contract, reads the record back from rwb-decision and asserts what the owners did. Nothing here is a deliverable of the Workbench.

##### 2. Business rationale

A deed in lieu negotiated on an asset that cannot transfer wastes the negotiation, and an agreement the bank cannot register exposes it to a void settlement after the customer has already relied on it. The defence is timing: the encumbrance, title and lien facts are checked before the offer is made and not at the transfer, so a case that cannot transfer is stopped while the officer has spent nothing. Those facts are not re-keyed; they are read from ACE's collateral, collateral detail and non-performing asset rows, a task is raised in rwb-case when the title set is incomplete, and every step is recorded with the rule and its version so the decision can be defended years later.

In the monolith this all sat inside one S2 module, so a defect showed up either as a negotiation on an untransferable asset or as a case that moved without a record. In v5 the same behaviour crosses four services: rwb-treatment evaluates R-DIL-01 and R-SET-22 and raises the task, rwb-case holds the case state, the task and its assignment, rwb-source-data owns the ACE view contract the collateral and asset facts are read through, and rwb-decision holds the record with its rule version. A defect at any of those four now looks like a negotiation that should never have started, and only a run that crosses all four can tell the difference between a check that ran and a check that was skipped.

This story owns the harness for FEAT-TRT-13 and its FEAT-TRT-12 parent, and it carries REQ-S2-005, REQ-RDF-004, REQ-DRI-001 and REQ-DRI-005 into evidence. It never reads another service's table (DP-01): the treatment comes from rwb-treatment, the case and the task from rwb-case, the collateral, title and asset facts from rwb-source-data's products contract (DP-05), the record from rwb-decision (DP-03) and the authorisation answer from rwb-access. Every call sits on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with one hop and a 2 s budget (DP-13), and the composed read a screen would make is exercised through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The published contracts of rwb-treatment, rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-decision and rwb-access are in the contract registry, a WireMock stub set is generated from each, and each contract version is pinned in the run report.
- A case is at ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL carrying its deed-in-lieu treatment, and a second case is at COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED whose title documents are missing. Both cases and both treatments are seeded through the owning services' published operations only; the seeding set is not specified in the source documents (GAP-0425; ASM-0601).
- The ACE collateral, collateral detail and non-performing asset rows for the accounts of both cases are available through the P1 products contract, with the lien rank, the title document number and the asset facts the check reads present as ACE holds them.
- The rule package in force carries R-DIL-01 and R-SET-22, and the version of each is readable on the decision record that cites it.
- An authorisation path exists through `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` for a role that holds Treatment and offer R, and for a caller whose role does not.
- The CCMS and Land Office check interface, its result codes and its fixtures are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0425; ASM-0601); where the check leaves the Workbench it is modelled by a fixture on that interface. So are the harness repository and its SIT environment, and the evidence format and its retention (GAP-0425; ASM-0601).
- No build dependency and no contract dependency. Day 1, with the fakes in place from the first run, and each fake replaced by the real service when RWB-S2-E3013-APP and RWB-P3-E3013-APP land.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: seeds both cases, their states and their deed-in-lieu treatments through the owning services' published operations only; the seeding set, its identifiers and its environment are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0425; ASM-0601).
2. Harness: reads the collateral row, its title detail and the non-performing asset row through `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP06/records` and asserts the lien rank, the title document number and the asset facts the check needs, without re-keying any of them (DP-05, REQ-RDF-004).
3. Harness: observes the R-DIL-01 move the owner applies to the route approval, from ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL to EARLY_READINESS_CHECK, and reads the state back with `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}`.
4. Harness: asserts, on the second case where the title set is incomplete, that a task exists and is assigned, through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/me/tasks` and the task read on the rwb-case contract, and that the task names the re-creation of the title set.
5. Harness: asserts that the second case still reads COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED on the R-SET-22 path, that the case did not move to another state, and that the treatment on the case is unchanged.
6. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` for both cases and asserts exactly one record per move, each naming R-DIL-01 or R-SET-22 with its rule version, and asserts `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the same two moves.
7. Harness: asserts that the case move is published as `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` once per move and that no personal data is present on any event it reads.
8. Harness: authorises each call through `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise`, records the refusal for a role that does not hold Treatment and offer R, and asserts the refusal message the owner returns.
9. Harness: asserts one hop per call, a 2 s budget and a circuit breaker per downstream on every call in the trace, and fails the run on a call chain deeper than the gateway and one owner.
10. Harness: writes one evidence report per business date, keyed by story, naming the two moves, the two records with their rule versions, the task and the contract versions; the evidence format and its retention are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0425; ASM-0601).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A fake answers a shape the published contract does not allow, or a reachable service answers on a contract version that differs from the registry | The run fails at that hop, before any later assertion; the report names the service, the operation and both contract versions | None | AC3 |
| X2 | No collateral row answers for the account of the case | The run fails and the report names the account, the data product and the operation; the run is not marked passed | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A lien rank or a title document number is present but the check cannot classify it | The run fails and the report names the field and the row; the harness never substitutes a value | None | AC1 |
| X4 | The case does not reach EARLY_READINESS_CHECK on the R-DIL-01 path | The run fails and the report names the two states and the case | None | AC1 |
| X5 | No task is raised when the title set is incomplete | The run fails and the report names the case, the treatment and the state | None | AC2 |
| X6 | The case moves when the title set is incomplete | The run fails on the R-SET-22 path and the report names the state it moved to | None | AC2 |
| X7 | Zero or two decision records exist for a move, or a record carries no rule version | The run fails and the report names the records it found and the version field it read | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X8 | A decision record cannot be written | The move does not happen, every state is left as it was, the owner answers MSG-P7-003, and the run asserts that nothing changed | MSG-P7-003 | AC3 |
| X9 | A caller whose role does not hold the right calls an operation | The call is refused with MSG-P4-002 and the run asserts the refusal, not a silent pass | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |

The report text is for the wave entry check and is not part of the message standard. R-DIL-01 and R-SET-22 carry no message ID in the rule set, so the harness asserts state, data and the decision record and names a message ID only where the owning service returns MSG-P7-003, MSG-P4-002 or MSG-GEN-001; the business messages this journey can produce are in section 14 and belong to the owning services.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs against published contracts and fakes from Day 1; the only waits are two I stories, RWB-S2-E3013-APP and RWB-P3-E3013-APP |
| Negotiable | The CCMS and Land Office fixture, the seeding set and the report shape are configuration agreed at the wave entry check, not business values in code |
| Valuable | The early encumbrance and title check, the title re-creation task and the record that carries the rule version are proven before the wave opens |
| Estimable | One harness runner, one stub set, one check fixture, one event probe, one report |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against its fakes on Day 1 and again against the real owners as the two app stories land |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Check encumbrance and eligibility before negotiation

  Background:
    Given the rule package in force carries R-DIL-01 and R-SET-22 with a readable version for each
    Given the published contracts of rwb-treatment, rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-decision and rwb-access are in the registry with a stub set generated from each
    Given the seeded case identifiers and the harness environment are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0425; ASM-0601)

  Scenario: AC1 The R-DIL-01 path reaches EARLY_READINESS_CHECK with one record naming the rule and its version (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a case in state ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL carrying its deed-in-lieu treatment
    And the collateral row, its title detail and the non-performing asset row are readable through the P1 products contract
    When the harness reads the collateral, the title document number, the lien rank and the asset facts through the P1 products contract
    And the owning service applies R-DIL-01 to the route approval
    Then the case reads at EARLY_READINESS_CHECK through the rwb-case contract
    And the move is published as rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1 for the case
    And exactly one decision record names R-DIL-01 with its rule version on rwb.decision-record.v1
    And the run is green with one trace and one hop per call

  Scenario: AC2 The R-SET-22 path holds the case and raises the task that re-creates the title set (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a second case in state COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED whose title documents are missing
    When the owning service applies R-SET-22 to the title check
    Then a task exists on the case and its assignment is readable through the rwb-case task read
    And the task names the re-creation of the title set before release
    And the case still reads at COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED
    And the treatment on the case is unchanged
    And exactly one decision record names R-SET-22 with its rule version

  Scenario: AC3 Refusals and a failure that changes nothing (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision-record write is forced to fail for one move
    When that move is attempted
    Then nothing changes on the case, the treatment or the task
    And the owning service answers MSG-P7-003
    And a caller whose role does not hold Treatment and offer R is refused with MSG-P4-002
    And a contract version that differs from the registry fails the run before any assertion
```

The legacy key owns AC1 to AC4 of RWB-E3-013; those criteria test the rwb-treatment behaviour and are held by RWB-S2-E3013-APP and RWB-P3-E3013-APP. This story owns no legacy AC. Its three criteria test only the harness deliverable named in the title: the early check read through the ACE views, the two rules observed as the owners apply them, the task raised when the title set is incomplete, the one record per move with its rule version, and the refusal and failure paths that must not change state.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The encumbrance and title checks run before negotiation starts, and a deed in lieu is not negotiated on an asset that cannot transfer | Legacy RWB-E3-013; REQ-S2-005; FEAT-TRT-13 |
| BR2 | At ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL with the route approved and the route set to R3, the lead is prioritised and the early readiness checks start, and the case moves to EARLY_READINESS_CHECK | R-DIL-01 |
| BR3 | At COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED with the title documents missing, a task re-creates the title set before release and the case stays at COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED | R-SET-22 |
| BR4 | The collateral, title and non-performing asset facts are read through the ACE views and never re-keyed | REQ-RDF-004; legacy RWB-E3-013 |
| BR5 | The decision record carries the rule and its version, and it is written with the state change in one transaction | REQ-DRI-001; R-UNI-39 |
| BR6 | No action proceeds if its decision record cannot be written | REQ-DRI-005; R-UNI-39 |
| BR7 | The treatment is the owner's and the harness writes no treatment row; a seeded treatment is placed through the rwb-treatment contract only | Legacy RWB-E3-013; DP-05 |
| BR8 | The checks run early and not at transfer, so a blocked asset is found before the offer rather than at registration | FEAT-TRT-13; FEAT-TRT-12 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL | ROUTE_APPROVED | decision.approved and route = R3 | EARLY_READINESS_CHECK (R-DIL-01) |
| COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED | TITLE_DOCUMENTS_MISSING | title documents not found | COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED, with a task to re-create the title set (R-SET-22) |

The case state is the owner's: rwb-treatment evaluates the rule and raises the task, the case move is published as `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1`, and both states are read back through the rwb-case contract. The rule table also carries R-DIL-02 and R-DIL-04 out of EARLY_READINESS_CHECK, the clear and the unresolved encumbrance; those belong to the check itself and are asserted by RWB-S2-E3013-APP, not by this harness.

The harness sets nothing by hand. It seeds through the owning services' published operations, lets the owner apply the rule, and then asserts the state the owner reached. A state the harness set by hand would prove nothing, so the report names the owner and the operation behind each move.

| RW-CASEOWN and the roles that hold the title re-creation task | Hold and read the task and its assignment through the rwb-case task read |

| Integration lead | Owns the harness code, the stub set and the swap from a fake to the real service |

| No approval level from the delegation of authority applies | The harness takes no business decision; the deed-in-lieu approval and the early readiness decision belong to the treatment story |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1/cases/{caseId}/treatments` | S2 rwb-treatment | Seed the deed-in-lieu treatment on each case and read its state (AC1, AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` | S2 rwb-treatment | The treatment type, its state and its decision_log_id after each rule applies (AC1, AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/{productCode}/records` | P1 rwb-source-data | The collateral row, its title detail and the non-performing asset row from DP06 (AC1) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case state at EARLY_READINESS_CHECK and at COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED (AC1, AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/me/tasks` | P3 rwb-case | The title re-creation task and its assignment after R-SET-22 (AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | The single record per move, with R-DIL-01 or R-SET-22 and its version (AC1, AC2) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Role, scope and right check for each call, including the refusal path (AC3) |

Every operation is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget and a circuit breaker per downstream (DP-13); where a screen would compose them, the harness calls the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). No operation is invented in this story, and no operation reaches another service's schema.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it seeds through the owners' operations and consumes the owners' events.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | every service, through the local decision-record library | One record per move, written with the state change (AC1, AC2) |
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case move on the R-DIL-01 path, and the absence of a move on the R-SET-22 path (AC1, AC2) |
| `rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1` | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | S2 rwb-treatment | The treatment was approved before the run (AC1) |

All three carry IDs and business facts only, keyed by caseId and treatmentId, and the harness asserts that no personal data is present (DP-03, DP-09).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness exercises the existing TreatmentWorkflow in rwb-treatment, which evaluates R-DIL-01 and R-SET-22, writes the record and raises the task, and the CaseWorkflow in rwb-case, which moves the case status and holds the task and its assignment. It asserts their effects through the services' contracts and the owners' topics. No workflow, activity or Schedule is created, changed or owned by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added. R-DIL-01 and R-SET-22 are triggered by facts and not by a Schedule, and this story sets no cron, overlap policy or catch-up window.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-01); the treatment is rwb-treatment's, the case, the task and the assignment are rwb-case's, the record is rwb-decision's, and the collateral, title and asset rows are ACE's, read through rwb-source-data's contract (DP-05).

| Fake | Contract | Use in the run |
|---|---|---|
| WireMock stub for rwb-treatment | `POST /cases/{caseId}/treatments`, `GET /treatments/{treatmentId}`, `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | Day-1 seeding and reads on both paths before RWB-S2-E3013-APP is live |
| WireMock stub for rwb-case | `GET /cases/{caseId}`, `GET /me/tasks`, `rwb.case.events.v1` | Day-1 assertions on both case states, the task and its assignment |
| WireMock stub for rwb-source-data | `GET /data-products/{productCode}/records` | Day-1 assertions on the collateral row, the title detail and the asset row |
| WireMock stub for rwb-decision | `GET /decision-log`, `rwb.decision-record.v1` | Day-1 assertion of one record per move with its rule version |
| WireMock stub for rwb-access | `POST /authorise` | Day-1 authorisation and refusal path |
| CCMS or Land Office check fixture | The check interface the rule leaves the Workbench through | The check result the owner reads, where the configured check is an outside interface |

Each stub is generated from the published contract and its version is pinned in the run report, so a contract change shows up as a run failure and not as a silent pass. The CCMS and Land Office interface codes, their result codes, their transports and layouts, their test endpoints and the fixture contents, the seeding set, the harness environment and the evidence format and retention are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0425; ASM-0601).

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 7 consumed, one hop each on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-13), composed through gateway-bff where a screen would (DP-19) |
| Kafka | None published; `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` and `rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1` consumed (DP-03, DP-09) |

| File | None. The CCMS or Land Office check is asserted through a fixture where the check leaves the Workbench, and no file is produced or read by the harness |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform H dependencies in the table above (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays None. The blocking dependencies are the two I stories, RWB-S2-E3013-APP and RWB-P3-E3013-APP: until they are live the run uses their stubs, and a stub pass is reported as a stub pass.

The decoupling is also the story's reading of the legacy behaviour. The monolith S2 module's check becomes rwb-treatment's behaviour, with the task raised in rwb-case; the ACE collateral, title and asset facts are read through the P1 products contract and never from a local view or a copy (DP-05); every call sits on the owner's per-service base with a single hop (DP-13); the record is read through the local decision-record library and its shared topic (DP-03); and the composed read a screen would make is exercised through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). Per-service schemas mean no service reads another's tables (DP-01), so the harness fails a run whose trace shows a cross-schema reference.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ReadinessRunner | Job | Runs the two paths in order for a business date and holds the run lock |
| StubSet | Fake | The five WireMock stubs and the check fixture, each generated from the published contract with its version pinned |
| CheckFixture | Fixture | The CCMS or Land Office check result the owner reads, keyed by case and by asset, where the check leaves the Workbench |
| SourceDataProbe | Assertion | Reads the collateral row, its title detail and the asset row through DP06 and asserts the lien rank, the title document number and the asset facts |
| TaskProbe | Assertion | Reads the title re-creation task and its assignment through the rwb-case task read and asserts that the task names the re-creation of the title set |
| RecordProbe | Assertion | Reads one record per move with its rule and rule version from rwb-decision, and cross-checks the same move on `rwb.decision-record.v1` |
| EventProbe | Service | Consumes `rwb.case.events.v1`, `rwb.treatment.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` and asserts the facts for both cases |
| TraceAssertion | Assertion | Fails the run on a call chain deeper than the gateway and one owner, on a call outside the 2 s budget, and on a missing breaker |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes the per-run report keyed by story and business date, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** The harness repository and its SIT environment are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0425; ASM-0601). The run is against the stub set from Day 1 and against each real owner as RWB-S2-E3013-APP and RWB-P3-E3013-APP land. The seed is two cases: one at ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL with its deed-in-lieu treatment, and one at COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED whose title documents are missing; the identifiers, the business date under test and the exact response values of the fakes are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0425; ASM-0601). The collateral, title and asset rows come from the ACE DP06 product as ACE holds them, and the harness copies no values into its fixture. Seeding uses only the owning services' published operations, never a schema write. The evidence format and its retention are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0425; ASM-0601).

**Build steps**

1. Generate the five stubs and the check fixture from the published contracts, pin each contract version in the report and fail the run on a version mismatch (X1).
2. Build the ReadinessRunner and the seed path: two cases, their states and their deed-in-lieu treatments through the owners' operations only, never a schema write.
3. Add SourceDataProbe for AC1: the collateral row, the title detail and the asset row through DP06, with the lien rank, the title document number and the asset facts asserted and none substituted (X2, X3).
4. Add the R-DIL-01 assertion: the move to EARLY_READINESS_CHECK read back through the rwb-case contract, and one record naming R-DIL-01 with its rule version (X4, X7).
5. Add TaskProbe and the R-SET-22 assertion: the task raised, its assignment, the task naming the re-creation of the title set, and the case still at COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED (X5, X6).
6. Add RecordProbe and EventProbe for `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1`, `rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`, and assert the key and the absence of personal data.
7. Add the forced record failure of AC3 and prove that nothing changes on the case, the treatment or the task and that the owner answers MSG-P7-003 (X8).
8. Add the access path through `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise`, including the refusal for a role that does not hold Treatment and offer R (X9).
9. Add TraceAssertion and the EvidenceReport, then swap each stub for its real owner when RWB-S2-E3013-APP and RWB-P3-E3013-APP land and rerun both paths.

**Feature switch.** The legacy key names no feature switch for this behaviour. The harness runs behind the platform feature-flag library as the wave releases it; the flag key for this harness is not specified in the source documents (GAP-0425; ASM-0601).

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass for AC1, AC2 and AC3; both paths pass against the fakes on Day 1 and again against rwb-treatment and rwb-case when RWB-S2-E3013-APP and RWB-P3-E3013-APP land; and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story and business date with the two moves, the two records with their rule versions and the contract and fixture versions named.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record for the move cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's role does not include the right, or the case is outside their scope | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required value is missing from the request | Enter {field}. |

R-DIL-01 and R-SET-22 carry no message ID in the rule set, so the harness asserts the state, the data and the decision record and names the message ID only where the owning service returns one of the three above. The harness produces none of these messages itself.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-16 Deed in lieu and SCR-14 Treatment record show the states this harness asserts. The harness renders no screen; it reads the states through the rwb-treatment, rwb-case and rwb-source-data contracts, so a passed run means the screens have the right data behind them.

| State | What the user sees and does |
|---|---|
| Checks | The early readiness check has started; the collateral, title and lien facts are read and the record names the rule and its version |
| Appraisal | The check cleared and the valuation was ordered; the harness asserts only the earlier readiness state |
| Approved | The deed in lieu is approved before negotiation; no offer exists yet |
| Transferred | The asset has been transferred to the bank; the states that lead here are the ones the harness asserts, and the transfer itself belongs to RWB-E3-012 |
| Broken | A title document is missing and a task re-creates the title set before release (R-SET-22) |

The case states EARLY_READINESS_CHECK and COLLATERAL_RELEASE_REQUESTED are read through the rwb-case contract and shown on the case record view, whose screen ID is not named for this feature in the source documents (GAP-0425; ASM-0601). What the wave entry check looks at instead is the evidence report, whose format and retention are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0425; ASM-0601).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the rule versions, the check fixture, the seeding set and the state names are data.
- No personal data in logs, fixtures, reports, tests or prompts: the events carry IDs and business facts only, and the harness asserts the absence of personal data.
- No read of another service's tables: every read and every seed goes through the owning contract (DP-01), and the collateral, title and asset rows are ACE's, read through rwb-source-data's DP06 product (DP-05).
- The harness never re-keys an ACE fact: a lien rank, a title document number, an area, a province or a value is asserted as ACE returns it and never copied into a fixture.
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would.
- A stub pass is never reported as a real-service pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and it never sets a case, treatment, task or record state by hand.
- A failing assertion is fixed in the service that owns it or reported as a gap; it is never waived in the script.
