The document is the one place where a business value could leak, so it fixes that a list is named by its code and never by its members, that a case status is not a claim element, and that the examples carry synthetic identifiers of the same kind as the legacy `SYN` values.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-guarantee (S3); base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` (DP-13). This story publishes the create; the update is published by RWB-S3-E4014-CON on the same base (ASM-4500).

| Method | Path | Request | Response | Access | Idempotency | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims` | `GuaranteeClaimRequest`; `caseId` from the path | 201 with `GuaranteeClaim` | Treatment and offer C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header required | 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 |

The operation, its purpose, its request and response entities, its right, its idempotency and its error statuses are those of TSD S3 T-A.1 and T-A.2 for API-S3-001, with the base renamed by DP-13. API-S3-002 is published by RWB-S3-E4014-CON and is named, not declared. No read operation is declared, because TSD S3 T-A.1 lists two operations only (GAP-2709; ASM-4501).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None — a contract document calls no service. The case status reaches the service on the case signal the parent `CaseWorkflow` forwards, and the rule package on `RulePackageInForce`; the rights and the lists arrive through the platform client libraries. Every one of them is a fact of the consuming story, and this contract adds no dependency of its own.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service topic is `rwb.guarantee.events.v1` with event names `rwb.guarantee.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and the ownership rows give S3 no event type, so no event of a preparation is declared here. The `DecisionRecorded` event of the library is written in the caller's transaction under RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and is not a type of this contract (DP-03).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The package event is consumed by RWB-S3-E4013-APP and never by a document; the contract names no subscription.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None — the contract defines no workflow and no activity. `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` is the application story's, on task queue `rwb-guarantee` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and it calls the create and the server-side service method behind it; the document describes the resource only (Temporal and Drools Design slide 13).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule and no Quartz job is declared, and the ownership rows give S3 no job; the claim deadline and the preparation window belong to the application story and to rwb-case.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guarantee_claim` | `rwb_guarantee` | S3 | The DDL template of section 13: DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022, the seven standard columns, the primary key on `id`, the index on `case_id` and no cross-schema key (DP-01, DP-15) |
| `decision_record` | `rwb_guarantee` | PLT library object applied in this schema | Named only: the shape is RWB-PLT-E1027-CON's and the row is written in the caller's transaction (DP-03) |

No table of another service is declared, read or keyed, and no checklist, document, case or channel table appears in the template.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| Claim resource fake | The create of 12.1 | A 201 create with a `GuaranteeClaim` in state PREPARING; a 403 and a 422 refusal; a 404 for an unknown case; a 409 for a case that already has an open claim; a 503 unavailability |
| Repeated-key fake | The `Idempotency-Key` rule | The first answer returned again for the same key, with no second claim |
| Template application | The `guarantee_claim` DDL template | The table created twice in two throwaway schemas, with the standard columns, the keys and no cross-schema reference |
| Problem fakes | The problem envelope | One `application/problem+json` body per error status, each with its `messageId` |
| Registry and drift fake | The compatibility and single-publisher rule | One accepted and one refused body in BACKWARD mode, and a drift failure for a private variant of an element or for a second document on the same base |

Every fake answers from the same example set as the document, so a change to the contract shows up as a contract-test failure in a consuming build rather than as a surprise in SIT.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 operation on `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` | 0 | OpenAPI 3.1, RFC 9457 problem bodies; the browser reaches it through gateway-bff (DP-19) |
| Kafka | 0 | 0 | The service topic is named and no event type is declared here |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 | The contract declares no workflow and no activity |
| File | 0 | 0 | No file crosses the contract; the scheme documents are rwb-document's |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Contract artefact of the service: the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the guarantee-claim resource, the two schemas with the published types in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.guarantee.api`, the `guarantee_claim` DDL template as a resource, and the fake set with the drift test. The implementation behind it is RWB-S3-E4013-APP. The artefact coordinates and the publication channel are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2709).

**Element surface**

| Element group | Elements | Required |
|---|---|---|
| Identity | `id`, `caseId` | `id` on the answer; `caseId` from the path |
| Claim | `claimType`, `claimDeadline`, `claimedAmount` | all three |
| Filing and payment | `filedAt`, `paidAmount` | none; null at preparation |
| Lifecycle | `status` | yes |
| Standard | `state`, `version`, `createdAt`, `createdBy`, `updatedAt`, `updatedBy`, `isActive` | none in the body; they are columns of the template |

The element names are the DF-TRT field names in camelCase; the mapping is one to one and is checked by the drift test. `GuaranteeClaimRequest` carries the create body without `id`, `filedAt`, `paidAmount` and `status`; `GuaranteeClaim` carries all eight fields. `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` is RWB-S3-E4014-CON's and appears here only as a name (ASM-4500).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the document names the writer and declares no record element | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`; the base of this resource is `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route; the resource is reached through it and the contract declares no composite route | referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency |

DP-13 is the pattern this story publishes. DP-03 is named and not declared: the record is the library's and the claim carries only its own eight fields. DP-19 is the route SCR-17 uses and is the platform edge story's.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| GuaranteeClaimOpenApi | Document | The base, the create, the schemas, the security, the error set and the versioning section (BR1 to BR4, BR6, BR9) |
| GuaranteeClaimSchema | Published schema | The two schemas with the DF-TRT elements and the required set (BR2, BR3) |
| GuaranteeClaimDdlTemplate | Resource | The `guarantee_claim` DDL: columns, types, keys, indexes and standard columns (BR5) |
| ProblemEnvelope | Reused schema | The platform RFC 9457 problem document with the `messageId` extension (BR6) |
| IdempotencyRule | Document | The `Idempotency-Key` header, the repeated-key answer and the 409 cause (BR7, BR12) |
| Fake set and fixtures | Test asset | The create, the refusals, the conflict, the unavailable and the repeated-key answers used by every consuming build (AC6) |
| DriftTest | Test asset | The comparison of a consuming build against sections 12 and 13 (BR9, AC6) |

**Database.** The template creates `guarantee_claim` in `rwb_guarantee` only, with the physical types of TSD S3 T3.1 and the standard columns of T3.0. `case_id` is a cross reference with an index and no foreign key, and no other schema is named in the template. The template is applied by the service's own Flyway sequence and never edits an applied migration (DP-15).

**Configuration and reference data.** The list codes are named and their members are read as values in force with their version (BR4). The capability area and the right are declared per operation and their role lists are rwb-access data (BR8). The problem envelope, its member names and its `messageId` extension are the platform style guide's and are reused, not redeclared.

**Build steps**

1. Write the document with the base and the create; lint the path and the right, and refuse a third operation and a legacy-base path (AC1).
2. Write the two schemas with the element mapping, the required set, the enumeration rule and the example; validate the example (AC2).
3. Write the DDL template and apply it twice in two throwaway schemas; assert the columns, the keys, the widths and the absence of a cross-schema key (AC3).
4. Write the error section with the problem envelope and the message identifiers, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the 409 cause (AC4).
5. Write the versioning and pinning section with one compatible and one breaking example, and record that the update pins this version (AC5).
6. Generate the fake set and the drift test, and wire the drift test into the build of RWB-S3-E4013-APP, of the four sibling stories and of RWB-S3-E4014-CON (AC6).
7. Publish v1 and record the pinned version of this contract and of each consuming story (AC5).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.guarantee.claim-resource-contract`.

**Done when.** The document lints, the two schemas validate, the template applies twice, the fake answers every status including the conflict and the repeated key, the drift test is green on the build of this story, of RWB-S3-E4013-APP and of RWB-S3-E4014-CON, and v1 is published with the pinned versions recorded.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Published as |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's role does not hold the right of the operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | 403, problem body with `messageId` MSG-P4-002 |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of the request is missing | Enter {field}. | 422, problem body with `messageId` MSG-GEN-001 and `field` |
| MSG-P7-003 | The preparation cannot be recorded and the action is not taken | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | Problem body of the create with `messageId` MSG-P7-003; the source fixes its text and no status beside it |

The texts are the legacy and platform texts carried unchanged, and this contract adds no message identifier of its own. The 401 carries the platform authentication problem and no business message; the 404 names the unknown case; the 409 of a case that already has an open claim is fixed by its status, its cause and its `messageId` slot, and its business text is not stated in any source read for this key (GAP-2709). The 503 carries the platform unavailability body; no module message names it for this key. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story, and the contract declares none: it publishes a resource. SCR-17 Guarantee claim (Not due; due; submitted; paid; refused) is reached through the gateway-bff composite route, which calls this resource and the case read in one hop each (DP-19). The screen field list and the composite route specification belong to the platform edge story and the screen owners; this contract fixes only the elements the create returns. Because TSD S3 T-A.1 declares no read operation, the `Not due` and `due` states are composed from the create answer and the case read, and the open question is recorded once (GAP-2709; ASM-4501).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the list members, the row states, the rights and the message texts are values in force, and the document names their codes only (BR4).
- No personal data in a schema, an example, a fake or a log: `id` and `caseId` are identifiers, and the personal-data scan fails the build otherwise.
- No cross-schema reference in the template and no foreign key across services: `case_id` is a cross reference, and the boundary test fails the build.
- No case status, no case table and no case column in any schema of this resource (BR10; DP-01).
- No decision-record element and no decision code list: the record is the library's and the code is the rule ID and version in force (DP-03).
- No checklist element, no document element and no retention rule, because no source gives them (BR11; GAP-2709).
- No read operation and no path outside the base: a GET, a submit path and a channel callback are named as out of scope and never declared.
- One resource, one document per major version on one base: a second document on the same base fails the registry and the drift test (BR9; ASM-4500).
- A published version is never edited in place: a breaking change raises major version 2 under a new base segment with a migration note (BR9).

##### 1. Story

As a **guarantee officer (RW-GUARANT)**, I want **the Workbench to assemble the TCG guarantee claim from the case facts and the documents the scheme requires, on the prepare branch of `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow`, with the claim written on `guarantee_claim`, its decision recorded in the same transaction and the deadline timer started when the guarantee is found** — so that **no guarantee claim misses its deadline, which is the failure the module exists to prevent**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E4-013. It owns:

- the four legacy acceptance criteria this story is given (AC1 to AC4), copied verbatim with their origin tag, and the rules, rows, states and messages they carry;
- the prepare branch of `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-guarantee` in namespace `rwb-recovery`: the steps that evaluate the `GUA` rule set (32 rules over 17 states) when the guarantee is found and when preparation falls due, and that record the claim (Temporal and Drools Design slides 5 and 13; TSD S3 T4);
- the three answers of the rule set this story builds: R-GUA-01 (guarantee found on the scheme and a scheme code present: start the claim deadline timer from the date the default conditions are met, to `DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING`), R-GUA-04 (days to `claim_deadline` at or inside the preparation window: assemble the claim against the scheme checklist, to `CLAIM_PREPARATION`, 5 working days) and R-GUA-02 (the scheme default conditions are not satisfied: record that no claim arises and hold the guarantee, to `NOT_ELIGIBLE`), with their conditions, owners and service levels carried unchanged (Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; FSD S3 A2.1.3.1);
- the claim row in `rwb_guarantee`: `claim_type`, `claim_deadline`, `claimed_amount` and `status` written from the case facts and the rules, with the local decision record of the step written through `DecisionRecordWriter.record(DecisionRecord)` in the caller's transaction (DP-03; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; DF-TRT-017 to DF-TRT-022);
- the scheme checklist assembled from the case facts and the document references the scheme requires, resolved through the platform document client library that rwb-document publishes, with no document row and no blob reference owned here (ASM-4494);
- the stage report to the parent `CaseWorkflow` carrying `DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING`, `CLAIM_PREPARATION`, `CLAIM_APPROVAL` or `NOT_ELIGIBLE` with the rule version, because the case status, the case task and the case timer are rwb-case's (DP-12);
- the officer's two operations of RWB-S3-E4013-CON implemented behind the published shape, and the `Not due` and `due` states of SCR-17 reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-13; DP-19);
- the refusal and failure paths: no record, nothing changes and MSG-P7-003; a role without the right is refused with MSG-P4-002; a missing value is named with MSG-GEN-001.

It does not own: the published resource shape, the DDL template, the error set, the versioning rule and the fakes, which are RWB-S3-E4013-CON; the approval of the assembled claim and its submission on the TCG claim channel, which are RWB-S3-E4014-APP; the tracking of the claim to payment, the lost claim and the service level breach, which are RWB-S3-E4015-APP; the subrogation position, which is RWB-S3-E4016-APP; the guarantor notices, which are RWB-S3-E4017-APP; the case, its status, its tasks and its timers, which are rwb-case's; the rule package, its approval and the central ledger, which are P7 rwb-decision's; the guarantee documents themselves, which are rwb-document's; the TCG portal, which is INT-29 and outside the cluster.

##### 2. Business rationale

In the monolith the preparation was a method of `GuaranteesAndGuarantorsService` behind `GuaranteesAndGuarantorsController`: it read the case from the one `recovery` schema, assembled the claim, wrote `recovery.guarantee_claim` and `recovery.decision_log_entry` beside it and moved the case status in the same transaction, all in one process and one schema (TSD S3 T2). The consequence was the one the module exists to prevent — the claim deadline and the assembly lived in the same code as the case, so a preparation that stopped left no trace of why, and the module's own note that "guarantee and TCG claims are late because deadlines are not tracked" was a statement about the code, not about the officers (FSD S3 A1.3).

D-RCV-60 changes the source of each input and the owner of each fact, and nothing about the officer's work. The claim becomes a row of `rwb_guarantee` with its own login and no cross-schema key (DP-01, DP-02). The decision is recorded locally in the same transaction as the preparation, so a preparation that cannot be recorded does not happen (DP-03; ADR-022). The case moves because the stage reports and the parent applies the rule, never because this service writes a case row (DP-01, DP-12). The preparation is a branch of the stage workflow the service owns: one child per case on the owner's queue `rwb-guarantee`, event in, rule decides, person signs, timer waits (Temporal and Drools Design slides 5 and 13).

Four facts of the target are recorded rather than designed away. The preparation window of R-GUA-04 is a value in force with no number in any source, so it is exported as a rule-row parameter and the only figure carried is the 5 working day service level of the rule (ASM-4493). The claim deadline is a date of the claim row while the timer is the platform's, so the date is written here and the durable timer runs in the workflow (ASM-4492). The scheme checklist names the Document Hub as its system, and no operation and no contract dependency exist for it, so the references are resolved through the platform document client library and the interface stays open (ASM-4494). The "claim preparation agent" of AC2 is bound to no runtime by any source, so it is the unattended preparation step of this service and no rwb-agent call is made (ASM-4495).

Delivery is EP04 in wave 3 on release 28 February 2027 (tentative). REQ-S3-001 of FSD S3 — "a guarantee claim is prepared from case data and submitted inside the guarantor's deadline" — is the requirement this story traces to, and REQ-S3-007 carries the eligibility filter of R-GUA-02 (Section 18).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S3-E4013-CON is published: the base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, `GuaranteeClaimRequest` and `GuaranteeClaim` over the eight DF-TRT fields, the `guarantee_claim` DDL template, the error set, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the fakes. The build starts against the Draft baseline, because every CON story of this run publishes on Day 1 at status Draft (realignment v1).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: `DecisionRecordWriter`, `DecisionRecord`, the `MANDATORY` propagation, the refusal with MSG-P7-009 and the failure with MSG-P7-003 (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-17 from the case read and this service's claim answer (DP-19).
- The `rwb_guarantee` schema and its login exist from the platform database story, and `guarantee_claim` is on the per-service Flyway sequence with DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 of TSD S3 T3.1 and the seven standard columns of T3.0; `decision_record` is created as the platform library object in the same schema (DP-01; DP-15).
- The case is signalled by the parent `CaseWorkflow` in `GUARANTEE_DETECTED` with the guarantee type, the scheme code and the date the default conditions are met, or in `DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING` with the claim row and its deadline (ASM-4497).
- The `GUA` package and route set are in this service's rule cache at the version the answer names; the rule identifiers, the conditions, the preparation window and the 5 working day service level are rule rows, not code (EV-30; BR-S3-001).
- The document references the scheme checklist requires are resolvable through the platform document client library; no document row and no blob is read directly (ASM-4494).
- No approval stop: FSD S3 v3 and TSD S3 v2 carry status "In review", and nothing in this story needs a human sign-off to start on Day 1 (ASM-4498).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-case: the parent `CaseWorkflow` starts the `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` child of the case and forwards the case signal when the valuation decides the guarantee route at D6.5 and D6.6, carrying the case ID, the case status `GUARANTEE_DETECTED`, the guarantee type, the scheme code and the date the default conditions are met (Architecture v5 slide 13; TSD S3 T4).
2. `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow`: the prepare branch opens the step, calls `EvaluateRules` and the `GUA` set in force answers R-GUA-01 when `guarantee_type` is the TCG scheme and a `scheme_code` is present, or R-GUA-02 when the scheme default conditions are not satisfied (R-GUA-01; R-GUA-02).
3. On R-GUA-01 the step computes the claim deadline from the date the default conditions are met and the rule's own period, and `RecordAndApply` writes the claim row and the decision record in one transaction (R-GUA-01; DF-TRT-018; DP-03).
4. The stage reports `DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING` with the rule version and the deadline; the parent applies the status and raises the case timer, and the workflow waits on a durable timer to the deadline (ASM-4492).
5. On R-GUA-02 the stage records that no claim arises and holds the guarantee: the claim row takes the hold with its reason code, the decision record is written, and the stage reports `NOT_ELIGIBLE` (R-GUA-02).
6. At the preparation window the timer fires and `EvaluateRules` answers R-GUA-04: `assembleChecklist` collects the scheme checklist from the case facts and the document references the scheme requires, resolved through the platform document client library, and names every missing item (R-GUA-04; ASM-4494).
7. `recordPreparation` builds the claim from the case facts — `claim_type` of LOV-CLAIM-TYPE, `claim_deadline`, `claimed_amount` — and, when the checklist is complete, presents it for approval; when it is not, the answer is the checklist-incomplete one (R-GUA-04; DF-TRT-017 to DF-TRT-019).
8. `RecordAndApply`, one transaction: the claim row takes `status = PREPARING` of LOV-CLAIM-STATUS and its standard columns, the decision record is written with the rule ID, the rule version and the checklist outcome, and the stage report is emitted (DP-03; TSD S3 T3.2).
9. The stage reports `CLAIM_PREPARATION`, and on a complete checklist `CLAIM_APPROVAL` with the rule version and the 5 working day service level; the parent applies the status and raises the case task for the officer (R-GUA-04; R-GUA-07 read from TSD S3 T4).
10. The officer sees the `due` state, the claim deadline and the checklist on SCR-17 through the gateway-bff composite route, which composes the case read and this service's claim answer in one hop each (DP-19).

The approval and the submission that follow are RWB-S3-E4014-APP's and start where step 9 leaves the claim.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The decision record cannot be written | The transaction rolls back: no claim row, no status, no stage report; the officer sees MSG-P7-003 and an incident is raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC4 |
| X2 | A required claim value is missing — the guarantee type, the scheme code or the claim amount | The step names the field, writes nothing and raises a guarantee officer task | MSG-GEN-001 | Section 12.8 |
| X3 | The scheme default conditions are not satisfied | No claim arises; the guarantee is held with its reason code and the stage reports `NOT_ELIGIBLE` | None | R-GUA-02 |
| X4 | The scheme checklist is incomplete at the preparation window | The claim stays in `PREPARING`, the missing items are named on the task and the defect hold answer is reported; nothing is filed | None | R-GUA-08 read; GAP-2708 |
| X5 | A role without the right in the capability area tries the action | 403 from the access guard on the operation, and nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | Section 10 |
| X6 | The document references cannot be resolved inside the retry budget | The activity is retried by the workflow's policy; when the attempts are exhausted the step stays where it was, the officer task names the missing items and no business message is fixed | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2708; ASM-4494) | Section 12.8 |
| X7 | A second case signal arrives while the branch is running | The inbox dedupes by the cloud event id and the branch is idempotent on the case, the rule version and the claim status, so no second claim row is written | None | Section 12.5 |
| X8 | The date the default conditions are met is absent from the signal | The step cannot compute the deadline, names the fact and reports nothing; the case stays in `GUARANTEE_DETECTED` | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2708; ASM-4497) | Section 9 |

X1 to X5 are the legacy paths of RWB-E4-013 carried onto the split; X6 to X8 are the boundaries the missing interface, the missing value and the missing fact record.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-S3-E4013-CON, its fakes and the gateway route; the case arrives on a signal fixture, the documents on a client fake and the rule package on a fake, so no deployment of P3, P5, P7 or rwb-document is needed |
| Negotiable | The activity names, the shape of the stage report, the retry numbers and the checklist representation are this story's choice; the rules, the condition terms, the states and the messages are fixed |
| Valuable | A guarantee that is found becomes a claim with a deadline, a checklist and a date, in one unattended step, and the case moves without a hand-written status |
| Estimable | One workflow branch, three activities, one checklist assembly, one claim write, one decision-record call and tests |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests against the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on a synthetic case, a document-reference fixture and a rule-package fake, plus component tests of the not-eligible, incomplete-checklist and refusal paths |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Prepare a TCG guarantee claim

  Background:
    Given case "RW-2026-000913" carries a TCG guarantee with a scheme code
    Given the rule package in force is version "GUA-2026.11"

  Scenario: AC1 Prepare a TCG guarantee claim (legacy RWB-E4-013 AC1)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case in state DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING
    Given the decision-record library mock returns an accepted record
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When its trigger arrives
    Then assembles the claim from the case facts and the documents the scheme requires
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Rule R-GUA-04 (legacy RWB-E4-013 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case in state DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING
    Given a case in state DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING
    When preparation due
    Then the claim preparation agent assembles the claim against the scheme checklist
    Then the case moves to CLAIM_PREPARATION

  Scenario: AC3 Rule R-GUA-01 (legacy RWB-E4-013 AC3)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case in state GUARANTEE_DETECTED
    Given a case in state GUARANTEE_DETECTED
    When guarantee found
    Then start the claim deadline timer from the date the default conditions are met
    Then the case moves to DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING

  Scenario: AC4 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E4-013 AC4)
    Given the decision-record library mock returns the failure MSG-P7-003
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

**Target reading.** Every legacy line above keeps its wording; what changes is where it runs, which service holds each fact and how it is reached. "Assembles the claim from the case facts and the documents the scheme requires" is no longer a method of `GuaranteesAndGuarantorsService` writing `recovery.guarantee_claim`: it is the prepare branch of `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` on queue `rwb-guarantee`, and the claim row is `rwb_guarantee.guarantee_claim`. The case facts arrive on the case signal the parent forwards; no case table and no case column is read, and no case status is written here (DP-01, DP-12).

"Writes the result to the decision log with the rule version" is the local `DecisionRecordWriter.record(DecisionRecord)` call in the same transaction as the claim write, with MSG-P7-003 on failure (DP-03; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON); `decision_log_entry` stays P7's and is never written here. "The claim preparation agent assembles the claim against the scheme checklist" is the unattended `assembleChecklist` activity of this service and not a call to rwb-agent, because no source binds FEAT-GUA-01 to the agent runtime (ASM-4495); the checklist's documents are resolved through the document client library of rwb-document (ASM-4494). "Start the claim deadline timer from the date the default conditions are met" writes `guarantee_claim.claim_deadline` and arms the durable workflow timer to it, while the case timer row stays rwb-case's and is raised from the stage report (ASM-4492). "The case moves to DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING" and "the case moves to CLAIM_PREPARATION" are the stage report and the rule the parent applies (ASM-4496). "Its trigger arrives" is the case signal the parent forwards, because the FSD names "a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer" and no source names which one.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | No value a business person may change is written in code: the rule IDs, the conditions, the preparation window, the 5 working day service level, the list members and the message texts are rule rows or governed rows with a version | BR-S3-001 of FSD S3 A2.1.3.1 |
| BR2 | A guarantee found on the TCG scheme with a scheme code starts the claim deadline timer from the date the default conditions are met, and the claim moves to `DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING` | R-GUA-01 |
| BR3 | Where the scheme default conditions are not satisfied, no claim arises, the guarantee is held and the claim moves to `NOT_ELIGIBLE` | R-GUA-02; FSD S3 A2.1.3.1 |
| BR4 | When days to `claim_deadline` are at or inside the preparation window, the claim is assembled against the scheme checklist and moves to `CLAIM_PREPARATION`, inside the 5 working day service level of the rule | R-GUA-04 |
| BR5 | The claim row is one write on `guarantee_claim`: `claim_type` from LOV-CLAIM-TYPE, `claim_deadline`, `claimed_amount` and `status = PREPARING` of LOV-CLAIM-STATUS, with `filed_at` and `paid_amount` left null until the filing | TSD S3 T3.1, T3.2 |
| BR6 | The claim write and its decision record are written in one transaction; if the record cannot be written nothing changes and MSG-P7-003 is shown | DP-03; ADR-022; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| BR7 | The case status, the case task and the case timer are never this service's: the stage reports the outcome, the rule version and the service level, and the parent applies the rule | DP-01; DP-12; ASM-4496 |
| BR8 | The scheme checklist is assembled from the case facts and the document references the scheme requires; no document row, blob reference or document content is owned or read directly here | ASM-4494; FSD S3 A2.1.3.1 |
| BR9 | The preparation is unattended under the service identity; the officer task is raised by rwb-case when a value is missing or the checklist is incomplete | FSD S3 A2.1.3.3; TSD S3 T6.2 |
| BR10 | The capability area is "Treatment and offer" with right C on the create and right U on the update; the right is declared per operation and checked by the platform guard | TSD S3 T6.1 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 is why the rules, the window and the service level are inputs of the step; BR2 and BR3 are the two answers at the finding of the guarantee; BR4 is the preparation-window evaluation and the checklist activity; BR5 is the single claim write; BR6 is the `MANDATORY` propagation of the library write; BR7 is the boundary to rwb-case; BR8 is the checklist assembly and the reason no document is owned; BR9 is the service identity and the officer task; BR10 is the `security` section of the two operations the contract publishes.

##### 9. State transitions

None of the case statuses below is this service's; the table shows what the stage reports and does not write, so a reader can see the boundary of this story.

| Rule | From (rwb-case) | Event | Condition | What this stage does | To (rwb-case) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-GUA-01 | `GUARANTEE_DETECTED` | `GUARANTEE_FOUND` | `guarantee_type` = TCG scheme and `scheme_code` present | Writes the claim row with its deadline, records the decision, arms the workflow timer and reports `DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING` | `DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING` |
| R-GUA-02 | `GUARANTEE_DETECTED` | `CONDITIONS_NOT_MET` | the scheme default conditions are not satisfied | Records that no claim arises, holds the guarantee with its reason code and reports `NOT_ELIGIBLE` | `NOT_ELIGIBLE` |
| R-GUA-03 (read only) | `NOT_ELIGIBLE` | `CONDITIONS_LATER_MET` | the default conditions are met later | Re-enters at R-GUA-01 on the next signal; the row is in force and this story writes nothing for it beyond the new deadline | `DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING` |
| R-GUA-04 | `DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING` | `PREPARATION_DUE` | days to `claim_deadline` at or inside the preparation window | Assembles the checklist and the claim, records the decision and reports `CLAIM_PREPARATION` with the 5 working day service level | `CLAIM_PREPARATION` |
| R-GUA-07 (reported, not owned) | `CLAIM_PREPARATION` | `CHECKLIST_COMPLETE` | every scheme item is present | Reports `CLAIM_APPROVAL` so the officer can verify the claim; the approval and the submission are RWB-S3-E4014-APP's | `CLAIM_APPROVAL` |
| R-GUA-08 (reported, not owned) | `CLAIM_PREPARATION` | `CHECKLIST_INCOMPLETE` | a scheme item is missing | Leaves the claim in `PREPARING`, names the missing items on the task and reports the defect hold | `CLAIM_DEFECT_HOLD` |

The states of this story's own row are the claim's, from LOV-CLAIM-STATUS: a row is written in `PREPARING` and takes no other member here. The seventeen rule states of TSD S3 T4 and this five-member list are two vocabularies and no source maps them, so only the one member this story needs is fixed (GAP-2708; ASM-4496). The `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` execution has the platform states RUNNING, COMPLETED and FAILED, and a FAILED execution restarts from the last recorded step, which is why the checklist assembly and the write are activities and not workflow-local computation. The claim deadline is the workflow's durable timer once armed, and a Continue-As-New at the stage end keeps the run inside the platform limit (Temporal and Drools Design slide 13).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The recovery squad (RW-TRIBE) | Writes the workflow branch, the checklist activity, the claim write and the tests |
| RW-GUARANT, guarantee officer | Sees the claim and its checklist, verifies the assembled claim at D6.5 and completes a missing value; holds rights C, R and U on Treatment and offer |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Owns the case the claim is prepared on; holds rights C, R and U |
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer (FCR) | Holds rights C, R, U and A; sees the preparation |
| RW-SPECIAL, hardship and vulnerability specialist | Holds rights C, R and U |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL and the read-only roles of TSD S3 T6.1 | Right R only: they read the claim and its checklist and cannot prepare or change it |
| SY-CASEWF, the case workflow module | Runs the step unattended under the service identity and reports to the parent |
| rwb-case (P3) | Owns the case, its status, its tasks, its timers and the parent `CaseWorkflow` |
| P7 rwb-decision | Owns the `GUA` package, the 32 rows, their approval, their effective date and the central ledger |
| rwb-document (P5) | Owns the guarantee documents, their metadata and their blob references |
| ACE and its DBA | Own the ACE database, its batch and the `recovery.v_ace_*` views this story does not read |
| The platform workflow and data owners | Own the task queue, the namespace, the ACE PostgreSQL grants and the decision-record library |

The check is the platform guard library's: this story declares the capability area "Treatment and offer" and the right C or U on each entry point, and no check is written in code. No credential and no personal name appears in the workflow input, the activity request or the logs, which carry the case ID, the claim ID, dates, amounts and versions only.

`guarantee_claim` and `decision_record` are this service's own objects in `rwb_guarantee`, written through its own repository and login (DP-01). The case fields arrive on the case signal and are never read from a table. The document rows are rwb-document's and only their references are used, so no document column, blob reference or content is stored in `rwb_guarantee` (ASM-4494). The rule rows are read through the rule loader and are never joined to this service's tables. The ACE database is not read by this story: the preparation needs no account fact, because the claimed amount comes from the case facts and the rule. The date the default conditions are met has no column of `guarantee_claim` and no field identifier anywhere, so it is carried on the signal (GAP-2708; ASM-4497).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

This story implements the two operations that RWB-S3-E4013-CON publishes on base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` (DP-13), and adds no path of its own.

| Method | Path | Request | Response | Access | Idempotency | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims` | `GuaranteeClaimRequest`; `caseId` from the path | 201 with `GuaranteeClaim` | Treatment and offer C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header required | 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 |
| PATCH | `/guarantee-claims/{claimId}` | `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` | 200 with `GuaranteeClaim` | Treatment and offer U, scope applied | Not applicable | 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 |

The two operations, their entities, their rights, their idempotency and their error statuses are TSD S3 T-A.1 and T-A.2 for API-S3-001 and API-S3-002 with the base renamed by DP-13; the shape, the DDL template, the message identifiers and the fakes are RWB-S3-E4013-CON's and are not restated here. The create is the officer's route to a claim opened by hand; the workflow opens the row by the same server-side service method the create uses, so one validation path serves both.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The case facts and the case status arrive on the case signal the parent `CaseWorkflow` forwards, and Architecture v5 slide 13 shows the P3 to S3 edge as a Temporal child started on this service's queue, with no REST line in either direction. The document references are resolved through the platform document client library that rwb-document publishes, which is a library binding and not an operation of this service (ASM-4494); the rule rows arrive on the package event of 12.4 and the screen is composed by the gateway route of 12.8 (DP-19). No source publishes an operation for this step and none is invented.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service's topic is `rwb.guarantee.events.v1` with names `rwb.guarantee.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and the ownership rows give S3 no event type; the connection matrix has rwb-reporting listening to S3, which no catalogued event satisfies, so the preparation raises no Kafka event and its signal is the stage report to the parent `CaseWorkflow` (GAP-2708; ASM-4499). The `DecisionRecorded` event of the library is written in the caller's transaction under RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and is not a type of this service (DP-03).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | Loads the `GUA` package and route set in force, verifies the checksum, swaps them atomically and keeps the last good set on failure; EV-30 |

The service also listens to P8 payment events on the connection matrix, and the event that opens R-GUA-20 sits with the tracking story RWB-S3-E4015-APP; no event name is published for it in the sources read here, so none is named. Both subscriptions are the service template's inbox and rule loader; this story adds no subscription of its own.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` (the prepare branch) | Child workflow of `CaseWorkflow`, one per case, on this service's own queue | `rwb-guarantee` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case ID, the case status on the signal, the guarantee type, the scheme code, the date the default conditions are met, the rule version and the case facts. Output: the stage report with the claim ID, the deadline, the checklist outcome, the rule version and the service level |
| `EvaluateRules` | Activity of the template | `rwb-guarantee` | The package and route set in force and the case facts in; the rule ID, the action and the next event out; `NoPackageInForce` is not retried |
| `assembleChecklist` | Activity | `rwb-guarantee` | The case facts and the document references in; the checklist with each item present or missing out; a missing reference is non-retryable |
| `recordPreparation` | Activity | `rwb-guarantee` | The rule answer and the checklist in; the `GuaranteeClaimRequest` of RWB-S3-E4013-CON out, with `status = PREPARING` |
| `RecordAndApply` | Activity of the template | `rwb-guarantee` | The request and the decision record in one transaction, then the stage report |

The workflow name is fixed by Temporal and Drools Design slide 13; the three activity names are this story's choice. The retry policy is the workflow kit's (1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts; a missing reference and `NoPackageInForce` non-retryable). A replay never re-resolves a document: the answer is recorded by the activity and read from history, and the branch is idempotent on the case, the rule version and the claim status, so a repeated signal writes no second claim. The claim deadline is a durable timer of this workflow, so a restart after Continue-As-New still fires at the same instant.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step is signal-driven and timer-driven inside the workflow and owns no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job; the ownership rows give S3 no job. The preparation window of R-GUA-04 and the claim deadline of R-GUA-01 are workflow timers driven by the platform, and the case timer row they raise is rwb-case's (ASM-4492).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guarantee_claim` | `rwb_guarantee` | S3 rwb-guarantee | Created by the per-service Flyway sequence and written here for the claim fields, `status` and the standard columns; DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 of TSD S3 T3.1 |
| `decision_record` | `rwb_guarantee` | PLT library object | Written only through `DecisionRecordWriter` in the caller's transaction (DP-03) |

No table of another service is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01). The case table, the timer table and the task rows of rwb-case, the document tables of rwb-document, the rule tables of rwb-decision and the ledger of P7 are never named in SQL, and no `recovery.v_ace_*` view is read by this story.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| RWB-S3-E4013-CON claim fake | The two operations of 12.1 | A 201 create with a `GuaranteeClaim` in `PREPARING`; a 200 update; a 409 for a claim already open; a 422 and a 403 refusal; a 404 and a 503 |
| Case-signal fake | The signal the parent forwards | `GUARANTEE_DETECTED` with a TCG scheme and a scheme code; the same with no scheme code; `DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING` at the preparation window; `DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING` with no default-conditions date |
| Document client fake | The scheme checklist references | Every item present; one item missing; an unresolvable reference |
| Decision-record writer fake (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON) | `DecisionRecordWriter` | An accepted record with its chain sequence; a refusal with MSG-P7-009 and the field; a failure with MSG-P7-003 |
| Rule-package fake | The `GUA` package and rows in force | Version `GUA-2026.11` with R-GUA-01, R-GUA-02 and R-GUA-04; a set with no matching row; a checksum mismatch |
| Gateway route fake (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) | The SCR-17 composite route | The case read and the claim answer composed in one response |

The case-signal fake and the document client fake are the Day-1 unblockers: the build and every test run against them, and no test reads a production view, needs a live case or reaches rwb-document.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.guarantee`, modules `claimprepare` and `workflow`, with the published types in `...guarantee.api`. Service base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, schema `rwb_guarantee`, topic `rwb.guarantee.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-guarantee` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-13; §R4).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the record of the preparation, DP-13 the base the two operations sit on, and DP-19 the path SCR-17 is read on. The outbox and inbox library, the workflow kit, the access guard, the embedded Drools runtime and the document client are the service template's wave-0 capabilities and add no build dependency of their own; the embedded Drools kit carries DP-04, which the Work Package does not record for this key and which adds no story-level dependency because the `GUA` rows arrive on the package event of 12.4.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `ClaimPrepareBranch` | Workflow | The branch of `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` that opens the step, arms the deadline timer, reports the outcome and waits |
| `EvaluateRules` | Activity | Runs the `GUA` package and route set in force and returns the rule ID, the action and the next event |
| `ChecklistAssembler` | Activity | Builds the scheme checklist from the case facts and the document references, and names each missing item |
| `ClaimPreparation` | Service | Builds the claim from the case facts, computes the deadline and decides between preparation and the not-eligible answer |
| `ClaimPrepareRepository` | Repository | Writes the claim fields and the standard columns on `guarantee_claim` |
| `DecisionRecorder` | Service | Assembles `DecisionRecord` and calls `DecisionRecordWriter.record` in the caller's transaction |
| `StageReporter` | Service | Builds the stage report with the claim ID, the deadline, the checklist outcome, the rule version and the service level |

**Database.** No new table and no new column beyond the contract's template: this story writes DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-019 and DF-TRT-022 with the standard columns in `rwb_guarantee`, and `decision_record` is the library object of DP-03. The date the default conditions are met is not given a column because no field identifier exists for it; if it must be persisted it becomes a field of the Logical Data Model first (GAP-2708; ASM-4497).

**Configuration and reference data.** The rule IDs, the conditions, the preparation window and the 5 working day service level are data of rwb-decision and the reference lists, read with their version and never configured here (BR-S3-001). The retry numbers, the activity names and the 2 s budget are configuration of the activity. The capability area "Treatment and offer" and the rights are access data of P4 read through the guard library.

**Build steps**

1. The prepare branch of `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` on `rwb-guarantee`, its input record and the stage report.
2. `EvaluateRules` against the package fake, with R-GUA-01, R-GUA-02 and R-GUA-04 as rule rows and the `NoPackageInForce` answer (AC2, AC3).
3. `ClaimPreparation` with the deadline computation from the date the default conditions are met, and the not-eligible answer (AC3, X3, X8).
4. `ChecklistAssembler` against the document client fake, with the complete, incomplete and unresolvable paths (AC2, X4, X6).
5. The claim write and the `GuaranteeClaimRequest` against the claim fake, with the 409 of a claim already open (AC1).
6. `RecordAndApply` with the record in the same transaction and the rollback path of MSG-P7-003 (AC4).
7. The stage report with the rule version, the service level and the claim ID, and the parent's `CLAIM_APPROVAL` report on a complete checklist (AC2).
8. Tests for AC1 to AC4 against the fakes, the component tests of X2, X3, X4, X6 and X8, and the replay test of X7.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.guarantee.claim-preparation`.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the branch runs from a synthetic case signal in SIT with the document client, the package and the parent faked, the claim shows `PREPARING` with its deadline and amount, the record is written in the same transaction and rolls back with the claim, the not-eligible path holds the guarantee, the incomplete checklist reports the defect hold without writing a filed claim, and the case reaches `DEADLINE_TIMER_RUNNING`, `CLAIM_PREPARATION` and `CLAIM_APPROVAL` on the report.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required claim value is missing and the step cannot build the claim | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right in the capability area tries the action | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written and the preparation is not made | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P7-009 | The record is refused for a missing or invalid field | The decision record was refused: {field} is missing or not valid. |

The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story, FSD S3 A2.1.3.1 and the platform message set, and this story adds no message ID. The 403 of a right the role does not hold and the 409 of a claim already open carry the platform problem body; the 409 has no business text in any source read for this key. A missing scheme document and an unresolvable reference have no message identifier in any source: the checklist names the item on the officer task and no text is invented (GAP-2708; ASM-4494). Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-17 Guarantee claim shows the guarantee, the claim deadline, the checklist and the claim result, in the states `Not due`, `due`, `submitted`, `paid` and `refused`. This story makes `Not due` and `due` real: the guarantee, the claim deadline, the claim type, the claimed amount and the checklist are read on the same screen through the gateway-bff composite route, which calls rwb-case and this service's claim answer in one hop each (DP-19; Architecture v5 slide 41). TSD S3 T-A.1 publishes no read operation, so the screen's claim content is what the create and update answers return and the composite route composes it with the case read (ASM-4501). The screen field list and the route specification belong to the platform edge story and the screen owner; this story fixes what the service writes. A held guarantee shows its reason code, never a claim deadline; an incomplete checklist shows the missing items, never a filed claim.

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-E4-013-01 | AC1 | End to end | Prepare a TCG guarantee claim |
| TC-E4-013-02 | AC2 | End to end | Rule R-GUA-04 |
| TC-E4-013-03 | AC3 | End to end | Rule R-GUA-01 |
| TC-E4-013-04 | AC4 | End to end | Not recorded |

The legacy test case IDs, their Covers and their Data are kept in order and character for character; the story level "System" of the legacy suite is carried as "End to end" and the two exception cases as "Component", as in the other stories of this run. TC-E4-013-05 and TC-E4-013-06 restate the same guard as the legacy suite, so they run once each. The claim, case-signal, document-client, decision-record, rule-package and gateway fakes of section 12.8 stand behind every case, and the full Given, When and Then of each is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same ID. The `-ITG` copies (TC-E4-013-01-ITG to TC-E4-013-06-ITG) belong to the wave 3 integration harness (RWB-ITG-W3) and are not written by this story. The contract's own tests are TC-S3-E4013-CON-01 to -05 and are owned by RWB-S3-E4013-CON.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No value a business person may change is written in code: the rule IDs, the conditions, the preparation window, the 5 working day service level, the list members and the four messages are rule rows or governed rows with a version (BR-S3-001; BR1).
- No personal data in logs, workflow inputs, activity requests, events or tests: the step carries the case ID, the claim ID, dates, amounts and versions only, and the fixture is synthetic.
- No read of another service's tables: the case arrives on the signal, the rule rows on the package event, the documents as references through the client library, and nothing joins across a schema (DP-01).
- No document content and no blob reference owned here: the checklist holds references only (BR8).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views, and this story reads neither: the claimed amount comes from the case facts and the rule.
- No business value in the record: the `DecisionRecord` carries the rule ID, the rule version, the claim amount and the result code, never a free-text reason or a customer field (DP-03).
- No status change from this service: the stage reports and the parent applies the rule (BR7).
- No live document store, no live case and no live rule package in any test: the client fake, the signal fake and the package fake are the only endpoints.
- No invented message for a missing document or an unresolvable reference: the item is named on the task and the gap stays open (GAP-2708).

##### 1. Story

As a **service contract owner**, I want **the published contract of the guarantee-claim resource of rwb-guarantee (S3) — the base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, `POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims` and `PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId}` with the entity names `GuaranteeClaimRequest`, `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` and `GuaranteeClaim` of TSD S3 T-A.2, the elements named in camelCase after DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022, the `guarantee_claim` DDL template with the T3.0 standard columns, the error set 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 with the RFC 9457 problem body, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the versioning rule and the fakes** instead of the monolith's in-process controller and the one `recovery.guarantee_claim` table of the shared schema, so that **RWB-S3-E4014-APP and every later story of the service build against one frozen shape from Day 1, with no wait on any other team**.

This story owns the contract of one resource and nothing else:

- the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the guarantee-claim resource: the base, the two operations, the three object schemas, the problem schema, the security and the error set;
- the `guarantee_claim` DDL template with the eight fields of TSD S3 T3.1 and the seven standard columns of T3.0, one template each environment applies in this service's own schema, with no cross-schema key;
- the element naming rule (camelCase after the DF-TRT identifiers), the required set and the enumeration rule that names a list code and no member;
- the `Idempotency-Key` rule on the POST, the compatibility rule and the pinning rule;
- the fake set generated from the document, and the drift test that every consuming build runs.

It does not own: the handlers, the workflow branch, the pack assembly, the filing write and the stage report, which are RWB-S3-E4014-APP; the claim preparation and its checklist, which are RWB-S3-E4013-APP; the tracking to payment, the query and the rejection, which are RWB-S3-E4015-APP; the subrogation position, which is RWB-S3-E4016-APP; the case status and the case signal, which are rwb-case's; the central ledger and the `GUA` rule rows, which are P7's; the roles and rights data, which are rwb-access's; the composite route, which is the platform edge story's; the TCG claim channel, which is INT-29 and has no interface.

##### 2. Business rationale

The monolith exposed the claim through one controller in the shared process on the legacy base, and the claim row lived in the one `recovery` schema beside 91 other tables (TSD S3 T2, T3.1). Three facts follow from the target and make a contract necessary before any code. First, the schema is now `rwb_guarantee` with its own login and no cross-schema access, so the table shape has to be a template every environment applies rather than one shared migration (DP-01, DP-02, DP-15). Second, the base is now `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, so the claim paths no longer collide with the case, the payment and the treatment services and every caller has one place to read them (DP-13). Third, four stories of this service and the reporting and integration builds read a claim, so the elements, the required set and the error set have to be frozen before the first of them starts.

TSD S3 already fixes most of it, and this story publishes what the source states rather than inventing: T-A.1 names the two paths, their rights and the first epic; T-A.2 names the request, the update and the response entities `GuaranteeClaimRequest`, `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` and `GuaranteeClaim` with the error statuses and the `Idempotency-Key` header on the create; T3.1 names the eight fields of `guarantee_claim` with their physical types, their required flag and their list; T3.0 names the standard record columns; T3.2 names the members of LOV-CLAIM-STATUS and LOV-CLAIM-TYPE.

What the source does not state is recorded, not filled. The legacy story says the submission reference is recorded on the case, and TSD S3 T3.1 gives the row no reference field, so v1 publishes no reference element and the filing shows as `status = FILED` with `filed_at` (GAP-2712; ASM-4503). The TCG claim channel is INT-29, "not available today; entered and filed by the guarantee officer", so the contract declares no channel operation, no channel callback and no channel file (GAP-2712; ASM-4504). The 409 cause of a claim that is already filed has a status here and no business text (GAP-2712; ASM-4509).

The fake is the Day-1 unblocker. RWB-S3-E4014-APP, the three sibling application stories and any reporting or integration build can create, read and update a claim before a single table exists in an environment, and the drift test turns a private variant of the shape into a build failure rather than a defect found in SIT.

##### 3. Preconditions

- TSD S3 T-A.1 fixes the endpoint inventory: API-S3-001 `POST` on `/cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims` with right C and the `Idempotency-Key` header, and API-S3-002 `PATCH` on `/guarantee-claims/{claimId}` with right U and idempotency not applicable; the base becomes `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` by DP-13.
- TSD S3 T-A.2 fixes the entity names `GuaranteeClaimRequest`, `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` and `GuaranteeClaim` and the error statuses 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 of both operations.
- TSD S3 T3.1 fixes DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 with their physical types, their required flags and their lists, and T3.0 fixes the seven standard record columns.
- TSD S3 T3.2 fixes the list codes LOV-CLAIM-STATUS and LOV-CLAIM-TYPE; their members are values in force and are not restated in the document (BR-S3-002).
- TSD S3 T6.1 fixes the capability area "Treatment and offer" and the rights of each role; the document declares the right of each operation and holds no role list.
- The problem envelope is the platform one, RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with the platform extension members; the platform API style guide fixes its member names, so this document reuses them and does not redeclare them.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON publishes the decision-record contract; this document names it as the writer behind the decision of a filing and declares no record element of its own (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-E1044-CON publishes the per-service Flyway conventions, so the DDL is a template applied by this service's own sequence and not one shared migration (DP-15).
- No source gives the submission reference a field, the TCG channel an interface or the 409 a business text; all three are outside this contract and are recorded once (GAP-2712; ASM-4503; ASM-4504; ASM-4509).
- No build dependency and no approval stop: a CON story is Day 1 by rule (§R5.7), it sits in contract group CG-W3 and it is published at status Draft (realignment v1).

##### 4. Flow

1. The contract author fixes the base and the two operations of section 12.1, taken character for character from TSD S3 T-A.1 with the DP-13 base.
2. The author fixes the element naming rule: every element of the three schemas is a DF-TRT field name in camelCase, and `caseId` is taken from the path on the POST and is not repeated in the request body.
3. The author fixes the required set from the required column of TSD S3 T3.1, so `id`, `caseId`, `claimType`, `claimDeadline`, `claimedAmount` and `status` are required and `filedAt` and `paidAmount` are optional.
4. The author fixes the enumeration rule: an enumerated element names its list code and no member, because the members are values in force (BR-S3-002).
5. The author writes the `guarantee_claim` DDL template: the columns, the physical types, the required set, the primary key, the indexes, the standard columns and the rule that no key crosses a schema.
6. The author writes the error set of each operation with the problem envelope and the message identifiers the platform catalogue already holds, the `Idempotency-Key` rule of the POST and the 409 cause of a claim already filed.
7. The author writes the versioning and pinning section: a compatible change keeps major version 1, a breaking change raises major version 2 under a new base segment, and v1 is never edited in place.
8. The lint and schema steps run: the document linted against the platform style, every example validated against its schema, the personal-data scan run on the examples, and the template applied twice in two throwaway schemas.
9. The fake set is generated from the document: the create, the update and the read answers, one refused answer per error status, the repeated-key answer and the unavailable answer, all from one example set.
10. The drift test is generated and wired into the build of RWB-S3-E4014-APP and of the three sibling application stories.
11. The document and the fakes are published at v1, and the pinned version of this contract and of each consuming story is recorded.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A path outside `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, or a third operation such as a submit or a channel callback, is added to the document | The lint fails the build; the base and the two operations are fixed (DP-13) | None | AC1 |
| X2 | An element is named after anything other than a DF-TRT field, or a required element is published optional | The schema validation fails the build | None | AC2 |
| X3 | The template is applied in another service's schema, or a foreign key crosses a schema | The boundary test fails the build; the template creates the table in the applying schema only | None | AC3 |
| X4 | An error body is not a problem document, or a status outside the declared set is returned | The envelope validation fails the build | None | AC4 |
| X5 | A published element is removed, renamed, made required or given a new error status under version 1 | The change raises major version 2 under a new base segment; v1 is never edited in place | None | AC5 |
| X6 | A consuming build ships without the drift test, or ships a private variant of an element | The registry refuses the change and the drift test fails the build | None | AC6 |
| X7 | A value the consumers need is fixed by no source — the submission reference, the channel interface, the 409 text | The value is published as the working read of the assumption and the gap stays open | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2712; ASM-4503) | Sections 12 and 13 |

X1 to X6 are the lint, schema, boundary, envelope, versioning and drift failures of a contract build; X7 is the boundary this key records, because the source fixes the two operations and the eight fields and nothing more.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Publishes a document, a DDL template and a fake set; builds against nothing, reads no business data and starts on Day 1 |
| Negotiable | The element order, the example values, the index list and the fake technology are open until v1 is frozen; the base, the two operations, the element names, the required set, the error set and the versioning rule are fixed |
| Valuable | Unblocks RWB-S3-E4014-APP and the three sibling stories on Day 1 and keeps one claim shape for four stories and every later reader |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, three schemas, one DDL template, one error set, one versioning rule and one fake set |
| Small | One sprint for the document, the template, the fakes and the drift test |
| Testable | Each criterion of section 7 is one lint, schema or fake assertion in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: guarantee-claim resource contract

  Background:
    Given the guarantee-claim resource contract document is published with major version 1
    Given the service has one schema, rwb_guarantee, and one login of its own
    Given the contract declares the two operations of TSD S3 T-A.1 and nothing more

  Scenario: AC1 The document publishes the base and the two operations, and nothing else (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI document of the guarantee-claim resource
    When it is linted against the platform contract style rules
    Then it declares the server base /api/recovery/guarantee/v1 and no path on the legacy base
    Then it declares POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims with the request body GuaranteeClaimRequest and the response GuaranteeClaim
    Then it declares PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId} with the request body GuaranteeClaimUpdate and the response GuaranteeClaim
    Then it declares no other path: no submit operation, no TCG channel callback, no delete and no read operation of a sibling resource
    Then each operation declares the capability area "Treatment and offer" with right C on the POST and right U on the PATCH, the bearer security scheme and the scope rule
    Then a path outside the base, or a third operation, fails the lint

  Scenario: AC2 The three schemas carry the DF-TRT elements, the required set and no list member (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the schema section of the document and its worked example
    When both schemas are validated and the example is checked against them
    Then GuaranteeClaimRequest, GuaranteeClaimUpdate and GuaranteeClaim are the three object schemas of this resource, with the platform problem schema reused and not redeclared
    Then every element of the three schemas is a DF-TRT field name in camelCase, from DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022
    Then id, caseId, claimType, claimDeadline, claimedAmount and status are required and filedAt and paidAmount are optional
    Then caseId is taken from the path on the POST and is not repeated in GuaranteeClaimRequest
    Then claimType and status name their list code LOV-CLAIM-TYPE and LOV-CLAIM-STATUS and no member value
    Then no submission-reference element, no channel element, no document element and no case status element is declared
    Then the validation fails on an unknown element, on a missing required element and on a list member written into a schema

  Scenario: AC3 The guarantee_claim DDL template creates the table with the standard columns and no cross-schema key (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the DDL template of the contract
    When it is applied twice, in two throwaway schemas, through the service's own Flyway sequence
    Then it creates guarantee_claim in the applying schema only, with the primary key on id and each column type as TSD S3 T3.1 states it
    Then it carries the standard columns is_active, state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at and updated_by
    Then case_id is a cross reference with an index and no foreign key, and no other schema is named
    Then claim_type and status keep their list widths and no check constraint repeats a list member
    Then the required elements of AC2 are NOT NULL and the optional ones are nullable
    Then a hand-written table that drifts from the template fails the drift test

  Scenario: AC4 The error set, the problem envelope, the Idempotency-Key and the 409 cause are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error section of the document
    When one refused answer per status is validated against it
    Then both operations declare 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503
    Then every error body is application/problem+json with type, title, status, detail, instance and the messageId extension
    Then 403 carries MSG-P4-002, 404 carries the unknown claim or case, 409 carries the conflict of a claim already in FILED, 422 carries MSG-GEN-001 with the field name and 503 carries MSG-GEN-006
    Then the POST declares Idempotency-Key as a required header and the PATCH declares it not applicable
    Then an error body that is not a problem document, a POST without the header and a success body that is a problem document all fail the validation

  Scenario: AC5 Versioning separates a compatible change from a new major version, and the consumer pins (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the versioning section of the document
    When a change is proposed to a published element
    Then an added optional element keeps major version 1 and is accepted by the registry in BACKWARD mode
    Then a removed element, a new required element, a renamed element, a new error status or a path change raises major version 2 under a new base segment
    Then v1 is never edited in place and stays readable after v2 is published
    Then each consuming story pins the published version and a private variant fails its drift test
    Then the document records the version pinned by RWB-S3-E4014-APP

  Scenario: AC6 The fake answers the document and the drift test catches every difference (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fake set generated from the document
    When the contract test runs the claim fake, the problem fakes, the template application and the drift test
    Then the claim fake answers a create with 201 and a GuaranteeClaim whose status is PREPARING, an update with 200 and the same claim in FILED, and no other operation
    Then it answers a refused create with 403 and 422, an unknown claim with 404, an already filed claim with 409 and an unavailable service with 503
    Then it returns the first answer for a repeated Idempotency-Key and never a second claim
    Then the template application proves the table twice in two schemas
    Then the drift test fails on any difference between the fake, the template and sections 12 and 13 of the document
```

These six criteria are new and test only the contract deliverable. **The four legacy acceptance criteria of RWB-E4-014 stay with RWB-S3-E4014-APP** and are not repeated here, and every identifier, path, entity name, field identifier and status is taken from TSD S3 T-A.1, T-A.2, T3.1 and T3.2, character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The guarantee-claim resource is published on one base, `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, with exactly two operations: the create and the update | TSD S3 T-A.1; DP-13 |
| BR2 | The three schemas are `GuaranteeClaimRequest`, `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` and `GuaranteeClaim`, and every element is a DF-TRT field name in camelCase | TSD S3 T-A.2, T3.1 |
| BR3 | The required set is the required column of TSD S3 T3.1: `id`, `caseId`, `claimType`, `claimDeadline`, `claimedAmount` and `status`; `filedAt` and `paidAmount` are optional; `caseId` comes from the path on the POST | TSD S3 T3.1 |
| BR4 | An enumerated element names its list code and no member, because the members are values in force with their version | TSD S3 T3.2; BR-S3-002 |
| BR5 | The `guarantee_claim` DDL template carries the eight fields of T3.1 with their physical types and the standard columns of T3.0, and creates the table in the applying schema only with no cross-schema key | DP-01; DP-15; TSD S3 T3.0, T3.1 |
| BR6 | The error set is fixed per operation, and every error body is an RFC 9457 problem document that names its `messageId` | TSD S3 T-A.2; platform API style |
| BR7 | The create is idempotent by the `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeated key returns the first answer and creates no second claim | TSD S3 T-A.2; legacy RWB-E4-014 endpoint table |
| BR8 | The create needs Treatment and offer C and the update needs Treatment and offer U; the right is declared in the document and checked by the platform guard, and no check is declared in code | TSD S3 T6.1 |
| BR9 | A published element is never edited in place: a compatible change keeps major version 1 and a breaking change raises major version 2 under a new base segment | Template and Rules §R7.2; §R5.4 class C |
| BR10 | The document declares no case status, no decision-record element and no decision code: the status is rwb-case's, the record is the library's and the code is the rule ID and version in force | DP-01; DP-03; ASM-4505 |
| BR11 | The document declares no submission-reference element, no channel operation and no channel schema, because no source gives the claim row a reference field or the TCG channel an interface | GAP-2712; ASM-4503; ASM-4504 |
| BR12 | The 409 of the update means the claim is already in `FILED`; its status, its cause and its `messageId` slot are fixed and its business text is not in any source | GAP-2712; ASM-4509 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 to BR4 are the paths, the schemas and the required set of the document and its lint. BR5 is the DDL template and its boundary test. BR6 is the error section and the platform problem schema it reuses. BR7 is the header rule of the POST and the fake's repeated-key answer. BR8 is the `security` section of each operation; the guard is the platform library's and the contract adds no dependency for it. BR9 is the versioning section. BR10, BR11 and BR12 are the three boundaries of this key: the case status and the decision code are not contract values, the reference and the channel are not published, and the 409 is a status with a cause and no text.

##### 9. State transitions

None in this story: a document has no runtime state. Two vocabularies are touched and neither is fixed here.

| Object | State | Meaning in the contract |
|---|---|---|
| GuaranteeClaim | PREPARING | The state a created claim carries in the fake and in the example |
| GuaranteeClaim | FILED | The state the update returns after the filing; the state RWB-S3-E4014-APP writes |
| GuaranteeClaim | DEFECT, PAID, REJECTED | Named by LOV-CLAIM-STATUS; the document carries them as members of the list in force and fixes none of them |
| Contract | v1 | The published version every consuming story pins |
| Contract | v2 | Raised by a breaking change under a new base segment; v1 stays readable and is never edited |

The claim journey itself is RWB-S3-E4014-APP's and the sibling stories', and the seventeen rule states of TSD S3 T4 are case statuses of rwb-case that appear nowhere in this document (GAP-2712; ASM-4505). The `state` column is declared as varchar(40) with no check constraint, so a new row state is a data change and not a contract change.

| The four application stories of this service | Consume the contract, pin the version and raise a change request rather than a private variant |

No personal name, no email address and no credential appears in the document, the template, an example or a fake. Where a caller must be named, the example uses a role code or a user identifier only.
