##### 1. Story

As a **contract owner for rwb-guarantee**, I want **the published contract of the guarantee claim — the two operations on the service base, the `GuaranteeClaimRequest`, `GuaranteeClaim` and `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` elements, the negotiation facts that travel with a request and are never stored, the `state` and `status` vocabularies kept apart, the single `subrogationShare` element, the error set with the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the compatibility rule and the fakes — instead of the monolith's one `recovery` schema, one set of in-process interfaces and one undivided status column**, so that **the application slice, the claim-preparation slices, the gateway-bff route, the decision-record library and the wave 3 integration harness all build against one frozen claim surface from Day 1**.

This story owns:

- the two operation entries — `POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims` and `PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId}` — on base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, with their access right, their request and answer elements, their errors and the `Idempotency-Key` on the create (DP-13);
- the `GuaranteeClaimRequest`, `GuaranteeClaim` and `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` elements, and the note that fixes, for each property, whether it is stored or context-only;
- the `state` property of the answer, which carries the GUARANTEE state of TSD S3 T4, and the `status` property, which carries LOV-CLAIM-STATUS, as two named vocabularies that are never merged;
- the `subrogationShare` element, which the subrogation answer carries because the legacy criterion records the share against the case and no source gives it a name or a type;
- the error set with MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P7-009 mapped to status codes, and the `Idempotency-Key` rule with its repeat answer;
- the compatibility rule, the pinning rule and the drift test, and the fake set every consumer uses.

It does not own: the behaviour behind the two operations, the range check, the two subrogation outcomes and the record write, which are RWB-S3-E4018-APP; the claim preparation, the checklist and the filing of FEAT-GUA-01 and FEAT-GUA-02; the balance claim of FEAT-GUA-03; the demand notice of FEAT-GUA-05; the closing of the guarantee of FEAT-GUA-07; the decision-record library, which is RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; the gateway-bff composite route, which is RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the case, its status and its party record, which are rwb-case's; and the ACE views, which are rwb-source-data's.

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E4-018 negotiated with a guarantor through one screen, two endpoints whose paths began with the shared base, and one `recovery` schema in which the claim row, the case and the decision log row sat in one process; there was nothing to publish and nothing to fake. The microservice split removes that option. The claim is now written by rwb-guarantee, its stage is a child of `CaseWorkflow` of rwb-case, the screen reaches it through gateway-bff, and the wave 3 harness proves the path across services, so four consumers need the same answer to the same questions before any of them writes code.

The contract has to exist first for four reasons. **The service publishes exactly two operations**: the ownership rows of S3 give rwb-guarantee `POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims` and `PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId}` and no third; the negotiation is therefore carried on the `PATCH` of the claim and no new operation is invented for it (GAP-2730; ASM-4533). **No read operation is published**: the same rows give the service no read, so SCR-17 cannot read the claim through this service, and the contract has to say so and hand the screen to the composite route rather than leave a caller guessing (GAP-2730; ASM-4533). **The negotiation facts have no home**: the approved range, the outcome and the share appear in the rules R-GUA-23, R-GUA-24 and R-GUA-29 and in the legacy criterion, while `guarantee_claim` stops at DF-TRT-022 and carries no range, no outcome and no share; if the body is not fixed, one consumer will send a range and another will store it (GAP-2728; ASM-4529). And **the two state vocabularies collide**: the legacy story moves the case to `SUBROGATION_POSITION`, TSD S3 T4 moves the GUARANTEE claim through the same names, and `LOV-CLAIM-STATUS` publishes a third list — so the contract must publish `state` and `status` as separate properties before any consumer writes a mapper (GAP-2729; ASM-4530).

The contract also fixes what it does not do: it declares no table, adds no column for the range or the notice expiry, publishes no event of its own, declares no workflow and no Schedule, and copies no part of the claim-preparation or the notice slice.

The fake is the Day-1 unblocker: the application slice, the claim-preparation slices, the gateway route and the harness can build the negotiation, the two subrogation answers, the refusal, the repeated key and the error answers before the live service, the live case workflow or the live payment exists (Template and Rules §R5.4 class C).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service identity is fixed by Template and Rules §R4 and the context pack: schema `rwb_guarantee`, base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, topic `rwb.guarantee.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-guarantee` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-13).
- The two operations are the ones the S3 ownership rows give the service, and the three element names are those of TSD S3 T-A.2 — `GuaranteeClaimRequest`, `GuaranteeClaim` and `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` — copied character for character.
- The negotiation body and the `subrogationShare` element are the working read of the assumption, because no source document gives the negotiation a field list, a column or an element name (GAP-2728, GAP-2730; ASM-4529).
- Capability area "Treatment and offer" with right C for the create and right U for the patch is the access declaration of TSD S3 T6.1 and T-A.2; the check is the guard library's and the contract declares the right only.
- The error codes are the ones TSD S3 T-A.2 lists — 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 — and the message identifiers are the legacy story's, with MSG-P7-009 added from the library.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published, so the contract can name the decision-record write the application slice makes in the same transaction, without redeclaring the library (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published, so the contract can name the composite route SCR-17 uses, without declaring a route (DP-19).
- The claim-preparation slices are named only: the create operation is published here and the behaviour behind it is theirs, so one contract answers for the whole claim shape.
- No build dependency and no approval stop: a CON story is Day 1 by rule (§R5.7), sits in contract group `CG-W3`, and is published at status Draft (realignment v1).

##### 4. Flow

1. The contract author fixes the two operation entries: the method, the path on the service base, the access right, the request element, the answer element, the errors and the idempotency rule of each.
2. The author fixes `GuaranteeClaimRequest`: `claimType`, `claimDeadline`, `claimedAmount` and the optional `filedAt` of the claim field catalog of the functional specification.
3. The author fixes `GuaranteeClaimUpdate`: `paidAmount`, `status`, `state`, the negotiation outcome, the outcome date and `subrogationShare`, and states for each one whether it is stored or context-only.
4. The author fixes the answer `GuaranteeClaim`: the eight claim fields of DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022, the `state` of TSD S3 T4, the `subrogationShare` and the standard version and timestamps.
5. The author fixes the two state vocabularies and the rule that `state` and `status` are never merged and never mapped inside the contract.
6. The author fixes the error set: the status codes, the message identifiers and their texts, and the `Idempotency-Key` rule with its repeat answer.
7. The author writes the compatibility rule — what a consumer may rely on and what raises a major version — and the pinning rule for the consumers.
8. The author records the negative rules: no read operation in v1, no table, no range or expiry column, no event and no workflow.
9. The lint and schema steps run: the operation entries compared against the ownership rows and TSD S3 T-A.1, the three schemas validated against the OpenAPI document, the examples scanned for personal data, and the error table checked against the legacy message identifiers.
10. The fake set is generated from the document and the contract test runs it on every change; the document and the fakes are published at v1 and every consumer pins the version.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The document publishes a third operation, or a read operation of its own, or drops one of the two | The lint fails the build; only the two entries the ownership rows give are published | None | AC1 |
| X2 | An element of the update has no place in the schema, or the document adds a range, an outcome or an expiry column | The schema validation fails the build; the facts are declared context-only and no table is declared | None | AC2 |
| X3 | The answer merges `state` and `status`, or publishes one without the other | The lint fails the build; both properties are required and the note that separates them is required | None | AC3 |
| X4 | The subrogation answer is published without `subrogationShare`, or with a type the schema does not fix | The answer schema fails the build; the element is required on the subrogation answer | None | AC3 |
| X5 | An error answer is published without a message identifier, or with a code the legacy story does not carry | The error-table check fails the build; every code is mapped to its identifier and its text | None | AC4 |
| X6 | The `Idempotency-Key` is declared optional on the create, or a repeat is declared to store a second row | The lint fails the build; the header is required on the create and a repeat returns the first answer | None | AC4 |
| X7 | A breaking change is made to a path, an element, an error code or the answer | The change raises major version 2; v1 is never edited in place and stays readable | None | AC5 |
| X8 | A consumer ships without the drift test, or its code drifts from the published schemas | The registry refuses the change and the drift test fails that consumer's build | None | AC6 |
| X9 | A consumer needs a value no source names — the share type, the outcome vocabulary or the range element | The value is published as the working read of the assumption and the gap stays open | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2730; ASM-4529) | Section 3 |

X1 and X7 are contract-governance paths, X2 to X6 are the paths a missing, merged or invented element adds, X8 is the drift rule of class C, and X9 is the reason the negotiation body is published as a working read and not as a value found in a source.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Publishes a document and fakes; builds against nothing, reads no business data and starts on Day 1 |
| Negotiable | The example values, the property order and the fixture set are open until v1 is frozen; the two paths, the elements, the two vocabularies, the errors and the compatibility rule are fixed |
| Valuable | Unblocks the application slice, the claim-preparation slices, the gateway route and the wave 3 harness on Day 1 and keeps the range and the share out of the schema |
| Estimable | Two operations, three elements, one answer, four messages, two rules and six fakes |
| Small | One sprint for the document, the schemas, the fakes and the lint rules |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one document, schema or fake assertion in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: guarantee claim contract

  Background:
    Given the rwb-guarantee contract document is published with major version 1
    Given the service base is /api/recovery/guarantee/v1, the schema rwb_guarantee and the topic rwb.guarantee.events.v1
    Given the contract declares the guarantee claim surface only, and no claim preparation and no notice

  Scenario: AC1 The claim surface is the two operations of the ownership rows and no read (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operation section of the contract document
    When it is validated against the S3 ownership rows and TSD S3 T-A.1
    Then it publishes POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims for opening a claim, under capability area Treatment and offer with right C
    Then it publishes PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId} for recording the claim result, under the same capability area with right U
    Then no other operation and no read operation is declared, so the screen read is the composite route's and not this service's
    Then the change note records that the negotiation is carried on the PATCH of the claim and that no third operation is invented for it
    Then the lint fails the build if a third operation or a read operation appears

  Scenario: AC2 The elements are fixed and the negotiation facts are not stored (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the request schemas of the two operations and the schema of the service
    When the schemas are validated
    Then GuaranteeClaimRequest carries claimType, claimDeadline, claimedAmount and filedAt
    Then GuaranteeClaimUpdate carries paidAmount, status, state, the negotiation outcome, the outcome date and subrogationShare
    Then the document states that the approved range, the notice expiry and the rule package version are request context facts and are not columns of rwb_guarantee
    Then the document declares no table and no column for a range, an outcome or an expiry
    Then an example carries amounts, dates and codes and no account number, national identifier or name

  Scenario: AC3 The answer keeps state and status apart and carries the TCG share (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the answer schema of the two operations
    When one subrogation answer and one refusal answer are validated
    Then GuaranteeClaim carries the eight claim fields of DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022, state, subrogationShare and the standard version and timestamps
    Then state carries the GUARANTEE state of TSD S3 T4 and status carries LOV-CLAIM-STATUS
    Then the document states that the two vocabularies are never merged and never mapped inside the contract, and that the screen labels are the screen's own
    Then a subrogation answer carries subrogationShare, whose name and type are the working read of the assumption
    Then a refusal answer carries RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE as its state and no share

  Scenario: AC4 The error set and the Idempotency-Key rule are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error section of the document
    When each declared answer is validated
    Then the operations declare 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409 on a state conflict, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503
    Then the document maps MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P7-009 to the answers that carry them, keeps their legacy texts and adds no message identifier
    Then the create requires the Idempotency-Key header and a repeated key answers with the first result and stores no second row
    Then the patch declares no idempotency key, as TSD S3 T-A.2 API-S3-002 states
    Then an error answer carries the message identifier, the merge fields and the trace identifier only

  Scenario: AC5 Versioning separates a compatible change from a new major version (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the versioning section of the document
    When a change is proposed to a published element
    Then a backward-compatible change keeps major version 1 and is accepted by the registry in BACKWARD mode
    Then a breaking change to a path, a required element, an error code or the answer raises major version 2 and v1 is never edited in place
    Then each consumer pins a published version and raises a change request rather than a private variant

  Scenario: AC6 The fake answers the document and every consumer runs the drift test (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fake set generated from the document
    When the contract test runs the claim fake, the negotiation fake, the subrogation fake, the error fake, the composite route fake and the decision-record fake
    Then the claim fake answers a created claim and a patched claim with the two vocabularies and the share
    Then the error fake answers 403, 422 and 503 with their message identifiers and no personal data
    Then the composite route fake answers one hop for SCR-17 and the decision-record fake answers an accepted record and a failed write
    Then the drift test fails the build of any consumer whose request, answer or error does not match section 12
```

These criteria are new and test only the contract deliverable: no legacy acceptance criterion is repeated here, because **AC1 to AC4 of RWB-E4-018 are owned by RWB-S3-E4018-APP**, and every identifier, path element, field identifier and message is taken from the ownership rows, the TSD appendix or the legacy story character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The claim surface is exactly two operations on the service base: the create under right C with an idempotency key, and the patch under right U | DP-13; S3 ownership rows; TSD S3 T-A.1 API-S3-001 and API-S3-002 |
| BR2 | No read operation is published in v1; SCR-17 is composed by the gateway-bff composite route | GAP-2730; ASM-4533; DP-19 |
| BR3 | The negotiation is carried on the patch of the claim; no third operation is created for it | GAP-2728; ASM-4529 |
| BR4 | `state` carries the GUARANTEE state of TSD S3 T4 and `status` carries LOV-CLAIM-STATUS; the contract never merges or maps them | GAP-2729; ASM-4530 |
| BR5 | `subrogationShare` is published on the update and on a subrogation answer, and its name and type are the working read, because the legacy criterion records the share and no source names it | GAP-2730; ASM-4529 |
| BR6 | The approved range, the notice expiry and the package version travel as request context and are never columns of `rwb_guarantee` | GAP-2728; ASM-4529; DP-01 |
| BR7 | The contract declares the access right only; the check is the guard library's on capability area "Treatment and offer" | TSD S3 T6.1 |
| BR8 | A published version is never edited: a compatible change stays in major version 1 and a breaking change raises major version 2 | Template and Rules §R7.2; §R5.4 class C |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 and BR7 are the operation table with its access column, and the guard is called by the application slice, not by the contract. BR2 is the negative rule of section 12.1 and the reason the composite route is named: the contract deliberately publishes no read, so no consumer builds against one. BR3 is the sentence that keeps the negotiation on the existing path instead of adding an operation the ownership rows do not give. BR4 is the two properties and the note that separates them, and it is the one place where a consumer could silently merge three vocabularies. BR5 is the one element whose name is not in a source, so it is published with the assumption tag and kept single. BR6 keeps the contract out of the schema, and BR8 is the compatibility section and the pinning rule.

##### 9. State transitions

None at run time: a document and a schema have no state. Three vocabularies are fixed here and the runtime transitions behind them are specified by RWB-S3-E4018-APP section 9.

| Object | State | Meaning in the contract |
|---|---|---|
| Claim answer | `PREPARING`, `FILED`, `DEFECT`, `PAID`, `REJECTED` | The `status` property, the values of LOV-CLAIM-STATUS |
| Claim answer | `CLAIM_PAID`, `CLAIM_PART_PAID`, `SUBROGATION_POSITION`, `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` | The `state` property, members of the GUARANTEE state set of TSD S3 T4 |
| Create request | New | The `Idempotency-Key` was not presented before; a claim row may be written |
| Create request | Repeated | The key was presented before; the first answer is returned and nothing is stored |
| Patch request | Accepted | The negotiation outcome is inside the approved range carried on the request context |
| Patch request | Refused | The answer carries an error code with its message identifier and merge fields |
| Contract version | v1 | The published version every consumer pins |
| Contract version | v2 | Raised by a breaking change; v1 stays readable and is never edited in place |

The screen labels of SCR-17 — Not due, due, submitted, paid, refused — are the screen's own and are not a third vocabulary of this contract (GAP-2729; ASM-4530).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The contract author (any team, per U3) | Writes and versions the document, the three schemas, the error table and the fakes |
| The service team of rwb-guarantee | Consumes the contract, pins the version and raises a change request rather than a private variant |
| The rwb-guarantee tech lead | Confirms that the two operations are the ones the application slice and the claim-preparation slices build |
| The solution architect | Confirms the negative rules — no read, no third operation, no table — against the S3 ownership rows and TSD S3 T-A.1 |
| The rwb-case owner (P3) | Confirms that the case status and the case-level keeping of the TCG share are the parent's, and that the contract carries neither |
| The platform edge owner | Confirms the composite route that serves SCR-17 without a read operation of this service |
| The wave 3 integration harness owner | Confirms the fake set is enough to prove the cross-service path |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A service contract is a technical artefact, not a credit decision |

No personal name, no email address and no credential appears in the document, an example or a fake. Where a caller must be named, the example uses a role code or a user identifier only.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Business data published | None. The document publishes operation entries, three element schemas, codes, message identifiers and examples; no customer, account or case value appears |
| Request context facts published | The approved range, the notice expiry and the rule package version on the request; all of them context-only |
| Stored fields referenced | The claim fields DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 and the standard columns of T3.0, referenced through the elements and declared by RWB-S3-E4018-APP, not redefined here |
| Field identifiers | The eight claim fields carry DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022; `state` and `status` carry the T3.0 column and DF-TRT-022; `subrogationShare` carries no field identifier, because no source gives it one (GAP-2730; ASM-4529) |
| Personal data | None. The examples carry amounts, dates, codes and a share, and the actor and trace references are identifiers, never names |
| Tables published | None. The contract declares no table and no column; `guarantee_claim` is the application slice's and `decision_record` is the library's (DP-01, DP-03) |
| ACE data | None, and no `v_ace_*` view is named as a source of the contract (DP-05) |

The one place where the contract could leak a value is the share: the document therefore fixes that `subrogationShare` is a property of the update and of the subrogation answer, that it is never an enumeration and never a default, and that no example value is presented as a value in force.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-guarantee (S3); base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` (DP-13). The contract declares the claim surface only: the claim preparation, the filing and the notice are other slices that use the same two operations.

| Method | Path | Request | Answer | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims` | `GuaranteeClaimRequest` | `GuaranteeClaim` | Treatment and offer, right C | `Idempotency-Key` header required; a repeat returns the first answer |
| PATCH | `/guarantee-claims/{claimId}` | `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` | `GuaranteeClaim` | Treatment and offer, right U | Not applicable, as TSD S3 T-A.2 API-S3-002 states |

Two operations and no more: the S3 ownership rows give the service exactly these two, so the contract publishes no read, no delete and no separate negotiation endpoint, and the negotiation travels on the patch (GAP-2730; ASM-4533). The error codes are those of TSD S3 T-A.2 — 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 — and the reference to the claim is the path parameter, never a body field. Whether a read operation is added to the service later, and which owner decides it, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2730; ASM-4533).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The contract declares the surface and calls no service: the case, its status, the party reference and the approved range arrive on the stage signal that the parent `CaseWorkflow` forwards, and the decision record is an in-process call of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (DP-03; ASM-4529).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic of the service is `rwb.guarantee.events.v1` with event names `rwb.guarantee.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and the S3 ownership rows give the service no event. The contract publishes no event schema and declares no outbox row.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The contract declares no subscription. The payment that triggers a subrogation reaches the stage as a signal the parent forwards, and the event that would carry it is named by no source (GAP-2728; ASM-4531).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The contract declares no workflow and no activity. It states only that the patch is written inside an activity of `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` on the owner's own task queue and that the decision record is called from that activity, so a replay reuses the recorded decision; the workflow itself is RWB-S3-E4018-APP's (DP-03).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The contract declares no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job; the ownership rows give the service no job, and the claim deadline and the notice expiry are durable timers inside the workflow and not part of the published surface.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The contract declares no table, no column and no key. It states the negative rules that matter: the approved range, the notice expiry, the negotiation outcome and the package version have no place in `rwb_guarantee`, because no source gives them one and storing them would copy another owner's facts into this schema; and `guarantee_claim` stops at DF-TRT-022 today, so `subrogationShare` is published as an element and its column is the application slice's (GAP-2728, GAP-2730; ASM-4529, ASM-4535; DP-01). `guarantee_claim` is RWB-S3-E4018-APP's business table and `decision_record` is the library object of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; `decision_log_entry` is P7's ledger and is named here only.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| Claim fake | `POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims` and `PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId}` | A created claim with `status` PREPARING and `state` of the GUARANTEE set; a patched claim with the outcome written |
| Negotiation fake | The patch of the negotiation | An outcome inside the approved range; an outcome outside it with 422 and the field |
| Subrogation fake | R-GUA-23 and R-GUA-24 answers | A claim at `CLAIM_PAID` and one at `CLAIM_PART_PAID`, each answering `SUBROGATION_POSITION` with `subrogationShare`; a refusal answering `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` with no share |
| Repeated-key fake | The idempotency rule of the create | The first answer returned for a repeated `Idempotency-Key`, with no second row and no second record |
| Error fake | The error table | 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409 on a state conflict, 422 with MSG-GEN-001, 503 with MSG-P7-003, each with its identifier, its merge fields and a trace identifier |
| Composite route fake and decision-record fake | RWB-PLT-N001-CON and RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | One hop for SCR-17 joining the case read with the claim the stage holds; an accepted record with an entry reference and a failed write with MSG-P7-003 |

The fakes answer from the same example set as the document, so a change to the contract shows up as a contract-test failure in a consumer rather than as a surprise at run time. The route and record fakes are published by their own stories and are referenced here, not redeclared.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 operation entries on `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` | 0 | OpenAPI 3.1 fragment; one hop to the service, 2 s timeout; no read operation |
| Kafka | 0 event schemas | 0 | The service topic is named; this contract declares no event |
| Temporal | 0 | 0 | The contract states the write happens in an activity and declares no workflow |
| File | 0 | 0 | No file crosses the contract; INT-29 is not a file path of this service |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Contract artefact of rwb-guarantee: the OpenAPI fragment and the three element schemas in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.guarantee.api`, the error table and the compatibility note in the contract document, and the fake set as a test asset. Service base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, schema `rwb_guarantee`, topic `rwb.guarantee.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-guarantee` in namespace `rwb-recovery`. The artefact coordinates and the publication channel are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2730; ASM-4533).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 enters the contract as one statement — the patch is a state change whose record is written in the caller's transaction — and the H dependency sits on the application slice, which calls the library. DP-05 is the negative rule of section 11: no `v_ace_*` view is a source of the contract, because the legacy customer read is dropped (ASM-4532). DP-13 is the base of the two operations and the reason the legacy base appears nowhere in the document. DP-19 is the route that serves SCR-17, named here because no read operation is published for the screen to call.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `GuaranteeClaimOpenApi` | OpenAPI 3.1 fragment | The two operation entries, their parameters, their errors and their access declaration |
| `GuaranteeClaimRequestSchema` | Request schema | `claimType`, `claimDeadline`, `claimedAmount`, `filedAt` |
| `GuaranteeClaimUpdateSchema` | Request schema | `paidAmount`, `status`, `state`, the negotiation outcome, the outcome date, `subrogationShare`, with the stored and context-only note on each |
| `GuaranteeClaimSchema` | Answer schema | The eight claim fields, `state`, `status`, `subrogationShare` and the standard version and timestamps |
| `ErrorCatalogue` | Document table | The status codes, the message identifiers, the legacy texts and the merge fields |
| `CompatibilityNote` | Document section | The negative rules, the compatible versus breaking rule and the pinning rule |
| `ClaimFakeSet` | Test asset | The six fakes of section 12.8 and the drift test every consumer runs |

**Database.** None. The contract creates no table, adds no column and declares no key; the negative rules of section 12.7 are the deliverable, and a review that finds a range, an outcome or an expiry column in `rwb_guarantee` fails this story.

**Configuration and reference data.** The contract fixes no business value. The approved range, the notice expiry and the scheme values are values in force in the owner's data; the only values in the document are examples, and they are marked as examples. Capability area "Treatment and offer" and rights C and U are read from rwb-access through the guard library, which the application slice calls.

**Build steps**

1. Write the two operation entries, their access rights and the idempotency rule; lint that no third or read operation appears (AC1).
2. Write `GuaranteeClaimRequest` and `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` and the stored-versus-context note for every property (AC2).
3. Write `GuaranteeClaim` with `state`, `status` and `subrogationShare` and the note that separates the vocabularies (AC3).
4. Write the error table with the four identifiers and their texts, and the repeated-key rule; validate one answer per code (AC4).
5. Write the compatibility note, the negative rules and the pinning rule (AC5).
6. Generate the six fakes and the drift test; wire the drift test into the build of RWB-S3-E4018-APP, the claim-preparation slices, the gateway route and the wave 3 harness (AC6).
7. Publish v1 and record the pinned version of each consumer.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.guarantee.claim-contract`.

**Done when.** The document and the three schemas validate, the operation lint passes with exactly two entries and no read, the error table matches the four message identifiers and texts, the six fakes answer every example including the two subrogation answers and the repeated key, the drift test is green on the build of this story and on the build of the application slice, and v1 is published with the pinned versions recorded.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Published as |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is absent or invalid, the negotiation outcome among them | Enter {field}. | 422, with the field name |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role does not hold right C or right U | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | 403, from the guard library |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | 503, from RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| MSG-P7-009 | The decision record is refused for a field | The decision record was refused: {field} is missing or not valid. | 422, from RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, with the field |

The first three texts are the legacy texts of RWB-E4-018 carried unchanged, and MSG-P7-009 is the library's; the contract adds no message identifier and renames none. The entry format of each message in a published catalogue is Not specified in the source documents and is published as the working read (GAP-2730; ASM-4533). Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story, and the contract declares none. SCR-17 Guarantee claim is reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and the contract fixes only the answers that screen consumes: the claim with its `state`, its `status` and its `subrogationShare` after a patch. Because the service publishes no read operation, the route composes the case read of rwb-case with the claim the stage holds, and that composition is the edge contract's (GAP-2730; ASM-4533). The screen states — Not due, due, submitted, paid, refused — are the screen's own and are named in section 9 only to keep the three vocabularies apart.

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |

| TC-S3-E4018-CON-01 | AC1 | Contract | The two operation entries linted against the S3 ownership rows and TSD S3 T-A.1; the access rights; the negative rules for a third operation and for a read |
| TC-S3-E4018-CON-02 | AC2 | Contract | `GuaranteeClaimRequest` and `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` validated; the stored and context-only note on every property; the absence of a column and a field identifier for the range, the outcome and the expiry; a personal-data scan of the examples |

The legacy test set of RWB-E4-018 — TC-E4-018-01 to TC-E4-018-06 — is carried by RWB-S3-E4018-APP and by the wave 3 integration harness, and no legacy id is renumbered here: these five are the contract's own tests.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the approved range, the notice expiry and the scheme values are values in force in the owner's data, and the only values in the document are examples, marked as examples.
- No personal data in a schema, an example, a fake or a log: the examples carry amounts, dates, codes and a share, and the scan fails the build otherwise.
- No table, no column and no key in the contract: the range, the outcome and the expiry stay out of `rwb_guarantee` (DP-01; ASM-4529).
- No third operation and no read operation: the lint of X1 fails any document that publishes one.
- No merged state vocabulary: `state` and `status` are two properties and the contract maps neither.
- No event and no outbox row of the contract's own: the service topic is named and the ownership rows give it no event.
- No REST call and no workflow in the contract: the record is written in process inside an activity and the case status stays the parent's.
- No ACE view: the contract names no `v_ace_*` view as a source, because the legacy customer read is dropped (DP-05; ASM-4532).
- A published version is never edited in place: a breaking change raises major version 2 with a migration note and a superseded marking.

##### 19. Out of scope

- The behaviour behind the two operations — the range check, the two subrogation outcomes, the refusal and the record write: RWB-S3-E4018-APP.
- The claim preparation, the checklist and the filing of FEAT-GUA-01 and FEAT-GUA-02, and the balance claim of FEAT-GUA-03: their own slices.
- The demand to the guarantor and co-borrowers, its template and its expiry: the FEAT-GUA-05 slice.
- Closing the guarantee and the case under R-GUA-26 and returning the residual under R-GUA-25: the FEAT-GUA-07 slice.
- The insurance claim on a collateral event: the FEAT-GUA-08 slice.
- The table `guarantee_claim`, its columns and the `subrogationShare` column: RWB-S3-E4018-APP and the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-01).
- The decision-record library, its `MANDATORY` transaction, its chain and its envelope: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-E1027-APP.
- The gateway-bff composite route, the screen field list of SCR-17 and the read the screen needs: RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the screen owners (GAP-2730; ASM-4533).
- The case, its status, its party record and the case-level keeping of the TCG share: rwb-case (P3).
- The GUA rule package, its authoring, its promotion and its version labels: P7 rwb-decision and the service-template runtime.
- The ACE views and the customer, account and payment data behind them: rwb-source-data (P1).
- The event that carries a guarantee payment and any subscription to it: the payment story and the event catalogue.
- The error and message catalogue of the platform, the Thai texts and the incident route: the platform library stories (DL10).
- The cross-service proof of the claim and the `-ITG` copies of the legacy test set: the wave 3 integration harness.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner**, I want **to negotiate with a guarantor inside the approved range on the guarantee claim of the case and to have the outcome recorded against the claim and the TCG share kept for every later recovery**, so that **no guarantee claim misses its deadline and no subrogation position is lost after the TCG pays**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E4-018. It owns:

- all four legacy acceptance criteria of the story, copied verbatim with their origin tag, and the rules, messages, screen and data rows they depend on;
- `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-guarantee` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, as the guarantee stage child of `CaseWorkflow` owned by rwb-case, with the activities `evaluateNegotiation`, `applyOutcome` and `recordAndApply` (context pack: one workflow; Architecture v5 slide 18 "Guarantee claim · GUA 32"; Temporal and Drools Design slide 13);
- the behaviour behind `PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId}` on base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, under capability area "Treatment and offer" with right U (DP-13; TSD S3 T-A.1 API-S3-002);
- the negotiation outcome against the claim: R-GUA-23 and R-GUA-24 to `SUBROGATION_POSITION` and R-GUA-29 to `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE`, evaluated in the GUA package version in force;
- the local decision record of the negotiation, written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the same transaction as the `guarantee_claim` row (DP-03);
- the writer of `guarantee_claim` in schema `rwb_guarantee` and the stage outcome the parent uses to move the case.

It does not own: the published shape of the two operations, the elements, the error set and the fakes, which are RWB-S3-E4018-CON; the preparation and filing of the claim and the balance claim, which are the claim-preparation slices of FEAT-GUA-01, FEAT-GUA-02 and FEAT-GUA-03; the demand to the guarantor and its expiry, which are the FEAT-GUA-05 slice; the closing of the guarantee and the case, which are FEAT-GUA-07 (legacy RWB-E4-019); the case status, which is rwb-case's; the decision-record library, which is RWB-PLT-E1027-APP; the gateway-bff composite route, which is RWB-PLT-N001-CON; and the deployment, which is the wave 3 integration harness and the platform DevOps stories.

##### 2. Business rationale

Guarantee and TCG claims are late because deadlines are not tracked (FSD S3 A1.3), and the position a guarantor may reclaim after payment is lost because nothing records it. The functional specification keeps the objective and its metric — claims filed inside the deadline at 100 percent, measured on the decision log and the Workbench records, reviewed monthly — and REQ-S3-005 states that a guarantor who answers a demand enters the same treatment paths as a borrower. The legacy guardrail BR-S3-006 stands unchanged: no value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version.

What D-RCV-60 changes is where the negotiation is decided, what it is written to and who owns the state:

- the guarantee stage is `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-guarantee`, the child of `CaseWorkflow` of rwb-case, so the case keeps one parent workflow from entry to closure and the stage runs where its rules and data live (Temporal and Drools Design slide 13);
- the outcome is written to `guarantee_claim` in `rwb_guarantee` (DP-01), reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) and the base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` (DP-13);
- the decision is recorded through the local decision-record library in the same transaction as the change (DP-03), because `decision_log_entry` is P7's ledger and no service writes it;
- the state the legacy story moves — `SUBROGATION_POSITION` — is the GUARANTEE state of TSD S3 T4 and belongs to this claim, while the case status stays with rwb-case: the stage reports an outcome and the parent moves the case (ASM-4530);
- the legacy read of `v_ace_customer` is not carried: the negotiation and the share need the claim, the party reference and the range, not the customer's personal fields, and the ACE views are read by rwb-source-data (DP-05; ASM-4532).

No business value moves. The approved range, the notice expiry and the rule package stay values in force in the owner's data, read with their version and never written in code (BR-S3-006).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S3-E4018-CON is published: the two operation entries on `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, the `GuaranteeClaimRequest`, `GuaranteeClaim` and `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` elements, the negotiation facts declared context-only, the error set, the idempotency rule and the fakes. The negotiation body has no source specification and is published as the working read (GAP-2730; ASM-4529).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: `DecisionRecordWriter.record(DecisionRecord)` runs with `@Transactional(propagation = MANDATORY)`, refuses with MSG-P7-009 and fails with MSG-P7-003, so the claim row and its record commit together or not at all (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-17 Guarantee claim is reached through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, and no screen calls a service directly (DP-19). The service publishes no read operation of its own, so the route composes the case read of rwb-case with the claim the stage holds (GAP-2730; ASM-4533).
- The signal the parent forwards carries the case, the claim reference, the GUARANTEE state, the guaranteed amount and the approved range as request context; the range, its unit and the identity of the list it comes from are named by no S3 source (GAP-2728; ASM-4529).
- The embedded Drools runtime and the GUA package (32 rules, TSD S3 T4) are the service template's capability, and the package version in force arrives on `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1`; this story names the package and adds no build dependency of its own (ASM-4534).
- The access guard, the outbox and inbox library and the workflow kit are service-template capabilities; this story declares capability area "Treatment and offer" and the rights C and U and adds no build dependency of its own.
- The per-service Flyway sequence of rwb-guarantee carries `guarantee_claim` with DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 and the library object `decision_record`; this story adds the TCG-share column and never edits an applied migration (GAP-2728; ASM-4535).
- No ACE view is opened by this story: `case_party`, `assignment` and `timer` are rwb-case's, and `v_ace_customer` is rwb-source-data's (DP-05; ASM-4532).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-S3-E4018-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-case's `CaseWorkflow` receives the case change through the case router and signals the running guarantee child on queue `rwb-guarantee`; the stage never calls rwb-case (Temporal and Drools Design slide 13, the four steps receive, ask, record and apply, wait).
2. The stage holds the facts it was started with: the case, the claim reference, the GUARANTEE state — `CLAIM_PAID` or `CLAIM_PART_PAID` — the guaranteed amount, the approved range as context and the package in force. Nothing about the range is copied into `rwb_guarantee` (ASM-4529).
3. Case owner or guarantee officer opens SCR-17 Guarantee claim through the gateway-bff composite route and reads the claim, the deadline and the checklist (DP-19).
4. The officer records the negotiation outcome with `PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId}` carrying `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` under right U; `evaluateNegotiation` validates the fields and applies the range check.
5. An outcome inside the approved range is accepted; an outcome outside the range is refused with 422 naming the field, because the rule that would authorise it is named by no S3 source (GAP-2728; ASM-4529).
6. `evaluateNegotiation` evaluates the GUA package in the version in force: on `SUBROGATION_DUE` with the claim at `CLAIM_PAID` it selects R-GUA-23, at `CLAIM_PART_PAID` it selects R-GUA-24, and on `GUARANTOR_REFUSED` it selects R-GUA-29.
7. A guarantor who refuses or does not answer by the notice expiry records the refusal and the stage reports `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` under R-GUA-29, so the parent returns the case to the route decision.
8. `applyOutcome` writes the claim result on `guarantee_claim` — `status` from LOV-CLAIM-STATUS, `state` from the GUARANTEE set, `paid_amount` and the TCG share — and keeps the range used on the decision record only.
9. `recordAndApply` assembles the `DecisionRecord` — the decision code, the case, the claim, the rule ID with the package version, the recommendation, the final call and the actor — and writes it through `DecisionRecordWriter.record` in the caller's transaction, then the `guarantee_claim` row in the same transaction (DP-03).
10. The stage publishes nothing: the outcome is reported to the parent `CaseWorkflow`, which moves the case and, for the subrogation, keeps the TCG share against the case for all future recoveries, because the case is rwb-case's record (ASM-4530).
11. A payment that arrives for the claim reaches the stage as the next signal the parent forwards; the event that carries it and any subscription of this service to it are named by no source (GAP-2728; ASM-4531).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The role does not hold right U on "Treatment and offer" | 403 before any read or write; the refusal is the guard library's and is logged by it | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, TC-E4-018-05 |
| X2 | The decision record cannot be written | `recordAndApply` throws before the `guarantee_claim` row is written and the transaction rolls back; nothing changes | MSG-P7-003 | AC4, TC-E4-018-06 |
| X3 | The decision record is refused for a missing or invalid field | Nothing is written and the field is named in the service log and the incident | MSG-P7-009 | AC4 |
| X4 | The negotiation outcome is outside the approved range | The request is refused with 422 and the field is named; no claim row changes and the range used is not recorded | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X5 | A required field of the negotiation is absent | The request is refused with 422 and the field is named | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X6 | The claim is not at a GUARANTEE state the stage accepts | The signal is recorded and the stage waits; no outcome is written and the parent keeps the case status | None | AC2, AC3 |
| X7 | The package in force is not the one the outcome was built on | The stage re-evaluates against the package named on `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` and records the version it used | None | AC1 |
| X8 | The guarantor refuses, or the notice expires with no answer | The refusal is recorded and the stage reports `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` under R-GUA-29 | None | Section 8 |

X1 to X5 are the exception paths of RWB-E4-018 carried onto the split, X6 and X7 belong to the parent-and-child workflow model of the target, and X8 is the refusal rule the functional specification lists next to the two subrogation rules. The range of X4 and the notice expiry of X8 are values in force, so neither is a constant of this story.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the published contract, the decision-record library and the gateway route with their fakes, on the tables of its own schema, and needs no live rwb-case, no live P7 and no live payment to start |
| Negotiable | The activity names, the decision code per outcome, the shape of the stage outcome and the share column are this story's choice; the rules, the messages, the screen and the two operations are fixed |
| Valuable | The officer records the negotiation and the TCG share in days, and every outcome carries the rule version it was evaluated with |
| Estimable | One workflow branch, three activities, one operation, one repository and one record write |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on synthetic claims and range facts through the contract fakes, plus the two component cases of the access answer and the failed record write |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Negotiate with a guarantor

  Scenario: AC1 Negotiate with a guarantor (legacy RWB-E4-018 AC1)
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When the user acts on the screen
    Then lets the case owner negotiate within the range and record the outcome against the customer
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Rule R-GUA-23 (legacy RWB-E4-018 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns case status CLAIM_PAID
    Given a case in state CLAIM_PAID
    When subrogation due
    Then record the TCG share against the case for all future recoveries
    Then the case moves to SUBROGATION_POSITION

  Scenario: AC3 Rule R-GUA-24 (legacy RWB-E4-018 AC3)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns case status CLAIM_PART_PAID
    Given a case in state CLAIM_PART_PAID
    When subrogation due
    Then record the TCG share against the case for all future recoveries
    Then the case moves to SUBROGATION_POSITION

  Scenario: AC4 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E4-018 AC4)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

**Target reading.** Every line and every value above is the legacy line and the legacy value, unchanged, including the repetition of `Then` and the legacy wording of `the action is taken` and `the decision log cannot be written`; what changes is where it runs, who produces the fact and how it is reached. The screen of AC1 is SCR-17 Guarantee claim, reached through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 on base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` (DP-13); the officer works on `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-guarantee` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, the guarantee stage child of `CaseWorkflow` of rwb-case, with the three activities `evaluateNegotiation`, `applyOutcome` and `recordAndApply` (Architecture v5 slide 18, "Guarantee claim · GUA 32"; Temporal and Drools Design slide 13). "The range" arrives as a context fact on the stage signal and is never a column: no S3 source defines its bounds, its unit or the list it comes from (GAP-2728; ASM-4529). "The outcome against the customer" is recorded against the claim and the party reference of the case, because the statement of the functional specification reads "the party" for the same feature and the difference is recorded, not resolved, here (GAP-2729; ASM-4530). "The decision log" of AC1 and AC4 is the local decision record of `decision_record` in `rwb_guarantee`, written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON with `@Transactional(propagation = MANDATORY)` in the same transaction as the `guarantee_claim` row, so a failed record leaves nothing behind (DP-03). `CLAIM_PAID`, `CLAIM_PART_PAID` and `SUBROGATION_POSITION` of AC2 and AC3 are the GUARANTEE states of TSD S3 T4, reached inside the stage; the case status is rwb-case's and the stage reports the outcome, so the two `Given` lines name the state the mock and the claim carry (ASM-4530). "The TCG share ... for all future recoveries" is kept on the claim row for the length of the claim and reported to the parent in the stage outcome so that the case carries it, because the case is rwb-case's record and this service writes no case row.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The guarantor negotiation is recorded against the claim inside the approved range; an outcome outside the range is refused and nothing is written | R-GUA-28 "inside the approved range"; FSD S3 A2.6; GAP-2728; ASM-4529 |
| BR2 | When the TCG holds a share of every later recovery and the claim is at `CLAIM_PAID`, the share is recorded against the case and the claim moves to `SUBROGATION_POSITION` | R-GUA-23; REQ-S3-005 |
| BR3 | When the TCG holds a share of every later recovery and the claim is at `CLAIM_PART_PAID`, the same share is recorded and the claim moves to `SUBROGATION_POSITION` | R-GUA-24; REQ-S3-005 |
| BR4 | When the guarantor refuses, or does not reply by the notice expiry, the refusal is recorded and the case returns to the route decision | R-GUA-29 |
| BR5 | The decision is recorded with the rule version in the same transaction as the change; if it cannot be recorded, nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; MSG-P7-003 |
| BR6 | A required field of the negotiation is refused with MSG-GEN-001 and the field name | VR-S3-006-1; MSG-GEN-001 |
| BR7 | No value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version | BR-S3-006 |
| BR8 | The approved range and the notice expiry are facts of the request and of the decision record, never columns of `rwb_guarantee` | GAP-2728; ASM-4529; DP-01 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 is the range check of `evaluateNegotiation`, with the bounds taken from the request context and no rule identifier available in any source. BR2 and BR3 are the two subrogation branches of the same activity, selected by the GUARANTEE state the stage holds. BR4 is the refusal branch of the activity and the `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` outcome the stage reports. BR5 is the `MANDATORY` transaction of the library, so the claim row and the record row commit together or not at all. BR6 is the field validation of the two operations. BR7 is the reason the range, the expiry and the package are not constants of this build. BR8 is the reason no range or expiry column is added: storing them would copy another owner's facts into this schema.

##### 9. State transitions

The case status is rwb-case's and is not changed by this story: the stage reports an outcome and the parent `CaseWorkflow` moves the case (ASM-4530). What this story owns is the `guarantee_claim` row and the execution of the stage.

| From | Event | Condition | To | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CLAIM_PAID` | SUBROGATION_DUE | The TCG holds a share of every later recovery | `SUBROGATION_POSITION` | R-GUA-23 |
| `CLAIM_PART_PAID` | SUBROGATION_DUE | The same share condition | `SUBROGATION_POSITION` | R-GUA-24 |
| `GUARANTOR_NOTICE` | GUARANTOR_REFUSED | The guarantor refuses or the notice expires with no answer | `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` | R-GUA-29 |
| any accepted GUARANTEE state | the officer records an outcome outside the approved range | X4 | no change | None |

| `guarantee_claim.state` | Event | To |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAIM_PAID` or `CLAIM_PART_PAID` | The stage reports `SUBROGATION_POSITION` | `SUBROGATION_POSITION` |
| `GUARANTOR_NOTICE` | The stage reports the refusal | `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` |

`state` carries the GUARANTEE state of TSD S3 T4 (the 17-state set, 32 rules) and `status` carries LOV-CLAIM-STATUS — `PREPARING`, `FILED`, `DEFECT`, `PAID`, `REJECTED` — so the two vocabularies are kept apart and the screen labels of SCR-17 — Not due, due, submitted, paid, refused — are the screen's own (GAP-2729; ASM-4530). `SUBROGATION_POSITION` to `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` under R-GUA-25 and the closing of the guarantee under R-GUA-26 belong to FEAT-GUA-07 and are not this story's.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The recovery squad (RW-TRIBE) | Writes the guarantee stage, the three activities, the operation and the repository |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Records the negotiation and the outcome; holds CRU, so right C, R and U |
| RW-GUARANT, guarantee officer | Records the negotiation and the outcome; holds CRU |
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer (FCR) | Records the negotiation and the outcome; holds CRUA |
| RW-SPECIAL, hardship and vulnerability specialist | Records the negotiation and the outcome; holds CRU |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL, RW-CONDUCT, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-BIANAL | Read the claim; right R only |
| RW-PRODHEAD, RW-CREDCOMM | Read, and approve where another story's matrix requires it; right RA |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-AGENT | Read as service identities, subject to the same checks |
| The case status and the case-level storage of the TCG share | Not this story: rwb-case owns them and the parent moves and keeps them |
| The closing of the guarantee, the balance claim and the demand notice | Not this story: FEAT-GUA-07, FEAT-GUA-02 and FEAT-GUA-05 slices |

The rights above are those of TSD S3 T6.1 and of the permission table of the legacy story, and the check itself is the platform guard library's: this story declares capability area "Treatment and offer" and rights C and U and calls the guard, and it owns no check of its own. No credential and no personal name appears in the request, the payloads or the logs, which carry case IDs, claim IDs, amounts, dates, codes and rule versions only.

`guarantee_claim` is the only business table this story writes, in schema `rwb_guarantee` and through this service's own login (DP-01). The `decision_record` row is a library object applied by the per-service Flyway sequence and written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the caller's transaction; `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision` is P7's and is neither written nor read. The TCG share has no field identifier and no column in TSD S3 T3.1, which stops at DF-TRT-022, so its name, type and unit are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2728; ASM-4535). No table of another service is read: `recovery_case`, `case_party`, `assignment` and `timer` of the legacy data table are rwb-case's, and `v_ace_customer` is read by rwb-source-data (DP-05).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-guarantee (S3); base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` (DP-13). The service publishes two operations; this story supplies the behaviour of the second and the contract publishes both.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency | This story |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PATCH | `/guarantee-claims/{claimId}` | `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` in, `GuaranteeClaim` out | Treatment and offer, right U | Not applicable (TSD S3 T-A.2) | Supplied here |
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims` | `GuaranteeClaimRequest` in, `GuaranteeClaim` out | Treatment and offer, right C | `Idempotency-Key` header (TSD S3 T-A.2) | Published by the contract; behaviour of the claim-preparation slice |

The errors are 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409 on a state conflict, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for a missing, invalid or out-of-range field, and 503 when the package or the library does not answer; the set is the one TSD S3 T-A.2 lists. The service publishes no read operation, so SCR-17 is composed by the gateway-bff route from the case read of rwb-case and the claim the stage holds (GAP-2730; ASM-4533). The field list of `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` is the working read of the contract story and is not restated here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. Nothing is called over REST: the case, its status, the claim reference and the approved range arrive on the signal the parent `CaseWorkflow` forwards, and the decision record is called in process inside the caller's transaction (DP-03). This is why the Work Package records no C dependency for this story.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic of the service is `rwb.guarantee.events.v1` with event names `rwb.guarantee.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and the ownership rows of S3 give the service no event: the outcome is reported to the parent `CaseWorkflow` as a stage outcome, so a replay of the stage produces no second message and no outbox row is written.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. No subscription is declared. The payment that triggers a subrogation and the refusal that triggers `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` reach the stage as signals the parent forwards, and the event that would carry a guarantee payment is named by no source, so the form of the subscription is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2728; ASM-4531). If the service must subscribe, the event name and the subscription belong to the payment story and to the event catalogue.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per guarantee stage, the child of `CaseWorkflow` | `rwb-guarantee` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the claim reference, the GUARANTEE state, the guaranteed amount and the approved range as context; signals: the case status forwarded by the parent, the rule package in force |
| `evaluateNegotiation` | Activity | `rwb-guarantee` | The negotiation outcome, the range and the claim state in; the selected rule, the range answer and the GUARANTEE event out |
| `applyOutcome` | Activity | `rwb-guarantee` | The `guarantee_claim` columns of the outcome — `status`, `state`, `paid_amount` and the TCG share |
| `recordAndApply` | Activity | `rwb-guarantee` | The `DecisionRecord` and the `guarantee_claim` row written in one transaction through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, and the stage outcome for the parent |

The workflow is the one the context pack owns for S3 and the one Architecture v5 slide 13 names as the guarantee child, and the parent-and-child model with the four steps of receive, ask, record and apply, wait is the one of the Temporal and Drools Design slides 12 and 13. The activity names are a target design choice of this story and are fixed by no source document. A workflow class never calls the record library directly: the call is made inside `recordAndApply`, so a replay reuses the recorded decision.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The ownership rows give S3 no job: the stage runs from the signal the parent forwards and from the officer's call, and the claim deadline and the notice expiry are durable timers inside the workflow and not Temporal Schedules. The deadline timer of R-GUA-01 and the notice timer of R-GUA-06 are set by the claim-preparation and notice slices on the same workflow.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guarantee_claim` | `rwb_guarantee` | S3 rwb-guarantee | Written by this story for DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022, the `state` value of TSD S3 T4, the TCG share and the standard columns of T3.0; created by the per-service Flyway sequence and never re-created here |
| `decision_record` | `rwb_guarantee` | PLT, library object | Not written directly: the row is written by RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the caller's transaction (DP-03) |

`guarantee_claim` is the single table the ownership rows give S3, and it holds the eight fields of TSD S3 T3.1 plus the standard columns of T3.0. No table of another service is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01); `recovery_case` and `case_party` are rwb-case's and are named here only. No range, expiry or notice column is added: those facts belong to the request context and to the decision record.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| RWB-S3-E4018-CON claim fake | The two operations, the elements and the error set | A `PATCH` answering a `SUBROGATION_POSITION` outcome and a `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` refusal; a repeated `Idempotency-Key` on the `POST`; 422 for a missing or out-of-range field; 403 for a role without right U |
| RWB-PLT-E1027-CON writer fake | The decision record | An accepted record with chain sequence and entry hash; a refusal with MSG-P7-009 and the field; a failed write raising MSG-P7-003; a call with no transaction refused before any write |
| RWB-PLT-N001-CON route fake | The gateway-bff composite route of SCR-17 | A composite answer that joins the case read of rwb-case with the claim the stage holds; a refused route for a role without the right |
| rwb-case status mock | The signal the parent forwards, used by AC2 and AC3 | A case at `CLAIM_PAID` and a case at `CLAIM_PART_PAID`; a GUARANTEE state the stage does not accept. Test-only; adds no contract dependency |
| Range fixture | The context fact of the approved range | One claim with its range on the signal and one outcome outside it. The bounds are synthetic because no source states them (GAP-2728; ASM-4529) |

The claim, writer and route fakes are the published contracts of those stories; the case-status mock and the range fixture stand in for the signal of the parent, which has no published contract of its own here.

|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 operations on `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` | None | One hop from the BFF, 2 s timeout; the two shapes are declared by RWB-S3-E4018-CON |
| Kafka | None | None | The topic `rwb.guarantee.events.v1` is named and unused; the service owns no event (DP-14) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.guarantee`, modules `negotiation` and `web`, with the published types in `...guarantee.api`. Service base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, schema `rwb_guarantee`, topic `rwb.guarantee.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-guarantee` in namespace `rwb-recovery`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the transaction rule of the negotiation: the record and the claim row commit together, and a failed record leaves nothing behind. DP-05 is applied as a removal: no `AceSourceQuery` and no `v_ace_*` read remains in this build, because the negotiation needs the claim, the party reference and the range (ASM-4532). DP-13 moves the base of the two operations and nothing else. DP-19 is how SCR-17 reaches the service, one hop through the gateway, so no screen reads a table and no screen calls another service.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` guarantee stage | Workflow | One execution per case per guarantee stage; the claim facts, the case signal, the package in force and the stage outcome |
| `evaluateNegotiation` | Activity | Field validation, the range check and the two subrogation rules of the GUA package with the version in force |
| `applyOutcome` | Activity | The `guarantee_claim` columns of the outcome, including the TCG share |
| `recordAndApply` | Activity | The `DecisionRecord` and the claim row in one transaction through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| `GuaranteeClaimController` | Controller | The `PATCH` operation, the right U check through the guard and the error mapping |
| `GuaranteeClaimRepository` | Repository | The claim columns and the TCG share in `rwb_guarantee`, with the optimistic lock of `version` |
| `StageOutcomeReporter` | Signal reporter | The outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` uses to move the case and to keep the share; it reports, it never writes a case row |

**Database.** `guarantee_claim` holds DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022, the `state` value of TSD S3 T4, the standard columns of T3.0 with the optimistic lock on `version`, and the TCG-share column this story adds, whose name, type and unit are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2728; ASM-4535). The range and the notice expiry are not columns. `decision_record` is the library object applied by the per-service Flyway sequence, and this story writes it only through the library.

**Configuration and reference data.** Capability area "Treatment and offer" and rights C and U are access rows of rwb-access, read through its guard. The approved range, the notice expiry and the guarantee scheme values are values in force with their version, read at run time and never written in code (BR-S3-006). The GUA package and its version come from `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` and are never configured here.

**Build steps**

1. The guarantee stage of `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` and its input record, registered on `rwb-guarantee` as the child of `CaseWorkflow`, with the case signal and the claim facts (AC2, AC3).
2. `evaluateNegotiation` with the field validation, the range check and the two subrogation rules, against the claim fake (AC1, AC2, AC3).
3. `applyOutcome` with the claim columns and the TCG share, plus the refusal branch of R-GUA-29.
4. `recordAndApply` with the `DecisionRecord`, the `MANDATORY` transaction and the claim row, plus the failed-write path (AC4).
5. The `PATCH` operation with the guard check and the error mapping of section 12.1 (AC1).
6. `StageOutcomeReporter` and the parent signal, with the subrogation outcome and the share.
7. Tests for AC1 to AC4 against the fakes and the range fixture, plus the two component cases of section 16.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.guarantee.guarantor-negotiation`.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the stage runs from a synthetic case signal in SIT, an in-range outcome writes the claim with its share and its GUARANTEE state, an out-of-range outcome writes nothing, a failed record write rolls the claim row back, the parent receives the `SUBROGATION_POSITION` or `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` outcome, and SCR-17 answers through the gateway-bff composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of the negotiation is absent or invalid, the range among them | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role does not hold right U on the capability area | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P7-009 | The decision record is refused for a field | The decision record was refused: {field} is missing or not valid. |

The first three texts are the legacy texts of RWB-E4-018 carried unchanged, and MSG-P7-009 is the library's answer, raised by RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and shown by this story. No message holds a constant: MSG-GEN-001 carries the field name, MSG-P4-002 the action and MSG-P7-009 the refused field. The entry format of each message in a published catalogue is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2730; ASM-4533). Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-17 Guarantee claim is the legacy screen of this story and keeps its state list unchanged: Not due; due; submitted; paid; refused. It is where the officer reads the claim, the claim deadline, the scheme checklist and the claim result, and where the negotiation outcome is recorded; it reaches the service through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, which joins the case read of rwb-case with the claim the stage holds (DP-19; ASM-4533). The screen labels are the screen's own and are not the stored `status` of LOV-CLAIM-STATUS or the GUARANTEE `state` of TSD S3 T4, whose mapping is a working read (GAP-2729; ASM-4530). The screen field list and the composite route specification belong to the platform edge story and the screen owners; this story fixes the service side of the answer only.

| TC-E4-018-02 | AC2 | End to end | Rule R-GUA-23 |

The six legacy test case IDs, their Covers and their Data are kept in order and character for character; the legacy level "System" maps to "End to end" and "Access" and "Principle 5" map to "Component", as in the other stories of this run. ##### 17. Guardrails

- No value that a business person may change is written in code: the approved range, the notice expiry and the scheme values are values in force in reference data, read with their version (BR-S3-006).
- No personal data in logs, events, workflow inputs, prompts or the fixture: the rows carry case IDs, claim IDs, amounts, dates, codes and rule versions only, and the test data is synthetic.
- No read of another service's table: the case status, the party reference and the range arrive as a signal, the claim facts are this service's own, and `decision_log_entry` is P7's and is never touched (DP-01).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views, and this story opens neither: the legacy `v_ace_customer` read is removed (DP-05; ASM-4532).
- No range, expiry or notice column in `rwb_guarantee`; a schema change that adds one fails the guardrail test (DP-01; ASM-4529).
- No event of this story and no outbox row: the outcome is reported to the parent, so a replay of the stage produces no second message.
- The decision record and the claim row commit in one transaction through the `MANDATORY` rule of the library; an action that commits without its record is a build failure, not a defect (DP-03).
- An applied migration is never edited: the TCG-share column and any correction are a new version on the service sequence.
- No screen calls a service directly and no screen reads a table: SCR-17 goes through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).
