##### 1. Story

As a **contract owner of rwb-guarantee**, I want **the published contract of the guarantee close — the `GuaranteeClose` element recorded against the claim, the read rule of the balance and payment views with the batch date and the no-copy rule, the close rules of the GUARANTEE route set with their conditions and to states, the stage report that closes the case or returns the balance, the claim operation and its base, the decision-record group, the versioning rule and the fakes — instead of the monolith's method reading the `recovery` schema and `rule_row` in one process**, so that **the application story of this feature, the sibling claim stories of this service and the wave 3 integration harness build and test on Day 1 without a P1, P7 or rwb-case deployment and without a production ACE balance, and no reader of a closed guarantee depends on a position that was never defined**.

This is the contract slice of legacy RWB-E4-019. It owns:

- the `GuaranteeClose` element: the claim and case identifiers, the closing time, the closing basis, the claim status and paid amount, the guaranteed share, the balance after the share with its as-at date, and the rule and set versions, with the rule that it is recorded against the claim and against nothing else;
- the read rule of the balance and payment evidence: the views `recovery.v_ace_account`, `recovery.v_ace_payment` and `recovery.v_ace_batch_status`, the columns consumed, the batch date, the no-copy ban and the availability answers (DP-05);
- the close rules: the four rows of the GUARANTEE route set that end the claim — R-GUA-19, R-GUA-25, R-GUA-26 and R-GUA-27 — their from states, events, conditions and to states, and the two condition tests of the balance after the guaranteed share (GAP-2731; ASM-4537);
- the stage report: the outcome, the reason code and the 5 working day owner task of R-GUA-27 reported to the parent `CaseWorkflow`, the case statuses the parent applies, and the statement that the case is closed by rwb-case and never here (GAP-2732; ASM-4538);
- the claim operation and its base: `PATCH /api/recovery/guarantee/v1/guarantee-claims/{claimId}` (API-S3-002) on base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, of which this element is a component, with the right, the errors and the compatibility rule (DP-13);
- the decision-record group of the same transaction, named as the local record of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, with its refusal and failure messages;
- the guard answers — MSG-P1-001 for a stale data product, MSG-GEN-001 for a missing value, MSG-GEN-006 for a view that does not answer and MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right — the versioning and pinning rule, the fakes and the drift test.

It does not own: the close branch of `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow`, the close activity, the three reads, the claim result, the record call and the tests against them, which are RWB-S3-E4019-APP; the four legacy acceptance criteria of RWB-E4-019, which are carried verbatim by RWB-S3-E4019-APP; the claim representation, its create and result operations and its states, which are RWB-S3-E4015-CON and the claim stories of this service; the subrogation position entered by R-GUA-23 and R-GUA-24, which are RWB-S3-E4016-CON; the case status, the case closure, the case task and the case timer, which are rwb-case's; the ACE views and their grants, which are ACE's; the GUARANTEE rule rows, their approval and the central ledger, which are P7 rwb-decision's; the posting and booking of the payment, which are P8 rwb-payment's and the core bank's; and SCR-17 and its composite route, which are the platform edge story's under DP-19.

##### 2. Business rationale

In the monolith the close had no contract at all. `GuaranteesAndGuarantorsService` read the balance and the payments from the `recovery` schema, read the GUARANTEE rows from `rule_row`, decided in code and wrote the claim status into `guarantee_claim` and the decision into `decision_log_entry` (TSD S3 T1 and T2). Nothing about that arrangement could be reused or tested alone: the balance was a live join, the policy was a row any module could read, and a closed guarantee had no shape — a reader of it had one option, which was to read the module's tables.

D-RCV-60 replaces three inputs and one output, and the contract is where each of them is written down. The balance and the payment stay in ACE and are read at the batch date from the service's own SELECT-only views (DP-05; D-RCV-35, ADR-010). The close becomes one of governed rows of the GUARANTEE route set, read with the version that decided (R-GUA-19, R-GUA-26, R-GUA-27). The decision becomes a local record in the same transaction (DP-03; ADR-022). And the output becomes an element with a field list, a required flag on each field, a version label and a set of fakes, recorded against the claim the officer already sees.

Two of the things this contract must fix are absences rather than decisions. The guaranteed share and the balance after it have no field in TSD S3 T3.1, no field identifier in the Logical Data Model and no governed row, so the contract states how they are composed — from the balance read at the batch date and the share the answered row names — and refuses to invent a column (GAP-2731; ASM-4537). And the routing logic says "close the guarantee and close the case" while `LOV-CLAIM-STATUS` offers `PREPARING`, `FILED`, `DEFECT`, `PAID` and `REJECTED` and no closed value; the contract therefore fixes the close as the element plus the case status `GUARANTEE_CLOSED` that rwb-case applies, and leaves the claim inside its published list (GAP-2732; ASM-4538).

The legacy key divides cleanly and the division is fixed. This WP delivers the **contract**. The **application** — the branch, the activity, the reads, the claim result and the guard paths — is **RWB-S3-E4019-APP**, and the **four legacy acceptance criteria stay with it**: AC1 to AC4 are listed in its section 7 with their origin tag and are not repeated here. The **cross-service proof** is **RWB-ITG-W3**. Every criterion in section 7 of this document is new and tests only the contract deliverable in this title.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The rules whose states, events, conditions and to states the element and the report carry are fixed by the Routing Logic v4: R-GUA-19 (`CLAIM_REJECTED`, `RESUBMISSION_NOT_POSSIBLE`, "the reason is not curable, or claim_deadline has passed", to `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE`), R-GUA-25 (`SUBROGATION_POSITION`, `RESIDUAL_REMAINS`, "the balance after the guaranteed share is greater than zero", to `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE`), R-GUA-26 (`SUBROGATION_POSITION`, `BALANCE_SATISFIED`, "the balance after the guaranteed share is zero", to `GUARANTEE_CLOSED`) and R-GUA-27 (`DEADLINE_MISSED`, `LOSS_RECORDED`, "the loss amount and the reason are recorded", to `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE`). The names are copied into the element and the report, character for character.
- The fields the claim result lands on exist in TSD S3 T3.1: `status` (DF-TRT-022, varchar(12), LOV-CLAIM-STATUS) and `paid_amount` (DF-TRT-021, numeric(18,2)).
- The evidence is fixed in kind: FSD S3 A2.7.3.1 VR-S3-007-1 reads `v_ace_batch_status` for the data-product date, and the legacy data table names `v_ace_account` with DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042 and `v_ace_payment` with DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054. The columns consumed and the grant path are the working read of ASM-4541, and the conflict with Architecture v5 slide 8 is GAP-2735.
- The decision record is the platform library's: `DecisionRecordWriter.record(DecisionRecord)` with `@Transactional(propagation = MANDATORY)`, refusing with MSG-P7-009 and failing with MSG-P7-003 (DP-03; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON).
- The element rides the claim representation on base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` (DP-13) and is served to SCR-17 through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19; RWB-PLT-N001-CON), so the contract fixes the element and the base, not a second path.
- No source publishes the element's own field list, the share or the position record, or the trigger of the feature (GAP-2731 to GAP-2734; ASM-4537 to ASM-4540). The document is published as that working read, at major version 1 and status Draft (realignment v1).
- No build dependency and no approval stop: a CON story is Day 1 by rule (§R5.7) and nothing in this story needs a human sign-off to start (ASM-4542).

##### 4. Flow

1. The contract author fixes the `GuaranteeClose` element: its eleven fields, which are required, and the rule that it is recorded against the claim.
2. The author fixes the read rule of the evidence: the three views, the columns consumed, the batch date and the ban on copying.
3. The author fixes the four close rows with their from states, events, conditions, to states and owner roles, and the two condition tests of the balance after the guaranteed share.
4. The author fixes the stage report: the outcome, the reason code and the 5 working day owner task, with the boundary stated — no case row, no case task and no case timer is written here.
5. The author fixes the claim operation and the base it sits on, with the right, the errors and the compatibility rule, and states that the element is a component of the claim representation.
6. The author writes the guard answers with their messages and the decision-record group with the two library messages.
7. The fake set and the drift fixture are generated from the document, and the contract test runs them against it on every change.
8. The document and the fakes are published at v1; RWB-S3-E4019-APP and RWB-ITG-W3 pin the version.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A published element drops a required field, or adds an optional one a consumer depends on | The schema check fails the build; required and optional fields are as published | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The read rule is published without the batch date, the column list or the no-copy ban, or allows a third view | The read lint and the no-copy check fail the build | None | AC2 |
| X3 | A close row is published with a fixed share, a renamed state or a missing to state | The rule lint fails the build; the share, the states and the conditions are named, never fixed | None | AC3 |
| X4 | The stage report is published as a case write, or without the reason or the owner task | The boundary check fails the build; the report carries the reason and the task and writes no case row | None | AC4 |
| X5 | The claim operation is published on the monolith base, or the element gets a path of its own | The base check fails the build; one base, `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` (DP-13) | None | AC5 |
| X6 | A breaking change is made to the element, the read rule or a guard answer | The change raises major version 2; v1 is never edited in place and stays readable | None | AC6 |
| X7 | A consuming story ships without the drift test, or a fake stops answering the document | The drift test fails the build of the consuming story | None | AC6 |
| X8 | A value a consumer needs is named by no source — the share, the balance after it, the closed claim status or the trigger | The value is published as the working read of the assumption and the gap stays open | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2731; ASM-4537) | Section 3 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Publishes a document and fakes; builds against nothing, reads no business data and starts on Day 1 |
| Negotiable | Field order, record widths and the fixture set are open until v1 is frozen; the element, the three views, the four rows, the report and the guards are fixed |
| Valuable | Unblocks the application story and the wave 3 harness on Day 1, and gives the claim stories of this service one definition of a closed guarantee |
| Estimable | One element, one read rule, one rule set, one report, one operation map, one versioning rule and five fakes |
| Small | One sprint for the document, the fakes and the drift test |
| Testable | Each criterion below is one schema, rule-lint, base check or fake assertion in section 16 |

These criteria are new and test only the contract deliverable. No legacy acceptance criterion is repeated here: **AC1 to AC4 of RWB-E4-019 are carried by RWB-S3-E4019-APP**. Every identifier used above comes from the legacy story, the Routing Logic v4, TSD S3 or the FSD, character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The element recorded against the claim carries the claim and case identifiers, the closing time and basis, the claim status and paid amount, the guaranteed share, the balance after the share with its as-at date and the rule and set versions, and nothing else | RWB-E4-019 AC1 to AC3; DF-TRT-015; DF-TRT-022; ASM-4537 |
| BR2 | The basis and the to states are the routing logic's: `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` from R-GUA-19 and R-GUA-27, `GUARANTEE_CLOSED` from R-GUA-26; no name is renamed by the element | R-GUA-19; R-GUA-26; R-GUA-27 |
| BR3 | The balance after the guaranteed share is composed per calculation from the balance read at the batch date and the share the answered row names; no share, balance or position column is declared | GAP-2731; ASM-4537 |
| BR4 | The claim status stays inside `LOV-CLAIM-STATUS` — `PREPARING`, `FILED`, `DEFECT`, `PAID`, `REJECTED`; the close of the guarantee is the element and the close of the case is the case status `GUARANTEE_CLOSED` applied by rwb-case | LOV-CLAIM-STATUS of TSD S3 T3.2; GAP-2732; ASM-4538 |
| BR5 | The balance and the payments are read at the ACE batch date from `recovery.v_ace_account`, `recovery.v_ace_payment` and `recovery.v_ace_batch_status` only, read only, and are never copied into `rwb_guarantee` | DP-05; VR-S3-007-1; D-RCV-35; ADR-010 |
| BR6 | A data product older than today's ACE batch is answered with MSG-P1-001, a missing value with MSG-GEN-001, a view that does not answer with MSG-GEN-006 and a role without the right with MSG-P4-002; none of them is an exception a consumer has to guess | VR-S3-007-1; FSD A2.7.3.1; legacy permission checks |
| BR7 | The claim result and the element are written with the local decision record in one transaction, through `DecisionRecordWriter` with `MANDATORY` propagation | DP-03; ADR-022; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| BR8 | The case status, the case closure, the case task and the case timer stay rwb-case's: the report carries the outcome, the reason and the task due date, and the parent applies the rule | DP-01; R-GUA-19; R-GUA-26; ASM-4538 |
| BR9 | One base, `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, and one claim representation: the element is a component of the claim operation and invents no second path | DP-13; TSD S3 T-A.1 |
| BR10 | A published version is never edited: a compatible change stays in major version 1 and a breaking change raises major version 2 | Template and Rules §R7.2; §R5.4 class C |

##### 9. State transitions

None of the case statuses are this contract's, and the claim's states are published by the claim contract. The table fixes the outcomes the contract names so that a consumer cannot invent a fifth.

| Object | State | Meaning in the contract |
|---|---|---|
| Close step | Answered, residual | R-GUA-19 or R-GUA-27 answered; the full balance goes back to the route decision and the element records the basis |
| Close step | Answered, closed | R-GUA-26 answered; the balance after the guarantee is zero and the case closes at `GUARANTEE_CLOSED` |
| Close step | No close | The balance after the guaranteed share is above zero at `SUBROGATION_POSITION`; R-GUA-25 answers and the sibling story takes the residual |
| Close step | Blocked, stale product | A data product is older than today's ACE batch; MSG-P1-001, nothing written |
| Close step | Blocked, missing value | A required value is missing; MSG-GEN-001 with the field, nothing written |
| Close step | Blocked, no answer | A view did not answer; MSG-GEN-006, nothing written |
| Close step | Refused or rolled back | The record was refused with MSG-P7-009 or could not be written with MSG-P7-003; no claim result, no element |
| Element | Recorded or absent | Written against the claim in the same transaction, or not written at all; there is no partial element |
| Contract version | v1 / v2 | v1 is the published version every consumer pins; v2 is raised by a breaking change and v1 stays readable |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The contract author (any team, per U3) | Writes and versions the document and the fakes |
| The service owner of rwb-guarantee | Approves a breaking change and freezes a version |
| The owner of P7 rwb-decision | Confirms the GUARANTEE rows, their conditions and their to states at the wave 3 contract freeze (ASM-4539) |
| The owner of P3 rwb-case | Confirms the case statuses the report triggers, the 5 working day task of R-GUA-27 and the case closure (ASM-4538) |
| The owner of the claim contract of this service | Confirms the claim representation and the result operation the element rides (BR9) |
| ACE and its DBA | Confirm the three views, the columns consumed and the SELECT-only grant to this service's login (ASM-4541) |
| The platform data and workflow owners | Confirm the decision-record library, the task queue and the retry policy |
| RW-GUARANT, guarantee officer | Consumes the element through SCR-17 and holds rights C, R and U on the capability area |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Works the returned case and its task; holds rights C, R and U; the step itself runs unattended under the service identity |
| The consumer stories of this service | Consume the element, pin the version and raise a change request rather than a private variant |
| RW-AUDIT, RW-COE | Read the recorded element and the decision records; they do not consume this document directly |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A contract is a technical artefact, not a credit decision |

No personal name, no email address and no credential appears in the document, an example or a fake; where an actor must be named, a role code or a service identity is used.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Business data published | None. The document publishes field names, the state and event names, the basis codes and the messages; no customer, account or case value appears |
| Element published | The eleven fields of section 12.1, with the required and optional flags and the claim columns they map to |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

One mapping of the element onto the claim representation; the contract declares no path of its own beyond the service base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` (DP-13).

| Operation | Right | Declared with | This contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PATCH /api/recovery/guarantee/v1/guarantee-claims/{claimId}` (API-S3-002) | Treatment and offer U | The claim contract of this service, which owns the claim representation | Fixes the `GuaranteeClose` component the operation carries: its fields, their required flags and the recording rule |
| `POST /api/recovery/guarantee/v1/cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims` (API-S3-001) | Treatment and offer C | The claim contract that opens the claim | Named only: it creates the claim this element is recorded against |

Both are the legacy operations of TSD S3 T-A.1 re-based per DP-13, with the errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 and the idempotency rule TSD S3 T-A.2 gives (Idempotency-Key on the create, not applicable on the result). SCR-17 reaches the element through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

**Element: `GuaranteeClose`**

| Field | Type | Required | Maps to | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claimId` | uuid | Yes | DF-TRT-015 `id` | The claim the element is recorded against |
| `caseId` | uuid | Yes | DF-TRT-016 `case_id` | The case the claim belongs to |
| `closedAt` | timestamptz | Yes | No claim column | The business time the guarantee was closed |
| `closeBasis` | string | Yes | No claim column | The to state of the answered row: `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` or `GUARANTEE_CLOSED` |
| `claimStatus` | string | Yes | DF-TRT-022 `status` | A value of LOV-CLAIM-STATUS; the close adds none |
| `claimPaidAmount` | numeric(18,2) | No | DF-TRT-021 `paid_amount` | The amount paid on the claim where the payment is recorded |
| `guaranteedShare` | numeric(18,2) | No | No claim column | The share the answered row names, read with its version (GAP-2731) |
| `balanceAfterShare` | numeric(18,2) | Yes | No claim column | The balance read at the batch date less the guaranteed share; the zero test of R-GUA-26 |
| `balancesAsAt` | date | Yes | No claim column | The ACE batch date the balance and the payments were read at |
| `ruleId` | string | No | No claim column | The row that answered: R-GUA-19, R-GUA-25, R-GUA-26 or R-GUA-27 |
| `ruleVersion` | string | No | The version group of the decision record | The version of the package in force |

The element is recorded against the `guarantee_claim` row and against no other record; it has no collection, no free-text field and no payment detail, because the evidence is a balance, a share and a date, not the payments themselves. The element's own BR Field IDs have no row in the Logical Data Model, so the field names are the working read of ASM-4537 and ASM-4539 (GAP-2731; GAP-2733); the basis codes, the state names and the claim list keep the names the routing logic and TSD S3 T3.2 already use (BR4).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The contract declares no REST read: the case status, the claim id and the payment reference arrive on the signal the parent `CaseWorkflow` forwards, the rule rows arrive with the package in force, and the evidence is the SQL read of 12.5. No source publishes an operation for this step, and the contract names the element rather than an invented path (GAP-2734; ASM-4540).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This contract owns no topic and publishes no event; the service's topic `rwb.guarantee.events.v1` carries no catalogued event, because the ownership rows give S3 none (TSD S3 T5.3; DP-14). The "event" of the step is the stage report to the parent `CaseWorkflow`, a Temporal signal inside the case. A Kafka event for a closed guarantee would need a name, a payload, an outbox row and the event platform of DP-09, which the plan does not give this legacy key; the name and its consumers are the open question recorded in ASM-4538.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None by this contract. The consumer's rule package arrives on the template's rule loader and the payment that clears the claim arrives on the case signal; the connection matrix of Architecture v5 slide 13 shows S3 listening to P6 and P8 and calling P7 by Temporal activity, and this contract adds no subscription and fixes none. What it does require is that the element and the record name the version that was in force.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None of its own: the contract defines no workflow, no activity and no task queue — `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` on `rwb-guarantee` and its activities are RWB-S3-E4019-APP. What it fixes is the reads the consumer's activity makes, the composition it applies and the report it sends, so that both sides of each read are written down in one place.

| Read element | Value |
|---|---|
| ACE read | SQL, SELECT-only, on `recovery.v_ace_account`, `recovery.v_ace_payment` and `recovery.v_ace_batch_status`, in the ACE database, at the ACE batch date |
| ACE columns | `account_key`, `account_code`, `account_status`, `contract_no`, `product_category_efs`, `total_balance` and the rest of DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042; `payment_code`, `account_key`, `payment_date`, `payment_amount`, `payment_channel`, `capital_amount` and the rest of DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054; the product date of the batch status |
| ACE rule | No copy is kept; no fourth ACE object is read; no write of any kind; no posting table of rwb-payment is named |
| Balance rule | The balance after the guaranteed share is composed per calculation from the balance read and the share the answered row names, tested against zero |
| Answer rule | R-GUA-19 and R-GUA-27 return the full balance; R-GUA-26 closes the guarantee and the case; R-GUA-25 keeps the residual at the same state |
| Claim rule | The claim status stays inside LOV-CLAIM-STATUS and the paid amount is written where the payment is recorded |
| Report | The outcome, the reason code, the balance tested and the 5 working day owner task of R-GUA-27, to the parent `CaseWorkflow` |
| On a stale product | MSG-P1-001 naming the product and its date; nothing decided |
| On a missing value | MSG-GEN-001 with the field; nothing decided |
| On no answer | MSG-GEN-006; nothing decided |

The column list, the grant path, the composition of the balance and the closed status are the working read of ASM-4537, ASM-4538 and ASM-4541, because no source document states them: the FSD names `v_ace_batch_status` in a validation rule, the legacy data table names the two other views with their field ranges, the routing logic states the conditions in words, and the Work Package records no contract dependency on P1 (GAP-2731, GAP-2732, GAP-2735). The owners confirm all of them at the wave 3 contract freeze.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The contract declares no Schedule: the step is entered on the case signal and reports the 5 working day task of R-GUA-27, and neither is a scheduled scan of this service. The ownership rows give S3 no job, and the legacy Quartz scheduler is retired.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The claim result and the element are written by the consumer against `guarantee_claim` in `rwb_guarantee`, a table of this service created on its own Flyway sequence with DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022, and `decision_record` is the platform library object of DP-03 applied in the same schema. The contract creates no table, declares no column and adds no foreign key: there is deliberately no share, balance or position column, and `decision_log_entry` is P7's ledger in `rwb_decision`, named only and never written or read here.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| Element fake | The `GuaranteeClose` shape | A complete element; one element per missing required field; an element with and without `ruleId`, `ruleVersion`, `guaranteedShare` and `claimPaidAmount` |
| ACE balance and payment fixture | The three views | A cleared balance; a balance above zero after the share; a payment inside the batch; a product dated yesterday; an unreachable view |
| Case-signal fake | The forwarded case signal | `CLAIM_REJECTED` with the deadline passed; `SUBROGATION_POSITION` with a zero balance; `DEADLINE_MISSED` with a recorded loss |
| Output fake | The guard answers | MSG-P1-001 with the product and its date, MSG-GEN-001 with the field, MSG-GEN-006 for no answer, MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right |
| Decision-record fake | The record group of AC3 | An accepted record with the rule and set versions; a refusal with MSG-P7-009 and the field; a failure with MSG-P7-003 |
| Drift fixture | The contract test | One accepted and one refused body per section of the document |

The fakes answer from the same example set as the document, so a change to the contract shows up as a contract-test failure in a consuming story rather than as a surprise at run time. The balance fixture and the case-signal fake are what make Day 1 possible for RWB-S3-E4019-APP and RWB-ITG-W3.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Contract artefact of rwb-guarantee: the element and the report types in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.guarantee.api`, the fakes as a test resource, and the versioning rule in the contract document. The implementation that performs the reads, composes the balance and writes the claim result is RWB-S3-E4019-APP. The artefact coordinates and the publication channel are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2731; ASM-4537).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is taken as the service's own SELECT-only views, because the Work Package records no contract dependency on P1 and the grant is the working read of ASM-4541 (GAP-2735). DP-13 fixes the one base the element rides, DP-03 is the record of the close, and DP-19 the path the closed claim is read on.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `GuaranteeClose` | Published type | The eleven fields, the required and optional flags and the recording rule (BR1, BR2) |
| `BalanceReadRule` | Document | The three views, the columns, the batch date, the composition of the balance and the no-copy ban (BR3, BR5, AC2) |
| `GuaranteeCloseRules` | Document | The four rows, their conditions, their to states and the claim status rule (BR2, BR4, AC3) |
| `CloseReport` | Published type | The outcome, the reason code, the balance tested, the owner task and the case boundary (BR8, AC4) |
| `ClaimOperationMap` | Document | The two operations, their rights, their errors and the one base (BR9, AC5) |
| `GuardAnswers` | Document | MSG-P1-001, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P4-002 and the two record messages (BR6) |
| `VersioningSpecification` | Document | Major version 1, the compatible versus breaking rule and the pinning rule (AC6) |
| Fake set and drift fixture | Test asset | The element, view, case-signal, output and record fakes and the drift test (AC6) |

**Database.** No table and no column in this contract. The claim result lands in `guarantee_claim.status` (DF-TRT-022) and `guarantee_claim.paid_amount` (DF-TRT-021), both TSD S3 T3.1 fields; the share, the balance and the position have no column and no field ID, which is why they exist only in the element (GAP-2731; GAP-2733).

**Configuration and reference data.** The share basis, the conditions and the four rule rows are data of rwb-decision with a version and are named here, never fixed. The 2 s budget and the retry policy are the activity's and the workflow kit's. The capability area, the rights C and U and the role set are access data of P4 and are named, not declared by this document.

**Build steps**

1. Write the element with its eleven fields, the required and optional flags and the claim columns (AC1).
2. Write the read rule with the three views, the columns, the batch date, the composition of the balance and the no-copy ban (AC2).
3. Write the four close rows with their from states, events, conditions and to states, the claim status rule and the guard answers with their messages (AC3).
4. Write the stage report and the case boundary, and lint them against rwb-case and the routing logic (AC4).
5. Write the operation map with the two operations, their rights, their errors and the one base, and lint it against DP-13 (AC5).
6. Write the versioning and pinning section with the compatible and breaking examples, generate the fake set and the drift fixture (AC6).
7. Publish v1 and record the pinned versions of RWB-S3-E4019-APP and RWB-ITG-W3.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.guarantee.guarantee-close-contract`.

**Done when.** The document and the schema validate, the read lint, the no-copy check, the base check and the case-boundary check are green, the fakes answer every criterion including the stale product, the missing value and the unreachable view, the drift test fails on an edited field and passes on the published version, and v1 is published with the pinned versions recorded.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Published as |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | A data product is older than today's ACE batch | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. | The stale-product answer of the read rule; the product named is the one the step read |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required value is missing, for example the claim deadline | Enter {field}. | The missing-value answer of the rule section |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A view does not answer | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. | The no-answer answer of the read rule |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right in the capability area tries the action | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | The access answer, named from the legacy permission checks |
| MSG-P7-009 | A record is refused for a missing or invalid field | The decision record was refused: {field} is missing or not valid. | The library's refusal, named by the record group |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record cannot be written and the action is not taken | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | The library's failure, named by the record group |

The six texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story, FSD S3 A2.7.3.1 and RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, and this contract adds no message ID. Thai text follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story, and the contract declares none. The element and the claim result are shown on SCR-17 Guarantee claim — the guarantee, the claim deadline, the checklist and the claim result — which is reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) and whose field list belongs to the platform edge story and the screen owner. The contract fixes what that screen may show of the close: the closing basis, the claim status, the balance tested with its batch date and the rule version, and no payment detail beyond the paid amount. The screen's existing states `Not due`, `due`, `submitted`, `paid` and `refused` are unchanged by the element; the case's `GUARANTEE_CLOSED` is the state the report produces on the case, not a new state of the screen.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the share, the balance and the conditions are named, never fixed as numbers, and the claim result lands on TSD S3 T3.1 fields (BR3, BR4).
- No personal data in the element, a read, an answer, a fake or a log: the element carries identifiers, a date, a basis code, a status, amounts of the claim and the balance, and versions, never a name, an account number or a payment reference.
- No copy of ACE data: no balance, share or position column is declared, and the consumer keeps no copy (BR5).
- One base and one representation: the element rides the claim operation on `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` and invents no second path (BR9; DP-13).
- No second source for the share and no fourth ACE object: the answered row and three views.
- The outcome of a stale input, a missing value, a dead view or a missing right is a written answer, never an exception a consumer has to guess (BR6).
- A published version is never edited in place: a breaking change raises major version 2 and a consumer pins rather than forks (BR10).
- The case status is never the contract's and never the consumer's: the element is recorded, the report is sent and rwb-case closes the case (BR8).

##### 1. Story

As a **guarantee officer (RW-GUARANT)**, I want **the Workbench to close the guarantee and the case when a guarantee payment clears the balance in full — the balance after the guaranteed share read at the ACE batch date, the claim outcome and the closing position written on the claim with the rule version that decided, and the case closed or returned to the route decision on the stage report** — so that **no guarantee claim misses its deadline and a case whose debt a guarantee has cleared is not left open while the deadline goes on being tracked by hand**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E4-019. It owns:

- the four legacy acceptance criteria this story is given (AC1 to AC4), copied verbatim with their origin tag, and the rules, data rows and messages they carry;
- the close branch of `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-guarantee` in namespace `rwb-recovery`: the step that evaluates the GUARANTEE route set in force (32 rules over 17 states, TSD S3 T4), records the answer and reports the stage outcome to the parent `CaseWorkflow` (context pack slides 5 and 13);
- the close activity: the account balance and the guarantee payments read at the ACE batch date from this service's own SELECT-only views `recovery.v_ace_account`, `recovery.v_ace_payment` and `recovery.v_ace_batch_status`, with no copy kept (DP-05);
- the balance after the guaranteed share: composed per calculation from the read balance and the guaranteed share the answer names, tested against zero, never held as a column and never written as a constant (GAP-2731; ASM-4537);
- the three answers of the route set: R-GUA-19 (close the guarantee and return the full balance to the route decision, to `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE`), R-GUA-26 (close the guarantee and close the case, to `GUARANTEE_CLOSED`) and R-GUA-27 (return the full balance to the route decision and close the guarantee on a recorded loss, to `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE`), with R-GUA-25 left to the sibling story at the same state;
- the claim result: `guarantee_claim.status` within its published list (LOV-CLAIM-STATUS, DF-TRT-022), `paid_amount` (DF-TRT-021) and the `GuaranteeClose` element of RWB-S3-E4019-CON, written against the claim row in `rwb_guarantee` with the local decision record of the step in the same transaction (DP-03; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON);
- the stage report to the parent: the outcome, the reason code of the answered row and the 5 working day owner task of R-GUA-27, ordered here and created by rwb-case, because the case status, the case tasks and the case timers are rwb-case's;
- the refusal and failure paths: no record, nothing changes and MSG-P7-003; a stale data product blocks with MSG-P1-001; a missing value is named with MSG-GEN-001; a role without the right is refused with MSG-P4-002.

It does not own: the published element, the read rule of the two ACE views, the close rule set, the versioning rule and the fakes, which are RWB-S3-E4019-CON; the claim representation, its create and result operations and its states, which are the claim stories of this service (RWB-S3-E4015-APP and RWB-S3-E4015-CON); the preparation of the claim, its submission and its tracking, which are RWB-S3-E4013-APP, RWB-S3-E4014-APP and RWB-S3-E4015-APP; the subrogation position entered by R-GUA-23 and R-GUA-24 and the residual of R-GUA-25, which are RWB-S3-E4016-APP; the guarantor notices, which are RWB-S3-E4017-APP; the negotiation with a guarantor, which is RWB-S3-E4018-APP; the insurance claim, which is RWB-S3-E4020-APP; the case, its status, its tasks, its timers and the parent `CaseWorkflow`, which are rwb-case's; the posting and the booking in ALS core and GL, which are rwb-payment's and the core bank's; the ACE views and their content, which are ACE's; the rule package, its approval and the central ledger, which are P7 rwb-decision's; the screen and its composite route, which are the platform edge story's and the screen owner's under DP-19.

##### 2. Business rationale

In the monolith the close was a method of `GuaranteesAndGuarantorsService`: it read the balance and the payments live from the `recovery` schema, read the GUARANTEE rows from `rule_row`, wrote the claim status into `guarantee_claim` and the decision into `decision_log_entry`, all in one process (TSD S3 T1 and T2). Two things followed. The close could only be exercised with a live ACE balance, and the claim's result, the position and the case status were written by the same code, so no reader could tell which of them was authoritative.

D-RCV-60 changes the source of each input and nothing else. The balance and the payment stay in ACE and are read at the ACE batch date through this service's own SELECT-only views, with the product's date on the answer (DP-05; D-RCV-35, ADR-010). The closing decision is a governed row of the GUARANTEE route set, read with the version that decided, so a change of policy is a rule release and not a build (R-GUA-19, R-GUA-26, R-GUA-27). The decision is recorded locally in the same transaction as the claim result, so a close that cannot be recorded does not happen (DP-03; ADR-022). And the case is closed or returned by rwb-case from the report, because the case is the case service's after the split (DP-01).

The step is a branch of the stage workflow the service already owns: one child workflow per case on the owner's queue, `rwb-guarantee`, with the rules evaluated from the package in force (context pack slides 5 and 13; Architecture v5 slide 18). What it does not change is the officer's work or the deadline: the guarantees that are not claimed in time are still lost claims, and the metric of the feature is unchanged — "claims filed inside the deadline, 100 percent, decision log and Workbench records, monthly" (FSD S3 A2.7.1).

Delivery is EP04 in wave 3 on release 28 February 2027 (tentative). REQ-S3-003 of FSD S3 names this feature — "a guarantee payment that clears the balance closes the case and records the subrogation position" — and is the requirement this story and its contract trace to; TSD S3 T8 maps the same set of IDs to FEAT-GUA-01, so the trace carries both (Section 18).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S3-E4019-CON is published: the `GuaranteeClose` element, its required and optional fields, the read rule of the three ACE views, the close rule set, the stage report, the messages and the fakes. The build starts against the Draft baseline, as every CON story of this run publishes on Day 1 at status Draft (realignment v1).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: `DecisionRecordWriter`, `DecisionRecord`, the `MANDATORY` propagation, the refusal with MSG-P7-009 and the failure with MSG-P7-003 (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-17 from the case read and this service's claim read (DP-19).
- The `rwb_guarantee` schema and its login exist from the platform database story, the `guarantee_claim` table is on the per-service Flyway sequence with DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 of TSD S3 T3.1, and `decision_record` is created as the platform library object in the same schema (DP-01; DP-15).
- SELECT on `recovery.v_ace_account`, `recovery.v_ace_payment` and `recovery.v_ace_batch_status` is granted to this service's login and on no other ACE object. Architecture v5 slide 8 says the `recovery.v_ace_*` views are read only by rwb-source-data while DP-05 allows the service's own SELECT-only views; the Work Package records no contract dependency on P1, so the grant is the working read of ASM-4541, and the conflict is GAP-2735.
- The claim exists in `rwb_guarantee` with `claim_type`, `claim_deadline`, `claimed_amount` and `status` (DF-TRT-017 to DF-TRT-022), and the case is in `CLAIM_REJECTED`, `SUBROGATION_POSITION` or `DEADLINE_MISSED` on the case signal with the claim id and the payment reference.
- The GUARANTEE route set in force is in this service's rule cache at the version the answer names; its rules, conditions and to states are rule rows, not code (BR-S3-007).
- No approval stop: the FSD S3 v3 and TSD S3 v2 documents carry status "In review" and nothing in this story needs a human sign-off to start on Day 1 (ASM-4542).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-case: the parent `CaseWorkflow` forwards the case signal to the `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` child of the case when the claim result of the case arrives, carrying the case status, the claim id and the payment reference (R-GUA-19, R-GUA-26 and R-GUA-27 from state).
2. `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow`: the close branch opens the step, calls `EvaluateRules` and the GUARANTEE route set in force returns the row that applies, with the rule ID and the package version (R-GUA-19 for `RESUBMISSION_NOT_POSSIBLE`, R-GUA-26 for `BALANCE_SATISFIED`, R-GUA-27 for `LOSS_RECORDED`).
3. `closeGuarantee` activity, step one: reads `recovery.v_ace_batch_status` and compares the data product date with today's business date; a product older than today's ACE batch stops the step with MSG-P1-001 naming the product and its date (VR-S3-007-1).
4. Step two: reads the balance of the accounts of the case from `recovery.v_ace_account` — `account_key`, `account_code`, `account_status`, `contract_no`, `product_category_efs`, `total_balance` and the rest of DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042 — and the guarantee payments from `recovery.v_ace_payment` — `payment_code`, `account_key`, `payment_date`, `payment_amount`, `payment_channel`, `capital_amount` and the rest of DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054 — read only, one hop, inside the 2 s budget, keeping no copy (DP-05).
5. Step three: composes the balance after the guaranteed share from the balance read and the guaranteed share the answer names, and tests it against zero (GAP-2731; ASM-4537). Zero answers R-GUA-26; a balance above zero answers R-GUA-25, which is the sibling's and moves nothing here.
6. Step four: composes the claim result — `status` within LOV-CLAIM-STATUS and `paid_amount` where the payment is recorded — and builds the `GuaranteeClose` element of RWB-S3-E4019-CON (GAP-2732; ASM-4538).
7. `RecordAndApply` activity, one transaction: the claim result and the element are written against the claim row in `rwb_guarantee`, the decision record is written through `DecisionRecordWriter.record(DecisionRecord)` with the rule ID, the rule version and the balance tested, and the stage report goes to the parent (DP-03).
8. The stage reports `GUARANTEE_CLOSED` for R-GUA-26, or `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` with the full balance for R-GUA-19 and R-GUA-27 and the 5 working day owner task of R-GUA-27; the parent applies the case status, closes the case or returns it to the route decision, and raises the case task and its timer (R-GUA-19; R-GUA-26; R-GUA-27).
9. The officer reads the claim result, the position and the case status on SCR-17 through the gateway-bff composite route and through the claim read of this service, and works the returned case where the residual went back to the route decision (DP-19).
10. The route decision runs again on a case returned at R-GUA-19 or R-GUA-27, which is S1's work and not this step's; the case closed at R-GUA-26 takes no further route.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A data product the step reads is older than today's ACE batch | The step blocks, names the product and its date, and decides nothing | MSG-P1-001 | AC1; VR-S3-007-1 |
| X2 | The balance after the guaranteed share is above zero on the R-GUA-26 path | The step answers R-GUA-25 and moves nothing; the residual is the sibling story's at the same state | None | Section 9 |
| X3 | The rejection reason is curable and the deadline has not passed | R-GUA-19 does not apply; the resubmission path of the claim story runs and the claim stays open | None | AC2 |
| X4 | The decision record cannot be written | The transaction rolls back: no claim result, no element, no stage report; the caller sees MSG-P7-003 and an incident is raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC4 |
| X5 | The record is refused for a missing or invalid field | Nothing is written, the field is named, the claim stays where it was | MSG-P7-009 | Section 12.8 |
| X6 | A role without the right tries to re-run the step or read its result | 403 from the access guard and nothing changes; the step itself runs unattended under the service identity | MSG-P4-002 | Section 10 |
| X7 | A second case signal arrives while the branch is running | The inbox dedupes by the cloud event id of the case signal and the activity is idempotent on the claim, the rule version and the batch date, so no second result is written | None | Section 12.5 |
| X8 | An ACE view is not reachable | The activity is retried by the workflow's retry policy; when the attempts are exhausted the stage stays where it was and the caller sees MSG-GEN-006 naming the system | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1 |

X1, X4 and the missing-value path are the legacy paths of RWB-E4-019 carried onto the split, with X6 the access path the legacy permission table already names. X2, X3 and X5 are the routing logic's other answers, the platform library's refusal, and X7, X8 the inbox dedupe and the availability path of the ACE read.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-S3-E4019-CON and its fakes, the decision-record library and the gateway route; the three views are replaced by a fixture and the rule package by a fake, so no deployment of P1, P7, ACE or rwb-case is needed |
| Negotiable | The activity name, the shape of the stage report and the retry numbers are this story's choice; the element, the rules, the conditions, the to states and the messages are fixed |
| Valuable | A guarantee that clears the debt closes the claim and the case the same day, with the position and the version of the policy that decided, and the deadline stops being tracked by hand |
| Estimable | One workflow branch, one close activity, three view reads, one claim result, one decision-record call and tests |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests against the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on a synthetic claim, an ACE fixture and a rule-package fake, plus one component test of the stale-input, the refusal and the unreachable-view paths |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Close the case when a guarantee clears the debt

  Background:
    Given guarantee claim "GCL-SYN-0419" of case "RW-2026-000419" is a claim in schema rwb_guarantee
    Given the GUARANTEE rule package in force is version "GUA-2026.11"

  Scenario: AC1 Close the case when a guarantee clears the debt (legacy RWB-E4-019 AC1)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case signal with the claim in state CLAIM_SUBMITTED and the balance after the guaranteed share at zero
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When its trigger arrives
    Then closes the case and records the position when a guarantee payment clears the balance in full
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Rule R-GUA-19 (legacy RWB-E4-019 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case in state CLAIM_REJECTED with claim_deadline passed
    Given a case in state CLAIM_REJECTED
    When resubmission not possible
    Then close the guarantee and return the full balance to the route decision
    Then the case moves to RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE

  Scenario: AC3 Rule R-GUA-26 (legacy RWB-E4-019 AC3)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case in state SUBROGATION_POSITION with the balance after the guaranteed share at zero
    Given a case in state SUBROGATION_POSITION
    When balance satisfied
    Then close the guarantee and close the case
    Then the case moves to GUARANTEE_CLOSED

  Scenario: AC4 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E4-019 AC4)
    Given the decision-record library mock returns the failure MSG-P7-003
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

**Target reading.** Every legacy line above keeps its wording; what changes is where it runs, which service holds each fact and how it is reached. "Closes the case and records the position when a guarantee payment clears the balance in full" is no longer a method of `GuaranteesAndGuarantorsService` reading the `recovery` schema and `rule_row`: the balance after the guaranteed share is composed by the `closeGuarantee` activity of `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` on queue `rwb-guarantee` from the balance read at the ACE batch date through `recovery.v_ace_account` (DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042) and the payments read through `recovery.v_ace_payment` (DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054), and the test is the condition of the answered row (DP-05).

"Records the position" is the `GuaranteeClose` element of RWB-S3-E4019-CON recorded against the claim row, with the closing basis and the balance tested; the position as a subrogation record belongs to RWB-S3-E4016-APP and has no field of its own yet (GAP-2733; ASM-4539). "Closes the case" and "the case moves to RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE / GUARANTEE_CLOSED" are the stage report to the parent and the status rwb-case applies from it: `guarantee_claim` has no closed value in LOV-CLAIM-STATUS, so the close of the guarantee is recorded as the claim result and the close of the case is the case's own status (GAP-2732; ASM-4538). "Writes the result to the decision log with the rule version" is the local `DecisionRecordWriter.record(DecisionRecord)` call in the same transaction as the claim result, with MSG-P7-003 on failure (DP-03); `decision_log_entry` stays P7's and is never written here. "Its trigger arrives" is the case signal the parent `CaseWorkflow` forwards, because the FSD names "a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer" and no source names which one (GAP-2734; ASM-4540).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | No value a business person may change is written in code: the rule IDs, the conditions, the to states, the rights and the messages are rule rows, governed rows or package content | BR-S3-007 of FSD A2.7.3.1 |
| BR2 | The balance after the guaranteed share is composed per calculation from the balance read at the batch date and the guaranteed share the answered row names; there is no balance, share or position column in `rwb_guarantee` | GAP-2731; ASM-4537 |
| BR3 | The close is one of three answers of the GUARANTEE route set in force: R-GUA-19 and R-GUA-27 return the full balance to the route decision and R-GUA-26 closes the guarantee and the case; R-GUA-25 keeps the residual route open and is not this step's | R-GUA-19; R-GUA-25; R-GUA-26; R-GUA-27 |
| BR4 | The balance and the payments are read only, at the ACE batch date, from this service's own SELECT-only views, one hop inside the 2 s budget, and nothing is copied into `rwb_guarantee` | DP-05; VR-S3-007-1; D-RCV-35; ADR-010 |
| BR5 | A data product older than today's ACE batch blocks the step and is named with its date; nothing is decided on a stale input | VR-S3-007-1; MSG-P1-001 |
| BR6 | The claim result, the element and the decision record are written in one transaction; if the record cannot be written nothing changes and MSG-P7-003 is shown | DP-03; ADR-022; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| BR7 | The case status, the case closure, the case task and the case timer are never this service's: the stage reports the outcome, the reason and the task due date and the parent applies the rule | DP-01; ASM-4538 |
| BR8 | The claim status stays inside its published list, PREPARING, FILED, DEFECT, PAID and REJECTED; the close adds no value to LOV-CLAIM-STATUS and the closing basis is carried in the element | LOV-CLAIM-STATUS of TSD S3 T3.2; GAP-2732 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 is why the rules and the rights are inputs of the activity; BR2 is the composition and the reason the schema gains no column; BR3 is the three condition tests of the answered row; BR4 is the SELECT-only grant and the as-at date on the element; BR5 is the guard before the comparison; BR6 is the `MANDATORY` propagation of the library write; BR7 is the boundary to rwb-case; BR8 is the reason the close is an element and a case status rather than a new claim status.

##### 9. State transitions

None of the case statuses below is this service's; the table shows what the stage reports and what it never writes, so a reader can see the boundary of this story.

| Rule | From (rwb-case) | Event | Condition | What this stage does | To (rwb-case) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-GUA-19 | `CLAIM_REJECTED` | `RESUBMISSION_NOT_POSSIBLE` | the reason is not curable, or `claim_deadline` has passed | Writes the claim result and the element, reports the full balance | `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` |
| R-GUA-26 | `SUBROGATION_POSITION` | `BALANCE_SATISFIED` | the balance after the guaranteed share is zero | Writes the claim result and the element, reports the closure | `GUARANTEE_CLOSED` |
| R-GUA-27 | `DEADLINE_MISSED` | `LOSS_RECORDED` | the loss amount and the reason are recorded | Writes the claim result and the element, reports the balance and the 5 working day owner task | `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` |
| R-GUA-25 (read only) | `SUBROGATION_POSITION` | `RESIDUAL_REMAINS` | the balance after the guaranteed share is greater than zero | Answers "residual remains" and moves nothing; the return is the sibling story's | `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` |
| R-GUA-22 (read only) | `CLAIM_SUBMITTED` | `FULL_PAYMENT_RECEIVED` | `claim_amount_paid = guaranteed_amount` | Nothing; it is the entry the payment side takes and it opens the subrogation position | `CLAIM_PAID` |

The states of this story's own object are the claim's: `status` takes `PREPARING`, `FILED`, `DEFECT`, `PAID` or `REJECTED` (LOV-CLAIM-STATUS) and the close writes the value the answered row leaves in force with `paid_amount` where the payment is recorded. The `GuaranteeClose` element has no state machine: it is written once per closed claim and is not rewritten, because a second close is a second case signal and the inbox dedupes it. The `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` execution has the platform states RUNNING, COMPLETED and FAILED, and a FAILED execution restarts from the last recorded step, which is why the reads and the write are activities and not workflow-local computation.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The recovery squad (RW-TRIBE) | Writes the workflow branch, the close activity, the reads, the claim result and the tests |
| RW-GUARANT, guarantee officer | Holds rights C, R and U on the capability area "Treatment and offer"; reads the claim result and the position on SCR-17; works a claim the deadline has put at risk |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Owns the answered state; works the case returned at R-GUA-19 and R-GUA-27 and the 5 working day task of R-GUA-27; holds rights C, R and U |
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer (FCR); RW-SPECIAL, hardship and vulnerability specialist | Hold rights C, R and U and see the closed claim and the returned case |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL and the read-only roles of TSD S3 T6.1 | Right R only: they read the result and cannot trigger a re-run |
| SY-CASEWF, the case workflow module | Runs the step unattended under the service identity and reports to the parent |
| rwb-case (P3) | Owns the case, its status, its closure, its tasks, its timers and the parent `CaseWorkflow` |
| P7 rwb-decision | Owns the rule package, the GUARANTEE rows, their approval, their effective date and the central ledger |
| P8 rwb-payment and ALS core and GL | Own the posting and the booking of the guarantee payment; this stage reads the result and never posts |
| ACE and its DBA | Own the `recovery.v_ace_*` views, their grants and the batch that dates them |
| The platform workflow and data owners | Own the task queue, the namespace, the ACE PostgreSQL grants and the decision-record library |

The check is the platform guard library's: this story declares the capability area "Treatment and offer" and the right U, C or R on each entry point. No credential and no personal name appears in the workflow input, the activity request or the logs, which carry the case ID, the claim ID, account keys, dates, amounts, a basis code and versions only.

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-TRT-015 | guarantee_claim | id | Write (the row the result and the element are recorded against) |
| DF-TRT-016 | guarantee_claim | case_id | Read |
| DF-TRT-017 | guarantee_claim | claim_type | Read |
| DF-TRT-018 | guarantee_claim | claim_deadline | Read (the R-GUA-19 condition) |
| DF-TRT-019 | guarantee_claim | claimed_amount | Read (the share basis of the answer) |
| DF-TRT-020 | guarantee_claim | filed_at | Read |
| DF-TRT-021 | guarantee_claim | paid_amount | Write |
| DF-TRT-022 | guarantee_claim | status | Write (within LOV-CLAIM-STATUS) |
| DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042 | v_ace_account | account_key, account_code, account_status, contract_no, product_category_efs, total_balance and 36 more | Read only |
| DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054 | v_ace_payment | payment_code, account_key, payment_date, payment_amount, payment_channel, capital_amount and 6 more | Read only |
| DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042 | v_ace_batch_status | the product date of the ACE batch | Read only |
| DF-DEC-002 to DF-DEC-016 | decision_record | the seven field groups | Write |
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case | id, case_no, product_group, primary_person_key, status, stage_code and 17 more | Read on the case signal only |
| DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036 | timer | id, case_id, task_id, timer_type, started_at, expires_at and 4 more | Read on the case signal only; never written |

`guarantee_claim` and `decision_record` are this service's own objects in `rwb_guarantee`, written through its own repository and login (DP-01). The account and payment columns are read through the read-only views at the batch date and are not copied into any column of this service: there is no balance field, no share field and no position field in `rwb_guarantee`, and the element of RWB-S3-E4019-CON is the only shape the evidence takes. The case and timer rows are rwb-case's and arrive on the case signal; they are never read from a table and never written (BR7; ASM-4538). The guaranteed share and the balance after it have no field identifier and no column in the Logical Data Model (GAP-2731; ASM-4537).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None of its own. The service publishes the two operations of TSD S3 T-A.1 on base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` (DP-13): `POST /api/recovery/guarantee/v1/cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims` (API-S3-001, right C) opens a claim and belongs to the claim story that creates it, and `PATCH /api/recovery/guarantee/v1/guarantee-claims/{claimId}` (API-S3-002, right U) records the claim result, which is the operation the close lands on. Its representation, its required fields, its errors and its idempotency are declared by the claim contract of this service and by RWB-S3-E4019-CON for the `GuaranteeClose` component, and are not restated here. The step itself is signal-driven and unattended; it has no command of its own.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The case status, the claim id and the payment reference arrive on the case signal the parent `CaseWorkflow` forwards, not on a REST read (DP-11 is not applied: there is no in-process call left to replace). The balance and the payment evidence are SQL reads of the views in 12.7, not REST reads, and the rule rows arrive with the package in force. No source publishes an operation for this step and none is invented (GAP-2734; ASM-4540).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service's topic is `rwb.guarantee.events.v1` with names `rwb.guarantee.<Event>.v1` and its retry and `.dlt` topics (DP-14), and the ownership rows give S3 no event (TSD S3 T5.3, "None"). The close is delivered as the stage report to the parent `CaseWorkflow`, a Temporal signal inside the case, because a Kafka event would need a name, a payload, an outbox row and the event platform of DP-09, which the plan does not give this legacy key. The report of a closed guarantee reaches reporting through the case, whose status the parent applies; if an S3 event is wanted it is a new name and a new dependency, not this story's (ASM-4538).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None of its own. The service's subscriptions are the template's inbox and the rule loader; the connection matrix of Architecture v5 slide 13 shows S3 listening to P6 and P8 events, calling P7 by Temporal activity, and publishing nothing that P9 reads by name in this story. The payment that clears the balance reaches the step on the case signal the parent forwards, not on a subscription this story adds. No event is named here that the service does not own (GAP-2734).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` (the close branch) | Child workflow of `CaseWorkflow`, one per case, on this service's own queue | `rwb-guarantee` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case ID, the claim ID, the case status on the signal and the payment reference. Output: the stage report with the outcome, the reason code and the rule version |
| `EvaluateRules` | Activity of the template | `rwb-guarantee` | The GUARANTEE route set in force and the case facts in; the rule ID, the action and the next event out; `NoPackageInForce` is not retried |
| `closeGuarantee` | Activity | `rwb-guarantee` | The three view reads at the batch date, the claim row and the guaranteed share in; the `GuaranteeClose` of RWB-S3-E4019-CON out; retried by the workflow, with the stale guard non-retryable |
| `RecordAndApply` | Activity of the template | `rwb-guarantee` | The claim result, the element and the decision record in one transaction, then the stage report |

The workflow name is fixed by the ownership rows and the context pack; the three activity names are this story's choice. The retry policy is the workflow kit's (1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts; `NoPackageInForce` and a stale product non-retryable). A replay never re-reads the views: the answer is recorded by the activity and read from history, and the branch is idempotent on the claim, the rule version and the batch date, so a repeated signal writes no second result.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step is signal-driven from the case and owns no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job; the ownership rows give S3 no job and the legacy scheduler is retired. The claim deadline that the feature is measured on is a case timer of rwb-case, driven by the workflow platform and created by the case, not a schedule of this service.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `guarantee_claim` | `rwb_guarantee` | S3 rwb-guarantee | Created by the per-service Flyway sequence and written here for `status`, `paid_amount` and the element; DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 of TSD S3 T3.1, with no balance, share or position column |
| `decision_record` | `rwb_guarantee` | PLT library object | Written only through `DecisionRecordWriter` in the caller's transaction (DP-03) |

No table of another service is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01). Three `recovery.v_ace_*` views of the ACE database are read, `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_payment` and `v_ace_batch_status`, read only at the ACE batch date and with no copy kept (ASM-4541); the case table, the task and timer rows of rwb-case, the rule tables of rwb-decision and the posting tables of rwb-payment are never named in SQL.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| RWB-S3-E4019-CON element fake | The `GuaranteeClose` shape | A complete element; one per missing required field; an element with and without the rule and set versions |
| ACE balance and payment fixture | `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_payment` and `v_ace_batch_status` | A cleared balance; a balance above zero after the share; a payment inside the batch; a product dated yesterday; an unreachable view |
| Case-signal fake | The signal the parent forwards | `CLAIM_REJECTED` with the deadline passed; `SUBROGATION_POSITION` with a zero balance; `DEADLINE_MISSED` with a recorded loss |
| Decision-record writer fake (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON) | `DecisionRecordWriter` | An accepted record with its chain sequence; a refusal with MSG-P7-009 and the field; a failure with MSG-P7-003 |
| Rule-package fake | The GUARANTEE route set in force | Version `GUA-2026.11` with R-GUA-19, R-GUA-25, R-GUA-26 and R-GUA-27; a set with no matching row; a checksum mismatch |

The balance fixture and the case-signal fake are the Day-1 unblockers: the build and every test run against them, and no test reads a production view or needs a live case.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 | 0 | The step is signal-driven; the result rides the claim representation of API-S3-002 |
| Kafka | 0 | 0 | Own topic with no catalogued event; inbox dedupe by cloud event id |
| Temporal | `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` and 3 activities on `rwb-guarantee` | The case signal forwarded by the parent `CaseWorkflow` | Namespace `rwb-recovery`; no Schedule |
| SQL view | 0 | 3 (`recovery.v_ace_account`, `recovery.v_ace_payment`, `recovery.v_ace_batch_status`) | Read only, at the batch date, no copy |
| File | 0 | 0 | No file is read or written |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.guarantee`, modules `close` and `workflow`, with the published types in `...guarantee.api`. Service base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, schema `rwb_guarantee`, topic `rwb.guarantee.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-guarantee` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-13; context pack).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is taken as the service's own SELECT-only views, because the Work Package records no contract dependency on P1 and the grant is the working read of ASM-4541 (GAP-2735). DP-03 is the record of the close, DP-13 the base the claim operations sit on, and DP-19 the path the closed claim is read on.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `GuaranteeCloseBranch` | Workflow | The branch of `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` that opens the step, reports the outcome and waits |
| `EvaluateRules` | Activity | Runs the GUARANTEE route set in force and returns the rule ID, the action and the next event |
| `closeGuarantee` | Activity | Reads the views, applies the stale guard, composes the balance after the share, builds the element |
| `AceBalanceReader` | Repository | The three read-only view queries; no entity and no cache beyond the request |
| `GuaranteeCloseRepository` | Repository | Writes `status`, `paid_amount` and the element against the claim row |
| `DecisionRecorder` | Service | Assembles `DecisionRecord` and calls `DecisionRecordWriter.record` in the caller's transaction |
| `StageReporter` | Service | Builds the stage report with the reason and the task due date, and the officer messages |

**Database.** No new table and no new column: the step writes `guarantee_claim.status` (DF-TRT-022) and `guarantee_claim.paid_amount` (DF-TRT-021) in `rwb_guarantee`, and `decision_record` is the library object of DP-03. A balance, share or position column is deliberately not added; if one must be persisted it becomes a field of the Logical Data Model first (GAP-2731; ASM-4537).

**Configuration and reference data.** The share basis, the conditions and the three rule rows are data of rwb-decision with a version and are read, never configured here. The retry numbers, the activity name and the 2 s budget are configuration of the activity. The capability area "Treatment and offer" and the rights are access data of P4 read through the guard library.

**Build steps**

1. The branch of `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` on `rwb-guarantee`, its input record and the stage report with the reason.
2. `EvaluateRules` against the package fake, with R-GUA-19, R-GUA-25, R-GUA-26 and R-GUA-27 as rule rows and the `NoPackageInForce` answer.
3. `AceBalanceReader` against the view fixture, with the batch-date test and MSG-P1-001 (AC1, X1).
4. `closeGuarantee` with the balance composition and the zero test (AC1, AC2, AC3).
5. The `GuaranteeClose` element of RWB-S3-E4019-CON and the claim result within LOV-CLAIM-STATUS (AC1, AC3).
6. `RecordAndApply` with the record in the same transaction and the rollback path of MSG-P7-003 (AC4).
7. The missing-value path with MSG-GEN-001, the refusal with MSG-P7-009 and the unreachable-view path with MSG-GEN-006 (X5, X8).
8. Tests for AC1 to AC4 against the fakes, the component tests of X1, X2, X5 and X8, and the replay test of X7.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.guarantee.guarantee-close`.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the branch runs from a synthetic case signal in SIT with the views and the package faked, the claim shows its result and its element, the record is written in the same transaction and rolls back with the action, the stale product path blocks with MSG-P1-001, and the case is closed or returned to the route decision on the report.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | A data product the step reads is older than today's ACE batch | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required value is missing, for example the claim deadline, and the step cannot decide | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | An ACE view does not answer | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right in the capability area tries the action | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written and the action is not taken | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P7-009 | A record is refused for a missing or invalid field | The decision record was refused: {field} is missing or not valid. |

The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story, FSD S3 A2.7.3.1 and the platform message set, and this story adds no message ID. MSG-GEN-001 is the required-field rule VR-S3-007-1's neighbour in the legacy validation table and covers a missing claim value; MSG-GEN-006 and MSG-P7-009 are the platform library's answers. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-17 Guarantee claim shows the guarantee, the claim deadline, the checklist and the claim result, in the states `Not due`, `due`, `submitted`, `paid` and `refused`. This story makes the end of that life visible: the claim result, the closing basis, the balance tested at its batch date and the case status `GUARANTEE_CLOSED` or `RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE` are read on the same screen through the gateway-bff composite route, which calls rwb-case and rwb-guarantee and composes the answer (DP-19; Architecture v5 slide 41). The screen field list and the route specification belong to the platform edge story and the screen owner; this story fixes what the service writes and what the claim read returns. A blocked step is shown as its message with the product and its date, never as a closed claim.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No value a business person may change is written in code: the rule IDs, the conditions, the to states, the share basis and the six messages are rule rows or package content, never constants (BR-S3-007; BR1, BR3).
- No personal data in logs, workflow inputs, activity requests, events or tests: the step carries the case ID, the claim ID, account keys, dates, amounts, a basis code and versions only, and the fixture is synthetic.
- No read of another service's tables: the case arrives on the signal, the rule rows with the package, and nothing joins across a schema (DP-01).
- No copy of ACE data: the balance and the payments are read at the batch date and no balance, share or position column exists in `rwb_guarantee` (BR4; DP-05).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views, and here only three views with SELECT granted to this service's login (ASM-4541).
- No live view and no live rule package in any test: the fixture and the fake are the only endpoints, so a red test never depends on the ACE batch or on P7's estate.
- No business value in the record: the `DecisionRecord` carries the rule ID, the rule version, the balance tested, the basis code and the result code, never a free-text reason or a customer field (DP-03).
- No status change from this service: the stage reports and the parent applies the rule and closes the case (BR7; BR8).
