| BR Field ID | Entity (owner) | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 | `guarantee_claim` (S3) | id, case_id, claim_type, claim_deadline, claimed_amount, filed_at, paid_amount, status | Write: the whole row on the create, then `filed_at`, `status`, `version`, `updated_at` and `updated_by` on the filing; read the rest |
| DF-ACE-091 to DF-ACE-098 | `v_ace_collateral` (P1 via contract) | collateral_no, asset_key, account_key, collateral_value, collateral_type, register_date and 2 more | Read through rwb-source-data's contract; no `v_ace_*` grant here (BR5) |
| DF-ACE-196 to DF-ACE-207 | `v_ace_collateral_detail` (P1 via contract) | asset_key, title_doc_no, plot_no, area_text, province, lien_rank and 6 more | Read through the same contract; no grant here |
| DF-ACE-187 to DF-ACE-195 | `v_ace_valuation` (P1 via contract) | valuation_key, asset_key, appraisal_no, appraisal_type, appraised_value, appraisal_date and 3 more | Read through the same contract, for the appraisal the claim is filed on |
| DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-011 | `document` (P5) | id, case_id, person_key, document_type, source, storage_ref and 5 more | Not read or written as a table: the claim's document set is rwb-document's and is referenced by identifier |
| DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036 | `timer` (P3) | id, case_id, task_id, timer_type, started_at, expires_at and 4 more | Not read or written: the claim clock and the 10 working days of R-LIT-79 are rwb-case's |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (PLT library, created in `rwb_guarantee`) | decision code, rule id, rule version, inputs reference, claim, collateral key, appraisal number, decided at, decider role | Write, one record per filing, before the claim moves |
| No Field ID published | the collateral-event fact of the case (rwb-deviation, S8) | deviation_code, raised_at, raised_by, paused_state, handler_user_id, contact_stop, cleared_at of FSD S8 A2.16.3.2 | Not read or written: X7 is rwb-deviation's, and this story takes no deviation row |

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8, of TSD S3 T3.1 and of the legacy Data table of the key, with the owners changed by the target. **No new table and no new column**: `guarantee_claim` already sits in `rwb_guarantee` with its eight fields, the claim type is a member of the list in force, and the decision record and the idempotency key are library objects created in the schema by the library's migration (DP-03, DP-15). The collateral, the appraisal and the deadline have no field identifier in this service's schema and are carried as elements of the claim answer and of the record (GAP-2736; ASM-4543; ASM-4545).

**No personal data.** The rows this story reads and writes carry identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and versions. No name, address, contact value or identity number enters `rwb_guarantee`, the decision record, a log or a workflow input; the officer is a role on the record and the parties are identifiers on the case and on the collateral.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-guarantee (S3); base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the collateral-event branch of the two operations the legacy Endpoints table names, and their shape is baselined by RWB-S3-E4020-CON.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims` | `GuaranteeClaimRequest` with `caseId` from the path, `claimType` = `COLLATERAL_INSURANCE`, `claimDeadline`, `claimedAmount` and the collateral-element fields; 201 with `GuaranteeClaim` (API-S3-001) | Treatment and offer, right C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` required; a repeated key returns the first answer |
| PATCH | `/guarantee-claims/{claimId}` | `GuaranteeClaimUpdate` with `status` = `FILED` and `filedAt` after the officer records the filing; 200 with `GuaranteeClaim` (API-S3-002) | Treatment and offer, right U, scope applied | Not applicable in TSD S3 T-A.2; a stale `version` is refused with 409 |

The errors are 400 for a malformed request, 401 for an unauthenticated call, 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope claim or case, 409 for a stale `version` or a claim already in `FILED`, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for an invalid element, and 503 when the decision library does not answer. The element set of the collateral event — the collateral key, the appraised value and the appraisal number — has no published field identifier and is the baseline's (GAP-2736; ASM-4549).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| The collateral and appraisal read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2736; ASM-4545)) | P1 rwb-source-data | The collateral of the case, its type and value, and its last appraisal with the number, the value and the date; used by `readCollateralFacts` and by the claimed amount |

One consumed operation, one hop, 2 s timeout (DP-11). DP-05 adds no dependency, so the plan's class C row is empty and the client is built against the documented use and a fake; the operation, its request and answer and its error set are the owner's and are recorded once (GAP-2736). No other REST call is made: the re-appraisal is not a call of this service, rwb-valuation is reached through the case, and no insurer, SVAF or TCG interface exists to call (BR6, BR8).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The ownership rows give rwb-guarantee no event type, so this story adds no name, no outbox row and no payload to `rwb.guarantee.events.v1`, and a build that publishes one here fails the absence test (BR9). The one publication of the step is the decision record, which the library of DP-03 sends to `rwb.decision-record.v1` in the transaction of the claim write.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` (EV-30 RulePackageInForce) | The rwb-decision topic, with `.retry` and `.dlt`; its topic name is not published for this key (GAP-2736) | P7 rwb-decision | The package code, the package version, the version id, the valid-from date and the approver role; the version the record carries and the version the claim rules are evaluated against |
| The X7 collateral event, when the case router signals it (event name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2736; ASM-4547)) | Through rwb-case, not directly | P3 rwb-case | The fact that a collateral event is open on the case; it starts or signals the branch and is never a subscription of this service |

One subscription with the inbox of the platform event library: the package event is stored once by its key, and the workflow reads the version in force. Slide 13 gives S3 event subscriptions from P6 and P8 and none from another service, so this story declares one subscription to the rule package and takes the collateral event from the case signal rather than from a topic.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` | Workflow, one child execution per case per guarantee stage, child of `CaseWorkflow`, continues-as-new | `rwb-guarantee` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the claim, the rule version in force; signal: the collateral event of the case; reports the stage outcome and the re-appraisal request to the parent |
| `readCollateralFacts` | Activity, this story | `rwb-guarantee` | The case and the collateral key in; the collateral, its type and value, the last appraisal and the claimed amount out |
| `evaluateClaimRules` | Activity, this story | `rwb-guarantee` | The collateral fact, the claim type and the package version in; the rule rows that fired, their versions, the required documents and the approval flag out |
| `recordAndApply` | Activity, this story | `rwb-guarantee` | The claim create and the filing in; the claim row, the decision record and the outbox row out, in one transaction |
| `reportCollateralEvent` | Activity, this story | `rwb-guarantee` | The stage outcome and the re-appraisal request in; the parent signal accept out, with no case row written |

`GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` is the one workflow the ownership rows give S3, and these four activities are this branch's; the preparation, submission, tracking and subrogation activities are the sibling stories'. The activity names are a target design choice, fixed by the baseline so that the workflow history is stable.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The branch runs from a case signal inside the workflow and owns no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job, because the ownership rows give S3 no job. The 10 working days of R-LIT-79 and the claim clock are the workflow timers of rwb-case and rwb-valuation, not a Schedule of this story (BR7).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `guarantee_claim` | S3 | The one table of this service: insert the collateral-insurance row and update `filed_at`, `status`, `version`, `updated_at` and `updated_by` |
| `decision_record` | PLT library, created in `rwb_guarantee` | The local hash-linked decision record of DP-03, one per filing |
| `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_guarantee` | The key of the repeated create and the answer it holds |

Not owned and never read as a table: `recovery_case`, `case_party`, `assignment`, `task` and `timer` (P3), `deviation` (S8), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `document` (P5), `valuation_ext` (S1) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No foreign key leaves `rwb_guarantee`: the case, the collateral and the appraisal are identifiers and values, not keys across schemas (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-source-data collateral read fake | The collateral of case `RC-2027-000420` with its type and value, its last appraisal with number, value and date, a case with no appraisal, a stale answer and an unavailable service | AC1, X4, TC-S3-E4020-APP-01 |
| rwb-case case-signal fake | A case signal accepted with the filed claim and the re-appraisal request; a rejected signal; a case in `DEVIATION_HOLD` | AC1, X6, TC-S3-E4020-APP-02 |
| Local decision-record library stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | AC2, X1 |
| rwb-decision package fake | A package in force with its version, and no package | AC1, TC-E4-020-01 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-17 answer for the claim, the collateral, the appraisal and the result, read once | TC-E4-020-01 |
| rwb-guarantee claim-resource fake (`RWB-S3-E4020-CON`) | A create in `PREPARING`, a filing in `FILED`, a repeated key, a stale `version` and a claim already filed | TC-E4-020-01, TC-S3-E4020-APP-02 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The collateral operation and the case-signal element set are not published, so their fakes are built from the documents and carry the placeholder until the owners confirm them (GAP-2736; ASM-4544; ASM-4545).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 1 consumed | `POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims` and `PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId}` on `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`; one read of rwb-source-data's contract; the screen reaches the service through gateway-bff (DP-19) |
| Kafka | 0 published, 1 consumed | `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1`; no event of this service; the decision record reaches `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the library of DP-03 |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 4 activities | `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow`, `readCollateralFacts`, `evaluateClaimRules`, `recordAndApply` and `reportCollateralEvent` on `rwb-guarantee`, as a child of `CaseWorkflow`; no Schedule |
| File | None of this service | The claim writes no file; the insurer and SVAF are not called, and the appraisal order is rwb-valuation's (BR6, BR8) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.guarantee`, module `collateralevent`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.guarantee.collateralevent`; front end `src/modules/recovery/guarantee/CollateralInsuranceClaim.tsx`, the fragment SCR-17 embeds.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the transaction rule of the filing: the claim row and the record commit together or not at all. DP-05 is applied through the owner's contract rather than a grant: the three legacy views are read through rwb-source-data and `rwb_guarantee` holds no `v_ace_*` grant, so the alternative of the service's own views is not taken and no dependency is added. DP-13 moves the base of the two operations and keeps the monolith path out of the build. DP-19 is how SCR-17 reaches this service, one hop through the gateway. No other DP applies: no rule package is embedded here beyond the package in force (no DP-04 row), no event is published (no DP-09), no job runs (no DP-10) and no file crosses the act.

**Dependencies the tables add and the plan does not hold.** The collateral read is class C in kind and the plan's C row is empty, so the client is built against the documented use and a fake on Day 1 and the absence is recorded as GAP-2736 (ASM-4545). The re-appraisal is a case signal and not a call, so it adds no dependency at all (ASM-4544). The three H rows of the metadata are the contract of this key and the two platform contracts of DP-03 and DP-19; no other H row is added, so the lane stays at depth two.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` collateral-event branch | Workflow | Waits for the collateral event, reads the facts, evaluates the rules, records the filing and reports the event with the re-appraisal request |
| `readCollateralFacts` | Activity | Reads the collateral and the last appraisal through the owner's contract and returns them with the claimed amount |
| `evaluateClaimRules` | Activity | Applies VR-S3-008-1, BR-S3-008 and the package in force, and returns the rule rows, their versions, the document set and the approval flag |
| `recordAndApply` | Activity | Inserts the claim row and updates the filing in one transaction with the record and the outbox row |
| `reportCollateralEvent` | Activity | Reports the stage outcome and the re-appraisal request to the parent `CaseWorkflow` |
| `CollateralReadClient` | Client | One hop to rwb-source-data with the 2 s timeout, the retry and the problem mapping |
| `PackageInForceConsumer` | Consumer | The inbox subscription on the rule-package event, keyed by the package and version |
| `GuaranteeClaimRepository` | Repository | Reads and writes `guarantee_claim` only, with the optimistic `version` |
| `ClaimRecordWriter` | Library adapter | Writes one record per filing, hash-linked, and refuses the step when the write fails (DP-03) |
| `CollateralClaimController` | Controller | The collateral-event slice of the two operations, its rights, its `version` check and the problem mapping |
| `CollateralInsuranceClaim` | React component | Shows the claim, its deadline, the collateral, the appraisal and the result on SCR-17, read only |

**Database and migrations.** No Flyway file. `rwb_guarantee` and its login arrive with the DB story of this service, `guarantee_claim` is already the service's table, and the decision record and the idempotency key are library objects created in the schema by the library's migration (DP-03, DP-15). No column is added for the collateral event, the collateral key or the appraisal: they are elements of the answer and of the record until the data owner names the fields (GAP-2736; ASM-4549).

**Configuration and reference data.**

- `LOV-CLAIM-TYPE` and `LOV-CLAIM-STATUS` with their identifiers, never enumerated in code (BR2).
- The claim deadline basis, the claimed-amount basis and the document set, as rows in force with their version (GAP-2736).
- The rule package in force and its version, read through the package event (R-UNI-38).
- The capability area Treatment and offer and its rights C and U, as access rows read through the guard.
- No insurer, SVAF or TCG endpoint, credential or file window: no interface is published (BR8).

**Build steps**

1. The collateral-event branch of `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` and its input record, registered on `rwb-guarantee` as a child of the case workflow (AC1).
2. `CollateralReadClient` against the read fake, with the no-appraisal, the stale and the unavailable paths (X4).
3. `PackageInForceConsumer` and the version in force the record carries (AC1).
4. `readCollateralFacts` with the collateral, the appraisal and the claimed amount (AC1).
5. `evaluateClaimRules` with VR-S3-008-1, BR-S3-008 and the missing-rule path (X8).
6. `GuaranteeClaimRepository` and the optimistic `version`, with the stale-version and repeated-key refusals (X5).
7. `recordAndApply` and the record with the rule id and version, the claim, the collateral key and the appraisal number (AC1).
8. `ClaimRecordWriter` against the library stub, with the failed-write path (AC2, X1).
9. `reportCollateralEvent` and the case signal, with the rejected-signal and the open-deviation paths (AC1, X6).
10. `CollateralClaimController` with the rights, the `version` check and the problem mapping (TC-E4-020-03).
11. `CollateralInsuranceClaim` and SCR-17 through the composite route fake, and the boundary test: no statement outside `rwb_guarantee`, no `v_ace_*` read, no write to a foreign schema, no outbox row of a claim event (X7, BR5, BR9).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.guarantee.collateral-event-claim-v1`, read as a flag of the platform library; off means the collateral event reaches the case with no claim created, the stage raises a task and no claim deadline is set.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, a collateral event files exactly one claim and one record in SIT, a repeated key and a repeated signal file nothing twice, a stale version is refused, a forced record failure changes nothing and shows MSG-P7-003, the re-appraisal request reaches the case, no case or deviation row and no `v_ace_*` read exists in the build, and SCR-17 answers through the gateway-bff composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required element of the claim, of the collateral fact or of the appraisal is absent or invalid (X3) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without right C or U of Treatment and offer calls the operation (X2) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the filing is applied (X1, AC2) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The three message IDs and their text are the rows of the legacy Validation and messages table of this key, copied unchanged. FSD S3 A2.8.3.1 adds VR-S3-008-1 with MSG-GEN-001 in the same words. No message is reworded, no new one is added, and no message carries a deadline, an amount or an insurer reference. The 403 carries MSG-P4-002 and the 409 of a stale version or an already filed claim has no business text in any source (GAP-2736). Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-17 Guarantee claim is served through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and this story fixes the collateral-insurance part of its answer and the states it can show.

| Screen | States | What this story sets |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-17 Guarantee claim | Not due; due; submitted; paid; refused | Loading while the claim, the collateral and the appraisal are read; due with the deadline, the appraised value and the document set; submitted with the filing date, the claim status `FILED` and the re-appraisal requested; held with the missing collateral fact or appraisal named; not recorded with MSG-P7-003; refused with MSG-P4-002 |

The legacy screen row of this key lists the five states and no state for a collateral event, so the event is shown inside the due and submitted states and SCR-17 needs no sixth state (GAP-2736). "Not due" and "paid" belong to the preparation and the payment stories of this service, and "refused" to the rejection path of FEAT-GUA-03. The screen's field list, its merge order and its other elements belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and to the sibling stories; the collateral, appraisal and filing elements are this story's and the baseline's.

| TC-E4-020-02 | AC2: the decision log cannot be written | Component | The decision-record stub stopped; the claim stays in `PREPARING`, nothing filed and MSG-P7-003 shown |

| TC-S3-E4020-APP-02 | The write edge: the repeated key, the repeated signal, the stale `version`, the claim already filed and the rejected case signal | Component | The same `Idempotency-Key` twice, the same case signal twice, a claim whose `version` has moved, a claim in `FILED` and a rejected parent signal |

The four legacy case IDs are the legacy cases of RWB-E4-020 in their legacy order, with the Level column added: TC-E4-020-01 and -02 cover the two criteria, -03 the access path and -04 the principle-5 failure. They are Component because the branch is tested on its fakes; the legacy wording of each case is kept in the Test Cases workbook, tab Story test cases. The two `TC-S3-E4020-APP-` cases are new and cover the parts no legacy case touches. The `-ITG` copies belong to the wave 3 harness, which owns the cross-service journey of this key; the X7 journey end to end is FEAT-DVF-07's.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the deadline basis, the claimed-amount basis, the document set, the claim lists and the rule version stay rows read with their version, never a constant, a default or a branch of the build.
- No personal data in `rwb_guarantee`, in a workflow input, in an answer or in a log: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and versions only, and the record names the officer's role and never the officer.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and reads no ACE table, and the legacy reads of `v_ace_collateral`, `v_ace_collateral_detail` and `v_ace_valuation` are retired rather than moved (DP-05).
- The case, the deviation and the appraisal stay with their owners: no `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task`, `timer` or `deviation` row is written, and no appraisal is ordered (BR6, BR7).
- A person approves an insurance claim: the branch never files from an agent or a rule alone (R-DEV-06).
- The claim is recorded before it moves and the fact is consumed once: a build that files a claim before its record, or twice for one event, fails the review (DP-03, BR3, BR4).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; no document, module or test names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no monolith base `/api/recovery/v1`, no shared job table, no Quartz row, no direct ACE view read and no claim event published by this step.

##### 19. Out of scope

- The contract artefact — the document, the schemas, the DDL template, the error set, the versioning rule and the fakes: RWB-S3-E4020-CON.
- The X7 deviation end to end — the flag, the pause, the states and the return: rwb-deviation and FEAT-DVF-07.
- The appraisal itself — the order to SVAF, the value, the outlier flag and the acceptance: rwb-valuation and FEAT-VAL-01 to FEAT-VAL-04.
- The case, its states, the stage clock and the parent workflow: rwb-case (P3).
- The documents of the claim and their retention: rwb-document (P5).
- The central decision ledger, the `GUA` rule rows and their approval: rwb-decision (P7); the local record contract: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON.
- The roles, the rights and the scope data: rwb-access (P4).
- The gateway-bff composite route, the SCR-17 field list and the layout: RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the screen owner (DP-19).
- Any interface to an insurer, to SVAF or to the TCG for this claim: no source publishes one, and INT-29 is TCG only and not available today (GAP-2736).
- The tracking, the rejection, the payment and the subrogation position of this claim: FEAT-GUA-03, FEAT-GUA-04 and FEAT-GUA-07.
- The deployment of this build: the chart values, the schema and login, the topic and the flag.
- The real cross-service proof against the live owners: the wave 3 integration harness.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of the notice step of rwb-litigation, split from RWB-E5-001. It fixes the three legal-action and notice operations on `/api/recovery/litigation/v1` (DP-13), the `NOTICE` action type and the stage vocabulary of the notice step, the create, read and approve shapes, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the error envelope, the consumed notice fact of rwb-comms (P6) and the stage answer of rwb-case, and the decision-record element of DP-03. The notice row, the templates and the WIN dispatch stay with rwb-comms (GAP-2743; ASM-4558); the consumed operation names and the case answer have no source specification and carry the placeholder (GAP-2743; ASM-4559); the requirement trace and the approval gate are resolved by assumption (ASM-4561, ASM-4562). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the notice step of rwb-litigation — the legal-action and notice operations on `/api/recovery/litigation/v1`, the `NOTICE` action type and the notice stage vocabulary, the create, read and approve shapes, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the error envelope and the rights, the consumed notice fact of rwb-comms, the stage answer of rwb-case, the decision-record element, the tables and the fakes**, so that **the app story, the screen and the tests of this legacy key build against one fixed, testable contract on Day 1 and an action type, a stage name, a notice state or an answer shape can never drift between rwb-litigation, rwb-comms and rwb-case without a failing build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy notice step of RWB-E5-001 crossed three boundaries at once: the notice and its template, the litigation stage and the decision record. The target splits them: the notice row, the template, the rendering, the D7.1 approval and the WIN dispatch stay with rwb-comms (P6), which TSD S4 T5.2 names as "P6 for notices" and whose FSD module scope is "letters, notices, SMS, LINE, proof of delivery" with the dispatch job JOB-10; the case of record and its route state stay with rwb-case (P3); the `NOTICE` legal action and its stage stay with rwb-litigation (S4). Each boundary is now a contract another team builds against, so each has to be fixed before the app story starts.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_litigation`, base `/api/recovery/litigation/v1`, topic `rwb.litigation.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-litigation` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.litigation` (Architecture v5 slide 41 notes). It records that the service holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant (Architecture v5 slide 29), so the notice and the template are consumed on the owner's contract only and never copied into `rwb_litigation`.

Four points are carried as a gap and its assumptions rather than decided quietly: the owner of the notice row and of the template rows while `POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve` is an operation of this service (ASM-4558, ASM-4560), the name of the consumed P6 operations and of the case answer (ASM-4558, ASM-4559), the reading of "no person in the path" against the built D7.1 approval (ASM-4561), and the requirement trace, because the legacy master carries no requirement row (ASM-4562).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the queue and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the pagination and filter convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline (Architecture v5 slide 11); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The ownership of the objects is taken from the Ownership Map only: `legal_action` and `hearing` are S4's; `notice` and `template` are outside S4's rows and the notice service is named as their owner (GAP-2743; ASM-4558); `recovery_case` is P3's; `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are P7's; `document` is P5's.
- The rwb-comms (P6) notice contract is published, so the consumed row of 12.2 names a real owner document; it is not in this story's contract-dependency row, which is None, and the absence is recorded (GAP-2743; ASM-4558).
- The stage answer of rwb-case is fixed here as a shape only; no source names a published operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage, and the name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2743; ASM-4559).
- The LITIGATION rule package and its row for R-LIT-03 are governed in rwb-decision (P7); this baseline names them and declares none of them (ASM-4561).
- The `legal_action` table and its columns arrive with the DB story of this service; this baseline declares shapes and creates no table, no column and no migration.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-litigation for this step: the three operations with their request and answer elements, the `NOTICE` action type, the stage vocabulary, the rights and the seven error responses.
2. Fix the shape of the create: the `LegalActionRequest` element, the action type `NOTICE` of `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE`, the case reference, the claim amount and the `Idempotency-Key` rule.
3. Fix the shape of the approval: `POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve` with no request body, the notice reference and its state in the answer, and the decision record that goes with it.
4. Fix the consumed notice fact of the P6 contract — the notice reference, the notice type, the template code and version, the template status and the notice state — and mark the fields the sources do not give with the placeholder.
5. Fix the stage answer of rwb-case: the move, the rule ID, the version and the decided-at time, with no case row read or written here.
6. Record the decision-record element of DP-03 on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, written before the legal action or the notice changes.
7. Record the closed vocabulary of the action type and the stage names, and the rule that no value is a constant of the code.
8. Publish the contract tables of section 12 and the five contract fakes.
9. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the additive rule, the vocabulary, the shapes, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the error envelope, the absence of a notice, template or `v_ace_*` read and of a `recovery_case` write, and the drift between a fake and the document.
10. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-S4-E5001-APP, the screen and the wave 3 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body or a request body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 400 or 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC2 |
| X2 | A field is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC7 |
| X4 | The consumed notice fact or the stage answer has a field list the sources do not give | The row carries the placeholder, the gap and the assumption, and the fake is derived from the published document | None | AC3, AC4 |
| X5 | A value outside `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` or the stage vocabulary appears in the document or in an example | The vocabulary test fails the build | None | AC1, AC8 |
| X6 | The document declares another service's operation as provided, a `notice` property, a `template` property, a `v_ace_*` view or a `recovery_case` row | The review fails the baseline; the boundary test fails the build | None | AC8 |
| X7 | A POST is repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key` | The stored answer is returned and no second effect is described | None | AC2, AC5 |
| X8 | The rights of an operation are not the ones TSD S4 T-A.1 declares | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the Ownership Map and the published owner contracts of rwb-comms and rwb-case only |
| Negotiable | The element names beyond the ones the sources give, the example values and the fake fixtures are settled in the baseline review; the operations, the action type, the base, the topic and the queue are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks RWB-S4-E5001-APP, SCR-18 and the wave 3 harness on Day 1, and the rwb-comms and rwb-case teams on the same day |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, one AsyncAPI fragment, nine contract tables, five fakes and four new contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

These eight criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only. They restate no business outcome owned by RWB-S4-E5001-APP and they copy no criterion of the legacy story, whose three criteria stay with the app story word for word.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The `NOTICE` legal action is rwb-litigation's, and the contract declares its action type and its columns on `legal_action` only | Architecture v5 slide 41; Ownership Map (legal_action owner S4); TSD S4 T3.1 and T3.2 |
| BR2 | The decision record is declared as an element written before the legal action or the notice changes, through the local library on the shared topic; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; TSD S4 T2; legacy RWB-E5-001 AC1 and AC3 |
| BR3 | The notice and the template stay with rwb-comms: the contract declares the notice generate and send as consumed, declares no notice or template property, and describes no rendering and no dispatch of rwb-litigation | TSD S4 T5.2; FSD P6 v3; GAP-2743 |
| BR4 | The stage move is answered and not written: the contract declares the answer that carries `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` and declares no `recovery_case` property and no case row write | Ownership Map (recovery_case owner P3); Architecture v5 slide 19; GAP-2743 |
| BR5 | No ACE view and no ACE table is read: the notice and the template are consumed on the owner's contract, and the service holds no `v_ace_*` grant | DP-01; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR6 | A POST declares the `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer; a GET declares none | Architecture v5 slide 11; TSD S4 T-A.2 |
| BR7 | The vocabulary is closed: `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` and the notice stage names are published as enumerations and no state name or list value is a constant of the code | TSD S4 T3.2 and T4; BR-S4-001 (FSD S4 A2.1.3.1) |
| BR8 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, an amount, dates, list values and a rule version only | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes; Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR9 | One REST base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; the document never declares another service's base or topic as its own | DP-13, DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR10 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes |
| BR11 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-litigation; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | Ownership Map; DP-11 |
| BR12 | The rule row of R-LIT-03 and the notice types and template statuses are governed in rwb-decision and in the notice service and named here, never declared here | ASM-4561; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 |

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of this document, not of a legal action:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The three operations, the vocabulary, the consumed rows and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, SCR-18, the wave 3 harness and the rwb-comms, rwb-case and rwb-decision owners accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example a new error code | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or the action type or a stage name changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | The absence test of AC8 fails: a notice or template property, a `v_ace_*` view, a `recovery_case` property, a second topic or a Schedule | In review |

The stage machine the document describes is the app story's: `NOTICE_GENERATED` to `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` under R-LIT-03 of the LITIGATION machine of TSD S4 T4, and this baseline fixes the names and moves no stage.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-litigation | Owns the OpenAPI document and the contract tables; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version, and the correction of the Ownership Map rows the baseline consumes |
| Consuming teams (the app story, SCR-18, the wave 3 harness and the owners of rwb-comms, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| Platform library owner | Owns the error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule and the decision-record library this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in an answer, an element or a fake |

The per-service login behind the security scheme of the document is named "the rwb-litigation login (DP-02)" and is not part of this baseline.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| LegalAction element | The columns of DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014: `id`, `case_id`, `law_firm_id`, `action_type`, `lawsuit_no`, `black_case_no`, `red_case_no`, `court_name`, `claim_amount`, `filed_date`, `judgment_date`, `judgment_amount`, `lit_status` and `status`; this step fixes `action_type` to `NOTICE` |
| Stage element | `NOTICE_GENERATED`, `NOTICE_DISPATCHED`, `NOTICE_BLOCKED`, `NOTICE_UNSERVED` of the LITIGATION machine (TSD S4 T4); a name of the workflow's stage, not a column |
| Decision record | DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 through the local library, written before the action changes (DP-03) |
| Notice | DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023 of the notice service, read only through its contract and never written, copied or joined here (GAP-2743; ASM-4558) |
| Template | DF-REF-045 to DF-REF-051, read only through the notice contract; owner Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2743; ASM-4560) |
| ACE facts | DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-054, not read: this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-05 is absent from the pattern set and the boundary is absolute) |
| Not written here | `recovery_case` (P3), `document` (P5), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `hearing` (S4, a sibling story's) |

The field-level types, lengths and required flags of the added elements are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the element names, the vocabulary of AC1 and the optionality rule of BR10. **No new table, no new column and no migration** is declared by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-litigation (S4); base `/api/recovery/litigation/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions` | LegalActionRequest in, LegalAction of status 201 out, with the action type `NOTICE` (API-S4-002) | Litigation, right C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header required; the answer is stored |
| GET | `/legal-actions/{legalActionId}` | LegalAction of status 200 out with its action type and status (API-S4-003) | Litigation, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/notices/{noticeId}/approve` | No request body, the NoticeApproval answer of status 200 with the notice reference and its state (API-S4-001) | Litigation, right A, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header required; the answer is stored |

The three operations answer 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, each with the error envelope and one message ID of section 14. The operation IDs are those of TSD S4 T-A.1; the paths are those of the target base and not the monolith form. API-S4-004 `PATCH /legal-actions/{legalActionId}` and API-S4-005 `POST /legal-actions/{legalActionId}/hearings` belong to the filing, judgment and hearing stories of this service and are not declared as this baseline's scope, though they share the document. The notice row behind API-S4-001 is the notice service's and is named as such (GAP-2743; ASM-4558).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| The generate and send operation of the notice contract (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2743; ASM-4558)) | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | P6 rwb-comms | The demand or recall notice generated from the named template version and sent on the dispatch run: the case reference, the notice type, the template code and version, the addressee role and the legal action reference in; the notice reference and its state out; faked |
| The stage answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2743; ASM-4559)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The move of the case of record to `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` with the rule ID and its version; on the workflow boundary it is the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). Both rows are contract dependencies of class C that the plan's C row does not carry, and the absence is recorded as GAP-2743 with ASM-4558 and ASM-4559.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic of the service is `rwb.litigation.events.v1` with event names `rwb.litigation.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and its three catalogue events `LawsuitFiled`, `JudgmentRecorded` and `AuctionResult` belong to the stories that own the filing, the judgment and the auction result. This baseline declares none of them, adds no outbox row and widens no topic; the decision record is relayed by the library of DP-03 on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and is not an event of this service.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The one notice fact on the S4 IN row of Architecture v5 slide 19 is `NoticeDelivered`, which is the proof of delivery and belongs to the sibling story of this legacy family; with DP-09 outside this story's pattern set, no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox is declared, and the notice fact of 12.2 arrives synchronously (GAP-2743; ASM-4563).

The activity name is a target design choice and the trigger of the step is read as the opening of the litigation stage for route R4, which is the event `ROUTE_APPROVED` of R-LIT-01, because the legacy story says the step runs with no person in the path while the FSD declares no background event (GAP-2743; ASM-4561). No activity is registered by this story.

None. The dispatch run JOB-10 at 16:00 is the notice service's; this baseline declares no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table, and no Job of Architecture v5 slide 44 is owned or moved here.

##### 13. Solution plan

**The CON declares shapes and moves nothing.** It writes no code, no migration and no table, and it changes no legal action, no notice, no case and no rule package. What it publishes is one OpenAPI 3.1 document, one AsyncAPI fragment that declares no event, nine contract tables and five fakes.

**Deliverables.** The additive document `openapi/rwb-litigation-v1.yaml` for this step, the `LegalActionRequest` and `NoticeApproval` elements, the stage enumeration, the vocabulary of `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` as a published enumeration, the contract README rows for the consumed rows and their placeholders, and the five WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-13 moves the base and nothing else. DP-19 is behind SCR-18, whose screen model is the edge contract's. DP-03 is the transaction rule the document declares. DP-01 is stated as the schema boundary, and DP-09 is not in the pattern set of this key, which is why no event is declared in 12.3 or 12.4. The template fact is consumed on the notice contract because DP-07 is not in the pattern set of this key either (GAP-2743; ASM-4560).

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds two H rows, `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` for DP-03 and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` for DP-19, while the plan's build list for this story is None; this baseline builds against their fakes until those platform contract stories publish. The notice contract and the case answer are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata row (GAP-2743; ASM-4558, ASM-4559).

**Build steps**

1. Write the three operations and validate the additive rule of AC1 in the pipeline.
2. Write the `LegalActionRequest`, `NoticeApproval` and stage elements of AC2 with the placeholder on the fields the sources do not give.
3. Record the consumed notice row of AC3 with its owner, its budget and its placeholder.
4. Record the stage answer of AC4 and the absence test for a `recovery_case` property and a notice property.
5. Record the error envelope, the rights and the `Idempotency-Key` rule of AC5.
6. Record the decision-record element of AC6 and validate it against the library schema.
7. Publish the five fakes of AC7 and the drift test.
8. Record the naming baseline and the boundary of AC8, then tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI document validates in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the five fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, and the app story, SCR-18 and the wave 3 harness have accepted the baseline.

| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request is absent or invalid, or a body fails schema validation | Enter {field}. |

The seven message IDs are contract elements and the text of the first five is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged; MSG-P6-003 is the notice service's hold message and MSG-P1-001 is carried because it is in the message set of this feature, and no path of this service raises either. No message is reworded and no new one is added (GAP-2743; ASM-4560).

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves SCR-18 Notice approval in its generated, approved, sent, delivered and unserved states, all through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The route calls rwb-litigation for the legal action and the rule outcome, rwb-comms for the notice, its template version and its state, and rwb-case for the case of record and its route state; this baseline fixes the rwb-litigation answers only, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The hold, refusal and failure states the app story shows — blocked, not recorded, refused, stale data — read the messages of section 14 on the same route.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the template statuses, the notice types, the stage names, the lists and the rule row stay data, reference data or the rule package, never a schema default or an enumeration member of the code.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, an amount, dates, list values and a rule version only; every example is synthetic and the addressee is a role.
- The notice stays with rwb-comms and the case with rwb-case: the document declares no notice property, no template property, no `recovery_case` property and no case row write (BR3, BR4).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the document declares no `v_ace_*` view and no grant on `rwb_comms` or any other `rwb_*` schema, and the boundary test fails a build that adds one (DP-01).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The document lists only operations owned by rwb-litigation; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided (DP-11).
- No retired element is reintroduced: the absence test of AC8 fails a build that declares a notice property, a `v_ace_*` read, a second topic, a Schedule, a Quartz row or a shared job table.
- The error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the naming rule come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: application slice split from RWB-E5-001 for rwb-litigation. The three legacy acceptance criteria are kept word for word with their origin tag and now run as one step of `LitigationWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-litigation`; the notices themselves are generated, approved and dispatched by rwb-comms (P6), which is the notice owner of TSD S4 T5.2, so this story evaluates R-LIT-03, writes the legal action of action type `NOTICE` and the local decision record of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (DP-03), and asks P6 to generate and send; the base becomes `/api/recovery/litigation/v1` (DP-13) and SCR-18 reads through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); the notice ownership, the consumed operation names, the case answer, the requirement trace and the approval gate have no single source statement and are declared as the working read of one gap and its assumptions (GAP-2742; ASM-4558 to ASM-4563). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **the Workbench to evaluate R-LIT-03 on the Legal-approved template in force, generate the demand and recall notices by rule with no manual drafting and no manual dispatch, write the decision record and the notice legal action before anything changes and answer rwb-case for the stage move**, so that **cases reach court faster with complete packs, on notices that no person typed and no person posted**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E5-001. It owns:

- all three legacy acceptance criteria of the story, copied verbatim with their origin tag, and the rule, message, screen and data rows they depend on;
- one notice step of `LitigationWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-litigation` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, the stage child of `CaseWorkflow` owned by rwb-case (Architecture v5 slide 19; Temporal and Drools Design slide 5, "S4 Litigation — notices, court dates, years");
- the evaluation of R-LIT-03 on the template fact and on the case product of the action, with the LITIGATION package version in force;
- `POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-actions` (API-S4-002), `GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId}` (API-S4-003) and `POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve` (API-S4-001) on base `/api/recovery/litigation/v1`, under capability area "Litigation" with the rights C, R and A (DP-13; TSD S4 T-A.1);
- the `legal_action` row of action type `NOTICE` in schema `rwb_litigation`, with the columns of DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014 and no new column;
- the local decision record of the outcome, written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON before the legal action or the notice changes (DP-03);
- the answer to rwb-case for the stage move `NOTICE_DISPATCHED`, with the rule ID and the version that produced it;
- SCR-18 Notice approval as this service's answer, read through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

It does not own: the published shape of the three operations, the notice action type and status vocabulary, the request and answer shapes, the error set and the fakes, which are RWB-S4-E5001-CON; the notice row, the template, the rendering of the letter and the WIN dispatch, which are rwb-comms (P6) on its notice contract; the case of record, its route state and the parent `CaseWorkflow`, which are rwb-case (P3); the approval routing, the delegation of authority and the decision ledger, which are rwb-decision (P7); the proof of delivery and the notice period timer, which are the sibling stories of this service; the document of the notice pack, which is rwb-document (P5); and the deployment of this build, which is the operations story of this legacy key and the wave 3 harness.

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E5-001 gave the Workbench one step that produced and sent the statutory notices by rule. Notices are prepared by hand today, a demand fee notice sent incomplete is a Bank of Thailand finding, and litigation takes 21 days to file. The functional specification keeps the objective, the metric and the requirement: a litigation turnaround of 6 days, measured on the decision log and the Workbench records, reviewed monthly, against the 21 days of today; and REQ-S4-001, "Demand and recall notices are generated by rule, approved, dispatched, and their notice periods are timed" (FSD S4 A2.1 and its requirements-served list; Business Requirements Program v4). The legacy master itself carries no requirement row, which is recorded (GAP-2742; ASM-4562).

What D-RCV-60 changes is who owns what, and the sources have answered the three questions:

- **the notice is rwb-comms' (P6).** TSD S4 T5.2 says the module reaches other modules "P6 for notices"; the FSD P6 module table gives P6 "E1 notices; E2 dispatch" with the scope "letters, notices, SMS, LINE, proof of delivery", its dispatch job JOB-10 at 16:00 writes the WIN file, and its notice types are DEMAND and RECALL. The Ownership Map gives S4 two tables, `legal_action` and `hearing`, and no notice table. This story therefore writes no notice row: it evaluates the rule, writes the notice legal action and the decision, and asks P6 to generate and send (GAP-2742; ASM-4558);
- **the case of record stays with rwb-case (P3).** `recovery_case`, its route state and the parent `CaseWorkflow` are P3's; the stage states `NOTICE_GENERATED` and `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` of the legacy criterion are states of the LITIGATION machine (TSD S4 T4) held by `LitigationWorkflow`, reported to the parent as the stage outcome, and applied to the case by rwb-case (GAP-2742; ASM-4559);
- **the legal action of action type `NOTICE` is this service's.** `legal_action` and its `action_type` value `NOTICE` of `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` are S4's (Ownership Map; TSD S4 T3.1 and T3.2), and the action is what the filing, judgment and enforcement stories of this service build on;
- **the decision is recorded first**, through the local decision-record library of DP-03 in the same transaction as the legal action change, which is what legacy AC1 asked for and what legacy AC3 tested;
- **the template is not read here.** The rule condition is `template_status = current for product and notice_type`; the template status and version arrive on the P6 notice fact, so no template row is read in `rwb_litigation` and no `rwb_template` table is created (GAP-2742; ASM-4560).

The approval is the one statement of the legacy story that does not settle by itself. AC1 says "with no person in the path", while the D7.1 approval of a generated demand or recall notice is a built Epic 2 capability (RWB-E2-014, on `POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve`, which the Ownership Map lists as an operation of S4). The two are read together: no person drafts, renders, addresses or posts a notice in this story, and the step raises no officer task of its own; the D7.1 approval stands as a gate of the notice service that the step waits on, and it is neither rebuilt nor bypassed here (GAP-2742; ASM-4561).

The step publishes and consumes nothing. DP-09 is not in this story's pattern set, the event catalogue of `rwb.litigation.events.v1` holds `LawsuitFiled`, `JudgmentRecorded` and `AuctionResult` and none of them is a notice event, and `NoticeDelivered` on the S4 IN row of Architecture v5 slide 19 is the fact of the proof-of-delivery sibling, which starts the notice period timer there and not here (GAP-2742; ASM-4563).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S4-E5001-CON is published: the three operations, the `NOTICE` action type, the stage vocabulary, the request and answer shapes, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the error set and the fakes are baselined and handed to this story.
- The rwb-comms (P6) notice contract is published with its fake, so a notice can be generated and sent on Day 1. It is a contract dependency of class C in fact and is not in this story's C row, which is None; the name of the operations is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2742; ASM-4558).
- The stage-outcome answer of rwb-case is available for the fake. No source names a published operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage: on the workflow boundary the answer is the stage outcome that the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies, and where rwb-case publishes a REST case-move operation for another caller its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2742; ASM-4559).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: the local decision-record library writes in the caller's transaction and a failed write stops the action with MSG-P7-003, so the legal action change and its record commit together or not at all (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-18 Notice approval reaches this service through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, and no screen calls a service directly (DP-19).
- `legal_action` exists in schema `rwb_litigation` from the DB story of this service, with the columns of DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014 and the standard record columns of TSD S4 T3.0; this story adds no table, no column and no migration.
- The LITIGATION rule package is in force at its version with R-LIT-03 in it; the package is authored, tested and approved in rwb-decision (P7) and loaded here on `RulePackageInForce` (GAP-2742; ASM-4561).
- The template facts the rule condition needs are answered by the P6 notice contract: the template code, its Legal-approved version and its status for the product and the notice type. No `template` row (DF-REF-045 to DF-REF-051) is read in `rwb_litigation`, and DP-07 is not in this story's pattern set (GAP-2742; ASM-4560).
- The service runs as its own login on schema `rwb_litigation`; it holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement outside its schema is refused by the database and fails the boundary test (DP-01).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-S4-E5001-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The route R4 of the case is approved and the litigation stage opens: `LitigationWorkflow` starts on task queue `rwb-litigation` as the child of `CaseWorkflow`, with the case, the product group and the rule package in force as its input.
2. The step reads the notice legal action of the case on `GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId}` (API-S4-003): the action type, the product group through the case reference and the status. Where the stage has no `NOTICE` action yet, it creates one on `POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-actions` (API-S4-002) with the action type `NOTICE` of `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE`, the case reference and the claim amount, and the create is idempotent on its `Idempotency-Key`.
3. The step reads the template fact the rule tests on the P6 notice contract: the template code, its version approved by Legal, its status for the product and the notice type (`DEMAND` or `RECALL`), one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker (GAP-2742; ASM-4558).
4. `NoticeRuleEvaluator` loads the LITIGATION package version in force from rwb-decision and evaluates R-LIT-03: where `template_status = current` for the product and the notice type, the demand and recall notices are generated from the Legal-approved template and the stage moves to `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` (FSD S4 A2.1.3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4).
5. The evaluation answers the rule ID, the package version, the template code and version it used, and the stage move.
6. `NoticeDecisionRecordWriter` writes one decision record through the local decision-record library, **before any change**: the case reference, the legal action reference, the rule ID with its version, the template version, the inputs reference, the outcome and the stage move. A failed write stops the step with nothing changed (DP-03; legacy AC1 and AC3).
7. `NoticeClient` asks rwb-comms (P6) to generate the demand and recall notices from the named template version and to send them on the dispatch run: the case reference, the notice type, the template code and version, the addressee role and the legal action reference. P6 renders the letter, holds it for the D7.1 approval where the approval is in force, writes it to the WIN file (JOB-10) and owns the notice state `Generated`, `Approved`, `Sent`, `Delivered` or `Unserved` (GAP-2742; ASM-4558).
8. `NoticeActionWriter` writes the standard columns of the `NOTICE` legal action in one `rwb_litigation` transaction with the decision record and the idempotency row. No business column of the action changes: `action_type` is `NOTICE`, `claim_amount` (DF-LEG-009) is read for the notice body, and `status` (DF-LEG-014) is left to the filing stories, which move it to `FILED` when the court filing is recorded.
9. The step answers the parent `CaseWorkflow` with the stage move `NOTICE_DISPATCHED`, the rule ID, the version, the template version, the notice reference P6 returned and the decided-at time. rwb-case writes the case of record and its route state; this service writes neither (GAP-2742; ASM-4559).
10. Where the template status is not current, the rule does not fire: the stage holds, a task is raised to the litigation officer with the message of the hold, and nothing is dispatched. That hold path is R-LIT-04 and is owned by the pack stories of this service; this step only reports it (FSD S4 A2.4.3.1).
11. A repeated trigger with the same case, legal action and template version writes nothing, sends no second notice request and counts the repeat.
12. The step sets a durable timer for the 1 working day of R-LIT-03, so a dispatch that has not answered inside the rule's window raises the stage on the workflow and never on a Quartz job.
13. SCR-18 Notice approval reads the notice, its template version, the case facts it was built from and the rule with its version from this service and from rwb-comms through the gateway-bff composite route, read only (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The local decision record cannot be written | The transaction writes nothing: the legal action keeps its state, no notice is requested and no stage move is answered | MSG-P7-003 | AC3, TC-E5-001-03, TC-E5-001-05 |
| X2 | The role does not hold the Litigation right of the operation | 403 before any read or write; nothing changes and no decision record is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, TC-E5-001-04 |
| X3 | The legal action does not exist or is outside the scope | 404 and nothing is written; the caller cannot tell an out-of-scope action from a missing one | None | AC1 |
| X4 | The action is not of action type `NOTICE`, or the case has no open litigation stage | 409 and nothing changes; no notice is requested | None | AC1 |
| X5 | The P6 notice contract does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The step waits and retries on the workflow's own schedule; nothing is written, no notice is requested and no stage move is answered, and the caller sees 503 with the platform error envelope | None | AC1, AC3 |
| X6 | The template status is not current for the product and the notice type | R-LIT-03 does not fire: nothing changes, no decision record is written, no notice is requested, and the hold task is the pack story's | MSG-P6-003 | AC2 |
| X7 | The same case, legal action and template version arrive twice, or the same `Idempotency-Key` is replayed | One write and one notice request; the repeat is counted and no second decision record is written | None | AC1 |
| X8 | The rule package in force is not the one the step was started on | The step re-evaluates on the package named on `RulePackageInForce` and records the version it used | None | AC1 |
| X9 | A required field of the create or of the approval is absent or invalid | 422 and nothing is written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC2 |
| X10 | A component, a statement or a test reaches another service's schema, a `notice` row or a `v_ace_*` view | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | Section 17, BR4, BR6 |

X1 to X4 are the exception paths of RWB-E5-001 carried onto the split, X5 to X9 are the paths the target call types add, and X10 is the DP-01 boundary. The template statuses and the notice types of X6 are values in force, so neither is a constant of this story.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-S4-E5001-CON, the P6 notice contract and the case answer fake, on the table of its own schema, and needs no live rwb-comms, no live rwb-case and no live rwb-decision |
| Negotiable | The activity name, the decision code and the shape of the stage outcome are this story's choice; the rule, the messages, the screen, the three operations and the action type are fixed |
| Valuable | A demand or recall notice is generated and sent by rule in one recorded step, with the template version on the decision record and no re-typing of a notice |
| Estimable | One workflow step, one evaluator, one record write, one action write, one client, one approval operation and one read-only screen fragment |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on synthetic cases and template facts through the contract fakes, plus the two component cases of the access answer and the failed record write |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Issue demand and recall notices

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-000501" carries the litigation legal action "LA-2026-000501" of action type "NOTICE"
    Given the LITIGATION rule package is in force at its version and carries R-LIT-03
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 Issue demand and recall notices (legacy RWB-E5-001 AC1)
    Given the rwb-comms contract mock returns the demand and recall notice generated from the Legal-approved template in force
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case route state "NOTICE_GENERATED" for case "RC-2026-000501"
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When its trigger arrives
    Then produces and sends the statutory notices by rule, with no person in the path
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Rule R-LIT-03 (legacy RWB-E5-001 AC2)
    Given the rwb-comms contract mock returns template "DEMAND-MTG" at its Legal-approved version with template_status "current" for the product and the notice type
    Given a case in state NOTICE_GENERATED
    When template selected
    Then generate the demand and recall notices from the Legal-approved template
    Then the case moves to NOTICE_DISPATCHED

  Scenario: AC3 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E5-001 AC3)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The three criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E5-001 word for word, with their origin tag added and nothing else changed: the repetition of `Then`, the legacy wording of `the action is taken`, `the decision log cannot be written` and `its trigger arrives` all stand. The cross-service parts are mocked, so AC1 and AC2 each carry one or two `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` lines, and those added `Given` lines are the only additions to the legacy text. What the legacy lines describe happens in three places in the target: rwb-comms renders, approves and dispatches the notice; this story evaluates R-LIT-03, writes the decision record with the rule version and writes the `NOTICE` legal action; and rwb-case writes the stage move on the case of record. The legacy `notice` write of the data table is not reproduced anywhere in this story (GAP-2742; ASM-4558).

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-LIT-03 | Litigation | D7 | NOTICE_GENERATED | TEMPLATE_SELECTED | template_status = current for product and notice_type | Generate the demand and recall notices from the Legal-approved template | NOTICE_DISPATCHED | Workbench | Rules component, letter engine, the Workbench document hub | 1 working day |

The row is the row of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, copied character for character. Its owner column is a role of the business and not a service: `Workbench` is the litigation stage, and in the target the letter engine and the document hub of the systems column are rwb-comms (P6) and rwb-document (P5), each reached on its own contract.

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The notice legal action is this service's: the action type `NOTICE` and the columns of `legal_action` are written in `rwb_litigation`, and no other service writes them | Architecture v5 slide 41; Ownership Map (legal_action owner S4); TSD S4 T3.1 and T3.2 |
| BR2 | The decision is recorded before the legal action changes, with the rule ID and the package version in force; a failed write changes nothing and the caller sees MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; TSD S4 T2; legacy RWB-E5-001 AC1 and AC3 |
| BR3 | The notice stays with rwb-comms: the row, the template, the rendering, the approval gate and the WIN dispatch are P6's, and this story reads the notice and asks for it on the P6 contract only | TSD S4 T5.2 ("P6 for notices"); FSD P6 v3 (scope, JOB-10, notice types DEMAND and RECALL); GAP-2742 |
| BR4 | No `notice` row, no `template` row and no `document` row is read or written here, and the service holds no grant outside `rwb_litigation` | DP-01; Ownership Map; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR5 | The stage move is answered and not written: `recovery_case` and its route state are rwb-case's, and the stage state `NOTICE_GENERATED` or `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` is held by `LitigationWorkflow` and reported to the parent | Ownership Map (recovery_case owner P3); Architecture v5 slide 19; GAP-2742 |
| BR6 | No ACE view and no ACE table is read or written here, and no cross-schema join is made | DP-01; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR7 | The same case, action and template version twice, or the same `Idempotency-Key` twice, writes once, requests one notice and counts the repeat | TSD S4 T-A.2; Architecture v5 slide 11 |
| BR8 | The vocabulary is closed: the action type is `NOTICE` of `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` (NOTICE, CIVIL_CASE, APPEAL, ENFORCEMENT, BANKRUPTCY_PETITION, LED_AUCTION) and the notice states are the notice service's; no state name and no list value is written in code | TSD S4 T3.2; BR-S4-001 (FSD S4 A2.1.3.1) |
| BR9 | No person name, address, contact value or identity number enters `rwb_litigation`, the decision record, a log or an event: the step carries case references, action references, codes, dates and amounts | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17); Architecture v5 slide 42 notes |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** R-LIT-03 is the one rule this story evaluates: the template fact answers the condition, the record is written, P6 is asked to generate and send, and the stage move `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` is answered. The hold rules of the same from-state — R-LIT-04 on a withdrawn template and R-LIT-05 on a contact stop — are named here and are the pack and deviation stories' to build; this step reports the hold and dispatches nothing. VR-S4-001-1 of the FSD tests the freshness of the ACE batch of the source and raises MSG-P1-001; this service holds no `v_ace_batch_status` read, so the check belongs to the owner of the data product and the message is carried in section 14 without a path here (GAP-2742; ASM-4560).

##### 9. State transitions

The case route state is rwb-case's and is not changed by this story: the step answers the move and the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies it (BR5). What this story does own is the state of the litigation stage and of the step.

| From (stage state) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| NOTICE_GENERATED | TEMPLATE_SELECTED under R-LIT-03 | template_status = current for product and notice_type | `NOTICE_DISPATCHED`, with the stage move answered and the notice requested |
| NOTICE_GENERATED | TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN under R-LIT-04 | A hold of the pack story | Unchanged here: no rule of this story fires, nothing is dispatched |
| NOTICE_GENERATED | CONTACT_STOP_APPLIED under R-LIT-05 | A hold of the deviation story | Unchanged here: no rule of this story fires, nothing is dispatched |
| NOTICE_DISPATCHED | Proof of delivery or proof window expiry | The sibling stories of this service | Unchanged here: the notice period and its timer are not this story's |
| A stage other than NOTICE_GENERATED | The step is triggered | X4 | Unchanged, refused with 409 |

| Step execution | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting | The litigation stage opens for route R4 | The package in force is loaded | Evaluating |
| Evaluating | R-LIT-03 fires | The decision record is written | Sending |
| Sending | P6 is asked to generate and send | The notice reference is returned and the transaction commits | Waiting for the next stage event |
| Sending | The record write or the transaction fails | X1 | Waiting, nothing changed |
| Sending | The 1 working day of R-LIT-03 passes with no dispatch answer | The rule's own timer | Waiting, the stage raised on the workflow |

The stage states `NOTICE_GENERATED`, `NOTICE_DISPATCHED`, `NOTICE_BLOCKED` and `NOTICE_UNSERVED` are the states of the LITIGATION machine of TSD S4 T4. The action status values are those of `LOV-LEGAL-STATUS` and this story moves none of them.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Litigation CRUA in the TSD S4 T6.1 matrix: the primary role of the feature, holding the create right C, the read right R and the approval right A |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Litigation RA: reads the action and the notice, and approves a notice for dispatch |
| RW-PRODHEAD and RW-HEADLIT | Litigation RA: read, and approve through the D7.1 approval path where the notice needs it |
| RW-ENFORCE, enforcement owner | Litigation CRU: reads the action and creates it, with no approval right |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-WRITEOFF, RW-CREDITAD, RW-GUARANT, RW-AGENCYMG, RW-CONDUCT, RW-HEADNPA, RW-HEADASL, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE | Litigation R: read only |
| PT-LAWFIRM, law firm user | Litigation RU: reads its own action and its notices, through the partner gateway |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-DATALOAD, SY-AGENT | Litigation R as the TSD S4 T6.1 matrix gives it: the service identities run the step and are subject to the same checks |
| rwb-litigation service identity | Runs the step, evaluates the rule, writes the decision record and the legal action, asks P6 for the notice and answers the stage move; it holds no grant on another schema and no `v_ace_*` grant |

The rights above are the rows of TSD S4 T6.1 and nothing wider. The legacy permission table names RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL, RW-PRODHEAD and RW-HEADLIT for right A and RW-LITOFF and RW-ENFORCE for right C, and both statements agree. The FSD says the feature "runs unattended" and that the litigation officer "also uses" it, and both hold here: the step runs under the service identity with no officer task on the generation path, and the officer acts on the approval operation and on SCR-18. DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set: the capability area and the right are declared per operation, and the guard is a service-template capability, so the check is stated here and not built here.

| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (PLT library, created in `rwb_litigation`) | rule id, rule version, template version, inputs reference, outcome, decided at | Write through the local library, before the legal action changes |
