| rwb-litigation service identity | Runs the step, evaluates the rules, writes the decision record, sets the timer and answers the case move; it holds no grant on another schema and no `v_ace_*` grant |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Litigation CRUA in the TSD S4 T6.1 matrix and the also-user of the FSD feature: reads the outcome on SCR-18 and SCR-19, and receives the task the unserved rules name |
| RW-ENFORCE, enforcement owner | Litigation CRU: reads the notice outcome of the case in scope |
| RW-LEGAL, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-HEADLIT | Litigation RA: read the notice outcome and the decision record |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-WRITEOFF, RW-CREDITAD, RW-GUARANT, RW-AGENCYMG, RW-CONDUCT, RW-HEADNPA, RW-HEADASL, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE | Litigation R: read only |
| PT-LAWFIRM, law firm user | Litigation RU as TSD S4 T6.1 gives it: no part of this step is taken by a firm user |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-AGENT, SY-DATALOAD | Litigation R or U as the TSD S4 T6.1 matrix gives it; the service identities run the step and are subject to the same checks |

The FSD declares the feature "runs unattended" with the litigation officer as also-user, and both statements hold: the step runs under the service identity with no officer task on the R-LIT-07 path, and the litigation officer is the role of the task that R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 raise. DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set: the capability area and the right are declared per operation on the contract, and the guard of the access service is a service-template capability, so the check is stated here and not built here.

Field IDs are those of the TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 T3.1 and the legacy data table of RWB-E5-002. **No new table, no new column and no migration**: this story writes no business row, `legal_action` and `hearing` arrive with the DB story of this service, and `decision_record` is a platform library object created in `rwb_litigation` by the library's own migration (DP-03). `notice` (P6), `recovery_case` and `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `document` (P5) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) are not created, not written and not read as tables.

**No personal data.** The rows and the record carry identifiers, dates, list values and a rule version. No name, address, contact value or identity number enters `rwb_litigation`, the decision record, a log or a workflow input; the fixture of the tests is synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This step is an unattended workflow step and publishes no operation of its own. The five operations of rwb-litigation (API-S4-001 to API-S4-005, TSD S4 T-A.1) belong to the notice approval, the legal action and the hearing stories of this service: API-S4-001 `POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve` is the dispatch approval that precedes this step, and API-S4-002 to API-S4-005 are the legal-action operations of the sibling stories. Declaring a delivery operation here would add a sixth operation to the ownership rows of this service, which name five (GAP-2744; ASM-4564).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The ACE-data read of `v_ace_pod` (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2744; ASM-4564)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The WIN proof of delivery of the notice: the notice or consignment reference, the served result, the delivered-at time and the recipient result; faked |
| The notice read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2744; ASM-4564)) | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | P6 rwb-comms | The notice of the case with its `notice_type`, `sent_date`, barcode, case and served result; faked |
| The case read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2745; ASM-4565)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case route state `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` that gates the three rules; faked |
| The case-stage answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2745; ASM-4565)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The case move `WITH_CUSTOMER_NOTICE_PERIOD` or `NOTICE_UNSERVED`, the case-stage timer and the officer task, with the rule ID and its version; on the workflow boundary it is the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies; faked |
| The rule package read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2748; ASM-4568)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The LITIGATION package at its version in force with R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). All five rows are contract dependencies of class C in fact that this story's metadata row does not carry, because the plan's C row is None; the two platform rows of the pattern set (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are its only H rows beside its own contract (GAP-2744, GAP-2745, GAP-2748; ASM-4564, ASM-4565, ASM-4568).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic of the service is `rwb.litigation.events.v1` with event names `rwb.litigation.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and the ownership rows of this service publish zero events. DP-09 is not in this story's pattern set, so it writes no outbox row and widens no topic; the only record it relays is the local decision record on the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1` of DP-03, which is the library's topic and not an event of this service (GAP-2745; ASM-4565).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The `PROOF_OF_DELIVERY_RECEIVED` of the state machine and EV-15 of the Temporal design are the names of the fact that starts R-LIT-07, not a Kafka subscription: this service has no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox of its own. The proof therefore arrives on the P1 contract of 12.2, synchronously, and the case state on the rwb-case read (GAP-2745; ASM-4565).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LitigationWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, the child of `CaseWorkflow`, continues-as-new across the years of the journey | `rwb-litigation` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the route R4 and the notice; signals: the proof of delivery, the case state answered by rwb-case, the rule package in force; the notice-period durable timer |
| `recordNoticeDelivery` | Activity, the one notice-served step of this story | `rwb-litigation` | The notice and the proof in; the rule ID with its package version, the served result, the timer fact and the case move out, with the decision record written in the same transaction |

The activity name and the workflow state names are target design choices of this story and are fixed by no source document; the trigger of the step is read as the arrival of a proof-of-delivery fact for a notice whose case is in `NOTICE_DISPATCHED`, because the legacy story says the step runs unattended while the FSD declares no background event (GAP-2745; ASM-4565). `JOB-10` of the dispatch belongs to the notice story, and no job of Architecture v5 is owned or registered here.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The notice-period clock is a durable timer of `LitigationWorkflow` started at `delivered_at` under R-LIT-07, and the proof window of 7 days is a durable timer of the same workflow started at dispatch under R-LIT-08. No Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row and no shared job table is declared, and no batch window is read or set by this story (GAP-2746; ASM-4566).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| legal_action | S4 (`rwb_litigation`) | This service's action row; this story writes none of its columns |
| hearing | S4 (`rwb_litigation`) | This service's hearing row; not touched by this story |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_litigation` | The local hash-linked decision record of the rule outcome (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_litigation` | The key of the repeated fact |

Not owned and never read as a table: `notice` (P6), `recovery_case`, `timer` and `task` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `document` (P5), and every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01, DP-05).

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |

| rwb-source-data pod fake | The proof of delivery of notice `NTC-2026-000602` with `served_result` delivered and `delivered_at` 2026-12-07; a refused, a returned and an undeliverable result; no proof inside the proof window; no answer beyond 2 s | AC1, AC2, AC3, X5, X6 |
| rwb-comms notice fake | The demand notice `NTC-2026-000602` of case `RC-2026-000602` sent on 2026-12-01 with its barcode and its served result; an unknown notice | AC1, AC2, AC3, X4 |
| rwb-case fake | The case state `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` and a case in another state; the moves `WITH_CUSTOMER_NOTICE_PERIOD` and `NOTICE_UNSERVED` accepted, and a move refused | AC1, AC2, AC3, X3 |

The operation names of the five consumed rows and the element of `v_ace_pod` are stubbed from the published documents and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-2744, GAP-2745, GAP-2748; ASM-4564, ASM-4565, ASM-4568).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.litigation`, module `notice`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.litigation.notice`; front end `src/modules/recovery/litigation/NoticeDelivery.tsx`, the fragment SCR-18 and SCR-19 embed, read only.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 applies only as a prohibition: this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant, reads no ACE view and no ACE table, and the proof arrives on rwb-source-data's contract (GAP-2744; ASM-4564). DP-03 is the transaction rule of the step: the record, the timer and the case answer commit together or not at all. DP-13 is the base of this service's five operations, none of which this story provides. DP-19 is how SCR-18 and SCR-19 reach this service, one hop through the gateway.

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds two H rows, `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` for DP-03 and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` for DP-19, which the plan already carries. The five consumed contracts are class C in fact and the plan's C row is None, so the story builds against their documents and fakes on Day 1 and the absence is recorded (GAP-2744, GAP-2745, GAP-2748).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `LitigationWorkflow` notice branch | Workflow | The stage of the journey that waits for the proof, holds the notice-period timer and the proof window, and reports the outcome to the parent |
| `recordNoticeDelivery` | Activity | The one step: read the notice and the case state, read the proof, evaluate R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 or R-LIT-09, write the record, set the timer and answer the case |
| `NoticeDeliveryEvaluator` | Service | The rule evaluation against the LITIGATION package version in force, with the served-result vocabulary and the proof window |
| `NoticeDeliveryDecisionRecordWriter` | Library adapter | Writes the decision record with the rule ID and the version before anything changes, hash-linked, and refuses the step when the write fails (DP-03) |
| `NoticeTimer` | Workflow timer | Starts the notice-period timer at `delivered_at` under R-LIT-07 and never starts it under R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 |
| `PodFactClient` | Client | The `v_ace_pod` read on the P1 contract, one hop, 2 s, breaker, no retry of its own |
| `NoticeFactClient` | Client | The notice and served-result read on the P6 contract, one hop, 2 s, breaker |
| `CaseAnswer` | Client and signal reporter | The case read and the case-stage answer to rwb-case; it reports, it never changes a case row |
| `NoticeDelivery` | React component | Shows the delivered and unserved states on SCR-18 and the pack state on SCR-19, read only, with the refusal and failure states |

**Database and migrations.** No Flyway file. `legal_action` and `hearing` arrive with the DB story of this service, and the decision record and the idempotency key are library objects created in `rwb_litigation` by the library's migration (DP-03). This story writes no business row, so no column is added for `served_result`, `delivered_at` or the notice period: those are facts of the consumed answer, of the record and of the timer, and storing them would copy two other services' facts into this schema (GAP-2744, GAP-2746).

**Configuration and reference data.**

- The served-result vocabulary and the proof window of 7 days, read as reference data with a version and never as constants (BR7).
- The notice period per product and notice type, read as a versioned reference row; its content is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2746; ASM-4566).
- The LITIGATION package and its version, authored, tested and approved in rwb-decision (P7) and loaded on `RulePackageInForce`.
- The capability area "Litigation" and its rights are access rows of rwb-access, read through the guard.
- No parameter is named in the sources for the step itself; the 2 s budget and the single hop are the platform rule of ADR-020.

**Build steps**

1. The notice branch of `LitigationWorkflow` and its input record, registered on `rwb-litigation` as the stage child of `CaseWorkflow`, with the proof as its trigger (GAP-2745; ASM-4565).
2. `PodFactClient` and `NoticeFactClient` against their fakes, with the 2 s budget, the breaker and the no-answer path (AC1, X4, X5).
3. `NoticeDeliveryEvaluator` over the LITIGATION package, with the three rules, the vocabulary, the proof window and the no-fire path (AC1, AC2, AC3, X6).
4. `NoticeDeliveryDecisionRecordWriter` against the library stub, with the failed-write path (AC4, X1).
5. `NoticeTimer` and the reference read of the notice period, with the missing-reference path (AC2, X9).
6. `CaseAnswer` with the move, the case-stage timer and the officer task (AC2, AC3, X3).
7. `NoticeDelivery` and the two screens through the composite route fake (AC1, AC3).
8. The boundary test: no statement outside `rwb_litigation`, no `v_ace_*` read, no write to `rwb_comms`, `rwb_case` or `rwb_decision` (X10, BR3, BR5).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.litigation.notice-delivery-v1`, read as a flag of the platform library; off means the step holds the proof and answers no move, and the sibling stories are unaffected.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the step runs from a synthetic proof in SIT, each of the three rules produces its record, its timer state and its move, a repeated fact writes once, a forced record failure changes nothing, no `notice` row and no `recovery_case` row is written from this service, and SCR-18 and SCR-19 answer through the gateway-bff composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S4-001 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names a missing item of the litigation pack, which is the pack story of this service, so no path of this story raises it | The pack is missing {item}. Add it before filing. |
| MSG-S4-002 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names the expiry of the claim on the case, which is the prescription fact of this service, so no path of this story raises it | The claim on this case expires on {date}. File before then. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of the fact or of the answer is absent or invalid (X6 of the contract) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Litigation right reads the step outcome (X2) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before anything changes (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The data product of the source is stale after a late or failed ACE batch, which is VR-S4-002-1 (FSD S4 A2.2.3.1). This service holds no ACE batch status read, so the check is the owner's and the message is carried here (GAP-2744; ASM-4564) | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The six texts are the legacy wording of RWB-E5-002 section 14 and of the FSD S4 A2.2 message list, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new message is added. `MSG-GEN-001` is displayed with the field it names. A downstream that does not answer (X5), a notice that is not found (X4) and a case in the wrong state (X3) carry no message of this set, and the platform error envelope is displayed as it is.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built in this story. Two existing surfaces show what it evaluates, read through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19):

| Screen | State | What the user sees |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Generated | The notice generated for the case, read only, owned by the notice story |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Approved | The dispatch approval of API-S4-001, read only |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Sent | `sent_date` of the notice on the P6 answer, read only |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Delivered | The served result, the `delivered_at` time, the proof reference and the notice-period timer started under R-LIT-07 |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Unserved | The served result or the expired proof window, and the reason the notice period did not start, under R-LIT-08 or R-LIT-09 |
| SCR-19 Litigation workspace | Pack | The step outcome next to the legal action of the case, read only |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Not recorded | The decision record could not be written, MSG-P7-003, and nothing changed |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Refused | A role without the Litigation right reads MSG-P4-002 and nothing changes |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Stale data | The message MSG-P1-001 shown where the owner reports the stale data product of the source |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Timer held | The notice period reference row of the product and notice type is missing, and the timer waits (X9) |

The route merges the answer of this service with rwb-comms for the notice and rwb-case for the case and its route state; the route path, the screen-model field list and the merge order belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the edge stories, not here. The two state lists are the legacy lists of RWB-E5-002 ("generated; approved; sent; delivered; unserved" and "pack; instructed; filed; hearing; judgment") with the refusal, failure and timer-held states this story adds.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the served-result vocabulary, the 7-day proof window, the notice period per product and notice type and the message texts are values and reference rows with a version; no list value, state name, day count or date appears in Java.
- No personal data in logs, events, workflow inputs, prompts or the fixture: the step carries references, dates, codes and a rule version only, and the test data is synthetic.
- The notice stays with rwb-comms: no `notice` row, no served result and no barcode is written here (BR3; DP-01).
- The case stays with rwb-case: no `recovery_case` row, no route state, no case-stage timer row and no task row is written here, and the move is answered with the rule and its version (BR4).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: no component of this story reads a `v_ace_*` view or an ACE table, and the service holds no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-05).
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema join: `notice`, `recovery_case`, `timer`, `rule_row`, `decision_log_entry` and `document` are reached only through their owners' contracts (DP-01).
- One hop and a 2 s budget on each consumed call, with a breaker per downstream and no call chain; the retry of the step is the workflow's own and never a silent second answer.
- The decision is never recorded after the effect: the record is written first through the library, and a failed write stops the step (DP-03, MSG-P7-003).
- No event, no topic, no outbox row and no Schedule: this story publishes nothing, consumes nothing and registers no job, and the catalogue of the service is not widened (12.3, 12.4, 12.6).
- The two screens are read only; SCR-18 posts nothing and its approval action is API-S4-001 of the notice story.

| ADR-013, ADR-014, ADR-015, ADR-016, ADR-020, ADR-022 | 19 services inside ACE, schema and login per service, the event platform this story adds no producer or consumer to, Temporal with durable timers, contract-first REST with one hop, and the local decision record with the central ledger |
| Wave 3 harness | The end-to-end proof of the same legacy key across rwb-litigation, rwb-source-data, rwb-comms and rwb-case, with the `-ITG` copies of the six cases |

##### 19. Out of scope

- The published shape of the consumed facts, the served-result vocabulary, the proof window, the errors and the fakes: RWB-S4-E5002-CON.
- The notice row, its barcode, its `sent_date`, the served result and the notice document: rwb-comms (P6) and rwb-document (P5), and the rwb-comms slice of this legacy key. **The notice is written by rwb-comms, and this story evaluates the rule, records the decision, starts the timer and answers the case move** (GAP-2744; ASM-4564).
- The case of record, its route state `WITH_CUSTOMER_NOTICE_PERIOD` or `NOTICE_UNSERVED`, the parent `CaseWorkflow`, the case-stage timer and the officer task: rwb-case (P3) and its slice of this legacy key (GAP-2745; ASM-4565).
- The WIN consignment, its file and its ACE ingestion, and the read of `v_ace_pod`: rwb-integration (P2) and rwb-source-data (P1).
- The generation, the template and the dispatch of the notice: FEAT-LIT-01 of this module, and API-S4-001 `POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve` of the notice story.
- The running and the expiry of the notice period after it starts, and the wake-up that opens pack assembly under R-LIT-15: FEAT-LIT-03 of this module, the sibling story of this key family.
- The authoring, testing and approval of the LITIGATION package and of the rule rows of R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09: rwb-decision (P7), with the embedded runtime as a service-template capability (GAP-2748; ASM-4568).
- The notice period value per product and notice type: the reference-data owner of rwb-case and the business owner of S4; the story reads the row and carries the placeholder (GAP-2746; ASM-4566).
- The rights, roles, scope and masking data themselves, and the screen field list and merge order of SCR-18 and SCR-19: rwb-access and RWB-PLT-N001-CON.
- The cross-service journey of the legacy key and its evidence: the wave 3 harness.
- The deployment of this capability, its flag, its dashboards, its alerts and its runbook: the operations story of this legacy key.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E5-002 for the rwb-comms slice of the proof of delivery, which records the returned delivery fact on the notice row and hands it to rwb-litigation on the published contract RWB-S4-E5002-CON. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **the proof of delivery that comes back from the post recorded on the notice that rwb-comms holds, with the delivery result and the delivered or callback date written once on the notice row, the notice state moved to Delivered or Unserved, and the same fact handed to rwb-litigation on the published contract RWB-S4-E5002-CON so that the case moves and the notice period starts there**, so that **the notice shows how and when it was served instead of the post room being chased by phone, and the case of record, its route state and its notice-period timer stay with the services that own them**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A statutory notice only starts its clock when it has been served, and a period counted from the print date can be challenged in court. The legacy story wrote the delivery confirmation onto the case, started the notice period from the delivered date (R-LIT-07) and marked the notice unserved when the proof window expired (R-LIT-08). Both moves are case moves: the case state, its route state and the notice-period clock are the case of record's. The delivery fact itself, however, is not a case fact: it belongs to the notice, and the notice belongs to communications, which owns the notice, the template, the merge fields and the proof of delivery (Architecture v5 slide 41 and slide 17, `notice` in `ownership.json`). This story is that half of the legacy step: the litigation officer records the returned proof on the notice, rwb-comms writes `notice.callback_date` (DF-LEG-021) and `notice.delivery_status` (DF-LEG-022) in schema `rwb_comms`, the notice moves on its own lifecycle to Delivered or Unserved, and the same fact leaves the service once, on the published S4 contract, for rwb-litigation to evaluate R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 or R-LIT-09 and for rwb-case to start the notice period behind its own timer.

Three facts are no longer this service's to reach, and the story is built so that it cannot reach them. The case route state, the notice-period timer and the task of the notice period are rwb-case's (P3), and the notice-period duration, its reference row and the raise of the breach are the case record's as well. The evaluation of the delivery rules, the proof-window expiry and the queue transfer of an unserved notice are rwb-litigation's (S4), reached only on the contract `RWB-S4-E5002-CON` that this story builds against and never as a table. And the ACE proof-of-delivery rows are read by rwb-source-data, not here: the automatic `v_ace_pod` loop that fills the notice from the WIN file is the dispatch story of Epic 2 (RWB-P6-E2021-APP) and the capture design of Epic 1 (RWB-P6-E1055-APP), and DP-05 applies to this story only as a prohibition (GAP-1194; ASM-2141). The proof this story records is the one the officer supplies or the one the S4 answer carries back; no ACE view and no ACE table is read by any component of it.

This document is the rwb-comms slice of legacy RWB-E5-002. It owns no legacy criterion: AC1 to AC4 of the story master are the S4 slice's (`RWB-S4-E5002-APP`, which keeps the case transitions and the legacy lines word for word) and the cross-service journey is the integration slice's (`RWB-ITG-E5002-ITG`). The other slices of the same key are the contract `RWB-S4-E5002-CON` and the case slice `RWB-P3-E5002-APP`, which applies the delivery answer to the case, its timer and its decision record. What this story owns is the notice deliverable of the title: the proof on the notice, its two columns, its state, the hand-off and the screen read. Its criteria are therefore new under D-RCV-60 and test only that deliverable.

The legacy in-process write is retired rather than restated: no component of this story writes `recovery_case`, `timer`, `task` or `decision_log_entry`, and the old monolith API base is not served by any path of this service (DP-13). The decision that a delivered or undeliverable letter produced is recorded, before the notice changes, through the local decision-record library with the rule and its version in force (DP-03, TSD P6 T2 "writes the decision log entry before any change"), which is what legacy AC1 asked for and what legacy AC4 tested (GAP-1190; ASM-2137). The screens are read through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and no screen calls an owner service directly.

It serves REQ-OCC-003 ("letters are dispatched for print and post, and proof of delivery returns to the case"), it carries the control CTL-15 by putting the delivered date on the notice and on the hand-off, and it holds the FSD P6 measure "notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent".

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S4-E5002-CON is published: the proof-record operation on `/api/recovery/litigation/v1`, its request and answer shape (the notice reference, the case reference, the delivery status, the delivered date, the rule ID and the package version of the S4 evaluation), its error envelope and its contract fake. The operation's own name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1189; ASM-2136); this story builds against the contract and its fake on Day 1 and never against a notice or case table.
- The `notice` table and its columns exist from RWB-P6-E1052-APP, including `callback_date` (DF-LEG-021), `delivery_status` (DF-LEG-022) and the lifecycle `state` column of the TSD P6 T3.0 standard columns; no new table and no new column is created by this story.
- The notice to be served exists in state Sent with its `sent_date` (DF-LEG-019) and `barcode` (DF-LEG-020), which are the WIN acknowledgment fields of RWB-P6-E1055-APP.
- The local decision-record library and the shared record format of DP-03 are live: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON. It is not in this story's build list, which is empty, so the story builds against its fake until the platform contract story publishes (GAP-1190; ASM-2137).
- The mapping of a LOV-DELIVERY value onto the notice state, and the version of that mapping row in force, are reference data owned by the business and read with their version, so no list value and no state name is written in code. The list itself is LOV-DELIVERY of the TSD P6 T3.2 (`DELIVERED`, `REFUSED`, `UNDELIVERABLE`, `PENDING`); its meaning for `REFUSED` and `PENDING`, and the contract the list is read on, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1192; ASM-2139).
- The gateway-bff composite route (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) serves SCR-18 Notice approval and SCR-19 Litigation workspace; it is not in this story's build list either (GAP-1190; ASM-2137).
- The caller holds a Workbench role with the Litigation right of the notice (TSD P6 T6.1: RW-LITOFF holds Litigation CRUA). The guard library of DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set: the declared right on the two operations is enforced at the edge for the screen path, and the right on the new write path is this story's design (GAP-1195; ASM-2142).
- The service runs as its own login on schema `rwb_comms` (the DP-01 and DP-13 rules of the story set); it holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant (GAP-1194; ASM-2141).

##### 4. Flow

1. The litigation officer opens SCR-18 Notice approval for a notice of the case, through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and the notice section answers from `GET /notices/{noticeId}` on base `/api/recovery/comms/v1` (API-P6-002): state, `notice_type`, `sent_date`, `barcode`, `callback_date` and `delivery_status`.
2. The officer records the returned proof with the delivery result, the delivered or callback date, and the barcode or reference the letter carries, on `POST /notices/{noticeId}/proof-of-delivery`.
3. `ProofOfDeliveryValidator` checks that the notice exists in the caller's scope and is in state Sent with a `sent_date`, that the delivery status is a value of LOV-DELIVERY, that a callback date is present when the status is one that carries a date, and that a barcode supplied with the proof is the barcode of the notice. A failed check answers 422 or 404 and nothing is read further.
4. `DeliveryOutcomeMapper` resolves the notice state from the delivery status through the mapping row in force (Delivered for a delivered proof, Unserved for a refused or undeliverable one); the row and its version are reference data, never code.
5. `ProofDecisionRecordWriter` writes one decision record through the local decision-record library, before any notice change: the outcome, the delivery status, the callback date, the notice reference, the case reference and the rule ID the outcome belongs to (R-LIT-07 for a served notice, R-LIT-08 for an unserved one) with the version in force. A failed write stops the request with nothing changed (DP-03; legacy AC1 and AC4).
6. `NoticeDeliveryWriter` writes, in one `rwb_comms` transaction, `callback_date` (DF-LEG-021), `delivery_status` (DF-LEG-022) and the notice `state`, plus the idempotency row of the request. No other owner's row is written.
7. `S4DeliveryClient` calls the proof-record operation of `RWB-S4-E5002-CON` with the notice reference, the case reference (DF-LEG-016), the delivery status, the callback date, the barcode where the contract asks for it and the rule ID it recorded; one hop, a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream. The operation name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1189; ASM-2136).
8. rwb-litigation evaluates R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 or R-LIT-09 on that fact, moves the case route state and answers; rwb-case starts or does not start the notice period behind its own durable timer. This service starts, stops and writes no timer and no case row, and it never evaluates a delivery rule itself.
9. The answer of the write operation returns the notice it wrote: state, delivery status, callback date and barcode, with the outcome of the hand-off.
10. A repeated request with the same notice, delivery status and callback date, or with the same Idempotency-Key, writes nothing on the notice and sends no second hand-off; the repeat is counted under R-UNI-40. Where the earlier hand-off did not complete, the repeat re-runs the hand-off only.
11. SCR-18 and SCR-19 read the notice state, the delivery status and the callback date from this service through the composite route, read only, next to the pack states of rwb-litigation and the case and timer of rwb-case.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The request carries no delivery status, or no callback date on a status that carries one | The answer is 422 and nothing is read beyond the validator; no decision record and no notice change | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The notice ID names no notice, or a notice outside the caller's scope | The answer is 404 and nothing is written; the caller cannot tell an out-of-scope notice from a missing one | None | AC4 |
| X3 | The notice is not in state Sent, or carries no `sent_date` | The answer is 409 and nothing changes; the proof of an undispatched notice is not recorded | None | AC4 |
| X4 | A barcode supplied with the proof is not the barcode of the notice | The answer is 409 and nothing changes; the mismatch is shown to the litigation officer team with the two barcodes | None | AC4 |
| X5 | A role without the Litigation right records or reads the proof | Refused before any read or write; nothing changes and no decision record is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | The local decision-record write fails | The transaction writes nothing: the notice keeps its state, its empty `delivery_status` and its empty `callback_date`, and no call leaves the service | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X7 | The same proof arrives twice for the same notice, or the same Idempotency-Key is replayed | One write and one hand-off; the repeat is counted under R-UNI-40 and no second decision record is written | None | AC5 |
| X8 | The S4 contract does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The notice keeps the proof it recorded, because that fact is true and this service's own; the hand-off is re-run when the request is repeated under the same key, and the caller sees status 503 with the platform error envelope; no message of this key's set applies to a downstream that did not answer (GAP-1189; ASM-2136) | None | AC3 |
| X9 | The S4 answer refuses the delivery fact (the case is not in the state the rule expects) | The notice keeps what it wrote, the refusal is recorded for the S4 owner and the caller reads the answer of the S4 contract unchanged; this service does not move the case itself and raises no message of its own set | None | AC3 |
| X10 | A component, a statement or a test reaches an ACE view, an ACE table or another `rwb_*` schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | BR6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against `RWB-S4-E5002-CON` and its fake; the decision-record library and the composite route are fakes until their platform stories publish (GAP-1190; ASM-2137) |
| Negotiable | The mapping of a delivery status to the notice state, the lists and the delivered-notice states are reference data with a version; the story fixes the behaviour, not the values |
| Valuable | The notice shows how and when it arrived, the officer stops chasing the post room, and the case and its timer move in the service that owns them |
| Estimable | Two operations, one validator, one mapper, one repository write, one library adapter, one client and one read-only screen fragment |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests, as the secondary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Each of the eight criteria of section 7 is one automated test; the cross-service answer is stubbed in the S4 contract fake |

The eight criteria are new under D-RCV-60 and test only the notice deliverable of this story. They assert nothing that belongs to another slice: the case route state, the notice-period timer and the notice-period task are `RWB-P3-E5002-APP`'s, the evaluation of R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 and the queue transfer of an unserved notice are `RWB-S4-E5002-APP`'s, and the cross-service journey is `RWB-ITG-E5002-ITG`'s. The four legacy criteria AC1 to AC4 of RWB-E5-002 are owned by the S4 slice and are not restated here; the three documents of this key use the same labels for different criteria, so a criterion is always quoted with its story ID (GAP-1193; ASM-2140).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The proof of delivery is a fact of the notice: the delivery status (DF-LEG-022) and the callback date (DF-LEG-021) are written on `notice` in `rwb_comms`, and the notice moves on its own lifecycle to Delivered or Unserved | TSD P6 T3.1; Architecture v5 slide 41 (P6 owns notices and proof of delivery); legacy RWB-E5-002 AC1 |
| BR2 | A delivered proof moves the notice to Delivered; a refused or undeliverable proof moves it to Unserved. The mapping of a LOV-DELIVERY value to the notice state is a reference row read with its version, never a constant | R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08; FSD P6 A2.2 AC-ALT-P6-002-01 and AC-ALT-P6-002-02; TSD P6 T3.2 (GAP-1192; ASM-2139) |
| BR3 | The case route state, the notice-period timer, the task of the notice period and the proof-window expiry are owned by rwb-case and rwb-litigation; rwb-comms writes no `recovery_case` row, no `timer` row and no `task` row, and it calls the S4 contract once per recorded proof | R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08; `ownership.json` (recovery_case, timer and task own P3); RWB-S4-E5002-CON |
| BR4 | The decision is recorded before the notice changes, with the rule ID the outcome belongs to and the version in force; a failed write changes nothing and the caller sees MSG-P7-003 | TSD P6 T2 ("writes the decision log entry before any change"); DP-03; legacy RWB-E5-002 AC1 and AC4 |
| BR5 | The same proof twice, or the same Idempotency-Key twice, writes once, sends no second hand-off and counts the repeat | R-UNI-40; FSD P6 A2.2 AC-EXC-P6-002-04 (the repeated request answers the first record) |
| BR6 | No ACE view and no ACE table is read or written here: the proof facts are the ones the caller supplies and the ones the S4 answer carries back, and the automatic `v_ace_pod` loop belongs to the Epic 1 and Epic 2 dispatch stories | DP-05; FSD P6 change note v3; Architecture v5 slide 17 (GAP-1194; ASM-2141) |
| BR7 | No person name, address or contact value enters `rwb_comms`, the decision record, a log or an event: the proof carries the notice reference, the case reference, the barcode, two list values and dates | TSD P6 T3.1 (notice carries no addressee); Template and Rules v1 section R7.2 (s17) |
| BR8 | A caller without the Litigation right is refused before any read or write, and nothing changes | TSD P6 T6.1; MSG-P4-002; legacy permission block of RWB-E5-002 |
| BR9 | The notice facts show on SCR-18 and SCR-19 through the gateway-bff composite route only; no screen calls an owner service directly and the screen model belongs to the edge contract | DP-19; legacy screen block of RWB-E5-002 (SCR-18 states "delivered; unserved") |
| BR10 | The service base is `/api/recovery/comms/v1` and the old monolith base is not served; the notice read keeps its legacy operation ID API-P6-002 | DP-13; TSD P6 T-A |
| R-LIT-07 | A notice whose proof of delivery is received is served: the proof is attached, the notice shows the delivery, and the notice period starts from `delivered_at` | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-07) |
| R-LIT-08 | A proof window that expires without proof marks the notice unserved, and the notice period does not start; the notice-period timer itself is not this story's | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-08); RWB-P3-E5002-APP |
| R-UNI-40 | The same event or the same proof twice produces one effect, and the repeat is counted | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-40); legacy TC-E5-002-01 |
| CTL-15 | A notice period starts only from the delivery date on the proof of delivery, never from the print date. This story writes the delivered date and hands it over; the timer is S4's and P3's, so the control holds on the fact, not on a clock here | RWB-E1-055 story and Build Notes (CTL-15); R-LIT-07 |

##### 9. State transitions

This story moves the notice state, not a case state. The notice moves on the lifecycle `state` column of the TSD P6 T3.0 standard columns, with the states the SCR-18 list names (generated; approved; sent; delivered; unserved):

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sent | A proof with delivery status `DELIVERED` is recorded | The notice has a `sent_date` and the callback date is present | Delivered, with `callback_date` and `delivery_status` written in one transaction |
| Sent | A proof with delivery status `REFUSED` or `UNDELIVERABLE` is recorded | The notice has a `sent_date` | Unserved, with the delivery status the proof carries and the callback date |
| Sent | A proof with delivery status `PENDING` is recorded | The status means the proof is not back yet | Refused: nothing changes and the caller is told the proof is not in (GAP-1192; ASM-2139) |
| Delivered or Unserved | The same proof is recorded again | Same delivery status and same callback date | Unchanged, and the repeat is counted |
| Generated, Approved or Held | A proof is recorded | The notice carries no `sent_date` | Refused with 409, because a notice that was not dispatched cannot be served |

The case route states of the legacy key are **not** this service's: `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` moves to `WITH_CUSTOMER_NOTICE_PERIOD` by R-LIT-07 or to `NOTICE_UNSERVED` by R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09, in rwb-litigation and rwb-case (`RWB-S4-E5002-APP`, `RWB-P3-E5002-APP`). Neither the case row nor the `NOTICE_PERIOD` timer row nor the durable timer inside the case workflow is read, written or asserted by this story; the hand-off on `RWB-S4-E5002-CON` is the only path by which the fact reaches them (GAP-1189; ASM-2136).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Litigation CRUA in the TSD P6 T6.1 matrix: records the proof on the notice, reads the notice and its delivery facts, and sees a barcode mismatch on the notice it records |
| RW-ENFORCE, enforcement owner | Litigation CRU: records the proof and reads the same facts in scope |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Litigation RA: reads the notice, its state and the delivery facts; records no proof |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Documents CRU and Litigation R: reads the notice state and the delivery facts on the case record |
| RW-HEADLIT, RW-PRODHEAD | Litigation RA: read only |
| RW-PHONECOL, phone collector | Litigation absent: refused on both operations with MSG-P4-002 |
| rwb-comms service identity | Validates the proof, writes the decision record, writes `callback_date`, `delivery_status` and the notice state, and calls the S4 operation; it holds no grant on another schema and no `v_ace_*` grant |
| rwb-litigation (S4) service identity | Evaluates R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 on the fact and answers; owns the legal action, the pack and the case move it announces |
| rwb-case (P3) service identity | Owns the case of record, its route state and the notice-period timer; it is not called by this story |

The rights above are the rows of TSD P6 T6.1 and nothing wider. DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set: the declared right on `GET /notices/{noticeId}` is Litigation R (TSD P6 T-A API-P6-002) and is enforced at gateway-bff for the screen path, and the right on the new write path is this story's design, because no source names a proof-record operation at all (GAP-1195; ASM-2142). A refusal keeps MSG-P4-002 and changes nothing.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity (owner) | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-LEG-015 | notice (P6, `rwb_comms`) | id | Read, as the notice reference of the answer and of the hand-off |
| DF-LEG-016 | notice (P6, `rwb_comms`) | case_id | Read, and sent on the hand-off as the case reference |
| DF-LEG-018 | notice (P6, `rwb_comms`) | notice_type | Read, for the context of the screens |
| DF-LEG-019 | notice (P6, `rwb_comms`) | sent_date | Read, as the condition that the notice was dispatched |
| DF-LEG-020 | notice (P6, `rwb_comms`) | barcode | Read, and matched against a barcode supplied with the proof |
| DF-LEG-021 | notice (P6, `rwb_comms`) | callback_date | Write |
| DF-LEG-022 | notice (P6, `rwb_comms`) | delivery_status | Write, against LOV-DELIVERY |
| Standard column | notice (P6, `rwb_comms`) | state | Write (Delivered or Unserved) |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (PLT library, created in `rwb_comms`) | rule id, rule version, inputs reference, outcome, decided at | Write through the local library, before the notice changes |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1189; ASM-2136) | the S4 answer | the outcome, the rule ID and the package version of the S4 evaluation | Read from the contract and stored nowhere: the notice keeps only its own columns |

Field IDs are those of the TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. **No new table, no new column and no migration**: `notice` and its columns arrive with RWB-P6-E1052-APP, this story writes three of them, and `idempotency_key` and `decision_record` are platform library objects created in `rwb_comms` by the library's own migration (DP-03). `recovery_case`, `timer`, `task` (P3), `decision_log_entry` (P7), `template` (P6, read only by the read operation), `document` (P5) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) are not created, not written and not read as tables: no foreign key leaves the schema and `notice.case_id` is an identifier, not a foreign key across schemas (DP-01, DP-05).

**No personal data.** The row this story writes carries identifiers, a barcode, two list values and two dates. The addressee, the address and the contact value never enter `rwb_comms`: they are held by rwb-source-data and used by the dispatch story's file build, and they are not logged here and not put on any message. The proof of delivery this story records is the returned result and its dates, not the scanned card or the letter image; a scanned proof is rwb-document's document and is not created by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-comms (P6); base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/notices/{noticeId}` | Read a notice with its serving facts: state, `notice_type`, `sent_date`, `barcode`, `callback_date` and `delivery_status` (TSD P6 T-A API-P6-002) | Litigation R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/notices/{noticeId}/proof-of-delivery` | Record the returned proof on the notice: the delivery status, the delivered or callback date and the barcode where it is supplied; write the decision record, the two columns and the notice state, and hand the fact to rwb-litigation | Litigation C on the notice, enforced at the edge | `Idempotency-Key` header required; a repeated key answers the first result and counts the repeat |

The read keeps the legacy operation ID API-P6-002 and is not redefined here; this story adds the serving fields to its answer. The write path, its request fields and its right are this story's design, because no source names a proof-record operation: the TSD P6 appendix T-A ends at API-P6-011 and none of the eleven operations records a proof (GAP-1195; ASM-2142). Errors: 401 no session; 403 no right (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown or out-of-scope notice; 409 a notice that was not dispatched, or a barcode that is not the notice's; 422 a missing field (MSG-GEN-001); 503 the decision-record library or the S4 contract unavailable. The answer carries the notice ID, the case ID, the state, the delivery status, the callback date, the barcode and the outcome of the hand-off.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| The proof-record operation, whose name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1189; ASM-2136) | `/api/recovery/litigation/v1` (path fixed by RWB-S4-E5002-CON) | S4 rwb-litigation (RWB-S4-E5002-CON) | Records the delivery fact of the notice reference and lets rwb-litigation evaluate R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 or R-LIT-09, move the case route state and start or withhold the notice period through rwb-case; one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020); built against the contract and its fake |

One operation is consumed and it is the only one: this service calls no case, access, document, source-data or decision operation in this story, and it composes no call chain. DP-11 is **not** in this story's pattern set, although a published interface is consumed, so the one-hop rule is stated here and the missing pattern row is recorded as GAP-1191 with ASM-2138.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. Architecture v5 slide 42 gives rwb-comms exactly three events on `rwb.comms.events.v1`, `NoticeGenerated`, `NoticeDispatched` and `NoticeDelivered`, and this story publishes none of them: the automatic WIN proof loop that reads the ACE rows and publishes `NoticeDelivered` is `RWB-P6-E2021-APP` and `RWB-P6-E1055-APP`, and the hand-off of this story is the S4 contract call, not an event. DP-09 is not in this story's pattern set, so no outbox row and no Kafka producer is added. The decision record is written through the local decision-record library of DP-03, and the library owns the relaying of its own record; this story declares no topic and no payload of its own.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The delivery fact arrives on the S4 answer and from the caller's request, so this story subscribes to no topic, holds no consumer and uses no inbox of its own. The notice state changes it reads for context come from its own `notice` row.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The proof is recorded in the request: one validator, one mapper, one library write, one row write and one contract call, with no workflow, no activity and no child workflow. `NoticeDispatchWorkflow` belongs to `RWB-P6-E1055-APP` and is untouched by this story, and no durable timer of any kind is created here.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. Nothing in this story runs on a schedule: the proof arrives when the returned post is recorded or when the S4 answer carries it, and no Job of Architecture v5 slide 44 is owned, moved or registered here. The WIN dispatch Schedule belongs to `RWB-P6-E1055-APP`.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| notice | P6 (rwb_comms) | The notice row and its serving fields `callback_date` (DF-LEG-021), `delivery_status` (DF-LEG-022) and `state` |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_comms` | The local hash-linked decision record of the delivery outcome (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_comms` | The key of the write operation and the hand-off outcome it holds |

Not owned and never read as a table: `recovery_case`, `timer`, `task` (P3), `legal_action`, `hearing` (S4), `decision_log_entry` (P7), `document` and `signature_request` (P5), `template` and `merge_field` (P6, read by the read operation only). No `v_ace_*` view and no ACE table is read here: the proof facts come from the caller and from the S4 answer (DP-01, DP-05).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-litigation contract fake (RWB-S4-E5002-CON) | The delivery answer applied with rule `R-LIT-07` and the package version for notice `N-0101` and case `RC-2026-000321`; the answer applied with `R-LIT-08` for an unserved notice; a refusal for a case that is not in the state the rule expects; no answer beyond 2 s; an unreadable answer | AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4 |
| Local decision-record library fake (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON) | One record of the delivery outcome with the rule ID and the version in force; a refused write on the failure path | AC5, AC6 |
| LOV-DELIVERY and mapping fake | `DELIVERED`, `REFUSED`, `UNDELIVERABLE` and `PENDING` at their version, with the mapping row of each to the notice state and its version | AC1, AC2, AC4 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-18 and SCR-19 answer for case `RC-2026-000321`, with the notice facts of this service read once | AC8 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT; the drift between a fake and the baseline is a build failure in the S4 contract.

| Kafka | None | No event published and none consumed by this story (12.3, 12.4) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms`, module `noticeproof`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms.noticeproof`; front end `src/modules/recovery/comms/NoticeProof.tsx`, the fragment SCR-18 and SCR-19 embed, read only.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 applies only as a prohibition: no component of this story reads an ACE view, an ACE table or `account_ext`, and the proof facts are the ones the caller supplies. The FSD P6 change note of v3 and its A2.2 criteria read `v_ace_pod` in process; that read is the automatic WIN loop of `RWB-P6-E2021-APP` and `RWB-P6-E1055-APP`, which is where it is built, and the difference is recorded as GAP-1194 with ASM-2141. DP-13 keeps the read on API-P6-002 and puts the new write on the service base. DP-19 covers the two screens only, and the screen model and the merge order stay with the edge contract.

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds two H rows, `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` for DP-03 and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` for DP-19, while the plan's `Depends on (build)` list for this story is None. The metadata table keeps the plan's list as it is, the story builds against the two fakes until those platform contract stories publish, and the absence is recorded as GAP-1190 with ASM-2137. DP-11 is absent from the pattern set although one operation is consumed, and that is recorded as GAP-1191 with ASM-2138.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| NoticeProofController | Controller | `POST /notices/{noticeId}/proof-of-delivery` and the serving fields of `GET /notices/{noticeId}`, with the problem mapping for 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 |
| ProofOfDeliveryValidator | Service | The notice exists in scope and is Sent, the status is a list value, the callback date is present where the status carries one, and a supplied barcode is the notice's |
| DeliveryOutcomeMapper | Service | Resolves the notice state from the delivery status through the mapping row in force; holds no value itself |
| ProofDecisionRecordWriter | Library adapter | Writes the decision record with the rule ID and the version in force before any change, hash-linked, and refuses the request when the write fails (DP-03) |
| NoticeDeliveryWriter | Repository | Writes `callback_date`, `delivery_status` and `state` in one `rwb_comms` transaction, with the idempotency row |
| S4DeliveryClient | Client | The proof-record call on `RWB-S4-E5002-CON`, one hop, 2 s, breaker, and no retry of its own (GAP-1189) |
| ProofIdempotency | Service | Builds the key from the notice ID, the delivery status and the callback date, recognises a repeat and re-runs only an incomplete hand-off |
| NoticeProof | React component | Shows the notice state, the delivery status, the callback date and the barcode on SCR-18 and SCR-19, read only, with the refusal states |

**Database and migrations.** No Flyway file. `notice` and its serving columns arrive with RWB-P6-E1052-APP, and the decision record and the idempotency key are library objects created in `rwb_comms` by the library's migration (DP-03). No column of another service's data is added, and no index is needed beyond the ones RWB-P6-E1052-APP and RWB-P6-E1055-APP create (the primary key of `notice` and its barcode index).

**Configuration and reference data.**

- The mapping of a LOV-DELIVERY value to the notice state, and the states a notice may be served from (Sent), as versioned reference rows of the business, read with their version. `PENDING` has no state mapping in any source (GAP-1192; ASM-2139).
- The LOV-DELIVERY list at its version in force (TSD P6 T3.2). The contract the list is read on and the owner of the mapping row are Not specified for this story, because the reference-data contract is not in its dependency rows (GAP-1192; ASM-2139).
- No parameter is named in the sources for the write path; the 2 s budget and the single hop are the platform rule of ADR-020 and not a value of this story.

**Build steps**

1. Build `ProofOfDeliveryValidator` over the `notice` row with the list and state checks; test AC4 and AC7.
2. Build `DeliveryOutcomeMapper` over the mapping row and its version; test AC1 and AC2.
3. Build `ProofDecisionRecordWriter` against the library fake, with the failed-write path; test AC6.
4. Build `NoticeDeliveryWriter` with the one transaction and the idempotency row; test AC5.
5. Build `S4DeliveryClient` against the contract fake, with the 2 s budget, the breaker, the no-answer path and the refusal path; test AC3.
6. Build `NoticeProofController` with the problem mapping of 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503; test AC4 and AC7.
7. Build `NoticeProof` and read the notice through the composite route fake; test AC8.
8. Add the boundary test: no statement outside `rwb_comms`, no `v_ace_*` read, no write to `rwb_case`, `rwb_litigation` or `rwb_decision`; test BR6.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.comms.notice-proof-v1`, read as a flag of the platform library; off means the write path answers 404 and the serving fields of the read are empty, while the automatic WIN loop of `RWB-P6-E2021-APP` is unaffected.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the contract tests of `RWB-S4-E5002-CON` stay green, the boundary test runs in the pipeline, and a SIT week shows one proof per notice, one hand-off per proof, no notice served twice, no write of a case row or a timer row from this service and no `v_ace_*` read in its logs.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S4-001 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names a missing item of the litigation pack, which is the pack of the S4 slice, so no path of this story raises it | The pack is missing {item}. Add it before filing. |
| MSG-S4-002 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names the expiry of the claim on the case, which is S4's fact and S4's screen text, so no path of this story raises it | The claim on this case expires on {date}. File before then. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A request with no delivery status, or with no callback date on a status that carries one (X1) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Litigation right records or reads the proof (X5, AC7) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the notice changes (X6, AC6) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The five texts are the legacy wording of RWB-E5-002 section 14 and are copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new message is added. `MSG-GEN-001` is displayed with the field it names ("delivery status", "callback date"). `MSG-S4-001` and `MSG-S4-002` are authored by the litigation module and belong to the pack and the claim of the S4 slice (`RWB-S4-E5002-APP`); they are carried here because they are the message set of the key, and this story raises neither of them. A downstream that does not answer (X8) and a notice that is not found (X2) carry no message of this set, and the platform error envelope is displayed as it is.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built in this story. Two existing surfaces show what it writes, read through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19):

| Screen | State | What the user sees or does |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Loading | The placeholder while the composite route answers |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Sent | The notice with its `sent_date`, `barcode` and notice type, and the proof form to record the delivery result, the delivered date and the barcode |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Delivered | The notice state "delivered", the delivery status `DELIVERED`, the callback date and the barcode, read only |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Unserved | The notice state "unserved" with the delivery status of the proof, and the reason the case moved is shown from the S4 side |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Incomplete | The proof refused with MSG-GEN-001 naming the missing field, and nothing changed |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Not dispatched | The proof refused with 409 because the notice has no sent date |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Not recorded | The decision record could not be written, MSG-P7-003, and nothing changed |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Refused | A role without the Litigation right reads MSG-P4-002 and nothing changes |
| SCR-19 Litigation workspace | Pack and notice | The same notice facts, read only, next to the pack states of rwb-litigation and the case and timers of rwb-case |

The route merges the answer of this service with rwb-litigation and rwb-case; the route path, the screen-model field list and the merge order belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the edge stories, not here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the mapping of a delivery status to the notice state, the states a notice may be served from, the lists and the message texts are data with a version; no role, list value, state name or date appears in Java.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow inputs or prompts: the notice row carries identifiers, dates, a barcode and list values only; the addressee, the address and the contact value never enter `rwb_comms` and are never logged, and the proof image is rwb-document's and is not created here.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: no component of this story reads an ACE view or an ACE table, and the service holds no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-05).
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema join: `recovery_case`, `timer`, `task`, `decision_log_entry`, `document` and every S4 table are reached only through their owners' contracts (DP-01).
- One hop and a 2 s budget on the single consumed call, with a breaker per downstream and no call chain; the retry of the hand-off is the repeat of the same idempotency key and never a silent resend.
- The decision is never recorded after the effect: the record is written first through the library, and a failed write stops the request (DP-03, MSG-P7-003).
- No event, no topic, no outbox row and no timer: this story publishes nothing and consumes nothing, and the notice facts reach the other services on the S4 contract only.
- The two screens are read only and write nothing; SCR-18 posts the proof through the one write operation and SCR-19 is a read.

- The legal action, the pack, the evaluation of R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09, the proof-window expiry and the queue transfer of an unserved notice: rwb-litigation (S4), `RWB-S4-E5002-APP`; the proof-record operation and its shape: `RWB-S4-E5002-CON`.
- The four legacy criteria of RWB-E5-002 proved end to end across the three services: `RWB-ITG-E5002-ITG`.
- The automatic WIN proof-of-delivery loop that reads the ACE rows and publishes `NoticeDelivered`, and the dispatch and acknowledgment fields it writes: `RWB-P6-E2021-APP` and `RWB-P6-E1055-APP`.
- Notice generation, the notice read baseline as a contract, and the template and merge-field catalog: `RWB-P6-E1052-APP`, `RWB-P6-E1055-CON` and `RWB-P6-E1046-APP`.
- The ACE ingestion of the proof file, the `v_ace_pod` rows, the freshness stamp and the interaction ledger: rwb-source-data (`RWB-P1-E1055-APP`, `RWB-P1-E1066-CON`).
- The scanned proof card, its custody and its retention: rwb-document (P5).
- The rights, roles, scope and masking data themselves, and the full screen model of SCR-18 and SCR-19: the rwb-access stories and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON`.
- The deployment of this capability, its flag, its dashboards, its alerts and its runbook: its own OPS story.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E5-002 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **the delivery answer of a notice applied to the case — the case moved to the notice period and its timer started from the delivery date when the proof of delivery is in, or the notice marked unserved when the proof window has expired — with the rule and the rule version recorded on a decision record**, so that **the notice period is counted from the day the customer actually received the notice, a notice nobody could serve is visible as such, and the pack is complete when the case goes to court**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A statutory notice only starts its clock when it has been served. The legacy story wrote the delivery confirmation onto the case and started the notice period from the delivery date, because a period counted from the dispatch date can expire before the customer had the notice, and a period never started leaves a case stuck in the litigation route with an incomplete pack. When nobody could serve the notice, the legacy story marked it unserved and did not start the period. The FSD S4 module measures exactly this: a litigation turnaround target of 6 days against 21 days to file today, with incomplete packs and untracked law firm progress as the problem (FSD S4 A2.2.1).

In the target the same journey is cut across three services. **rwb-comms (P6)** owns the notice, the notice template, the merge fields and the proof of delivery itself — the ownership map and the Architecture v5 slide 41 row name exactly those four things for P6, and slide 17 gives P6 the `rwb_comms` schema with notices and proof of delivery (DP-01). **rwb-litigation (S4)** owns the legal action, the pack and the evaluation of rules R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 on the notice fact, and answers the delivery outcome through its own contract on `/api/recovery/litigation/v1`. **rwb-case (P3)** owns the case of record: it holds the case state, starts and shows the notice-period timer, places the task of the notice period, and writes the local decision record that names the rule and the rule version in force, in the same transaction as the state change (DP-03). This story is the rwb-case slice: it applies the delivery fact it receives through the S4 contract, performs the R-LIT-07 transition on a delivery, the R-LIT-08 or R-LIT-09 transition when the notice was not served, creates or does not create the notice-period timer with its durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow, and publishes the state change.

The split is what keeps the three services independent. rwb-case stores three facts of the case — the notice reference, the delivery date and the outcome — and never the notice row, the proof document or the barcode: it holds no foreign key into `rwb_comms` and reads no notice table, which is the DP-01 rule stated as an acceptance criterion. Proof of delivery itself and the notice stay with P6, the legal action stays with S4, and the legacy in-process write of the delivery confirmation is replaced by one contract answer on one side and one `rwb_case` transaction with its outbox rows on the other. The legacy legal-action and notice-approval operations of the monolith keep their owners: they are served on `/api/recovery/litigation/v1` and `/api/recovery/comms/v1` (DP-13), and no operation of this story is added (DP-19 covers only the screen read through gateway-bff).

No ACE view is read here. The legacy data table of RWB-E5-002 lists the `v_ace_customer` view (DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074); in the target the customer attributes travel inside the S4 answer when a rule needs them, and rwb-case reads no `v_ace_*` view for this step (DP-05 resolves to the owner's contract, not to a direct ACE read).

The legacy story master of the Epics 3 to 8 set carries no requirement ID for RWB-E5-002: the entry has the feature, the module, the data table, the endpoints, the screens, the rights and the test cases, but no REQ identifier (GAP-0737; ASM-1326). Traceability therefore runs to feature FEAT-LIT-02, to rules R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 and to the test cases until the Epics 3 to 8 PRDs add the requirement IDs.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S4-E5002-CON is published: the delivery-answer resource shape (the notice reference, `deliveredAt`, the proof-window outcome, the rule ID and the package version of the S4 evaluation), its operation on `/api/recovery/litigation/v1`, its error envelope and its contract fake. This story builds against that contract and its fake and never against a notice table (DP-01).
- The `rwb_case` schema baseline and the case of record exist from the Epic 1 case story (RWB-P3-E1018-APP): `recovery_case`, `task`, `timer`, `queue` and the outbox, inbox and idempotency objects.
- The local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` are published by the platform contract story of DP-03; the workflow kit that holds a durable timer inside a workflow is published by the platform contract story of DP-10. Those platform dependencies are held by the platform stories and are not repeated in the metadata rows.
- A litigation rule package version is IN_FORCE on the business date and carries the rows R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 with their `action_text`, `owner_role` and `timer_spec`, and the version has the passing scenarios and the approval its governance requires. The package code that carries the three rows is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0737; ASM-1327); the story reads the version in force from the rwb-decision registry on every evaluation and names no code.
- The notice-period duration is in force as a SERVICE_LEVEL reference row of the rwb-case reference data, read through the reference-data contract of the service (DP-07). The reference row code and its value are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0737; ASM-1323).
- The case is in route state `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` with a notice reference that P6 dispatched and reported through NoticeDispatched (EV-14), which is what makes the S4 answer addressable by the notice reference.
- The rwb-access guard library is published by the platform contract story of DP-08 and answers the Litigation R right and the caller's scope.
- The login is the rwb-case login (DP-02).

##### 4. Flow

1. The legal stage runs as LitigationWorkflow, the child workflow on task queue `rwb-litigation` started by CaseWorkflow. When the stage has a delivery answer for the notice of the case, it signals CaseWorkflow on `rwb-case` with the case ID and the notice reference. The hand-over direction between the two services is the direction recorded in GAP-0737: the contract names the answer, and the parent receives only the reference, so the answer itself is read once, by the service that owns the case.
2. CaseWorkflow runs its single step, EvaluateAndApply, on task queue `rwb-case`. The step calls the RWB-S4-E5002-CON operation inside the workflow kit activity with one hop, a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11), and the call is recorded in the workflow history, so a replay reuses the recorded answer and never re-evaluates.
3. The answer names the notice reference, `deliveredAt` or the expiry of the proof window, the outcome and the rule ID with the package version of the S4 evaluation. A field that the contract marks as required and that is missing is a refusal: the step writes nothing and reports the field through MSG-GEN-001.
4. The step builds the idempotency key from the case ID, the notice reference and the answer (the delivery date, or the proof-window expiry). A key that `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` already hold is dropped: no state move, no second timer row and no second event, which is the inbox rule of DP-09.
5. A delivery answer moves the case from `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` to `WITH_CUSTOMER_NOTICE_PERIOD` by R-LIT-07 (`PROOF_OF_DELIVERY_RECEIVED`, `served_result = delivered`): the notice period starts at `deliveredAt`, and the timer row carries `timer_type` of the notice period, `started_at` = `deliveredAt` and `expires_at` = `deliveredAt` plus the duration of the SERVICE_LEVEL reference row.
6. A proof-window expiry answer moves the case from `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` to `NOTICE_UNSERVED` by R-LIT-08 (`PROOF_WINDOW_EXPIRED`): the notice is marked unserved with its reason, no notice-period timer row is written and no timer is started. A served result of refused, returned or undeliverable takes the same end by R-LIT-09 (`DELIVERY_FAILED`), also without a timer.
7. EvaluateAndApply writes, in one `rwb_case` transaction: the case state `route_state`, the `rule_version` of the move, the notice reference, the delivery date and the outcome (`served_result`) on `recovery_case`; the timer row on the delivery path only; the task of the notice period when the fired rule row names a timer spec; the local decision record with the rule ID (R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 or R-LIT-09) and the package version; and the outbox rows CaseStateChanged and DecisionRecorded (DP-03, DP-09). A failed write rolls the whole transaction back, so neither the state nor the timer moves.
8. The workflow signals CaseWorkflow with the expiry of the notice period and holds it as a durable timer of the workflow kit (DP-10): the workflow ID is the case ID, so exactly one timer per case is open at a time in the namespace `rwb-recovery`. When the timer passes, the workflow raises TimerBreached through its own state; this story creates and holds the timer and does not own the breach (RWB-P3-E1028-APP).
9. A repeat of the same notice reference and the same delivery date, or of the same expiry answer, is dropped in step 4. The case keeps its state, its expiry and its single decision record.
10. Litigation officer: SCR-18 Notice approval and SCR-19 Litigation workspace read the case through the gateway-bff composite route, which calls rwb-case `GET /cases/{caseId}` and `GET /cases/{caseId}/timers` and merges the two answers (DP-19). The notice row itself, its states and the proof are served by rwb-comms; the pack states are served by rwb-litigation. The rwb-case fragment shows the case state and the notice-period end, read only, and shows "unserved" with its reason.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The S4 answer does not arrive within 2 seconds or the service is unavailable | The step keeps the case in `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` and raises no timer and no decision record; the workflow retries the activity with the kit's retry policy and the answer is read again | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1, AC2 |
| X2 | The S4 answer cannot be read (an unreadable envelope or a missing required field) | Nothing is written; the breach is recorded for the S4 owner and the case stays in `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X3 | No litigation rule package version is IN_FORCE on the business date | `NoPackageInForce`; no state move, no timer row and no decision record; the case is placed in the exception queue for role RW-TEAMMGR | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X4 | The local decision-record write fails | The transaction rolls back: the state, the notice columns and the timer do not move, the step fails, and the answer is retried | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X5 | The same notice reference and the same answer arrive twice | The second arrival is dropped by the inbox and the idempotency key; no second state change, no second timer row and no second event | None | AC4 |
| X6 | A delivery date arrives for a case that is not in `NOTICE_DISPATCHED` | The transition is refused; the case keeps its state and the arrival is recorded as an exception with the state it found | None | AC1 |
| X7 | A role without the Litigation R right reads the case | Refused before any read; nothing is returned and nothing is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC7 |
| X8 | A case outside the caller's scope is read | The response is 404, so the caller cannot tell an out-of-scope case from a case that does not exist | MSG-P4-003 | AC7 |

A served result of refused, returned or undeliverable is not an exception: R-LIT-09 marks the notice unserved exactly as R-LIT-08 does and the served-result values come from the FSD S4 A2.2 rule table, not from code.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on Day 1 against the RWB-S4-E5002-CON fake and the platform kits; no work order sits inside another team's lane, and the notice row and the proof are out of the lane by design |
| Negotiable | The notice-period duration, the rule rows, the package version in force and the timer type are rows and reference data; the story fixes the behaviour, not the values |
| Valuable | The notice period is counted from the day the notice was served, an unserved notice is visible with its reason, and every move carries the rule and the version that made it |
| Estimable | One step, one client, one validator, one repository, one transaction, one durable timer and one read-only screen fragment |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each of the eight criteria of section 7 is one automated test; the cross-service answer is stubbed in the S4 contract fake |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

