**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of the pack-recovery step of rwb-litigation, split from RWB-E5-006. It fixes the two legal-action operations the legacy story names on `/api/recovery/litigation/v1` (DP-13), the recovery element and the outcome vocabulary `DOCUMENT_UNRECOVERABLE` and `PRESCRIPTION_WARNING` of R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20 with `DOCUMENT_RETRIEVED` as the hand-back value of the sibling R-LIT-18, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the error envelope, the consumed checklist and case-document reads of rwb-document (P5), the case-move answer of rwb-case and the decision-record element of DP-03. The document stays with rwb-document and no `document` property is declared here (GAP-2760; ASM-4594); the recovery element, the reason list and the case-move operation name have no source specification and are carried with the placeholder (GAP-2761; ASM-4595); the CCMS path has no owner in the target (GAP-2764; ASM-4598). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the pack-recovery step of rwb-litigation — the two legal-action operations on `/api/recovery/litigation/v1`, the recovery element and its outcome vocabulary, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the error envelope, the consumed checklist and case-document facts of rwb-document, the case-move answer of rwb-case, the decision-record element, the tables and the fakes**, so that **the app story, the screen and the tests of this legacy key build against one fixed, testable contract on Day 1 and a document type, an outcome value, a reason or an answer shape can never drift between rwb-litigation, rwb-document and rwb-case without a failing build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy step of RWB-E5-006 crossed three boundaries at once: an officer screen, a document row of the pack, and a case state. The target splits them: the document, the checklist item and the custody of the file are rwb-document's (P5), the case of record and its route states stay with rwb-case (P3), and the pack-recovery decision and the legal action it repairs stay with rwb-litigation (S4). Each boundary is now a contract that another team builds against, so each has to be fixed before the app story starts: the two operations, the recovery element, the outcome vocabulary of the three rules, the facts the P5 contract answers, the case-move answer and the record of the decision.

The baseline also fixes the naming that the checks require: schema `rwb_litigation`, base `/api/recovery/litigation/v1`, topic `rwb.litigation.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-litigation` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.litigation` (Architecture v5 slide 41 notes). It records that rwb-litigation holds no `v_ace_*` grant and no grant on `rwb_document` or any other `rwb_*` schema (Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41), so DP-05 is declared as a prohibition and the document facts are consumed on the owner's contract only. It records that the three catalogue events of the service — `LawsuitFiled`, `JudgmentRecorded` and `AuctionResult` — belong to the filing, the judgment and the auction result, so this baseline declares no event (GAP-2763; ASM-4597).

Three points are carried as gaps and assumptions rather than decided quietly: the three consumed contracts of the step have no C row and the plan's contract row is None (GAP-2760), the recovery element, the reason list of R-LIT-19 and the fields that would hold them have no field list in any source (GAP-2761), and the CCMS path of the FSD integration points has no owner in the target (GAP-2764). The boundary with the sibling story is fixed too: the defect check and its re-run on a supplied item are RWB-S4-E5005-APP's, so this baseline fixes only the unrecoverable and prescription outcomes and the hand-back value of R-LIT-18.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the queue and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the pagination and filter convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline (Architecture v5 slide 11); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The ownership of the objects is taken from the Ownership Map only: `legal_action` and `hearing` are S4's, `document` and `document_checklist_item` are P5's, `recovery_case` is P3's, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are P7's. This document never declares another service's operation as provided.
- The two P5 operations are the published surface of their owner stories: `GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist` (API-P5-008) of RWB-P5-E1040-APP and `GET /cases/{caseId}/documents` (API-P5-002) of RWB-P5-E1026-APP. No P5 contract story carries either as a baseline, so both are class C dependencies in fact and the contract-dependency row here is None (GAP-2760; ASM-4594).
- The case-move answer of rwb-case is fixed here as a shape only; no source names a published operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage, and the name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2760; ASM-4594).
- The LITIGATION rule package, its rows for R-LIT-18, R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20 and the Head of Litigation approval are governed in rwb-decision (P7); this baseline names them and declares none of them. R-LIT-18 is evaluated by RWB-S4-E5005-APP and its outcome value is declared here only as the hand-back of a supplied item.
- The `legal_action` and `hearing` tables and their columns arrive with the DB story of this service; this baseline declares shapes and creates no table, no column and no migration.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-litigation for this step: the two operations with their request and answer elements, the recovery element, the rights and the seven error responses.
2. Fix the recovery element: the case reference, the legal action reference, the checklist item by its `LOV-DOC-TYPE` document type, the outcome value, the reason where the item is unrecoverable, the rule ID, the package version and the decided-at time.
3. Fix the consumed document facts of the P5 contract: the checklist read with its version and item counts, and the case document page, and mark the fields the sources do not give with the placeholder.
4. Fix the case-move answer of rwb-case: the move `PACK_VERIFIED`, the rule ID, the version and the decided-at time, with no case row read or written here, and record that `PACK_ASSEMBLY` is the sibling story's move.
5. Record the decision-record element of DP-03 on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, written before the case-move answer.
6. Record the closed vocabulary of the outcome values and of the hand-back, and the rule that no list value is a constant of the code.
7. Publish the contract tables of section 12 and the five contract fakes.
8. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the additive rule, the vocabulary, the shapes, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the error envelope, the absence of a `v_ace_*` read and of a `document` or `recovery_case` write, and the drift between a fake and the document.
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-S4-E5006-APP, SCR-19 and the wave 3 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body or a request body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 400 or 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC2 |
| X2 | A field is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC7 |
| X4 | The consumed document fact or the case-move answer has a field list the sources do not give | The row carries the placeholder, the gap and the assumption, and the fake is derived from the published document | None | AC3, AC4 |
| X5 | An outcome value outside the ones the rules name appears in the document or in an example | The vocabulary test fails the build | None | AC1, AC8 |
| X6 | The document declares another service's operation as provided, a `v_ace_*` view, a `document` row or a `recovery_case` row | The review fails the baseline; the boundary test fails the build | None | AC8 |
| X7 | A POST is repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key` | The stored answer is returned and no second effect is described | None | AC2, AC5 |
| X8 | The rights of an operation are not the ones TSD S4 T-A.1 declares | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the Ownership Map and the published P5 document surfaces and the rwb-case answer only |
| Negotiable | The element names beyond the ones the sources give, the example values and the fake fixtures are settled in the baseline review; the operations, the outcome values, the base, the topic and the queue are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks RWB-S4-E5006-APP, SCR-19 and the wave 3 harness on Day 1, and the rwb-document and rwb-case teams on the same day |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, one AsyncAPI fragment that declares no event, nine contract tables, five fakes and four new contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the pack-recovery step of rwb-litigation

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the ownership of legal_action and hearing is S4, of document and document_checklist_item is P5 and of recovery_case is P3
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 The two legal-action operations are declared with the recovery element and the outcome vocabulary (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-litigation is published with this change
    When it is validated against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-actions with the LegalAction answer of status 201 and GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId} with the LegalAction answer of status 200, both under the base /api/recovery/litigation/v1 and owned by rwb-litigation
    Then the recovery answer declares the outcome against the rule vocabulary with the values DOCUMENT_UNRECOVERABLE and PRESCRIPTION_WARNING of R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20, and DOCUMENT_RETRIEVED of R-LIT-18 as the hand-back to RWB-S4-E5005-APP
    Then every other property of the LegalAction element is copied from the baseline of the legal action and is not redefined here
    Then the document type of the checklist item is declared against LOV-DOC-TYPE and the action type against LOV-LEGAL-TYPE, with no list value written in the document as a constant of the consumer

  Scenario: AC2 The recovery element and its answer are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the recovery section of the baseline
    When it is compared with the pack-recovery step of RWB-S4-E5006-APP
    Then the recovery element carries the case reference, the legal action reference, the checklist item by its LOV-DOC-TYPE document type, the outcome value and the reason where the outcome is DOCUMENT_UNRECOVERABLE
    Then its answer carries the same item, the outcome, the rule ID, the package version in force, the case move the rule names and the decided-at time, and no case state
    Then the POST declares the Idempotency-Key header and its stored answer, and the GET declares neither

    Then the element names of the recovery element and of its reason that no source gives are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2761; ASM-4595) and the document marks them so

  Scenario: AC3 The consumed document facts of rwb-document are declared and the document stays there (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed rows of the baseline
    When they are compared with API-P5-008 and API-P5-002 of P5 rwb-document
    Then the case checklist is declared as consumed from P5, with its checklist version and each item with its document type against LOV-DOC-TYPE, its required flag and its present count
    Then the documents of the case are declared as consumed from P5, paged with type, page and size, each with its identifier, its document type and its stored date, and no field value and no content
    Then the document declares no document property, no storage reference, no retention class and no write-once flag, and no write of a document row from rwb-litigation
    Then the retrieval request of a missing item is named as rwb-document's and is not declared as an operation of this service
    Then every call on the two rows is one hop with a 2 s budget, a breaker and no retry of its own (DP-11, ADR-020)

  Scenario: AC4 The case-move answer is declared and the case row is never written here (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the case boundary of the baseline
    When it is compared with rwb-case as the owner of recovery_case and of the route states
    Then the case move is declared as an answer to rwb-case with the move PACK_VERIFIED, the rule ID, the package version and the decided-at time
    Then the move PACK_ASSEMBLY is named as RWB-S4-E5005-APP's and not as a move of this step
    Then the document declares no recovery_case property, no case route-state column and no write of a case row from rwb-litigation
    Then the answer carries the stage outcome that the parent CaseWorkflow applies, and the operation name of a REST case-move call for another caller is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2760; ASM-4594)
    Then the states PACK_ASSEMBLY, PACK_DEFECT_HOLD and PACK_VERIFIED are named as the case of record's and are read from its answer only

  Scenario: AC5 The Idempotency-Key rule, the error envelope and the rights are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error and access sections of the baseline
    When they are compared with TSD S4 T-A.1 and T-A.2 and with TSD S4 T6.1
    Then the operations answer 400 for a malformed request, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409 on a closed, withdrawn or wrong-state action, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503 when a downstream does not answer, each with one envelope and one message ID per condition
    Then POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-actions declares Litigation right C and GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId} declares Litigation right R, each with the scope applied
    Then RW-LITOFF holds Litigation CRUA, RW-ENFORCE holds CRU, RW-LEGAL and RW-PRODHEAD and RW-HEADLIT hold RA, PT-LAWFIRM holds RU and every other role of TSD S4 T6.1 holds R
    Then a repeated POST with the same Idempotency-Key returns the stored answer and describes no second effect

  Scenario: AC6 The decision-record element is declared and written before the change (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision section of the baseline
    When it is compared with the local decision-record library of DP-03
    Then one decision record is declared per rule outcome with the case reference, the legal action reference, the document type of the item, the outcome, the reason where the item is unrecoverable, the rule ID, the package version in force and the decided-at time
    Then the record is written through the library on the shared rwb.decision-record.v1 before the case-move answer, and a failed write leaves the case unchanged with MSG-P7-003
    Then the document declares no event of its own for the record and no second topic for this capability
    Then the record carries IDs, codes, dates and a rule version only

  Scenario: AC7 The five contract fakes answer the document (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fakes of the baseline
    When each is compared with the operation or the element it serves
    Then the rwb-document checklist fake answers the checklist of case "RC-2026-000606" at its version with one item of LOV-DOC-TYPE missing, a checklist with every item present, a case with no checklist and no answer beyond 2 s
    Then the rwb-document document-page fake answers the stored documents of the case paged, with the item absent and with the item present after retrieval
    Then the rwb-case fake answers the case state PACK_DEFECT_HOLD and an accepted and a refused move
    Then the rwb-decision rule-package fake answers the LITIGATION package at its version with R-LIT-18, R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20 and one approval answer
    Then the decision-record library stub answers a healthy chain and a stopped chain
    Then the drift test compares every fake with the document and fails the build on any difference

  Scenario: AC8 The naming baseline and the no-v_ace_ boundary are fixed and no cross-schema read is declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the naming and data sections of the baseline
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner from the Ownership Map, with None where the element is empty
    Then the schema is rwb_litigation, the login is rwb_litigation, the topic is rwb.litigation.events.v1, the queue is rwb-litigation and the Java package is th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.litigation
    Then the tables named as owned are legal_action read only and the library objects decision_record and idempotency_key, and document, document_checklist_item, recovery_case, decision_log_entry, rule_row and hearing are named as other owners' or another story's and are consumed only through their contracts
    Then the document declares no read of a v_ace_* view and no grant on rwb_document, rwb_case or any other rwb_* schema, and the boundary test fails a build that adds one
    Then the document declares no event published, no event consumed and no Schedule for this step, and the absence test fails a build that adds one
```

These eight criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only. They restate no business outcome owned by RWB-S4-E5006-APP and they copy no criterion of the legacy story, whose two criteria stay with the app story word for word.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The pack-recovery decision and the legal action it repairs are rwb-litigation's, and the contract declares their elements on the two operations only | Architecture v5 slide 41; Ownership Map (legal_action and hearing owner S4); TSD S4 T-A.1 |
| BR2 | The decision record is declared as an element written before the case-move answer, through the local library on the shared topic; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; TSD S4 T2; legacy RWB-E5-006 AC1 and AC2 |
| BR3 | The document stays with rwb-document: the contract declares the checklist read and the case document page as consumed, names the retrieval request as P5's, declares no `document` property and describes no custody, retention or write-once fact of rwb-litigation | Ownership Map (`document` owner P5); Architecture v5 slide 41; GAP-2760 |
| BR4 | The case move is answered and not written: the contract declares the answer that carries `PACK_VERIFIED` and declares no `recovery_case` property and no case row write; `PACK_ASSEMBLY` is the sibling story's move | Ownership Map (`recovery_case` owner P3); Architecture v5 slide 41; GAP-2760 |
| BR5 | No ACE view and no ACE table is read: this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and no grant on `rwb_document` or `rwb_case` | DP-05; Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41 |
| BR6 | A POST declares the `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer; a GET declares none | Architecture v5 slide 11; TSD S4 T-A.2 |
| BR7 | The vocabulary is closed: the outcome values are those of R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20 and the hand-back value is R-LIT-18's, and `LOV-DOC-TYPE`, `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` and `LOV-LEGAL-STATUS` are published as enumerated reference values, never as constants of the code | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; TSD S4 T3.2; BR-S4-006 (FSD S4 A2.6.3.1) |
| BR8 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, a document type code, a reason code, dates and a rule version only | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes; Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR9 | One REST base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; the document never declares another service's base or topic as its own | DP-13, DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR10 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR11 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-litigation; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | Ownership Map; DP-11 |
| BR12 | The rule rows of R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20 and the Head of Litigation approval are governed in rwb-decision and named here, never declared here; the defect check and its re-run are RWB-S4-E5005-APP's and are not restated | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; GAP-2760 |

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of this document, not of a case:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The two operations, the vocabulary, the consumed rows and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, SCR-19, the wave 3 harness and the rwb-document, rwb-case and rwb-decision owners accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example a new error code | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or an outcome value changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | The absence test of AC8 fails: a `v_ace_*` view, a `document` or `recovery_case` property, a second topic or a Schedule | In review |

The route states the document describes are the case of record's: `PACK_ASSEMBLY`, `PACK_DEFECT_HOLD` and `PACK_VERIFIED` are read from the rwb-case answer, and this baseline fixes only the one move the two rules name and moves no case.

| Recovery element | The case reference, the legal action reference, the checklist item by its `document_type` against `LOV-DOC-TYPE` (DF-DOC-004), the outcome, the reason where the item is unrecoverable, the rule ID, the package version and the decided-at time; the element names that no source gives are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2761; ASM-4595) |

The field-level types, lengths and required flags of the added elements are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the element names, the vocabulary of AC1 and the optionality rules of AC2 and BR10. **No new table, no new column and no migration** is declared by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-litigation (S4); base `/api/recovery/litigation/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions` | LegalActionRequest in, LegalAction of status 201 out, with the recovery element and the action type of `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` (API-S4-002) | Litigation, right C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header required; the answer is stored |
| GET | `/legal-actions/{legalActionId}` | LegalAction of status 200 out with its action type, its status, its pack and the recovery answer (API-S4-003) | Litigation, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The two operations answer 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, each with the error envelope and one message ID of section 14. The operation IDs are those of TSD S4 T-A.1; the paths are those of the target base and not the monolith form. API-S4-004 `PATCH /legal-actions/{legalActionId}` and API-S4-005 `POST /legal-actions/{legalActionId}/hearings` belong to the sibling stories of this service and are not declared by this baseline.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/document-checklist` (API-P5-008 of `RWB-P5-E1040-APP`) | P5 rwb-document | The checklist of the case type with its version and each item with its document type against `LOV-DOC-TYPE`, its required flag and its present count; faked |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` (API-P5-002 of `RWB-P5-E1026-APP`) | P5 rwb-document | The documents stored on the case, paged with `type`, `page` and `size`: identifier, document type, stored date; the file and the retention are P5's, faked |
| The case-move answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2760; ASM-4594)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The move of the case of record to `PACK_VERIFIED` with the rule ID and its version; on the workflow boundary it is the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The three rows are contract dependencies of class C that the plan's C row does not carry, and the absence is recorded as GAP-2760 with ASM-4594. The retrieval request of a missing item is rwb-document's and its hub's and is not declared here. The CCMS path of the FSD integration points is not declared because no source assigns it an owner in the target (GAP-2764; ASM-4598).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic of the service is `rwb.litigation.events.v1` with event names `rwb.litigation.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and its three catalogue events `LawsuitFiled`, `JudgmentRecorded` and `AuctionResult` belong to the stories that own the filing, the judgment and the auction result. This baseline declares none of them, adds no outbox row and widens no topic; the decision record is relayed by the library of DP-03 on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and is not an event of this service. No event for a recovered, re-created or unrecoverable document exists in the catalogue, and the assignment is recorded (GAP-2763; ASM-4597).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The S4 IN row of Architecture v5 slide 19 lists `NoticeDelivered` and `PartnerResultSubmitted`, which belong to the notice and partner-result stories of this service, and the catalogue gives no document event to rwb-litigation. The document facts therefore arrive on the P5 contract of 12.2 and the case state on the rwb-case answer; this baseline declares no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox of its own.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LitigationWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, the child of `CaseWorkflow`, continues-as-new | `rwb-litigation` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | The stage that hosts the pack-recovery step; its input, its signals and its outcome for the parent are declared, not built |
| `recoverMissingDocument` | Activity, the one pack-recovery step | `rwb-litigation` | The case, the legal action and the checklist item in; the rule ID with its package version, the outcome, the reason, the action of the rule and the case move out |

The activity name is a target design choice and is fixed by no source document. The checklist read and the case document page are P5's operations and are declared here as another owner's, never as this service's; the defect list check and its re-run are the sibling step of RWB-S4-E5005-APP and are signalled to, not declared as this step's. No timer is declared, because the 10 working days and the prescription date are durable timers of the journey's sibling stories (GAP-2761; ASM-4595). No activity is registered by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step starts from the parent `CaseWorkflow` when the pack stage finds a missing item; this baseline declares no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table, and no Job of Architecture v5 slide 44 is owned or moved here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| legal_action | S4 (`rwb_litigation`) | The action, its action type and its status; read by the two operations; no column written by this step |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_litigation` | The local hash-linked decision record of the rule outcome (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_litigation` | The key of the repeated POST and the answer it holds |

`document` and `document_checklist_item` (P5), `recovery_case` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7) and `hearing` (S4, the sibling stories') are not owned by this baseline; it names them only as answers, rule versions or a later story's table, and no foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

| rwb-document document-page fake (API-P5-002) | The stored documents of case `RC-2026-000606` paged, with the item absent and with the item present after retrieval; no answer beyond 2 s | AC3, AC7 |

##### 13. Solution plan

**The CON declares shapes and moves nothing.** It writes no code, no migration and no table, and it changes no document, no case, no decision and no rule package. What it publishes is one OpenAPI 3.1 document, one AsyncAPI fragment that declares no event, nine contract tables and five fakes.

**Deliverables.** The additive document `openapi/rwb-litigation-v1.yaml` for this step, the recovery element, the vocabulary of `LOV-DOC-TYPE`, `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` and `LOV-LEGAL-STATUS` as published enumerations, the contract README rows for the consumed rows and their placeholders, and the five WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the transaction rule of the step and the element the baseline declares. DP-13 moves the base and nothing else. DP-19 is behind SCR-19, whose screen model is the edge contract's. DP-05 is declared as a prohibition: the document declares no `v_ace_*` read and no grant on `rwb_document`, `rwb_case` or `rwb_payment`, because rwb-litigation holds neither (Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41). DP-09 is not in the pattern set of this key, which is why no event is declared in 12.3 or 12.4.

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds two H rows, `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` for DP-03 and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` for DP-19, while the plan's build list for this story is None; this baseline builds against their fakes until those platform contract stories publish. The three consumed rows are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata row (GAP-2760; ASM-4594).

**Build steps**

1. Write the two operations and validate the additive rule of AC1 in the pipeline.
2. Write the recovery element of AC2 with the placeholder on the names the sources do not give.
3. Record the two P5 consumed rows of AC3 with their owner, their budget and the boundary of the retrieval request.
4. Record the case-move answer of AC4 and the absence test for a `recovery_case` property.
5. Record the error envelope, the rights and the `Idempotency-Key` rule of AC5.
6. Record the decision-record element of AC6 and validate it against the library schema.
7. Publish the five fakes of AC7 and the drift test.
8. Record the naming baseline and the boundary of AC8, then tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI document validates in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the five fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, and the app story, SCR-19 and the wave 3 harness have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S4-001 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names a missing item of the litigation pack at filing, which is the filing story of this service, so no path of this step raises it | The pack is missing {item}. Add it before filing. |
| MSG-S4-002 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names the expiry of the claim on the case, which is the prescription fact of this service, so no path of this step raises it | The claim on this case expires on {date}. File before then. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request is absent or invalid, or a body fails schema validation | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the Litigation right the operation declares | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the case-move answer | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The five message IDs are contract elements and the text is the legacy wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new one is added. No source gives the wording of a retrieval failure on the P5 side, so that path answers the platform error envelope and carries no message of its own (GAP-2761; ASM-4595).

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves SCR-19 Litigation workspace in its `PACK_ASSEMBLY`, `PACK_DEFECT_HOLD` and `PACK_VERIFIED` states through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The route calls rwb-litigation for the legal action and the recovery answer, rwb-document for the checklist and the case documents, and rwb-case for the case and its route state; this baseline fixes the rwb-litigation answers only, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. SCR-20 Enforcement workspace is listed by the legacy story and is served by the sibling stories' answers; this baseline adds nothing to it. The refusal and failure states the app story shows — refused, not on hold, no reason, not recorded — read the messages of section 14 on the same route.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the working-day timers, the 90-day warning, the reason set, the lists and the rule rows stay data, reference data or the rule package, never a schema default or an enumeration member of the code.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, a document type code, a reason code, dates and a rule version only; every example is synthetic.
- The document stays with rwb-document and the case with rwb-case: the document declares no `document` property, no storage reference, no retention class, no `recovery_case` property and no case row write (BR3, BR4).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the document declares no `v_ace_*` view and no grant on `rwb_document`, `rwb_case` or any other `rwb_*` schema, and the boundary test fails a build that adds one (DP-05).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The document lists only operations owned by rwb-litigation; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided (DP-01, DP-11).
- The defect check and its re-run are not restated: a supplied item is the sibling story's outcome and this baseline fixes only the hand-back value (BR12).
- No retired element is reintroduced: the absence test of AC8 fails a build that declares a `v_ace_*` read, a second topic, a Schedule, a Quartz row or a shared job table.

| Rules | R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20, named from the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 and governed in rwb-decision; R-LIT-18 is RWB-S4-E5005-APP's |
| Decoupling patterns | DP03, DP13, DP19 |
| Architecture decisions | ADR-013 (19 services inside ACE), ADR-014 (schema and login per service), ADR-020 (contract-first REST, one hop, 2 s timeout), ADR-022 (local decision record with the central ledger) |

##### 19. Out of scope

- The behaviour behind the two operations, the evaluation of R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20, the decision record and the case-move answer: RWB-S4-E5006-APP.
- The document, the checklist per case type, the checklist item, the retrieval request, the intake and the OCR text, the custody of the file, the retention class and the write-once rule: rwb-document (P5), whose contract this baseline declares as consumed and faked. **The document stays with rwb-document and no part of this baseline moves it** (GAP-2760; ASM-4594).
- The case of record, its route states and the parent `CaseWorkflow`: rwb-case (P3), whose case-move answer this baseline declares as consumed and faked.
- The defect list check and its re-run on a supplied item, and the move to `PACK_ASSEMBLY`: RWB-S4-E5005-APP, whose outcome value this baseline only declares.
- The assembly of the pack (FEAT-LIT-04), the verification and filing (FEAT-LIT-07), the notice path and the firm instruction: the sibling stories of this service.
- The authoring, testing, approval and versioning of the LITIGATION package and of R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20, and the Head of Litigation approval: rwb-decision (P7).
- The CCMS path of the FSD integration points: no source assigns it an owner in the target (GAP-2764; ASM-4598).
- The ACE account, customer and batch facts and the freshness of a data product: rwb-source-data (P1).
- The gateway-bff composite route and the screen field list of SCR-19 and SCR-20: RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the edge stories.
- The cross-service journey of the legacy key and its evidence: the wave 3 harness, which copies none of these criteria.
- The deployment of this capability, its flag, its dashboards, its alerts and its runbook: the operations story of this legacy key.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: application slice split from RWB-E5-006 for rwb-litigation. The two legacy acceptance criteria are kept word for word with their origin tag and now run as one step of `LitigationWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-litigation`; the `document` row is rwb-document's (P5), so the legacy read and write of the document and its pack item become consumed calls on the P5 contract and no `document` row is read or written here (DP-01); the supplied item is handed back to the defect check of R-LIT-18, which is RWB-S4-E5005-APP's, and this step owns only the unrecoverable and prescription outcomes of R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20; the legacy `decision_log_entry` write becomes the local decision record of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON written before the case move (DP-03); the base becomes `/api/recovery/litigation/v1` (DP-13); SCR-19 reads through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); the recovery element and the reason list and the CCMS path have no source specification and are carried as the working read of the assumptions (GAP-2760, GAP-2761, GAP-2762, GAP-2763, GAP-2764; ASM-4594, ASM-4595, ASM-4596, ASM-4597, ASM-4598). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **the Workbench to open the recovery path for a document the pack needs and the bank cannot find — read the checklist the pack is checked against, record that the item cannot be re-created and hand a supplied item back to the defect check, record the decision with its rule version before anything moves and answer rwb-case for the case move**, so that **a pack that is short of one document moves forward in one recorded step, with the affidavit route named where the item cannot be re-created, instead of the officer chasing the document outside the case**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E5-006. It owns:

- both legacy acceptance criteria of the story, copied verbatim with their origin tag, and the rules, messages, screens and data rows they depend on;
- one pack-recovery step of `LitigationWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-litigation` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, as the stage child of `CaseWorkflow` owned by rwb-case (Architecture v5 slide 19, "TMP LitigationWorkflow (years; continues-as-new)"; Temporal and Drools Design slide 13);
- the evaluation of R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20 of the LITIGATION package on the recovery outcome of an item and on the remaining prescription days, with the package version in force, and the hand-back of a supplied item to the defect check of R-LIT-18, which is RWB-S4-E5005-APP's;
- `GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId}` (API-S4-003) and `POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-actions` (API-S4-002) on base `/api/recovery/litigation/v1`, under capability area "Litigation" with the rights R and C (DP-13; TSD S4 T-A.1);
- the read of the case checklist and of the case documents from rwb-document, on the P5 contract and its fake;
- the local decision record of the outcome, written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON before the case move (DP-03);
- the answer to rwb-case for the case move `PACK_VERIFIED`, with the rule ID and the version that produced it;
- SCR-19 Litigation workspace in its pack state, as this service's answers, read through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

It does not own: the published shape of the two operations, the recovery element, the outcome vocabulary, the error set and the fakes, which are RWB-S4-E5006-CON; the `document`, the checklist item, the retrieval request, the custody of the file and its retention, which are rwb-document (P5); the case of record, the route states `PACK_ASSEMBLY`, `PACK_DEFECT_HOLD` and `PACK_VERIFIED` and the parent `CaseWorkflow`, which are rwb-case (P3); the defect check itself and its re-run on a supplied item (R-LIT-16, R-LIT-17, R-LIT-18 and R-LIT-32), which are RWB-S4-E5005-APP's; the authoring and approval of the LITIGATION package and the Head of Litigation approval of R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20, which are rwb-decision (P7); the CCMS path of the external system, whose owner is not specified (GAP-2764; ASM-4598); and the deployment of this build, which is the operations story of this legacy key and the wave 3 harness.

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E5-006 gave the Workbench one user step that opened the recovery path for a document the pack needs and the bank cannot find. The functional specification keeps the objective and its metric — a litigation turnaround of 6 days, measured on the decision log and the Workbench records, reviewed monthly, against the 21 days a filing takes today — and its problem statement names the cause it addresses: packs are incomplete and law firm progress is not tracked (FSD S4 A2.6.1 and A1.3). The module requirements carry the same intent: REQ-S4-002, "a litigation pack is assembled and checked against the document checklist, and missing documents are requested" (FSD S4 requirements served; Business Requirements Program v4).

What D-RCV-60 changes is who owns the document and who owns the case. In the monolith the pack, the document row, the case state and the decision log row sat in one `recovery` schema and one process. In the target:

- **the document is rwb-document's (P5).** The `document` table of the legacy data table (DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-011), the checklist item, the retrieval request, the stored file, the OCR text and the retention class are P5's; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives rwb-document "metadata, custody, OCR text and fields, signatures, retention" (Ownership Map: `document` owner P5). This story reads the checklist and the case documents on the owner's contract and its fake, and it writes no `document` row, no file, no retention class and no retrieval request (GAP-2760; ASM-4594);
- **the case of record stays with rwb-case (P3).** `recovery_case`, its route state and the parent `CaseWorkflow` are P3's; `PACK_DEFECT_HOLD`, `PACK_ASSEMBLY` and `PACK_VERIFIED` are written there and not here. This story evaluates the rule, records the decision and **answers** the case move (GAP-2760; ASM-4594);
- **the recovery decision stays with rwb-litigation (S4).** The judgement that an item cannot be re-created, the referral to Legal for the affidavit route and the escalation of a pack that is close to prescription are S4's, and `legal_action` and `hearing` are S4's tables (Ownership Map; Architecture v5 slide 41);
- **the defect check stays with its own story.** The check of the pack against the defect list and the re-run on a supplied item are R-LIT-16, R-LIT-17, R-LIT-18 and R-LIT-32, which RWB-S4-E5005-APP owns; this step hands a supplied item back to that check and answers no move of its own (BR9);
- **the decision is recorded first**, through the local decision-record library of DP-03 in the same transaction as the case-move answer, which is what legacy AC1 asked for and what legacy AC2 tested;
- **no ACE view is read here.** rwb-litigation holds no `v_ace_*` grant and no grant on another `rwb_*` schema (Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41), so the case facts arrive on the P3 answer and the document facts on the P5 contract only.

The recovery vocabulary is the rule vocabulary and not a new one. R-LIT-19 fires on `DOCUMENT_UNRECOVERABLE` — "the document cannot be re-created" — refers to Legal for the affidavit route, records the gap with a reason and moves to `PACK_VERIFIED`; R-LIT-20 is the escape when 90 days or less remain to prescription and the Head of Litigation approves filing with the gap recorded, also to `PACK_VERIFIED` (Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; TSD S4 T4). The step carries those two event codes as its outcome values, and `DOCUMENT_RETRIEVED` of R-LIT-18 as the value that hands the item back to the sibling check; the reason list of R-LIT-19 has no source specification and is carried as a gap (GAP-2761; ASM-4595).

Nothing is published and nothing is consumed as an event. Architecture v5 slide 43 gives rwb-litigation three catalogue events — `LawsuitFiled`, `JudgmentRecorded` and `AuctionResult` — and none of them is the recovery of a pack item, while the S4 IN row of slide 19 lists `NoticeDelivered` and `PartnerResultSubmitted`, which belong to the notice and partner-result stories. DP-09 is not in this story's pattern set, so the document fact arrives on the P5 contract synchronously and the case state on the P3 answer; the missing event assignment is recorded (GAP-2763; ASM-4597).

No business value moves: the 10 working days of R-LIT-19, the 90-day prescription warning of R-LIT-20 and the reason list are values in force in the rule package and in reference data, read with their version and never written in code (BR-S4-006).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S4-E5006-CON is published: the two legal-action operations, the recovery element, the outcome vocabulary, the case-move answer, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the error set and the fakes are baselined and handed to this story.
- The P5 contract is available with its fake: `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/document-checklist` (API-P5-008) of RWB-P5-E1040-APP and `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` (API-P5-002) of RWB-P5-E1026-APP are consumed one hop with a 2 s budget. No P5 contract story carries either as its own baseline, so both are class C dependencies in fact while this story's contract row is None (GAP-2760; ASM-4594).
- The case-move answer of rwb-case is available for the fake. No source names a published operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage; on the workflow boundary the answer is the stage outcome that the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies, and where rwb-case publishes a REST case-move operation for another caller its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2760; ASM-4594).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: the local decision-record library writes in the caller's transaction and a failed write stops the step with MSG-P7-003, so the case-move answer and its record commit together or not at all (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-19 Litigation workspace reaches this service through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, and no screen calls a service directly (DP-19).
- `legal_action` and `hearing` exist in schema `rwb_litigation` from the DB story of this service, with the columns of DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-029 and the standard record columns of TSD S4 T3.0; this story adds no table, no column and no migration.
- The LITIGATION rule package is in force at its version, with R-LIT-18, R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20 in it; the package is authored, tested and approved in rwb-decision (P7) and loaded here on `RulePackageInForce`. The Head of Litigation approval of R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20 is routed on the rwb-decision approval contract and is not built here.
- RWB-S4-E5005-APP holds the defect check and its re-run; the hand-back of a supplied item is a signal to that step and not a second check in this one (BR9).
- The service runs as its own login on schema `rwb_litigation`; it holds no grant on `rwb_document`, `rwb_case` or any other `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `document`, `document_checklist_item` or `recovery_case` is refused by the database and fails the boundary test (DP-01, DP-05).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-S4-E5006-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. A case reaches `PACK_DEFECT_HOLD` under R-LIT-17 of RWB-S4-E5005-APP with at least one missing item, and the parent `CaseWorkflow` forwards the stage to the litigation child on task queue `rwb-litigation`.
2. The step reads the legal action on `GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId}` (API-S4-003): the case reference `case_id` (DF-LEG-002), the action type `action_type` (DF-LEG-004) and the status `status` (DF-LEG-014), so the pack it repairs is the pack of a live action.
3. The step reads the case checklist on API-P5-008 and the documents stored on the case on API-P5-002, one hop each with a 2 s budget and a breaker: the item, its document type (`LOV-DOC-TYPE`, DF-DOC-004) and whether the item is still missing (FSD S4 A2.6.2 step 1).
4. The officer opens the recovery path on SCR-19 for one missing item and records the outcome of the attempt: the item was supplied, re-signed or re-created, or it cannot be re-created. The retrieval request itself is raised by rwb-document and its hub on the same checklist answer, not here (FSD S4 A2.6.2 step 2; BR1).
5. Where the item was supplied, the step hands the item back to the defect check of R-LIT-18, which re-reads the checklist and answers its own move; this step writes no record and answers no move for that outcome (BR9).
6. `PackRecoveryEvaluator` loads the LITIGATION package version in force from rwb-decision and evaluates the outcome: R-LIT-19 on `DOCUMENT_UNRECOVERABLE`, and R-LIT-20 when `prescription_days_remaining` is 90 or less and the pack is still on hold (Business Rules and Routing Logic v4).
7. The evaluation answers the rule ID, the package version, the action of the rule and the case move the rule names: `PACK_VERIFIED` under R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20.
8. `PackRecoveryDecisionRecordWriter` writes one decision record through the local decision-record library, **before any move**: the case reference, the legal action reference, the document type of the item, the outcome, the reason where the item is unrecoverable, the rule ID with its version and the decided-at time. A failed write stops the step with nothing changed (DP-03; legacy AC1 and AC2).
9. Under R-LIT-19 the gap is recorded with its reason on the record of step 8 and referred to Legal for the affidavit route; under R-LIT-20 the Head of Litigation approves filing with the gap recorded on the rwb-decision approval contract, and the step waits for that answer.
10. `PackRecoveryAnswer` answers rwb-case with the case move `PACK_VERIFIED` and its rule, in one transaction with the decision record and the idempotency row. rwb-case writes the `recovery_case` row and its route state; this service writes neither (GAP-2760; ASM-4594).
11. A repeated answer for the same case, document type and rule version writes nothing and sends no second case-move answer; the repeat is counted.
12. SCR-19 Litigation workspace reads the legal action, the checklist state and the recovery outcome from this service and from rwb-document through the gateway-bff composite route, read only, next to the case and its route state of rwb-case (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The local decision record cannot be written | The transaction writes nothing and no case-move answer leaves the service | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, TC-E5-006-02, TC-E5-006-04 |
| X2 | The role does not hold the Litigation right of the operation | 403 before any read or write; nothing changes and no decision record is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, TC-E5-006-03 |
| X3 | The legal action does not exist or is outside the scope | 404 and nothing is written; the caller cannot tell an out-of-scope action from a missing one | None | AC1 |
| X4 | The legal action is `CLOSED` or `WITHDRAWN`, or the case is not at `PACK_DEFECT_HOLD` | 409 and nothing changes; no pack is recovered on a closed action | None | AC1 |
| X5 | The P5 checklist read or the case document page does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The step waits and retries on the workflow's own schedule; nothing is written and no move is answered, and the caller sees 503 with the platform error envelope | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X6 | The item names a document type outside `LOV-DOC-TYPE`, or a required field of the request is absent | 422 with MSG-GEN-001; nothing is written and no record is made | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X7 | The outcome is `DOCUMENT_UNRECOVERABLE` and no reason is given | 422 with MSG-GEN-001: R-LIT-19 records the gap with a reason, so the step refuses an unrecoverable outcome without one | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, TC-E5-006-01 |
| X8 | The outcome is `DOCUMENT_UNRECOVERABLE` or `PRESCRIPTION_WARNING` and the Head of Litigation has not answered the approval | The step waits on the approval; no gap is recorded as accepted and no case move is answered | None | AC1 |
| X9 | The same case, document type and rule version arrives twice | One record, one answer; the repeat is counted and no second decision record is written | None | AC1 |
| X10 | A component, a statement or a test reaches a `document` row, a checklist item, a `recovery_case` row, a `v_ace_*` view or another service's schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | Section 17, BR3, BR6 |

X1 to X4 are the exception paths of RWB-E5-006 carried onto the split, X5 to X9 are the paths the target call types and rules add, and X10 is the DP-01 and DP-05 boundary. The 90-day warning of R-LIT-20 and the reason set of R-LIT-19 are values in force, so neither is a constant of this story.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-S4-E5006-CON, the two P5 reads and the case-move fake, on the tables of its own schema, and needs no live rwb-document, no live rwb-case and no live rwb-decision |
| Negotiable | The activity name, the decision code per rule and the shape of the stage outcome are this story's choice; the rules, the messages, the screen, the two operations and the outcome vocabulary are fixed |
| Valuable | A pack that is short of one document moves forward in one recorded step, with the affidavit route named where the item cannot be re-created |
| Estimable | One workflow step, one evaluator, one record write, one client, one case-move answer and one read-only screen fragment |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on synthetic cases and checklist items through the contract fakes, plus the component cases of the access answer and the failed record write |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Recover a missing or lost document

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-000606" is at "PACK_DEFECT_HOLD" and carries legal action "LA-2026-000606" of action type "CIVIL_CASE" with status "OPEN"
    Given the LITIGATION rule package is in force at its version and carries R-LIT-18, R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 Recover a missing or lost document (legacy RWB-E5-006 AC1)
    Given the rwb-document contract mock returns the checklist of case "RC-2026-000606" with one item of LOV-DOC-TYPE missing and no document row for it
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case state "PACK_DEFECT_HOLD" for "RC-2026-000606"
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When the user acts on the screen
    Then opens the recovery path for a document the pack needs and the bank cannot find
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E5-006 AC2)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The two criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E5-006 word for word, with their origin tag added and nothing else changed: the repeated `Then`, the legacy wording of `the action is taken`, `the decision log cannot be written` and `the user acts on the screen` all stand. The cross-service parts are mocked, so AC1 carries two `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` lines, and those added `Given` lines are the only additions to the legacy text. What the legacy lines describe happens in three places in the target: rwb-document supplies the checklist and the case documents; this story evaluates R-LIT-19 or R-LIT-20, writes the decision record with the rule version and answers the case move to `PACK_VERIFIED`, and hands a supplied item back to the defect check of R-LIT-18 in RWB-S4-E5005-APP; and rwb-case writes the move. The legacy `document` row of the legacy data table is not read or written as a table anywhere in this story (GAP-2760, GAP-2761; ASM-4594, ASM-4595).

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-LIT-19 | Litigation | D7 | PACK_DEFECT_HOLD | DOCUMENT_UNRECOVERABLE | the document cannot be re-created | Refer to Legal for the affidavit route and record the gap with a reason | PACK_VERIFIED | Head of Litigation | Workbench, the Workbench document hub | 10 working days |
| R-LIT-20 | Litigation | D7 | PACK_DEFECT_HOLD | PRESCRIPTION_WARNING | prescription_days_remaining <= 90 | Escalate; the Head of Litigation approves filing with the gap recorded | PACK_VERIFIED | Head of Litigation | Workbench, Workbench scheduler | To the prescription date |

The two rows are the rows of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, copied character for character. Their owner column is a role of the business and not a service: the Head of Litigation approves on the rwb-decision approval contract, and the case move is written by rwb-case on this story's answer. The systems column names the Workbench document hub, which is rwb-document (P5) in the target. **R-LIT-18 (`PACK_DEFECT_HOLD` → `DOCUMENT_RETRIEVED` → `PACK_ASSEMBLY`) is not this story's**: the re-run of the defect check on a supplied item is RWB-S4-E5005-APP's, and this step hands the item back to it.

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The pack-recovery decision and the legal action it repairs are this service's; the document, the checklist item, the retrieval request and the custody of the file are rwb-document's and are read on the owner's contract only | Architecture v5 slide 41; Ownership Map (`document` owner P5; `legal_action` and `hearing` owner S4); TSD S4 T3.1 |
| BR2 | The decision is recorded before the case move, with the rule ID and the package version in force; a failed write changes nothing and the caller sees MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; TSD S4 T2 ("writes the decision log entry before any change"); legacy AC1 and AC2 |
| BR3 | The case move is answered and not written: `recovery_case` and the route states `PACK_DEFECT_HOLD`, `PACK_ASSEMBLY` and `PACK_VERIFIED` are rwb-case's, and this story sends the move with the rule and its version | Ownership Map (`recovery_case` owner P3); Architecture v5 slide 41; GAP-2760 |
| BR4 | The outcome vocabulary is the rule vocabulary: `DOCUMENT_UNRECOVERABLE` for R-LIT-19, `PRESCRIPTION_WARNING` for R-LIT-20 and `DOCUMENT_RETRIEVED` as the hand-back value of the sibling R-LIT-18; no state name and no list value is written in code | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; TSD S4 T4; BR-S4-006 (FSD S4 A2.6.3.1) |
| BR5 | The gap of an unrecoverable item is recorded with a reason and referred to Legal for the affidavit route, and a pack close to prescription is escalated to the Head of Litigation, never filed on this step's own authority | R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20; FSD S4 A2.6.3.1 (VR-S4-006-1) |
| BR6 | No ACE view and no ACE table is read, and no cross-schema join is made: this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and no grant on `rwb_document` or `rwb_case` | DP-05; Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41 |
| BR7 | The same case, document type and rule version twice, or the same `Idempotency-Key` twice, writes once, answers the move once and counts the repeat | TSD S4 T-A.2 (`Idempotency-Key` on the write operations); Architecture v5 slide 11 |
| BR8 | No person name, address, contact value or identity number enters `rwb_litigation`, the decision record, a log or an event: the step carries case references, document type codes, dates, reason codes and a rule version | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17); Architecture v5 slide 42 notes |
| BR9 | The defect check and its re-run are not rebuilt here: a supplied item is handed back to R-LIT-18 of RWB-S4-E5005-APP, and this step writes no record and answers no move for that outcome | R-LIT-18 (Business Rules and Routing Logic v4); RWB-S4-E5005-APP sections 1 and 4 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** R-LIT-19 is the outcome that closes the hold on an item that cannot be re-created, and R-LIT-20 the outcome that closes it when the prescription is 90 days or less away. The timer column of the two rows (10 working days, to the prescription date) is a value of the rule package and of the case timers, not of this build: this story owns no timer and reads the remaining days from the P3 answer. VR-S4-006-1 of the FSD raises MSG-S4-001 when a pack is incomplete at filing; the message is carried in section 14 and raised by the filing story, not by this step.

##### 9. State transitions

The case route state is rwb-case's and is not changed by this story: the step answers the move and the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies it (BR3). What this story owns is the decision record and the state of the step.

| From (case route state, rwb-case) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| PACK_DEFECT_HOLD | DOCUMENT_UNRECOVERABLE under R-LIT-19 | The document cannot be re-created and the gap is recorded with a reason | `PACK_VERIFIED`, answered by this story |
| PACK_DEFECT_HOLD | PRESCRIPTION_WARNING under R-LIT-20 | prescription_days_remaining <= 90 | `PACK_VERIFIED`, answered by this story on the Head of Litigation approval |
| PACK_DEFECT_HOLD | DOCUMENT_RETRIEVED under R-LIT-18 | The item is supplied, re-signed or re-created | `PACK_ASSEMBLY`, answered by RWB-S4-E5005-APP and not by this step |
| PACK_DEFECT_HOLD | An unrecoverable outcome with no reason, or a document type outside `LOV-DOC-TYPE` | X6, X7 | Unchanged, refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-001 |
| CLOSED, WITHDRAWN or a case not on hold | Any outcome | X4 | Unchanged, refused with 409 |

| Step execution | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting | The parent forwards the stage with at least one missing item | The package in force is loaded | Reading the pack |
| Reading the pack | The P5 checklist and document page answer and the legal action is open | The officer records one item outcome | Evaluating |
| Evaluating | The item was supplied | BR9 | Waiting, handed back to the defect check |
| Evaluating | R-LIT-19 or R-LIT-20 fires | The decision record is written | Answering |
| Answering | The case-move answer is sent | The transaction commits | Waiting for the stage end |
| Answering | The record write or the transaction fails | X1 | Waiting, nothing changed |
| Answering | The outcome needs the Head of Litigation approval | X8 | Waiting on the approval answer |

| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Litigation CRUA in the TSD S4 T6.1 matrix and the primary role of the FSD A2.6.3.3: opens the recovery path, records the outcome of an item and reads the pack |
| RW-ENFORCE, enforcement owner | Litigation CRU: reads the pack and records an item outcome in scope |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Litigation RA: the "also uses" role of the FSD; receives the affidavit route of R-LIT-19 and records its outcome |
| RW-PRODHEAD, RW-HEADLIT | Litigation RA: read, and approve through the approval path of R-LIT-19 and R-LIT-20 |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-WRITEOFF, RW-CREDITAD, RW-GUARANT, RW-AGENCYMG, RW-CONDUCT, RW-HEADNPA, RW-HEADASL, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE | Litigation R: read only |
| PT-LAWFIRM, law firm user | Litigation RU: reads its own action and supplies an item through the partner gateway |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-AGENT, SY-DATALOAD | Litigation R or U as the TSD S4 T6.1 matrix gives it; the service identities run the step and are subject to the same checks |

The rights above are the rows of TSD S4 T6.1 and nothing wider. DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set: the capability area and the right are declared per operation, and the guard of the access service is a service-template capability, so the check is stated here and not built here.

Field IDs are those of the TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 T3.1, the Physical Schema and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8, and the `document` rows are the rows the legacy story lists in its Data table, with their owner changed to P5 by the target. **No new table, no new column and no migration**: `legal_action` and `hearing` arrive with the DB story of this service, and `decision_record` and `idempotency_key` are platform library objects created in `rwb_litigation` by the library's own migration (DP-03). The **`document` row, the checklist item, the retrieval request and the file are not created, written or read as tables**; `recovery_case` (P3), `decision_log_entry` (P7) and `rule_row` (P7) are not read as tables either. The recovery element and the "gap with a reason" have no column in `legal_action` and no field list of their own in any source, so they are carried as elements of the CON with the placeholder (GAP-2761; ASM-4595).

**No personal data.** The records this story writes carry identifiers, a document type code, a reason code, dates and a rule version. No name, address, contact value or identity number enters `rwb_litigation`, the decision record, a log or a workflow input, and the fixture data of the tests is synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-litigation (S4); base `/api/recovery/litigation/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the behaviour behind two operations whose shapes are declared by RWB-S4-E5006-CON.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions` | LegalActionRequest in, LegalAction of status 201 out, with the action type of `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` and its pack (API-S4-002) | Litigation, right C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header required |
| GET | `/legal-actions/{legalActionId}` | LegalAction of status 200 out with its action type, its status and its pack (API-S4-003) | Litigation, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The errors are 400 for a malformed request, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope action, 409 for a closed, withdrawn or wrong-state action, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for a missing or invalid field, and 503 when the decision library, the P5 contract or the rule package does not answer. API-S4-004 `PATCH /legal-actions/{legalActionId}` and API-S4-005 `POST /legal-actions/{legalActionId}/hearings` belong to the sibling stories of this service and are not built here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/document-checklist` (API-P5-008 of `RWB-P5-E1040-APP`) | P5 rwb-document | The checklist of the case type with its version and each item with its document type against `LOV-DOC-TYPE` and its present count; faked |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` (API-P5-002 of `RWB-P5-E1026-APP`) | P5 rwb-document | The documents stored on the case, paged with `type`, `page` and `size`: identifier, document type, stored date; faked |
| The case-move answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2760; ASM-4594)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The move of the case of record to `PACK_VERIFIED` with the rule ID and its version; on the workflow boundary it is the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The three rows are contract dependencies in fact and are not in this story's contract-dependency row, which is None; the absence is recorded as GAP-2760 with ASM-4594. The retrieval request of a missing item is raised by rwb-document and its hub on the same checklist answer and is not a call of this service (BR1). The CCMS path of the FSD integration points is not declared here because no source assigns it an owner (GAP-2764; ASM-4598).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic of the service is `rwb.litigation.events.v1` with event names `rwb.litigation.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and its three catalogue events `LawsuitFiled`, `JudgmentRecorded` and `AuctionResult` belong to the stories that own the filing, the judgment and the auction result (Architecture v5 slides 19 and 43). This story publishes none of them: DP-09 is not in its pattern set, it writes no outbox row, and its two outputs are the local decision record of DP-03 and the case-move answer of 12.2. No event of a recovered, re-created or unrecoverable document exists on any topic in the catalogue, and the assignment is recorded rather than decided here (GAP-2763; ASM-4597).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The S4 IN row of Architecture v5 slide 19 lists `NoticeDelivered` and `PartnerResultSubmitted`, which belong to the notice and partner-result stories of this service, and `ProceedsMatched` does not list rwb-litigation among its consumers (slide 43). The document fact therefore arrives on the P5 contract of 12.2, synchronously, and the case state on the P3 answer; this story holds no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox row of its own.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LitigationWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, the child of `CaseWorkflow`, continues-as-new across the years of the journey | `rwb-litigation` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the route R4, the legal action, the missing checklist items and the rule package in force; signals: the case state answered by rwb-case, the rule package in force and the approval answer |
| `recoverMissingDocument` | Activity, the one pack-recovery step of this story | `rwb-litigation` | The case, the legal action and the checklist item in; the rule ID with its package version, the outcome, the reason, the action of the rule and the case move out, with the decision record written before the answer |

The activity name is a target design choice of this story and is fixed by no source document; the defect list check itself, and its re-run on a supplied item, are the step of RWB-S4-E5005-APP and are signalled to, not re-implemented. No timer is registered by this story: the 10 working days and the prescription date are durable timers of the journey's sibling stories (GAP-2761; ASM-4595).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step starts from the parent `CaseWorkflow` when the pack stage finds a missing item, and owns no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job. The defect check of the pack, the notice timers and the prescription clock of the journey belong to the sibling stories; no Job of Architecture v5 slide 44 is owned, moved or registered here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| legal_action | S4 (`rwb_litigation`) | Read only in this story: the action type, the status and the case reference; no column is written and none is added |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_litigation` | The local hash-linked decision record of the rule outcome (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_litigation` | The key of the repeated request and the answer it holds |

Not owned and never read as a table: `document` and `document_checklist_item` (P5), `recovery_case` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `hearing` (S4, the sibling stories'), and every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No foreign key leaves the schema and `legal_action.case_id` is an identifier, not a foreign key across schemas (DP-01, DP-05). The `document` row that the legacy story lists is P5's and this story writes no part of it.

| rwb-document document-page fake (API-P5-002) | The stored documents of case `RC-2026-000606` paged, with the item absent and with the item present after retrieval; no answer beyond 2 s | AC1, X5 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The case-move answer is stubbed from the published documents and carries the placeholder until its owner confirms it (GAP-2760; ASM-4594).
