##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.litigation`, module `pack`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.litigation.pack`; front end `src/modules/recovery/litigation/PackApproval.tsx`, the fragment SCR-19 embeds and SCR-18 reads, read only.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/litigation/v1`; the three operations keep API-S4-002, API-S4-003 and API-S4-004 | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 carries legacy AC1's "writes the result to the decision log with the rule version" and legacy AC4's fail-closed behaviour, and it is the only pattern of the three that adds a write. DP-13 renames the base and keeps the operation IDs, which is why the legacy endpoint block of RWB-E5-007 names two of the three operations and this story serves all three. DP-19 covers the two screens only; the screen model, the merge order and the route path stay with the edge contract.

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds the two H rows the metadata also carries, `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON`, and nothing else. Five consumed surfaces have no row at all: the pack of rwb-document, the notice and template status of rwb-comms, the case with its task and route fact of rwb-case, the D7 approval of rwb-decision, and the reference data of rwb-case. They are recorded once with GAP-2765 with ASM-4599, and the story builds against their fakes on Day 1; no C dependency blocks the build (Template and Rules section R5.7 rule 2).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| LegalActionController | Controller | API-S4-002, API-S4-003 and API-S4-004 with the problem mapping for 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 |
| PackValidator | Service | The case and the caller's scope, the `actionType` value of LOV-LEGAL-TYPE, the required fields and the case state the step needs |
| PackReadClient | Client | The pack and defect-list answer of rwb-document, one hop, 2 s, breaker; never a document table read (BR4) |
| NoticeStateClient | Client | The notice and template-status answer of rwb-comms, one hop, 2 s, breaker |
| TemplateWithdrawnCheck | Service | R-LIT-04 and the task raise; it holds the generation and blocks nothing that is not a generation |
| PrescriptionWarningCheck | Service | The 90-day condition of R-LIT-11 and the MSG-S4-002 warning with the date read from the case |
| RuleEvaluation | Service through the embedded Drools kit | R-LIT-04, R-LIT-11, R-LIT-16 and R-LIT-21 on the answers and the reference rows in force; the version is pinned and recorded |
| PackDecisionWriter | Library adapter | One hash-linked record per rule answer, before any change; refuses the request when the write fails (DP-03) |
| LegalActionWriter | Repository | The `legal_action` facts of the verification and the authorisation, and the idempotency row, in one `rwb_litigation` transaction |
| CaseRouteClient | Client | The case read, the task raise and the route fact to rwb-case, one hop, 2 s, breaker |
| ApprovalClient | Client | The D7 approval item of R-LIT-11 to rwb-decision, one hop, 2 s, breaker |
| LitigationWorkflow | Workflow | The stage on `rwb-litigation` and its pack step |
| PackApproval | React component | Shows the legal action, the pack and defect list, the template hold and the approval state on SCR-18 and SCR-19, read only, with the refusal and failure states |

**Database and migrations.** No Flyway file. `legal_action` arrives with the S4 schema and the DDL template of `RWB-S4-E5007-CON`; the decision record and the idempotency key are library objects created in `rwb_litigation` by the library's migration (DP-03). The index set of `legal_action` is `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2767; ASM-4601)`; this story needs a lookup by `case_id` for the workspace read and by `id` for the two single-row operations.

**Configuration and reference data.**

- The checklist rows and the version of the defect list behind R-LIT-16 and MSG-S4-001, as versioned reference rows of the business, read with their version. Their content is `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2767; ASM-4601)`.
- The 90-day threshold of R-LIT-11, as a versioned reference row. Its value is `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2767; ASM-4601)`; the rule row states 90.
- The template-status values `current` and `withdrawn` of R-LIT-04, read as values in force of the communications service.
- LOV-LEGAL-TYPE and LOV-LEGAL-STATUS at their version in force (TSD S4 T3.2), and the decision code of the verification and of the authorisation, read as values of LOV-DECISION at its version in force.
- The 2 s budget and the single hop are the platform rule of ADR-020 and not a value of this story.

**Build steps**

1. Build `PackValidator` and `LegalActionWriter` over the `legal_action` row and the contract fake; test AC1 and X1 to X3.
2. Build `PackReadClient` and the verification path with `RuleEvaluation` and `PackDecisionWriter` against the library fake; test AC1 and AC4.
3. Build `NoticeStateClient` and `TemplateWithdrawnCheck`, with the task raise on the case fake; test AC2 and X5.
4. Build `PrescriptionWarningCheck` and `ApprovalClient` against the approval fake, with the granted, refused and delayed answers; test AC3, X6 and X11.
5. Build `CaseRouteClient` with each route fact, its refusal and its delayed answer; test AC1, AC2, AC3 and X10.
6. Build the rejection path of R-LIT-21 and its `PACK_ASSEMBLY` announcement; test X4.
7. Build `PackApproval` and read the legal action through the composite route fake; test AC1.
8. Add the boundary test: no statement outside `rwb_litigation`, no `v_ace_*` read, no write to `rwb_case`, `rwb_document`, `rwb_comms` or `rwb_decision`; test BR8.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.litigation.pack-approval-v1`, read as a flag of the platform library; off means the verification and the authorisation answer 404 and the pack screen shows no approval action, while the read of an existing legal action is unaffected.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the contract tests of `RWB-S4-E5007-CON` stay green, the boundary test runs in the pipeline, and a SIT week shows one decision record per rule answer, one task per withdrawn template, one route fact per answer, no write of a case, task, timer, document, notice or ledger row from this service, and no `v_ace_*` read in its logs.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S4-001 | One or more defect list items are missing when the filing is approved (X4, VR-S4-007-1) | The pack is missing {item}. Add it before filing. |
| MSG-S4-002 | The prescription date of the case falls inside 90 days (X6, R-LIT-11) | The claim on this case expires on {date}. File before then. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of the request is missing or invalid (X1) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's role does not hold the Litigation right of the operation (X7) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the legal action changes (X8, AC4) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The five texts are the legacy wording of RWB-E5-007 section 14 and the FSD S4 A2.7.3.1 message set, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no message identifier is added. `MSG-GEN-001` is displayed with the field it names and `MSG-S4-001` with the missing item. The 90-day window behind `MSG-S4-002` is a versioned reference row whose content is `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2767; ASM-4601)`; the date itself is the case's. A downstream that does not answer (X9) and a reference that is not found (X2) carry no message of this set, and the platform error envelope is displayed as it is.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built in this story. Two existing surfaces show what it writes and what it holds, read through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19):

| Screen | State | What the user sees or does |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Generated | The generated notice of the case with its template version, and the pack the verification reads |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Approved | The filing authorisation recorded on the legal action, read only here |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Sent | The notice dispatched by the communications service, read only |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Delivered | The delivery proof of the communications service, read only |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Unserved | The notice unserved, with MSG-S4-002 and the prescription date, and the R-LIT-11 escalation available |
| SCR-19 Litigation workspace | Pack | The pack, the defect-list result with its missing items, the template status and the verification with R-LIT-16 |
| SCR-19 Litigation workspace | Instructed | The filing authorised and the `PACK_APPROVED` fact announced; the firm is selected by `RWB-S4-E5008-APP` |
| SCR-19 Litigation workspace | Filed | The filing date and the court references, read only here |
| SCR-19 Litigation workspace | Hearing | The hearings of the legal action, read only, from the hearing story of this service |
| SCR-19 Litigation workspace | Judgment | The judgment date and amount, read only |
| SCR-19 Litigation workspace | Not recorded | MSG-P7-003, and the legal action unchanged with no task and no route fact |
| SCR-19 Litigation workspace | Refused | A role without the Litigation right reads MSG-P4-002 and nothing changes |
| SCR-19 Litigation workspace | Held | The R-LIT-04 hold of SCR-18: the generation held, the case at `NOTICE_BLOCKED` and the task raised to the litigation officer |
| SCR-19 Litigation workspace | Failed | The answer of a refused approval with its reason, or a 503 when a consumed contract did not answer; the legal action keeps what it wrote |

The five SCR-18 states and the five SCR-19 states are the ones the legacy screen block of RWB-E5-007 gives, copied unchanged: SCR-18 carries generated, approved, sent, delivered and unserved, and SCR-19 carries pack, instructed, filed, hearing and judgment. The four message and hold states below them are the states of the exception paths of section 5. Neither screen moves the case: rwb-case moves it on the announced fact (BR3), and the route merges this service's answer with the pack of rwb-document, the notice of rwb-comms and the case of rwb-case. The route path, the screen-model field list and the merge order belong to `RWB-PLT-N001-CON`, not here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the checklist rows, the template-status values, the 90-day threshold, the list values and the decision codes are data with a version; no role, list value, state name or amount appears in Java.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow inputs or prompts: the row carries identifiers, list values, dates and one amount, and the customer's identity never enters this service or its history.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the owner's `v_ace_*` views: no component of this story reads an ACE view or an ACE table, and the service identity holds no `v_ace_*` grant (BR8).
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema join: the pack, the notice, the case, the task, the timer and the ledger are reached only on their contracts and their fakes (DP-01, BR3, BR4, BR5).
- One hop and a 2 s budget on each consumed call, with a breaker per downstream and no call chain; a hand-off is re-run by repeating the same `Idempotency-Key` and never by a silent resend.
- The decision is never recorded after the effect: the record is written first through the library, and a failed write stops the request with nothing changed (DP-03, R-UNI-39, MSG-P7-003).
- No event, no topic, no outbox row, no Schedule and no timer of this service: the prescription clock and the R-LIT-04 service level are the case's and the approval's (12.3, 12.4, 12.6).
- The two screens are read only; SCR-19 posts the verification and the authorisation through the operations of section 12.1 and SCR-18 is a read of the notice and the pack.

##### 19. Out of scope

- The case of record, its route states, the task of R-LIT-04 and the prescription timer: rwb-case (P3), and the case-side stories of this legacy family (GAP-2766).
- The pack, its documents, the checklist and the defect list, and MSG-S4-001 as an authored message: rwb-document (P5) and the pack stories of this service; this story consumes the result.
- The notice, its template and its dispatch, and the approval of a notice through API-S4-001: rwb-comms (P6) and the E2 notice story of this service (GAP-2766).
- The approval item at D7, the delegation of authority table and its clock: rwb-decision (P7) and `RWB-P7-E2013-CON`.
- The firm selection of R-LIT-23, the panel, the instruction and the firm's result: `RWB-S4-E5008-APP` and rwb-partner (S9).
- The filing itself, the court receipt, the hearings, the judgment and the enforcement steps of the same legal action: the sibling S4 stories.
- The contract document itself: `RWB-S4-E5007-CON`.
- The roles, rights, scope and masking data themselves: rwb-access (P4).
- The gateway-bff composite route, the screen field list and the layout of SCR-18 and SCR-19: `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` and the edge stories.
- The deployment of this build, its flag, its dashboards, its alerts and its runbook: its own OPS story.
- The cross-service journey of the pack across rwb-litigation, rwb-document, rwb-comms, rwb-case and rwb-decision with live owners: the wave 3 integration harness.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of the firm-selection step of rwb-litigation, split from RWB-E5-008. It fixes the three legal-action operations on `/api/recovery/litigation/v1` (DP-13), the `law_firm_id` element of `LegalAction` and `LegalActionUpdate` and the closed vocabularies of `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` and `LOV-LEGAL-STATUS`, the consumed panel and decline reads of rwb-partner (S9), the case-move answer of rwb-case, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the error envelope, and the decision-record element of DP-03. The panel is answered by rwb-partner and this contract declares no `partner` property (GAP-2773, GAP-2778; ASM-4607, ASM-4612); `PartnerResultSubmitted` is not consumed here (GAP-2774; ASM-4608); the score, capacity, court coverage and conflict fields and the operation names have no source specification and are carried with the placeholder. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead of rwb-litigation (S4)**, I want **the published contract baseline of the firm-selection step — the base `/api/recovery/litigation/v1` with API-S4-002 create, API-S4-003 read and API-S4-004 patch, the `LegalAction`, `LegalActionRequest` and `LegalActionUpdate` schemas with the `law_firm_id` element and no panel property, the two closed vocabularies of `action_type` and `status`, the consumed panel and decline reads of rwb-partner, the case-move answer to rwb-case, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the error envelope, the declared right of each operation, the decision-record element, the tables and the fakes**, so that **RWB-S4-E5008-APP, the screens and the wave 3 harness build against one frozen, testable shape on Day 1 and a firm reference, a status value, a panel field or an answer shape can never drift between rwb-litigation, rwb-partner and rwb-case without a failing build**.

It owns the shapes and nothing that moves: the selection, the write of the firm, the decision record, the case-move answer and the re-selection are `RWB-S4-E5008-APP`'s; the panel, the scorecard, the capacity, the court coverage, the conflict status and the decline are rwb-partner's (S9) and `RWB-S4-E5009-APP`'s instruction; the case of record and its route states are rwb-case's (P3); the rule rows and the package version are rwb-decision's (P7).

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy step of RWB-E5-008 crossed three boundaries at once: a panel row, a case route state and a decision log row, all in one `recovery` schema and one process. The target splits them: the panel is rwb-partner's (S9), the case of record and the route states `FIRM_SELECTION` and `FIRM_DECLINED` stay with rwb-case (P3), and the legal action and the selected firm stay with rwb-litigation (S4). Each boundary is now a contract that another team builds against, so each has to be fixed before the app story starts: the `law_firm_id` element, the closed vocabularies, the panel read, the decline read and the case-move answer.

The baseline also fixes the naming that the checks require: schema `rwb_litigation`, base `/api/recovery/litigation/v1`, topic `rwb.litigation.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-litigation` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.litigation` (Architecture v5 slide 41 notes). It records that rwb-litigation holds no `v_ace_*` grant and no grant on `rwb_partner` (Architecture v5 slide 29), so DP-05 is declared as a prohibition and the panel and score facts are consumed on the owner's contract only. It records that `PartnerResultSubmitted` is an event of rwb-partner whose consumer row lists rwb-litigation while DP-09 is not in this key's pattern set, so this contract declares no consumed event and the decline arrives synchronously.

Three points are carried as gaps and assumptions rather than decided quietly: the plan gives the panel read, the decline read and the case-move answer no C row and no contract story (GAP-2773), the score, capacity, court coverage and conflict fields of a panel firm have no field list anywhere and the legacy `v_ace_score` read has no grant here (GAP-2778), and the rule rows of R-LIT-23 and R-LIT-27 with their weights, thresholds and window are governed in rwb-decision and named here only (GAP-2777).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the queue and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the pagination and filter convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline (Architecture v5 slide 11); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The ownership of the objects is taken from the Ownership Map only: `legal_action` and `hearing` are S4's, `partner` and `partner_instruction` are S9's, `recovery_case` is P3's, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are P7's, `document` is P5's. This document never declares another service's operation as provided.
- The panel list operation of rwb-partner (API-S9-001 `GET /partners` "List partners with panel status and score", on base `/api/recovery/partner/v1`) and the instruction read that answers a decline (API-S9-003 and API-S9-004 of the partner set) are published, so the consumed rows of 12.2 name a real owner document; no plan slice gives them a story key and neither is in this story's contract-dependency row, which is None, so the absence is recorded (GAP-2773; ASM-4607).
- The case-move answer of rwb-case is fixed here as a shape only; no source names a published operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage, and the name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2773; ASM-4607).
- The LITIGATION rule package, its rule rows for R-LIT-23 and R-LIT-27, its scorecard weights, capacity test, court coverage set, conflict check and 2-working-day window are governed in rwb-decision (P7); this baseline names them and declares none of them (GAP-2777; ASM-4611).
- The `legal_action` table and its columns arrive with the DB story of this service; this baseline declares shapes and creates no table, no column and no migration.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-litigation for this step: the three operations with their request and answer elements, the closed vocabularies, the `law_firm_id` element, the rights and the six error responses.
2. Fix the firm element: `law_firm_id` (DF-LEG-003) on `LegalAction` and `LegalActionUpdate` as an identifier of the S9 partner, optional, with no panel property and no score property added to `legal_action`.
3. Fix the consumed panel read of rwb-partner and its facts — panel status, type, contract end, score, capacity, court coverage and conflict status — and mark the fields the sources do not give with the placeholder.
4. Fix the consumed decline read and the case-move answer of rwb-case: the move `FIRM_SELECTION` or `FIRM_DECLINED`, the rule ID, the version and the decided-at time, with no case row read or written here.
5. Record the decision-record element of DP-03 on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, written before the legal action changes.
6. Record the closed vocabulary of the action types and the action status, and the rule that no value is a constant of the code.
7. Publish the contract tables of section 12 and the five contract fakes.
8. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the additive rule, the vocabulary, the shapes, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the error envelope, the absence of a `v_ace_*` read and of a `partner` or `recovery_case` property, and the drift between a fake and the document.
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-S4-E5008-APP, the screens and the wave 3 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body or a request body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 400 or 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC2 |
| X2 | A field is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC7 |
| X4 | The consumed panel read, the decline read or the case-move answer has a field list the sources do not give | The row carries the placeholder, the gap and the assumption, and the fake is derived from the published document | None | AC2, AC3, AC4 |
| X5 | A value outside `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` or `LOV-LEGAL-STATUS` appears in the document or in an example | The vocabulary test fails the build | None | AC1, AC8 |
| X6 | The document declares another service's operation as provided, a `v_ace_*` view, a `partner` row or a `recovery_case` row | The review fails the baseline; the boundary test fails the build | None | AC8 |
| X7 | A POST is repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key` | The stored answer is returned and no second effect is described | None | AC2, AC5 |
| X8 | The rights of an operation are not the ones TSD S4 T-A.1 declares | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the Ownership Map and the published owner documents of rwb-partner and rwb-case only |
| Negotiable | The element names beyond the ones the sources give, the example values and the fake fixtures are settled in the baseline review; the operations, the vocabularies, the base, the topic and the queue are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks RWB-S4-E5008-APP, the screen and the wave 3 harness on Day 1, and the rwb-partner and rwb-case teams on the same day |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, one AsyncAPI fragment, nine contract tables, five fakes and four new contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

These eight criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only. They restate no business outcome owned by RWB-S4-E5008-APP and they copy no criterion of the legacy story, whose four criteria stay with the app story word for word.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The legal action and the selected firm are rwb-litigation's, and the contract declares `law_firm_id`, the vocabularies and the outcome fields on `legal_action` only | Architecture v5 slide 41; Ownership Map (legal_action owner S4); TSD S4 T3.1 and T3.2 |
| BR2 | The decision record is declared as an element written before the legal action changes, through the local library on the shared topic; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; TSD S4 T2; legacy RWB-E5-008 AC1 and AC4 |
| BR3 | The panel stays with rwb-partner: the contract declares the panel and the decline as consumed, declares no `partner` or `partner_instruction` property, and describes no score, panel status or conflict write of rwb-litigation | Ownership Map (partner and partner_instruction owner S9); TSD S9 T3.1 and API-S9-001; GAP-2778 |
| BR4 | The case move is answered and not written: the contract declares the answer that carries `FIRM_SELECTION` or `FIRM_DECLINED` and declares no `recovery_case` property and no case row write | Ownership Map (recovery_case owner P3); Architecture v5 slide 41; GAP-2773 |
| BR5 | No ACE view and no ACE table is read: the panel and score facts are consumed on the owner's contract, and the service holds no `v_ace_*` grant | DP-05; Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41 |
| BR6 | A POST declares the `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer; a GET and a PATCH declare none | Architecture v5 slide 11; TSD S4 T-A.2 |
| BR7 | The vocabulary is closed: `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` and `LOV-LEGAL-STATUS` are published as enumerated values and no state name, list value, weight, threshold or window is a constant of the code or a schema default | TSD S4 T3.2; BR-S4-008 (FSD S4 A2.8.3.1) |
| BR8 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, scores, dates, list values and a rule version only | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes; Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR9 | One REST base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; the document never declares another service's base or topic as its own | DP-13, DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR10 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR11 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-litigation; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | Ownership Map; DP-11 |
| BR12 | The rule rows of R-LIT-23 and R-LIT-27, their weights, thresholds, court set, conflict check and window, and the D7 decision level are governed in rwb-decision and named here, never declared here | GAP-2777; ASM-4611; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 |

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of this document, not of a legal action:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The three operations, the vocabularies, the firm element, the consumed rows and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, the screen, the wave 3 harness and the rwb-partner, rwb-case and rwb-decision owners accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example a new error code | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or a list value changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | The absence test of AC8 fails: a `v_ace_*` view, a `partner` or `recovery_case` property, a second topic or a Schedule | In review |

The status machine of `legal_action` that the document describes is the app story's: `LOV-LEGAL-STATUS` is OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED and WITHDRAWN, and a selection or a re-selection writes `law_firm_id` and moves no status; this baseline fixes the vocabulary and moves no action and no case.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-litigation | Owns the OpenAPI document and the contract tables; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version, and the correction of the Ownership Map rows the baseline consumes |
| Consuming teams (the app story, the screen, the wave 3 harness and the owners of rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-access and rwb-source-data) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| Platform library owner | Owns the error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule and the decision-record library this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in an answer, an element or a fake |

The per-service login behind the security scheme of the document is named "the rwb-litigation login (DP-02)" and is not part of this baseline.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Firm element | `law_firm_id` (DF-LEG-003), an identifier of the S9 partner, optional on the action and on the update; no other property is added for a selection |

| Partner | DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 of `partner` in `rwb_partner`, read only through the S9 owner and never written, copied or joined here |
| Partner instruction | DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 of `partner_instruction` in `rwb_partner`, read only through the S9 owner, and the instruction itself is `RWB-S4-E5009-APP`'s |
| ACE score facts | DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279 of `v_ace_score`, not read: this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-05) |
| Not written here | `recovery_case` (P3), `document` (P5), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `hearing` (S4, the sibling stories') |
| Panel facts | The score, the capacity, the court coverage and the conflict status of a firm: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2778; ASM-4612) |

The field-level types, lengths and required flags of the added elements are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the element names, the vocabularies of AC1 and the optionality rule of BR10. **No new table, no new column and no migration** is declared by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-litigation (S4); base `/api/recovery/litigation/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions` | LegalActionRequest in, LegalAction of status 201 out, with the action type of `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` (API-S4-002) | Litigation, right C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header required; the answer is stored |
| GET | `/legal-actions/{legalActionId}` | LegalAction of status 200 out with `law_firm_id`, `court_name` and `status` (API-S4-003) | Litigation, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| PATCH | `/legal-actions/{legalActionId}` | LegalActionUpdate in, LegalAction out with the selected firm (API-S4-004) | Litigation, right U, scope applied | Not applicable |

The three operations answer 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, each with the error envelope and one message ID of section 14. The operation IDs are those of TSD S4 T-A.1; the paths are those of the target base and not the monolith form. API-S4-001 `POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve` and API-S4-005 `POST /legal-actions/{legalActionId}/hearings` belong to the notice and hearing stories of this service and are not declared by this baseline.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| The panel list operation, API-S9-001 `GET /partners` (operation name of the S9 contract Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2773; ASM-4607)) | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` | S9 rwb-partner | The panel of firms with the partner reference, code, type, panel status, contract end, score, capacity, court coverage and conflict status; faked |
| The instruction read that answers a decline, API-S9-003 and API-S9-004 of the partner set (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2773; ASM-4607)) | `/api/recovery/partner/v1` | S9 rwb-partner | The decline of the instruction of the case, which is the fact of R-LIT-27; the instruction, its pack and its clock are `RWB-S4-E5009-APP`'s and the partner stories'; faked |
| The case-move answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2773; ASM-4607)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The move of the case of record to `FIRM_SELECTION` or `FIRM_DECLINED` with the rule ID and its version; on the workflow boundary it is the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). None of the three is a contract dependency of this story, whose C row is None, and the panel and decline rows additionally have no contract story in the plan; the absence is recorded as GAP-2773 with ASM-4607.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic of the service is `rwb.litigation.events.v1` with event names `rwb.litigation.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and its three catalogue events `LawsuitFiled`, `JudgmentRecorded` and `AuctionResult` belong to the stories that own the filing, the judgment and the auction result. This baseline declares none of them, adds no outbox row and widens no topic; the decision record is relayed by the library of DP-03 on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and is not an event of this service.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `PartnerResultSubmitted` is produced by rwb-partner on `rwb.partner.events.v1` and its consumer row lists rwb-litigation, rwb-asset and rwb-case, but DP-09 is not in the pattern set of this key, the S4 IN row of Architecture v5 slide 19 names the event without assigning it to this step, and no source states that a decline of an instruction is its trigger (GAP-2774; ASM-4608). The decline therefore arrives on the rwb-partner contract of 12.2 and the case state on the rwb-case answer; this baseline declares no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox of its own, and the trigger of the step is a workflow step rather than an event (GAP-2775; ASM-4609).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LitigationWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, the child of `CaseWorkflow`, continues-as-new | `rwb-litigation` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | The stage that hosts the firm-selection step; its signals and its outcome for the parent are declared, not built |
| `selectPanelFirm` | Activity, the one firm-selection step | `rwb-litigation` | The case and the legal action in; the rule ID with its package version, the selected firm, the ranked shortlist and the case move out |

`issueInstruction` is rwb-partner's activity on queue `rwb-partner` and is declared here as another owner's, never as this service's. The activity name is a target design choice, and the trigger of the step is read as the arrival of the pack-approved fact for a case in `PACK_VERIFIED`, because the legacy story says the step runs unattended while the FSD declares no background event (GAP-2775; ASM-4609). No activity is registered by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step runs from the pack-approved fact and from the decline the partner contract answers, and the 2-working-day window of R-LIT-27 is a durable timer of the step, not a Schedule; this baseline declares no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table, and no Job of Architecture v5 slide 44 is owned or moved here.

`partner` and `partner_instruction` (S9), `recovery_case` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `document` (P5) and `hearing` (S4, the sibling stories') are not owned by this baseline; it names them only as answers, rule versions or a later story's table, and no foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

##### 13. Solution plan

**The CON declares shapes and moves nothing.** It writes no code, no migration and no table, and it changes no legal action, no case, no panel row and no rule package. What it publishes is one OpenAPI 3.1 document, one AsyncAPI fragment that declares no event, nine contract tables and five fakes.

**Deliverables.** The additive document `openapi/rwb-litigation-v1.yaml` for this step, the `law_firm_id` element on `LegalAction` and `LegalActionUpdate`, the vocabularies of `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` and `LOV-LEGAL-STATUS` as published enumerations, the contract README rows for the consumed rows and their placeholders, and the five WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is declared as a prohibition here: the document declares no `v_ace_*` read and no grant on `rwb_partner`, because rwb-litigation holds neither (Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41; GAP-2778; ASM-4612). DP-13 moves the base and nothing else. DP-19 is behind SCR-19, whose screen model is the edge contract's. DP-09 is not in the pattern set of this key, which is why no event is declared in 12.3 or 12.4.

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds two H rows, `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` for DP-03 and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` for DP-19, while the plan's build list for this story is None; this baseline builds against their fakes until those platform contract stories publish. The panel read, the decline read and the case-move answer are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata row, and no plan slice gives the two partner rows a contract story key (GAP-2773; ASM-4607).

**Build steps**

1. Write the three operations and validate the additive rule of AC1 in the pipeline.
2. Write the `law_firm_id` element of AC2 with the placeholder on the fields the sources do not give.
3. Record the two rwb-partner consumed rows and the panel facts of AC3 with their owner, their budget and their placeholders.
4. Record the case-move answer of AC4 and the absence test for a `recovery_case` property.
5. Record the error envelope, the rights and the `Idempotency-Key` rule of AC5.
6. Record the decision-record element of AC6 and validate it against the library schema.
7. Publish the five fakes of AC7 and the drift test.
8. Record the naming baseline and the boundary of AC8, then tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI document validates in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the five fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, and the app story, the screen and the wave 3 harness have accepted the baseline.

The six message IDs are contract elements and the text is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new one is added. MSG-P1-001 is carried because it is in the message set of this feature, and no path of this service raises it (GAP-2779; ASM-4613).

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves SCR-19 Litigation workspace in its pack, selected, declined, instructed, filed, hearing and judgment states, through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The route calls rwb-litigation for the legal action and the selected firm, rwb-case for the case and its route state and rwb-partner for the panel and the instruction; this baseline fixes the rwb-litigation answers only, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The refusal and failure states the app story shows — not recorded, refused, stale data — read the messages of section 14 on the same route.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the scorecard weights, the capacity test, the court coverage set, the conflict check, the 2-working-day window, the D7 level and the lists stay data, reference data or the rule package, never a schema default or an enumeration member of the code.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, scores, dates, list values and a rule version only; every example is synthetic.
- The panel stays with rwb-partner and the case with rwb-case: the document declares no `partner`, `partner_instruction` or `recovery_case` property, no panel write and no case row write (BR3, BR4).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the document declares no `v_ace_*` view and no grant on `rwb_partner`, `rwb_case` or any other `rwb_*` schema, and the boundary test fails a build that adds one (DP-05).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The document lists only operations owned by rwb-litigation; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided (DP-01, DP-11).
- No retired element is reintroduced: the absence test of AC8 fails a build that declares a `v_ace_*` read, a second topic, a Schedule, a Quartz row or a shared job table.
- The error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the naming rule come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: application slice split from RWB-E5-008 for rwb-litigation. The four legacy acceptance criteria are kept word for word with their origin tag and now run as one step of `LitigationWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-litigation`; the panel, the scorecard and the firm decline come from rwb-partner (S9) on its published contract, because `partner` and `partner_instruction` are S9's tables and not this service's; the legacy `recovery_case` route states `FIRM_SELECTION` and `FIRM_DECLINED` stay with rwb-case (P3) and are answered, not written; the legacy `DecisionLogWriter` write becomes the local decision record of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON written before the legal action changes (DP-03); the base becomes `/api/recovery/litigation/v1` (DP-13); SCR-19 and SCR-20 read through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); the legacy `v_ace_score` read has no grant here, so DP-05 applies as a prohibition (GAP-2778; ASM-4612). The panel read, the decline read and the case-move answer have no contract story in the plan and no C row (GAP-2773; ASM-4607). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer**, I want **the Workbench to pick the firm by the panel rule: scorecard, capacity, court and conflict, so that cases reach court faster with complete packs**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E5-008. It owns:

- all four legacy acceptance criteria of the story, copied verbatim with their origin tag, and the rules, messages, screens and data rows they depend on;
- the firm-selection step of `LitigationWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-litigation` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, as the stage child of `CaseWorkflow` owned by rwb-case (Architecture v5 slide 19, "LitigationWorkflow (years; continues-as-new)"; Temporal and Drools Design slides 5, 7 and 20);
- the evaluation of R-LIT-23 on the pack-verified fact and of R-LIT-27 on the decline fact, with the LITIGATION package version in force;
- the write of `law_firm_id` (DF-LEG-003) on the `legal_action` of the case in schema `rwb_litigation`, once per selection and once per re-selection, with no new column;
- the local decision record of the selection with the rule ID and the version, written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON before the legal action changes (DP-03);
- the answer to rwb-case for the case move `FIRM_SELECTION` or `FIRM_DECLINED`, with the rule and the version that produced it;
- `GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId}` and `PATCH /legal-actions/{legalActionId}` on base `/api/recovery/litigation/v1` under capability area "Litigation" with the rights R and U (DP-13; TSD S4 T-A.1);
- SCR-19 Litigation workspace in its pack and instructed states, read through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

It does not own: the published shape of the three legal-action operations, the `law_firm_id` element, the panel and case-move rows, the error set and the fakes, which are RWB-S4-E5008-CON; the panel, its scorecard, its capacity, its court coverage and its conflict status, which are rwb-partner's (S9); the issue of the instruction itself and the partner clock, which are `RWB-S4-E5009-APP`'s and rwb-partner's; the case of record and the route states `FIRM_SELECTION` and `FIRM_DECLINED`, which are rwb-case's (P3); the authoring and approval of the LITIGATION package and of the two rule rows, which are rwb-decision's (P7); the pack and its documents, which are rwb-document's (P5); and the deployment, the flag and the runbook, which are the operations story of this legacy key.

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E5-008 gave the Workbench one unattended step that read the panel, scored the firms, weighed capacity, court and conflict and picked the firm, and it kept two rule outcomes: R-LIT-23 selected the firm by rule once `pack_verified_at` was set, and R-LIT-27 recorded the decline and re-selected the next firm on the scorecard. The functional specification keeps the objective and its metric — a litigation turnaround of 6 days against the 21 days a filing takes today, measured on the decision log and the Workbench records, reviewed monthly — and the program keeps the requirement: REQ-S4-004, "A law firm is selected from the panel by rule using panel performance, and instructed through the partner portal" (FSD S4 A2.8 and its requirements-served list).

What D-RCV-60 changes is who owns the panel and who owns the case. In the monolith the panel row, the instruction row, the case state and the decision log row sat in one `recovery` schema and one process. In the target:

- **the panel is rwb-partner's (S9).** `partner` and `partner_instruction` are S9's tables, and the panel status, the scorecard, the capacity, the court coverage and the conflict check are answered there (Ownership Map: partner and partner_instruction owner S9; TSD S9 T3.1 and API-S9-001 "List partners with panel status and score"). This story reads them on the owner's contract and its fake, holds no panel row and writes none (GAP-2778; ASM-4612);
- **the case of record stays with rwb-case (P3).** `recovery_case` and the route states `FIRM_SELECTION` and `FIRM_DECLINED` are P3's; this story evaluates the rule, writes the selected firm on its own legal action, records the decision and **answers** rwb-case for the case move (GAP-2773; ASM-4607);
- **the legal action and the selected firm stay with rwb-litigation (S4).** `legal_action.law_firm_id` (DF-LEG-003) is this service's column and the firm reference it holds is the S9 partner reference, an identifier and not a foreign key across schemas (DP-01);
- **the selection rule is rwb-decision's.** The rule rows of R-LIT-23 and R-LIT-27, the package version and the scorecard weights are authored, tested and approved in rwb-decision (P7) and loaded here; no weight, threshold, window or role is a constant of this build (GAP-2777; ASM-4611);
- **the decision is recorded first**, through the local decision-record library of DP-03 in the same transaction as the legal action change, which is what legacy AC1 asked for and legacy AC4 tested;
- **no ACE view is read here.** The legacy data table lists `v_ace_score`; the ACE view contract and the score facts are rwb-source-data's (P1) and the scorecard of a panel firm is S9's, so DP-05 applies to this story as a prohibition and the service holds no `v_ace_*` grant (GAP-2778; ASM-4612).

The decline is not carried by an event here. rwb-partner produces `PartnerResultSubmitted`, whose consumer row lists rwb-litigation, but DP-09 is not in this story's pattern set, it writes no inbox row, and the S4 IN row of the service card names the event without assigning it to this step; the decline therefore arrives on the rwb-partner contract, one hop with a 2 s budget, and this story publishes and consumes nothing (GAP-2774; ASM-4608). The agreement between the legacy wording and the target is exactly this: the panel and the scorecard are rwb-partner's, the case route state is rwb-case's, and this story evaluates the rule, writes the firm on its legal action and answers the case move.

No business value moves. The scorecard weights, the capacity test, the court coverage set, the conflict check, the 2-working-day window of R-LIT-27 and the D7 decision level are values and reference rows with a version, read from the package and from reference data.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S4-E5008-CON is published: the three legal-action operations, the `law_firm_id` element of `LegalAction` and `LegalActionUpdate`, the panel and case-move rows, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the error set and the fakes are baselined and handed to this story.
- The panel list operation of rwb-partner (API-S9-001 `GET /partners` "List partners with panel status and score", on base `/api/recovery/partner/v1`) and the instruction read that answers a decline (API-S9-003/API-S9-004 of the partner set) are published with their fakes. Neither names a contract story in the plan and neither operation shape is fixed for the S9 side: the operation names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2773; ASM-4607).
- The case-move answer of rwb-case is available for the fake. No source names a published operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage; on the workflow boundary the answer is the stage outcome that the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies to the case of record, and where rwb-case publishes a REST case-move operation its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2773; ASM-4607).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: the local decision-record library writes in the caller's transaction and a failed write stops the action with MSG-P7-003, so the legal action change and its record commit together or not at all (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-19 Litigation workspace reaches this service through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, and no screen calls a service directly (DP-19).
- `legal_action` exists in schema `rwb_litigation` from the DB story of this service, with the columns of DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014 and the standard record columns of TSD S4 T3.0; this story writes one of the existing columns and adds no table, no column and no migration.
- The LITIGATION rule package is in force at its version, with R-LIT-23 and R-LIT-27 in it. The rule rows, the scorecard weights, the capacity test, the court coverage set, the conflict check and the 2-working-day accept window have no content in any source read for this key and are governed in rwb-decision (GAP-2777; ASM-4611).
- The service runs as its own login on schema `rwb_litigation`; it holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `rwb_partner`, `rwb_case` or `v_ace_score` is refused by the database and fails the boundary test (DP-05; GAP-2778; ASM-4612).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-S4-E5008-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The pack of the case is verified and approved in the pack stories of this service; the fact that starts the selection is the arrival of the pack-approved fact for a case in `PACK_VERIFIED` (R-LIT-23). The legacy story says the step runs unattended and the FSD declares no background event, so the trigger is this story's design and is carried as the working read of the assumption (GAP-2775; ASM-4609).
2. The step reads the legal action of the case on `GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId}` (API-S4-003): the action type, `case_id` (DF-LEG-002), `court_name` (DF-LEG-008) and the current `law_firm_id` (DF-LEG-003).
3. `PanelClient` reads the panel on the rwb-partner contract (API-S9-001): for each firm its partner reference, `partner_type` (DF-PRT-004), `panel_status` (DF-PRT-005), contract end (DF-PRT-007), its score and its capacity, court coverage and conflict status, one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker (GAP-2778; ASM-4612).
4. `FirmSelectionEvaluator` loads the LITIGATION package version in force from rwb-decision and evaluates R-LIT-23 on the pack-verified fact and on the panel answer: the firm is scored, it has capacity, it covers the court of the case and it passes the conflict check.
5. The evaluation answers the rule ID, the package version, the selected firm reference, the ranked shortlist and the case move the rule names (FSD S4 A2.8.3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4).
6. `SelectionDecisionRecordWriter` writes one decision record through the local decision-record library, **before any change**: the case reference, the legal action reference, the rule ID with its version, the ranked shortlist reference, the selected firm and the case move. A failed write stops the step with nothing changed (DP-03; legacy AC1 and AC4).
7. `LegalActionFirmWriter` patches the legal action on `PATCH /legal-actions/{legalActionId}` (API-S4-004) in one `rwb_litigation` transaction with the decision record and the idempotency row: `law_firm_id` (DF-LEG-003) becomes the selected firm reference. No other column changes; `status` stays `OPEN` until a filing is recorded, and `hearing` is untouched.
8. `CaseMoveAnswer` answers rwb-case with the case move `FIRM_SELECTION`, the rule ID, the version and the decided-at time. rwb-case writes the `recovery_case` row and its route state; this service writes neither.
9. On R-LIT-27 the decline of the instruction arrives on the rwb-partner contract: the step records the decline on the decision record, re-selects the next firm on the ranked shortlist of the scorecard with the same evaluation, patches `law_firm_id` to the next firm, and answers the case move `FIRM_DECLINED` with the rule and the version.
10. A repeated pack-approved fact, or the same `Idempotency-Key`, writes nothing, sends no second case-move answer and counts the repeat.
11. SCR-19 Litigation workspace shows the selected firm, the ranked shortlist and the case state through the gateway-bff composite route, read only, next to the case and the route state of rwb-case and the instruction of rwb-partner (DP-19).
12. Where no panel firm covers the court, has capacity, or passes the conflict check, no rule of this story fires: the case is escalated by R-LIT-25 on the sibling story of this service and this step writes nothing.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The local decision record cannot be written | The transaction writes nothing: `law_firm_id` keeps its value and no case-move answer leaves the service | MSG-P7-003 | AC4, TC-E5-008-04, TC-E5-008-06 |
| X2 | The role does not hold the Litigation right of the operation | 403 before any read or write; nothing changes and no decision record is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC2, AC3, TC-E5-008-05 |
| X3 | The legal action does not exist or is outside the scope | 404 and nothing is written; the caller cannot tell an out-of-scope action from a missing one | None | AC2, AC3 |
| X4 | The legal action is `CLOSED` or `WITHDRAWN`, or is not the action type the rule needs | 409 and nothing changes; no firm is selected on a closed action | None | AC2, AC3 |
| X5 | The rwb-partner panel read or the rwb-case answer does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The step waits and retries on the workflow's own schedule; nothing is written and no case move is answered, and the caller sees 503 with the platform error envelope | None | AC1, AC3 |
| X6 | No panel firm covers the court, has capacity, or passes the conflict check | No rule fires: nothing changes, no decision record is written, and the escalation of R-LIT-25 is the sibling story's | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X7 | The instruction is declined, or is not accepted inside the window of R-LIT-27 | The decline is recorded on the decision record, the next firm on the scorecard is selected and the case move `FIRM_DECLINED` is answered | None | AC3 |
| X8 | The same pack-approved fact or the same `Idempotency-Key` arrives twice | One write and one case-move answer; the repeat is counted and no second decision record is written | None | AC1 |
| X9 | The rule package in force is not the one the step was started on | The step re-evaluates on the package named on `RulePackageInForce` and records the version it used | None | AC1 |
| X10 | A component, a statement or a test reads a `partner` or `partner_instruction` row, a `recovery_case` row, a `v_ace_*` view or another service's schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | Section 17, BR5, BR8 |

X1 to X4 and X7 are the exception paths of RWB-E5-008 carried onto the split, X5, X6, X8 and X9 are the paths the target call types and the rule package add, and X10 is the DP-05 and DP-01 boundary. The weights, the window and the court set of X6 and X7 are values in force, so none is a constant of this story.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-S4-E5008-CON, the rwb-partner and rwb-case fakes and the rule-package fake, on the table of its own schema, and needs no live rwb-partner, no live rwb-case and no live rwb-decision |
| Negotiable | The activity name, the decision code per rule, the shape of the ranked shortlist and the stage outcome are this story's choice; the rules, the messages, the screens, the operations and the `law_firm_id` element are fixed |
| Valuable | The firm is picked once by rule, with the reason and the version recorded, and the case moves in the service that owns it |
| Estimable | One workflow step, one evaluator, one record write, one column write, one case-move answer, two clients and one read-only screen fragment |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on synthetic cases and panel answers through the contract fakes, plus the access answer and the failed record write |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Select the law firm from the panel

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-000805" carries the legal action "LA-2026-000805" of action type "CIVIL_CASE" with status "OPEN" and no firm selected
    Given the LITIGATION rule package is in force at its version and carries R-LIT-23 and R-LIT-27
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 Select the law firm from the panel (legacy RWB-E5-008 AC1)
    Given the rwb-partner contract mock returns the panel of firms with their scorecard, capacity, court coverage and conflict status
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case state "PACK_VERIFIED" for "RC-2026-000805"
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When its trigger arrives
    Then picks the firm by the panel rule: scorecard, capacity, court and conflict
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Rule R-LIT-23 (legacy RWB-E5-008 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case state "PACK_VERIFIED" for "RC-2026-000805"
    Given the rwb-partner contract mock returns the panel firm selected for legal action "LA-2026-000805"
    Given a case in state PACK_VERIFIED
    When pack approved
    Then select the law firm by rule from the panel
    Then the case moves to FIRM_SELECTION

  Scenario: AC3 Rule R-LIT-27 (legacy RWB-E5-008 AC3)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case state "FIRM_INSTRUCTED" for "RC-2026-000805"
    Given the rwb-partner contract mock returns the instruction declined and the next firm on the scorecard for legal action "LA-2026-000805"
    Given a case in state FIRM_INSTRUCTED
    When instruction declined
    Then record the decline and re-select the next firm on the scorecard
    Then the case moves to FIRM_DECLINED

  Scenario: AC4 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E5-008 AC4)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The four criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E5-008 word for word, with their origin tag added and nothing else changed: the repetition of `Then`, the legacy wording of `the action is taken`, `the decision log cannot be written` and `its trigger arrives` all stand. The cross-service parts are mocked, so AC1 to AC3 each carry their `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` lines and those added `Given` lines are the only additions to the legacy text. What the legacy lines describe happens in three places in the target: rwb-partner answers the panel, the scorecard and the decline; this story evaluates R-LIT-23 or R-LIT-27, writes the decision record with the rule version and the selected firm on the legal action; and rwb-case writes the case move to `FIRM_SELECTION` or `FIRM_DECLINED`. No `partner`, `partner_instruction`, `recovery_case` or `v_ace_score` row is read or written as a table here (GAP-2773, GAP-2778; ASM-4607, ASM-4612).

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-LIT-23 | Litigation | D7 | PACK_VERIFIED | PACK_APPROVED | pack_verified_at set | Select the law firm by rule from the panel | FIRM_SELECTION | Workbench | Rules component, partner performance data | Same day |
| R-LIT-27 | Litigation | D7 | FIRM_INSTRUCTED | INSTRUCTION_DECLINED | the firm declines, or does not accept inside the window | Record the decline and re-select the next firm on the scorecard | FIRM_DECLINED | Workbench | Partner Portal | 2 working days |

The two rows are the rows of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, copied character for character, and they are the two rules the legacy criteria of this story name. Their owner column is a role of the business and not a service: the `Workbench` of both rows is the record this story writes on the legal action and on the decision record, while the to state is a case route state of rwb-case and is answered, not written. The systems column names the Rules component, which is rwb-decision, and the partner performance data and the Partner Portal, which are rwb-partner's.

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The legal action and the selected firm are this service's: `law_firm_id` (DF-LEG-003) is a column of `legal_action` in `rwb_litigation`, and no other service writes it | Architecture v5 slide 41 (rwb-litigation owns legal actions, hearings, judgments); Ownership Map (legal_action owner S4); TSD S4 T3.1 |
| BR2 | The decision is recorded before the legal action changes, with the rule ID and the package version in force; a failed write changes nothing and the caller sees MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; TSD S4 T2 ("writes the decision log entry before any change"); legacy RWB-E5-008 AC1 and AC4 |
| BR3 | The panel stays with rwb-partner: this story holds no `partner` or `partner_instruction` row, reads them on the owner's contract only, and writes no score, no panel status and no decline | Ownership Map (partner and partner_instruction owner S9); TSD S9 T3.1 and API-S9-001; GAP-2778 |
| BR4 | The case move is answered and not written: `recovery_case` and the route states `FIRM_SELECTION` and `FIRM_DECLINED` are rwb-case's, and this story sends the move with the rule and its version | Ownership Map (recovery_case owner P3); Architecture v5 slide 41; GAP-2773 |
| BR5 | No ACE view and no ACE table is read or written here, and no cross-schema join is made: the scorecard and the score facts arrive on the owners' contracts, and the court facts are this service's own columns | DP-05; Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41 (the ACE view contract is P1's); GAP-2778 |
| BR6 | One firm per selection, and one re-selection per decline: a second selection without a decline or a new pack-approved fact writes nothing | R-LIT-23 and R-LIT-27 of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; TSD S4 T4 |
| BR7 | The same fact twice, or the same `Idempotency-Key` twice, writes once and answers the case move once | TSD S4 T-A.2 (Idempotency-Key on the write operations); Architecture v5 slide 11 |
| BR8 | The vocabulary is closed: `LOV-LEGAL-TYPE` is NOTICE, CIVIL_CASE, APPEAL, ENFORCEMENT, BANKRUPTCY_PETITION, LED_AUCTION and `LOV-LEGAL-STATUS` is OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED, WITHDRAWN; no state name, list value, weight, window or threshold is written in code | TSD S4 T3.2; BR-S4-008 (FSD S4 A2.8.3.1); Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR9 | No person name, address, contact value or identity number enters `rwb_litigation`, the decision record, a log or an event: the step carries case references, partner references, codes, dates and scores | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17); Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (events carry IDs and facts, never personal data) |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** R-LIT-23 is the selection: the evaluator tests the panel answer against the court, capacity and conflict facts of the case, the record is written, `law_firm_id` takes the selected firm and the case-move answer carries `FIRM_SELECTION`. R-LIT-27 is the re-selection: the decline answered on the rwb-partner contract is recorded, the next firm on the ranked shortlist is written to `law_firm_id` and the case-move answer carries `FIRM_DECLINED`. VR-S4-008-1 of the FSD tests the freshness of the ACE batch of the source and raises MSG-P1-001; this service holds no `v_ace_batch_status` read, so the check belongs to the owner of the data product and the message is carried in section 14 without a path here (GAP-2779; ASM-4613).

##### 9. State transitions

The case route state is rwb-case's and is not changed by this story: the step answers the move and the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies it to the case of record (BR4). What this story does own is the firm on the legal action and the state of the step.

| From (`legal_action.law_firm_id`) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Empty, action type `CIVIL_CASE` or `NOTICE` | PACK_APPROVED under R-LIT-23 | A panel firm is scored, has capacity, covers the court and passes the conflict check | The selected firm reference, with the case-move answer `FIRM_SELECTION` |
| A firm reference, after the case is at `FIRM_INSTRUCTED` | INSTRUCTION_DECLINED under R-LIT-27 | The firm declines, or does not accept inside the window | The next firm on the scorecard, with the decline recorded and the case-move answer `FIRM_DECLINED` |
| CLOSED or WITHDRAWN | Any of the two rules | X4 | Unchanged, refused with 409 |
| Empty | A panel answer with no firm that covers the court, has capacity or passes the conflict check | X6 | Unchanged, no rule fires and no record is written |

| Step execution | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting | The pack-approved fact arrives for a case in `PACK_VERIFIED` | The package in force is loaded | Evaluating |
| Evaluating | The rule fires | The decision record is written | Applying |
| Applying | `law_firm_id` is patched and the case-move answer is sent | The transaction commits | Waiting for the next fact |
| Applying | The record write or the transaction fails | X1 | Waiting, nothing changed |
| Waiting | The instruction is declined | X7 | Evaluating on the next firm |

`status` (DF-LEG-014) is not moved by this story: it stays `OPEN` until a filing writes `FILED`. The route states `PACK_VERIFIED`, `FIRM_SELECTION`, `FIRM_INSTRUCTED` and `FIRM_DECLINED` of the legacy criteria are case route states and are read from rwb-case and asserted on its answer, not on a column of this service.

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| None; runs unattended (the feature of FSD S4 A2.8.3.3) | The primary actor: the step runs under the service identity with no officer task on the happy path |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Litigation CRUA in the TSD S4 T6.1 matrix and "Also uses" in the FSD: reads the action and the shortlist, patches the selection and the re-selection, reads the case move |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Litigation RA: reads the action, the selected firm and the outcome; records no selection |
| RW-HEADLIT, Head of Litigation | Litigation RA: reads, and acts on the nomination and panel-widening paths of the sibling stories, not here |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-ENFORCE, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-WRITEOFF, RW-CREDITAD, RW-GUARANT, RW-AGENCYMG, RW-CONDUCT, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-HEADNPA, RW-HEADASL, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE | Litigation R: read only |
| PT-LAWFIRM, law firm user | Litigation RU on its own instruction, through the partner gateway: it records the decline that produces the fact of R-LIT-27, which is read here on the rwb-partner contract |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-AGENT, SY-DATALOAD | Litigation R or U as the TSD S4 T6.1 matrix gives it: the service identities are subject to the same checks |

The rights above are the rows of TSD S4 T6.1 and nothing wider. The FSD says the feature "runs unattended" with the litigation officer as also-user, and both statements hold: the step runs under the service identity, and the officer acts on SCR-19 and on the re-selection path. DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set: the capability area and the right are declared per operation, and the guard of the access service is a service-template capability, so the check is stated here and not built here.
