Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8, and the notice and ACE rows are the rows the legacy story lists in its Data table, with their owners changed to P6 and P1 by the target. **No new table, no new column and no migration**: this story writes no business table at all, and `decision_record`, `idempotency_key` and `outbox_event` are platform library objects created in `rwb_asset` by the library's own migration (`GAP-2852`; `ASM-4720`).

**No personal data.** The rows this story handles carry identifiers, codes and dates. No name, address, contact value or identity number enters `rwb_asset`, the decision record, a log or a workflow input, and the fixture data of the tests is synthetic. The confirmed address stays in the rwb-comms contact repository and is referenced by its contact key only.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This legacy key owns no REST operation: the Ownership Map gives rwb-asset six operations, `GET /assets`, `GET /assets/{assetId}`, `GET /assets/{assetKey}`, `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings`, `POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings` and `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds`, and none of them is a notice operation. The two operations the legacy story lists are named in 12.2 and 12.8 as other keys' or other services': `GET monolith-base/assets/{assetId}` is API-S5-002, declared by RWB-S5-E3019-CON on `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13), and `POST monolith-base/assets/{assetId}/valuations` is API-S5-003, which belongs to rwb-valuation under the Ownership Map ruling ASM-0043 (`GAP-2853`; `ASM-4722`).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /cases/{caseId}/notices` (API-P6-001) | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | P6 rwb-comms | Requests the statutory sale notice of the case with its type of `LOV-NOTICE`, the addressee role and the `Idempotency-Key`; answers `noticeId`, the sent date, the barcode and the dispatch state; faked |
| `GET /notices/{noticeId}` (API-P6-002) | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | P6 rwb-comms | Reads the notice, its dispatch fields and its proof-of-delivery fields; faked |
| `GET /proof-of-delivery?businessDate=` | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The WIN proof of delivery of the business date: `pod_key`, `account_key`, `notice_ref`, `sent_date`, `barcode`, `callback_date`, `delivery_status`, `sent_type`, `source_system` and `data_as_of`; faked |
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family (read) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case state and the case reference the notice request carries; read only, faked |
| The case-move answer with the failed notice task request (operation name Not specified in the source documents (`GAP-2854`; `ASM-4721`)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The move `FAILED_NOTICE_QUEUE` or `ASSET_PENDING_TAKE_ON` with the rule ID and its version, and the failed notice task with its due date; on the workflow boundary it is the stage outcome the parent applies; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The five rows are contract dependencies of class C that the plan does not carry, because the C row of this slice is None; the absence is recorded as `GAP-2853` and `GAP-2854` with `ASM-4722`.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service's catalogue event is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` on `rwb.asset.events.v1` (Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT and slide 43 row 22), published by the take-on stories of this service; a notice hold, a re-serve and a status read change no asset, so this story publishes nothing. A build that adds an event, a topic or a second producer fails the absence test (`GAP-2853`; `ASM-4723`).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. Architecture v5 slide 19 IN gives rwb-asset `JudgmentRecorded`, `AuctionResult` and `ProceedsMatched`, and none of them is a notice fact, a proof of delivery or a case state; the step starts from the take-on fact of the case and from the re-issue signal the parent forwards. This story therefore holds no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox row of its own.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, the child of `CaseWorkflow`, continues-as-new | `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the route and the rule package in force; signals: the case state answered by rwb-case, the rule package in force, the re-issue answer of the failed notice task and the dispatch answer of rwb-comms |
| `serveStatutoryNotice` | Activity, the one notice step of this story | `rwb-asset` | The case and the notice fact in; the `noticeId`, the barcode, the delivery status, the rule ID with its package version, the case move and the task request out, with the decision record written in one transaction |
| `FailedNoticeTask` | Human task of the workflow kit with an SLA | `rwb-asset` | The task request of the case move answer: the case, the notice reference, the reason and the two-working-day due date |

No child workflow for the case and none for the notice exists in this service; the notice is a request to rwb-comms and not a workflow of its own. The activity name and the task name are target design choices and are fixed by no source document.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step runs from the take-on fact and from the re-issue signal the parent forwards, and owns no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job. The single Schedule of this service is JOB-19 Re-appraisal monthly, which belongs to RWB-S5-E3026-APP (Architecture v5 slide 44; context pack jobs JOB-19). No other Job of slide 44 is owned, moved or registered here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None of this story's own, beyond the platform library objects.

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The local hash-linked record of the notice decision (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated proof row and the answer it holds |

Not owned and never read as a table: `notice` (P6), `recovery_case` and `task` (P3), `document` (P5), `asset` and `asset_sale` and `listing` (S5, the take-on, sale and pricing stories'), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), and every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01, DP-05).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-comms notice fake | The statutory sale notice `N-000622` for case `RC-2026-000622` with barcode `RR123456789TH` and sent date 2026-11-20; the re-issued notice `N-000623` for a confirmed address; a request refused for a withdrawn template; no answer beyond 2 s | AC1, AC3, X5, X6 |
| rwb-source-data proof fake | The delivered proof for `RR123456789TH` with `callback_date` 2026-11-23; the same barcode with `UNDELIVERABLE`; a stale product with its date; a closed batch gate; no row for the date; no answer beyond 2 s | AC1, AC2, X4, X5 |
| rwb-case case-state fake | The states `ASSET_PENDING_TAKE_ON` and `FAILED_NOTICE_QUEUE` of case `RC-2026-000622`; a case in another state | AC1, AC2, AC3, X3 |
| rwb-case move and task fake | The move `FAILED_NOTICE_QUEUE` accepted with the task created and dated; the move `ASSET_PENDING_TAKE_ON` accepted; a move refused because the case is not in the state the rule expects | AC2, AC3, X3 |
| rwb-decision rule-package fake | The DISPOSAL package at its version in force with R-DIS-04 and R-DIS-05 | AC1, AC2, AC3 |
| Local decision-record library stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | AC4, X1 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-21 and SCR-22 answer for case `RC-2026-000622`, with the asset read once from this service and the notice read from rwb-comms | AC1 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The operation name of the case-move answer and of the task request is stubbed from the published documents and carries the placeholder until its owner confirms it (`GAP-2854`; `ASM-4721`).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 5 consumed | The rwb-comms notice request and read, the rwb-source-data proof read, the rwb-case state read and the case-move answer with the task request; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | No event of this step; the decision record goes on the library's `rwb.decision-record.v1` and is not an event of this service |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 1 activity and 1 human task | `AssetDisposalWorkflow`, `serveStatutoryNotice` and `FailedNoticeTask` on `rwb-asset`; no Schedule |
| File | None | No file is read, built or delivered here; the WIN registered-mail file is rwb-comms' through the rwb-integration adapter (DP-16) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset`, module `notice`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset.notice`; no front-end module, because this step adds no screen state and the notice is shown by rwb-comms through the composite route.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 applies only as a prohibition: this service holds no `v_ace_pod` and no `v_ace_contact` grant, reads no ACE view and no ACE table, and the proof is the one the rwb-source-data read answers (`GAP-2854`; `ASM-4724`). DP-03 is the transaction rule of the step: the record and the answer commit together or not at all. DP-13 moves the base of the reads the legacy story names and nothing else. DP-19 is how SCR-21 and SCR-22 reach this service and rwb-comms, one hop through the gateway.

**Dependencies the tables add and the plan does not hold.** The five consumed rows are class C dependencies of this story and the plan's C row is None, so the story builds against their documents and fakes on Day 1 and the absence is recorded as `GAP-2853` and `GAP-2854`. The outbox and inbox library of DP-09 is not needed, because this step publishes and consumes nothing (`ASM-4723`).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` notice branch | Workflow | The step of the journey that waits for the take-on fact or the re-issue signal, loads the package in force and reports the outcome to the parent |
| `serveStatutoryNotice` | Activity | The one step: read the case, request the notice, read the proof, evaluate R-DIS-04 or R-DIS-05, write the record, answer the move and the task |
| `NoticeRequestClient` | Client | `POST /cases/{caseId}/notices` and `GET /notices/{noticeId}` of rwb-comms, one hop, 2 s, breaker, `Idempotency-Key` |
| `ProofOfDeliveryClient` | Client | The `GET /proof-of-delivery?businessDate=` read of rwb-source-data, with its freshness stamp and its batch gate, one hop, 2 s |
| `NoticeServingEvaluator` | Service | The rule evaluation over the DISPOSAL package in force, with the delivery-status and notice-type lists |
| `NoticeDecisionRecordWriter` | Library adapter | Writes the decision record with the rule ID and the version before any change, and refuses the step when the write fails (DP-03) |
| `CaseMoveAnswer` | Client | The case state read, the move and the failed notice task request of rwb-case, one hop, 2 s |
| `FailedNoticeTask` | Workflow kit task | The human task with its SLA, carrying the case, the notice reference, the reason and the due date |

**Database and migrations.** No Flyway file. This story writes no business table; the decision record and the idempotency key are library objects created in `rwb_asset` by the library's migration (DP-03).

**Configuration and reference data.**

- `LOV-NOTICE`, `LOV-DELIVERY` and `LOV-SENT-TYPE` at their version in force (TSD P6 T3.2), read as reference data and never as constants.
- The DISPOSAL package and its version, loaded on `RulePackageInForce`; the two-working-day target and the hold reasons are values of the package and of reference data.
- The capability area "Asset and disposal" and its rights are access rows of rwb-access, read through the guard.
- No parameter is named in the sources for the step itself; the 2 s budget and the single hop are the platform rule of ADR-020.

**Build steps**

1. The notice branch of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` and its input record, registered on `rwb-asset` as the stage child of `CaseWorkflow`.
2. `NoticeRequestClient` against the rwb-comms fake, with the `Idempotency-Key`, the refusal path and the no-answer path (AC1, X5, X6).
3. `ProofOfDeliveryClient` against the rwb-source-data fake, with the freshness stamp, the batch gate, the absent row and the no-answer path (AC1, X4, X5).
4. `NoticeServingEvaluator` over the DISPOSAL package, with R-DIS-04 and R-DIS-05 and the no-fire path (AC1, AC2, AC3).
5. `NoticeDecisionRecordWriter` against the library stub, with the failed-write path (AC4, X1).
6. `CaseMoveAnswer` with the two moves and the failed notice task request with its due date (AC2, AC3, X3).
7. `FailedNoticeTask` with its SLA and the confirmed contact key of the rwb-comms contact repository (AC3).
8. The idempotency and repeat path (AC1, AC3, X7).
9. The boundary test: no statement outside `rwb_asset`, no `v_ace_pod` and no `v_ace_contact` read, no write to `rwb_case`, `rwb_comms` or `rwb_decision` (X8, BR3, BR5).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.asset.notice-serving-v1`, read as a flag of the platform library; off means the step holds the fact, writes nothing and answers no move, and the take-on stories keep their own path.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the step requests a notice and reads a proof against the fakes, each of the two rules produces its record, its move and its task, a repeated proof row answers once, a forced record failure changes nothing, no `notice` and no `v_ace_*` read exists in the build, and SCR-21 and SCR-22 answer through the gateway-bff composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S5-001 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names the floor percentage and the approval limit, which are the pricing story's, so no path of this story raises it | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names the age of an appraisal, which is the re-appraisal story's, so no path of this story raises it | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of the notice request or of a request body is absent or invalid (X3, X6) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Asset and disposal right acts on the failed notice task (X2) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the notice answer (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The WIN proof-of-delivery data product is stale, gated or absent (X4, VR-S5-004-1) | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The six message IDs are those of the legacy message set and of FSD S5 A2.4.3.1, and the text is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new one is added. MSG-S5-001 and MSG-S5-002 are carried because they are in the message set of the feature, and no path of this story raises them.

##### 15. Screens and states

The legacy story names SCR-21 Asset list in its loading and list states and SCR-22 Asset record in its take-on, held, listed and sold states, all served through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). Neither screen carries a notice state: the composite route calls this service for the asset and its holding status, rwb-case for the case and its route state, rwb-comms for the notice and its delivery status, rwb-source-data for the ACE asset fact and rwb-valuation for the valuation references, and this story fixes no screen field.

The states this story produces are on the case and in the workflow, not on a screen: the case in `FAILED_NOTICE_QUEUE` with its failed notice task, the task in its open, confirmed and closed states, and the hold on the take-on. The officer's work is the failed notice task of rwb-case's worklist, where MSG-P4-002, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P1-001 are shown by the owner of that screen. The composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID; the `-ITG` copies belong to the wave 2 harness and are not owned here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the notice types, the delivery statuses, the hold reasons, the two-working-day target and the rule rows stay data, reference data or the rule package, never a constant, a default or a branch of the build.
- No personal data in `rwb_asset`, in a decision record, in a workflow input or in a log: identifiers, codes and dates only, the address stays in the rwb-comms contact repository, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: this service holds no `v_ace_pod` and no `v_ace_contact` grant, and a build that adds one fails the boundary test (DP-05).
- The notice stays with rwb-comms, the case and its task with rwb-case, the proof with rwb-source-data and the record of the decision with rwb-decision: this story writes none of their rows (BR1, BR3, BR4).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; no document, module or test names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no shared job table, no Quartz row, no monolith base `/api/recovery/v1`, no second producer on `rwb.asset.events.v1`.
- The decision is recorded before the answer leaves the service; a build that answers a move before the record commits fails the review (DP-03).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of the holding-age and provision-step step of rwb-asset, split from RWB-E3-023. It fixes the two read operations on `/api/recovery/asset/v1` with the holding section (DP-13), the holding-age and provision-step elements with their placeholder where no source gives a field name, the provision input element handed to the Finance provision feed, the durable timer contract of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`, the consumed rwb-source-data, rwb-case and rwb-payment rows, the decision-record element of DP-03, the fakes and the absence tests. The plan's C row is None although four owner contracts are consumed, no source gives the thresholds or the feed route, and DP-09, DP-10 and DP-14 are held as prohibitions (GAP-2855, GAP-2856; ASM-4726, ASM-4727, ASM-4730). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the holding-age and provision-step step of rwb-asset — the two asset reads with the holding section, the holding-age and provision-step elements, the provision input element, the timer contract, the consumed rwb-source-data, rwb-case and rwb-payment rows, the decision-record element, the tables and the fakes**, so that **the app story, the two screens and the wave 2 harness build against one fixed, testable contract on Day 1 and a holding field, a threshold, a provision input or an answer shape can never drift between rwb-asset, rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-payment without a failing build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy holding step of RWB-E3-023 crossed four boundaries at once: an officer screen, the ACE asset fact, the case state and a monthly charge. The target splits them: rwb-source-data owns the ACE asset fact, rwb-case owns the case and its route states, rwb-payment owns the charge and the ledger, rwb-decision governs the thresholds, and rwb-asset owns the holding age, the provision step and the decision that applies it. Each boundary is a contract another team builds against, so each is fixed before the app story starts.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_asset`, base `/api/recovery/asset/v1`, topic `rwb.asset.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset`. It records that rwb-asset holds no `v_ace_*` grant and no grant on `rwb_case` or `rwb_payment`, so DP-05 is declared as a prohibition and the asset fact is consumed on the owner's contract only.

Four points are carried as gaps and assumptions rather than decided quietly: no source available to this WP prints the provision thresholds, the step percentages or the cost-of-carry rate, and the FSD S5 and TSD S5 files named by the WP are absent from `_work/msr/extract` (GAP-2855), the provision input element, the Finance feed route and the rwb-payment activity have no published name (GAP-2856), the plan's C row is None although four owner contracts are consumed (GAP-2856), and the clocks replace Quartz jobs without a Schedule, so DP-10 is a prohibition rather than a dependency (ASM-4726).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the queue and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the pagination and filter convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline; where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The ownership of the objects is taken from the Ownership Map only: `listing` and `asset_sale` are S5's, `recovery_case`, `timer` and `task` are P3's, `proceeds` is P8's, `document` is P5's, `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` and `rule_package` are P7's. This document never declares another service's table or operation as its own.
- The rwb-source-data data-product contract of DP06 Collateral and assets, the rwb-case state and move rows and the rwb-payment activity are published with their fakes, so the consumed rows name a real owner document; they are not in this story's contract-dependency row, which is None, and the absence is recorded (GAP-2856; ASM-4730).
- The DISPOSAL rule package and its rule rows for R-DIS-06 and R-DIS-09 are governed in rwb-decision (P7); this baseline names them, declares none of them and prints none of their values.
- The `asset` table and its columns arrive with the DB story of this service; this baseline declares shapes and creates no table, no column and no migration (GAP-2855).
- The Finance provision feed publishes its own interface; where it does not, the row carries the placeholder and the fake derives from this document (ASM-4729).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7), and the missing approval of the sources is recorded rather than waited on (GAP-2858; ASM-4734).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-asset for this step: the two reads with their request and answer elements, the filters, the rights and the error responses.
2. Fix the holding section of the `Asset` element: the fields the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 gives (DF-COL-031 to DF-COL-040) and the holding age, the cost to date and the next provision step date, each with the placeholder where no source gives a name or a type.
3. Fix the provision input element: what leaves for the Finance provision feed, with the case reference, the asset reference, the threshold, the step applied, the rule ID with its version and no personal data.
4. Fix the timer contract of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`: the two timer names, their start dates, their end dates, their rearm rule and their pause behaviour, and state that they are durable timers and not Schedules.
5. Fix the consumed rows: the rwb-source-data asset read, the rwb-case state read and move answer, and the rwb-payment cost-of-carry activity, marking the fields the sources do not give with the placeholder.
6. Record the decision-record element of DP-03, written before the asset changes.
7. Record the closed vocabulary, the naming baseline and the rule that no threshold, percentage or rate is a constant of the code.
8. Publish the contract tables of section 12 and the fakes of 12.8.
9. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the additive rule, the vocabulary, the shapes, the placeholder rule, the error envelope, the absence of a `v_ace_*` read, of a `recovery_case` write, of a `timer` write, of an event and of a Schedule, and the drift between a fake and the document.
10. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-S5-E3023-APP, the two screens and the wave 2 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body or a request body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 400 or 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC5 |
| X2 | A property is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X3 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC5 |
| X4 | A consumed row or a holding property has a name or a type the sources do not give | The row carries the placeholder, the gap and the assumption, and the fake is derived from the published document | None | AC2, AC3, AC4 |
| X5 | A threshold, a step percentage or a rate appears as a schema default, an enumeration member or an example value | The vocabulary test fails the build; a value that is not in the package is never published | None | AC2 |
| X6 | The document declares another service's operation as provided, a `v_ace_*` view, a `recovery_case`, `timer` or `proceeds` row | The review fails the baseline; the boundary test fails the build | None | AC5 |
| X7 | The document declares a consumed or published event, a second topic or a Temporal Schedule | The absence test fails the build | None | AC5 |
| X8 | The rights of an operation are not the ones the legacy permission table and the access matrix declare | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the Ownership Map, the Logical Data Model and the published owner contracts of rwb-source-data, rwb-case and rwb-payment only |
| Negotiable | The element names beyond the ones the sources give, the example values and the fake fixtures are settled in the baseline review; the operations, the base, the queue, the timers and the prohibitions are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks RWB-S5-E3023-APP, the two screens and the wave 2 harness on Day 1, and the rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-payment and rwb-decision teams on the same day |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, one AsyncAPI absence statement, nine contract tables, eight fakes and five new contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

These six criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only. They restate no business outcome owned by RWB-S5-E3023-APP and they copy no criterion of the legacy story, whose three criteria stay with the app story word for word.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The holding section, the age and the provision-step elements are rwb-asset's, and the contract declares them on the `Asset` element and on the provision input only | Architecture v5 slide 41; FEAT-AST-05; REQ-S5-003 |
| BR2 | The decision record is declared as an element written before the asset changes, through the local library on the shared topic; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; legacy RWB-E3-023 AC1 and AC3 |
| BR3 | The clocks are declared as durable timers of the workflow: no Schedule, no Quartz row and no job table is declared, and the `timer` row stays P3's | DP-10 as a prohibition; ASM-4726, ASM-4728 |
| BR4 | The ACE asset fact stays with rwb-source-data: the contract declares the data-product read as consumed, declares no `v_ace_*` property and describes no ACE table read of rwb-asset | DP-05; Architecture v5 slides 29, 37 and 45; ASM-4731 |
| BR5 | The case move is answered and not written: the contract declares the state read and the answer, and no `recovery_case` property and no case row write | Ownership Map (recovery_case owner P3); ASM-4730 |
| BR6 | The money is rwb-payment's: the cost of carry and the ledger effect of the provision step are declared as its activity and its feed, never as a property of this service | Architecture v5 slide 13 (S5 to P8, Temporal and events); ASM-4729 |
| BR7 | The vocabulary is closed and the values are not published: the thresholds, the step percentages and the rate are package and reference values, named as inputs and never printed as defaults or members | FEAT-AST-05; BR2; GAP-2855 |
| BR8 | A property whose name or type no source gives carries the placeholder and one gap row; a placeholder is resolved by its owner and never by a guess | Template and Rules v1 §R9; GAP-2855, GAP-2856 |
| BR9 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version only | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR10 | One REST base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; the document never declares another service's base, topic or queue as its own | DP-13, DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR11 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version | Platform versioning rule |
| BR12 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-asset; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | Ownership Map; DP-11 |

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of this document, not of an asset:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The two reads, the holding section, the provision input, the timers, the consumed rows and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, the two screens, the wave 2 harness and the rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-payment and rwb-decision owners accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example a new filter or a new optional holding field | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or the meaning of a timer changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | The absence tests of AC3 and AC6 fail: an event, a topic, a Schedule, a job row, a `v_ace_*` view, a `recovery_case` or `timer` property | In review |
| Baselined | A value is published | The vocabulary test of AC2 fails because a threshold or a rate appears in the document | In review |

The clock and step states the document describes are the app story's, and this baseline fixes only their names, their inputs and their pause rule; it moves no asset and arms no timer itself.

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-asset | Owns the OpenAPI document and the contract tables; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version, and the removal of a placeholder when its owner publishes the name |
| Consuming teams (the app story, the two screens, the wave 2 harness and the owners of rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-payment, rwb-decision and rwb-access) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |

The per-service login behind the security scheme of the document is named "the rwb-asset login (DP-02)" and is not part of this baseline.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Asset element | The properties of DF-COL-031 to DF-COL-040: `asset_ref`, `asset_code`, `asset_type`, `transfer_in_type`, `from_segment`, `transfer_in_date`, `book_value`, `auction_purchase_price`, `repossessed_date` and `stock_date` |
| Holding section | A holding start date, a holding age in days, a cost to date and a next provision step date, read only; the names and types not given by a source carry the placeholder Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2855; ASM-4726) |
| Provision-step element | The threshold, the step applied, the rule ID, the package version in force and the Finance input reference, with the placeholder for the names the sources do not give |
| Provision input | The case reference, the asset reference, the threshold, the step applied and the rule ID with its version; the element name and the feed route are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2856; ASM-4729) |
| Timers | The holding age timer and the provision step timer of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`: start date, end date, rearm rule and pause behaviour (ASM-4726) |
| Decision record | DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 through the local library, written before the asset changes (DP-03) |
| Not declared here | `recovery_case`, `timer` and `task` (P3), `document` (P5), `proceeds` (P8), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` and `rule_package` (P7), `listing` and `asset_sale` (S5, later stories'), every `v_ace_*` view (P1) |

The field-level types, lengths and required flags of the added elements are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the element names, the placeholders, the vocabulary rule of AC2 and the optionality rule of BR11. **No new table, no new column and no migration** is declared by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated by page and size | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not declared |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out, with its holding section, its cost to date and its next provision step date | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not declared |

The two operations answer 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503, each with the error envelope and one message ID of section 14. The paths are those of the target base, not the monolith form. `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings` and `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds` belong to the pricing and auction stories of this service and are not declared by this baseline.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| The read of DP06 Collateral and assets (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2856; ASM-4730)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The ACE NPA asset fact: stock date, book value, asset type, transfer-in type and the freshness stamp; faked |
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family (read) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case state, the case reference and the title status the confirmation carries; faked |
| The case-move answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2856; ASM-4730)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The move `ASSET_HELD` with the rule ID and its version; on the workflow boundary it is the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The three rows are contract dependencies of class C that the plan's C row does not carry, and the absence is recorded as GAP-2856 with ASM-4730. The cost-of-carry request and the Finance provision input are not REST rows of this service: the first is a Temporal activity (12.5) and the second leaves on the feed (12.3).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT gives rwb-asset `AssetTakenOn` and `AssetSold`, and neither is a holding-age or provision-step event; the provision input leaves on the Finance provision feed and not on a Kafka topic. This baseline therefore declares no published event, no consumer group of its own and no outbox row, and the absence test of AC3 fails a build that adds one (GAP-2856; ASM-4727).

| Element published outside Kafka | Owner of the target | Documented content |
|---|---|---|
| The provision input to the Finance provision feed | The feed's owner; the route is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2856; ASM-4729) | The case reference, the asset reference, the threshold, the step applied and the rule ID with its version; no amount, balance or personal data |

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. Architecture v5 slide 19 IN gives rwb-asset `JudgmentRecorded`, `AuctionResult` and `ProceedsMatched`, and none of them starts a holding-age or provision-step step; the step is started by the confirmation signal the parent forwards and by its own durable timer. This baseline therefore declares no consumer group, no subscription, no inbox of its own and no Kafka call from this step, and the absence test of AC3 fails a build that adds one.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, the child of `CaseWorkflow`, continues-as-new across the years of the holding | `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | The stage that hosts the holding and provision steps; its signals, its two timers and its outcome for the parent are declared, not built |
| `applyHoldingStep` | Activity, the confirmation step | `rwb-asset` | The case and the confirmation in; the rule ID with its package version, the holding start date, the next provision step date, the cost to date and the case move out |
| `applyProvisionStep` | Activity, the provision step | `rwb-asset` | The case, the threshold and the asset in; the rule ID with its package version, the step applied, the provision input reference and the next threshold out |
| `requestCostOfCarry` | Activity, on the owner's queue, activity name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2856; ASM-4729) | `rwb-payment` | The case, the asset, the month, the book value and the rule version in; the posted amount and its posting reference out |

No child workflow for the case and none for the money exists in this service, and this baseline registers no activity. The two activity names of rwb-asset are a target design choice and no source document fixes them (ASM-4735).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The clocks are durable timers inside the workflow and not Temporal Schedules; this baseline declares no Schedule, no Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table, and no Job of Architecture v5 slide 44 is owned or moved here. JOB-19 Re-appraisal monthly is the service's single Schedule and belongs to RWB-S5-E3026-APP (ASM-4726).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| asset | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The held asset, its properties and its holding section; the table the two reads answer from |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The local hash-linked decision record of the rule outcome (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated confirmation and the threshold it holds |

`recovery_case`, `timer` and `task` (P3), `proceeds` (P8), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` and `rule_package` (P7), `listing` and `asset_sale` (S5, later stories') and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) are not owned by this baseline; it names them only as answers, rule versions or a later story's table, and no foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-source-data data-product fake | The asset facts of asset `AST-2026-000511` with stock date, book value, asset type and transfer-in type; a stale product with its date; no answer beyond 2 s; an unreadable answer | AC1, AC4, AC5 |
| rwb-case state fake | The states `ASSET_ON_BOOKS`, `ASSET_HELD` and `DISPOSAL_PAUSED_DEVIATION`, with title status `clear`, `under_transfer` and `encumbered` | AC4, AC5 |
| rwb-case move fake | The move `ASSET_HELD` accepted and the same move refused | AC4, AC5 |
| rwb-payment cost-of-carry fake | The monthly cost of carry recorded with its posting reference; no answer beyond 2 s | AC4, AC5 |
| Finance provision feed fake | The provision input accepted with its reference, and the feed refusing the input and refusing it again after the retry limit | AC3, AC5 |
| rwb-decision rule-package fake | The DISPOSAL package at its version in force with R-DIS-06 and R-DIS-09, and the thresholds as values of the package | AC2, AC5 |
| Local decision-record library stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | AC5 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-21 and SCR-22 answer for case `RC-2026-000511` with the holding section read once | AC1 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The operation names of the rwb-source-data read, of the case-move answer, of the Finance feed and of the rwb-payment activity are derived from the published documents and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-2856; ASM-4729, ASM-4730, ASM-4735).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 3 consumed | The two asset reads on `/api/recovery/asset/v1`; the rwb-source-data data-product read, the rwb-case state read and the case-move answer; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | No event on this step; the decision record is the library's on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and is not an event of this service |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 3 activities declared, 0 registered | `AssetDisposalWorkflow` with `applyHoldingStep` and `applyProvisionStep` on `rwb-asset` and `requestCostOfCarry` on `rwb-payment`; two timers; no Schedule |
| File | None | No file is read, built or delivered here; the Finance feed is not a file of this service |

##### 13. Solution plan

**The CON declares shapes and moves nothing.** It writes no code, no migration and no table, and it changes no asset, no case, no balance and no rule package. What it publishes is one OpenAPI 3.1 document, one absence statement for events, nine contract tables and eight fakes.

**Deliverables.** The additive document `openapi/rwb-asset-v1.yaml`, the `Asset`, `AssetPage`, `HoldingSection` and `ProvisionStep` elements, the provision input element with its placeholder, the timer contract rows of the workflow catalogue entry, the contract README rows for the consumed rows and their placeholders, and the eight WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is declared as a prohibition: the document declares no `v_ace_*` path, no `v_ace_*` property and no grant on any other owner's schema, because rwb-asset holds none (ASM-4731). DP-13 moves the base and nothing else. DP-19 is behind SCR-21 and SCR-22, whose screen model is the edge contract's. DP-09, DP-10 and DP-14 are held as prohibitions and are not declared: no event, no Schedule and no second topic belongs to this step, and the clocks replace the legacy Quartz jobs (ASM-4726, ASM-4727).

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds two H rows, `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` for DP-03 and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` for DP-19, which the plan's build list for this key already carries. The three REST rows and the rwb-payment activity are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata row, and the Finance feed has no owner document (GAP-2856; ASM-4729, ASM-4730).

**Build steps**

1. Write the two reads and validate the additive rule of AC1 in the pipeline.
2. Write the `Asset` properties, the holding section and the provision-step element of AC2, with the placeholder where a name or type is unstated and the vocabulary test on every threshold and rate.
3. Write the provision input element, the feed row, the timer contract and the absence statement of AC3.
4. Record the consumed rwb-source-data, rwb-case and rwb-payment rows of AC4 with their owners, budgets and placeholders.
5. Record the decision-record element, the rights and the eight fakes of AC5 with the drift test.
6. Record the naming baseline and the boundary of AC6, then tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI document validates in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, every placeholder names its gap and assumption, and the app story, the two screens and the wave 2 harness have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S5-001 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names the floor percentage and the approval limit, which are the pricing story's, so no path of this step raises it | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names the age of an appraisal, which is the re-appraisal story's, so no path of this step raises it | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request is absent or invalid, or a body fails schema validation | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the Asset and disposal right the operation declares | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the asset changes | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The five message IDs are contract elements and the text is the legacy wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new one is added. The Finance feed refusal of X6 has no message ID in any source available to this file, so the contract declares only its error code row and the app story raises a task (GAP-2856).

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves SCR-21 Asset list in its loading and list states and SCR-22 Asset record in its take-on, held, listed and sold states, all through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The route calls rwb-asset for the asset and its holding section, rwb-case for the case and its route state, and rwb-source-data for the ACE asset fact; this baseline fixes the rwb-asset answers only, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The refusal and not-recorded states the app story shows read the messages of section 14 on the same route.

| TC-S5-E3023-CON-04 | AC5, AC6 | Contract | The eight fakes match the document, a drifted fake fails the build, and the naming baseline and boundary rows are complete |

The five legacy cases are the legacy cases of RWB-E3-023 in their legacy order, carried as the contract half: their Covers column names the criterion of this story that fixes the surface each one exercises, their Data keeps the legacy intent, and the business outcome of each is proved by RWB-S5-E3023-APP. Legacy level `System` maps to `Contract` here because the artefact under test is the contract, and the access and forced-failure cases map to `Contract` for the same reason. The four cases `TC-S5-E3023-CON-01` to `-04` are new. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID; the `-ITG` copies belong to the wave 2 harness.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the thresholds, the step percentages, the rate, the lists and the rule rows stay data, reference data or the rule package, never a schema default or an enumeration member.
- No personal data in a schema, an example, a provision input or a fake: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version only; every example is synthetic.
- The ACE asset fact stays with rwb-source-data, the case with rwb-case and the money with rwb-payment: the document declares no `v_ace_*` path, no `recovery_case`, `timer` or `proceeds` property and no posting (BR4, BR5, BR6).
- The clocks are durable timers: a document that declares a Schedule, a Quartz row or a job table fails the absence test.
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; a document that names another service's base, topic or queue as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The document lists only operations owned by rwb-asset; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided (DP-01, DP-11).
- Every placeholder names its gap and assumption, and no placeholder is filled by a guess.
- The error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule, the timer kit and the decision-record library come from the platform; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the application slice of RWB-E3-023 split out for rwb-asset. The three legacy criteria are kept word for word with their origin tag; the clocks become durable timers of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` on queue `rwb-asset`, the outcome is recorded through the local decision-record library before anything changes (DP-03), the ACE asset fact arrives on the rwb-source-data contract instead of a `v_ace_*` read (DP-05), the base becomes `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13) and SCR-21 and SCR-22 read through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The thresholds, the step percentages and the cost-of-carry rate are rule and reference values of rwb-decision and are in no source available to this file (GAP-2855; ASM-4726). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As an **nPA and asset manager**, I want **the Workbench to count the days held and apply the provision step the policy sets at each threshold**, so that **assets sell sooner at approved prices**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E3-023. It owns the three legacy criteria; R-DIS-06 on the confirmed record and R-DIS-09 at the next provision step date, with the DISPOSAL package in force; the two clocks as durable timers of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`; the monthly cost-of-carry request on queue `rwb-payment`; the record of every step; the `ASSET_HELD` move answer; and the holding facts the two screens read (Architecture v5 slide 19; Temporal and Drools Design slide 13).

It does not own the shapes of RWB-S5-E3023-CON; the take-on and the `asset` row (RWB-S5-E3019-APP, -E3020-APP, -E3021-APP); the case, its route states, the parent `CaseWorkflow` and the `timer` row (rwb-case, P3); the ACE asset fact (rwb-source-data, P1); the posting and the ledger (rwb-payment, P8); the thresholds, the percentages and the rate (rwb-decision, P7); or the deployment (the operations story of this key).

##### 2. Business rationale

The program keeps the requirement as **REQ-S5-003, "Holding age drives re-appraisal and the provision step by rule"** (Business Requirements Program v4, Must, Epic E3), and the feature extract keeps FEAT-AST-05 with the same scope: it counts the days held, applies the provision step at each threshold, runs unattended, touches AMIS, ALS and GL, and depends on FEAT-AST-01 (Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3).

What D-RCV-60 changes is who owns the asset, the case, the money and the policy. In the monolith the clock, the step, the charge and the log row were one process in one `recovery` schema. In the target the holding facts are this service's (slide 41 gives rwb-asset "assets taken on, holding, floor price, listings, auction rounds"), the case and the `timer` row are P3's, the money is P8's (the S5 row of slide 13 gives P8 a Temporal call, never a posting here), and the policy is versioned rule and reference data read with its version, never written in code.

The case move is not carried by a consumed event: slide 19 IN gives `JudgmentRecorded`, `AuctionResult` and `ProceedsMatched`, none of them a case state, so the state is taken on the rwb-case contract one hop with a 2 s budget. The feature's measure, the NPA sales cycle read on the decision log, does not move.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S5-E3023-CON is published: the two reads, the holding and provision elements, the provision input, the move answer shape, the error set and the fakes are baselined.
- The rwb-source-data data-product contract of DP06 Collateral and assets and the rwb-case state read and move answer are published with their fakes; the operation names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2856; ASM-4730).
- The rwb-payment cost-of-carry activity is published on queue `rwb-payment` with its fake, because the S5 row of slide 13 gives P8 a Temporal call and the charge is P8's; its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2856; ASM-4729).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: the record is written in the caller's transaction and a failed write stops the step with MSG-P7-003 (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the two screens reach this service through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).
- `asset` exists in `rwb_asset` from the DB story with the columns of DF-COL-031 to DF-COL-040 and the standard record columns; this story adds no table, no column and no migration (GAP-2855; ASM-4726).
- The DISPOSAL package is in force at its version with R-DIS-06 and R-DIS-09, governed in rwb-decision (P7); the thresholds, the percentages and the rate are its values and appear in no source available to this file (GAP-2855; ASM-4727).
- The service runs as its own login on `rwb_asset` with no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `recovery.v_ace_npa_asset` or `rwb_case` fails the boundary test (DP-05; ASM-4731).
- The Finance provision feed is reachable through the route its owner publishes; the transport and the element name are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2856; ASM-4729).
- The missing approval of the sources is recorded rather than waited on (GAP-2858; ASM-4734).

##### 4. Flow

1. The take-on step confirms the asset record: the `asset` row exists in `HELD` with its stock date, book value and asset facts; no ACE data is read as a table here (RWB-S5-E3019-APP; DP-05).
2. The holding branch of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` receives the confirmation for a case in `ASSET_ON_BOOKS` and reads the case state, the case reference and the title status on the rwb-case contract, read only (ASM-4730).
3. `HoldingAgeEvaluator` loads the package in force and evaluates R-DIS-06 on the asset fact and title_status in (clear, under_transfer).
4. The evaluation answers the rule ID, the package version, the holding start date, the next provision step date and the case move; where no rule fires the step changes nothing and reports the reason.
5. `HoldingDecisionRecordWriter` writes one record through the library **before any change**: case, asset, rule ID with its version, inputs reference, holding start date and move; a failed write stops the step with nothing changed (DP-03; legacy AC1 and AC3).
6. `HoldingClockArmer` arms the holding age clock from the holding start date and the provision step clock to the next provision step date, both as durable timers that survive a restart, a redeploy and a Continue-As-New (ASM-4726).
7. `CostOfCarryRequester` asks rwb-payment for the monthly charge on queue `rwb-payment` with the case, asset, month, book value and rule version, and writes the cost to date where the DB story publishes a column (ASM-4729).
8. `HoldingWriter` updates `asset` in one `rwb_asset` transaction with the record, the idempotency row and the fields the dictionary gives (DF-COL-031 to DF-COL-040), leaving what the model does not give empty rather than inventing it (GAP-2855).
9. `CaseMoveAnswer` answers rwb-case with `ASSET_HELD`, the rule ID, the version and the decided-at time; rwb-case writes the `recovery_case` row and its route state (ASM-4730).
10. The provision step clock fires when the age reaches the next step date: `ProvisionStepEvaluator` evaluates R-DIS-09, records the outcome before any change, applies the step and hands the input to the Finance provision feed (GAP-2856; ASM-4729).
11. The step rearms the clock for the next threshold and repeats while the case is in `ASSET_HELD`; a deviation pause holds it until the case resumes (ASM-4732).
12. A repeated confirmation with the same case, asset and holding start date writes nothing, arms no clock, answers nothing and counts the repeat.
13. SCR-21 and SCR-22 read the asset, its age, its cost to date and its next step date through the composite route, read only (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The local decision record cannot be written | The transaction writes nothing: no asset change, no clock armed, no cost-of-carry request, no provision input, no answer | MSG-P7-003 | AC3, TC-E3-023-03, TC-E3-023-05 |
| X2 | The role does not hold the Asset and disposal right | 403 before any read or write; nothing changes and no record is written | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E3-023-04 |
| X3 | The case is not in `ASSET_ON_BOOKS` on the confirmation, or not in `ASSET_HELD` when the clock fires | 409 and nothing is written; the step is not re-evaluated on a case that has moved | None | AC2 |
| X4 | The title status is neither clear nor under transfer | No rule fires under R-DIS-06: nothing changes, no clock starts | None | AC2 |
| X5 | A consumed contract does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The step waits and retries on the workflow schedule; nothing is written and no move is answered, and the caller sees 503 | None | AC1 |
| X6 | The Finance provision feed refuses the provision input | The step records the refusal, keeps the asset unchanged, retries, and raises a task after the retry limit; no threshold is skipped | None | AC1 |
| X7 | The same confirmation or the same threshold arrives twice | One record, one asset change and one answer; the repeat is counted | None | AC1 |
| X8 | A component or a test reaches a `v_ace_*` view, a `recovery_case` row, a `timer` row or another schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | Section 17, BR4, BR6 |

X1 to X4 are the legacy exception paths carried onto the split, X5 to X7 are the paths the target call types and the two clocks add, and X8 is the DP-01, DP-05 and DP-10 boundary. No threshold and no rate is a constant of this story.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-S5-E3023-CON, the three owner fakes and the record stub, on its own schema, with no live P1, P3, P7 or P8 |
| Negotiable | The activity names, the decision code per rule and the stage outcome are this story's choice; the rules, messages, screens, reads and timers are fixed |
| Valuable | A held asset carries one holding age and one provision step at a time, recorded with its rule version, and the step reaches Finance without a person |
| Estimable | One workflow branch, two evaluators, one record write, one row update, one cost-of-carry request, one provision input, one move answer, two read fragments |
| Small | Two weeks with its tests on the fakes; the timer rearm loop is the only state it adds |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on synthetic cases and asset facts through the fakes with a shortened interval, plus the access and failed-record cases |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Track holding age against the provision steps

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-000511" holds asset "AST-2026-000511"
    Given the DISPOSAL rule package is in force at its version and carries R-DIS-06 and R-DIS-09
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 Track holding age against the provision steps (legacy RWB-E3-023 AC1)
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns the asset facts of asset "AST-2026-000511" with the stock date and the book value
    Given the rwb-payment contract mock returns the monthly cost of carry recorded for "RC-2026-000511"
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When its trigger arrives
    Then counts the days held and applies the provision step the policy sets at each threshold
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Rule R-DIS-06 (legacy RWB-E3-023 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case state "ASSET_ON_BOOKS" for "RC-2026-000511"
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the title status "clear" for "RC-2026-000511"
    Given the rwb-payment contract mock returns the monthly cost of carry recorded for "RC-2026-000511"
    Given a case in state ASSET_ON_BOOKS
    When asset record confirmed
    Then start the holding age clock and the provision step clock, and charge cost of carry monthly
    Then the case moves to ASSET_HELD

  Scenario: AC3 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E3-023 AC3)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The three criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E3-023 word for word, with their origin tag added and nothing else changed: the repetition of `Then` and the legacy wording of `the action is taken`, `the decision log cannot be written` and `its trigger arrives` all stand. The cross-service parts are mocked, so the `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` lines are the only additions. What they describe happens in four places: rwb-source-data answers the asset fact, rwb-case answers the state, the title status and the move, rwb-payment records the monthly charge, and this story counts the age, applies the step, records the decision, updates the asset and answers the move. AC1 names the provision step of R-DIS-09 and AC2 names R-DIS-06; this story owns both. AC2 is also a legacy criterion of RWB-E3-019, whose story owns its copy for the take-on while this one owns the clocks, and neither runs a second clock (GAP-2855; ASM-4726).

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-DIS-06 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | ASSET_ON_BOOKS | ASSET_RECORD_CONFIRMED | title_status in (clear, under_transfer) | Start the holding age clock and the provision step clock, and charge cost of carry monthly | ASSET_HELD | Sale officer | Workbench, Finance provision feed | None |
| R-DIS-09 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | ASSET_HELD | PROVISION_STEP_DUE | holding_age reaches next_provision_step_date | Apply the provision step and send the input to Finance | ASSET_HELD | Workbench | Finance provision feed, ALS core and GL | None |

Both rows are the rows of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, copied character for character. The owner column is a business role, not a service: rwb-case writes the case move on this story's answer, the asset and its holding facts are written here, and the posting and the feed are P8's and the feed owner's.

|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The holding age and the provision step are this service's facts, derived from the asset dates and the package; no other service computes them | Architecture v5 slide 41; FEAT-AST-05; REQ-S5-003 |
| BR2 | The decision is recorded before the asset changes, with the rule ID and the version in force; a failed write changes nothing and shows MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; legacy AC1 and AC3 |
| BR3 | The clocks are durable timers of the workflow: no Quartz job, no job table, no Schedule, and a redeploy or Continue-As-New neither loses nor restarts a clock | DP-10 as a prohibition; ASM-4726 |

##### 9. State transitions

The case route state is rwb-case's: the step answers the move and the parent applies it (BR7). What this story owns is the clock and step state of the asset.

| From (`asset.holding_status`) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| HELD, no clock | The confirmation under R-DIS-06 | title_status in (clear, under_transfer) | HELD unchanged, both clocks armed, answer `ASSET_HELD` |
| HELD, clock armed | The clock fires under R-DIS-09 | holding_age reaches next_provision_step_date | HELD unchanged, step applied, record written, clock rearmed |
| HELD, clock armed | The case pauses on a deviation | R-DIS-66 | HELD unchanged, step holds, clock state kept (BR10) |
| HELD, step held | The deviation clears | R-DIS-68 | HELD unchanged, step resumes where it paused |
| HELD, clock armed | A second confirmation or the same threshold | X7 | Unchanged, the repeat is counted |
| LISTED, UNDER_OFFER, RENTED, SOLD, TRANSFERRED | The clock fires late | The asset has left the hold | No step applied; the firing is recorded and dropped |

| Step execution | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting | The confirmation arrives for a case in `ASSET_ON_BOOKS` | The package is loaded | Evaluating |
| Evaluating | R-DIS-06 fires | The record is written | Arming |
| Arming | The clocks are armed, the charge is answered and the asset is updated | The transaction commits | Waiting for the provision clock, answer sent |
| Waiting | The clock fires for a case in `ASSET_HELD` | R-DIS-09 fires and the input is accepted | Waiting, rearmed |
| Arming or Waiting | The record write, the transaction or the feed fails | X1, X6 | Waiting, nothing changed, retry scheduled |
| Waiting | The case is in `DISPOSAL_PAUSED_DEVIATION` | R-DIS-66 | Waiting, held |

No new holding-status value is introduced: the story writes no holding status of its own (GAP-2855).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-NPAMGR, NPA and asset manager | The primary role: reads the holding age, the cost to date and the provision step |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-FIELDCOL, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-LEGAL, RW-SALEOFF and the roles the access matrix adds | Asset and disposal R: read only, in scope |
| RW-PRODHEAD, RW-HEADNPA, RW-HEADASL | Asset and disposal R, and the approval path where a step needs it |
| PT-AUCTION, PT-RAMC, PT-VALUER | Asset and disposal R only, through the partner gateway; never the provision step |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-DATALOAD, SY-AGENT | Asset and disposal R, C or U as the matrix gives: the service identities run the step under the same checks |
| rwb-asset service identity | Runs the step, evaluates the rules, writes the record and the asset, requests the charge, sends the input and answers the move; no grant outside `rwb_asset` |

The legacy permission table gives the Asset and disposal area the right R and no C right, and that is the whole authority of the story: the feature runs unattended with the NPA and asset manager as the reader. DP-08 is not in this pattern set, so the check is stated here and not built here.
