The baseline declares no new table, no new column and no migration, and it enumerates no business value: every list, code and threshold is referenced with its identifier and its version. **No personal data** appears in any element, fake or example; the fixture identifiers are synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13). These are the reads that answer SCR-23 and SCR-21 and the write the ladder steps the price with.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated (API-S5-001) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out, with its title, its listing, the price of the round, the floor and the round number (API-S5-002) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetKey}` | Asset of status 200 out on the business key of the Ownership Map | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/assets/{assetId}/listings` | ListingRequest in, the listing and its round out, 409 when the listing is not in the state the write expects (API-S5-004) | Asset and disposal, right C, scope applied | Idempotency-Key header |
| POST | `/assets/{assetKey}/listings` | The same write on the business key of the Ownership Map | Asset and disposal, right C, scope applied | Idempotency-Key header |

The listings write is declared once for two stories: the pricing story of FEAT-AST-11 sets the start price and the floor and takes the approval, and the application story of this key steps the price at each round. No source splits the operation, and the split is recorded as GAP-2897 with ASM-4794. `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds` (API-S5-005) is the rounds story's and is not declared here; `POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations` (API-S5-003) is rwb-valuation's under ASM-0043.

The error envelope of the declared operations: 400 for a malformed request, 401 for an unauthenticated call, 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope asset, 409 for a listing that is not in the state the write expects, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for a missing field and with MSG-S5-001 for a floor under the approver's limit, and 503 when the decision library or a consumed contract does not answer, in one problem document with a code, a message ID and a correlation reference.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The appraisal and asset data product (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2895; ASM-4792)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The appraised value, the appraisal date, the outlier flag and the book value, with the freshness stamp; faked |
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family (read) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference and the case state the rules check before they fire; faked |
| The case-move answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2895; ASM-4792)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The answer that carries the stage outcome with its rule version; on the workflow boundary it is the outcome the parent applies; faked |

Each row is one hop, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). Where a name is not published the row carries the placeholder and no path, so the consumer adapts at the tag rather than inventing a surface (BR2).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The owned event row of this service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn`, published by the take-on story when the asset record opens, and the sale event is the sale story's. This baseline declares neither as its own, adds nothing to `rwb.asset.events.v1`, and the step writes no outbox row: its outward surface is the case-move answer and its own reads.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The round-close fact and the accepted appraisal arrive as signals of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`, so the baseline declares no topic subscription, no consumer group and no inbox row, and a build that subscribes to a topic not listed by Architecture v5 fails the naming check (BR5, DP-14).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, continues-as-new | `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the route, the asset reference, the listing reference and the rule package in force; signals: the round-close fact, the accepted re-appraisal and the rule package in force |
| `stepDownPrice` | Activity, the price-ladder step | `rwb-asset` | The case, the listing and the round-close or appraisal fact in; the rule IDs with their versions, the price before and after, the round number and the stage outcome out, in one transaction |

The workflow is the same execution the take-on, holding and sale stories of this service use; this baseline fixes its input and signal elements and the one activity it adds, and it declares no child workflow and no second queue. The activity name is a design choice of the application story, and the baseline carries it so that the workflow's history is stable.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. R-DIS-38 runs "per schedule" as a durable timer inside the workflow, so the baseline declares no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job for the ladder. The single Schedule of the service is JOB-19, which the re-appraisal story of this service owns and which is not declared here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| listing | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The listing record; the baseline declares the elements of its price and round, not its schema |
| asset | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | Read only; the baseline declares the elements the screens read |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The local decision record of DP-03, declared through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated signal or request and the answer it holds |

The baseline declares no column, no index and no migration, and it declares no table of another owner: `asset_sale` (S5, the sale story's), `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task` and `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` and `approval` (P7), `valuation` (S1), `document` (P5), `deviation` (S8) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) are named by their owner and never declared here. The per-round price column is Not specified in the source documents and is declared only once its owner names it (GAP-2896; ASM-4793).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-source-data appraisal and asset fake | The appraisal `AP-2026-000531` of asset `AST-2026-000531` with its value, its date and a clear outlier flag, and the NPA asset with its book value; an appraisal more than a year old; a stale product with its date; no answer beyond 2 s | C4, C6 |
| rwb-case case-state and case-move fake | The case states `ROUND_OPEN` and `REAPPRAISAL_RECEIVED` of the fixture cases; the moves accepted and a move refused for a state the rule does not expect | C4, C6 |
| rwb-decision rule-package fake | The DISPOSAL package at its version in force with R-DIS-38 and R-DIS-17 | C6 |
| Decision-record stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | C6 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-23 and SCR-21 answer for case `RC-2026-000531`, with the listing and price elements read once | C2, C6 |
| Floor and ladder data fake | A listing whose price of the round is above the floor, one at the floor and one below the approver's limit (MSG-S5-001) | C2, C5, C6 |

Each fake answers only what its owner documents, and a fake that answers more than the document fails the review. The operation names that are not published are stubbed from the documents and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-2895; ASM-4792).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 5 provided, 2 consumed | The asset reads and the listings write on `/api/recovery/asset/v1`; the rwb-source-data data-product row and the rwb-case state and case-move rows; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | The round-close fact is a workflow signal; nothing is published |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 1 activity | `AssetDisposalWorkflow` and `stepDownPrice` on `rwb-asset`; no Schedule |
| File | None | No file element is declared; the portal and HOME.SCB publication is FEAT-AST-12's |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Document.** `04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-S5 rwb-asset (Asset)/RWB S5 E4022 CON Run the descending price schedule - contract v1.md`, with the schema and the examples in the service contract folder of RWB-S5-E4022.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Sections and owners of the review.** The document is written in nine parts: the provided operations, the consumed rows, the published and consumed events, the workflow and its activity, the schedules, the tables, the fakes, the call-type summary and the lifecycle. Each part is reviewed by the owner of the rows it names, and the tag waits for every reviewer.

**Compatibility check.** The schema is published as JSON Schema with `additionalProperties: false` on the closed objects, and the check runs on three inputs: the previous tag, the new draft and a corpus of recorded answers from the fakes. A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element fails the check and forces a new major version (C1, BR3).

**Open shapes carried into the tag.** Three shapes are carried as placeholders and not invented: the operation names of the rwb-source-data product and of the case-move answer (GAP-2895; ASM-4792), the per-round price column (GAP-2896; ASM-4793) and the ownership of the listings write across the two stories (GAP-2897; ASM-4794). A placeholder is a declared forthcoming shape, not a permission to guess.

**Done when.** The seven criteria pass, the reviewers of the three consumed owners have closed their comments, the compatibility check passes on the tag, the fakes are published with their documented answers, and RWB-S5-E4022-APP can start against the tag with no open shape question.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Asset and disposal right calls one of the declared operations | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a declared request is absent or invalid | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-S5-001 | A declared write carries a floor under the approver's limit | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | A declared read carries an appraisal more than a year old | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written, as the decision-record element declares it | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| Document rule | A change fails the compatibility check | A breaking change needs a new major version. |
| Document rule | A consumed row has no published operation name | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2895; ASM-4792). |

The five message IDs are carried from the service and platform sets and are declared only as the envelope rows of the operations in this baseline; the two document rules are checks of this story and are not service messages.

##### 15. Screens and states

The baseline serves SCR-23 Listing and price and SCR-21 Asset list through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). What this story fixes is the element list of the declared responses and the empty, loading, refused, conflict, at-floor and stale states the route can show from this service's answers. The route itself, its merge order and its field list are RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the screens' transitions are the application and pricing stories'.

No screen is built here, no component is delivered and no state machine is declared: the screen section of a contract story lists the elements the screens read and the states their answers can carry.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the baseline: the ladder, the floor rule, the outlier test, the codes and every threshold are referenced with their identifier and version, never enumerated as a constant or a default.
- No personal data in any element, fake, example or log: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the baseline declares no `v_ace_*` element and no ACE table, and the appraisal and asset facts appear only as the rwb-source-data data product (DP-05).
- The case stays with rwb-case and the rules with rwb-decision: no `recovery_case` element and no rule row is declared as this service's own.
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; no document, module or test names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no monolith base `/api/recovery/v1`, no shared job table, no Schedule for the ladder, no event published or consumed by this step.
- Additive only: a breaking change needs a new major version and a re-tag, and the code never moves ahead of the document (BR3).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the application slice of RWB-E4-022 for rwb-asset. The four legacy criteria are kept word for word with their origin tag and the six legacy test cases keep their IDs. The step becomes the ladder branch of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` on queue `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery`: it evaluates R-DIS-38 and R-DIS-17 on the DISPOSAL package in force, writes the next price and the reset inputs on `listing` in `rwb_asset`, records each outcome before the row changes (DP-03), answers `ROUND_OPEN` and `ASSET_HELD` to rwb-case and publishes nothing. The `v_ace_*` reads arrive on the rwb-source-data contract (DP-05), the base becomes `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13), and the screens read through the gateway-bff route (DP-19). Gaps: consumed operation names (GAP-2895; ASM-4792); no round-price column (GAP-2896; ASM-4793); API-S5-004 shared by two stories (GAP-2897; ASM-4794); no requirement id (GAP-2898; ASM-4795); DP-04 outside the pattern set (GAP-2899; ASM-4796). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **sale officer**, I want **the Workbench to step the price down on the ladder at each round until a bid clears the floor**, so that **assets sell sooner at approved prices**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E4-022. It owns the four legacy criteria with their origin tag; the ladder branch of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` on `rwb-asset` as a child of the case workflow (Architecture v5 slide 13); R-DIS-38 on a round closed with no bid and R-DIS-17 on an accepted re-appraisal, on the package in force; the next price and round number and the reset list and floor inputs on `listing` in `rwb_asset`; the decision record before each change (DP-03) and the answers `ROUND_OPEN` and `ASSET_HELD`; and the reads of SCR-23 and SCR-21 on `/api/recovery/asset/v1` through the gateway-bff route (DP-13, DP-19).

It does not own: the shapes, the consumed rows and the fakes, which are RWB-S5-E4022-CON; the start price, the floor and its approval (FEAT-AST-11's story); the listing publication (FEAT-AST-12); the rounds and bids (the rounds story of RWB-E4-024); the appraisal order (rwb-valuation, S1); the case and its states (rwb-case, P3); the ACE facts (rwb-source-data, P1); the rule package (rwb-decision, P7); and the deployment (the operations story of this key).

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E4-022 kept a listing moving: on a round with no bid the price stepped down the approved ladder, the next round opened, and an accepted re-appraisal rewrote the list and floor inputs. The FSD keeps it as FEAT-AST-13 in module S5, running unattended with the sale officer as acting role, against an NPA sales cycle of 1,095 days (FSD S5 A2.13).

What D-RCV-60 changes:

- **the price is this service's.** `listing` is S5's in `rwb_asset` (Ownership Map; Architecture v5 slide 41); the ladder is reference data with a version, never a constant.
- **the value stays with rwb-source-data (P1).** Only that service reads the `recovery.v_ace_*` views (Architecture v5 slide 8), so DP-05 is a **prohibition** and the facts arrive on the owner's product with a freshness stamp.
- **the case stays with rwb-case (P3).** This story evaluates, writes, records and **answers** the move; it writes no case row.
- **the decision is recorded first**, one per outcome, in the row's transaction — what AC1 asked and AC4 tested.
- **nothing is published.** EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is the take-on story's (TSD S5 T5.3); §12.3 states the absence and a build that adds an event fails it.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S5-E4022-CON tagged: reads, listings write, consumed rows, record element, error set, fakes.
- `listing` and `asset` exist in `rwb_asset` with the TSD S5 T3.1 and T3.0 columns; no column is added for the round price (GAP-2896; ASM-4793).
- The DISPOSAL package is in force with the two rules from rwb-decision (P7), loaded through the service template; DP-04 is outside the pattern set (GAP-2899; ASM-4796).
- The ladder, its step and unit and the `LOV-*` lists are reference data with a version (TSD S5 T3.2).
- The rwb-case state read and the case-move answer sit behind fakes; the move's name is not published (GAP-2895; ASM-4792).
- The rwb-source-data product with the appraisal and asset facts is published with a fake and a freshness stamp; its name is not published (GAP-2895).
- The round-close fact arrives as a workflow signal from the rounds story; no subscription is added.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON writes in the caller's transaction (DP-03); RWB-PLT-N001-CON serves the screens, one hop each (DP-19).
- The service holds its own login on `rwb_asset`, no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-01, DP-05).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft baseline; the contract is tagged when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. A round of a live listing closes with no bid; the rounds story signals the workflow with case, asset, listing and round, and the step confirms the case state on the rwb-case contract.
2. The step reads the listing: start price, floor, round number, sale channel, status.
3. It reads the appraisal and asset facts on the rwb-source-data product, one hop, 2 s: appraised value, appraisal date, outlier flag, book value.
4. `LadderEvaluator` loads the package in force and evaluates R-DIS-38: from `ROUND_OPEN`, on `ROUND_CLOSED_NO_BID`, with `bid_count = 0` and the round price above the floor, the price steps down and the next round opens, the case staying in `ROUND_OPEN` (Business Rules and Routing Logic v4).
5. `AssetDecisionRecordWriter` writes one record **before any change**; a failed write stops the step (DP-03; AC1, AC4).
6. `ListingWriter` writes the next price and round number in one transaction with the record and the idempotency row; where no column holds the round price the value is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2896).
7. `CaseMoveAnswer` answers `ROUND_OPEN` with the round number, the new price, the rule and its version; rwb-case writes the case.
8. Where the round price is already at the floor, R-DIS-38 does not fire: nothing is written and the floor is reported to the parent (X4).
9. On an accepted re-appraisal R-DIS-17 applies: from `REAPPRAISAL_RECEIVED`, on `VALUE_ACCEPTED`, with the outlier flag clear or the value accepted by an officer, the appraised value is written, the list and floor inputs are reset, and the case moves to `ASSET_HELD`.
10. A second record is written before the reset commits; no event and no outbox row leaves the service (§12.3).
11. A repeated signal or `Idempotency-Key` writes once and is counted; the step returns to its durable timer and the workflow continues as new at each stage end and at least every 28 days.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The record cannot be written | Nothing written, no move answered | MSG-P7-003 | AC4, TC-E4-022-04, -06 |
| X2 | The role lacks the right | 403 before any read or write | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, TC-E4-022-05 |
| X3 | The case is in another state | The rule does not fire; nothing written, state reported | None | AC2, AC3 |
| X4 | The round price is at the floor | No step, no record, no move; floor reported | MSG-S5-001 where under the limit | AC2 |
| X5 | A contract misses 2 s or its breaker is open | Retry on the workflow schedule; 503 | None | AC1, AC3 |
| X6 | The ACE product is stale | Held, nothing written, the data date shown | MSG-P1-001 | AC3 |
| X7 | The appraisal is more than a year old | The reset is held and a new appraisal asked for | MSG-S5-002 | AC3 |
| X8 | The same signal arrives twice | One step, one answer, no second record | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X9 | A statement reaches a `v_ace_*` view, `recovery_case` or a foreign schema | The grant refuses it and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | §17, BR6 |

X1 to X3 are the legacy paths on the split, X4 to X8 what the ladder, the call types and the appraisal age add, and X9 the DP-01 and DP-05 boundary.

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Run the descending price schedule

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-000531" holds asset "AST-2026-000531" in listing "LS-2026-000531"
    Given the DISPOSAL rule package is in force at its version and carries R-DIS-38 and R-DIS-17
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 Run the descending price schedule (legacy RWB-E4-022 AC1)
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns the appraisal "AP-2026-000531" and the NPA asset "AST-2026-000531" of case "RC-2026-000531"
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case state ROUND_OPEN for "RC-2026-000531"
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When its trigger arrives
    Then steps the price down on the ladder at each round until a bid clears the floor
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Rule R-DIS-38 (legacy RWB-E4-022 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case state ROUND_OPEN for "RC-2026-000532"
    Given a case in state ROUND_OPEN
    When round closed no bid
    Then step the price down on the published schedule and open the next round
    Then the case moves to ROUND_OPEN

  Scenario: AC3 Rule R-DIS-17 (legacy RWB-E4-022 AC3)
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns the appraisal "AP-2026-000533" of asset "AST-2026-000533" with the outlier flag clear
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case state REAPPRAISAL_RECEIVED for "RC-2026-000533"
    Given a case in state REAPPRAISAL_RECEIVED
    When value accepted
    Then update the appraised value and reset the list and floor price inputs
    Then the case moves to ASSET_HELD

  Scenario: AC4 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E4-022 AC4)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The four criteria are the legacy criteria word for word with the origin tag added: the repeated `Then`, `the action is taken`, `its trigger arrives` and `the decision log cannot be written` stand, and the `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` lines are the only additions. The work happens in three places: rwb-source-data answers the facts, rwb-case writes the moves, and this story evaluates, writes, records and answers. AC3 resets the inputs; the floor itself is approved by the head of NPA in FEAT-AST-11's story (GAP-2897; ASM-4794).

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-DIS-38 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | ROUND_OPEN | ROUND_CLOSED_NO_BID | bid_count = 0 and price_at_round above floor_price | Step the price down on the published schedule and open the next round | ROUND_OPEN | Workbench | Rules component, Workbench scheduler | per schedule |
| R-DIS-17 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | REAPPRAISAL_RECEIVED | VALUE_ACCEPTED | outlier_flag = N or officer_accepted = Y | Update the appraised value and reset the list and floor price inputs | ASSET_HELD | Workbench | SVAF, Workbench | None |

Both rows are copied character for character from the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; their owner column is a business role, so rwb-case holds the states on this story's answer while the `listing` row is written here. FSD S5 A2.13 also lists R-DIS-28 (the pricing agent's proposal, moving to `PRICE_PROPOSED`); it is FEAT-AST-11's and is not evaluated here.

##### 9. State transitions

The case route state is rwb-case's and is applied by the parent `CaseWorkflow` on this story's answer (BR4).

| From (`listing` status) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live, round closed with no bid | `ROUND_CLOSED_NO_BID` under R-DIS-38 | Bid count 0 and round price above the floor | Live at the stepped price; answer `ROUND_OPEN` |
| Live, round closed with no bid | `ROUND_CLOSED_NO_BID` under R-DIS-38 | Round price at the floor | Unchanged (X4) |
| Live, re-appraisal accepted | `VALUE_ACCEPTED` under R-DIS-17 | Outlier flag clear or officer accepted | Live, inputs reset; answer `ASSET_HELD` |
| Live, re-appraisal accepted | `VALUE_ACCEPTED` under R-DIS-17 | Appraisal more than a year old | Unchanged, reset held (X7) |
| Any | The same signal again, or an unexpected state | X8, X3 | Unchanged |

| Step execution | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting on the timer | A round-close signal for a live listing | The package in force is loaded | Evaluating |
| Evaluating | A rule fires | The record is written | Applying |
| Applying | The row is written and the answer sent | The transaction commits | Waiting |
| Applying | The record or the transaction fails | X1 | Waiting, nothing changed |
| Waiting | The product is stale | X6 | Held |

The statuses are the `LOV-LISTING` rows of TSD S5 T3.2; the route states are the DISPOSAL machine's (TSD S5 T4).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the behaviour behind the shapes of RWB-S5-E4022-CON.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated (API-S5-001) | Asset and disposal, R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out with title, listing, round price, floor and round number (API-S5-002) | Asset and disposal, R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetKey}` | The same answer on the business key of the Ownership Map | Asset and disposal, R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/assets/{assetId}/listings` | Price of the round and floor in, listing and round out (API-S5-004) | Asset and disposal, C, scope applied | Idempotency-Key |
| POST | `/assets/{assetKey}/listings` | The same write on the business key | Asset and disposal, C, scope applied | Idempotency-Key |

The listings write is shared with FEAT-AST-11's pricing story and no source splits it (GAP-2897; ASM-4794). `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds` (API-S5-005) is the rounds story's. Errors: 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409 for a listing in the wrong state, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 or MSG-S5-001, 503.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Appraisal and asset product (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2895; ASM-4792)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | Appraised value, date, outlier flag, book value with the freshness stamp; faked |
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case state the rules check; faked |
| Case-move answer (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2895; ASM-4792)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | `ROUND_OPEN` and `ASSET_HELD` with the rule and its version; faked |

One hop, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). They are class C rows the plan does not carry, the C row of this slice being None (GAP-2895).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is the take-on story's and the sale event the sale story's; a stepped price writes no outbox row and adds nothing to `rwb.asset.events.v1`. A build that publishes here fails the absence test.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The round-close fact is a signal of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` from the rounds story: no subscription, no consumer group, no inbox row.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one per case per stage, continues-as-new | `rwb-asset` in `rwb-recovery` | Input: case, route, asset, listing, package in force; signals: round-close fact, accepted appraisal |
| `stepDownPrice` | Activity, the ladder step | `rwb-asset` | Case, listing and fact in; rule IDs with versions, price before and after, round number and case move out, one transaction |

No child workflow and no second queue. The activity name is a design choice of this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. R-DIS-38 runs "per schedule" as a durable timer inside the workflow; the step owns no Temporal Schedule and no Quartz job. The service's single Schedule is JOB-19, the re-appraisal story's.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| asset | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | Read only here |
| decision_record | PLT library in `rwb_asset` | One record per outcome (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated signal or request |

Not owned and never read as a table: `asset_sale` (the sale story's), `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task`, `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row`, `approval` (P7), `valuation` (S1), `document` (P5), `deviation` (S8), every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

The fakes are test-only; the placeholder rows carry their gap until their owners confirm the names (GAP-2895).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset.pricing`; front end `src/modules/recovery/asset/AssetPriceLadder.tsx`, read only.

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is a prohibition (no `v_ace_*` grant, no ACE read); DP-03 is the transaction rule of the step; DP-13 moves the base; DP-19 is how the screens reach the service. The three consumed rows are class C and the plan's C row is None, so they are built on documents and fakes on Day 1 (GAP-2895). The package in force is loaded through the service template without the DP-04 platform row (GAP-2899).

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Ladder branch of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow | Waits on the timer and signals, loads the package in force, reports to the parent |
| `stepDownPrice` | Activity | Read, evaluate, write, answer |
| `LadderEvaluator` / `ReappraisalEvaluator` | Services | R-DIS-38 on bid count, round price and floor; R-DIS-17 on the value, outlier flag and age |
| `AssetDecisionRecordWriter` | Library adapter | One hash-linked record per outcome before any change (DP-03) |
| `ListingWriter` | Repository | `listing` in one transaction with the idempotency row and the lock |
| `CaseMoveAnswer`, `CaseStateClient`, `SourceDataProductClient` | Clients | The two moves and the two reads, one hop, 2 s |
| `AssetController` | Controller | The reads and the write, rights, key and the 400/401/403/404/409/422/503 map |
| `AssetPriceLadder` | React component | The ladder, round prices, floor and reset value on SCR-23 |

**Database.** No Flyway file: tables from the DB story, library objects from the library's migration, no column for the round price (GAP-2896).

**Configuration.** The ladder, step and unit and the `LOV-*` lists at their version; the DISPOSAL package from rwb-decision; the capability rows from rwb-access; the flag and the 2 s budget as platform configuration (ADR-020).

**Build steps.** (1) the ladder branch and its input record; (2) `LadderEvaluator` with the floor and no-fire paths (AC2, X3, X4); (3) `ReappraisalEvaluator` with the outlier and age paths (AC3, X7); (4) the clients against their fakes (AC1, AC3, X5, X6); (5) the record writer against the stub (AC4, X1); (6) `ListingWriter` (AC2, X8); (7) `CaseMoveAnswer` (AC2, AC3); (8) `AssetController` (AC1); (9) the screen fragment (AC1); (10) the boundary test (X9, BR6, BR7).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.asset.price-ladder-v1`; off means the signal is held, nothing is written and no move is answered.

**Done when.** §16 passes, a closed round steps the price and answers `ROUND_OPEN` in SIT, an accepted appraisal answers `ASSET_HELD`, a price at the floor steps nothing, a repeat writes once, a forced record failure changes nothing, no case row and no `v_ace_*` read exists, and the screens answer through the composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S5-001 | A floor under the approver's limit on the price write (X4) | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | An appraisal more than a year old at the reset (X7) | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request or signal is absent or invalid (X3) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right reads or writes (X2) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record cannot be written before the listing changes (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE product is stale after a late or failed batch (X6) | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The six IDs are the legacy and platform sets, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and none is added.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-23 Listing and price (draft, below limit, approved, published) and SCR-21 Asset list (loading, list) are served through the gateway-bff route (DP-19), which calls rwb-asset for the asset, listing, round prices and floor, rwb-case for the state and rwb-source-data for the appraisal. This story fixes the rwb-asset answers only; the route and field list are RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

The states it produces are the published ladder state of SCR-23 — round number, round price, floor, reset value — and the refusal, not-recorded, at-floor, old-appraisal and stale states with MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003, MSG-S5-001, MSG-S5-002 and MSG-P1-001. Draft, below-limit and approved are the pricing story's.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the ladder, floor rule, outlier test and statuses stay reference data or rule rows with a version.
- No personal data in the schema, a workflow input or a log; every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: no `v_ace_*` grant, no ACE read (DP-05).
- The case stays with rwb-case: no `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task` or `timer` row here (BR4).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element returns: no shared job table, no Quartz row, no monolith base.
- The record precedes the change and the repeated signal is deduped (DP-03, BR8).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract slice of RWB-E4-023, the baseline the vendor-allocation step of rwb-asset builds against on Day 1. The baseline declares the two asset reads that answer SCR-21 and SCR-23 on `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13), the three consumed REST rows of rwb-case and rwb-source-data (DP-05), the vendor-panel activity element of rwb-partner on the call type the connection matrix gives S5→S9, the workflow signal elements `VENDOR_REQUIRED` and `VENDOR_UNAVAILABLE`, the decision-record element of DP-03, the rights and the error envelope, and the fakes. No event is published or consumed, and no Schedule is declared. No source names a published operation for the allocation step itself, and the panel element of the partner activity, the four-vendor list and the allocation reference have no published field (GAP-2905; ASM-4803); the split plan carries no requirement id for this slice (GAP-2903; ASM-4801). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the vendor-allocation step of rwb-asset — its two asset reads, its consumed rows, its two workflow signals, its panel element, its rights, its error envelope and its fakes — baselined and tagged before the build starts**, so that **the application story, the pricing and auction stories and every consumer can build and test on Day 1 against one fixed, versioned surface instead of guessing the shape of a neighbour's answer**.

This is the contract slice of legacy RWB-E4-023. It owns:

- the document that fixes the two reads of the asset and its allocation on base `/api/recovery/asset/v1`, with their parameters, their documented answer, their rights and their idempotency (DP-13);
- the three consumed REST rows: the rwb-case case state read, the rwb-case case-move answer and the rwb-source-data asset and scorecard data product, each with its owner, its use and its placeholder where the operation name is not published (DP-05);
- the vendor-panel element of the rwb-partner activity on queue `rwb-partner`, the call type the connection matrix gives S5→S9, with its request, its documented answer and its timeout;
- the two workflow signal elements, `VENDOR_REQUIRED` at `FLOOR_APPROVED` and `VENDOR_UNAVAILABLE` at `VENDOR_ALLOCATED`, with the fields the rules R-DIS-30 and R-DIS-31 test;
- the decision-record element and the local library dependency that carries it (DP-03);
- the capability area, the rights and the error envelope of the operations it declares;
- the fakes and their documented answers, so that every downstream answer has a stub on Day 1;
- the naming and boundary rules of the baseline: one base, one topic, one queue, no foreign schema, no monolith base, no consumed event, no Schedule.

It does not own: the allocation behaviour, the rule evaluation, the decision records and the case moves, which are RWB-S5-E4023-APP; the panel, its capacity, its panel status and the partner instruction, which are rwb-partner's (S9); the case of record and its route states, which are rwb-case's (P3); the ACE asset and scorecard facts, which are rwb-source-data's (P1); the rule package, which is rwb-decision's (P7); the listing, the floor price and the auction rounds, which are the pricing and auction stories of this service; the screen field list and the composite route, which are RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19).

##### 2. Business rationale

A contract baseline is what lets ten teams build at once. Without it the allocation step would be written against whatever shape the partner panel or the data product happened to expose that week, and the first integration would find the mismatches instead of the review. With it, the application story builds on Day 1 against a tagged document and its fakes, the listing stories know what the asset answer must carry for the allocation to be shown, and rwb-partner and rwb-source-data see exactly which facts of theirs this service consumes.

The three rules the baseline applies:

- **the owner publishes, the consumer adapts.** Every consumed row names its owner and its use, and where the source documents do not publish an operation name, a field or a list value, the row carries the placeholder rather than an invented surface (GAP-2905; ASM-4803).
- **the call type is the matrix's.** The panel is reached by a Temporal activity on the owner's queue and not by REST, because the connection matrix gives S5→S9 a Temporal call only and the architecture notes say route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal, never REST (Architecture v5 slide 13).
- **additive only.** The baseline moves forward without breaking: a new optional element is a minor version, and a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version and a new document (s9).

The business outcome the baseline protects is the one FEAT-AST-14 of the FSD names: one of the four vendors is chosen by the rule so that the NPA sales cycle shortens. The baseline does not state that outcome, and no criterion here asserts a business value or a chosen vendor.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The ownership rows are in force: S5 owns the six operations of the Ownership Map, of which `GET /assets` and `GET /assets/{assetId}` are declared here; `POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations` is rwb-valuation's under ASM-0043; `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings` and `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds` are the listing and auction stories' (API-S5-004, API-S5-005); `asset_sale` and `listing` are S5's tables (GAP-2905; ASM-4803).
- The service naming is fixed: schema `rwb_asset`, login `rwb_asset`, base `/api/recovery/asset/v1`, topic `rwb.asset.events.v1` with `.retry` and `.dlt`, task queue `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset`.
- Architecture v5 slides 13 and 19 are in force: S5→S9 is a Temporal call and an event subscription, and rwb-asset publishes `AssetTakenOn` and `AssetSold` only; this baseline touches neither event.
- The platform CON stories are published: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for the decision record (DP-03) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the composite route (DP-19).
- The rwb-partner (S9) vendor-panel activity is declared by its owner as reachable on that owner's queue; where the owner has not published it, the fake carries its documented answer and the row keeps its placeholder (GAP-2901; ASM-4799).
- No approval is needed to publish a Draft baseline, and the missing approval of the realigned stories is recorded rather than waited for (GAP-2904; ASM-4802); the document is baselined by this story's own review, and the build waits only for its tag.

##### 4. Flow

1. The author drafts the baseline from the ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 13 and 19, the TSD S5 T-A.1 operations and the TSD S5 T3.1 tables.
2. Every operation is declared with its method, path, request, documented answer, rights, idempotency and error set.
3. Every consumed REST row is declared with its owner, its use, its budget and a placeholder where the operation name is not published.
4. The panel element is declared with the call type of the matrix, the request fields, the documented answer fields and the timeout.
5. The two workflow signals are declared with the fields the rules test: the case reference, the asset reference and, on the re-allocation, the allocated vendor with its capacity flag and its panel status.
6. The decision-record element is declared with the library dependency that carries it.
7. The fakes are declared with their documented answers, one per consumed row and one for the composite route.
8. The schema, the open lists and the closed lists are published, and the compatibility check runs: a breaking change fails the check.
9. The document goes to review as Draft; the reviewers are the owners of the consumed rows and the tech lead of the service.
10. On the review's close the document is tagged and baselined; the application story starts against the tag and the fakes.
11. A defect found in the build that needs a shape change is raised against this document, and the document moves to a new minor or major version; the code never moves ahead of the document.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A consumer asks for a shape the sources do not publish | The row carries the placeholder and the gap; no path, field or list value is invented | C4, C5 |
| X2 | A change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element | The compatibility check fails, the version becomes a new major and the document is re-reviewed | C1 |
| X3 | A declared operation or activity reaches another service's data, base or queue as its own | The review refuses the baseline and the boundary test fails the build | C2, C7 |
| X4 | A consumed row or the panel activity has no fake, or its fake has no documented answer | The baseline is not tagged; the application story cannot start | C6 |
| X5 | The rights of an operation are not one of the rows of the access matrix, or a right is widened | The operation is not declared and the error set of the operation is incomplete | C3 |
| X6 | An owner changes its documented answer after the tag | The owner publishes a new version, this document follows with a minor or major version, and the application story re-tests against the new fake | X2, s9 |
| X7 | Two documents claim the same path, queue, table or event | The naming and boundary rule resolves it: the owner named in the ownership rows keeps it, and the other document changes | C7 |

X1 to X3 are the paths of an incomplete or a leaking source, X4 to X6 are the paths of a baseline moving under a build, and X7 is the naming boundary.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs no build, no live service and no approval; starts on Day 1 and is finished before the application story's first line |
| Negotiable | The wording, the order of the sections and the fake data are this story's choice; the paths, the owners, the queue, the signals and the error set are fixed by their sources |
| Valuable | Ten teams build at once against one tagged surface, and the first integration finds behaviour, not shape |
| Estimable | One document, two provided operations, three consumed rows, one panel element, two signals, one library element, seven fakes and one compatibility check |
| Small | Finished inside a week; the review is the only gate |
| Testable | Every criterion is a document check that runs in the contract test suite, plus the compatibility check on the published schema |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the vendor-allocation step

  Scenario: C1 The baseline validates and only additive changes pass (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published schema and the open and closed lists of the baseline
    When a change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element
    Then the compatibility check fails and the change needs a new major version
    And a change that adds an optional element passes as a minor version

  Scenario: C2 The two declared reads carry their elements, their rights and their error envelope (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operations the baseline provides on base /api/recovery/asset/v1
    When the element list, the rights and the error set of each operation are read
    Then each element carries its type, its nullability and its source
    And each operation names the capability area and the right of the access matrix, and the error set names 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503 in one problem envelope

  Scenario: C3 The three consumed REST rows name their owners, their use and their budget (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed operation table of the baseline
    When the rows of rwb-case and rwb-source-data are read
    Then each row names its owner, its use and its 2 s budget
    And where the operation name is not published the row carries the placeholder and the gap identifier and no path

  Scenario: C4 The vendor-panel element is declared on the call type of the matrix (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed activity table of the baseline
    When the vendor-panel row is read
    Then it names queue rwb-partner, the request fields of the asset and the documented answer fields of the four vendors with their capacity, their panel status and their distance
    And it declares no REST path of rwb-partner and no table of another service
    And where a field is not published the row carries the placeholder and the gap identifier

  Scenario: C5 The two workflow signals carry the fields the rules test (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the workflow element table of the baseline
    When the signals VENDOR_REQUIRED and VENDOR_UNAVAILABLE are read
    Then VENDOR_REQUIRED carries the case and asset references and the rule package in force at FLOOR_APPROVED
    And VENDOR_UNAVAILABLE carries the case reference and the allocated vendor with its capacity flag and its panel status at VENDOR_ALLOCATED
    And the closed lists of the capacity flag and the panel status are referenced with their identifier and version and are not enumerated in code

  Scenario: C6 The decision-record element and the fakes are declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the baseline document
    When the decision-record element and the fake table are read
    Then the element names RWB-PLT-E1027-CON as its library and the transaction it joins
    And every consumed row and the panel activity have a fake with a documented answer, including the stopped decision-record stub

  Scenario: C7 The naming and the boundary of the baseline hold (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the base, the topic, the queues and the schema of the baseline
    When the document is checked against the naming rule and the ownership rows
    Then no foreign schema, no foreign topic and no monolith base /api/recovery/v1 is declared
    And no Schedule is declared, no event is published and none is consumed by this step
```

The seven criteria are new to this run and are tagged as such: they test the contract deliverable only — the schema, the elements, the consumed rows, the panel element, the two signals, the rights, the envelope, the decision-record element, the fakes and the boundary. No criterion states a business outcome or a business value of the application story, and none asserts that a rule fires, that a vendor is chosen or that a case moves.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One owner per operation, activity, event and table: the baseline declares only the rows the ownership rows and Architecture v5 give to S5, and names every other row with its owner | Ownership rows of S5; Architecture v5 slide 13 |
| BR2 | A consumed row, a field or a list value with no published name carries the placeholder and its gap, and never an invented surface | Template and Rules v1 §R9; GAP-2905 |
| BR3 | The baseline is additive: a new optional element is a minor version, and a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version | ADR-020; s9 |
| BR4 | The panel is reached by a Temporal activity on queue `rwb-partner` and never by REST or a table, because the connection matrix gives S5→S9 a Temporal call only | Architecture v5 slide 13 and its notes |
| BR5 | Every consumed REST row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and no chain, and the panel activity carries the workflow kit's timeout | ADR-020 |
| BR6 | The step publishes no event and consumes none: the topic `rwb.asset.events.v1` carries `AssetTakenOn` (EV-22) and `AssetSold`, and the two triggers are workflow signals | Architecture v5 slide 19; TSD S5 T5.3 |
| BR7 | The decision record is written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the caller's transaction before the case-move answer, and its element is declared once for the service | DP-03 |
| BR8 | No business value is declared in the baseline: the panel size, the capacity codes, the panel statuses and every threshold are referenced with their identifier and version | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s16); legacy Guardrails |
| BR9 | No personal data in any element, fake or example of the baseline | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR10 | The baseline never declares another service's table, operation, queue or topic as its own, and a check fails the build where one names it | DP-01, DP-13, DP-14 |

##### 9. State transitions

The document itself is the object of this section: the lifecycle of the contract baseline.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | The draft is complete | Every operation, row, element, signal, fake and error is declared | Draft |
| Draft | The review is opened | The owners of the consumed rows are named as reviewers | In review |
| In review | The review closes with no open comment | The compatibility check passes | Baselined, tagged for the application story |
| In review | A comment needs a shape change | The change is applied to the draft | Draft |
| Baselined | An additive change is approved | New optional element only, compatibility check passes | Baselined, new minor version |
| Baselined | A breaking change is approved | A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element | Draft of a new major version, and the consumers are notified |
| Baselined | An owner changes its answer | X6 | Draft of a new minor or major version, and the fake is updated |

| Step | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Being authored | A consumed row or a panel field has no published name | X1 | The row carries the placeholder and the gap and the draft continues |
| In review | A row reaches a foreign schema, base or queue | X3, X7 | The baseline is refused |
| Ready to tag | A consumed row or the panel activity has no fake | X4 | Not tagged, the review reopens |

The route states `FLOOR_APPROVED` and `VENDOR_ALLOCATED` of the rules appear in this document only as the from-state and to-state of the two declared signals; their transitions belong to rwb-case and to RWB-S5-E4023-APP.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13). These are the reads that answer SCR-21 and SCR-23 for this step; the step's own surface is the two workflow signals and the case-move answer.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated (API-S5-001) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out, with its type, its book value, its allocation, the chosen vendor and the basis (API-S5-002) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| None | The step's own operation | No source names a published operation for the allocation step; it is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2905; ASM-4803) and is not declared as a path here | Not applicable | Not applicable |

The legacy endpoint row `POST assets/{assetId}/listings` of this key (written in the monolith on base `/api/recovery/v1`) becomes `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings` (API-S5-004) in the target and is declared by the listing and pricing baseline of this service, not by this one, because the allocation step creates no listing; `POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations` (API-S5-003) is rwb-valuation's under ASM-0043.

The error envelope of the two reads: 400 for a malformed request, 401 for an unauthenticated call, 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope asset, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for an invalid filter, and 503 when the decision library or a consumed contract does not answer, in one problem document with a code, a message ID and a correlation reference.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family (read) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference and the case state the rule checks before it fires; faked |
| The case-move answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2905; ASM-4803)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The answer that carries `VENDOR_ALLOCATED` with the rule, the vendor reference and its version; on the workflow boundary it is the stage outcome the parent applies; faked |
| The asset and scorecard data product (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2905; ASM-4803)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The asset fact and the predicted price of each vendor with its model version, and the freshness stamp; faked |

Each row is one hop, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). Where a name is not published the row carries the placeholder and no path, so the consumer adapts at the tag rather than inventing a surface (BR2).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT gives rwb-asset exactly two events, `AssetTakenOn` (EV-22) and `AssetSold`; the take-on is the take-on story's and the sale the sale story's, and this baseline declares neither as its own and adds nothing to `rwb.asset.events.v1`. The step's outward surface is the case-move answer and its own two reads, and no outbox row is declared here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. No source gives the allocation step a Kafka event: the four events Architecture v5 slide 19 IN gives rwb-asset (`JudgmentRecorded`, `AuctionResult`, `ProceedsMatched`, `PartnerResultSubmitted`) serve the litigation, auction, proceeds and partner-result steps, and the two triggers of this step are signals of the DISPOSAL machine forwarded by the parent `CaseWorkflow`. The baseline therefore declares no consumer group, no inbox row and no dedupe key for this step, and DP-09 is held as a prohibition (GAP-2901; ASM-4798).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, continues-as-new | `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the route, the asset reference and the rule package in force; signals: `VENDOR_REQUIRED`, `VENDOR_UNAVAILABLE` and the rule package in force |
| `allocateVendor` | Activity, the vendor-allocation step | `rwb-asset` | The case and the asset reference in; the chosen vendor, the basis, the score, the rule IDs with their versions and the stage outcome out, in one transaction |
| The rwb-partner vendor-panel activity (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2901; ASM-4799)) | Activity on the owner's queue, called by this step | `rwb-partner` | The asset reference, its region and its type in; the four vendors with their capacity flag, their panel status and their distance out; one call per evaluation, no child workflow and no Nexus |

The workflow is the same execution the take-on and holding stories use; this baseline fixes its input, its two signals and the two activities it adds, and it declares no child workflow and no second queue of this service. The activity names are design choices of the application story and of rwb-partner, and the baseline carries them so that the workflow's history is stable.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step runs from the signals the parent forwards, and this baseline declares no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job. The single Schedule of the service, JOB-19 Re-appraisal monthly, belongs to the re-appraisal story of this service and is not declared here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The local decision record of DP-03, declared through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and holding the chosen vendor, the basis and the score |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated signal and the answer it holds |

The baseline declares no column, no index and no migration, and it declares no table of another owner: `recovery_case` and `assignment` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `proceeds` (P8), the vendor panel (S9), every `v_ace_*` view (P1) and `asset_sale` and `listing` — which are this service's but not this step's — are named by their owner and never declared here. The allocation's column is Not specified in the source documents and is declared only once its owner names it (GAP-2902; ASM-4800).

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-source-data asset and score data-product fake | The asset `AST-2026-000623` with its type and book value and the predicted price of each vendor with its model version; a stale product with its date; no answer beyond 2 s | C3, C4, C6 |
| rwb-case case-state and case-move fake | The case state of `RC-2026-000623`; the move accepted and the move refused for a state the rule does not expect | C2, C3, C6 |

Each fake answers only what its owner documents, and a fake that answers more than the document fails the review. The operation names and the panel field names that are not published are stubbed from the documents and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-2901, GAP-2905; ASM-4799, ASM-4803).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Document.** `04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-S5 rwb-asset (Asset)/RWB S5 E4023 CON Allocate the asset to an auction vendor by distance - contract v1.md`, with the schema and the examples in the service contract folder of RWB-S5-E4023.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Sections and owners of the review.** The document is written in nine parts: the two provided operations, the three consumed rows, the panel element, the two signals, the published and consumed events, the tables, the fakes, the call-type summary and the lifecycle. Each part is reviewed by the owner of the rows it names, and the tag waits for every reviewer.

**Compatibility check.** The schema is published as JSON Schema with `additionalProperties: false` on the closed objects, and the check runs on three inputs: the previous tag, the new draft and a corpus of recorded answers from the fakes. A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element fails the check and forces a new major version (C1, BR3).

**Fakes.** One fake per consumed row plus the panel activity and the composite route, each built from the document and not from the real service, so that the fake can be published before the owner's build finishes (C6).

**Done when.** The seven criteria pass, the reviewers of the three consumed owners and of the panel have closed their comments, the compatibility check passes on the tag, the fakes are published with their documented answers, and RWB-S5-E4023-APP can start against the tag with no open shape question.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Asset and disposal right calls one of the declared reads | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a declared request or of a signal is absent or invalid | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written, as the decision-record element declares it | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The declared data product is stale and the step declares that it holds | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| Document rule | A change fails the compatibility check | A breaking change needs a new major version. |
| Document rule | A consumed row or a panel field has no published name | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2905; ASM-4803). |

The four message IDs are carried from the service and platform sets and are declared only as the envelope and element rows of the operations in this baseline; the two document rules are checks of this story and are not service messages.

##### 15. Screens and states

The baseline serves SCR-21 Asset list and SCR-23 Listing and price through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). What this story fixes is the element list of the two asset reads, including the allocation element, and the empty, loading, refused, stale and held states the route can show from this service's answers.

No screen is built here, no component is delivered and no state machine is declared: the screen section of a contract story lists the elements the screens read and the states their answers can carry. The draft, below-limit, approved and published states of SCR-23 belong to the pricing and listing story, and the route itself, its merge order and its field list are RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the baseline: the panel size, the capacity codes, the panel statuses, the score rules and every threshold are referenced with their identifier and version, never enumerated as a constant or a default.
- No personal data in any element, fake, example or log: identifiers, codes, a score, a basis, dates and a rule version only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the baseline declares no `v_ace_*` element and no ACE table, and the asset and scorecard facts appear only as the rwb-source-data data product (DP-05).
- The panel stays with rwb-partner and the case with rwb-case: no panel element, no case row and no assignment row is declared as this service's own, and the panel is a Temporal activity and never a REST path or a table (BR4).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; no document, module or test names another service's base, topic or queue as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no monolith base `/api/recovery/v1`, no shared job table, no Schedule, no consumed event and no outbox row.
- Additive only: a breaking change needs a new major version and a re-tag, and the code never moves ahead of the document (BR3).
