The baseline declares no new table, no new column and no migration, and it enumerates no business value: every list, code and threshold is referenced with its identifier and its version. **No personal data** appears in any element, fake or example; the fixture identifiers are synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13). These are the reads that answer SCR-24 and SCR-21 and the write the vendor reports a round with.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated, with the round of each listing (API-S5-001) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out, with its title, its listing, the round number and the round price (API-S5-002) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/listings/{listingId}/rounds` | AuctionRoundRequest in — roundNo, heldOn, result, price — and `AssetSale` out at 200, the sale record the round opens; 409 when the listing is not live or the round is out of order (API-S5-005) | Asset and disposal, right U, scope applied | Idempotency-Key header |

The listings write `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings` (API-S5-004) belongs to the pricing story of FEAT-AST-11 and is not declared here; `POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations` (API-S5-003) is rwb-valuation's and is not declared here. The round write's answer is the published `AssetSale` schema, so the sale record it opens carries the mandatory contract, sale and price elements: where a reported round has no contract or sale date yet, the value is Not specified in the source documents and the accept and award stories complete it (GAP-2911; ASM-4809).

The error envelope of the declared operations: 400 for a malformed request, 401 for an unauthenticated call, 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope asset or listing, 409 for a listing that is not live or a round that is out of order, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for a missing field and with MSG-S5-001 for a bid or a floor under the approver's limit, and 503 when the decision library or a consumed boundary does not answer, in one problem document with a code, a message ID and a correlation reference.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family (read) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference and the case state the rules check before they fire; faked |
| The case-move answer (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2907; ASM-4805)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The answer that carries the stage outcome with its rule version; on the workflow boundary it is the outcome the parent applies; faked |
| The payment-fact activity (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2907; ASM-4805)) | queue `rwb-payment` | P8 rwb-payment | The payment due date and whether the payment arrived, in place of the legacy `v_ace_payment` read (DP-05); faked |
| The vendor-score activity (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2907; ASM-4805)) | queue `rwb-partner` | S9 rwb-partner | The score of the vendor whose award was cancelled, in place of the legacy `v_ace_score` read (DP-05); faked |

Each row is one hop or one activity, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). Where a name is not published the row carries the placeholder and no path, so the consumer adapts at the tag rather than inventing a surface (BR2).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The owned event row of this service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn`, published by the take-on story when the asset record opens, and the sale event is the sale stories'. This baseline declares neither as its own, adds nothing to `rwb.asset.events.v1`, and the round branch writes no outbox row: its outward surface is the case-move answer and its own reads.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The round due fact, the payment-term expiry and the vendor score arrive as signals and activities of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`, so the baseline declares no topic subscription, no consumer group and no inbox row; the rwb-payment subscription of the connection matrix belongs to FEAT-AST-18's story, and a build that subscribes to a topic not listed by Architecture v5 fails the naming check (BR5, DP-14).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, continues-as-new | `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the route, the asset reference, the listing reference and the rule package in force; signals: the round due fact, the reported round, the payment-term expiry and the rule package in force |
| `reportAuctionRound` | Activity, the round write | `rwb-asset` | The listing, the round and the report in; the rule IDs with their versions, the round number, the status, the sale record reference and the stage outcome out, in one transaction |

The workflow is the same execution the take-on, holding and sale stories of this service use; this baseline fixes its input and signal elements and the one activity it adds, and it declares no child workflow and no second queue. The activity name is a design choice of the application story, and the baseline carries it so that the workflow's history is stable.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. R-DIS-36 runs "per schedule" as a durable timer inside the workflow, so the baseline declares no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job for the round. The single Schedule of the service is JOB-19, which the re-appraisal story of this service owns and which is not declared here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| listing | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The listing record; the baseline declares the elements of its round and status, not its schema |
| asset_sale | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The sale a round opens; the baseline declares the `AssetSale` answer, not its schema |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The local decision record of DP-03, declared through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated report and the answer it holds |

The baseline declares no column, no index and no migration, and it declares no table of another owner: `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task` and `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` and `approval` (P7), `valuation` (S1), `document` (P5), `deviation` (S8), the payment tables (P8), the partner tables (S9) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) are named by their owner and never declared here. No bids table exists and none is declared (GAP-2906; ASM-4804).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case case-state and case-move fake | The case states `ROUND_OPEN`, `BID_RECEIVED`, `SALE_AGREED` and `AWAITING_PAYMENT` of the fixture cases; the moves accepted and a move refused for an unexpected state | C3, C4, C6 |
| rwb-payment payment-fact fake | No payment by the due date; a payment received before it; a stale fact with its date; no answer inside 2 s | C4, C6 |
| rwb-partner vendor-score fake | The score of vendor `VN-2026-0012`; no answer inside 2 s | C4, C6 |
| rwb-decision rule-package fake | The DISPOSAL package at its version in force with the five rules | C6 |
| Decision-record stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | C6 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-24 and SCR-21 answer for case `RC-2026-000541`, with the round and its price read once | C2, C6 |
| Round report fake | A report at or above the floor, one below it, one out of order and one repeated on the same key | C2, C3, C5 |
| Sale answer fake | The `AssetSale` answer with its mandatory dates and price, and one with those values absent | C2, C3 |

Each fake answers only what its owner documents, and a fake that answers more than the document fails the review. The names that are not published are stubbed from the documents and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-2907; ASM-4805).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 3 provided, 2 consumed | The two asset reads and the round write on `/api/recovery/asset/v1`; the rwb-case state read and the case-move answer; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | The round and payment facts are workflow signals; nothing is published |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 1 activity | `AssetDisposalWorkflow` and `reportAuctionRound` on `rwb-asset`; the consumed payment and vendor-score activities on their owners' queues; no Schedule |
| File | None | No file element is declared; the publication of the listing is FEAT-AST-12's |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Document.** `04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-S5 rwb-asset (Asset)/RWB S5 E4024 CON Run auction rounds and report bids - contract v1.md`, with the schema and the examples in the service contract folder of RWB-S5-E4024.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Sections and owners of the review.** The document is written in nine parts: the provided operations, the consumed rows, the published and consumed events, the workflow and its activity, the schedules, the tables, the fakes, the call-type summary and the lifecycle. Each part is reviewed by the owner of the rows it names, and the tag waits for every reviewer.

**Compatibility check.** The schema is published as JSON Schema with `additionalProperties: false` on the closed objects, and the check runs on three inputs: the previous tag, the new draft and a corpus of recorded answers from the fakes. A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element fails the check and forces a new major version (C1, BR3).

**Open shapes carried into the tag.** Three shapes are carried as placeholders and not invented: the bids of a round (GAP-2906; ASM-4804), the names of the four consumed rows (GAP-2907; ASM-4805) and the sale elements a reported round leaves open (GAP-2911; ASM-4809). A placeholder is a declared forthcoming shape, not a permission to guess.

**Done when.** The seven criteria pass, the reviewers of the three consumed owners have closed their comments, the compatibility check passes on the tag, the fakes are published with their documented answers, and RWB-S5-E4024-APP can start against the tag with no open shape question.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Asset and disposal right calls one of the declared operations | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a declared request is absent or invalid | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-S5-001 | A declared write carries a bid or a floor under the approver's limit | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | A declared read carries an appraisal more than a year old | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written, as the decision-record element declares it | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| Document rule | A change fails the compatibility check | A breaking change needs a new major version. |
| Document rule | A consumed row has no published name | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2907; ASM-4805). |

The five message IDs are carried from the service and platform sets and are declared only as the envelope rows of the operations in this baseline; the two document rules are checks of this story and are not service messages.

##### 15. Screens and states

The baseline serves SCR-24 Auction rounds and SCR-21 Asset list through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). What this story fixes is the element list of the declared responses and the empty, loading, refused, conflict, out-of-order, stale-payment and unanswered-score states the route can show from this service's answers. The route itself, its merge order and its field list are RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the screens' transitions are the application story's.

No screen is built here, no component is delivered and no state machine is declared: the screen section of a contract story lists the elements the screens read and the states their answers can carry.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the baseline: the price schedule, the floor, the re-list limit, the codes and every threshold are referenced with their identifier and version, never enumerated as a constant or a default.
- No personal data in any element, fake, example or log: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates, a vendor code and a rule version only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the baseline declares no `v_ace_*` element and no ACE table, and the payment and vendor facts appear only as the P8 and S9 rows (DP-05).
- The case stays with rwb-case and the rules with rwb-decision: no `recovery_case` element and no rule row is declared as this service's own.
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; no document, module or test names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no monolith base `/api/recovery/v1`, no shared job table, no Schedule for the round timer, no event published or consumed by this branch.
- Additive only: a breaking change needs a new major version and a re-tag, and the code never moves ahead of the document (BR3).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the application slice of RWB-E4-024 for rwb-asset. The three legacy criteria are kept word for word with their origin tag and the five legacy test cases keep their IDs. The round becomes the auction branch of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` on queue `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery`: it opens each round at the price step the schedule sets, records the reported round on `listing` and the sale record it opens in `rwb_asset`, evaluates R-DIS-36, R-DIS-37, R-DIS-40, R-DIS-49 and R-DIS-50 on the DISPOSAL package in force, records each outcome before the row changes (DP-03), answers the case in rwb-case and publishes nothing. The legacy `v_ace_payment` and `v_ace_score` reads leave the service: the payment fact arrives on the rwb-payment boundary and the vendor score on the rwb-partner boundary (DP-05). The base becomes `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13) and SCR-24 and SCR-21 read through the gateway-bff route (DP-19). Gaps: no element holds a round's bids (GAP-2906; ASM-4804); consumed operation names not published (GAP-2907; ASM-4805); R-DIS-49 sits across the payment-term story (GAP-2908; ASM-4806); no requirement id (GAP-2909; ASM-4807); DP-04 outside the pattern set (GAP-2910; ASM-4808); the award and its cancellation have no element (GAP-2911; ASM-4809). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As an **auction vendor**, I want **the Workbench to let the vendor run each round and report the bids back into the case**, so that **assets sell sooner at approved prices** (legacy RWB-E4-024, word for word).

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E4-024. It owns:

- the three legacy criteria with their origin tag, and the rules, messages and screens they depend on;
- the round branch of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` on `rwb-asset`, a child of the case workflow (Architecture v5 slide 13);
- the opening of a round at the price step the schedule sets (R-DIS-36) and the record of the reported round and its bids (R-DIS-37) on `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds`;
- the outcome of a reported bid at or above the floor (R-DIS-40) and the cancellation of the award with the vendor score and the reopened round when the payment term expires (R-DIS-49, R-DIS-50);
- the write of the round number and the listing status on `listing`, and of the sale record a round opens, in `rwb_asset`;
- the decision record of each outcome before the change (DP-03) and the case answers `ROUND_OPEN`, `BID_RECEIVED`, `SALE_AGREED` and `AWARD_CANCELED`;
- the reads of SCR-24 and SCR-21 on `/api/recovery/asset/v1` through the gateway-bff route (DP-13, DP-19).

It does not own: the shape of the round write and the reads and the consumed rows, which are RWB-S5-E4024-CON; the start price, the floor and its approval, which are FEAT-AST-11's story; the listing publication, FEAT-AST-12; the step down on a round with no bid and the re-list, which are FEAT-AST-13 and FEAT-AST-17's stories; the second signature of a bid below the floor, FEAT-AST-16's story; the five-day payment term itself and the title transfer, FEAT-AST-18 to FEAT-AST-20's stories; the vendor allocation, FEAT-AST-14's story; the case and its states, rwb-case (P3); the payment and its posting, rwb-payment (P8); the vendor panel and scorecard, rwb-partner (S9); the rule package, rwb-decision (P7); the deployment, the operations story of this key.

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E4-024 kept a listing moving through its auction rounds: the vendor ran each round on the portal, the bids came back into the case, and a bid at or above the floor became a sale. The FSD keeps it as FEAT-AST-15 in module S5, run by the auction vendor on the partner portal and the auction portals, after FEAT-AST-14 allocates the asset to a vendor and before FEAT-AST-16 tests a bid below the floor.

What D-RCV-60 changes:

- **the round is this service's.** `listing` in `rwb_asset` carries the round number, and the standard columns carry the status (Ownership Map; Architecture v5 slide 41). No source names an element for the bids of a round, so the bids are a gap and not an invented table (GAP-2906; ASM-4804).
- **the picture stays with its owners.** The case state is rwb-case's, the payment is rwb-payment's and the vendor score is rwb-partner's; the legacy `v_ace_*` reads leave the service (DP-05).
- **the decision is recorded first**, one per outcome, in the row's transaction — what AC1 asked and AC3 tested.
- **nothing is published.** EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is the take-on story's (TSD S5 T5.3); §12.3 states the absence and a build that adds an event fails it.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S5-E4024-CON tagged: the round write, the two reads, the consumed rows, the decision-record element, the rule-package element, the error set and the fakes.
- `listing` exists in `rwb_asset` with TSD S5 T3.1 columns including `round_no`; `asset_sale` exists with its sale elements; no column holds a bid and none is added (GAP-2906; ASM-4804).
- The DISPOSAL package is in force with R-DIS-36, R-DIS-37, R-DIS-40, R-DIS-49 and R-DIS-50 from rwb-decision (P7), loaded through the service template; DP-04 is outside the pattern set (GAP-2910; ASM-4808).
- The price step of the round is the schedule `listing` already holds; the ladder and its step are reference data with their version (TSD S5 T3.2).
- The `LOV-LISTING` and `LOV-SALE-CHANNEL` lists are reference data with their version.
- The rwb-case state read, the case-move answer, the rwb-payment payment fact and the rwb-partner vendor score are behind fakes; none of their names is published (GAP-2907; ASM-4805).
- The round due fact and the payment-term expiry arrive as signals of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`; no subscription is added.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON writes in the caller's transaction (DP-03); RWB-PLT-N001-CON serves the two screens, one hop each (DP-19).
- The service holds its own login on `rwb_asset`, no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-01, DP-05).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft baseline; the contract is tagged when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The listing is live and its schedule step falls due; `AssetDisposalWorkflow` wakes on the durable timer, confirms the case state on the rwb-case contract and opens round `n`.
2. The step writes the round number and the status on `listing`, records the opening (DP-03) and answers `ROUND_OPEN` to rwb-case.
3. The auction vendor runs the round on the portal; the portal reports it as `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds` with the round number, the date, the result and the price of the round, and an `Idempotency-Key`.
4. `AssetController` checks the Asset and disposal right U, the listing and its status, and the round number; a listing that is not live and a round out of order are refused (X4).
5. `RoundEvaluator` loads the package in force and evaluates R-DIS-37: from `ROUND_OPEN`, on `BID_PLACED`, the bid is recorded against the round and the asset and the case moves to `BID_RECEIVED`.
6. `AssetDecisionRecordWriter` writes one record **before any change**; a failed write stops the request (DP-03; AC1, AC3).
7. `RoundWriter` writes the round number and the status on `listing` in one transaction with the record and the idempotency row; the round price and the result are held where an element carries them and are Not specified in the source documents elsewhere (GAP-2906; ASM-4804).
8. The answer carries the round and the sale record the round opens (`AssetSale`), and `CaseMoveAnswer` answers `BID_RECEIVED` with the round, the price and the rule version; rwb-case writes the case (GAP-2911; ASM-4809).
9. On a bid at or above the floor R-DIS-40 fires: the bid is accepted, the sale is agreed, one record is written and the answer carries `SALE_AGREED`. A bid below the floor is not accepted here: the case moves to `SECOND_SIGNATURE_PENDING` on the second-signature story's step (X3).
10. The payment term runs on the awarded sale; when it expires with no payment, R-DIS-49 fires from `AWAITING_PAYMENT`: the award is cancelled, the vendor is scored and the round is reopened, one record is written and the answer carries `AWARD_CANCELED` (AC2).
11. R-DIS-50 then reopens the round at the same price step: the round number and the status are written again, a record is written and the answer carries `ROUND_OPEN`; no price steps down here.
12. A repeated request or key writes once and is counted; the workflow returns to its durable timer and continues as new at each stage end and at least every 28 days.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The record cannot be written | Nothing written, no move answered, the sale record not opened | MSG-P7-003 | AC3, TC-E4-024-03, TC-E4-024-05 |
| X2 | The role lacks the Asset and disposal right | 403 before any read or write | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, TC-E4-024-04 |
| X3 | The case is in another state, or the bid is below the floor | The rule does not fire; nothing accepted, the state reported | MSG-S5-001 where under the limit | AC2 |
| X4 | The listing is not live, or the round number is out of order | 409 with the stage the listing is in; nothing written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X5 | The same report or key arrives twice | One round, one record, one answer | None | AC1 |
| X6 | The payment fact is missing or stale at the due date | The cancellation is held until the fact confirms no payment; the data date is shown | None | AC2 |
| X7 | The vendor score boundary does not answer | The award is still cancelled and the score is queued on the workflow | None | AC2 |
| X8 | A contract misses 2 s or its breaker is open | Retry on the workflow schedule; 503 in the platform envelope | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X9 | A statement reaches a `v_ace_*` view, `recovery_case` or a foreign schema | The grant refuses it and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | §17, BR9 |

X1 to X3 are the legacy paths on the split, X4 to X8 what the round write, the boundaries and the payment fact add, and X9 the DP-01 and DP-05 boundary.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Day 1 against the CON baseline and the fakes; no live P1, P3, P8 or S9 |
| Negotiable | Activity name, decision code and outcome shape are ours; rules, messages, screens, rows and reads are fixed |
| Valuable | The vendor reports a round and the case sees its result the same hour; the award reopens when the term is missed |
| Estimable | One branch, two evaluators, one record per outcome, two row changes, four answers, two clients, one screen fragment |
| Small | Two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion on synthetic cases through the fakes, plus the access, wrong-state, repeat, stale-payment and failed-record cases |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Run auction rounds and report bids

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-000541" holds asset "AST-2026-000541" in live listing "LS-2026-000541"
    Given the DISPOSAL rule package is in force at its version and carries R-DIS-36, R-DIS-37, R-DIS-40, R-DIS-49 and R-DIS-50
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 Run auction rounds and report bids (legacy RWB-E4-024 AC1)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case "RC-2026-000541" in state ROUND_OPEN with round 1 open on the listing
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When the user acts on the screen
    Then lets the vendor run each round and report the bids back into the case
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Rule R-DIS-49 (legacy RWB-E4-024 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case "RC-2026-000542" in state AWAITING_PAYMENT with an award on the sale
    Given the rwb-payment contract mock returns no payment received by the payment due date for "RC-2026-000542"
    Given a case in state AWAITING_PAYMENT
    When payment term expired
    Then cancel the award, score the vendor and reopen the round
    Then the case moves to AWARD_CANCELED

  Scenario: AC3 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E4-024 AC3)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The three criteria are the legacy criteria word for word with the origin tag added: the repeated `Then`, `the action is taken`, `payment term expired` and `the decision log cannot be written` stand, and the `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` lines are the only additions. The work happens in three places: rwb-case writes the four moves, rwb-payment and rwb-partner answer the payment and the score, and this story opens the round, records the report, evaluates the rules, writes the row, records and answers. AC2's "reopen the round" is R-DIS-50's step; the award and the term it expires are FEAT-AST-18's story (GAP-2908; ASM-4806).

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-DIS-36 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | LISTING_LIVE | ROUND_OPENED | schedule step due | Open the round at the scheduled price step | ROUND_OPEN | Auction and remarketing vendor | auction portal, Workbench scheduler | per schedule |
| R-DIS-37 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | ROUND_OPEN | BID_PLACED | Any | Record the bid against the round and the asset | BID_RECEIVED | Workbench | auction portal | None |
| R-DIS-40 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | BID_RECEIVED | BID_AT_OR_ABOVE_FLOOR | bid_amount at or above floor_price | Accept the bid and agree the sale | SALE_AGREED | Sale officer | Case Workspace, auction portal | 1 working day |
| R-DIS-49 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | AWAITING_PAYMENT | PAYMENT_TERM_EXPIRED | payment absent and payment_due_date passed | Cancel the award, score the vendor and reopen the round | AWARD_CANCELED | Sale officer | auction portal, Partner Portal | None |
| R-DIS-50 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | AWARD_CANCELED | ROUND_REOPENED | Any | Reopen the round at the same price step | ROUND_OPEN | Auction and remarketing vendor | auction portal | None |

The five rows are copied character for character from the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; their owner column is a business role, so the case stays in these states and moves in rwb-case on this story's answer, while the `listing` row and the sale record are written here. ##### 9. State transitions

The case route state is rwb-case's and is applied by the parent `CaseWorkflow` on this story's answer (BR4).

| From (case state) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| LISTING_LIVE | `ROUND_OPENED` under R-DIS-36 | The schedule step is due | ROUND_OPEN, answer `ROUND_OPEN` |
| ROUND_OPEN | `BID_PLACED` under R-DIS-37 | Any reported bid | BID_RECEIVED, answer `BID_RECEIVED` |
| BID_RECEIVED | `BID_AT_OR_ABOVE_FLOOR` under R-DIS-40 | Bid amount at or above the floor | SALE_AGREED, answer `SALE_AGREED` |
| AWAITING_PAYMENT | `PAYMENT_TERM_EXPIRED` under R-DIS-49 | Payment absent and the due date passed | AWARD_CANCELED, answer `AWARD_CANCELED` |
| AWARD_CANCELED | `ROUND_REOPENED` under R-DIS-50 | Any | ROUND_OPEN, answer `ROUND_OPEN` |
| Any | An unexpected state, a bid below the floor or a repeated report | X3, X5 | Unchanged |

| `listing` status | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live | The round opens | R-DIS-36 fires | Live, `round_no` = n |
| Live | A round is reported | R-DIS-37 fires | Live, `round_no` = n, result recorded |
| Live | A bid at or above the floor is accepted | R-DIS-40 fires | Under offer, sale record opened |
| Under offer | The term expires | R-DIS-49 and R-DIS-50 fire | Live, same `round_no` |
| Any | A duplicate request or key | X5 | Unchanged |

The statuses are the `LOV-LISTING` rows of TSD S5 T3.2; the case states are the DISPOSAL machine's (TSD S5 T4).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| PT-AUCTION, auction and remarketing vendor | Asset and disposal U: reports a round and its bids on the portal |
| RW-SALEOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-NPAMGR, SY-DATALOAD | Asset and disposal U: the round write, the award cancellation and the reopen |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-FIELDCOL, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL and the further roles of the read row | Asset and disposal R, in scope |
| PT-RAMC | Asset and disposal R and U on its own listings |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-AGENT | The matrix's right, under the same checks as a person |
| rwb-asset service identity | Runs the branch; no grant on another schema and no `v_ace_*` grant |

The rights are the rows of the legacy permission table and TSD S5 T6.1, nothing wider. DP-08 is not in the pattern set: the right is declared per operation and the guard is a service-template capability.

Field IDs follow TSD S5 T3.1 and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. **No new table, no column, no migration**: the tables come with the DB story, and `decision_record` and `idempotency_key` are library objects in `rwb_asset` (DP-03). **No personal data**: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates, a vendor code and a rule version only; every fixture is synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the behaviour behind the shapes of RWB-S5-E4024-CON.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated, with the round of each listing (API-S5-001) | Asset and disposal, R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out with title, listing, round number and round price (API-S5-002) | Asset and disposal, R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/listings/{listingId}/rounds` | AuctionRoundRequest in — roundNo, heldOn, result, price — and the sale record the round opens out, `AssetSale`, 200 (API-S5-005) | Asset and disposal, U, scope applied | Idempotency-Key |

The round write is the only write of this slice; the listings write `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings` (API-S5-004) is the pricing story's and is not changed here. Errors: 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409 for a listing that is not live or a round out of order, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 or MSG-S5-001, 503 when a library or a contract does not answer.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case state and the round the case sees; faked |
| Case-move answer (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2907; ASM-4805)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | `ROUND_OPEN`, `BID_RECEIVED`, `SALE_AGREED` and `AWARD_CANCELED` with the rule and its version; faked |
| Payment fact activity (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2907; ASM-4805)) | queue `rwb-payment` | P8 rwb-payment | The payment due date and whether the payment arrived; the legacy `v_ace_payment` read becomes this row (DP-05); faked |
| Vendor score activity (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2907; ASM-4805)) | queue `rwb-partner` | S9 rwb-partner | The score of the vendor whose award was cancelled; the legacy `v_ace_score` read becomes this row (DP-05); faked |

One hop, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). They are the cross-service rows the plan does not carry, so this story builds on their documents and fakes and its C and I rows are None; the wave 3 harness holds the real journey.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is the take-on story's and the sale event the sale stories'; a round, a bid and a cancelled award write no outbox row and add nothing to `rwb.asset.events.v1`. A build that publishes here fails the absence test.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The round due fact, the payment-term expiry and the vendor score arrive as signals and activities of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`; the rwb-payment subscription of the connection matrix belongs to FEAT-AST-18's story, so this slice adds no consumer group and no inbox row.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one per case per stage, continues-as-new across the holding | `rwb-asset` in `rwb-recovery` | Input: case, route, asset, listing, package in force; signals: round due, round reported, payment-term expiry, package in force |
| `reportAuctionRound` | Activity, the round write | `rwb-asset` | Listing, round and report in; rule IDs with versions, round number, status, sale record reference and case move out, one transaction |

No child workflow and no second queue. The activity name is a design choice of this story; the two boundary activities run on the owner's queue.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. R-DIS-36 runs "per schedule" as a durable timer inside the workflow; the step owns no Temporal Schedule and no Quartz job. The service's single Schedule is JOB-19, the re-appraisal story's.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| listing | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The listing; this story writes `round_no` and the status |
| asset_sale | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The sale a round opens; written here, read on the cancellation |
| decision_record | PLT library in `rwb_asset` | One record per outcome (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated report |

Not owned and never read as a table: `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task`, `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row`, `approval` (P7), `valuation` (S1), `document` (P5), `deviation` (S8), every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No bid table exists (GAP-2906; ASM-4804). No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

The fakes are test-only; the placeholder rows carry their gap until their owners confirm the names (GAP-2907; ASM-4805).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset.rounds`; front end `src/modules/recovery/asset/AuctionRounds.tsx`, the fragment SCR-24 embeds, read only.

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is a prohibition here: the legacy `v_ace_payment` and `v_ace_score` reads leave the service for the P8 and S9 boundaries, and no `v_ace_*` grant is kept. DP-03 is the transaction rule of the round write, DP-13 moves the base, DP-19 is how the screens reach the service. The two boundary rows are built on documents and fakes on Day 1 (GAP-2907). The package in force is loaded through the service template without the DP-04 platform row (GAP-2910).

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` round branch | Workflow | Waits on the timer and the signals, loads the package in force, reports to the parent |
| `reportAuctionRound` | Activity | The one step: read, evaluate, write, answer |
| `RoundEvaluator` | Service | R-DIS-36, R-DIS-37 and R-DIS-40 on the round, the bid and the floor |
| `AwardCancellationEvaluator` | Service | R-DIS-49 and R-DIS-50 on the due date and the payment |
| `AssetDecisionRecordWriter` | Library adapter | One hash-linked record per outcome before any change (DP-03) |
| `RoundWriter` | Repository | `listing` and `asset_sale` in one transaction with the idempotency row and the lock |
| `CaseMoveAnswer`, `CaseStateClient`, `PaymentFactActivity`, `VendorScoreActivity` | Clients | The four answers and boundary calls, one hop, 2 s |
| `AuctionRoundController` | Controller | The round write and the reads, rights, key and the 400/401/403/404/409/422/503 map |
| `AuctionRounds` | React component | The rounds, the bids reported and the result on SCR-24, read only |

**Database.** No Flyway file: tables from the DB story, library objects from the library's migration, no bid table and no column added (GAP-2906).

**Configuration.** The price schedule, the floor and the re-list limit at their version (TSD S5 T3.2); the DISPOSAL package and version from rwb-decision; the capability rows from rwb-access; the flag and the 2 s budget as platform configuration (ADR-020).

**Build steps.** (1) the round branch and its input record; (2) `RoundEvaluator` with the opening, the report and the below-floor paths (AC1, X3); (3) the round write with the round-number and status checks (AC1, X4); (4) the two boundary clients against their fakes for the payment and the score (AC2, X6, X7); (5) `AwardCancellationEvaluator` with R-DIS-49 and R-DIS-50 (AC2); (6) the record writer against the stub (AC3, X1); (7) `RoundWriter` with the idempotency row (AC1, X5); (8) `CaseMoveAnswer` (AC1, AC2); (9) `AuctionRoundController` with the rights and the error map (AC1, X2); (10) the screen fragment through the route fake; (11) the boundary test (X9, BR6, BR7).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.asset.auction-rounds-v1`; off means the report is held, nothing is written and no move is answered.

**Done when.** §16 passes, a reported round moves the case and records its outcome in SIT, a bid at or above the floor answers `SALE_AGREED`, an expired term answers `AWARD_CANCELED` and then `ROUND_OPEN`, a repeat writes once, a forced record failure changes nothing, no case row and no `v_ace_*` read exists, and the two screens answer through the composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S5-001 | A bid or a floor under the approver's limit on the round write (X3) | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | An appraisal more than a year old when the round is opened (X6) | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request or signal is absent or invalid (X4) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right reports or reads (X2) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record cannot be written before the round changes (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The five IDs are the legacy set, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and none is added.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-24 Auction rounds (scheduled, open, result, settled) and SCR-21 Asset list (loading, list) are served through the gateway-bff route (DP-19), which calls rwb-asset for the asset, the listing, the round and its price, rwb-case for the state, rwb-payment for the term and rwb-partner for the vendor. This story fixes the rwb-asset answers only; the route and field list are RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

The states it produces are the round state of SCR-24 — round number, date, result, price, the sale it opened and the reopened round — and the refusal, not-recorded, wrong-state and stale-payment states with MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-S5-001. Scheduled and settled are the schedule and the sale stories'.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the price schedule, the floor, the re-list limit and the statuses stay reference data or rule rows with a version.
- No personal data in the schema, a workflow input or a log; a bidder is a vendor or buyer code and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: no `v_ace_*` grant, no ACE read (DP-05).
- The case stays with rwb-case: no `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task` or `timer` row here (BR4).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element returns: no shared job table, no Quartz row, no monolith base, no data-lake export of a round.
- The record precedes the change and the repeated report is deduped (DP-03, BR8).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract slice of RWB-E4-025, the baseline the below-floor branch of rwb-asset builds against on Day 1. The baseline declares the three asset reads and the round write that answer SCR-23 Listing and price and SCR-21 Asset list on `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13), the three consumed rows of rwb-source-data and rwb-case (DP-05), the decision-record element of DP-03, the approval item the second signature is raised on and the sale elements of an accepted bid, the rights and the error envelope, and the fakes. The step publishes no event and consumes none, because the owned event of the service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` and the bid, the signature and the case state are workflow facts. No source publishes the operation names of the consumed rows (GAP-2912; ASM-4810); no source names a field for the bid or the signature (GAP-2913; ASM-4811); the legacy endpoints table names the listings write while the TSD gives the round write the sale answer (GAP-2914; ASM-4812); no operation raises an approval item (GAP-2915; ASM-4813); the split plan carries no requirement id (GAP-2916; ASM-4814); and the rule package and the approval template are declared without a pattern or platform row of the slice (GAP-2917; ASM-4815). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the below-floor accept step of rwb-asset — its asset and listing reads, its round write, its consumed rows, its decision-record and approval elements, the sale elements of an accepted bid, its rights, its error envelope and its fakes — baselined and tagged before the build starts**, so that **the application story, the rounds story and every consumer can build and test on Day 1 against one fixed, versioned surface instead of guessing the shape of a neighbour's answer**.

This is the contract slice of legacy RWB-E4-025. It owns:

- the document that fixes the three asset reads and the round write on base `/api/recovery/asset/v1`, with their parameters, their documented answer, their rights and their idempotency (DP-13);
- the three consumed rows: the rwb-source-data appraisal and asset data product, the rwb-case case state read and the rwb-case case-move answer, each with its owner, its use and its placeholder where the operation name is not published (DP-05);
- the decision-record element and the local library dependency that carries it (DP-03);
- the approval element: the item a below-floor bid is routed on, its level, its clock and its outcome, declared as rwb-decision's reference and not as a table or a rule of this service;
- the sale elements of an accepted bid on `asset_sale` and the status element of `listing`, with their fields of TSD S5 T3.1 and their closed lists of T3.2;
- the capability area, the rights and the error envelope of the operations it declares;
- the fakes and their documented answers, so that every downstream answer has a stub on Day 1;
- the naming and boundary rules of the baseline: one base, one topic, one queue, no foreign schema, no monolith base, no Schedule for the approval clock.

It does not own: the below-floor behaviour, the rule evaluation, the approval request, the sale write, the decision records and the case moves, which are RWB-S5-E4025-APP; the rounds and their bids, which are the rounds story's (RWB-E4-024); the start price and the floor, which are FEAT-AST-11's; the re-list after a refusal, which is RWB-E4-026; the appraisal and NPA asset facts, which are rwb-source-data's (P1); the approval record, the DoA levels and limits, which are rwb-decision's and rwb-access's; the rule package, which is rwb-decision's; the screen field list and the composite route, which are RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19).

##### 2. Business rationale

A contract baseline is what lets the stories of one wave build at once. Without it the below-floor step would be written against whatever shape the round answer happened to expose that week, and the first integration would find the mismatches instead of the review. With it, the application story builds on Day 1 against a tagged document and its fakes, the rounds story knows what its write must carry for the accept to ride on it, and rwb-decision knows which elements of its approval the asset side reads.

The three rules the baseline applies:

- **the owner publishes, the consumer adapts.** Every consumed row names its owner and its use, and where the source documents do not publish an operation name the row carries the placeholder rather than an invented path (GAP-2912; ASM-4810).
- **one hop, one budget.** Every consumed row is a single hop with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and no chain, which is ADR-020; the approval is not a REST row because it runs on rwb-decision's queue over Temporal (Architecture v5 slide 13).
- **additive only.** The baseline moves forward without breaking: a new optional element is a minor version, and a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version and a new document (C1).

The business outcome the baseline protects is the one FEAT-AST-16 of the FSD names: a bid under the floor is routed for a second approval before it can be accepted. The baseline does not state that outcome, and no criterion here asserts a business value.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The Ownership Map rows are in force: S5 owns `GET /assets`, `GET /assets/{assetId}`, `GET /assets/{assetKey}`, `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings`, `POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings` and `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds`; `asset_sale` and `listing` are S5's tables; the `asset` extension is named only.
- The service naming is fixed: schema `rwb_asset`, login `rwb_asset`, base `/api/recovery/asset/v1`, topic `rwb.asset.events.v1` with `.retry` and `.dlt`, task queue `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset`.
- The owned event row of the service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` (TSD S5 T5.3), and the elements of this baseline touch none of the events of the service: the round, the bid and the signature are workflow facts.
- The platform CON stories are published: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for the decision record (DP-03) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the composite route (DP-19). The rules kit and the approval template of the workflow kit are platform capabilities and add no H row to this slice (GAP-2917; ASM-4815).
- The approval record `approval` and the delegation facts `delegation_limit` are P7's and P4's; the baseline names them and declares none of their fields (GAP-2915; ASM-4813).
- The accept surface is fixed at `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds` (API-S5-005) because its documented answer is the `AssetSale` and its right is U, which the legacy endpoints table does not say (GAP-2914; ASM-4812).
- The bid amount and the signature have no column in TSD S5 T3.1, so their elements carry the placeholder until an owner names them (GAP-2913; ASM-4811).
- No approval is needed to publish a Draft baseline; the document is baselined by this story's own review, and the build waits only for its tag.

##### 4. Flow

1. The author drafts the baseline from the Ownership Map, the TSD S5 T-A.1 operations, the TSD S5 T3.1 fields and the lists of T3.2.
2. Every operation is declared with its method, path, request, documented answer, rights, idempotency and error set.
3. Every consumed row is declared with its owner, its use, its budget and a placeholder where the operation name is not published.
4. The decision-record element is declared with the library that carries it, and the approval element with its owner, its level, its clock and its outcome — as a reference, never as a table or a rule of this service.
5. The sale elements of an accepted bid and the listing status element are declared with their field IDs and their closed lists.
6. The fakes are declared with their documented answers, one per consumed row, one for the approval and one for the composite route.
7. The schema, the open lists and the closed lists are published, and the compatibility check runs: a breaking change fails the check.
8. The document goes to review as Draft; the reviewers are the owners of the consumed rows, the rounds story owner and the tech lead of the service.
9. On the review's close the document is tagged and baselined; the application story starts against the tag and the fakes.
10. A defect found in the build that needs a shape change is raised against this document, and the document moves to a new minor or major version; the code never moves ahead of the document.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A consumer asks for a shape the sources do not publish | The row or element carries the placeholder and the gap; no path and no field is invented | C2, C4 |
| X2 | A change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element | The compatibility check fails, the version becomes a new major and the document is re-reviewed | C1 |
| X3 | A declared operation reaches another service's data or base | The review refuses the baseline and the boundary test fails the build | C7 |
| X4 | A consumed row has no fake, or its fake has no documented answer | The baseline is not tagged; the application story cannot start | C6 |
| X5 | The rights of an operation are not one of the rows of the access matrix | The operation is not declared and the error set of the operation is incomplete | C5 |
| X6 | An owner changes its documented answer after the tag, or the rounds story claims the round write differently | The owner publishes a new version, this document follows with a minor or major version, and the application story re-tests against the new fake | X2 |
| X7 | Two documents claim the same path, or a document claims a column the sources do not name | The naming rule and the placeholder rule resolve it: the owner in the Ownership Map keeps the path, and the column stays Not specified in the source documents | C2, C3, C7 |

X1 to X3 are the paths of an incomplete source, X4 to X6 the paths of a baseline moving under a build, and X7 the naming and placeholder boundary.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs no build, no live service and no approval; starts on Day 1 and is finished before the application story's first line |
| Negotiable | The wording, the order of the sections and the fake data are this story's choice; the paths, the owners, the base, the error set and the element names are fixed by their sources |
| Valuable | The stories of wave 3 build at once against one tagged surface, and the first integration finds behaviour, not shape |
| Estimable | One document, four provided operations, three consumed rows, three element groups, seven fakes and one compatibility check |
| Small | Finished inside a week; the review is the only gate |
| Testable | Every criterion is a document check that runs in the contract test suite, plus the compatibility check on the published schema |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the below-floor accept step

  Scenario: C1 The baseline validates and only additive changes pass (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published schema and the open and closed lists of the baseline
    When a change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element
    Then the compatibility check fails and the change needs a new major version
    And a change that adds an optional element passes as a minor version

  Scenario: C2 The elements and the closed lists are published as declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the baseline document of this story
    When the sale elements of an accepted bid, the listing status and the element lists are read
    Then every element carries its type, its nullability, its source field ID and its closed list
    And the sale elements are the fields DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019 and the status is the LOV-LISTING list, referenced with its identifier and version and never enumerated in code
    And the bid amount and the signature reference carry the placeholder and its gap identifier because no source names a column for them

  Scenario: C3 The provided reads and the round write are declared once with their rights (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operations the baseline provides on base /api/recovery/asset/v1
    When the method, path, documented answer, right and idempotency of each are read
    Then the three asset reads carry the Asset and disposal right R with scope applied and no idempotency
    And POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds carries the right U, the Idempotency-Key header, the AssetSale answer and the 409 and 422 errors
    And the round write is named as shared with the rounds story of RWB-E4-024 and the legacy endpoints table of RWB-E4-025 is recorded as the conflicting row

  Scenario: C4 The consumed rows carry their owners, their budgets and their placeholders (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed operation table of the baseline
    When the rows of rwb-source-data and rwb-case are read
    Then each row names its owner, its use and its 2 s budget
    And where the operation name is not published the row carries the placeholder and the gap identifier and no path

  Scenario: C5 The error envelope is declared per operation (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operations the baseline provides
    When the error set and the rights of each operation are read
    Then the error set names 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409, 422 with MSG-GEN-001, MSG-S5-001 or MSG-S5-002 and 503 in one problem envelope
    And the capability area and the right of each operation are the rows of the access matrix

  Scenario: C6 The decision-record, approval and fake elements are declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the baseline document
    When the decision-record element, the approval element and the fake table are read
    Then the decision-record element names RWB-PLT-E1027-CON as its library and the transaction it joins
    And the approval element names rwb-decision as its owner, the level and the two-working-day clock as values in force and the outcome as its only answer, and declares no approval table and no rule row
    And every consumed row and the approval have a fake with a documented answer, including the stopped decision-record stub, the refused signature and the expired clock

  Scenario: C7 The naming and the boundary of the baseline hold (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the base, the topic, the queue and the schema of the baseline
    When the document is checked against the naming rule and the ownership map
    Then the base /api/recovery/asset/v1, the queue rwb-asset and the topic rwb.asset.events.v1 are the only ones declared as this service's own
    And no foreign schema, no foreign topic, no monolith base /api/recovery/v1 and no Schedule for the approval clock is declared
    And no event is published or consumed by the step and no approval row is declared as this service's
```

The seven criteria are new to this run and are tagged as such: they test the contract deliverable only — the schema, the elements, the lists, the operations, the consumed rows, the rights, the envelope, the two library elements, the fakes and the boundary. No criterion states a business outcome or a business value of the application story, and none asserts that a rule fires, that a signature is given or that a case moves.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One owner per operation, event and table: the baseline declares only the rows the Ownership Map gives to S5, and names every other row with its owner | Ownership Map; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | A consumed row or element with no published name carries the placeholder and its gap, and never an invented path or field | Template and Rules v1 §R9; GAP-2912; GAP-2913 |
| BR3 | The baseline is additive: a new optional element is a minor version, and a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version | ADR-020; C1 |
| BR4 | Every consumed row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and no chain | ADR-020 |
| BR5 | No event is published and none is consumed by the step: the owned event is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn`, the take-on story's, and the bid, the signature and the case state are workflow facts | TSD S5 T5.3; C7 |
| BR6 | The decision record is written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the caller's transaction before any change, and its element is declared once for the service | DP-03 |
| BR7 | The approval is rwb-decision's and the delegation facts are rwb-access's: the baseline names the item, the level and the clock and declares no approval table, no DoA row and no approval operation | DP-01; Ownership Map rows `approval` and `delegation_limit`; GAP-2915 |
| BR8 | No business value is declared in the baseline: the floor, the approver's limit, the two clocks, the codes and the thresholds are referenced with their identifier and version | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s16); legacy Guardrails |
| BR9 | No personal data in any element, fake or example of the baseline: the bidder and the approver are references, never names | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR10 | The baseline never declares another service's table, operation or topic as its own, and a check fails the build where one names it | DP-01, DP-13, DP-14 |

##### 9. State transitions

The document itself is the object of this section: the lifecycle of the contract baseline.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | The draft is complete | Every operation, row, element, fake and error is declared | Draft |
| Draft | The review is opened | The owners of the consumed rows and the rounds story owner are named as reviewers | In review |
| In review | The review closes with no open comment | The compatibility check passes | Baselined, tagged for the application story |
| In review | A comment needs a shape change | The change is applied to the draft | Draft |
| Baselined | An additive change is approved | New optional element only, compatibility check passes | Baselined, new minor version |
| Baselined | A breaking change is approved | A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element | Draft of a new major version, and the consumers are notified |
| Baselined | An owner changes its answer, or the rounds baseline claims the round write differently | X6 | Draft of a new minor or major version, and the fake is updated |

| Step | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Being authored | A consumed row has no published name, or an element has no column | X1 | The row or element carries the placeholder and the gap and the draft continues |
| In review | A row reaches a foreign schema, base or topic, or declares an approval table | X3, X7 | The baseline is refused |
| Ready to tag | A consumed row or the approval has no fake | X4 | Not tagged, the review reopens |

The baseline declares no new table, no new column and no migration, and it enumerates no business value: every list, code and threshold is referenced with its identifier and its version. **No personal data** appears in any element, fake or example; the fixture identifiers are synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13). These are the reads that answer SCR-23 and SCR-21 and the write the accepted bid rides on.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated (API-S5-001) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out, with its title, its listing, the round price, the floor and the round number (API-S5-002) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetKey}` | Asset of status 200 out on the business key of the Ownership Map | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/listings/{listingId}/rounds` | AuctionRoundRequest in; AssetSale out on a recorded round and an accepted bid; 409 when the round or the listing is not in the state the write expects; 422 on a missing field or a floor under the approver's limit (API-S5-005) | Asset and disposal, right U, scope applied | Idempotency-Key header |

The round write is declared once for two stories: the rounds story of RWB-E4-024 records the round and its bids, and this slice records the accepted bid and the sale it agrees. No source splits the operation. The legacy endpoints table of RWB-E4-025 names `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings` (API-S5-004) instead, which the TSD documents as the price-and-floor write answered with an `Approval`; the TSD outranks the story master under §R3, so the accept rides API-S5-005 and the conflict is recorded as GAP-2914 with ASM-4812. `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings` is declared by the pricing story and by RWB-S5-E4022-CON and is not declared here.

The error envelope of the declared operations: 400 for a malformed request, 401 for an unauthenticated call, 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope asset or listing, 409 for a round or a listing not in the state the write expects, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for a missing field, with MSG-S5-001 for a floor under the approver's limit and with MSG-S5-002 for an appraisal more than a year old, and 503 when the decision library or a consumed contract does not answer, in one problem document with a code, a message ID and a correlation reference.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The appraisal and asset data product (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2912; ASM-4810)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The appraised value, the appraisal date, the outlier flag and the book value, with the freshness stamp; faked |
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family (read) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference and the case state the rules check before they fire; faked |
| The case-move answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2912; ASM-4810)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The answer that carries the stage outcome with its rule version; on the workflow boundary it is the outcome the parent applies; faked |

Each row is one hop, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). Where a name is not published the row carries the placeholder and no path, so the consumer adapts at the tag rather than inventing a surface (BR2). The second signature is not a consumed row: it is raised and answered on rwb-decision's queue over Temporal (§12.5).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The owned event row of this service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn`, published by the take-on story when the asset record opens, and no source names an `AssetSold` event. This baseline declares neither as its own, adds nothing to `rwb.asset.events.v1`, and the step writes no outbox row: its outward surface is the sale row, the approval request and the case-move answer.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The round, the bid, the signature and the accepted appraisal arrive as signals of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`, so the baseline declares no topic subscription, no consumer group and no inbox row, and a build that subscribes to a topic not listed by Architecture v5 fails the naming check (BR5, DP-14).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, continues-as-new | `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the route, the asset reference, the listing reference and the rule package in force; signals: the round and its bid, the second signature, the accepted re-appraisal |
| The below-floor branch activity | Activity, one per outcome, named by the application story | `rwb-asset` | The case, the listing and the bid in; the rule IDs with their versions, the approval request, the sale reference and the stage outcome out, in one transaction |
| `ApprovalWorkflow` | Child workflow, the workflow kit's approval | rwb-decision (P7) | The item: the amount, the floor, the asset reference, the rule and its version, the level and the two-working-day clock of R-DIS-41 |

The workflow is the same execution the take-on, holding, sale and ladder stories of this service use; this baseline fixes its input and signal elements, the shape of the approval request it raises and the sale it agrees, and it declares no second queue. The activity name is a design choice of the application story, and the baseline leaves it open.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. R-DIS-41's two-working-day clock belongs to the approval routing on rwb-decision's side and the stage's wait is a durable timer inside the workflow, so the baseline declares no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job for the accept. The single Schedule of the service is JOB-19, which the re-appraisal story of this service owns and which is not declared here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| asset_sale | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The agreed sale; the baseline declares the elements of DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019, not its schema |
| listing | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | Read, and the status written; the baseline declares the elements of its price, round and status |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The local decision record of DP-03, declared through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated signal or request and the answer it holds |
| asset | S5 (`rwb_asset`), named only | The ACE asset extension of TSD S5 T3.1; read on the asset answer, never written here |

The baseline declares no column, no index and no migration, and it declares no table of another owner: `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task` and `timer` (P3), `approval`, `delegation_limit`, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7 and P4), `valuation` (S1), `document` (P5), `deviation` (S8) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) are named by their owner and never declared here. No bid table and no signature column is declared: both are Not specified in the source documents and are declared only once their owner names them (GAP-2913; ASM-4811).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-source-data appraisal and asset fake | The appraisal `AP-2026-000541` of asset `AST-2026-000541` with its value, its date and a clear outlier flag, and the NPA asset with its book value; an appraisal more than a year old; a stale product with its date; no answer beyond 2 s | C4, C6 |
| rwb-case case-state and case-move fake | The case states `BID_RECEIVED` and `SECOND_SIGNATURE_PENDING` of the fixture cases; the moves accepted and a move refused for a state the rule does not expect | C4, C6 |
| rwb-decision approval fake | An approval item open with its level and its clock; a given signature with the approver role; a refused signature; an expired clock | C6 |
| rwb-decision rule-package fake | The DISPOSAL package at its version in force with R-DIS-41 and R-DIS-42 | C6 |
| Decision-record stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | C6 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-23 and SCR-21 answer for case `RC-2026-000541`, with the listing, the round price and the approval state read once | C2, C6 |
| Bid and floor data fake | A bid under the floor, a bid at the floor and a bid above it, with a floor under the approver's limit (MSG-S5-001) | C2, C5, C6 |

Each fake answers only what its owner documents, and a fake that answers more than the document fails the review. The operation names that are not published are stubbed from the documents and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-2912; ASM-4810).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 4 provided, 2 consumed | The three asset reads and the round write on `/api/recovery/asset/v1`; the rwb-source-data data-product row and the rwb-case state and case-move rows; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | The bid, the signature and the case state are workflow facts; nothing is published |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 1 activity, 1 approval child | `AssetDisposalWorkflow` on `rwb-asset` and the approval on rwb-decision's queue; no Schedule |
| File | None | No file element is declared; the portal and HOME.SCB publication is FEAT-AST-12's |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Document.** `04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-S5 rwb-asset (Asset)/RWB S5 E4025 CON Accept a bid below the floor with a second signature - contract v1.md`, with the schema and the examples in the service contract folder of RWB-S5-E4025.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Sections and owners of the review.** The document is written in nine parts: the provided operations, the consumed rows, the published and consumed events, the workflow, its activity and the approval child, the schedules, the tables, the fakes, the call-type summary and the lifecycle. Each part is reviewed by the owner of the rows it names, and the tag waits for every reviewer.

**Compatibility check.** The schema is published as JSON Schema with `additionalProperties: false` on the closed objects, and the check runs on three inputs: the previous tag, the new draft and a corpus of recorded answers from the fakes. A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element fails the check and forces a new major version (C1, BR3).

**Open shapes carried into the tag.** Four shapes are carried as placeholders and not invented: the operation names of the rwb-source-data product and of the case-move answer (GAP-2912; ASM-4810), the bid and signature elements (GAP-2913; ASM-4811), the shared round write against the legacy endpoints row (GAP-2914; ASM-4812) and the approval item's create path (GAP-2915; ASM-4813). A placeholder is a declared forthcoming shape, not a permission to guess.

**Done when.** The seven criteria pass, the reviewers of the three consumed owners and of the rounds story have closed their comments, the compatibility check passes on the tag, the fakes are published with their documented answers, and RWB-S5-E4025-APP can start against the tag with no open shape question.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Asset and disposal right calls one of the declared operations | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a declared request is absent or invalid | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-S5-001 | A declared write carries a floor under the approver's limit | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | A declared write carries an appraisal more than a year old | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written, as the decision-record element declares it | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| Document rule | A change fails the compatibility check | A breaking change needs a new major version. |
| Document rule | A consumed row has no published operation name, or an element no column | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2912; ASM-4810). |

The five message IDs are carried from the service and platform sets and are declared only as the envelope rows of the operations in this baseline; the two document rules are checks of this story and are not service messages.

##### 15. Screens and states

The baseline serves SCR-23 Listing and price and SCR-21 Asset list through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). What this story fixes is the element list of the declared responses and the empty, loading, refused, conflict, below-floor, second-signature, at-floor and stale states the route can show from this service's answers and from the approval state. The route itself, its merge order and its field list are RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the screens' transitions are the application, pricing and rounds stories'.

No screen is built here, no component is delivered and no state machine is declared: the screen section of a contract story lists the elements the screens read and the states their answers can carry.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the baseline: the floor, the approver's limit, the two clocks, the codes and every threshold are referenced with their identifier and version, never enumerated as a constant or a default.
- No personal data in any element, fake, example or log: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the baseline declares no `v_ace_*` element and no ACE table, and the appraisal and asset facts appear only as the rwb-source-data data product (DP-05).
- The case stays with rwb-case, the rules, the approval and the DoA stay with rwb-decision, and the limits with rwb-access: no `recovery_case` element, no rule row, no approval table and no delegation row is declared as this service's own.
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; no document, module or test names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no monolith base `/api/recovery/v1`, no shared job table, no Schedule for the approval clock, no event published or consumed by this step.
- Additive only: a breaking change needs a new major version and a re-tag, and the code never moves ahead of the document (BR3).
