| DF-ACE-208 to DF-ACE-219 | `v_ace_npa_asset` (P1) | asset_ref, asset_key, transfer_in_type, from_segment, book_value and 7 more | Not read: rwb-source-data contract |
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case (P3) | id, case_no, status, stage_code and 19 more | Not read: rwb-case contract |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | rule_row (P7) | rule_id, rule_version, route_set, from_state, event_code and 10 more | Not read or written: rwb-decision |

Field IDs follow TSD S5 T3.1 and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. **No new table, no column, no migration**: the tables come with the DB story, and `decision_record` and `idempotency_key` are library objects in `rwb_asset` (DP-03). **No personal data**: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version only; every fixture is synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the behaviour behind the shapes of RWB-S5-E4026-CON.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated (API-S5-001) | Asset and disposal, R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out with the listing, the round number, its price and the floor (API-S5-002) | Asset and disposal, R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetKey}` | The same answer on the business key of the Ownership Map | Asset and disposal, R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/assets/{assetId}/listings` | The next round and its price, the floor, the reserve and the step schedule in; the listing and round out (API-S5-004) | Asset and disposal, C, scope applied | Idempotency-Key |
| POST | `/assets/{assetKey}/listings` | The same write on the business key | Asset and disposal, C, scope applied | Idempotency-Key |

The listings write is shared with the pricing story (FEAT-AST-11) and the ladder story (RWB-S5-E4022) and no source splits it (GAP-2919; ASM-4817). `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds` (API-S5-005) is the rounds story's and is not declared here. Errors: 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409 for a listing in the wrong state, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 or MSG-S5-001, 503.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Asset and valuation product (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2921; ASM-4819)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | Asset class, title status, appraised value and book value with the freshness stamp; faked |
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case state the rules check; faked |
| Case-move answer (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2921; ASM-4819)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | `ROUND_OPEN` and `FLOOR_APPROVED` with the rule and its version; faked |

One hop, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). They are class C rows the plan does not carry, the C row of this slice being None (GAP-2921).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is the take-on story's and the sale event the sale story's; a re-listed round writes no outbox row and adds nothing to `rwb.asset.events.v1`. The re-published price reaches the auction portals through FEAT-AST-12, which no operation covers today (GAP-2922). A build that publishes here fails the absence test.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The round-close fact and the floor approval are signals of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`: no subscription, no consumer group, no inbox row.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one per case per stage, continues-as-new | `rwb-asset` in `rwb-recovery` | Input: case, route, asset, listing, package in force; signals: round-close fact, floor approval |
| `relistOnNoBid` | Activity, the no-bid re-list | `rwb-asset` | Case, listing and round in; rule ID with version, price and round before and after, case move out, one transaction |
| `fixFloorAsReserve` | Activity, the floor approval | `rwb-asset` | Case, listing and approval fact in; reserve, asset-class step schedule, case move out, one transaction |

No child workflow and no second queue. The two activity names are design choices of this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. R-DIS-38 runs "per schedule" as a durable timer inside the workflow; the step owns no Temporal Schedule and no Quartz job. The service's single Schedule is JOB-19, the re-appraisal story's.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| listing | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The listing; this story writes the next round, its price, the floor, the reserve and the step schedule |
| asset | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | Read only here |
| decision_record | PLT library in `rwb_asset` | One record per outcome (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated signal or request |

Not owned and never read as a table: `asset_sale` (the sale story's), `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task`, `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row`, `approval` (P7), `valuation` (S1), `document` (P5), `deviation` (S8), every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-source-data product fake | Asset `AST-2026-000526` with its class and title status and the appraisal value and date; an old appraisal; a stale product; no answer inside 2 s | AC1, AC3, X5 to X7 |
| rwb-case state fake | `ROUND_OPEN` and `PRICE_PROPOSED`; a case in another state | AC1 to AC3, X3 |
| rwb-case move fake | The two answers accepted; an answer refused for an unexpected state | AC2, AC3 |
| rwb-decision package fake | The DISPOSAL package at its version with the two rules | AC1 to AC3 |
| Decision-record stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | AC4, X1 |
| Composite route fake | The merged SCR-23 and SCR-21 answer for `RC-2026-000526` | AC1 |
| Ladder and re-list data fake | A round price above the floor, one at the floor and one under the approver's limit (MSG-S5-001) | AC2, X4 |

The fakes are test-only; the placeholder rows carry their gap until their owners confirm the names (GAP-2921).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 5 provided, 3 consumed | The asset reads and the listings write on `/api/recovery/asset/v1`; the product read, the case state read and the case-move answers; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | The round-close fact and the floor approval are workflow signals |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 2 activities | `AssetDisposalWorkflow`, `relistOnNoBid` and `fixFloorAsReserve` on `rwb-asset`; no Schedule |
| File | None | The portal and HOME.SCB publication is FEAT-AST-12's (GAP-2922) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset.relist`; front end `src/modules/recovery/asset/AssetRelist.tsx`, read only.

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is a prohibition; DP-03 is the transaction rule of both activities; DP-13 moves the base; DP-19 is how the screens reach the service. The consumed rows are built on documents and fakes on Day 1 (GAP-2921) and the package is loaded through the service template without the DP-04 row (GAP-2924).

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| No-bid edge of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow | Waits on the timer and signals, loads the package in force, reports to the parent |
| `relistOnNoBid` | Activity | Read, evaluate R-DIS-38, write the next round, answer |
| `fixFloorAsReserve` | Activity | Read, evaluate R-DIS-29, write the reserve and the schedule, answer |
| `RelistEvaluator` / `FloorReserveEvaluator` | Services | R-DIS-38 on bid count, round price and floor; R-DIS-29 on the approval and the asset class |
| `AssetDecisionRecordWriter` | Library adapter | One hash-linked record per outcome before any change (DP-03) |
| `ListingWriter` | Repository | `listing` in one transaction with the idempotency row and the lock |
| `CaseMoveAnswer`, `CaseStateClient`, `SourceDataProductClient` | Clients | The two answers and the two reads, one hop, 2 s |
| `AssetController` | Controller | The reads and the write, rights, key and the 400/401/403/404/409/422/503 map |
| `AssetRelist` | React component | The next round, its price, the reserve and the step schedule on SCR-23 |

**Database.** No Flyway file: tables from the DB story, library objects from the library's migration, no column for the re-list count (GAP-2920).

**Configuration.** The ladder, its step and unit, the asset-class step schedule and the `LOV-*` lists at their version; the DISPOSAL package from rwb-decision; the capability rows from rwb-access; the flag and the 2 s budget as platform configuration (ADR-020).

**Build steps.** (1) the no-bid edge and its input record; (2) `RelistEvaluator` with the floor and no-fire paths (AC2, X3, X4); (3) `FloorReserveEvaluator` with the age path (AC3, X7); (4) the clients against their fakes (AC1, AC3, X5, X6); (5) the record writer against the stub (AC4, X1); (6) `ListingWriter` (AC2, X8); (7) `CaseMoveAnswer` (AC2, AC3); (8) `AssetController` (AC1); (9) the screen fragment (AC1); (10) the boundary test (X9, BR6, BR7).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.asset.relist-no-bid-v1`; off means the signal is held, nothing is written and no answer is sent.

**Done when.** §16 passes, a closed round re-lists at the next price and answers `ROUND_OPEN` in SIT, an approved floor answers `FLOOR_APPROVED`, a price at the floor re-lists nothing, a repeat writes once, a forced record failure changes nothing, no case row and no `v_ace_*` read exists, and the screens answer through the composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S5-001 | A floor under the approver's limit on the floor write (X4) | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | An appraisal more than a year old at the floor write (X7) | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request or signal is absent or invalid (X3) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right reads or writes (X2) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record cannot be written before the listing changes (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE product is stale after a late or failed batch (X6) | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The six IDs are the legacy and platform sets, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and none is added.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-23 Listing and price (draft, below limit, approved, published) and SCR-21 Asset list (loading, list) are served through the gateway-bff route (DP-19), which calls rwb-asset for the asset, the listing, the round number and price, the floor and the reserve, rwb-case for the state and rwb-source-data for the appraisal. This story fixes the rwb-asset answers only; the route and field list are RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

The states it produces are the re-listed round of SCR-23 — next round number, its price, the reserve and the step schedule — and the refusal, not-recorded, at-floor, old-appraisal and stale states with MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003, MSG-S5-001, MSG-S5-002 and MSG-P1-001. Draft, below-limit and published are the pricing and publication stories'.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the ladder, the asset-class schedule, the floor rule and the appraisal test stay reference data or rule rows with a version.
- No personal data in the schema, a workflow input or a log; every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: no `v_ace_*` grant, no ACE read (DP-05).
- The case stays with rwb-case: no `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task` or `timer` row here (BR4).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element returns: no shared job table, no Quartz row, no monolith base.
- The record precedes the change and the repeated signal is deduped (DP-03, BR8).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract slice of RWB-E4-027, the baseline the payment branch of rwb-asset builds against on Day 1. The baseline declares the two asset reads that carry the sale, the award and the term to SCR-22 and SCR-21 on `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13), the four consumed rows — the rwb-case state read, the case-move answer and the rwb-payment payment fact on its queue and its event on `rwb.payment.events.v1` (DP-05, DP-09) — the decision-record element of DP-03, the rule-package element the branch evaluates, the rights and the error envelope, and the fakes. No event is published, because the owned event of the service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn`. No source names an element for the award, its payment due date, the received-at time, the buyer or the term (GAP-2925; ASM-4822); the term rules sit across this story and RWB-S5-E4024-APP (GAP-2926; ASM-4823); AC2 and AC3 name rules of other features (GAP-2927; ASM-4824); no requirement row names the term (GAP-2928; ASM-4825); no source publishes the names of the consumed rows or of the payment event (GAP-2929; ASM-4826); and the package is declared without the DP-04 platform row (GAP-2930; ASM-4827). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the five-day payment-term capability of rwb-asset — the asset reads that carry the sale and the term, the consumed rows of rwb-case and rwb-payment, the decision-record and rule-package elements, the rights, the error envelope and the fakes — baselined and tagged before the build starts**, so that **the application story and every consumer of a sale can build and test on Day 1 against one fixed, versioned surface instead of guessing the shape of a neighbour's answer**.

This is the contract slice of legacy RWB-E4-027. It owns:

- the document that fixes the two asset reads on base `/api/recovery/asset/v1`, with their parameters, their documented answer, their rights and their idempotency (DP-13);
- the four consumed rows: the rwb-case case state read and case-move answer, the rwb-payment payment fact and the rwb-payment payment event, each with its owner, its use and its placeholder where the name is not published (DP-05, DP-09);
- the decision-record element and the local library dependency that carries it (DP-03);
- the rule-package element: the DISPOSAL package, its version and the four rules this branch evaluates, declared as a reference and not as a rule table of this service;
- the capability area, the rights and the error envelope of the operations it declares;
- the fakes and their documented answers, so that every downstream answer has a stub on Day 1;
- the naming and boundary rules of the baseline: one base, one topic, one queue, no foreign schema, no monolith base, no Schedule for a term that is a workflow timer.

It does not own: the term behaviour, the rule evaluation, the sale write, the decision records and the case moves, which are RWB-S5-E4027-APP; the award cancellation, the vendor score and the reopened round, which are RWB-S5-E4024-APP; the agreed sale and the bid acceptance, FEAT-AST-16's story; the title transfer, FEAT-AST-19 and FEAT-AST-20's stories; the payment and its posting, rwb-payment's (P8); the case of record, rwb-case's (P3); the rule package, rwb-decision's (P7); the screen field list and the composite route, which are RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19).

##### 2. Business rationale

A contract baseline is what lets the stories of one wave build at once. Without it the term would be written against whatever payment answer the service happened to receive that week, and the first integration would find the mismatches instead of the review. With it, the application story builds on Day 1 against a tagged document and its fakes, the rounds and title-transfer stories know what the sale record must carry for the term to run, and the consumers of the asset reads know exactly which elements they can rely on.

The three rules the baseline applies:

- **the owner publishes, the consumer adapts.** Every consumed row names its owner and its use, and where the source documents do not publish a name the row carries the placeholder rather than an invented path or payload (GAP-2929; ASM-4826).
- **one hop, one budget.** Every consumed row is a single hop or a single activity with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and no chain, which is ADR-020 and is what the application story's exception paths assume.
- **additive only.** The baseline moves forward without breaking: a new optional element is a minor version, and a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version and a new document (C1).

The business outcome the baseline protects is the one FEAT-AST-18 of the FSD names: the winning bidder's payment is tracked against the term and the asset is released if it is missed. The baseline does not state that outcome, and no criterion here asserts a business value.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The Ownership Map rows are in force: S5 owns `GET /assets`, `GET /assets/{assetId}`, `GET /assets/{assetKey}`, `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings`, `POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings` and `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds`; `asset_sale` and `listing` are S5's tables.
- The service naming is fixed: schema `rwb_asset`, login `rwb_asset`, base `/api/recovery/asset/v1`, topic `rwb.asset.events.v1` with `.retry` and `.dlt`, task queue `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset`.
- The published shapes of the declared operations are the API Specification v4: `AssetPage` and `Asset`, the two reads of API-S5-001 and API-S5-002.
- The owned event row of the service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` (TSD S5 T5.3); the assets of this baseline touch none of the events of the service, and the term and the payment arrive as signals and as the P8 event.
- The platform CON stories are published: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for the decision record (DP-03) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the composite route (DP-19). DP-04 is not in the pattern set of this slice, so no platform row for the rules kit is claimed and the package is referenced as rwb-decision's (GAP-2930; ASM-4827).
- The term elements — the award, the due date, the received-at time, the buyer and the term length — have no column in TSD S5 T3.1, so the baseline declares them as open shapes (GAP-2925; ASM-4822).
- No approval is needed to publish a Draft baseline; the document is baselined by this story's own review, and the build waits only for its tag.

##### 4. Flow

1. The author drafts the baseline from the Ownership Map, the TSD S5 T-A.1 operations, the TSD S5 T3.1 tables and the lists of T3.2.
2. Every operation is declared with its method, path, request, documented answer, rights, idempotency and error set.
3. Every consumed row is declared with its owner, its use, its budget and a placeholder where the name is not published.
4. The decision-record element is declared with the library dependency that carries it, and the rule-package element with its owner and its version.
5. The fakes are declared with their documented answers, one per consumed row, one for the composite route and one for the award signal.
6. The schema, the open lists and the closed lists are published, and the compatibility check runs: a breaking change fails the check.
7. The document goes to review as Draft; the reviewers are the owners of the consumed rows and the tech lead of the service.
8. On the review's close the document is tagged and baselined; the application story starts against the tag and the fakes.
9. A defect found in the build that needs a shape change is raised against this document, and the document moves to a new minor or major version; the code never moves ahead of the document.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A consumer asks for a shape the sources do not publish | The row carries the placeholder and the gap; no path is invented and no field is guessed | C2, C4 |
| X2 | A change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element | The compatibility check fails, the version becomes a new major and the document is re-reviewed | C1 |
| X3 | A declared operation reaches another service's data or base | The review refuses the baseline and the boundary test fails the build | C7 |
| X4 | A consumed row has no fake, or its fake has no documented answer | The baseline is not tagged; the application story cannot start | C6 |
| X5 | The rights of an operation are not one of the rows of the access matrix | The operation is not declared and the error set of the operation is incomplete | C5 |
| X6 | An owner changes its documented answer after the tag | The owner publishes a new version, this document follows with a minor or major version, and the application story re-tests against the new fake | X2 |
| X7 | Two documents claim the same path or queue, or a document invents an award element that no table names | The naming rule and the placeholder rule resolve it: the owner in the Ownership Map keeps the path, and the award stays Not specified in the source documents | C2, C7 |
| X8 | The term rule set is claimed twice, by this baseline and by the rounds baseline | The rule rows stay single in the package and each baseline references the same four rows with the same versions | C5, C6 |

X1 to X3 are the paths of an incomplete source, X4 to X6 are the paths of a baseline moving under a build, and X7 and X8 are the naming and rule-ownership boundaries.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs no build, no live service and no approval; starts on Day 1 and is finished before the application story's first line |
| Negotiable | The wording, the order of the sections and the fake data are this story's choice; the paths, the owners, the base, the error set and the element names are fixed by their sources |
| Valuable | The stories of wave 3 build at once against one tagged surface, and the first integration finds behaviour, not shape |
| Estimable | One document, two provided operations, four consumed rows, two library elements, eight fakes and one compatibility check |
| Small | Finished inside a week; the review is the only gate |
| Testable | Every criterion is a document check that runs in the contract test suite, plus the compatibility check on the published schema |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the five-day payment-term capability

  Scenario: C1 The baseline validates and only additive changes pass (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published schema and the open and closed lists of the baseline
    When a change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element
    Then the compatibility check fails and the change needs a new major version
    And a change that adds an optional element passes as a minor version

  Scenario: C2 The term elements and the closed lists are published as declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the baseline document of this story
    When the element list, the required and optional flags and the closed lists of the sale read are read
    Then every element carries its type, its nullability and its source
    And every closed list is referenced with its identifier and its version and is not enumerated in code
    And the award, payment_due_date, payment_received_at, the buyer and the term length carry the placeholder and its gap identifier because no table or request element holds them

  Scenario: C3 The asset reads are declared with their rights and no write is added (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operations the baseline provides on base /api/recovery/asset/v1
    When the method, path, documented answer, right and idempotency of each are read
    Then GET /assets and GET /assets/{assetId} carry the Asset and disposal right R with scope applied and no idempotency
    And the baseline declares no write, because the term starts and is confirmed inside AssetDisposalWorkflow
    And POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations is named as rwb-valuation's and POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds as RWB-S5-E4024's, and neither is declared here

  Scenario: C4 The consumed rows carry their owners, their budgets and their placeholders (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed operation and event tables of the baseline
    When the rows of rwb-case and rwb-payment are read
    Then each row names its owner, its use and its 2 s budget or its consumer group
    And where the name is not published the row carries the placeholder and the gap identifier and no path
    And the payment event row names the topic rwb.payment.events.v1 and the consumer group of this service

  Scenario: C5 The error envelope and the rule ownership are declared per operation (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operations the baseline provides and the rule-package element
    When the error set, the rights and the rule rows of each operation are read
    Then the error set names 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503 in one problem envelope
    And the rule-package element names R-DIS-11, R-DIS-37, R-DIS-47 and R-DIS-48 only, and R-DIS-49 and R-DIS-50 are named as RWB-S5-E4024-APP's
    And the capability area and the right of each operation are the rows of the access matrix

  Scenario: C6 The decision-record, rule-package and fake elements are declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the baseline document
    When the decision-record element, the rule-package element and the fake table are read
    Then the decision-record element names RWB-PLT-E1027-CON as its library and the transaction it joins
    And the rule-package element names the DISPOSAL package, its owner, its version in force and the four rules, and declares no rule row
    And every consumed row has a fake with a documented answer, including the stopped stub, the stale payment fact, the duplicate event and the award signal without its sale date

  Scenario: C7 The naming and the boundary of the baseline hold (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the base, the topic, the queue and the schema of the baseline
    When the document is checked against the naming rule and the ownership map
    Then the base /api/recovery/asset/v1, the queue rwb-asset, the topic rwb.asset.events.v1 and the consumed topic rwb.payment.events.v1 are the only ones declared
    And no foreign schema, no foreign topic as this service's own, no monolith base /api/recovery/v1 and no Schedule for the term timer is declared
    And no event is published by the payment branch
```

The seven criteria are new to this run and are tagged as such: they test the contract deliverable only — the schema, the elements, the lists, the operations, the consumed rows, the rights, the envelope, the two library elements, the fakes and the boundary. No criterion states a business outcome or a business value of the application story, and none asserts that a rule fires, that a payment arrives or that a case moves.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One owner per operation, event and table: the baseline declares only the rows the Ownership Map gives to S5, and names every other row with its owner | Ownership Map; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | A consumed row with no published name carries the placeholder and its gap, and never an invented path or payload | Template and Rules v1 §R9; GAP-2929 |
| BR3 | The baseline is additive: a new optional element is a minor version, and a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version | ADR-020; C1 |
| BR4 | Every consumed row is one hop or one activity with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and no chain | ADR-020 |
| BR5 | No event is published: the owned event is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn`, the take-on story's, and the payment event is consumed, never produced here | TSD S5 T5.3 |
| BR6 | The decision record is written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the caller's transaction before any change, and its element is declared once for the service | DP-03 |
| BR7 | The rule package is referenced, never redefined: the DISPOSAL package, its version and the four rules are rwb-decision's rows and no rule table of this service is declared | DP-04 (not claimed); GAP-2930 |
| BR8 | No business value is declared in the baseline: the term length, the reminder point, the statuses, the codes and the thresholds are referenced with their identifier and version | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s16); legacy Guardrails |
| BR9 | No personal data in any element, fake or example of the baseline; a buyer is a code, never a person | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR10 | The baseline never declares another service's table, operation or topic as its own, and a check fails the build where one names it | DP-01, DP-13, DP-14 |

##### 9. State transitions

The document itself is the object of this section: the lifecycle of the contract baseline.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | The draft is complete | Every operation, row, element, fake and error is declared | Draft |
| Draft | The review is opened | The owners of the consumed rows are named as reviewers | In review |
| In review | The review closes with no open comment | The compatibility check passes | Baselined, tagged for the application story |
| In review | A comment needs a shape change | The change is applied to the draft | Draft |
| Baselined | An additive change is approved | New optional element only, compatibility check passes | Baselined, new minor version |
| Baselined | A breaking change is approved | A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element | Draft of a new major version, and the consumers are notified |
| Baselined | An owner changes its answer | X6 | Draft of a new minor or major version, and the fake is updated |

| Step | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Being authored | A consumed row has no published name | X1 | The row carries the placeholder and the gap and the draft continues |
| In review | A row reaches a foreign schema, base or topic | X3, X7 | The baseline is refused |
| Ready to tag | A consumed row has no fake | X4 | Not tagged, the review reopens |
| Tagged | A rule row is claimed by the rounds baseline too | X8 | The rule set stays single and the reference is recorded, not duplicated |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13). These are the reads that answer SCR-22 and SCR-21 with the sale, the award and the term.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated, with the sale status and the term of each asset (API-S5-001) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out, with its title, its listing, its sale, the award, the due date and the days remaining (API-S5-002) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

No write is declared: the term starts at the award (R-DIS-47) and is confirmed on the payment fact (R-DIS-48) inside `AssetDisposalWorkflow`, so the API surface of the service does not grow for this capability. The legacy Endpoints table names `POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations` (API-S5-003), which is rwb-valuation's under ASM-0043, and `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds` (API-S5-005), which is RWB-S5-E4024's; neither is declared here, and either would need its owner's document before this baseline could carry it.

The error envelope of the declared operations: 400 for a malformed request, 401 for an unauthenticated call, 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope asset, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for an invalid filter and with MSG-S5-001 where an accepted price is under the limit, and 503 when the decision library or a consumed boundary does not answer, in one problem document with a code, a message ID and a correlation reference.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family (read) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference and the case state the rules check before they fire; faked |
| The case-move answer (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2929; ASM-4826)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The answer that carries `AWAITING_PAYMENT`, `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING`, `ASSET_HELD` and `BID_RECEIVED` with the rule version; on the workflow boundary it is the outcome the parent applies; faked |
| The payment-fact activity (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2929; ASM-4826)) | queue `rwb-payment` | P8 rwb-payment | The due date, `payment_received_at` and the freshness stamp, in place of the legacy `v_ace_payment` read (DP-05); faked |

Each row is one hop or one activity, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). Where a name is not published the row carries the placeholder and no path, so the consumer adapts at the tag rather than inventing a surface (BR2).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The owned event row of this service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn`, published by the take-on story when the asset record opens, and the sale event is the sale stories'. This baseline declares neither as its own, adds nothing to `rwb.asset.events.v1`, and the payment branch writes no outbox row: its outward surface is the case-move answer and its own reads.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Topic | Event | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.payment.events.v1` | Payment event (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2929; ASM-4826)) | P8 rwb-payment | One consumer group of this service, deduplicated by event id through the inbox library (DP-09); the event wakes the workflow and is a signal, never the record of truth, which is the fact |

The row is the one subscription Architecture v5 slide 13 gives the S5 row against the P8 column. The baseline declares no other topic, no other consumer group and no outbox row, and a build that subscribes to a topic not listed by Architecture v5 fails the naming check (BR5, DP-14).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, continues-as-new | `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the route, the asset reference, the listing reference, the sale reference and the rule package in force; signals: the award made, the payment received, the payment-term expiry and the rule package in force |
| `startPaymentTerm` | Activity, the term start | `rwb-asset` | The sale, the award and the package in; the rule IDs with their versions, the due date, the holding status and the stage outcome out, in one transaction |
| `confirmSalePayment` | Activity, the confirmation | `rwb-asset` | The payment fact in; the rule IDs with their versions, the confirmation, the title-transfer start and the stage outcome out, in one transaction |

The workflow is the same execution the take-on, holding and sale stories of this service use; this baseline fixes its input and signal elements and the two activities it adds, and it declares no child workflow and no second queue. The activity names are design choices of the application story, and the baseline carries them so that the workflow's history is stable. R-DIS-49 and R-DIS-50 are evaluated by RWB-S5-E4024-APP on this story's expiry signal, so the baseline declares them as another story's rules and not as its own activities (GAP-2926).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The five calendar days run as a durable timer inside the workflow, so the baseline declares no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job for the term. The single Schedule of the service is JOB-19, which the re-appraisal story of this service owns and which is not declared here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| asset_sale | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The sale and the award; the baseline declares the elements of the term against it, not its schema |
| asset | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The holding status while the term runs; declared as an element, not a schema |
| listing | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | Read in this baseline; the reopen is the rounds story's write |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The local decision record of DP-03, declared through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated signal or fact and the answer it holds |

The baseline declares no column, no index and no migration, and it declares no table of another owner: `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task` and `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` and `approval` (P7), the payment and posting tables (P8), `valuation` (S1), `document` (P5), `deviation` (S8), the partner tables (S9) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) are named by their owner and never declared here. No award table exists and none is declared (GAP-2925; ASM-4822).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case case-state and case-move fake | The case states `SALE_AGREED`, `AWAITING_PAYMENT`, `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING`, `WORK_ORDER_OPEN` and `ROUND_OPEN` of the fixture cases; the moves accepted and a move refused for an unexpected state | C3, C4, C6 |
| rwb-payment payment-fact fake | No payment by the due date; a payment received one day early; a payment on the due date; a stale fact with its date; no answer inside 2 s | C4, C6 |
| rwb-payment event fake | The payment event of sale `SL-2026-000527`, a duplicate on the same event id and an event that disagrees with the fact | C4, C6 |
| rwb-decision rule-package fake | The DISPOSAL package at its version in force with the four rules | C5, C6 |
| Decision-record stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | C6 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-22 and SCR-21 answer for case `RC-2026-000527`, with the term read once | C2, C6 |
| Award signal fake | An award with every field, one without the sale date and one repeated on the same key | C2, C6 |
| Sale answer fake | The declared sale answer with its mandatory dates and price, and one with the term values absent | C2, C3 |

Each fake answers only what its owner documents, and a fake that answers more than the document fails the review. The names that are not published are stubbed from the documents and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-2929; ASM-4826).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 2 consumed | The two asset reads on `/api/recovery/asset/v1`; the rwb-case state read and the case-move answer; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 1 consumed | `rwb.payment.events.v1`, one consumer group, read as a signal through the inbox library (DP-09) |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 2 activities | `AssetDisposalWorkflow`, `startPaymentTerm` and `confirmSalePayment` on `rwb-asset`; the payment fact on its owner's queue; no Schedule |
| File | None | No file element is declared; the portal publication is FEAT-AST-12's |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Document.** `04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-S5 rwb-asset (Asset)/RWB S5 E4027 CON Enforce the five-day payment term - contract v1.md`, with the schema and the examples in the service contract folder of RWB-S5-E4027.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-09 is applied through the service template — the inbox library and the consumer group — and it is not converted into a platform row here, because the outbox and inbox library comes with the template.

**Sections and owners of the review.** The document is written in nine parts: the provided operations, the consumed rows, the published and consumed events, the workflow and its activities, the schedules, the tables, the fakes, the call-type summary and the lifecycle. Each part is reviewed by the owner of the rows it names, and the tag waits for every reviewer.

**Compatibility check.** The schema is published as JSON Schema with `additionalProperties: false` on the closed objects, and the check runs on three inputs: the previous tag, the new draft and a corpus of recorded answers from the fakes. A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element fails the check and forces a new major version (C1, BR3).

**Open shapes carried into the tag.** Three shapes are carried as placeholders and not invented: the award and its term (GAP-2925; ASM-4822), the names of the consumed rows and of the payment event (GAP-2929; ASM-4826) and the rule references of the rounds story (GAP-2926; ASM-4823). A placeholder is a declared forthcoming shape, not a permission to guess.

**Done when.** The seven criteria pass, the reviewers of the two consumed owners have closed their comments, the compatibility check passes on the tag, the fakes are published with their documented answers, and RWB-S5-E4027-APP can start against the tag with no open shape question.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Asset and disposal right calls one of the declared operations | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a declared request is absent or invalid | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-S5-001 | A declared read carries an accepted price under the approver's limit | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | A declared read carries an appraisal more than a year old | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written, as the decision-record element declares it | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The payment fact is stale at the due date | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| Document rule | A change fails the compatibility check | A breaking change needs a new major version. |
| Document rule | A consumed row has no published name | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2929; ASM-4826). |

The six message IDs are carried from the service and platform sets and are declared only as the envelope rows of the operations in this baseline; the two document rules are checks of this story and are not service messages.

##### 15. Screens and states

The baseline serves SCR-22 Asset record and SCR-21 Asset list through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and SCR-24 Auction rounds reads the award from the same answers. What this story fixes is the element list of the declared responses and the empty, loading, refused, invalid-filter, stale-payment and unanswered-fact states the route can show from this service's answers. The route itself, its merge order and its field list are RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the screens' transitions are the application story's.

No screen is built here, no component is delivered and no state machine is declared: the screen section of a contract story lists the elements the screens read and the states their answers can carry.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the baseline: the term length, the reminder point, the statuses, the codes and every threshold are referenced with their identifier and version, never enumerated as a constant or a default.
- No personal data in any element, fake, example or log: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates, a buyer code and a rule version only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the baseline declares no `v_ace_*` element and no ACE table, and the payment appears only as the P8 rows (DP-05).
- The case stays with rwb-case and the rules with rwb-decision: no `recovery_case` element and no rule row is declared as this service's own.
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; no document, module or test names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no monolith base `/api/recovery/v1`, no shared job table, no Schedule for the term timer, no event published by the payment branch.
- Additive only: a breaking change needs a new major version and a re-tag, and the code never moves ahead of the document (BR3).

##### 18. Traceability

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the application slice of RWB-E4-027 for rwb-asset. The four legacy criteria are kept word for word with their origin tag and the six legacy test cases keep their IDs. The payment term becomes the payment branch of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` on queue `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery`: it starts the five-day term at the award (R-DIS-47), confirms the sale on the payment fact and starts the title transfer (R-DIS-48), raises the expiry signal that releases the asset (R-DIS-49 and R-DIS-50 stay the rounds story's), evaluates R-DIS-11 and R-DIS-37 exactly as AC2 and AC3 name them, records each outcome before the row changes (DP-03), answers `AWAITING_PAYMENT` and `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING` to rwb-case, and consumes the rwb-payment fact and event (DP-05). The base becomes `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13) and SCR-22 and SCR-24 read through the gateway-bff route (DP-19). Gaps: no element holds the award, the due date, the received-at time, the buyer or the term (GAP-2925; ASM-4822); the term rules sit across this story and RWB-S5-E4024-APP (GAP-2926; ASM-4823); AC2 and AC3 name rules of other features (GAP-2927; ASM-4824); no requirement row names the term (GAP-2928; ASM-4825); the consumed rows and the payment event carry no published name (GAP-2929; ASM-4826); DP-04 is outside the pattern set (GAP-2930; ASM-4827). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **sale officer**, I want **the Workbench to track the winning bidder's payment against the term and release the asset if it is missed**, so that **assets sell sooner at approved prices** (legacy RWB-E4-027, word for word).

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E4-027. It owns:

- the four legacy criteria with their origin tag, and the rules, messages and screens they depend on;
- the payment-term branch of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` on `rwb-asset`, a child of the case workflow (Architecture v5 slide 13);
- the start of the five-calendar-day term at the award (R-DIS-47) and the durable timer that measures it;
- the confirmation of the sale on the payment fact and the start of the title transfer (R-DIS-48), with the term status the asset record shows;
- the expiry signal that releases the asset to the rounds story: the award cancellation, the vendor score and the reopened round (R-DIS-49, R-DIS-50) are RWB-S5-E4024-APP's steps (GAP-2926; ASM-4823);
- R-DIS-11 and R-DIS-37 exactly as AC2 and AC3 state them, on the DISPOSAL package in force (GAP-2927; ASM-4824);
- the decision record of each outcome before the row changes (DP-03) and the case answers `AWAITING_PAYMENT` and `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING`;
- the consumption of the rwb-payment payment fact and payment event, in place of the legacy `v_ace_payment` read (DP-05) (GAP-2929; ASM-4826);
- the reads of SCR-22 Asset record and SCR-21 Asset list on `/api/recovery/asset/v1` through the gateway-bff route (DP-13, DP-19).

It does not own: the shapes of the reads, the consumed rows and the fakes, which are RWB-S5-E4027-CON; the acceptance of the bid and the agreed sale, which are FEAT-AST-16's story and RWB-S5-E4024; the award cancellation, the vendor score and the reopened round (R-DIS-49, R-DIS-50); the transfer of the vehicle registration and the Land Office transfer, which are FEAT-AST-19 and FEAT-AST-20's stories (R-DIS-51 to R-DIS-53); the proceeds and the shortfall, FEAT-AST-21; the case and its states, rwb-case (P3); the payment, its matching and its posting, rwb-payment (P8); the vendor scorecard, rwb-partner (S9); the rule package, rwb-decision (P7); the composite route, RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the deployment, which is the operations story of this key.

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E4-027 watched the winning bidder's payment after a sale was agreed: the buyer paid inside the term, or the asset was put back on the market. The NPA sales cycle it serves is measured in years and the FSD keeps the behaviour as FEAT-AST-18 in module S5, run unattended on the auction portals, ALS and the general ledger, after the sale is agreed and before the title transfer (FSD S5 A2.18; REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010 name no term) (GAP-2928; ASM-4825).

What D-RCV-60 changes:

- **the clock is Temporal's.** The five calendar days are a durable timer inside `AssetDisposalWorkflow`, not a Quartz job and not a database scan; the timer survives a restart and the workflow continues as new at each stage end (ADR-016).
- **the payment is rwb-payment's (P8).** The legacy `v_ace_payment` and `v_ace_npa_sale` reads leave the service (DP-05): the term records the due date when the award is made, and the payment arrives as the owner's fact and event with a freshness stamp. Only rwb-source-data reads the `recovery.v_ace_*` views (Architecture v5 slide 8).
- **the case stays with rwb-case (P3).** The rules decide and this story **answers** the move; it writes no case row.
- **the decision is recorded first**, one per outcome, in the transaction that changes the sale record — what AC1 asked and AC4 tested.
- **the release is one signal.** The expiry is detected here and executed by RWB-S5-E4024-APP, so no rule row is evaluated twice (GAP-2926; ASM-4823).
- **nothing is published.** EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is the take-on story's and the sale event is the sale stories' (TSD S5 T5.3); §12.3 states the absence and a build that publishes fails it.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S5-E4027-CON tagged: the asset reads, the four consumed rows, the decision-record and rule-package elements, the error set and the fakes.
- `asset_sale`, `listing` and `asset` exist in `rwb_asset` with the TSD S5 T3.1 and T3.0 columns; no column holds the award, the due date, the received-at time, the buyer or the term, and none is added (GAP-2925; ASM-4822).
- The DISPOSAL package is in force with R-DIS-11, R-DIS-37, R-DIS-47 and R-DIS-48 from rwb-decision (P7), loaded through the service template; DP-04 is outside the pattern set (GAP-2930; ASM-4827).
- The term length, the reminder point and the `LOV-HOLDING` and `LOV-LISTING` lists are reference data with their version (TSD S5 T3.2).
- The rwb-case state read and the case-move answers sit behind fakes; their names are not published (GAP-2929; ASM-4826).
- The rwb-payment payment fact activity and the rwb-payment event row are published with a fake, a freshness stamp and a correlation key; their names are not published (GAP-2929).
- The award and the payment-term expiry arrive as signals of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`; the award is raised by the sale step of RWB-S5-E4024 (GAP-2926).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON writes in the caller's transaction (DP-03); RWB-PLT-N001-CON serves the two screens, one hop each (DP-19).
- The service holds its own login on `rwb_asset`, no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-01, DP-05).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft baseline; the contract is tagged when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The sale of asset `AST-2026-000527` is agreed and the award is made; the sale step signals `AssetDisposalWorkflow` with case, asset, listing, sale record and buyer code.
2. The workflow confirms the case state on the rwb-case contract: `SALE_AGREED`.
3. `PaymentTermEvaluator` loads the package in force and evaluates R-DIS-47: from `SALE_AGREED`, on `AWARD_MADE`, the five-day payment term starts and the case moves to `AWAITING_PAYMENT`.
4. The due date is computed from the award date and the term length in reference data, five calendar days; where no column holds it the value is Not specified in the source documents and is held against the sale record (GAP-2925; ASM-4822).
5. `AssetDecisionRecordWriter` writes one record **before any change**, with the rule and the package version; a failed write stops the step (DP-03; AC1, AC4).
6. `SaleTermWriter` writes the award, the due date and the holding status on the sale record and the asset in one transaction with the record and the idempotency row; the asset is shown as under offer while the term runs.
7. `CaseMoveAnswer` answers `AWAITING_PAYMENT` with the sale reference, the due date, the rule and its version; rwb-case writes the case.
8. A durable timer runs to the due date. When the payment fact arrives through R-DIS-48 — `payment_received_at` at or before `payment_due_date` — the sale is confirmed, the title transfer is started, one record is written and the answer carries `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING` (X6).
9. Where the timer fires and the payment fact is absent or shows no payment, the expiry is detected and the case answer carries `PAYMENT_TERM_EXPIRED`; the award cancellation, the vendor score and the reopened round are RWB-S5-E4024-APP's steps (GAP-2926; ASM-4823).
10. AC2's rule R-DIS-11 is evaluated on the same package: from `WORK_ORDER_OPEN`, on `WORK_ACCEPTED` with `sale_officer_accepted = Y`, the invoice is released for payment and the asset returns to hold, and the case moves to `ASSET_HELD`.
11. AC3's rule R-DIS-37 is evaluated on the bid event: from `ROUND_OPEN`, on `BID_PLACED`, the bid is recorded against the round and the asset and the case moves to `BID_RECEIVED`; the rounds story owns the behaviour and this story keeps the state gate the criterion names.
12. A repeated signal, fact or `Idempotency-Key` writes once and is counted; the workflow returns to its durable timer and continues as new at each stage end and at least every 28 days.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The record cannot be written | Nothing written, no move answered, the term not started | MSG-P7-003 | AC4, TC-E4-027-04, -06 |
| X2 | The role lacks the Asset and disposal right | 403 before any read or write | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, TC-E4-027-05 |
| X3 | The case is in another state, or the payment fact arrives after the timer fired | The rule does not fire; nothing written, the state reported | None | AC2, AC3 |
| X4 | A required field of the award signal is absent or invalid | The term does not start; the signal is counted and shown | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X5 | The same signal, fact or key arrives twice | One term, one record, one answer | None | AC1 |
| X6 | The payment fact is stale at the due date | The confirmation is held until the fact is fresh; the data date is shown | MSG-P1-001 | AC1 |
| X7 | The payment event and the payment fact disagree | The fact wins, the event is held for replay and the difference is flagged | None | AC1 |
| X8 | A contract misses 2 s or its breaker is open | Retry on the workflow schedule; 503 in the platform envelope | None | AC1, AC3 |
| X9 | A statement reaches a `v_ace_*` view, `recovery_case` or a foreign schema | The grant refuses it and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | §17, BR6 |

X1 to X3 are the legacy paths on the split, X4 to X8 what the term clock, the payment fact and the boundaries add, and X9 the DP-01 and DP-05 boundary.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Day 1 against the CON baseline and its fakes; no live P1, P3, P8, S9 or P7 |
| Negotiable | Activity name, decision code and outcome shape are ours; rules, messages, screens, rows and reads are fixed |
| Valuable | A sale is paid or released inside five calendar days without a manual chase or a database scan |
| Estimable | One branch, two evaluators, one record per outcome, two row changes, two answers, three clients, one screen fragment |
| Small | Two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion on synthetic cases through the fakes, plus the access, wrong-state, stale-payment, disagreement and failed-record cases |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Enforce the five-day payment term

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-000527" holds asset "AST-2026-000527" in listing "LS-2026-000527" with sale "SL-2026-000527"
    Given the DISPOSAL rule package is in force at its version and carries R-DIS-11, R-DIS-37, R-DIS-47 and R-DIS-48
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 Enforce the five-day payment term (legacy RWB-E4-027 AC1)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case "RC-2026-000527" in state SALE_AGREED with the sale "SL-2026-000527" agreed
    Given the rwb-payment contract mock returns no payment yet for "RC-2026-000527" and its due date five calendar days after the award
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When its trigger arrives
    Then tracks the winning bidder's payment against the term and releases the asset if it is missed
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Rule R-DIS-11 (legacy RWB-E4-027 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case "RC-2026-000528" in state WORK_ORDER_OPEN
    Given a case in state WORK_ORDER_OPEN
    When work accepted
    Then release the invoice for payment and return the asset to hold
    Then the case moves to ASSET_HELD

  Scenario: AC3 Rule R-DIS-37 (legacy RWB-E4-027 AC3)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case "RC-2026-000529" in state ROUND_OPEN
    Given a case in state ROUND_OPEN
    When bid placed
    Then record the bid against the round and the asset
    Then the case moves to BID_RECEIVED

  Scenario: AC4 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E4-027 AC4)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The four criteria are the legacy criteria word for word with the origin tag added: the repeated `Then`, `the action is taken`, `its trigger arrives` and `the decision log cannot be written` stand, and the `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` lines are the only additions. The work happens in three places: rwb-case writes the four moves, rwb-payment answers the fact, and this story starts the term, confirms the payment, detects the expiry, writes the sale record, records and answers. AC1's release is executed by RWB-S5-E4024-APP on this story's expiry signal (GAP-2926). AC2 and AC3 are kept because the legacy story and FSD S5 A2.18 carry R-DIS-11 and R-DIS-37, though both are rules of other features (GAP-2927; ASM-4824).

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-DIS-11 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | WORK_ORDER_OPEN | WORK_ACCEPTED | sale_officer_accepted = Y | Release the invoice for payment and return the asset to hold | ASSET_HELD | Sale officer | Partner Portal, ALS core and GL | 3 working days |
| R-DIS-37 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | ROUND_OPEN | BID_PLACED | Any | Record the bid against the round and the asset | BID_RECEIVED | Workbench | auction portal | None |
| R-DIS-47 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | SALE_AGREED | AWARD_MADE | Any | Start the five-day payment term | AWAITING_PAYMENT | Buyer | auction portal, ALS core and GL | 5 calendar days |
| R-DIS-48 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | AWAITING_PAYMENT | PAYMENT_RECEIVED | payment_received_at at or before payment_due_date | Confirm the sale and start the title transfer | TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING | Sale officer | ALS core and GL | None |

The four rows are copied character for character from the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; their owner column is a business role, so the case stays in these states and moves in rwb-case on this story's answer, while the sale record and the holding status are written here. R-DIS-49 and R-DIS-50 (the cancellation and the reopened round) are RWB-S5-E4024-APP's and are not evaluated here (GAP-2926; ASM-4823). R-DIS-11 and R-DIS-37 are declared once for the service (GAP-2927; ASM-4824).

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The term is this service's: the award, its due date and the received-at time are held against `asset_sale` in `rwb_asset`, and the term length is versioned reference data | Ownership Map; TSD S5 T3.1; GAP-2925 |
| BR2 | The record precedes the change, one per outcome, with the rule and package version; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; AC1, AC4 |
| BR3 | The term length, the reminder point, the holding statuses and the listing statuses are rule rows or reference data with a version, never a constant | TSD S5 T3.2; legacy Guardrails |

| BR5 | The payment fact and the payment event are rwb-payment's; no `v_ace_payment` read and no `v_ace_npa_sale` read here | DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 8 |
| BR6 | The expiry is one signal: the cancellation, the vendor score and the reopened round are RWB-S5-E4024-APP's and no rule row is evaluated twice | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-49, R-DIS-50; GAP-2926 |
| BR7 | No event is published; EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is the take-on story's and the sale event is the sale stories' | TSD S5 T5.3 |

##### 9. State transitions

The case route state is rwb-case's and is applied by the parent `CaseWorkflow` on this story's answer (BR4).

| From (case state) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| SALE_AGREED | `AWARD_MADE` under R-DIS-47 | Any award of the agreed sale | AWAITING_PAYMENT, answer `AWAITING_PAYMENT` |
| AWAITING_PAYMENT | `PAYMENT_RECEIVED` under R-DIS-48 | `payment_received_at` at or before `payment_due_date` | TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING, answer `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING` |
| AWAITING_PAYMENT | `PAYMENT_TERM_EXPIRED` under R-DIS-49 | Payment absent and the due date passed | AWARD_CANCELED, raised as the expiry signal (RWB-S5-E4024-APP writes the move) |
| WORK_ORDER_OPEN | `WORK_ACCEPTED` under R-DIS-11 | `sale_officer_accepted = Y` | ASSET_HELD, answer `ASSET_HELD` |
| ROUND_OPEN | `BID_PLACED` under R-DIS-37 | Any reported bid | BID_RECEIVED, answer `BID_RECEIVED` |
| Any | An unexpected state, a late fact or a repeated signal | X3, X5 | Unchanged |

| `asset_sale` and `asset` view | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sale agreed | The term starts | R-DIS-47 fires | Award, due date and received-at recorded; asset under offer |
| Award, term running | The payment arrives | R-DIS-48 fires | Sale confirmed, title transfer pending |
| Award, term running | The timer fires with no payment | The expiry signal is raised | Unchanged here; the rounds story cancels and reopens (BR6) |
| Any | A duplicate signal, fact or key | X5 | Unchanged |

The holding and listing statuses are the `LOV-HOLDING` and `LOV-LISTING` rows of TSD S5 T3.2; the case states are the DISPOSAL machine's (TSD S5 T4). The award and its cancellation have no dedicated element, which is GAP-2925.

The rights are the rows of the legacy permission table and TSD S5 T6.1, nothing wider. DP-08 is not in the pattern set: the right is declared per operation and the guard is a service-template capability.

| DF-ACE-220 to DF-ACE-230 | `v_ace_npa_sale` (P1) | npa_sale_key, npa_asset_key, contract_date, sale_date, sale_price, transfer_fee and 5 more | Not read: the sale is this service's, the ACE fact is rwb-source-data's |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | rule_row (P7) | id, rule_id, rule_version, route_set, from_state, event_code and 9 more | Not read or written: rwb-decision |

Field IDs follow TSD S5 T3.1 and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. **No new table, no column, no migration**: the tables come with the DB story, and `decision_record` and `idempotency_key` are library objects in `rwb_asset` (DP-03). **No personal data**: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates, a buyer code and a rule version only; every fixture is synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the behaviour behind the shapes of RWB-S5-E4027-CON; it adds no write, because the term starts and is confirmed inside the workflow.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated, with the sale status and the term of each asset (API-S5-001) | Asset and disposal, R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out with title, listing, sale, award, due date and the days remaining (API-S5-002) | Asset and disposal, R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The legacy Endpoints table also names `POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations` (API-S5-003) and `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds` (API-S5-005); neither is this story's — the valuation write is rwb-valuation's under ASM-0043 (DP-11) and the round write and the reopen are RWB-S5-E4024's. Errors: 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 422 with MSG-GEN-001, 503 when a library or a contract does not answer.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case state the rules check before they fire; faked |
| Case-move answer (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2929; ASM-4826)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | `AWAITING_PAYMENT`, `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING`, `ASSET_HELD` and `BID_RECEIVED` with the rule and its version; faked |
| Payment fact activity (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2929; ASM-4826)) | queue `rwb-payment` | P8 rwb-payment | The due date, `payment_received_at` and the freshness stamp, in place of the legacy `v_ace_payment` read (DP-05); faked |
| Sale and award read (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2925; ASM-4822)) | rwb-asset (S5) | S5 | The sale record and the award the term belongs to, where no column names them |

One hop, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The two placed rows are the cross-service rows the plan does not carry, so this story builds on their documents and fakes and its C and I rows are None; the wave 3 harness holds the real journey.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is the take-on story's and the sale event the sale stories'; starting a term, confirming a payment and detecting an expiry write no outbox row and add nothing to `rwb.asset.events.v1`. A build that publishes here fails the absence test.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Topic | Event | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.payment.events.v1` | Payment event (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2929; ASM-4826)), one per matched payment | P8 rwb-payment | Correlates a confirmed payment to the award and wakes the workflow; the row comes from Architecture v5 slide 13, which marks S5 as listening to P8. Consumed through the inbox library (DP-09) with the event as a signal, never as the record of truth |

One consumer group on the owner's topic, deduplicated by event id; where the event and the fact disagree the fact wins (X7). No other subscription is added.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one per case per stage, continues-as-new across the holding | `rwb-asset` in `rwb-recovery` | Input: case, route, asset, listing, sale, package in force; signals: award made, payment received, payment-term expiry, package in force |
| `startPaymentTerm` | Activity, the term start and its record | `rwb-asset` | Sale, award and package in; rule IDs with versions, due date, holding status and case move out, one transaction |
| `confirmSalePayment` | Activity, the confirmation | `rwb-asset` | Payment fact in; rule IDs with versions, confirmation, title-transfer start and case move out, one transaction |

No child workflow and no second queue. The two activity names are design choices of this story; the payment fact runs on the owner's queue.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The five calendar days run as a durable timer inside the workflow, not as a Temporal Schedule and not as a Quartz job. The service's single Schedule is JOB-19, the re-appraisal story's.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| asset_sale | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The sale and the award; this story writes the award, the due date and the confirmation |
| asset | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The holding status while the term runs |
| listing | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | Read only here; the reopen is the rounds story's write |
| decision_record | PLT library in `rwb_asset` | One record per outcome (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated signal or fact |

Not owned and never read as a table: `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task`, `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row`, `approval` (P7), `payment`, `payment_match`, `posting` (P8), `valuation` (S1), `document` (P5), `deviation` (S8), the partner tables (S9), every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No award table exists (GAP-2925). No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case state fake | `SALE_AGREED`, `AWAITING_PAYMENT`, `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING`, `WORK_ORDER_OPEN` and `ROUND_OPEN` for the fixture cases; a case in another state | AC1 to AC3, X3 |
| rwb-case move fake | The four moves accepted; a move refused for an unexpected state | AC1 to AC3 |
| rwb-payment fact fake | No payment by the due date; a payment received one day early; a payment on the due date; a stale fact; no answer inside 2 s | AC1, X6 |
| rwb-payment event fake | The payment event of `SL-2026-000527`; a duplicate event; an event that disagrees with the fact | AC1, X5, X7 |
| rwb-decision package fake | The DISPOSAL package at its version with the four rules | AC1 to AC3 |
| Decision-record stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | AC4, X1 |
| Composite route fake | The merged SCR-22 and SCR-21 answer for `RC-2026-000527` | AC1 |
| Award signal fake | An award with every field; one without the sale date; one repeated on the same key | AC1, X4, X5 |

The fakes are test-only; the placeholder rows carry their gap until their owners confirm the names (GAP-2929; ASM-4826).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 2 consumed | The two asset reads on `/api/recovery/asset/v1`; the case state read and the case-move answer; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 1 consumed | `rwb.payment.events.v1`, one consumer group, read as a signal (DP-09) |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 2 activities owned, 1 consumed | `AssetDisposalWorkflow`, `startPaymentTerm` and `confirmSalePayment` on `rwb-asset`; the payment fact on `rwb-payment`; no Schedule |
| File | None | No file element; the portal publication is FEAT-AST-12's |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset.paymentterm`; front end `src/modules/recovery/asset/PaymentTerm.tsx`, the fragment SCR-22 embeds, read only.

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is a prohibition here: the legacy `v_ace_payment` read leaves the service for the P8 boundary and the `v_ace_npa_sale` read for rwb-source-data, and no `v_ace_*` grant is kept. DP-03 is the transaction rule of both steps, DP-13 moves the base, DP-19 is how the screens reach the service. DP-09 is used without a platform row of its own, because the inbox library comes with the service template. The package in force is loaded through the template without the DP-04 platform row (GAP-2930; ASM-4827).

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` payment branch | Workflow | Waits on the durable timer and the signals, loads the package in force, reports to the parent |
| `startPaymentTerm`, `confirmSalePayment` | Activities | The two steps: read, evaluate, write, answer |
| `PaymentTermEvaluator` | Service | R-DIS-47 and R-DIS-48 on the award, the due date and the payment fact |
| `WorkOrderGateEvaluator`, `BidGateEvaluator` | Service | R-DIS-11 and R-DIS-37 as the state gates AC2 and AC3 name |
| `AssetDecisionRecordWriter` | Library adapter | One hash-linked record per outcome before any change (DP-03) |
| `SaleTermWriter` | Repository | `asset_sale` and `asset` in one transaction with the idempotency row and the lock |
| `CaseMoveAnswer`, `CaseStateClient`, `PaymentFactActivity`, `PaymentEventInbox` | Clients | The four answers, the fact and the one subscription, one hop, 2 s |
| `AssetController` | Controller | The two reads, the rights and the 400/401/403/404/422/503 map |
| `PaymentTerm` | React component | The award, the due date, the days remaining and the result on SCR-22, read only |

**Database.** No Flyway file: tables from the DB story, library objects from the library's migration, no award table and no column added (GAP-2925).

**Configuration.** The term length, the reminder point and the lists at their version (TSD S5 T3.2); the DISPOSAL package and version from rwb-decision; the capability rows from rwb-access; the flag and the 2 s budget as platform configuration (ADR-020).

**Build steps.** (1) the branch and its input record; (2) `PaymentTermEvaluator` with the award and the confirmation paths (AC1); (3) `SaleTermWriter` with the due date and the lock (AC1, X4); (4) the payment fact client against its fake (AC1, X6); (5) the expiry detection and the signal to the rounds story (AC1); (6) the record writer against the stub (AC4, X1); (7) `WorkOrderGateEvaluator` and `BidGateEvaluator` (AC2, AC3); (8) `CaseMoveAnswer` (AC1 to AC3); (9) the inbox and the payment event row (X5, X7); (10) `AssetController` with the rights and the error map (X2); (11) the screen fragment through the route fake; (12) the boundary test (X9, BR5, BR7).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.asset.payment-term-v1`; off means the award keeps the case at `SALE_AGREED`, nothing is written and the timer is not armed.

**Done when.** §16 passes, an award starts the five-day term in SIT, a payment inside the term answers `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING`, an unpaid term raises exactly one expiry signal and the rounds story cancels and reopens, a repeat writes once, a forced record failure changes nothing, no case row and no `v_ace_*` read exists, and the two screens answer through the composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S5-001 | A floor or an accepted price under the approver's limit on the confirmation (X3) | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | An appraisal more than a year old when the term starts (X3) | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request or signal is absent or invalid (X4) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right reads or acts (X2) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record cannot be written before the sale changes (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The payment fact is stale at the due date, under VR-S5-018-1 (X6) | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The five legacy IDs are copied unchanged, no message is reworded and none is added; MSG-P1-001 is the message of VR-S5-018-1 in FSD S5 A2.18.3.1 and the only row this story brings with it.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-22 Asset record (take-on; held; listed; sold) and SCR-21 Asset list (loading; list) are served through the gateway-bff route (DP-19), which calls rwb-asset for the asset, the sale and the term, rwb-case for the state and rwb-payment for the payment. SCR-24 Auction rounds shows the award and its result and is read here, not written. This story fixes the rwb-asset answers only; the route and field list are RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

The states it produces are the term state of SCR-22 — the award, the due date, the days remaining, the confirmation and the expiry signal — and the refusal, not-recorded, wrong-state, stale-payment and disagreement states with MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P1-001 and MSG-S5-001. The take-on and listed states are the earlier stories' of this service.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the term length, the reminder point, the statuses and the thresholds stay reference data or rule rows with a version.
- No personal data in the schema, a workflow input or a log; a buyer is a code and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: no `v_ace_*` grant, no ACE read (DP-05).
- The case stays with rwb-case: no `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task` or `timer` row here (BR4).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element returns: no shared job table, no Quartz row, no monolith base, no data-lake export of a sale.
- The record precedes the change and the repeated signal is deduped (DP-03, BR8); the expiry is one signal, never a second evaluation of R-DIS-49.
