**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract slice of RWB-E4-028, the baseline the title-transfer branch of rwb-asset builds against on Day 1. The baseline declares the two asset reads that answer SCR-21 Asset list and SCR-22 Asset record on `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13), the four consumed rows of rwb-integration (the SCIS transfer, INT-28), rwb-source-data (the asset and sale product, DP-05) and rwb-case (the state read and the move answer), the decision-record element of DP-03, the rule-package element the branch evaluates against, the rights and the error envelope, and the fakes. No event is published and none is consumed, because the owned event of the service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` and the transfer facts are workflow signals. No source gives the SCIS interface a row in TSD S5 T5.1 or a call type, and DP-16 is outside the pattern set (GAP-2931; ASM-4828); the FSD makes the step a system submission while INT-28 has the officer prepare it (GAP-2932; ASM-4829); no element holds the vehicle registration particulars or the submission reference (GAP-2933; ASM-4830); R-DIS-53 has no owning story (GAP-2934; ASM-4831); the rule package is declared without the DP-04 platform row (GAP-2935; ASM-4796); and REQ-S5-008 is claimed twice (GAP-2936; ASM-4832). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the vehicle-registration transfer capability of rwb-asset — its two asset reads, its four consumed rows, its decision-record and rule-package elements, its rights, its error envelope and its fakes — baselined and tagged before the build starts**, so that **the application story and every consumer of a transfer can build and test on Day 1 against one fixed, versioned surface instead of guessing the shape of a neighbour's answer or of an interface no source describes**.

This is the contract slice of legacy RWB-E4-028. It owns:

- the document that fixes the two asset reads on base `/api/recovery/asset/v1`, with their parameters, documented answer, right and idempotency (DP-13);
- the four consumed rows: the rwb-integration SCIS transfer (INT-28), the rwb-source-data asset and sale product, the rwb-case state read and the case-move answer, each with its owner, its use and a placeholder where no name is published (DP-05; GAP-2931);
- the decision-record element and the local library dependency that carries it (DP-03);
- the rule-package element: the DISPOSAL package, its version and R-DIS-51, declared as a reference and not as a rule table of this service;
- the capability area, the right and the error envelope of the operations it declares;
- the fakes and their documented answers, one per consumed row, so that every downstream answer has a stub on Day 1;
- the naming and boundary rules of the baseline: one base, one topic, one queue, no foreign schema, no monolith base, no direct external call and no Schedule for a workflow timer.

It does not own: the branch behaviour, the pack, the submission, the record, the row writes and the case answer, which are RWB-S5-E4028-APP; the payment term and its confirmation, FEAT-AST-18's story; the property transfer at the Land Office, FEAT-AST-20's story; the rejected transfer R-DIS-53, which no story row owns (GAP-2934); the proceeds, FEAT-AST-21; the SCIS adapter itself, rwb-integration (P2); the case, rwb-case (P3); the rules, rwb-decision (P7); the documents, rwb-document (P5); the screen field list and the composite route, which are RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19).

##### 2. Business rationale

A contract baseline is what lets the stories of one wave build at once. Here it matters more than usual, because the SCIS interface has no technical entry: the FSD names SCIS as an integration point of A2.19, INT-28 records it as "Not available today; prepared by the officer", and the TSD S5 T5.1 table does not list it at all. Without a tagged baseline the branch would be written against whatever the adapter happened to answer, and the first integration would find the mismatch instead of the review. With it, the application story builds on Day 1 against a tagged document and its fakes, and rwb-integration, rwb-source-data and rwb-case know exactly which elements the transfer needs.

The three rules the baseline applies:

- **the owner publishes, the consumer adapts.** Every consumed row names its owner and its use, and where no name is published the row carries the placeholder rather than an invented path (GAP-2931; ASM-4828).
- **one hop, one budget.** Every consumed row is a single hop with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and no chain, which is ADR-020 and what the application story's exception paths assume.
- **additive only.** A new optional element is a minor version; a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version and a new document (C1).

The business outcome the baseline protects is the one FEAT-AST-19 of the FSD and BR-029 of the Epic 4 BRD name: the title transfer is prepared and submitted for a vehicle through SCIS. The baseline does not state that outcome, and no criterion here asserts a business value.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The Ownership Map rows are in force: S5 owns `GET /assets`, `GET /assets/{assetId}`, `GET /assets/{assetKey}`, `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings`, `POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings` and `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds`; `asset_sale` and `listing` are S5's tables, and `asset` is the service's ACE extension table of TSD S5 T3.1.
- The service naming is fixed: schema `rwb_asset`, login `rwb_asset`, base `/api/recovery/asset/v1`, topic `rwb.asset.events.v1` with `.retry` and `.dlt`, task queue `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset`.
- The published shapes of the declared operations are the API Specification v4: `AssetPage` and `Asset`.
- The owned event row of the service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` (TSD S5 T5.3); the transfer facts are signals of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`.
- The platform CON stories are published: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for the decision record (DP-03) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the composite route (DP-19). DP-04 is not in the pattern set, so no platform row for the rules kit is claimed (GAP-2935; ASM-4796), and DP-16 is not in it either, so no C row to rwb-integration is claimed (GAP-2931; ASM-4828).
- No approval is needed to publish a Draft baseline; the document is baselined by this story's own review, and the build waits only for its tag.

##### 4. Flow

1. The author drafts the baseline from the Ownership Map, the TSD S5 T-A.1 operations, the TSD S5 T3.1 tables and the lists of T3.2.
2. Every operation is declared with its method, path, documented answer, right, idempotency and error set.
3. Every consumed row is declared with its owner, its use, its budget and a placeholder where no name is published, including the SCIS row that TSD S5 T5.1 omits (GAP-2931; ASM-4828).
4. The decision-record element is declared with the library that carries it, and the rule-package element with its owner and version.
5. The fakes are declared with their documented answers, one per consumed row and one per screen route and pack shape.
6. The schema, the open lists and the closed lists are published, and the compatibility check runs: a breaking change fails it.
7. The document goes to review as Draft; the reviewers are the owners of the consumed rows and the tech lead of the service.
8. On the review's close the document is tagged and baselined; the application story starts against the tag and the fakes.
9. A defect in the build that needs a shape change is raised against this document; the document moves to a new minor or major version and the code never moves ahead of it.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A consumer asks for a shape the sources do not publish | The row carries the placeholder and the gap; no path is invented and no field is guessed | C2, C4 |
| X2 | A change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element | The compatibility check fails, the version becomes a new major and the document is re-reviewed | C1 |
| X3 | A declared operation reaches another service's data or base, or the service calls SCIS directly | The review refuses the baseline and the boundary test fails the build | C7 |
| X4 | A consumed row has no fake, or its fake has no documented answer | The baseline is not tagged; the application story cannot start | C6 |
| X5 | The right of an operation is not one of the rows of the access matrix | The operation is not declared and its error set is incomplete | C3, C5 |
| X6 | An owner changes its documented answer after the tag | The owner publishes a new version, this document follows, and the application story re-tests against the new fake | X2 |
| X7 | Two documents claim the same path or queue, or a document invents a registration element that no table names | The owner in the Ownership Map keeps the path and the placeholder rule resolves the element | C2, C7 |

X1 to X3 are the paths of an incomplete source, X4 to X6 the paths of a baseline moving under a build, and X7 the naming and placeholder boundary.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs no build, no live service and no approval; starts on Day 1 and is finished before the application story's first line |
| Negotiable | The wording, the order and the fake data are this story's choice; the paths, the owners, the base, the error set and the element names are fixed by their sources |
| Valuable | The stories of wave 3 build at once against one tagged surface, and the first integration finds behaviour, not shape |
| Estimable | One document, two provided operations, four consumed rows, two library elements, eight fakes and one compatibility check |
| Small | Finished inside a week; the review is the only gate |
| Testable | Every criterion is a document check in the contract test suite, plus the compatibility check on the published schema |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the vehicle-registration transfer capability

  Scenario: C1 The baseline validates and only additive changes pass (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published schema and the open and closed lists of the baseline
    When a change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element
    Then the compatibility check fails and the change needs a new major version
    And a change that adds an optional element passes as a minor version

  Scenario: C2 The elements and the closed lists are published as declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the baseline document of this story
    When the element list, the required and optional flags and the closed lists are read
    Then every element carries its type, its nullability and its source
    And every closed list is referenced with its identifier and its version and is not enumerated in code
    And the vehicle registration particulars and the submission reference carry the placeholder and the gap identifier because no table or request element holds them

  Scenario: C3 The asset reads are declared with their right and the submission is declared as an activity (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operations the baseline provides on base /api/recovery/asset/v1
    When the method, path, documented answer, right and idempotency of each are read
    Then the two asset reads carry the Asset and disposal right R with scope applied and no idempotency
    And no REST operation is declared for the transfer submission, because the step runs unattended in the workflow
    And GET /assets/{assetKey} and the listings and rounds writes are named as the sibling stories' and are not declared here

  Scenario: C4 The consumed rows carry their owners, their budgets and their placeholders (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed operation table of the baseline
    When the rows of rwb-integration, rwb-source-data and rwb-case are read
    Then each row names its owner, its use and its 2 s budget
    And the SCIS row is declared although TSD S5 T5.1 lists no interface row for it, and its call type is an activity on the owner's queue
    And where no name is published the row carries the placeholder and the gap identifier and no path

  Scenario: C5 The error envelope is declared per operation (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operations the baseline provides
    When the error set and the right of each operation are read
    Then the error set names 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 and 503 in one problem envelope
    And the capability area and the right of each operation are the row of the access matrix

  Scenario: C6 The decision-record, rule-package and fake elements are declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the baseline document
    When the decision-record element, the rule-package element and the fake table are read
    Then the decision-record element names RWB-PLT-E1027-CON as its library and the transaction it joins
    And the rule-package element names the DISPOSAL package, its owner, its version in force and R-DIS-51, and declares no rule row
    And every consumed row has a fake with a documented answer, including the stopped stub, the stale product, the rejected transfer and the unanswered adapter

  Scenario: C7 The naming and the boundary of the baseline hold (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the base, the topic, the queue and the schema of the baseline
    When the document is checked against the naming rule and the ownership map
    Then the base /api/recovery/asset/v1, the queue rwb-asset and the topic rwb.asset.events.v1 are the only ones declared as this service's own
    And no foreign schema, no foreign topic, no monolith base /api/recovery/v1 and no Schedule for the transfer timer is declared
    And no external call to SCIS is declared from this service and no event is published or consumed by the branch
```

The seven criteria are new to this run and are tagged as such: they test the contract deliverable only — the schema, the elements, the lists, the operations, the consumed rows, the right, the envelope, the two library elements, the fakes and the boundary. No criterion states a business outcome, and none asserts that R-DIS-51 fires, that a transfer is accepted or that a case moves.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One owner per operation, event and table: the baseline declares only the rows the Ownership Map gives to S5, and names every other row with its owner | Ownership Map; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | A consumed row with no published name carries the placeholder and its gap, and never an invented path | Template and Rules v1 §R9; GAP-2931 |
| BR3 | The baseline is additive: a new optional element is a minor version; a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version | ADR-020; C1 |
| BR4 | Every consumed row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and no chain; the SCIS row is an activity on the owner's queue | ADR-020; Architecture v5 slide 13 |
| BR5 | No event is published and none is consumed by the branch: the owned event is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn`, the take-on story's, and the transfer facts are workflow signals | TSD S5 T5.3 |
| BR6 | The decision record is written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the caller's transaction before any change, and its element is declared once for the service | DP-03 |
| BR7 | The rule package is referenced, never redefined: the DISPOSAL package, its version and R-DIS-51 are rwb-decision's rows and no rule table of this service is declared | DP-04 (not claimed); GAP-2935 |
| BR8 | The registration particulars and the submission reference are declared only once an owner names them; until then they carry the placeholder | GAP-2933; ASM-4830 |
| BR9 | No personal data in any element, fake or example: a vehicle is a reference and a code, and every fixture is synthetic | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR10 | The baseline never declares another service's table, operation or topic as its own, and no document or test declares a direct SCIS call from this service | DP-01, DP-05, DP-13, DP-14 |

##### 9. State transitions

The document itself is the object of this section: the lifecycle of the contract baseline.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | The draft is complete | Every operation, row, element, fake and error is declared | Draft |
| Draft | The review is opened | The owners of the consumed rows are named as reviewers | In review |
| In review | The review closes with no open comment | The compatibility check passes | Baselined, tagged for the application story |
| In review | A comment needs a shape change | The change is applied to the draft | Draft |
| Baselined | An additive change is approved | New optional element only, compatibility check passes | Baselined, new minor version |
| Baselined | A breaking change is approved | A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element | Draft of a new major version, and the consumers are notified |
| Baselined | An owner changes its answer | X6 | Draft of a new minor or major version, and the fake is updated |

| Step | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Being authored | A consumed row has no published name | X1 | The row carries the placeholder and the gap and the draft continues |
| In review | A row reaches a foreign schema, base or topic, or a direct SCIS call | X3, X7 | The baseline is refused |
| Ready to tag | A consumed row has no fake | X4 | Not tagged, the review reopens |

The baseline declares no new table, no new column and no migration, and it enumerates no business value: every list, code and timer is referenced with its identifier and its version. **No personal data** appears in any element, fake or example; the fixture identifiers are synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13). These are the reads that answer SCR-21 and SCR-22.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated, with the transfer status of each asset (API-S5-001) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out, with its title, its sale, its `holding_status` and its transfer status (API-S5-002) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

`GET /assets/{assetKey}` is the sibling stories' row of the same base, and the writes `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings`, `POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings` and `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds` belong to the pricing and round stories; none is declared here. No REST operation is declared for the transfer submission: the step runs unattended in the workflow and reaches SCIS through rwb-integration (C3, BR4).

The error envelope of the declared operations: 400 for a malformed request, 401 for an unauthenticated call, 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope asset, and 503 when the decision library or a consumed boundary does not answer, in one problem document with a code, a message ID and a correlation reference.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family (read) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference and the case state the rule checks before it fires; faked |
| The case-move answer (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2931; ASM-4828)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | `ASSET_SOLD` with its rule version; on the workflow boundary it is the outcome the parent applies; faked |
| The asset and sale product (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2931; ASM-4828)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The asset, sale and registration facts with their data date, in place of the legacy `v_ace_npa_asset` and `v_ace_npa_sale` reads (DP-05); faked |
| The SCIS transfer (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2931; ASM-4828)) | queue `rwb-integration` | P2 rwb-integration | The transfer pack out and its accepted or rejected answer with the submission reference back (INT-28); faked |

Each row is one hop or one activity, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The SCIS row is an activity on the owner's queue, because a route service reaches a shared capability through Temporal, never REST (Architecture v5 slide 13), and because INT-28 records the interface as not available today (GAP-2931; GAP-2932). Where no name is published the row carries the placeholder and no path, so the consumer adapts at the tag rather than inventing a surface (BR2).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The owned event row of this service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn`, published by the take-on story when the asset record opens. This baseline declares it as no part of its own, adds nothing to `rwb.asset.events.v1`, and the branch writes no outbox row: its outward surface is the case-move answer, its own reads and the consumed adapter (BR5).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The transfer due fact, the payment confirmation and the adapter answer arrive as signals and activity results of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`, so the baseline declares no topic subscription, no consumer group and no inbox row; a build that subscribes to a topic not listed by Architecture v5 fails the naming check (BR5, DP-14).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, continues-as-new | `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the route, the asset reference, the sale reference and the rule package in force; signals: the transfer due fact, the payment confirmation, the adapter answer and the rule package in force |
| `submitRegistrationTransfer` | Activity, the pack, the submission and the write | `rwb-asset` | The asset, the sale and the case in; the rule ID with its version, `holding_status`, the transfer status, the submission reference and the stage outcome out, in one transaction |
| The SCIS transfer activity (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2931; ASM-4828)) | Activity, consumed | `rwb-integration` | The pack in; the accepted or rejected answer with its submission reference out (INT-28) |

The workflow is the same execution the take-on, holding and sale stories of this service use; this baseline fixes its input and signal elements and the one activity it adds, and declares no child workflow and no second queue. The activity names are design choices of the application story, carried here so that the workflow history is stable.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The 5 working days of R-DIS-51 run as a durable timer inside the workflow, so the baseline declares no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job for the transfer. The single Schedule of the service is JOB-19, the re-appraisal story's, and it is not declared here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| asset | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The asset record; the baseline declares the elements of `holding_status` and the transfer pack, not its schema |
| asset_sale | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The sale; the baseline declares the elements the pack reads and the transfer status, not its schema |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The local decision record of DP-03, declared through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated signal and the answer it holds |

The baseline declares no column, no index and no migration, and it declares no table of another owner: `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task` and `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` and `approval` (P7), `listing` (S5 but the sibling stories'), `document` and `document_custody` (P5), `proceeds` (P8), `deviation` (S8) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) are named by their owner and never declared here. No element holds the registration particulars or the submission reference and none is declared (GAP-2933; ASM-4830).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case case-state and case-move fake | `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING` for the fixture cases; the move accepted and a move refused for an unexpected state | C3, C4, C6 |
| rwb-source-data product fake | Vehicle asset `AST-2026-000541` with its sale at today's date; a stale product with its date; a property asset; no answer inside 2 s | C2, C4, C6 |
| SCIS transfer fake (INT-28) | Accepted with a submission reference; rejected with its reason; unavailable, as INT-28 records the interface today; no answer inside 2 s | C4, C6 |
| rwb-decision rule-package fake | The DISPOSAL package at its version in force with R-DIS-51 | C6 |
| Decision-record stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | C6 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-21 and SCR-22 answer for case `RC-2026-000541`, with the transfer status read once | C2, C6 |
| Pack fake | A pack built from a vehicle asset and its sale, and the same pack with a required element absent and with the particulars absent | C2, C3 |
| Read fake | An asset page and an asset answer, and one of each of `404` and `403` | C3, C5 |

Each fake answers only what its owner documents, and a fake that answers more than the document fails the review. The names that are not published are stubbed from the documents and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-2931; ASM-4828).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 3 consumed | The two asset reads on `/api/recovery/asset/v1`; the case state read, the case-move answer and the source-data product; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | The transfer facts are workflow signals; nothing is published |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 2 activities | `AssetDisposalWorkflow` and `submitRegistrationTransfer` on `rwb-asset`; the SCIS transfer activity on `rwb-integration`; no Schedule |
| File | None | INT-28 names no file and no API approach, and the baseline declares neither (GAP-2931) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Document.** `04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-S5 rwb-asset (Asset)/RWB S5 E4028 CON Transfer vehicle registration - contract v1.md`, with the schema and the examples in the service contract folder of RWB-S5-E4028.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Sections and owners of the review.** The document is written in nine parts: the provided operations, the consumed rows, the published and consumed events, the workflow and its activities, the schedules, the tables, the fakes, the call-type summary and the lifecycle. Each part is reviewed by the owner of the rows it names, and the tag waits for every reviewer.

**Compatibility check.** The schema is published as JSON Schema with `additionalProperties: false` on the closed objects, and the check runs on three inputs: the previous tag, the new draft and a corpus of recorded answers from the fakes. A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element fails the check and forces a new major version (C1, BR3).

**Open shapes carried into the tag.** Three shapes are carried as placeholders and not invented: the names and peculiarities of the four consumed rows (GAP-2931; ASM-4828), whether the submission is automatic or officer-prepared (GAP-2932; ASM-4829) and the registration particulars with the submission reference (GAP-2933; ASM-4830). A placeholder is a declared forthcoming shape, not permission to guess.

**Done when.** The seven criteria pass, the reviewers of the three consumed owners have closed their comments, the compatibility check passes on the tag, the fakes are published with their documented answers, and RWB-S5-E4028-APP can start against the tag with no open shape question.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Asset and disposal right calls one of the declared operations | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a declared request or of the pack is absent or invalid | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The consumed asset and sale product is stale at the tag | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written, as the decision-record element declares it | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-S5-001 | A declared read carries a floor under the approver's limit | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | A declared read carries an appraisal more than a year old | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |
| Document rule | A change fails the compatibility check | A breaking change needs a new major version. |
| Document rule | A consumed row has no published name | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2931; ASM-4828). |

The six message IDs are carried from the service and platform sets and are declared only as the envelope rows of the operations in this baseline; the two document rules are checks of this story and are not service messages. No message exists for a rejected transfer at this level (GAP-2934).

##### 15. Screens and states

The baseline serves SCR-21 Asset list and SCR-22 Asset record through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). What this story fixes is the element list of the declared responses and the empty, loading, refused, not-found, stale and rejected states the route can show from this service's answers. The route itself, its merge order and its field list are RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the screens' transitions are the application story's.

No screen is built here, no component is delivered and no state machine is declared: the screen section of a contract story lists the elements the screens read and the states their answers can carry.

The five legacy case IDs are mapped onto this contract deliverable in their legacy order, and their `Covers` names the criterion of this story that fixes the surface each legacy case touches: the asset elements and the reads (01), the consumed rows (02), the error path (03), the right (04) and the boundary (05); the legacy case 05, a forced record failure, is covered by the decision-record element of C6 and TC-S5-E4028-CON-02. The four `TC-S5-E4028-CON-` cases are new and test the parts of the baseline that no legacy case touches: the registration placeholder, the fakes, the compatibility check and the absence of an event. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID; the `-ITG` copies belong to the wave 3 harness.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the baseline: the 5 working days, the asset type, the transfer-in type and the statuses are referenced with their identifier and version, never enumerated as a constant or a default.
- No personal data in any element, fake, example or log: a vehicle reference, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the baseline declares no `v_ace_*` element and no ACE table, and the asset and sale facts appear only as the P1 row (DP-05).
- The case stays with rwb-case and the rules with rwb-decision: no `recovery_case` element and no rule row is declared as this service's own.
- No direct external call: the SCIS submission appears only as the P2 row, and a document or a test that declares a SCIS client in this service fails the boundary check (BR10).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; no document, module or test names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no monolith base `/api/recovery/v1`, no shared job table, no Schedule for the transfer timer, no event published or consumed by this branch.
- Additive only: a breaking change needs a new major version and a re-tag, and the code never moves ahead of the document (BR3).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the application slice of RWB-E4-028 for rwb-asset. The three legacy criteria are kept word for word with their origin tag and the five legacy test cases keep their IDs. The transfer becomes the title-transfer branch of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` on queue `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery`: from `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING` it prepares the transfer pack from the asset, the sale and the registration facts, submits it through the adapter that fronts SCIS (INT-28), evaluates R-DIS-51 on the DISPOSAL package in force, records the outcome before the row changes (DP-03), answers `ASSET_SOLD` to rwb-case and publishes nothing. The legacy `v_ace_npa_asset` and `v_ace_npa_sale` reads leave the service for the rwb-source-data data-product contract (DP-05), the base becomes `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13) and SCR-21 and SCR-22 read through the gateway-bff route (DP-19). Gaps: no interface row or call type for SCIS, and DP-16 outside the pattern set (GAP-2931; ASM-4828); the FSD submits while INT-28 says the officer prepares it (GAP-2932; ASM-4829); no element holds the registration particulars or the submission reference (GAP-2933; ASM-4830); R-DIS-53 has no owning story (GAP-2934; ASM-4831); the package load without the DP-04 platform row (GAP-2935; ASM-4796); REQ-S5-008 is claimed twice (GAP-2936; ASM-4832). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **sale officer**, I want **the Workbench to prepare and submits the registration transfer through SCIS**, so that **assets sell sooner at approved prices** (legacy RWB-E4-028, word for word).

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E4-028. It owns:

- the three legacy criteria with their origin tag, and the rule, messages and screens they depend on;
- the title-transfer branch of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` on `rwb-asset`, a child of the case workflow (Architecture v5 slide 13): from `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING`, on `REGISTRATION_TRANSFERRED`, under R-DIS-51 and `asset_type = vehicle`, to `ASSET_SOLD`;
- the preparation of the transfer pack from the asset, the sale and the registration facts, and its submission through the adapter that fronts SCIS (INT-28) — the adapter row is stubbed and faked on Day 1 (GAP-2931; ASM-4828);
- the decision record of the submission and its answer **before** the `asset` and `asset_sale` rows change (DP-03);
- the write of `holding_status` on `asset` and of the transfer status on the sale in `rwb_asset`;
- the case answer `ASSET_SOLD` to rwb-case, with the rule and its version;
- the reads behind SCR-21 and SCR-22 on `/api/recovery/asset/v1` through the gateway-bff route (DP-13, DP-19).

It does not own: the shape of the pack, the reads, the consumed rows, the decision-record and rule-package elements, the error set and the fakes, which are RWB-S5-E4028-CON; the five-day payment term and its confirmation, FEAT-AST-18's story; the property transfer at the Land Office (R-DIS-52), FEAT-AST-20's story; the rejected transfer (R-DIS-53), which no story row of the split owns (GAP-2934; ASM-4831); the proceeds and the shortfall, FEAT-AST-21; the documents and their custody, rwb-document (P5); the case and its states, rwb-case (P3); the rules and their package, rwb-decision (P7); the SCIS adapter itself, rwb-integration (P2); the deployment, the flag and the runbook, the operations story of this key.

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E4-028 closed the sale of a vehicle: once the buyer had paid, the bank could not call the asset sold until the registration book had changed hands at the Department of Land Transport through SCIS, and the case waited on an officer's errand. The FSD keeps it as FEAT-AST-19 in module S5, run by the system, between FEAT-AST-18, which confirms the payment under R-DIS-48 (into `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING`), and FEAT-AST-21, which applies the proceeds under R-DIS-54 (out of `ASSET_SOLD`). BR-029 of the Epic 4 BRD states the outcome: the title transfer is prepared and submitted for a vehicle through SCIS and recorded for a property at the Land Office.

What D-RCV-60 changes:

- **the transfer state is this service's.** `asset` and `asset_sale` are S5's tables in `rwb_asset`; `holding_status` carries `SOLD` and the sale carries its transfer status (Ownership Map; TSD S5 T3.1, `LOV-HOLDING`).
- **SCIS is a boundary, not a read.** The legacy data table read `v_ace_npa_asset` and `v_ace_npa_sale`; under DP-05 those facts arrive on the rwb-source-data data-product contract, and the submission leaves through rwb-integration (INT-28). Neither interface publishes an operation name or an approach, so both rows carry the placeholder and a fake (GAP-2931; ASM-4828).
- **the decision is recorded first**, once per submission, in the row's transaction — what AC1 asked and AC3 tested.
- **nothing is published.** EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is the take-on story's (TSD S5 T5.3); §12.3 states the absence and a build that adds an event fails it.

The timer the rule row names — 5 working days — is the transfer clock; it stays a rule-row value and is never a constant (BR3).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S5-E4028-CON tagged: the two reads, the four consumed rows, the decision-record element, the rule-package element, the error set and the fakes.
- `asset` exists in `rwb_asset` with DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042 and `asset_sale` with DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019 (TSD S5 T3.1), plus the standard columns of T3.0; no column is added (GAP-2933; ASM-4830).
- The case is in `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING`, written by rwb-case on FEAT-AST-18's answer under R-DIS-48; the asset carries `asset_type = VEHICLE` from `LOV-ASSET-TYPE` and `holding_status` from `LOV-HOLDING`.
- The DISPOSAL package is in force at its version and carries R-DIS-51, loaded through the service template; DP-04 is outside the pattern set of this slice (GAP-2935; ASM-4796).
- The SCIS adapter row (INT-28) and the rwb-source-data product are answered by their fakes; neither operation name is published (GAP-2931; ASM-4828).
- The transfer due fact, the payment confirmation and the adapter answer arrive as signals and activity results of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`; no subscription is added.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON writes in the caller's transaction (DP-03); RWB-PLT-N001-CON serves the two screens, one hop each (DP-19).
- The service holds its own login on `rwb_asset`, no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-01, DP-05).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft baseline; the contract is tagged when its tests pass (ASM-4829).

##### 4. Flow

1. The buyer's payment is confirmed and R-DIS-48 moves the case to `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING`; the running `AssetDisposalWorkflow` enters its title-transfer branch on the durable timer of the rule row (5 working days).
2. `TitleTransferEvaluator` reads the case state on the rwb-case contract and the asset and sale facts on the rwb-source-data contract, with their data date; a stale product is refused (X5).
3. It confirms `asset_type = VEHICLE` from `LOV-ASSET-TYPE`; a property or another type is not this branch's and is answered as out of scope (X3).
4. `RegistrationPackBuilder` assembles the pack from `asset_ref`, `asset_code`, `asset_type`, `transfer_in_type`, the sale dates, the sale price and the transfer fee; the registration particulars of the vehicle and the submission reference are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2933; ASM-4830).
5. `submitRegistrationTransfer` submits the pack through the adapter that fronts SCIS (INT-28) as an activity on the owner's queue; where the interface answers "not available", the officer's submission is recorded instead of an automatic one (GAP-2932; ASM-4829).
6. `AssetDecisionRecordWriter` writes one record **before any change**, with the rule id, the rule version and the package version; a failed write stops the step (DP-03; AC1, AC3).
7. `TitleTransferWriter` writes `holding_status` = `SOLD` on `asset` and the transfer status on the sale in one `rwb_asset` transaction with the record and the idempotency row.
8. `CaseMoveAnswer` answers `ASSET_SOLD` with the rule and its version; rwb-case writes the case state, and the workflow records the stage outcome for its parent.
9. R-DIS-51's condition holds, so the branch ends: the workflow returns to the parent and the stage closes; the proceeds step of FEAT-AST-21 is started by the parent, not here.
10. An adapter answer that rejects the transfer moves nothing: the step holds, the pack and the answer are recorded, and R-DIS-53's `TITLE_BLOCKED` is not taken here because no story row owns it (GAP-2934; ASM-4831) — the branch fails closed and raises an alert.
11. A repeated signal or key writes once and is counted; the workflow continues-as-new at each stage end and at least every 28 days.
12. Nothing is published: no outbox row, no topic write, no consumer group (BR7, §12.3).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The record cannot be written | Nothing written, no move answered, the asset and the sale unchanged | MSG-P7-003 | AC3, TC-E4-028-03, TC-E4-028-05 |
| X2 | The role lacks the Asset and disposal right | 403 before any read or write | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, TC-E4-028-04 |
| X3 | The asset is not a vehicle, or the case is in another state | The rule does not fire; nothing written; the state reported to the parent | None | AC2 |
| X4 | A required element of the pack is absent or invalid | 422 or a held step with the field named; nothing submitted | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X5 | The source-data product is stale after a late or failed batch | The step holds, writes nothing and shows the data date; it resumes on the next fresh answer | MSG-P1-001 | AC1 |
| X6 | The adapter answers rejected, or no answer inside 2 s | Nothing moves; the pack and the answer are recorded; the rejection alert is raised; `TITLE_BLOCKED` is not taken (GAP-2934; ASM-4831) | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X7 | The same signal or key arrives twice | One submission, one record, one answer | None | AC1 |
| X8 | The composite route or a consumed contract does not answer | Retry on the workflow schedule; 503 in the platform envelope | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X9 | A statement reaches a `v_ace_*` view, `recovery_case` or a foreign schema | The grant refuses it and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | §17, BR9 |

X1 to X3 are the legacy paths on the split, X4 to X8 what the pack, the boundaries and the adapter add, and X9 the DP-01 and DP-05 boundary.

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Transfer vehicle registration

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-000541" holds vehicle asset "AST-2026-000541" of type VEHICLE with a sale agreed
    Given the DISPOSAL rule package is in force at its version and carries R-DIS-51
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 Transfer vehicle registration (legacy RWB-E4-028 AC1)
    Given the rwb-integration contract mock returns the SCIS transfer of vehicle asset "AST-2026-000541" accepted with its submission reference
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns the asset "AST-2026-000541" of type VEHICLE and its sale at today's data date
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When its trigger arrives
    Then prepares and submits the registration transfer through SCIS
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Rule R-DIS-51 (legacy RWB-E4-028 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case "RC-2026-000542" in state TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING
    Given the rwb-integration contract mock returns the SCIS transfer of vehicle asset "AST-2026-000542" accepted
    Given a case in state TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING
    When registration transferred
    Then transfer the registration through SCIS
    Then the case moves to ASSET_SOLD

  Scenario: AC3 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E4-028 AC3)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The three criteria are the legacy criteria word for word with the origin tag added: `its trigger arrives`, `registration transferred`, `the action is taken` and `the decision log cannot be written` stand unchanged, and the `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` lines are the only additions. The work happens in three places: rwb-case writes `ASSET_SOLD`, rwb-integration carries the SCIS submission, rwb-source-data answers the asset and sale facts; this story prepares the pack, evaluates R-DIS-51, writes the two rows, records and answers. AC2's `registration transferred` is the adapter's accepted answer, not an officer's confirmation (GAP-2932; ASM-4829).

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-DIS-51 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING | REGISTRATION_TRANSFERRED | asset_type = vehicle | Transfer the registration through SCIS | ASSET_SOLD | Workbench | SCIS | 5 working days |

The row is copied character for character from the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4. Its owner column is a business role, so the case stays in the state and moves in rwb-case on this story's answer, while the `asset` and `asset_sale` rows are written here. R-DIS-48 (the payment confirmation into `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING`) is FEAT-AST-18's, R-DIS-52 (property) is FEAT-AST-20's, and R-DIS-53 (rejection) belongs to no story row of the split (GAP-2934; ASM-4831).

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The transfer is this service's: `holding_status` on `asset` and the transfer status on `asset_sale` are elements of `rwb_asset`, and no other service writes them | Ownership Map; TSD S5 T3.1; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | The record precedes the change, one per submission, with the rule and package version; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; AC1, AC3 |
| BR3 | The 5 working days of the rule row, the asset type, the transfer-in type and the statuses are rule rows or reference data with a version, never a constant | TSD S5 T3.2; legacy Guardrails |
| BR4 | The case move is answered, not written; the states are rwb-case's | Ownership Map (P3); GAP-2931 |
| BR5 | The pack is built only from elements the sources name; the registration particulars and the submission reference carry the placeholder and are not invented as columns | GAP-2933; ASM-4830 |
| BR6 | The ACE facts are rwb-source-data's and the SCIS submission is rwb-integration's: no `v_ace_*` read and no direct external call from this service | DP-05; Architecture v5 slides 8 and 13 |
| BR7 | No event is published and none is consumed; EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is the take-on story's | TSD S5 T5.3 |
| BR8 | A repeated signal or key writes once, answers once and is counted | TSD S5 T-A.2 |
| BR9 | No cross-schema join and no foreign key leaves `rwb_asset` | DP-01; TSD S5 T3.3 |
| BR10 | No personal data in the schema, a record, a log or a workflow input; the pack carries a vehicle reference and amounts, never a person | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |

##### 9. State transitions

The case state is rwb-case's and is applied by the parent `CaseWorkflow` on this story's answer (BR4).

| From (case state) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING | `REGISTRATION_TRANSFERRED` under R-DIS-51 | `asset_type = vehicle` and the adapter accepted the transfer | ASSET_SOLD, answer `ASSET_SOLD` |
| TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING | The adapter rejected the transfer under R-DIS-53 | `asset_type = vehicle` | Unchanged here: `TITLE_BLOCKED` is not taken (GAP-2934) |
| Any | Another state, another asset type or a repeated signal | X3, X7 | Unchanged |

| `holding_status` (asset) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Under offer | The transfer is accepted under R-DIS-51 | The record is written | SOLD, with the sale's transfer status |
| Any | The adapter rejects or does not answer | X6 | Unchanged |

The statuses are the `LOV-HOLDING` rows of TSD S5 T3.2; the case states are the DISPOSAL machine's (TSD S5 T4).

The rights are the row of the legacy permission table and TSD S5 T6.1, nothing wider: the legacy story declares Asset and disposal R only, and this step runs unattended, so no role is given a write here. ##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the behaviour behind the shapes of RWB-S5-E4028-CON; the transfer itself is submitted by the workflow, not by a REST call.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated, with the transfer status of each asset (API-S5-001) | Asset and disposal, R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out with title, sale and transfer status (API-S5-002) | Asset and disposal, R, scope applied | Not applicable |

`GET /assets/{assetKey}` and `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings`, `POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings` and `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds` are the other stories' rows of this service. Errors: 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope asset, 503 when a library or a contract does not answer.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case state and the stage it is in; faked |
| Case-move answer (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2931; ASM-4828)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | `ASSET_SOLD` with the rule and its version; faked |
| Asset and NPA sale data product (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2931; ASM-4828)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The asset, sale and registration facts with their data date, in place of the legacy `v_ace_npa_asset` and `v_ace_npa_sale` reads (DP-05); faked |
| SCIS vehicle-registration transfer (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2931; ASM-4828)) | queue `rwb-integration` | P2 rwb-integration | The transfer pack out and its accepted or rejected answer with the submission reference back (INT-28); faked |

One hop, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The rwb-integration row is an activity on the owner's queue because a route service reaches a shared capability through Temporal, never REST (Architecture v5 slide 13). DP-16 is outside the pattern set of this slice, so the row carries no C dependency and the story builds on the adapter's document and fake (GAP-2931; ASM-4828).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is the take-on story's and the sale events are the sale stories'; a completed transfer writes no outbox row and adds nothing to `rwb.asset.events.v1`. A build that publishes here fails the absence test.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The transfer due fact, the payment confirmation and the adapter answer arrive as signals and activity results of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`, so this slice adds no consumer group and no inbox row.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one per case per stage, continues-as-new across the holding | `rwb-asset` in `rwb-recovery` | Input: case, route, asset, sale, package in force; signals: transfer due, payment confirmed, adapter answer, package in force |
| `submitRegistrationTransfer` | Activity, the pack, the submission and the write | `rwb-asset` | Asset, sale and case in; rule IDs with versions, `holding_status`, transfer status, submission reference and case move out, one transaction |

No child workflow and no second queue. The activity name is a design choice of this story; the SCIS submission runs as an activity on `rwb-integration`'s queue.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The 5 working days of R-DIS-51 run as a durable timer inside the workflow; the step owns no Temporal Schedule and no Quartz job. The service's single Schedule is JOB-19, the re-appraisal story's.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| asset | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | This story writes `holding_status` |
| asset_sale | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | This story writes the transfer status of the sale |
| decision_record | PLT library in `rwb_asset` | One record per submission (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated signal |

Not owned and never read as a table: `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task`, `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row`, `approval` (P7), `listing` (S5 but the sibling stories'), `document`, `document_custody` (P5), `proceeds` (P8), `deviation` (S8), every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case state fake | `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING` for the fixture cases; a case in another state | AC2, X3 |
| rwb-case move fake | `ASSET_SOLD` accepted; a move refused for an unexpected state | AC1, AC2 |
| rwb-source-data product fake | Vehicle asset `AST-2026-000541` with its sale at today's date; a stale product; a property asset | AC1, X3, X5 |
| SCIS transfer fake | Accepted with the submission reference; rejected; no answer inside 2 s | AC1, AC2, X6 |
| rwb-decision package fake | The DISPOSAL package at its version with R-DIS-51 | AC1 to AC3 |
| Decision-record stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | AC3, X1 |
| Composite route fake | The merged SCR-21 and SCR-22 answer for `RC-2026-000541` | AC1 |
| Repeat-signal fake | The same signal twice and the same key twice | AC1, X7 |

The fakes are test-only; the placeholder rows carry their gap until their owners confirm the names (GAP-2931; ASM-4828).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 3 consumed | The two asset reads on `/api/recovery/asset/v1`; the case state read, the case-move answer and the source-data product; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | The transfer facts are workflow signals |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 1 activity owned, 1 consumed | `AssetDisposalWorkflow` and `submitRegistrationTransfer` on `rwb-asset`; the SCIS transfer activity on `rwb-integration`; no Schedule |
| File | None | INT-28 names no file and no API approach (GAP-2931) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset.titletransfer`; front end `src/modules/recovery/asset/TitleTransfer.tsx`, the fragment SCR-22 embeds, read only.

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is a prohibition here: the legacy `v_ace_npa_asset` and `v_ace_npa_sale` reads leave the service for the P1 boundary and no `v_ace_*` grant is kept. DP-03 is the transaction rule of the step, DP-13 moves the base, DP-19 is how the screens reach the service. The SCIS boundary and the source-data row are built on documents and fakes on Day 1 (GAP-2931), and the package in force is loaded through the service template without the DP-04 platform row (GAP-2935).

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` title-transfer branch | Workflow | Waits on the timer and the signals, loads the package in force, reports to the parent |
| `submitRegistrationTransfer` | Activity | The one step: read, prepare, submit, evaluate, write, answer |
| `TitleTransferEvaluator` | Service | R-DIS-51 on the asset type, the case state and the adapter answer |
| `RegistrationPackBuilder` | Service | The pack from the asset, the sale and the registration facts |
| `AssetDecisionRecordWriter` | Library adapter | One hash-linked record per submission before any change (DP-03) |
| `TitleTransferWriter` | Repository | `asset` and `asset_sale` in one transaction with the idempotency row and the lock |
| `ScisTransferActivity`, `SourceDataClient`, `CaseStateClient`, `CaseMoveAnswer` | Clients | The adapter activity and the three consumed rows, one hop, 2 s |
| `TitleTransferController` | Controller | The two reads, the right and the 400/401/403/404/503 map |
| `TitleTransfer` | React component | The transfer state on SCR-22, read only |

**Database.** No Flyway file: tables from the DB story, library objects from the library's migration, no column added for the particulars (GAP-2933).

**Configuration.** The 5 working days of the rule row, the asset type and the transfer-in type at their version (TSD S5 T3.2); the DISPOSAL package and version from rwb-decision; the capability row from rwb-access; the flag and the 2 s budget as platform configuration (ADR-020).

**Build steps.** (1) the branch and its input record; (2) `RegistrationPackBuilder` from the source-data fake (AC1, X4); (3) the adapter activity against its fake, accepted, rejected and timed out (AC1, AC2, X6); (4) `TitleTransferEvaluator` with R-DIS-51 and the asset-type guard (AC2, X3); (5) the record writer against the stub (AC3, X1); (6) `TitleTransferWriter` with the idempotency row (AC1, X7); (7) `CaseMoveAnswer` (AC1, AC2); (8) `TitleTransferController` with the right and the error map (X2); (9) the screen fragment through the route fake; (10) the staleness path (X5) and the boundary test (X9, BR6, BR7).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.asset.vehicle-registration-transfer-v1`; off means the branch holds, nothing is submitted, nothing is written and no move is answered.

**Done when.** §16 passes, an accepted transfer moves the case to `ASSET_SOLD` and shows the submission record in SIT, a rejected or timed-out transfer changes nothing and alerts, a repeat writes once, a forced record failure changes nothing, no case row and no `v_ace_*` read exists, and the two screens answer through the composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required element of the pack or of a request is absent or invalid (X4) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right reads or the step is called without it (X2) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record cannot be written before the rows change (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The asset or sale fact is stale after a late or failed batch (X5) | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-S5-001 | A floor price arrives under the approver's limit on a read of the sale (X3) | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | An appraisal more than a year old is carried on the asset read (X5) | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |

The six IDs are the legacy and platform sets, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and none is added. The legacy staleness rule VR-S5-019-1 is carried by MSG-P1-001 on the source-data row. No message exists for a rejected transfer: the rejection is recorded and alerted, not shown (GAP-2934).

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-22 Asset record (take-on, held, listed, sold) and SCR-21 Asset list (loading, list) are served through the gateway-bff route (DP-19), which calls rwb-asset for the asset, the sale and the transfer status, rwb-case for the state and rwb-source-data for the facts. This story fixes the rwb-asset answers only; the route and field list are RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

The state it produces is the sold state of SCR-22 — the submission reference, the date, the accepted answer and the sale's transfer status — plus the refusal, not-recorded, wrong-type, stale, rejected and repeated states with MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P1-001 and the rejection alert. Take-on, held and listed belong to the take-on, holding and pricing stories.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the 5 working days, the asset type, the transfer-in type and the statuses stay reference data or rule rows with a version.
- No personal data in the schema, a workflow input or a log; a vehicle is identified by its asset reference and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: no `v_ace_*` grant, no ACE read, and no direct external call to SCIS from this service (DP-05, BR6).
- The case stays with rwb-case: no `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task` or `timer` row here (BR4).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element returns: no shared job table, no Quartz row, no monolith base, no data-lake export of a transfer.
- The record precedes the change and the repeated signal is deduped (DP-03, BR8).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract slice of RWB-E4-029, the baseline the title-transfer branch of rwb-asset builds against on Day 1. It declares the two asset reads that answer SCR-21 and SCR-22 on `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13), the status elements of `listing` and `asset`, the three consumed rows of rwb-case and rwb-document (DP-05), the decision-record element of DP-03, the rule-package element the branch evaluates against, the rights and the error envelope, and the fakes. No event is published and none is consumed: the owned event of the service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn`, the take-on story's. No operation publishes the officer's registration, so the baseline declares the signal instead of an invented path (GAP-2937; ASM-4833); no element holds the title status or the Land Office reference (GAP-2938; ASM-4834); the document custody release has no published name and the C row of the plan is empty (GAP-2939; ASM-4835); AC3 of the application slice names R-DIS-02, which RWB-S5-E3020-APP builds (GAP-2940; ASM-4836); R-DIS-53 has no owner (GAP-2941; ASM-4837); the plan carries no requirement id (GAP-2942; ASM-4838); the sources are in review (GAP-2943; ASM-4839). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the Land Office transfer capability of rwb-asset — its asset reads, its status elements, its consumed rows, its decision-record and rule-package elements, its rights, its error envelope and its fakes — baselined and tagged before the build starts**, so that **the application story and every consumer of an asset's sold state can build and test on Day 1 against one fixed, versioned surface instead of guessing the shape of a neighbour's answer**.

This is the contract slice of legacy RWB-E4-029. It owns:

- the document that fixes the two asset reads on base `/api/recovery/asset/v1`, with their parameters, their documented answer, their rights and their idempotency (DP-13);
- the status elements the branch writes, `listing.status` and `asset.holding_status`, declared against `LOV-LISTING` and `LOV-HOLDING` and never enumerated in code;
- the three consumed rows: the rwb-case case state read, the rwb-case case-move answer and the rwb-document custody release, each with its owner, its use and its placeholder where the name is not published (DP-05, GAP-2939);
- the decision-record element and the local library dependency that carries it (DP-03);
- the rule-package element: the DISPOSAL package, its version and the two rows this branch evaluates with the remaining rows named as other stories' (GAP-2940);
- the capability area, the rights and the error envelope of the operations it declares;
- the fakes and their documented answers, so that every downstream answer has a stub on Day 1;
- the naming and boundary rules of the baseline: one base, one topic, one queue, one schema, no foreign base, no monolith base, no Schedule for a workflow timer, no interface to the Land Office (GAP-2937).

It does not own: the transfer behaviour, the rule evaluation, the release call, the status writes, the decision records and the case moves, which are RWB-S5-E4029-APP; the payment term and the award, FEAT-AST-18's story; the vehicle registration, FEAT-AST-19's story; the property take-on, RWB-S5-E3020-APP; the documents and their custody, rwb-document's (P5); the case of record and its states, rwb-case's (P3); the rule rows and the package version, rwb-decision's (P7); the proceeds, rwb-payment's (P8); the screen field list and the composite route, which are RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19).

##### 2. Business rationale

A contract baseline is what lets the stories of one wave build at once. Without it the application story would write the sold state against whatever shape the document hub happened to answer that week, and the first integration would find the mismatches instead of the review. With it, the application story builds on Day 1 against a tagged document and its fakes, the payment, vehicle and proceeds stories know what the sold state and the listing must carry, and the consumers of the asset reads know exactly which elements they can rely on.

The three rules the baseline applies:

- **the owner publishes, the consumer adapts.** Every consumed row names its owner and its use, and where the source documents do not publish a name the row carries the placeholder rather than an invented path (GAP-2939; ASM-4835).
- **one hop, one budget.** Every consumed row is a single hop with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and no chain, which is ADR-020 and is what the application story's exception paths assume.
- **additive only.** A new optional element is a minor version; a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version and a new document (C1).

The business outcome the baseline protects is the one FEAT-AST-20 of the FSD names: the Land Office transfer is tracked and stays a person and officer step. The baseline does not state that outcome, and no criterion here asserts a business value or a title registration.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The Ownership Map rows are in force: S5 owns `GET /assets`, `GET /assets/{assetId}`, `GET /assets/{assetKey}`, `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings`, `POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings` and `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds`; `asset_sale` and `listing` are S5's tables, and `asset` is read as S5 from TSD S5 T3.1 while the map names no row for it (GAP-2938; ASM-4834).
- The service naming is fixed: schema `rwb_asset`, login `rwb_asset`, base `/api/recovery/asset/v1`, topic `rwb.asset.events.v1` with `.retry` and `.dlt`, task queue `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset`.
- The published shapes of the declared operations are the API Specification v4: `AssetPage` and `Asset` (API-S5-001, API-S5-002).
- The owned event row of the service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` (TSD S5 T5.3); the title branch touches no event of the service.
- The platform CON stories are published: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for the decision record (DP-03) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the composite route (DP-19).
- The lists `LOV-HOLDING`, `LOV-LISTING`, `LOV-ASSET-TYPE` and `LOV-SALE-CHANNEL` are reference data with their version (TSD S5 T3.2), referenced and never enumerated.
- The sources of the slice are In review with empty sign-off tables; a Draft baseline is published without approval and the build waits only for its tag (GAP-2943; ASM-4839).

##### 4. Flow

1. The author drafts the baseline from the Ownership Map, the TSD S5 T-A.1 operations, the TSD S5 T3.1 elements and the lists of T3.2.
2. Every operation is declared with its method, path, documented answer, rights, idempotency and error set; the registration itself is declared as a workflow signal because no source gives it an operation (GAP-2937; ASM-4833).
3. Every consumed row is declared with its owner, its use, its budget and a placeholder where the name is not published.
4. The decision-record element is declared with the library dependency that carries it, and the rule-package element with its owner, its version and the rows this branch evaluates.
5. The fakes are declared with their documented answers, one per consumed row, one for the composite route and one for the registration signal.
6. The schema, the open lists and the closed lists are published, and the compatibility check runs: a breaking change fails the check.
7. The document goes to review as Draft; the reviewers are the owners of the consumed rows and the tech lead of the service.
8. On the review's close the document is tagged and baselined; the application story starts against the tag and the fakes.
9. A defect found in the build that needs a shape change is raised against this document, and the document moves to a new minor or major version; the code never moves ahead of the document.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A consumer asks for a shape the sources do not publish | The row carries the placeholder and the gap; no path is invented and no field is guessed | C2, C4 |
| X2 | A change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element | The compatibility check fails, the version becomes a new major and the document is re-reviewed | C1 |
| X3 | A declared surface reaches another service's data, base or queue | The review refuses the baseline and the boundary test fails the build | C7 |
| X4 | A consumed row has no fake, or its fake has no documented answer | The baseline is not tagged; the application story cannot start | C6 |
| X5 | The rights of an operation are not one of the rows of the access matrix | The operation is not declared and the error set of the operation is incomplete | C5 |
| X6 | An owner changes its documented answer after the tag | The owner publishes a new version, this document follows with a minor or major version, and the application story re-tests against the new fake | X2 |
| X7 | A draft declares a Land Office interface, a title column or an event for the transfer | The baseline is refused: no source names an interface, a column or an event for this step | C2, C7 |

X1 to X3 are the paths of an incomplete source, X4 to X6 are the paths of a baseline moving under a build, and X7 is the boundary this slice must not cross.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs no build, no live service and no approval; starts on Day 1 and is finished before the application story's first line |
| Negotiable | The wording, the order of the sections and the fake data are this story's choice; the paths, the owners, the base, the error set and the element names are fixed by their sources |
| Valuable | The stories of wave 3 build at once against one tagged surface, and the first integration finds behaviour, not shape |
| Estimable | One document, two provided operations, three consumed rows, two library elements, seven fakes and one compatibility check |
| Small | Finished inside a week; the review is the only gate |
| Testable | Every criterion is a document check that runs in the contract test suite, plus the compatibility check on the published schema |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the Land Office transfer capability

  Scenario: C1 The baseline validates and only additive changes pass (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published schema and the open and closed lists of the baseline
    When a change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element
    Then the compatibility check fails and the change needs a new major version
    And a change that adds an optional element passes as a minor version

  Scenario: C2 The elements, the status elements and the closed lists are published as declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the baseline document of this story
    When the element list, the required and optional flags and the closed lists are read
    Then every element carries its type, its nullability and its source
    And listing status and asset holding status are declared against LOV-LISTING and LOV-HOLDING and are not enumerated in code
    And the title status and the Land Office registration reference carry the placeholder and its gap identifier because no element holds them

  Scenario: C3 The asset reads are declared with their rights (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operations the baseline provides on base /api/recovery/asset/v1
    When the method, path, documented answer, right and idempotency of each are read
    Then both asset reads carry the Asset and disposal right R with scope applied and no idempotency
    And no write operation is declared for the registration, and POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations and POST /assets/{assetId}/listings are named as other stories'

  Scenario: C4 The consumed rows carry their owners, their budgets and their placeholders (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed operation table of the baseline
    When the rows of rwb-case and rwb-document are read
    Then each row names its owner, its use and its 2 s budget
    And where the name is not published the row carries the placeholder and the gap identifier and no invented path

  Scenario: C5 The error envelope is declared per operation (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operations the baseline provides
    When the error set and the rights of each operation are read
    Then the error set names 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503 in one problem envelope
    And the capability area and the right of each operation are the rows of the access matrix

  Scenario: C6 The decision-record, rule-package and fake elements are declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the baseline document
    When the decision-record element, the rule-package element and the fake table are read
    Then the decision-record element names RWB-PLT-E1027-CON as its library and the transaction it joins
    And the rule-package element names the DISPOSAL package, its owner, its version in force and R-DIS-52 with R-DIS-02, and declares no rule row
    And every consumed row has a fake with a documented answer, including the stopped stub, the refused release and the repeated registration

  Scenario: C7 The naming and the boundary of the baseline hold (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the base, the topic, the queue and the schema of the baseline
    When the document is checked against the naming rule and the ownership map
    Then the base /api/recovery/asset/v1, the queue rwb-asset and the topic rwb.asset.events.v1 are the only ones declared as this service's own
    And no Land Office interface, no title column, no foreign schema, no monolith base and no Schedule for the transfer timer is declared
    And no event is published or consumed by the title branch
```

The seven criteria are new to this run and are tagged as such: they test the contract deliverable only — the schema, the elements, the lists, the operations, the consumed rows, the rights, the envelope, the two library elements, the fakes and the boundary. No criterion states a business outcome or a business value of the application story, and none asserts that a rule fires, that a document is released or that a case moves.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One owner per operation, event and table: the baseline declares only the rows the Ownership Map gives to S5, and names every other row with its owner | Ownership Map; Architecture v5 slide 41; GAP-2938 |
| BR2 | A consumed row with no published name carries the placeholder and its gap, and never an invented path | §R9; GAP-2939 |
| BR3 | The baseline is additive: a new optional element is a minor version, and a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version | ADR-020; C1 |
| BR4 | Every consumed row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and no chain | ADR-020 |
| BR5 | No event is published and none is consumed by the title branch: the owned event is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn`, the take-on story's, and the registration is a workflow signal | TSD S5 T5.3 |
| BR6 | The decision record is written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the caller's transaction before any change, and its element is declared once for the service | DP-03 |
| BR7 | The rule package is referenced, never redefined: the DISPOSAL package, its version and the rows are rwb-decision's, and no rule table of this service is declared | GAP-2940 |
| BR8 | No business value and no business list is enumerated: the ten working days, the statuses and the types are referenced with their identifier and version | §R7.2 (s16); legacy Guardrails |
| BR9 | No personal data in any element, fake or example of the baseline; a buyer is a code and the property address stays an ACE fact | §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR10 | The baseline never declares another service's table, operation, topic or interface as its own, and it declares no Land Office interface at all | DP-01, DP-13, DP-14; GAP-2937 |

##### 9. State transitions

The document itself is the object of this section: the lifecycle of the contract baseline.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | The draft is complete | Every operation, row, element, fake and error is declared | Draft |
| Draft | The review is opened | The owners of the consumed rows are named as reviewers | In review |
| In review | The review closes with no open comment | The compatibility check passes | Baselined, tagged for the application story |
| In review | A comment needs a shape change | The change is applied to the draft | Draft |
| Baselined | An additive change is approved | New optional element only, compatibility check passes | Baselined, new minor version |
| Baselined | A breaking change is approved | A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element | Draft of a new major version, and the consumers are notified |
| Baselined | An owner changes its answer | X6 | Draft of a new minor or major version, and the fake is updated |

| Step | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Being authored | A consumed row has no published name | X1 | The row carries the placeholder and the gap and the draft continues |
| In review | A row reaches a foreign schema, base, queue or the Land Office | X3, X7 | The baseline is refused |
| Ready to tag | A consumed row has no fake | X4 | Not tagged, the review reopens |
