The baseline declares no new table, no new column and no migration, and it enumerates no business value: every list, code and threshold is referenced with its identifier and its version. **No personal data** appears in any element, fake or example; the fixture identifiers are synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13). These are the reads that answer SCR-21 and SCR-22.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated, with the holding status and the listing status of each asset (API-S5-001) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out, with its title, its sale, its holding status and the status of its listing (API-S5-002) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

No write operation is declared for the registration. `POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations` (API-S5-003) is rwb-valuation's, `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings` (API-S5-004) is the pricing story's and `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds` (API-S5-005) is the auction story's; the title transfer enters as a workflow signal because no source publishes an operation for it (GAP-2937; ASM-4833).

The error envelope of the declared operations: 400 for a malformed request, 401 for an unauthenticated call, 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope asset, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for a missing field, and 503 when the decision library or a consumed boundary does not answer, in one problem document with a code, a message ID and a correlation reference.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family (read) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference and the case state the rule checks before it fires; faked |
| The case-move answer (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2939; ASM-4835)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The answer that carries `ASSET_SOLD` with its rule version; on the workflow boundary it is the outcome the parent applies; faked |
| The custody release (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2939; ASM-4835)) | `/api/recovery/document/v1` | P5 rwb-document | The release of the documents of the asset from custody, with an idempotency key, in place of the legacy `document_custody` write (DP-05); faked |

Each row is one hop or one activity, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). Where a name is not published the row carries the placeholder and no path, so the consumer adapts at the tag rather than inventing a surface (BR2, GAP-2939).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The owned event row of this service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn`, published by the take-on story when the asset record opens (TSD S5 T5.3). This baseline declares it as another story's, adds nothing to `rwb.asset.events.v1`, and the title branch writes no outbox row: its outward surface is the case-move answer and its own reads.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The registration, the case state and the package in force arrive as signals of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`, so the baseline declares no topic subscription, no consumer group and no inbox row; a build that subscribes to a topic not listed by Architecture v5 fails the naming check (BR5, DP-14).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, continues-as-new | `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the route, the asset reference, the listing reference and the rule package in force; signals: the registration recorded, the case state and the rule package in force |
| `recordLandOfficeTransfer` | Activity, the title-transfer step | `rwb-asset` | The registration and the case in; the rule IDs with their versions, the listing and holding statuses, the release answer and the stage outcome out, in one transaction |

The workflow is the same execution the take-on, holding and sale stories of this service use; this baseline fixes its input and signal elements and the one activity it adds, and it declares no child workflow and no second queue. The activity name is a design choice of the application story, and the baseline carries it so that the workflow's history is stable.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. R-DIS-52's ten working days run as a workflow timer and a case SLA, so the baseline declares no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job for the transfer. The single Schedule of the service is JOB-19, which the re-appraisal story owns and which is not declared here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| asset | S5 (`rwb_asset`), read as S5 from TSD S5 T3.1 while the map names no row (GAP-2938; ASM-4834) | The baseline declares its status element, not its schema |
| listing | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The baseline declares its status element, not its schema |
| asset_sale | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | Referenced for the sale of the case; not written by this step |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The local decision record of DP-03, declared through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated registration and of the release |

The baseline declares no column, no index and no migration, and it declares no table of another owner: `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task` and `timer` (P3), `document` and `document_custody` (P5), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` and `approval` (P7), `proceeds` (P8) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) are named by their owner and never declared here. No title column exists and none is declared (GAP-2938).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case case-state and case-move fake | The case states `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING` and `ASSET_PENDING_TAKE_ON` of the fixture cases; `ASSET_SOLD` and `ASSET_ON_BOOKS` accepted, and a move refused for an unexpected state | C3, C4, C6 |
| rwb-document custody release fake | Documents released; custody already released; a refusal; no answer inside 2 s | C4, C6 |
| rwb-decision rule-package fake | The DISPOSAL package at its version in force with R-DIS-52 and R-DIS-02 | C6 |
| Decision-record stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | C6 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-21 and SCR-22 answer for case `RC-2026-000591`, with the statuses read once | C2, C6 |
| Registration signal fake | A property registration, a vehicle registration and a repeated registration on the same key | C2, C3, C5 |
| Asset answer fake | The `Asset` answer with its mandatory elements and one with an optional element absent | C2, C3 |

Each fake answers only what its owner documents, and a fake that answers more than the document fails the review. The names that are not published are stubbed from the documents and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-2939; ASM-4835).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 3 consumed | The two asset reads on `/api/recovery/asset/v1`; the rwb-case state read and move answer and the rwb-document custody release; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | The registration is a workflow signal; nothing is published |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 1 activity | `AssetDisposalWorkflow` and `recordLandOfficeTransfer` on `rwb-asset`; no Schedule |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Document.** `04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-S5 rwb-asset (Asset)/RWB S5 E4029 CON Record a property transfer at the Land Office - contract v1.md`, with the schema and the examples in the service contract folder of RWB-S5-E4029.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Sections and owners of the review.** The document is written in nine parts: the provided operations, the consumed rows, the published and consumed events, the workflow and its activity, the schedules, the tables, the fakes, the call-type summary and the lifecycle. Each part is reviewed by the owner of the rows it names, and the tag waits for every reviewer.

**Compatibility check.** The schema is published as JSON Schema with `additionalProperties: false` on the closed objects, and the check runs on three inputs: the previous tag, the new draft and a corpus of recorded answers from the fakes. A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element fails the check and forces a new major version (C1, BR3).

**Open shapes carried into the tag.** Three shapes are carried as placeholders and not invented: the title status and the registration reference (GAP-2938; ASM-4834), the names of the three consumed rows (GAP-2939; ASM-4835) and the registration signal's own elements, which are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2937; ASM-4833). A placeholder is a declared forthcoming shape, not a permission to guess.

**Done when.** The seven criteria pass, the reviewers of rwb-case and rwb-document have closed their comments, the compatibility check passes on the tag, the fakes are published with their documented answers, and RWB-S5-E4029-APP can start against the tag with no open shape question.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Asset and disposal right calls one of the declared operations | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a declared request is absent or invalid | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-S5-001 | Carried from the service set and declared as the envelope row it is; no path of this baseline raises it | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | Carried from the service set and declared as the envelope row it is; no path of this baseline raises it | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written, as the decision-record element declares it | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| Document rule | A change fails the compatibility check | A breaking change needs a new major version. |
| Document rule | A consumed row has no published name | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2939; ASM-4835). |

The five message IDs are carried from the service and platform sets and are declared only as the envelope rows of the operations in this baseline; the two document rules are checks of this story and are not service messages.

##### 15. Screens and states

The baseline serves SCR-21 Asset list and SCR-22 Asset record through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). What this story fixes is the element list of the declared responses and the empty, loading, refused, wrong-state, refused-release and repeated-registration states the route can show from this service's answers. The route itself, its merge order and its field list are RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the screens' transitions are the application story's.

No screen is built here, no component is delivered and no state machine is declared: the screen section of a contract story lists the elements the screens read and the states their answers can carry.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the baseline: the ten working days, the statuses, the types and every threshold are referenced with their identifier and version, never enumerated as a constant or a default.
- No personal data in any element, fake, example or log: identifiers, codes, dates and a rule version only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the baseline declares no `v_ace_*` element and no ACE table, and the sale facts appear only through `asset_sale` (DP-05).
- The case stays with rwb-case, the documents with rwb-document and the rules with rwb-decision: no `recovery_case` element, no custody element and no rule row is declared as this service's own.
- No interface, file or operation is declared for the Land Office (BR10).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; no document, module or test names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no monolith base `/api/recovery/v1`, no shared job table, no Schedule for the transfer timer, no event published or consumed by this branch.
- Additive only: a breaking change needs a new major version and a re-tag, and the code never moves ahead of the document (BR3).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the application slice of RWB-E4-029 for rwb-asset. The four legacy criteria are kept word for word with their origin tag, and the six legacy test cases keep their IDs. The title transfer becomes a branch of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` on queue `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery`: it takes the registration the officer records, releases the documents from custody on the rwb-document contract (DP-05 boundary, name not published), writes the status on `listing` and the holding status on `asset` in `rwb_asset`, records the outcome before any change through the local decision-record library (DP-03), and answers `ASSET_SOLD` to rwb-case; it publishes nothing. The Land Office itself stays a person and officer step with no service and no interface (GAP-2937; ASM-4833), and no element of the service holds the registration reference or the title status (GAP-2938; ASM-4834). AC3 owns R-DIS-02, whose behaviour is RWB-S5-E3020-APP's (GAP-2940; ASM-4836). The base becomes `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13) and SCR-21 and SCR-22 read through the gateway-bff route (DP-19). Gaps: the custody release has no published operation and the C row is empty (GAP-2939; ASM-4835); R-DIS-53 has no owner (GAP-2941; ASM-4837); the plan carries no requirement id (GAP-2942; ASM-4838); the sources are in review (GAP-2943; ASM-4839). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **sale officer**, I want **to track the Land Office transfer, which stays a person and officer step**, so that **assets sell sooner at approved prices** (legacy RWB-E4-029, word for word).

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E4-029. It owns:

- the four legacy criteria with their origin tag, and the rules, messages and screens they depend on;
- the title-transfer branch of `AssetDisposalWorkflow` on `rwb-asset`, the child of the case workflow for the disposal stage (Architecture v5 slide 13);
- the evaluation of R-DIS-52 on the registration the officer records, with the DISPOSAL package version in force; R-DIS-02 is tabled in §8 because AC3 names it (GAP-2940; ASM-4836);
- the release of the documents from custody on a document-hub operation that carries the placeholder until P5 publishes it (GAP-2939; ASM-4835);
- the status writes of this step in `rwb_asset`: `listing.status` and `asset.holding_status` set to the sold value of their lists, in one transaction with the record and the idempotency row (GAP-2938; ASM-4834);
- the decision record of the outcome before the change (DP-03) and the case answer `ASSET_SOLD` with the rule and its version;
- the reads of SCR-21 and SCR-22 on `/api/recovery/asset/v1` through the gateway-bff route (DP-13, DP-19).

It does not own: the published shapes and the fakes, which are RWB-S5-E4029-CON; the payment term, the award and the confirmation that starts the title transfer, which are FEAT-AST-18's story (R-DIS-47 to R-DIS-49); the vehicle registration through SCIS, FEAT-AST-19's story (R-DIS-51); the take-on of the property after a deed in lieu, which is RWB-S5-E3020-APP (R-DIS-02); the rejection of a transfer and its blocked title (R-DIS-53) (GAP-2941; ASM-4837); the documents, their custody and their retention, rwb-document (P5); the case and its route states, rwb-case (P3); the proceeds and their posting, rwb-payment (P8) and FEAT-AST-21's story; the rule package, rwb-decision (P7); the deployment, the operations story of this key.

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E4-029 tracked the last person step of a property sale: after the buyer paid, the title moved at the Land Office and the asset left the stock only when the registration was in hand. The FSD keeps it as FEAT-AST-20 in module S5, run by the sale officer with Legal counsel as the second user, between the payment term of FEAT-AST-18 and the proceeds of FEAT-AST-21 (FSD S5 A2.20.2). The metric is unchanged: the NPA sales cycle moves from 1,486 days to a target of 1,095 days, measured on the decision log and the Workbench records, reviewed monthly (FSD S5 A2.20.1). R-DIS-52 allows ten working days for the step.

What D-RCV-60 changes:

- **the step is this service's case branch.** `AssetDisposalWorkflow` on `rwb-asset` receives the registration, evaluates the rule and writes the status of the asset and of its listing; the case state stays with rwb-case (DP-13, DP-19).
- **the registration itself stays outside every service.** The feature says so in one sentence, and no integration id, no operation and no system row models the Land Office; the officer's act is a case task and the registration reference has no element in `rwb_asset` (GAP-2937, GAP-2938; ASM-4833, ASM-4834).
- **the custody release crosses one boundary.** The legacy `document` and `document_custody` rows are rwb-document's; this story calls its release operation with an idempotency key and never reads those tables (DP-05; GAP-2939).
- **the decision is recorded first**, one per registration, in the row's transaction — what AC1 asked and AC4 tested.
- **nothing is published.** EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is the take-on story's, and the sale event is not in any source for this step; §12.3 states the absence and a build that publishes here fails it.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S5-E4029-CON tagged: the two reads, the status writes, the consumed rows, the decision-record and rule-package elements, the error set and the fakes.
- `asset`, `asset_sale` and `listing` exist in `rwb_asset` with the TSD S5 T3.1 columns and the standard record columns of T3.0; the DB story creates them and this story adds no table, no column and no migration (GAP-2938; ASM-4834).
- The DISPOSAL package is in force at its version with R-DIS-52 and R-DIS-02, authored in rwb-decision (P7) and loaded through the service template.
- The officer's registration arrives as the `TITLE_REGISTERED` signal of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`, recorded on the case task in rwb-case; no operation and no interface exist for it (GAP-2937; ASM-4833).
- The rwb-document release operation is baselined with its fake; its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2939; ASM-4835).
- The rwb-case state read and the case-move answer are behind fakes; no source publishes their names.
- The `LOV-HOLDING`, `LOV-LISTING` and `LOV-ASSET-TYPE` lists are reference data with their version (TSD S5 T3.2).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON writes in the caller's transaction (DP-03); RWB-PLT-N001-CON serves the two screens, one hop each (DP-19).
- The service holds its own login on `rwb_asset`, no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-01, DP-05).
- The sources of the slice are In review with empty sign-off tables; both stories stand at Draft and no approval is needed to build against a Draft baseline (GAP-2943; ASM-4839).

##### 4. Flow

1. R-DIS-48 in the payment story has confirmed the sale and started the title transfer; the case is in `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING` and the asset is held or sold in its listing.
2. The sale officer registers the transfer at the Land Office outside the Workbench, receives the registered title and records it on the case task; no service calls the Land Office (GAP-2937; ASM-4833).
3. `AssetDisposalWorkflow` on `rwb-asset` wakes on the `TITLE_REGISTERED` signal, which carries the case reference, the asset reference, the registration date and the reference the officer entered.
4. The step confirms `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING` on the rwb-case contract and reads the asset and its sale from `rwb_asset`: asset type, holding status, the listing and its status, and the `asset_sale` row of the case (GAP-2938; ASM-4834).
5. `TitleTransferEvaluator` loads the package in force and evaluates R-DIS-52: from `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING`, on `TITLE_REGISTERED`, with `asset_type` a property value, release the documents from custody and record the transfer. Where no rule fires the step changes nothing and reports the reason to the parent (X3, X6).
6. `AssetDecisionRecordWriter` writes one record **before any change**: case, asset, listing, rule ID with its version, the registration date and reference as the inputs reference, the outcome and the case move. A failed write stops the step (DP-03; AC1, AC4).
7. The step calls the rwb-document release with the asset and document-custody scope and an idempotency key derived from the case, the asset and the registration date; the call is one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker. It answers "released" or refuses; a refusal or a timeout leaves nothing committed and the workflow retries (X4).
8. `TitleTransferWriter` writes the status of the listing and the holding status of the asset in one `rwb_asset` transaction with the record and the idempotency row, under the optimistic lock: `listing.status` takes the sold value of `LOV-LISTING` and `asset.holding_status` takes the sold value of `LOV-HOLDING` (GAP-2938; ASM-4834).
9. `CaseMoveAnswer` answers rwb-case with `ASSET_SOLD`, the rule ID, the version and the decided-at time; rwb-case writes the case and its route state.
10. A repeated registration for the same case, asset and date writes nothing, releases nothing and sends no second answer; the repeat is counted (X5).
11. A registration rejected at the Land Office is not this branch: R-DIS-53 holds the transfer and blocks the title (GAP-2941; ASM-4837).
12. SCR-21 and SCR-22 read the asset, its holding status and the status of its listing from this service through the composite route, read only; the workflow returns to its durable timer and continues as new at the stage end and at least every 28 days.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The record cannot be written | Nothing written, nothing released, no move answered; the statuses stay as they were | MSG-P7-003 | AC4, TC-E4-029-04, TC-E4-029-06 |
| X2 | The role lacks the Asset and disposal right | 403 before any read or write | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, TC-E4-029-05 |
| X3 | The case is not in `TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING` | The rule does not fire; nothing written; the state is reported to the parent | None | AC2 |
| X4 | The custody release refuses, or does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | Nothing committed; the step retries on the workflow schedule; the caller sees 503 in the platform envelope | None | AC2 |
| X5 | The same registration arrives twice, or the same key twice | One release, one write, one answer | None | AC1 |
| X6 | The asset type is a vehicle, not a property | R-DIS-52 does not fire; the vehicle path is R-DIS-51 on FEAT-AST-19's story | None | AC2 |
| X7 | A required element of the registration or of a request is absent or invalid | 422 with the field named; nothing written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X8 | A statement reaches a `v_ace_*` view, `recovery_case`, `document`, `document_custody` or a foreign schema | The grant refuses it and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | §17, BR6 |
| X9 | The Land Office rejects the transfer | Held for R-DIS-53, which no story of this split owns; the branch writes nothing | None | GAP-2941 |

X1 to X3 are the legacy paths carried onto the split, X4 to X7 come from the one boundary the step crosses and the shape of its input, X8 is the DP-01 and DP-05 boundary and X9 is the rule the split leaves without an owner.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Day 1 against the CON baseline and the rwb-case, rwb-document and rwb-decision fakes; no live P3 or P5 |
| Negotiable | Activity name, decision code and signal shape are ours; the rules, messages, screens, statuses and reads are fixed |
| Valuable | The asset leaves the stock on the day the title registers, and the officer's step is tracked without a paper chase |
| Estimable | One branch, one evaluator, one record per registration, one boundary call, two status writes, one answer, two read-only screen fragments |
| Small | Two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion on synthetic cases through the fakes, plus the access, wrong-state, refused-release, repeat and failed-record cases |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Record a property transfer at the Land Office

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-000591" holds property asset "AST-2026-000591" in listing "LS-2026-000591"
    Given the DISPOSAL rule package is in force at its version and carries R-DIS-52 and R-DIS-02
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 Record a property transfer at the Land Office (legacy RWB-E4-029 AC1)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case "RC-2026-000591" in state TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING
    Given the rwb-document contract mock returns the documents of asset "AST-2026-000591" held in custody
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When the user acts on the screen
    Then tracks the Land Office transfer, which stays a person and officer step
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Rule R-DIS-52 (legacy RWB-E4-029 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case "RC-2026-000592" in state TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING
    Given the rwb-document contract mock returns the documents of asset "AST-2026-000592" held in custody
    Given a case in state TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING
    When title registered
    Then release the documents from custody and record the transfer at the Land Office
    Then the case moves to ASSET_SOLD

  Scenario: AC3 Rule R-DIS-02 (legacy RWB-E4-029 AC3)
    Given the rwb-treatment contract mock returns the registered deed in lieu transfer of the property with the opening book value
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case "RC-2026-000593" in state ASSET_PENDING_TAKE_ON
    Given a case in state ASSET_PENDING_TAKE_ON
    When dil transfer registered
    Then create the asset record from AMIS with the opening book value
    Then the case moves to ASSET_ON_BOOKS

  Scenario: AC4 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E4-029 AC4)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The four criteria are the legacy criteria word for word with the origin tag added: the repeated `Then`, `the user acts on the screen`, `title registered`, `dil transfer registered` and `the decision log cannot be written` stand, and the `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` lines are the only additions. AC2's release and the case move happen in three places: rwb-document releases the documents, rwb-case writes the move to `ASSET_SOLD`, and this story evaluates the rule, writes the statuses, records and answers. AC3 is R-DIS-02, whose asset record is created by RWB-S5-E3020-APP; here it is asserted at the take-on boundary and not built twice (GAP-2940; ASM-4836).

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-DIS-52 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING | TITLE_REGISTERED | asset_type = property | Release the documents from custody and record the transfer at the Land Office | ASSET_SOLD | Sale officer | the Land Office, Document Hub | 10 working days |
| R-DIS-02 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | ASSET_PENDING_TAKE_ON | DIL_TRANSFER_REGISTERED | asset_type = property and transfer registered | Create the asset record from AMIS with the opening book value | ASSET_ON_BOOKS | Sale officer | AMIS, the Land Office | 1 working day |

Both rows are copied character for character from the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4. Their owner column is a business role, so the case moves in rwb-case on this story's answer while the statuses, the record and the release are handled here. The Land Office in the systems column stays a person and officer step with no interface (GAP-2937; ASM-4833). R-DIS-53, R-DIS-54 and R-DIS-55 are FEAT-AST-21's and the rejection's; R-DIS-47 to R-DIS-49 are FEAT-AST-18's; R-DIS-51 is FEAT-AST-19's.

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The status of the listing and the holding status of the asset are this service's: they are written here on the values of `LOV-LISTING` and `LOV-HOLDING`, in `rwb_asset` | TSD S5 T3.1, T3.2; GAP-2938 |
| BR2 | The record precedes the change, one per registration, with the rule and package version; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; AC1, AC4 |
| BR3 | The Land Office is never called: the registration enters as the officer's signal and the service holds no interface, no file and no screen for it | GAP-2937; ASM-4833 |
| BR4 | The documents and their custody stay with rwb-document: one release call with an idempotency key, no read of `document` or `document_custody` | DP-05; GAP-2939 |
| BR5 | The case move is answered, not written; `recovery_case` and `assignment` are rwb-case's | TSD S5 T3.3; GAP-2938 |
| BR6 | No cross-schema join and no foreign key leaves `rwb_asset` | DP-01; TSD S5 T3.3 |
| BR7 | Every value a business person may change is rule data or reference data with a version: the ten working days, the statuses and the asset types | FSD S5 BR-S5-020; TSD S5 T3.2 |
| BR8 | No event is published: EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is the take-on story's and no source gives this step one | TSD S5 T5.3 |
| BR9 | A repeated registration or key writes once, releases once and answers once | TSD S5 T-A.2 |
| BR10 | No personal data in a row, a record, a log or a workflow input; a buyer is a code and the property address stays an ACE fact | §R7.2 (s17) |

##### 9. State transitions

The case route state is rwb-case's and is applied by the parent `CaseWorkflow` on this story's answer (BR5).

| From (case state) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| TITLE_TRANSFER_PENDING | `TITLE_REGISTERED` under R-DIS-52 | `asset_type` is a property value | ASSET_SOLD, answer `ASSET_SOLD` |
| ASSET_PENDING_TAKE_ON | `DIL_TRANSFER_REGISTERED` under R-DIS-02 | Property and transfer registered | ASSET_ON_BOOKS, built by RWB-S5-E3020-APP and asserted here |
| Any | A registration in another state, a vehicle, or a repeat | X3, X6, X5 | Unchanged, no answer |

| `listing.status` | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live or under offer | The registration is recorded | R-DIS-52 fires and the release answered | SOLD |
| Any | The state is wrong, the type is a vehicle, or the release refuses | X3, X4, X6 | Unchanged |

| `asset.holding_status` | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| HELD, LISTED, UNDER_OFFER or SOLD | The registration is recorded | R-DIS-52 fires | The sold value of `LOV-HOLDING`, written in the same transaction |
| Any | The record or the transaction fails | X1 | Unchanged |

The status values are the `LOV-LISTING` and `LOV-HOLDING` rows of TSD S5 T3.2 and the states are the DISPOSAL machine's (TSD S5 T4). The registration reference and the title status have no element of their own (GAP-2938; ASM-4834).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-SALEOFF, sale officer | Asset and disposal CRUA (TSD S5 T6.1): the primary role of the feature; records the registration on the case task and reads the asset |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Asset and disposal R: the second user of the feature, reads the asset, its listing and its status |
| RW-NPAMGR, RW-ENFORCE | Asset and disposal CRU: read, and correct a registration recorded in error |
| The further roles of the legacy read row and of TSD S5 T6.1 that hold R | Asset and disposal R, in scope |
| RW-HEADNPA, RW-HEADASL, RW-PRODHEAD | Asset and disposal RA: read, and approve where a sale-level limit is involved |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES | The matrix's right, under the same checks as a person |
| rwb-asset service identity | Runs the branch, evaluates the rule, writes the statuses and records; no grant on another schema and no `v_ace_*` grant |

The rights are the legacy permission table and the rows of TSD S5 T6.1, nothing wider: the legacy table gives the capability area R to the 30 roles of the read row and C to RW-ENFORCE, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR and SY-DATALOAD, and the matrix adds the officer's write through RW-SALEOFF CRUA and RW-NPAMGR CRU. DP-08 is not in the pattern set: the right is declared per operation and the guard is a service-template capability.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the behaviour behind the shapes of RWB-S5-E4029-CON.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated, with the holding status and the listing status of each asset (API-S5-001) | Asset and disposal, R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out with its title, its sale, its holding status and the status of its listing (API-S5-002) | Asset and disposal, R, scope applied | Not applicable |

No write operation is declared: the officer's registration is a case task and enters as a workflow signal, because no source gives the step an operation (GAP-2937; ASM-4833). `POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations` (API-S5-003) is rwb-valuation's and `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings` (API-S5-004) is the pricing story's. Errors: 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 422 with MSG-GEN-001, 503 when a library or a contract does not answer.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case state before the rule fires; faked |
| The case-move answer (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2939; ASM-4835)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | `ASSET_SOLD` with the rule and its version; on the workflow boundary it is the stage outcome the parent applies; faked |
| The document custody release (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2939; ASM-4835)) | `/api/recovery/document/v1` | P5 rwb-document | The release of the documents of the asset, with an idempotency key, in place of the legacy `document_custody` write (DP-05); faked |

Three rows, one hop each, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The custody release is a class C dependency in fact that the plan's empty C row does not carry (GAP-2939; ASM-4835).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is the take-on story's (TSD S5 T5.3) and no source gives the title transfer an event; the branch writes no outbox row and adds nothing to `rwb.asset.events.v1`. A build that publishes here fails the absence test.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The registration, the case state and the package in force arrive as signals of `AssetDisposalWorkflow`; the branch adds no consumer group and no inbox row.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one per case per stage, continues-as-new across the holding | `rwb-asset` in `rwb-recovery` | Input: case, route, asset, listing, package in force; signals: registration recorded, case state, package in force |
| `recordLandOfficeTransfer` | Activity, the title-transfer step | `rwb-asset` | Registration and case in; rule ID with version, the two statuses, the release answer and the case move out, one transaction |

No child workflow and no second queue. The activity name is a design choice of this story; the two boundary calls run on their owners' queues.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. R-DIS-52's ten working days run as a workflow timer and a case SLA, not as a Temporal Schedule. The service's single Schedule is JOB-19, the re-appraisal story's.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| asset | S5 (`rwb_asset`); read as S5 from TSD S5 T3.1 while the Ownership Map names only `listing` and `asset_sale` (GAP-2938; ASM-4834) | This story writes `holding_status` |
| listing | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | This story writes `status` |
| asset_sale | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | Read only here; written by the auction-round and proceeds stories |
| decision_record | PLT library in `rwb_asset` | One record per registration (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library in `rwb_asset` | The key of the repeated registration and of the release |

Not owned and never read as a table: `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task`, `timer` (P3), `document`, `document_custody` (P5), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` (P7), `proceeds` (P8), every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

The fakes are test-only; the release and move rows carry their placeholder until their owners confirm the names (GAP-2939; ASM-4835).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |

| REST | 2 provided, 3 consumed | The two asset reads on `/api/recovery/asset/v1`; the case state read, the case-move answer and the custody release; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | The registration and the case state are workflow signals |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 1 activity owned | `AssetDisposalWorkflow` and `recordLandOfficeTransfer` on `rwb-asset`; the release and case calls on their owners' queues; no Schedule |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset.title`; front end `src/modules/recovery/asset/TitleTransfer.tsx`, the fragment SCR-22 embeds, read only.

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is a prohibition here: the legacy `v_ace_npa_sale` read leaves the service and `asset_sale` carries the AMIS sale facts, while the custody release goes to rwb-document and never to its tables. DP-03 is the transaction rule of the step, DP-13 moves the base and DP-19 is how the screens reach the service.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` title branch | Workflow | Waits on the registration signal and the case state, loads the package in force, reports to the parent |
| `recordLandOfficeTransfer` | Activity | The one step: read, evaluate, record, release, write, answer |
| `TitleTransferEvaluator` | Service | R-DIS-52 on the state, the event and the asset type |
| `AssetDecisionRecordWriter` | Library adapter | One record per registration before any change (DP-03) |
| `TitleTransferWriter` | Repository | `listing.status` and `asset.holding_status` in one transaction with the idempotency row and the lock |
| `DocumentReleaseClient`, `CaseStateClient`, `CaseMoveAnswer` | Clients | The release, the state read and the answer, one hop, 2 s |
| `AssetController` | Controller | The two reads, the rights and the 400/401/403/404/422/503 map |
| `TitleTransfer` | React component | The registration, the statuses and the refusal states on SCR-22, read only |

**Database.** No Flyway file: the tables come with the DB story and the record and key are library objects created in `rwb_asset`; no column is added for the registration reference (GAP-2938; ASM-4834).

**Configuration.** The ten working days, the lists `LOV-HOLDING`, `LOV-LISTING` and `LOV-ASSET-TYPE` at their version (TSD S5 T3.2); the DISPOSAL package and its version from rwb-decision; the capability rows from rwb-access; the flag and the 2 s budget as platform configuration (ADR-020).

**Build steps.** (1) the title branch and its input record; (2) `TitleTransferEvaluator` with the property, vehicle and wrong-state paths (AC2, X3, X6); (3) `AssetDecisionRecordWriter` against the stub (AC1, AC4, X1); (4) `DocumentReleaseClient` with the key, the refusal and the timeout (AC2, X4); (5) `TitleTransferWriter` with the two statuses and the idempotency row (AC2, X5); (6) `CaseMoveAnswer` (AC2, AC3); (7) `AssetController` with the rights and the error map (AC1, X2); (8) the screen fragment through the route fake (AC1); (9) the boundary test (X8, BR4, BR5, BR6, BR8).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.asset.title-transfer-v1`; off means the registration is held, nothing is released and no move is answered.

**Done when.** §16 passes, a synthetic registration releases the documents, writes the two statuses, records the outcome and answers `ASSET_SOLD`, a repeat writes once, a refused release leaves nothing committed, a forced record failure changes nothing, no case, document or `v_ace_*` read exists, and the two screens answer through the composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required element of the registration or of a request is absent or invalid (X7) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Asset and disposal right reads or acts (X2) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record cannot be written before the statuses change (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-S5-001 | Carried from the legacy message set; it names the floor and the approval limit, which are the pricing story's, so no path here raises it | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | Carried from the legacy message set; it names the age of an appraisal, which is the re-appraisal story's, so no path here raises it | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |

The five IDs are the legacy and platform sets copied unchanged; no message is reworded and none is added. The Land Office rejection of X9 has no message in any source (GAP-2941; ASM-4837).

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-21 Asset list (loading, list) and SCR-22 Asset record (take-on, held, listed, sold) are served through the gateway-bff route (DP-19), which calls rwb-asset for the asset, its holding status and its listing, rwb-case for the route state and rwb-document for the custody state. This story fixes the rwb-asset answers only; the route and the field list are RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

The states it produces are the sold state of SCR-22 — the registration date, the sold status of the listing and the holding status of the asset — and the refusal, not-recorded, wrong-state, refused-release and vehicle states with MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003, MSG-GEN-001 and X4 to X6. Take-on and held are the take-on and holding stories'.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the ten working days, the statuses, the asset types and the rule rows stay reference data or rule rows with a version.
- No personal data in the schema, a workflow input or a log; a buyer is a code, the property address stays an ACE fact and every fixture is synthetic.
- The Land Office is never called: no interface, no file and no screen is built for it (BR3).
- The documents stay with rwb-document: no `document` or `document_custody` row is read or written here (DP-05, BR4).
- The case stays with rwb-case: no `recovery_case` or `assignment` row here (BR5).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: no `v_ace_*` grant and no ACE read (DP-05).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service (DP-13, DP-14).
- The record precedes the change, the release is idempotent and the repeat is deduped (DP-03, BR2, BR9).
- No retired element returns: no shared job table, no Quartz row, no monolith base, no data-lake export of a transfer.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 23 November 2026: the contract slice of RWB-E4-030, the baseline the proceeds-and-shortfall branch of rwb-asset builds against on Day 1. The baseline declares the two asset reads that answer SCR-21 and SCR-22 on `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13), the four consumed rows of rwb-case, rwb-payment and rwb-source-data (DP-05), the `ProceedsMatched` subscription on `rwb.payment.events.v1`, the decision-record element of DP-03, the rule-package element the branch evaluates, the rights, the error envelope and the fakes. No write operation and no published event are declared, because the step runs unattended and the service's owned event EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` belongs to the take-on story. Gaps: the consumed names are not published and no C row exists (GAP-2944; ASM-4840); EV-25's consumer list does not name this service (GAP-2945; ASM-4841); no S5-to-P1 edge exists for the two ACE facts (GAP-2946; ASM-4842); no element holds the residual (GAP-2947; ASM-4843); the balance application is FEAT-PAY-10's (GAP-2948; ASM-4844); the vendor fee has no element here (GAP-2949; ASM-4845); five adjacent rules own no legacy criterion (GAP-2950; ASM-4846); no requirement id (GAP-2951; ASM-4847); the screen states do not match the lists (GAP-2952; ASM-4848); DP-09 and DP-04 sit outside the pattern set (GAP-2953; ASM-4849). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the proceeds-and-shortfall capability of rwb-asset — its two reads, its one consumed event, its consumed operation rows, its decision-record and rule-package elements, its rights, its error envelope and its fakes — baselined and tagged before the build starts**, so that **the application story and every consumer of the sale outcome build and test on Day 1 against one fixed, versioned surface instead of guessing the shape of a neighbour's answer**.

This is the contract slice of legacy RWB-E4-030. It owns:

- the document that fixes `GET /assets` and `GET /assets/{assetId}` on base `/api/recovery/asset/v1`, with their parameters, their documented answer, their rights and their idempotency (DP-13);
- the subscription: EV-25 `ProceedsMatched` on `rwb.payment.events.v1` as `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1`, its CloudEvents envelope, its consumer group, its inbox row, its retry and `.dlt` topics and its dedupe;
- the four consumed rows: the rwb-case case-state read and case-move answer, the rwb-payment proceeds-fact activity and the rwb-source-data data product, each with its owner, its use and its placeholder where the name is not published (DP-05);
- the decision-record element and the library that carries it (DP-03);
- the rule-package element: the DISPOSAL package, its version and the two rows this branch evaluates, declared as a reference and not as a rule table of this service;
- the capability area, the rights and the error envelope of the operations it declares;
- the fakes and their documented answers, one per consumed row and one for the event;
- the naming and boundary rules: one base, one topic, one queue, no foreign schema, no monolith base, no Schedule for an event-started step.

It does not own: the branch behaviour, the rule evaluation, the sale write, the records and the case moves, which are RWB-S5-E4030-APP; the sale and its award, FEAT-AST-18 to FEAT-AST-20's stories; the balance application and the posting, which are FEAT-PAY-10 of rwb-payment (P8) (GAP-2948); the case of record and its states, rwb-case's (P3); the ACE facts, rwb-source-data's (P1); the rule package, rwb-decision's (P7); the screen field list and the composite route, which are RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

##### 2. Business rationale

A contract baseline is what lets the stories of a wave build at once. Without it the sale outcome would be written against whatever shape the payment service happened to publish that week, and the first integration would find the mismatches instead of the review. With it, the application story builds on Day 1 against a tagged document and its fakes, the sale, pricing and payment stories know what the sale and the residual must carry for the branch to run, and the consumers of the two reads know exactly which elements they can rely on.

The three rules the baseline applies:

- **the owner publishes, the consumer adapts.** Every consumed row and the event name its owner, and where the sources do not publish a name the row carries the placeholder rather than an invented path (GAP-2944; GAP-2946).
- **one hop, one budget.** Every consumed row is a single hop or one activity with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and no chain, which is ADR-020 and what the application story's exception paths assume.
- **additive only.** A new optional element is a minor version; a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version and a new document (C1).

The business outcome the baseline protects is the one FEAT-AST-21 of the FSD names: the sale money is applied and any residual is raised to the next decision. The baseline does not state that outcome, and no criterion here asserts a business value.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The Ownership Map rows are in force: S5 owns `GET /assets`, `GET /assets/{assetId}`, `GET /assets/{assetKey}`, `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings`, `POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings` and `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds`; `asset_sale` and `listing` are S5's tables.
- The naming is fixed: schema `rwb_asset`, login `rwb_asset`, base `/api/recovery/asset/v1`, topic `rwb.asset.events.v1` with `.retry` and `.dlt`, task queue `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.asset` (Template and Rules v1 §R4).
- The published shapes of the declared reads are the API Specification v4: `AssetPage` and `Asset`, with the sale, the fee, the proceeds state and the residual named by the baseline (API-S5-001, API-S5-002).
- EV-25 `ProceedsMatched` is the event of Payments and posting on `rwb.payment.events.v1`, with an envelope, an event id and an idempotency key (Event and Messaging Design v4, EV-25; Template and Rules v1 §R4).
- The owned event of this service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn`, the take-on story's; no event is published by this capability.
- The platform CON stories are published: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for the decision record (DP-03) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the composite route (DP-19). DP-09 and DP-04 are outside the pattern set, so the inbox and the package load are declared as platform capabilities with no new H row (GAP-2953; ASM-4849).
- No approval is needed to publish a Draft baseline; the document is baselined by this story's own review and the build waits only for its tag (ASM-4850).

##### 4. Flow

1. The author drafts the baseline from the Ownership Map, the TSD S5 T-A.1 operations, the TSD S5 T3.1 tables, the lists of T3.2 and the event catalogue.
2. Every read is declared with its method, path, request, documented answer, rights, idempotency and error set; no write operation is declared.
3. The one consumed event is declared with its topic, its event name, its envelope, its consumer group, its inbox row, its retry and `.dlt` topics and its dedupe rule.
4. Every consumed row is declared with its owner, its use, its budget and a placeholder where the name is not published.
5. The decision-record element is declared with the library that carries it, and the rule-package element with its owner, its version and the two rows the branch evaluates.
6. The fakes are declared with their documented answers, one per consumed row, one for the event, one for the composite route and one for the record chain.
7. The schema, the open and closed lists and the compatibility check are published; a breaking change fails the check.
8. The document goes to review as Draft; the reviewers are the owners of the consumed rows and the tech lead of the service.
9. On the review's close the document is tagged and baselined; the application story starts against the tag and the fakes. A defect that needs a shape change is raised against this document and the code never moves ahead of it.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A consumer asks for a shape the sources do not publish | The row carries the placeholder and its gap; no path and no field is invented | C2, C4 |
| X2 | A change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element | The compatibility check fails, the version becomes a new major and the document is re-reviewed | C1 |
| X3 | A declared read reaches another service's data or base | The review refuses the baseline and the boundary test fails the build | C3, C7 |
| X4 | A consumed row has no fake, or its fake has no documented answer | The baseline is not tagged and the application story cannot start | C6 |
| X5 | The rights of a read are not one of the rows of the access matrix | The read is not declared and its error set is incomplete | C3, C5 |
| X6 | An owner changes its documented answer after the tag | The owner publishes a new version, this document follows with a minor or major version and the fakes are re-cut | C1, C6 |
| X7 | The event and a consumed row claim different owners or topics | The owner in the Ownership Map keeps the topic and the row is corrected | C6, C7 |

X1 to X3 are the paths of an incomplete source, X4 to X6 the paths of a baseline moving under a build, and X7 the naming boundary of the event.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs no build, no live service and no approval; starts on Day 1 and is finished before the application story's first line |
| Negotiable | The wording, the order of the sections and the fake data are this story's choice; the paths, the owners, the base, the envelope, the error set and the element names are fixed by their sources |
| Valuable | The wave 3 stories build at once against one tagged surface and the first integration finds behaviour, not shape |
| Estimable | One document, two provided reads, one subscription, four consumed rows, two library elements, ten fakes and one compatibility check |
| Small | Finished inside a week; the review is the only gate |
| Testable | Every criterion is a document check that runs in the contract suite, plus the compatibility check on the published schema |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the proceeds-and-shortfall capability

  Scenario: C1 The baseline validates and only additive changes pass (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published schema and the open and closed lists of the baseline
    When a change removes, renames, retypes or newly requires an element
    Then the compatibility check fails and the change needs a new major version
    And a change that adds an optional element passes as a minor version

  Scenario: C2 The elements and the closed lists are published as declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the baseline document of this story
    When the element list, the required and optional flags and the closed lists are read
    Then every element carries its type, its nullability and its source
    And every closed list is referenced with its identifier and its version and is not enumerated in code
    And the residual, its route and its D9 hand-off carry the placeholder and its gap identifier because no element holds them

  Scenario: C3 The two reads are declared with their rights and no write is declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operations the baseline provides on base /api/recovery/asset/v1
    When the method, path, documented answer, right and idempotency of each are read
    Then GET /assets and GET /assets/{assetId} carry the Asset and disposal right R with scope applied and no idempotency
    And no write operation is declared, because the step runs unattended inside the workflow
    And POST /assets/{assetId}/listings, POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings and POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds are named as other stories' and are not declared

  Scenario: C4 The consumed rows carry their owners, their budgets and their placeholders (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed operation table of the baseline
    When the rows of rwb-case, rwb-payment and rwb-source-data are read
    Then each row names its owner, its use and its 2 s budget
    And where the name is not published the row carries the placeholder and the gap identifier and no path

  Scenario: C5 The error envelope is declared per read (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the operations the baseline provides
    When the error set and the rights of each read are read
    Then the error set names 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503 in one problem envelope
    And the capability area and the right of each read are the rows of the access matrix
    And MSG-P7-003 is declared as the record-chain message and not as a message of a read

  Scenario: C6 The event, the decision-record, rule-package and fake elements are declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the baseline document
    When the subscription, the decision-record element, the rule-package element and the fake table are read
    Then the subscription names EV-25 ProceedsMatched, the topic rwb.payment.events.v1, the event rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1 and the consumer group rwb-asset with its inbox, retry and .dlt topics
    And the decision-record element names RWB-PLT-E1027-CON as its library and the transaction it joins
    And the rule-package element names the DISPOSAL package, its owner, its version in force and the two rules, and declares no rule row
    And every consumed row and the event have a fake with a documented answer, including the stopped stub, the stale proceeds fact, the unmatched fee and the repeated event

  Scenario: C7 The naming and the boundary of the baseline hold (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the base, the topic, the queue and the schema of the baseline
    When the document is checked against the naming rule and the ownership map
    Then the base /api/recovery/asset/v1, the queue rwb-asset, the schema rwb_asset and the topic rwb.asset.events.v1 are the only ones declared as this service's own
    And rwb.payment.events.v1 is declared as consumed and never as this service's
    And no foreign schema, no foreign topic, no monolith base /api/recovery/v1 and no Schedule for an event-started step is declared
    And no event is published by this capability
```

The seven criteria are new to this run and are tagged as such: they test the contract deliverable only — the schema, the elements, the lists, the reads, the consumed rows, the rights, the envelope, the subscription, the two library elements, the fakes and the boundary. No criterion states a business outcome, and none asserts that a rule fires or that a case moves.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One owner per operation, event and table: the baseline declares only the rows the Ownership Map gives to S5 and names every other row with its owner | Ownership Map; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | A consumed row with no published name carries the placeholder and its gap, and never an invented path | Template and Rules v1 §R9; GAP-2944 |
| BR3 | The baseline is additive: a new optional element is a minor version, and a removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element is a major version | ADR-020; C1 |
| BR4 | Every consumed row is one hop or one activity with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and no chain | ADR-020 |
| BR5 | Exactly one event is consumed and none is published: EV-25 `ProceedsMatched` is the proceeds fact and EV-22 `AssetTakenOn` is another story's | Event and Messaging Design v4 (EV-22, EV-25); Architecture v5 slide 13 |
| BR6 | The decision record is written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the caller's transaction before any change, and its element is declared once for the service | DP-03 |
| BR7 | The rule package is referenced, never redefined: the DISPOSAL package, its version and the two rules are rwb-decision's rows and no rule table of this service is declared | DP-04 (not claimed); GAP-2953 |
| BR8 | No business value is declared in the baseline: every list, code, amount and threshold is referenced with its identifier and version | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17); legacy Guardrails |
| BR9 | No personal data in any element, fake or example of the baseline; a buyer is a code, never a person | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR10 | The baseline never declares another service's table, operation or topic as its own, and a check fails the build where one names it | DP-01, DP-13, DP-14 |

##### 9. State transitions

The document itself is the object of this section: the lifecycle of the contract baseline.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | The draft is complete | Every read, row, element, fake and error is declared | Draft |
| Draft | The review is opened | The owners of the consumed rows are named as reviewers | In review |
| In review | The review closes with no open comment | The compatibility check passes | Baselined, tagged for the application story |
| In review | A comment needs a shape change | The change is applied to the draft | Draft |
| Baselined | An additive change is approved | New optional element only, the check passes | Baselined, new minor version |
| Baselined | A breaking change is approved | A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element | Draft of a new major version, and the consumers are notified |
| Baselined | An owner changes its answer | X6 | Draft of a new minor or major version, and the fakes are re-cut |

| Step | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Being authored | A consumed row has no published name | X1 | The row carries the placeholder and the gap and the draft continues |
| In review | A read reaches a foreign schema, base or topic | X3 | The baseline is refused |
| Ready to tag | A consumed row or the event has no fake | X4 | Not tagged, the review reopens |
| Ready to tag | The event and a row disagree on the owner or the topic | X7 | The row is corrected and the review reopens |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-asset (S5); base `/api/recovery/asset/v1` (DP-13). These are the reads that answer SCR-21 and SCR-22.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/assets` | AssetPage out, filtered by type, status and region, paginated, with the sale and the proceeds state of each asset (API-S5-001) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/assets/{assetId}` | Asset of status 200 out, with its sale, its fee, its proceeds state and its residual (API-S5-002) | Asset and disposal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

No write operation is declared: the step is event-started and unattended, and its writes belong to the `applyProceeds` activity. `POST /assets/{assetId}/listings` (API-S5-004) and `POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds` (API-S5-005) are the pricing and round stories' and `POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations` (API-S5-003) is rwb-valuation's; the `{assetKey}` variants of the Ownership Map have no API Specification entry and are not declared. The error envelope: 400 for a malformed request, 401 for an unauthenticated call, 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope asset, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for a missing or invalid parameter and 503 when the decision library or a consumed boundary does not answer, in one problem document with a code, a message ID and a correlation reference. The residual element of the asset answer carries its placeholder until its owner names it (GAP-2947; ASM-4843).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family (activity on queue `rwb-case`) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference and the case state the rules check before they fire; faked |
| The case-move answer (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2944; ASM-4840)) | rwb-case (P3), Temporal | P3 rwb-case | The stage outcome with its rule version, applied by the parent; faked |
| The proceeds-fact activity (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2944; ASM-4840)) | queue `rwb-payment` | P8 rwb-payment | The proceeds, the vendor fee and the balance state, in place of the legacy `v_ace_account` read (DP-05); faked |
| The account and NPA-sale data product (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2946; ASM-4842)) | rwb-source-data (P1) | P1 rwb-source-data | The account balance and the NPA sale facts, in place of the legacy `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_npa_sale` reads (DP-05); faked |

Each row is one hop or one activity, 2 s, a retry once for a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). Where a name is not published the row carries the placeholder and no path, so the consumer adapts at the tag rather than inventing a surface (BR2). The plan carries no C row for this pair; the legacy "Depends on FEAT-PAY-10" is a consumed contract and not a build gate (GAP-2944; ASM-4840).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The owned event of this service is EV-22 `AssetTakenOn`, published by the take-on story, and the sale event belongs to the sale and auction stories. This capability writes no outbox row, adds nothing to `rwb.asset.events.v1` and a build that publishes here fails the absence test (BR5).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Element | Declared value |
|---|---|
| Event | EV-25 `ProceedsMatched`, payload proceedsId, caseId and amount |
| Topic and event name | `rwb.payment.events.v1`, event `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1`, with the `.retry` and `.dlt` topics of the platform |
| Envelope | CloudEvents, schema version, event id, idempotency key, correlation reference, no personal data |
| Subscription | Consumer group `rwb-asset`, inbox row in `rwb_asset`, then a signal to `AssetDisposalWorkflow` |
| Dedupe and failure | A repeated event id or key is ignored and counted (R-UNI-40); after the retry limit the event goes to `.dlt` with its owner |
| Versioning | The consumer accepts the current and the previous schema version |

EV-25 stands as published by Payments and posting with "Case and workflow" as its only named consumer, while Architecture v5 slide 13 gives S5 an event subscription to P8; the catalogue slide wins under R-PREC and the subscription is declared here (GAP-2945; ASM-4841). No other topic is consumed by this capability: the litigation events of the matrix's S4 column serve other steps of the service.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AssetDisposalWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, continues-as-new | `rwb-asset` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the route, the asset reference, the sale reference and the rule package in force; signals: `ProceedsMatched`, residual computed and the package in force |
| `applyProceeds` | Activity, the proceeds-and-shortfall step | `rwb-asset` | The case, the sale and the proceeds fact in; the rule IDs with their versions, the sale outcome, the residual and the stage outcome out, in one transaction |

This baseline fixes the input and signal elements and the one activity it adds, and it declares no child workflow and no second queue. The activity name is a design choice of the application story, and the baseline carries it so the workflow's history stays stable.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step is event-started from the inbox, so the baseline declares no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job for it. The single Schedule of the service is JOB-19, which the re-appraisal story owns and which is not declared here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| asset_sale | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The settled sale; the baseline declares the elements of the sale answer, not its schema |
| listing | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The listing of the sale; the baseline declares the elements it reads |
| asset | S5 (`rwb_asset`) | The asset of the sale; the baseline declares the elements it reads |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The local decision record of DP-03, declared through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| idempotency_key, inbox | PLT library, created in `rwb_asset` | The dedupe of the event and the key of a repeated call |

The baseline declares no column, no index and no migration, and declares no table of another owner: `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task` and `timer` (P3), `proceeds` (P8), `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` and `approval` (P7), `valuation` (S1), `document` (P5), `deviation` (S8) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) are named by their owner and never declared here. No residual column exists and none is declared (GAP-2947; ASM-4843).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case state and case-move fake | The case states `ASSET_SOLD` and `PROCEEDS_APPLIED` of the fixture cases; the two moves accepted and one refused | C4, C6 |
| rwb-payment proceeds-fact fake | A posted sale with its fee matched; a fee with no match; a stale fact with its date; no answer inside 2 s | C4, C6 |
| rwb-payment `ProceedsMatched` event fake | One event; the same event id twice; an event with no sale; an event past the retry budget | C4, C6 |
| rwb-source-data data-product fake | The account balance and the NPA sale of the fixture cases; a stale business date | C4, C6 |
| rwb-decision rule-package fake | The DISPOSAL package at its version in force with the two rules | C6 |
| Decision-record stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | C5, C6 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-21 and SCR-22 answer for case `RC-2026-000593` | C2, C6 |
| Read answer fake | The asset answer with its sale, its fee, its proceeds state and its residual, and one with the residual absent | C2, C3 |
| Placeholder fake | A consumed row answered with the placeholder name and no path | C2, C4 |

Each fake answers only what its owner documents, and a fake that answers more than the document fails the review. The names that are not published are stubbed from the documents and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-2944; GAP-2946).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 2 consumed | The two asset reads on `/api/recovery/asset/v1`; the case-state read and the case-move answer; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 1 consumed | EV-25 `ProceedsMatched` on `rwb.payment.events.v1` as `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1`, with the inbox of `rwb-asset`, the retry topic and `.dlt` |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 1 activity | `AssetDisposalWorkflow` and `applyProceeds` on `rwb-asset`; the consumed proceeds-fact and case activities on their owners' queues; no Schedule |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Document.** `04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-S5 rwb-asset (Asset)/RWB S5 E4030 CON Apply proceeds and raise the shortfall - contract v1.md`, with the schema and the examples in the service contract folder of RWB-S5-E4030.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Sections and owners of the review.** The document is written in nine parts: the provided reads, the consumed rows, the published and consumed events, the workflow and its activity, the schedules, the tables, the fakes, the call-type summary and the lifecycle. Each part is reviewed by the owner of the rows it names, and the tag waits for every reviewer.

**Compatibility check.** The schema is published as JSON Schema with `additionalProperties: false` on the closed objects, and the check runs on three inputs: the previous tag, the new draft and a corpus of recorded answers from the fakes. A removal, a rename, a type change or a new required element fails the check and forces a new major version (C1, BR3).

**Open shapes carried into the tag.** Three shapes are carried as placeholders and not invented: the residual and its D9 hand-off (GAP-2947; ASM-4843), the names of the consumed rows (GAP-2944; GAP-2946) and the vendor-fee match of the sale answer (GAP-2949; ASM-4845). A placeholder is a declared forthcoming shape, not a permission to guess.

**Subscription.** The inbox and the envelope are platform capabilities of the event platform; the subscription is declared here and claims no new H row because DP-09 is outside the pattern set (GAP-2953; ASM-4849). The consumer group name, the retry and `.dlt` topics and the 2 s budget are platform configuration (ADR-020).

**Done when.** The seven criteria pass, the reviewers of the three consumed owners and of the event have closed their comments, the compatibility check passes on the tag, the fakes are published with their documented answers, and RWB-S5-E4030-APP can start against the tag with no open shape question.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Asset and disposal right calls one of the declared reads | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required or invalid parameter of a declared read is supplied | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-S5-001 | A declared read carries a sale price or a floor under the approver's limit | The floor is {pct} of fair market value, below the {limit} this level may approve. |
| MSG-S5-002 | A declared read carries an appraisal more than a year old | The appraisal is from {date}, more than a year ago. Order a new one before pricing. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written, as the decision-record element declares it | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| Document rule | A change fails the compatibility check | A breaking change needs a new major version. |
| Document rule | A consumed row has no published name | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2944; ASM-4840). |

The five message IDs are carried from the service and platform sets and are declared only as the envelope rows of the reads in this baseline; the two document rules are checks of this story and are not service messages.

##### 15. Screens and states

The baseline serves SCR-21 Asset list and SCR-22 Asset record through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). What this story fixes is the element list of the declared responses and the empty, loading, refused, not-recorded, wrong-state and stale-proceeds states the route can show from this service's answers. The route itself, its merge order and its field list are RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the screens' transitions are the application story's.

No screen is built here and no state machine is declared: the screen section of a contract story lists the elements the screens read and the states their answers can carry. The legacy screen states and the holding lists do not match one for one, and the contract declares the `LOV-HOLDING` and `LOV-LISTING` identifiers rather than their values (GAP-2952; ASM-4848).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the baseline: the package, its version, the fee, the codes and every threshold are referenced with their identifier and version, never enumerated as a constant or a default.
- No personal data in any element, fake, example or log: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the baseline declares no `v_ace_*` element and no ACE table, and the account and NPA-sale facts appear only as the P1 row (DP-05).
- The case stays with rwb-case and the money with rwb-payment: no `recovery_case` element and no `proceeds` element is declared as this service's own.
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; no document, module or test names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no monolith base `/api/recovery/v1`, no shared job table, no Schedule for an event-started step.
- Additive only: a breaking change needs a new major version and a re-tag, and the code never moves ahead of the document (BR3).
