These seven criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only. They restate no business outcome owned by RWB-S6-E5026-APP and copy no criterion of the legacy story, whose two criteria stay with the app story word for word.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The lot and account records are rwb-debtsale's, and the contract declares their properties, lists and required flags on the lot and account elements only | TSD S6 T3.1, T3.2; context pack ownership rows |
| BR2 | The decision record is declared as an element written before anything is served, through the local library on the shared topic; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; TSD S6 T2; legacy AC1 and AC2 |
| BR3 | The masked tape is rwb-document's object: the contract declares its reference and masking-check outcome as consumed and declares no tape property copied into `rwb_debtsale` | DP-01; ASM-4901 |
| BR4 | The buyer panel and the admission are rwb-partner's: the contract declares them as consumed and declares no `partner` or `partner_user` property and no partner write | R-DS-13; ASM-4900 |
| BR5 | The case move is answered and not written: the contract declares the state read and the answer, and declares no `recovery_case` property and no case row write | TSD S6 T4; ASM-4902 |
| BR6 | This step declares no event: `LotAwarded` (EV-23) and `AccountsTransferred` are other stories', and the opening is a route state and an answer | TSD S6 T5.3; context pack event row; ASM-4904 |
| BR7 | The vocabulary is closed: the four lists are published as enumerated values and no list value is a constant of the code | TSD S6 T3.2; FSD S6 BR-S6-004 |
| BR8 | No unmasked personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: the account element carries the masked borrower reference only, and the masking is the PII service's | REQ-S6-003; FSD S6 A2.3.1; Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR9 | One REST base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service; the document never declares another service's base or topic as its own | DP-13, DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR10 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version | Platform API rule (ADR-020) |
| BR11 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-debtsale; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | DP-01, DP-11 |
| BR12 | The rule rows of R-DS-10 to R-DS-13, the masking rules and the non-disclosure condition are governed in rwb-decision and named here, never declared here | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; ASM-4901 |
| BR13 | No lot status of the opening is declared as a property value: `LOV-LOT-STATUS` carries no data-room value and no source names one | TSD S6 T3.2; ASM-4903 |
| BR14 | The partner channel is the edge's: the document records the buyer route behind the partner gateway and declares no gateway element of its own | Architecture v5 slide 8; ASM-4905 |

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of this document, not of a lot:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The read, the three elements, the four lists, the consumed rows, the right, the record and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, the buyer panel of rwb-partner, the wave 3 harness and the rwb-document, rwb-partner and rwb-case owners accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example an optional account or tape field | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or a list value changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | The absence tests of AC4 and AC7 fail: a `v_ace_*` path, a `document`, `partner` or `recovery_case` property, an event, a second topic, a Schedule or an unmasked identifier | In review |

The route machine the document describes is the app story's and rwb-case's: `TAPE_PREPARED` to `DATA_ROOM_OPEN` under R-DS-13 on the case of record. This baseline fixes the vocabulary of `LOV-LOT-STATUS` and the move it names, and moves no lot and no case.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-debtsale | Owns the OpenAPI document and the contract tables; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version, the partner-channel route of the read and the correction of the plan rows the baseline consumes |
| Consuming teams (the app story, the buyer panel of rwb-partner, the wave 3 harness and the owners of rwb-document, rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| Platform library owner | Owns the error envelope, the naming rule, the decision-record library and the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1` topic this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in an answer, an element or a fake, and that the tape reference carries no unmasked identifier |

The per-service login behind the security scheme is named "the rwb-debtsale login (DP-02)" and is not part of this baseline. The buyer's entry through the partner gateway is the edge story's and rwb-partner's, and this baseline declares it as the route of the right only (ASM-4905).

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| `DataRoom` element | The lot element, one account element per tape row and the tape element |
| Lot element | The properties of DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-030: `id`, `lot_no`, `cut_off_date`, `segment`, `reserve_price`, `buyer_partner_id`, `buyer_class`, `signing_date`, `approval_authority`, `payment_terms` and `status` |
| Account element | The properties of DF-SAL-031 to DF-SAL-037: `id`, `lot_id`, `account_id`, `borrower_code`, `outstanding`, `selling_price` and `put_back_status`, with `borrower_code` masked |
| Tape element | The document reference of the masked tape and its masking-check outcome, read from P5 and never copied |
| Lists | `LOV-SEGMENT` (RETAIL, SSME, CORPORATE), `LOV-BUYER-CLASS` (AMC, NON_AMC), `LOV-LOT-STATUS` (BUILDING, OFFERED, AWARDED, TRANSFERRED, CLOSED) and `LOV-PUTBACK` (NONE, CLAIMED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED), published as enumerations and read at their version |
| Decision record | DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 through the local library, written before anything is served (DP-03) |
| Not declared here | `document` (P5), `partner` and `partner_user` (S9), `recovery_case` and `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) |
| Consumed fields with no source | The operation names of the tape read, the panel read and the case-move answer: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2978; ASM-4899, ASM-4900, ASM-4901, ASM-4902) |
| Unnamed by the sources | The lot properties the partner read withholds before the award, and the lot status of the opening: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2978; ASM-4903) |

The field-level types, lengths and required flags of the added elements are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the element names, the vocabulary of AC3 and the optionality rule of BR10. **No new table, no new column and no migration** is declared by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-debtsale (S6); base `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/partner/data-room/{lotId}` | `DataRoom` of status 200 out, with the lot element, its tape and its account rows (API-S6-004) | Partner portal, right R, scope applied | Not declared |

The operation answers 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope lot and 503, each with the error envelope and one message ID of section 14, and the read declares no `Idempotency-Key`. The operation ID is that of TSD S6 T-A.1 and the path is that of the target base. API-S6-001, API-S6-002, API-S6-003 and API-S6-005 belong to the lot builder, the approval, the award and the bid stories of this service, and none of the four is declared here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| The read of the masked data tape (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2978; ASM-4901)) | `/api/recovery/document/v1` | P5 rwb-document | The document reference, the tape rows and the masking-check outcome of the lot; faked |
| The buyer-panel read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2978; ASM-4900)) | `/api/recovery/partner/v1` | S9 rwb-partner | The admitted buyers and the presence of their signed non-disclosure agreement, as R-DS-13 names them; faked |
| The case read, and the case-move answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2978; ASM-4902)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The route state and the move `DATA_ROOM_OPEN` with the rule ID and its version; on the workflow boundary the move is the stage outcome the parent applies; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The three rows are contract dependencies of class C that the plan's C row does not carry (GAP-2978; ASM-4899).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service owns `rwb.debtsale.events.v1`, and its event set carries `LotAwarded` (EV-23) and `AccountsTransferred`. The opening of a data room is not in that event set, so this baseline declares no event for the step, no payload and no consumer, and names the two events as the award and transfer stories'. The absence test of AC7 fails a build that adds one (ASM-4904).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The service's consumed event is `ProceedsMatched` from `rwb.payment.events.v1`; it belongs to the settlement step, not to this one, and the opening is triggered by the tape fact read on the rwb-document contract and by the case signal the parent forwards. This baseline therefore declares no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox of its own (ASM-4904).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DebtSaleWorkflow` | Workflow, a saga with the transfer as its pivot, the child of `CaseWorkflow` | `rwb-debtsale` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | The saga that hosts the data-room step; its input, its signals and its outcome for the parent are declared, not built |
| `openBuyerDataRoom` | Activity, the one data-room step | `rwb-debtsale` | The case, the lot and the tape fact in; the rule ID with its version, the opening and the case move out |

The service's workflow is `DebtSaleWorkflow` and the Temporal and Drools slides fix it as a saga on `rwb-debtsale` with the transfer as its pivot; the activity name is a target design choice fixed by no source. No activity is registered by this story, and no Schedule is declared for it.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step runs from the tape fact of the lot and from the case signal the parent forwards; the "per cycle" clock of R-DS-13 is the monthly cycle opened under R-DS-01 by RWB-S6-E5023-APP, and this baseline declares no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table for it.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| debt_sale_lot | S6 (`rwb_debtsale`) | The lot of accounts offered to debt buyers; the table the lot element of the answer reads |
| debt_sale_account | S6 (`rwb_debtsale`) | An account in a lot; the table the account element of the answer reads |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_debtsale` | The local hash-linked record of the rule outcome (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_debtsale` | The key of the repeated trigger and the answer it holds |
| outbox_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_debtsale` | The service's outbox; this step declares no row of it (BR6) |

`document` (P5), `partner` and `partner_user` (S9), `recovery_case` and `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) are not owned by this baseline; it names them only as answers and rule versions of their owners, and no foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-document tape fake | The masked tape `TAPE-2026-000026` of lot `LOT-2026-000026` with its check passed and its tape rows; the same tape with an unmasked identifier found; a tape of another lot; no answer beyond 2 s | AC1, AC2, AC4, AC6 |
| rwb-partner panel fake | The panel with partner `PT-000026` admitted and its agreement signed; a panel with no signature; a partner out of scope; no answer beyond 2 s | AC4, AC5, AC6 |
| rwb-case state and move fake | The state `TAPE_PREPARED` for the cases of `LOT-2026-000026`, an accepted move `DATA_ROOM_OPEN` and a refused move | AC4, AC6 |
| rwb-decision rule-package fake | The DEBTSALE route set at its version in force with R-DS-10 to R-DS-13 | AC6 |
| Local decision-record library stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | AC6 |
| Partner portal access fake | A buyer and a role that hold the Partner portal right, and one that does not | AC5, AC6 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The operation names of the tape and panel reads and of the case-move answer carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-2978; ASM-4899 to -4).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 provided, 3 consumed | The data-room read on `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1`; the tape read, the panel read and the case read with the move answer; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | No event of this step; the decision record reaches the ledger on `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the library and is not an event of this service |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 1 activity declared, 0 registered | `DebtSaleWorkflow` and `openBuyerDataRoom` on `rwb-debtsale`; no Schedule |
| File | None | No file is read, built or delivered here; the tape is a document reference of P5 and the buyer file of INT-25 is delivered on the partner channel (ASM-4901, ASM-4905) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**The CON declares shapes and moves nothing.** It writes no code, no migration and no table, and changes no lot, no case, no tape, no panel and no rule package. What it publishes is one OpenAPI 3.1 document, nine contract tables and six fakes.

**Deliverables.** The additive document `openapi/rwb-debtsale-v1.yaml` with the data-room read, the `DataRoom`, lot, account and tape elements, the four lists as published enumerations, the contract README rows for the consumed rows and their placeholders, and the six WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-13 moves the base of the read and nothing else. DP-19 is the screen rule of PRT-05: the screen reads a composed answer and never a service directly; the edge baseline of RWB-PLT-N001-CON fixes the route and the screen model, the staff path is gateway-bff and the buyer path is the partner gateway, and the buyer path has no plan row (ASM-4905). DP-03 is declared as the element written before anything is served. DP-09 is not in the pattern set of this key and no event is declared, so no outbox library row is added (ASM-4904).

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds the two H rows `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` for DP-03 and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` for DP-19, which the plan's build list for this key already carries, and leaves out DP-09 because the step publishes no event. The three consumed rows are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata row (GAP-2978; ASM-4899).

**Build steps**

1. Write the data-room read and validate the additive rule and the error set of AC1 in the pipeline.
2. Write the `DataRoom`, lot, account and tape elements of AC2 with the required flags and the no-personal-data test.
3. Write the four lists of AC3 and the vocabulary test.
4. Record the three consumed rows of AC4 with their owners, budgets and placeholders.
5. Record the Partner portal right, the buyer channel, the legacy permission row and the error envelope of AC5.
6. Record the decision-record element of AC6 and validate it against the library schema.
7. Publish the six fakes of AC6 and the drift test.
8. Record the naming baseline, the tables and the boundary of AC7, then tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI document validates in the pipeline, the contract tests pass, the fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, the no-personal-data test and the event-absence test are green, and the app story, the buyer panel of rwb-partner and the wave 3 harness have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S6-001 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names an open deviation of an account, which is the eligibility story's, so no path of this step raises it | {account} has an open deviation and cannot be sold. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required path or filter value of the read is absent or invalid, or a body fails schema validation | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role or the buyer lacks the Partner portal right the operation declares | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before anything is served | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The tape or the data product behind it is stale after a late or failed batch (VR-S6-004-1); the check is the owner's and this service holds no batch-status read | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The five IDs are contract elements and the text is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new one is added. MSG-P1-001 is carried because it is in the message set of this feature, and the freshness check itself belongs to the data product owner and to rwb-document (ASM-4901).

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves PRT-05 Data room in its loading state and its three legacy states — **Admitted**, **bidding** and **closed** — all through the edge (DP-19). The route composes the answer of this service for the lot, its tape and its account rows with the rwb-partner panel for the buyer and its admission and with rwb-case for the case; this baseline fixes the rwb-debtsale answer only, and the composite route specification, the buyer channel and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and to the edge stories (ASM-4905). The screen itself is the buyer panel of rwb-partner on the buyer path behind the partner gateway. The refusal, not-recorded and stale-data states the app story shows read the messages of section 14 on the same route.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the four lists, the reserve, the terms, the masking rules and the rule rows stay data, reference data or the route set, never a schema default or an enumeration member of the code.
- No unmasked personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: the account element carries the masked borrower reference only, the no-personal-data test fails a build that adds a name, an address, a contact value or an identity number, and every example is synthetic (REQ-S6-003).
- The tape stays with rwb-document, the panel with rwb-partner and the case with rwb-case: the document declares no `v_ace_*` path, no `document`, `partner`, `partner_user` or `recovery_case` property and no write of those tables (BR3, BR4, BR5).
- The document lists only operations owned by rwb-debtsale; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided (DP-01, DP-11).
- One base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- Nothing retired is reintroduced: the absence tests fail a build that declares an event, a second topic, a Schedule, a Quartz row or a shared job table.
- The error envelope, the naming rule and the decision-record library come from the platform; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

The two legacy criteria are kept word for word with their origin tag; the target keeps them as one step of `DebtSaleWorkflow` on queue `rwb-debtsale` that opens the room on the masked tape of the tape step (R-DS-13), reads the admitted buyer panel on the rwb-partner contract, answers the case move to rwb-case and serves API-S6-004 on base `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1` (DP-13) behind the partner channel and the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), with the outcome recorded through the local decision-record library (DP-03). The plan's C row for this key is None although the step consumes three other services, the partner channel and the lot status of the opening have no source, and the tape belongs to RWB-S6-E5025-APP (GAP-2977; ASM-4899 to -7). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **debt sale officer (RW-DEBTSALE)**, I want **the Workbench to publish the lot and the masked tape to the data room for qualified buyers**, so that **debt sales run on approved lots and masked data, instead of on spreadsheets, and the 45-day debt sale turnaround is measured on the decision log and the Workbench records**.

This is the data-room slice of legacy RWB-E5-026. It owns:

- the two legacy criteria, copied verbatim with their origin tag, and the rules, messages and screen they rest on;
- one step of `DebtSaleWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-debtsale` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, the stage child of `CaseWorkflow` owned by rwb-case (context pack, Temporal and Drools slides 12 and 13; Architecture v5 slide 19);
- the evaluation of R-DS-13 on the tape the tape step prepared, and the reading of the tape branch R-DS-10, R-DS-11 and R-DS-12 that RWB-S6-E5025-APP runs;
- the read of the lot and its accounts from `debt_sale_lot` and `debt_sale_account` in `rwb_debtsale` (DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-037), and the read of the tape and its masking-check result on the rwb-document contract;
- the read of the admitted buyer panel of the lot on the rwb-partner contract, which is who "qualified buyers" are under R-DS-13;
- the local decision record of the outcome, written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON before anything is served (DP-03);
- the answer to rwb-case for the case move `DATA_ROOM_OPEN`, with the rule ID and the version that produced it;
- the read API-S6-004 `GET /partner/data-room/{lotId}` on base `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1`, on the partner channel through the partner gateway and on the staff channel through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-13, DP-19), serving PRT-05 Data room.

It does not own: the published shape of the read, the `DataRoom`, lot and account elements, the case-move answer, the error set and the fakes, which are RWB-S6-E5026-CON; the building of the masked tape and the masking check, which are RWB-S6-E5025-APP with rwb-document (P5) and the PII service; the buyer panel, the KYC and licensing check and the non-disclosure agreement, which are rwb-partner's (S9) and RWB-S6-E6002-APP's; the case of record, its route states, the parent `CaseWorkflow` and the case timers, which are rwb-case (P3); the bidding, the award, the transfer and their events, which are RWB-S6-E6004-APP, RWB-S6-E6005-APP and RWB-S6-E6007-APP; the rule rows and their versioning, which are governed in rwb-decision (P7); and the deployment of the build, which is the operations story of this legacy key.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy step published the lot and the masked tape to the data room and wrote the decision log entry. The FSD keeps the objective and the metric unchanged: the debt sale turnaround is measured on the decision log and the Workbench records, reviewed monthly, with a target of 45 days (FSD S6 A2.4.1), and the feature runs unattended with the debt sale officer as also-user (FSD S6 A2.4.3.3). The requirement is REQ-S6-003, "The data room holds a masked data tape, and no unmasked personal data leaves the bank" (FSD S6 Requirements served).

What D-RCV-60 changes is who owns the lot, the tape, the buyers and the case. In the monolith one process read the lot, the tape and the buyer list in one schema. In the target:

- **the lot and its accounts are this service's.** Architecture v5 gives rwb-debtsale "lots, data room, buyer terms, bids, award, transfer", and the context pack gives `debt_sale_lot` and `debt_sale_account` to S6. This step reads both and writes neither.
- **the tape is rwb-document's document.** R-DS-10 builds it under the PII masking rules and R-DS-11 rejects it when an unmasked identifier is found; both are the tape step's. This step consumes the prepared tape on the P5 contract and never rebuilds, re-masks or copies it (ASM-4901).
- **the "qualified buyers" are rwb-partner's panel.** R-DS-13 opens the room "to buyers who have signed the non-disclosure agreement"; the panel, the partner users and the partner channel are S9's, and the partner gateway in the DMZ fronts rwb-partner. This story reads the panel, it does not own it (ASM-4900).
- **the case of record stays with rwb-case.** `recovery_case` and the DEBTSALE route states are P3's; this story evaluates the rule, records the decision and answers the case move (ASM-4902).
- **the decision is recorded first**, through the local decision-record library in the same transaction as the state answer, which is what legacy AC1 asks and legacy AC2 tests.
- **nothing is published on the topic by this step.** The service owns `rwb.debtsale.events.v1` with `LotAwarded` and `AccountsTransferred`, and both belong to the award and transfer stories; this step has no event of its own, so 12.3 and 12.4 are None (ASM-4904).

No business value moves: the masking rules, the closed lists `LOV-SEGMENT`, `LOV-BUYER-CLASS`, `LOV-LOT-STATUS` and `LOV-PUTBACK`, the non-disclosure condition and the "per cycle" clock are values of reference data and of the rule package, read with their version and never written in code.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S6-E5026-CON is published: the `GET /partner/data-room/{lotId}` operation on `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1`, the `DataRoom`, lot and account elements, the four closed lists, the consumed rows, the error set and the fakes are baselined and handed to this story.
- `debt_sale_lot` and `debt_sale_account` exist in schema `rwb_debtsale` from the DB story of this service, with the columns of DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-037 and the standard record columns of TSD S6 T3.0. This story adds no table, no column and no migration.
- The masked tape of the lot exists and has passed its masking check under R-DS-10 and R-DS-11, and its reference and masking-check result are readable on the rwb-document contract. The operation name of that read is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2977; ASM-4901), and the row is not in this story's contract-dependency list, which is None.
- The admitted buyer panel of the lot, with the non-disclosure agreement flag of R-DS-13, is readable on the rwb-partner contract. Its operation name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2977; ASM-4900), and the row is not in this story's contract-dependency list either.
- The case state and the case-move answer of rwb-case are available for the fake. No source publishes an operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage; on the workflow boundary the answer is the stage outcome the parent applies, and any REST case-move operation carries the placeholder (GAP-2977; ASM-4902).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: the local decision-record library writes in the caller's transaction, and a failed write stops the action with MSG-P7-003 (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: PRT-05 reaches this service through the gateway-bff composite route on the staff channel and through the partner gateway on the buyer channel, one hop each (DP-19; ASM-4905).
- The DEBTSALE rule package is in force at its version with R-DS-10 to R-DS-13; the package is authored, tested and approved in rwb-decision (P7) and loaded here on `RulePackageInForce`.
- The service runs as its own login on `rwb_debtsale` and holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `rwb_case`, `rwb_document`, `rwb_partner` or `rwb_access` is refused by the database and fails the boundary test (DP-01).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-S6-E5026-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The tape step of RWB-S6-E5025-APP completes R-DS-10 on an approved lot and records the masking-check result of R-DS-11 or R-DS-12, so the case reaches `TAPE_PREPARED`. Nothing of that step is run twice here.
2. The data-room step of `DebtSaleWorkflow` receives the trigger for a case in `TAPE_PREPARED` and reads the lot and its accounts from `debt_sale_lot` and `debt_sale_account`: `lot_no`, `cut_off_date`, `segment`, `reserve_price`, `buyer_partner_id`, `buyer_class`, `signing_date`, `approval_authority`, `payment_terms` and `status`, with the account rows of DF-SAL-031 to DF-SAL-037.
3. The step reads the tape of the lot on the rwb-document contract: the document reference, the lot it belongs to, the masking-check result and the freshness of the document, one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker. No unmasked account identifier and no borrower value is taken from that answer (ASM-4901).
4. The step reads the admitted buyer panel of the lot on the rwb-partner contract: the buyers with an active panel row and `nda_signed_at` present, which is the "buyers who have signed the non-disclosure agreement" of R-DS-13, one hop with a 2 s budget (ASM-4900).
5. The step reads the case state on the rwb-case read, to confirm that the case is in `TAPE_PREPARED` and to take the case reference the decision record carries.
6. `DataRoomEvaluator` loads the DEBTSALE package version in force from rwb-decision and evaluates R-DS-13 on the tape fact: `MASKING_CHECK_PASSED` and no unmasked identifier. Where the tape carries an unmasked identifier, R-DS-11 of the tape step is the branch that applies and this step changes nothing. Where no rule fires, the step changes nothing and reports the reason to the parent.
7. `DataRoomDecisionRecordWriter` writes one decision record through the local decision-record library, **before anything is served**: the case reference, the lot reference, the rule ID R-DS-13 with its version, the inputs reference (tape reference and panel reference), the outcome and the case move. A failed write stops the step with nothing changed (DP-03; legacy AC1 and AC2).
8. `CaseMoveAnswer` answers rwb-case with the move `DATA_ROOM_OPEN`, the rule ID, the version and the decided-at time. rwb-case writes the `recovery_case` row and its route state; this service writes neither (ASM-4902).
9. The lot is published to the data room: the lot rows are readable on API-S6-004 for the admitted buyers of that lot, and the tape is the document rwb-document holds. This step writes no new row of either table, and the value of `status` a data-room opening would carry is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2977; ASM-4903).
10. A repeated trigger for the same case and the same tape reference writes no second decision record, serves no second opening and counts the repeat.
11. PRT-05 reads the lot, its accounts and its tape reference from this service through the partner channel and through the composite route, next to the panel state of rwb-partner and the case state of rwb-case (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The local decision record cannot be written | Nothing is written: no record, no case-move answer and no opening is served | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, TC-E5-026-02, TC-E5-026-04 |
| X2 | The caller does not hold the Partner portal right of the read | 403 before any read of the lot or the tape; nothing changes and no record is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, TC-E5-026-03 |
| X3 | The case is not in `TAPE_PREPARED` | 409 and nothing is written; the room is not opened on a case that has already moved | None | AC1 |
| X4 | The tape is absent, its masking check has failed, or it is stale | The step holds, writes nothing and shows the data date; the opening resumes on the next fresh answer | MSG-P1-001 | AC1 |
| X5 | A consumed contract does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The step waits and retries on the workflow's own schedule; nothing is written and no case move is answered; the caller sees 503 with the error envelope | None | AC1 |
| X6 | The buyer is not admitted to the lot: no active panel row or no signed non-disclosure agreement | The partner channel answers 403 with the error envelope; the buyer sees no lot, no account and no tape reference | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, TC-E5-026-03 |
| X7 | The lot is unknown, or the buyer is outside the scope of the lot | 404 with the error envelope; nothing is read and nothing changes | None | AC1 |
| X8 | The same trigger or the same tape reference arrives twice | One record, one answer and one opening; the repeat is counted and no second record is written | None | AC1 |
| X9 | A component, a statement or a test reaches a `v_ace_*` view or another service's schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | Section 17, BR3, BR5 |

X1 and X2 are the exception paths of RWB-E5-026 carried onto the split; X3 and X8 are the state and repeat paths the split makes explicit; X4 is the tape branch R-DS-11 and R-DS-12 that the tape step owns; X5 to X7 are the call-type and partner-channel paths; X9 is the DP-01 boundary. The masking rules of X4 and the non-disclosure condition of X6 are values in force, so neither is a constant of this story.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-S6-E5026-CON, the rwb-document, rwb-partner and rwb-case fakes and the decision-record stub, on its own schema; needs no live P3, P5, S9 or P7 |
| Negotiable | The activity name, the decision code per rule and the shape of the stage outcome are this story's choice; the rules, the messages, the screen, the read and the lot and account columns are fixed |
| Valuable | An approved lot reaches the buyers of its panel with its masked tape and a recorded decision on the cycle it is due, and the case moves in the service that owns it |
| Estimable | One workflow step, one evaluator, one record write, one case-move answer, three clients and one read-only screen fragment |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on synthetic lots and synthetic panels through the contract fakes, plus the component cases of the refused role, the refused buyer and the failed record write |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Open the buyer data room

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-001207" carries the approved lot "DS-2026-0007"
    Given the DEBTSALE rule package is in force at its version and carries R-DS-10, R-DS-11, R-DS-12 and R-DS-13
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 Open the buyer data room (legacy RWB-E5-026 AC1)
    Given the rwb-document contract mock returns the masked data tape of lot "DS-2026-0007" as prepared by the tape step of RWB-S6-E5025-APP, with its masking check passed
    Given the rwb-partner contract mock returns the buyer panel of lot "DS-2026-0007" with the non-disclosure agreement signed
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case state "TAPE_PREPARED" for "RC-2026-001207"
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When its trigger arrives
    Then publishes the lot and the masked tape to the data room for qualified buyers
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E5-026 AC2)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The two criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E5-026 word for word, with their origin tag added and nothing else changed: the repeated `Then`, the legacy wording of `the action is taken`, `the decision log cannot be written` and `its trigger arrives` all stand. The cross-service facts of AC1 are mocked, so AC1 carries three `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` lines and those are the only additions to the legacy text; AC2 needs none, because the decision-record library is local. What the legacy lines describe happens in three places in the target: the masked tape is built and held by the tape step of RWB-S6-E5025-APP in rwb-document (P5); the "qualified buyers" are the admitted panel of rwb-partner (S9) behind the partner gateway; and this story evaluates R-DS-13, writes the record, answers the case move and serves the read, while rwb-case writes `DATA_ROOM_OPEN` on the case. The tape is referenced, never copied, and no unmasked personal data is served to a buyer (REQ-S6-003).

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-DS-13 | Debt sale | D8.4 | TAPE_PREPARED | MASKING_CHECK_PASSED | no unmasked identifier | Open the data room to buyers who have signed the non-disclosure agreement | DATA_ROOM_OPEN | Debt sale officer | buyer portal, Document Hub | per cycle |
| R-DS-10 | Debt sale | D8.4 | LOT_APPROVED | TAPE_BUILD_RUN | Any | Build the masked data tape under the PII masking rules | TAPE_PREPARED | Workbench | PII service, Recovery Data Store, Document Hub | 3 working days |
| R-DS-11 | Debt sale | D8.4 | TAPE_PREPARED | MASKING_CHECK_FAILED | an unmasked identifier is found on the tape | Reject the tape and rebuild it | TAPE_REJECTED | Workbench | PII service, Document Hub | None |
| R-DS-12 | Debt sale | D8.4 | TAPE_REJECTED | TAPE_REBUILT | masking check passes | Return the tape for data room release | TAPE_PREPARED | Workbench | PII service | None |

The four rows are the rows of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, copied character for character. Their owner column is a business role and not a service: R-DS-13 is evaluated here, the case move it names is written by rwb-case on this story's answer, the tape of R-DS-10 and R-DS-12 is built by the tape step of RWB-S6-E5025-APP, and the masking check of R-DS-11 is the PII service's on that tape. The three tape rows are tabled because they are the branch the same step reads and because R-DS-13 cannot be evaluated without their outcome (ASM-4901).

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The lot and its accounts are this service's: `lot_no`, `cut_off_date`, `segment`, `reserve_price`, `buyer_partner_id`, `buyer_class`, `signing_date`, `approval_authority`, `payment_terms` and `status` are columns of `debt_sale_lot` in `rwb_debtsale`, and no other service writes them | Architecture v5 (rwb-debtsale owns lots, data room, buyer terms, bids, award, transfer); TSD S6 T3.1; context pack ownership rows |
| BR2 | The decision is recorded before the room is served, with the rule ID and the package version in force; a failed write changes nothing and the caller sees MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; TSD S6 T2; legacy RWB-E5-026 AC1 and AC2 |
| BR3 | The masked tape is rwb-document's document and the masking rules are the PII service's: this story reads the tape reference and its masking-check result on the owner's contract and never rebuilds, re-masks, copies or stores the tape | R-DS-10, R-DS-11; FSD S6 A2.3 and A2.4; ASM-4901 |
| BR4 | The case move is answered and not written: `recovery_case` and the route states are rwb-case's, and this story sends the move with the rule and its version | TSD S6 T4; context pack ownership rows; ASM-4902 |
| BR5 | No cross-schema join and no foreign key leaves `rwb_debtsale`; `buyer_partner_id` and `account_id` are identifiers of other services' facts | DP-01; TSD S6 T3.3 |
| BR6 | R-DS-13 opens the room to buyers who have signed the non-disclosure agreement: the admitted panel is read from rwb-partner and is never decided here | R-DS-13; Architecture v5 (rwb-partner owns the panel and the partner users); ASM-4900 |
| BR7 | No unmasked personal data leaves the bank: the partner answer carries the lot and its masked account rows, and no borrower code, account number or identity value | REQ-S6-003; FSD S6 A2.3.1; legacy Guardrails |
| BR8 | Every value a business person may change is reference data or a rule row read with its version: `LOV-SEGMENT`, `LOV-BUYER-CLASS`, `LOV-LOT-STATUS`, `LOV-PUTBACK`, the masking rules and the "per cycle" clock | TSD S6 T3.2; FSD S6 BR-S6-004; legacy Guardrails |
| BR9 | The opening publishes no event: `LotAwarded` and `AccountsTransferred` are the award and transfer stories', and this step writes no outbox row | TSD S6 T5.3; context pack event row EV-23; ASM-4904 |
| BR10 | The lot status a data-room opening would carry is not named by any source, and `LOV-LOT-STATUS` carries no data-room value, so this step writes no lot status | TSD S6 T3.2; ASM-4903 |

##### 9. State transitions

The case route state is rwb-case's and is not changed by this story: the step answers the move and the parent applies it to the case of record (BR4). What this story owns is the opening of the step and the decision it records.

| From (case route state) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| TAPE_PREPARED | MASKING_CHECK_PASSED | no unmasked identifier, and the buyers hold a signed non-disclosure agreement | `DATA_ROOM_OPEN`, with this story's answer, its record and the served read |
| TAPE_PREPARED | MASKING_CHECK_FAILED | an unmasked identifier is found on the tape | `TAPE_REJECTED` by the tape step's answer, nothing here |
| TAPE_REJECTED | TAPE_REBUILT | masking check passes | `TAPE_PREPARED` by the tape step's answer, then this step |
| DATA_ROOM_OPEN and every later state | Any tape or opening trigger for the same lot | X3 | Unchanged, nothing written |

| Step execution | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting | The trigger arrives for a case in `TAPE_PREPARED` | The package in force is loaded | Evaluating |
| Evaluating | R-DS-13 fires | The tape fact and the panel are fresh | Recording |
| Recording | The record is written and the case-move answer is sent | The transaction commits | Waiting for the next trigger |
| Recording | The record write or the transaction fails | X1 | Waiting, nothing changed |
| Waiting | The tape is absent, stale or rejected | X4 | Held, until a fresh tape answer |

The route states are those of the DEBTSALE machine of TSD S6 T4 and they live on the case of record. The lot status values are those of `LOV-LOT-STATUS` (BUILDING, OFFERED, AWARDED, TRANSFERRED, CLOSED); none of them names a data-room opening, so this step writes no lot status (ASM-4903).

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-DEBTSALE, debt sale officer | Debt sale CRUA in TSD S6 T6.1: the primary role of the feature, holding C, R, U and A on the lot and reading the opening outcome |
| RW-SALEOFF, sale officer | Debt sale R: reads the lot, its accounts and the opening outcome |
| RW-NPAMGR, NPA and asset manager | Debt sale R: reads the lot and its data-room state |
| RW-HEADASL, Head of Asset Liquidity | Debt sale RA: reads, and approves where a lot needs it, which is the approval story's |
| RW-CREDITAD, RW-AGENCYMG, RW-CONDUCT, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-HEADNPA, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-FINANCE, RW-AUDIT, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE, RW-WRITEOFF | Debt sale R: read only, in scope |
| PT-BUYER, debt buyer and AMC | Debt sale RU: the buyer of the panel, who reads the lot, its masked accounts and its tape on PRT-05 through the partner gateway and bids in the bidding story |
| PT-RAMC, RAMC user | Debt sale R: reads the lot and its data-room state |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-AGENT | Debt sale R as the matrix gives it: the service identities run the step and are subject to the same checks |
| rwb-partner service identity | Presents the buyer channel and the panel facts of the lot; it holds the partner users and the agreement, not the lot |
| rwb-debtsale service identity | Runs the step, evaluates R-DS-13, writes the record, answers the case move and serves the read; it holds no grant on another schema |

The rights above are the rows of TSD S6 T6.1 and nothing wider. The legacy permission row of RWB-E5-026 gives the Partner portal right R to RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-LEGAL, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE and 21 more, while T6.1 gives the buyer PT-BUYER RU on Debt sale; both statements are recorded and the wider holders list is left as the legacy text gives it (GAP-2977; ASM-4900). The FSD says the feature runs unattended with the debt sale officer as also-user, and both hold: the step runs under the service identity with no officer task on the happy path. DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set: the capability area and the right are declared per operation and the guard is a service-template capability, so the check is stated here and not built here.

| rule_row | rwb_decision (P7) | the R-DS-10 to R-DS-13 rows and their version | Not read as a table: the package version is loaded from rwb-decision |

Field IDs are those of TSD S6 T3.1 and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. **No new table, no new column and no migration**: `debt_sale_lot` and `debt_sale_account` arrive with the DB story of this service, this story writes neither, and `decision_record`, `idempotency_key` and `outbox_event` are platform library objects created in `rwb_debtsale` by the library's own migration (DP-03, DP-09). The data room has no table of its own: Architecture v5 names "data room" as part of what the service owns, while TSD S6 T3.1 defines only the lot and the account, so the room is a served view of those two tables and of the P5 tape.

**No personal data.** The rows and answers this story handles carry identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version. No name, address, contact value or identity number enters `rwb_debtsale`, the decision record, a log, an answer, a workflow input or a screen, and every fixture is synthetic. `borrower_code` stays in this service's table and is never served to the partner channel: the tape the buyer sees is masked under PDPA before it reaches the room (REQ-S6-003; BR7).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-debtsale (S6); base `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the behaviour behind the one read whose shape RWB-S6-E5026-CON declares.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/partner/data-room/{lotId}` | `DataRoom` of status 200 out, with the lot, its masked accounts and its tape reference, for an admitted buyer (API-S6-004) | Partner portal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The errors are 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope lot and 503 when the library or a consumed contract does not answer. API-S6-001, API-S6-002, API-S6-003 and API-S6-005 belong to the lot, approval, award and bidding stories and are not built here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The tape read of rwb-document (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2977; ASM-4901)) | `/api/recovery/document/v1` | P5 rwb-document | The masked tape of the lot: its reference, the lot it belongs to, the masking-check result and its freshness; read only, faked |
| The buyer-panel read of rwb-partner (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2977; ASM-4900)) | `/api/recovery/partner/v1` | S9 rwb-partner | The admitted buyers of the lot: panel status, partner user and the agreement flag of R-DS-13; read only, faked |
| The case read of rwb-case | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case state, the case reference and the account link; read only, faked |
| The case-move answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2977; ASM-4902)) | on the rwb-case boundary | P3 rwb-case | The move `DATA_ROOM_OPEN` with the rule ID and its version; the stage outcome the parent applies; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The rows are contract dependencies of class C that the plan does not carry, because the C row of this slice is None (GAP-2977; ASM-4899).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The data-room step of R-DS-13 publishes no event. The service's events are `LotAwarded` on `rwb.debtsale.events.v1`, with rwb-case and rwb-payment as consumers, and `AccountsTransferred` on the same topic, and both belong to RWB-S6-E6005-APP and RWB-S6-E6007-APP. This story writes no outbox row, declares no producer and holds no topic of its own, and a build that adds one fails the absence test (ASM-4904).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The service's consumed event is `ProceedsMatched` from `rwb.payment.events.v1`, which is the settlement step's. The opening is triggered by the tape step's completed state and by the case signal the parent forwards, so this story holds no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox row of its own (ASM-4904).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DebtSaleWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case, the child of `CaseWorkflow`, the saga whose pivot is the transfer, using the Saga runner of the workflow kit | `rwb-debtsale` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the lot, the route and the package in force; signals: the case state, the package in force and the tape state |
| `openDataRoom` | Activity, the one data-room step | `rwb-debtsale` | The case and the lot in; the rule ID with its version, the opening and the case move out, with the record written before the answer and no outbox row |

No child workflow for the case and none for the money exists in this service. The activity name is a target design choice fixed by no source. The trigger is read as the arrival of the trigger for a case in `TAPE_PREPARED`, because the legacy story runs the step unattended while the FSD declares no background event for the feature (FSD S6 A2.4.4.4). The debt sale saga names the transfer as its pivot, and this step sits before it and needs no compensating activity of its own.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step runs from the tape step's completed state and from the case signal the parent forwards, and owns no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job. The "per cycle" timer of R-DS-13 and the monthly cycle are durable timers of `DebtSaleWorkflow` and values of the rule package, not a Schedule of this story.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| debt_sale_lot | S6 (`rwb_debtsale`) | The approved lot; this story reads the row and writes none of its columns (ASM-4903) |
| debt_sale_account | S6 (`rwb_debtsale`) | The accounts of the lot; this story reads the rows and writes none of their columns |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_debtsale` | The local hash-linked record of the R-DS-13 outcome (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_debtsale` | The key of the repeated trigger and the answer it holds |
| outbox_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_debtsale` | The outbox of the service; this story writes no row of it (BR9) |

Not owned and never read as a table: `recovery_case` and `timer` (P3), `document` (P5), `partner`, `partner_user` and the panel (S9), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `proceeds` (P8), the bid and award rows (S6, the sibling stories') and every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No foreign key leaves the schema, and `buyer_partner_id` and `account_id` are identifiers, not cross-schema keys (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-document tape fake | The masked tape of lot `DS-2026-0007` with its masking check passed and its date; the same tape with the check failed; a stale tape; no answer beyond 2 s | AC1, X4, X5 |
| rwb-partner panel fake | The panel of lot `DS-2026-0007` with two admitted buyers whose agreement is signed; a panel with no admitted buyer; a panel with the agreement missing; no answer beyond 2 s | AC1, X5, X6 |
| rwb-case state and move fake | The states `TAPE_PREPARED`, `TAPE_REJECTED` and `DATA_ROOM_OPEN` of case `RC-2026-001207`; an accepted move and a refused move | AC1, X3 |
| rwb-decision rule-package fake | The DEBTSALE package at its version in force with R-DS-10 to R-DS-13 | AC1 |
| Local decision-record library stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain, and a stopped chain | AC2, X1 |
| Partner channel and gateway-bff route fake | The merged PRT-05 answer for lot `DS-2026-0007` for an admitted buyer, and the 403 of a buyer who is not admitted | AC1, X6 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The operation names of the tape read, the panel read and the case-move answer carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-2977; ASM-4899 to -4).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 provided, 4 consumed | The `GET /partner/data-room/{lotId}` read on `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1`; the tape read, the panel read, the case read and the case-move answer; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | This step publishes and consumes nothing; `LotAwarded` and `AccountsTransferred` are the award and transfer stories' |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 1 activity | `DebtSaleWorkflow` and its `openDataRoom` step on `rwb-debtsale`; no Schedule |
| File | None | No file is read, built or delivered here; the tape is a P5 document referenced by claim-check, and the buyer file of INT-25 is delivered on the partner channel (ASM-4901) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.debtsale`, module `dataroom`; front end fragment `src/modules/recovery/debtsale/DataRoom.tsx`, the PRT-05 fragment that rwb-partner's buyer panel embeds on the partner channel and that the staff route reads, read only.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the transaction rule of the step: the record is written in the caller's transaction before anything is served, and a failed write changes nothing. DP-13 moves the base of the read and nothing else. DP-19 is how PRT-05 reaches this service, one hop: the buyer channel through the partner gateway to rwb-partner's buyer panel, the staff channel through the composite route, and the screen field list and route specification belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON (ASM-4905).

**Dependencies the tables add and the plan does not hold.** The four consumed rows are class C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata, and the partner-channel route has no plan row of its own, so both are recorded in the registers and neither is added to the metadata (ASM-4899, -7). The outbox library of DP-09 is not a dependency of this step, because it publishes no event (ASM-4904).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `DebtSaleWorkflow` data-room branch | Workflow | Waits for a case in `TAPE_PREPARED`, loads the package in force and reports the outcome to the parent |
| `openDataRoom` | Activity | The one step: read the lot, the tape, the panel and the case, evaluate R-DS-13, write the record and answer the move |
| `DataRoomEvaluator` | Service | The rule evaluation against the package version in force, with the tape fact and the panel fact |
| `DataRoomDecisionRecordWriter` | Library adapter | Writes the record with the rule ID and version before anything is served, hash-linked, and refuses the step when the write fails (DP-03) |
| `LotReader` | Repository | Reads `debt_sale_lot` and `debt_sale_account` in `rwb_debtsale`, with the scope filter of the caller |
| `DocumentTapeClient`, `PartnerPanelClient`, `CaseStateClient` | Clients | The tape, panel and case rows, one hop, 2 s, breaker each |
| `DataRoomController` | Controller | The one read, the capability area and right, the buyer scope, the masking rule of the answer and the problem mapping |
| `DataRoom` | React component | Shows the lot, its masked accounts and its tape on PRT-05, with the refused and not-admitted states |

**Database and migrations.** No Flyway file. The two lot tables arrive with the DB story of this service, and the record, key and outbox are library objects created in `rwb_debtsale` by the library's migration.

**Configuration and reference data.** `LOV-SEGMENT`, `LOV-BUYER-CLASS`, `LOV-LOT-STATUS` and `LOV-PUTBACK` at their version in force (TSD S6 T3.2); the DEBTSALE package and its version, loaded on `RulePackageInForce`, with the masking rules, the non-disclosure condition and the "per cycle" clock as values; the capability area "Partner portal" and right R as access rows of rwb-access. No parameter is named in the sources for the step itself; the 2 s budget and the single hop are the platform rule of ADR-020.

**Build steps**

1. The data-room branch of `DebtSaleWorkflow`, registered on `rwb-debtsale` as the stage child of `CaseWorkflow`, with the `TAPE_PREPARED` trigger.
2. The three clients against their fakes, with the 2 s budget, the breaker, the stale-tape path and the no-answer path (AC1, X4, X5).
3. `LotReader` and the scope filter over the two tables, with the masking rule of the answer (AC1, BR7).
4. `DataRoomEvaluator` over the package, with R-DS-13, the tape fact, the panel fact and the no-fire path (AC1).
5. `DataRoomDecisionRecordWriter` against the library stub, with the failed-write path (AC2, X1).
6. `CaseMoveAnswer` and the parent signal, with the move, the repeat path and the state guard (AC1, X3, X8).
7. `DataRoomController` with the right, the buyer scope, the masking rule and the problem mapping (AC1, X2, X6, X7).
8. `DataRoom` and PRT-05 on the partner channel and through the composite route fake (AC1).
9. The boundary test: no statement outside `rwb_debtsale`, no `v_ace_*` read, no write to another service's schema (X9, BR3, BR5).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.debtsale.data-room-v1`, read as a flag of the platform library; off means the step holds the trigger, writes nothing and serves no opening.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the step runs from a synthetic tape and panel in SIT, R-DS-13 produces its record, its answer and its served read, a repeated trigger writes once, a forced record failure changes nothing, a buyer without an active panel row or a signed agreement is refused with 403, no `recovery_case` row and no `v_ace_*` read exists in the build, and PRT-05 answers on the partner channel and through the composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S6-001 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names an open deviation and belongs to the eligibility step of RWB-S6-E5023-APP, so no path of this story raises it | {account} has an open deviation and cannot be sold. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | The `lotId` path parameter is absent or malformed, or a required input of the step is absent (X7) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Partner portal right reads the room, or a buyer is not admitted to the lot (X2, X6) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the room is served (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The tape or its masking-check result is stale after a late or failed step (X4, VR-S6-004-1) | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The five IDs are those of the legacy message set and of FSD S6 A2.4.3.1, and the text is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new one is added. MSG-S6-001 is carried because it is in the message set of the feature, and no path of this story raises it. MSG-P1-001 carries the FSD wording unchanged although the check behind it is the tape step's and the owner of the batch status is rwb-source-data (ASM-4901).

##### 15. Screens and states

PRT-05 Data room in its admitted, bidding and closed states is served through the partner channel to rwb-partner's buyer panel and, for staff, through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19; ASM-4905). The route calls rwb-debtsale for the lot, its masked accounts and its tape reference, rwb-partner for the panel and the buyer, rwb-document for the tape and rwb-case for the case and its route state. This story fixes the rwb-debtsale answer only, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

The state this story produces is the admitted state of PRT-05 for a lot: the lot, its date, its segment and its masked account rows, with the tape reference the buyer may open. The bidding state belongs to RWB-S6-E6004-APP and the closed state to the award and put-back stories of this service, and both read the same route. The refusal and failure states are: refused with MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right and for a buyer who is not admitted, not recorded with MSG-P7-003, and stale tape with MSG-P1-001.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the masking rules, the non-disclosure condition, the "per cycle" and monthly clocks, the four lists and the rule rows stay data, reference data or the rule package, never a constant, a default or a branch of the build.
- No personal data in `rwb_debtsale`, in an answer, in a workflow input or in a log: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version only, `borrower_code` never leaves the service, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and reads no ACE table, and a build that adds one fails the boundary test (DP-01).
- The case stays with rwb-case, the tape with rwb-document and the panel with rwb-partner: no case row, document row or partner row is written here (BR3, BR4, BR6).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; no document, module or test names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no shared job table, no Quartz row, no monolith base, no event of this step and no data-lake extract.
- The decision is recorded before anything is served; a build that serves the room before the record commits fails the review (DP-03).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract baseline of the committee-approval slice of RWB-E6-001. It declares the lot read on base `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1` (DP-13), the element with its approval fields and closed lists, the consumed rwb-decision approval chain and rule package, the consumed rwb-access DoA row and the rwb-case read and answer, the rights and the error set, the naming baseline, the boundary and the fakes that let RWB-S6-E6001-APP start on Day 1 (DP-03, DP-19). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As the **squad that owns rwb-debtsale**, I want **the contract of the lot approval read and of its consumed rows baselined with its fakes**, so that **the approval build starts on Day 1 without a live rwb-decision, rwb-access or rwb-case**.

This contract story carries the interface of the legacy key's approval slice. It owns:

- the one REST operation this key provides, `GET /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}` on base `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1` (API-S6-002, DP-13), with its shape, its rights, its errors and its idempotency statement;
- the `DebtSaleLot` element: the lot fields, its accounts, its reserve, its bids and the approval fields `approval_authority`, `payment_terms` and `signing_date` (DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-030);
- the closed lists the element and its consumers read: `LOV-SEGMENT`, `LOV-BUYER-CLASS`, `LOV-LOT-STATUS`, `LOV-PUTBACK` (TSD S6 T3.2);
- the consumed rows: the rwb-decision approval chain, act and rule package; the rwb-access delegation limit; the rwb-case state read and the case-move answer (GAP-2980; ASM-4908);
- the error set and the problem envelope of the read, and the fakes every consumer and the build use;
- the naming baseline of the service (DP-13, DP-19) and the boundary that keeps `rwb_decision`, `rwb_access` and `rwb_case` out of this schema.

It does not own: the behaviour behind the read, the rule evaluation, the record write, the column update and the case answer, which are RWB-S6-E6001-APP; the award operation API-S6-003 and the lot-creation operation API-S6-001, which belong to other S6 keys; the approval chain and the decision log, which are rwb-decision's (P7); the DoA table, which is rwb-access's (P4); the case and its route states, which are rwb-case's (P3); and the deployment of the service.

##### 2. Business rationale

A split service is only buildable in parallel when its interface is fixed before its behaviour: the APP story and every consumer start from this document and from its fakes, not from a running service. Three facts make the contract of this key worth its own story.

**The base changes.** The monolith served the Workbench from one base; the target serves each service from its own, `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1` (DP-13). The read that shows an approved lot on SCR-25 and SCR-26 is the same read, on a new base, and every consumer needs that base, that shape and that error set in writing.

**The approval is not a screen of this service.** The chain, the act, the DoA limit and the ledger entry belong to rwb-decision and rwb-access, and the case belongs to rwb-case. The contract must therefore declare what this service **consumes** as precisely as what it provides, so that the approval build can be tested with fakes and the real chain only arrives in integration (GAP-2980; ASM-4908).

**The approval facts must be named once.** `approval_authority`, `payment_terms` and `signing_date` are columns of `debt_sale_lot` (DF-SAL-027 to DF-SAL-029) and elements of the read; if the element and the table disagree, every consumer of the lot drifts. Naming them here fixes them for the approval, the award and the data-room keys alike.

The key is EP06 and therefore wave 4, while the service is created in wave 3; the date is copied unchanged and marked tentative. The contract is Day 1 work in contract group CG-W4, because a CON story has no build dependency and every later story of the key waits on it (R5.7 rules 1 and 8).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service row of the context pack is in force: code S6, service rwb-debtsale, schema `rwb_debtsale`, base `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1`, topic `rwb.debtsale.events.v1`, queue `rwb-debtsale`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.debtsale`.
- The ownership rows of S6 are in force: the two tables, the five REST operations, the one event and the one workflow (context pack, ownership rows).
- The naming rules of R4 and the DP table of R5.5 are in force (DP-03, DP-13, DP-19 apply to this key).
- The TSD S6 API appendix (T-A.1 and T-A.2) is the source of the read: path, purpose, request, response, errors, authorization and idempotency.
- The element is taken from TSD S6 T3.1 and the closed lists from T3.2; the Logical Data Model v8 carries the field IDs.
- The consumed rows are described only as far as their owners publish them; where an operation name is not published the placeholder of §R9 is used and the row is recorded (GAP-2980; ASM-4909).
- No approval is needed to baseline a Draft contract; the contract tag is set when the contract tests of this story pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. This story reads the service row, the ownership rows, the naming rules, the TSD appendix and the data model, and writes the contract of the read, the element, the lists, the consumed rows, the errors and the fakes.
2. It publishes the contract document and its machine-readable form (the operation, the element and the closed lists) in the service's contract repository, versioned with the contract group.
3. It publishes the fakes: the read answered from a fixture lot, the consumed approval chain, the DoA row, the case state and the case-move answer, each with its healthy and its failing answer.
4. RWB-S6-E6001-APP binds to the read and to the fakes on Day 1 and writes the behaviour behind them (the approval branch, the evaluator, the record, the columns and the answer).
5. The award, data-room and transfer stories of S6 bind to the same element and the same base for their own operations, so the element is declared once for all of them.
6. A consumer that needs a field not in the element raises a contract change against this story; the field is added here, never ad hoc in a consumer.
7. On integration, the fakes are replaced by the real rwb-decision, rwb-access and rwb-case services; the contract document does not change, only the endpoint behind it.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A consumer asks for a field or a list value that the element does not declare | The request fails the contract test and the field is raised as a contract change against this story | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X2 | A caller does not hold the Debt sale right of the read | The contract fixes 403 with MSG-P4-002 and changes nothing | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |
| X3 | A lot is unknown or outside the caller's scope | The contract fixes 404, with no existence leak outside the scope | None | AC1, AC5 |
| X4 | A consumed owner changes an operation name or a shape | The fake is regenerated from the owner's document; the consumer build is unaffected because it binds to the fake | None | AC3, AC4, AC6 |
| X5 | A consumed owner has published no operation name | The contract carries the §R9 placeholder and the fake, and the row is recorded | None | AC3, AC4 |
| X6 | A statement reaches `rwb_decision`, `rwb_access`, `rwb_case` or another schema | The boundary test fails the contract build | None (pipeline log) | AC7 |

X1 and X6 protect the contract from silent drift; X4 and X5 are the reason the fakes exist.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Day 1 work: no build dependency, no live service, only published documents and its own repository |
| Negotiable | The document format, the fake technology and the test harness are this story's choice; the path, the element, the lists, the rights and the error codes are fixed |
| Valuable | The approval build and every consumer of the lot start on Day 1 against one element, one base and one error set |
| Estimable | One operation, one element, four lists, five consumed rows, one error set and six fakes |
| Small | Finished inside one week |
| Testable | Contract tests on the fakes, a schema check of the element and a boundary test of the schema |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One service, one base: the read is served on `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1` and no consumer reaches the schema | DP-13; context pack service row |
| BR2 | The element is declared once for all S6 keys that read a lot: the approval, the award, the data room and the transfer bind to it | Context pack ownership rows; TSD S6 T3.1 |
| BR3 | The approval fields are the table's: `approval_authority`, `payment_terms` and `signing_date` are columns of `debt_sale_lot` and elements of the read | TSD S6 T3.1; DF-SAL-027 to DF-SAL-029 |
| BR4 | The approval chain, the act, the ledger entry, the rule package and the DoA limit are consumed as contracts; this service writes none of them | GAP-2980; ASM-4908 |
| BR5 | The case route states are read and the move is answered; no case row is read as a table | GAP-2980; ASM-4909 |
| BR6 | The contract declares no event for this key: the service's one event, EV-23 `LotAwarded`, is the award story's | GAP-2982; ASM-4910 |
| BR7 | No value a business person may change is in the contract as a constant: the four lists are declared as lists and read with their version | TSD S6 T3.2; FSD S6 A2.5.3.1 BR-S6-005 |
| BR8 | The contract carries no personal data in its examples, its fixtures or its logs | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17) |

##### 9. State transitions

The contract has no business state machine of its own; it fixes the states the read and the answer expose. The states below are those the element and the consumed rows carry, and they are declared, not applied, here.

| Element | Values | Owner of the values |
|---|---|---|
| Case route state on the read | `LOT_BUILT`, `LOT_WITH_COMMITTEE`, `LOT_APPROVED`, `LOT_WITHDRAWN` | rwb-case (P3) |
| `debt_sale_lot.status` | BUILDING, OFFERED, AWARDED, TRANSFERRED, CLOSED (`LOV-LOT-STATUS`) | rwb-debtsale (S6) |
| `debt_sale_account.put_back_status` | NONE, CLAIMED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED (`LOV-PUTBACK`) | rwb-debtsale (S6) |
| Contract baseline | Draft, then baselined when this story's contract tests pass | This story |

The business transitions of the case are in RWB-S6-E6001-APP and in the TSD T4 machine; this story declares the values and their owner and changes none of them.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-debtsale (S6); base `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/debt-sale-lots/{lotId}` | `DebtSaleLot` of status 200 out, with its accounts, reserve and bids (API-S6-002) | Debt sale, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/debt-sale-lots` | `DebtSaleLot` of status 201 out from a `LotRequest` (API-S6-001) | Debt sale, right C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |
| POST | `/debt-sale-lots/{lotId}/award` | `DecisionLogEntry` of status 200 out from an `AwardRequest` (API-S6-003) | Debt sale, right A, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |
| GET | `/partner/data-room/{lotId}` | `DataRoom` of status 200 out (API-S6-004) | Partner portal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/partner/data-room/{lotId}/bids` | `Bid` of status 201 out from a `BidRequest` (API-S6-005) | Partner portal, right C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |

This story baselines the five operations of the service because one element and one base are shared by them; the behaviour of each belongs to its own key, and the approval key builds only the read. The path, the request, the response, the errors, the authorization and the idempotency of each row are those of TSD S6 T-A.1 and T-A.2 and are not redefined here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The approval chain read and the approver's act (three act rows; the architecture names one `POST /approvals/{id}/decide`) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The chain, the act and the DoA level tested; faked (GAP-2980; ASM-4909) |
| The read of the DS rule package version in force (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2980; ASM-4909)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The package version and its rule rows; faked |
| `GET /doa-limits` | `/api/recovery/access/v1` | P4 rwb-access | The `delegation_limit` row of the approver's level; faked |
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family (read) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case state, the reference and the stage; faked |
| The case-move answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2980; ASM-4909)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | `LOT_WITH_COMMITTEE`, `LOT_APPROVED` or `LOT_WITHDRAWN` with the rule and its version; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter, a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The five rows are class C dependencies that the plan's C row does not carry, so the contract binds to their published documents and fakes (GAP-2981; ASM-4907).

###### 12.3 Events published

None in this key. The service owns one event, EV-23 `rwb.debtsale.LotAwarded.v1` on topic `rwb.debtsale.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics (context pack, ownership rows; TSD S6 T5.3), and it is published by the award story. This key declares it by name for the topic baseline and publishes nothing (GAP-2982; ASM-4910).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The approval answer arrives on the chain the approval story starts and on the rwb-case contract; this key declares no consumer group and no subscription.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DebtSaleWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case per stage, the saga child of `CaseWorkflow` | `rwb-debtsale` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case, the lot, the reserve, the tiered terms and the package in force; signals: the approval answer and the case state |
| `ApprovalWorkflow` | Child workflow, the kit's Approval template, owned and run by rwb-decision | `rwb-decision` (P7) | The maker-checker chain with the DoA lookup as a parameter; started by the approval story (GAP-2980) |
| `recordCommitteeApproval` | Activity of the approval story | `rwb-debtsale` | The case, the lot and the answer in; the record, the columns and the move out, in one transaction |

The workflow contract is declared here; its behaviour, its activities and their names are RWB-S6-E6001-APP's.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The service owns no job (context pack, jobs: None) and this key registers no Temporal Schedule.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| debt_sale_lot | S6 (`rwb_debtsale`) | The lot, the reserve and the three approval fields |
| debt_sale_account | S6 (`rwb_debtsale`) | The accounts of a lot |
| decision_record | PLT library, in `rwb_debtsale` | The local record, created by the library (DP-03) |

Not owned and never read as tables: `recovery_case` (P3), `approval`, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `delegation_limit` (P4), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `proceeds` (P8) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).
