Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. The lot and its accounts are S6's, the case is P3's, the decision log and the rule rows are P7's, and the ACE side is DP01 and DP09 of P1's contract; the harness reads them only through those contracts and never from a schema. The harness owns no table and writes no row. The DP09 rows it reads are `debt_sale_lot` DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-030 and `debt_sale_account` DF-SAL-031 to DF-SAL-035, and the ACE side is `v_ace_account` DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042 read through DP01.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1/debt-sale-lots/{lotId}/award` | S6 rwb-debtsale | Starts the saga; the trigger of every criterion, with one Idempotency-Key (AC1, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1/debt-sale-lots/{lotId}` | S6 rwb-debtsale | Lot number, cut-off date, winner, lot status and the recorded posting reference (AC4, AC6) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbound-items` | P2 rwb-integration | The lot's posting item, its file run and the delivered answer (AC4, AC5) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbound-items/{itemId}/resend` | P2 rwb-integration | The re-post after a cleared rejection (AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP01/records?caseId={caseId}` | P1 rwb-source-data | The sold accounts and their status in v_ace_account (AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP09/records?caseId={caseId}` | P1 rwb-source-data | The lot and account rows, their outstanding and selling price (AC4, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness?product=DP01` | P1 rwb-source-data | The business date and the load time behind the ACE read (AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | P7 rwb-decision | The decision record of the derecognition and the posting, with the rule version (AC1, AC4, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case state after the posting, the rejection and the correction (AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The caller's roles and rights before a read (AC6) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13). No operation is invented in this story: each path is the owner's published operation, and where a screen would compose them the path would be the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The award's own criteria, its reserve and the 54% cap are RWB-S6-E6005-* and are not asserted here.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it writes its report to the wave record.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use in the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.debtsale.AccountsTransferred.v1` | `rwb.debtsale.events.v1` | S6 rwb-debtsale | Counts one publication after the transfer and, with the replay, proves one processed row per consumer (AC4) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | S6 rwb-debtsale through the local decision-record library (DP-03) | Proves the record of the derecognition and the posting was published and confirmed by the central ledger before the posting reference was recorded (AC4, AC5) |

The harness subscribes to both topics under one consumer group of its own, counts publications and replays each event once. The consumer effect it reads is the case through the rwb-case operation of §12.2; the inbox row counts of rwb-payment and rwb-reporting come from the consumer evidence in the run fixture, because neither consumer exposes an operation in this story. `rwb.debtsale.LotAwarded.v1` on the same topic is produced by the award and is observed by count only, since rwb-case and rwb-payment are its consumers.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness exercises DebtSaleWorkflow, S6's saga on the task queue `rwb-debtsale` in the `rwb-recovery` namespace, and observes the activities it runs after the transfer: the transfer of the accounts, the derecognition, the general ledger posting and the proceeds step, each on its owning service's queue as the saga runs them. They are stated here as observed and not built here; no workflow, activity or Schedule is created, changed or owned by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added. The sale cycle is monthly and DebtSaleWorkflow is started by the award, so the harness starts the journey with the award operation and sets no cron, overlap policy or catch-up window.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-01); debt_sale_lot and debt_sale_account are S6's, recovery_case is P3's, decision_log_entry and rule_row are P7's, outbound_item is P2's, and the ACE side belongs to the views behind P1's contract.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Contract | Stubbed answer in the run |
|---|---|---|
| Stub for rwb-debtsale | `POST /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}/award`, `GET /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}` | Accepts the award once per Idempotency-Key, then returns lot `LOT-SYN-2027-0001` with cut_off_date 2027-03-31, status transferred, then closed, and the posting reference once it is recorded |
| Stub for rwb-integration | `GET /admin/outbound-items`, `POST /admin/outbound-items/{itemId}/resend` | One outbound item for the lot with its file run, the delivered answer, the ledger entry id, and a resend that keeps the same itemId |
| Stub for rwb-source-data | DP01 records, DP09 records, freshness | Both accounts in v_ace_account with their derecognised status, the two debt_sale_account rows, and business date 2027-03-31 with a load time |
| Stub for rwb-decision | `GET /decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | One entry for the derecognition and one for the posting, each with its rule id and rule version, and the ledger confirmation |
| Stub for rwb-case | `GET /cases/{caseId}` | Case `RW-2027-000801` with its state after the posting, the rejection and the correction |
| Stub for rwb-access | `GET /me/session` | Allows RW-CREDITAD with Debt sale R; refuses RW-OFF with 403 and MSG-P4-002 |
| Posting fixture (ACE side) | The ALS and general ledger result of the job | The delivered answer of the outbound item, the ledger entry, one ALS rejection with its code and a cleared correction, at the point where the real adapters would answer |

Each stub is generated from the published contract and its version is pinned in the run report, so a contract change shows up as a run failure and not as a silent pass. The harness environment and base hosts, the stub answer for the ALS and general ledger posting reference with its shape, its reference format and its rejection codes, the retry and back-off settings, the evidence format and retention, the pass or fail gate, and the synthetic lot and account keys are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0454; ASM-0646).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 10 consumed, one hop each on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13) |
| Kafka | None published; two consumed, `rwb.debtsale.AccountsTransferred.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`, counted and replayed once |
| Temporal | None added; DebtSaleWorkflow on `rwb-debtsale` exercised from the award, with its transfer, derecognition, posting and proceeds activities |
| File | The outbound item's file run, read through the rwb-integration contract, and the posting fixture of the ACE side |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H dependency DP-03 adds, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, is a platform story delivered by the platform wave and is not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays empty; the same holds for RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The one blocking dependency is the I story RWB-S6-E6008-APP, which replaces its stub; until it is live the run uses the stub, and a stub pass is reported as a stub pass.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the six owned criteria in order for a lot and holds the run lock |
| AwardDriver | Service | Calls the award once per lot with one Idempotency-Key and reads the lot before and after each step |
| PostingProbe | Service | Reads the outbound item, its file run and the delivered answer, asserts the recorded posting reference, and resends the same item after a cleared rejection |
| AceReadBack | Service | Reads DP01 and DP09 with the freshness stamp, and names every account that still shows its old status |
| EventObserver | Service | Subscribes to `rwb.debtsale.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`, counts publications and replays each event once |
| LedgerConfirm | Service | Reads the decision log and asserts the ledger confirmation arrived before the posting reference was recorded |
| StubSet | Fake | The six stubs and the posting fixture of §12.8, generated from the published contracts with the version pinned |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes one report per lot keyed by story and lot_no, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the stubs from Day 1 and the real services as RWB-S6-E6008-APP lands, on the synthetic lot `LOT-SYN-2027-0001`, accounts `ACC-SYN-000801` and `ACC-SYN-000802`, case `RW-2027-000801` and business date 2027-03-31. The harness seeds nothing by hand and never writes a schema row. The environment and base hosts, the stub answer for the posting reference with its shape, its reference format and its rejection codes, the retry and back-off settings, the evidence format and retention, the pass or fail gate, and the synthetic lot and account keys are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0454; ASM-0646).

**Build steps**

1. Generate the six stubs and the posting fixture from the published contracts and pin each contract version in the run report; fail the run on a mismatch (X1).
2. Build the AwardDriver and prove the award is accepted once per Idempotency-Key and the lot read moves from awarded to transferred (AC1).
3. Add AC2 and AC3 against a case in DERECOGNISED and a case in POSTING_REJECTED_DS, asserting the posting, the provision input to Finance and the move to GL_POSTED from both.
4. Build the PostingProbe for AC4: one outbound item, its file run, the delivered answer and the recorded posting reference matched to the DP09 amount and account count (X2, X3).
5. Add the AceReadBack for AC4: both accounts with their derecognised status in v_ace_account through DP01 with the freshness stamp, so a stale product fails the run (X4).
6. Add the EventObserver for AC4: one LotAwarded and one AccountsTransferred publication, the case effect once, and a replay that changes nothing because the inbox holds one row per consumer.
7. Add the LedgerConfirm for AC5: hold the ledger answer back, assert no posting reference is recorded, then release the rejection and assert POSTING_REJECTED_DS with its exception task (X5, X6).
8. Add the resend path for AC5 and assert one outbound item, one posting reference and one ledger entry after the correction (X7).
9. Add the R-DS-34 lot close assertion, the access path for AC6 through the session read and the lot read, then the EvidenceReport and the gate, and swap a stub for the real owner as RWB-S6-E6008-APP lands (X8).

**Feature switch.** None. The harness has no production flag and runs in the test environment only.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass against the fakes and again against RWB-S6-E6008-APP when it lands, and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story and lot_no.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S6-001 | Error | {account} has an open deviation and cannot be sold. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values on the answer it reads, and owns no message text. MSG-S6-001 is asserted with the account_key of the sold account when the deviation screening refuses a sale, MSG-GEN-001 with the missing field when a read is made short of a required parameter, MSG-P4-002 with the refused action on the lot read, and MSG-P7-003 when the decision record cannot be written and nothing changes.

##### 15. Screens and states

The legacy story has no screen of its own for this journey, and neither does this harness: it observes the owners' operations and writes a report. The states are read through those operations, not rendered.

| State | Read through | What the run asserts |
|---|---|---|
| DERECOGNISED | rwb-debtsale lot read and rwb-case case read | The sold accounts are derecognised and the posting has not yet been accepted |
| GL_POSTING_RUN | the outbound item and its file run | The posting has left and the answer has not arrived, and no posting reference is recorded yet |
| GL_POSTED | rwb-case case read and DP01 | The posting is accepted, the reference is recorded and the accounts carry their derecognised status |
| POSTING_REJECTED_DS | rwb-case case read | The rejection is held with its exception task and the two-working-day clock of R-DS-32 runs |
| POSTING_CORRECTED | the outbound item and its file run | One resend of the same item, one posting reference and one ledger entry |
| LOT_CLOSED | rwb-debtsale lot read, DF-SAL-030 | The lot closes under R-DS-34 with realized recovery by lot and by buyer |

The harness renders no screen. SCR-25 Lot builder and SCR-26 Award are RWB-S6-E6005's and RWB-S6-E6009's and neither builds nor reads them here. What the wave entry check looks at instead is the run report, whose environment, layout and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0454; ASM-0646).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the synthetic lot, its accounts, the business date, the posting reference, the rejection codes, the retry settings and the report layout are data.
- No personal data in logs, events or reports: every key is synthetic, and the events carry IDs and facts only.
- ACE data only through the P1 contract: DP01 and DP09 with their freshness stamp, never a direct view read and never another service's schema (DP-01, DP-05).
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would (DP-11, DP-13).
- A stub pass is never reported as a real pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and it never writes a row by hand or sets a state it then asserts.
- A failing criterion is fixed in the owning service or raised as a gap; it is never waived in the script.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of the put-back claim step of rwb-debtsale, split from RWB-E6-009. It fixes the claim element and the answer shape it appears in (DP-13), the lot and account elements and their closed lists, the six consumed rows for the rwb-partner claim and sale terms, the rwb-case move answer and claim-window parameter, the rwb-decision package and the rwb-access right, the decision-record element of DP-03, the realized-recovery element, the rights and the error envelope, the fakes and the absence tests. TSD S6 appendix T-A publishes no claim operation, so the baseline declares no operation as provided and records the two legacy endpoint rows as RWB-S6-E6005-APP's and RWB-S6-E5026-APP's; the claim and the sale terms belong to rwb-partner (S9), the case states to rwb-case (P3), and the realized recovery has no column and no event. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the put-back claim step of rwb-debtsale — the claim element and the answer shape it appears in, the lot and account elements with their closed lists, the six consumed rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access rows, the decision-record element, the realized-recovery element, the rights, the error envelope and the fakes**, so that **the app story, SCR-26 Award, PRT-05 Data room and the wave 4 harness build against one fixed, testable contract on Day 1 and a claim state, a list value, a move name, a window parameter or an answer shape can never drift between rwb-debtsale, rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access without a failing build**.

This is the contract slice of legacy RWB-E6-009 and it copies none of the legacy criteria, which stay word for word with RWB-S6-E6009-APP. It owns the shapes and the absence tests only: no table, no row and no workflow is created here.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy claim of RWB-E6-009 crossed four boundaries at once: a buyer's claim, the sale terms, a case route state and a decision log. The target splits them: rwb-partner owns the buyer, the sale terms and the claim, rwb-case owns the case and its route states, rwb-access owns the right, rwb-decision owns the package and the claim-window parameter with its ledger, and rwb-debtsale owns the sold account, its claim state and the lot close. Each boundary is a contract that another team builds against, so each has to be fixed before the app story starts.

The baseline also fixes the naming that the checks require: schema `rwb_debtsale`, base `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1`, topic `rwb.debtsale.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-debtsale` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.debtsale` (Architecture v5 slide 19 notes).

Five points are carried as gaps and assumptions rather than decided quietly. The plan's C row for this slice is None while the step needs six consumed contracts (GAP-3009; ASM-4969). TSD S6 T-A publishes no claim operation, and the two endpoint rows of the legacy story are the award path and the data room read of two sibling stories (GAP-3009; ASM-4970). The claim window has no length, no parameter name and no column (ASM-4971). The realized recovery by lot and by buyer has no column and no event, and the data lake behind the monolith's Power BI is removed by DP-17 (ASM-4972). And the transfer and posting whose states the criteria start from belong to two sibling stories (ASM-4973). The wave is EP06's wave 4 while the service is created in wave 3, recorded once for the service and the epic (ASM-4974).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the queue and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the pagination and filter convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline (Architecture v5 slide 11); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The ownership of the objects is taken from the Ownership Map only: `debt_sale_lot` and `debt_sale_account` are S6's, `partner` and `partner_user` are S9's, `recovery_case` and `assignment` are P3's, `role` and `permission` are P4's, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are P7's, `document` is P5's and `notice` is P6's. This document never declares another service's table or operation as its own.
- The rwb-partner claim and sale-terms contract, the rwb-case state and move rows, the rwb-access authorise contract and the rwb-decision package and parameter rows are published with their fakes; they are not in this story's contract-dependency row, which is None, and the absence is recorded (GAP-3009; ASM-4969).
- The Debt sale rule package and its rows for R-DS-29, R-DS-34 and R-DS-35 to R-DS-39, and the claim-window parameter, are governed in rwb-decision (P7); this baseline names them and declares none of them.
- `debt_sale_lot` and `debt_sale_account` arrive with the DB story of this service; this baseline declares shapes and creates no table, no column and no migration (GAP-3009; ASM-4972).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 fragment of rwb-debtsale for this step: the claim element and the answer shape it is embedded in, with the rights and the error responses, and no operation of its own (GAP-3009; ASM-4970).
2. Fix the lot and account elements: the lot reference, the account set, the selling price, the claim state against `LOV-PUTBACK`, the lot status against `LOV-LOT-STATUS` and the realized-recovery element.
3. Fix the consumed rows: the rwb-partner claim and sale-terms read, the rwb-case state read and move answer, the rwb-access authorise call, the rwb-decision package read and the claim-window parameter read, marking the fields the sources do not give with the placeholder.
4. Record the decision-record element of DP-03, written before the claim row changes.
5. Record the closed vocabulary of the lists, the naming baseline and the rule that no value is a constant of the code.
6. Record that the buyer is an organisation and that no person name, identity number, date of birth or contact value is a property of any element, example or fake.
7. Publish the contract tables of section 12 and the fakes of 12.8.
8. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the additive rule, the vocabulary, the shapes, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the error envelope, the absence of a provided operation, the absence of a `partner`, `recovery_case` or `proceeds` property, the drift between a fake and the document, and the absence of published and consumed events of this step.
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-S6-E6009-APP, SCR-26 Award, PRT-05 Data room and the wave 4 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body or a request body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 400 or 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC5 |
| X2 | A field is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC5 |
| X4 | A consumed row has a field list the sources do not give | The row carries the placeholder, the gap and the assumption, and the fake is derived from the published document | None | AC2, AC3, AC4 |
| X5 | A value outside `LOV-PUTBACK`, `LOV-LOT-STATUS`, `LOV-SEGMENT` or `LOV-BUYER-CLASS` appears in the document or in an example | The vocabulary test fails the build | None | AC1 |
| X6 | The document declares a provided operation, a `partner`, `recovery_case` or `proceeds` property, or a write of another owner's row | The review fails the baseline; the boundary test fails the build | None | AC4, AC6 |
| X7 | The document declares a published or a consumed event for this step, a second topic or a Schedule | The absence test fails the build | None | AC6 |
| X8 | A person field — a name, an identity number, a date of birth or a contact value — appears in any element, example or fake | The schema test and the review fail the baseline | None | AC1, AC5 |
| X9 | The rights of a surface are not the ones TSD S6 T6.1 declares | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the Ownership Map and the published owner contracts of rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision only |
| Negotiable | The element names beyond the ones the sources give, the example values and the fake fixtures are settled in the baseline review; the element set, the lists, the base, the topic and the queue are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks RWB-S6-E6009-APP, SCR-26 Award, PRT-05 Data room and the wave 4 harness on Day 1, and the rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision teams on the same day |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI fragment, nine contract tables, seven fakes and six new contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

These six criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only. They restate no business outcome owned by RWB-S6-E6009-APP and they copy no criterion of the legacy story, whose four criteria stay with the app story word for word.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The sold account and the lot are rwb-debtsale's, and the contract declares their fields, their lists and their required flags on the lot and account elements only | Architecture v5 slide 41; TSD S6 T3.1 and T3.2; GAP-3009 |
| BR2 | The claim state is declared as the single value of `LOV-PUTBACK`, and one account carries one state; the contract declares no claim history element | TSD S6 T3.2; R-DS-35 to R-DS-38 |
| BR3 | The decision record is declared as an element written before the claim row changes, through the local library on the shared topic; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; TSD S6 T2; legacy RWB-E6-009 AC1 and AC4 |
| BR4 | The claim and the sale terms stay with rwb-partner: the contract declares the claim read as consumed and declares no partner property and no sale-terms storage | Architecture v5 slide 41; Ownership Map (`partner`, `partner_user` owner S9); GAP-3009 |
| BR5 | The case move is answered and not written: the contract declares the state read and the five moves, and declares no `recovery_case` property, no `assignment` property and no case row write | Ownership Map (recovery_case owner P3); ASM-4975 |
| BR6 | This baseline declares no provided operation: the step runs behind the lot read and the data room read of its siblings | TSD S6 T-A.1; GAP-3009 |
| BR7 | A POST declares the `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer; a GET declares none; the surfaces this element appears in are reads | Architecture v5 slide 11; TSD S6 T-A.2 |
| BR8 | The claim window is declared as a versioned parameter whose length is a placeholder; no window length is an enumeration member or a schema default | R-DS-34 ("per claim window"); ASM-4971 |
| BR9 | The realized recovery is declared by lot and by buyer from the selling price and is not a column of either table; no data lake output is declared (DP-17) | R-DS-34 and R-DS-39; TSD S6 T3.1; ASM-4972 |
| BR10 | The vocabulary is closed: `LOV-PUTBACK`, `LOV-LOT-STATUS`, `LOV-SEGMENT` and `LOV-BUYER-CLASS` are published as enumerated values and no list value is a constant of the code | TSD S6 T3.2; FSD S6 BR-S6-013 |
| BR11 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: the buyer is a partner organisation, the account is a masked reference, and no name, identity number, date of birth or contact value is declared | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17); FSD S6 A2.3 |
| BR12 | One REST base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; the document never declares another service's base or topic as its own | DP-13; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR13 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of this document, not of a claim:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The element, the lists, the consumed rows, the parameter and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, SCR-26 Award, PRT-05, the wave 4 harness and the rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision owners accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example an optional claim date | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, a list value changes, or a provided operation is added | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | The absence tests of AC4 and AC6 fail: a provided operation, a `partner`, `recovery_case` or `proceeds` property, an event or a Schedule | In review |

The claim state machine that the document describes is the app story's: a sold account moves from `NONE` to `CLAIMED`, then to `ACCEPTED` or `REJECTED`, and the lot closes when the window closes. This baseline fixes the vocabulary of those states and moves no account.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Claim element | The lot reference, the account reference, the claim reference, the claim state against `LOV-PUTBACK`, the rule ID with its version and the decided-at time |
| Lot and account elements | DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-037 of TSD S6 T3.1, with `status` (DF-SAL-030), `selling_price` (DF-SAL-036) and `put_back_status` (DF-SAL-037) as the columns the step writes, and no claim reason, claim date or window column declared because none exists (GAP-3009; ASM-4972) |
| Lists | `LOV-PUTBACK` (`NONE`, `CLAIMED`, `ACCEPTED`, `REJECTED`), `LOV-LOT-STATUS` (`BUILDING`, `OFFERED`, `AWARDED`, `TRANSFERRED`, `CLOSED`), `LOV-SEGMENT` (`RETAIL`, `SSME`, `CORPORATE`) and `LOV-BUYER-CLASS` (`AMC`, `NON_AMC`), published as enumerations and read as reference data at their version |
| Realized recovery | An element by lot and by buyer, derived from the `selling_price` of the closed lot's account set, on the lot read only; no column and no event (ASM-4972) |
| Decision record | DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 through the local library, written before the claim row changes (DP-03) |
| Claim and sale terms | The claim reference, the sold account reference, the sale terms in force and the buyer organisation, of S9 rwb-partner, read only through the owner's contract and never copied or joined here (GAP-3009; ASM-4969) |
| Not declared here | `recovery_case` and `assignment` (P3), `partner` and `partner_user` (S9), `role` and `permission` (P4), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `proceeds` (P8), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) |
| Consumed fields with no source | The operation names of the rwb-partner claim read, the rwb-case state read and move answer, the rwb-access authorise call and the rwb-decision parameter read, and the claim-window length: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3009; ASM-4969; ASM-4971) |

The field-level types, lengths and required flags of the added elements are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the element names, the vocabulary of AC2 and the optionality rule of BR13. **No new table, no new column and no migration** is declared by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None of its own. TSD S6 appendix T-A publishes five operations for the module: API-S6-001 `POST /debt-sale-lots` (C), API-S6-002 `GET /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}` (R), API-S6-003 `POST /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}/award` (A), API-S6-004 `GET /partner/data-room/{lotId}` (Partner portal R) and API-S6-005 `POST /partner/data-room/{lotId}/bids` (Partner portal C), and none of them is a claim or a claim-decision operation. The two endpoint rows of the legacy story are API-S6-003 and API-S6-004; they are RWB-S6-E6005-APP's and RWB-S6-E5026-APP's, and API-S6-005 belongs to the take-bids story of this service. This baseline therefore declares no operation as provided, records the two sibling rows by name, and fixes only the claim element and the answer shape it is embedded in. The absence is recorded as GAP-3009 with ASM-4970.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| The buyer claim and sale-terms read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3009; ASM-4969)) | `/api/recovery/partner/v1` | S9 rwb-partner | The claim reference, the sold account reference, the sale terms in force and the buyer organisation; faked. The read family of the Ownership Map is `GET /partners` |
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family (read) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case state, the case reference and the lot and account link; faked |
| The case-move answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3009; ASM-4969)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The move `PUTBACK_RAISED`, `PUTBACK_UPHELD`, `PUTBACK_REFUSED`, `BACK_TO_CASE_LIST` or `LOT_CLOSED` with the rule ID and its version; on the workflow boundary it is the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies; faked |
| The authorise call and the capability area read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3009; ASM-4969)) | `/api/recovery/access/v1` | P4 rwb-access | The capability areas "Debt sale" and "Partner portal", the right of the caller and the scope of its own lots; faked |
| The rule package in force (read) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The Debt sale package at its version with R-DS-29, R-DS-34 and R-DS-35 to R-DS-39; faked |
| The claim-window parameter and its version (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3009; ASM-4971)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The claim-window parameter of R-DS-34 and R-DS-39 at its version, on the parameters contract the default ruling gives rwb-case, with a placeholder for its length; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The six rows are contract dependencies of class C that the plan's C row does not carry, and the absence is recorded as GAP-3009 with ASM-4969.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT gives rwb-debtsale the topic `rwb.debtsale.events.v1` with `LotAwarded` (EV-23) and `AccountsTransferred`. `LotAwarded` is RWB-S6-E6005-APP's and `AccountsTransferred` is RWB-S6-E6007-APP's; the claim outcome and the lot close produce neither, and the service's event set carries no recovery or claim event, so the baseline declares no event of its own, no outbox row and no producer, and the absence test of AC6 fails a build that adds one (ASM-4972).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. Architecture v5 slide 19 IN gives rwb-debtsale the event `ProceedsMatched`, which belongs to the settlement step of this service, and no event of the module carries a buyer claim or a claim-window close. This baseline therefore declares no consumer group, no subscription, no inbox of its own and no Kafka call from this step, and the absence test of AC6 fails a build that adds one.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DebtSaleWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per lot, the child of `CaseWorkflow` on rwb-case (P3), a saga with pivot = transfer and continues-as-new across the settlement and the claim window | `rwb-debtsale` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | The stage that hosts the claim step; its signals, its durable window timer and its outcome for the parent are declared, not built |
| `reviewPutbackClaim` | Activity, the one claim step | `rwb-debtsale` | The lot, the case, the account and the claim in; the rule ID with its package version, the claim state and the case move out |
| `closeLotOnClaimWindow` | Activity, the claim-window close | `rwb-debtsale` | The lot, the account set and the window parameter in; the lot close, the realized recovery and the case move out |

No child workflow for the case and none for the money exists in this service. The activity names are a target design choice. No activity is registered by this story, and the saga steps of reserve, approval, payment, transfer, proceeds, case closure and customer notices belong to the award, settlement, transfer and posting stories of this service.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step runs from the claim and from a durable timer of the workflow; this baseline declares no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table, and no Job of Architecture v5 slide 44 is owned or moved here.

##### 13. Solution plan

**The CON declares shapes and moves nothing.** It writes no code, no migration and no table, and it changes no claim, lot, case, buyer record or rule package. What it publishes is one OpenAPI 3.1 fragment, nine contract tables, seven fakes and six new contract tests.

**Deliverables.** The additive fragment `openapi/rwb-debtsale-v1.yaml` for the claim element, the `Lot`, `SoldAccount`, `PutbackClaim` and `RealizedRecovery` elements, the vocabulary of the four lists as published enumerations, the contract README rows for the six consumed rows and their placeholders, and the seven WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the transaction rule the element describes: the record and the claim update commit together or not at all. DP-13 moves the base and nothing else. DP-19 is behind SCR-26 Award and PRT-05, whose screen model is the edge contract's, and the partner channel reaches the same element behind the partner gateway, which the plan does not carry (ASM-4970).

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds two H rows, `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` for DP-03 and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` for DP-19, which the plan's build list for this key already carries. It leaves out the six consumed rows, which are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata row, and the DP-06 parameter and DP-08 guard the step uses; neither is added to the metadata rows (GAP-3009; ASM-4969; ASM-4971).

**Build steps**

1. Write the claim element and the answer shape of AC1, with the no-provided-operation record, and validate the additive rule in the pipeline.
2. Write the `Lot` and `SoldAccount` elements, their required flags and the four lists of AC2 with the placeholder where a type is unstated.
3. Record the rwb-partner row of AC3 with its owner, its budget and its placeholder.
4. Record the rwb-case rows of AC4, the five move names and the state vocabulary, and the rwb-decision package and claim-window parameter rows.
5. Record the rwb-access rights and the error envelope of AC4.
6. Record the realized-recovery element of AC5 and the decision-record element, and validate both against the library schema.
7. Publish the seven fakes of AC5 and the drift test.
8. Record the naming baseline, the boundary and the partner channel of AC6, then tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI fragment validates in the pipeline, the five contract tests pass, the fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, and the app story, SCR-26 Award, PRT-05 and the wave 4 harness have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S6-001 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names an open deviation on an account selected for a lot, which is the eligibility story's, so no path of this step raises it | {account} has an open deviation and cannot be sold. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request is absent or invalid, or a body fails schema validation | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role or the partner identity lacks the Debt sale or the Partner portal right the surface declares | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the claim row changes | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE product that carries the account balance is stale after a late or failed batch; the check is the owner's and this service holds no ACE batch status read | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The five message IDs are contract elements and the text is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new one is added. MSG-P1-001 is carried because it is in the message set of this feature, and the check itself belongs to rwb-source-data.

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves SCR-26 Award in its open, closed, awarded and transferred states and PRT-05 Data room in its data room, bid and claimed states, all read only. The staff route is the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); the partner route is the partner gateway in the DMZ, which fronts rwb-partner and reaches the same claim element scoped to the buyer's own lots (ASM-4970). The route calls rwb-debtsale for the lot, the account set, the claim element and the realized recovery, rwb-case for the case and its route state and rwb-partner for the claim and the sale terms; this baseline fixes the claim element only, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The refusal, not-recorded, wrong-state and stale-data states the app story shows read the messages of section 14 on the same routes.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the claim-window length, the `LOV-PUTBACK` and `LOV-LOT-STATUS` values, the 10-working-day target and the rule rows stay data, reference data, parameters or the rule package, never a schema default or an enumeration member of the code.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: the buyer is a partner organisation, the account is a masked reference, and no name, identity number, date of birth, address or contact value is declared; every example is synthetic.
- The claim and the sale terms stay with rwb-partner, the case with rwb-case, the settlement with rwb-payment and the posting with the GL story: the document declares no `partner`, `recovery_case`, `assignment` or `proceeds` property and no ACE table read (BR4, BR5).
- The central ledger stays with rwb-decision: the document declares no `decision_log_entry` column and no rule-row column as its own.
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13).
- No operation of a sibling is claimed: API-S6-003 and API-S6-004 are named as the surfaces the step runs behind and as RWB-S6-E6005-APP's and RWB-S6-E5026-APP's, never as provided here (GAP-3009).
- No retired element is reintroduced: the absence tests fail a build that declares a published or consumed event, a second topic, a Schedule, a Quartz row, a shared job table or a data lake extract (DP-17).
- The error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule and the decision-record library come from the platform; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

- The sale documents and the notices of a returned account: rwb-document (P5) and rwb-comms (P6).
- The cross-service journey of the legacy key and its evidence: the wave 4 harness, which copies none of these criteria.
- The deployment of this capability, its flag, its dashboards, its alerts and its runbook: the operations story of this legacy key.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the application slice of RWB-E6-009 split out for rwb-debtsale. The four legacy acceptance criteria are kept word for word with their origin tag; the put-back review becomes one activity of `DebtSaleWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-debtsale`, which evaluates R-DS-35 on the claim, R-DS-36 or R-DS-38 on the sale terms, R-DS-37 on the return of the account and R-DS-34 on the claim window, writes the claim state against the sold account in `rwb_debtsale`, records the decision through the local decision-record library before the row changes (DP-03), answers rwb-case for the moves to `PUTBACK_RAISED`, `PUTBACK_UPHELD`, `PUTBACK_REFUSED` and `LOT_CLOSED`, and serves the claim element to SCR-26 Award and PRT-05 Data room on `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1` (DP-13) through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). TSD S6 appendix T-A publishes no put-back operation of its own, and the two legacy endpoint rows, the award path and the data room read, belong to RWB-S6-E6005-APP and RWB-S6-E5026-APP; the transfer of R-DS-29 and the posting that creates `GL_POSTED` belong to RWB-S6-E6007-APP and RWB-S6-E6008-APP. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **debt sale officer**, I want **to review a claim that an account should not have been sold, and settle or reject it**, so that **debt sales run on approved lots and masked data**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E6-009, the FEAT-DBS-13 step of the S6 Debt sale module, and it is one step of the saga that the Temporal and Drools Design gives S6 ("Monthly sale cycle; Award within reserve and cap"; the saga runner is used by S2, S5, S6 and S7). It owns:

- the four legacy acceptance criteria of the story, copied verbatim with their origin tag, and the rules, messages and screens they name;
- the put-back review of `DebtSaleWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-debtsale` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, as the stage child of `CaseWorkflow` owned by rwb-case, under the DEBTSALE route set of 41 rules over 29 states;
- R-DS-35 on the claim, R-DS-38 on a claim outside the sale terms, R-DS-36 on a claim inside them, R-DS-37 on the return of the account and R-DS-34 on the claim window that closes the lot; R-DS-29 is tabled with them because the legacy criteria name it and its transfer precedes the claim window;
- the claim state of the sold account on `debt_sale_account.put_back_status` (DF-SAL-037 against `LOV-PUTBACK`), the account's `selling_price` (DF-SAL-036) and the lot status of `debt_sale_lot.status` (DF-SAL-030 against `LOV-LOT-STATUS`), in schema `rwb_debtsale`;
- the realized recovery by lot and by buyer that R-DS-34 and R-DS-39 record when the lot closes;
- the local decision record of every claim outcome, written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON before any row changes (DP-03), which is what legacy AC1 and AC4 test;
- the answer to rwb-case for the moves `PUTBACK_RAISED`, `PUTBACK_UPHELD`, `PUTBACK_REFUSED` and `LOT_CLOSED`, with the rule ID and the version that produced each move;
- the claim element served read only on `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1` (DP-13) to SCR-26 Award and PRT-05 Data room through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

It does not own: the published shape of the claim and lot elements, the consumed rows, the case-move answer, the error set and the fakes, which are RWB-S6-E6009-CON; the transfer of the account data to the buyer under R-DS-29, which is RWB-S6-E6007-APP's; the derecognition and general ledger posting of R-DS-30 and R-DS-31 that create the `GL_POSTED` state, and the reversal on an upheld claim, which are RWB-S6-E6008-APP's; the settlement adjustment of an upheld claim, which is rwb-payment's (P8) and the settlement story's; the award operation API-S6-003 and its `DecisionLogEntry` answer, RWB-S6-E6005-APP's; the data room read API-S6-004 and its `DataRoom` answer, RWB-S6-E5026-APP's; the bid submission of API-S6-005; the buyer panel, the partner users and the buyer's identity, which are rwb-partner's (S9); the case of record, its route states and the parent `CaseWorkflow`, rwb-case's (P3); the central decision ledger and the rule rows, rwb-decision's (P7); the capability area and the right, rwb-access's (P4); the sale documents and the notices, rwb-document's (P5) and rwb-comms's (P6); the read model that R-DS-34's "Power BI" names under the monolith, rwb-reporting's (P9); and the deployment of this build, the operations story of this legacy key.

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E6-009 gave the Workbench one step that reviewed a claim that an account should not have been sold and settled or rejected it, and the FSD keeps the objective and the metric unchanged: the debt sale turnaround is measured on the decision log and the Workbench records, reviewed monthly, with a 45-day target (FSD S6 A2.13.1). The program keeps the requirement as REQ-S6-009, "A put-back claim from a buyer is reviewed against the sale terms and either accepted or refused with a reason" (FSD S6 Requirements served). The FSD glossary defines the object: "Put-back — a buyer returning an account under the sale terms".

What D-RCV-60 changes is where each fact of the claim lives and who acts on it.

- **The claim is a fact of the sold account, and the account set is this service's.** `debt_sale_account.put_back_status` with `LOV-PUTBACK` (`NONE`, `CLAIMED`, `ACCEPTED`, `REJECTED`) is the only claim column in TSD S6 T3.1 and it is S6's. The review therefore writes here, and the case moves are answered to rwb-case, which owns `recovery_case` and every route state (GAP-3008; ASM-4975).
- **The claim arrives through the partner channel, and no operation publishes it.** TSD S6 appendix T-A publishes five operations and none is a claim or a claim decision; the two endpoint rows of the legacy story are the award path API-S6-003 and the data room read API-S6-004, which are two sibling stories' (GAP-3008; ASM-4970).
- **Two of the four criteria execute rules that sit in sibling stories.** AC2 is R-DS-29, the transfer step of RWB-S6-E6007-APP, and AC3 starts from `GL_POSTED`, which R-DS-30 and R-DS-31 create in RWB-S6-E6008-APP; the criteria stay here word for word because the plan assigns them here, and the sibling activity is faked (GAP-3008; ASM-4973).
- **The claim window has no value and no column.** R-DS-34 fires on `CLAIM_WINDOW_CLOSED` with the timer "per claim window", and neither the workbook, the FSD nor the TSD gives its length. It is read as a parameter with its version and is never a constant of the build (GAP-3008; ASM-4971).
- **Realized recovery has no column and no event.** R-DS-34 and R-DS-39 record recovery by lot and by buyer; neither table carries such a column, the service's only event is EV-23 `LotAwarded`, and DP-17 removes the data lake and Power BI behind it. The figure is held on the lot and account rows and served on the lot read, and the reporting path is recorded (GAP-3008; ASM-4972).
- **The decision is recorded first**, through the local library of DP-03 in the same transaction as the claim change, which is what legacy AC1 asked for and what legacy AC4 tested.
- **The wave is EP06's and the service is wave 3.** §R5.6 keeps the W-MAP wave of a story when it is later than the service's Arch v5 wave, so this story is wave 4 while rwb-debtsale is created in wave 3; the conflict is recorded once for the service and the business epic (GAP-3008; ASM-4974).

No business value moves: the `LOV-PUTBACK` and `LOV-LOT-STATUS` values, the claim-window parameter, the 10-working-day review target of R-DS-35 and the sale terms are reference data, parameters and rule rows, read with their version.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S6-E6009-CON is published: the claim, lot and account elements, the closed lists, the six consumed rows, the case-move answer, the error set and the fakes are baselined and handed to this story.
- The rwb-partner contract of the buyer, the sale terms and the claim is published with its fake, so a claim can be read on Day 1. Its operation names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3008; ASM-4969), and the row is not in this story's contract-dependency list, which is None.
- The rwb-case state read and the case-move answer are available for the fake: the states `SETTLED`, `DATA_TRANSFERRED`, `GL_POSTED`, `PUTBACK_RAISED`, `PUTBACK_UPHELD`, `PUTBACK_REFUSED` and `LOT_CLOSED` are read and answered, never written here. No source publishes a REST operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage; on the workflow boundary the answer is the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies (GAP-3008; ASM-4975).
- The Debt sale rule package is in force at its version with R-DS-29, R-DS-34 and R-DS-35 to R-DS-39; the package is authored, tested and approved in rwb-decision (P7) and loaded here on `RulePackageInForce`.
- The claim-window parameter and its version are in force. The default ruling gives parameters to rwb-case (P3) and DP-06 is not in this story's pattern set, so the value is read through the parameters contract with a placeholder for its operation name and is stated here rather than built as a guard (GAP-3008; ASM-4971).
- The access contract of rwb-access (P4) answers the capability area "Debt sale" with its right and the scope of the caller, so a role without it is refused before any read.
- The RuleAndParameterClient reads the package in force from rwb-decision and the claim-window parameter from rwb-case, each with its version; the two rows are separate clients and separate fakes.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: the library writes in the caller's transaction and a failed write stops the action with MSG-P7-003, so the claim change and its record commit together or not at all (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-26 Award and PRT-05 Data room reach this service through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop each, and no screen calls a service directly (DP-19).
- `debt_sale_lot` and `debt_sale_account` exist in schema `rwb_debtsale` from the DB story of this service, with the columns of DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-037 and the standard record columns of TSD S6 T3.0; this story adds no table, no column and no migration of its own.
- The service runs as its own login on schema `rwb_debtsale` and holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema, so a statement on `rwb_case`, `rwb_partner`, `rwb_payment` or `rwb_decision` is refused by the database and fails the boundary test.
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-S6-E6009-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. A lot is awarded, settled and its account data transferred; the claim window of R-DS-34 opens at `GL_POSTED`. This story reads those states and owns none of them: the transfer is RWB-S6-E6007-APP's, the posting that creates `GL_POSTED` is RWB-S6-E6008-APP's, and the settled lot and signed sale terms arrive on the lot and account rows (GAP-3008; ASM-4973).
2. A buyer raises a claim against one sold account inside the sale terms. The claim reaches the Workbench through the partner channel and the partner portal; the claim read on the rwb-partner contract gives the claim reference, the sold account reference, the sale terms in force and the buyer organisation, and no operation of TSD S6 T-A carries it (GAP-3008; ASM-4970).
3. The claim branch of `DebtSaleWorkflow` on queue `rwb-debtsale` signals the review with the lot and the account, and reads the case state on the rwb-case contract to confirm that the case is in `GL_POSTED`.
4. `PutbackClaimEvaluator` loads the Debt sale package version in force from rwb-decision and applies R-DS-35: the claim is inside the sale terms and the case is in `GL_POSTED`. Where the claim falls outside the terms on its face, R-DS-38 applies rather than R-DS-35.
5. `PutbackDecisionRecordWriter` writes one decision record through the local decision-record library **before any change**: the case reference, the lot reference, the account reference, the claim reference, the rule ID with its version, the inputs reference, the outcome and the case move. A failed write stops the step with nothing changed (DP-03; legacy AC1 and AC4).
6. `PutbackClaimWriter` records the claim in one `rwb_debtsale` transaction: `put_back_status = CLAIMED` on the `debt_sale_account` row (DF-SAL-037), the account and lot references, the claim reference in the decision record, the idempotency row, and the optimistic lock on `version`. The buyer and the terms are referenced, never copied.
7. The step answers rwb-case with the move `PUTBACK_RAISED`, the rule ID, the version and the decided-at time. rwb-case writes the case row and its route state; this service writes neither.
8. On the decision inside the sale terms, R-DS-36 is applied: `put_back_status = ACCEPTED` (DF-SAL-037), the account is returned to the bank, and the step answers the move `PUTBACK_UPHELD`. R-DS-37's reversal of the derecognition and the settlement adjustment are the GL story's and rwb-payment's, and are recorded here as answered facts (GAP-3008; ASM-4973).
9. On a decision outside the sale terms, R-DS-38 is applied: `put_back_status = REJECTED` with the reason in the decision record, and the step answers the move `PUTBACK_REFUSED`.
10. When the claim window closes with no put-back claim inside it, R-DS-34 is applied: the lot moves to `status = CLOSED` (DF-SAL-030), the realized recovery is recorded by lot and by buyer from `selling_price` (DF-SAL-036) and the account set, and the step answers the move `LOT_CLOSED`. R-DS-39 applies the same close to a lot whose one claim was refused. The figure has no column of its own and no event, and both are recorded (GAP-3008; ASM-4972).
11. A repeated claim, a repeated decision or a repeated claim-window close with the same claim reference or `Idempotency-Key` writes nothing, answers no second move and counts the repeat; a claim on a lot that is not in `GL_POSTED` is refused with 409 and writes nothing.
12. The claim element is served read only on `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1` for SCR-26 Award and for PRT-05 Data room through the gateway-bff composite route: the lot reference, the account reference, the claim reference, the claim state against `LOV-PUTBACK`, the rule ID with its version and the decided-at time, with no personal data (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The local decision record cannot be written | The transaction writes nothing: no claim state, no lot close and no case-move answer leaves the service | MSG-P7-003 | AC1, AC4, TC-E6-009-04, TC-E6-009-06 |
| X2 | The role does not hold the Debt sale right of the capability area | 403 before any read or write; nothing changes and no record is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, TC-E6-009-05 |
| X3 | The case is not in the state the rule expects (`GL_POSTED` for R-DS-35 and R-DS-34, or one claim per account) | 409 and nothing is written; a second claim on the same account does not overwrite the first | None | AC1, AC3 |
| X4 | The ACE product that carries the account balance is stale after a late or failed batch | The step holds, writes nothing and shows the data date; the review resumes on the next fresh answer | MSG-P1-001 | AC1, AC3 |
| X5 | The rwb-partner, rwb-case or rwb-access contract does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The step waits and retries on the workflow's own schedule; nothing is written and no move is answered, and the caller sees 503 with the platform error envelope | None | AC1, AC3 |
| X6 | The claim lies plainly outside the sale terms | R-DS-38 refuses it with the reason recorded and the move `PUTBACK_REFUSED`; nothing is returned to the bank here | None | AC1 |
| X7 | The claim window parameter or its version is absent, or the window cannot be resolved | No rule fires: the lot is not closed, nothing changes and the reason is reported to the parent | None | AC3 |
| X8 | A claim, a decision or a claim-window close arrives twice for the same lot, account and reference | One row, one answer and one decision record; the repeat is counted | None | AC1, AC3 |
| X9 | A component, a statement or a test reaches `rwb_case`, `rwb_partner`, `rwb_payment`, `rwb_decision` or another service's schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | Section 17, BR2, BR8 |

X1 to X3 and X6 are the exception paths of RWB-E6-009 carried onto the split, X4, X5, X7 and X8 are the paths the target call types, the parameter and the idempotency rule add, and X9 is the DP-01 boundary. The claim-window length and the list values are values in force, so neither is a constant of this story.

| Negotiable | The activity name, the decision code per rule and the shape of the stage outcome are this story's choice; the rules, the messages, the screen, the claim element and the two tables are fixed |
| Valuable | A buyer's claim is settled or rejected with a recorded reason, and the lot closes with its realized recovery recorded, in the service that owns the sold account |
| Estimable | One workflow step, one evaluator, one record write, two claim writes, one lot close, one case-move answer, four clients and one read-only screen fragment |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on synthetic lots, claims and accounts through the contract fakes, plus the component cases of the access answer and the failed record write |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Handle a buyer put-back claim

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-000842" carries the debt sale lot "LOT-2026-000042" of segment "RETAIL" and the sold account "ACC-2026-000451"
    Given the Debt sale rule package is in force at its version and carries R-DS-29, R-DS-34, R-DS-35, R-DS-36, R-DS-37, R-DS-38 and R-DS-39
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 Handle a buyer put-back claim (legacy RWB-E6-009 AC1)
    Given the rwb-partner contract mock returns the put-back claim "PB-2026-000017" on the sold account "ACC-2026-000451" with the sale terms of the lot
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case state "GL_POSTED" for "RC-2026-000842"
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When the user acts on the screen
    Then reviews a claim that an account should not have been sold, and settles or rejects it
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Rule R-DS-29 (legacy RWB-E6-009 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case state "SETTLED" for "RC-2026-000842"
    Given a case in state SETTLED
    When data transfer run
    Then transfer the account data to the buyer
    Then the case moves to DATA_TRANSFERRED

  Scenario: AC3 Rule R-DS-34 (legacy RWB-E6-009 AC3)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case state "GL_POSTED" for "RC-2026-000842"
    Given a case in state GL_POSTED
    When claim window closed
    Then close the lot and record realized recovery by lot and by buyer
    Then the case moves to LOT_CLOSED

  Scenario: AC4 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E6-009 AC4)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The four criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E6-009 word for word: the repetition of `Then`, the legacy wording of `the action is taken`, `the decision log cannot be written`, `data transfer run`, `claim window closed` and `the user acts on the screen` all stand, and nothing is reworded or dropped. The cross-service parts are mocked, so AC1, AC2 and AC3 each carry one `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` line, and those added `Given` lines are the only additions to the legacy text.

What the legacy lines describe happens in four places in the target. The claim and the sale terms are rwb-partner's (S9), read on its contract and never as a table. The claim state is this service's, on `debt_sale_account.put_back_status` against `LOV-PUTBACK`, and the lot status on `debt_sale_lot.status` against `LOV-LOT-STATUS`. The case moves `DATA_TRANSFERRED`, `PUTBACK_RAISED`, `PUTBACK_UPHELD`, `PUTBACK_REFUSED` and `LOT_CLOSED` are **answered** to rwb-case, which writes the `recovery_case` row and its route state. Two points are recorded rather than smoothed over: AC2's transfer is the transfer step of RWB-S6-E6007-APP and AC3's `GL_POSTED` is created by RWB-S6-E6008-APP, so both are faked here while the criteria stay owned by this story; and the realized recovery of AC3 has no column and no event, so it is held on the account's `selling_price` and the closed lot and recorded as such (GAP-3008; ASM-4972; ASM-4973). The buyer is an organisation and the fixture data is synthetic: no name, identity number, date of birth or contact value appears in a fixture, and the account is carried by its masked reference.

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-DS-29 | Debt sale | D8.4 | SETTLED | DATA_TRANSFER_RUN | Any | Transfer the account data to the buyer | DATA_TRANSFERRED | Workbench | buyer portal | 5 working days |
| R-DS-34 | Debt sale | D8.4 | GL_POSTED | CLAIM_WINDOW_CLOSED | no put-back claim inside the claim window | Close the lot and record realized recovery by lot and by buyer | LOT_CLOSED | Debt sale officer | Recovery Data Store, Power BI | per claim window |
| R-DS-35 | Debt sale | D8.4 | GL_POSTED | PUTBACK_CLAIMED | buyer raises a claim inside the sale terms | Record the claim and review it against the terms | PUTBACK_RAISED | Debt sale officer | buyer portal, Decision Log | 10 working days |
| R-DS-36 | Debt sale | D8.4 | PUTBACK_RAISED | PUTBACK_ACCEPTED | the claim is valid under the sale terms | Return the account to the bank and adjust the settlement | PUTBACK_UPHELD | Debt sale officer | ALS core and GL, buyer portal | None |
| R-DS-37 | Debt sale | D8.4 | PUTBACK_UPHELD | ACCOUNT_RETURNED | Any | Reverse the derecognition and return the account to the case list | BACK_TO_CASE_LIST | Case owner | ALS core and GL, Workbench | None |
| R-DS-38 | Debt sale | D8.4 | PUTBACK_RAISED | PUTBACK_REFUSED_BY_BANK | the claim falls outside the sale terms | Refuse the claim with a recorded reason | PUTBACK_REFUSED | Debt sale officer | Decision Log, buyer portal | None |
| R-DS-39 | Debt sale | D8.4 | PUTBACK_REFUSED | CLAIM_CLOSED | Any | Close the lot with realized recovery recorded | LOT_CLOSED | Debt sale officer | Recovery Data Store | None |

The seven rows are the rows of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, copied character for character. Their owner column is a role of the business and not a service: the claim state and the lot close are written here, the case route states are written by rwb-case on this story's answer, the claim and the sale terms are rwb-partner's, the transfer of R-DS-29 is RWB-S6-E6007-APP's, and the derecognition reversal of R-DS-37 and the settlement adjustment of R-DS-36 are RWB-S6-E6008-APP's and rwb-payment's. R-DS-29 is tabled because AC2 names it and no claim can be raised before the account data is transferred; the transfer itself is not this story's step.

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|

| BR2 | The decision is recorded before the claim row changes, with the rule ID and the package version in force; a failed write changes nothing and the caller sees MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; TSD S6 T2 ("writes the decision log entry before any change"); legacy RWB-E6-009 AC1 and AC4 |
| BR3 | The claim, the sale terms and the buyer stay with rwb-partner (S9): this story reads no `partner`, `partner_user` or sale-terms table and takes the facts on the owner's contract only | Architecture v5 slide 41; Ownership Map (`partner` and `partner_user` owner S9); GAP-3008 |
| BR4 | The case move is answered and not written: `recovery_case` and the route states are rwb-case's, and this story sends the move with the rule and its version | Ownership Map (recovery_case owner P3); Architecture v5 slide 41; ASM-4975 |
| BR5 | One account carries one claim state: a second claim on the same account is refused with 409 and does not overwrite the first; the state follows `LOV-PUTBACK` only | TSD S6 T3.2 (`NONE`, `CLAIMED`, `ACCEPTED`, `REJECTED`); R-DS-35 to R-DS-38 |
| BR6 | The claim window and the review target are parameters read with their version, and no list value or window length is a constant of the code | FSD S6 BR-S6-013; R-DS-34 ("per claim window") and R-DS-35 (10 working days); GAP-3008 |
| BR7 | The realized recovery of a closed lot is the sum of the `selling_price` of its account set, held on the lot and account rows; no separate column and no event exists for it | R-DS-34 and R-DS-39; TSD S6 T3.1; ASM-4972 |
| BR8 | No cross-schema join and no foreign key leaves `rwb_debtsale`; `buyer_partner_id` and `account_id` are identifiers of other services' facts | DP-01; TSD S6 T3.3 (relationships inside the module only) |

| BR10 | No person name, identity number, date of birth, contact value or unmasked account identifier enters `rwb_debtsale`, the decision record, a log or a workflow input | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17); FSD S6 A2.3 (masked tape under PDPA) |

##### 9. State transitions

The case route state is rwb-case's and is not changed by this story: the step answers the move and the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies it to the case of record (BR4). What this story owns is the claim state of the sold account and the state of the lot.

| From (claim state of the sold account) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| NONE | A claim arrives under R-DS-35 | The case is in `GL_POSTED` and the claim is inside the sale terms | CLAIMED, with the case-move answer `PUTBACK_RAISED` |
| NONE | A claim arrives that falls outside the sale terms | R-DS-38 on its face | REJECTED with the reason recorded, with the case-move answer `PUTBACK_REFUSED` |
| CLAIMED | The decision under R-DS-36 | The claim is valid under the sale terms | ACCEPTED, with the case-move answer `PUTBACK_UPHELD` |
| CLAIMED | The decision under R-DS-38 | The claim falls outside the sale terms | REJECTED with the reason recorded, with the case-move answer `PUTBACK_REFUSED` |
| NONE | The claim window closes under R-DS-34 | No put-back claim inside the window | Unchanged on the account; the lot closes and the answer is `LOT_CLOSED` |
| ACCEPTED, REJECTED | The claim window closes under R-DS-39 or R-DS-34 | The lot is in `GL_POSTED` | Unchanged on the account; the lot closes and the answer is `LOT_CLOSED` |
| Any | A repeated claim, decision or close for the same reference | X8 | Unchanged, the repeat is counted |

| Lot status | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| TRANSFERRED | The transfer completes under R-DS-29, the transfer story's step | Any | Unchanged here; the case moves to `DATA_TRANSFERRED` and then to `GL_POSTED` |
| GL_POSTED | A claim inside the window under R-DS-35 | One claim per account | Still open for the window; the claim state is CLAIMED |
| GL_POSTED | The claim window closes under R-DS-34, or the claim is refused under R-DS-39 | No claim inside the window, or the one claim refused | CLOSED, with the realized recovery recorded |

The route states `SETTLED`, `DATA_TRANSFERRED`, `GL_POSTED`, `PUTBACK_RAISED`, `PUTBACK_UPHELD`, `PUTBACK_REFUSED`, `BACK_TO_CASE_LIST` and `LOT_CLOSED` are those of the DEBTSALE machine of TSD S6 T4 and of the legacy criteria, and they live on the case of record except `LOT_CLOSED`, which is answered with the lot close. The claim states are those of `LOV-PUTBACK` and the lot states those of `LOV-LOT-STATUS` in TSD S6 T3.2.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-DEBTSALE, debt sale officer | Debt sale CRUA in TSD S6 T6.1: the primary role of the feature, holding C, R, U and A; records the claim, decides it and closes the lot |
| RW-PRODHEAD, product head (Mortgage, HP, SSME) | Debt sale RA: reads the claim and approves through the approval path where a claim needs it; the DoA approval itself is `ApprovalWorkflow` of rwb-decision (P7) |
| RW-HEADASL, Head of Asset Liquidity | Debt sale RA: the approval authority of the sale and of an upheld claim; the authority itself is a parameter of the package |
| PT-BUYER, debt buyer and AMC | Partner portal RU, own lots only and scoped: raises a claim and reads its own outcome; sees no other buyer's claim |
| PT-RAMC | Partner portal R: reads its own lots and the claim state of its own accounts |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-AGENT | Debt sale R as the TSD S6 T6.1 matrix gives the service identities: the step runs under the service identity and is subject to the same checks |
| rwb-debtsale service identity | Runs the step, evaluates the rules, writes the decision record, the claim state and the lot close, answers the case move and serves the claim element; it holds no grant on another schema |

The rights above are the rows of TSD S6 T6.1 and nothing wider. The legacy permission table gives the Partner portal right R to the internal case roles with a long role list; in the target that read is the partner's own, scoped to its lots, and the internal roles read the same claim element on SCR-26 Award under their Debt sale right. DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set: the capability area and the right are declared per surface, and the guard of the access service is a service-template capability (GAP-3008; ASM-4969).

| BR Field ID | Entity (owner) | Field | Read or write |

| DF-SAL-020 | debt_sale_lot (S6, `rwb_debtsale`) | id | Read, the lot the claim and the close are recorded against |
| DF-SAL-021 | debt_sale_lot (S6, `rwb_debtsale`) | lot_no | Read, the lot reference of the screen answer |
| DF-SAL-022 | debt_sale_lot (S6, `rwb_debtsale`) | cut_off_date | Read, the window is counted from the cut-off and the transfer |

| DF-SAL-024, DF-SAL-029 | debt_sale_lot (S6, `rwb_debtsale`) | reserve_price, payment_terms | Read only: the sale terms are the buyer's contract fact and the settlement adjustment is rwb-payment's |
| DF-SAL-025, DF-SAL-026 | debt_sale_lot (S6, `rwb_debtsale`) | buyer_partner_id, buyer_class | Read, the buyer the claim is raised by, against `LOV-BUYER-CLASS` |
| DF-SAL-027, DF-SAL-028 | debt_sale_lot (S6, `rwb_debtsale`) | signing_date, approval_authority | Read, the signed sale the claim is judged against |

| DF-SAL-035 | debt_sale_account (S6, `rwb_debtsale`) | outstanding | Read, the balance the realized recovery is measured against (source Core bank (ALS) via COLLINS) |

| DF-SAL-037 | debt_sale_account (S6, `rwb_debtsale`) | put_back_status | Write, against `LOV-PUTBACK` (`NONE`, `CLAIMED`, `ACCEPTED`, `REJECTED`) |
| Standard columns | debt_sale_lot, debt_sale_account (S6, `rwb_debtsale`) | `state`, `version`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `is_active` | Write, with the optimistic lock of `version` |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (PLT library, created in `rwb_debtsale`) | rule id, rule version, inputs reference, outcome, reason, case move, decided at | Write through the local library, before the claim row changes |
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case (P3) | id, case_no, status, stage_code and the route state | Not read as a table: the case state arrives on the rwb-case contract and the move is answered to it |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | rule_row (P7) | rule id, rule version, route set, from state, event code | Not read as a table: the rule rows arrive in the package in force from rwb-decision |
