Field IDs are those of TSD S6 Debt sale v2 T3.1 and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. The four rows of the legacy Data table, `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row`, are the rows of other owners in the target: `recovery_case` and `assignment` are P3's, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are P7's, and this story reads none of them as a table. **No new table, no new column and no migration**: this story writes two existing columns and reads the rest, and `decision_record`, `idempotency_key` and `outbox_event` are platform library objects created in `rwb_debtsale` by the library's own migration.

**No personal data.** The rows this story writes carry identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version. The buyer is a partner organisation: no name, no identity number, no date of birth, no address and no contact value enters `rwb_debtsale`, the decision record, a log, an event or a workflow input, the account is carried by its masked reference, and the fixture data of the tests is synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None of its own. TSD S6 appendix T-A publishes five operations for the module: API-S6-001 `POST /debt-sale-lots`, API-S6-002 `GET /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}`, API-S6-003 `POST /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}/award`, API-S6-004 `GET /partner/data-room/{lotId}` and API-S6-005 `POST /partner/data-room/{lotId}/bids`, and none of them is a claim or a claim-decision operation. The two endpoint rows of the legacy story are API-S6-003 and API-S6-004, which belong to RWB-S6-E6005-APP and RWB-S6-E5026-APP. This story therefore provides no operation of its own, claims no sibling's operation, and is reached through the lot read and the data room read; the claim itself arrives on the rwb-partner contract. The absence is recorded as GAP-3008 with ASM-4970.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The buyer claim read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3008; ASM-4969)) | `/api/recovery/partner/v1` | S9 rwb-partner | The claim reference, the sold account reference, the sale terms in force and the buyer organisation; read only, faked. The read family of the Ownership Map is `GET /partners` |
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family (read) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case state and the lot and account link, read only, faked |
| The case-move answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3008; ASM-4969)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The move `PUTBACK_RAISED`, `PUTBACK_UPHELD`, `PUTBACK_REFUSED`, `BACK_TO_CASE_LIST` or `LOT_CLOSED` with the rule and its version; on the workflow boundary it is the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies; faked |
| The authorise call and the capability area read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3008; ASM-4969)) | `/api/recovery/access/v1` | P4 rwb-access | The capability area "Debt sale" with right C, R, U or A and "Partner portal" with right R, and the scope of the caller; faked |
| The rule package in force (read) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The Debt sale package at its version with R-DS-29, R-DS-34 and R-DS-35 to R-DS-39; read only, faked |
| The claim-window parameter and its version (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3008; ASM-4971)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The claim-window parameter of R-DS-34 and R-DS-39 at its version, on the parameters contract the default ruling gives rwb-case; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The six rows are contract dependencies of class C that the plan does not carry, because the C row of this slice is None, and the absence is recorded as GAP-3008 with ASM-4969.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT gives rwb-debtsale the topic `rwb.debtsale.events.v1` with `LotAwarded` (EV-23, consumers rwb-case and rwb-payment) and `AccountsTransferred`, and this story produces neither: `LotAwarded` is RWB-S6-E6005-APP's and `AccountsTransferred` is RWB-S6-E6007-APP's. The claim outcome and the lot close are answered to rwb-case on the move, and the realized recovery is held on the lot and account rows because the service's event set carries no recovery event (GAP-3008; ASM-4972). This story writes no outbox row, opens no producer and declares no event of its own, and a build that publishes one fails the absence test.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. Architecture v5 slide 19 IN gives rwb-debtsale the event `ProceedsMatched`, which belongs to the settlement step of this service, and no event of the module carries a buyer claim or a claim-window close; the window is a durable timer of the workflow, not an event. This story therefore holds no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox row of its own, and a build that adds one fails the absence test.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DebtSaleWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per lot, the child of `CaseWorkflow` on rwb-case (P3), a saga with pivot = transfer and continues-as-new across the settlement and the claim window | `rwb-debtsale` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the lot, the case, the claim and the rule package in force; signals: the claim, the claim decision and the case state answered by rwb-case; the claim-window timer is a durable timer of this workflow |
| `reviewPutbackClaim` | Activity, the one claim step of this story | `rwb-debtsale` | The lot, the case, the account and the claim in; the rule ID with its package version, the claim state, the lot close, the realized recovery and the case move out, with the decision record and the claim update in one transaction |
| `closeLotOnClaimWindow` | Activity, the claim-window close of R-DS-34 and R-DS-39 | `rwb-debtsale` | The lot, the account set and the window parameter in; the lot close, the realized recovery by lot and by buyer and the case move out |

No child workflow for the case and no workflow for the money exists in this service. The activity names are a target design choice of this story and are fixed by no source document. The saga steps of the workflow — reserve accounts, approve sale, buyer pays, transfer accounts, post proceeds, close cases and tell customers — belong to the award, settlement, transfer and posting stories of this service; this story owns the claim step and the claim-window close alone.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step runs from the claim and from a durable timer of the workflow, and owns no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job; the monthly debt sale cycle and the overnight jobs of Architecture v5 slide 44 are not owned, moved or registered here. The claim window of R-DS-34 is a timer of this workflow and not a Schedule, because it is per lot and starts at the posting.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| debt_sale_lot | S6 (`rwb_debtsale`) | The lot, its buyer, its terms and its status; this story writes `status` and reads the rest |
| debt_sale_account | S6 (`rwb_debtsale`) | The sold account, its `outstanding`, its `selling_price` and its `put_back_status`; this story writes `put_back_status` and reads the rest |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_debtsale` | The local hash-linked decision record of the rule outcome (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_debtsale` | The key of the repeated claim or close and the answer it holds |
| outbox_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_debtsale` | The library object exists; this step writes no row to it (ASM-4972) |

Not owned and never read as a table: `recovery_case` and `assignment` (P3), `partner`, `partner_user` and the sale-terms rows (S9), `role` and `permission` (P4), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `proceeds` and the settlement rows (P8), the rwb-reporting read model (P9) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No foreign key leaves the schema and `debt_sale_lot.buyer_partner_id` is an identifier, not a foreign key across schemas (DP-01).

| rwb-case state fake | The states `SETTLED`, `DATA_TRANSFERRED`, `GL_POSTED`, `PUTBACK_RAISED`, `PUTBACK_UPHELD`, `PUTBACK_REFUSED` and `LOT_CLOSED` of case `RC-2026-000842`, and a case that is not in the state the rule expects | AC1, AC2, AC3, X3 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The operation names of the rwb-partner claim read, the rwb-case move answer, the rwb-access authorise call and the rwb-decision parameter read are stubbed from the published documents and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-3008; ASM-4969).

| Call type | Count | Detail |

| REST | 0 provided, 6 consumed | The rwb-partner claim read, the rwb-case state read and move answer, the rwb-access authorise call, the rwb-decision package read and the rwb-case claim-window parameter read; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | `LotAwarded` (EV-23) and `AccountsTransferred` are sibling stories' and `ProceedsMatched` is the settlement step's; no claim event exists |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 2 activities | `DebtSaleWorkflow`, `reviewPutbackClaim` and `closeLotOnClaimWindow` on `rwb-debtsale`; the claim window is a durable timer, not a Schedule |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.debtsale`, module `putbackclaim`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.debtsale.putbackclaim`; front end `src/modules/recovery/debtsale/PutbackClaim.tsx`, the fragment SCR-26 Award and PRT-05 Data room embed, read only.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the transaction rule of the step: the record and the claim update commit together or not at all. DP-13 moves the base of the claim element and nothing else. DP-19 is how SCR-26 Award and PRT-05 reach this service, one hop through the gateway; the buyer's claim itself arrives over the partner channel, which has no plan row (GAP-3008; ASM-4970). DP-06 is not in the pattern set although the claim window is a parameter, DP-08 is not in it although the right is checked on every surface, and neither is added to the metadata rows; both are named here and in the registers (GAP-3008; ASM-4969; ASM-4971).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `DebtSaleWorkflow` claim branch | Workflow | The branch that waits for the claim, the decision and the window, loads the package in force and reports the outcome to the parent |
| `reviewPutbackClaim` | Activity | The one step: read the claim and the case, evaluate R-DS-35, R-DS-36 or R-DS-38, write the record and the claim state, answer the case move |
| `closeLotOnClaimWindow` | Activity | The close under R-DS-34 and R-DS-39: check the window against the parameter, close the lot, record the realized recovery and answer the move |
| `PutbackClaimEvaluator` | Service | The rule evaluation against the Debt sale package version in force, with the `LOV-PUTBACK` and `LOV-LOT-STATUS` values of the closed lists |
| `PutbackDecisionRecordWriter` | Library adapter | Writes the decision record with the rule ID and the version before any change, hash-linked, and refuses the step when the write fails (DP-03) |
| `PutbackClaimWriter` | Repository | Writes `put_back_status` on the `debt_sale_account` row and `status` on the `debt_sale_lot` row in one `rwb_debtsale` transaction, with the idempotency row and the optimistic lock |
| `PartnerClaimClient` | Client | The claim and sale-terms read of rwb-partner (S9), one hop, 2 s, breaker, no retry of its own |
| `CaseStateClient` | Client | The case state read and the case-move answer of rwb-case, one hop, 2 s |
| `AccessGuardClient` | Client | The capability area and the right of rwb-access (P4), through the service-template guard |
| `RuleAndParameterClient` | Client | The package in force and the claim-window parameter with their versions, from rwb-decision (P7) and rwb-case (P3) |
| `PutbackClaimController` | Controller | Serves the claim element on the service base with the capability area and right, and maps 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503; it declares no operation that TSD S6 T-A does not publish (GAP-3008; ASM-4970) |
| `PutbackClaim` | React component | Shows the claim state, the reason of a refusal and the closed lot on SCR-26 Award and PRT-05, read only |

**Database and migrations.** No Flyway file of this story. `debt_sale_lot` and `debt_sale_account` arrive with the DB story of this service, the decision record and the idempotency key are library objects created in `rwb_debtsale` by the library's migration (DP-03), and no realized-recovery column is added here; the absence of that column is recorded (GAP-3008; ASM-4972).

**Configuration and reference data.**

- `LOV-PUTBACK` (`NONE`, `CLAIMED`, `ACCEPTED`, `REJECTED`), `LOV-LOT-STATUS`, `LOV-SEGMENT` and `LOV-BUYER-CLASS` at their version in force (TSD S6 T3.2), read as reference data and never as constants.
- The Debt sale package with R-DS-29, R-DS-34 and R-DS-35 to R-DS-39 and the claim-window parameter, both with their versions, authored and approved in rwb-decision (P7); the 10-working-day target of R-DS-35 is a value of the package.
- The capability area "Debt sale" and its rights are access rows of rwb-access, read through the guard.
- No parameter of the claim step itself is named in the sources beyond the window; the 2 s budget and the single hop are the platform rule of ADR-020.

**Build steps**

1. The claim branch of `DebtSaleWorkflow` and its input record on `rwb-debtsale`, with the claim, the decision and the claim-window timer as its triggers.
2. `PartnerClaimClient` and `CaseStateClient` against their fakes, with the 2 s budget, the breaker, the stale-data path and the no-answer path (AC1, AC3, X4, X5).
3. `AccessGuardClient` and the two capability areas, with the refusal path (AC1, X2).
4. `RuleAndParameterClient` and `PutbackClaimEvaluator` over the package, with R-DS-35, R-DS-36, R-DS-38 and the no-fire path of an absent window (AC1, AC3, X7).
5. `PutbackDecisionRecordWriter` against the library stub, with the failed-write path (AC1, AC4, X1).
6. `PutbackClaimWriter` with the one transaction, the two columns, the idempotency row and the optimistic lock (AC1, X8).
7. `closeLotOnClaimWindow` with the window check, the lot close and the realized recovery by lot and by buyer (AC3).
8. `CaseMoveAnswer` and the parent signal, with the five moves (AC1, AC2, AC3).
9. `PutbackClaimController` with the rights and the problem mapping, declaring no unpublished operation, and `PutbackClaim` on the two screen fragments through the composite route fake (AC1).
10. The boundary test: no statement outside `rwb_debtsale`, no read of `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `partner`, `role`, `rule_row` or a `v_ace_*` view, and no write to another service's schema (X9, BR8, BR10).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.debtsale.putback-claim-v1`, read as a flag of the platform library; off means the step holds the claim, writes nothing and answers no move, and the award, transfer and posting stories are unaffected.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the step runs from a synthetic claim in SIT, each of the five rules produces its record, its claim state and its move, the lot closes with its realized recovery, a repeated claim or close writes once, a forced record failure changes nothing, no `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `partner` or `v_ace_*` read exists in the build, and SCR-26 Award and PRT-05 answer through the composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S6-001 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names an open deviation on an account selected for a lot, which is the eligibility story's, so no path of this story raises it | {account} has an open deviation and cannot be sold. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of the claim or of the decision is absent or invalid (X3, X6) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role or a partner identity without the right of the capability area raises, decides or closes a claim (X2) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the claim row changes (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE product that carries the account balance is stale after a late or failed batch (X4) | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The five message IDs are those of the legacy message set and of FSD S6 A2.13.3.1, and the text is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new one is added. MSG-S6-001 is carried because it is in the message set of the feature, and no path of this story raises it.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-26 Award in its open, closed, awarded and transferred states is served through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and PRT-05 Data room, "Lot data tapes and documents for admitted buyers, with bids" (FSD S6 Screens), is served to the partner on the same service base through the partner gateway in the DMZ. The route calls rwb-debtsale for the lot, the account set and the claim element, rwb-case for the case and its route state and rwb-partner for the claim and the sale terms; this story fixes the claim element only, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

The states this story produces on the claim element are `CLAIMED`, `ACCEPTED` and `REJECTED` against `LOV-PUTBACK`, the closed lot against `LOV-LOT-STATUS`, the refusal reason and the rule version, and it shows the failure states it reads: refused with MSG-P4-002, not recorded with MSG-P7-003, stale data with MSG-P1-001 and a case in the wrong state with 409. The award, settlement and transfer states of SCR-26 belong to the award, settlement and transfer stories and are read from the same route.

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID; the `-ITG` copies belong to the wave 4 harness and no `-ITG` copy is written here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the `LOV-PUTBACK`, `LOV-LOT-STATUS`, `LOV-SEGMENT` and `LOV-BUYER-CLASS` values, the claim-window length, the 10-working-day review target and the rule rows stay data, reference data, parameters or the rule package, never a constant, a default or a branch of the build.
- No personal data in `rwb_debtsale`, in a workflow input or in a log: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version only, every fixture synthetic, and the account carried by its masked reference. The buyer is a partner organisation, so no name, identity number, date of birth or contact value is written.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: this service reads no ACE table and no `v_ace_*` view, and a build that adds one fails the boundary test.
- The case stays with rwb-case, the claim and the sale terms with rwb-partner, the settlement adjustment with rwb-payment, the posting with the GL story and the central ledger with rwb-decision: no `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `partner`, `proceeds` or `decision_log_entry` row is written here (BR2, BR3, BR4).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; no document, module or test names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13).
- No operation of a sibling is claimed: the award path is RWB-S6-E6005-APP's and the data room read is RWB-S6-E5026-APP's, and a story that declares them as its own fails the review (GAP-3008).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no shared job table, no Quartz row, no monolith base, no data lake extract and no second event on the topic (DP-17).
- The decision is recorded before the change and the move is answered, not written; a build that writes a case row or records after the update fails the review (DP-03).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of the case-closure step of rwb-debtsale, split from RWB-E6-010. It fixes the closure element and the shape it appears in (DP-13), the closure answer and its vocabulary of end state and lot status, the consumed rows for the rwb-case case read and closure answer, the rwb-access right and the rwb-decision package, the decision-record element of DP-03, the rights, the error envelope, the fakes and the absence tests. TSD S6 T-A publishes no closure operation, so the baseline declares no provided operation and records the single legacy endpoint row as RWB-S6-E6005-APP's award path; the case of record stays with rwb-case (P3) and the transfer, derecognition and posting stay with RWB-S6-E6007-APP and RWB-S6-E6008-APP. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the case-closure step of rwb-debtsale — the closure element and the answer shape it appears in, the closure answer with its end state and its lot status vocabulary, the consumed rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision rows, the decision-record element, the rights, the error envelope and the fakes**, so that **the app story, SCR-26 Award and the wave 4 harness build against one fixed, testable contract on Day 1 and a closure state, a list value, a case reference or an answer shape can never drift between rwb-debtsale, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access without a failing build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy closure of RWB-E6-010 crossed four boundaries at once: a case with its open actions, a rule row with its version, a decision log and a lot. The target splits them: rwb-case owns the case, its state, its tasks and its timers; rwb-decision owns the UNIVERSAL package, R-UNI-47 and its ledger; rwb-access owns the right; rwb-debtsale owns the lot, the account set and the closure decision. Each boundary is now a contract that another team builds against, so each has to be fixed before the app story starts: the end state `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD`, the `LOV-LOT-STATUS`, `LOV-PUTBACK`, `LOV-SEGMENT` and `LOV-BUYER-CLASS` vocabulary, the closure answer, the case state and open actions of rwb-case, the right of rwb-access and the record of the decision.

The baseline also fixes the naming that the checks require: schema `rwb_debtsale`, base `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1`, topic `rwb.debtsale.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-debtsale` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.debtsale`.

Four points are carried as gaps and assumptions rather than decided quietly. The plan's C row for this slice is None while the step needs three consumed contracts (GAP-3011; ASM-4976). TSD S6 appendix T-A publishes no case-closure operation, and the single endpoint row of the legacy story is the award path of a sibling story (GAP-3011; ASM-4977). No source publishes the operation name of the closure answer, the case read or the authorise call (GAP-3011; ASM-4981). The feature is unattended in the FSD while the legacy permission row holds Debt sale right A for three human roles and TSD S6 T6.1 gives the service identities the right R, so the baseline fixes the right per surface and not per step (GAP-3011; ASM-4979). The integration points of FEAT-DBS-14 name ALS and GL while the derecognition and the posting are rules of FEAT-DBS-12, so the baseline declares no adapter and no posting (GAP-3011; ASM-4980). The wave of the story is EP06's wave 4 while the service is created in wave 3; the conflict is recorded once for the service and the business epic and is not raised again here.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the queue and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the pagination and filter convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline (Architecture v5 slide 11); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The ownership of the objects is taken from the Ownership Map only: `debt_sale_lot` and `debt_sale_account` are S6's, `recovery_case` and `timer` are P3's, `role` and `permission` are P4's, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are P7's, `deviation` is S8's, `document` is P5's and `notice` is P6's. This document never declares another service's table or operation as its own.
- The rwb-case state read and closure answer, the rwb-access authorise contract and the rwb-decision package read are published with their fakes, so each consumed row names a real owner document; they are not in this story's contract-dependency row, which is None, and the absence is recorded (GAP-3011; ASM-4976).
- The UNIVERSAL package and its row R-UNI-47, and the DEBTSALE package and its row R-DS-23, are governed in rwb-decision (P7); this baseline names them and declares none of them.
- `debt_sale_lot` and `debt_sale_account` arrive with the DB story of this service; this baseline declares shapes and creates no table, no column and no migration.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 fragment of rwb-debtsale for this step: the closure element and the answer shape it is embedded in, with the rights and the error responses, and no operation of its own (GAP-3011; ASM-4977).
2. Fix the closure element: the lot reference, the case reference, the account reference, the end state, the rule ID with its version and the decided-at time.
3. Fix the closure answer that leaves the service for rwb-case: the case reference, the end state `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD`, the rule ID with its version, the decided-at time and the instruction to stop every open action on the case.
4. Fix the consumed rows: the rwb-case case read and closure answer, the rwb-access authorise call and the rwb-decision package read, marking with the placeholder every field the sources do not give.
5. Record the decision-record element of DP-03, written before the closure answer.
6. Record the closed vocabulary: the end state, the lot status, the put-back, the segment and the buyer class, the naming baseline and the rule that no value is a constant of the code.
7. Record that the case and the account are named by reference and identifier only, and that no person field is a property of any element, example or fake.
8. Publish the contract tables of section 12 and the fakes of 12.8.
9. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the additive rule, the vocabulary, the shapes, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the error envelope, the absence of a provided operation, the absence of a `recovery_case` property, the drift between a fake and the document, and the absence of published and consumed events of this step.
10. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-S6-E6010-APP, SCR-26 Award and the wave 4 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body or a request body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 400 or 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC6 |
| X2 | A field is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC5 |
| X4 | A consumed row has a field list or an operation name the sources do not give | The row carries the placeholder, the gap and the assumption, and the fake is derived from the published document | None | AC3, AC4 |
| X5 | A value outside `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD` or one of the four lists appears in the document or in an example | The vocabulary test fails the build | None | AC2 |
| X6 | The document declares a provided operation, a `recovery_case` property, a `partner` property or a write of another owner's row | The review fails the baseline; the boundary test fails the build | None | AC6 |
| X7 | The document declares a published or a consumed event for this step, a second topic or a Schedule | The absence test fails the build | None | AC6 |
| X8 | A person field — a name, an identity number, a date of birth or a contact value — appears in any element, example or fake | The schema test and the review fail the baseline | None | AC2, AC5 |
| X9 | The rights of a surface are not the ones TSD S6 T6.1 declares | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the Ownership Map and the published owner contracts of rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision only |
| Negotiable | The element names beyond the ones the sources give, the example values and the fake fixtures are settled in the baseline review; the end state, the lists, the base, the topic and the queue are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks RWB-S6-E6010-APP, SCR-26 Award and the wave 4 harness on Day 1, and the rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision teams on the same day |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI fragment, nine contract tables, six fakes and five new contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

These six criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only. They restate no business outcome owned by RWB-S6-E6010-APP and they copy no criterion of the legacy story, whose two criteria stay with the app story word for word.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The lot, the account set and the closure decision are rwb-debtsale's, and the contract declares their fields, their lists and their required flags on the closure element and the closure answer | Architecture v5 slide 41; TSD S6 T3.1 and T3.2 |
| BR2 | The decision record is declared as an element written before the closure answer, through the local library on the shared topic; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; TSD S6 T2; legacy RWB-E6-010 AC1 and AC2 |
| BR3 | The case stays with rwb-case: the contract declares the case read and the closure answer as consumed and declares no `recovery_case` property, no case task and no timer | Ownership Map (`recovery_case`, `timer` owner P3); GAP-3011 |
| BR4 | The end state is closed: the document declares `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD` and no other case state, and the lot status vocabulary carries the transition the sibling stories make | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-47 and state table; TSD S6 T4 |
| BR5 | This baseline declares no provided operation: the step runs behind the lot read API-S6-002 and the composite route, and is signalled by the award operation API-S6-003 of RWB-S6-E6005-APP | TSD S6 T-A.1; GAP-3011 |
| BR6 | A POST declares the `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer; a GET declares none; the surfaces of this step are a read and an answer | Architecture v5 slide 11; TSD S6 T-A.2 |
| BR7 | The vocabulary is closed: `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD` and the four lists are published as enumerated values and no list value is a constant of the code | TSD S6 T3.2; FSD S6 BR-S6-014 |
| BR8 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: the account is an identifier and the case a reference, and no name, identity number, date of birth or contact value is declared | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17); FSD S6 A2.3 (masked tape under PDPA) |
| BR9 | One REST base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; the document never declares another service's base or topic as its own | DP-13; Template and Rules §R4 |

| BR11 | The rule rows R-UNI-47 and R-DS-23 and the reference data of the end state, the lot status and the put-back values are governed in rwb-decision and named here, never declared here | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; GAP-3011 |
| BR12 | The rights are fixed per surface, not per step: the unattended closure declares no right of its own, the element read declares Debt sale R and the award operation that triggers it declares Debt sale A | TSD S6 T6.1; FSD S6 A2.14.3.3; GAP-3011; ASM-4979 |

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of this document, not of a case:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The element, the answer, the lists, the consumed rows and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, SCR-26 Award, the wave 4 harness and the rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision owners accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example an optional closure reason | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, a list value changes or a provided operation is added | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | The absence tests of AC3 and AC6 fail: a provided operation, a `recovery_case` property, an event or a Schedule | In review |

The closure state machine that the document describes is the app story's: a case of an awarded lot answers `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD` once, and a case already closed answers nothing. This baseline fixes the vocabulary of that answer and moves no case and no lot.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-debtsale | Owns the OpenAPI fragment and the contract tables; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version, and the correction of the Ownership Map rows the baseline consumes, including the absent closure operation and the unattended-step right |
| Consuming teams (the app story, SCR-26 Award, the wave 4 harness and the owners of rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| Platform library owner | Owns the error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule and the decision-record library this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in an answer, an element or a fake, and that the account and the case are named by reference only |

The per-service login behind the security scheme of the document is named "the rwb_debtsale login (DP-02)" and is not part of this baseline.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Closure element | The lot reference, the case reference, the account reference, the end state, the rule ID with its version and the decided-at time |
| Closure answer | The case reference, the end state `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD`, the rule ID with its version, the decided-at time and the instruction to stop every open action on the case |
| Lot and account elements | The lot properties of DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-030, of which `id`, `lot_no`, `buyer_partner_id`, `signing_date` and `status` are read by this step, and the account set of DF-SAL-031 to DF-SAL-037, read only |
| Lists | `LOV-LOT-STATUS` (`BUILDING`, `OFFERED`, `AWARDED`, `TRANSFERRED`, `CLOSED`), `LOV-PUTBACK` (`NONE`, `CLAIMED`, `ACCEPTED`, `REJECTED`), `LOV-SEGMENT` (`RETAIL`, `SSME`, `CORPORATE`) and `LOV-BUYER-CLASS` (`AMC`, `NON_AMC`), published as enumerations and read as reference data at their version |
| End state | `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD`, the end state of the UNIVERSAL route set ("Case closed as sold", "Debt sold or asset cleared the balance") |
| Decision record | DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 through the local library, written before the closure answer (DP-03) |
| Not declared here | `recovery_case`, `timer`, `assignment` and `task` (P3), `deviation` (S8), `role` and `permission` (P4), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `proceeds` (P8), `partner` (S9) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) |
| Consumed fields with no source | The operation names of the case read, the closure answer and the authorise call: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3011; ASM-4981) |

The field-level types, lengths and required flags of the added elements are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the element names, the vocabulary of AC2 and the optionality rule of BR10. **No new table, no new column and no migration** is declared by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None of its own. TSD S6 appendix T-A publishes five operations for the module: API-S6-001 `POST /debt-sale-lots` (Debt sale C), API-S6-002 `GET /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}` (Debt sale R), API-S6-003 `POST /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}/award` (Debt sale A), API-S6-004 `GET /partner/data-room/{lotId}` (Partner portal R) and API-S6-005 `POST /partner/data-room/{lotId}/bids` (Partner portal C), and none of them is a case-closure operation. The single endpoint row of the legacy story is API-S6-003, which is RWB-S6-E6005-APP's award operation and on which the closure step is signalled. This baseline therefore declares no operation as provided, records the sibling row by name, and fixes only the closure element and the closure answer. The absence is recorded as GAP-3011 with ASM-4977.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /cases/{caseId}` family (read, operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3011; ASM-4981)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference, the case number, the route state and the open actions of each case of the awarded lot; faked |
| The case-closure answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3011; ASM-4981)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The end state `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD` with the rule ID, its version and the instruction to stop every open action; on the workflow boundary it is the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies; faked |
| The authorise call and the capability area read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3011; ASM-4981)) | `/api/recovery/access/v1` | P4 rwb-access | The capability areas "Debt sale" and "Case workflow", the right of the caller and the scope; faked |
| The rule package in force (read) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The UNIVERSAL package at its version with R-UNI-47 and the DEBTSALE package with R-DS-23; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The four rows are contract dependencies of class C that the plan's C row does not carry, and the absence is recorded as GAP-3011 with ASM-4976.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT gives rwb-debtsale the topic `rwb.debtsale.events.v1` with `LotAwarded` (event 23, consumers rwb-case and rwb-payment) and `AccountsTransferred` (consumers rwb-case and rwb-reporting). `LotAwarded` is RWB-S6-E6005-APP's and `AccountsTransferred` is RWB-S6-E6007-APP's; the closure step produces neither, so the baseline declares no event of its own, no outbox row and no producer, and the absence test of AC6 fails a build that adds one.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. Architecture v5 slide 19 IN gives rwb-debtsale the event `ProceedsMatched` (event 25), which belongs to RWB-S6-E6011-APP, and the closure is signalled inside the service's own workflow by the award confirmation. This baseline therefore declares no consumer group, no subscription, no inbox of its own and no Kafka call from this step, and the absence test of AC6 fails a build that adds one.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DebtSaleWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per lot, the child of `CaseWorkflow` on rwb-case (P3), a saga with pivot = transfer and continues-as-new across the settlement and the put-back window | `rwb-debtsale` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | The stage that hosts the closure step; its signals and its outcome for the parent are declared, not built |
| `closeCase` | Activity, the closure step, one execution per case of the lot | `rwb-debtsale` | The lot, the account set and the case in; the rule ID with its version, the end state, the decision record and the closure answer out |

No child workflow for the case and none for the money exists in this service. The activity name is a target design choice and the trigger is read as the award confirmation of the lot, because the FSD declares no background event for the feature (FSD S6 A2.14.4.4) while R-UNI-47 bounds it to the same day. No activity is registered by this story, and the saga steps of approval, agreement and notices, payment, transfer, derecognition, posting, the lot close and the customer notices belong to the sibling stories of this service.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step runs from the award confirmation and its bound is a durable timer inside the workflow; this baseline declares no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table, and no Job of Architecture v5 slide 44 is owned or moved here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |

| debt_sale_lot | S6 (`rwb_debtsale`) | The lot of the awarded accounts; the element the closure reads, with no column written |
| debt_sale_account | S6 (`rwb_debtsale`) | The account set of the lot whose cases are closed; read only |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_debtsale` | The local hash-linked decision record of the closure (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_debtsale` | The key of the repeated award signal and the answer it holds |
| outbox_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_debtsale` | The library object the service's sibling stories relay their events through; this step declares no row |

`recovery_case`, `timer`, `assignment` and `task` (P3), `deviation` (S8), `role` and `permission` (P4), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `proceeds` (P8), `partner` (S9) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) are not owned by this baseline; it names them only as answers, rule versions or a later story's table, and no foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The operation names of the case read, the closure answer and the authorise call are derived from the published documents and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-3011; ASM-4981).

##### 13. Solution plan

**The CON declares shapes and moves nothing.** It writes no code, no migration and no table, and it changes no lot, no account, no case and no rule package. What it publishes is one OpenAPI 3.1 fragment, nine contract tables, six fakes and five new contract tests.

**Deliverables.** The additive fragment `openapi/rwb-debtsale-v1.yaml` for the closure element and the closure answer, the `Closure` and `ClosureAnswer` elements, the vocabulary of the end state and the four lists as published enumerations, the contract README rows for the consumed rows and their placeholders, and the six WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the transaction rule the element describes: the record and the closure answer commit together or not at all. DP-13 moves the base of the closure element and of the award path, whose legacy base `/api/recovery/v1` the story master carries. DP-19 is behind SCR-26 Award, whose screen model is the edge contract's.

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds two H rows, `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` for DP-03 and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` for DP-19, which the plan's build list for this key already carries. It leaves out the four consumed rows, which are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata row, and the DP-08 guard, which the element read uses for the right but the pattern set does not carry; neither is added to the metadata rows (GAP-3011; ASM-4976).

**Build steps**

1. Write the closure element and the answer shape of AC1, with the no-provided-operation record, and validate the additive rule in the pipeline.
2. Write the closure answer of AC2 and the vocabulary of the end state and the four lists, with the placeholder where a type is unstated.
3. Record the rwb-case rows of AC3, their placeholders and the no-`recovery_case` boundary.
4. Record the rwb-decision package, the rwb-access rights and the error envelope of AC4.
5. Record the decision-record element of AC5 and validate it against the library schema.
6. Publish the six fakes of AC5 and the drift test.
7. Record the naming baseline and the boundary of AC6, then tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI fragment validates in the pipeline, the five contract tests pass, the fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, and the app story, SCR-26 Award and the wave 4 harness have accepted the baseline.

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S6-001 | Carried from the legacy message set of this key. It names an open deviation on an account, which the eligibility check of FEAT-DBS-01 raises at lot building, so no path of this step raises it | {account} has an open deviation and cannot be sold. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request is absent or invalid, or a body fails schema validation | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller lacks the Debt sale or the Case workflow right the surface declares | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the closure answer | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The four message IDs are contract elements and the text is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new one is added.

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves SCR-26 Award in its open, closed, awarded and transferred states, all read only. The staff route is the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which also calls rwb-case for the case and its state and rwb-partner for the buyer; this baseline fixes the closure element only, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The refusal and the not-recorded states the app story shows read the messages of section 14 on the same route. No new screen, no new field and no new user action is declared by this baseline.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the end state, the four lists, the same-day timer and the rule rows stay data, reference data or the rule package, never a schema default or an enumeration member of the code.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: the account is an identifier and the case a reference, and no name, identity number, date of birth, address or contact value is declared; every example is synthetic.
- The case stays with rwb-case and the deviation with rwb-deviation: the document declares no `recovery_case` property, no task, no timer, no deviation property and no case row write (BR3).
- No posting and no adapter: the derecognition, the ledger, the ALS update and the file transfer are the sibling stories' rules, and the document declares no posting, no balance and no file (GAP-3011).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13).
- No operation of a sibling is claimed: API-S6-003 is named as the surface that signals the step and as RWB-S6-E6005-APP's, never as provided here (GAP-3011).
- No retired element is reintroduced: the absence tests fail a build that declares a published or consumed event, a second topic, a Schedule, a Quartz row or a shared job table.
- The error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule and the decision-record library come from the platform; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the application slice of RWB-E6-010 split out for rwb-debtsale. The two legacy acceptance criteria are kept word for word with their origin tag; the closure becomes one step of `DebtSaleWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-debtsale`, which evaluates R-UNI-47 with the UNIVERSAL package in force when the lot is awarded, writes the decision record through the local decision-record library before anything changes (DP-03), answers rwb-case to stop every open action on the case and close it as sold, and carries the closure element read only on the service base `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1` (DP-13) through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The case of record, its state, its tasks, its timers and its open route children stay with rwb-case (P3); the transfer of the account data stays with RWB-S6-E6007-APP and the derecognition and posting with RWB-S6-E6008-APP. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **debt sale officer**, I want **the Workbench to stop every open action on a case whose account is sold in a lot, and close it**, so that **debt sales run on approved lots and masked data**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E6-010, the FEAT-DBS-14 step of the S6 Debt sale module. It owns:

- the two legacy acceptance criteria of the story, copied verbatim with their origin tag, and the rules, messages and screen states they depend on;
- the closure step of `DebtSaleWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-debtsale` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, the stage child of `CaseWorkflow` owned by rwb-case (Architecture v5 slides 19 and 23; Temporal and Drools Design slide 13);
- the evaluation of R-UNI-47 of the UNIVERSAL route set, at the award confirmation of the lot, with the package version in force recorded with the outcome; R-DS-23 is tabled with it because its `AWARD_CONFIRMED` signal is the trigger of the step;
- the local decision record of the closure, written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON before the case is closed (DP-03), which is what legacy AC1 and AC2 test;
- the answer to rwb-case, one per case of the awarded lot, that stops every open action on the case and closes it as sold with the rule ID, the version and the decided-at time;
- the closure element served read only on `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1` (DP-13) for SCR-26 Award in its closed state, reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

It does not own: the published shape of the closure element, the closure answer and its vocabulary, the consumed rows, the error set and the fakes, which are RWB-S6-E6010-CON; the award operation API-S6-003 `POST /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}/award` and its `DecisionLogEntry` answer, which are RWB-S6-E6005-APP's; the lot create and lot read operations API-S6-001 and API-S6-002, which are the lot stories'; the transfer of the awarded account data under R-DS-29, which is RWB-S6-E6007-APP's; the derecognition under R-DS-30 and the general ledger posting under R-DS-31, which are RWB-S6-E6008-APP's; the sale agreement and the customer notices under R-DS-23, which are RWB-S6-E6006-APP's and rwb-comms's and rwb-document's; the lot close under R-DS-34 and R-DS-39, which is the put-back story's; the case of record, its route states, its tasks, its timers and its open stage children, which are rwb-case's (P3); the deviation records and their pause of the stage clock, which are rwb-deviation's (S8); the central decision ledger, the rule rows and their approval, which are rwb-decision's (P7); the capability area, the right and the scope, which are rwb-access's (P4); the buyer panel, which is rwb-partner's (S9); and the deployment of this build, which is the operations story of this legacy key.

##### 2. Business rationale

Legacy RWB-E6-010 gave the Workbench one step that stopped every open action on a case whose account is sold in a lot and closed it, and the FSD keeps the objective and the metric unchanged: the debt sale turnaround is measured on the decision log and the Workbench records, reviewed monthly, with a 45-day target (FSD S6 A2.14.1). The program keeps the requirement as REQ-S6-007, "An account awarded in a lot stops every other open action on its case the same day" (Business Requirements Program v4).

What D-RCV-60 changes is who owns each fact the closure stands on. In the monolith the case, its tasks, its timers, the decision log and the lot sat in one `recovery` schema and one process. In the target:

- **the case of record stays with rwb-case (P3).** `recovery_case`, its route state, its tasks, its timers and the child workflows of the other routes are rwb-case's; this story evaluates the rule, writes its own record and **answers** the closure with the end state `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD`, and rwb-case applies it (GAP-3010; ASM-4976).
- **the trigger is the award, not a screen.** R-UNI-47 fires on `ACCOUNT_IN_SOLD_LOT`, and R-DS-23 records `AWARD_CONFIRMED` at the price test. The step therefore runs inside `DebtSaleWorkflow` and its timer is the same day of R-UNI-47, so no person is the primary role, which is what FSD S6 A2.14.3.3 says ("None; runs unattended").
- **"every open action" is applied on the workflow and case boundary.** No source enumerates the set: the FSD states only the outcome. The answer names the case and the end state, and rwb-case cancels its own tasks, timers and open deviations while the parent `CaseWorkflow` cancels the open stage children (GAP-3010; ASM-4978).
- **the decision is recorded first**, through the local decision-record library of DP-03 in the caller's transaction, which is what legacy AC1 asked for and what legacy AC2 tested.
- **the step publishes no operation of its own.** TSD S6 appendix T-A publishes five operations for the module and none is a case closure; the closure arrives as the award signal on API-S6-003, which is RWB-S6-E6005-APP's, and the closure element is embedded in the lot read answer API-S6-002 of the lot stories. This story claims no sibling's operation (GAP-3010; ASM-4977).
- **the unattended step has no human right of its own.** The FSD makes the feature unattended, the legacy permission table gives Debt sale right A to three human roles, and TSD S6 T6.1 gives the service identities the right R only. The step therefore runs under the rwb-debtsale service identity and the right A stays with the three roles for the award and for the read of the closure element (GAP-3010; ASM-4979).
- **ALS and GL are not this step's.** The integration points of FEAT-DBS-14 read "Workbench, ALS and GL", while the ALS derecognition and the ledger posting are R-DS-30 and R-DS-31 of FEAT-DBS-12. The closure holds no adapter, no posting and no balance (GAP-3010; ASM-4980).
- **the wave is EP06's and the service is wave 3.** Template and Rules §R5.6 keeps the W-MAP wave of a story when it is later than the service's Arch v5 wave, so this story is wave 4 while rwb-debtsale is created in wave 3; the conflict is recorded once for the service and the business epic and is not raised again here.

The metric of the feature is unchanged and is the review of the closure records, so no business value moves: the `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD` end state, the `LOV-LOT-STATUS` and `LOV-PUTBACK` values and the same-day timer of R-UNI-47 are values of reference data and of the rule package, read with their version and never written in code.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S6-E6010-CON is published: the closure element, the closure answer and its vocabulary, the consumed rows, the error set and the fakes are baselined and handed to this story.
- The rwb-case state read and the closure answer are available for the fake. No source publishes an operation that closes a case on behalf of a stage; on the workflow boundary the answer is the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies, and where rwb-case publishes a REST closure operation its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3010; ASM-4976, ASM-4981).
- The rwb-access authorise contract answers the capability areas "Debt sale" and "Case workflow" with their rights and the scope, so a caller without the right is refused before any read. The operation name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3010; ASM-4976).
- The UNIVERSAL package of 50 rules is in force at its version with R-UNI-47, and the DEBTSALE package at its version; both are authored, tested and approved in rwb-decision (P7) and loaded here on the package read. The rule rows and the reference data of the lot status are governed there. The operation name of the package read is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3010; ASM-4976).
- The lot of the case is `AWARDED` with its buyer reference and its signing date from the award story, and `debt_sale_lot` and `debt_sale_account` exist in schema `rwb_debtsale` from the DB story of this service, with the columns of DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-037; this story adds no table, no column and no migration of its own.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: the library writes in the caller's transaction and a failed write stops the step with MSG-P7-003, so the record and the answer commit together or not at all (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-26 Award reaches this service through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, and no screen calls a service directly (DP-19).
- The service runs as its own login on schema `rwb_debtsale`; it holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema, so a statement on `rwb_case`, `rwb_decision`, `rwb_access` or `rwb_deviation` is refused by the database and fails the boundary test.
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-S6-E6010-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The award operation API-S6-003 of RWB-S6-E6005-APP records `AWARD_CONFIRMED` on the lot and the lot reaches `LOT_AWARDED` under R-DS-23; that signal is the trigger of this step, and no screen starts it.
2. The closure branch of `DebtSaleWorkflow` on queue `rwb-debtsale` starts one execution of the step per case of the awarded lot, and arms the same-day timer of R-UNI-47.
3. The step reads its own lot on `debt_sale_lot` in `rwb_debtsale`: the lot reference, the buyer reference, the signing date and the status `AWARDED`, and the account set of `debt_sale_account` for that lot (DF-SAL-031 to DF-SAL-037). No other schema is read.
4. It reads the case of each awarded account on the rwb-case contract: the case reference, the case number, the route state and the count of open actions, read only, one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker (GAP-3010; ASM-4976).
5. It loads the UNIVERSAL package version in force from rwb-decision and evaluates R-UNI-47 on the fact: an account of the case is awarded in this debt sale lot while the case is active. Where the case is already closed, no rule fires, nothing changes and the repeat is counted.
6. `ClosureDecisionRecordWriter` writes one decision record through the local decision-record library, **before any change**: the case reference, the lot reference, the account reference, the rule ID `R-UNI-47` with its package version, the inputs reference, the outcome `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD` and the decided-at time. A failed write stops the step with nothing changed (DP-03; legacy AC1 and AC2).
7. `SoldCaseClient` answers rwb-case with the closure of that case: the end state `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD`, the rule ID with its version and the instruction to stop every open action on the case. rwb-case writes the `recovery_case` row, its state and its timer rows; this service writes none of them.
8. rwb-case stops the open actions it owns and reports the closed case; the parent `CaseWorkflow` cancels the open stage children of the other routes on the case, and the open deviations of rwb-deviation (S8) are closed against the sold case with their outcome recorded there.
9. The transfer of the awarded account data under R-DS-29 and the derecognition and posting under R-DS-30 and R-DS-31 follow in RWB-S6-E6007-APP and RWB-S6-E6008-APP against the case that is now closed; this step waits for none of them and posts nothing (GAP-3010; ASM-4980).
10. A repeated award signal or a repeated closure answer for the same case and `Idempotency-Key` writes nothing, answers no second closure and counts the repeat.
11. The closure element is served read only on `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1` (DP-13) with the lot reference, the case reference, the end state, the rule ID with its version and the decided-at time, for SCR-26 Award in its closed state through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and it carries no personal data.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The local decision record cannot be written | The transaction writes nothing: no case closure answer leaves the service and the case keeps its state | MSG-P7-003 | AC1, AC2, TC-E6-010-02, TC-E6-010-04 |
| X2 | The caller does not hold the Debt sale or the Case workflow right of the capability area on the read of the closure element | 403 before any read; nothing changes and no decision record is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, TC-E6-010-03 |
| X3 | The case is already closed when the award signal arrives | No rule fires: nothing changes, no record is written and the repeat is counted | None | AC1 |
| X4 | The rwb-case, rwb-access or rwb-decision contract does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The step waits and retries on the workflow's own schedule; nothing is written and no closure is answered, and the read of the element answers 503 with the platform error envelope | None | AC1 |
| X5 | An account of the lot has no open case | Nothing is done for that account and the lot closure count records the absence; the case that is already closed is not re-closed | None | AC1 |
| X6 | A statement or a component reaches `rwb_case`, `rwb_decision`, `rwb_access`, `rwb_deviation` or another service's schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | Section 17, BR5, BR10 |
| X7 | The request body of the element read fails validation | 400 with the platform error envelope, and the closure itself is untouched | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |

X1 and X2 are the exception paths of RWB-E6-010 carried onto the split; X3 to X7 are the paths the workflow trigger, the call types and the DP-01 boundary add. The `MSG-S6-001` row of the legacy message set names an open deviation on an account, which the eligibility check of FEAT-DBS-01 raises at lot building, so no path of this step raises it.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-S6-E6010-CON, the rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision fakes and the decision-record stub, on its own schema, and needs no live P3, P4 or P7 |
| Negotiable | The activity name, the decision code and the shape of the stage outcome are this story's choice; the rule row, the end state, the messages, the screen states and the two tables are fixed |
| Valuable | A case whose account is sold stops every open action and closes the same day, in one record, and the case owner sees the end state |
| Estimable | One workflow step, one evaluator, one record write, one closure answer per case, one answer to the parent, three clients and one read-only element |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on synthetic lots and cases through the contract fakes, plus the component cases of the failed record write and the refused caller |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Close a case awarded in a sold lot

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-000842" carries an account sold in the debt sale lot "LOT-2026-000042" of segment "RETAIL"
    Given the UNIVERSAL package is in force at its version and carries R-UNI-47
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 Close a case awarded in a sold lot (legacy RWB-E6-010 AC1)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case "RC-2026-000842" in the state "LOT_AWARDED" with its open actions
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns the UNIVERSAL package at its version in force with R-UNI-47
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When its trigger arrives
    Then stops every open action on a case whose account is sold in a lot, and closes it
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E6-010 AC2)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The two criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E6-010 word for word, with their origin tag added and nothing else changed: the repeated `Then`, the wording of `its trigger arrives`, `the action is taken` and `the decision log cannot be written` all stand. The cross-service parts are mocked, so AC1 carries two `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` lines, and those added `Given` lines are the only additions to the legacy text. What the legacy lines describe happens in three places in the target. The case and its open actions are rwb-case's: the step answers the closure with the end state `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD` and rwb-case cancels its own tasks, timers and open deviations, while the parent `CaseWorkflow` cancels the open stage children of the other routes. The decision is recorded through the local decision-record library before the answer leaves the service, which is the `decision log` of the legacy text and the central ledger of rwb-decision behind it. The step is triggered by the award confirmation of the lot, its timer is the same day of R-UNI-47, and it publishes no operation of its own. The set of "open actions" is not enumerated by any source, so the answer names the case and the end state and the owners apply it inside their own boundaries (GAP-3010; ASM-4978).

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-DS-23 | Debt sale | D8.4 | AWARD_PENDING | AWARD_CONFIRMED | price tested against the reserve and the 54 percent cap, and recorded | Award the lot and generate the sale agreement and the customer notices | LOT_AWARDED | Debt sale officer | Document Hub, buyer portal | None |
| R-UNI-47 | Universal rules | All | ANY_ACTIVE | ACCOUNT_IN_SOLD_LOT | the account is awarded in a debt sale lot while on another route | Stop every open action, close the case as sold, transfer the data | CASE_CLOSED_SOLD | Debt sale officer | ALS and GL, Workbench | same day |

The two rows are the rows of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, copied character for character. Their owner and systems columns name business roles and systems, not services: in the target "Workbench" is rwb-case and SCR-26, "Document Hub" is rwb-document (P5), "ALS and GL" are the derecognition and posting steps of R-DS-30 and R-DS-31 in RWB-S6-E6008-APP, and "buyer portal" is the partner channel of rwb-partner. R-DS-23 is tabled because its `AWARD_CONFIRMED` signal is the trigger of this step; the award itself, the agreement and the notices belong to RWB-S6-E6005-APP and RWB-S6-E6006-APP, and the data transfer named in the action of R-UNI-47 belongs to RWB-S6-E6007-APP. The from state of R-UNI-47 is `ANY_ACTIVE`, "Any non-terminal state on any route", so the row applies to a case whose only route is the debt sale as well as to one that sits on another route (ASM-4978).

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The closure is this service's decision and rwb-case's write: this story evaluates R-UNI-47, records it and answers `CASE_CLOSED_SOLD`; `recovery_case`, its state, its tasks and its timers are never written here | Ownership Map (`recovery_case` owner P3); TSD S6 T4; GAP-3010 |
| BR2 | The decision is recorded before the closure answer leaves the service, with the rule ID and the package version in force; a failed write changes nothing and the caller sees MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; TSD S6 T2 ("writes the decision log entry before any change"); legacy RWB-E6-010 AC1 and AC2 |
| BR3 | The step is triggered by the award confirmation of the lot and bounded by the same-day timer of R-UNI-47; no screen, no batch and no schedule starts it | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DS-23 and R-UNI-47; FSD S6 A2.14.2 |
| BR4 | "Every open action" is applied by the owners: rwb-case cancels its tasks, timers and open deviations and the parent cancels the open stage children; this service sends the case reference, the end state and the rule with its version only | FSD S6 A2.14.1; GAP-3010; ASM-4978 |
| BR5 | No cross-schema join and no foreign key leaves `rwb_debtsale`; `buyer_partner_id` and `account_id` are identifiers of other services' facts | DP-01; TSD S6 T3.3 |
| BR6 | Every value a business person may change is reference data or a rule row read with its version: `LOV-LOT-STATUS` (`BUILDING`, `OFFERED`, `AWARDED`, `TRANSFERRED`, `CLOSED`), `LOV-PUTBACK`, `LOV-SEGMENT`, `LOV-BUYER-CLASS` and the same-day timer of R-UNI-47 | TSD S6 T3.2; FSD S6 BR-S6-014; legacy Guardrails |
| BR7 | This story declares no REST operation of its own: the closure element is embedded in the lot read answer API-S6-002 and read through the composite route, and the award operation API-S6-003 is RWB-S6-E6005-APP's | TSD S6 T-A.1; GAP-3010 |
| BR8 | The same award signal or the same closure answer twice, or the same `Idempotency-Key` twice, closes once, answers once and counts the repeat | TSD S6 T-A.2; Architecture v5 slide 11 |

| BR10 | The staff screen reads the closure element through the gateway-bff composite route and no screen calls a service directly; the service holds no grant on another schema | DP-19; DP-01; Architecture v5 slides 8 and 13 |

##### 9. State transitions

The case state is rwb-case's and is not changed by this story: the step answers the closure and the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies it to the case of record (BR1). What this story does own is the state of the step.

| From (case of record, answered) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANY_ACTIVE | `ACCOUNT_IN_SOLD_LOT` under R-UNI-47 | An account of the case is awarded in the lot | CASE_CLOSED_SOLD, with the rule ID and its version |
| CASE_CLOSED_SOLD | Any repeated award signal | X3 | Unchanged, the repeat is counted |
| Any state | The same-day timer of R-UNI-47 passes without a closure answer | X4 | The step is retried; the case keeps its state until the answer lands |

| Step execution | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting | The award confirmation of the lot arrives | The package in force is loaded | Evaluating |
| Evaluating | R-UNI-47 fires for a case of the lot | The decision record is written | Applying |
| Applying | The closure answer is sent and rwb-case accepts it | The transaction commits | Waiting for the next case or the end of the lot |
| Applying | The record write or the answer fails | X1, X4 | Waiting, nothing changed |
| Waiting | The case is already closed | X3 | Done, nothing written |

`CASE_CLOSED_SOLD` is the end state of the UNIVERSAL route set in the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 ("Case closed as sold", "Debt sold or asset cleared the balance") and lies on the case of record of rwb-case. The lot status stays `AWARDED` here and moves to `TRANSFERRED` under R-DS-29 in RWB-S6-E6007-APP and to `CLOSED` under R-DS-34 or R-DS-39 in the put-back story; `LOV-LOT-STATUS` carries those values.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-DEBTSALE, debt sale officer | Debt sale CRUA in TSD S6 T6.1: the role of the legacy permission row, reading the closure element on SCR-26 and holding the award that triggers the closure; the closure itself runs unattended |
| RW-PRODHEAD, product head (Mortgage, HP, SSME) | Debt sale RA: reads the closure element and approves through the approval path where a lot needs it; the DoA approval is `ApprovalWorkflow` of rwb-decision (P7) |
| RW-HEADASL, Head of Asset Liquidity | Debt sale RA: reads the closure element and holds the authority of the sale |
| RW-CREDITAD, Credit Administration officer | Debt sale R: reads the closure element of a sold lot for the remittance and posting work of RWB-S6-E6011-APP and RWB-S6-E6008-APP |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the closure state on the case of record, which is rwb-case's surface, and takes no action of this story |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-AGENT | Debt sale R as the TSD S6 T6.1 matrix gives the service identities: the step runs under the service identity and is subject to the same checks |
| rwb-debtsale service identity | Runs the closure step, evaluates R-UNI-47, writes the decision record and answers the closure; it holds no grant on another schema |

The rights above are the rows of TSD S6 T6.1 and nothing wider. The legacy permission table gives Debt sale right A to `RW-DEBTSALE`, `RW-PRODHEAD` and `RW-HEADASL`, and that row stays with the award operation and the read of the closure element, because the FSD makes the closure unattended and no service identity holds the right A in the target matrix (GAP-3010; ASM-4979). DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set: the capability area and the right are declared per surface and the guard is a service-template capability, so the check is stated here and not built here.
