AC1 to AC8 are new for the rwb-case slice: the four legacy criteria of RWB-E6-017 are proved end to end by RWB-ITG-E6017-ITG and by the S7 slice RWB-S7-E6017-APP, so this story owns no legacy criterion and copies none. The rule version label "WO-2026.07", the pack and meeting references and the case ID are synthetic test fixtures of the same kind as the legacy "SYN" values; the version in force, the meeting reference and its date of a real case come from the S7 routing answer (GAP-0738; ASM-1335).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | When the amount is inside the write-off committee limit, the pack is routed to the committee and the meeting is scheduled before the scheduled meeting, and the case moves from PACK_PREPARED to WITH_COMMITTEE | R-WO-11 |
| BR2 | A case with an open deviation in X1 to X7 is held out of the population, routed to the deviation handler and moved from POPULATION_PROPOSED to CASE_REMOVED_BY_TEAM | R-WO-06 |
| BR3 | The case stage, the queue, the task and the timer are rwb-case's and are never written by the caller that routes the pack | Architecture v5 slide 41 (P3 owns case, CMMN state, queues, tasks, allocation, timers); DP-01 |
| BR4 | The committee, the write-off pack, the amount, the tax criteria and the committee approval are rwb-writeoff's; rwb-case holds the meeting reference and its date and nothing of the write-off record | Architecture v5 slide 41 (S7 owns eligibility, committee, posting, recovery after charge-off); slide 20 S7 DB line |
| BR5 | The case's own `deviation_open` flag drives the hold-out, so a deviation raised after the population is proposed still keeps the case out of the committee | DF-CAS-019; R-WO-06 |
| BR6 | A route answer must name the rule ID, a rule version in force, the meeting reference and its date; an answer with no version in force is refused as NoPackageInForce and no state changes | D-RCV-36 T7 (no package in force is a refusal); MSG-P3-027 |
| BR7 | The booking is held as a durable timer of CaseWorkflow, not as a Temporal Schedule, a Quartz job or a five-minute check, so the meeting date survives a worker restart | Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 14; Architecture v5 slide 44 |
| BR8 | The decision record, the state change and the outbox rows are one transaction: a decision that cannot be recorded does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; DP-03 |
| BR9 | The same answer arriving twice writes no row and raises no event a second time | R-UNI-40 |
| BR10 | The routing step names the rule ID and the rule version on every decision record; the rule ID and the version arrive in the answer and are never written in code | R-WO-11; R-WO-06; DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 |
| BR11 | The stage move and the queue placement are one move: a case is never on the committee queue in one stage and off it in the next | R-WO-11; R-WO-06; P3 queue ownership |
| BR12 | The read of a case is guarded by the Case record right and the scope, and a read writes nothing | DP-08; MSG-P4-002; MSG-P4-003 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| PACK_PREPARED | PACK_ROUTED | The amount is inside the committee limit, the answer names R-WO-11 and a meeting date, and `deviation_open` is false | WITH_COMMITTEE |
| POPULATION_PROPOSED | CASE_HAS_OPEN_DEVIATION | `deviation_open` is true and the answer names R-WO-06 | CASE_REMOVED_BY_TEAM |
| PACK_PREPARED | The answer names no rule version in force | NoPackageInForce | PACK_PREPARED, unchanged |
| PACK_PREPARED | The decision record cannot be written | The transaction rolls back | PACK_PREPARED, unchanged |

These are the case stage code of `recovery_case` (`stage_code`, in the range DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023); the case status stays IN_PROGRESS through both moves. The story also writes `committee_meeting_ref` and `committee_meeting_date`, which are facts of the meeting booking and not stages. A case on the hold-out path is returned to the next monthly scan by R-WO-08 once the deviation is cleared, and that return is rwb-writeoff's scan and not this story.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-case service identity (the rwb-case login, DP-02) | Applies the routing answer, moves the stage, places the case on the committee queue or on `DEV-HANDLER`, writes the task, the timer, the meeting reference and the decision record |
| CaseWorkflow | Holds the committee-meeting durable timer and raises TimerBreached through its own state; moves no stage by itself |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the local decision record and its outbox row (Decision log C) |
| RW-WOCOMM, write-off committee member | Reads the committee queue, the case and the meeting date (Case record R) |
| RW-WRITEOFF, write-off team | Runs the scan and the route in rwb-writeoff; reads the case and its stage (Case record R) |
| RW-CREDITAD, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-FINANCE | Hold the committee decision (Write-off and posting A); they read the case and take the decision in the write-off service, not here |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Receives the case in the exception queue on the no-package path (Case record R) |
| RW-COE | Owns the committee queue row, the committee-meeting timer type and the meeting calendar as reference data |
| RW-REFADM | Holds no Case record right; refused on the case read with MSG-P4-002 |

The committee decision itself, the Write-off and posting A right and the DoA limit are answered in rwb-writeoff and are outside this story.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity in rwb_case | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case | id, case_no, product_group, primary_person_key, status, stage_code and the rest of the range | Read, and `stage_code`, `queue_id` and `owner_user_id` written with the move |
| DF-CAS-019 | recovery_case | deviation_open | Read, decides the hold-out and the refusal |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0738; ASM-1333) | recovery_case | committee_meeting_ref, committee_meeting_date (two new fields, no field ID in the Logical Data Model v8) | Write |
| DF-WRK-001 to DF-WRK-008 | queue | id, queue_code, queue_name, team_code, role_code, assignment_method and the rest of the range | Read, for the committee queue and `DEV-HANDLER` |
| DF-WRK-018, DF-WRK-019, DF-WRK-024 | task | case_id, task_code, due_at | Write, the committee task of the booking |
| DF-WRK-030, DF-WRK-031, DF-WRK-032, DF-WRK-035 | timer | timer_type, started_at, expires_at, status | Write, the projection of the meeting date behind the timers read; the clock is the durable timer |
| DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 | deviation (rwb_deviation, owner S8) | id, case_id, deviation_code, raised_at, raised_by, paused_state and the rest of the range | Not read and not written: the case's own `deviation_open` flag stands in, and the rows are S8's |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local library) and decision_log_entry (rwb_decision, owner P7) | all fields | Write locally; the central entry is sealed by rwb-decision |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | rule_row (rwb_decision, owner P7) | rule_id, rule_version, from_state, event_code, to_state and the rest of the range | Not read here: the rule ID and the rule version arrive in the routing answer |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. `deviation`, `write_off` (with its `committee_date`, DF-FIN-015), `rule_row` and `decision_log_entry` are other services' tables and are not read or written directly; `rwb_case` holds no foreign key into another schema (DP-01). The committee meeting reference and its date are the only facts of the committee that rwb-case keeps, and the amount, the tax criteria and the posting are never copied.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This story adds no operation: the case of record is served by the existing `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and the queue by the existing `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` of rwb-case, both extended only by the optional fields `committeeMeetingRef`, `committeeMeetingDate` and `stageCode` on the Case resource, which the Epic 1 contract already carries.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0738; ASM-1331) | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0738; ASM-1331) | rwb-writeoff (S7) | The committee routing answer of RWB-S7-E6017-CON: pack reference, decision, rule ID R-WO-11 or R-WO-06, rule version, package version and, on a route, the meeting reference and its date (DP-11, built against the RWB-S7-E6017-CON fake) | One hop, 2 s |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | rwb-access (P4) | The Case record right and the scope before a case read, cached by the guard library (DP-08) | One hop, 2 s |

Two calls, no chain. The rwb-case side is called by rwb-writeoff and makes no call back, so a route never becomes a cycle of two services. The path and the field names of the first row are fixed by the S7 contract story and not by this one.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (EV-05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId | caseId, fromStageCode, toStageCode, eventCode (PACK_ROUTED or CASE_HAS_OPEN_DEVIATION), ruleId, ruleVersion, packRef, meetingRef |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 owns the type and the central ledger; every service writes its own record | caseId | decision record reference, rule ID R-WO-11 or R-WO-06, rule version, business date |

Both are written to the outbox in the same transaction as the stage change and relayed with the CloudEvents envelope; no personal data is carried and no amount is in any payload (DP-09).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The routing answer arrives as a call of the S7 contract and is not a Kafka subscription of this story: `DeviationRaised` and `DeviationCleared` are consumed by the case router of the Epic 1 and Epic 2 stories into the `deviation_open` flag, and this story reads the flag and subscribes to nothing.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow (parent, one per case, workflow ID = case ID) | `rwb-case` | Receives the meeting date and other state signals and holds the committee-meeting date as a durable timer of the workflow kit |
| CommitteeRoutingStep | Step of the case router | `rwb-case` | Validates the answer, chooses R-WO-11 or R-WO-06, records and applies, and signals CaseWorkflow |
| RecordAndApply | Transactional step (decision-record library) | `rwb-case` | Writes the stage, the queue, the task, the timer, the meeting reference, the decision record and the outbox rows in one transaction |

No other activity is added, and no child workflow: the committee approval child of the write-off stage belongs to rwb-writeoff.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added by this story. The meeting date is a durable timer of CaseWorkflow and not a Temporal Schedule, because a booking is one date for one case and not a cadence; no Schedule, no Quartz row and no timer-check job is created. The monthly eligibility scan JOB-16 stays a Temporal Schedule in rwb-writeoff (monthly, third working day), and the committee meeting calendar stays the write-off service's. Whether a committee meeting cadence should also be a Schedule is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0738; ASM-1328).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | P3 (rwb_case) | The story writes `stage_code`, `queue_id` and `owner_user_id` on the move and adds `committee_meeting_ref` and `committee_meeting_date` |
| queue, assignment | P3 (rwb_case) | The placement on the committee queue and on `DEV-HANDLER` |
| task | P3 (rwb_case) | The committee task with its `task_code` and `due_at` |
| timer | P3 (rwb_case) | The projection of the meeting date behind the timers read; the clock is the durable timer of CaseWorkflow |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in rwb_case | The local record of the routing decision, hash-linked, written in the same transaction (DP-03) |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_case | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects (DP-09) |

`write_off` is S7's (rwb_writeoff) and `deviation` is S8's (rwb_deviation): this story holds no foreign key into either schema, no cross-schema join and no copy of a row (DP-01). `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are rwb-decision's and are reached only through its contracts.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `committeerouting`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.committeerouting`; front end `src/modules/recovery/case/CommitteeRoutingPanel.tsx`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | The monolith base path of the legacy API (Template and Rules §R5.5, DP-13) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The two H dependencies this table adds are held by the platform contract stories and are not repeated in the metadata rows, which carry only the contract dependency of the legacy route: RWB-S7-E6017-CON (ASM-1330). The committee queue row, the timer type and the meeting calendar are reference data of rwb-case and are read as rows, not as code (ASM-1329).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RoutingAnswerController | Controller | The rwb-case side of the S7 contract: accepts the routing answer, applies the access check of the caller identity and hands it to the step |
| RoutingAnswerValidator | Service | Checks the pack reference, the rule ID, the rule version in force and, on a route, the meeting reference and its date; refuses with NoPackageInForce, MSG-P3-027 or MSG-GEN-001 |
| CommitteeRoutingStep | Step of the case router | Reads the case, chooses R-WO-11 or R-WO-06 from the answer and the `deviation_open` flag, and drives the record and the apply |
| CaseStageRepository | Repository | Writes `stage_code`, `queue_id`, `owner_user_id`, `committee_meeting_ref` and `committee_meeting_date` in schema rwb_case only |
| CommitteeQueuePlacer | Service | Places the case on the committee queue or on `DEV-HANDLER` and writes the task with its due date; holds no queue code in code |
| MeetingTimerWriter | Service | Writes the timer projection row and signals CaseWorkflow with the meeting date |
| DecisionRecordWriter | Library adapter | Writes the local decision record with the rule ID and the rule version, hash-linked, in the same transaction (DP-03) |
| InboxDedupe | Library adapter | Dedupes the answer on the pack reference and the message key (DP-09) |
| CaseCommitteePanel | React component | Shows the stage, the committee queue and the meeting date on SCR-27, read only |

**Database and migrations**

- Migration `V6017_1__committee_meeting.sql` adds `committee_meeting_ref` varchar(40) and `committee_meeting_date` date to `recovery_case` and one reference row type for the committee-meeting timer in LOV-TIMER; no database check constraint holds a list value.
- No new table: the queue, the assignment, the task, the timer, the decision record and the library objects already exist in `rwb_case`.
- One index for the read: `ix_recovery_case_stage_committee ON recovery_case (stage_code) WHERE stage_code = 'WITH_COMMITTEE'`, so the committee queue page is read without a scan.
- The migration runs in the rwb-case Flyway sequence of the service's own schema; no other schema is touched (DP-01).

**Configuration and reference data**

- The committee queue row (RW-COE) with role RW-WOCOMM, and the committee-meeting timer type in LOV-TIMER; the code and the value are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0738; ASM-1329).
- The deviation handler queue `DEV-HANDLER`, from the P3 queue template and rule R-DEV-01.
- The committee meeting calendar rows (meeting month, meeting date, meeting reference), read as data by rwb-writeoff and carried in the routing answer; rwb-case stores the reference and the date it is given and holds no calendar.
- The rule version in force per environment is the one named in the routing answer; rwb-case holds no package and evaluates no rule, so no KieBase and no lock file is involved.

**Build steps**

1. RoutingAnswerController and RoutingAnswerValidator against the S7 contract fake, with the refusal of the no-version path; tests for AC1 and AC5.
2. InboxDedupe on the pack reference and the message key; test for AC4.
3. CaseStageRepository and CommitteeQueuePlacer with the committee queue and `DEV-HANDLER`, one transaction with the decision record; tests for AC1 and AC2.
4. MeetingTimerWriter, the timer row and the CaseWorkflow signal; test for AC1 and the no-Schedule assertion.
5. The hold-out path from the `deviation_open` flag, including the case where the answer proposes a route; tests for AC2 and AC3.
6. The failed decision-record write and the rollback; tests for AC6 and the NFR case.
7. The read path with the access guard and the scope, and the composite-route contract test of SCR-27; tests for AC7 and AC8.
8. Contract-fake run of every S7 answer in isolation, so the story builds before rwb-writeoff lands.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.p3.committee-routing`, a service configuration value read as a parameter. Off: the answer is stored as a pending inbox entry, no stage moves and no placement is written; on: the routing step applies the answer.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the S7 contract tests stay green, every routed case carries exactly one meeting reference, one meeting date and one committee-meeting timer, and no case in the SIT run with an open deviation has reached WITH_COMMITTEE.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S7-001 | The write-off service reports that the scan is on hold for the missing tax criteria and sends no routing answer | The scan is on hold until Finance publishes the tax criteria. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | The routing answer carries no pack reference, no rule ID, or no meeting reference on a route | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P3-027 | The routing answer names no rule version in force | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The local decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Case record right reads a routed case | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

For MSG-P3-027 in this story, {check} is "no package in force" and {detail} names the rule ID "R-WO-11" and the business date only, never a case fact. For MSG-GEN-001, {field} is the name of the field the answer left empty, such as "packRef" or "meetingRef". MSG-S7-001 is rwb-writeoff's message and this story passes it through unchanged; it owns none of these texts.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-27 Write-off proposal, states Scan, proposed, in committee and approved: this story serves the case-side facts of that screen, which are the stage code, the committee queue and the meeting reference with its date, and it serves them read only. The amount, the tax criteria, the posting reference and the committee approval are read from rwb-writeoff on the same composite route.

SCR-27 is composed by the gateway-bff composite route, which calls rwb-case and rwb-writeoff in parallel, one hop each, and merges the answers into the screen model (DP-19); the browser calls one route and no owner service. The screen field order, the masking and the merge order are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0738; ASM-1334). The full write-off screen, its buttons and the committee decision remain with RWB-S7-E6017-APP.

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the committee queue code, the timer type, the meeting calendar, the rule ID and the rule version are rows, reference data or contract fields.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts: logs hold case IDs, pack references and meeting references, never account numbers, names or identity numbers; the workflow payloads pass the payload codec.
- No read of another service's tables and no ACE view: the routing answer comes from the S7 contract, the rights from rwb-access, and `rwb_case` holds no foreign key into another schema (DP-01).
- The committee decision, the amount, the tax criteria and the posting are not stored, echoed or validated by rwb-case.
- A read of a routed case writes nothing and raises no event.
- The decision record is written before the stage moves, in one transaction with it; a failed write rolls the whole move back (R-UNI-39).
- NoPackageInForce is never caught and turned into a default move; the case goes to the exception queue.
- The meeting date is a durable timer and not a Schedule; no Quartz row and no timer-check job is added.
- Every outbound event is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the state change and carries IDs and facts only (DP-09).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E6-017 as the wave 4 integration proof that the write-off pack reaches the committee queue, that the case and its meeting clock are set in rwb-case, and that the decision is in the ledger. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **write-off committee member**, I want **a wave 4 harness that proves the pack for a cut-off date reaches the committee queue, that the case state and its meeting clock are set by rwb-case, and that the route decision is in the central ledger with its rule version, against the owning services' published contracts and their fakes**, so that **no write-off waits in the wrong queue or misses its meeting because a cross-service step failed silently between the scan and the committee**.

This story builds the harness and the evidence, and nothing else. The scan, the pack and the route are S7's, built in RWB-S7-E6017-APP; the committee queue, the case state and the meeting clock are P3's, built in RWB-P3-E6017-APP; the central ledger is P7's and the deviation is S8's. The story builds no production endpoint, no table, no workflow, no schedule and no screen. It drives the population from the one operation the Ownership Map publishes for a scan, and asserts only what is observable through the owners' published operations.

This story owns no legacy acceptance criterion. All four legacy acceptance criteria of RWB-E6-017 sit with RWB-S7-E6017-APP and RWB-P3-E6017-APP; the six criteria in section 7 are new and test the cross-service wiring alone.

##### 2. Business rationale

R-WO-11 says a pack inside the committee limit is routed to the committee and the meeting is scheduled before the scheduled meeting. The rule is one row in a routing table, but it lands in three services at once: rwb-writeoff builds and routes the pack, rwb-case moves the case to WITH_COMMITTEE and places it in the committee queue with a meeting clock, and the route is written to the local decision record and to the central ledger with its rule version. Each service can pass its own tests while the seam between them fails.

The failure is quiet, which is why the seam needs its own proof. A case can sit in WITH_COMMITTEE and still be in the recovery officer's queue, so the officer keeps working a case the committee already owns. A pack can be routed twice in one meeting month and the case can carry two meeting clocks, so the committee meets on the wrong date. A route can be taken with no ledger entry, so the decision exists in the workflow and nowhere that an auditor, a complaint handler or a reporting measure can find it. A deviation raised after the population is proposed can reach the committee because nothing on the seam re-reads the case before the route. Each of these is a wrong decision on a charged-off balance, and none of them shows up as an error in a service log.

The harness is decoupled the way the services are. Every path is the owner's published operation on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` (DP-13), one hop and a 2 s budget (DP-11, ADR-020), and no service reads another service's schema (DP-01). The route decision goes through the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), and where a screen would compose the queue, the case and the clock the path would be the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). It carries REQ-S7-002, REQ-S7-003 and REQ-S7-004 into evidence rather than restating them.

The map publishes no read operation for a write-off record and no meeting-booking operation. This story states that plainly and does not invent one: the harness identifies the case through the DP13 records read of P1 and the case contract of P3, and it observes the routing through the state, the queue, the clock and the ledger rather than through a write-off read.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The published contracts of S7 rwb-writeoff (the scan and the committee decision), P3 rwb-case (case, queues, queue cases, timers), P7 rwb-decision (the decision log), S8 rwb-deviation (deviations), P1 rwb-source-data (DP13 records) and P4 rwb-access (session) are in the contract registry, and a stub set is generated from each one with its version pinned.
- The case under test is in PACK_PREPARED for cut-off date 2026-07-03, with the pack built under R-WO-05 (PACK_BUILT to PACK_PREPARED) and the balance and the provision carried in the pack read from DP13 Money and closure.
- The write-off committee queue WO-COMM-MTG exists in rwb-case with role RW-WOCOMM, and the recovery officer queue MTG-BKK-CO exists as the queue the case came from.
- The committee meeting calendar fixture holds one meeting date, 2026-07-15, for meeting month 2026-07, and it is read as data.
- RWB-S7-E6017-APP and RWB-P3-E6017-APP own the scan, the route, the queue placement and the meeting clock. Until they land, the stubs of section 12.8 answer in their place on Day 1.
- The harness environment and base hosts, the committee queue code in the real environment, the committee meeting calendar, the shape of the scan answer and how the population and its removals are listed, the timer type and warning settings of the meeting clock, the evidence format and retention, the pass or fail gate, and the synthetic case keys: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0455; ASM-0647).
- No build dependency. Day 1, with the stubs in place from the first run; the two I stories replace their stubs and never block the lane.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: loads the fixture for cut-off date 2026-07-03: case RW-2026-000617 in PACK_PREPARED, its balance and provision carried from DP13 Money and closure, queue WO-COMM-MTG for the committee, the source queue MTG-BKK-CO, and the meeting date 2026-07-15 for meeting month 2026-07.
2. Harness: posts the population for the cut-off date through `POST /api/recovery/writeoff/v1/write-off-scans` with the cut-off date, the meeting month and one Idempotency-Key. On Day 1 the stub of section 12.8 answers in place of RWB-S7-E6017-APP.
3. Harness: reads the case through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and asserts the state before the route is PACK_PREPARED and after it is WITH_COMMITTEE (R-WO-11).
4. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues` to find queue WO-COMM-MTG by its code, then `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` and asserts case RW-2026-000617 is in the committee queue and is no longer returned for queue MTG-BKK-CO.
5. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` and asserts exactly one committee meeting timer, with expires_at equal to the booked meeting date 2026-07-15 and status running.
6. Harness: reads the money carried in the pack through `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP13/records?caseId={caseId}` and asserts the balance and the provision are the ones the fixture holds. The write-off record has no published read operation in the map, so the case is identified through DP13 and the rwb-case contract and never through a write-off read.
7. Harness: posts the same cut-off date again for the same meeting month with the same Idempotency-Key, and asserts that no second timer and no second queue placement is written for the case.
8. Harness: raises the deviation path: a deviation on the case (rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1 on rwb.deviation.events.v1, whose consumer is rwb-case) holds the case out of the next population, moves it to CASE_REMOVED_BY_TEAM (R-WO-06), names the deviation owner on the case, and keeps it out of WITH_COMMITTEE.
9. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` and asserts exactly one entry for the routing of the case, with rule R-WO-11 and its rule version, hash-chained to the previous entry of the case.
10. Harness: forces the failure path: with the central ledger and the local decision record unavailable, the route is not taken, the case stays in PACK_PREPARED, no queue placement and no timer is written, and the answer carries MSG-P7-003.
11. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` for the caller and posts the scan as a synthetic caller with role RW-OFF and no Write-off and posting C, and asserts 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no scan started.
12. Harness: writes one run report keyed by story and cut-off date, naming the contract version of each hop, whether the hop was a stub or the owner, the meeting month, the queue, the clock, the ledger entry and the six criteria.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A stub answers a shape the published contract does not allow | The run fails at that hop and the report names the service, the operation and the contract version; no criterion is marked passed | None | TC-E6-017-01-ITG (ITG AC1) |
| X2 | The pack under test is not in PACK_PREPARED when the route runs | The run fails on AC1 and the report names the case and the state it read; a route with no prepared pack is never reported as routed | None | TC-E6-017-01-ITG (ITG AC1) |
| X3 | The case is in the committee queue and still in the officer queue | The run fails on AC1 and the report names both queue codes and the case, so a double placement is a failure and not a pass | None | TC-E6-017-01-ITG (ITG AC1) |
| X4 | A second route in one meeting month adds a second timer or a second placement | The run fails on AC2 and the report names the meeting month, the two timer rows and the two placements | None | TC-E6-017-02-ITG (ITG AC2) |
| X5 | A case with an open deviation reaches WITH_COMMITTEE | The run fails on AC3 and the report names the deviation code, the deviation owner and the state it read | None | TC-E6-017-03-ITG (ITG AC3) |
| X6 | The route is taken with no ledger entry, or the chain does not link to the previous entry | The run fails on AC4 and the report names the case, the operation and the chain position; an unrecorded route is never reported as recorded | MSG-P7-003 (expected, and missing) | TC-E6-017-04-ITG (ITG AC5) |
| X7 | A caller without Write-off and posting C starts a scan | The run fails on AC6 and the report names the caller role and the operation; a scan that started is reported as started | MSG-P4-002 (expected, and missing) | TC-E6-017-05-ITG (ITG AC6) |

The report text is for the wave entry check and is not part of the message standard. The business messages the run touches are in section 14 and are asserted by ID and by their substituted values.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs against the published contracts and the stubs from Day 1; the only waits are RWB-S7-E6017-APP and RWB-P3-E6017-APP, and their stubs answer until they land |
| Negotiable | The fixture layout, the queue code, the meeting calendar, the report shape and the gate are configuration agreed at the wave entry check, not business values in code |
| Valuable | The seam from the scan to the committee queue, the meeting clock and the ledger is proven once, end to end, before wave 4 opens |
| Estimable | One runner, one stub set, two fixtures, four assertions and one report |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its six tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against the stubs and again against the real owners as the two I stories land |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Route the population to the committee and schedule it - wave 4 committee routing harness

  Background:
    Given the population for cut-off date "2026-07-03" has proposed case "RW-2026-000617" and its pack is in "PACK_PREPARED"
    Given the pack for case "RW-2026-000617" carries the balance and the provision of DP13 "Money and closure"
    Given the write-off committee queue "WO-COMM-MTG" exists in rwb-case with role "RW-WOCOMM"
    Given the recovery officer queue "MTG-BKK-CO" holds case "RW-2026-000617"
    Given the committee meeting calendar fixture holds meeting date "2026-07-15" for meeting month "2026-07"

  Scenario: AC1 The pack reaches the committee queue and the case waits there (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000617" is in state "PACK_PREPARED" under "PACK_BUILT" of rule "R-WO-05"
    When the route step runs for the case against rule "R-WO-11" and its rule version
    Then the case read through "GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}" is in state "WITH_COMMITTEE"
    And "GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases" for queue "WO-COMM-MTG" returns case "RW-2026-000617"
    And queue "MTG-BKK-CO" no longer returns case "RW-2026-000617"

  Scenario: AC2 The meeting is booked once and the case carries the meeting clock (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000617" has been routed to the committee for meeting month "2026-07"
    When "GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers" is read for the case
    Then the answer holds one committee meeting timer
    And its expires_at equals the booked meeting date "2026-07-15"
    And its status is "RUNNING"
    When the same case is routed again for meeting month "2026-07"
    Then no second timer is added and no second queue placement is written

  Scenario: AC3 An open deviation holds the case out of the population (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000617" is in state "POPULATION_PROPOSED"
    And a deviation is raised on the case and "rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1" is published
    When the scan runs for the next cut-off date
    Then the case is left out of the population
    And the case read through "GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}" is in state "CASE_REMOVED_BY_TEAM"
    And the deviation owner is named on the case
    And the case never reaches "WITH_COMMITTEE"

  Scenario: AC4 The decision is recorded with the rule version and the ledger holds it once (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000617" has been routed to the committee under rule "R-WO-11"
    When the route decision is written
    Then the entry carries rule "R-WO-11" and its rule version
    And "GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}" returns exactly one entry for the case and the routing
    And the entry is hash-chained to the previous entry of the case

  Scenario: AC5 The route is not taken when the decision cannot be recorded (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000617" is in state "PACK_PREPARED"
    And the central ledger and the local decision record are both unavailable
    When the route step runs for the case
    Then the case stays in "PACK_PREPARED"
    And no queue placement and no timer is written
    And the answer carries "MSG-P7-003"

  Scenario: AC6 A caller without the right is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a synthetic caller with role "RW-OFF" and no Write-off and posting C
    When the caller posts a population for cut-off date "2026-07-03"
    Then the answer is 403 with "MSG-P4-002"
    And no scan starts
```

The four legacy acceptance criteria belong to RWB-S7-E6017-APP and RWB-P3-E6017-APP, and the six criteria above are the ones this ITG story owns.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A pack inside the committee limit is routed to the committee and its meeting is scheduled before the scheduled meeting | R-WO-11 |
| BR2 | A prepared pack is prepared from case and provision data with no manual assembly, and PACK_BUILT leaves it in PACK_PREPARED | R-WO-05; REQ-S7-002 |
| BR3 | A case with an open deviation in X1 to X7 is held out of the population, routed to the deviation handler and moved to CASE_REMOVED_BY_TEAM | R-WO-06; REQ-S7-004 |
| BR4 | The committee decision is recorded against the case, and the route that put it there is recorded with its rule version | R-WO-11; REQ-S7-003 |
| BR5 | The case state and the queue placement are held by rwb-case, never written by the caller of the scan | Arch v5 slide 41; DP-01 |
| BR6 | The route decision is written locally and published as DecisionRecorded on the shared topic, and the ledger is rwb-decision's | Arch v5 slides 20 and 42; DP-03 |
| BR7 | The scan runs from JOB-16 on the 3rd working day of the month | Arch v5 slide 44; JOB-16 |

The harness asserts these rules and changes none of them.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| PACK_PREPARED | PACK_ROUTED | The pack is inside the committee limit and the meeting is scheduled | WITH_COMMITTEE (R-WO-11) |
| POPULATION_PROPOSED | CASE_HAS_OPEN_DEVIATION | A deviation in X1 to X7 is open on the case | CASE_REMOVED_BY_TEAM (R-WO-06) |
| POPULATION_PROPOSED | PACK_BUILT | The pack is prepared from case and provision data | PACK_PREPARED (R-WO-05) |
| PACK_PREPARED | The route cannot be recorded | The central ledger and the local decision record are unavailable | PACK_PREPARED, unchanged |

The harness changes no state. Every change in the table is made by the owner: S7 rwb-writeoff scans, builds and routes the pack, P3 rwb-case moves the case, places it in the queue and sets the meeting clock, S8 rwb-deviation raises the deviation, and P7 rwb-decision holds the central ledger. The harness reads and asserts, and the report names the owner and the operation behind every value it asserts.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-WOCOMM, write-off committee member | Reads the committee queue and the meeting clock of a case; the role the committee queue is worked by |
| RW-WRITEOFF | Holds Write-off and posting C and runs the population for a cut-off date |
| RW-CREDITAD, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-FINANCE | Hold Write-off and posting A and the committee decision; they sit outside this story and its out of scope |
| RW-OFF, recovery officer | Reads the case and its queue; the synthetic caller of AC6 holds this role and no Write-off and posting C |
| RW-TRIBE, RW-PLATADM | Read the same run report and the queue configuration; they hold no write-off right |
| QA lead | Owns the harness configuration, the fixtures, the report shape and the pass or fail gate |
| Integration lead | Owns the harness code, the stub set and the swap from a stub to the real service |
| The owning services' identities | S7 rwb-writeoff scans and routes, P3 rwb-case holds the case, the queue and the timer, P7 rwb-decision holds the ledger, S8 rwb-deviation raises the deviation, P1 rwb-source-data answers DP13 and P4 rwb-access answers the session; they make every change the harness asserts |
| No delegation of authority level applies | The harness takes no business decision; the authorisation is answered by rwb-access and the committee decision is out of scope |

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023, DF-CAS-046 to DF-CAS-055 | recovery_case | case_no, status, stage_code, route_state, owner_user_id, queue_id, deviation_open, rule_version | Read through the rwb-case contract |
| DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 | deviation | case_id, deviation_code, raised_at, raised_by, paused_state, handler_user_id, cleared_at, outcome | Read through the rwb-deviation contract; S8 owns the table |
| DF-WRK-001 to DF-WRK-008, DF-WRK-037, DF-WRK-038 | queue | queue_code, queue_name, team_code, role_code, assignment_method | Read through the rwb-case contract |
| DF-WRK-045 to DF-WRK-052 | queue_member | queue_id, user_id, capacity, skill_codes | Read through the rwb-case contract |
| DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036, DF-WRK-041 to DF-WRK-044 | timer | case_id, timer_type, started_at, expires_at, warn_at, paused, status | Read through the rwb-case contract |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018, DF-DEC-028 to DF-DEC-031 | decision_log_entry | case_id, decision_code, rule_id, rule_version, inputs_ref, final_call, prev_hash, entry_hash, chain_seq | Read through the rwb-decision contract; P7 owns the ledger |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | rule_row | rule_id, rule_version, from_state, event_code, to_state, owner_role, timer_spec | Read through the rwb-decision contract |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. queue, queue_member and timer are P3's tables; deviation is S8's; decision_log_entry and rule_row are P7's; recovery_case is P3's. The harness owns no table and writes no row. The balance and the provision carried in the pack are read from DP13 Money and closure through the rwb-source-data data-product contract, never from a view and never from a table.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/writeoff/v1/write-off-scans` | S7 rwb-writeoff | The population for a cut-off date, with one Idempotency-Key (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC6) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The state of the case, PACK_PREPARED, WITH_COMMITTEE or CASE_REMOVED_BY_TEAM (AC1, AC3, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/queues` | P3 rwb-case | The committee queue and the officer queue, by queue_code (AC1) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` | P3 rwb-case | The case in the committee queue and its absence from the officer queue (AC1) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` | P3 rwb-case | The meeting clock: one committee meeting timer, its expires_at and its status (AC2, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | P7 rwb-decision | Exactly one ledger entry for the routing, the rule version and the hash chain (AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP13/records?caseId={caseId}` | P1 rwb-source-data | The balance and the provision carried in the pack (AC1, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The caller's role and rights before the scan (AC6) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13, ADR-020). No operation is invented in this story: each path is the owner's published operation. The map publishes no read operation for a write-off record and no meeting-booking operation, so the harness identifies the case through DP13 and rwb-case and observes the booking through the timers of rwb-case. Where a screen would compose these calls the path would be the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it writes its report to the wave record.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Consumers in the sources | Use in this run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | rwb-comms, rwb-reporting | Waits for the move to WITH_COMMITTEE and to CASE_REMOVED_BY_TEAM (AC1, AC3) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | every service, rwb-writeoff for this route | rwb-decision, rwb-reporting | Waits for the route decision to be published before the ledger is read (AC4) |

The harness also observes `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` on `rwb.deviation.events.v1`, produced by S8 rwb-deviation with rwb-case, rwb-comms and rwb-treatment as consumers, to know that the deviation is open before the scan (AC3). The harness neither produces nor consumes that event itself; the move of the case is rwb-case's.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

Observed, not built here. `WriteOffWorkflow` runs on task queue `rwb-writeoff` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and carries the monthly write-off stages: the scan proposes the population (R-WO-01 and R-WO-03), the pack is built in 3 working days (R-WO-05), the pack is routed and the committee decides (R-WO-11 to R-WO-17), and the later posting and provision steps follow. The harness triggers the first stage through the owner's scan operation and observes the route and committee stage through the case state, the queue, the clock and the ledger. It builds no workflow, no activity and no child workflow; the committee approval child of rwb-decision is out of scope.

###### 12.6 Schedules

JOB-16, observed and not changed: a Temporal Schedule in rwb-writeoff that runs the write-off scan monthly on the 3rd working day (Architecture v5 slide 44; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 23; Ownership Map). The harness runs its population for a cut-off date through the scan operation and sets no cron; it neither creates, pauses nor changes the Schedule. The committee meeting cadence and the booking target behind the meeting clock are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0455; ASM-0647).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-01). queue, queue_member and timer are P3's, recovery_case is P3's, deviation is S8's, decision_log_entry and rule_row are P7's, and the pack's money comes from P1's DP13.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Contract | Stubbed answer in the run |
|---|---|---|
| Stub for rwb-writeoff | `POST /write-off-scans` and `POST /write-offs/{writeOffId}/committee-decision` | Accepts one population per cut-off date and Idempotency-Key, proposes case RW-2026-000617, and records the route for meeting month 2026-07; refuses a caller without Write-off and posting C with 403 and MSG-P4-002; answers MSG-P7-003 when the decision record cannot be written |
| Stub for rwb-case | `GET /cases/{caseId}`, `/queues`, `/queues/{queueId}/cases`, `/cases/{caseId}/timers` | The case RW-2026-000617 moving from PACK_PREPARED to WITH_COMMITTEE, or to CASE_REMOVED_BY_TEAM on the deviation path; queue WO-COMM-MTG holding the case and queue MTG-BKK-CO not; one committee meeting timer with expires_at 2026-07-15 and status RUNNING |
| Stub for rwb-decision | `GET /decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | Exactly one entry for the routing of case RW-2026-000617 with rule R-WO-11 and its rule version, prev_hash equal to the entry_hash of the previous entry of the case, and an empty answer when the ledger is forced unavailable |
| Stub for rwb-deviation | `POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations` and `PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}` | Raises one deviation on the case with its code, its raised_at and a handler, and publishes the deviation as open for the scan |
| Stub for rwb-source-data | `GET /data-products/DP13/records?caseId={caseId}` | The balance and the provision of DP13 Money and closure for case RW-2026-000617, with the business date and the load time |
| Stub for rwb-access | `GET /me/session` | Allows RW-WRITEOFF with Write-off and posting C; answers RW-OFF with the role and without Write-off and posting C |
| Committee calendar fixture | The committee meeting calendar | One meeting date, 2026-07-15, for meeting month 2026-07, and no second meeting inside the month |

Each stub is generated from the published contract and its version is pinned in the run report, so a contract change shows up as a run failure and not as a silent pass. The harness environment and base hosts, the committee queue code in the real environment, the committee meeting calendar, the shape of the scan answer, the timer type and warning settings of the meeting clock, the evidence format and retention, the pass or fail gate, and the synthetic case keys are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0455; ASM-0647).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 8 consumed, one hop each on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13) |
| Kafka | None published; two consumed, CaseStateChanged and DecisionRecorded, and DeviationRaised observed through its consumer rwb-case |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H dependency that DP-03 adds, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, is a platform story delivered by the platform wave and is not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays empty; the same holds for RWB-PLT-N001-CON from DP-19. The two blocking dependencies are the I stories RWB-S7-E6017-APP and RWB-P3-E6017-APP, which replace their stubs; until they are live the run uses the stub, and a stub pass is reported as a stub pass.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the six owned criteria in order for a cut-off date and holds the run lock |
| StubSet | Fake | The six stubs of section 12.8 generated from the published contracts, with each contract version pinned |
| CommitteeCalendarFixture | Fixture | The meeting date 2026-07-15 for meeting month 2026-07, and the queue codes of the committee and the officer queue |
| StateAssertion | Service | Reads the case state and both queue member lists and names any case that is in two queues or in none |
| ClockAssertion | Service | Reads the timers of the case: one committee meeting timer, its expires_at equal to the booked meeting, its status running, and no second timer on a repeated route |
| LedgerAssertion | Service | Reads the decision log for the case: exactly one entry for the routing, the rule and its version, and the hash chain to the previous entry |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes one report per cut-off date keyed by story, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the stubs from Day 1 and the real services as the two I stories land, on synthetic case RW-2026-000617, cut-off date 2026-07-03, meeting month 2026-07, meeting date 2026-07-15, committee queue WO-COMM-MTG, officer queue MTG-BKK-CO, role RW-WOCOMM for the committee queue and a synthetic RW-OFF caller for the refusal path. Every value is fixture data and none is written in code. The harness environment and base hosts, the committee queue code, the committee meeting calendar, the shape of the scan answer, the timer type and warning settings, the evidence format and retention, the pass or fail gate, and the synthetic case keys are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0455; ASM-0647). The harness seeds nothing by hand and never writes a schema row.

**Build steps**

1. Generate the six stubs from the published contracts and pin each contract version in the run report; fail the run on a mismatch (X1).
2. Build the CommitteeCalendarFixture and prove the meeting date and the queue codes are read as data for cut-off date 2026-07-03.
3. Build the JourneyRunner for AC1: post the population for the cut-off date with one Idempotency-Key, read the state through rwb-case, and assert it reaches WITH_COMMITTEE (X2).
4. Add StateAssertion for AC1: the case is in queue WO-COMM-MTG through `/queues/{queueId}/cases` and no longer in queue MTG-BKK-CO (X3).
5. Add ClockAssertion for AC2: one committee meeting timer with expires_at 2026-07-15 and status running, and a repeated route for the same meeting month adds no second timer and no second placement (X4).
6. Add AC3: raise the deviation, post the next population, and assert the case is out of the population, in CASE_REMOVED_BY_TEAM, with the deviation owner named and never in WITH_COMMITTEE (X5).
7. Add LedgerAssertion for AC4 and the failure path of AC5: one entry with rule R-WO-11 and its version, hash-chained to the previous entry, and with the ledger and the local record forced unavailable the case stays in PACK_PREPARED with MSG-P7-003 and no placement or timer (X6).
8. Add the access path for AC6 through `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` and the scan as a synthetic RW-OFF caller, then the EvidenceReport and the gate, and swap a stub for the real owner as its I story lands (X7).

**Feature switch.** None. The harness has no production flag and runs in the test environment only.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass against the fakes and again against RWB-S7-E6017-APP and RWB-P3-E6017-APP when they land, and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story and cut-off date.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S7-001 | Error | The scan is on hold until Finance publishes the tax criteria. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values on the answer it reads, and owns no message text. MSG-S7-001 is asserted when the scan is held for the unpublished tax criteria, MSG-GEN-001 on a scan posted without its cut-off date, MSG-P4-002 on the refusal of AC6 and MSG-P7-003 on the route that cannot be recorded in AC5.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built. The states are read through rwb-case and the write-off record the owner holds.

| State | What the harness reads |
|---|---|
| Scan | The population is proposed for the cut-off date and the case is in POPULATION_PROPOSED |
| Proposed | The pack is built and the case is in PACK_PREPARED with its balance and provision carried |
| In committee | The case is in WITH_COMMITTEE, in queue WO-COMM-MTG, with one committee meeting timer |
| Approved | The committee decision is taken on the write-off; the route into it is in the ledger |

The four states are the ones SCR-27 Write-off proposal shows. That screen belongs to RWB-S7-E6017-APP and is out of scope here, and the committee view is not built in this story either. What the wave entry check looks at instead is the run report; its environment, layout and retention are the same missing values named in section 3 and section 12.8.

The AC column names the ITG AC each copy asserts, and the four legacy ACs stay with the two APP stories.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the case key, the cut-off date, the meeting month and date, the queue codes, the rule version and the report layout are data.
- No personal data in logs, fixtures, events or reports: every key is synthetic and no customer record is read at all.
- ACE data only through the P1 contract, and no read of another service's schema or tables: the case, the queues and the timers come from rwb-case, the ledger from rwb-decision, the deviation from rwb-deviation, and the money from DP13 through rwb-source-data (DP-01, DP-03).
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would (DP-11, DP-13).
- A stub pass is never reported as a real pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and it never writes a row by hand.
- A failing criterion is fixed in the service that owns it or raised as a gap; it is never waived in the script.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of the committee approval of rwb-writeoff, split from RWB-E6-018. It fixes `POST /write-offs/{writeOffId}/committee-decision` (API-S7-002) on `/api/recovery/writeoff/v1` (DP-13) with the `CommitteeDecision` request and the decision-record answer, the `write_off` element over the fields DF-FIN-010 to DF-FIN-020, the approver and the limit applied as record properties with no `write_off` column, the delegation element of DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026, the five consumed rows with their placeholders, the decision-record element of DP-03, the `WriteOffApproved` event element on `rwb.writeoff.events.v1`, the rights of TSD S7 T6.1, the fakes and the absence tests. DP-06, DP-07, DP-08 and DP-09 are not in the plan's pattern set although the step reads reference data, a package, an authorise answer and publishes an event, and the five consumed rows are absent from the plan's None C row. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the committee approval of rwb-writeoff — the committee-decision operation on `/api/recovery/writeoff/v1`, the `CommitteeDecision` request and the decision-record answer, the write-off element, the approver and the limit applied, the delegation element, the five consumed rows, the decision-record element, the `WriteOffApproved` event element, the rights, the error envelope and the fakes**, so that **the app story, SCR-27 and the wave 4 harness build against one fixed, testable contract on Day 1, and a field, a limit, a consumed row or an event shape can never drift between rwb-writeoff, rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-access and rwb-payment without a failing build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy approval of RWB-E6-018 crossed four boundaries at once: the case of record, the delegation table, the rule version and a screen, and its Endpoints table named the scan and the committee decision with the monolith base and no element of its own. The target splits them: rwb-case owns the case, its route states and the reference data, rwb-decision owns the WO package and the ledger, rwb-access owns the capability area and the right, rwb-payment consumes the approval event, and rwb-writeoff owns the write-off stage, its record and the committee act. Each boundary is a contract another team builds against, so each is fixed before the app story starts.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema and login `rwb_writeoff`, base `/api/recovery/writeoff/v1`, topic `rwb.writeoff.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, event name `rwb.writeoff.WriteOffApproved.v1`, task queue `rwb-writeoff` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.writeoff` (Template and Rules §R4; context pack). It records that this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and no grant on `rwb_case`, so DP-05 is declared as a prohibition.

Five points are carried as gaps and assumptions rather than decided quietly: the answer element is named `DecisionLogEntry` by the TSD while the record is the local one (ASM-5042, ASM-5049); the delegation table and its owner are unstated and read as reference data (ASM-5043); the approver and the limit applied have no `write_off` column (ASM-5046); the case move is a workflow boundary with no published operation (ASM-5047); and the credit committee's own outcome is claimed by no story (ASM-5044).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL and RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the queue and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the pagination and filter convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline; where this document narrows them it says so.
- Ownership is taken from the context pack and the Ownership Map only: `recovery_case` is P3's, `write_off` is S7's, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are P7's, every `v_ace_*` view is P1's, `document` is P5's, `notice` is P6's and `proceeds` is P8's. `delegation_limit` carries reference-data field IDs (DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026) and no source this story may read names its owner, so it is declared as reference data consumed on the rwb-case reference-data contract under the default ruling (ASM-5043).
- The rwb-case case state and case-move answers, the delegation row, the rwb-decision package row and the rwb-access authorise answer are published with their fakes, so every consumed row names a real owner document; they are not in this story's contract-dependency row, which is None, and the absence is recorded (GAP-3028; ASM-5043, ASM-5047, ASM-5048).
- The committee-decision operation is published by the TSD as API-S7-002 with the request and answer element names and its error codes, so no operation is invented here; the app story's behaviour behind it is RWB-S7-E6018-APP's.
- The WO package and its rows R-WO-12 and R-WO-15 are governed in rwb-decision (P7); this baseline names them and declares none of them.
- The `write_off` table arrives with the DB story of this service; this baseline declares shapes and creates no table, no column and no migration.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 and sits in contract group `CG-W4` by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-writeoff for this step: the committee-decision operation with its request and answer elements, the rights, the `Idempotency-Key` and the error responses.
2. Fix the `CommitteeDecision` request element and the decision-record answer over the write-off columns of DF-FIN-010 to DF-FIN-020, adding the approver, the limit applied, the rule ID with its version and the states.
3. Fix the delegation element of the `delegation_limit` row of DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026 and its use as the limit applied, with no value as a schema default.
4. Fix the five consumed rows: the case state read, the case-move answer, the delegation read, the package read and the authorise check, marking with the placeholder what the sources do not give.
5. Fix the event element of `WriteOffApproved` (`EV-24`) on `rwb.writeoff.events.v1`, its CloudEvents envelope and its no-personal-data rule, and record the outbox row of DP-09 as a missing H row.
6. Record the decision-record element of DP-03, written before the case moves and before the event is published, and the rights of the capability area.
7. Publish the contract tables of section 12 and the fakes of 12.8.
8. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the additive rule, the shapes, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the error envelope, the absence of a `v_ace_*` read and of a `recovery_case` write, the drift between a fake and the document, and the absence of a consumed event and of a Schedule.
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-S7-E6018-APP, SCR-27 and the wave 4 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response or request body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 400 or 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC2, AC6 |
| X2 | A field is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X3 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X4 | A consumed row has a field list the sources do not give | The row carries the placeholder and the fake is derived from the published document | None | AC3, AC4 |
| X5 | The approver or the limit applied is declared as a `write_off` column | The element test fails the build: no such column exists in TSD S7 T3.1 and both are record properties | None | AC2 |
| X6 | The document declares another service's operation as provided, a `v_ace_*` view, a `recovery_case` row or a rule row | The review fails the baseline and the boundary test fails the build | None | AC3, AC7 |
| X7 | The document declares a consumed event, a second topic, a schedule or a second event on the topic | The absence test fails the build | None | AC7 |
| X8 | The rights of the operation are not the ones TSD S7 T6.1 gives the capability area for the act | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the context pack, the FSD and TSD S7 appendices and the published owner contracts of rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access only |
| Negotiable | The element names beyond the ones the sources give, the example values and the fake fixtures are settled in the baseline review; the base, the rights, the topic, the queue, the schema and the state values are fixed by the architecture and the rule package |
| Valuable | Unblocks RWB-S7-E6018-APP, SCR-27, rwb-payment's consumer and the wave 4 harness on Day 1, and the rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access teams on the same day |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, nine contract tables, six fakes and eleven contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

These seven criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only. They restate no business outcome owned by RWB-S7-E6018-APP and copy no criterion of the legacy story, whose four criteria stay with the app story word for word. ##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The committee act is rwb-writeoff's, and the contract declares the fields and the required flags on the `CommitteeDecision` element, the decision-record answer and the `write_off` element only | TSD S7 T3.1, T-A.1 and T-A.2; context pack ownership row `write_off` |
| BR2 | The decision record is declared as an element written before the write-off row changes, through the local library on the shared topic; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; TSD S7 T2; legacy AC1, AC2 and AC4 |
| BR3 | The case stays with rwb-case: the contract declares the case state read and the case-move answer as consumed, declares no `recovery_case` property and describes no case row write | ASM-5047; TSD S7 T4 |
| BR4 | The delegation stays with reference data: the contract declares the `delegation_limit` row as consumed with its version and declares no limit, no approval level and no product group as a property of `write_off` | DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026; ASM-5043 |
| BR5 | The package and the ledger are rwb-decision's: the contract declares the package read as consumed and declares no rule row, no threshold and no rule version as a property of its own | DP-05 as a prohibition for ACE data; ASM-5049 |
| BR6 | The approval event is declared once: `WriteOffApproved` (`EV-24`) on `rwb.writeoff.events.v1` as `rwb.writeoff.WriteOffApproved.v1`, written to the outbox in the same transaction, with the missing DP-09 H row recorded | TSD S7 T5.3; DP-14; ASM-5045 |
| BR7 | A POST declares the `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer | TSD S7 T-A.2 |
| BR8 | No personal data in a schema, an example, an event or a fake: identifiers, amounts, dates, a rule version and an approval identity only, and every example is synthetic | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17); TSD S7 T6.2 |
| BR9 | One REST base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service; the document never declares another service's base or topic as its own | DP-13, DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR10 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version | Platform API rule (ADR-020) |
| BR11 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-writeoff; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | DP-01, DP-11 |
| BR12 | The rights of the operation are the capability area's act right A, held per TSD S7 T6.1 and the legacy permission table, and not the C of the scan | TSD S7 T6.1; legacy permission table of RWB-E6-018 |
| BR13 | The approver and the limit applied are record properties, not `write_off` columns: no source gives them a field ID and TSD S7 T3.1 lists none | ASM-5046; TSD S7 T3.1 |
| BR14 | The states `WITH_COMMITTEE`, `PACK_PREPARED`, `APPROVED` and `ESCALATED_TO_CREDIT_COMMITTEE` are declared as the vocabulary of the answer and of the machine, and the credit committee's own outcome is declared as unclaimed | ASM-5044; TSD S7 T4; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-12 and R-WO-15 |

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of this document, not of a case:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The operation, the elements, the delegation rule, the consumed rows, the decision element, the event element and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, SCR-27, the wave 4 harness, rwb-payment's consumer and the owners of rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example an optional reference or a new filter | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or a limit becomes a schema default | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | The absence tests of AC3 and AC7 fail: a `v_ace_*` view, a `recovery_case` property, a consumed event, a second topic or a Schedule | In review |

The state machine the document describes is the app story's: `WITH_COMMITTEE` and `PACK_PREPARED` are the from states of R-WO-15 and R-WO-12, `APPROVED` and `ESCALATED_TO_CREDIT_COMMITTEE` their to states, and `RETURNED_TO_PURSUE` and `POSTED` follow from steps this baseline does not declare (TSD S7 T4). This document fixes the vocabulary and the answer shape and moves no case.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Write-off element | The columns of DF-FIN-010 to DF-FIN-020: `id`, `case_id`, `decision_log_id`, `amount`, `tax_criteria_met`, `committee_date`, `posted_date`, `responsibility_center`, `cost_center`, `gl_product` and `recovered_after` |
| Request element | The write-off reference, the decision as approve, the rule ID `R-WO-15` or `R-WO-12` with its version, and the request reference |
| Answer element | The record identifier, the approver, the limit applied, the matched delegation row, the from state, the to state `APPROVED` or `ESCALATED_TO_CREDIT_COMMITTEE` and the decided-at time |
| Delegation element | The `delegation_limit` properties of DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026: decision code, approval level, product group, principal limit, loss percentage limit, the remaining five and the version |
| Required flags | The write-off reference, the decision and the rule ID required on the request; `id`, `case_id`, `amount` and `tax_criteria_met` required on the write-off element; the other properties optional; the approver and the limit applied required on the answer |
| Lists | None: TSD S7 T3.2 publishes no list of values, so the baseline declares no enumeration beyond the state vocabulary of the answer |
| Event data | `writeOffId`, `caseId`, `amount`, the rule ID with its version and the decided-at time on `rwb.writeoff.events.v1`, in a CloudEvents envelope, with no personal data |
| Decision record | DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 through the local library, written before the row changes (DP-03) |
| Case, delegation and rule facts | DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 of `recovery_case` in P3, DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026 of `delegation_limit` in reference data and DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 of `rule_row` in P7, read only through the owners' rows and never written, copied or joined here |
| Not declared here | `recovery_case` and `queue` (P3), every `v_ace_*` view (P1), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `proceeds` (P8) |
| Consumed fields with no source | The operation names of the five consumed rows and the owner of `delegation_limit`: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3028; ASM-5043, ASM-5047, ASM-5048) |

The field-level types, lengths and required flags of the added elements are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the element names, the property rule of AC2 and the optionality rule of BR10. **No new table, no new column and no migration** is declared by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-writeoff (S7); base `/api/recovery/writeoff/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/write-offs/{writeOffId}/committee-decision` (API-S7-002) | `CommitteeDecision` in; the decision record of status 200 out, carrying the record identifier, the approver, the limit applied, the rule `R-WO-15` or `R-WO-12` with its version and the state `APPROVED` or `ESCALATED_TO_CREDIT_COMMITTEE` | Write-off and posting, right A, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |

The operation answers 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 for a write-off that is not found, 409 for a write-off that has left the state the rule expects, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503, each with the error envelope and one message ID of section 14 (TSD S7 T-A.2). The element names are the ones the TSD publishes; the answer is the local decision record of DP-03, which is why the record element and the ledger element are declared separately (ASM-5042, ASM-5049). The module's other published operation, `POST /write-off-scans` (API-S7-001, right C), belongs to RWB-S7-E6013-APP and is not declared here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| The case state read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3028; ASM-5047)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference, case number, product group, stage and state of the write-off's case; faked |
| The case-move answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3028; ASM-5047)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The move `APPROVED` or `ESCALATED_TO_CREDIT_COMMITTEE` with the rule ID and its version; on the workflow boundary it is the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies; faked |
| The delegation-limit read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3028; ASM-5043)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The `delegation_limit` row by decision code, approval level and product group, with its limits and its version; faked |
| The rule-package read in force (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3028; ASM-5049)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The WO package at its version, with R-WO-12 and R-WO-15 among its 51 rules over 27 states; faked |
| The authorise check (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3028; ASM-5048)) | `/api/recovery/access/v1` | P4 rwb-access | The capability area "Write-off and posting" and the right A, with the scope; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The five rows are contract dependencies of class C that the plan's C row does not carry, and the absence is recorded (GAP-3028; ASM-5043, ASM-5047, ASM-5048).

###### 12.3 Events published

| `WriteOffApproved` (`EV-24`) | `rwb.writeoff.WriteOffApproved.v1` | `rwb.writeoff.events.v1`, with its retry and `.dlt` topics | `writeOffId`, `caseId`, `amount`, the rule ID with its version and the decided-at time, in a CloudEvents envelope | rwb-payment (P8) and rwb-reporting (P9) |

The event is declared as written to the outbox in the same `rwb_writeoff` transaction as the state change and published only on the approved path; the escalation approves nothing and publishes nothing. The outbox and inbox library `RWB-PLT-TE006-CON` is the platform object behind the declaration and is absent from the plan's H row (ASM-5045).

None. The service listens to the rwb-source-data and rwb-payment events in its scan and recovery steps (context pack connection matrix, row S7), not in the committee act: the act is a request on API-S7-002. This baseline therefore declares no consumer group, no subscription, no inbox of its own and no Kafka call from this step, and the absence test of AC7 fails a build that adds one.

No child workflow for the case and none for the money exists in this service. The activity name is a target design choice, and the step runs from the committee's request. No activity is registered by this story.

None. The monthly committee meeting booked at RWB-S7-E6017-APP has no published calendar and no `write_off` column (ASM-5051).
