**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the closure slice of RWB-E6-025 in rwb-writeoff. The four legacy criteria are kept word for word with their origin tag; the step evaluates R-WO-36 and R-WO-47 on the WO package in force, records the outcome through the local decision-record library before any change (DP-03), writes `write_off.state`, answers rwb-case with the moves `RETENTION_RUNNING` and `CASE_CLOSED` and stops the case timers, and its read on SCR-27 arrives through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) because the service keeps base `/api/recovery/writeoff/v1` (DP-13) and provides no operation of its own. The retention period length is not set in any source (DL26), the placement record has no column and no published owner operation, the closing entry names a loss no field carries, the plan's C and I rows are empty while the step consumes two services, and TSD S7 T4 does not print either rule (GAP-3041; ASM-5098, ASM-5100, ASM-5101, ASM-5102). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **Credit Administration officer** — and as the step the FSD gives no primary person, because it runs unattended — I want **the Workbench to close the case once the retention period has run and no action is open**, so that **write-offs follow the criteria and the committee's decision**.

This is the closure slice of legacy RWB-E6-025 (feature FEAT-WOF-13). It owns:

- the four legacy criteria (AC1 to AC4), copied verbatim with their origin tag, and the rules R-WO-36 and R-WO-47, the messages and the screen state they depend on;
- the retention branch of `WriteOffWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-writeoff` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, as the stage child of `CaseWorkflow` and as the last step of the write-off stage (context pack Temporal slides 5, 12 and 13);
- the evaluation of R-WO-36 and R-WO-47 against the WO package version in force, the retention timer they start and stop, and the hold of R-WO-48 when a document carries no retention class;
- the closing entry: one decision record per closure with the rule ID, the package version, cash recovered, loss and the two states, written **before** the case moves (DP-03);
- the write of `write_off.state` and the answer to rwb-case with the moves `RETENTION_RUNNING` and `CASE_CLOSED` and the stop of every case timer, so that the service that owns the case writes the case;
- the read-only closure state of SCR-27 Write-off proposal behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), on the service base `/api/recovery/writeoff/v1` (DP-13).

It does not own: the published shapes, the consumed rows, the state vocabulary this step adds, the error set and the fakes, which are RWB-S7-E6025-CON; the scan and the tax criteria (RWB-S7-E6013-APP, RWB-S7-E6014-APP); the pack, the removal and the routing (RWB-S7-E6015-APP to RWB-S7-E6017-APP); the committee decision and the posting (RWB-S7-E6018-APP to RWB-S7-E6021-APP); the reconciliation that also starts a retention timer under R-WO-42 (RWB-S7-E6023-APP); the payment on a closed case under R-WO-49 (RWB-S7-E6027-APP); the case of record, its route states, the `timer` rows and the parent `CaseWorkflow`, which are rwb-case (P3); the WO package and its 51 rules, which are rwb-decision (P7); and the deployment of this build, which is the operations story of this legacy key.

##### 2. Business rationale

The feature objective, the problem and the metric are unchanged from the legacy story and the module FSD: the case closes once the retention period has run and no action is open, because write-off populations were assembled by hand each month (FSD S7 A1.3, A2.13.1), and the packs accepted first time are measured on the decision log and the Workbench records against a target that rises each month, reviewed monthly (FSD S7 A2.13.1). The requirement is REQ-S7-008, a case closes after its retention period and reopening it needs a written rule, a reason and an approver (Program BRD v4; FSD S7 Requirements served). What D-RCV-60 changes is who owns the case, the timer, the record and the screen.

- **The closure is this service's step.** `write_off` is S7's only table in `rwb_writeoff` (context pack ownership rows; TSD S7 T3.1), the WO route set of 51 rules over 27 states is the write-off stage's (TSD S7 T4), and R-WO-36 and R-WO-47 are the two transitions that end that stage.
- **The case stays with rwb-case.** `recovery_case`, the route states and the `timer` rows are P3's (legacy Data table lists both tables; context pack ownership rows), so this step evaluates the rules, writes its own row, records the entry and **answers** the two moves and the timer stop.
- **The retention period is not a constant.** No source sets its length: NFR-028, NFR-030 and NFR-031 are open under DL26, and REQ-S7-008 names the period without a value, so the period is reference data read with its version and the value stays a placeholder here (GAP-3041; ASM-5102).
- **The timer is a durable timer, not a scheduler row.** The two rules name the "Workbench scheduler", and in the target the stage waits on a Temporal durable timer inside `WriteOffWorkflow`; no Quartz row, no shared job table and no Schedule is created, and the only job of the service, JOB-16, is the monthly scan of R-WO-01 (ASM-5100).
- **Two ways in.** A case reaches `RETENTION_RUNNING` from `PLACED_WITH_AGENCY` on a placement whose term expired with nothing recovered (R-WO-36), or from `POSTED` when the approved and posted populations reconcile (R-WO-42, RWB-S7-E6023-APP). This step owns the first and the timer from both, and reads the second as an outcome it did not produce (ASM-5100).
- **Closure is a decision, so it is recorded.** Legacy AC1 asks for the result in the decision log with the rule version and legacy AC4 stops the action when the log cannot be written; the record is written through the local library in the same transaction as the move, so no case closes without its entry (DP-03).
- **The closing entry is the record, not a new table.** R-WO-47 asks for "cash recovered and loss"; no column of `write_off` carries a loss and `recovered_after` is the only recovered amount field, so the two amounts are attributes of the closing entry and their binding to a column is left open (GAP-3041; ASM-5103).
- **The hold is a document fact.** R-WO-48 holds the closure when a document on the case has no retention class and raises a Document Hub task; the class is rwb-document's and the task is P5's, so this step refuses the closure and changes nothing (GAP-3041).
- **Nothing leaves the service.** The connection matrix gives S7 REST and events to P1 and Temporal and events to P8, and no row to P9 or to a data lake; a closure is a case fact, so no event is published here (ASM-5099).

No business value moves: the period, the retention class, the states, the rule IDs and the package version are reference data and rule rows, read with their version and never written in code.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S7-E6025-CON is published: the `write_off` element, the state values this step writes, the consumed rows, the closing-entry element, the rights, the error set and the fakes are baselined and handed to this story.
- The rwb-case case read is published with its fake: the case reference, the case number, the product group, the stage and the state `PLACED_WITH_AGENCY`, `RETENTION_RUNNING` or `CASE_CLOSED`. The operation name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3041; ASM-5098).
- The case-move answer of rwb-case is available for the fake: the moves `RETENTION_RUNNING` and `CASE_CLOSED` with the rule version. No source publishes an operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage; on the workflow boundary the answer is the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies (GAP-3041; ASM-5098).
- The timer read and stop of rwb-case is available for the fake: the open timers of the case and their close. The `timer` rows are P3's, and the operation name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3041; ASM-5098).
- The rwb-decision rule-package read is published with its fake and answers the WO package at its version in force, with R-WO-36, R-WO-47 and R-WO-48 among its 51 rules over 27 states (GAP-3041; ASM-5005).
- The retention period and the retention classes are reference data with their version; no source sets a period, so the value is a placeholder at build time (GAP-3041; ASM-5102).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: the local decision-record library writes in the caller's transaction, and a failed write stops the action with MSG-P7-003, so no move is answered and nothing changes (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-27 reaches this service through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, and no screen calls a service directly (DP-19).
- `write_off` exists in schema `rwb_writeoff` from the DB story of this service, with the columns of DF-FIN-010 to DF-FIN-020 and the standard record columns of TSD S7 T3.0; this story adds no table, no column and no migration.
- The service runs as its own login on schema `rwb_writeoff`; it holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `rwb_case`, on `recovery_case` or on an ACE view is refused by the database and fails the boundary test.
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-S7-E6025-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. A case reaches `RETENTION_RUNNING`: R-WO-36 fires from `PLACED_WITH_AGENCY` when the placement term has expired with `recovered_amount = 0`, or R-WO-42 has already published the reconciliation completeness of RWB-S7-E6023-APP (Business Rules and Routing Logic v4).
2. The retention branch of `WriteOffWorkflow` on queue `rwb-writeoff` starts on that signal and reads the package in force, the case and the open timers (DP-12; ASM-5100).
3. R-WO-36 closes the placement and starts the retention timer for the period of the reference data (placeholder). The timer is a durable timer of the workflow, not a job (ASM-5100, ASM-5102).
4. The step writes `write_off.state = RETENTION_RUNNING` and answers rwb-case with the same move; rwb-case writes the `recovery_case` row and parks the stage (ASM-5035).
5. The retention timer expires. `RetentionClosureEvaluator` tests R-WO-47: no open placement, no open sale, no open exception, and a retention class on every document.
6. Where a document carries no retention class, R-WO-48 holds the closure, the state stays `RETENTION_RUNNING`, the Document Hub task of P5 is raised by the document owner and this step changes nothing (X4).
7. Where every condition holds, the evaluator answers the rule ID, the package version, the action, the closing amounts and the move `CASE_CLOSED` (AC3).
8. `WriteOffDecisionRecordWriter` writes the closing entry **before any change**: the case reference, the write-off reference, the rule ID `R-WO-47` with its package version, cash recovered, loss, the from state, the to state and the closed-at time. A failed write stops the step with nothing changed (DP-03; legacy AC1 and AC4).
9. `CaseMoveAnswer` answers rwb-case with the move `CASE_CLOSED`; `TimerStopClient` closes every timer the case still holds. rwb-case writes its row, its state and its timers; this service writes none of them (ASM-5098, ASM-5035).
10. The step writes `write_off.state = CASE_CLOSED` in the same transaction as the entry, and publishes nothing (ASM-5099).
11. The officer reads the closed case and its closing entry on SCR-27 through the composite route, read only (DP-19).
12. A repeated timer expiry, or a resume after a worker restart, is idempotent: one entry, one move answer and one timer close per case, and a case that has left `RETENTION_RUNNING` answers 409 with no change.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The local decision record cannot be written | Nothing changes: no move is answered, `write_off.state` is unchanged and no timer is stopped | MSG-P7-003 | AC4, TC-E6-025-04, TC-E6-025-06 |
| X2 | The role does not hold the Write-off and posting right | 403 before any read or write; the unattended step runs under the service identity with the same check | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E6-025-05 |
| X3 | The retention period or the retention class reference data has no version in force | The step waits, the state is unchanged and the case stays at `RETENTION_RUNNING`; the closure is never taken on an unversioned period | None | AC1, AC3 |
| X4 | A document on the case carries no retention class | R-WO-48 holds the closure, the state stays `RETENTION_RUNNING`, the task to the document owner is raised and nothing is written | None | AC3 |
| X5 | An open placement, an open sale or an open exception exists at expiry | R-WO-47 does not fire, the case stays at `RETENTION_RUNNING` with a fresh timer and nothing is written | None | AC3 |
| X6 | The rwb-case or rwb-decision contract does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The step retries on the workflow's own schedule; nothing is written and no move is answered; the caller sees 503 with the platform error envelope | None | AC1, AC3 |
| X7 | A repeated timer expiry, or a case that has left `RETENTION_RUNNING` | One entry and one answer; the repeat answers the outcome that exists, and a moved case is refused with 409 | None | AC1, AC3 |
| X8 | A component, a statement or a test reaches a `v_ace_*` view, a `recovery_case` row, a `timer` row or another service's schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | Section 17, BR5, BR6 |

X1 is the legacy not-recorded path and X2 the legacy access path carried onto the slice; X3 to X7 are the paths the timer, the document class and the target call types add, and X8 is the ACE and schema boundary. X4 is the hold of R-WO-48, which no legacy criterion of this key covers.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-S7-E6025-CON, the rwb-case and rwb-decision fakes and the decision-record stub, on its own schema, and needs no live P1, P3 or P7 |
| Negotiable | The activity names and the closing-entry attribute names are this story's choice; the rules, the messages, the states, the period source and the screen are fixed |
| Valuable | A closed case is a closed case with its closing entry, its stopped timers and its recorded amounts, so no retention period runs on the books untracked |
| Estimable | One workflow branch, two rule evaluations, one record write, one row write, one case-move answer, one timer stop, three clients and one read-only screen state |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on a synthetic retained case through the contract fakes, plus the hold, the not-recorded, the access and the repeat cases |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Close the case after the retention period

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-000884" is at the write-off stage with write-off "WO-2027-000402" in state "RETENTION_RUNNING"
    Given the WO rule package is in force at its version and carries R-WO-36, R-WO-47 and R-WO-48
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 Close the case after the retention period (legacy RWB-E6-025 AC1)
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns the WO package at its version in force with R-WO-47
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case of record at "RETENTION_RUNNING" and accepts the move "CASE_CLOSED"
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When its trigger arrives
    Then closes the case once the retention period has run and no action is open
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Rule R-WO-36 (legacy RWB-E6-025 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case of record at "PLACED_WITH_AGENCY" and accepts the move "RETENTION_RUNNING"
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns the WO package at its version in force with R-WO-36
    Given a case in state PLACED_WITH_AGENCY
    When placement term expired
    Then close the placement and start the retention timer
    Then the case moves to RETENTION_RUNNING

  Scenario: AC3 Rule R-WO-47 (legacy RWB-E6-025 AC3)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case of record at "RETENTION_RUNNING" with no open placement, no open sale and no open exception, and accepts the move "CASE_CLOSED"
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns the WO package at its version in force with R-WO-47
    Given a case in state RETENTION_RUNNING
    When retention timer expired
    Then close the case, stop every timer and write the closing entry with cash recovered and loss
    Then the case moves to CASE_CLOSED

  Scenario: AC4 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E6-025 AC4)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The four criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E6-025 word for word, with their origin tag added and nothing else changed: the repeated `Then`, the wording of `its trigger arrives`, `placement term expired`, `retention timer expired` and `the decision log cannot be written` all stand. The cross-service parts are mocked, so AC1, AC2 and AC3 carry `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` lines, and those are the only additions; AC4 has no cross-service part and is copied with nothing added. What the legacy lines describe now happens in three places: rwb-case holds the case, its states and its timers, rwb-decision holds the package at its version, and this story evaluates the rules, writes `write_off.state`, writes the closing entry and answers the moves. The `decision log` of the legacy text is the local decision record of DP-03 in `rwb_writeoff`, with the central `decision_log_entry` ledger of rwb-decision behind it.

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-WO-36 | Write-off | D9 | PLACED_WITH_AGENCY | PLACEMENT_TERM_EXPIRED | ends_at passed and recovered_amount = 0 | Close the placement and start the retention timer | RETENTION_RUNNING | Workbench | Partner Portal, Workbench scheduler | None |
| R-WO-47 | Write-off | D9 | RETENTION_RUNNING | RETENTION_TIMER_EXPIRED | no open placement, no open sale, no open exception, and a retention class on every document | Close the case, stop every timer and write the closing entry with cash recovered and loss | CASE_CLOSED | Workbench | Workbench scheduler, Document Hub, Decision Log | on expiry |

The two rows are the rows of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, copied character for character. Their owner and systems columns name a business role and systems, not services: "Workbench" is this service and its stage, the "Workbench scheduler" is the durable timer of `WriteOffWorkflow` and not a Quartz job, the "Partner Portal" is the agency placement fact that reaches the case, the "Document Hub" is rwb-document (P5) for the retention class and its task, and the "Decision Log" is the local record of DP-03 with the rwb-decision ledger behind it (ASM-5098, ASM-5100, ASM-5101). R-WO-48, the hold when a document carries no retention class, is the refusal of X4 and is evaluated here; R-WO-42, the reconciliation that also reaches `RETENTION_RUNNING`, is RWB-S7-E6023-APP's and is read, not written; R-WO-49, a payment on a closed case, is RWB-S7-E6027-APP's.

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The closure is the last transition of the write-off stage: it runs in `WriteOffWorkflow` on `rwb-writeoff` and writes `write_off.state` only | TSD S7 T3.1, T4; context pack ownership rows (table and workflow); FSD S7 A2.13.2 |
| BR2 | The closing entry is recorded before the case moves, with the rule ID, the package version, cash recovered, loss and the two states; a failed write changes nothing and the caller sees MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; TSD S7 T2 ("writes the decision log entry before any change"); legacy AC1 and AC4 |
| BR3 | Two rules close a stage and one holds it: R-WO-36 from `PLACED_WITH_AGENCY` on an expired placement term with nothing recovered, R-WO-47 from `RETENTION_RUNNING` on the expiry where nothing is open and every document has a retention class, R-WO-48 as the hold | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-36, R-WO-47 and R-WO-48; FSD S7 A2.13.3.1 |
| BR4 | The move is answered, not written: `recovery_case`, its route states and the `timer` rows are rwb-case's, and this service answers `RETENTION_RUNNING` and `CASE_CLOSED` with the rule and its version and asks for the timer stop | ASM-5098, ASM-5035; TSD S7 T3.3 |
| BR5 | No cross-schema join and no foreign key leaves `rwb_writeoff`; `case_id` and `decision_log_id` are identifiers of another service's fact | DP-01; TSD S7 T3.3 |
| BR6 | ACE data only through the owner's contract: this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and reads no ACE table, and the balance and the recovered amounts reach it on the case and the write-off of their owners | DP-05 as a prohibition; FSD S7 A1.1; TSD S7 T1 |
| BR7 | Every value a business person may change is a rule row or reference data read with its version: the two rules, the states, the retention period, the retention classes and the package version | FSD S7 BR-S7-013; legacy Guardrails |
| BR8 | The expiry is idempotent: one entry, one move answer and one timer close per case, and a case that has left `RETENTION_RUNNING` is refused with 409 | TSD S7 T-A.2; platform delivery rule (at least once, consumers idempotent) |
| BR9 | No person name, address, contact value or identity number enters `rwb_writeoff`, the closing entry, a log or a workflow input; the case reference is a number and not an identity | Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17); TSD S7 T6.2 |

##### 9. State transitions

The case route state is rwb-case's and is not changed by this story: the step answers the move and the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies it (BR4). What this story owns is the step, the row and the entry; the states it writes are the ones of the WO machine.

| From (case state, rwb-case) | Event | Condition | To | Written by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PLACED_WITH_AGENCY` | `PLACEMENT_TERM_EXPIRED` | `ends_at` passed and `recovered_amount = 0` | `RETENTION_RUNNING` | rwb-case, on this story's answer (R-WO-36) |
| `PLACED_WITH_AGENCY` | `PLACEMENT_TERM_EXPIRED` | The term has not passed, or an amount was recovered | Unchanged | none; the placement keeps running |
| `POSTED` | `POPULATION_RECONCILED` | Approved and posted populations equal | `RETENTION_RUNNING` | rwb-case, on the answer of RWB-S7-E6023-APP (R-WO-42) |
| `RETENTION_RUNNING` | `RETENTION_TIMER_EXPIRED` | Nothing open and a retention class on every document | `CASE_CLOSED` | rwb-case, on this story's answer (R-WO-47) |
| `RETENTION_RUNNING` | `RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING` | A document on the case has no retention class | Unchanged | none; R-WO-48 holds the closure and P5 raises the task |
| `RETENTION_RUNNING` | `RETENTION_TIMER_EXPIRED` | An open placement, an open sale or an open exception exists | Unchanged | none; R-WO-47 does not fire and the timer restarts |
| `CASE_CLOSED` | `PAYMENT_RECEIVED_AFTER_CHARGEOFF` | A payment matches the closed case with no placement | `PAYMENT_MATCHED` | rwb-case, on the answer of RWB-S7-E6027-APP (R-WO-49) |

| Step execution | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting | The stage enters `RETENTION_RUNNING` | The package in force is read and the period has a version | Timing |
| Timing | The durable timer fires | The period has run | Evaluating |
| Evaluating | R-WO-47 fires | Nothing open and every document has a retention class | Recording |
| Evaluating | R-WO-48 holds | A document has no retention class | Waiting, nothing changed |
| Recording | The entry is written and the answer sent | The transaction commits | Closed |
| Recording | The entry write fails | X1 | Waiting, nothing changed |

The states `PLACED_WITH_AGENCY`, `RETENTION_RUNNING` and `CASE_CLOSED` are those of the WO machine of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 and live on the case of record; this step writes `write_off.state` and none of the case columns.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| None; runs unattended | The primary actor of FSD S7 A2.13.3.3: the placement expiry and the retention expiry start the step |
| RW-CREDITAD, Credit Administration officer | Write-off and posting CRUA in TSD S7 T6.1: the role of the legacy story, reading the closure and its entry |
| RW-WOCOMM, write-off committee member; RW-PRODHEAD, product head; RW-FINANCE, Finance and CFO delegate | Write-off and posting RA: the other holders of right A on the write-off and posting area |
| RW-WRITEOFF, write-off team member | Write-off and posting CRU: holds right C and reads the closure |
| RW-FRAUD, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-CONDUCT, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE | Write-off and posting R: read only, in scope |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-AGENT, SY-DATALOAD | Write-off and posting R or U as the matrix gives it: the service identities run the step and are subject to the same checks |
| rwb-writeoff service identity | Evaluates the rules, writes the row and the entry, answers the moves and asks for the timer stop; it holds no grant on another schema and no `v_ace_*` grant |

The rights are the rows of TSD S7 T6.1 and nothing wider. The legacy permission table gives right A to RW-CREDITAD, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-WOCOMM and RW-FINANCE and right C to RW-WRITEOFF and RW-CREDITAD; the closure itself is unattended, so no operation of this story declares a user right. DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set: the capability area and the right are declared per operation of the service and the access guard is a service-template capability, so the check is stated here and not built here.

| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (PLT library, created in `rwb_writeoff`) | rule id, rule version, decision code, cash recovered, loss, from and to state, closed at | Write through the local library, before the case moves |
| DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036 | timer (P3) | id, case_id, task_id, timer_type, started_at, expires_at and 4 more | Not read as a table and not written: the timers are read and stopped on the rwb-case contract |
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case (P3) | id, case_no, product_group, primary_person_key, status, stage_code and 17 more | Not read as a table and not written: the state arrives on the contract and the move returns on its answer |

Field IDs are those of TSD S7 T3.1 and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary, and the case, timer, partner, ledger and rule rows are the rows the legacy Data table lists, with their owners changed to P3, S9 and P7 by the target. **No new table, no new column and no migration**: the table arrives with the DB story of this service, and `decision_record`, `idempotency_key` and `outbox_event` are library objects created in `rwb_writeoff` by the library's own migration (DP-03).

**No personal data.** The rows carry identifiers, amounts, dates, list values, a rule version and a state. No name, address, contact value or identity number enters `rwb_writeoff`, the entry, a log or a workflow input, and the fixtures are synthetic; `primary_person_key` is P3's and is never copied here, and the partner row's name is the agency's commercial name and is never copied either.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. Owner rwb-writeoff (S7); base `/api/recovery/writeoff/v1` (DP-13). The closure is unattended and this story provides no operation. The two operations of this legacy key are other stories' of the same service: `POST /write-off-scans` (API-S7-001, right C) is RWB-S7-E6013-APP's and `POST /write-offs/{writeOffId}/committee-decision` (API-S7-002, right A) carries the committee outcomes at RWB-S7-E6018-APP to RWB-S7-E6020-APP. The read of the closure state behind SCR-27 is Not specified in the source documents and carries the placeholder (GAP-3041; ASM-5098).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The case read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3041; ASM-5098)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference, case number, product group, stage and state at `PLACED_WITH_AGENCY`, `RETENTION_RUNNING` or `CASE_CLOSED`; read only, faked |
| The case-move answer (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3041; ASM-5098)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The moves `RETENTION_RUNNING` and `CASE_CLOSED` with the rule ID, its version and the closing amounts; on the workflow boundary it is the stage outcome the parent `CaseWorkflow` applies; faked |
| The timer read and stop (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3041; ASM-5098)) | rwb-case (P3) | P3 rwb-case | The open timers of the case and their close, the `timer` rows of DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036; faked |
| The rule-package read in force (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3041; ASM-5005)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The WO package at its version, with R-WO-36, R-WO-47 and R-WO-48 among its 51 rules over 27 states; faked |
| The placement read (operation name and owner Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3041; ASM-5101)) | rwb-case (P3) or the agency record's owner | The placement of `PLACED_WITH_AGENCY` with `ends_at` and `recovered_amount`; no source publishes the operation and the connection matrix gives S7 no row to rwb-partner (S9); faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The five rows are contract dependencies of class C that the plan does not carry, because this story's C row is None; the absence is recorded (GAP-3041; ASM-5098, ASM-5005, ASM-5101).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service publishes on `rwb.writeoff.events.v1` and its event set carries `WriteOffApproved` (`rwb.writeoff.WriteOffApproved.v1`, `EV-24`, with `writeOffId`, `caseId` and `amount`, consumed by Posting), and that event belongs to the approval and posting steps, which are RWB-S7-E6018-APP's and RWB-S7-E6021-APP's. A closure approves nothing, posts nothing and changes no amount, so this story declares no event, no producer group and no outbox row, and a build that publishes one fails the absence test. The topic carries the retry and `.dlt` topics of the platform (DP-14), and the outbox library of DP-09 is the dependency the plan does not carry for this key (ASM-5099).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The service listens to the rwb-source-data and rwb-payment events in its scan and recovery steps (context pack connection matrix, row S7: REST and events to P1, Temporal and events to P8), and none belongs to the closure: the two triggers are the placement expiry and the retention expiry, which are timers of the stage. This story therefore holds no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox row, and a build that adds one fails the absence test (ASM-5099, ASM-5100).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WriteOffWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per case at the write-off stage, the child of `CaseWorkflow`, continues-as-new at each stage end | `rwb-writeoff` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case reference, the write-off reference and the package in force; signals: the placement expiry, the retention expiry and the case answered by rwb-case; outcome for the parent: the case move |
| `closeAfterRetention` | Activity, the one closure step, with R-WO-36, R-WO-47 and the R-WO-48 hold | `rwb-writeoff` | The case reference, the write-off reference, the package version and the period in; the rule ID with its version, the state, the record reference and the case move out, with the entry written before the answer |
| `retentionTimer` | Durable timer of the workflow, the wait of R-WO-36 and R-WO-47, not an activity and not a Schedule | `rwb-writeoff` | The period of the reference data with its version; the expiry is the event `RETENTION_TIMER_EXPIRED` |

No child workflow for the case and none for the money exists in this service, and the activity names are a target design choice fixed by no source document. The stage waits on the durable timer of the platform kit (L3 Scheduled job and the workflow timers of the kit), not on a scheduler row.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The retention wait is a durable timer inside the workflow, not a Temporal Schedule, not a Quartz row and not a shared job table; the FSD declares the monthly scan as the module's only background event (FSD S7 A2.13.4.4) and JOB-16 is RWB-S7-E6013-APP's. DP-10 is not in this key's pattern set, and the "Workbench scheduler" of the two rules is read as the durable timer (ASM-5100).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| write_off | S7 (`rwb_writeoff`) | The write-off of the balance on a case; this story writes its `state`, its lock version and its audit columns and reads the rest |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_writeoff` | The local hash-linked closing entry (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_writeoff` | The key of the repeated expiry and the outcome it holds |
| outbox_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_writeoff` | Present as a library object; this step writes no row to it (§12.3) |

Not owned and never read as a table: `recovery_case` and `timer` (P3), every `v_ace_*` view (P1), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `partner` (S9), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `payment` (P8). No foreign key leaves the schema and `case_id` is an identifier, not a foreign key across schemas (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case case fake | `RC-2026-000884` at `PLACED_WITH_AGENCY`, at `RETENTION_RUNNING` with nothing open, at `RETENTION_RUNNING` with an open placement or sale or exception, and at `CASE_CLOSED` | AC1, AC2, AC3, X5 |
| rwb-case case-move fake | The moves `RETENTION_RUNNING` and `CASE_CLOSED` accepted with the rule and its version; a move refused because the case is not in the expected state | AC2, AC3, X7 |
| rwb-case timer fake | Two open timers of the case closed in one answer; a timer that is already closed; no answer beyond 2 s | AC3, X6 |
| rwb-decision rule-package fake | The WO package at its version in force with R-WO-36, R-WO-47 and R-WO-48 among its 51 rules over 27 states | AC1, AC2, AC3 |
| Placement fake | A placement with `ends_at` passed and `recovered_amount = 0`, and one with an amount recovered; the placement read carries the placeholder (GAP-3041; ASM-5101) | AC2, X5 |
| Local decision-record library stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain, and a stopped chain | AC1, AC4, X1 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-27 answer for `RC-2026-000884` in its retention and its closed state | AC1 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The operation names of the case read, the case-move answer, the timer read and stop, the package read and the placement read carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-3041; ASM-5098, ASM-5005, ASM-5101).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 5 consumed | The case read, the case-move answer, the timer read and stop, the package read and the placement read; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | `WriteOffApproved` (`EV-24`) belongs to the approval and posting stories and no event is consumed here (§12.3, §12.4) |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 1 activity and 1 durable timer | `WriteOffWorkflow`, its `closeAfterRetention` activity and the retention timer on `rwb-writeoff`; no Schedule |
| File | None | No file is read, built or delivered here |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.writeoff`, module `closure`; front end `src/modules/recovery/writeoff/WriteOffProposal.tsx`, the fragment SCR-27 embeds, read only for this story's state.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the transaction rule of the step: the entry and the move answer commit together or not at all. DP-13 fixes the base of the service and gives the closure no element of its own. DP-19 is how SCR-27 reaches the closure state, one hop through the gateway. These three are the whole pattern set of the key and the story adds no fourth: DP-04 (the embedded Drools kit), DP-09 (the outbox and inbox library), DP-10 (the scheduler row) and DP-05 (the ACE read) are real dependencies or markers of the stage that the plan does not hold, and they are recorded in the registers instead of the metadata table (GAP-3041; ASM-5005, ASM-5099, ASM-5100).

**Dependencies the tables add and the plan does not hold.** The five consumed rows are class C dependencies in fact and the plan's C row is None, so the story builds against their documents and fakes on Day 1. The Drools kit of DP-04 would add `RWB-PLT-E1072-CON` and `RWB-P7-E1073-CON`; the package is read as data and evaluated by this service's own evaluator, so no kit is declared. The outbox library of DP-09 would add `RWB-PLT-TE006-CON` and is needed only by the stories that publish. The plan's H row stands unchanged.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `WriteOffWorkflow` retention branch | Workflow | Receives the placement and retention expiries as signals, reads the package and the period in force, waits on the durable timer and reports the outcome to the parent |
| `closeAfterRetention` | Activity | Reads the case and its timers, evaluates R-WO-36 and R-WO-47 with the R-WO-48 hold, writes the row and the entry, sends the answer |
| `RetentionClosureEvaluator` | Service | The rule evaluation over the package in force: the two rules, the four closure conditions, the hold and the no-fire path |
| `WriteOffDecisionRecordWriter` | Library adapter | Writes the closing entry with the rule ID, the version and the two amounts before any change, hash-linked; refuses the step when the write fails |
| `CaseClient` | Client | The case read of rwb-case, one hop, 2 s, breaker, no retry of its own |
| `RulePackageClient` | Client | The WO package read of rwb-decision at its version in force |
| `CaseMoveAnswer` | Client | The `RETENTION_RUNNING` and `CASE_CLOSED` answers with the rule, its version and the amounts |
| `TimerStopClient` | Client | The timer read and stop of rwb-case, one hop, idempotent per timer |
| `PlacementClient` | Client | The placement facts of the case at `PLACED_WITH_AGENCY`; the read is a placeholder |
| `WriteOffProposal` | React component | Shows the case, its write-off and its closure entry on SCR-27, read only |

**Database and migrations.** No Flyway file. The `write_off` table arrives with the DB story of this service, and the record and idempotency key are library objects created in `rwb_writeoff` by the library's migration (DP-03). No column is added for the retention period, the loss or the placement: the period and the class are reference data, the loss is an attribute of the entry and the placement is another owner's fact (ASM-5101, ASM-5102, ASM-5103).

**Configuration and reference data.**

- R-WO-36, R-WO-47 and R-WO-48, their from and to states and the closure conditions: rule rows of the WO package with their version, never written in code (ASM-5005).
- The retention period of the timer and the retention classes of the documents: reference data with their version; no source sets a period (ASM-5102).
- The capability area "Write-off and posting" and its rights: access rows of rwb-access, read through the guard.
- The 2 s budget, the single hop and the breaker are the platform rule of ADR-020.

**Build steps**

1. The retention branch of `WriteOffWorkflow` and its input record, registered on `rwb-writeoff` as the stage child of `CaseWorkflow`, with the two expiries as signals and the durable timer between them.
2. `CaseClient` and `TimerStopClient` against their fakes, with the 2 s budget, the breaker, the open-timer path and the closed-timer path (AC1, AC3, X6).
3. `RulePackageClient` and `PlacementClient` against their fakes, with the version in force recorded with the outcome and the placement placeholder (AC1, AC2).
4. `RetentionClosureEvaluator` over the package, with R-WO-36, R-WO-47, the R-WO-48 hold, the four conditions and the no-fire path (AC2, AC3, X4, X5).
5. `WriteOffDecisionRecordWriter` against the stub, with the failed-write path (AC1, AC4, X1).
6. `CaseMoveAnswer` with the two moves and the amounts, and the write of `write_off.state` in the same transaction (AC2, AC3).
7. The read-only closure state of `WriteOffProposal` on SCR-27 through the composite route fake (AC1).
8. The boundary test: no statement outside `rwb_writeoff`, no `v_ace_*` read, no write to `rwb_case`, `recovery_case`, `timer` or any other schema (X8, BR4, BR5, BR6).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.writeoff.retention-closure-v1`, a flag of the platform library; off means the step takes no closure, the case stays at `RETENTION_RUNNING` and SCR-27 hides the closing entry, and the scan, the pack and the posting stories are unaffected.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the step runs from a synthetic retained case in SIT, R-WO-36 moves a case to `RETENTION_RUNNING`, R-WO-47 closes it with its entry and its stopped timers, the R-WO-48 hold and an open dependency are refused, a repeated expiry writes once, a forced entry failure changes nothing, no `recovery_case` row, no `timer` row and no `v_ace_*` read exists in the build, and SCR-27 answers through the composite route.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-27 Write-off proposal, in its retention and its closed state, is served through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The route calls rwb-writeoff for the write-off, its state and its closing entry, and rwb-case for the case and its route state; this story fixes the rwb-writeoff answers only, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

The legacy screen table gives the states "Scan; proposed; in committee; approved". Those four are the earlier stories' of this key set; this story produces the two states after them: a retained case shows the retention timer running, its period and its class status, and a closed case shows the closure, its entry, cash recovered and loss and the closed-at time, read only. The scan state is RWB-S7-E6013-APP's, the proposed state RWB-S7-E6015-APP's, the committee states RWB-S7-E6017-APP to RWB-S7-E6020-APP's and the posted state RWB-S7-E6021-APP's. The hold, refused, not-recorded and unavailable states read the messages of section 14.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the two rules, R-WO-48, the states, the retention period, the retention classes, the closure conditions and the package version stay rule rows and reference data, never a constant, a default or a branch.
- No personal data in `rwb_writeoff`, in a workflow input or in a log: identifiers, amounts, dates, states and a rule version only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and reads no ACE table, and a build that adds one fails the boundary test (BR6).
- The case and its timers stay with rwb-case: no `recovery_case` row, no `timer` row and no case state write here (BR4).
- The write-off row is written in one column only: `state` with its lock version and audit columns; no amount, no date and no GL value is set by a closure (BR1).
- The period is never hard-coded and never defaulted: a period with no version in force holds the step (X3, ASM-5102).
- One base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service; no document names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no shared job table, no Quartz row, no monolith base, no event published by this step, no `recovery_log` write and no data-lake path.
- The entry is written before the change; a build that answers the move outside the entry's transaction fails the review (DP-03).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E6-025 for rwb-case, case side of the retention closure. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **Credit Administration officer (RW-CREDITAD)**, I want **the case of record to start the retention timer when the placement term has run, to close the case when that timer expires and the write-off service answers that the closure conditions hold, stopping every timer and cancelling every open task, and to keep the closed case readable with its closing date and its closure reason**, so that **a charged-off case ends on the date the rules name, with no clock still running and no open action left on a closed case**.

This is the case side of legacy RWB-E6-025 (FEAT-WOF-13). rwb-case owns the case, its stage, its timers, its tasks and its closing facts (Architecture v5 slide 14, P3 OUT row: schema `rwb_case` holds case, CMMN state, queues, tasks, allocation and timers; slide 41, P3 ownership row). rwb-writeoff owns the placement, the scan, the committee, the posting, the cash recovered, the loss and the closing entry (slide 20, S7 OUT row). The two answers of the write-off route set that land on the case — the retention-start answer of R-WO-36 and the closure answer of R-WO-47, with the hold of R-WO-48 — cross one service boundary through the contract of RWB-S7-E6025-CON, and this story applies them exactly once.

Inside `rwb-case` the slice is served on the service's own base `/api/recovery/case/v1` (DP-13), from schema `rwb_case`, in Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, on topic `rwb.case.events.v1` and task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`.

The slice holds no legacy acceptance criterion. The four criteria of RWB-E6-025 describe the feature across S7 and P3 and are proved end to end by RWB-ITG-E6025-ITG and on the write-off side by RWB-S7-E6025-APP; the eight criteria of section 7 are new and test only the case-side deliverable (ASM-1361).

##### 2. Business rationale

R-WO-36 closes the placement and starts the retention timer when the placement term has run and nothing was recovered; R-WO-47 closes the case, stops every timer and writes the closing entry when no placement, no sale and no exception is open and every document carries a retention class; R-WO-48 holds the closure and raises a document task when a class is missing. All three are rows of the write-off route set, and all three land on facts that belong to the case: its stage, its clocks, its tasks and its closing date. The requirement is REQ-S7-008 and the business rule is BR-057 of the Epics 3 to 8 requirements: a case closes after its retention period with no action open, and reopening a closed case needs a written rule, a reason and an approver. RULE-022 carries the same statement, and NFR-031 states that case records carry a retention and archive rule by record class and that a case closes after its retention period, with the period itself still open under DL26.

In the monolith the timer, the state move, the closing entry and the case update were four statements inside one process and one Quartz job. In the target the rule answer is rwb-writeoff's and the case, the clocks, the tasks and the closing facts are rwb-case's, so the answer crosses a service boundary and must be applied exactly once, in one transaction, on a durable clock.

The case side is where a failure becomes visible. If the closure answer is dropped, the case sits in RETENTION_RUNNING for ever and its service-level timers keep escalating on a case nobody will work again. If the answer is applied twice, the case carries two closing dates. If the expiry is a table scan and a five-minute check, a restart loses the expiry and the case closes late or not at all. If the timers and the tasks are not stopped with the closure, a closed case reappears in a queue with an open action on it. Each of those is a wrong record on a charged-off balance, and none of them raises an error of its own.

The boundary must hold as well. rwb-case keeps the stage, the retention clock, the closing date and the closure reason, and keeps nothing of the write-off record: no placement, no sale, no exception, no document, no cash recovered, no loss, no closing entry. The retention period and the retention timer type are rows read at run time and never constants, because NFR-031 leaves the period open and a period in code would be a release. The expiry is a durable timer of CaseWorkflow, so it fires in a later year, after many releases, without a Quartz row. The case is served on `/api/recovery/case/v1` (DP-13), SCR-27 composes the case and the write-off through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and every decision is written locally and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03).

##### 3. Preconditions

The paths and the element names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0741; ASM-1356) because that contract story fixes them; this story builds against the contract and its fake and never against a write-off table |
| The `rwb_case` baseline exists | `recovery_case`, `timer`, `task`, `queue`, the local decision-record table and the outbox, inbox and idempotency objects, from the Epic 1 case story of this service (RWB-P3-E1018-APP) |
| CaseWorkflow runs one per case | Task queue `rwb-case`, workflow ID `case-{caseId}`, Continue-As-New at each stage end and at least every 28 days, and the workflow kit holds durable timers, so this story adds a timer and a step and no workflow and no Schedule (TSD P3 v3 T2.4) |

| The retention timer type is a reference row | LOV-TIMER holds SERVICE_LEVEL, NOTICE_PERIOD, CURE_PERIOD, PRESCRIPTION, HEARING_DEADLINE, OFFER_VALIDITY, HOLDING_AGE, CLAIM_DEADLINE and INSTALLMENT_DUE, and none of them is a retention timer; the new row is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0741; ASM-1358) |

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-writeoff applies R-WO-36 when the placement term has run and nothing was recovered, and sends the retention-start answer through the operation of RWB-S7-E6025-CON: one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream.
2. The case router of rwb-case consumes the answer, dedupes it in its inbox on the write-off reference and the message key, and starts the retention-start step for the case. A duplicate never acts twice (R-UNI-40).
3. The step reads the case row: its stage code, which must be PLACED_WITH_AGENCY, its open tasks and its timers. It reads `rwb_case` rows only.
4. The step validates the answer: write-off reference, rule ID, rule version and business date present, and MSG-GEN-001 names the field when one is missing; a case not in PLACED_WITH_AGENCY is refused with MSG-P3-005 and nothing changes.
5. The step reads the retention period in force for the product group from the parameter row and computes the expiry from the business date of the answer.
6. RecordAndApply, in one `rwb_case` transaction: `stage_code` RETENTION_RUNNING by R-WO-36, `stage_clock_start`, `rule_version` (DF-CAS-021), the timer row with the retention type, `started_at`, `expires_at`, `status` RUNNING (DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036), the local decision record naming R-WO-36 and the rule version, and the outbox rows of `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`. A failed write rolls the whole transaction back (R-UNI-39).
7. The step signals CaseWorkflow with the expiry. CaseWorkflow holds it as a durable timer of the workflow kit; when it fires the workflow starts the closure step on task queue `rwb-case`. No Quartz row, no timer-check job and no Schedule is involved.
8. The closure step asks the write-off service for the decision of R-WO-47 through the same contract, carrying the case reference, the write-off reference and the business date, and receives Close with the rule version, or Hold with R-WO-48.
9. On Close the step checks the case's own open actions — no task in status OPEN and no timer other than the retention timer in status RUNNING — and then closes: `stage_code` CASE_CLOSED, `closed_date` (DF-CAS-022) the business date of the answer, `closure_reason` (DF-CAS-023) WRITTEN_OFF of LOV-CLOSURE, every timer of the case to status STOPPED, every open task to status CANCELED, and the next-action fields cleared.
10. On Hold the step records the hold under R-WO-48 and leaves the stage, the clocks and the tasks untouched; the document task that follows is raised by rwb-document and not here.
11. The closure writes one decision record naming R-WO-47 and the rule version, and the outbox rows of `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1`, `rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`, in the same transaction as the closure.
12. Officers read the closed case: `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` returns the stage, the closing date, the closure reason and the stopped timers, `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/next-action` returns no next action, and both are guarded by the Case record right and the scope, cached per request.
13. SCR-27: the gateway-bff composite route calls rwb-case for the case, its clocks and its closing facts, rwb-writeoff for the write-off state and rwb-document for the documents of the case, one hop each, and merges them into the screen model (DP-19); the browser calls one route and no owner service.
14. Nothing of the placement, the sale, the exception, the documents, the cash recovered, the loss or the closing entry is written or served by rwb-case; those stay with their owners, and the closure answer carries only the decision, the rules and the business date.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The same retention-start or closure answer arrives twice | The inbox ignores the second answer and records the idempotency hit; no row, no clock, no closure and no event is written twice | None | AC4 |
| X2 | An answer names a case that is not in the stage its rule starts from | The answer is refused, the stage and the clocks do not change, and the refusal is recorded with the rule the answer carried | MSG-P3-005 | AC5 |
| X3 | The local decision record cannot be written | The transaction rolls back: the stage, the clock, the closing date and the closure reason do not change, and the answer is retried | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | The closure answer is Hold under R-WO-48 because a document carries no retention class | The case stays in RETENTION_RUNNING, every clock keeps running and no closing fact is written | None | AC3 |
| X5 | The case still holds a task in status OPEN when the closure answer is Close | The case is not closed, the retention clock keeps running and the open task stays on the case | None | AC4 |
| X6 | An answer carries no write-off reference, no rule ID or no business date | The answer is refused, nothing changes and the missing field is named | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X7 | The write-off answer does not arrive within 2 s or the service is unavailable | Nothing moves; the retention clock keeps its expiry and the closure step retries the ask | None | AC2 |
| X8 | The write-off service reports that the scan is on hold for the missing tax criteria and sends no answer | The case stays where it is and the reason carried by the answer is passed through unchanged | MSG-S7-001 | AC1 |
| X9 | A role without the Case record right reads a closed case | Refused; nothing is returned and nothing is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC7 |
| X10 | A closed case outside the caller's scope is read | Refused as not found; nothing is returned and nothing is written | MSG-P4-003 | AC7 |

X1 is the duplicate rule R-UNI-40 and X3 is the no-unlogged-action rule R-UNI-39; both are applied through the inbox and the decision-record library and are platform behaviour, not this story's code. X5 is the case-side reading of "no action is open": the guards that look at the placement, the sale, the exception and the document class are the write-off service's and arrive as the decision of the answer (ASM-1359).

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on Day 1 against the rwb-writeoff contract fake of RWB-S7-E6025-CON, the authorise fake and the workflow kit; no work order sits inside another team's lane |
| Negotiable | The retention period, the retention timer type, the closure reason, the rule version and the contract element names are parameter rows, reference rows or contract fields; the story fixes the behaviour and no value |
| Valuable | A charged-off case closes on the date the rules name, with no clock still running and no open action on it |
| Estimable | One consumer, one durable timer, one closure step, one ask to the write-off service, one transaction, two read operations and one panel |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests: no new table, no new column, no new workflow and no Schedule |
| Testable | Each of the eight criteria of section 7 is one automated test, and every cross-service answer is stubbed in the contract fakes |

The eight criteria are this slice's own, because the plan allocates no legacy criterion to it: AC1 to AC4 of RWB-E6-025 are proved by RWB-S7-E6025-APP and end to end by RWB-ITG-E6025-ITG (ASM-1361). Where a criterion needs another service, the `Given` names its contract mock: rwb-writeoff for the two answers of R-WO-36 and R-WO-47 and the hold of R-WO-48, rwb-document for the documents and their retention class, rwb-access for the right and the scope. "P1" is a fixture value of the retention period parameter row and not a business value: the period is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0741; ASM-1357), and the write-off reference, the case ID, the rule version label "WO-2026.11" and the dates are synthetic fixtures of the same kind as the legacy "SYN" values. The cash recovered and the loss carry no value here, because they are the write-off service's and this story never stores or echoes them.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | When the placement term has run and nothing was recovered, the placement is closed, the retention timer starts and the case moves from PLACED_WITH_AGENCY to RETENTION_RUNNING | R-WO-36 |
| BR2 | When the retention timer expires, no placement, no sale and no exception is open and every document carries a retention class, the case closes to CASE_CLOSED, every timer stops, every open task is canceled and the closing facts are written | R-WO-47 |
| BR3 | A document without a retention class holds the closure: the case stays in RETENTION_RUNNING and the hold is recorded under R-WO-48 | R-WO-48; REQ-DCM-010 |
| BR4 | The retention period and the retention timer type are a parameter row and a reference row of this service, read at run time; neither is a constant, because NFR-031 leaves the period open under DL26 | NFR-031; BRD Q-012; ASM-1357 |
| BR5 | The expiry is a durable timer of CaseWorkflow, not a Quartz job, a Schedule or a five-minute check, so the date survives a restart and fires after any number of releases | TSD P3 v3 T2.3 and T2.4; ADR-011 |
| BR6 | The case stage, the clocks, the tasks, the closing date and the closure reason are rwb-case's and are never written by the caller that answers the closure | Architecture v5 slide 14 and slide 41; ASM-1359 |
| BR7 | The placement, the sale, the exception, the documents, the cash recovered, the loss and the closing entry are other services'; rwb-case holds the decision, the rule ID and the rule version and nothing of the write-off record | Architecture v5 slide 20 (S7 OUT) and slide 41 |
| BR8 | The decision record, the state change and the outbox rows are one transaction: a closure that cannot be recorded does not happen | R-UNI-39 |
| BR9 | The same answer arriving twice writes no row and raises no event a second time | R-UNI-40 |
| BR10 | The closing step names the rule ID and the rule version on every decision record; both arrive in the answer and are never written in code | R-WO-36; R-WO-47; DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 |
| BR11 | A closed case has no next action and no open task, so it never appears in a list of active cases with no next action | FSD P3 v4 AC-EXC-P3-050-03 |
| BR12 | The read of a case is guarded by the Case record right and the scope, and a read writes nothing | TSD P3 v3 T6.1 and T6.2; MSG-P4-002; MSG-P4-003 |

How the rules hold in `rwb-case`: BR1 and BR2 are two steps of the case router, each writing one stage change, one clock state and one decision record; the rule ID and the version come in the answer, so no Drools package is loaded and no KieBase is built on this path. BR3 is the Hold branch of the closure step: the answer decides, and this service only records it. BR4 is one parameter read and one reference read, so a period change is a data change with no release. BR5 is the workflow kit's timer, and the TimerScheduler port of TSD P3 v3 T2.3 is where the replacement of the retired five-minute check by durable timers happens, behind the same interface, with no caller change. BR6 and BR7 are the repository and an architecture test that fails a statement naming another schema. BR8 and BR9 are the one transaction and the inbox. BR10 is the decision-record writer. BR11 is the cleared next-action fields and the canceled tasks. BR12 is one authorise call per request, cached.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLACED_WITH_AGENCY | PLACEMENT_TERM_EXPIRED | The placement term has run, the recovered amount is 0 and the answer names R-WO-36 | RETENTION_RUNNING |
| RETENTION_RUNNING | RETENTION_TIMER_EXPIRED | The retention durable timer fired, the answer names R-WO-47 Close and the case holds no task in status OPEN | CASE_CLOSED |
| RETENTION_RUNNING | RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING | A document on the case has no retention class and the answer names R-WO-48 Hold | RETENTION_RUNNING, unchanged |
| RETENTION_RUNNING | A retention-start answer of R-WO-36 | The case is not in PLACED_WITH_AGENCY | Unchanged, MSG-P3-005 |
| RETENTION_RUNNING | The decision record cannot be written | The transaction rolls back | RETENTION_RUNNING, unchanged |

These four state names are the from-state and to-state values of R-WO-36, R-WO-47 and R-WO-48 in the write-off route set, written to `stage_code` of `recovery_case` (DF-CAS-006) together with `status` CLOSED of LOV-CASE-STATUS at the closure. They are not values of LOV-STAGE, which lists the route stages RESTRUCTURE to DEVIATIONS; the mapping from a route-set state name to a case stage code is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0741; ASM-1358), and this story writes the rule's own names unchanged so a decision record and a case row can be read side by side. The closing facts are `closed_date` (DF-CAS-022) and `closure_reason` (DF-CAS-023); the reason written by a retention closure is WRITTEN_OFF of LOV-CLOSURE. A legal hold that is open on the case is not lifted here, because a hold overrides expiry and is rwb-access's and rwb-document's row under NFR-072. A payment after the closure is R-WO-49 and belongs to rwb-writeoff.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-case service identity | Applies the two answers, moves the stage, writes the retention clock, stops the clocks, cancels the tasks, writes the closing facts and the decision record |
| CaseWorkflow | Holds the retention durable timer and starts the closure step when it fires; moves no stage by itself |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the local decision record and its outbox row (Decision log C) |
| RW-CREDITAD, Credit Administration officer | Reads the closed case and its closing facts (Case record R); takes no closure action on the case |
| RW-PRODHEAD, RW-WOCOMM, RW-FINANCE | Hold the write-off rights of the capability area; they read the case and act in the write-off service, not here |
| RW-WRITEOFF, write-off team | Runs the placement, the scan and the closure answer in rwb-writeoff (Write-off and posting C) |
| RW-COE | Owns the retention period parameter row, the retention timer type and the LOV-CLOSURE rows as reference data |
| RW-REFADM | Holds no Case record right; refused on the case read with MSG-P4-002 |
| No approval applies | The story takes no decision; the approval of a write-off is the committee's in rwb-writeoff |

The Write-off and posting rights A and C named in the legacy permission table (RW-CREDITAD, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-WOCOMM, RW-FINANCE; RW-WRITEOFF, RW-CREDITAD) are checked in rwb-writeoff and are outside this story. No person is named anywhere in this story; the actor is a role and the record carries a user reference only.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity in rwb_case | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-CAS-001, DF-CAS-002, DF-CAS-003 | recovery_case | id, case_no, product_group | Read |
| DF-CAS-005 | recovery_case | status | Read, and CLOSED written with the closure |
| DF-CAS-006 | recovery_case | stage_code | Read, and RETENTION_RUNNING and CASE_CLOSED written with the two moves |
| DF-CAS-018 | recovery_case | stage_clock_start | Write: the start of the retention clock |
| DF-CAS-021 | recovery_case | rule_version | Write: the rule version in force named by the answer |
| DF-CAS-022 | recovery_case | closed_date | Write: the business date of the closure answer |
| DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case | closure_reason | Write: WRITTEN_OFF of LOV-CLOSURE |
| DF-CAS-019, DF-CAS-020 | recovery_case | deviation_open, legal_hold | Read only, to show the state of the case; neither changes here |
| DF-CAS-049 to DF-CAS-053 | recovery_case | next_action_text, next_action_owner_role, next_action_due_date, next_action_rule_id, next_action_waiting | Write: cleared on the closure |
| DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036 | timer | id, case_id, task_id, timer_type, started_at, expires_at, warn_at, paused, status, escalation_level | Write: one retention timer at the start, and status STOPPED on every timer of the case at the closure |
| DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-026 | task | id, case_id, task_code, element_type, discretion, status, owner_role, due_at, completed_at, outcome_code | Read the open tasks, and write status CANCELED on each of them at the closure |
| DF-WRK-001 to DF-WRK-008 | queue | id, queue_code, queue_name, team_code, role_code, assignment_method, capacity_cap, overflow_queue_id | Read only: the queue the case was last on; the closure writes no placement |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local library) | all fields | Write locally; the central entry in `decision_log_entry` is rwb-decision's (P7) |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0741; ASM-1357) | parameter_catalog, parameter_value | the retention period row per product group, with the version in force | Read, in process through the parameters contract of this service |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0741; ASM-1358) | reference_row, reference_version | the retention timer type in LOV-TIMER, WRITTEN_OFF in LOV-CLOSURE and STOPPED in LOV-TIMER-STATUS | Read, in process through the reference-data contract of this service |
| DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 | partner (owner S9) | id, partner_code, partner_name, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end | Not read and not written: the placement is rwb-partner's and its end date arrives in the answer |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | rule_row (owner P7) | rule_id, rule_version, from_state, event_code, to_state | Not read here: the rule ID and the rule version arrive in the answer |

Field IDs are those of the Technical Specifications by Module and the Logical Data Model. Every row written is a `rwb_case` row: the parameters and the reference rows are read through the contracts of this same service and never joined in SQL, and `rwb_case` holds no foreign key into another schema. `write_off`, `debt_sale`, `deviation`, `document`, `partner`, `rule_row` and `decision_log_entry` are other services' and are reached only through their owners' contracts. The legacy data block of RWB-E6-025 names `recovery_case`, `timer`, `partner`, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row`; the first two are this service's and the last three are not read or written here.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This story adds no operation. The closed case is read through the operations of this base that already exist — `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` for the case with its stage, its closing date and its closure reason, `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` for the stopped clocks and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/next-action` for the empty next action — all three owned by rwb-case (P3) in the ownership map. The two closing fields are added to the Case resource those operations answer; their spelling `closedDate` and `closureReason` follows the column names and the rest of the element spelling is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0741; ASM-1362). All three declare the Case record right R with the scope applied, and all three are read only.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0741; ASM-1356) | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0741; ASM-1356) | rwb-writeoff (S7) | The retention-start answer of R-WO-36 on the placement term, and the closure decision of R-WO-47 or the hold of R-WO-48 on the retention expiry: decision, rule ID, rule version, package version and business date; built against the RWB-S7-E6025-CON fake | One hop, 2 s |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | rwb-access (P4) | The Case record right and the scope before a case read, cached per request by the guard library | One hop, 2 s |

Two calls and no chain. The closure step asks the write-off service once per expiry and makes no second call for the same expiry; the write-off service makes no call back into rwb-case on this path. The path and the element names of the write-off operation are fixed by RWB-S7-E6025-CON and are not invented here.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (EV-05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId | caseId, fromStageCode, toStageCode, eventCode (PLACEMENT_TERM_EXPIRED or RETENTION_TIMER_EXPIRED), ruleId, ruleVersion, writeOffRef, businessDate |
| `rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1` (EV-19) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId | caseId, timerType, expiresAt, ruleId, ruleVersion |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 owns the type and the central ledger; every service writes its own record | caseId | decision record reference, rule ID R-WO-36, R-WO-47 or R-WO-48, rule version, business date |

All three are written to the outbox in the same transaction as the state change and relayed with the CloudEvents envelope; no personal data and no amount is in any payload. rwb-case publishes no separate case-closed event: the closure is carried by CaseStateChanged with its event code, because the six published events of this module are CaseCreated, CaseAllocated, CaseAllocationFailed, CaseTransferred, CaseStateChanged and TimerBreached, and TimerDue is retired inside the workflow.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The closure decision arrives as a call of the S7 contract and is not a Kafka subscription of this story, and the case router that consumes the state signals of a case is the Epic 1 and Epic 2 work of this service. A payment after the closure (R-WO-49) is consumed by rwb-writeoff and rwb-payment. This story adds no consumer group and no inbox use beyond the dedupe of the two answers.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow (parent, one per case, workflow ID `case-{caseId}`) | `rwb-case` | Holds the retention expiry as a durable timer of the workflow kit and starts the closure step when it fires |
| RetentionStartStep | Step of the case router | `rwb-case` | Validates the R-WO-36 answer, reads the period, computes the expiry, records and applies the move, and signals CaseWorkflow |
| CaseClosureStep | Step of the case router | `rwb-case` | Asks the write-off service for the R-WO-47 decision, checks the case's own open actions, records and applies the closure |
| RecordAndApply | Transactional step (decision-record library) | `rwb-case` | Writes the stage, the closing facts, the clock and task statuses, the decision record and the outbox rows in one transaction |

No other activity and no child workflow is added: the write-off steps before the start and after the closure belong to rwb-writeoff, and the stage children of CaseWorkflow belong to the route services.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added. The retention expiry is a durable timer of CaseWorkflow and not a Temporal Schedule, because an expiry is one date for one case and not a cadence; the retired five-minute timer check (JOB-05) is replaced by the workflow kit's timers behind the same timers port, and no caller changes (TSD P3 v3 T2.3). No Schedule, no Quartz row and no timer-check job is created, and no scheduler job of rwb-case reads the timer table for this story. The document-side retention job (JOB-17, monthly, owner rwb-document) and the legal-hold override are P5's and are not this story's. Whether the retention period should also be reviewed on a bank-wide cadence is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0741; ASM-1360).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `recovery_case` | rwb_case | P3 | The story writes `stage_code`, `status`, `stage_clock_start`, `rule_version`, `closed_date`, `closure_reason` and the cleared next-action fields |
| `timer` | rwb_case | P3 | One retention timer at the start, and status STOPPED on every timer of the case at the closure |
| `task` | rwb_case | P3 | Read to find an open action, and status CANCELED written on every open task at the closure |
| `queue`, `assignment` | rwb_case | P3 | Read only: the closure writes no placement and no transfer |
| `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version` | rwb_case | P3 | The retention period, the retention timer type, the closure reason and the timer status, read through this service's contracts and never joined in SQL |
| decision record (local library) | created in rwb_case | Platform library | The local record of the two moves, hash-linked, written in the same transaction |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | created in rwb_case | Platform library | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects |

`write_off`, `debt_sale`, `deviation`, `document` and `partner` are other services' tables: this story holds no foreign key into any of their schemas, no cross-schema join and no copy of a row. `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are rwb-decision's and are reached only through its contracts. `outbox_event` and `outbox_delivery` are the platform library's.
