Legacy AC2 (the R-DEV-03 assignment and the DEV_WITH_OWNER move) is asserted here in AC3, and legacy AC4 (the decision log cannot be written) in AC7; the build of those steps stays with RWB-S8-E7003-APP. Legacy AC3 is not asserted as written: it is an X3 scenario tagged with R-DEV-06, and R-DEV-06 belongs to X6 and X7, so the published X3 branch is asserted instead, R-DEV-11 in AC4 and R-DEV-12 in AC5, with no approval step invented (GAP-0467; ASM-0659). The legacy criterion stays with RWB-S8-E7003-APP as a build criterion and is not copied here.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A death confirmed from the registry or a document raises X3, stops all contact and holds the case for the specialist and Legal, on the same day | R-UNI-05, line 409 |
| BR2 | A deviation in any state pauses the stage clock, keeps the prescription clock running and routes the case to the named owner | R-DEV-01, line 383; Temporal design slide 8 |
| BR3 | An X3 deviation is assigned to the specialist, and Legal joins X3 for the estate claim | R-DEV-03, line 385 |
| BR4 | An X3 case whose insurance clears the balance closes on CASE_ENDED | R-DEV-11, line 393 |
| BR5 | An X3 case whose insurance does not clear returns to the route decision against the estate, DEV_REROUTE | R-DEV-12, line 394 |
| BR6 | After the reroute the case reopens the route decision with the segment recomputed and the hard gates re-run, ending in ROUTE_D6 | R-DEV-19, line 401 |
| BR7 | A deviation that sits with its owner past the deviation service level escalates to the team manager and the breach is reported | R-DEV-20, line 402 |
| BR8 | Every X1 to X7 deviation runs end to end with its own flow, approver, contact rules and return point | REQ-S8-001, BRD Program v4 line 417 |
| BR9 | ACE data is read only through rwb-source-data's data-product contract with its freshness stamp, never from a view and never from another service's schema; the screening consumes `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` with the deceased and bankrupt flags | DP-01, DP-05; Arch v5 slide 15 S8 IN and slide 42 row 26 |
| BR10 | The decision record is written by the owning service through the local decision-record library on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the central ledger in rwb-decision confirms it | DP-03; ADR-022 |
| BR11 | Every hop in the run is one REST call on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s timeout | DP-11, DP-13 |

The harness asserts these rules and changes none of them; the rules themselves are evaluated in RWB-S8-E7003-APP and the states are held by P3 rwb-case. R-DEV-06 is deliberately absent: the rule table applies it to X6 and X7, and no approval step is asserted for X3 (GAP-0467).

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To | Owner of the change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ANY_STATE | CUSTOMER_DECEASED | a death is confirmed from the registry or a document; deviation_code = X3 | DEV_FLAGGED | S8 rwb-deviation, DeviationWorkflow, R-UNI-05 and R-DEV-01; `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` |
| DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code = X3 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | S8 rwb-deviation, R-DEV-03, the specialist with Legal for the estate claim |
| DEV_WITH_OWNER | INSURANCE_SETTLED | deviation_code = X3 and insurance clears the balance | CASE_ENDED | S8 rwb-deviation, R-DEV-11; P3 stops the stage clock and the prescription clock |
| DEV_WITH_OWNER | ESTATE_CONFIRMED | deviation_code = X3 and insurance does not clear | DEV_REROUTE | S8 rwb-deviation, R-DEV-12 |
| DEV_REROUTE | ROUTE_REOPENED | any | ROUTE_D6 | P3 rwb-case for the case state and S1 rwb-valuation for the D6 route decision, R-DEV-19 |

The states are the deviation states of R-DEV-01, R-DEV-03, R-DEV-11, R-DEV-12 and R-DEV-19, and the case state is read through the P3 contract after every step. The two clocks are read through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers`: the stage clock is paused from DEV_FLAGGED and the prescription clock is never paused, and both stop only when the case closes on CASE_ENDED. The documents that carry the evidence are P5's and are read through its contract. The harness changes no state. Every change in the table is made by the owner: S8 holds the deviation and drives DeviationWorkflow, P3 holds the case state and the timers, P5 holds the documents, S1 produces the D6 route decision and P7 holds the central ledger. A state the harness had set by hand would prove nothing, so the report names the owner and the operation behind every value it asserts.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-SPECIAL, hardship and vulnerability specialist | Is the named handler of X3 under R-DEV-03; holds Case record U; is the role the journey is written for |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Is the Legal handler who joins X3 for the estate claim under R-DEV-03; holds Case record U |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Owns the case after the reroute and holds Case record U; the team manager is the escalation point of R-DEV-20 |
| RW-OFF, RW-TRIBE, RW-PLATADM | Read only where their rights allow; RW-OFF is the refused caller of AC8 |
| QA lead | Owns the harness configuration, the fixtures, the branch answers, the report shape and the pass or fail gate |
| Integration lead | Owns the harness code, the stub set and the swap from a stub to the real service |
| The owning services' identities | S8 runs DeviationWorkflow and writes the decision record, P3 holds the case and the timers, P1 answers DP02 and the freshness read, P5 holds the documents, P7 holds the ledger and P4 answers the session; they make every change the harness asserts |
| No delegation of authority level applies | The harness takes no business decision and asserts no approval, because the published X3 branch names none; authorisation is answered by rwb-access and the DoA is P4's |

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case | case_no, status, stage_code, primary_person_key | Read through the rwb-case contract |
| DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 | deviation | deviation_code, raised_at, raised_by, paused_state, handler | Written through the rwb-deviation raise and patch, read back through the case and the timers |
| DF-WRK-009 to DF-WRK-016 | assignment | assignee_user_id, assigned_at, ended_at | Read through the rwb-case contract |
| DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036 | timer | timer_type, started_at, expires_at, paused_at | Read through the rwb-case timers contract |
| DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074 | v_ace_customer, DP02 Customer and party | person_key, cif_no, date_of_birth, customer_status, deceased flag | Read through the rwb-source-data DP02 contract with its freshness stamp, never the view |
| DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-011 | document, DP10 Documents and extracted fields | document_type, source, storage_ref, person_key | Read through the rwb-document contract |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | decision_code, rule_id, rule_version | Read through the rwb-decision contract |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. The ACE side is DP02 Customer and party behind P1's contract: the legacy `v_ace_customer` is not read by the harness, and no schema is named in it. The document side is DP10 Documents and extracted fields behind P5's contract. The case, the deviation, the assignment and the timers belong to P3 and S8, and the decision log belongs to P7; the harness reads them only through those contracts and never from a schema. The harness owns no table and writes no row. The two writes it makes are the owner's published operations of §12.2, taken with one Idempotency-Key each.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations` | S8 rwb-deviation | Raises the X3 deviation and starts DeviationWorkflow, with one Idempotency-Key (AC1, AC2, AC6, AC8) |
| PATCH | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/deviations/{deviationId}` | S8 rwb-deviation | The assignment to the specialist and Legal, the branch outcome and the forced failure, with one Idempotency-Key (AC3, AC4, AC5, AC7) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case state after the flag, the assignment, the close and the reroute, and the handler (AC1 to AC5, AC7) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` | P3 rwb-case | The stage clock, the prescription clock and their stop on the close (AC2, AC4, AC5, AC7) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP02/records?caseId={caseId}` | P1 rwb-source-data | The deceased flag, the party and the contact points of the case, through the contract and not the view (AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness?product=DP02` | P1 rwb-source-data | The business date and the load time behind the DP02 read (AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` | P5 rwb-document | The death certificate and the claim evidence on the case (AC1, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | P5 rwb-document | The metadata and extracted fields of the death certificate and the claim evidence (AC1, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | P7 rwb-decision | The decision record of the flag, the assignment and the branch outcome, with the rule version and the ledger confirmation (AC1, AC6, AC7) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The caller's roles and rights before a write (AC8) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13). No operation is invented in this story: each path is the owner's published operation in the Ownership Map, and where a screen would compose them the path would be the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

The map publishes no `GET /deviations` and no `POST /deviations/{id}/clear` for S8, and this story does not pretend otherwise. The deviation is therefore asserted through three published reads — the case read for the state and the handler, the timers read for the two clocks, and the decision log for the record — plus the `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` and `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` publications. The two writes above are the only deviation operations the run uses, and both are the map's own.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it writes its report to the wave record.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use in the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | Starts the X3 screening with the deceased flag, counted once and consumed once by rwb-deviation (AC2, AC6) |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | Counts one publication after the X3 flag and, with the replay, proves one processed row per consumer (AC2, AC6) |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | Counts one publication when the deviation clears on the close or on the reroute (AC4, AC5) |
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | Proves the states observed are the states published for the case (AC2 to AC5) |
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 rwb-document | Counts one publication for the death certificate and one for the claim evidence (AC4, AC6) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation through the local decision-record library (DP-03) | Proves the record was published once with its rule version and confirmed by the central ledger (AC6, AC7) |

The harness subscribes to the four topics under one consumer group of its own, counts publications and replays `AceDataReady` and `DeviationRaised` once each. The consumer effect it reads is the case through the rwb-case operation of §12.2; the inbox row counts of the other consumers are read from the consumer evidence in the run fixture, because they expose no operation in this story.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness exercises DeviationWorkflow, S8's child workflow on the task queue `rwb-deviation` in the `rwb-recovery` namespace, started through the deviation raise and continued through the patch: it is the workflow that carries the X3 route, the pause of the stage clock, the contact stop and the branch on the insurance answer. It observes CaseWorkflow on `rwb-case`, the parent that receives the deviation through the case router as a signal and pauses and resumes the stage clock for the case. Both are stated here as observed and not built here; no workflow, activity or Schedule is created, changed or owned by this story. The D6 route decision is S1's product and is only read as the case state ROUTE_D6.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added. The deceased flag arrives on the overnight `AceDataReady` event and the branch arrives with the insurance answer, so nothing in the journey is on a cron: the harness starts the run from the screening event and holds the insurance and estate answers in its own fixture instead of waiting on a schedule. The timer check of JOB-05 is retired in favour of durable timers inside the workflows (Arch v5 slide 44), which is why the two clocks are read through the timers operation and not through a job.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-01); deviation is S8's, recovery_case, assignment and timer are P3's, document is P5's, decision_log_entry is P7's, and the party side belongs to DP02 behind P1's contract.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Contract | Stubbed answer in the run |
|---|---|---|
| Stub for rwb-deviation | `POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations`, `PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}` | Accepts the raise once per Idempotency-Key and answers MSG-S8-001 with deviation `DEV-SYN-000203` and the specialist as the handler; the patch accepts the assignment and the branch outcome and keeps the same deviationId |
| Stub for rwb-case | `GET /cases/{caseId}`, `GET /cases/{caseId}/timers` | Case `RW-2027-001203` in DEV_FLAGGED, then DEV_WITH_OWNER with the specialist and Legal, then CASE_ENDED in branch A or DEV_REROUTE and ROUTE_D6 in branch B; the stage clock paused, the prescription clock running and both stopped on the close |
| Stub for rwb-source-data | DP02 records, freshness | The deceased flag and the party of the case, no live outbound contact point, and business date `2027-05-14` with a load time |
| Stub for rwb-document | `GET /cases/{caseId}/documents`, `GET /documents/{documentId}` | The death certificate `DOC-SYN-000203` and the claim evidence `DOC-SYN-000204`, each with its type, source and extracted fields |
| Stub for rwb-decision | `GET /decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | One entry per action with its rule id and rule version, and the central ledger confirmation |
| Stub for rwb-access | `GET /me/session` | Allows RW-SPECIAL with Case record U; refuses RW-OFF with 403 and MSG-P4-002 |
| Insurer and estate fixture | The insurance answer and the estate position | The claim `CLM-SYN-000203` clears the balance in branch A and does not clear it in branch B, with the estate position and the heirs to notify held at the point where the real insurer answer would arrive |

Each stub is generated from the published contract and its version is pinned in the run report, so a contract change shows up as a run failure and not as a silent pass. The harness environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the stub answer shapes, the insurer and estate answer shapes, the heir-notification content, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0468; ASM-0660).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 10 consumed, one hop each on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13) |
| Kafka | None published; six consumed, `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1`, `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1`, `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1`, `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`, counted and two of them replayed once |
| Temporal | None added; DeviationWorkflow on `rwb-deviation` exercised from the raise, with CaseWorkflow on `rwb-case` observed as the parent that pauses and resumes the stage clock |
| File | None. The insurer and estate answers are held in the run fixture; no file or claim-check is transferred by this story |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H dependencies DP-03 and DP-19 add, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, are platform stories delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays None; DP-05 adds none in the pattern table, but this story takes the stricter reading of it and reads the ACE side only through P1's DP02 contract, never through a `v_ace_*` view; DP-13 adds nothing. The one blocking dependency is the I story RWB-S8-E7003-APP, which replaces its stub; until it is live the run uses the stub, and a stub pass is reported as a stub pass.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the eight owned criteria in order for a case and a branch, and holds the run lock |
| DeviationDriver | Service | Raises the X3 deviation and patches the assignment and the branch outcome, once per Idempotency-Key |
| ScreeningProbe | Service | Reads DP02 with the freshness stamp, asserts the deceased flag, the party and the absent outbound contact, and watches `AceDataReady` reach rwb-deviation |
| OwnerProbe | Service | Reads the case after the assignment and asserts the specialist and Legal are the named handlers |
| ClockProbe | Service | Reads the timers and asserts the stage clock paused, the prescription clock running and both stopped on the close |
| DocumentProbe | Service | Reads the case document list and each document, and asserts the death certificate and the claim evidence with their types and extracted fields |
| BranchDriver | Service | Holds the insurance answer and the estate position, and drives the close or the return without inventing an approval |
| DecisionProbe | Service | Reads the decision log and asserts one record per action, with its rule version and the ledger confirmation |
| EventObserver | Service | Subscribes to the four topics of §12.4, counts publications and replays `AceDataReady` and `DeviationRaised` once |
| StubSet | Fake | The six stubs and the insurer and estate fixture of §12.8, generated from the published contracts with the version pinned |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes one report per case and branch keyed by story, case_no and branch, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the stubs from Day 1 and the real services as RWB-S8-E7003-APP lands, on synthetic case `RW-2027-001203`, deviation `DEV-SYN-000203`, documents `DOC-SYN-000203` and `DOC-SYN-000204`, claim `CLM-SYN-000203` and business date `2027-05-14`. The harness seeds nothing by hand and never writes a schema row. The environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the insurer and estate answer shapes, the heir-notification content, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0468; ASM-0660).

**Build steps**

1. Generate the six stubs and the insurer and estate fixture from the published contracts and pin each contract version in the run report; fail the run on a mismatch (X1).
2. Build the ScreeningProbe for AC2: DP02 through the contract with its freshness stamp, the deceased flag, no live outbound contact, and one `AceDataReady` consumed by rwb-deviation (X2, X3).
3. Build the DeviationDriver for the raise and prove it is accepted once per Idempotency-Key and answers MSG-S8-001 with the deviation and the handler (AC1, AC2).
4. Add AC2 on the case read and the timers read: DEV_FLAGGED on the same business date, the stage clock paused and the prescription clock still running.
5. Add AC3 on the assignment patch and the case read: DEV_WITH_OWNER with the specialist and Legal named, and no approval step (X4).
6. Add AC4 on branch A: the close on CASE_ENDED with both clocks stopped, and the death certificate and claim evidence read through the P5 contract (X5).
7. Add AC5 on branch B: DEV_REROUTE under R-DEV-12 and the case read in ROUTE_D6 under R-DEV-19, with no route operation called (X6).
8. Add the EventObserver for AC6: one `AceDataReady`, one `DeviationRaised`, one `DeviationCleared` per branch, one `CaseStateChanged` per state and one `DocumentStored` per document, with a replay that changes nothing (X7).
9. Add the DecisionProbe for AC6 and AC7: one entry per action with its rule version, the ledger confirmation, then a forced write failure that leaves the case and the timers untouched and answers MSG-P7-003 (X8).
10. Add the access path for AC8 through the session read and the raise operation, and assert 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no state change (X9).
11. Add the EvidenceReport and the gate, and swap a stub for the real owner as RWB-S8-E7003-APP lands.

**Feature switch.** None. The harness has no production flag and runs in the test environment only.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass against the fakes and again against RWB-S8-E7003-APP when it lands, and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story, case_no and branch.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S8-001 | Information | {deviation} was raised. The case is with {handler}. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values on the answer it reads, and owns no message text. MSG-S8-001 is asserted with the deviation code and the specialist and Legal as the handler when the X3 flag is raised, MSG-GEN-001 with the missing field when a write is made short of a required parameter, MSG-P4-002 with the refused raise for a caller without Case record U, and MSG-P7-003 when the decision record cannot be written and nothing changes.

##### 15. Screens and states

The legacy story's screens are SCR-08 Deviation queue and SCR-06 Raise deviation, and neither is built or rendered here: the harness calls the two operations behind them and reads the states through the owners. What the wave entry check looks at instead is the run report, whose environment, layout and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0468; ASM-0660).

| State | Read through | What the run asserts |
|---|---|---|
| DEV_FLAGGED | rwb-case case read, timers read and DP02 read | The X3 flag is raised on the same business date, no outbound contact is read, and the stage clock is paused while the prescription clock runs |
| DEV_WITH_OWNER | rwb-case case read and timers read | The specialist is the handler and Legal joins for the estate claim, the clocks hold, and the decision record exists with its rule version |
| CASE_ENDED | rwb-case case read, timers read and rwb-document reads | Branch A: the insurance cleared the balance, the case closed, both clocks stopped, and the death certificate and claim evidence are on the case |
| DEV_REROUTE | rwb-case case read | Branch B: the insurance did not clear and the case returns to the route decision against the estate |
| ROUTE_D6 | rwb-case case read | Branch B: the route decision reopened under R-DEV-19, and the deviation cleared |
| A refused raise | rwb-access session read and the raise answer | 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no state change |

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the synthetic case, deviation, document and claim keys, the business date, the timer names, the two branch answers and the report layout are data.
- No personal data in logs, events or reports: every party key is synthetic, the death certificate is a fixture, and the events carry IDs and facts only.
- ACE data only through the P1 contract: DP02 with its freshness stamp, never a direct `v_ace_*` view read and never another service's schema (DP-01, DP-05).
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would (DP-11, DP-13).
- No invented operation and no invented approval: only the two deviation writes and the eight reads of §12.2, and the X3 branch is asserted as R-DEV-11 and R-DEV-12 name it.
- A stub pass is never reported as a real pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and it never writes a row by hand or sets a state it then asserts.
- A failing criterion is fixed in the owning service or raised as a gap; it is never waived in the script.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of the X4 fraud deviation of rwb-deviation, split from RWB-E7-004. It fixes the two operations on `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13), the `DeviationRequest`, `DeviationOutcome` and `Deviation` elements with the field IDs DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 and the three lists, the consumed rows of rwb-case and rwb-decision, the two events of the service on `rwb.deviation.events.v1`, the decision-record element of DP-03, the rights of TSD S8 T6.1, the fakes and the absence tests. No operation re-assigns or clears a deviation by hand, because the map publishes two operations and the patch body carries an outcome and a note only. DP-04, DP-05, DP-09 and DP-16 are not in the plan's pattern set although the step evaluates a package, consumes an event and reaches no external system. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the X4 deviation of rwb-deviation — the two operations on `/api/recovery/deviation/v1`, the request, outcome and deviation elements, the two events, the consumed rows, the decision-record element, the rights, the error envelope, the tables and the fakes**, so that **the app story, SCR-06, SCR-08 and the wave 4 harness build against one fixed, testable contract on Day 1, and a property, a consumed row or an event shape can never drift between rwb-deviation, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-comms without a failing build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy X4 flow of RWB-E7-004 crossed four boundaries at once: the case and its two clocks, the rule version and the record, the referral to the fraud team and two screens. The target splits them: rwb-case owns the case, the route states and the timers; rwb-decision owns the rule rows and the central ledger; rwb-deviation owns the deviation row, the two operations and the two events; rwb-comms and rwb-treatment consume the events for the contact rules. Each boundary is a contract another team builds against, so each is fixed before the app story starts: the shapes of the request and the outcome, the ten properties of `Deviation` with their required list and their three enumerations, the two events with their data and their consumers, and the consumed case and rule rows.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema and login `rwb_deviation`, base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1`, topic `rwb.deviation.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-deviation` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.deviation` (Template and Rules §R4; context pack). It records that this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and no grant on `rwb_case` or `rwb_decision`, so DP-05 is declared as a prohibition and the case and rule facts are consumed on their owners' contracts only (ASM-5162). The four open points are the ones section 13 lists: the five consumed rows against an empty C row and the absent DP-04, DP-09 and DP-16 rows, the absent library and kit rows, the Aric referral that is P4's, and the missing state vocabulary and clear operation.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL and RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the queue and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the pagination and filter convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline; where this document narrows them it says so.
- Ownership is taken from the context pack and the Ownership Map only: `deviation` is S8's, `recovery_case` and `timer` are P3's, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are P7's, every `v_ace_*` view is P1's, `document` is P5's, `notice` is P6's and `write_off` is S7's. This document never declares another service's table or operation as its own.
- The rwb-case case read and timers read and the rwb-decision package and decision-log reads are published with their fakes, so every consumed row names a real owner document; they are not in this story's contract-dependency row, which is None, and the absence is recorded (GAP-3058; ASM-5162, ASM-5163).
- The outbox and inbox library of DP-09 is the platform dependency of the topic and of the consumed case event; the plan's H row for this key does not carry it (ASM-5164).
- The DEVIATIONS route set of 22 rules over 9 states and the UNIVERSAL package of 50 rules are governed in rwb-decision (P7), with R-UNI-08, R-DEV-01, R-DEV-04, R-DEV-13, R-DEV-14, R-DEV-19, R-DEV-20 and R-DEV-21 among them; this baseline names them and declares none of them.
- The `deviation` table arrives with the DB story of this service; this baseline declares shapes and creates no table, no column and no migration.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 and sits in contract group `CG-W4` by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-deviation for this key: the two operations with their request and answer elements, their rights and their error responses.
2. Fix the `DeviationRequest` element: `deviationCode` in the seven values, `reason` and `documentIds`, as API Specification v4 publishes them, with the requiredness the source does not give.
3. Fix the `DeviationOutcome` element: `outcome` in the three values and `note`, which is the whole published surface of a manual action on a deviation.
4. Fix the `Deviation` element: the ten properties of DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045, the three enumerations, the three maximum lengths and the required list API Specification v4 publishes.
5. Fix the two events: `DeviationRaised` (EV-06) with `caseId`, `deviationCode` and `raisedBy`, and `DeviationCleared` (EV-07) with `caseId`, `deviationCode` and `outcome`, on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, and their consumers.
6. Fix the consumed rows: the case read, the timers read, the stage pause and resume signal, the package read and the decision-log read, marking with the placeholder what the sources do not give.
7. Record the decision-record element of DP-03, written before the row and the state change, and the rights of TSD S8 T6.1 and the legacy permission table.
8. Record the naming baseline, the absence of a job and of an Aric operation, and the rule that no value is a constant of the code.
9. Publish the contract tables of section 12, the fakes of 12.8 and the contract tests, then tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-S8-E7004-APP, SCR-06, SCR-08 and the wave 4 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A request or answer body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 422 or 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC6 |
| X2 | A property is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X3 | The `Deviation` element is declared without the required list or with a different enumeration | The schema test fails the build | None | AC2 |
| X4 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X5 | A consumed row has a name or a field list the sources do not give | The row carries the placeholder and the fake is derived from the published document | None | AC4, AC5 |
| X6 | A property is declared that no source publishes, for example an assignment field, a clear operation or a case property | The review fails the baseline and the absence test fails the build | None | AC1, AC4, AC7 |
| X7 | The document declares another service's operation or table as provided, or a `v_ace_*` view | The review fails the baseline and the boundary test fails the build | None | AC4, AC7 |
| X8 | The document declares an Aric operation, a second topic or a job | The absence test fails the build | None | AC5, AC7 |
| X9 | The rights of an operation are not the ones TSD S8 T-A.1 and T6.1 declare | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the context pack, the FSD and TSD S8 appendices, API Specification v4 and the published owner contracts of rwb-case and rwb-decision only |
| Negotiable | The element names beyond the ones the sources give, the example values and the fake fixtures are settled in the baseline review; the operations, the base, the topic, the queue and the schema are fixed by the architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks RWB-S8-E7004-APP, SCR-06, SCR-08, the wave 4 harness and the rwb-comms and rwb-treatment consumers on Day 1 |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, nine contract tables, seven fakes and eight contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

```gherkin
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

    Then it declares PATCH /deviations/{deviationId} with a DeviationOutcome body in and a Deviation answer, under the same base
    Then the create declares the Idempotency-Key header and the answers 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 with one envelope and one message ID per condition, as TSD S8 T-A.2 gives the error set of API-S8-001 and API-S8-002
    Then the patch declares no Idempotency-Key, as TSD S8 T-A.2 gives it, and a repeated outcome is described as 409
    Then no clear operation, no GET /deviations, no assignment operation and no Aric operation is declared, because the map publishes these two operations only (GAP-3058; ASM-5163, ASM-5168)

    Then the DeviationOutcome element declares outcome in RETURNED, RE_ROUTED and CASE_ENDED and note of type string, and nothing else
    Then the Deviation element declares the ten properties of DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045: id, caseId, deviationCode, raisedAt, raisedBy, pausedState, handlerUserId, contactStop, clearedAt and outcome
    Then its required list is id, caseId, deviationCode, raisedAt, raisedBy, pausedState and contactStop, as API Specification v4 publishes it
    Then deviationCode keeps maxLength 3, raisedBy maxLength 20 and pausedState maxLength 60, and the three enumerations are the lists LOV-DEVIATION, LOV-RAISED-BY and LOV-DEV-OUTCOME
    Then no property is added for a case state, a timer, a clock, a rule row or a handler role

  Scenario: AC3 The two events are declared with their data and their consumers (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the event section of the baseline
    When it is compared with TSD S8 T5.3 and the event catalogue rows 06 and 07
    Then DeviationRaised is declared as EV-06 on rwb.deviation.events.v1 as rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1, with caseId, deviationCode and raisedBy and no personal data
    Then DeviationCleared is declared as EV-07 on the same topic as rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1, with caseId, deviationCode and outcome and no personal data
    Then the topic carries its retry and .dlt topics, and the two events are the only events of this key
    Then the consumers are declared as rwb-case, rwb-comms and rwb-treatment, and no consumer is added
    Then the document declares no event of an assignment and no third event, and names the target names as the naming rule's while the catalogue publishes the monolith names (GAP-3058; ASM-5164)

  Scenario: AC4 The consumed rows of rwb-case and rwb-decision are declared and the facts stay there (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed rows of the baseline
    When they are compared with the ownership of the context pack
    Then the case read and the timers read are declared as consumed from P3 rwb-case, with the case state, the paused state, the handler, the stage clock, the prescription clock and the deviation service level
    Then the stage pause and the stage resume are declared as the signal the parent CaseWorkflow applies on the workflow boundary, and no REST path is invented for them
    Then the DEVIATIONS route set and the UNIVERSAL package are declared as consumed from P7 rwb-decision at their version in force, with R-UNI-08 and R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-21 among their rows
    Then the decision log of the case is declared as consumed from P7 rwb-decision with its rule version and its central confirmation
    Then the operation names of the five rows are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3058; ASM-5162, ASM-5163) and the rows carry the placeholder
    Then the document declares no v_ace_* path, no recovery_case property, no timer property and no grant on any rwb_* schema of another owner
    Then each row is one hop with a 2 s budget, a breaker and no retry of its own (DP-11, ADR-020)

  Scenario: AC5 The decision-record element, the rights and the error envelope are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision, access and error sections of the baseline
    When they are compared with the library schema and with TSD S8 T-A.1 and T6.1
    Then one decision record is declared per action with the case reference, the deviation reference, the rule ID, the package version in force, the code, the raised-by value, the paused state, the outcome, the case move and the decided-at time
    Then the record is declared as written through the local library on the shared rwb.decision-record.v1 before the row and the state change, and a failed write leaves them unchanged with MSG-P7-003
    Then the record carries no rule row, no threshold as a literal and no personal data
    Then the two operations declare the capability area Case record with right U and the scope applied
    Then RW-FRAUD and RW-CASEOWN hold RU, RW-TEAMMGR holds R, and every other role and every SY-* service identity of TSD S8 T6.1 holds the right the matrix gives it
    Then a role without the right is described as refused with MSG-P4-002, and the error envelope carries one message ID per condition

  Scenario: AC6 The seven fakes answer the document and the drift test fails a build (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fakes of the baseline
    When each is compared with the operation or the element it serves
    Then the rwb-case case fake answers ANY_STATE, DEV_FLAGGED, DEV_WITH_OWNER with the fraud team, DEV_REROUTE and ROUTE_D6 for case "RW-2026-001204", and a case already closed
    Then the rwb-case timers fake answers the stage clock paused, the prescription clock running and a pause refused because no timer runs, and the pause and resume fake accepts the signal
    Then the rwb-decision fakes answer the package at its version in force and an absent version, the decision log with its rule version and a ledger that does not confirm
    Then the decision-record stub answers a healthy chain and a stopped chain, and the gateway-bff fake answers the merged SCR-06 and SCR-08 answers
    Then the drift test compares every fake with the document and fails the build on any difference

  Scenario: AC7 The naming baseline, the absent trigger and the boundary are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the naming and data sections of the baseline
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner, with None where the element is empty
    Then the schema is rwb_deviation, the login is rwb_deviation, the base is /api/recovery/deviation/v1, the topic is rwb.deviation.events.v1 with its retry and .dlt topics, the queue is rwb-deviation in namespace rwb-recovery and the Java package is th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.deviation
    Then the tables named as owned are deviation and the library objects decision_record, idempotency_key, outbox_event and inbox_event, and recovery_case, timer, every v_ace_* view, decision_log_entry and rule_row are named as other owners' and are consumed only through their contracts
    Then no job and no Schedule is declared, because the context pack gives S8 none and the service level of R-DEV-20 is a durable timer inside the workflow
    Then no Aric operation, endpoint, topic or status word is declared, and the referral of INT-31 is named as FEAT-ADM-13 in P4 and not available today (ASM-5165)
    Then the absence test fails a build that adds a published property, a clear operation, an assignment operation, a job, a v_ace_* read or an Aric call
```

These seven criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only. They restate no business outcome owned by RWB-S8-E7004-APP and copy no criterion of the legacy story: legacy AC2 stays with the app story word for word and legacy AC1 stays with RWB-ITG-E7004-ITG, and this baseline copies neither.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The deviation is rwb-deviation's, and the contract declares the fields, the required list and the enumerations of the `Deviation` element only | TSD S8 T3.1 and T3.2; API Specification v4, `Deviation`; context pack ownership row (table `deviation`) |
| BR2 | The decision record is declared as an element written before the row and the state change, through the local library on the shared topic; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; TSD S8 T2; legacy AC2 |
| BR3 | The case and the two clocks stay with rwb-case: the contract declares the reads and the boundary signal as consumed, and declares no case property, no timer property and no pause operation | R-DEV-01; ASM-5163 |
| BR4 | The rule rows and the central ledger stay with rwb-decision: the contract declares the package read and the decision-log read, and declares no rule, no threshold and no service level as a property | ASM-5162 |
| BR5 | No Aric operation is declared: INT-31 is not available today and the referral is FEAT-ADM-13 in P4 | Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3, INT-31 and FEAT-ADM-13; ASM-5165 |
| BR6 | The two events are the two published in TSD S8 T5.3 and the catalogue rows 06 and 07, with their data and their consumers; no third event and no second topic | TSD S8 T5.3; Event and Messaging Design v4; ASM-5164 |
| BR7 | A create declares the `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer; the patch declares none, as TSD S8 T-A.2 gives it, and a repeated outcome is a conflict | TSD S8 T-A.2 |
| BR8 | The lists are the three published by TSD S8 T3.2 and no enumeration is invented: no list of values exists for the deviation state, which the contract therefore does not declare | TSD S8 T3.2; ASM-5167 |
| BR9 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, a code, a date, a state and a rule version only | Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17); TSD S8 T6.2 |
| BR10 | One REST base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service; the document never declares another service's base or topic as its own | DP-13, DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR11 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version | Platform API rule (ADR-020) |
| BR12 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-deviation; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | DP-01, DP-11 |
| BR13 | R-UNI-08 and R-DEV-01, R-DEV-04, R-DEV-13, R-DEV-14, R-DEV-19, R-DEV-20 and R-DEV-21 are governed in rwb-decision and named here, never declared here | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; FSD S8 A2.13.3.1; ASM-5162 |

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of this document, not of a deviation:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The two operations, the three elements, the two events, the consumed rows, the decision element and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, SCR-06, SCR-08, the wave 4 harness and the owners of rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-comms and rwb-treatment accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example an optional answer field | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or the required list or an enumeration changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | The absence tests of AC1 and AC7 fail: a clear operation, an assignment or Aric operation, a case property, a `v_ace_*` view, a job or a third event | In review |

The state machine the document describes is the app story's and rwb-case's: `DEV_FLAGGED`, `DEV_WITH_OWNER`, `DEV_REROUTE` and `ROUTE_D6` are the states of TSD S8 T4 and of the case of record. This baseline fixes the vocabulary of the request, the outcome, the answer and the two events, and moves no case and no row.

The per-service login behind the security scheme is named "the rwb-deviation login (DP-02)" and is not part of this baseline. The referral of Aric is not this baseline's to sign off: it is FEAT-ADM-13 in P4.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Request element | `deviationCode` in X1 to X7, `reason` of type string and `documentIds` as an array of uuid, as API Specification v4 publishes them; the source publishes no required list |
| Outcome element | `outcome` in `RETURNED`, `RE_ROUTED` and `CASE_ENDED` and `note` of type string, which is the whole published surface of a manual action on a deviation |
| Deviation element | The ten properties of DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045: `id`, `caseId`, `deviationCode`, `raisedAt`, `raisedBy`, `pausedState`, `handlerUserId`, `contactStop`, `clearedAt` and `outcome` |
| Required list | `id`, `caseId`, `deviationCode`, `raisedAt`, `raisedBy`, `pausedState` and `contactStop`, as API Specification v4 publishes them |
| Lengths and formats | `deviationCode` at maxLength 3, `raisedBy` at maxLength 20, `pausedState` at maxLength 60, `id`, `caseId` and `handlerUserId` of format uuid, `raisedAt` and `clearedAt` of format date-time |
| Lists | `LOV-DEVIATION`, `LOV-RAISED-BY` and `LOV-DEV-OUTCOME` of TSD S8 T3.2 and no other; no list of values exists for the deviation state, so no enumeration is declared for it (ASM-5167) |
| Event data | `DeviationRaised`: `caseId`, `deviationCode`, `raisedBy`; `DeviationCleared`: `caseId`, `deviationCode`, `outcome`; no personal data in either |
| Decision record | DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 through the local library, written before the row and the state change (DP-03) |
| Case and rule facts | DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 and DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036 of P3, and DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 of P7, read only through the owners' rows and never written, copied or joined here |
| Not declared here | `recovery_case` and `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), every `v_ace_*` view (P1), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `write_off` (S7), an Aric operation and the later stories' data |
| Consumed fields with no source | The operation names of the five consumed rows and the REST path of the stage pause and resume: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3058; ASM-5162, ASM-5163) |

The field-level types of the consumed rows are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the property names, the required list, the three enumerations and the optionality rule of BR11. **No new table, no new column and no migration** is declared by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-deviation (S8); base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/deviations` | DeviationRequest in, Deviation of status 200 out, the raise of the deviation (API-S8-001) | Case record, right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |
| PATCH | `/deviations/{deviationId}` | DeviationOutcome in, Deviation out, the outcome and the case move (API-S8-002) | Case record, right U, scope applied | None declared, as TSD S8 T-A.2 gives it; a repeated outcome is 409 |

The operations answer 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503, each with the error envelope and one message ID of section 14, as TSD S8 T-A.2 gives the error set of both operation IDs. The map publishes these two operations and no more: there is no clear operation, no `GET /deviations` and no assignment operation, so the assignment of R-DEV-04 is the rule's inside the raise and the clear is the outcome of R-DEV-13 and R-DEV-14 through the patch (ASM-5163, ASM-5168).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| The case read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3058; ASM-5163)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case state, the paused state and the handler after each step; faked |
| The timers read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3058; ASM-5163)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` | P3 rwb-case | The stage clock, the prescription clock and the deviation service level; faked |
| The stage pause and resume signal (no REST path is published) | the parent `CaseWorkflow` on `rwb-case` | P3 rwb-case | The pause at the raise and the resume at the clear, as the boundary element the parent applies; faked |
| The DEVIATIONS route set and the UNIVERSAL package in force (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3058; ASM-5162)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The 22 rules over 9 states with R-UNI-08, at their version; faked |
| The decision log of the case (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3058; ASM-5164)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | P7 rwb-decision | The record and its central confirmation; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The five rows are contract dependencies of class C that the plan's C row does not carry, and the absence is recorded (GAP-3058; ASM-5162).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Data | Consumers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` (EV-06) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics | `caseId`, `deviationCode`, `raisedBy` | rwb-case, rwb-comms, rwb-treatment |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` (EV-07) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics | `caseId`, `deviationCode`, `outcome` | rwb-case, rwb-comms, rwb-treatment |

The two events are the service's event set in TSD S8 T5.3 and the catalogue rows 06 and 07, and their target names follow the naming rule of §R4 while the catalogue publishes the monolith names (ASM-5164). Each is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the `deviation` row and the record, and relayed as a CloudEvent (DP-09, ADR-015). The outbox and inbox library `RWB-PLT-TE006-CON` is the platform dependency the plan does not carry for this key.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | The state of record the resume point is taken from; consumed through the inbox, one processed row per event; the target name follows the naming rule and is published in no source document (GAP-3058; ASM-5164) |

One subscription and nothing else. The events of rwb-payment and rwb-agent that the connection matrix gives row S8 belong to the other deviation stories. The inbox is the DP-09 library object the plan's H row does not hold.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DeviationWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per deviation, the child of `CaseWorkflow`, started at any time in the case, continues-as-new at each stage end | `rwb-deviation` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Its input, its signals and its outcome for the parent are declared, not built; it pauses the stage timer through the parent and never the prescription timer |
| `EvaluateDeviationRules` | Activity | `rwb-deviation` | The case and the code in; the rule ID with its package version and the case move out |
| `RecordAndApplyDeviation` | Activity | `rwb-deviation` | The rule outcome in; the record, the row, the outbox row and the case-move answer out, in one transaction |

No child workflow for the case exists in this service. The three names are a target design choice and no workflow or activity is registered by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The context pack gives S8 no job, and the X4 flag arrives as a request or an event and never on a cron; the service level of R-DEV-20 is a durable timer inside the workflow. This baseline declares no Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table, and the absence test of AC7 fails a build that registers a Schedule.

`recovery_case` and `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), every `v_ace_*` view (P1), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `write_off` (S7), an Aric referral table and the later stories' data are not owned by this baseline; it names them only as answers, rule versions or a later story's table, and no foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

##### 13. Solution plan

**The CON declares shapes and moves nothing.** It writes no code, no migration and no table, and changes no case, no row and no package. What it publishes is one OpenAPI 3.1 document, nine contract tables and seven fakes.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is declared as the element of the decision record written before the row and the state change. DP-13 moves the base and nothing else. DP-19 sits behind SCR-06 and SCR-08, whose screen models are the edge contract's. DP-04, DP-05, DP-09 and DP-16 are not in the pattern set: the package is declared as a consumed row rather than an embedded kit, the case facts as consumed data and never views, the outbox and inbox as an absent library row, and Aric as out of scope rather than an adapter (GAP-3058; ASM-5162, ASM-5164, ASM-5165).

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds two H rows, `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` for DP-03 and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` for DP-19, which the plan carries; it leaves out the outbox and inbox library `RWB-PLT-TE006-CON`, the Drools kit rows `RWB-PLT-E1072-CON` and `RWB-P7-E1073-CON`, the access guard `RWB-PLT-E1037-CON` and `RWB-P4-E1037-CON`, and the integration adapter `RWB-P2-E1007-CON`. The five consumed rows are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata row.

**Deliverables and build steps**

1. Write the two operations and validate the additive rule of AC1 in the pipeline.
2. Write the `DeviationRequest`, `DeviationOutcome` and `Deviation` elements, the required list, the three enumerations and the three lengths of AC2, with the placeholder where a requiredness is unstated.
3. Publish the two events and their consumers of AC3 on the naming rule's names.
4. Record the two rwb-case rows, the boundary signal and the two rwb-decision rows of AC4 with their owner, their budget and their placeholders.
5. Record the decision-record element, the rights and the error envelope of AC5.
6. Publish the seven fakes of AC6 and the drift test.
7. Record the naming baseline, the absent trigger and the boundary of AC7, then tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off.

The deliverables are `openapi/rwb-deviation-v1.yaml`, the three elements, the contract README rows for the five consumed rows and their placeholders, the two events, and the seven fakes of 12.8.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI document validates in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, and the app story, SCR-06, SCR-08, the wave 4 harness and the consumers of the two events have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S8-001 | The contract describes the information answer of the raise, which the app story returns with the deviation and the handler | {deviation} was raised. The case is with {handler}. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request is absent or invalid, or a body fails schema validation | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the Case record right the operation declares | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the row and the state change | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The four IDs are contract elements and the text is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new one is added. The escalation of R-DEV-20 and the unmapped code of R-DEV-21 have no message ID in any source and are not bound to one here (GAP-3058).

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves SCR-06 Raise deviation in its form and saved states and SCR-08 Deviation queue in its loading and list states, through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The route calls rwb-deviation for the deviation and its state, rwb-case for the case and its route state and rwb-decision for the record; this baseline fixes the rwb-deviation answers only, and the composite route specification and the screen field lists belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The refusal, not-recorded and re-routed states read the messages of section 14 on the same route.

The four legacy cases are those of RWB-E7-004 in their legacy order, carried as the contract half: their Covers column names the criterion of this story that fixes the surface each one exercises, their Data keeps the legacy intent, and the business behaviour of each is proved by RWB-S8-E7004-APP or by RWB-ITG-E7004-ITG. The legacy level maps to `Contract` here because the artefact under test is the contract. The five cases `TC-S8-E7004-CON-01` to `-05` are new. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same ID; no `-ITG` copy is written by this story.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the codes, the raised-by list, the outcome list, the state names, the service level and the rule rows stay data, reference data or the rule package, never a schema default or an enumeration invented here.
- No personal data in a schema, an example, an event or a fake: identifiers, a code, a date, a state and a rule version only, and every example is synthetic.
- The case and the two clocks stay with rwb-case and the rule rows with rwb-decision: the document declares no `v_ace_*` path, no `recovery_case` property, no `timer` property and no rule row (BR3, BR4).
- The money stays with rwb-payment and the write-off route with rwb-writeoff: the document declares no posting, no settlement and no write-off property.
- No Aric operation is invented: INT-31 is not available today and the referral is FEAT-ADM-13 in P4 (BR5).
- The schedule stays absent: this story registers no Schedule and creates no Quartz row and no job table.
- One base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The document lists only operations owned by rwb-deviation; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided (DP-01, DP-11).
- The error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule, the decision-record library and the outbox and inbox library come from the platform; this story narrows them but never redefines them.
