##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H dependencies DP-03 and DP-19 add, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, are platform stories delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays None. The only blocking dependency is the I story RWB-S8-E7007-APP, which replaces its stub; until it is live the run uses the stub, and a stub pass is reported as a stub pass. DP-05 and DP-13 add no dependency: the data products and the per-service base are already in the owners' contracts.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the six owned criteria in order for a case and holds the run lock |
| DeviationDriver | Service | Raises and transitions the deviation once per Idempotency-Key and reads the case and its timers before and after each step |
| ClaimDriver | Service | Files the insurance claim and moves it to filed, and asserts one claim id for the event |
| ReappraisalDriver | Service | Records the re-appraisal through S1 and reads the asset through S5, so the claim and the new value belong to the same security |
| AceReadBack | Service | Reads DP01 and DP13 with the freshness stamp, and names any figure that is stale or any money that moved early |
| EventObserver | Service | Subscribes to `rwb.deviation.events.v1`, `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`, counts publications and replays each event once |
| LedgerConfirm | Service | Reads the decision log and asserts one entry per transition with its rule version, and the ledger confirmation |
| StubSet | Fake | The eight stubs of §12.8, generated from the published contracts with the version pinned |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes one report per case keyed by story and case_no, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the stubs from Day 1 and the real services as RWB-S8-E7007-APP lands, on the synthetic case `RW-2027-000701`, collateral `COL-SYN-000701`, asset `AST-SYN-000701` and one business date. The harness seeds nothing by hand and never writes a schema row. The harness environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic case, asset and collateral keys, the insurance-claim answer shape, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0472; ASM-0664).

**Build steps**

1. Generate the eight stubs from the published contracts and pin each contract version in the run report; fail the run on a mismatch (X1).
2. Build the DeviationDriver and prove the transition is accepted once per Idempotency-Key and the case state moves from DEV_FLAGGED to DEV_WITH_OWNER (AC2).
3. Add the timer read to AC2 and prove the stage clock is paused while the prescription clock runs, and that the two reads agree with the state (X8).
4. Build the ClaimDriver for AC3: one claim for the event, one claim id, and a replay that returns the same claim (X2).
5. Build the ReappraisalDriver for AC3: one valuation for the asset and an asset read that carries the collateral key and the new valuation (X3).
6. Add the AceReadBack for AC3: DP01 and DP13 with the freshness stamp, and no money moved for the claim before the approval.
7. Drive ESTATE_CONFIRMED and ROUTE_REOPENED and assert DEV_REROUTE and then ROUTE_D6, and that no next decision record exists when the case reaches ROUTE_D6 (AC3, X4).
8. Add the EventObserver for AC4: one DeviationRaised, one CaseStateChanged per transition, one DecisionRecorded per entry, and a replay that changes nothing because the inbox holds one row per consumer.
9. Add the forced decision-record failure for AC5 and the session and case path for AC6, then the EvidenceReport and the gate, and swap a stub for the real owner as RWB-S8-E7007-APP lands (X5, X6, X7).

**Feature switch.** None. The harness has no production flag and runs in the test environment only.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass against the fakes and again against RWB-S8-E7007-APP when it lands, and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story and case_no.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S8-001 | Information | {deviation} was raised. The case is with {handler}. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values on the answer it reads, and owns no message text. MSG-S8-001 is asserted with the deviation code and the handler on the assignment of AC2, MSG-GEN-001 with the missing field when a read is made short of a required parameter, MSG-P4-002 with the refused action on the case read of AC6, and MSG-P7-003 when the decision record cannot be written and nothing changes.

##### 15. Screens and states

The legacy story names SCR-08 Deviation queue and SCR-06 Raise deviation, and the harness renders neither: it observes the owners' operations and writes a report. The states are read through those operations, not rendered.

| State | Read through | What the run asserts |
|---|---|---|
| DEV_FLAGGED | rwb-case case read and rwb-case timers | The X7 deviation is open, the stage clock is paused and the prescription clock runs |
| DEV_WITH_OWNER | rwb-case case read and the decision log | A person approved the insurance claim and the case is with the named handler |
| DEV_REROUTE | rwb-case case read | The claim is filed and the collateral re-appraised, and the case has returned to the route decision |
| ROUTE_D6 | rwb-case case read and the decision log | The segment is recomputed and the hard gates re-run, and no next decision record exists yet |

SCR-08 and SCR-06 belong to the S8 stories and neither is built or read here. What the wave entry check looks at instead is the run report, whose environment, layout and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0472; ASM-0664).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the synthetic case, asset, collateral and claim keys, the business date, the transition event codes, the report layout and the gate are data.
- No personal data in logs, events or reports: every key is synthetic, and the events carry IDs and facts only.
- ACE data only through the P1 contract: DP01 and DP13 with their freshness stamp, never a direct view read and never another service's schema (DP-01, DP-05).
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would (DP-11, DP-13).
- The deviation is never read back to prove a transition: its contract publishes the raise and the transition only, so the effect is asserted through the case, the timers and the decision log.
- A stub pass is never reported as a real pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and it never writes a row by hand or sets a state it then asserts.
- A failing criterion is fixed in the owning service or raised as a gap; it is never waived in the script.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of the override review of rwb-deviation, split from RWB-E7-008. It fixes the review branch of the published `PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}` (API-S8-002) on `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13) with the `DeviationOutcome` request of the API Specification v4 (`outcome`, `note`) and the `Deviation` answer, the ten properties and seven required flags of the deviation element over DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045, the outcome list LOV-DEV-OUTCOME, the reason riding `note`, the package read of rwb-decision at its version in force, the decision-record element of DP-03 with the rule ID and the package version, the rights of TSD S8 T6.1, the fakes and the absence tests. No source defines the override as a record of S8, gives the reason a field or publishes a deviation-list read; the plan's C row is empty while the package read is consumed; the primary role holds R only; and no requirement row traces to FEAT-DVF-08 (GAP-3067; ASM-5202, ASM-5203, ASM-5204, ASM-5205, ASM-5206, ASM-5207, ASM-5210). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the override review of rwb-deviation — the review branch of the deviation-outcome operation on `/api/recovery/deviation/v1`, the deviation and outcome elements with their required flags and lists, the reason carried by `note`, the package read as a consumed row, the decision-record element with the rule ID and the package version, the rights, the error envelope, the tables and the fakes**, so that **the app story, SCR-08 and the wave 4 harness build against one fixed, testable contract on Day 1, and an outcome value, a consumed row or an answer shape can never drift between rwb-deviation, rwb-decision and rwb-case without a failing build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy override review of RWB-E7-008 crossed four boundaries at once: the deviation of the case, the rule version in force, the outcome it records and a screen, and it named two endpoints that carry every deviation action of the module with no element published for the review. The target splits them: rwb-case owns the case, its states and the clock, rwb-decision owns the DEVIATION package and its 22 rules, and rwb-deviation owns the deviation row, its stage and the record of the review. Each boundary is a contract another team builds against, so each is fixed before the app story starts.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema and login `rwb_deviation`, base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1`, topic `rwb.deviation.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-deviation` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.deviation` (Template and Rules §R4; context pack). It records that this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and no grant on `rwb_case`, so DP-05 is declared as a prohibition.

Six points are carried as gaps and assumptions rather than decided quietly: the override is the open deviation record and not an entity of its own (ASM-5202); the reason has no published field and rides `note` (ASM-5203); the plan's C row is None although one consumed row is declared, and DP-04, DP-05, DP-07, DP-08 and DP-09 are absent from the pattern set (ASM-5204, ASM-5206); the review records, it does not clear, so no `cleared_at` property and no stop-lift is declared (ASM-5205); the primary role holds R only while both operations declare U (ASM-5207); and no requirement row traces to FEAT-DVF-08 (ASM-5210).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL and RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the queue and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the pagination and filter convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline; where this document narrows them it says so.
- Ownership is taken from the context pack and the Ownership Map only: `deviation` is S8's, `recovery_case` and `timer` are P3's, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are P7's, every `v_ace_*` view is P1's, `document` is P5's, `notice` is P6's and `payment` is P8's. This document never declares another service's table or operation as its own.
- The two operations are published: TSD S8 T-A.1 gives API-S8-001 `POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations` and API-S8-002 `PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}` with their access and idempotency rules, T-A.2 gives the request and answer elements with the error set 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, and the API Specification v4 publishes `Deviation`, `DeviationRequest` and `DeviationOutcome`. The review branch is declared inside API-S8-002 and needs no new path.
- The rwb-decision package row is published with its fake, so the consumed row names a real owner document; it is not in this story's contract-dependency row, which is None, and the absence is recorded (GAP-3067; ASM-5204).
- The DEVIATION package and its rows R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-22 over 9 states are governed in rwb-decision (P7); this baseline names them and declares none of them.
- The `deviation` table arrives with the DB story of this service; this baseline declares shapes and creates no table, no column and no migration. The reason has no column in it (ASM-5203).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 and sits in contract group `CG-W4` by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the review branch of the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-deviation for API-S8-002: the operation with its request and answer elements, the review properties, the right and the error responses.
2. Fix the `Deviation` element over the columns of DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045, with its seven required flags and the lists of TSD S8 T3.2 published unchanged.
3. Fix the `DeviationOutcome` request: `outcome` over LOV-DEV-OUTCOME and `note`, and record that `note` carries the forum's reason because no source gives the reason a field of its own.
4. Record that the override is the open deviation record and that the baseline declares no override entity, no second path and no new column.
5. Record the consumed row: the DEVIATION package read of rwb-decision at its version in force, with its placeholder operation name.
6. Record the decision-record element of DP-03, written before the review is answered, with the rule ID that fired and the package version.
7. Record the rights of the operation, the naming baseline, the boundary and the rule that no value is a constant of the code.
8. Publish the contract tables of section 12 and the fakes of 12.8.
9. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the additive rule, the shapes, the lists, the scope, the error envelope, the absence of a `v_ace_*` read and of a `recovery_case` write, the drift between a fake and the document, and the absence of a published and of a consumed event.
10. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-S8-E7008-APP, to the other deviation stories that share the two operations, to SCR-08 and to the wave 4 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response or request body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 400 or 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC2 |
| X2 | A field is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X3 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X4 | A consumed row has a field list or an operation name the sources do not give | The row carries the placeholder and the fake is derived from the published document | None | AC3, AC6 |
| X5 | The outcome list or a deviation state is declared as a code enumeration taken from no source | The vocabulary test fails the build: the list is LOV-DEV-OUTCOME and nothing else | None | AC2 |
| X6 | The document declares another service's operation as provided, a `v_ace_*` view, a `recovery_case` row, a timer row or a rule row | The review fails the baseline and the boundary test fails the build | None | AC7 |
| X7 | The document declares an event published by this step, a consumed event, a second topic, a Schedule or a `cleared_at` write | The absence test fails the build | None | AC7 |
| X8 | The rights of the operation are not the ones TSD S8 T6.1 and T-A.1 give the deviation outcome | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the context pack, the FSD and TSD S8 appendices, the API Specification and the published owner contract of rwb-decision only |
| Negotiable | The example values and the internal record shape are settled in the baseline review; the base, the operations, the right, the lists, the topic, the queue and the schema are fixed by the architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks RWB-S8-E7008-APP, the other deviation stories that share the two operations, SCR-08 and the wave 4 harness on Day 1, and the rwb-decision team on the same day |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, nine contract tables, three fakes and eleven contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the override review of rwb-deviation

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the ownership of deviation is S8, of recovery_case and timer is P3, and of every v_ace_* view, decision_log_entry and rule_row is P1 or P7
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 The deviation-outcome operation is declared with its review branch and its errors (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-deviation is published with this change
    When it is validated against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares PATCH /deviations/{deviationId} as API-S8-002 with a DeviationOutcome body in and a Deviation answer of status 200, under the base /api/recovery/deviation/v1 and owned by rwb-deviation
    Then the review branch is declared inside API-S8-002 as the action the request carries, with no second path and no override path of its own
    Then it declares POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations as API-S8-001 with a DeviationRequest body in and a Deviation answer, with the Idempotency-Key header, and names the raise stories of the module as its builders
    Then API-S8-002 declares no Idempotency-Key and a repeat is matched on the deviation reference and the outcome
    Then the answers 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 are declared with one envelope and one message ID per condition
    Then no operation of the screening, the clearance, the breach path or a deviation-list read is declared by this document

  Scenario: AC2 The deviation and outcome elements, their required flags and their lists are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the element section of the baseline
    When it is compared with TSD S8 T3.0, T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.2, and with the API Specification v4
    Then the Deviation element declares the ten columns of DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045: id, caseId, deviationCode, raisedAt, raisedBy, pausedState, handlerUserId, contactStop, clearedAt and outcome
    Then the required flags are id, caseId, deviationCode, raisedAt, raisedBy, pausedState and contactStop, id is read-only, and the other properties are optional
    Then the lists are LOV-DEVIATION X1 to X7, LOV-RAISED-BY SCREENING_AGENT, RULE, OFFICER and CUSTOMER_CONTACT, and LOV-DEV-OUTCOME RETURNED, RE_ROUTED and CASE_ENDED, copied from TSD S8 T3.2 and published unchanged
    Then the DeviationOutcome request declares outcome over LOV-DEV-OUTCOME and the note string of the API Specification v4, and the note is declared as the field that carries the forum's reason
    Then the document declares no property, field ID or enumeration for the reason, no override entity, no override property and no second outcome set, and the reason's name and value format carry the placeholder Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3067; ASM-5202, ASM-5203)
    Then the document declares no property for a contact value, a rule row, an ACE extract, a case state or a cleared_at write

  Scenario: AC3 The package read is declared as consumed and the facts stay with their owners (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed rows of the baseline
    When they are compared with the ownership of the context pack
    Then the package read is declared as consumed from P7 rwb-decision, with the DEVIATION package, its version and its R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-22 over 9 states
    Then the operation name of the row is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3067; ASM-5204) and the row carries the placeholder and a fake
    Then the document declares no v_ace_* path, no v_ace_* property, no recovery_case property, no timer property, no rule_row property and no grant on any rwb_* schema of another owner
    Then the row is one hop with a 2 s budget, a breaker and no retry of its own (DP-11, ADR-020)
    Then the case move is declared on the parent-child workflow edge and not as a REST row

  Scenario: AC4 The rights and the error envelope are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the access section of the baseline
    When it is compared with TSD S8 T-A.1, T-A.2 and T6.1
    Then both operations declare Case record right U with the scope applied
    Then RW-CASEOWN holds CRU and RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-SALEOFF, RW-DEBTSALE and RW-GUARANT hold RU, and they are the twelve identities the legacy permission table's eight roles and its four further holders resolve to
    Then RW-RISK, RW-CONDUCT and RW-COE hold R and need the operation's right U to record a review, and the conflict is recorded (ASM-5207, ASM-5208)
    Then every other role and every PT-* and SY-* identity of TSD S8 T6.1 holds R or U as the matrix gives it
    Then a role without the right is described as refused with MSG-P4-002, and the error envelope carries one message ID per condition

  Scenario: AC5 The decision-record element is declared and written before the review is answered (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision section of the baseline
    When it is compared with the library schema and with TSD S8 T2
    Then one decision record is declared per review with the case reference, the deviation reference and code, the rule ID that fired, the package version in force, the reason, the outcome, the from state and the to state
    Then the record is declared as written through the local library on the shared rwb.decision-record.v1 before the answer leaves the service, and a failed write leaves everything unchanged with MSG-P7-003
    Then the rule IDs that may be recorded are R-DEV-09, R-DEV-10 and R-DEV-22 only, and R-DEV-11 is named as the X3 path's row on INSURANCE_SETTLED
    Then the record carries no rule row, no personal data and no contact value

  Scenario: AC6 The three fakes answer the document and the drift test fails a build (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fakes of the baseline
    When each is compared with the operation or the element it serves
    Then the rwb-decision package fake answers the DEVIATION package at its version with R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-22
    Then the decision-record stub answers a healthy chain and a stopped chain, and the gateway-bff fake answers the merged SCR-08 answer before and after the review
    Then the drift test compares every fake with the document and fails the build on any difference

  Scenario: AC7 The naming baseline and the boundary are fixed and no event is declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the naming and data sections of the baseline
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner, with None where the element is empty
    Then the schema is rwb_deviation, the login is rwb_deviation, the base is /api/recovery/deviation/v1, the topic is rwb.deviation.events.v1 with its retry and .dlt topics, the queue is rwb-deviation in namespace rwb-recovery and the Java package is th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.deviation
    Then the tables named as owned are deviation and the library objects decision_record, idempotency_key and outbox_event, and recovery_case, timer, every v_ace_* view, decision_log_entry and rule_row are named as other owners' and consumed only through their contracts
    Then the document declares no event published by this step, no consumed event, no second topic, no Schedule and no cleared_at property
    Then the absence test fails a build that adds a published event, a consumed event, a second topic, a Schedule, a v_ace_* read or a case write (ASM-5205, ASM-5206)
```

These seven criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only. They restate no business outcome owned by RWB-S8-E7008-APP and copy no criterion of the legacy story, whose two criteria stay with the app story word for word. The review records an outcome and a reason: no case closes, no clock resumes and no event is declared here (ASM-5202, ASM-5205, ASM-5206).

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of this document, not of a case:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The operation, the elements, the reason, the consumed row, the decision element and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, the other deviation stories that share the two operations, SCR-08, the wave 4 harness and the owners of rwb-decision, rwb-case and rwb-access accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | The reason field is confirmed | The business lead replaces the placeholder inside major version 1 | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example an optional reason code | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or an outcome becomes a set the list does not hold | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | The absence tests of AC1, AC3 and AC7 fail: an override entity, a second path, a `v_ace_*` view, a `recovery_case` property, a `cleared_at` property, a published or consumed event, a second topic or a Schedule | In review |

The state machine the document describes is the app story's: `DEV_WITH_OWNER` is the state the review reads, `DEV_RESOLVED` and `DEV_REROUTE` are the states R-DEV-09, R-DEV-10 and R-DEV-22 give, `CASE_ENDED` follows `INSURANCE_SETTLED` on R-DEV-11 and belongs to the X3 path, and R-DEV-18 resumes the clock on clearance. This baseline fixes the vocabulary and the answer shape and moves no deviation.

The field-level types, lengths and required flags of the declared elements are those of the API Specification v4 and TSD S8 T3.1; this story fixes the element names, the required flags of AC2 and the optionality rule of BR11. **No new table, no new column and no migration** is declared by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-deviation (S8); base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PATCH | `/deviations/{deviationId}` (API-S8-002) | `DeviationOutcome` in, `Deviation` of status 200 out, carrying the recorded outcome, the state and the decision-record reference of the review | Case record, right U, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/deviations` (API-S8-001) | `DeviationRequest` in, `Deviation` out, carrying the code, the raise source and the contact stop; declared here and built by the raise stories of the module | Case record, right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |

API-S8-002 answers 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 for a deviation that is not on the case, 409 for a deviation that is not open at `DEV_WITH_OWNER`, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for a missing or unlisted outcome, and 503, each with the error envelope and one message ID of section 14. The paths, the operation IDs, the element names, the rights and the error codes are published in TSD S8 T-A.1 and T-A.2 and the API Specification v4; the review branch, the meaning of `note` and the fact that no deviation-list read is published carry the placeholder (GAP-3067; ASM-5202, ASM-5203, ASM-5206). The outcome branch of the same operation, the screening and the breach path belong to other stories of the module and none of them is declared here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| The rule-package read in force (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3067; ASM-5204)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The DEVIATION package at its version, with R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-22 over 9 states, read once per review; faked |

The row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). It is a contract dependency of class C that the plan's C row does not carry, and the S8 row of the connection matrix carries no P7 edge although the default ruling gives the rule package registry to rwb-decision; the absence is recorded (GAP-3067; ASM-5204).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service owns the topic `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and its event set carries EV-06 `DeviationRaised` (`caseId`, `deviationCode`, `raisedBy`, consumed by Timers and Communications for the contact stop) and EV-07 `DeviationCleared` (`caseId`, `deviationCode`, `outcome`, consumed by Timers and Communications), both belonging to the raise and clearance steps of the stage (Event and Messaging Design v4; TSD S8 T5.3). A review sets the outcome and the state the rule gives, lifts no stop and closes no case, so this baseline declares no event, no producer group and no outbox row, and the absence test of AC7 fails a build that adds one. The outbox that relays the events is the platform library object of DP-09, which the pattern set for this key does not carry (ASM-5206).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The service listens to rwb-case, rwb-source-data and rwb-agent events on the connection matrix's columns P3, P1 and P10 (context pack connection matrix, row S8), and none of them belongs to the review: the trigger is the officer's confirmation on SCR-08, and the FSD declares no background event for the feature (FSD S8 A2.17.4.4). This baseline therefore declares no consumer group, no subscription, no inbox of its own and no Kafka call from this step, and the absence test of AC7 fails a build that adds one.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DeviationWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per deviation, can start at any time on a case, continues-as-new with the case stage | `rwb-deviation` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | The stage that hosts the review step; its signals and its outcome for the parent are declared, not built |
| `recordDeviationReview` | Activity, the one review step of the stage | `rwb-deviation` | The deviation reference, the outcome, the reason and the package version in; the record reference, the state and the outcome out |
| the stage outcome for the parent | Parent-child workflow edge to `CaseWorkflow` | `rwb-case` | The deviation state and the outcome as the stage result; no REST row is declared for the case move |

No child workflow for the case and none for the money exists in this service, and the service owns one workflow and no job in the context pack's ownership rows. The activity name is a target design choice, and the step runs from the officer's confirmation. No activity is registered by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The review is an officer-driven step; this baseline declares no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table. The service's job list is empty in the context pack's ownership rows, and the escalation timer of R-DEV-20, the clearance and the screening run are other stories'.

| deviation | S8 (`rwb_deviation`) | The deviation X1 to X7 of a case, its code, its raise facts, its handler, its stop, its state and its outcome; the table the answer element is drawn from |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_deviation` | The local hash-linked decision record of the review (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_deviation` | The key of the raise operation and the answer it holds; the review declares none |
| outbox_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_deviation` | The library object present in the schema; this step declares no row in it (§12.3) |

`recovery_case` and `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), every `v_ace_*` view (P1), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6) and `payment` (P8) are not owned by this baseline; it names them only as answers, rule versions or another story's data, and no foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

##### 13. Solution plan

**The CON declares shapes and moves nothing.** It writes no code, no migration and no table, and changes no case, no deviation and no rule package. What it publishes is one OpenAPI 3.1 document, nine contract tables and three fakes.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is declared as the element of the decision record written before the review is answered. DP-13 moves the base of the legacy paths and gives the deviation-outcome operation its home. DP-19 sits behind SCR-08, whose screen model is the edge contract's. DP-04, DP-05, DP-07, DP-08 and DP-09 are not in the pattern set: the package is declared as a consumed row rather than an embedded kit, ACE data is declared as a prohibition, the lists are published as values of TSD S8 T3.2 and not as a reference-data contract, the access guard is a template capability, and the outbox is an absent library row rather than an event of this step (GAP-3067; ASM-5204, ASM-5206).

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds two H rows, `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` for DP-03 and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` for DP-19, which the plan carries; it leaves out the outbox and inbox library `RWB-PLT-TE006-CON` that the topic needs, and the Drools kit rows `RWB-PLT-E1072-CON` and `RWB-P7-E1073-CON` that a rule evaluation would add. The package row is a C dependency in fact and not in the metadata row.

**Deliverables and build steps**

1. Write the review branch of API-S8-002 and validate the additive rule of AC1 in the pipeline.
2. Write the `Deviation` element with its ten properties and seven required flags, the `DeviationRequest` element and the lists of AC2.
3. Record the `DeviationOutcome` element with `outcome` and `note`, and the statement that `note` carries the reason with its placeholder.
4. Record the package row of AC3 with its owner, its budget and its placeholder, and the parent-child edge of the case move.
5. Record the rights and the error envelope of AC4, with the primary role's R as a recorded conflict.
6. Record the decision-record element of AC5 and validate it against the library schema.
7. Publish the three fakes of AC6 and the drift test.
8. Record the naming baseline and the boundary of AC7, then tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off.

The deliverables are `openapi/rwb-deviation-v1.yaml`, the three elements, the contract README rows for the consumed row and its placeholder, and the three fakes of 12.8.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI document validates in the pipeline, the eleven contract tests pass, the fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, and the app story, the other deviation stories, SCR-08 and the wave 4 harness have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-S8-001 | The contract describes the raised state from which the review is taken, raised by the raise story of the module and not by this operation | {deviation} was raised. The case is with {handler}. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request is absent or invalid, the outcome among them, or a body fails schema validation | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the case record right U the operation declares | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the review is answered | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The four IDs are contract elements and the text is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new one is added.

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves SCR-08 Deviation queue in its list state, before and after the review, through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The route calls rwb-deviation for the deviations, their handlers and the recorded outcome, and rwb-case for the case and its route state; this baseline fixes the rwb-deviation answers only, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The legacy screen table gives SCR-08 "Loading; list" and SCR-06 Raise deviation "Form; saved": the raise form is the raise stories'.

No source publishes a deviation-list read, so the list the screen shows has no operation and carries the placeholder (GAP-3067; ASM-5206); and neither screen is described as a review screen, so the place of the review action on SCR-08 is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3067; ASM-5202). The refusal, not-open, bad-outcome and not-recorded states read the messages of section 14 on the same route.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the review conditions, the deviation codes, the outcome list, the states, the right and the package version stay rule rows and reference data, never a schema default, an enumeration member taken from no source or a constant of the code.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, dates, a list value, a rule ID, a package version and a reason text only, and every example is synthetic.
- The case stays with rwb-case: the document declares no `recovery_case` property, no case row write and no case state write.
- The rule rows stay with rwb-decision: the document declares no rule row, no threshold and no rule ID set.
- The review records and does not clear: no `cleared_at` property, no contact-stop write, no timer property and no clock resume is declared (BR7).
- One base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The document lists only operations owned by rwb-deviation; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided (DP-01, DP-11).
- No retired element is reintroduced: the absence tests fail a build that declares a published event of this step, a consumed event, a second topic, a Schedule, a Quartz row or an override entity.
- The error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule, the decision-record library and the outbox library come from the platform; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the override-review slice of RWB-E7-008 in rwb-deviation. The two legacy criteria are kept word for word with their origin tag; the step reads the open deviations of a case at `DEV_WITH_OWNER`, records the forum's outcome and its reason on `deviation` (DF-CAS-045), moves the deviation on R-DEV-09, R-DEV-10 and R-DEV-22, writes the local decision record with the rule ID and the package version in force before any change (DP-03), and serves the review branch of the published `PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}` (API-S8-002) on base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13), reached from SCR-08 Deviation queue through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). No source defines the override as a record of S8 or gives the reason a field, no rule row names the review forum, no requirement row traces to FEAT-DVF-08, the plan's C row is empty while the package read is consumed, the S8 row of the connection matrix carries no P7 edge, and the primary role holds R on the case record while the review needs U (GAP-3066; ASM-5202, ASM-5203, ASM-5204, ASM-5205, ASM-5207, ASM-5210). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **risk and model risk officer**, I want **to put overrides in front of the review forum, with the reason and the outcome of each**, so that **every deviation has a handler and a clock**.

This is the override-review slice of legacy RWB-E7-008. It owns:

- the two legacy criteria this story owns (AC1, AC2), copied verbatim with their origin tag, and the operation, the messages and the screen they depend on;
- one step of `DeviationWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-deviation` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, the deviation stage that can start at any time on a case and pauses the stage clock (context pack, Temporal and Drools slide 13);
- the review of the open deviations of a case: each one is presented with its code, its raise facts, its paused state and its named handler, and the forum records its outcome and its reason on the deviation row (FSD S8 A2.17.2; TSD S8 T3.1);
- the evaluation of the DEVIATION rows that fire on the recorded outcome — R-DEV-09, R-DEV-10 and R-DEV-22 — over the package version in force (TSD S8 T4; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4);
- the local decision record of the review, written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON with the rule ID, the package version, the reason and the outcome, **before any change** (DP-03);
- the review branch of the published `PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}` (API-S8-002) on base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1`, case-record right U, scope applied (DP-13);
- the review panel of SCR-08 Deviation queue behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

It does not own: the published shapes of the two operations, the `Deviation` and `DeviationOutcome` elements, the review properties, the consumed row, the error set, the rights of the document and the fakes, which are RWB-S8-E7008-CON; raising a deviation (API-S8-001, RWB-E1-062, FEAT-DVH-01); pausing the stage clock and keeping the prescription clock running (FEAT-DVH-02, FEAT-DVH-03, R-DEV-01); routing a deviation to its named owner (FEAT-DVH-04, R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06, R-DEV-21); clearing a deviation, lifting the contact stop, writing `cleared_at` and resuming the timers (FEAT-DVH-06, R-DEV-18); reopening the route decision (R-DEV-19); the X1 to X7 journeys and the breach path (RWB-S8-E7001-APP to RWB-S8-E7007-APP, RWB-S8-E7010-APP); the case of record, its states and the parent workflow, which are rwb-case (P3); the DEVIATION package and its 22 rules, which are rwb-decision (P7); and the deployment of this build, which is the operations story of this legacy key.

##### 2. Business rationale

The feature objective, the problem and the metric are unchanged from the legacy story and the module FSD: overrides go in front of the review forum with the reason and the outcome of each, because complaints, hardship, death, fraud, bankruptcy, lost contact and collateral events are handled case by case with no clock (FSD S8 A1.3, A2.17.1), and the deviations closed within the service level are measured on the decision log and the Workbench records against a target set with DL22, reviewed monthly (FSD S8 A2.17.1). What D-RCV-60 changes is who owns the record, the rule, the decision and the screen.

- **The reviewed record is this service's.** `deviation` is S8's only table in `rwb_deviation` (context pack ownership rows; TSD S8 T3.1), and the DEVIATION route set of 22 rules over 9 states is the deviation stage's (TSD S8 T4). No source defines a separate override entity, and the FSD field catalog of A2.17.3.2 lists the deviation fields only, so the override the forum reviews is the open deviation of the case (GAP-3066; ASM-5202).
- **The outcome is a published list.** LOV-DEV-OUTCOME holds `RETURNED`, `RE_ROUTED` and `CASE_ENDED` (TSD S8 T3.2) and the request element carries it (API Specification v4 `DeviationOutcome`); the legacy "outcome of each" is recorded on DF-CAS-045 and never invented (ASM-5203).
- **The reason has no field of its own.** `DeviationOutcome` carries `outcome` and `note`, the FSD names no reason field, and no column of `deviation` carries one, so the forum's reason rides `note` and the local decision record (GAP-3066; ASM-5203).
- **Three rows fire, not four.** On `DEVIATION_RESOLVED` the set gives R-DEV-09 (`X1`, `X7`), R-DEV-10 (`X2`) and R-DEV-22 (an outcome that names no next step); R-DEV-11 reaches `CASE_ENDED` on `INSURANCE_SETTLED` and belongs to the X3 path (ASM-5205).
- **The review records an outcome, it does not clear.** `cleared_at`, the contact stop and the resumption of the stage clock are FEAT-DVH-06, whose outcome recording is the clearance step of the stage; this story ends at the recorded outcome and the rule-driven state move (GAP-3066; ASM-5205).
- **The package is read, not embedded.** The DEVIATION set is governed in rwb-decision, DP-04 is not in this key's pattern set, and the S8 row of the connection matrix carries no P7 edge, so the version in force arrives on a read with a fake and the kit rows are recorded as absent (GAP-3066; ASM-5204).
- **The case stays with rwb-case.** The deviation row holds `case_id` and the paused state; the stage outcome returns to the parent `CaseWorkflow`, which owns the case, the clock and the route (ASM-5205, ASM-5206).
- **The forum's right is short.** FSD S8 A2.17.3.3 names the Risk and model risk officer as primary and TSD S8 T6.1 gives RW-RISK R on the case record, while both operations declare right U; the right is taken over the operation matrix and the conflict is recorded rather than resolved by a new grant (GAP-3066; ASM-5207).
- **No requirement row names the feature.** TSD S8 T8 maps every REQ-DVH and REQ-S8 row to FEAT-DVH-01, FEAT-DVF-01 or a placeholder, and none names FEAT-DVF-08, so the story cites no requirement ID until the E7 BRD and the PRD publish one (GAP-3066; ASM-5210).

No business value moves: the outcome values, the deviation states, the rule IDs, the package version and the right are values of reference data and of the rule package, read with their version and never written in code.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S8-E7008-CON is published: the review branch of `PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}` with the `DeviationOutcome` request and the `Deviation` answer, the review properties, the consumed row, the rights, the error set and the fakes are baselined and handed to this story.
- The rwb-decision rule-package read is published with its fake and answers the DEVIATION package at its version in force, with R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-22 over its 9 states. The operation name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3066; ASM-5204).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: the local decision-record library writes in the caller's transaction, and a failed write stops the action with MSG-P7-003, so nothing changes (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-08 Deviation queue reaches this service through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, and no screen calls a service directly (DP-19).
- `deviation` exists in schema `rwb_deviation` from the DB story of this service, with the columns of DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 and the standard record columns of TSD S8 T3.0; this story adds no table, no column and no migration, and writes `outcome`, `state` and the standard columns only.
- The case is in place: at least one deviation of the case is open at `DEV_WITH_OWNER` with its handler set by the routing step (FEAT-DVH-04, R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06), and the stage clock is paused (R-DEV-01). This story reads that state and moves it no further than the outcome rows allow.
- The DEVIATION package is in force at its version; the rule rows, the outcome list and the states are governed in rwb-decision and are not a build item of this story.
- The service runs as its own login on schema `rwb_deviation`; it holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `rwb_case` or on an ACE view is refused by the database and fails the boundary test.
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-S8-E7008-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. A deviation of the case is open at `DEV_WITH_OWNER` with the handler the routing step named (FEAT-DVH-04); the deviation stage runs as the child of `CaseWorkflow` on `rwb-deviation` and can start at any time on a case (context pack, Temporal and Drools slide 13).
2. The risk and model risk officer opens SCR-08 Deviation queue through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, and reads the open deviations of the case with their codes, their raise facts, their handlers and their ages (DP-19).
3. The officer selects one deviation, records the forum's outcome and its reason, and confirms. The screen sends the deviation reference, the outcome, the reason and the member's identity (FSD S8 A2.17.2); the operation declares no `Idempotency-Key` header (TSD S8 T-A.2).
4. `DeviationReviewController` serves the review branch of `PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}` (API-S8-002) on base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1`, declares case-record right U with the scope applied and validates the request (DP-13).
5. The service reads the deviation row in `rwb_deviation`: its reference, its case, its code, its from state, its paused state, its handler and its current outcome. A deviation that is not open at `DEV_WITH_OWNER` is refused with 409 and nothing is written.
6. The service reads the DEVIATION package in force on the rwb-decision contract and holds its version for the record; the package read is one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker (ASM-5204).
7. `DeviationOutcomeEvaluator` evaluates the `DEVIATION_RESOLVED` rows of the package over the deviation: `X1` and `X7` fire R-DEV-09 and give `DEV_RESOLVED`; `X2` fires R-DEV-10 and gives `DEV_REROUTE`; any outcome that names no next step fires R-DEV-22 and gives `DEV_REROUTE`. The condition is a rule of the package in force and never a branch of the code (ASM-5205).
8. `DeviationDecisionRecordWriter` writes one decision record through the local decision-record library, **before any change**: the case reference, the deviation reference and code, the rule ID that fired, the package version in force, the reason, the outcome, the from state, the to state and the decided-at time. A failed write stops the step with nothing changed (DP-03; AC1, AC2).
9. `RecordAndApply` writes in one transaction: `outcome` (DF-CAS-045), the deviation `state` the rule gives and the standard columns `updated_at` and `updated_by`. `cleared_at`, `contact_stop` and the timers are not touched (ASM-5205).
10. The answer returns the deviation element with its outcome, its state and the decision-record reference; the officer sees the recorded outcome on SCR-08, read back from this service (DP-19).
11. The stage outcome returns to the parent `CaseWorkflow`: the deviation state and the outcome. The parent owns the clock and the route, so the resume of R-DEV-18 and the reopen of R-DEV-19 are its steps and the clearance stories', not this one (ASM-5205, ASM-5206).
12. A repeat of the same review answers the record that exists and writes no second one, matched on the deviation reference and the outcome. No phone number, address, identity number or other personal value is copied into the record, the answer or a log.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The local decision record cannot be written | Nothing changes: no outcome is recorded and the deviation stays where it was, with no record | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, TC-E7-008-02, TC-E7-008-04 |
| X2 | The role does not hold the case record right U | 403 before any read or write; nothing changes and no record is written | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E7-008-03 |
| X3 | The deviation is not open at `DEV_WITH_OWNER`, is not on that case, or the outcome is absent | 409 or 422 with nothing written; an outcome is never recorded on a deviation the forum cannot see | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, X7 |
| X4 | The outcome is not one of LOV-DEV-OUTCOME | 422 with nothing written; the value stays the list's and never the code's | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X5 | The rwb-decision package read does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The step retries on the workflow's own schedule; nothing is written; the caller sees 503 with the platform error envelope | None | AC1, X2 |
| X6 | The outcome is `CASE_ENDED` | Recorded on the deviation, and no case is closed here: R-DEV-11 closes on `INSURANCE_SETTLED` and belongs to the X3 path | None | AC1, X8 |
| X7 | A repeated request for the same deviation and outcome | One record and one answer; the repeat answers the record that exists and is counted | None | AC1 |
| X8 | A component, a statement or a test reaches a `v_ace_*` view, a `recovery_case` row or another service's schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | Section 17, BR5, BR8 |

X1 and X2 are the legacy exception paths carried onto the slice (the legacy set also carries MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-S8-001, kept in section 14), X3 to X7 are the paths the target call types and the interactive trigger add, and X8 is the ACE and schema boundary.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-S8-E7008-CON, the rwb-decision package fake and the decision-record stub, on its own schema, and needs no live P3 or P7 |
| Negotiable | The activity name, the record's internal shape and the front-end component are this story's and the baseline's choice; the operation, the right, the outcome list, the messages, the screen and the two criteria are fixed |
| Valuable | Every reviewed override carries the forum's outcome and its reason with the rule ID and the package version that were in force, instead of an outcome known only to the forum |
| Estimable | One workflow step, one evaluator, one record write, one operation branch, one client and one read-only screen state |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on a synthetic open deviation through the contract fakes, plus the access, not-open, bad-outcome and failed-record cases |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Review an override

  Background:
    Given case "RW-2026-000502" has the deviation "X3" open at state "DEV_WITH_OWNER" with the specialist as its handler and paused state "WITH_FCR_OFFICER"
    Given the DEVIATION rule package is in force at its version and carries R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-22
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 Review an override (legacy RWB-E7-008 AC1)
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns the rule version in force
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When the user acts on the screen
    Then puts overrides in front of the review forum, with the reason and the outcome of each
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E7-008 AC2)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The two criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E7-008 word for word, with their origin tag added and nothing else changed: the repeated `Then`, the wording of `the user acts on the screen`, `the action is taken` and `the decision log cannot be written` all stand. The cross-service part of AC1 is the rule version, so AC1 carries one `Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns the rule version in force` line and that is the only addition. AC2 has no cross-service part and is copied with nothing added. The same outcome is the one FSD S8 AC-S8-017-01 records as written one epic ahead — "The data and rules it needs are in place / The user acts / The result is recorded with its rule version" — so the legacy line and the module line agree. The `decision log` of the legacy text is the local decision record of DP-03 in `rwb_deviation`, with the central `decision_log_entry` ledger of rwb-decision behind it.

##### 8. Business rules

The review is the step that emits `DEVIATION_RESOLVED`; the rows below are the three of the 22-row DEVIATION set that fire on it, copied character for character, plus the row that reaches `CASE_ENDED` and is **not** fired here (Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, Rules sheet; TSD S8 T4).

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-DEV-09 | Deviations | X1 to X7 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | DEVIATION_RESOLVED | deviation_code in (X1,X7) | Record the outcome; the same decision resumes | DEV_RESOLVED | Case owner | Workbench | None |
| R-DEV-10 | Deviations | X1 to X7 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | DEVIATION_RESOLVED | deviation_code = X2 | Route to the restructure assessment | DEV_REROUTE | Restructuring officer | Workbench | None |
| R-DEV-22 | Deviations | X1 to X7 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | DEVIATION_RESOLVED | otherwise, the outcome does not name a next step | Return the case to the route decision and record that the outcome was not mapped | DEV_REROUTE | Case owner | Workbench | 2 working days |
| R-DEV-11 | Deviations | X1 to X7 | DEV_WITH_OWNER | INSURANCE_SETTLED | deviation_code = X3 and insurance clears the balance | Close the case | CASE_ENDED | Workbench | ALS, Workbench | None |

Their owner and systems columns name a business role and systems, not services: "Workbench" is the case of rwb-case and this service's own record read through the composite route, "ALS" is reached through rwb-integration, and "Case owner", "Restructuring officer" and "Specialist" are read as the roles the permission table gives right U on the case record (GAP-3066; ASM-5207, ASM-5208). No rule row of the set names the review forum, so the forum's act is the outcome the officer records and the row that fires on it (ASM-5202).

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The review is a step of the deviation stage: it runs in `DeviationWorkflow` on `rwb-deviation`, writes `outcome`, `state` and the standard columns of `deviation` and nothing else | TSD S8 T3.0, T3.1, T4; context pack ownership rows (table and workflow); FSD S8 A2.17.2 |
| BR2 | The result is recorded before the change, with the rule ID, the package version in force, the reason and the outcome; a failed write changes nothing and the caller sees MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; TSD S8 T2 ("writes the decision log entry before any change"); legacy AC1 and AC2 |
| BR3 | Only a deviation open at `DEV_WITH_OWNER` of that case is reviewed, and only one of LOV-DEV-OUTCOME is recorded; any other state, case or value is refused | TSD S8 T4; TSD S8 T3.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-09, R-DEV-10 and R-DEV-22 |
| BR4 | The state move is the rule's: `X1` and `X7` to `DEV_RESOLVED`, `X2` and an unmapped outcome to `DEV_REROUTE`; `CASE_ENDED` on the row is not a close of the case | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; ASM-5205 |
| BR5 | No cross-schema join and no foreign key leaves `rwb_deviation`; `case_id` is an identifier of another service's fact | DP-01; TSD S8 T3.3 |
| BR6 | The package version in force is read from rwb-decision and recorded with the review; a row that fires is recorded by its ID and no rule ID is invented for the forum | ASM-5204, ASM-5205; TSD S8 T4 |
| BR7 | Every value a business person may change is a rule row or reference data read with its version: the deviation codes, the outcome list, the states, the right and the package version | FSD S8 BR-S8-017; legacy Guardrails |
| BR8 | No personal data in `rwb_deviation`, the decision record, a log or a workflow input; the member's identity is a key and not a name | Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17); TSD S8 T6.2 |
| BR9 | The clearance stays outside: `cleared_at`, `contact_stop`, the timers and the clock resume of R-DEV-18 are FEAT-DVH-06's and no column of them is written here | FSD S8 A2.6; ASM-5205 |
| BR10 | The same review twice writes one record and sends one answer; the operation declares no `Idempotency-Key`, so the repeat is matched on the deviation reference and the outcome | TSD S8 T-A.2; ASM-5203 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From (deviation state, rwb-deviation) | Event | Condition | To | Written by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DEV_WITH_OWNER` | `DEVIATION_RESOLVED` with the outcome recorded | `deviation_code in (X1,X7)` | `DEV_RESOLVED` | rwb-deviation, on R-DEV-09, by this story |
| `DEV_WITH_OWNER` | `DEVIATION_RESOLVED` with the outcome recorded | `deviation_code = X2` | `DEV_REROUTE` | rwb-deviation, on R-DEV-10, by this story |
| `DEV_WITH_OWNER` | `DEVIATION_RESOLVED` with an outcome that names no next step | `deviation_code` is none of the rows above | `DEV_REROUTE` | rwb-deviation, on R-DEV-22, by this story |
| `DEV_WITH_OWNER` | `DEV_RESOLVED` (the answer of the review) | Any | `DEV_RESOLVED`, unchanged by R-DEV-18 | rwb-deviation, on the clearance step (FEAT-DVH-06, R-DEV-18) |
| `DEV_REROUTE` | `ROUTE_REOPENED` | Any | `ROUTE_D6` | rwb-deviation, on R-DEV-19, by the route stories |
| `DEV_WITH_OWNER` | `INSURANCE_SETTLED` | `deviation_code = X3` and insurance clears the balance | `CASE_ENDED` | rwb-deviation, on R-DEV-11, by the X3 path |
| Any state but `DEV_WITH_OWNER` | A review request | The deviation is not open at `DEV_WITH_OWNER` | Unchanged | none; 409 (X3) |

| Step execution | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting | A review request for an open deviation | The package in force is read | Evaluating |
| Evaluating | A row of the package fires | The code and the outcome are the row's | Recording |
| Evaluating | No row fires with a mapped outcome | The outcome names no next step | Recording, on R-DEV-22 |
| Recording | The record and the row commit | The transaction commits | Waiting for the next request |
| Recording | Either write fails | X1 | Waiting, nothing changed |

The states `DEV_WITH_OWNER`, `DEV_RESOLVED`, `DEV_REROUTE`, `CASE_ENDED` and `RESUMED` are those of the DEV machine of TSD S8 T4 and the States sheet of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (9 states over 22 rules). This story writes the three states the `DEVIATION_RESOLVED` rows give and none of the others.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Case record R in TSD S8 T6.1: the primary role of FSD S8 A2.17.3.3, reviewing an override through the operation's right U (ASM-5207) |
| RW-CONDUCT, conduct and QA officer | Case record R: an also-uses role of FSD S8 A2.17.3.3, reading the review and needing the operation's U to record one |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Case record R: the second also-uses role of FSD S8 A2.17.3.3 |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-SALEOFF | Case record U: the roles the legacy permission table names with right U |
| RW-DEBTSALE, RW-GUARANT, SY-CASEWF, SY-DATALOAD | Case record U: the four further identities TSD S8 T6.1 gives U, which are the legacy table's "and 4 more" (ASM-5208) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-LEGAL, RW-NPAMGR, RW-WRITEOFF, RW-CREDITAD, RW-AGENCYMG, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE and the other PT-* and SY-* identities | Case record R: read only, in scope, and refused the review |
| rwb-deviation service identity | Reads the package, evaluates the rows, writes the record and the row and serves the operation; it holds no grant on another schema and no `v_ace_*` grant |

The rights are the rows of TSD S8 T6.1 and nothing wider. The right this story needs is U: the legacy permission table gives right U on the case record to the eight roles it names plus four more, and TSD S8 T-A.2 declares right U on API-S8-002. The primary role holds R only, and the matrix row is not widened here. DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set: the capability area and the right are declared per operation and the access guard is a service-template capability, so the check is stated and not built.

| DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036 | timer (P3) | id, case_id, task_id, timer_type, started_at, expires_at and 4 more | Not read as a table and not written: the stage clock is paused by the raise step and resumed by R-DEV-18 |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | rule_row (P7) | id, rule_id, rule_version, route_set, from_state, event_code and 9 more | Not read as a table: the package version arrives on the package read |

| the reason of the forum | the review request | Read as `note` of the request and recorded in the decision record; it has no column in `deviation` (TSD S8 T3.1), no field ID and no value format in any source: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3066; ASM-5203) |

Field IDs are those of TSD S8 T3.1 and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary, and the timer, rule and case rows are the rows the legacy Data table lists, with their owners changed to P3 and P7 by the target. **No new table, no new column and no migration**: the table arrives with the DB story of this service, and `decision_record` and `idempotency_key` are library objects created in `rwb_deviation` by the library's own migration (DP-03). `outbox_event` also sits in the schema as a library object, and this step writes no row to it because it publishes no event (§12.3).

**No personal data.** The rows carry identifiers, codes, dates, list values, a rule ID, a package version and a reason text. The member's identity is a key: no name, e-mail, phone number, address or identity number is read into the record, the answer, a log or a workflow input, and the fixtures are synthetic. `primary_person_key` is P3's and is never copied here.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-deviation (S8); base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the review branch of the deviation-outcome operation, whose shape RWB-S8-E7008-CON declares.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PATCH | `/deviations/{deviationId}` (API-S8-002) | `DeviationOutcome` in with the outcome and the note that carries the reason, `Deviation` out with the recorded outcome, the state and the decision-record reference | Case record, right U, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/deviations` (API-S8-001) | `DeviationRequest` in, `Deviation` out; declared by the same baseline and built by the raise stories of the module, not here | Case record, right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |

The errors are 400, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 for a deviation that is not on the case, 409 for a deviation that is not open at `DEV_WITH_OWNER`, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for a missing or unlisted outcome, and 503 when the library or the package read does not answer. TSD S8 T-A.1 publishes both operations with their requests, answers and the error set 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, so the mutation is published and needs no placeholder. The ownership rows of the context pack give this service two operations and no read of the deviation list, and the legacy SCR-08 "Loading; list" state needs one; the list read is therefore Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3066; ASM-5206) and is reached, until it is published, through the composite route of SCR-08 (§15).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The rule-package read in force (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3066; ASM-5204)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The DEVIATION package at its version, with R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-22 over its 9 states, read once per review; faked |

The row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). It is a contract dependency of class C that the plan does not carry, because this story's C row is None, and the S8 row of the connection matrix carries no P7 edge although the default ruling gives the rule package registry to rwb-decision; the absence is recorded (GAP-3066; ASM-5204).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service publishes on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and its event set carries EV-06 `DeviationRaised` (`caseId`, `deviationCode`, `raisedBy`, consumed by Timers and Communications for the contact stop) and EV-07 `DeviationCleared` (`caseId`, `deviationCode`, `outcome`, consumed by Timers and Communications), and both belong to the raise and clearance steps of the stage (Event and Messaging Design v4; TSD S8 T5.3). A review sets the outcome and the state the rule gives and lifts no stop, so this story declares no event, no producer group and no outbox row, and a build that publishes EV-07 here fails the absence test. The topic carries the retry and `.dlt` topics of the platform (DP-14), and the outbox and inbox library that relays it is the DP-09 dependency the plan does not carry (GAP-3066; ASM-5206).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The service listens to rwb-case events on the connection matrix's column P3 and to P1 and P10 events (context pack connection matrix, row S8: events from P3, REST and events to P1, Temporal and events to P10), and none of them belongs to the review, whose trigger is the officer's confirmation on SCR-08. This story therefore holds no consumer group, no subscription of its own and no inbox row, and a build that adds one fails the absence test. The FSD declares no background event for the feature (FSD S8 A2.17.4.4).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DeviationWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per deviation, can start at any time on a case, continues-as-new with the case stage | `rwb-deviation` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case reference, the deviation reference and the package in force; signals: the review request, the clearance and the routing; outcome for the parent: the deviation state and the outcome |
| `recordDeviationReview` | Activity, the one review step of the stage | `rwb-deviation` | The deviation reference, the outcome, the reason and the package version in; the record reference and the state out, with the record written before the row |

The parent is `CaseWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-case`, which starts this stage as a child and applies the clock and the route; the stage outcome travels on the parent-child edge and never on a REST call (context pack, Temporal and Drools slide 13; ASM-5206). No child workflow for the case and none for the money exists in this service. The activity name is a target design choice fixed by no source document.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The review is an officer-driven step and owns no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row and no shared job table. The service owns no job in the context pack's ownership rows (Jobs: None), and nothing of the pause, the escalation timer of R-DEV-20 or the screening run is built or declared here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| deviation | S8 (`rwb_deviation`) | The deviation X1 to X7 of a case; this story writes its `outcome`, its `state` and the audit columns |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_deviation` | The local hash-linked decision record of the review (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_deviation` | The key of the raise operation, provided by the same baseline; the review declares none (§12.1) |
| outbox_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_deviation` | Present as a library object; this step writes no row to it (§12.3) |

Not owned and never read as a table: `recovery_case` and `timer` (P3), every `v_ace_*` view (P1), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `payment` (P8). No foreign key leaves the schema and `case_id` is an identifier, not a foreign key across schemas (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-decision rule-package fake | The DEVIATION package at its version in force, with R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-22 over 9 states | AC1 |
| Local decision-record library stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and outbox, and a stopped chain | AC2, X1 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-08 answer for the open deviations of `RW-2026-000502`, before and after the review | AC1 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The operation name of the package read carries the placeholder until its owner confirms it (GAP-3066; ASM-5204).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 1 consumed | The review branch of `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/deviations/{deviationId}` and the raise operation of the same base; the package read of rwb-decision; one hop, 2 s. The SCR-08 list read is not published (§12.1) |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | EV-06 and EV-07 belong to the raise and clearance steps; no event of this step (§12.3, §12.4) |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 1 activity | `DeviationWorkflow` and `recordDeviationReview` on `rwb-deviation`; the stage outcome returns to `CaseWorkflow` on `rwb-case`; no Schedule |
