These seven criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only. They copy no criterion of the legacy story, whose AC2 stays with the app story word for word and whose AC1 is RWB-ITG-E6029-ITG's.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The panel is rwb-partner's: the contract declares the fields, the required list and the optionality of `Partner` and declares no other service's table | TSD S9 T3.1; ownership rows; DP-01 |
| BR2 | The decision record is declared as an element written before the row changes, through the local library; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; TSD S9 T2; legacy AC2 |
| BR3 | The two lists are published enumerations copied from TSD S9 T3.2 and read at their version; no value is a constant of a client | BR-S9-001; ASM-5345 |
| BR4 | No case is declared: the contract declares no `recovery_case` property and no case write, and no ACE view is named as a source | DP-01, DP-05 |
| BR5 | The fee schedule, the service levels and the scope are reference data of FEAT-PRM-02; the contract declares no property and no link for them | FSD S9 A2.2; ASM-5341 |
| BR6 | No event is declared: `EV-20` and `EV-21` are the sibling stories', and DP-09 is not in the pattern set | TSD S9 T5.3; ASM-5344 |
| BR7 | A write declares the `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer; no second topic and no second base is declared | TSD S9 T-A.2; DP-13, DP-14 |
| BR8 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: a code, a firm's registered name, a type, a state and a date | Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17); NFR-050 |
| BR9 | One REST base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service; no other service's base or topic is named as this one's | DP-13, DP-14; §R4 |
| BR10 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version | ADR-020 |
| BR11 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-partner; a consumed row is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | DP-01, DP-11 |
| BR12 | The partner gateway scopes a firm's token to its own record; the baseline declares the scope and the edge owns the gateway | Architecture v5 slide 8; ASM-5346 |

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of this document, not of a partner:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The operations, the element, the enumerations, the consumed row, the fakes and the record are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, the two screens, the partner portal and the wave 4 harness accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1 | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or the required list changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | An absence test of AC5 or AC7 fails | In review |

The state machine the document describes is the app story's: `ACTIVE`, `ON_NOTICE`, `SUSPENDED` and `EXITED` are `LOV-PANEL` values written by FEAT-PRM-01 and its siblings (TSD S9 T4 gives the module no case state machine). This baseline fixes the vocabulary and moves no row.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-partner | Owns the OpenAPI document and the contract tables; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version and the correction of the plan rows the baseline consumes, including the absent C row of the list read and the unplaced write operation |
| Consuming teams (the app story, SCR-34, SCR-35, the partner portal and the owners of rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| Platform library owner | Owns the error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule, the decision-record library and the gateway route this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in an element or a fake |

The per-service login behind the security scheme is named "the rwb-partner login (DP-02)" and is not part of this baseline.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Partner element | `id` uuid, `partnerCode` varchar(20), `partnerName` varchar(160), `partnerType` varchar(15), `panelStatus` varchar(12), `contractEnd` date, `score` numeric(5,2), as DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 give them |
| Required list | `partnerCode`, `partnerName`, `partnerType` and `panelStatus`, and `id` in the answer; `contractEnd` and `score` are optional, as the TSD's required column gives them |
| Enumerations | `LOV-PANEL`: ACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED, EXITED. `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE`: AGENCY, LAW_FIRM, VALUER, AUCTION_VENDOR, BROKER, DEBT_BUYER, AMC, RAMC (TSD S9 T3.2) |
| Read filters | `type` and `status` of API-S9-001; the pagination of the platform, and no other parameter |
| Request element | The same seven properties; the element name, the method and the path are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3107; ASM-5340) |
| Decision record | DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 through the local library, written before the row changes (DP-03) |
| Portal user | `partner_user` of S9 with its field list Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3107; ASM-5343); the scope follows NFR-050 |
| Not declared here | `recovery_case` and `timer` (P3), every `v_ace_*` view (P1), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `document` (P5), `partner_instruction`'s instruction fields, a terms column and the later stories' data |

The field-level types of the request element are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the property names, the required list, the enumerations and the additive rule of BR10. **No new table, no new column and no migration** is declared here.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-partner (S9); base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/partners` | Query `type`, `status` in, `Partner[]` out (API-S9-001) | Partner portal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST or PATCH | `/partners` (method and path Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3107; ASM-5340)) | The seven properties in, the `Partner` element of 201 or 200 out | Partner portal, right C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |

The read answers 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002 and 503 as TSD S9 T-A.2 gives API-S9-001; the write adds 404, 409 and 422 with MSG-GEN-001. API-S9-001 is also declared by RWB-S9-E6030-CON as the panel read of FEAT-PRM-02, so the two fragments must stay identical on its shape and this baseline adds the onboarding write; the instruction operations API-S9-002 to API-S9-006 are not declared here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| The reference-data read of `LOV-PANEL` and `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE` at their version (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3107; ASM-5345)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The list code, the value and the version in force that the two enumerations are validated against; faked |

One hop, 2 s, one GET retry with jitter and a breaker (ADR-020). The row is class C in fact while the plan's C row is None, and the absence is recorded (ASM-5345). The decision record is not a call: it is the DP-03 library on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, carried as RWB-PLT-E1027-CON.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service owns `rwb.partner.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, and its event set carries `InstructionIssued` (`EV-20`, `instructionId`, `partnerId`, `type`, `dueOn`), which the instruction story publishes. Onboarding publishes nothing, so this baseline declares no event, no producer group and no outbox row, and the absence test of AC7 fails a build that adds one (ASM-5344).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None of this feature's own. `PartnerResultSubmitted` (`EV-21`, `instructionId`, `result`, `documents`) is consumed from the partner portal by RWB-S9-E6033-APP, and its target name `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` follows §R4 and is published in no catalogue (ASM-5344).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `InstructionWorkflow` | Workflow per instruction, the child of `CaseWorkflow` in the stages that instruct a partner | `rwb-partner` in `rwb-recovery` | The service's only workflow (ownership rows); declared, not built and not registered here |
| None | Activity | `rwb-partner` | Onboarding is a synchronous command; no activity and no child workflow is declared |

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The ownership rows give S9 no job, and no clock is declared: the contract end is a date and the recall it may start is RWB-S9-E7015-APP's under R-UNI-26. This baseline registers no Schedule and creates no Quartz row or shared job table.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| partner | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The firm on the panel, its fields, its required list and the two enumerations |
| partner_user | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The portal user of the firm; shape not published (ASM-5343) |
| decision_record | PLT library, in `rwb_partner` | The local record of the onboarding (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, in `rwb_partner` | The key of the repeat and the answer it holds |
| outbox_event | PLT library, in `rwb_partner` | Present; this feature declares no row in it (§12.3) |

`recovery_case` and `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), every `v_ace_*` view (P1), `document` (P5) and `partner_instruction`'s instruction fields are not owned by this baseline and are named only as other owners' facts. No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Reference-data fake | The four panel states and the eight types at their version; a value outside both; no answer beyond 2 s | AC1, AC3, AC6 |
| Local decision-record stub | A healthy chain and outbox, and a stopped chain | AC5, AC6 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-34 answer, loading and list | AC6 |
| Partner-gateway fake | The firm's own scope, and a token of another firm refused | AC4, AC6 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT; the consumed row keeps its placeholder until its owner confirms it (GAP-3107; ASM-5345).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 1 consumed | `GET /partners` and the onboarding write on `/api/recovery/partner/v1`; the list read; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | `EV-20` and `EV-21` are the sibling stories' |
| Temporal | 1 workflow declared, 0 registered | `InstructionWorkflow` on `rwb-partner` |
| File | None | No file is read, built or delivered here |

##### 13. Solution plan

**The CON declares shapes and moves nothing.** It writes no code, no migration and no table, and changes no partner, no row and no case. What it publishes is one OpenAPI 3.1 document, nine contract tables and four fakes.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is declared as the element written before the row changes; DP-13 moves the base and nothing else; DP-19 sits behind SCR-34 and SCR-35, whose screen model is the edge contract's. DP-07 and DP-09 are not in the pattern set: the lists are declared as a consumed row and the event set as the siblings' (GAP-3107; ASM-5344, ASM-5345).

**Dependencies the tables add and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds two H rows the plan already carries; it leaves out `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON` and `C RWB-P3-E1043-CON` of the list read, and `RWB-PLT-TE006-CON` of the outbox and inbox library. The consumed list row is a C dependency in fact and not in the metadata row.

**Deliverables and build steps**

1. Write the two operations and validate the additive rule of AC1 in the pipeline.
2. Write the `Partner` element, the required list, the lengths and the two enumerations of AC2, with the write's placeholder.
3. Record the consumed list row of AC3 with its owner, its budget and its placeholder.
4. Record the rights and the error envelope of AC4.
5. Record the decision-record element, the `partner_user` shape and its placeholder of AC5.
6. Publish the four fakes of AC6 and the drift test.
7. Record the naming baseline, the tables and the boundary of AC7, then tag the baseline and collect the sign-off.

The deliverables are `openapi/rwb-partner-v1.yaml`, the two elements, the contract README rows for the consumed row and its placeholder, and the fakes of 12.8.

**Done when.** The document validates in the pipeline, the ten contract tests pass, the fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, and the app story, the two screens, the partner portal and the wave 4 harness have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request is absent or invalid, or a body fails schema validation | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the right the operation declares | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record cannot be written before the row changes | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The three IDs are contract elements and the text is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged. The 409 of a duplicate `partner_code` has no message ID in any source and is not bound to one here (GAP-3107).

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation in their loading and list states through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and the same operations to a firm through the partner gateway on FAPI 2.0, scoped to its own record (ASM-5346). This baseline fixes the rwb-partner answers only; the route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the edge stories. The refusal, invalid and not-recorded states read the messages of section 14.

| TC-S9-E6029-CON-04 | AC5, AC6 | Contract | The record element matches the library schema; the four fakes match the document and a drifted fake fails the build |
| TC-S9-E6029-CON-05 | AC7 | Contract | The naming baseline, the tables owned, and the absence of a published event, a second topic and a terms column |

The four legacy cases keep their IDs and order and are carried as the contract half: their Covers column names the criterion that fixes the surface each one exercises, and the business outcome of each is proved by RWB-S9-E6029-APP and, for AC1, by RWB-ITG-E6029-ITG. The five cases `TC-S9-E6029-CON-01` to `-05` are new, and no `-ITG` copy is written here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the states, the types, the required fields and the contract end are enumerations and properties, never a schema default or a branch of a client.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: a code, a firm's registered name, a type, a state and a date, with synthetic examples (s17, NFR-050).
- The case stays with rwb-case and the facts with their owners: no `recovery_case` property, no `v_ace_*` path and no other service's base or topic named as this one's (DP-05, DP-13, DP-14).
- The money and the instruction data stay with rwb-payment and the instruction stories: no invoice, result or proceeds property is declared here.
- The schedule stays declarative: this story registers no Schedule and creates no Quartz row or job table.
- The error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule, the decision-record library and the gateway route come from the platform; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the onboarding slice of RWB-E6-029 in rwb-partner. Legacy AC2 is kept word for word; the command writes one `partner` row in `rwb_partner`, records the decision first (DP-03), serves API-S9-001 on `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13) and answers SCR-34 and SCR-35 through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). AC1 is RWB-ITG-E6029-ITG's. The write has no published operation, `partner_user` has no published field list and no field links a partner to its terms; all three are recorded as gaps and assumptions. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **partner and agency manager (RW-AGENCYMG)**, I want **to take a partner onto the panel with its contract, fee schedule, service levels and scope**, so that **partners are placed, paid and measured by rule**.

This is the onboarding slice of legacy RWB-E6-029 (FSD S9 A2.1, FEAT-PRM-01). It owns:

- AC2 of the key, verbatim with its origin tag, and the two exception paths the FSD publishes for the feature;
- the command behind the panel: VR-S9-001-1, the uniqueness of `partner_code`, the type, panel status and contract end, as one `partner` row within DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 (§11);
- the portal user of the firm in `partner_user`, the third table of S9, where access is requested (ASM-5343);
- the decision record, written before the row changes (DP-03; legacy AC2);
- the panel read API-S9-001 `GET /partners` and the served states of SCR-34 and SCR-35 (DP-13, DP-19);
- the read of `LOV-PANEL` and `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE` with their version, so no value is a constant (ASM-5345).

It does not own: AC1 and its cross-service evidence (RWB-ITG-E6029-ITG); the shape of the write and the read, the `Partner` element, the rights, the error set and the fakes (RWB-S9-E6029-CON); the panel and fee schedule as reference data (RWB-S9-E6030-APP) and the sibling stories of FEAT-PRM-03 to FEAT-PRM-15; the case and its states (rwb-case, P3); documents (P5); access (P4); the partner gateway of the edge; and the deployment of this build.

##### 2. Business rationale

The objective, the problem and the metric are unchanged: the feature takes a partner onto the panel with its contract, fee schedule, service levels and scope (FSD S9 A2.1.1), because "Partners are instructed and paid by email and spreadsheet; allocation is not based on performance" (FSD S9 A1.3), and the measure is "Placements by scorecard | 100 percent | Decision log and Workbench records | Monthly". The requirements served are REQ-S9-001 to REQ-S9-004 and REQ-S9-008 (TSD S9 T8) and the plan carries none (GAP-3106). What D-RCV-60 changes is who owns the panel, where the terms live and who writes the record.

- **The panel is this service's.** `partner`, `partner_instruction` and `partner_user` are the three tables of `rwb_partner`, and no other service writes them (DP-01).
- **The terms are data.** The contract end is the only term the table carries (DF-PRT-006); the fee schedule, the service levels and the scope are the reference data of FEAT-PRM-02 (FSD S9 A2.2) and no field links a partner to their version (ASM-5341).
- **The decision comes first.** A failed record write leaves the panel unchanged with MSG-P7-003, as AC2 asks and AC-EXC-S9-001-02 repeats (DP-03; TSD S9 T2).
- **The write has no published operation.** API-S9-001 is the only panel operation in the inventory (TSD S9 T-A.1), so the story names the missing one rather than inventing it (ASM-5340).
- **The portal user is a firm's.** NFR-050 scopes a partner account to its own cases with multi-factor authentication (TSD S9 T7), so it holds no bank role and no customer data.
- **Contract end is not recall.** R-UNI-26, R-UNI-28 and R-UNI-29 recall open cases on exit, insolvency and conduct (Business Rules and Routing Logic v4); that is RWB-S9-E7015-APP's and RWB-S9-E7016-APP's.
- **Two edges, one service.** Staff reach rwb-partner through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) and firms through the partner gateway on FAPI 2.0 (Architecture v5 slide 8), which no dependency row carries (ASM-5346).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S9-E6029-CON is published: the `Partner` element, the required list, the two enumerations, the rights, the error set, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the fakes, with the write's placeholder (GAP-3106; ASM-5340).
- `partner`, `partner_instruction` and `partner_user` exist in `rwb_partner` from the DB story, with the standard columns of TSD S9 T3.0; this story adds no table, no column and no migration.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: the record is written in the caller's transaction and a failed write stops the command with MSG-P7-003 (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-34 and SCR-35 reach this service through the composite route, one hop (DP-19).
- The reference-data read answers the two lists at their version; its operation name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3106; ASM-5345).
- The access rows of "Partner portal" and its rights are those of TSD S9 T6.1, read through the guard; this story builds no guard.
- FEAT-OCC-13 is a feature dependency of the business epic and no build dependency, and its owner is named by no S9 source (GAP-3106).
- The service runs as its own login on `rwb_partner`, with no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and none on a `v_ace_*` view (DP-01, DP-05).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft baseline; RWB-S9-E6029-CON tags it when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The officer opens SCR-34 and chooses to onboard a partner; the guard checks "Partner portal" with right C before any read (FSD S9 A2.1.2 step 1; DP-19).
2. The service reads `LOV-PANEL` and `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE` at their version and keeps no copy (TSD S9 T3.2; ASM-5345).
3. The officer enters `partner_code`, `partner_name`, `partner_type`, `panel_status`, `contract_end` and, where access is opened, the firm's portal user (FSD S9 A2.1.3.2; TSD S9 T3.1).
4. VR-S9-001-1 validates every required field with MSG-GEN-001; `partner_code` must be unique, and a duplicate answers 409 with no row and no record (TSD S9 T-A.2).
5. `PartnerOnboardingService` builds the outcome with the two list versions in force and the caller's scope (FSD S9 A2.1.2 step 2).
6. `PartnerDecisionRecordWriter` writes one record **before any change**: the partner code, type, panel status, contract end, list versions, outcome and decided-at time; a failed write stops the command (DP-03; legacy AC2).
7. `PartnerRepository` inserts the `partner` row in one transaction with the record and the idempotency row, `score` empty for RWB-S9-E7011-APP (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007).
8. Where access was requested, one `partner_user` row is inserted for the firm, scoped as NFR-050 gives it and holding no bank role (ASM-5343).
9. The command answers the `Partner` element; a repeated `Idempotency-Key` returns the stored answer and writes no second row (TSD S9 T-A.2).
10. SCR-34 and SCR-35 show the partner, its type and panel status from this service, read only, next to the case answers of rwb-case (DP-19).
11. The contract end is a date and not a trigger: nothing is recalled, no case is touched and no timer is set here (§9).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The record cannot be written | Nothing changes: no `partner` row, no `partner_user` row, no answer | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, TC-E6-029-02, TC-E6-029-04 |
| X2 | The role lacks the Partner portal right C | 403 before any read, no record | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E6-029-03 |
| X3 | A required field is empty or invalid | 422 with the field named, no record and no row | MSG-GEN-001 | TC-E6-029-01 |
| X4 | `partner_code` already exists | 409 with no row and no record | None named for the conflict | TC-E6-029-01 |
| X5 | A value is not in either list at its version | 422 with the field named; no value is coerced to a default | MSG-GEN-001 | TC-E6-029-01 |
| X6 | The list read or the record library misses 2 s, or its breaker is open | One retry, then 503 with the platform envelope; nothing written | None | TC-E6-029-01 |
| X7 | The same submission with the same `Idempotency-Key` | One row set, one record, one answer; the repeat is counted | None | TC-E6-029-01 |
| X8 | A statement reaches another schema, a `v_ace_*` view or a case row | The grant refuses it and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | s17, BR6, BR7 |

X1 and X2 are the FSD paths, X3 to X5 the validations of VR-S9-001-1 and the lists, X6 to X8 the call type, the repeat and the boundary.

| Independent | Day 1 against RWB-S9-E6029-CON, the list fake and the record stub, on its own schema |
| Negotiable | The command name, the decision code and the answer mapping are this story's; the fields, lists, messages and columns are fixed |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Onboard a partner and set terms

  Background:
    Given the rwb-partner service runs as its own login on schema rwb_partner
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC2 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E6-029 AC2)
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns the local decision-record chain and its central ledger entry for a healthy write
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The criterion is legacy AC2 word for word with its origin tag and nothing else changed; the added `Given` mocks the decision path, and the legacy `decision log` is the local record of DP-03 in `rwb_partner` with the central ledger behind it. AC1 of the key, "takes a partner onto the panel with its contract, fee schedule, service levels and scope" and "the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version", is owned by RWB-ITG-E6029-ITG; the command behind it is built here (sections 4, 8, 16).

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Message |
|---|---|
| VR-S9-001-1 Required field empty | MSG-GEN-001 Enter {field}. |
| BR-S9-001 No value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version | None |

Both rows are those of FSD S9 A2.1.3.1, copied character for character.

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The panel is this service's: `partner` and `partner_user` are tables of `rwb_partner` and no foreign key leaves the schema | Ownership rows; TSD S9 T3.1, T3.3; DP-01 |
| BR2 | The record is written before the row changes, with the list versions in force; a failed write changes nothing with MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; TSD S9 T2; legacy AC2 |
| BR3 | The panel states and the partner types are reference data read with their version, never a constant or a coercion | BR-S9-001; TSD S9 T3.2; ASM-5345 |
| BR4 | The contract end is a date, not a trigger: no recall, no case write and no timer here | R-UNI-26; RWB-S9-E7015-APP |
| BR5 | The fee schedule, service levels and scope are reference data of FEAT-PRM-02, and no `partner` field links a partner to their version | FSD S9 A2.2; ASM-5341 |
| BR6 | No case and no ACE data is read or written: `recovery_case` is rwb-case's, every `v_ace_*` view is rwb-source-data's | DP-01, DP-05; TSD S9 T4 |
| BR7 | The service holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and none on a `v_ace_*` view; the boundary test fails a build that adds one | DP-01, DP-05; ASM-5346 |
| BR8 | One partner per `partner_code` and one row set per `Idempotency-Key` | TSD S9 T-A.2 |
| BR9 | A portal user is scoped to its own firm's cases with multi-factor authentication and holds no bank role | TSD S9 T7 NFR-050; T6.1 |
| BR10 | No person name, address, contact value or identity number enters a row, the record, a log or an answer | Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17) |

##### 9. State transitions

The partner has a panel state of its own; the case route state is rwb-case's and untouched (BR6). The vocabulary is the published list `LOV-PANEL` (TSD S9 T3.2).

| From (`partner.panel_status`) | Event | Condition | To | Written by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| None, no row | Onboarding | The command validates and the record is written | `ACTIVE` | this story |
| `ACTIVE` | A panel or fee schedule change | A new version in force | unchanged | RWB-S9-E6030-APP |
| `ACTIVE` | A missed target | FEAT-PRM-11 | `ON_NOTICE` | RWB-S9-E7014-APP |
| `ACTIVE`, `ON_NOTICE` | An upheld conduct breach | R-UNI-29 | `SUSPENDED` | RWB-S9-E7016-APP |
| `ACTIVE`, `ON_NOTICE`, `SUSPENDED` | The contract ends or the panel is exited | R-UNI-26 | `EXITED`, with the recall | RWB-S9-E7015-APP |

| From (command) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Idle | The officer submits the partner | Right C and the fields validate | Reading the lists |
| Reading the lists | The lists answer at their version | The values are in them | Recording |
| Recording | The record is written | The write commits | Writing |
| Writing | The rows are inserted | The transaction commits | Answered |
| Recording, Writing | The record or the transaction fails | X1 | Idle, nothing changed |

Field IDs are those of TSD S9 T3.1 and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. **No new table, no new column and no migration**: the two tables arrive with the DB story, and `decision_record` and `idempotency_key` are DP-03 library objects created in `rwb_partner`.

**No personal data.** A partner is a firm: a code, a registered name, a type, a state and a date. The portal user carries the firm's identity and no customer identity; every fixture is synthetic (s17, NFR-050).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-partner (S9); base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the behaviour behind the two operations whose shape RWB-S9-E6029-CON declares.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST or PATCH | `/partners` (method and path Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3106; ASM-5340)) | The seven properties of DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 in, the `Partner` element of 201 or 200 out | Partner portal, right C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |
| GET | `/partners` | `Partner[]` filtered by type and status (API-S9-001) | Partner portal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The read answers 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002 and 503; the write adds 409 for a duplicate code and 422 with MSG-GEN-001. API-S9-001 is also the panel read that RWB-S9-E6030-CON declares for FEAT-PRM-02, so the two baselines must stay identical on its shape and this story adds the onboarding write. API-S9-002 to API-S9-006 belong to sibling stories and are neither built nor declared here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The reference-data read of the two lists at their version (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3106; ASM-5345)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The panel states and partner types in force, with their version, on every validation; faked |

One hop, 2 s, one GET retry with jitter and a breaker (ADR-020). The row is class C in fact while the plan's C row is None (ASM-5345). The record is not a call: it is the DP-03 library on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, carried as RWB-PLT-E1027-CON.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service owns `rwb.partner.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, and its event set carries `InstructionIssued` (`EV-20`, `instructionId`, `partnerId`, `type`, `dueOn`), which the instruction story publishes. Onboarding issues no instruction, so no event, producer group or outbox row is declared and a build that adds one fails the absence test; the outbox is the DP-09 library the pattern set does not carry (ASM-5344).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `PartnerResultSubmitted` (`EV-21`, `instructionId`, `result`, `documents`) is consumed from the partner portal by RWB-S9-E6033-APP, and its target name `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` follows §R4 and is published in no catalogue (ASM-5344). Onboarding waits for no event.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `InstructionWorkflow` | Workflow per instruction, the child of `CaseWorkflow` in the stages that instruct a partner | `rwb-partner` in `rwb-recovery` | The service's only workflow (ownership rows); the instruction stories', not registered here |
| None | Activity | `rwb-partner` | Onboarding is a synchronous command in its own transaction; no activity is added |

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The ownership rows give S9 no job: the contract end is a date and the recall it may start is RWB-S9-E7015-APP's under R-UNI-26.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner`, module `onboarding`; front end `src/modules/recovery/partner/PartnerPanel.tsx`, read only.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the transaction rule the legacy AC2 tests; DP-13 moves the base and no shape; DP-19 is how SCR-34 and SCR-35 reach the service. These three are the whole pattern set and no fourth is added: DP-07, the list read, is a real dependency the plan holds in neither row (GAP-3106; ASM-5345).

**Dependencies the tables add and the plan does not hold.** The list read is class C in fact (DP-07 would add `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON` and `C RWB-P3-E1043-CON`) and the C row is None, so the story builds on its fake. The partner gateway is a second surface and not a row (ASM-5346), and the DP-09 outbox is recorded, not added (ASM-5344). The H row stands.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `PartnerOnboardingController` | Controller | The two operations, the right, the `Idempotency-Key` and the problem mapping |
| `PartnerOnboardingService` | Service | VR-S9-001-1, the code uniqueness, the panel outcome and the list versions |
| `PartnerDecisionRecordWriter` | Library adapter | The record before any change; refuses the command on a failed write |
| `PartnerRepository` | Repository | The `partner` and `partner_user` rows in one transaction with the idempotency row |
| `ReferenceDataClient` | Client | The two lists, one hop, 2 s, breaker, one GET retry |
| `PanelQueryService`, `PartnerPanel` | Service, component | The panel read, and the two fragments with their refusal and not-recorded states |

**Database and migrations.** None: the tables arrive with the DB story and the record and key are library objects (DP-03). No column is added for a fee schedule, a service level, a scope or a list version (ASM-5341).

**Configuration and reference data.** The lists are read with their version (ASM-5345); the capability area and rights are rwb-access rows read through the guard; the 2 s budget and the single hop are ADR-020.

**Build steps**

1. The controller and the two operations, with the right and the `Idempotency-Key` (AC2, X2, X7).
2. `ReferenceDataClient` against its fake, with the outside-the-list and no-answer paths (X5, X6).
3. `PartnerOnboardingService` with VR-S9-001-1 and the 409 (X3, X4).
4. `PartnerDecisionRecordWriter` against the stub, with the failed-write path (AC2, X1).
5. `PartnerRepository` with one transaction, the optional `partner_user` row and the idempotency row (§11).
6. `PanelQueryService` and `PartnerPanel` on both screens through the route fake (§15).
7. The boundary test: nothing outside `rwb_partner`, no `v_ace_*` read, no write to a sibling schema (X8).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.partner.onboarding-v1`; off means the write answers 503 with the flag named and the panel read is unaffected.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, a partner is onboarded on synthetic lists in SIT with one row, one record and one answer, a duplicate and an invalid value write nothing, a forced record failure changes nothing, and SCR-34 answers through the composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is empty or invalid, or a value is not in force (X3, X5) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without right C calls the write (X2) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record cannot be written before the row changes (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The three IDs are those of the legacy message set and of FSD S9 A2.1.3.1, copied unchanged. The 409 of a duplicate code has no message ID in any source (GAP-3106).

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation are served through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls rwb-partner for the panel and rwb-case for the case; this story fixes the rwb-partner answers only, and the route specification belongs to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The partner gateway serves the same operations to a firm on FAPI 2.0, scoped to its own record (ASM-5346).

The legacy states are "Loading; list". This story serves the list with the new partner, its type and panel status, and the loading state of the composite answer; the refusal, invalid and not-recorded states read the messages of section 14. `ON_NOTICE`, `SUSPENDED` and `EXITED` are read only here. SCR-35 shows the partner as a choice and allocates nothing (RWB-S9-E6031-APP).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the states, the types, the required fields and the contract end are reference data or request values.
- No personal data in the rows, the record, a log or an answer: a code, a firm's name, a type, a state and a date, with synthetic fixtures (s17, NFR-050).
- No ACE data: no `v_ace_*` grant and no ACE table read (DP-05, BR7).
- The case stays with rwb-case and the terms with FEAT-PRM-02: no case row, timer, fee schedule, service level, scope or document column (BR4, BR5, BR6).
- The record comes before the row and the command is idempotent (DP-03, BR2, BR8).
- One base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element returns: no Quartz row, no shared job table, the monolith base, no event published here and no `v_ace_*` read.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E6-029 as the wave 4 integration proof that a partner is on the panel with its contract, fee schedule, service levels and scope read back as data through rwb-partner, that the same panel and terms reach the boundary product DP08, that a partner outside the panel cannot be instructed, and that the onboarding carries one decision record with its rule version; the onboarding and the terms are RWB-S9-E6029-APP. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **partner and agency manager**, I want **the onboarding of a partner proved end to end on the real services: the partner and its contract end, fee schedule, service levels and scope read back through rwb-partner as versioned data, the same panel and terms read through DP08 Partner performance, a partner outside the panel refused for a new instruction, and one decision record with the rule version**, so that **no partner is instructed before its terms are in force and no panel the rest of the bank sees differs from the panel the bank holds**.

This story builds the wave 4 integration harness and its evidence, and nothing else. The onboarding, the panel and the terms are built by S9 rwb-partner in RWB-S9-E6029-APP and its CON story; the case is P3's, the decision record and the central ledger are P7's, DP08 Partner performance is P1's product over S9's records, and the right that answers the read is P4's. The harness drives the onboarding through S9's own path, reads the partner and its terms through S9's published read, reads the same panel through DP08, reads the decision log through P7, counts the events and writes a run report per run. It provides no endpoint, no table, no workflow, no activity, no schedule and no screen, and it writes no code in any service.

##### 2. Business rationale

Partners are instructed and paid by email and spreadsheet today, and allocation is not based on performance (FSD S9 A1.3). The failure this story is written against is a firm instructed before it is on the panel, or after its contract has ended: the bank places work with an agency it has not contracted, or keeps placing work with one whose terms have lapsed, and neither the fee nor the service level nor the scope the case was placed under can be said afterwards. REQ-S9-001 puts every partner type on the same six points — selection, contract and fees, targets and incentives, data exchange, performance reviews, notice and exit — and REQ-S9-002 gives each partner type one named owner, so the onboarding is the point where those six are fixed for a firm. R-UNI-26 then makes the exit real: a panel exit or a contract end recalls every open case held by that partner and forces a re-selection, and R-WO-30 places work only with an agency that is on the panel. Read together, the two rules mean the panel status and the contract end are not paperwork: they decide whether an instruction may be issued at all.

The second half of the rationale is the boundary. DP08 Partner performance is a Workbench product over `partner` and `partner_instruction`, refreshed on change, so a panel the bank holds but the product does not carry is a panel nobody else can see — not the review forum, not the reporting that runs off the products, not the screen a head of the partner type opens. A partner onboarded in one place and read differently in another is the same class of failure as a partner instructed off the panel.

The harness is decoupled the way the services are. Every call is one hop on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13); there is no in-process call and no second hop. The partner and the instruction are S9's; the case is P3's; the decision log, the rule rows and the central ledger are P7's; DP08 is P1's product over S9's records. DP-01 forbids reading another service's schema, and ACE-side or boundary data is read only through P1's contract (DP-05). The decision record is written by S9 through the local decision-record library on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) and read back through rwb-decision's contract. On the edge, DP-19 sends partners through the **partner gateway** (FAPI 2.0) that fronts rwb-partner and reserves gateway-bff composite routes for staff screens; this run calls S9's own operation at the service boundary, which is the same operation the partner gateway fronts.

One limit is stated plainly because it shapes the run. The Ownership Map publishes `GET /partners` and `GET /partner/instructions` but no partner create and no panel-change operation, so the harness reads the onboarded partner and its terms through the published read, drives the write through S9's own path inside RWB-S9-E6029-APP, and asserts the step through that read, through DP08 and through the decision log. It never invents a partner endpoint, and where a screen would compose the panel read with the case view, the path is the partner gateway for the partner and the gateway-bff composite route for staff (DP-19).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The published contracts of S9 rwb-partner (the partner read, the instruction placement and the partner instruction read), P1 rwb-source-data (DP08 Partner performance and its freshness), P3 rwb-case (the case), P7 rwb-decision (the decision log) and P4 rwb-access (the session) are in the contract registry, and a stub set is generated from each one.
- S9 owns the panel, the partner users, the instructions, the results, the fees and the scorecards in `rwb_partner` (Arch v5 slide 41, line 2891), so the partner, its terms and its instructions have one named owner before a value is asserted.
- The onboarding and the terms are RWB-S9-E6029-APP and its CON story; until they land, the S9 stub of §12.8 stands in for their effect and the story is reported as a stub pass.
- FEAT-PRM-01 is the S9 feature and FEAT-OCC-13 is its prerequisite (Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3, line 134); the fixture presupposes the block and contact work FEAT-OCC-13 delivers, so this story never asserts it.
- The lists of values are LOV-PARTNER-TYPE, LOV-PANEL, LOV-INSTRUCTION and LOV-INSTR-STATUS, with the values in TSD S9 lines 93 to 98.
- The rules in force for this journey are R-WO-30, R-WO-31, R-UNI-25, R-UNI-26, R-UNI-27, R-UNI-29 and R-UNI-45.
- The synthetic partner, its contract, the fee schedule version, the service levels, the scope, the business date and the gate: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0459; ASM-0651).
- The synthetic partner, its terms, the second partner and the business date are held in the fixture as data, never written in code.
- No build dependency. Day 1, with the stubs in place from the first run; the one wait is RWB-S9-E6029-APP, which replaces its stub and never blocks the lane.

##### 4. Flow

1. Preflight: the harness pins the contract version of each of the seven operations of §12.2 and the version of the terms fixture, and fails the run where a version is missing (X1).
2. Harness: loads the fixture — partner `PRT-SYN-0029` with its partner_code, partner_type `AGENCY`, panel_status `ACTIVE`, its contract_end, the fee schedule version `FS-SYN-0029-v2`, the service levels by partner type, the scope and business date `2027-04-30`, plus a second partner `PRT-SYN-0029-X` at `SUSPENDED` with an ended contract. On Day 1 the stubs of §12.8 return the same records.
3. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` and asserts the partner with its partner_code, partner_type, panel_status `ACTIVE`, contract_end and latest score, and that no second row is returned for the same partner code (AC2).
4. Harness: asserts the fee schedule version, the service levels and the scope are the versions in force for business date `2027-04-30` and are the values held in the fixture, never constants in the harness, and that the decision record names the same version of the terms (AC2).
5. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP08/records?partnerId={partnerId}` and asserts the same partner_code, the same panel_status and the same contract_end as the owner holds, with its business date, so the boundary view the rest of the bank sees is the panel the bank holds (AC3).
6. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` and asserts exactly one entry for the onboarding, with its rule_id and its rule_version, and no second entry after a re-read (AC2).
7. Harness: places a work item with the partner through `POST /api/recovery/partner/v1/cases/{caseId}/instructions` with one Idempotency-Key, and asserts the answer names the partner and the case (AC4).
8. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions` and asserts one instruction for the partner and the case, with its instruction_type, instructed_at, due_at and status `SENT` (AC4).
9. Harness: replays the same placement with the same Idempotency-Key, asserts the answer is the first answer unchanged, and re-reads the instruction and asserts one instruction and no second `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` (AC4).
10. Harness: attempts a placement naming the suspended partner `PRT-SYN-0029-X`, and asserts 409 with no instruction created and no `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` published; it then reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` before and after and asserts the case did not move (AC4).
11. Harness: resets the fixture to the pre-onboarding snapshot, turns the fault switch on the decision-record hop on, runs the onboarding step through S9's own path, and asserts the answer carries MSG-P7-003 with no partner change and no instruction; the switch is reset before the next run (AC5).
12. Harness: calls `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` as a synthetic caller without Partner portal R, then `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners`, and asserts 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no partner row returned (AC6).
13. Harness: writes one run report per run, keyed by story and partner code, naming the contract version of each hop, whether the hop was a stub or the owner, the partner and its terms version, the business date, the DP08 read, the one decision entry with its rule version, the instruction and both event counts, the workflow run and the gate verdict.

| X4 | A second instruction is created for the same work item | The run fails on AC4 and the report names both instructions, the Idempotency-Key each carried and the instructed_at of each | None | TC-E6-029-01-ITG (ITG AC4) |
| X5 | The onboarding decision record is written twice, written without its rule version, or names a different version of the terms than the fixture pins | The run fails on AC2 and the report names the entries, their rule versions, the version of the terms each names and the missing confirmation | None | TC-E6-029-04-ITG (ITG AC2) |
| X6 | A forced decision-record failure leaves a partner change or an instruction, or answers without MSG-P7-003 | The run fails on AC5 and the report names the partner read before and after, the instruction count and the event count | MSG-P7-003 (expected, and missing) | TC-E6-029-02-ITG (ITG AC5) |
| X7 | A caller without Partner portal R is allowed the partner read, or the read answers a body instead of 403 | The run fails on AC6 and the report names the caller role, the right the session answered, the operation and the answer; a 200 is a failure even when the body is empty | MSG-P4-002 (expected, and missing) | TC-E6-029-03-ITG (ITG AC6) |

The report text is for the wave entry check and is not part of the message standard. The business messages the run touches are in section 14 and are asserted by ID and by their substituted values.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs against the published contracts and the stubs from Day 1; the only wait is RWB-S9-E6029-APP, and its fixture answers until it lands |
| Negotiable | The fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the terms fixture, the fault switch, the report shape and the gate are configuration agreed at the wave entry check, not business values in code |
| Valuable | The partner and its terms are proved to be on the panel and in force as data, the same panel is proved to reach DP08, a firm off the panel is proved to be refused, and the refused and failed paths are proved to change nothing |
| Estimable | One runner, one stub set, one partner fixture with its terms, one second partner off the panel, one placement, two reads of the panel, one probe of the product, one decision probe, one event observer and one report |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its four tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against the stubs and again against RWB-S9-E6029-APP as it lands |

```gherkin
  Scenario: AC3 The same panel and terms reach the boundary product (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the partner is onboarded and DP08 Partner performance is refreshed on change
    When GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP08/records?partnerId={partnerId} is read
    Then the product carries the same partner_code, panel_status and contract_end that the owner holds
    And the product carries its business date

  Scenario: AC4 A partner outside the panel cannot be instructed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given partner "PRT-SYN-0029-X" is at SUSPENDED and its contract has ended
    When a placement is attempted through POST /api/recovery/partner/v1/cases/{caseId}/instructions naming "PRT-SYN-0029-X"
    Then the answer is 409
    And no instruction is read through GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions for that partner
    And no "rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1" is published
    And GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} answers the same status and stage as before

  Scenario: AC5 A forced decision-record failure stops the onboarding with nothing changed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision record cannot be written for the onboarding
    When the onboarding step is run through S9's own path with the fault switch on
    Then the answer carries "MSG-P7-003"
    And the partner is read unchanged through GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners
    And no instruction is created and no "rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1" is published

  Scenario: AC6 A caller without Partner portal R is refused the partner read (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a synthetic caller with role "RW-CASEOWN" whose session answers without the Partner portal right R
    When the caller reads GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners
    Then the answer is 403 with "MSG-P4-002"
    And no partner row is returned
```

Legacy AC1 is the only legacy criterion this story owns, and it is the business outcome the S9 onboarding has to reach: a partner on the panel with its contract, fee schedule, service levels and scope, and the result written to the decision log with the rule version. Legacy AC2 (the decision log cannot be written, so nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003) stays with RWB-S9-E6029-APP as its build criterion, and this story asserts the same failure across the service boundary in AC5, where the partner read, the instruction count and the event count are taken before and after the refused onboarding. The read of the onboarded partner in AC2 is the published path and not a create operation, because the Ownership Map publishes no partner create and no panel change; the write itself is S9's own path, asserted through the read, DP08 and the decision log.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every partner type is managed on the same six points: selection, contract and fees, targets and incentives, data exchange, performance reviews, notice and exit | REQ-S9-001 |
| BR2 | Each partner type has one named owner | REQ-S9-002 |
| BR3 | Work is placed only with an agency that is on the panel, chosen on measured return, and the instruction is sent the same day on the portal | R-WO-30 |
| BR4 | When no agency on the panel has capacity the placement is held and escalated on the timer, so nothing is placed with a firm off the panel | R-WO-31 |
| BR5 | A partner panel exit or a contract end recalls every open case held by that partner and forces a re-selection, inside 5 working days | R-UNI-26 |
| BR6 | When the partner misses the service level on the portal the work is chased once, then recalled and re-selected on the scorecard | R-UNI-25 |
| BR7 | A declared conflict withdraws the instruction and re-selects the next partner; an upheld conduct breach suspends allocation and recalls the affected cases; the re-selection re-issues the instruction and restarts the partner clock | R-UNI-27, R-UNI-29, R-UNI-45 |
| BR8 | No value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version | BR-S9-001, FSD S9 A2.1.3.1 |
| BR9 | The onboarding writes one decision record through the local decision-record library on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the central ledger in rwb-decision confirms it; nothing changes when it cannot be written | DP-03; ADR-022 |
| BR10 | Every hop is one REST call on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget, and no service reads another service's schema or reaches ACE data except through P1's contract | DP-11, DP-13, DP-01, DP-05 |

The harness asserts these rules and changes none of them; the rules themselves are evaluated in RWB-S9-E6029-APP, the panel and the terms are S9's, the case is P3's, and the rule versions and the central ledger are P7's.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To | Owner of the change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ACTIVE | none | the partner is onboarded with its contract, fee schedule, service levels and scope, and the terms are in force on the business date | ACTIVE, in force | S9 rwb-partner, RWB-S9-E6029-APP |
| ACTIVE | PARTNER_PANEL_EXIT | the partner leaves the panel or the contract ends | EXITED, and every open case held by the partner recalled and re-selected | S9 rwb-partner under R-UNI-26, 5 working days; outside the run |
| SUSPENDED | none | a placement naming the suspended partner is attempted | SUSPENDED, unchanged | S9 rwb-partner refuses before any write, under R-WO-30 |
| no instruction | instruction issued on the case | the partner is on the panel and the placement is accepted | SENT | S9 rwb-partner, InstructionWorkflow `issueInstruction`, R-WO-30; `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` |
| SENT | PARTNER_NO_RESPONSE | the partner misses the service level on the portal | RECALLED, then re-selected | S9 rwb-partner under R-UNI-25 and R-UNI-45; outside the run |
| any | none | the onboarding is refused for want of Partner portal R, or stops on a decision-record failure | unchanged | S9 rwb-partner refuses before any write; nothing changes |

`LOV-PANEL` gives the partner the four states ACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED and EXITED, and `LOV-INSTR-STATUS` gives the instruction SENT, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, IN_PROGRESS, DONE and RECALLED (TSD S9 lines 95 and 97); S9 owns both. The harness changes no state: it drives the onboarding and the placement through S9's published operations and reads every state back, and it never sets a state it then asserts. The case is read through P3 before and after each attempt and is asserted unchanged, because an onboarding and a placement are partner decisions, not case transitions; the case status and stage are whatever P3 already held. A partner the bank suspends or whose contract ends is recalled under R-UNI-26, and that recall is asserted as a rule this run respects, not as a state it moves.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-AGENCYMG Partner and agency manager | Primary role of the journey: holds Partner portal CRUDA in the TSD RBAC matrix, owns the panel, the terms and the placement, and is the role the six points of REQ-S9-001 belong to |
| RW-HEADLIT Head of Litigation, RW-HEADNPA Head of NPA, RW-HEADASL Head of Asset Liquidity | Also use the panel, with RA in the matrix; the run records that the read and the onboarding right answer for them where their scope allows |
| RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-GUARANT | Hold Partner portal CRU and place work with a partner where their scope allows; the run asserts C on the placement path |
| RW-CASEOWN | Holds Partner portal R in the matrix (TSD S9 line 136) and holds no onboarding right; because the map publishes no onboarding operation to refuse, the refusal this run proves is the read right R, and the AC6 fixture answers the RW-CASEOWN session without that right so the 403 is real |
| RW-TRIBE, RW-PLATADM, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-BIANAL, RW-CONDUCT, RW-CAPACITY, RW-PRODHEAD | Hold Partner portal R and read the panel; they place nothing and onboard nothing |
| PT-AGENCY and the other partner-side roles | Read and update their own instructions through the partner portal; the run neither drives nor asserts them |
| QA lead | Owns the harness configuration, the fixtures, the terms fixture, the fault switch, the report shape and the pass or fail gate |
| Integration lead | Owns the harness code, the stub set and the swap from a stub to the real service |
| The owning services' identities | S9 holds the partner, the terms and the instruction and runs InstructionWorkflow, P1 holds DP08, P3 holds the case, P7 holds the decision log and the central ledger, and P4 answers the session; they make every change the harness asserts |
| No delegation of authority level applies | The harness takes no business decision; authorisation is answered by rwb-access and the DoA is P4's |

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 | partner | id, partner_code, partner_name, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end, score | Read through the rwb-partner contract and through DP08; written by S9's onboarding, not by the harness |
| DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 | partner_instruction | id, case_id, partner_id, instruction_type, instructed_at, due_at, status, result_code, fee_amount | Read through the rwb-partner contract; the row is written by S9's placement, not by the harness |
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case | case_no, status, stage_code, route_state, primary_person_key | Read through the rwb-case contract, before and after every attempt |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | decision_code, rule_id, rule_version, inputs_ref, model_version | Read through the rwb-decision contract |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | rule_row | rule_id, rule_version, route_set, from_state, event_code | Read through the rwb-decision contract |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8, and the legacy data table of RWB-E6-029 cites the partner, the decision log entry and the rule rows under these IDs. The partner and the instruction are S9's in `rwb_partner`; `partner` carries seven fields and `partner_instruction` nine (LDM lines 20 and 21, TSD S9 lines 63 to 89). The case is P3's in `rwb_case`. The decision log entry and the rule rows are P7's in `rwb_decision`, and the entry's `inputs_ref` is the field the run reads when it asserts that the decision names the version of the terms in force. The legacy data table also cites the timer under DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036; the harness reads no timer, because the partner clock is a workflow timer inside InstructionWorkflow and not a scheduled job (Temporal design slide 25). The harness owns no table and writes no row: the two changes it drives are S9's own published operations of §12.2, each with one Idempotency-Key, and everything else it reads is a contract read.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` | S9 rwb-partner | The onboarded partner with its partner_code, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end and latest score, and no second row for the same code (AC2, AC5, AC6) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/cases/{caseId}/instructions` | S9 rwb-partner | Places one instruction with one Idempotency-Key, and is the refused operation of AC4 (AC1, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions` | S9 rwb-partner | The one instruction with its instruction_type, instructed_at, due_at and status `SENT`, and the absence of one after the refusal (AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP08/records?partnerId={partnerId}` | P1 rwb-source-data | DP08 Partner performance, refreshed on change, as the boundary view of the same panel and terms (AC3) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case status and stage before and after the placement and the refused placement (AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | P7 rwb-decision | Exactly one onboarding entry with its rule_id and rule_version, and no second entry after a re-read (AC1, AC2, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The caller's roles and rights before the partner read (AC6) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13). No operation is invented in this story: each path is the owner's published operation in the Ownership Map, which lists `GET /partners`, `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions`, `GET /partner/instructions`, `GET /data-products/{productCode}/records`, `GET /cases/{caseId}`, `GET /decision-log` and `GET /me/session` under those owners. Two things the map does not publish shape the run. First, there is no partner create and no panel-change operation, so the onboarding write is RWB-S9-E6029-APP's, reached through S9's own path, and the step is asserted through the published read, DP08 and the decision log; the harness never calls an endpoint the map does not carry. Second, the `InstructionRequest` body of the placement is S9's contract shape from RWB-S9-E6029-CON, so the harness pins that version and reads the body from the fixture rather than composing it. For a partner the edge path to the instruction operations is the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) that fronts rwb-partner, and for a staff screen the same values would be composed by a gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); the run itself calls the service boundary the gateway fronts.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it writes its report to the wave record.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use in the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1` | S9 rwb-partner (EV-20) | Counts one publication per accepted placement and proves that a replay and the refused placement add none; the consumer Arch v5 gives it is the partner portal (AC4) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | S9 rwb-partner through the local decision-record library (DP-03) | Proves the onboarding and its rule version were published once and confirmed by the central ledger, and that the forced failure published none (AC2, AC5) |

The harness subscribes to both topics under one consumer group of its own and counts publications; it replays the placement once and asserts the event count is unchanged. The partner portal, which Arch v5 slide 43 row 20 gives as the consumer of `InstructionIssued`, exposes no operation for this story, so its consumer effect is read from the consumer evidence in the run fixture; this story reads no portal state of its own.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness exercises InstructionWorkflow, S9's workflow on the task queue `rwb-partner` in the `rwb-recovery` namespace, through the placement: its SLA timer for the partner type and its `issueInstruction` activity are the ones the run observes in the workflow history (Arch v5 slide 17, line 1247; Temporal design slide 25). It observes CaseWorkflow on `rwb-case` as the parent that holds the case the instruction is placed against, and observes it only: the placement does not signal it and moves no case state. Neither workflow, activity nor Schedule is created, changed or owned by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added, and none needed. The onboarding is a user act and the partner clock is a workflow timer, not a job: the recall at 5 working days and the re-selection at 2 working days are timers inside the workflow (Temporal design slide 25, lines 1744 to 1745), and the partner SLA by type is a timer per partner type. JOB-05 Timer check is retired in favour of durable timers inside the workflows (Arch v5 slide 44, line 2981), so the run has nothing to schedule and starts from its own fixture and business date.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-01): `partner`, `partner_user` and `partner_instruction` are S9's in `rwb_partner`, `recovery_case` is P3's in `rwb_case`, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are P7's in `rwb_decision`, and DP08 is P1's published product over S9's records.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Contract | Stubbed answer in the run |
|---|---|---|
| Stub for rwb-partner (S9), the panel | `GET /partners` | Partner `PRT-SYN-0029` with its partner_code, partner_type `AGENCY`, panel_status `ACTIVE`, contract_end and latest score, one row per code; partner `PRT-SYN-0029-X` at `SUSPENDED` with an ended contract when asked; 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a caller without Partner portal R |
| Stub for rwb-partner (S9), the placement | `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions` | One instruction accepted per Idempotency-Key with its instruction_type, instructed_at and due_at, and a repeat of the key returning the first answer unchanged; 409 for `PRT-SYN-0029-X` with no instruction created |
| Stub for rwb-partner (S9), the instruction read | `GET /partner/instructions` | The one instruction in `SENT`, and no instruction for the refused partner |
| Stub for rwb-source-data (P1), DP08 | `GET /data-products/DP08/records?partnerId={partnerId}` | The partner and its terms as the published product carries them, refreshed on change, with its business date |
| Stub for rwb-case (P3) | `GET /cases/{caseId}` | The case with the same status and stage before and after every attempt |
| Stub for rwb-decision (P7) | `GET /decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | No entry before the onboarding; exactly one entry with its rule_id, its rule_version and the version of the terms in `inputs_ref` after it, and the central ledger confirmation once; unchanged by the forced failure |
| Stub for rwb-access (P4) | `GET /me/session` | Allows RW-AGENCYMG on the panel and the placement; answers the RW-CASEOWN session without Partner portal R for AC6 |
| Partner and terms fixture | The partner, the contract, the terms and the second partner | Partner `PRT-SYN-0029`, its contract_end, fee schedule `FS-SYN-0029-v2`, the service levels by partner type, the scope, business date `2027-04-30`, and `PRT-SYN-0029-X` at `SUSPENDED` with an ended contract, all held as data with the fixture version pinned |

Each stub is generated from the published contract and its version is pinned in the run report, so a contract change shows up as a run failure and not as a silent pass. The harness environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic partner and contract keys, the terms fixture, the business date, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0459; ASM-0651).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 7 consumed, one hop each on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13) |
| Kafka | None published; two consumed, `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`, counted and replayed once |
| Temporal | None added; InstructionWorkflow on `rwb-partner` exercised through the placement, with its SLA timer and its `issueInstruction` activity, and CaseWorkflow on `rwb-case` observed only |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery-w4/partner-onboarding`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H dependencies DP-03 and DP-19 add, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, are platform stories delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays None. DP-13 adds nothing: the panel and instruction paths are rewritten onto each owner's own base and there is no shared base left. DP-19 has two edges in this journey and the run names both: for the **partner** the route is the **partner gateway** in the DMZ under FAPI 2.0, which fronts rwb-partner and is the only path a partner has (Arch v5 slide 20, line 1458, and slide 35, line 2517), and **gateway-bff** composes the **staff** screens only, including the panel a partner and agency manager opens. The one blocking dependency is the I story RWB-S9-E6029-APP, which replaces its stub; until it is live the run uses the stub, and a stub pass is reported as a stub pass.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the six owned criteria in order for one partner and holds the run lock and the fixture reset |
| PanelReadBack | Service | Reads the partner through `GET /partners` and asserts its code, type, panel status, contract end, latest score and single row |
| TermProbe | Service | Asserts the fee schedule version, the service levels and the scope against the pinned terms fixture, the business date and the version the decision record names |
| ProductReadBack | Service | Reads DP08 and asserts the same partner_code, panel_status and contract_end as the owner holds, with its business date |
| InstructionDriver | Service | Places one instruction per Idempotency-Key, reads it back, replays the key, and attempts the refused placement naming the suspended partner |
| DecisionProbe | Service | Reads the one onboarding entry and its rule version, reads the published decision record, and holds the fault switch |
| EventProbe | Service | Subscribes to `rwb.partner.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`, counts publications and replays the placement once |
| AccessProbe | Service | Answers the session for the allowed caller and for the caller without Partner portal R |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes one report per run, keyed by story and partner code, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the stubs from Day 1 and the real services as RWB-S9-E6029-APP lands, on the synthetic partner `PRT-SYN-0029` with fee schedule `FS-SYN-0029-v2`, the second partner `PRT-SYN-0029-X` at `SUSPENDED` with an ended contract, and business date `2027-04-30`. The harness seeds nothing by hand and never writes a schema row. The environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic partner and contract keys, the terms fixture, the business date, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0459; ASM-0651).

**Build steps**

1. Generate the stubs and the partner and terms fixture from the published contracts, pin each contract version and the fixture version in the run report, and fail the run on a mismatch (X1).
2. Build the PanelReadBack for AC2: the partner with its code, type, panel status, contract end and latest score, and no second row for the same code.
3. Add the TermProbe for AC2: the fee schedule version, the service levels and the scope are the versions in force on `2027-04-30` and the values in the pinned fixture, and the decision record names the same version (X5).
4. Add the ProductReadBack for AC3: DP08 carries the same partner_code, panel_status and contract_end as the owner, with its business date (X2).
5. Add the DecisionProbe for AC1 and AC2: one onboarding entry with its rule_id and rule_version, one published decision record, the central ledger confirmation, and no second entry after a re-read.
6. Add the InstructionDriver for AC4: one placement with one Idempotency-Key, the read back in `SENT`, a replay that returns the first answer unchanged, 409 for the suspended partner with no instruction and no partner event, and the case read before and after (X3, X4).
7. Add the EventProbe: one `InstructionIssued` per accepted placement, none for the replay and none for the refusal, and the confirmation the decision record carries.
8. Add the fault switch for AC5 and the AccessProbe for AC6, then the EvidenceReport and the gate, and swap a stub for the real owner as RWB-S9-E6029-APP lands (X6, X7).

**Feature switch.** None. The harness has no production flag; the fault switch of step 8 exists in the test environment only and is reset by the runner before and after each run.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass against the fakes and again against RWB-S9-E6029-APP when it lands, and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story and partner code.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values on the answer it reads, and owns no message text and no S9 message of its own. MSG-GEN-001 is the S9 validation message of VR-S9-001-1: it is asserted where the placement body leaves a required field out and S9 answers 422 with the field named, which is the same omission the X1 shape check runs against the stub (FSD S9 A2.1.3.1, line 121). MSG-P4-002 is asserted with the refused action when the caller answers without Partner portal R (AC6, AC-EXC-S9-001-01, FSD S9 A2.1.4.3 line 162). MSG-P7-003 is asserted when the decision record cannot be written and nothing changes (AC5, AC-EXC-S9-001-02, FSD S9 A2.1.4.3 line 163).

##### 15. Screens and states

The legacy story's screens are SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation, and neither is built or rendered here: the harness calls the operations behind them and reads the states through the owners. What the wave entry check looks at instead is the run report, whose environment, layout and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0459; ASM-0651).

| State | Read through | What the run asserts |
|---|---|---|
| ACTIVE, in force | S9 partner read, the terms fixture and the decision record | The partner is on the panel with its contract end, fee schedule version, service levels and scope, and the version of the terms is the one in force on the business date |
| The boundary view | DP08 through P1 | The same partner_code, panel_status and contract_end as the owner holds, with its business date |
| One instruction at SENT | S9 instruction read and the InstructionWorkflow history | One instruction for the partner and the case with its due_at, and one partner event; a replay adds none |
| A refused action | P4 session read, S9 answer, the instruction read and the case read | 409 for the suspended partner or 403 with MSG-P4-002 for the caller without R, no instruction, no partner event and no case change |
| A failed action | The decision log, the partner read and the instruction read | MSG-P7-003, the partner read unchanged and no instruction |

SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation belong to the S9 stories of the legacy key, and neither is built or read here. The partner reaches the portal through the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) and staff reach a screen through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); this harness renders neither and asserts the operations behind them. The run report replaces the screen for the wave entry check, and its environment, layout and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0459; ASM-0651).
