| TC-E6-029-04-ITG | Principle 5; ITG AC3 and the decision record of AC2 | Integration | The DP08 read beside the owner's partner read on the same business date, one onboarding decision entry with its rule version, a re-read, and the central ledger confirmation |

The AC column names the legacy test each copy derives from and the ITG acceptance criteria it asserts, and the full legacy test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx under the same legacy test case ID: TC-E6-029-01 Onboard a partner and set terms, TC-E6-029-02 Not recorded, TC-E6-029-03 the access refusal, and TC-E6-029-04 the forced decision log failure. Legacy AC2 stays with RWB-S9-E6029-APP, which owns the failure inside the service; the -ITG copy here asserts the same failure across the service boundary. ITG AC4, the refusal of a partner off the panel, is asserted inside the run of TC-E6-029-01-ITG, which places the instruction and attempts the refused one; it adds no test case ID because the legacy set has four.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the synthetic partner, its contract, the fee schedule version, the service levels, the scope, the second partner, the business date, the fault switch and the report layout are data.
- No personal data in logs, events, workflow inputs or reports: every key is synthetic, the partner is read by code and the case by id, and the events carry IDs and facts only.
- Service data only through the owner's contract: the partner and the instruction from S9, DP08 from P1, the case from P3, the decision log and the rule rows from P7, the session from P4; never a direct schema read and never another service's table (DP-01, DP-05).
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would (DP-11, DP-13).
- No invented operation: only the three S9 operations and the four reads of §12.2, and no partner create or panel change is composed, because the map publishes neither.
- A stub pass is never reported as a real pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner.
- The fault switch is reset by the runner before and after each run and is never left on, so a forced failure cannot be mistaken for a real one.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, never writes a row by hand, and never sets a state it then asserts; a failing criterion is fixed in the owning service or raised as a gap, and never waived in the script.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract baseline of RWB-E6-030 for rwb-partner (S9, service wave 4, business wave 4) is published as its own story so the app slice can build on Day 1. The baseline fixes the two panel reads on `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13), the `Partner` element with the fields of DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007, `LOV-PANEL` and `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE`, the reference-data stamp that carries the version in force, the reference-data row consumed from rwb-case (DP-07), the decision-record element of DP-03, the error set and the five fakes. It declares no write operation, no event, no workflow and no Schedule, because no source publishes one for this key (GAP-3109; ASM-5348 to ASM-5359; ASM-5360, ASM-5361). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **service team and the consumers of rwb-partner (the panel app slice, SCR-34 and SCR-35, the placement and scorecard stories and the wave 4 harness)**, we want **one tagged contract for the panel and its reference data — its two reads, its `Partner` element, its two lists, its version stamp, its consumed reference-data row, its error set and its fakes**, so that **the panel is built and tested in parallel on both sides of every boundary without waiting for the live services**.

This story owns the shapes and nothing else:

- the OpenAPI 3.1 fragment with `GET /partners` and `GET /partner/instructions` on the target base, their queries, their answer elements, their right, their scope and their error statuses (DP-13);
- the `Partner` element with the fields of DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 and the required flags of TSD S9 T3.1, and the `PartnerList` and `InstructionPage` answers of API-S9-001 and API-S9-003;
- the two closed lists `LOV-PANEL` and `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE` of TSD S9 T3.2, published as enumerations and bound to the version in force;
- the reference-data stamp: `listCode`, `version`, `values[]` and the `dataAsOf` instant, declared on every answer that names a list;
- the consumed reference-data row of rwb-case with its owner, its budget and its placeholder, and the decision-record element of DP-03 with its write-before-change rule and its failure behaviour;
- the error envelope, the message set of section 14, the naming baseline and the five fakes of section 12.8.

It does not own: any business outcome, row or answer instance (RWB-S9-E6030-APP); the firm record and its users (RWB-S9-AD022-APP); the six operations themselves, which the service contract baseline of rwb-partner declares and this fragment binds to its two reads (ASM-5359); the reference data and its lists (rwb-case, P3); the ledger and the rule rows (rwb-decision, P7); the roles (rwb-access, P4); and the implementations of the library, the edge route and the fakes' platforms, which are platform stories.

##### 2. Business rationale

A contract is what lets wave 4 start on Day 1. The panel crosses three boundaries - the reference data of rwb-case, the decision record and the edge route - and the plan carries one C row for the first of them and none for the others, so without a tagged baseline the app slice would wait for live services and the wave would slip (GAP-3109; ASM-5349).

The baseline also settles the facts the sources leave open:

- the fee schedule and the service levels have no table of this service, so the baseline declares them as reference-data rows read at their version and not as an owned entity (GAP-3109; ASM-5348);
- no write operation is published for the panel, so the baseline declares two reads and records the absence rather than inventing a maintenance operation (GAP-3109; ASM-5350);
- the version has no column in DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007, so it is declared as a stamp on the answer and on the decision record (GAP-3109; ASM-5350);
- `partner_user` has no field catalogue, so no element is declared for it (GAP-3109; ASM-5358).

The business effect is the one the legacy story promises - the panel, the schedule and the levels are data a business person may change, read with their version, and every change is recorded (BR-S9-002; legacy AC2) - and the baseline adds nothing to it. No business value is fixed here: the panel statuses, the partner types, the schedule and the levels stay reference data, so a business person changes them without a contract release.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service contract baseline of rwb-partner is in force: the six operations of TSD S9 T-A.1 on `/api/recovery/partner/v1`, the one error envelope and the one naming rule (ASM-5359).
- RWB-PLT-E1043-CON is published with the reference-data client schema, so the consumed reference-data row is declared against the library and not invented (DP-07).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer schema and stub, so the decision-record element is declared against the library (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published, so SCR-34 and SCR-35 are served on the composite route's terms and no screen contract is duplicated here (DP-19).
- TSD S9 T3.1, T3.2, T6.1, T6.2 and T-A.1 are available as the source of the element, the lists, the rights and the two operations; FSD S9 A2.2.3.2 gives the panel field catalogue.
- The path of the rwb-case reference-data read is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3109; ASM-5349).
- No approval is needed to publish a Draft baseline; the tag is applied when the contract tests pass and the consumers sign off.

##### 4. Flow

1. The fragment is drafted from TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2: the two reads with their purposes, their queries, their answer elements and their error sets, on `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13).
2. The `Partner` element is written from DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 with the required flags of T3.1 and its two lists as published enumerations bound to the version in force.
3. The reference-data stamp is declared on every answer that names a list: `listCode`, `version`, `values[]` and `dataAsOf`.
4. The consumed row of rwb-case is recorded with its owner, its budget and its placeholder name.
5. The decision-record element is recorded against the library schema with the write-before-change rule and the MSG-P7-003 failure path.
6. The error set, the message texts, the Partner portal right R of both reads, the scope rule and the absence of an `Idempotency-Key` are recorded.
7. Five fakes are published, each answering the paths its consumers exercise, and the drift test compares each one with the document.
8. The baseline is reviewed by the panel app slice, the two screens, the placement and scorecard stories and the wave 4 harness, tagged and handed over.
9. A later additive change is published inside major version 1; a removal, a rename or a retype opens a new major version.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A consumer asks for a property this document does not declare | The answer fails schema validation at the consumer, not at the service | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | A fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails and the baseline returns to review | None (pipeline log) | AC6 |
| X3 | A `v_ace_*` property, a `recovery_case` property or an owned fee-schedule table appears in the document | The absence test fails the build and the change is refused | None (pipeline log) | AC4, AC6 |
| X4 | A write operation, a second topic, an event or a Schedule is declared | The absence test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | AC5, AC6 |
| X5 | A list value is fixed in the document instead of being bound to the version | The schema test fails and the value is moved to the enumeration reference | None (pipeline log) | AC3 |
| X6 | A property carries personal data | The schema test fails and the property is removed | None (pipeline log) | AC2 |

X1 to X6 are the failure paths of the artefact, not of a business transaction; the business failure paths are RWB-S9-E6030-APP's.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; it starts on Day 1 from TSD S9, the Ownership Map and the four platform baselines and needs no running service |
| Negotiable | The element names, the wording of the descriptions and the shape of the fakes are the author's choice; the operations, the fields, the lists, the version stamp and the budgets are fixed by the sources |
| Valuable | The panel app slice, the two screens, the placement and scorecard stories and the wave 4 harness build on Day 1 against a tagged fragment and five fakes |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI fragment, one AsyncAPI absence note, nine contract tables, one contract README and five fake mapping sets |
| Small | Finished inside one week with the consumer sign-off |
| Testable | Each criterion is a validation of the document or a drift test of a fake, run in the pipeline |

These six criteria are new under D-RCV-60 and test the artefact only. They restate no business outcome of RWB-S9-E6030-APP and copy no legacy criterion: the legacy criterion this key owns stays with the app slice word for word.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The panel is rwb-partner's and the fragment declares its fields, its two lists and their required flags on the `Partner` element only | Context pack ownership rows; TSD S9 T3.1 and T3.2 |
| BR2 | The fee schedule, the service levels and the two lists are reference data of rwb-case: the document declares the version stamp and the consumed row, and no owned table for them | DP-07; Template and Rules v1 R3 default ruling; ASM-5348 |
| BR3 | The decision record is declared as an element written before the panel row changes, through the local library; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; TSD S9 T2; legacy AC2 of RWB-E6-030 |
| BR4 | Two reads and no write: the fragment declares no maintenance operation, because the Ownership Map publishes none for the panel | Context pack ownership rows; GAP-3109; ASM-5350 |
| BR5 | Both reads declare Partner portal R with scope applied; no read answers a firm the caller does not own | TSD S9 T6.1 and T-A.2 |
| BR6 | No event is declared: EV-20 and EV-21 are the instruction events of TSD S9 T5.3 and belong to other keys | Context pack Events; ASM-5351 |
| BR7 | The vocabulary is closed and versioned: the two lists are published as enumerations bound to the version in force, and no list value is a constant of the document | TSD S9 T3.2; FSD S9 BR-S9-002 |
| BR8 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: the firm's registration data, codes, instants and a version only | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 s17 |
| BR9 | A change is additive inside major version 1; a removal, a rename or a retype opens a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of the document, not of a partner:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The two reads, the element, the lists, the stamp, the consumed row, the decision element and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The panel app slice, the two screens, the placement and scorecard stories and the wave 4 harness accept the fragment and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property or a status is added inside major version 1 | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or a published enumeration changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | A write, a `v_ace_*` property, an event, a Schedule or a hard-coded list value | In review |

The panel statuses the document describes are the app slice's to drive, over `LOV-PANEL` ACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED and EXITED; this baseline fixes the vocabulary and moves no record.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-partner | Owns the OpenAPI fragment and the contract tables; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change and confirms the reference-data placeholder and the version stamp (GAP-3109) |
| Consuming teams (the panel app slice, SCR-34 and SCR-35, the placement and scorecard stories and the wave 4 harness) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| Platform library owner | Owns the error envelope, the naming rule, the reference-data client schema, the decision-record library and the composite route this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data property is declared in an answer, an element or a fake |

##### 11. Data

The baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Partner element | `id`, `partner_code`, `partner_name`, `partner_type`, `panel_status`, `contract_end`, `score` (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007) |
| Required flags | `id`, `partner_code`, `partner_name`, `partner_type` and `panel_status`; `contract_end` and `score` optional |
| Lists | `LOV-PANEL` (ACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED, EXITED) and `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE` (AGENCY, LAW_FIRM, VALUER, AUCTION_VENDOR, BROKER, DEBT_BUYER, AMC, RAMC), published as enumerations bound to a version |
| Reference-data stamp | `listCode`, `version`, `values[]`, `dataAsOf`, declared on every answer that names a list |
| Answers | `PartnerList` for API-S9-001 and `InstructionPage` for API-S9-003 |
| Decision record | The library element of DP-03, written before the panel row changes |
| Consumed fields | The list values of `lov_value` (DF-REF-027 to DF-REF-033) and the rule rows of `rule_row` (DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015), read at the version in force and never copied |
| Not declared here | `partner_user`, `recovery_case`, `timer`, `decision_log_entry`, any fee-schedule or service-level table and every `v_ace_*` view |
| Consumed with no source | The operation name of the reference-data read and the status-to-message mapping: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3109; ASM-5349, ASM-5361) |

No table, no column and no migration is declared by this story; the schema and its Flyway sequence belong to the DB story of this service (DP-15).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-partner (S9); base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13). The two rows are this fragment's; the four partner-portal operations of the service baseline belong to the instruction stories (ASM-5359).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/partners` | Query `type`, `status`; `PartnerList` out (API-S9-001) | Partner portal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/partner/instructions` | Query `status`, `page`, `size`; `InstructionPage` out (API-S9-003) | Partner portal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

Both answer 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002 and 503, each in the platform error envelope. The operation ids are those of TSD S9 T-A.1 and the paths are the target base, not the monolith form. No write operation is declared for the panel, the fee schedule or the service level (GAP-3109; ASM-5350).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| The reference-data list read; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3109; ASM-5349) | P3 rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | `LOV-PANEL`, `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE` and the schedule and level values behind them, returned with the version in force; faked |

One hop with a 2 s budget, one GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-07, DP-11, ADR-020). The plan's C row for this key sits on the app slice and is RWB-P3-E1043-CON; the fragment declares the row as consumed against its placeholder until the owner publishes it.

None. The Ownership Map gives S9 EV-20 and EV-21 and both are the instruction events `InstructionIssued` and `PartnerResultSubmitted` of TSD S9 T5.3, on `rwb.partner.events.v1`; this baseline declares no envelope, no producer group and no outbox row, and the absence test fails a build that adds one (GAP-3109; ASM-5351).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The panel and its version are read on the reference-data contract and not from an event; this baseline declares no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox row.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. `InstructionWorkflow` is the one workflow the Ownership Map gives S9 and it belongs to the instruction stories; the panel version load runs as a service command in one transaction and crosses no Temporal boundary, so this baseline declares no workflow element and no activity element (ASM-5350).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. This baseline declares no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table; the Ownership Map gives S9 no job.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application** (§R5.5)

| DP | Legacy marker | Pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON`; C `RWB-P3-E1043-CON` |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/partner/v1` | None |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` |

DP-03 and DP-07 are declared here as elements and consumed rows; their H and C rows sit on the app slice, because a CON story carries no build dependency (R5.7.1). DP-13 moves the base of the two reads. DP-19 puts the two screens behind the composite route.

**Deliverables.** The additive fragment `openapi/rwb-partner-panel-v1.yaml`, the `Partner`, `PartnerList`, `InstructionPage` and `ReferenceDataStamp` elements, the two lists as published enumerations, the contract README rows for the consumed reference-data placeholder, the decision-record element against the library schema, and the five WireMock mapping sets.

**Build steps.** (1) Write the two reads and validate the additive rule. (2) Write the elements, their required flags and the two lists. (3) Write the version stamp and its tests. (4) Record the consumed row with its owner, its budget and its placeholder. (5) Record the decision element and the absence section. (6) Publish the five fakes and the drift test. (7) Record the naming baseline and the absence tests, tag the baseline and collect the sign-off.

**Done when.** The document validates in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the five fakes answer every declared path, the drift and absence tests are green, and the consumers have accepted the baseline.

| MSG-GEN-001 | A required value of a read is absent, invalid or fails schema validation | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the Partner portal right R the read declares | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the panel row changes | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The status-to-message mapping is not published by any source: 403 is the legacy refusal with MSG-P4-002 and 503 the platform envelope, and the rest carry the platform's own conditions (GAP-3109; ASM-5361). The text of every message is the legacy and FSD S9 wording, copied unchanged.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the panel statuses, the partner types, the schedule and the levels stay reference data bound to a version, never a schema default or a code constant.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: the firm's registration data, codes, instants and a version only; every example is synthetic.
- The reference data stays with rwb-case: no owned fee-schedule or service-level table, no `v_ace_*` path, no `recovery_case` property (BR2, BR4).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The fragment lists only operations owned by rwb-partner; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided (DP-01, DP-11).
- No retired element is reintroduced: the absence tests fail a build that declares a write, a consumed event, a second topic, a workflow, a Schedule, a Quartz row or a shared job table.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the application slice of RWB-E6-030 is realigned onto rwb-partner (S9, service wave 4, business wave 4). The legacy criterion this slice owns is kept word for word with its origin tag and only the `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` lines are added. The panel is held as versioned rows of `partner` in `rwb_partner` and served with the reference-data version in force; the fee schedule, the service levels and the two lists are reference data of rwb-case read on its reference-data contract and never copied here (DP-07); the decision record is written through the local library before any panel version changes (DP-03); the two reads move onto `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13) and the two screens are reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The maintenance surface of the panel has no published write operation, the version has no column, and FEAT-PRM-02 has no requirement row (GAP-3108; ASM-5348 to ASM-5358; ASM-5360, ASM-5361). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **reference data administrator**, I want **to keep every panel, fee schedule and service level as versioned reference data**, so that **partners are placed, paid and measured by rule**.

This story owns:

- the one legacy criterion of RWB-E6-030 that the plan assigns to this slice (AC2, verbatim with its origin tag), and the rules, messages and screens it depends on;
- the panel as versioned data: the `partner` rows in `rwb_partner` with `panel_status`, `contract_end`, `score` and the standard record columns over DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007, and the panel version load that puts a set of values in force;
- the reference-data version in force: `LOV-PANEL` and `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE` and the fee schedule and service levels behind them, read on rwb-case's reference-data contract and stamped on every answer, never copied into this schema (DP-07);
- the decision record of a version load or a panel change, written through the local decision-record library **before** the row changes (DP-03);
- the two reads on base `/api/recovery/partner/v1`: `GET /partners` and `GET /partner/instructions`, each with the caller's scope applied (DP-13);
- the read-only slices of SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

It does not own: the published shapes, the `Partner` element, the two lists, the version stamp, the error set and the fakes (RWB-S9-E6030-CON); AC1 and the end-to-end panel read, which RWB-ITG-E6030-ITG owns (ASM-5357); the firm record and its portal users, the contract-end pass and the recall, which are RWB-S9-AD022-APP (ASM-5356); the reference data and its lists (rwb-case, P3); the ledger and the rule rows (rwb-decision, P7); the roles and rights (rwb-access, P4); the instruction lifecycle and the two events EV-20 and EV-21, which belong to the instruction stories (ASM-5351); and the schema, migration and deployment of this service (the DB, INF and OPS stories of this key).

##### 2. Business rationale

The objective and the metric do not move: every partner type is managed on the same six points, selection and contract and fees among them, and fees are calculated from the contracted schedule and paid against recorded results (FSD S9 Requirements served, REQ-S9-001 and REQ-S9-004); the metric is "Placements by scorecard, 100 percent, measured on the decision log and the Workbench records, reviewed monthly" (FSD S9 A2.2.1).

The problem is the one the module is built for: partners are instructed and paid by email and spreadsheet, and allocation is not based on performance (FSD S9 A1.3). A panel that sits in a spreadsheet cannot be placed by rule, cannot be scored and cannot be the basis of a fee.

D-RCV-60 changes who owns each fact, not what the administrator gets:

- **The panel is this service's, and so is its version.** `partner` is one of the three tables the Ownership Map gives S9; `panel_status`, `contract_end` and `score` are its columns and its `version` is the optimistic lock (context pack ownership rows; TSD S9 T3.1, T3.0).
- **The fee schedule and the service levels are reference data, not tables of this service.** The Ownership Map gives S9 no fee-schedule and no service-level table, and the default ruling of Template and Rules v1 R3 puts parameters and reference data with P3 rwb-case; DP-07 is the pattern of the key, so the schedule, the levels and the two lists are read at the version in force (GAP-3108; ASM-5348).
- **No value is a constant.** BR-S9-002 and legacy AC1 both say it: every value a business person may change is read from reference data with its version (FSD S9 A2.2.3.1).
- **The decision is recorded first**, in the transaction of the change, which is what legacy AC2 tests (DP-03; TSD S9 T2 writes the decision log entry before any change).
- **One base and one route.** The monolith path `monolith-base/partners` becomes `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` (DP-13) and the screens are served on the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, 2 s (DP-19).

No business value moves: the panel statuses, the partner types, the schedule and the levels stay data rows read with their version, never a constant of the code.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S9-E6030-CON is published and tagged: the two reads on `/api/recovery/partner/v1`, the `Partner` element, `LOV-PANEL` and `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE`, the version stamp, the consumed reference-data row, the error set and the fakes are baselined and handed to this story.
- RWB-PLT-E1043-CON is published with the reference-data client library: one read per list set, the version in force returned with the values, one hop and a 2 s budget (DP-07).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer stub: the local decision-record library writes in the caller's transaction and a failed write stops the action with MSG-P7-003 (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-34 and SCR-35 reach this service through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop each, and no screen calls a service directly (DP-19).
- `partner` and `partner_instruction` exist in `rwb_partner` from the DB story of this service with the columns of DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-016 and the standard record columns of TSD S9 T3.0; this story adds no table, no column and no migration.
- The reference data of rwb-case is in force at its version with `LOV-PANEL` (ACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED, EXITED) and `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE` (AGENCY, LAW_FIRM, VALUER, AUCTION_VENDOR, BROKER, DEBT_BUYER, AMC, RAMC), authored in rwb-case and loaded here through the library (FSD S9 A2.2.3.2; TSD S9 T3.2; ASM-5349).
- The Partner portal right R is declared on both reads and checked through the rwb-access guard; the FSD primary role Reference data administrator is not a role of TSD S9 T6.1, so the rights checked are the ones the two operations declare (GAP-3108; ASM-5352).
- The service runs as its own login on `rwb_partner` and holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `rwb_case` or on a `recovery.v_ace_*` view is refused by the database and fails the boundary test (DP-01, DP-05).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-S9-E6030-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The reference data administrator opens SCR-34 Partner list. The screen calls `GET /partners` on `/api/recovery/partner/v1` with the optional `type` and `status` filters (API-S9-001).
2. The handler asks the reference-data library of rwb-case for `LOV-PANEL` and `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE` at the version in force, one hop and 2 s, and keeps neither value (DP-07; ASM-5349).
3. The handler reads `partner` in `rwb_partner` with the caller's scope applied and answers `PartnerList`: `partner_code`, `partner_name`, `partner_type`, `panel_status`, `contract_end` and `score`, each row carrying the reference-data version in force (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007).
4. On SCR-35 Placement and allocation the same panel is read for the placement view, and `GET /partner/instructions` answers the instructions placed with the caller's firm from `partner_instruction` with `status`, `page` and `size` and no value beyond the caller's scope (API-S9-003).
5. A panel version load begins with the values to be put in force and the reason; the guard checks the Partner portal right of the caller before anything is read or written.
6. `loadPanelVersion` evaluates the change against the reference data in force and writes **one decision record before any row changes**: the version reference, the rule ID with its version, the inputs reference (the version in force and the version loaded), the outcome and the decided-at time (DP-03; TSD S9 T2).
7. In the same `rwb_partner` transaction the activity writes the panel rows: `panel_status`, `contract_end`, `score` and the standard record columns, with `version` incremented per row by the optimistic lock.
8. The version in force moves; every later answer of section 12.1 carries the new version, and no instruction already issued is re-priced or re-stated (GAP-3108; ASM-5350).
9. A required value that is absent or invalid is refused with the field named and nothing is written (VR-S9-002-1; MSG-GEN-001); a repeated load of the same version answers the record it already wrote and writes nothing.
10. No event leaves this story: the two events of this service are EV-20 and EV-21 and both belong to the instruction stories (ASM-5351).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The local decision record cannot be written | Nothing changes: no `partner` row, no new version, no answer | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, TC-E6-030-02, TC-E6-030-04 |
| X2 | The caller lacks the Partner portal right R of the read or of the load | 403 before any read and before any decision record | MSG-P4-002 | AC2, TC-E6-030-03 |
| X3 | A required value is absent or invalid: code, name, type, panel status | Refused with the field named; nothing written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC2 |
| X4 | The reference-data read of rwb-case does not answer inside 2 s or its breaker is open | The panel shows as unavailable, no value is substituted and no local copy is used | None (platform 503 envelope) | AC2 |
| X5 | A list value is not in `LOV-PANEL` or `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE` at the version in force | The value is refused and the version is named in the error detail | MSG-GEN-001 | AC2 |
| X6 | The version loaded is older than the version in force | The load is refused as stale and nothing changes | None (domain refusal) | AC2 |
| X7 | The same version is loaded twice | One decision record and one move: the repeat is counted and nothing is written | None | AC2 |
| X8 | A component, a statement or a test reaches a `v_ace_*` view, a `rwb_case` row or another service's schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | Section 17, BR5, BR6 |

X1 to X3 are the paths RWB-E6-030 carries; X4 to X7 are the paths DP-07 and the version rule add; X8 is the DP-01 and DP-05 boundary.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-S9-E6030-CON, the reference-data library stub, the decision-record stub, the gateway-bff fake and the access fake, on its own schema, and needs no live P3, P4 or P7 |
| Negotiable | The element names, the load command and the shape of the version stamp are this story's choice; the operations, the fields, the two lists, the rights and the messages are fixed |
| Valuable | The panel, its status, its contract end and its score are read as the version in force, and every change is recorded before it is made |
| Estimable | Two read handlers, one load command with its decision record, two screen fragments and the access and failure tests |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Every path runs on synthetic partners through the contract fakes, plus the access refusal and the forced record-write failure |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Hold the partner panel and fee schedule as data

  Background:
    Given the reference data of rwb-case is in force at its version and carries LOV-PANEL and LOV-PARTNER-TYPE
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC2 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E6-030 AC2)
    Given the rwb-partner contract mock returns partner "PTN-2026-000030" of type "AGENCY" on panel status "ACTIVE" with contract end 2027-03-31 and score 72.50
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns reference data version "RD-2026-11-01" with LOV-PANEL ACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED, EXITED
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

AC2 is the criterion of RWB-E6-030 word for word: `the decision log cannot be written`, `the action is taken`, `nothing changes` and `the user sees MSG-P7-003` all stand, and the only additions are the two mock lines that stand in for the contract this service publishes and for the reference data it does not own. On this story "the action" is a panel version load or a panel change: both write the decision record first, so both change nothing when the record cannot be written, and neither leaves a partner row, a new version or an answer behind (DP-03).

AC1 of RWB-E6-030 is not copied here: the split plan gives this slice AC2 only and gives the end-to-end panel read to RWB-ITG-E6030-ITG, which carries AC1 word for word with its `-ITG` test copies (ASM-5357). The partner code, the version reference and the dates in the mock lines are synthetic test data and no source value (section 16).

##### 9. State transitions

This story owns the panel status of the record it writes, over the four values of `LOV-PANEL` (TSD S9 T3.2), and the lifecycle of a panel version.

| From (`panel_status`) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| No row | A partner is put on the panel | Type, name and status valid at the version in force | ACTIVE, or ON_NOTICE where the contract says so |
| ACTIVE | A missed target or an upheld conduct breach | The rule of the owning story fires | ON_NOTICE |
| ON_NOTICE | The cure period lapses | The rule of the owning story fires | SUSPENDED |
| SUSPENDED or ON_NOTICE | The contract ends or the exit is approved | `contract_end` passes or the exit is approved | EXITED |
| EXITED | A re-entry is approved | A new contract is in force | ACTIVE |

| Version state | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None in force | A version is loaded | Newer than the version in force and the record is written | In force |
| In force | A newer version is loaded | The record is written and the rows commit | New version in force, the previous one superseded |
| In force | A load older than the version in force | X6 | Unchanged, refused |

The moves to ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED and EXITED are driven by the notice, review and exit stories of this service; this story fixes the values and the record, not their triggers.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application** (§R5.5)

| DP | Legacy marker | Pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON`; C `RWB-P3-E1043-CON` |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/partner/v1` | None |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` |

DP-13 moves the base of the two reads and nothing else. DP-19 puts SCR-34 and SCR-35 behind the composite route. DP-07 is the heart of the story: it is what makes the fee schedule and the service levels data of their owner rather than a copy here. DP-08 and DP-09 are not in the pattern set of this key although the guard is used in fact and no outbox is needed (ASM-5353, ASM-5354).

**Deliverables.** The two read handlers with their scope filter and their version stamp, the reference-data client wiring with its breaker, the panel version load with its record and its optimistic lock, the two screen fragments and the five fakes.

**Build steps.** (1) Wire the reference-data client behind the library and its breaker. (2) Implement `GET /partners` with its filters and its scope. (3) Implement `GET /partner/instructions` with its paging and its firm scope. (4) Write `loadPanelVersion` with the record first, the row update and the version check. (5) Add the two screen fragments on the composite route. (6) Prove AC2 and the eight exception paths on the fakes.

**Done when.** AC2 passes at component level on the fakes, a load with a stopped record stub changes nothing, the boundary test shows no `v_ace_*` read and no `rwb_case` statement, and the two screens answer through the gateway-bff route with the version in force.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E6-030 as the wave 4 integration proof that the partner panel, the fee schedule and the service levels are read as versioned data through rwb-partner, that the list values behind them come from rwb-case's reference-data contract and not from a copy, that a new version leaves an instruction issued under the old version untouched, and that each version carries one decision record with its rule version; the panel and the versions are RWB-S9-E6030-APP. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **reference data administrator**, I want **the partner panel, the fee schedule and the service levels proved end to end on the real services as versioned data: read back through rwb-partner with the version in force for the business date, their list values read through rwb-case's reference-data contract, an instruction issued under one version left untouched when the next version comes into force, and one decision record per version with its rule version**, so that **a placement is priced and timed by the terms that were in force when it was made and no business value is ever written in code**.

This story builds the wave 4 integration harness and its evidence, and nothing else. The partner panel, the fee schedule, the service levels and the versions are built by S9 rwb-partner in RWB-S9-E6030-APP and its CON story; the list values behind them are P3's reference data under the default ruling; the decision record and the central ledger are P7's; the case the instruction sits on is P3's; and the right that answers the read is P4's. The harness loads the fixture, reads the panel and the terms through S9's published operations, resolves every list value through P3's reference-data contract, advances the fixture's business date across a version boundary, reads the decision log and the published decision record, and writes a run report per version. It provides no endpoint, no table, no workflow, no activity, no schedule and no screen, and it writes no code in any service.

##### 2. Business rationale

Partners are instructed and paid by email and spreadsheet today, and the fee is worked out by hand. A fee schedule that lives in a spreadsheet cannot be defended a year later: nobody can say which rate applied on the day the work was placed, and the person who maintained the file has usually moved on. REQ-S9-001 puts contract and fees on the six points every partner type is managed on, and REQ-S9-004 makes the contracted schedule the basis of the fee actually paid — so a schedule that changes in place re-prices work already done and pays a partner a rate that was never agreed for that placement. BR-S9-002 (FSD S9 A2.2.3.1) is the rule this story is written against: no value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version. A panel, a fee schedule and a service level that live in a class constant break that rule silently, because the run still passes and only the money is wrong.

The second half of the rationale is the boundary. DP-07 makes the list values a contract of rwb-case, so a list copied into the partner service drifts the moment the list changes; the panel status the bank uses, the partner types it recognises and the instruction types and statuses it issues have to come from one source, or a status read in one service stops matching the status read in another. That is why this harness asserts the list values through P3's contract and not through a second copy, and why the version boundary is asserted on an instruction that was already issued: the version in force changes the next placement, not the one already made.

The harness is decoupled the way the services are. Every call is one hop on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13); there is no in-process call and no second hop. The decision record is written by S9 through the local decision-record library on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) and confirmed by the central ledger in rwb-decision (ADR-022). DP-01 forbids reading another service's schema, so the panel and the instructions are read through S9's contract, the lists through P3's, and the case through P3's; ACE-side data is read only through P1's published contract (DP-05). On the edge, DP-19 sends partners through the partner gateway in the DMZ and reserves gateway-bff composite routes for the staff screens; this run calls S9's own operations at the service boundary, which are the operations both edges front.

One limit is stated plainly because it shapes the run. The Ownership Map publishes `GET /partners` and the partner-instruction operations but no panel-version or fee-schedule load operation, and it publishes no parameter that carries a panel version or a fee-schedule version. The harness therefore reads the versions in force through the published reads and the reference-data contract, drives the load through S9's own path inside RWB-S9-E6030-APP, and asserts it through those reads and the decision log; it never invents a reference-load endpoint of its own.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The published contracts of S9 rwb-partner (the partner list and the partner-instruction operations), P3 rwb-case (the reference-data contract `GET /admin/lists/{listCode}` and `GET /admin/parameters`, DP-07, and the case read), P7 rwb-decision (the decision log) and P4 rwb-access (the session) are in the contract registry, and a contract fake is generated from each one with its version pinned.
- S9 owns `partner` and `partner_instruction` in `rwb_partner` (Arch v5 slide 41, line 2891), so the panel row and the instruction this run reads have one named owner before a value is asserted.
- The panel and the versions are RWB-S9-E6030-APP until it lands; until then the fixture of §12.8 stands in for its effect and the story is reported as a stub pass.
- P3 owns `lov_value` and publishes the reference-data contract of DP-07, so the list values are read through that contract and never from a copy.
- FEAT-PRM-02 Hold the partner panel and fee schedule as data is the S9 feature, with FEAT-CWC-23 as its prerequisite (Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3, line 135); this story asserts the feature across the service boundary and builds neither.
- The lists are LOV-PANEL (ACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED, EXITED), LOV-PARTNER-TYPE, LOV-INSTRUCTION and LOV-INSTR-STATUS, with the values the TSD S9 gives at lines 93 to 98.
- The rules in force are R-WO-30, R-WO-31, R-UNI-25, R-UNI-26 and R-UNI-45; the harness reads them with their version and evaluates none of them.
- The synthetic partner, panel version, fee schedule versions, service levels, business date, evidence format and gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0460; ASM-0652), and are held in the fixture as data, not written in code.
- No build dependency. Day 1, with the contract fakes in place from the first run; the one wait is RWB-S9-E6030-APP, which replaces its stub and never blocks the lane.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: runs preflight. It reads the six contracts of §12.2, pins each version in the run report, loads the panel and fee-schedule fixture, and stops the run before any assertion if a contract is missing or a pinned version has moved (X1).
2. Harness: loads the fixture: partner `PRT-SYN-0030` with its partner_type, panel_status, contract_end and scope, panel version `PNLV-SYN-0030-v2`, fee schedule `FS-SYN-0030-v2` in force and `FS-SYN-0030-v3` effective from the next business date, the service levels held by partner type, business date `2027-04-30`, and case `RW-2027-000830`. On Day 1 the stubs of §12.8 return the same records.
3. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` and asserts the panel row with its partner_code, partner_type, panel_status and contract_end, and the version of the fee schedule the row points at, which is `FS-SYN-0030-v2` (AC2).
4. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` for LOV-PANEL, LOV-PARTNER-TYPE, LOV-INSTRUCTION and LOV-INSTR-STATUS and asserts that every code the partner read returns has its list row, its label_en and its valid_from through P3, that one source answers all four lists, and that no list value is read from a copy inside rwb-partner (AC3).
5. Harness: asserts the version in force and its valid-from are the ones the partner read applies, and that the decision entry of the load records the same two values. The map publishes no parameter that carries a panel or fee-schedule version, so the version is asserted where the partner read applies it and in the decision entry, and if a later contract publishes such a parameter the run reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` and fails on a second copy (AC2, AC3).
6. Harness: places an instruction under `FS-SYN-0030-v2` through `POST /api/recovery/partner/v1/cases/{caseId}/instructions` with one Idempotency-Key, reads it back through `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions`, and asserts instruction `INS-SYN-2027-0030` on case `RW-2027-000830`, its instruction_type from LOV-INSTRUCTION, its status `SENT` from LOV-INSTR-STATUS and its fee_amount (AC4).
7. Harness: counts one `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` per instruction on `rwb.partner.events.v1`, and asserts a replay of the same placement with the same Idempotency-Key adds no second instruction and no second event (AC4).
8. Harness: advances the fixture to the business date on which `FS-SYN-0030-v3` is in force, reads the partner and the instruction again, and asserts the partner now names v3 while the instruction still carries v2 and its fee_amount has not changed (AC4).
9. Harness: reads the four lists again on the later business date and asserts the same values as before, because a new fee schedule does not fork the list (AC3).
10. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` and asserts one entry per version load with its rule_id, its rule_version and the valid-from date it applied, and reads `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and asserts one publication per version, confirmed once by the central ledger, with no second entry after a re-read (AC1).
11. Harness: resets the fixture to the snapshot before the v3 load, turns the fault switch on the decision-record hop on, drives the v3 load again through S9's own path, and asserts the answer carries MSG-P7-003, that the partner read still names v2 in force, and that the decision log holds no entry for the refused load; the version in force keeps running and the switch is reset after the run (AC5).
12. Harness: calls `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` as a synthetic caller whose session carries no Partner portal R and asserts 403 with MSG-P4-002 with no panel row and no version returned (AC6).
13. Harness: writes one run report per version, keyed by story and business date, naming the contract version of each hop, whether the hop was a stub or the owner, the panel row, the version in force, the list values and their source, the instruction and its fee, the decision entries with their rule versions, both event counts and the gate verdict.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A stub answers a shape the published contract does not allow, or the load is driven short of a required field | The run fails at that hop and the report names the service, the operation, the contract version and the missing field; no criterion is marked passed | MSG-GEN-001 (expected, and missing) | TC-E6-030-01-ITG (ITG AC1) |
| X2 | A code the partner read returns has no row in the list the reference-data contract answers, or the contract answers a different label or valid_from from a copy held elsewhere | The run fails on AC3 and the report names the code, the list, the contract answer and the copy, because a list with two sources is the drift DP-07 forbids | None | TC-E6-030-04-ITG (ITG AC3) |
| X3 | A version change re-prices an instruction that was already issued, or moves it to the new version | The run fails on AC4 and the report names the instruction, its fee_amount before and after, and both versions | None | TC-E6-030-04-ITG (ITG AC4) |
| X4 | Two versions are in force for one partner on one business date, or the partner read names a version whose valid-from is later than the business date | The run fails on AC2 and the report names both versions, their valid-from dates and the business date | None | TC-E6-030-01-ITG (ITG AC2) |
| X5 | The decision record is written twice for one version load, written without its rule_version, or written without the valid-from date it applied | The run fails on AC1 and the report names the entries, their rule ids, their rule versions and the missing valid-from | None | TC-E6-030-01-ITG (ITG AC1) |
| X6 | A forced decision-record failure leaves the new version in force, adds a decision entry, or answers without MSG-P7-003 | The run fails on AC5 and the report names the version read before and after, the entry count and the answer | MSG-P7-003 (expected, and missing) | TC-E6-030-02-ITG (ITG AC5) |
| X7 | A caller without Partner portal R is allowed the partner read | The run fails on AC6 and the report names the caller role, the right, the operation and the answer; a 200 is a failure even when no data changed | MSG-P4-002 (expected, and missing) | TC-E6-030-03-ITG (ITG AC6) |

The report text is for the wave entry check and is not part of the message standard. The business messages the run touches are in section 14 and are asserted by ID and by their substituted values.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs against the published contracts and their stubs from Day 1; the only wait is RWB-S9-E6030-APP, and its fixture answers until it lands |
| Negotiable | The fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the two versions and their dates, the fault switch, the report shape and the gate are configuration agreed at the wave entry check, not business values in code |
| Valuable | Proves that the panel and the terms are read as data with a version, that their lists come from one source, that a new version does not re-price issued work, and that a version load without its decision record changes nothing |
| Estimable | One runner, one stub set, one panel and fee-schedule fixture, one partner, one instruction, two version loads, one list probe, one decision probe, one event observer and one report |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its four tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against the stubs and again against RWB-S9-E6030-APP as it lands |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Hold the partner panel and fee schedule as data - wave 4 integration harness

  Background:
    Given the synthetic partner "PRT-SYN-0030" is on the panel on panel version "PNLV-SYN-0030-v2"
    Given fee schedule "FS-SYN-0030-v2" is in force on business date "2027-04-30" and "FS-SYN-0030-v3" is effective from the next business date
    Given LOV-PANEL, LOV-PARTNER-TYPE, LOV-INSTRUCTION and LOV-INSTR-STATUS answer from the rwb-case reference-data contract

  Scenario: AC1 Hold the partner panel and fee schedule as data (legacy RWB-E6-030 AC1)
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When the user acts on the screen
    Then keeps every panel, fee schedule and service level as versioned reference data
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 The panel and its terms are read as the version in force (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the partner "PRT-SYN-0030" is on the panel with its partner_type, panel_status and contract_end
    When GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners is called on business date "2027-04-30"
    Then the panel row names panel version "PNLV-SYN-0030-v2" and fee schedule "FS-SYN-0030-v2" in force
    And the row carries the service levels held for its partner type
    And the version and its valid-from date are the ones the decision entry of the load records

  Scenario: AC3 The list values come from rwb-case's reference-data contract and not from a copy (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners returns panel, partner type, instruction type and instruction status codes
    When GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode} is called for LOV-PANEL, LOV-PARTNER-TYPE, LOV-INSTRUCTION and LOV-INSTR-STATUS
    Then every code the partner read returns has its list row, its label_en and its valid_from through rwb-case
    And the same values answer for both fee schedule versions, so a new schedule does not fork the list

  Scenario: AC4 A new version leaves an instruction issued under the old version untouched (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given instruction "INS-SYN-2027-0030" is placed on case "RW-2027-000830" under "FS-SYN-0030-v2" with its fee_amount
    When the fixture advances to the business date on which "FS-SYN-0030-v3" is in force
    Then GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners names "FS-SYN-0030-v3"

  Scenario: AC5 A forced decision-record failure stops the version load with nothing changed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision record cannot be written for the load of "FS-SYN-0030-v3"
    When the load is driven through rwb-partner's own path in RWB-S9-E6030-APP

  Scenario: AC6 A caller without Partner portal R is refused the partner read (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a synthetic caller with role "RW-CASEOWN" whose session carries no Partner portal R
```
