```gherkin
    Then the answer is 403 with "MSG-P4-002"
    And no panel row and no version is returned
```

Legacy AC1 is the only legacy criterion this story owns. Legacy AC2 (the decision log cannot be written and nothing changes) stays with RWB-S9-E6030-APP as its build criterion and is asserted here across the service boundary in AC5, where the panel, the version in force and the decision log are read before and after the refused load. The versions are asserted through the published reads and the decision log because the Ownership Map publishes no reference-load operation for the partner panel; the harness never calls an operation the map does not publish.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every partner type is managed on the same six points: selection, contract and fees, targets and incentives, data exchange, performance reviews, notice and exit | REQ-S9-001 |
| BR2 | Fees are calculated from the contracted schedule and paid against recorded results, so the contracted schedule is the basis of the fee actually paid | REQ-S9-004 |
| BR3 | No value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version | BR-S9-002 (FSD S9 A2.2.3.1) |
| BR4 | The list values behind the panel, the partner types, the instruction types and the instruction statuses are the reference-data contract of rwb-case; a list has one source and is never copied into rwb-partner | DP-07 |
| BR5 | An agency on the panel with capacity takes the placement and the instruction is sent, so the panel a placement reads is the panel in force for the business date | R-WO-30 |
| BR6 | No agency on the panel has capacity: the placement is held and escalated on the timer | R-WO-31 |
| BR7 | When the partner leaves the panel or the contract ends, every open case held by that partner is recalled and re-selected | R-UNI-26 |
| BR8 | When the next partner is selected on the scorecard, the instruction is re-issued and the partner clock restarts | R-UNI-45 |
| BR9 | The decision record is written by S9 through the local decision-record library on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the central ledger in rwb-decision confirms it; nothing moves when the record cannot be written | DP-03; ADR-022 |
| BR10 | Every hop is one REST call on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s timeout and no second hop; ACE data only through P1's contract; never another service's schema or table | DP-11; DP-13; DP-01; DP-05 |

The harness asserts these rules and changes none of them; the rules themselves are evaluated in RWB-S9-E6030-APP, the list values are P3's, the decision log and the rule rows are P7's, and the case is P3's. R-UNI-24 is read for one principle only — a recorded decision is corrected by a correcting entry naming the original and never overwritten — so a version and its decision entry are never rewritten in place; the run makes no correction and claims none.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To | Owner of the change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ACTIVE | none in the rule set read here | a partner is on the panel and the read carries its contract_end and score | ACTIVE, unchanged | S9 writes the panel value; the placement is RWB-S9-E6031's |
| ON_NOTICE | none in the rule set read here | the contract is running to its end and contract_end is the field the read carries | ON_NOTICE | S9 through the reference-data load of RWB-S9-E6030-APP |
| SUSPENDED | R-UNI-29 conduct breach suspends allocation | a conduct breach is recorded; the panel value is data and the rule's effect is on allocation | SUSPENDED | S9 for the panel value; the allocation effect is the rule's |
| EXITED | R-UNI-26 partner leaves the panel or the contract ends | the partner leaves the panel or the contract ends, and every open case is recalled and re-selected | EXITED, with PARTNER_RECALLED on the cases | S9 for the panel value; the recall is the partner and agency manager's |
| SENT | R-UNI-25 partner misses the service level | the work is chased once, then recalled and re-selected on the scorecard | RECALLED | S9 rwb-partner |
| SENT | R-UNI-26 partner exits the panel | the partner exits, so its open instructions are recalled | RECALLED | S9 rwb-partner |

The panel states are the four values LOV-PANEL holds — ACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED and EXITED — and the instruction states run from SENT to RECALLED on the two rules above; S9 owns both changes and the harness observes them. The version states are two, and neither is a case state:

| Version state | What it means | Owner of the change | Read that shows it |
|---|---|---|---|
| In force | the version's valid-from is on or before the business date | S9 rwb-partner through the load of RWB-S9-E6030-APP | `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` names it, and the decision entry of the load records it |
| Effective from a future date | the version's valid-from is after the business date | S9 rwb-partner through the load of RWB-S9-E6030-APP | the same read still names the version in force, and the future version is not applied to any instruction |

The harness changes no state and writes no row: it reads the panel, the instruction and the versions, advances the fixture's business date instead of waiting for a schedule, and asserts the reads. The list values are read, never written; a list change is P3's reference-data change and is not part of this run.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-AGENCYMG (Partner and agency manager) | Primary role of the S9 module, holding Partner portal CRUDA (TSD S9 T6.1, line 145); the run reads the panel and places the instruction under this role |
| The reference data administrator | The actor of the legacy story: keeps the panel, the fee schedule and the service levels as versioned data; the load itself is RWB-S9-E6030-APP's and this story only observes it |
| RW-CASEOWN and RW-TEAMMGR | Read the partner panel and the instructions at R (TSD S9 T6.1, lines 136 and 137), and are the reading callers of AC2, AC3 and AC4 |
| RW-RISK and RW-COE | Read the versions and the rule version at R (TSD S9 T6.1, lines 152 and 153) where the run records the rule version behind a load |
| The refused caller of AC6 | A synthetic caller whose session carries role RW-CASEOWN with no Partner portal R: every published Recovery role in the S9 matrix holds at least R, so the negative fixture is a session in which the grant is absent, and the run asserts the refusal only, never that the role lacks the right |
| QA lead | Owns the harness configuration, the fixture, the fault switch, the report shape and the pass or fail gate |
| Integration lead | Owns the harness code, the stub set and the swap from a stub to the real service |
| The owning services' identities | S9 holds the panel, the instruction and the version load, P3 holds the lists and the case, P7 holds the decision log and the central ledger, and P4 answers the session; they make every change the harness asserts |
| No delegation of authority level applies | The harness takes no business decision; authorisation is answered by rwb-access and the DoA is P4's |

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 | partner | id, partner_code, partner_name, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end, score | Read through the rwb-partner contract; S9 owns the table in `rwb_partner` |
| DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 | partner_instruction | id, case_id, partner_id, instruction_type, instructed_at, due_at, status, result_code, fee_amount | Read through the rwb-partner instruction read; S9 owns the table in `rwb_partner` |
| DF-REF-027 to DF-REF-033 | lov_value | id, lov_code, value_code, label_en, label_th, sort_order, valid_from | Read through P3's reference-data contract; P3 owns the table |
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case | id, case_no, status, stage_code, route_state, rule_version | Read through the rwb-case case contract; the case the instruction sits on; P3 owns the table |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | id, case_id, decision_code, rule_id, rule_version, model_version, decided_at | Read through the rwb-decision contract; written by S9's load through the local decision-record library; P7 owns the table |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | rule_row | id, rule_id, rule_version, valid_from, valid_to, approved_by | Read through the rwb-decision contract; P7 owns the table |

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8, and the legacy data table of RWB-E6-030 cites the partner, the decision log entry, the rule row and `lov_value` under these ranges. The panel and the instruction are S9's in `rwb_partner`, and the fee_amount the version boundary is asserted on is DF-PRT-016; the list values are P3's and are read only through the reference-data contract the legacy table cites as `lov_value` DF-REF-027 to DF-REF-033; the decision entry and the rule rows are P7's; the case is P3's. No source publishes a table for the panel version or the fee schedule version, so the versions are held as data inside S9's own contract and no field ID is asserted for them here. The harness owns no table and writes no row: the two changes it drives are S9's own published operation of §12.2 and the load inside RWB-S9-E6030-APP, and everything else it reads is a contract read.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` | S9 rwb-partner | The panel row with its partner_type, panel_status and contract_end, and the fee schedule version in force (AC2, AC5, AC6) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/cases/{caseId}/instructions` | S9 rwb-partner | Places the instruction under the version in force, once per Idempotency-Key (AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions` | S9 rwb-partner | The instruction, its type, its status and its fee_amount, read back before and after the version boundary (AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | The rows and labels of LOV-PANEL, LOV-PARTNER-TYPE, LOV-INSTRUCTION and LOV-INSTR-STATUS, the reference-data contract of DP-07 (AC3) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | P7 rwb-decision | One entry per version load with its rule_id, its rule_version and the valid-from it applied (AC1, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The caller's roles and rights before the partner read (AC6) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13). No operation is invented in this story: each path is the owner's published operation in the Ownership Map. DP-07 makes the list read a C dependency — RWB-P3-E1043-CON — and that story is built against the published reference-data contract and its fake, so it never blocks this run. The map publishes no panel-version or fee-schedule load operation, and no parameter that carries either version; the version in force is therefore asserted where the partner read applies it and in the decision entry, and if a later contract publishes such a parameter the run reads it and fails on a second copy.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it writes its report to the wave record.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use in the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1` | S9 rwb-partner (EV-20) | Counts one publication per instruction and proves a replay of the same placement adds none (AC4) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | S9 rwb-partner through the local decision-record library (DP-03), confirmed by P7 rwb-decision | Proves one decision record per version load, with its rule version, published once and confirmed once by the central ledger (AC1, AC5) |

The harness subscribes to both topics under one consumer group of its own and counts publications; the effect it reads for rwb-decision is the decision log through the operation of §12.2, because the central ledger confirmation is read there and not from a schema.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness observes `InstructionWorkflow`, S9's workflow on the task queue `rwb-partner` in the `rwb-recovery` namespace, through the placement of §4 step 6: its `issueInstruction` step and its due_at timer are the ones the run sees in the workflow history (Arch v5 slide 17, line 1247). Neither the workflow, an activity nor a Schedule is created, changed or owned by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added, and none needed. A version takes effect by its valid-from date and not by a job, so nothing in the journey is on a cron: the harness advances the fixture's business date across the boundary instead of waiting for a schedule.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-01): `partner` and `partner_instruction` are S9's in `rwb_partner`, `lov_value` and `recovery_case` are P3's, and `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are P7's in `rwb_decision`.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Contract | Stubbed answer in the run |
|---|---|---|
| Stub for rwb-partner (S9) | `GET /partners`, `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions`, `GET /partner/instructions` | Partner `PRT-SYN-0030` on panel version `PNLV-SYN-0030-v2` with fee schedule `FS-SYN-0030-v2` in force and `FS-SYN-0030-v3` effective from the next business date; instruction `INS-SYN-2027-0030` on case `RW-2027-000830` in `SENT` under v2 with its fee_amount; on the later business date the panel names v3 and the instruction keeps v2; with the fault switch on, the load answers MSG-P7-003 and the panel stays on v2 |
| Stub for rwb-case (P3), reference data | `GET /admin/lists/{listCode}` | The rows, labels and valid_from of LOV-PANEL, LOV-PARTNER-TYPE, LOV-INSTRUCTION and LOV-INSTR-STATUS, unchanged across both business dates |
| Stub for rwb-decision (P7) | `GET /decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | No entry before a load; one entry per version load with its rule_id, rule_version and the valid-from it applied; the central ledger confirmation once; nothing added by the refused load |
| Stub for rwb-access (P4) | `GET /me/session` | Allows RW-AGENCYMG and the reading callers where the run needs them; for the refused caller of AC6 answers 403 with MSG-P4-002 |
| Panel and fee-schedule fixture | The version and the terms, held as data | Partner `PRT-SYN-0030` with its type, status, contract_end and scope; panel version `PNLV-SYN-0030-v2`; fee schedules `FS-SYN-0030-v2` and `FS-SYN-0030-v3`; the service levels by partner type; business date `2027-04-30` and the next effective date |

Each stub is generated from the published contract and its version is pinned in the run report, so a contract change shows up as a run failure and not as a silent pass. The harness environment, base hosts, fixture layout, synthetic partner and case keys, the panel version and the two fee schedule versions, the service levels, the business date and the next effective date, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0460; ASM-0652).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 6 consumed, one hop each on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13) |
| Kafka | None published; two consumed, `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`, counted once each |
| Temporal | None added; `InstructionWorkflow` on `rwb-partner` observed through the placement |
| File | None. The versions and the terms are S9's own request bodies and the report is the harness's own output; no file or claim-check is transferred by this story |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery-w4/partner-panel-versions`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H dependencies these patterns add — RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON — are platform stories delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays None. DP-13 adds nothing: the panel, the instruction, the list and the decision log are each called on the owner's own base and there is no shared base left. DP-07's C is RWB-P3-E1043-CON, and C never blocks: the run builds against the published reference-data contract and its fake from Day 1. DP-19 has two edges and the run names both: for a **partner** the route is the **partner gateway** in the DMZ under FAPI 2.0, and **gateway-bff** composes the **staff** screens only, including the panel list and the placement view; the harness renders neither and calls the operations behind them. The one blocking dependency is the I story RWB-S9-E6030-APP, which replaces its stub; until it is live a stub pass is reported as a stub pass.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the six owned criteria in order for one partner and one business date, holds the run lock and the fixture reset |
| PanelVersionReadBack | Service | Reads the panel row, its partner_type, panel_status and contract_end, and the fee schedule version in force on the business date |
| ListReadBack | Service | Resolves every code the partner read returns through the rwb-case reference-data contract for the four lists, and asserts one source |
| InstructionVersionProbe | Service | Places the instruction once under v2, advances the business date, and asserts the instruction still carries v2 and its fee_amount |
| DecisionProbe | Service | Reads one decision entry per version load with its rule_id, rule_version and valid-from, reads the published decision record, and holds the fault switch |
| EventProbe | Service | Subscribes to `rwb.partner.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`, counts publications and asserts a replay adds none |
| AccessProbe | Service | Reads the session, calls the partner read as the refused caller, and asserts the 403 and the message |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes one report per version and business date, keyed by story, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the stubs from Day 1 and the real service as RWB-S9-E6030-APP lands, on the synthetic partner `PRT-SYN-0030`, the case `RW-2027-000830`, the panel version `PNLV-SYN-0030-v2`, the fee schedules `FS-SYN-0030-v2` and `FS-SYN-0030-v3`, and business date `2027-04-30`. The harness seeds nothing by hand and never writes a schema row. The environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the panel version and the two fee schedule versions, the service levels, the business date and the next effective date, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0460; ASM-0652).

**Build steps**

1. Generate the stub set and the panel and fee-schedule fixture from the published contracts, pin each contract version in the run report, and fail the run on a mismatch (X1).
2. Build the PanelVersionReadBack and the ListReadBack and prove the panel row, its terms, the version in force and every list code through P3, with one source and no copy (AC2, AC3, X2, X4).
3. Add the InstructionVersionProbe: one placement under v2 with one Idempotency-Key, the instruction read back with its type, status and fee_amount, and the EventProbe counting one InstructionIssued (AC4).
4. Advance the fixture business date and assert the boundary: the panel names v3, the instruction still carries v2 and its fee is unchanged, and the lists answer the same values (AC4, AC3, X3).
5. Add the DecisionProbe: one entry per version load with its rule_id, rule_version and valid-from, one published decision record, the central ledger confirmation, and no second entry after a re-read (AC1, X5).
6. Add the fault switch: force the decision-record failure on the v3 load, assert MSG-P7-003, the panel still on v2, no decision entry and the version in force still running; reset the fixture and the switch after the run (AC5, X6).
7. Add the AccessProbe: the refused caller at 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no panel row returned (AC6, X7).
8. Add the EvidenceReport and the gate, and swap a stub for the real owner as RWB-S9-E6030-APP lands; a stub pass is never reported as a real pass.

**Feature switch.** None. The harness has no production flag; the fault switch of step 6 exists in the test environment only and is reset by the runner before and after each run.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass against the fakes and again against RWB-S9-E6030-APP when it lands, and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story and business date.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values on the answer it reads, and owns no message text and no S9 message of its own. MSG-GEN-001 is asserted with the missing field when a version load is driven short of a required field, the validation rule VR-S9-002-1 of FSD S9 A2.2.3.1 (X1); MSG-P4-002 is asserted with the refused action when the caller carries no Partner portal R (AC6, X7); and MSG-P7-003 is asserted when the decision record cannot be written and nothing changes (AC5, X6).

##### 15. Screens and states

The legacy story's screens are SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation, and neither is built or rendered here: the harness calls the partner and instruction operations behind them and reads the states through the owners. What the wave entry check looks at instead is the run report, whose environment, layout and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0460; ASM-0652).

| State | Read through | What the run asserts |
|---|---|---|
| The version in force | `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` and the decision log | The panel names `FS-SYN-0030-v2` on business date `2027-04-30`, with its valid-from and one decision entry |
| The version effective from a future date | the same reads on the later business date | `FS-SYN-0030-v3` is named once the business date reaches its valid-from, and v2 is no longer named |
| The instruction issued under v2 | `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions` | The instruction still carries v2 and its fee_amount has not changed after v3 is in force |
| The refused or failed load | the S9 answer, the partner read and the decision log | 403 with MSG-P4-002 or MSG-P7-003, the panel and the version unchanged, and no decision entry for the refused load |

SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation belong to the S9 stories of the legacy key, and neither is built or read here. A partner would reach its own instruction view through the partner gateway and a staff member would reach the panel and the placement through a gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); this harness renders neither and asserts the operations behind them.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code, first and without exception: the panel, the fee schedule and the service levels are data rows with a version, read from reference data, and the synthetic partner, the versions, the service levels, the business date and the lists are fixture and reference data (BR-S9-002).
- No personal data in logs, events, workflow inputs or reports: every key is synthetic and the reads carry codes, dates and amounts only.
- Service data only through the owner's contract: the panel and the instruction from S9, the lists and the case from P3, the decision log and the rule rows from P7, the session from P4; never a direct schema read and never another service's table (DP-01, DP-07).
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would (DP-11, DP-13).
- No invented operation: only the six operations of §12.2, and no reference-load endpoint, because the map publishes none for the partner panel.
- A list has one source: a value the partner read returns that the reference-data contract does not hold fails the run, and no copy is accepted as a pass (DP-07).
- A new version never re-prices issued work: an instruction read under a different version from the one it was issued under fails the run.
- A stub pass is never reported as a real pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner, and the fault switch is reset before and after each run.
- A failing criterion is fixed in the owning service or raised as a gap; it is never waived in the script.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of the placement slice of rwb-partner, split from RWB-E6-031. It fixes the three operations on `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13) — the placement, the firm's instruction read and the panel read — the `InstructionRequest`, `Instruction` and `Partner` elements, the decision-record element of DP-03 with the scorecard and rule versions, the consumed rows of rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-decision and rwb-access, the one event of the placement, the rights, the error envelope, the tables and the fakes. It declares no enumeration for the instruction status and no body that a source publishes. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the placement slice of rwb-partner — the three operations on `/api/recovery/partner/v1`, the request and answer elements, the instruction event, the decision record with its rule and scorecard versions, the four consumed rows, the rights, the error envelope and the fakes**, so that **the app story, SCR-35, the firm-facing portal and the wave 4 harness build against one fixed, testable contract on Day 1, and a property, a consumed row or an answer shape can never drift between rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-decision and rwb-access without a failing build**.

It is the contract half of legacy RWB-E6-031. It owns:

- the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the placement slice and the naming baseline of the service;
- the `InstructionRequest`, `Instruction` and `Partner` elements, their required lists and their limits;
- the decision-record element, with the rule ID, the rule version and the scorecard version as required properties;
- the four consumed rows and the placeholder wherever a source gives no operation name;
- `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` on `rwb.partner.events.v1` with its outbox rule;
- the rights of each operation and the error envelope with one message ID per condition;
- the tables the slice touches and the seven fakes;
- the contract tests: schema validation, the additive rule, the drift test, the absence tests and the boundary test.

It does not own the behaviour behind the operations, which is RWB-S9-E6031-APP; the panel data of FEAT-PRM-02; the override of FEAT-PRM-04; the accept, result and invoice operations of the later stories; the case, the products, the rule package, the ledger and the right, which belong to P3, P1, P7 and P4; and the composite route of SCR-35, which is RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy feature touched five boundaries at once — the panel, the scorecard, the score, the decision log and a screen — inside one module. The target splits them: rwb-case owns the case, rwb-source-data owns the measured return and the score, rwb-decision owns the rule package and the ledger, rwb-access owns the right, and rwb-partner owns the panel, the instruction and the pick. Each boundary is a contract another team builds against, so each is fixed before the app story starts.

Three properties make the baseline worth its own story. The **scorecard version** is required in the record: a pick recorded against "current" cannot be replayed, and the panel and the scorecard are versioned data (BR-S9-003). The **rank order** is answerable, so a pick can be defended without the app exposing its internals. And the **partner is absent from the request**: the caller says what work it is and the service picks; naming a partner is the override of FEAT-PRM-04 and never the default path, which keeps rotation and favouritism out of the contract itself.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema and login `rwb_partner`, base `/api/recovery/partner/v1`, topic `rwb.partner.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner` (Template and Rules §R4; context pack). It records that this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and no grant on `rwb_case`, so DP-05 is declared as a prohibition and the score and the measured return are consumed on the owner's contract only.

Five points are carried as gaps and assumptions rather than decided quietly: the plan's C row is None while the slice consumes four rows, and DP-04, DP-07, DP-08, DP-09 and DP-10 are absent from the pattern set although the slice evaluates a rule, reads versioned reference data, checks a right, publishes a fact and starts a workflow (ASM-5374, ASM-5375); no source publishes the placement request body or the instruction's property names (ASM-5372, ASM-5373); no source publishes a status vocabulary for an instruction (GAP-3111); and the error set of the three operations beyond the legacy messages is not published (ASM-5376).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL and RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the queue and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the pagination and filter convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline; where this document narrows them it says so.
- Ownership is taken from the context pack and the Ownership Map only: `partner`, `partner_instruction` and `partner_user` are S9's, `recovery_case` and the work assignment are P3's, every `v_ace_*` view and the two products are P1's, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are P7's, the capability area and the right are P4's. This document never declares another service's table or operation as its own.
- The rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-decision and rwb-access rows of §12.2 are published with their fakes, so every consumed row names a real owner document; they are not in this story's contract-dependency row, which is None, and the absence is recorded (GAP-3111; ASM-5374).
- The panel of FEAT-PRM-02 is populated and versioned; the scorecard and the panel carry the version the record requires (ASM-5371).
- The rule package of rwb-decision carries the scorecard rule with its ID and version in force (ASM-5374).
- The three tables arrive with the DB story of this service; this baseline declares shapes and creates no table, no column and no migration.
- The outbox and inbox library (DP-09) and the workflow kit (DP-10) are the platform dependencies of the event and the clock this baseline declares, and neither is in the plan's H row (ASM-5375).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 and sits in contract group `CG-W4` by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-partner for this slice: the three operations with their requests, answers, rights and error responses.
2. Fix the `InstructionRequest` and `Instruction` elements, with the scorecard version and the rule version in the record, and with no partner in the request (ASM-5372, ASM-5373).
3. Fix the `Partner` element against the panel fields DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-006, and carry DF-PRT-007 as a gap rather than a guessed property.
4. Fix the decision-record element of DP-03, written before the instruction exists and carrying the rank order behind the pick.
5. Fix the four consumed rows and mark with the placeholder every operation name a source does not give.
6. Declare the one event of the placement, its topic, its key and its payload, and declare that nothing is consumed.
7. Record the naming baseline, the tables, the capability area and the rights, and that no value of the scorecard is a property.
8. Publish the contract tables of section 12 and the fakes of 12.8.
9. Add the contract tests of section 16, including the drift test against the fakes and the absence tests.
10. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-S9-E6031-APP, SCR-35, SCR-34, the partner gateway and the wave 4 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A request or answer body fails schema validation | The schema lint fails the build; a deployed service answers 400 or 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC2 |
| X2 | A property is renamed or removed inside major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC2, AC7 |
| X3 | A fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC7 |
| X4 | A consumed row carries a field list or an operation name no source gives | The row carries the placeholder and the fake is derived from the published document | None | AC3 |
| X5 | The document declares a property the sources do not publish, such as a score, a weight, a threshold, a partner share, a rotation position or a status enumeration | The review fails the baseline and the absence test fails the build | None | AC2, AC5 |
| X6 | The document declares another service's operation as provided, a `v_ace_*` path, a `recovery_case` property or a rule row | The review fails the baseline and the boundary test fails the build | None | AC3, AC7 |
| X7 | The document declares a second event of this slice, a subscription or a Schedule | The absence test fails the build | None | AC5 |
| X8 | The rights of the operations are not the ones the API sheet and the legacy permission table give | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC6 |
| X9 | A partner is named in the placement request | The review fails the baseline: the pick is the service's and naming a partner is the override story | None | AC2 |

X1 to X3 are the shape and drift paths, X4 and X5 are the "no invented value" rule, X6 and X7 are the ownership and the call-type boundary, and X8 and X9 are the access and the anti-override rules.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the context pack, the API sheet, the legacy story and the published owner contracts of rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-decision and rwb-access only |
| Negotiable | The example values and the fake fixtures are settled in the baseline review; the operations, the base, the topic, the queue and the schema are fixed by the architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks RWB-S9-E6031-APP, SCR-35, the firm-facing portal and the wave 4 harness on Day 1, and the four owner teams on the same day |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, nine contract tables, seven fakes and eight contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the placement slice of rwb-partner

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the ownership of partner, partner_instruction and partner_user is S9, of recovery_case is P3, of every v_ace_* view and the two products is P1, of decision_log_entry and rule_row is P7 and of the right is P4
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 The three operations are declared on the partner base with their rights and errors (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-partner is published with this change
    When it is validated against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions with the case reference in the path and status 201 on success, GET /partner/instructions and GET /partners, under the base /api/recovery/partner/v1 and owned by rwb-partner
    Then the placement declares the Idempotency-Key header and the repeated key answering the first instruction, and declares no partner in its body
    Then the answers 401, 403, 409, 422 and 503 are declared with one envelope and one message ID per condition
    Then no operation of accept, decline, result, invoice, override, panel maintenance or scorecard publication is declared by this document

  Scenario: AC2 The request, instruction and partner elements are fixed and no scorecard value is a property (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the element section of the baseline
    When it is compared with the legacy Data table, the API sheet and the panel fields
    Then the InstructionRequest element declares the instruction type, the placement type and the rule version the caller expects, and nothing else; the placement request carries no partner
    Then the Instruction element declares the instruction reference, the case reference, the partner reference, the partner code, the instruction type, the status, instructed_at and due_at
    Then the Partner element declares partner code, partner name, partner type, panel status, contract end and the capacity state
    Then no element declares a score, a weight, a threshold, a partner share, a rotation position or a rank as a number of its own, and the rank order is returned as evidence and never accepted as input
    Then no enumeration is declared for the instruction status, because no source read for this WP publishes one (GAP-3111; ASM-5373)
    Then the property names the sources do not give are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3111; ASM-5372) and are fixed by this baseline as design, not as a business value

  Scenario: AC3 The four consumed rows are declared and the facts stay with their owners (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed rows of the baseline
    When they are compared with the ownership of the context pack
    Then the case read is declared as consumed from P3 rwb-case, with the case reference, its state, its placement requirement and the assignment reference
    Then the measured return, the score and the freshness are declared as consumed from P1 rwb-source-data as DP08, DP11 and the freshness read, with the business date and the load time of each product
    Then the scorecard rule and its version are declared as consumed from P7 rwb-decision, and the session and the right from P4 rwb-access
    Then the operation names of the four rows are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3111; ASM-5374) and each row carries the placeholder
    Then the document declares no v_ace_* path, no v_ace_* property, no recovery_case property and no grant on any rwb_* schema of another owner
    Then each row is one hop with a 2 s budget, a breaker and no retry of its own (DP-11, ADR-020)

  Scenario: AC4 The decision-record element is declared with its rule and scorecard versions (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision and data sections of the baseline
    When they are compared with the library schema and the tables of S9
    Then one decision record is declared per placement, written through the local library on the shared rwb.decision-record.v1 before the instruction exists, and a failed write leaves nothing placed with MSG-P7-003
    Then the record requires the rule ID, the rule version, the scorecard version, the case reference, the instruction type, the candidate set with each partner's measured return, the pick and the decided-at time
    Then the record carries no personal data and no scorecard value as a literal
    Then the document declares the three tables of S9 and the library objects created in rwb_partner, and creates no table, column or migration
    Then the scorecard and the panel are declared as versioned reference data of the service, and the absence of DP-07 from the pattern set is recorded rather than added (ASM-5371, ASM-5374)

  Scenario: AC5 The instruction event is declared once on the partner topic and nothing is consumed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the event section of the baseline
    When it is compared with the naming rule, the ownership rows and the call-type rules
    Then rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1 is declared as the one event of the slice, on rwb.partner.events.v1 with its retry and .dlt topics, keyed by the case reference
    Then its payload carries identifiers, the instruction type, instructed_at, due_at, the rule version and the scorecard version, and no customer data
    Then the event is written through the outbox in the placement transaction, one per placement, and its legacy identifier is EV-20 or EV-21 with the mapping Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3111; ASM-5375)
    Then the document declares no subscription of this slice and no Temporal Schedule, because the placement is commanded by the issueInstruction activity and S9 owns no job
    Then the workflow InstructionWorkflow is declared with its partner clock on queue rwb-partner in namespace rwb-recovery

  Scenario: AC6 The rights and the error envelope are fixed per operation (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the access sections of the baseline
    When they are compared with the API sheet and the legacy permission table
    Then POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions declares the capability area Partner portal with right C and the scope applied
    Then GET /partner/instructions and GET /partners declare right R, and the accept, result and invoice rights of the module are not declared here
    Then the roles of the legacy permission table are carried unchanged and the C holders are read from its U row, which is recorded as an assumption (ASM-5377)
    Then a role without the right is described as refused with MSG-P4-002, and the envelope carries one message ID per condition

  Scenario: AC7 The seven fakes, the drift test and the absence tests close the baseline (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fakes of the baseline
    When each is compared with the document and the document with the ownership map
    Then seven fakes answer the document, including the case, the two products with freshness, the rule, the session, the decision-record stub and the two edge routes
    Then a property added, renamed or removed inside major version 1 fails a contract test
    Then a declared score, weight, threshold, rank input, status enumeration, second event, subscription, Schedule, v_ace_* path or recovery_case property fails an absence test
    Then the partner gateway is declared as the edge for the firm-facing read and gateway-bff for the staff screen, and neither is declared as provided by this service (ASM-5378)
```

The seven criteria are new and test only the contract. The four legacy criteria of RWB-E6-031 are not copied here: they are owned by RWB-S9-E6031-APP and RWB-ITG-E6031-ITG, and the four legacy cases appear in section 16 as the contract half of the surfaces they exercise.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The contract is the only place the shape is fixed; the app story, the screens and the harness build against it and never against a service's internal type | ADR-020; Template and Rules §R5.4 |
| BR2 | The base is `/api/recovery/partner/v1`, the topic `rwb.partner.events.v1`, the queue `rwb-partner`, the schema `rwb_partner` and the package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner`; no document names another service's base or topic as its own | DP-13, DP-14; context pack |
| BR3 | The pick is the service's: the placement request carries no partner, and naming one is the override of FEAT-PRM-04 | R-WO-30; legacy RWB-E6-031; ASM-5372 |
| BR4 | The record requires the rule ID, the rule version and the scorecard version, written before the instruction exists | DP-03; BR-S9-003 |
| BR5 | The measured return, the score, the case, the rule and the right stay with their owners: the document declares them as consumed, never as provided, and no `v_ace_*` property exists | DP-05, DP-01; context pack slide 8 |
| BR6 | No score, weight, threshold, share, rotation position or status enumeration enters the document; every such value is reference data or a rule row | Legacy Guardrails; ASM-5373, ASM-5376 |
| BR7 | One event per placement, through the outbox, with identifiers only; nothing in this slice consumes an event or registers a Schedule | ADR-015; ASM-5375 |
| BR8 | Within major version 1 the document is additive only; a rename or a removal needs a new major version | ADR-020 |
| BR9 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, a type, a status, two timestamps and a version only | Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17) |

The rule rows the slice answers to are those of R-WO-30 (place the account with the agency chosen on measured return and send the instruction the same day), R-WO-31 (no agency on the panel has capacity: hold and escalate), R-UNI-29 (a conduct breach suspends allocation) and R-UNI-45 (re-select on the scorecard, re-issue and restart the clock), governed in rwb-decision and copied character for character in RWB-S9-E6031-APP section 8. This baseline names them and declares none of them as a property.

##### 9. State transitions

The contract fixes the values an instruction may carry, not the machine that moves them.

| Element | Property | Fixed by the baseline |
|---|---|---|
| Instruction | status | A string, with `SENT` as the value the placement writes; no enumeration, because no source read for this WP publishes the vocabulary (GAP-3111; ASM-5373) |
| Instruction | instructed_at | Required, set by the service at the placement, never by the caller |
| Instruction | due_at | Required, derived from the service level of the instruction type and the partner type |
| Instruction | partner reference and code | Required on the answer, absent from the request |
| Partner | panel status and capacity | Read-only on the panel answer; the values are reference data of the panel story |

The transitions themselves belong to the app story and to the accept, decline, result and recall stories of the module; a baseline that published a state machine would publish a vocabulary no source holds.

| The owners of rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-decision and rwb-access | Confirm the four consumed rows and their operation names; the placeholder stands until each confirms |
| rwb-access | Confirms the capability area "Partner portal" and the rights C and R of the three operations |
| RWB-S9-E6031-APP | Consumes the baseline; a change it needs is a change of this document, not a private variant |
| RWB-ITG-E6031-ITG | Consumes the baseline as the stub set of the wave 4 run |

No right is exercised through this document: it declares the rights of operations that the app story builds and the guard of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON enforces. DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set, and the absence is recorded (ASM-5374).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-partner (S9); base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13). Frozen by this baseline.

| Method | Path | Request | Answer | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/instructions` | `InstructionRequest`: instruction type, placement type, rule version; no partner | `Instruction`, status 201 | Partner portal C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |
| GET | `/partner/instructions` | Filters by status and instruction type, paged | A page of `Instruction`, the firm's own only | Partner portal R | None, a safe read |
| GET | `/partners` | Filters by partner type, panel status and capacity, paged | A page of `Partner` | Partner portal R | None, a safe read |

The operations are the three the API sheet gives the module on this path family (Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3: "Issue an instruction to a partner by rule", "List the instructions placed with the caller's firm", and the panel read of the ownership rows). The error set is 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 for an unknown case, 409 for a replay that conflicts, 422 with MSG-GEN-001, 503 when a consumed contract or the library does not answer, and the data-freshness answer of MSG-P1-001 where the score product is behind its business date.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The case read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3111; ASM-5374)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference, its state, its placement requirement and the assignment reference |
| DP08 Partner performance, DP11 Scores and route economics and the freshness read (operation names Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3111; ASM-5374)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The measured return per partner, the score behind the pick, the business date and load time of each product |
| The scorecard rule read in force (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3111; ASM-5374)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The rule, its version and the ledger confirmation of the record |
| The session and the right of the caller (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3111; ASM-5377)) | `/api/recovery/access/v1` | P4 rwb-access | The capability area and the right of the caller |

Each row is one hop with a 2 s budget, a breaker and a GET retried once with jitter (ADR-020). The rows are class C dependencies in fact while this story's C row is None; the story declares them, fakes them and records the absence (GAP-3111; ASM-5374).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Key | Payload | Delivery |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1`, with its retry and `.dlt` topics | the case reference | The instruction, the case, the partner, the instruction type, `instructed_at`, `due_at`, the rule version, the scorecard version | Outbox in the placement transaction, relayed after the commit, one per placement, CloudEvents envelope |

Its legacy identifier is EV-20 or EV-21 and the mapping of the two identifiers to their names is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3111; ASM-5375); the name follows the naming rule of §R4. DP-09 is not in this key's pattern set, and the outbox and inbox library it requires is recorded (ASM-5375).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The placement is a command and the result is needed, so the call type is the `issueInstruction` activity of §12.5 (context pack, slide 12 notes). The baseline therefore declares no subscription, and a stub set that subscribes to the write-off topic to learn of a placement fails the absence test.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `InstructionWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per instruction | `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the instruction reference, the partner, the partner type, the instruction type and the due date; signals: accept, decline, result and recall; query: the remaining partner clock |
| `issueInstruction` | Activity | `rwb-partner` | The case reference, the instruction type, the placement type and the rule version in; the `Instruction` out. The activity name is the one the context pack's call-type notes give |

The workflow ID is the instruction reference, so a replay resolves to the same execution. DP-10 is not in this key's pattern set and the workflow kit RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is recorded (ASM-5375).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. S9 owns no job, so the baseline registers no Temporal Schedule and no Quartz row; the partner clock of §12.5 is a timer, not a schedule.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |

| partner | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The panel; read by this slice and written by the panel story |
| partner_instruction | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The instruction of one placement |
| partner_user | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The portal user of a firm; named for the ownership record, not touched here |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_partner` | The local decision record of the pick (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_partner` | The replay key and the answer it holds |
| outbox_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_partner` | The row of `InstructionIssued` |

Not owned and never declared as a property: `recovery_case` and `assignment` (P3), every `v_ace_*` view (P1), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6). No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01), and no table is created by this baseline.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Artefacts.** One OpenAPI 3.1 document `rwb-partner.openapi.v1.yaml` for the placement slice, one JSON Schema library for the three elements and the two event rows, one fake set and one contract test suite. Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner`; no business code is written here.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 fixes the record element and the transaction rule; DP-05 is declared as a prohibition, because the service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and takes the score and the measured return on the P1 contract; DP-13 fixes the base of the three operations; DP-19 fixes the two edges, gateway-bff for the staff screen and the partner gateway for the firm-facing read. DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-08, DP-09 and DP-10 are absent from the pattern set although the slice names a rule, versioned reference data, a right, an event and a workflow; each absence is recorded (ASM-5374, ASM-5375, ASM-5377).

**Components of the baseline**

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| OpenAPI document | The three operations, their parameters, their bodies, their answers and their error responses |
| Element library | `InstructionRequest`, `Instruction`, `Partner` and the decision-record element, with their required lists and limits |
| Event schema | `InstructionIssued` and the envelope of the topic |
| Fake set and stub generator | Seven fakes derived from the document |
| Contract test suite | Schema lint, additive rule, drift, absence and boundary tests |
| Naming and access annex | The base, the topic, the queue, the schema, the package, the capability area and the rights |

**Contract tests.** Schema validation of every request and answer; the additive rule inside major version 1; the drift test of each fake against the document; the absence tests for a score, a weight, a threshold, a rank input, a status enumeration, a second event, a subscription, a Schedule, a `v_ace_*` path and a `recovery_case` property; the boundary test that no operation of another owner is declared as provided; and the access test that the rights are the ones the API sheet and the legacy permission table give.

**Configuration and reference data.** The examples and the fixtures are synthetic and are configuration of the test suite, never of the document. The scorecard weights, the panel thresholds, the capacity rule, the instruction types and the service levels stay reference data and rule rows of their owners; the document declares none of them.

**Done when.** The document validates, the nine contract tables of section 12 are complete, the seven fakes match it, the drift and absence tests pass, the four owners have confirmed their rows or their placeholder stands, and the baseline is tagged and handed to RWB-S9-E6031-APP, SCR-35, the partner gateway and the wave 4 harness.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request, a case or a panel row is absent or invalid | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right of the operation calls it | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the instruction exists | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | A data product behind the pick is behind its business date | The text is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3111; ASM-5376) |

The first three IDs and their text are the legacy message set of RWB-E6-031, copied unchanged. MSG-P1-001 is the data-freshness message the wave 4 key uses for the same condition; its text is not in this WP's read set, so the row carries the placeholder and the baseline declares no further message text of its own (ASM-5376).

##### 15. Screens and states

The baseline fixes no screen. SCR-35 Placement and allocation reads the placement answer through the gateway-bff composite route and SCR-34 Partner list reads the panel; the field list of both belongs to RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the composite route is declared here only as a consumed edge (DP-19). The firm-facing view is `GET /partner/instructions` behind the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0), and its route table is the edge story's (ASM-5378).

The legacy level maps to `Contract` here because the artefact under test is the contract. The five `TC-S9-E6031-CON-` cases are new. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: no score, weight, threshold, share, rotation position, instruction-type value or status enumeration appears in the document or in a schema default.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, a type, a status, two timestamps and a version only, and every example is synthetic.
- The score and the measured return stay with rwb-source-data, the case with rwb-case, the rule with rwb-decision and the right with rwb-access: the document declares them as consumed and never as provided, and no `v_ace_*` path exists (BR5).
- The partner is never an input: the request carries the work, not the partner, and the override is a separate contract (BR3).
- One base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- Nothing is consumed and nothing is scheduled by this slice: an event subscription or a Schedule in the document fails the absence test (BR7).
- The error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule, the decision-record library and the outbox library come from the platform; this story narrows them and never redefines them.
- Within major version 1 the document is additive only; a rename or a removal opens a new major version (BR8).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the placement slice of RWB-E6-031 in rwb-partner. Legacy AC2 is kept word for word with its origin tag and is the only legacy criterion this story owns; AC1 of the legacy key is proved end to end by RWB-ITG-E6031-ITG. The story builds the scorecard pick over the panel of `rwb_partner` and the measured return of rwb-source-data, the local decision record written before the instruction exists (DP-03), one `partner_instruction` row and one `InstructionIssued` fact per placement, and the three operations the API sheet gives this module on base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13, API-S9-002 and API-S9-003 as the sheet numbers them), reached by staff through the gateway-bff composite route and by partners through the partner gateway (DP-19). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **partner and agency manager**, I want **the Workbench to place work with the partner the scorecard rule picks, not by rotation or habit**, so that **partners are placed, paid and measured by rule**.

This is the placement slice of legacy RWB-E6-031. It owns:

- legacy AC2, copied verbatim with its origin tag, and the message and the record it depends on;
- the scorecard pick: the eligible partners of the panel, ranked on measured return, with the top-ranked partner chosen and the rank order kept as evidence;
- the anti-rotation rule in code form: no rotation counter, no round-robin position, no fixed share and no last-placed memory is read, stored or honoured anywhere on the path;
- the hold of R-WO-31 when no partner on the panel has capacity;
- the decision record of the pick, written before the instruction exists (DP-03), carrying the rule ID, the rule version and the scorecard version;
- one `partner_instruction` row per placement in `rwb_partner`, with the partner, the case, the instruction type, the status and the two clock dates;
- `InstructionWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and its partner clock, started once per instruction;
- `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions`, `GET /partner/instructions` and `GET /partners` on `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13), the SCR-35 placement state behind the gateway-bff composite route and the partner-facing read behind the partner gateway (DP-19);
- the one event of the placement, `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` on `rwb.partner.events.v1`.

It does not own: the published shape of the three operations, the elements, the rights, the error set and the fakes, which are RWB-S9-E6031-CON; the panel and fee schedule as data (FEAT-PRM-02, legacy RWB-E6-030); the override with a reason (FEAT-PRM-04, RWB-S9-E6032-APP); the result received into the case (FEAT-PRM-05, RWB-S9-E6033-APP); the agency placement of a charged-off account (FEAT-PRM-06) and the fee (FEAT-PRM-07); the monthly scorecard (FEAT-PRM-08); the case of record and the work assignment, which are rwb-case's (P3); the measured return and the score products, which are rwb-source-data's (P1); the rule package and the decision ledger, which are rwb-decision's (P7); the right, which is rwb-access's (P4); and the deployment of this build, which is the operations story of this legacy key.

##### 2. Business rationale

The objective is one sentence of the specification: FEAT-PRM-03 "Allocate work by measured return — Places work with the partner the scorecard rule picks, not by rotation or habit" (Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3, feature row; legacy RWB-E6-031). What D-RCV-60 changes is where each part of that sentence lives.

- **The panel is this service's data.** `partner`, `partner_instruction` and `partner_user` are S9's three tables in `rwb_partner` (context pack ownership rows), so the eligible set, the capacity state and the instruction that carries the pick are written here and nowhere else.
- **The number behind the pick is not this service's to invent.** The measured return of a partner is held as DP08 Partner performance, the Workbench product over this service's own partner and instruction records, and the score the pick rests on is DP11 Scores and route economics over `v_ace_score`; both are read on rwb-source-data's contract with their business date, and this service never reads an ACE view (DP-05).
- **The rule is governed, not coded.** The scorecard rule and its version are rule rows governed in rwb-decision; the evaluation runs here, so the same facts give the same pick and the version is recorded with the outcome. DP-04 is not part of this key's pattern set, and the absence is recorded rather than papered over (ASM-5364).
- **The version is what makes a pick defensible.** A pick recorded against "current" cannot be replayed after the panel or the scorecard moves, so the record carries the rule ID, the rule version and the scorecard version, and the panel and the scorecard are versioned data (BR-S9-003 as the wave 4 key states it).
- **Rotation is the failure this story removes.** A partner that improves gets work and a partner whose measured return falls stops getting it; nothing on the path counts what it placed last, and the rank order is kept in the record so the choice can be read back.
- **No capacity is a hold, not a placement.** R-WO-31 places nothing and escalates on the timer; a queue is never cleared by placing work where it cannot be worked.
- **The clock is the partner's service level, not a job.** S9 owns no job (context pack, jobs: none); the clock of an instruction is the `InstructionWorkflow` timer for the instruction type and partner type, and a Temporal Schedule is neither needed nor declared.
- **The edge has two faces.** Staff reach the placement on SCR-35 through gateway-bff; a firm reads its instructions and accepts them through the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) that fronts rwb-partner (context pack, slide 8). DP-19 covers the composite route that carries the staff screen.

No business value moves: the scorecard weights, the panel thresholds, the capacity rule, the instruction types, the service level of each partner type and the ranking order are reference data or rule rows read with their version, never constants of the code.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S9-E6031-CON is published: the three operations, their elements, the rights, the error envelope, the consumed rows and the fakes are baselined and handed to this story.
- The panel is populated as FEAT-PRM-02 leaves it: partner code, name, type, panel status, contract end, capacity state, fee schedule and service level, each with its version. Where a field of the panel beyond the seven the legacy Data table lists is needed, its name and list of values are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3110; ASM-5362).
- The rwb-source-data products are published with their fakes: DP08 Partner performance, DP11 Scores and route economics and the freshness read that carries the business date and the load time of each product. Their operation names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3110; ASM-5362).
- The rwb-decision rule read is published with its fake and answers the scorecard rule at the version in force; its operation name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3110; ASM-5364).
- The rwb-case case read is published with its fake and answers the case reference, its state, its placement requirement and the work assignment reference; its operation name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3110; ASM-5368).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: the local decision-record library writes in the caller's transaction and a failed write stops the placement, so the row and its record commit together or not at all (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-35 reaches this service through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, and no screen calls a service directly (DP-19). The partner-facing reads pass the partner gateway, whose route table is the edge story's.
- `partner`, `partner_instruction` and `partner_user` exist in schema `rwb_partner` from the DB story of this service; this story adds no table, no column and no migration.
- The service runs as its own login on `rwb_partner`, holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `v_ace_score` or `rwb_case` is refused by the database and fails the boundary test.
- The partner clock of each instruction type is the service level of the panel row; its duration per partner type is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3110; ASM-5367).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-S9-E6031-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. A caller stage starts the placement: on R-WO-30 the write-off stage moves the case to `PLACEMENT_DECIDED` and calls the `issueInstruction` activity on queue `rwb-partner` with the case reference, the instruction type, the placement type and the rule version; the litigation, asset and debt-sale stages use the same activity when they instruct a firm, a vendor or a broker (context pack, slide 12 notes; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, R-WO-30). A staff caller may drive the same path through `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions`.
2. The activity reads the case on rwb-case, one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker: the case reference, its state, its placement requirement and the assignment reference. It reads no `recovery_case` row (ASM-5368).
3. It builds the eligible set from `rwb_partner`: the partners of the required type whose `panel_status` admits allocation, whose `contract_end` has not passed and whose capacity is open. A partner under a conduct suspension is out of the set (R-UNI-29).
4. It reads the scorecard rule at its version in force from rwb-decision and the measured return of each eligible partner from DP08, with the business date of the product (ASM-5364).
5. It reads the score the pick rests on from DP11 and the freshness of that product. Where the product is behind its business date the run stops as X4: nothing is placed (DP-05; ASM-5369).
6. `ScorecardRanker` orders the eligible partners on measured return as the scorecard rule defines it and returns the order with the value behind each position. The order is kept for the record; it is never replaced by a rotation counter, a round-robin position, a last-placed pointer or a fixed share, and no such field exists in `rwb_partner`.
7. The top-ranked partner is the pick. Where the panel has no eligible partner or no open capacity, the run is held under R-WO-31 with no row, no event and the case unchanged, and the escalation is the timer of the caller's stage.
8. `PartnerDecisionRecordWriter` writes one decision record through the local decision-record library, **before the instruction exists**: the case reference, the instruction type, the candidate set with each partner's measured return, the pick, the rule ID, the rule version, the scorecard version, the business date of the products and the decided-at time. A failed write stops the run with nothing changed (legacy AC2; DP-03).
9. `InstructionWriter` inserts one `partner_instruction` row and its idempotency row in one `rwb_partner` transaction, with the instruction type, the partner, the case, `instructed_at`, the `due_at` the partner type's service level gives and the status `SENT` (ASM-5367).
10. `InstructionWorkflow` starts once for the instruction on queue `rwb-partner` with the instruction reference, the partner type and the due date, and holds the partner clock for that instruction type.
11. The outbox relay publishes `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` on `rwb.partner.events.v1` with the identifiers only. The event is written by the same transaction as the row, so the row and the fact cannot disagree (DP-09 is a real dependency of this step and is not in the plan's H row: ASM-5365).
12. The activity answers the caller with the instruction, the partner, the instruction type, `instructed_at`, `due_at` and the status; the caller's stage applies its own case move. This service writes no case state.
13. SCR-35 Placement and allocation shows the pick, the partner and the instruction in its loading and list states from this service through the gateway-bff composite route; the firm reads the same instruction through `GET /partner/instructions` behind the partner gateway (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The local decision record cannot be written | The transaction writes nothing: no instruction row, no event, no clock, and the caller gets no instruction | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, TC-E6-031-02, TC-E6-031-04 |
| X2 | The caller does not hold the Partner portal C right of the placement | 403 before any read; nothing is placed and no record is written | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E6-031-03, AC7 |
| X3 | No partner on the panel is eligible, or none has open capacity | R-WO-31 holds the placement: no row, no event, no clock, the case unchanged, escalation on the caller's timer; no message ID is named for the hold | None named | AC4, TC-S9-E6031-01 |
| X4 | The DP11 score product is behind its business date | The run stops before any write; nothing is placed and the hold is reported with the product and its date | MSG-P1-001, whose text is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3110; ASM-5369) | AC5 |
| X5 | A consumed contract does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The activity retries on the workflow's own schedule; nothing is written; a screen caller sees 503 with the platform envelope | None | AC1, X3 |
| X6 | The same placement arrives twice, or with the same `Idempotency-Key` | One row, one record, one event and one clock; the repeat returns the first answer | None | AC6, TC-S9-E6031-02 |
| X7 | The picked partner is suspended or its contract ends between the read and the write | The writer re-reads the panel row once inside the transaction and re-picks from the remaining rank order; if none remains, X3 | None | AC4 |
| X8 | A statement reaches another `rwb_*` schema, a `v_ace_*` view or a `recovery_case` row | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | AC7, section 17 |

X1 is legacy AC2 carried onto the slice, X2 is the third and fourth legacy test case, X3 to X7 are the panel, product and replay paths the rule names, and X8 is the schema and ACE boundary. The override with a reason is not an exception here: it is FEAT-PRM-04 and RWB-S9-E6032-APP.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-S9-E6031-CON, the decision-record stub and the rwb-case, rwb-source-data and rwb-decision fakes, on its own schema, and needs no live P1, P3 or P7 |
| Negotiable | The component names, the record's input payload and the activity's input shape are this story's choice; the rule, the messages, the operations, the tables, the topic and the queue are fixed |
| Valuable | Work goes to the partner with the best measured return, the choice is replayable with its versions, and no case is placed by habit |
| Estimable | One activity, one ranker, one record write, one row writer, one workflow start, four clients, one event and one read-only screen fragment |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on a synthetic panel, synthetic products with a business date and the contract fakes, plus the hold, the stale product, the replay and the boundary cases |
