AC2 is the legacy criterion word for word with its origin tag, and nothing else is added to it. AC1, AC3 to AC7 are new and test only what this story builds; the cross-service journey that legacy AC1 describes is proved by RWB-ITG-E6031-ITG and is not copied here. The `decision log` of the legacy text is the local decision record of DP-03 in `rwb_partner`, with the central `decision_log_entry` ledger of rwb-decision behind it.

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Decision | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-WO-30 | Write-off | D9 | PLACEMENT_DECIDED | SOFT_RECOVERY_SELECTED | placement_type = soft_recovery and an agency on the panel has capacity | Place the account with the agency chosen on measured return and send the instruction | PLACED_WITH_AGENCY | Outsourced agency | Partner Portal, OA portal | same day on the portal |
| R-WO-31 | Write-off | D9 | PLACEMENT_DECIDED | NO_AGENCY_CAPACITY | no agency on the panel has capacity | Hold the placement and escalate on the timer | PLACEMENT_DECIDED | Partner and agency manager | Partner Portal | 5 working days |
| R-UNI-29 | Universal rules | All | ANY_ACTIVE | PARTNER_CONDUCT_BREACH | a conduct or complaint breach is upheld against the partner | Suspend allocation, recall the affected cases, report to the partner review | PARTNER_RECALLED | Partner and agency manager | Partner Portal | same day |
| R-UNI-45 | Universal rules | All | PARTNER_RECALLED | PARTNER_RESELECTED | the next partner is selected on the scorecard | Re-issue the instruction and restart the partner clock | ROUTE_D6_REOPEN | Partner and agency manager | Partner Portal | 2 working days |
| R-LIT-23 | Litigation | D7 | PACK_VERIFIED | PACK_APPROVED | pack_verified_at set | Select the law firm by rule from the panel | FIRM_SELECTION | Workbench | Rules component, partner performance data | Same day |
| R-DIS-30 | Asset disposal | D8.1 to D8.3 | FLOOR_APPROVED | VENDOR_REQUIRED | asset_type = vehicle | Allocate the asset to the vendor with the highest predicted price on the scorecard, not by distance | VENDOR_ALLOCATED | Auction and remarketing vendor | Rules component, Partner Portal | 2 working days |

The six rows are the rows of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, copied character for character. Their owner and systems columns name business roles and systems, not services: in the target the "Rules component" and the "partner performance data" are the scorecard rule of rwb-decision and the measured return of rwb-source-data read on their contracts, "Partner Portal" and "OA portal" are screens of this service's edge, and the case moves are written by rwb-case on the answer of this story. R-WO-30 and R-WO-31 are the placement itself; R-UNI-29 and R-UNI-45 are the suspension and the re-selection that re-enter the same pick; R-LIT-23 and R-DIS-30 show that one scorecard rule serves the law-firm, vendor and agency panels, which is why the pick is a service capability and not a write-off-only branch.

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The panel, the partner users and the instructions are S9's: `partner`, `partner_instruction` and `partner_user` in `rwb_partner`, and no other service writes them | Context pack ownership rows; Arch v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | The pick is by measured return against the scorecard, never by rotation, fixed share or last placed; the rank order is kept with the pick | REQ-S9-003; R-WO-30; legacy RWB-E6-031 |
| BR3 | The scorecard and the panel are versioned data and the version is recorded with every pick | ASM-5371; R-WO-30 |
| BR4 | The decision record is written before the instruction exists; a failed write leaves nothing placed and answers MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; legacy AC2 |
| BR5 | The ACE score and the measured return stay with rwb-source-data: this story holds no `v_ace_*` grant and takes both on the owner's contract with their business date | DP-05; context pack slide 8 |
| BR6 | No capacity is a hold and not a placement: R-WO-31 writes nothing and escalates on the caller's timer | R-WO-31 |
| BR7 | One placement carries one instruction, one fact and one clock; the `Idempotency-Key` makes the replay safe | TSD S9 (not in this WP's read set); ASM-5365 |
| BR8 | The case state and the work assignment are rwb-case's: this story reads them and answers the caller, and writes neither | ASM-5368 |
| BR9 | No person name, address, contact value or identity number enters `rwb_partner`, the record, the event, a log or a workflow input | Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR10 | No business value in code: the scorecard weights, the panel thresholds, the capacity rule, the instruction types, the service level by partner type and the rank order are reference data or rule rows read with their version | Legacy Guardrails; FEAT-PRM-02; ASM-5367 |

##### 9. State transitions

The case state is rwb-case's and is not changed here: the caller's stage applies its own move on this story's answer (BR8). What this story owns is the state of the run and the row it writes.

| From (run) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting | The `issueInstruction` activity starts | The case and the panel are read | Ranking |
| Ranking | The rule and the measured return are read | The score product is current | Picking |
| Ranking | The score product is behind its business date | X4 | Held, nothing written, MSG-P1-001 |
| Picking | The rank order has an eligible partner with open capacity | The top-ranked partner is the pick | Recording |
| Picking | No partner is eligible or none has capacity | R-WO-31, X3 | Held, nothing written, escalation on the caller's timer |
| Recording | The record is written | X1 does not fire | Writing the row |
| Recording | The record write fails | X1 | Waiting, nothing changed, MSG-P7-003 |
| Writing the row | The row, the idempotency key and the outbox row commit | The workflow starts | Answered |
| Answered | The clock is running and the fact is relayed | The activity returns | Done for this instruction |

| From (`partner_instruction.status`) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None, no row | A placement under R-WO-30 | The record is written and the panel row still admits allocation | One row, `SENT` |
| None, no row | A hold under R-WO-31 or a stale product | No capacity, no eligible partner, X4 | No row and no clock |
| `SENT` | The partner accepts or declines | The accept operation of this service, a later story of the module | Written there, not here |
| `SENT` | The partner clock passes its due date | R-UNI-25 or R-LIT-28 on the caller's route | Written on the caller's route, not here |

The status vocabulary beyond `SENT` is published by no source read for this WP, so the accept, decline, breach and recall values are recorded as a gap (GAP-3110; ASM-5362) and are not invented here.

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-NPAMGR, RW-AGENCYMG, RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR | Place the work: the Partner portal right C on `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions`, and read the panel and the instructions |
| RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-SALEOFF, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-GUARANT, PT-AGENCY | Hold the Partner portal rights the legacy permission table gives them on the instruction: the U right belongs to the accept and result stories, not to this one |
| The 21 further R roles and 5 further U roles of the legacy permission table | R and U exactly as the table gives them, and no C |
| rwb-partner service identity | Runs the activity and the workflow, reads the case, the products and the rule, writes the record and the row, starts the clock and publishes the fact; it holds no grant on another schema and no `v_ace_*` grant |

The legacy permission table gives the capability area "Partner portal" with right R to the first row's roles and right U to the second row's roles, and the API sheet gives the placement right C ("Partner portal C", Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3). The C holders are read from the legacy U row because the sources name no separate C list, and that reading is an assumption (ASM-5370). DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set: the capability area and the right are declared per operation on the contract and the guard is a service-template capability, so the check is stated here and built on RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-CON (ASM-5370).

##### 11. Data

| Field ID | Entity (owner) | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-PRT-001 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | id | Write: the partner reference the pick names, carried on the instruction |
| DF-PRT-002 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | partner_code | Read: reported on the panel and the instruction answer |
| DF-PRT-003 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | partner_name | Read: the name the screen shows |
| DF-PRT-004 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | partner_type | Read: with the instruction type, the filter of the eligible set and the source of the service level |
| DF-PRT-005 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | panel_status | Read: only a partner whose status admits allocation may be picked; R-UNI-29 suspends allocation |
| DF-PRT-006 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | contract_end | Read: a partner past its contract end is out of the set (R-UNI-26) |
| DF-PRT-007 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | the seventh field of the legacy list | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3110; ASM-5362) |
| partner_instruction (columns) | partner_instruction (S9, `rwb_partner`) | instruction reference, case reference, partner reference, instruction type, status, `instructed_at`, `due_at` | Write: one row per placement. The column list and its field IDs are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3110; ASM-5362) |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (PLT library, created in `rwb_partner`) | rule id, rule version, scorecard version, inputs reference, outcome, decided at | Write through the local library, before the row exists |
| DF-WRK-009 to DF-WRK-016 | assignment (P3 rwb-case) | id, case_id, task_id, assignee_user_id, assigned_at, ended_at and 2 more | Not written and not read as a table: the case and its assignment arrive on the rwb-case contract (ASM-5368) |
| DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279 | v_ace_score (P1) | score_key, account_key, model_code, model_version, score_value, estimate_value and 4 more | Not read: no `v_ace_*` grant. The score arrives on the DP11 contract with its business date |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | rule_row (P7) | rule_id, rule_version, route_set, from_state, event_code and 9 more | Not read as a table: the rule and its version arrive on the package read |
| Scorecard and panel version | panel reference data (S9, `rwb_partner`) | the version of the scorecard and of the panel in force | Read and recorded with the pick (ASM-5371) |

**No new table, no new column and no migration**: the three tables arrive with the DB story of this service, this story writes the instruction row and reads the panel row, and `decision_record`, `idempotency_key` and `outbox_event` are library objects created in `rwb_partner` by the library's own migration (DP-03).

**No personal data.** The rows carry identifiers, a type, a status, two timestamps and a version. No name of a person, address, contact value or identity number enters `rwb_partner`, the record, the event, a log or a workflow input, and every fixture is synthetic. The instruction carries the partner organisation, never the customer.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-partner (S9); base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the behaviour behind the operations whose shape RWB-S9-E6031-CON declares.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/instructions` | The placement request in, the instruction of status 201 out, with the partner the scorecard picks (API-S9-002, "Issue an instruction to a partner by rule") | Partner portal C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |
| GET | `/partner/instructions` | The instructions placed with the caller's firm, with their partner, instruction type, `instructed_at`, `due_at` and status (API-S9-003) | Partner portal R | None, a safe read |
| GET | `/partners` | The panel: partner code, name, type, panel status, contract end and the capacity state | Partner portal R | None, a safe read |

The errors are 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 409 for a replay that conflicts, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503 when a consumed contract or the library does not answer. The element names beyond the three the sources give are the contract's (RWB-S9-E6031-CON), and the accept, result and invoice operations of the module are neither built nor declared here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The case read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3110; ASM-5368)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference, its state, its placement requirement and the assignment reference; read only, faked |
| DP08 Partner performance, DP11 Scores and route economics and their freshness (operation names Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3110; ASM-5362)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The measured return per partner, the score the pick rests on and the business date and load time of each product; faked |
| The scorecard rule read in force (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3110; ASM-5364)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The rule and its version; faked |
| The access session of the caller (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3110; ASM-5370)) | `/api/recovery/access/v1` | P4 rwb-access | The capability area and the right of the caller; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The four rows are contract dependencies of class C in fact while this story's C row is None, so the story builds against their documents and fakes on Day 1 and the absence is recorded (GAP-3110; ASM-5362).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1`, with its retry and `.dlt` topics | the case reference | Identifiers only: the instruction, the case, the partner, the instruction type, `instructed_at`, `due_at`, the rule version and the scorecard version; no customer data |

The event is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the row and relayed after the commit, one event per placement (CloudEvents envelope, ADR-015). Its legacy identifier is EV-20 or EV-21 and the mapping of the two identifiers to their names is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3110; ASM-5363); the name follows the naming rule of §R4. DP-09 is not in this key's pattern set and the outbox and inbox library it needs is recorded (ASM-5365).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The placement is a command, not a fact: the caller's stage calls the `issueInstruction` activity of §12.5 and needs the result, which is the call-type answer the architecture gives for "another service must do a step and we need the result" (context pack, slide 12 notes). The service therefore declares no subscription for this story, and a build that subscribes to the write-off topic to learn of a placement fails the absence test. The instructions this service relays onwards are read by the firm on `GET /partner/instructions`, and the results, invoices and acceptances arrive on the operations of the other stories of the module.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `InstructionWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per instruction, started by the placement | `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the instruction reference, the partner, the partner type, the instruction type and the due date; signals: the accept, decline, result and recall answers of the later stories; query: the remaining partner clock. Holds the partner clock of the instruction type and closes when the instruction ends |
| `issueInstruction` | Activity, the placement step | `rwb-partner` | The case reference, the instruction type, the placement type and the rule version in; the instruction, the partner, `instructed_at`, `due_at` and the status out, with the record, the row and the outbox written in one transaction |

The activity name is the one the context pack's call-type notes give as the example (`issueInstruction` on rwb-partner) and its input shape is a design choice fixed by no source document (ASM-5366). The workflow kit that hosts it is RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, which DP-10 would add and the plan's H row does not carry (ASM-5366). No child workflow for the case and no Schedule exists in this service.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. S9 owns no job (context pack ownership rows, jobs: none), so this story registers no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row and no shared job table; the only clock is the workflow timer of §12.5, which is a timer and not a schedule.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| partner | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The panel row of each partner; read for the eligible set, the capacity and the service level, and written only by the panel story |
| partner_instruction | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The instruction of one placement; this story inserts one row and writes the columns of §11 |
| partner_user | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The portal user of a firm; not touched by this story and named so the ownership is complete |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_partner` | The local hash-linked decision record of the pick (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_partner` | The key of the replay and the answer it holds |
| outbox_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_partner` | The row of `InstructionIssued`, written in the same transaction |

Not owned and never read as a table: `recovery_case`, `assignment` and `timer` (P3), every `v_ace_*` view (P1), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6). No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case case-read fake | Case `RW-2027-000831` at `PLACEMENT_DECIDED` with an instruction requirement and an assignment reference; a case that has moved on; no answer beyond 2 s | AC1, AC4, X5 |
| rwb-source-data DP08 fake | The measured return of four eligible partners for business date `2027-04-30`, ranking `PRT-SYN-0031-A` first; a partner with no record | AC1, AC3 |
| rwb-source-data DP11 and freshness fake | The score of each pick with its business date; a product behind its date; a product whose load failed | AC1, AC5 |
| rwb-decision rule fake | The scorecard rule at its version in force, with its weights and its thresholds as rows | AC1, AC3 |
| rwb-access session fake | A caller holding Partner portal C, and a caller holding R only | TC-E6-031-03, AC7 |
| Local decision-record stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and outbox, and a stopped chain | AC2, X1 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-35 answer for the case, in its placement state | AC1 |
| Partner gateway fake | The firm-facing read of `GET /partner/instructions` behind FAPI 2.0 | AC6 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The operation names of the four consumed rows carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-3110; ASM-5362, ASM-5364, ASM-5368, ASM-5370).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 3 provided, 4 consumed | `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions`, `GET /partner/instructions` and `GET /partners` on `/api/recovery/partner/v1`; the case, the two products with freshness, the rule and the session reads; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 1 published, 0 consumed | `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` on `rwb.partner.events.v1`; no subscription |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 1 activity, 0 schedules | `InstructionWorkflow` with the partner clock and `issueInstruction` on `rwb-partner` |
| File | None | No file is read, built or delivered here; the instruction and its pack travel through the document and edge contracts, not as a file of this story |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner`, module `placement`; front end `src/modules/recovery/partner/PlacementAllocation.tsx`, the fragment SCR-35 embeds, read only.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the transaction rule of the step: the record and the row commit together or not at all. DP-05 is a prohibition in practice rather than a grant: `v_ace_score` is DP11's source and this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant, so the score and the measured return arrive on the owner's contract with their business date. DP-13 moves the base of the three operations and nothing else. DP-19 is how SCR-35 reaches this service, one hop through the gateway; the partner-facing read uses the partner gateway of the same edge epic. DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-08, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-14 are not in this key's pattern set although the step evaluates a rule, reads versioned reference data, checks a right, publishes a fact, starts a workflow and names a topic; each absence is recorded rather than added to the metadata (GAP-3110; ASM-5364, ASM-5365, ASM-5366, ASM-5370, ASM-5371).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `issueInstruction` | Activity | The placement step: reads the case, the panel, the rule and the products, writes the record, the row and the outbox row, starts the clock and answers |
| `EligibilityFilter` | Service | The eligible set: partner type, panel status, contract end, capacity and the conduct suspension of R-UNI-29 |
| `ScorecardRanker` | Service | The rank order on measured return as the rule defines it, with the value behind each position, and no rotation path |
| `PartnerDecisionRecordWriter` | Library adapter | Writes the record with the rule and scorecard versions before the row, hash-linked; refuses the run when the write fails |
| `InstructionWriter` | Repository | Inserts the row, the idempotency key and the outbox row in one `rwb_partner` transaction with the optimistic lock |
| `CaseClient` | Client | The case read of rwb-case, one hop, 2 s, breaker |
| `SourceDataClient` | Client | DP08, DP11 and the freshness read, with the business date, the load time and the stale path |
| `RulePackageClient` | Client | The scorecard rule at its version in force |
| `InstructionWorkflow` | Workflow | The partner clock of the instruction type, one execution per instruction |
| `PartnerInstructionController` | Controller | The three operations, the capability area and rights, the `Idempotency-Key` and the problem mapping |
| `PlacementAllocation` | React component | Shows the pick, the partner and the instruction on SCR-35, read only, with the hold, stale and refusal states |

**Database and migrations.** No Flyway file. The three tables arrive with the DB story of this service; the record, the idempotency key and the outbox row are library objects created in `rwb_partner` by the library's migration (DP-03, DP-09). No column is added for the case, the score, the measured return or the rule: those are facts of their owners and are referenced, not copied.

**Configuration and reference data.**

- The scorecard weights, the panel thresholds, the capacity rule, the instruction types and the service level of each partner type: reference data or rule rows with their version, never a constant (ASM-5367, ASM-5371).
- The capability area "Partner portal" and its rights: access rows of rwb-access, read through the guard.
- The 2 s budget, the single hop and the breaker are the platform rule of ADR-020; the business date of a run is a parameter of the activity and not a constant.

**Build steps**

1. `issueInstruction` and its input record, registered on `rwb-partner`, with the transaction boundary of the step.
2. `CaseClient` and `SourceDataClient` against their fakes, with the business date, the load time of each product and the stale path (AC1, AC5, X5).
3. `RulePackageClient` against its fake, with the version in force recorded with the pick (AC1, AC3).
4. `EligibilityFilter` and `ScorecardRanker` over the panel, with the suspension, the contract end, the capacity and the no-eligible-partner path (AC1, AC4, X3, X7).
5. `PartnerDecisionRecordWriter` against the stub, with the failed-write path (AC2, AC3, X1).
6. `InstructionWriter` with the one transaction, the row, the idempotency row and the outbox row (AC1, AC6).
7. `InstructionWorkflow` and its partner clock, started once per instruction (AC6).
8. `PartnerInstructionController` with the three operations, the rights, the `Idempotency-Key` and the problem mapping, and `PlacementAllocation` on SCR-35 through the composite route fake and the partner gateway fake (AC1, AC6, X2).
9. The boundary test: no statement outside `rwb_partner`, no `v_ace_*` read, no write to `rwb_case`, `rwb_source_data` or `rwb_decision`, and no rotation field anywhere (AC7, BR2, BR5).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.partner.placement-v1`, a flag of the platform library; off means the activity holds the placement with no write, and the other stories of the service are unaffected.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the pick runs on a synthetic panel and synthetic products in SIT, the rank order decides and rotation never does, R-WO-31 holds with nothing written, a stale product stops the run, a replay writes once, a forced record failure changes nothing, no `v_ace_*` read and no foreign schema write exists in the build, and SCR-35 answers through the composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the instruction exists (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Partner portal C right calls the placement (X2) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of the request, the case or the panel row is absent or invalid | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P1-001 | A data product the pick rests on is behind its business date (X4) | The text is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3110; ASM-5369) |

The first three IDs and their text are the legacy message set of RWB-E6-031, copied unchanged; no message is reworded. MSG-P1-001 is the data-freshness message the wave 4 key uses for the same condition; its text is not in this WP's read set, so the row carries the placeholder and the gap, and the build must not invent wording of its own. The hold of R-WO-31 and the incident of X4 raise no message ID beyond this row.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-35 Placement and allocation is served through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19): the route calls rwb-partner for the pick and the instruction, rwb-case for the case and its state and rwb-source-data for the measured return and its business date; this story fixes the rwb-partner answers only, and the composite route and the field list of the screen belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. SCR-34 Partner list reads the panel of §12.1.

The legacy screen table gives the states "Loading; list" for both screens. The loading state is the read of the three contracts; the list state is the pick, the partner, the instruction type, `instructed_at`, `due_at` and the status, with the rank order behind the pick available as evidence. The hold of R-WO-31, the stale product of X4 and the refusals of §14 are the further states this story must render, and the override form of the partner manager is not one of them: it is FEAT-PRM-04. The firm's own view is `GET /partner/instructions` behind the partner gateway and carries no staff field.

| TC-E6-031-02 | AC2 | Component | The decision-record stub stopped; nothing written, no event, no clock and MSG-P7-003 |

The four legacy cases are those of RWB-E6-031 in their legacy order, with the Level column added: every case is tested on the fakes, so every case is `Component`. Their business journey, including legacy AC1, is proved by RWB-ITG-E6031-ITG with the `-ITG` copies, and this story writes none. The two `TC-S9-E6031-` cases are new and cover the criteria the split adds. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the scorecard weights, the panel thresholds, the capacity rule, the instruction types, the service level by partner type and the rank order stay reference data or rule rows with their version, never a constant, a default or a branch.
- No rotation: no counter, round-robin index, last-placed pointer, fixed share or queue position exists in the schema, the code, a cache or a workflow input, and a build that adds one fails the review (BR2).
- No personal data in `rwb_partner`, the record, the event, a workflow input or a log: identifiers, a type, a status, two timestamps and a version only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and reads no ACE table, and a build that adds one fails the boundary test (BR5).
- The case stays with rwb-case: no `recovery_case` row, no case-state column, no assignment write here (BR8).
- One base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service; no document names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- The decision is recorded before the change; a build that writes a row outside the record's transaction fails the review (DP-03).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no Quartz job row, no shared job table, no monolith base, no data-lake extract and no event consumed as a command.

##### 19. Out of scope

- The published shape of the three operations, the elements, the rights, the error set, the tables and the fakes: RWB-S9-E6031-CON.
- The panel and the fee schedule as data, FEAT-PRM-02 and legacy RWB-E6-030: RWB-S9-E6030-APP.
- The override with a reason, FEAT-PRM-04 and R-WO-31's escalation beyond the hold: RWB-S9-E6032-APP.
- The result received into the case, FEAT-PRM-05, and the accept, decline, invoice and result operations of the module: the later stories of this service.
- The agency placement of a charged-off account and the fee (FEAT-PRM-06, FEAT-PRM-07), the monthly scorecard (FEAT-PRM-08) and the panel review, notice and contract exit (FEAT-PRM-10 to FEAT-PRM-12).
- The case of record, its state, the work assignment and the parent `CaseWorkflow`: rwb-case (P3).
- The measured return, the score and the freshness of their products: rwb-source-data (P1). The rule package and the decision ledger: rwb-decision (P7). The right and the guard: rwb-access (P4).
- The composite route and the screen field list of SCR-35 and SCR-34: RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the partner gateway route table: the edge stories of the same epic.
- The cross-service journey, its `-ITG` copies and the evidence: RWB-ITG-E6031-ITG.
- The deployment of this capability, its flag, its dashboards, its alerts and its runbook: the operations story of this legacy key.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E6-031 as the wave 4 integration proof that work is placed with the partner the scorecard picks on measured return, proved across rwb-partner, rwb-source-data and rwb-decision: the measured return read through DP08 and the score and route economics through DP11, the pick recorded with its scorecard version, the instruction issued once with its partner clock, and the freshness of the score read gating the placement; the allocation is RWB-S9-E6031-APP. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **partner and agency manager**, I want **the placement of work by measured return proved end to end on the real services: the partner the scorecard picks read back on the instruction, the measured return behind the pick read through DP08 and the score through DP11 as of the business date, the pick recorded once with its scorecard version and rule version, two identical cases on the same business date going to the same partner rather than by rotation, and a stale score product stopping the placement**, so that **work goes where the measured return is best and no case is placed by rotation, habit or a product that has not been refreshed**.

This story builds the wave 4 integration harness and its evidence, and then stops. The scorecard evaluation, the pick of the partner and the instruction that carries it are built by S9 rwb-partner in RWB-S9-E6031-APP and its CON story. The measured return this run asserts is P1's DP08 Partner performance product over S9's own partner and instruction records, and the score the pick rests on is P1's DP11 Scores and route economics product over `v_ace_score`; the case, the assignment and the queue are P3's, the decision record and the rule rows are P7's, and the right on the placement is answered by P4. The harness reads those published values, drives the one placement operation, counts the events, observes the workflow and writes a run report per case. It provides no endpoint, no table, no workflow, no activity, no schedule and no screen, and it writes no code in any service.

##### 2. Business rationale

Today partner work runs on email and spreadsheets and allocation is not based on performance (FSD S9 A1.3, line 80). The consequence is the failure this story is written against: a firm can keep receiving work after its measured return has fallen, and a firm that improves gets nothing, because nothing in the path compares one firm with another on what it actually recovered. REQ-S9-003 states the rule the story is written against — work is allocated to partners **by measured return against a scorecard, not by a fixed share** — and R-WO-30 gives the placement its concrete form: where `placement_type = soft_recovery` and an agency on the panel has capacity, the account is placed **with the agency chosen on measured return** and the instruction is sent **the same day on the portal**. R-WO-31 gives the other half: where no agency on the panel has capacity, the placement is **held** and escalated on the timer, and nothing is placed to keep a queue moving.

The second half of the story is the evidence, because a pick is only defensible if the number behind it can be read back as of the day it was used. That number is DP08 Partner performance — the Workbench product over partner and partner_instruction, refreshed on change — and DP11 Scores and route economics, the ACE product over `v_ace_score`, refreshed daily at 08:00 (FSD P1, lines 290 and 293). Both are read through rwb-source-data's published contract and never from a view or another service's schema. The decision entry the placement writes has to name the scorecard version it was taken under, because BR-S9-003 keeps the scorecard and the panel as versioned reference data and a pick whose version is unrecorded cannot be replayed. A stale score product is the quiet failure of this journey: the placement looks right, the instruction goes out, and it rests on a number from an earlier day, which is exactly what VR-S9-003-1 refuses with MSG-P1-001.

The harness is decoupled the way the services are. Every call is one hop on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13); there is no in-process call and no second hop. ACE data reaches the run only through P1's published contract (DP-05), never by reading `v_ace_score` in a query of the harness's own, and DP-01 forbids reading another service's schema at all. The decision record is written by S9 through the local decision-record library on rwb.decision-record.v1 (DP-03) and confirmed by the central ledger in rwb-decision (ADR-022); the harness reads it back through P7's contract. On the edge, DP-19 sends partners through the **partner gateway** (FAPI 2.0) that fronts rwb-partner, and reserves gateway-bff composite routes for staff screens; the run calls S9's own operation at the service boundary, which is the operation the partner gateway fronts.

One limit is stated plainly because it shapes the whole run. The Ownership Map publishes one placement operation, `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions`, described as "Issue an instruction to a partner by rule", and it publishes `GET /partner/instructions`. It publishes no scorecard read and no allocation read of its own. The harness therefore reads the pick from the instruction, the measured return from DP08 and the score from DP11, and it never invents an allocation endpoint to make an assertion look cleaner. The `InstructionRequest` body shape is not published either, so the body the run sends is held in the fixture from S9's CON story and is asserted only for the fields the published response returns.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The published contracts of S9 rwb-partner (the placement and the instruction read), P1 rwb-source-data (DP08 and DP11 records and the freshness read), P3 rwb-case (the case), P7 rwb-decision (the decision log) and P4 rwb-access (the session) are in the contract registry, and a stub set is generated from each one.
- S9 owns the panel, the partner users and the instructions in `rwb_partner` (Arch v5 slide 41, line 2891), so the instruction this run asserts and the pick it records have one named owner before any value is compared.
- The placement and the scorecard evaluation are RWB-S9-E6031-APP until it lands; until then the partner fixture of §12.8 stands in for its effect and the story is reported as a stub pass.
- FEAT-PRM-03 Allocate work by measured return is the S9 feature, with FEAT-PRM-02 Hold the partner panel and fee schedule as data as its prerequisite (Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3, lines 135 and 136).
- The scorecard and the panel are versioned data read from reference data **with their version**, so a pick is recorded against the version it was taken under and not against "current" (BR-S9-003, FSD S9 A2.3.3.1).
- The rules the placement answers to are R-WO-30 (place with the agency chosen on measured return, send the instruction the same day on the portal), R-WO-31 (no agency on the panel has capacity, hold and escalate on the timer), R-UNI-25, R-UNI-26, R-UNI-27, R-UNI-29 (a conduct breach suspends allocation) and R-UNI-45 (re-select and re-issue with the clock restarted).
- The right on the placement is **Partner portal C** as API-S9-002 declares it, and the instruction read is **Partner portal R** as API-S9-003 declares it (TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2).
- The synthetic partners, the two cases, the instruction keys, the scorecard version, the business date and the next business date, the measured-return values, the capacity state, the freshness cut-off, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0461; ASM-0653).
- The synthetic partners, cases, instruction keys, scorecard version and measured-return values are held in the fixture as data, never written in code.
- No build dependency. Day 1, with the stubs in place from the first run; the one wait is RWB-S9-E6031-APP, which replaces its stub and never blocks the lane.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: runs preflight. It reads the eight contracts, pins each version in the run report, resets the fixture and the freshness switch, and stops the run before any assertion if a contract is missing or a pinned version has moved.
2. Harness: loads the fixture: cases `RW-2027-000831` and `RW-2027-000832` both at `PLACEMENT_DECIDED` with instruction type `COLLECT`, partners `PRT-SYN-0031-A` and `PRT-SYN-0031-B` on the panel with capacity, partner `PRT-SYN-0031-C` on the panel with no capacity, and the measured return for business date `2027-04-30` held so that A ranks first.
3. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP11/records?caseId={caseId}` and asserts the score the pick will rest on, then reads `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness?product=DP11` and asserts the business date `2027-04-30` and the load time of the 08:00 daily refresh (AC2, AC4).
4. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP08/records?caseId={caseId}` for the three partners and asserts the measured return the pick rests on, as the published product carries it, refreshed on change (AC2).
5. Harness: places the work on the first case through `POST /api/recovery/partner/v1/cases/{caseId}/instructions` with one Idempotency-Key, as a caller holding Partner portal C, and asserts the answer names partner A (AC2).
6. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions` and asserts one instruction with its instruction type `COLLECT`, its partner A, its `instructed_at`, its `due_at` and its status `SENT` (AC2, AC5).
7. Harness: places the work on the second identical case and asserts the same partner A, which is the proof that the pick is not a rotation; it then reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` and asserts one entry per placement, each naming the pick, the scorecard version and the rule id (AC2, AC3).
8. Harness: replays the first placement with the same Idempotency-Key, asserts the first answer is returned unchanged and one instruction remains, counts one `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` per placement on `rwb.partner.events.v1`, and observes `InstructionWorkflow` on `rwb-partner` with one partner SLA timer for the instruction type (AC3, AC5).
9. Harness: resets the fixture to its pre-placement snapshot and moves the measured return so that B ranks first for the next business date, then places the same case again and asserts the pick follows B; the next business date is held in the fixture and is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0461; ASM-0653) (AC3).
10. Harness: runs the no-capacity variant with C only, and asserts the placement is held under R-WO-31 with the case read unchanged at `PLACEMENT_DECIDED` through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and a decision entry naming the hold (AC2).
11. Harness: makes DP11 stale after a late or failed ACE batch for its source and places the work again; the answer must carry MSG-P1-001 with the product and the date substituted, no instruction may be read and no `InstructionIssued` may be published (AC4).
12. Harness: resets the product and turns the fault switch on the decision-record hop, places the work under a new Idempotency-Key, and asserts the answer carries MSG-P7-003 with no instruction, no event and the case unchanged; the switch is reset before the next run (AC6).
13. Harness: calls `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` as a synthetic RW-CASEOWN caller holding Partner portal R and not C, places the work, and asserts 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no instruction; then it writes one run report per case, keyed by story and case id (AC7).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A stub answers a shape the published contract does not allow | The run fails at that hop and the report names the service, the operation and the contract version; no criterion is marked passed | None | TC-E6-031-01-ITG (ITG AC2) |
| X2 | The pick is not the top-ranked partner on the measured return, or two identical cases are split across two partners | The run fails on AC2 and AC3 and the report names both picks, their DP08 measured return, their DP11 score and the two decisions | None | TC-E6-031-01-ITG (ITG AC3) |
| X3 | The pick does not follow a change in the measured return, and the same partner is picked again | The run fails on AC3 and the report names the old pick, the new measured return, the partner the product ranks first and the partner the instruction names | None | TC-E6-031-01-ITG (ITG AC3) |
| X4 | A second instruction is created for one placement, or a replay publishes a second event or starts a second clock | The run fails on AC5 and the report names both instruction ids, the Idempotency-Key each carried, both event ids and both workflow runs | None | TC-E6-031-01-ITG (ITG AC5) |
| X5 | The decision record is written twice, written without its scorecard version, or the central ledger has not confirmed it | The run fails on AC2 and AC5 and the report names the entries, the scorecard version each carries and the missing confirmation | MSG-P7-003 (expected only where the record cannot be confirmed) | TC-E6-031-01-ITG (ITG AC2, AC5) |
| X6 | A placement is made on a stale score product | The run fails on AC4 unless the answer carries MSG-P1-001 with the product and the date, and no instruction and no event exist | MSG-P1-001 (expected, and missing) | TC-E6-031-04-ITG (ITG AC4) |
| X7 | A forced decision-record failure leaves an instruction, an event or a case change, or answers without MSG-P7-003 | The run fails on AC6 and the report names the instruction count, the event count and the case read before and after | MSG-P7-003 (expected, and missing) | TC-E6-031-02-ITG (ITG AC6) |
| X8 | A caller without Partner portal C is allowed to place work | The run fails on AC7 and the report names the caller role, the right, the operation and the answer; a 200 is a failure even when nothing was written | MSG-P4-002 (expected, and missing) | TC-E6-031-03-ITG (ITG AC7) |

The report text is for the wave entry check and is not part of the message standard. The business messages the run touches are in section 14 and are asserted by ID and by their substituted values.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs against the published contracts and the stubs from Day 1; the only wait is RWB-S9-E6031-APP, and its fixture answers until it lands |
| Negotiable | The fixture layout, the synthetic partners and keys, the measured-return values, the scorecard version, the freshness cut-off, the report shape and the gate are configuration agreed at the wave entry check, not business values in code |
| Valuable | Proves across services that work reached the partner the scorecard picks, that the pick tracked the measured return and not a rotation, and that a stale score product and a refused or failed placement changed nothing |
| Estimable | One runner, one stub set, one scorecard and capacity fixture, two placements, one capacity probe, one freshness probe, one decision probe, one event observer, one workflow observation, one access probe and one report |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its four tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is asserted on an observable: an instruction, its partner and status, a DP08 record, a DP11 record, a freshness stamp, a decision entry with its scorecard and rule version, an event count, a workflow timer and a response code |

```gherkin
Feature: Allocate work by measured return - wave 4 integration harness

  Background:
    Given the synthetic partners "PRT-SYN-0031-A" and "PRT-SYN-0031-B" are on the panel with capacity and partner "PRT-SYN-0031-C" is on the panel with no capacity

    Given the rule package in force holds R-WO-30, R-WO-31 and R-UNI-29 with its rule version and the scorecard and the panel are versioned reference data

    And GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness?product=DP11 answers business date "2027-04-30" and its load time
    And GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId} holds one entry naming the pick, the scorecard version and the rule id
    When no agency on the panel has capacity and the work is placed with partner "PRT-SYN-0031-C" only
    Then the placement is held under R-WO-31 and no instruction is created
    And GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} reads the case unchanged at PLACEMENT_DECIDED
    And the decision log holds one entry naming the hold

  Scenario: AC3 The pick follows the measured return and not a rotation (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the measured return for business date "2027-04-30" is held so that "PRT-SYN-0031-A" ranks first

    And the decision log holds one entry per placement, each naming the same scorecard version

    Then the next placement picks "PRT-SYN-0031-B"
    And no placement in the run is made by rotation, habit or a fixed share

    Given the placement of case "RW-2027-000831" is accepted and carried one Idempotency-Key

    And InstructionWorkflow on "rwb-partner" holds one partner SLA timer for the instruction type
    And the replay adds no instruction, no event and no second clock

  Scenario: AC6 A forced decision-record failure stops the placement with nothing issued (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision record cannot be written for the placement
    When the work is placed through POST /api/recovery/partner/v1/cases/{caseId}/instructions
    Then the answer carries "MSG-P7-003"

    And no "rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1" is published

  Scenario: AC7 A caller without Partner portal C is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a synthetic caller with role "RW-CASEOWN" holding Partner portal R and not Partner portal C

    Then the answer is 403 with "MSG-P4-002"
    And no instruction is created and no case state changes
```

Legacy AC1 is the only legacy criterion this story owns, and it is the business outcome the S9 allocation has to reach: the work goes to the partner the scorecard picks and the decision log carries the rule version. Legacy AC2 (the decision log cannot be written, nothing changes) stays with RWB-S9-E6031-APP as its build criterion and is asserted here across the boundary in AC6, where the instruction, the event and the case state are read before and after the refused placement. The measured return and the score are read as data products through P1's contract — DP08 and DP11 — and never from `v_ace_score` or another service's schema.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Work is allocated to partners by measured return against a scorecard, not by a fixed share | REQ-S9-003 |
| BR2 | Where `placement_type = soft_recovery` and an agency on the panel has capacity, the account is placed with the agency chosen on measured return and the instruction is sent the same day on the portal | R-WO-30 |
| BR3 | Where no agency on the panel has capacity, the placement is held and escalated on the timer, and no instruction is issued to keep a queue moving | R-WO-31 |
| BR4 | A data product that is stale after a late or failed ACE batch for its source refuses the placement, and the answer names the product and the date it is from | VR-S9-003-1; MSG-P1-001 |
| BR5 | No value a business person may change is written in code: the panel, the scorecard and the service levels are read from reference data with their version, and the decision entry names the scorecard version the pick was taken under | BR-S9-003 (FSD S9 A2.3.3.1) |
| BR6 | A partner that misses its service level on the portal is chased once, then the work is recalled and re-selected on the scorecard | R-UNI-25 |
| BR7 | A panel exit or the end of a contract recalls every open case held by that partner and re-selects, so a recalled case never stays with the exiting firm | R-UNI-26 |
| BR8 | A declared conflict of interest withdraws the instruction and re-selects the next partner on the scorecard | R-UNI-27 |
| BR9 | An upheld conduct or complaint breach suspends allocation and recalls the affected cases, and a re-selected partner gets the instruction re-issued with the partner clock restarted | R-UNI-29; R-UNI-45 |
| BR10 | The measured return is read as DP08 Partner performance (refreshed on change) and the score as DP11 Scores and route economics (daily at 08:00), both through rwb-source-data's contract; the run never reads `v_ace_score` directly and no service reads another service's schema | DP-05; DP-01; FSD P1, lines 290 and 293 |
| BR11 | The decision record is written by S9 through the local decision-record library on rwb.decision-record.v1 and confirmed by the central ledger, so nothing is placed when it cannot be recorded; every hop is one REST call on the owner's base with a 2 s timeout and no second hop | DP-03; ADR-022; DP-11; DP-13 |

The harness asserts these rules and changes none of them; the rules themselves are evaluated in RWB-S9-E6031-APP, the panel and the scorecard are versioned reference data in S9, the case is P3's, the decision log is P7's and the session is P4's.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To | Owner of the change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLACEMENT_DECIDED | SOFT_RECOVERY_SELECTED | `placement_type = soft_recovery` and an agency on the panel has capacity | PLACED_WITH_AGENCY | S7 rwb-writeoff rules component moves the case stage under R-WO-30; S9 rwb-partner writes the instruction through InstructionWorkflow `issueInstruction` and publishes `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` |
| PLACEMENT_DECIDED | NO_AGENCY_CAPACITY | no agency on the panel has capacity | PLACEMENT_DECIDED, held | S7 rwb-writeoff rules component under R-WO-31; S9 writes no instruction and the hold is recorded in the decision log |
| PLACEMENT_DECIDED | none | the placement is refused for want of Partner portal C, MSG-P1-001 or MSG-P7-003 | PLACEMENT_DECIDED, unchanged | S9 rwb-partner refuses before any write; the rule engine is not reached |
| PARTNER_RECALLED | PARTNER_RESELECTED | the next partner is selected on the scorecard | ROUTE_D6_REOPEN, then PLACED_WITH_AGENCY on re-issue | Partner and agency manager under R-UNI-45; S9 re-issues the instruction and restarts the clock |
| PARTNER_RECALLED | PARTNER_CONDUCT_BREACH | a conduct or complaint breach is upheld against the partner | allocation suspended, cases recalled | Partner and agency manager under R-UNI-29 |
| Instruction `SENT` | partner acceptance on the portal | the partner accepts the instruction | `ACCEPTED` | S9 rwb-partner, InstructionWorkflow |
| Instruction `ACCEPTED` | result recorded or timer expiry | the result is recorded, or the partner misses the service level | `DONE` or `RECALLED` | S9 rwb-partner, InstructionWorkflow; R-UNI-25 |

The case stages are the rule table's own from-states and to-states, and the harness sets none of them: it reads the case through P3's contract before and after every attempt and asserts it is unchanged where the rule says the placement is held or refused. The instruction statuses are S9's own LOV values `SENT`, `ACCEPTED`, `DECLINED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `DONE` and `RECALLED` (TSD S9 T3.2), and the run asserts only `SENT` on a fresh placement. The harness changes no state; every change in the table belongs to S9 or to the rule engine under the write-off legacy key.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-AGENCYMG Partner and agency manager | Holds Partner portal CRUDA and is the primary role of the journey and of the placement it asserts |
| RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-GUARANT and PT-AGENCY | Hold Partner portal C (or RU on the portal for the partner user) per the TSD RBAC matrix, and are the other callers the placement accepts |
| RW-CASEOWN Case owner | Holds Partner portal R and not C, and is the refused caller of AC7 |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-LEGAL, RW-CONDUCT, RW-CAPACITY, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-HEADLIT, RW-HEADNPA, RW-HEADASL, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE, PT-LAWFIRM, PT-VALUER, PT-AUCTION, PT-BUYER, PT-RAMC | Hold Partner portal R and read the partner and the instruction; the run records the right each operation answered with |
| QA lead | Owns the harness configuration, the fixture, the freshness switch, the report shape and the pass or fail gate |
| Integration lead | Owns the harness code, the stub set and the swap from a stub to the real service |
| The owning services' identities | S9 holds the panel, the partner users and the instructions and runs InstructionWorkflow, P1 holds DP08 and DP11 and the freshness stamp, P3 holds the case, P7 holds the decision log and the central ledger, P4 answers the session; they make every change the harness asserts |
| No delegation of authority level applies | The harness takes no business decision; authorisation is answered by rwb-access and the DoA is P4's, so no delegation level is asserted here |

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Owner | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 | partner | id, partner_code, partner_name, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end, score | S9 rwb-partner | Read through the S9 contract and through DP08 |
| DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 | partner_instruction | id, case_id, partner_id, instruction_type, instructed_at, due_at, status, result_code, fee_amount | S9 rwb-partner | Written only by S9's placement; read through the instruction read and DP08 |
| DF-WRK-009 to DF-WRK-016 | assignment | id, case_id, task_id, assignee_user_id, assigned_at, ended_at, reason, rule_id | P3 rwb-case | Read through the P3 contract; not written by the harness |
| DF-WRK-001 to DF-WRK-008 | queue | id, queue_code, queue_name, team_code, role_code, assignment_method, capacity_cap, overflow_queue_id | P3 rwb-case | Read through the P3 contract |
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case | id, case_no, status, stage_code, primary_person_key and the case attributes | P3 rwb-case | Read through the P3 contract before and after every attempt |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | id, case_id, decision_code, rule_id, rule_version, model_version, entry_hash | P7 rwb-decision | Read through the P7 contract |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | rule_row | id, rule_id, rule_version, route_set, from_state, event_code, test_case_id | P7 rwb-decision | Read through the P7 contract |
| DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279 | v_ace_score behind DP11 | score_key, account_key, model_code, model_version, score_value, estimate_value, route_code, scored_at, source_system, data_as_of | P1 rwb-source-data, over the ACE view | Read only through DP11; never read directly |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. The partner and the instruction are S9's in `rwb_partner`; the case, the assignment and the queue are P3's in `rwb_case`; the decision entries and the rule rows are P7's in `rwb_decision`. The ACE score fields sit behind `v_ace_score` and reach the run only as DP11 Scores and route economics through P1's contract, which is the only way a caller outside P1 may see them (DP-05). The queue's own `assignment_method` carries `ROUND_ROBIN` as a staff-queue default, and the partner pick is not that mechanism: the run proves the partner is chosen on measured return while the queue's staff allocation stays what it is. The harness owns no table and writes no row; the only change it drives is S9's own placement operation of §12.2, and everything else it reads is a contract read.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/cases/{caseId}/instructions` | S9 rwb-partner | Issues the instruction to the partner chosen by rule, with one Idempotency-Key; the accepted, the held, the stale, the failed and the refused operation of the run (AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions` | S9 rwb-partner | The one instruction, its instruction type, its partner, its instructed_at, its due_at and its status (AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP08/records?caseId={caseId}` | P1 rwb-source-data | DP08 Partner performance, refreshed on change, carrying the measured return the pick rests on (AC2, AC3) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP11/records?caseId={caseId}` | P1 rwb-source-data | DP11 Scores and route economics, daily at 08:00, carrying the score the pick rests on (AC2, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness?product=DP11` | P1 rwb-source-data | The business date and the load time of the score product, and the stale state that stops the placement (AC2, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case status and stage at `PLACEMENT_DECIDED`, before and after the held, the stale, the failed and the refused attempts (AC2, AC4, AC6, AC7) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | P7 rwb-decision | One entry per placement, naming the pick, the scorecard version and the rule id, and one entry naming the hold (AC2, AC3, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The caller's roles and rights before a placement (AC7) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13). No operation is invented in this story: each path is the owner's published operation in the Ownership Map. The map publishes no allocation read and no scorecard read, so the pick is asserted through the instruction S9 issues, the measured return through DP08 and the score through DP11, and the harness never calls an endpoint the map does not publish. The `InstructionRequest` body shape is not published either; the body the run sends is held in the fixture from S9's CON story, and only the fields the published `PartnerInstruction` response returns are asserted. For a partner the edge path to the portal operations is the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) that fronts rwb-partner, and for a staff screen the same values would be composed by a gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); the run itself calls the service boundary the gateway fronts.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it writes its report to the wave record.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use in the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1` | S9 rwb-partner | Counts one publication per placement, proves a replay adds none, and carries the partner clock the partner portal consumes (AC5) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | S9 rwb-partner through the local decision-record library (DP-03) | Proves the placement decision and its scorecard and rule version were published once and confirmed by the central ledger, and that the forced failure publishes none (AC2, AC5, AC6) |

The harness subscribes to both topics under one consumer group of its own and replays the instruction event once. `InstructionIssued` is EV-20 in the event catalogue with the partner portal as its consumer (Arch v5 slide 43, row 20, line 2946); the run counts the publication and reads the portal effect through the instruction read of §12.2, because the partner portal exposes no operation of its own to this story.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness exercises `InstructionWorkflow`, S9's workflow on the task queue `rwb-partner` in the `rwb-recovery` namespace, through the placement: its `issueInstruction` activity issues the instruction and starts the partner SLA timer for the instruction type, and both are read in the workflow history (Arch v5 slide 17, line 1247; Temporal design slide 25, step 3 and the clocks at lines 1742 to 1745). It observes CaseWorkflow on `rwb-case` as the parent that holds the case the placement acts on, and observes it only: the placement does not signal it and moves no case state. Neither workflow, activity nor Schedule is created, changed or owned by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added, and none needed. The scorecard is refreshed by its own product — DP11 daily at 08:00 and DP08 on change — and the partner clock is a durable workflow timer, so nothing in the journey is on a cron: the harness starts each run itself and holds the business date in the fixture. JOB-05 Timer check is retired in favour of durable timers inside the workflows (Arch v5 slide 44), and the partner SLA is read as a timer on `InstructionWorkflow`, not as a scheduled job.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-01): partner, partner_user and partner_instruction are S9's in `rwb_partner`, assignment, recovery_case and queue are P3's in `rwb_case`, decision_log_entry and rule_row are P7's in `rwb_decision`, and DP08 and DP11 are P1's published products.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Contract | Stubbed answer in the run |
|---|---|---|
| Stub for rwb-partner (S9) | `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions`, `GET /partner/instructions` | Partners `PRT-SYN-0031-A` and `PRT-SYN-0031-B` with panel status `ACTIVE` and capacity; partner C with no capacity; a placement accepted once per Idempotency-Key with partner A, instruction type `COLLECT` and status `SENT`; the same instruction returned on a replay of the key; a held placement under R-WO-31 with no instruction; a stale answer carrying MSG-P1-001; with the fault switch on, an answer carrying MSG-P7-003 and no instruction |
| Stub for rwb-source-data (P1), DP08 | `GET /data-products/DP08/records?caseId={caseId}` | The three partners and their measured return for business date `2027-04-30` as the published product carries them, refreshed on change, with A ranked first and, on the next business date, B ranked first |
| Stub for rwb-source-data (P1), DP11 | `GET /data-products/DP11/records?caseId={caseId}` | The score, expected return and route code of each partner as the published product carries them, daily at 08:00, with its `data_as_of` |
| Stub for rwb-source-data (P1), freshness | `GET /data-products/freshness?product=DP11` | Business date `2027-04-30` and its load time on a fresh run, and a stale answer naming the product and the date it is from on the stale run |
| Stub for rwb-case (P3) | `GET /cases/{caseId}` | Cases `RW-2027-000831` and `RW-2027-000832` at `PLACEMENT_DECIDED`, with the same status and stage before and after every attempt |
| Stub for rwb-decision (P7) | `GET /decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | Exactly one entry per placement, naming the pick, the scorecard version and the rule id; one entry naming the hold; nothing after the stale, the forced failure or the refusal; the central ledger confirmation once |
| Stub for rwb-access (P4) | `GET /me/session` | Allows RW-AGENCYMG with Partner portal CRUDA and the other holders of C where the run needs them; refuses RW-CASEOWN with 403 and MSG-P4-002 on the placement |
| Scorecard and capacity fixture | The panel, the scorecard version and the capacity state | The three partners, their panel status, their capacity, their measured return for the two business dates and the scorecard version in force, held as data with the `InstructionRequest` body from S9's CON |

Each stub is generated from the published contract and its version is pinned in the run report, so a contract change shows up as a run failure and not as a silent pass. The harness environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic partners, cases and instruction keys, the scorecard version, the measured-return values, the capacity state, the business date and the next business date, the freshness cut-off, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0461; ASM-0653).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 8 consumed, one hop each on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13) |
| Kafka | None published; two consumed, `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`, counted and replayed once |
| Temporal | None added; InstructionWorkflow on `rwb-partner` exercised through the placement, with its partner SLA timer and its `issueInstruction` activity, and CaseWorkflow on `rwb-case` observed as the parent that holds the case |
| File | None. The placement body is S9's own request and the report is the harness's own output; no file or claim-check is transferred by this story |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery-w4/partner-allocation`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H dependencies DP-03 and DP-19 add, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, are platform stories delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays None. DP-05 adds nothing: the legacy story's `v_ace_score` read becomes DP11 Scores and route economics through P1's contract, and nothing in the harness reads the view. DP-13 adds nothing: the partner paths are rewritten onto S9's own base and there is no shared base left. DP-19 has two edges in this journey and the run names both: for the **partner** the route is the **partner gateway** in the DMZ under FAPI 2.0, which fronts rwb-partner (Arch v5 slide 17, line 1251, and slide 20, line 1458), and **gateway-bff** composes the **staff** screens only, including SCR-35 Placement and allocation. The one blocking dependency is the I story RWB-S9-E6031-APP, which replaces its stub; until it is live the run uses the stub, and a stub pass is reported as a stub pass.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the seven criteria in order for one case and holds the run lock, the fixture reset and the freshness switch |
| ScoreboardReadBack | Service | Reads DP08 and DP11, names the measured return and the score of each partner, and holds the ranking for the business date |
| FreshnessProbe | Service | Reads the DP11 freshness stamp, asserts the business date and the load time, and turns the product stale for AC4 |
| PlacementDriver | Service | Places the work once per Idempotency-Key through S9's operation and holds the accepted, the held, the stale, the failed and the refused attempt |
| InstructionReadBack | Service | Reads the instruction, its partner, its type, its `instructed_at`, its `due_at` and its status |
| RotationProbe | Service | Places the second identical case, compares the two picks, and moves the measured return for the next business date |
| CapacityProbe | Service | Runs the no-capacity variant with partner C and asserts the hold under R-WO-31 |
| DecisionProbe | Service | Reads the entries, the scorecard version and the rule id, reads the published decision record, and holds the fault switch |
| EventProbe | Service | Subscribes to `rwb.partner.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`, counts publications and replays the instruction event once |
| WorkflowProbe | Service | Observes InstructionWorkflow in the `rwb-recovery` namespace, its partner SLA timer and its `issueInstruction` step, and observes CaseWorkflow only |
| AccessProbe | Service | Reads the session and drives the refused placement of AC7 |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes one report per case, keyed by story and case id, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the stub set from Day 1 and the real services as RWB-S9-E6031-APP lands, on the synthetic partners `PRT-SYN-0031-A`, `PRT-SYN-0031-B` and `PRT-SYN-0031-C`, the cases `RW-2027-000831` and `RW-2027-000832`, instruction type `COLLECT`, business date `2027-04-30` and the next business date in the fixture. The harness seeds nothing by hand and never writes a schema row. The environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the scorecard version, the measured-return values, the capacity state, the freshness cut-off, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0461; ASM-0653).

**Build steps**

1. Generate the stub set and the scorecard and capacity fixture from the published contracts, pin each contract version in the run report, and fail the run on a mismatch (X1).
2. Build the ScoreboardReadBack and the FreshnessProbe: DP08 carries the measured return, DP11 carries the score, and the freshness read answers the business date `2027-04-30` with its load time (AC2, AC4).
3. Add the PlacementDriver: one placement on the first case with one Idempotency-Key, and the answer naming partner A (AC2, X2).
4. Add the InstructionReadBack: one instruction of type `COLLECT`, partner A, its `instructed_at`, its `due_at` and status `SENT` (AC2, AC5).
5. Add the DecisionProbe: one entry per placement naming the pick, the scorecard version and the rule id, one published decision record and the central ledger confirmation, and no second entry after a re-read (AC2, AC5, X5).
6. Add the RotationProbe: the second identical case picks A, and after the fixture reset the next business date picks B (AC3, X2, X3).
7. Add the EventProbe and the WorkflowProbe: one `InstructionIssued` per placement, one partner SLA timer, and a replay that adds no instruction, no event and no second clock (AC5, X4).
8. Add the CapacityProbe for the hold: partner C only, the case read unchanged at `PLACEMENT_DECIDED`, and a decision entry naming the hold under R-WO-31 (AC2).
9. Add the three negative paths — the stale product with MSG-P1-001, the forced decision-record failure with MSG-P7-003, and the caller without Partner portal C with 403 and MSG-P4-002 — then add the EvidenceReport and the gate, and swap a stub for the real owner as RWB-S9-E6031-APP lands (AC4, AC6, AC7, X6, X7, X8).

**Feature switch.** None. The harness has no production flag; the freshness switch and the fault switch of steps 8 and 9 exist in the test environment only and are reset by the runner before and after each run.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass against the fakes and again against RWB-S9-E6031-APP when it lands, and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story and case id.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | Error | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The FSD S9 row reads `MSG-P1-001 {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived.` and the message text above is copied word for word from it (FSD S9 A2.3.3.1, line 289); MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003 are copied word for word from the legacy story's validation table (lines 12045 to 12051). The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values it reads on the answer, and owns no message text: MSG-P1-001 with the product `DP11` and the date it is from when the score product is stale (AC4, X6), MSG-GEN-001 with the missing field when a placement is made short of a required parameter (X1), MSG-P4-002 with the refused action when the caller holds Partner portal R and not C (AC7, X8), and MSG-P7-003 when the decision record cannot be written and nothing is placed (AC6, X7).

##### 15. Screens and states

The legacy story's screens are SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation, and neither is built or rendered here: the harness calls the placement and the instruction read behind them and reads the states through the owners. What the wave entry check looks at instead is the run report, whose environment, layout and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0461; ASM-0653).

| State | Read through | What the run asserts |
|---|---|---|
| PLACEMENT_DECIDED | P3 case read, DP08 and the instruction read | The case is at the stage the rule table gives, no instruction exists, and the measured return of the three partners is present |
| PLACED_WITH_AGENCY | S9 instruction read, the decision log and the InstructionWorkflow history | One instruction of type `COLLECT` with partner A, its `instructed_at`, its `due_at` and status `SENT`, one decision entry naming the pick and the scorecard version, and one SLA timer running |
| The held placement | P3 case read, the decision log and the instruction read | The case is unchanged at `PLACEMENT_DECIDED`, no instruction exists, and one decision entry names the hold under R-WO-31 |
| The stale product | P1 freshness read, the S9 answer and the instruction read | The freshness read names the product and the date it is from, the answer carries MSG-P1-001, and no instruction and no event exist |
| A refused or failed placement | P4 session read, S9 answer, P7 decision log, the event count and the case read | 403 with MSG-P4-002 or MSG-P7-003, no instruction, no event and no state change |

SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation belong to the S9 stories of the legacy key, and neither is built or read here. The partner reaches the portal operations through the partner gateway and a staff member reaches the placement screen through a gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); this harness renders neither and asserts the operations behind them.

ITG AC2, AC3 and AC5 are asserted inside the run of TC-E6-031-01-ITG, which is the end-to-end case that places the work twice, reads the one instruction per case, counts the one event per placement and moves the measured return; they add no test case ID because the legacy set has four.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the synthetic partners, the cases, the panel and capacity state, the measured-return values, the scorecard version, the business dates, the freshness cut-off, the switches and the report layout are data.
- No personal data in logs, events, workflow inputs or reports: every key is synthetic, the partner is read by code and the case by case number, and the events carry IDs and facts only.
- Service data only through the owner's contract: the partner and the instruction from S9, DP08, DP11 and the freshness stamp from P1, the case from P3, the decision log and the rule rows from P7, the session from P4; never a direct schema read and never another service's table (DP-01, DP-05).
- **DP-05 is explicit here:** the score is read through DP11 and never from `v_ace_score`, and no service reads another service's schema; the same rule covers DP08, the measured return.
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would (DP-11, DP-13).
- No invented operation: only the one placement and the seven reads of §12.2, and the pick is never asserted through an allocation or scorecard read the map does not publish.
- A stub pass is never reported as a real pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner.
- The freshness switch and the fault switch are reset by the runner before and after each run and are never left on, so a forced failure cannot be mistaken for a real one; the harness never runs against UAT or production and never writes a row by hand or sets a state it then asserts.
