Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. The partner and the instruction are S9's, the case is P3's, and the decision log entry and the rule rows are P7's; the proceeds record the result is matched against is P8's and is read through `GET /api/recovery/payment/v1/proceeds`, whose rows are not named here because this story cites only the field IDs the dictionary gives for the four entities above. The harness owns no table and writes no row. The fee amount of DF-PRT-016 is read as the claim carries it; the harness asserts the comparison and the naming, never a rate, an amount or a business value of its own.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` | S9 rwb-partner | The partner, its panel status and its contract, and the schedule the claim is checked against (AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions` | S9 rwb-partner | The instruction, its status and the recorded result the claim is checked against (AC2, AC3) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results` | S9 rwb-partner | Submits the result once, and is the refused and failed operation of AC4 and AC5 (AC3, AC4, AC5) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/invoices` | S9 rwb-partner | Submits the invoice once; its answer is the invoice submission outcome, because the map publishes no invoice read (AC2, AC3) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/payment/v1/proceeds` | P8 rwb-payment | The proceeds record the result is matched against (AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | P7 rwb-decision | Exactly one approval entry with its rule version, and no second entry after a re-read (AC1, AC3, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case state before and after the submission and the replay (AC3, AC4, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The caller's roles and rights before a submission (AC5) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13). No operation is invented in this story: each path is the owner's published operation, and where a screen would compose them the path would be the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The Ownership Map publishes no fee-approval operation and no invoice read for this step, so the approval is asserted through the decision log and through the invoice submission outcome, and never through an endpoint that does not exist. The legacy permission table of RWB-E7-012 carries Partner portal R and U, the S9 TSD publishes the invoice operation with Partner portal C (API-S9-006), and the run records the right each operation answered with and asserts U on the result path, which is the right AC5 names. The fee calculation itself is FEAT-PRM-07 and is not called here.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it writes its report to the wave record.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use in the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1` | S9 rwb-partner | Counts one publication when the instruction is issued, and proves a replay changes nothing (AC3) |
| `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1` | S9 rwb-partner | Counts one publication when the result is recorded, and proves a replay changes nothing (AC3) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | S9 rwb-partner through the local decision-record library (DP-03) | Proves the approval and its rule version were published once and accepted by rwb-decision (AC1, AC3, AC4) |

The harness subscribes to both topics under one consumer group of its own, counts publications and replays each partner event once. The consumer effect it reads is the case through the rwb-case operation of §12.2 and the instruction through the S9 instruction read; the inbox row counts of rwb-litigation, rwb-asset and rwb-case, which Arch v5 slide 43 gives as the consumers of `PartnerResultSubmitted`, come from the consumer evidence in the run fixture, because neither rwb-litigation nor rwb-asset exposes an operation in this story.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness exercises InstructionWorkflow, S9's workflow on the task queue `rwb-partner` in the `rwb-recovery` namespace, and observes its SLA timers and its `issueInstruction` and `recordResult` activities (Arch v5 slide 17). They are stated here as observed and not built here; no workflow, activity or Schedule is created, changed or owned by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added. InstructionWorkflow is started by the instruction and runs on its SLA timers, so the harness starts the journey with the result and invoice submissions and sets no cron, overlap policy or catch-up window.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-01); partner and partner_instruction are S9's in `rwb_partner`, decision_log_entry and rule_row are P7's in `rwb_decision`, recovery_case is P3's in `rwb_case`, and the proceeds records are P8's in `rwb_payment`.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Contract | Stubbed answer in the run |
|---|---|---|
| Stub for rwb-partner (S9) | `GET /partners`, `GET /partner/instructions`, `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results`, `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/invoices` | Partner `PRT-SYN-0007` with its panel status and contract; instruction `INS-SYN-2027-0007` on case `RW-2027-000901` with its status and result_code; a result accepted once per Idempotency-Key; an invoice accepted once per Idempotency-Key with its submission outcome; a repeat of either key returns the first answer unchanged. No invoice read is offered, because the map publishes none |
| Stub for rwb-payment (P8) | `GET /proceeds` | The proceeds record the result is matched against, with the case it belongs to, so the check has a money side and no amount is invented by the harness |
| Stub for rwb-decision (P7) | `GET /decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | One approval entry with its rule_id and rule_version once the approval is taken, and none before; a second read returns the same single entry |
| Stub for rwb-case (P3) | `GET /cases/{caseId}` | Case `RW-2027-000901` with its state before the submission and after it |
| Stub for rwb-access (P4) | `GET /me/session` | Allows the partner and agency manager with Partner portal R and U; refuses RW-CASEOWN with 403 and MSG-P4-002, and a submission short of a required field with MSG-GEN-001 |

Each stub is generated from the published contract and its version is pinned in the run report, so a contract change shows up as a run failure and not as a silent pass. The harness environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the fee claim and schedule answer shape, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0473; ASM-0665).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 8 consumed, one hop each on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13) |
| Kafka | None published; three consumed, `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1`, `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`, counted and replayed once |
| Temporal | None added; InstructionWorkflow on `rwb-partner` observed from its history, with its SLA timers and its issueInstruction and recordResult activities |
| File | None owned. The result upload is the multipart body of S9's results operation and the invoice is S9's own request body; both are exercised through the owner's contract and neither is staged here |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-13 adds nothing: the partner-portal and proceeds paths are rewritten onto each owner's own base and there is no shared base left. The H dependency DP-03 adds, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, is a platform story delivered by the platform wave and is not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays None; the same holds for RWB-PLT-N001-CON, which DP-19 adds for the composite route behind the partner portal and the screens. The one blocking dependency is the I story RWB-S9-E7012-APP, which replaces its stub; until it is live the run uses the stub, and a stub pass is reported as a stub pass.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the five owned criteria in order for one instruction and its invoice, and holds the run lock |
| PartnerDriver | Service | Reads the partner and its contract, and names the schedule the claim is checked against |
| InstructionDriver | Service | Reads the instruction and its recorded result, submits one result and one invoice with one Idempotency-Key each, and reads the answer back |
| ProceedsReadBack | Service | Reads the P8 proceeds record the result is matched against and names it in the report |
| DecisionProbe | Service | Reads the approval entry and its rule version, and holds the fault switch that forces the decision-record failure |
| EventObserver | Service | Subscribes to `rwb.partner.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`, counts publications and replays each partner event once |
| WorkflowProbe | Service | Observes InstructionWorkflow in the `rwb-recovery` namespace: its SLA timer, its issueInstruction and recordResult steps and the run it belongs to |
| StubSet | Fake | The five stubs of §12.8, generated from the published contracts with the version pinned |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes one report per instruction and invoice, keyed by story and instruction id, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the stubs from Day 1 and the real services as RWB-S9-E7012-APP lands, on the synthetic partner `PRT-SYN-0007`, the case `RW-2027-000901`, the instruction `INS-SYN-2027-0007`, the invoice against it and the recorded result, with the fixture's business date. The harness seeds nothing by hand and never writes a schema row. The environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the fee claim and schedule answer shape, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0473; ASM-0665).

**Build steps**

1. Generate the five stubs from the published contracts and pin each contract version in the run report; fail the run on a mismatch (X1).
2. Build the PartnerDriver and prove the partner read returns the partner, its panel status and its contract, and that the schedule is named from it (AC2).
3. Add the InstructionDriver: one instruction read, one result submission and one invoice submission, each with one Idempotency-Key, and a repeat that changes nothing (AC3, X3).
4. Add the ProceedsReadBack for AC2: the proceeds record the result is matched against, named in the report beside the schedule and the result, so a claim checked against neither fails the run (X2).
5. Add the DecisionProbe for AC1 and AC3: exactly one approval entry with its rule_id and rule_version, and no second entry after a re-read (X3).
6. Add the EventObserver for AC3: one InstructionIssued and one PartnerResultSubmitted publication, one DecisionRecorded publication, the consumer effect once, and a replay that changes nothing because the inbox holds one row per consumer (X5).
7. Add the WorkflowProbe for AC3: the InstructionWorkflow run for the instruction, its SLA timer, and the issueInstruction and recordResult steps, so a result that is submitted but never recorded fails the run (X4).
8. Add the fault switch for AC4: force the decision-record failure, assert MSG-P7-003 and assert the instruction, the invoice, the case and the decision log are unchanged (X6).
9. Add the access path for AC5 through the session read and the two submissions, then the EvidenceReport and the gate, and swap a stub for the real owner as RWB-S9-E7012-APP lands (X7, X8).

**Feature switch.** None. The harness has no production flag; the fault switch of step 8 exists in the test environment only and is reset by the runner before each run.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass against the fakes and again against RWB-S9-E7012-APP when it lands, and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story and instruction id.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values on the answer it reads, and owns no message text and no S9 message of its own. MSG-GEN-001 is asserted with the missing field when a result or an invoice submission is made short of a required parameter, MSG-P4-002 with the refused action when the caller holds Partner portal R but not U, and MSG-P7-003 when the decision record cannot be written and nothing changes.

##### 15. Screens and states

The legacy story names SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation, and this harness renders neither: it observes the owners' operations and writes a report. The states are read through those operations, not rendered.

| State | Read through | What the run asserts |
|---|---|---|
| SENT | S9 partner instruction read, and InstructionWorkflow | The instruction is with the partner with its due_at, and its SLA timer is running |
| DONE | S9 partner instruction read, and InstructionWorkflow | The result is recorded with its result_code, and the recordResult step has run once |
| The approval | P7 decision log, S9 invoice submission answer and the P7 decision record event | Exactly one approval entry with its rule version, and no second entry after a re-read |

The harness renders no screen. SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation belong to the S9 stories of the legacy key and of the features around it, and neither is built or read here. What the wave entry check looks at instead is the run report, whose environment, layout and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0473; ASM-0665).

##### 16. Test cases

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-E7-012-01-ITG | AC1 (legacy); ITG AC1 | End to end | Partner `PRT-SYN-0007` with its contract, instruction `INS-SYN-2027-0007` with its recorded result, the invoice, and the approval taken once |
| TC-E7-012-02-ITG | AC2 not recorded (legacy); ITG AC4 | Integration | A forced decision-record failure at the approval, after the result and the invoice are submitted |
| TC-E7-012-03-ITG | Access; ITG AC5 | Component | A synthetic RW-CASEOWN caller holding Partner portal R and not U |
| TC-E7-012-04-ITG | Principle 5; ITG AC4 | Integration | A forced decision-record failure with the instruction, the invoice, the case and the decision log read before and after |

The AC column names the legacy AC the copy derives from and the ITG AC it asserts, and the full legacy test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx under the same legacy test case ID. Legacy AC2 stays with RWB-S9-E7012-APP, which owns the failure inside the approval. ITG AC2 and ITG AC3 are asserted inside the run of TC-E7-012-01-ITG, which is the end-to-end case that names the schedule, the result and the proceeds and counts the single approval and its events; they add no test case ID because the legacy set has four.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the synthetic partner, its contract, the instruction, the result, the invoice, the business date, the fault switch, the retry settings and the report layout are data.
- No personal data in logs, events or reports: every key is synthetic, and the events carry IDs and facts only.
- Service data only through the owner's contract: the partner and the instruction from S9, the proceeds from P8, the decision log and the rule rows from P7, the case from P3; never a direct schema read and never another service's table (DP-01).
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would (DP-11, DP-13).
- A stub pass is never reported as a real pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and it never writes a row by hand or sets a state it then asserts.
- The fault switch is reset by the runner before each run and is never left on, so a forced failure cannot be mistaken for a real one.
- A failing criterion is fixed in the owning service or raised as a gap; it is never waived in the script.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of the partner review of rwb-partner, split from RWB-E7-013. It fixes the review-entry element, the unchanged `partner` and `partner_instruction` elements, the consumed rule-row and reference-data rows, the rights and the error set of the act, the fakes, and the three absences the act has — no operation, no event and no column of its own — on the base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13) behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The six operations of the service are declared as the earlier stories' and the review act is not given a seventh. Two consumed operation names, the review read and the action list are unpublished, and the plan's C row is empty although the act consumes rwb-decision and rwb-case (GAP-3126; ASM-5446 to ASM-5449). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead of rwb-partner**, I want **the published contract baseline of the partner review — the review-entry element, the unchanged `partner` and `partner_instruction` elements, the consumed rule-row and reference-data rows, the rights and the error set of the act, the fakes and the three absences**, so that **the app story, the SCR-34 and SCR-35 review slice and the wave 4 harness build against one fixed, testable contract on Day 1, and a point, a list or a right can never drift between rwb-partner, rwb-decision and rwb-case without a failing build**.

The baseline is deliberately narrow: it declares one element of this service, two unchanged elements, two consumed rows and the absences the act has. It declares no operation, no event and no Schedule of its own.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy review of RWB-E7-013 ran inside one process and one schema: it read the partner, the instructions, the rule row and the decision log without a boundary. The target splits them: rwb-partner owns the partner and its instructions, rwb-decision owns the package, the rule rows and the central ledger, rwb-case owns the parameters and the reference data by the R3 default ruling, and rwb-access owns the rights and the lists of values. Each boundary is a contract another team builds against, so the shapes have to be fixed before the app story starts: the partner element it reads, the six points and the actions it records, the entry it writes and the rights of the act.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_partner`, login `rwb_partner`, base `/api/recovery/partner/v1`, topic `rwb.partner.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner` (Template and Rules v1 §R4; context pack service row). It records that rwb-partner holds no grant on `rwb_case`, `rwb_decision` or `rwb_access`, so the reference data, the rule rows and the rights are consumed on their owners' contracts only.

Four points are carried as gaps and assumptions rather than decided quietly: the baseline declares no operation for the review, because the six the Ownership Map gives S9 all belong to earlier stories of the service and the review read is unpublished (GAP-3126; ASM-5446); no column of `partner` or `partner_instruction` carries the review, so both elements are unchanged and the review lives on its entry (ASM-5447); the rule-row read and the reference-data read carry placeholders because no source publishes their operation names and DP-04, DP-06 and DP-07 are not in the pattern set (ASM-5448); and the six points and the action list are declared as reference data with no published action list (GAP-3126; ASM-5449).

The wave and the date are the plan's: this key is EP07, wave 4, release 31 May 2027, and rwb-partner is itself wave 4, so the business wave and the service wave agree and no W-MAP conflict is raised; the date is copied unchanged and marked tentative (ASM-5449).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the queue and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the pagination and filter convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline (Architecture v5 slide 11); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The ownership of the objects is taken from the context pack and the Ownership Map only: `partner`, `partner_instruction` and `partner_user` are S9's, `recovery_case`, `queue`, `assignment` and `timer` are P3's, `rule_row` and `decision_log_entry` are P7's, `document` is P5's, `notice` is P6's and `interaction` is P1's. This document never declares another service's table or operation as its own.
- The rule-package read and the reference-data read are published with fakes so the consumed rows name a real owner document; neither is a row of this story's dependency list, which is None, and the absence is recorded (GAP-3126; ASM-5448).
- TSD S9 T6.1 is the only rights source for this service, and the legacy permission table of the key gives the same intent for the act (right U) and for the read (right R); no right is widened here (ASM-5449).
- The three tables and their columns arrive with the DB story of this service; this baseline declares shapes and creates no table, no column and no migration.
- The six operations of this legacy key's service, API-S9-001 to API-S9-006, are outside this baseline and belong to the earlier stories of the service.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules v1 §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-partner for this step and record that it declares no operation for the review, with the six operations of the service named as the earlier stories' and their rights restated.
2. Declare the `partner` and `partner_instruction` elements exactly as TSD S9 T3.1 gives them, and record that no field of either carries the review, a point or an action.
3. Declare the consumed rule-row read of rwb-decision and the reference-data read of rwb-case, with the fields the review needs, and record that their operation names are unpublished.
4. Fix the review-entry element of DP-03 with its attributes, its write order and its failure behaviour.
5. Publish the rights of the act and of the read from TSD S9 T6.1, and record the two heads of function as readers and approvers rather than writers.
6. Publish the error set, the status codes and the message IDs of the act and of the read.
7. Publish the fakes of 12.8 and the three absence tests: no operation, no event and no column.
8. Fix the naming baseline and the boundary, then tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-S9-E7013-APP, the SCR-34 and SCR-35 review slice and the wave 4 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A body fails schema validation or an element carries a value outside a list of values | The build fails on the schema and vocabulary lint; a deployed service answers 400 or 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC2, AC4, AC7 |
| X2 | A field is renamed or removed within major version 1, or a list value changes | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC2 |
| X3 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X4 | A consumed row has a field list or a name the sources do not give | The row carries the placeholder, the gap and the assumption, and the fake is derived from the published document | None | AC3 |
| X5 | The document declares a review operation, an event, a Schedule, a queue table, a foreign table property or a new column of `partner` | The absence and boundary tests fail the build | None | AC1, AC2, AC7 |
| X6 | The rights of the act and of the read are not the ones TSD S9 T6.1 declares, or the unattended identity is given a user right | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |
| X7 | A point, a status, an action or a rule version is declared with a value no source gives, or as a schema default | The review fails the baseline; the element carries the placeholder | None | AC4, AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the context pack and the published owner contracts of rwb-decision and rwb-case only |
| Negotiable | The element attribute names beyond the ones the sources give, the example values and the fake fixtures are settled in the baseline review; the fields, the lists, the base, the topic and the queue are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks RWB-S9-E7013-APP, the SCR-34 and SCR-35 review slice and the wave 4 harness on Day 1 |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, nine contract tables, five fakes and seven new contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The `partner` and `partner_instruction` elements are this service's and are declared exactly as TSD S9 T3.1 gives them, with no review field and no added list value | Context pack ownership rows; TSD S9 T3.1 and T3.2; DP-01 |
| BR2 | The review is declared as an entry written before anything else, through the local library on the shared topic; a failed write changes nothing | DP-03; TSD S9 T2; R-UNI-39; legacy RWB-E7-013 AC2 |
| BR3 | The rule rows stay with rwb-decision: the contract declares the read as consumed and declares no `rule_row` property and no rule ID of its own | TSD S9 T2, T5.2; ASM-5448 |
| BR4 | The reference data stays with rwb-case under the R3 default ruling: the contract declares the read as consumed and declares no reference-data property | R3 default rulings; DP-06, DP-07; ASM-5448 |
| BR5 | The six points are REQ-S9-001's and are declared in its order; a status or an action with no published list carries the placeholder | REQ-S9-001; FSD S9 BR-S9-010; GAP-3126 |
| BR6 | No event belongs to this act: the contract declares no published event and no consumed event, and names `InstructionIssued` (EV-20) and `PartnerResultSubmitted` (EV-21) as the instruction stories' | Context pack ownership rows; TSD S9 T5.3; ASM-5446 |
| BR7 | No Schedule belongs to this act: the Ownership Map gives S9 no job and FSD S9 A2.10.4.4 declares no background event | Context pack ownership rows (Jobs 0); FSD S9 A2.10.4.4; ASM-5449 |
| BR8 | The rights are TSD S9 T6.1's and nothing wider: Partner portal U for the act, R for the read, and the two heads of function keep RA | TSD S9 T6.1; FSD S9 A2.10.3.3; ASM-5449 |
| BR9 | The partner and instruction vocabularies are closed: the values of TSD S9 T3.2 are declared and this step adds none | TSD S9 T3.2; ASM-5447 |
| BR10 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, list values, a rule version and an instant only, and the registered name of the firm is not personal data | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 (s17); FSD S9 A2.10.3.2 |
| BR11 | One REST base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; the document never declares another service's base or topic as its own | DP-13, DP-14; Template and Rules v1 §R4 |
| BR12 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 11 notes |
| BR13 | No point, no status, no action and no rule version is a schema default or a constant | FSD S9 BR-S9-010; ASM-5449 |

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of this document, not of a partner:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The entry, the unchanged elements, the consumed rows and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, the SCR-34 and SCR-35 review slice, the wave 4 harness, the rwb-decision owner and the rwb-case owner accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | An attribute is added within major version 1 | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | An attribute is removed, renamed or retyped, or a list value changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | An operation, an event, a Schedule, a new column or a foreign table property | In review |

The panel status of a partner is a value of `LOV-PANEL` and moves on the notice and the contract end, not here: this baseline declares the vocabulary on which `panel_status` is declared and adds no value to it.

|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-partner | Owns the OpenAPI document and the contract tables; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version, the correction of a consumed row and the reading of the rights |
| Consuming teams (the app story, the SCR-34 and SCR-35 review slice, the wave 4 harness, the rwb-decision owner and the rwb-case owner) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| Platform library owner | Owns the error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule and the decision-record library this document reuses |

The per-service login behind the security scheme of the document is named "the rwb-partner login (DP-02)" and is not part of this baseline.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |

| Partner element | The seven columns of DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 as TSD S9 T3.1 gives them, unchanged: `id`, `partner_code`, `partner_name`, `partner_type`, `panel_status`, `contract_end`, `score` |
| Instruction element | The nine columns of DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 as TSD S9 T3.1 gives them, unchanged: `id`, `case_id`, `partner_id`, `instruction_type`, `instructed_at`, `due_at`, `status`, `result_code`, `fee_amount` |
| Required flags | `partner_code`, `partner_name`, `partner_type` and `panel_status` required and `contract_end` and `score` optional; `case_id`, `partner_id`, `instruction_type`, `instructed_at` and `status` required and `due_at`, `result_code` and `fee_amount` optional, as TSD S9 T3.1 gives them |
| Lists of values | `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE` with AGENCY, LAW_FIRM, VALUER, AUCTION_VENDOR, BROKER, DEBT_BUYER, AMC and RAMC; `LOV-PANEL` with ACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED and EXITED; `LOV-INSTRUCTION` with COLLECT, FILE_SUIT, ENFORCE, APPRAISE, REPOSSESS, LIST and SELL; `LOV-INSTR-STATUS` with SENT, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, IN_PROGRESS, DONE and RECALLED, all as TSD S9 T3.2 gives them |
| Review entry | The DP-03 entry attributes: partner reference, the six point values, their actions, the rule ID and package version, the reviewer and the instant; no column of `partner` or `partner_instruction` carries any of them (ASM-5447) |
| Consumed rule-row shape | The rule ID, the package, the version and the route set of the row read from rwb-decision, declared as consumed and faked (ASM-5448) |
| Consumed reference shape | The six points of REQ-S9-001, the status list, the action list and the four lists of TSD S9 T3.2, each with its version, declared as consumed and faked; the action list is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3126; ASM-5449) |
| Not declared here | `recovery_case`, `queue`, `assignment` and `timer` (P3), `rule_row` and `decision_log_entry` (P7), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `interaction` (P1), every `v_ace_*` view (P1), and the six operations API-S9-001 to API-S9-006 (the earlier stories of the service) |

The field-level formats of the entry are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the element names, the two unchanged elements, the consumed fields and the additive rule of BR12. **No new table, no new column and no migration** is declared by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. Owner rwb-partner (S9); base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13). The Ownership Map gives this service exactly six operations — `GET /partners` (API-S9-001), `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions` (API-S9-002), `GET /partner/instructions` (API-S9-003), `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/accept` (API-S9-004), `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results` (API-S9-005) and `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/invoices` (API-S9-006) — and all six are the frozen baseline of RWB-S9-AD022-CON, with a first-in epic of Epic 2 to Epic 6 (TSD S9 T-A.1). None of them records a review, so the act has no published entry point and the review read behind SCR-34 and SCR-35 is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3126; ASM-5446). A build that declares a seventh operation here fails the absence test of AC1.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| The rule-package and rule-row read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3126; ASM-5448)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The package, the rule ID and the version in force at the review instant, and any row that names a partner review; read only, faked |
| The reference-data read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3126; ASM-5448)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case, as the owner of parameters and reference data (R3 default ruling) | The six points of REQ-S9-001, the status list, the action list and the four lists of TSD S9 T3.2, each with its version; read only, faked |

Each row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, one retry with jitter on a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020, DP-11). Both are contract dependencies of class C that the plan's C row does not carry, and the absence is recorded as GAP-3126 with ASM-5448.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service owns `InstructionIssued` (EV-20) and `PartnerResultSubmitted` (EV-21) on `rwb.partner.events.v1` — an instruction reference with its case, partner, type and due date for the first, and an instruction reference with its result code and fee for the second — and both report an instruction or a result: their schemas are declared in the service baseline RWB-S9-AD022-CON and their behaviour belongs to the instruction stories of this service (context pack ownership rows; TSD S9 T5.3). A review issues no instruction and submits no result, so this baseline declares no producer, no envelope and no outbox row of its own, and the absence test of AC7 fails a build that adds one (ASM-5446).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. No source gives rwb-partner a consumed event for this act: the service acts on the events of rwb-case for its instruction stories, and the review is started by a person on a screen. This baseline declares no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox of its own (ASM-5446).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `InstructionWorkflow` | Workflow, the service's only one | `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | The workflow of the instruction stories; this baseline names it and declares no branch of it |
| The review act | Synchronous service act, no workflow | `rwb-partner` | The read, the reference load, the rule version and the entry, in one request |
| `recordReview` | Synchronous step of the act, one transaction | `rwb-partner` | The entry, the reviewer and the answer out |

The service has no case state machine of its own and no job (TSD S9 T4; context pack Jobs 0), so the review is a synchronous act whose only durable artefact is the decision record. No source puts the review inside `InstructionWorkflow`, and this baseline declares no child workflow, no activity registration and no durable timer (ASM-5449).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The Ownership Map gives S9 no job and FSD S9 A2.10.4.4 declares no background event for the feature, so this baseline declares no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table (ASM-5449).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| `partner` | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The partner, its type, its panel status, its contract end and its score; the element the baseline declares unchanged and the app story reads |
| `partner_instruction` | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The work placed with the partner; the element the baseline declares unchanged and the app story reads |
| `partner_user` | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The partner portal identities of the firm; declared as owned and not read by the review |
| `decision_record` | PLT library, created in `rwb_partner` | The local hash-linked review entry (DP-03) |
| `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_partner` | The key of the repeat and the answer it holds (R-UNI-40) |

`recovery_case`, `queue`, `assignment` and `timer` (P3), `rule_row` and `decision_log_entry` (P7), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `interaction` (P1) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1) are not owned by this baseline; it names them only as answers, rule versions or records of their owners, and no foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Local decision-record stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain, a stopped chain and a hash break | AC4, AC6 |
| rwb-decision rule-version fake | The package at its version in force with no row naming a partner review, and a package with no version in force; the operation name carries the placeholder (GAP-3126; ASM-5448) | AC3, AC6 |
| rwb-case reference-data fake | The six points in REQ-S9-001's order with their version, the four lists of TSD S9 T3.2, an unpublished action list and no answer inside 2 s; the operation name carries the placeholder (GAP-3126; ASM-5448) | AC3, AC6 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-34 and SCR-35 answer for a synthetic partner, with the review slice of this service read once | AC1, AC6 |
| Authorise stub of the service template | Partner portal right U held, a caller without it, and a partner portal user scoped to another firm | AC5, AC6 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The two operation names are derived from the published documents and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-3126; ASM-5448).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 2 consumed | The rwb-decision rule-package read and the rwb-case reference-data read; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | EV-20 and EV-21 are the instruction stories'; the decision record is the library's on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and is not an event of this service |
| Temporal | 0 branches, 0 activities and 0 timers declared | `InstructionWorkflow` is the service's and belongs to the instruction stories; no Schedule and no child workflow |
| File | None | No file is read, built or delivered here |

##### 13. Solution plan

**The CON declares shapes and moves nothing.** It writes no code, no migration and no table, and it changes no partner, no instruction, no rule package and no case. What it publishes is one OpenAPI 3.1 document, nine contract tables, the rights of the act and the read, and five fakes.

**Deliverables.** The additive document `openapi/rwb-partner-v1.yaml` with the two unchanged elements and no review operation, the contract README rows for the two consumed rows and their placeholders, the review-entry schema of the library, and the five WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | the monolith API base | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the element the baseline declares before anything else is answered. DP-13 moves the base of the service and adds no operation, because this step owns none. DP-19 is behind SCR-34 and SCR-35, whose screen model is the edge contract's. No other pattern is claimed: the rule package is a consumed contract (DP-04, recorded and not claimed), the reference data is consumed at a version (DP-06 and DP-07, recorded and not claimed), so none of the three appears in the metadata row and all three are in the registers (GAP-3126; ASM-5448).

**Build steps**

1. Record the absence of a review operation and the six operations as the earlier stories', with the absent-operation test of AC1.
2. Publish the `partner` and `partner_instruction` elements unchanged with their sixteen properties, their required flags and their four lists, and record the no-review-column rule of AC2.
3. Record the two consumed rows of AC3 with their owners, their fields, their lists, their budget and the placeholders.
4. Publish the review-entry element of AC4, with the six points, the actions, the rule ID and version, the reviewer and the instant, and validate it against the library schema.
5. Record the rights, the roles and the identity of AC5.
6. Publish the five fakes of AC6 and the drift test.
7. Record the naming baseline and the boundary of AC7, then tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI document validates in the pipeline, the seven contract tests pass, the fakes answer every path and the drift test is green, and the app story, the SCR-34 and SCR-35 review slice and the wave 4 harness have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. | A required field of an element is absent or invalid, or a body fails schema validation, or a list value is outside its enumeration |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | The role lacks the Partner portal right of the act or of the read, and a scope outside the caller's firm is refused the same way |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | The review entry cannot be written before anything else |

The three message IDs are those of the legacy message set of this key; the text is the legacy and FSD S9 wording, copied unchanged, and no message is reworded or added. R-UNI-39's incident is raised by the platform on the same failure and is not a message of this service.

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves the review slice of SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The route calls rwb-partner for the partner, its instructions and the review entry, rwb-case for the case label and rwb-decision for the rule version; this baseline fixes the rwb-partner answer only, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON (ASM-5446). The review read behind the list is a placeholder, because no source publishes it. The legacy screen table's two screens are accounted for, and SCR-36 Partner scorecard is FEAT-PRM-08's screen and is not answered here. The loading, list, review-open, recorded, refused, not-recorded, empty-score and unavailable states read the messages of section 14 on the same route.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the six points, the statuses, the actions, the partner types, the panel states, the instruction lists and the rule versions stay reference data or an enumeration, never a schema default or a constant of the code.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, list values, a rule version and an instant only; no contact value, number or address appears anywhere in the document.
- The rule rows and the central ledger stay with rwb-decision, the reference data and the case with rwb-case and the rights with rwb-access: the document declares no `rule_row`, `recovery_case`, `queue`, `timer` or `v_ace_*` property (BR3, BR4).
- This step owns no operation and no event: the document declares none for it and records the six operations of the service as the earlier stories' (BR6, AC1).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13).
- The `partner` and `partner_instruction` elements are declared unchanged: a build that adds a review column, a point or an action list to them fails the absence test (BR1, ASM-5447).
- No retired element is reintroduced: the absence tests fail a build that declares an event, a second topic, a Schedule, a Quartz row or a shared job table (BR7).
- The rights are TSD S9 T6.1's and are never widened in a contract; a partner portal user sees its own firm only, and that scope is tested (BR8).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the review slice of RWB-E7-013 is realigned onto rwb-partner (S9, service wave 4, business wave 4). The one legacy criterion this story owns, AC2, is kept word for word with its origin tag and needs no mock line, because its only dependency is the local decision record; AC1 of the key is owned by RWB-ITG-E7013-ITG and the review behind it is built and tested here. The review reads the partner and its instructions from `rwb_partner`, reads the six points and their action values as reference data at a version, evaluates the rule package in force in rwb-decision, writes one hash-linked decision record before anything is shown as done (DP-03) and answers SCR-34 and SCR-35 through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) on the base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13). No rule row names a partner review, no operation records one, no list of action values is published and no column carries the outcome, so those values carry the placeholder (GAP-3125; ASM-5438 to ASM-5445). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **partner and agency manager (RW-AGENCYMG)** — and as a role that holds the Partner portal write right where the matrix gives another role only the read — I want **the Workbench to run the review of a partner against the six points every partner type is managed on and to record the actions**, so that **partners are placed, paid and measured by rule and the review is on the decision log with the rule version it was judged under**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E7-013, feature FEAT-PRM-10 of module S9 Partner management (FSD S9 A2.10; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3). It owns:

- the one legacy criterion this slice keeps, AC2, copied word for word with its origin tag; AC1 of the key is owned by RWB-ITG-E7013-ITG;
- the review of a partner against the six points of REQ-S9-001 — selection, contract and fees, targets and incentives, data exchange, performance reviews, notice and exit — with the observation and the action of each point held as data at a version (FSD S9 A2.10.2; REQ-S9-001);
- the partner facts of the review: `partner` (`partner_code`, `partner_name`, `partner_type`, `panel_status`, `contract_end`, `score`) and the instructions placed with the partner on `partner_instruction`, read on this service's own schema (TSD S9 T3.1, DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-016);
- the record of the review: one hash-linked entry per review through the local decision-record library, written **before** anything is shown as done, carrying the partner, the six point values, the actions, the rule ID and the package version in force, the reviewer and the instant (DP-03; legacy AC2; BR-S9-010);
- the read of the rule package and of the reference data at their versions, on the owners' contracts, so that no point, no status, no action and no rule version is written in code (DP-06, DP-07 recorded and not claimed; VR-S9-010-1; BR-S9-010);
- the review answer behind SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), on base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13).

It does not own: AC1 of the legacy key and the cross-service evidence of the review, which are RWB-ITG-E7013-ITG's; the published shapes, the review-entry element, the consumed rows, the rights, the error set and the fakes, which are RWB-S9-E7013-CON's; the six REST operations of the service, which belong to the earlier stories of this service (API-S9-001 to API-S9-006, first in Epic 2 to Epic 6); the monthly scorecard itself (FEAT-PRM-08, RWB-S9-E7011-APP); the approval of partner fees (FEAT-PRM-09, RWB-S9-E7012-APP); the notice on a missed target (FEAT-PRM-11, RWB-S9-E7014-APP); the end of a contract and the recall of the work (FEAT-PRM-12, RWB-S9-E7015-APP); the conduct check and the breach report (FEAT-PRM-13, RWB-S9-E7016-APP); the partner panel and the fee schedule as data (FEAT-PRM-02, RWB-S9-E6030-APP); the case of record and its workflow (rwb-case P3); the rule rows and the central ledger (rwb-decision P7); the roles and the lists of values (rwb-access P4); the documents and the notices (rwb-document P5, rwb-comms P6); and the schema, the migration and the deployment of this service (the DB, INF and OPS stories of this key).

##### 2. Business rationale

Partners are instructed and paid by email and spreadsheet, and allocation is not based on performance (FSD S9 A1.3, repeated in A2.10.1). The requirement is REQ-S9-001: "Every partner type is managed on the same six points: selection, contract and fees, targets and incentives, data exchange, performance reviews, notice and exit", with REQ-S9-007 for the forum the review reports to (FSD S9 Requirements served, Must, E6 and E7). The metric is the module's: placements by scorecard at 100 percent, measured on the decision log and the Workbench records and reviewed monthly (FSD S9 A2.10.1).

A review that is not recorded is a conversation: the placement that follows it, the notice that follows that and the exit that follows the notice all have to point at one decision taken against one version of the rules. The legacy criterion says exactly that — "the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version" — and stops the act dead when the record cannot be written. Under D-RCV-60 the facts of that act split three ways, and none of them moves:

- **The partner is this service's fact.** `partner` carries the code, the registered name, the type, the panel status, the contract end and the score of the partner, and `partner_instruction` carries the work placed with it (TSD S9 T3.1; DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-016). The review reads its own schema and needs no second service to say what the partner is.
- **The rule version is rwb-decision's.** Legacy AC1 asks for the result "with the rule version"; the rule rows and their versions are governed in rwb-decision (P7), so this service evaluates the package in force and records the ID and version on its own entry, exactly as the local-record pattern asks (DP-03).
- **The points are reference data, not constants.** BR-S9-010 forbids any value a business person may change from being written in code. The six points, the statuses the reviewer records and the action list are therefore rows read at a version — and where no list is published, the placeholder stays and the gap is raised rather than a value invented (GAP-3125; ASM-5438, ASM-5442).
- **The review moves nothing else.** The panel status, the contract end, the recall and the notice are separate acts of FEAT-PRM-11, 12 and 13 on their own criteria and rules (R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-29, R-UNI-45). This story records the review and its actions and leaves the partner row exactly as it found it (ASM-5439).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S9-E7013-CON is published and tagged: the review-entry element, the unchanged `partner` and `partner_instruction` elements, the consumed rows, the rights, the error set and the fakes are baselined and handed to this story.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer stub: the local decision-record library writes in the caller's transaction, and a failed write stops the act with MSG-P7-003 (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-34 and SCR-35 reach this service through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, and no screen calls a service directly (DP-19).
- `partner`, `partner_instruction` and `partner_user` exist in `rwb_partner` from the DB story of this service, with the standard record columns of TSD S9 T3.0, and at least one partner of each `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE` value and one instruction per status of `LOV-INSTR-STATUS` are available as test data (TSD S9 T3.1, T3.2).
- The rule package in force is available at its version, authored, tested and approved in rwb-decision (P7) and loaded here; no source gives a rule row whose event is a partner review, so the review records the package version it evaluated and invents no rule ID (GAP-3125; ASM-5440).
- The reference-data read of rwb-case is published with its fake: `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE`, `LOV-PANEL`, `LOV-INSTRUCTION`, `LOV-INSTR-STATUS` and the six-point list, each with its version; its operation name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3125; ASM-5443).
- The scorecard this review reads is the `partner.score` of FEAT-PRM-08, written by RWB-S9-E7011-APP inside this service; the plan carries no H row to that story, so the review builds against a seeded score and treats a missing score as a stated absence (GAP-3125; ASM-5443).
- The service runs as its own login on `rwb_partner`, holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `rwb_case`, on `rwb_decision` or on a `recovery.v_ace_*` view is refused by the database and fails the boundary test (DP-01, DP-05).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-S9-E7013-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The partner and agency manager opens SCR-34 Partner list and selects a partner, or opens SCR-35 Placement and allocation and selects the partner from a placement (legacy screens table; FSD S9 Screens).
2. The gateway-bff composite route merges the partner answer of this service with the case label of rwb-case and the scorecard block of this service, one hop each, in parallel (DP-19; ASM-5441).
3. `readReviewFacts` reads the partner row (`partner_code`, `partner_name`, `partner_type`, `panel_status`, `contract_end`, `score`) and the instructions placed with it (`instruction_type`, `status`, `due_at`, `result_code`, `fee_amount`) on `rwb_partner`, read only (TSD S9 T3.1).
4. `loadReviewReference` reads the six points of REQ-S9-001 in their order, the statuses the reviewer may record and the list of actions, each with its version, on the reference-data contract of rwb-case; where a list is not published the value is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3125; ASM-5438, ASM-5442).
5. `evaluateReviewRules` loads the package version in force from rwb-decision and returns the rule ID and version the review is judged under; the review records the version whether or not a row names the review (GAP-3125; ASM-5440).
6. The manager records, for each of the six points, the observation and the action taken, and confirms the reviewer and the review date; a required value left empty is refused with MSG-GEN-001 (VR-S9-010-1).
7. `recordReview` writes one hash-linked entry through the local library **before any other effect**: the partner reference, the six point values with their action, the rule ID and package version, the reviewer identity and the instant. A failed write changes nothing and returns MSG-P7-003 (DP-03; legacy AC2).
8. The review answer is returned to the composite route with the entry reference, the six points, the actions and the rule version, and SCR-34 and SCR-35 show it as the recorded review of the partner (FSD S9 A2.10.2 step 3).
9. The partner row is not written: `panel_status` and `contract_end` stay as they were, and the review raises no instruction, no notice and no recall — those are FEAT-PRM-11, 12 and 13 on their own criteria and rules (ASM-5439).
10. A repeated submission for the same partner and the same review date is idempotent on its key: the stored answer is returned, one entry exists, and the repeat is recorded as an idempotency hit (R-UNI-40).
11. A role without the Partner portal right of the act is refused before any read of the partner and before any record, with MSG-P4-002 (TSD S9 T6.1; legacy permission table).
12. A conduct breach found during the review is not acted on here: R-UNI-29's suspend, recall and report is the partner conduct story's separate act and is recorded against the review for its evidence (R-UNI-29; ASM-5439).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The local decision record cannot be written | Nothing changes: no entry, no action recorded, no review shown as done, and the partner row is untouched | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, TC-E7-013-02, TC-E7-013-04 |
| X2 | The role does not hold the Partner portal right of the act | 403 before any read and before any record, with the same check on the composite route and on any service identity | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E7-013-03 |
| X3 | A required value is absent or invalid: no partner, no point, no status, no reviewer or no review date | The act is refused, nothing is written and the field is named | MSG-GEN-001 (VR-S9-010-1) | AC2 |
| X4 | The reference-data read or the rule-package read does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The screen shows no review form, nothing is written and the platform 503 envelope is returned; the read is retried once with jitter on a GET | None (platform envelope) | Section 12.2 |
| X5 | No list is published for the statuses or the actions of a point | The point is shown with its observation and the action value carries the placeholder; the review may be recorded with the placeholder, and the gap is reported | None | GAP-3125 |
| X6 | `partner.score` is empty because the monthly scorecard has not run | The performance-review point shows the absence and its date, and the review records that absence; no score is invented | None | ASM-5443 |
| X7 | The same partner and review date are submitted twice | One entry per key; the stored answer is returned and the repeat is counted | None | R-UNI-40 |
| X8 | The action recorded against a point would change the panel status, send a notice or end the contract | The review records the observation only; the action is refused as out of this story and routed to FEAT-PRM-11, 12 or 13 | None | Section 19 |
| X9 | A component, a statement or a test reaches a `v_ace_*` view, a `rwb_case` row, a `rwb_decision` row or another service's schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | Section 17, BR6, BR7 |

X1 and X2 are the legacy not-recorded and access paths of this key carried onto the slice; X3 to X8 are the paths the reference data, the scorecard and the target call types add; X9 is the schema and ACE boundary.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-S9-E7013-CON, the decision-record stub, the reference-data fake, the rule-version fake and the gateway-bff fake, on its own schema, and needs no live P3 or P7 |
| Negotiable | The activity names, the shape of the review entry and the screen layout are this story's choice; the six points, the lists, the messages, the rule version and the rights are fixed |
| Valuable | A partner is reviewed on the same six points as every other partner type, the actions are recorded, and the result is on the decision log with the rule version it was judged under |
| Estimable | One read step, one reference step, one rule step, one record write, three clients and one screen slice |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Every path runs on synthetic partners through the contract fakes, plus the refused-right, the missing-value, the empty-score and the forced record-write failure |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Hold a partner review

  Background:
    Given the rule package in force and the reference data of the six points are read at their versions
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC2 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E7-013 AC2)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The criterion is the legacy AC2 of the key, word for word, and is the only criterion this slice owns; it needs no mock line because its only dependency is the local decision record, which is not a cross-service call, and every value of the legacy text is kept. AC1 of the same key — "Then runs the review against the six points every partner type is managed on, and records the actions / Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version" — is owned by RWB-ITG-E7013-ITG, which carries the cross-service journey of the key in wave 4; the review behind it is built and tested here and is stated in sections 4, 8 and 16. On this story "the action" is the review act of a partner against the six points, and "the decision log" is the local decision record of DP-03 in `rwb_partner`, with the `decision_log_entry` ledger of rwb-decision behind it.

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Codes | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-UNI-25 | Universal rules | All | ANY_ACTIVE | PARTNER_NO_RESPONSE | the partner misses the service level on the portal | Chase once, then recall the work and re-select on the scorecard | PARTNER_RECALLED | Partner and agency manager | Partner Portal | per partner type |
| R-UNI-26 | Universal rules | All | ANY_ACTIVE | PARTNER_PANEL_EXIT | the partner leaves the panel or the contract ends | Recall every open case held by that partner and re-select | PARTNER_RECALLED | Partner and agency manager | Partner Portal | 5 working days |
| R-UNI-27 | Universal rules | All | ANY_ACTIVE | PARTNER_CONFLICT_DECLARED | the partner declares a conflict of interest | Withdraw the instruction, re-select the next partner on the scorecard | PARTNER_RECALLED | Partner and agency manager | Partner Portal | 2 working days |
| R-UNI-28 | Universal rules | All | ANY_ACTIVE | PARTNER_INSOLVENT | the partner enters insolvency | Recall the work, secure the documents and any cash held, stop fee payments | PARTNER_RECALLED | Head of the partner type | Partner Portal, Workbench | same day |
| R-UNI-29 | Universal rules | All | ANY_ACTIVE | PARTNER_CONDUCT_BREACH | a conduct or complaint breach is upheld against the partner | Suspend allocation, recall the affected cases, report to the partner review | PARTNER_RECALLED | Partner and agency manager | Partner Portal | same day |
| R-UNI-39 | Universal rules | All | ANY_ACTIVE | DECISION_LOG_WRITE_FAILED | the decision log entry cannot be written | Block the action and raise an incident. No action proceeds unlogged | EXCEPTION_QUEUE | Platform team | Workbench | immediate |
| R-UNI-40 | Universal rules | All | ANY_ACTIVE | DUPLICATE_EVENT | the same event arrives twice with the same key | Ignore the second event, record the idempotency hit | RESUME_STATE | Workbench | Workbench | None |
| R-UNI-45 | Universal rules | All | PARTNER_RECALLED | PARTNER_RESELECTED | the next partner is selected on the scorecard | Re-issue the instruction and restart the partner clock | ROUTE_D6_REOPEN | Partner and agency manager | Partner Portal | 2 working days |

The eight rows are copied character for character from the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4. R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-29 and R-UNI-45 are the partner rules of the module: they are the consequences of a review outcome and belong to FEAT-PRM-11 to FEAT-PRM-13, so this story reads them and fires none of them. R-UNI-39 is the record-first rule of the act and R-UNI-40 is the repeat rule. Their owner column names a business role and a system, not a service: "Workbench" is this service, and "Partner Portal" is the external gateway in front of it.

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The review is a decision first: one hash-linked entry per review is written through the local library with the partner, the six point values and their actions, the rule ID and package version, the reviewer and the instant, and a failed write changes nothing and answers MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; TSD S9 T2; R-UNI-39; legacy AC2 |
| BR2 | The six points are REQ-S9-001's: selection, contract and fees, targets and incentives, data exchange, performance reviews, notice and exit; they are read at a version and never written in code | REQ-S9-001; FSD S9 BR-S9-010; ASM-5438 |
| BR3 | The partner is this service's fact and is read only: `partner` and `partner_instruction` are read on `rwb_partner` and no column of them carries the review or its actions | TSD S9 T3.1, T3.3; ASM-5439 |
| BR4 | The review moves nothing else: `panel_status`, `contract_end`, the recall, the notice and the conduct report are the acts of FEAT-PRM-11 to FEAT-PRM-13 and of R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-29 | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; ASM-5439 |
| BR5 | The rule version is read from rwb-decision and recorded with the entry; no rule ID is invented where no row names the review | TSD S9 T2; DP-03; GAP-3125 |
| BR6 | The lists of values and the six-point list are reference data read on the owner's contract; a status or an action that has no published list is recorded as Not specified in the source documents, not as a value | Template and Rules §R9; ASM-5442 |
| BR7 | No cross-schema join and no foreign key leaves `rwb_partner`; `case_id` and `partner_id` are identifiers of other services' or other modules' facts | DP-01; TSD S9 T3.3 |
| BR8 | No person name, address, contact value or identity number enters `rwb_partner`, the entry, a log or a workflow input; the registered name of the firm is not personal data and every example is synthetic | Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17); FSD S9 A2.10.3.2 |
| BR9 | Every refusal is one problem document with a code, the message ID and a correlation reference, and no message text is assembled in code | VR-S9-010-1; BR-S9-010 |

##### 9. State transitions

The service has no case state machine of its own: it acts on the case's events and writes through the decision log (TSD S9 T4). The panel status of a partner is a value of `LOV-PANEL` — ACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED, EXITED — and **this story writes none of it**: the review records an observation and an action, and the status moves only on the separate acts of the notice and the contract end (ASM-5439).

| From (`partner.panel_status`, read) | The review act | Condition | What this story writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ACTIVE` | A review is recorded against the six points | The reviewer holds the right and every required value is present | One entry; the partner row is unchanged |
| `ON_NOTICE` | A review is recorded | The partner is inside its cure period | One entry; the cure period and its clock are not touched |
| `SUSPENDED` | A review is recorded | The suspension has its own reason row | One entry; the suspension is not lifted |
| `EXITED` | A review is recorded | The contract has already ended | One entry as historical evidence; no case is recalled here |
| Any | The record write fails | X1 | Nothing; the partner row and the screen are unchanged |
| Any | The same partner and review date are submitted again | X7 | Nothing new; the stored entry is answered |

| Review step execution | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open | The manager selects the partner | The right and the scope are checked | Reading |
| Reading | The partner, the instructions and the reference data are read | The six points and their versions are in place | Evaluating |
| Reading | A consumed read does not answer inside 2 s | X4 | Closed, nothing written |
| Evaluating | The rule package in force is loaded and the values are confirmed | Every required value is present | Recording |
| Recording | The entry is written | The transaction commits | Recorded |
| Recording | The entry write fails | X1 | Open, nothing changed, MSG-P7-003 |
| Recorded | A repeat arrives for the same key | R-UNI-40 | Recorded; the stored answer is returned |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Partner and agency manager (RW-AGENCYMG) | The primary actor of FSD S9 A2.10.3.3: holds Partner portal CRUDA (TSD S9 T6.1), runs the review and records its actions |
| Litigation officer (RW-LITOFF), enforcement owner (RW-ENFORCE), sale officer (RW-SALEOFF), NPA and asset manager (RW-NPAMGR), debt sale officer (RW-DEBTSALE), guarantee officer (RW-GUARANT) | Partner portal CRU: hold the write right of the act on the partner their work touches, as the legacy permission table lists them under right U |
| Head of Litigation (RW-HEADLIT), Head of Asset Liquidity (RW-HEADASL) | The "also uses" roles of FSD S9 A2.10.3.3; TSD S9 T6.1 gives them RA, so they read and approve and take no U act |
| Partner portal users (PT-AGENCY, PT-LAWFIRM, PT-VALUER, PT-AUCTION, PT-BUYER, PT-RAMC) | Partner portal RU: see the review outcome of their own firm and its scope; they never run the bank's review |
| Case owner (RW-CASEOWN), team manager (RW-TEAMMGR), legal counsel (RW-LEGAL) and the remaining read roles | Partner portal R: read the review and its rule version |
| rwb-decision (P7) | Owns the package, the rule rows and the central ledger; this story evaluates the version and records locally |
| rwb-case (P3) | Owns the case, its stage and its timers, and answers the case label on the composite route; this story writes no case fact |
| rwb-access (P4) | Owns the roles, the capability rights and the lists of values this story reads through the guard |

No delegated authority limit applies: the review takes no credit decision and approves no money, and the only approvals in the module are the fee approval of FEAT-PRM-09 and the route approvals of the other modules.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 | `partner` | S9, `rwb_partner` | **Read** only: `id`, `partner_code`, `partner_name`, `partner_type`, `panel_status`, `contract_end` and `score`; no column carries the review, a point or an action (ASM-5439) |
| DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 | `partner_instruction` | S9, `rwb_partner` | **Read** only: `id`, `case_id`, `partner_id`, `instruction_type`, `instructed_at`, `due_at`, `status`, `result_code` and `fee_amount`, as the evidence of the work placed with the partner |
| None: library table | `decision_record` | Platform library in `rwb_partner` | **Write**: one hash-linked review entry per review, before anything else (DP-03) |
| None: library table | `idempotency_key` | Platform library in `rwb_partner` | The key of the repeat (partner and review date) and the answer it holds (R-UNI-40) |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | `decision_log_entry` | P7 rwb-decision | Not written: the local entry is copied to the central ledger by its owner, and its identifier is not stored here |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | `rule_row` | P7 rwb-decision | Not read as a table: the package arrives loaded at its version in force (ASM-5440) |
| `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE`, `LOV-PANEL`, `LOV-INSTRUCTION`, `LOV-INSTR-STATUS` | reference data and lists of values | P3 rwb-case (default ruling) | Read at their version; `LOV-PARTNER-TYPE` carries AGENCY, LAW_FIRM, VALUER, AUCTION_VENDOR, BROKER, DEBT_BUYER, AMC and RAMC, and `LOV-PANEL` carries ACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED and EXITED (TSD S9 T3.2) |
| The six points and the action list | reference data | P3 rwb-case (default ruling) | Read at their version; the six points are REQ-S9-001's and the action list is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3125; ASM-5438, ASM-5442) |

No new table, no new column and no migration: the three tables arrive with the DB story of this service, and `decision_record` and `idempotency_key` are library objects created in `rwb_partner` by the library's own migration (DP-03). `partner_user` is this service's third table and is not read by this act, because the reviewer is a Workbench user and not a partner portal identity (ASM-5439).

**No personal data.** The entry carries identifiers, point values, action values, a rule version and an instant. No name of a person, address, contact value or identity number enters `rwb_partner`, the entry, a log or a workflow input; the partner's registered name is a firm name and is marked not personal in FSD S9 A2.10.3.2 (BR8).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None declared by this story. Owner rwb-partner (S9); base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13). The Ownership Map gives this service exactly six operations — `GET /partners` (API-S9-001), `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions` (API-S9-002), `GET /partner/instructions` (API-S9-003), `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/accept` (API-S9-004), `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results` (API-S9-005) and `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/invoices` (API-S9-006) — and none of them records a review: their shapes are the frozen baseline of RWB-S9-AD022-CON, their first-in epics are Epic 2 to Epic 6, and they serve the panel, the instructions, an acceptance, a result and an invoice (TSD S9 T-A.1). The two endpoints of the legacy story are those results and instructions operations, which are the earlier stories' of this service. The review act therefore has no published entry point, and the review read behind SCR-34 and SCR-35 is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3125; ASM-5441). A build that declares a review operation here fails the absence test of RWB-S9-E7013-CON.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The rule-package and rule-row read; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3125; ASM-5440) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The package and the rule-row version in force at the review instant, and any row that names a partner review; read only, faked |
| The reference-data read; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3125; ASM-5443) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case, as the owner of parameters and reference data (R3 default ruling) | The six points of REQ-S9-001, the status list, the action list and the four lists of TSD S9 T3.2, each with its version; read only, faked |

Each row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, one retry with jitter on a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020, DP-11). Both are contract dependencies of class C that the plan does not carry, because this story's C row is None; the absence is recorded (GAP-3125; ASM-5440, ASM-5443).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service publishes on `rwb.partner.events.v1` and its event set is `InstructionIssued` (EV-20) and `PartnerResultSubmitted` (EV-21), both of which report an instruction or a result and therefore belong to the instruction stories of this service (context pack ownership rows; TSD S9 T5.3). A review issues no instruction and submits no result, so this story declares no producer group, no envelope and no outbox row, and RWB-S9-E7013-CON fails a build that adds one (ASM-5444).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The service listens to the case events of rwb-case on the module's published interfaces, and that subscription belongs to the case alignment of the partner stories (TSD S9 T4, T5.2). The review is started by a person on a screen and needs no event, so this story declares no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox of its own (ASM-5444).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `InstructionWorkflow` | Workflow, the service's only one | `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Owned by the instruction stories of this service; this story registers no workflow, no activity and no durable timer |
| `readReviewFacts` | Activity, synchronous step of the act | `rwb-partner` | Not a Temporal activity of its own: the read is a service call inside the request, with the same 2 s budget |
| `loadReviewReference` | Synchronous step | `rwb-partner` | The reference-data read and the six-point list with its version |
| `evaluateReviewRules` | Synchronous step | `rwb-partner` | The package in force in; the rule ID and version out |
| `recordReview` | Synchronous step, one transaction | `rwb-partner` | The entry, the reviewer and the answer out, one transaction |

The service has no case state machine of its own and no job (TSD S9 T4; context pack Jobs 0), so the review is a synchronous act whose only durable artefact is the decision record. No source puts the review inside `InstructionWorkflow`, and this story starts no workflow and no child workflow (ASM-5445).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The Ownership Map gives S9 no job (context pack ownership rows, Jobs: 0), and FSD S9 A2.10.4.4 declares no background event for the feature. DP-10 is not in this key's pattern set and no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row and no shared job table is declared (ASM-5445).

| `partner` | S9, `rwb_partner` | The partner, its type, its panel status, its contract end and its score; read only here |

| `partner_user` | S9, `rwb_partner` | The partner portal identities of the firm; not read by this act |

| `idempotency_key` | Platform library in `rwb_partner` | The key of the repeat and the answer it holds |

Not owned and never read as a table: `recovery_case`, `queue`, `assignment` and `timer` (P3), `rule_row` and `decision_log_entry` (P7), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `interaction` (P1) and every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The two consumed operation names are placeholders until their owners publish them (GAP-3125; ASM-5440, ASM-5443).
