**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the notice slice of RWB-E7-014 in rwb-partner. The legacy criterion AC2 is kept word for word with its origin tag; the step reads the partner and its latest score, compares it with the target in reference data, sets the panel status to `ON_NOTICE`, requests the contractual notice from rwb-comms (which owns the `notice` row), writes the local decision record with the rule ID and the version in force before any change (DP-03), and is submitted on the published `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions` (API-S9-002) on base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13), reached from SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). No source owns the notice in S9 (FSD S9 T5.2 gives notices to P6), no rule row decides a missed target, no source gives the cure period a length or the target a threshold, and EV-21 is published in TSD S9 T5.3 while the event catalogue reads it as consumed (GAP-3127; ASM-5450, ASM-5451, ASM-5452, ASM-5453, ASM-5454, ASM-5459). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **partner and agency manager**, I want **to send the contractual notice when a partner misses its targets, and to start the cure period**, so that **partners are placed, paid and measured by rule**.

This is the notice slice of legacy RWB-E7-014. It owns:

- the legacy criterion this story owns (AC2), copied verbatim with its origin tag, and the messages and the screens it depends on;
- one step of `InstructionWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, the notice step of the partner panel;
- the reading of the partner row (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007) and of its latest score (DF-PRT-007) against the target held as reference data, both with their version;
- the setting of the panel status to `ON_NOTICE` (LOV-PANEL) on the partner row, and the audit columns of the update;
- the request for the contractual notice through the rwb-comms contract, which owns the `notice` row and its dispatch (FSD S9 T5.2);
- the local decision record written through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON with the rule ID, the version in force, the score, the target, the notice reference and the from and to panel status, **before any change** (DP-03);
- the submission of the notice on the published `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions` (API-S9-002) on base `/api/recovery/partner/v1`, partner portal right C, scope applied (DP-13);
- the partner panel read on SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

It does not own: the published shapes, the elements, the lists, the rights of the document, the error envelope and the fakes, which are RWB-S9-E7014-CON; the scorecard that measures the partner (FEAT-PRM-08, RWB-S9-E7011-APP); the panel, the fee schedule and the service levels as versioned reference data (FEAT-PRM-02, RWB-S9-E6030); the allocation and its override (RWB-S9-E6031, RWB-S9-E6032); the partner result (RWB-S9-E6033); the fee approval (RWB-S9-E7012); the partner review (RWB-S9-E7013); ending the contract and recalling the work (FEAT-PRM-12, RWB-S9-E7015); the conduct check (RWB-S9-E7016); the notice document, its template and its dispatch, which are rwb-comms (P6); the case, its states and its clock, which are rwb-case (P3); and the cross-service journey of AC1, which is RWB-ITG-E7014-ITG.

##### 2. Business rationale

The objective, the problem and the metric are unchanged from the legacy story and the module FSD: the notice is sent when a partner misses its targets and the cure period starts, because partners are instructed and paid by email and spreadsheet and allocation is not based on performance (FSD S9 A1.3, A2.11.1), and placements by scorecard are measured on the decision log and the Workbench records against 100 percent set with DL22, reviewed monthly (FSD S9 A2.11.1). What D-RCV-60 changes is who owns the notice, the panel, the rule, the record and the screen.

- **The notice is not this service's row.** FSD S9 T5.2 gives notices to P6, the event catalogue gives `NoticeGenerated` and `NoticeDispatched` to Communications (EV-13, EV-14), and the ownership rows give S9 three tables, none of them a notice. The legacy Data table's `notice` (DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023) is therefore read as rwb-comms' element, requested through its contract, and never written here (ASM-5450).
- **The panel status is this service's.** `partner` is S9's in `rwb_partner` (context pack ownership rows; TSD S9 T3.1) and LOV-PANEL already carries `ON_NOTICE`, so the notice's own effect on this service is the panel status of the partner row and the audit columns (ASM-5455).
- **No rule row decides the notice.** The Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 has no partner route set: the nearest rows are R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-29, which recall work on a missed service level, a panel exit, a conflict, insolvency or a conduct breach, and none of them issues a notice or starts a cure period. The rule ID and the version in force the record must carry have no row to cite and carry the placeholder (ASM-5451).
- **The cure period has no length.** `cure_period_days` exists for a broken treatment plan (R-RES-27 to R-RES-29) and no partner parameter of that name exists; the FSD names the cure period as an effect of the notice and gives it no length, no list and no parameter (ASM-5452).
- **The measure has no threshold.** `partner.score` is the latest scorecard result (DF-PRT-007) and the targets and incentives are kept as versioned reference data (FEAT-PRM-02, REQ-S9-001), but no target value, no measure and no threshold for a missed target is published (ASM-5459).
- **The instruction surface carries the act.** The legacy endpoint table of RWB-E7-014 gives `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions` and `GET /partner/instructions`, TSD S9 T-A.1 publishes them as API-S9-002 and API-S9-003, and no notice path is published by any source, so the notice is submitted on the instruction operation and carries the placeholder for the request property the notice facts would use (ASM-5453).
- **Events are not this step's.** The service owns EV-20 and EV-21 only: an instruction issued and a partner result. A notice is a Communications fact, its dispatch is EV-14, and this step publishes nothing (ASM-5454).
- **No requirement row names the feature.** TSD S9 T8 maps every REQ-S9 row to FEAT-PRM-01 or FEAT-PRM-08, and REQ-S9-001 is the only row that names notice and exit at the level of the six points, so the story cites no requirement ID until the E7 BRD and the PRD publish one (ASM-5458).

No business value moves: the panel list, the partner type list, the target, the cure period, the rule ID and its version are reference data and rule values, read with their version and never written in code.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S9-E7014-CON is published: the instruction operations on `/api/recovery/partner/v1`, the partner and instruction elements, the lists, the rights, the error envelope, the consumed rows and the fakes are baselined and handed to this story.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: the local decision record is written in the caller's transaction, and a failed write stops the action with MSG-P7-003, so nothing changes (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-34 and SCR-35 reach this service through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop, and no screen calls a service directly (DP-19).
- `partner` and `partner_instruction` exist in schema `rwb_partner` from the DB story of this service, with the columns of DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-016 and the standard record columns of TSD S9 T3.0; this story adds no table, no column and no migration.
- The partner is on the panel at `ACTIVE` with a contract that has not ended, and its latest score (DF-PRT-007) is published by the scorecard of FEAT-PRM-08 (RWB-S9-E7011-APP).
- The target the score is measured against and the cure period are in force as reference data with their version. The parameter names, the values and the read are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3127; ASM-5452, ASM-5459).
- The rwb-comms notice contract is published with its fake and answers a notice reference for a partner notice. Its operation name and the notice's property for a partner are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3127; ASM-5450, ASM-5453).
- The service runs as its own login on schema `rwb_partner`; it holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `rwb_case`, `rwb_comms` or an ACE view is refused by the database and fails the boundary test.
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-S9-E7014-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. The scorecard of FEAT-PRM-08 publishes the partner's latest score on `partner.score` (DF-PRT-007) against the target in reference data; the manager reads the panel on SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop (DP-19).
2. The partner and agency manager selects a partner whose score is below its target, confirms the missed target and the notice, and the screen sends the partner reference, the case reference, the instruction type, the due date and the manager's identity.
3. `PartnerInstructionController` serves `POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions` (API-S9-002) on base `/api/recovery/partner/v1`, declares partner portal right C with the scope applied, requires the `Idempotency-Key` header and validates the request (DP-13).
4. The step reads the partner row in `rwb_partner`: its reference, its panel status, its contract end and its latest score. A partner at `SUSPENDED` or `EXITED`, a contract that has ended, or a partner already at `ON_NOTICE` is refused and nothing is written (X3).
5. The step reads the target and the cure period from reference data at their version in force and holds the pair for the record. The parameter names and the values carry the placeholder (ASM-5452, ASM-5459).
6. `PartnerNoticeDecisionRecordWriter` writes one decision record through the local decision-record library **before any change**: the partner reference, the case reference, the rule ID and the version in force, the score, the target, the notice type, the from panel status and `ON_NOTICE`, and the decided-at time. A failed write stops the step with nothing changed (DP-03; AC2).
7. `NoticeClient` requests the contractual notice from rwb-comms with its type, the partner and the case, one hop, a 2 s budget and a breaker; rwb-comms answers the notice reference and owns the row, its template and its dispatch (ASM-5450).
8. `RecordAndApply` commits in one transaction: `partner.panel_status = ON_NOTICE` (DF-PRT-005), the standard columns `updated_at` and `updated_by`, and the optimistic-lock version. The record written at step 6 is void if this commit does not happen, so no record exists without a change (DP-03).
9. The answer returns the instruction element with the notice reference, the from and to panel status and the decision-record reference; the manager sees the partner at `ON_NOTICE` on SCR-34, read back from this service.
10. The cure period starts at the notice's `sent_date`; its length is reference data and its expiry is tracked by the case stage's timer in P3, which owns `timer`. This service holds no timer and starts no Schedule (ASM-5452).
11. No event is published: the notice's own facts are rwb-comms' (`NoticeGenerated` EV-13, `NoticeDispatched` EV-14) and the instruction's `InstructionIssued` (EV-20) belongs to the instruction stories.
12. A repeat of the same submission with the same `Idempotency-Key` answers the instruction and the notice that exist and writes no second record; no phone number, address, identity number or other personal value is copied into the record, the answer or a log.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The local decision record cannot be written | Nothing changes: the panel status stays where it was, no notice is requested and no record exists | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, TC-E7-014-02, TC-E7-014-04 |
| X2 | The role does not hold partner portal right C | 403 before any read or write; nothing changes and no record is written | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E7-014-03 |
| X3 | The partner is at `SUSPENDED` or `EXITED`, its contract has ended, or it is already at `ON_NOTICE` | 409 with nothing written; a notice is never issued twice and never to a partner off the panel | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3127; ASM-5455) | AC2 |
| X4 | The target or the cure period is absent from reference data at its version | 422 or 503 with nothing written; the step never falls back to a value of the code | MSG-GEN-001 | Section 17, BR7 |
| X5 | The rwb-comms notice request does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The transaction rolls back, the activity retries on the workflow's schedule under the same `Idempotency-Key`, and nothing is committed | None | BR4 |
| X6 | The same submission arrives twice | One instruction, one notice and one record; the repeat answers what exists | None | BR10 |
| X7 | A component, a statement or a test reaches a `v_ace_*` view, a `recovery_case` or `timer` row, a `notice` row or another service's schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | Section 17, BR5, BR6 |

X1 and X2 are the legacy exception paths, carried onto the slice with the legacy messages; X3 to X6 are the paths the trigger, the reference data and the two contracts add; X7 is the ACE, notice and schema boundary.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-S9-E7014-CON, the rwb-comms notice fake, the reference-data fake and the decision-record stub, on its own schema, and needs no live P3 or P6 |
| Negotiable | The activity and component names, the internal record shape and the front-end placement are this story's and the baseline's choice; the operation, the right, the panel list, the messages and the criterion are fixed |
| Valuable | A partner that misses its target receives one dated contractual notice and starts a cure period, and the panel change is provable from the decision record instead of an e-mail |
| Estimable | One workflow step, one comparator against reference data, one record write, one notice request, one operation branch, one client and one read-only screen state |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | AC2 runs on the decision-record stub; the step runs on a synthetic partner at `ACTIVE` through the fakes, plus the refused, not-in-force, no-answer and repeat cases |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Issue a notice on a missed target

  Background:
    Given the partner "PRT-0007" of type "AGENCY" is on the panel at state "ACTIVE" with its contract in force and its latest score published
    Given the target and the cure period are in force as reference data with their version
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC2 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E7-014 AC2)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

AC2 is the legacy criterion of RWB-E7-014 word for word, with its origin tag added and nothing else changed: the wording of `the decision log cannot be written`, `the action is taken` and the single `Then` all stand. AC2 has no cross-service part that could be mocked, so no `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>` line is added to it and the notice, the reference data and the record are reached at the level the criterion names.

The other legacy criterion of RWB-E7-014 is AC1, and it is not owned by this story: the split plan gives AC1 to RWB-ITG-E7014-ITG, which runs the journey across the partner panel, the notice and the case, and it is not restated here. The step this story builds is the one AC1 describes, so the business outcome is proved by TC-E7-014-01 at component level until the integration story runs it end to end. The `decision log` of the legacy text is the local decision record of DP-03 in `rwb_partner`, with the central `decision_log_entry` ledger of rwb-decision behind it.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The notice step is a step of `InstructionWorkflow` on `rwb-partner`: it reads `partner` and `partner_instruction`, writes `partner.panel_status` and the audit columns, and writes nothing else in `rwb_partner` | TSD S9 T3.0, T3.1, T4; context pack ownership rows (3 tables, 1 workflow, no job); FSD S9 A2.11.2 |
| BR2 | The result is recorded before the change, with the rule ID, the version in force, the score, the target, the notice reference and the from and to panel status; a failed write changes nothing and the caller sees MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; TSD S9 T2 ("writes the decision log entry before any change"); legacy AC2 |
| BR3 | A notice is issued only to a partner at `ACTIVE` with a contract in force and a score below its target; a partner at `ON_NOTICE`, `SUSPENDED` or `EXITED`, or a contract that has ended, is refused | TSD S9 T3.2 (LOV-PANEL); ASM-5455; legacy AC1 |
| BR4 | The notice is a rwb-comms element, requested on one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker; this service holds no notice row, no notice template and no dispatch status | FSD S9 T5.2; Event and Messaging Design v4 events EV-13 and EV-14; ASM-5450 |
| BR5 | No cross-schema join and no foreign key leaves `rwb_partner`; `case_id` and `partner_id` are identifiers of other services' facts | DP-01; TSD S9 T3.3 |
| BR6 | The service reads no `v_ace_*` view and holds no grant on one; ACE data reaches the panel only through rwb-source-data or the owner's contract | DP-01, DP-05; Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR7 | Every value a business person may change is reference data or a rule value read with its version: the panel list, the partner type list, the target, the cure period and the rule in force. The target, the cure period and the rule ID have no published row and carry the placeholder | FSD S9 BR-S9-011; ASM-5451, ASM-5452, ASM-5459 |
| BR8 | No personal data in `rwb_partner`, the decision record, a log or a workflow input: partner identifiers, codes, list values, dates, an amount, a rule ID and a version only | Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17); TSD S9 T6.2 |
| BR9 | The cure period starts at the notice's `sent_date`; its length is reference data, its expiry is the case stage's timer in P3 and this service starts no Schedule and holds no timer row | ASM-5452; TSD S9 T4; context pack ownership rows (jobs: None) |
| BR10 | The same submission twice writes one record, one instruction and one notice: the operation declares the `Idempotency-Key` header and stores the key and its answer | TSD S9 T-A.2 |
| BR11 | This step publishes and consumes no event; the partner result (EV-21) and the instruction (EV-20) belong to other steps of the service | Event and Messaging Design v4 events EV-20 and EV-21; TSD S9 T5.3; ASM-5454 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From (panel status, rwb-partner) | Event | Condition | To | Written by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ACTIVE` | The contractual notice is issued and the record is written | The score is below the target and the contract is in force | `ON_NOTICE` | rwb-partner, by this story (ASM-5455) |
| `ON_NOTICE` | A further notice request | The partner is already on notice | `ON_NOTICE`, unchanged | none; 409 (X3) |
| `ON_NOTICE` | The cure period is met | The targets are met again inside the cure period | `ACTIVE` | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3127; ASM-5455) |
| `ON_NOTICE` | The cure period lapses | The targets are not met inside the cure period | `SUSPENDED` | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3127; ASM-5455) |
| `ON_NOTICE` | The contract ends, or a conduct breach is upheld | FEAT-PRM-12 or FEAT-PRM-13 applies | `SUSPENDED` or `EXITED` | RWB-S9-E7015-APP and RWB-S9-E7016-APP, not this story |
| `SUSPENDED`, `EXITED` | A notice request | The partner is off the panel | Unchanged | none; 409 (X3) |

| Step execution | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting | A notice submission | The partner, the target and the cure period are read | Evaluating |
| Evaluating | The score is below the target | The partner is at `ACTIVE` with a contract in force | Recording |
| Evaluating | The partner is off the panel or already on notice | X3 | Waiting, nothing changed |
| Recording | The record and the panel status commit | The notice reference is held and the transaction commits | Waiting for the next submission |
| Recording | The record, the notice call or the commit fails | X1, X5 | Waiting, nothing changed |

LOV-PANEL is `ACTIVE`, `ON_NOTICE`, `SUSPENDED` and `EXITED` (TSD S9 T3.2). This story writes `ON_NOTICE` only; the two exits from `ON_NOTICE` — back to `ACTIVE` when the cure is met and to `SUSPENDED` when it lapses — have no trigger, no rule row and no story in any source, so they carry the placeholder and are not built here.

| RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-LEGAL, RW-CONDUCT, RW-CAPACITY, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-HEADLIT, RW-HEADNPA, RW-HEADASL, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE | Partner portal R in TSD S9 T6.1: read only and refused the notice; they are part of the legacy "and 21 more" (ASM-5456) |

DP-08 is not in this story's pattern set: the capability area and the right are declared per operation and the access guard is a service-template capability, so the check is stated and not built.

Field IDs are those of TSD S9 T3.1 and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. **No new table, no new column and no migration**: the two tables arrive with the DB story of this service, and `decision_record` and `idempotency_key` are library objects created in `rwb_partner` by the library's own migration (DP-03). `outbox_event` also sits in the schema as a library object, and this step writes no row to it because it publishes no event (§12.3).

**No personal data.** The rows carry partner identifiers, codes, dates, list values, an amount, a rule ID and a version. A partner firm is a legal person: no contact name, e-mail, phone number or identity number is read into the record, the answer, a log or a workflow input, and the fixtures are synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-partner (S9); base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the notice branch of the instruction operation, whose shape RWB-S9-E7014-CON declares.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/instructions` (API-S9-002) | `InstructionRequest` in; `PartnerInstruction` out with the notice reference, the from and to panel status and the decision-record reference | Partner portal, right C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |
| GET | `/partner/instructions` (API-S9-003) | `InstructionPage` out: the instructions placed with the caller's firm with status, page and size | Partner portal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/partners` (API-S9-001) | `Partner[]` out: the panel with panel status and score, query type and status | Partner portal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The errors of API-S9-002 are 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 for a case that is not in scope, 409 for a partner off the panel or already on notice, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for a missing or unformed request, and 503. TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2 publish the three operations, their requests, answers and error sets, so the surface needs no placeholder; what has no published property is the notice itself, its type value and the target, and they carry the placeholder (GAP-3127; ASM-5450, ASM-5453). API-S9-004 accept, API-S9-005 results and API-S9-006 invoices are the result and invoice stories' (RWB-S9-E6033, RWB-S9-E6035) and are not built here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The notice request (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3127; ASM-5450)) | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | P6 rwb-comms | The contractual notice of the partner with its type, its template and its document; answers the notice reference; faked |
| The reference-data read at its version (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3127; ASM-5459)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The target, the cure period and the panel list at their version in force, per the R3 default ruling that gives parameters and reference data to rwb-case; faked |

Both rows are one hop with a 2 s timeout, a breaker per downstream and a retry governed by the workflow's own schedule (ADR-020). They are contract dependencies of class C that this story's C row does not carry, and DP-07, the reference-data pattern, is not in the pattern set of the key; the absence is recorded (GAP-3127; ASM-5450, ASM-5459).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service owns the topic `rwb.partner.events.v1` and its event set carries EV-20 `InstructionIssued` (`instructionId`, `partnerId`, `type`, `dueOn`, consumed by the partner portal) and EV-21 `PartnerResultSubmitted` (`instructionId`, `result`, `documents`), and both belong to the instruction and result steps of the service (Event and Messaging Design v4; TSD S9 T5.3). A notice is a Communications fact: rwb-comms publishes `NoticeGenerated` (EV-13) and `NoticeDispatched` (EV-14), and this step only requests the notice and records the panel change. It therefore declares no event, no producer group and no outbox row, and a build that publishes EV-20 or an event of its own here fails the absence test. The topic carries the retry and `.dlt` topics of the platform (DP-14), and the outbox and inbox library that relays an event is the DP-09 dependency the plan does not carry (GAP-3127; ASM-5454).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The service's only consumed event is EV-21 `PartnerResultSubmitted`, which arrives from the partner portal when a firm reports a result and belongs to the result step (RWB-S9-E6033); the trigger of this step is the manager's confirmation on SCR-34 and SCR-35, and the FSD declares no background event for the feature (FSD S9 A2.11.4.4). The direction of EV-21 is itself in conflict between the event catalogue, which reads it as consumed, and TSD S9 T5.3, which lists it as published; the conflict is recorded and does not touch this step (ASM-5454). This story holds no consumer group, no subscription of its own and no inbox row.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `InstructionWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per partner instruction; the notice step rides it | `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the case reference, the partner reference and the instruction; the notice request is the step's input |
| `issuePartnerNotice` | Activity, the one notice step | `rwb-partner` | The partner reference, the case reference, the score, the target, the cure period and the notice type in; the notice reference, the panel status and the record reference out, with the record written before the row |
| the stage outcome for the parent | Parent-child workflow edge to `CaseWorkflow` | `rwb-case` | The panel status and the notice reference as the stage result; the case stage, its clock and its timer are P3's and no REST row is declared for them |

The service owns one workflow and no job in the context pack's ownership rows, and TSD S9 T4 gives it no case state machine of its own. The activity name is a target design choice fixed by no source document, and the parent edge is declared, not built.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The notice is an officer-driven step and owns no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row and no shared job table. The service owns no job in the context pack's ownership rows (Jobs: None), and the cure expiry of BR9 is the case stage's timer in P3, not a Schedule of this service.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| partner | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The panel firm, its type, its panel status, its contract end and its latest score; this story writes `panel_status` and the audit columns |
| partner_instruction | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The work placed with a partner on a case; read here, written by the instruction stories |
| partner_user | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The partner's own users, owned by the service; this story neither reads nor writes it |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_partner` | The local hash-linked decision record of the notice (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_partner` | The key of the instruction operation and the answer it holds |
| outbox_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_partner` | Present as a library object; this step writes no row to it (§12.3) |

Not owned and never read as a table: `notice` (P6), `recovery_case` and `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), every `v_ace_*` view (P1), `document` (P5) and `payment` (P8). No foreign key leaves the schema, and `case_id` and `partner_id` are identifiers, not foreign keys across schemas (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-comms notice fake | A notice reference for a partner notice of the type requested, with its template and its sent date | AC2, X5, TC-E7-014-01 |
| rwb-case reference-data fake | The target, the cure period and the panel list at their version in force | AC2, X4, TC-E7-014-01 |
| Local decision-record library stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and a stopped chain | AC2, X1, TC-E7-014-02, TC-E7-014-04 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-34 and SCR-35 answer for the panel of the manager, before and after the notice | TC-E7-014-01, TC-E7-014-03 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The notice operation and the reference-data read carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-3127; ASM-5450, ASM-5459).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 3 provided, 2 consumed | API-S9-001, API-S9-002 and API-S9-003 on `/api/recovery/partner/v1`; the notice request of rwb-comms and the reference-data read of rwb-case, one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | EV-20 and EV-21 belong to other steps of the service; the notice's facts are rwb-comms' (EV-13, EV-14) |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 1 activity | `InstructionWorkflow` and `issuePartnerNotice` on `rwb-partner`; the stage outcome returns to `CaseWorkflow` on `rwb-case`; no Schedule |
| File | None | No file is read, built or delivered here |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner`, module `notice`; front end `src/modules/recovery/partner/PartnerPanel.tsx`, the fragment SCR-34 and SCR-35 embed.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the transaction rule of the step: the record and the panel status commit together or not at all, and the legacy "writes the result to the decision log with the rule version" is that record. DP-13 moves the base of the legacy `/api/recovery/v1` paths and gives the instruction operation its home. DP-19 is how SCR-34 and SCR-35 reach this service, one hop through the gateway. These three are the whole pattern set of the key and the story adds no fourth: DP-07 (the reference-data contract of rwb-case) and DP-06 (the parameters contract) are the real dependencies of the target and the cure period, DP-08 (the access guard of the template) and DP-09 (the outbox and inbox library) are real dependencies of the service, and they are recorded in the registers instead of the metadata table (GAP-3127; ASM-5459).

**Dependencies the tables add and the plan does not hold.** The plan gives this story H RWB-S9-E7014-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and C, I and X empty. The two consumed rows of §12.2 are class C dependencies in fact: the notice request of rwb-comms and the reference-data read of rwb-case, both built against their documents and fakes on Day 1. DP-07 would add RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON; the reference-data read is declared with the placeholder instead, so no row is added.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `InstructionWorkflow` notice branch | Workflow | Receives the notice submission, reads the target and the cure period in force and reports the panel status and the notice reference to the parent |
| `issuePartnerNotice` | Activity | Reads the partner and the score, compares the score with the target, requests the notice, writes the record and the panel status and answers |
| `PartnerTargetComparator` | Service | Compares the score with the target in force and refuses a partner off the panel or already on notice; the threshold is reference data and never a constant |
| `PartnerNoticeDecisionRecordWriter` | Library adapter | Writes the record with the rule ID, the version, the score, the target, the notice reference and the two panel statuses before anything else; refuses the step when the write fails |
| `NoticeClient` | Client | The rwb-comms notice request, one hop, 2 s, breaker; holds the returned notice reference |
| `ReferenceData.java` | Client | The target, the cure period and the panel list at their version in force, one hop, 2 s |
| `PartnerInstructionController` | Controller | The notice branch of the instruction operation, the capability area and right C, the scope, the `Idempotency-Key` and the problem mapping |
| `PartnerPanel` | React component | Shows the partner, its panel status and its score on SCR-34 and SCR-35 |

**Database and migrations.** No Flyway file. `partner` and `partner_instruction` arrive with the DB story of this service, and the record and the key are library objects created in `rwb_partner` by the library's migration (DP-03). No column is added for the target, the cure period or the notice: none has a source (ASM-5452, ASM-5459).

**Configuration and reference data.**

- The panel list, the partner type list, the target and the cure period: reference data with their version, read through the owner's contract, never written in code (ASM-5452, ASM-5459).
- The rule ID and the version in force: recorded from the value in force; no partner route set exists in the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, so the value carries the placeholder (ASM-5451).
- The capability area "Partner portal" and its rights: access rows of rwb-access, read through the guard of the template.
- The 2 s budget, the single hop and the breaker are the platform rule of ADR-020; the service holds no timer.

**Build steps**

1. The notice branch of `InstructionWorkflow` and its input record, registered on `rwb-partner`, with the manager's confirmation as its trigger.
2. `ReferenceData.java` against its fake, with the target, the cure period, the version and the not-in-force path (X4).
3. `PartnerTargetComparator`, with the below-target path and the off-panel and already-on-notice paths (X3).
4. `PartnerNoticeDecisionRecordWriter` against the stub, with the failed-write path (AC2, X1).
5. `NoticeClient` against the rwb-comms fake, with the 2 s budget, the breaker and the no-answer path (X5).
6. `PartnerInstructionController` with the notice branch, right C, the scope, the `Idempotency-Key` and the problem mapping of the declared errors, and `PartnerPanel` through the composite route fake (X2, X6).
7. The transaction step: the record, `panel_status` and the audit columns in one commit, with the optimistic-lock version (X1, X5).
8. The boundary test: no statement outside `rwb_partner`, no `v_ace_*` read, no write to `rwb_case`, `rwb_comms`, `rwb_decision` or any other schema, and no write to a `notice` or `timer` row (X7, BR4, BR5, BR9).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.partner.notice-v1`, a flag of the platform library; off means the operation answers 503 with no write and SCR-34 hides the notice action, and the panel, allocation and result stories are unaffected.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the step runs from a synthetic partner at `ACTIVE` in SIT, the notice reference and the panel status are recorded with the target, the cure period and the version in force, a partner off the panel and an already-noticed partner are refused, a repeated submission writes once, a forced record failure changes nothing, no `recovery_case`, `notice` or `timer` row and no `v_ace_*` read exists in the build, and SCR-34 answers through the composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required element is absent or invalid, or the target and the cure period are not in force (X4) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without partner portal right C calls the notice (X2) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the notice is requested (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| the refusal of X3 | The partner is at `SUSPENDED` or `EXITED`, its contract has ended, or it is already at `ON_NOTICE` | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3127; ASM-5455) |

The three IDs are those of the legacy message set; the text is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged, and no message is reworded and no new one is added. The refusal of X3 has no message in any source, so it carries the placeholder and no invented text.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation are served through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The route calls rwb-partner for the partner, its panel status, its contract end and its score, and rwb-case for the case and its stage; this story fixes the rwb-partner answers only, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

The legacy screen table gives both screens "Loading; list", so this story produces the notice from the list state: the manager sees the partner with its panel status and its score against its target, and confirms the notice. The partner-side screens PRT-01 to PRT-04 (FSD S9) show the partner its own instructions and hold no notice action, and the rights of §10 confirm it: a partner user holds R and U and never C. No source describes a notice form or a cure-period panel, so the place of the notice action on SCR-34 and the return of the panel status after the cure period are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3127; ASM-5455). The refusal, not-in-force, no-answer and not-recorded states read the messages of section 14.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the panel and partner type lists, the target, the cure period, the rule ID and its version stay reference data and rule values with a version, never a constant, a default or a branch.
- No personal data in `rwb_partner`, in a workflow input or in a log: partner identifiers, codes, dates, list values, an amount, a rule ID and a version only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and reads no ACE table.
- The case stays with rwb-case: no `recovery_case` row, no case state column and no case write here; the stage outcome returns to the parent workflow.
- The notice stays with rwb-comms: no `notice` row, no template and no dispatch status is written here (BR4).
- The cure period stays with P3: no `timer` row and no Schedule is created by this step (BR9).
- One base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service; no document names another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no shared job table, no Quartz row, no monolith base and no event published by this step.
- The record is written before the row; a build that answers outside the record's transaction fails the review (DP-03).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E7-014 as the wave 4 integration proof of the notice on a missed target and the start of the cure period, driven through the S9 partner and instruction reads, the P6 notice write and read-back, the P6 notice events and the P7 decision record; the build of the notice itself is RWB-S9-E7014-APP and P6 rwb-comms in its own stories. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **partner and agency manager**, I want **the contractual notice to go out when a partner misses its target and the cure period to start, proved end to end through the real partner, notice and decision contracts**, so that **partners are placed, paid and measured by rule, and a notice that cannot be recorded changes nothing**.

This story builds the wave 4 integration harness and its evidence, and nothing else. The feature itself, the screen and the data are built by S9 in RWB-S9-E7014-APP, and the notice, its template and its dispatch are built by P6 rwb-comms in its own stories. The harness loads the fixture, compares the score with the contractual target of the rule version the fixture names, drives the notice write and the notice read-back through P6's published operations, observes the notice events on P6's topic and the decision record on the shared topic, reads the case and the session back through their owners, and writes one run report per case and partner. It builds no production endpoint, no table, no workflow, no activity, no schedule and no screen, and it writes no code in any service.

##### 2. Business rationale

A partner can be measured every month and still never be told, in writing, that it missed. That is the gap this story is written against. The notice on a missed target is the point of the six points every partner type is managed on at which measurement turns into a contractual consequence: the partner is served the notice its contract provides for, and the cure period it has to put the miss right starts to run (REQ-S9-001, FEAT-PRM-11). Without it, a miss is a number on a scorecard and nothing follows, the cure period has no start, and the same partner is allocated the same work next month.

The notice also sits inside the recall and conduct context. A partner that misses its service level on the portal is chased once and then has the work recalled (R-UNI-25, REQ-S9-005); an upheld conduct or complaint breach suspends allocation, recalls the affected cases and is reported to the partner review (R-UNI-29); a service level exceeded in the current state is raised to the named escalation point while the case does not move (R-UNI-30); and partner performance, conduct and complaint data are reported to the partner review forum (REQ-S9-007). A notice is the evidence those processes are run on, which is why this harness asserts the notice, its type, its sent date and the cure period start as named facts rather than as a narrative.

The score is the monthly scorecard (FEAT-PRM-08) and the legacy story depends on it; the harness reads the score through S9's partner read and leaves the scorecard's calculation out of scope. The contractual target and the length of the cure period are versioned reference data under FEAT-PRM-02, and a new rule version applies to decisions taken from its effective date while open cases keep the version they were decided under (R-UNI-38), which is why the fixture names the rule version and the harness never writes one in code. Every call is one hop on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13). The decision record is written by the owning service through the local decision-record library on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) and confirmed by the central ledger in rwb-decision; where a screen would compose these calls the path is the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The harness carries REQ-S9-001, REQ-S9-005 and REQ-S9-007 into evidence rather than restating them.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The published contracts of S9 rwb-partner (the partner read and the instruction read), P6 rwb-comms (the notice write and the notice read), P7 rwb-decision (the decision log), P3 rwb-case (the case) and P4 rwb-access (the session) are in the contract registry, and a stub set is generated from each one.
- The partner portal rights are in force for the run: Partner portal C to issue a notice and Partner portal R to read the partner and the instructions. The right lists in the legacy section name RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-GUARANT and RW-AGENCYMG among the holders of C; the harness itself holds no business right.
- A synthetic partner on the panel with a score below the contractual target of the named rule version, one instruction on one case, and one approved notice template for the notice type are held in the fixture as data, and the fixture names the rule version, the target, the score, the notice type and the cure period length rather than a value written in code.
- The cure period length is read from versioned reference data under FEAT-PRM-02, dated and read back; the harness asserts the start it records against that length and never counts the period itself.
- RWB-S9-E7014-APP owns the notice action, its screen and its data; until it lands, the stub set of §12.8 stands in for its effect and the story is reported as a stub pass.
- The monthly scorecard (FEAT-PRM-08) is not asserted here: the partner read carries the score of DF-PRT-007 and its calculation is RWB-S9-E7014-*'s sibling scope.
- The harness environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic partner, instruction, case and notice keys, the stub answer shapes, the conduct of the missed-target comparison against the named rule version, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0475; ASM-0667).
- No build dependency. Day 1, with the stubs in place from the first run; the one wait is RWB-S9-E7014-APP, which replaces its stub as it lands and never blocks the lane.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: loads the fixture: the synthetic partner with partner_code, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end and score, one instruction on one case, the notice type, the approved template for it, the rule version, the contractual target of that version, the cure period length, and the case and partner keys. On Day 1 the stub set of §12.8 returns the same records (GAP-0475; ASM-0667).
2. Harness: reads the partner through `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` and asserts partner_code, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end and score (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007).
3. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions` and asserts the instruction on the case with its case_id, partner_id, instruction_type, instructed_at, due_at and status (DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016).
4. Harness: compares the score with the contractual target of the rule version the fixture names and records the miss as a fact of the run, with the rule version beside it; the comparison never uses a target taken from the code (R-UNI-38).
5. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and holds the case state before the notice, so that "nothing changes" can be asserted later rather than assumed.
6. Harness: issues the notice through `POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices` with the notice type and the template the fixture names, and asserts 201 with the notice carrying notice_type and sent_date (DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023).
7. Harness: reads the notice back through `GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` and asserts the same notice, field for field, and asserts that the cure period start is recorded and read back with its length taken from the versioned reference data.
8. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` and asserts one record for the notice with its decision_code, rule_id and rule_version, and that the rule version is the one the fixture named.
9. Harness: counts one `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and asserts the central ledger in rwb-decision confirmed the record.
10. Harness: counts one `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` and one `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` on `rwb.comms.events.v1`, asserts each was consumed once by the consumer the event catalogue names, replays each event once, and asserts nothing changed.
11. Harness: forces the local decision-record library to fail for the notice and asserts the notice stops with MSG-P7-003, no notice and no decision entry are written, and the partner and the instruction are unchanged when they are read again.
12. Harness: calls `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` as a synthetic caller holding Partner portal R and not C, then attempts the notice write and asserts 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no state change.
13. Harness: writes one run report per case and partner, keyed by story, caseId and partner_code, naming the contract version of each hop, whether the hop was a stub or the owner, the score and the target with the rule version, the notice with its type and sent date, the cure period start and its length and version, the decision record, the two notice events with their consumer effects, and the pass or fail gate.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A stub answers a shape the published contract does not allow | The run fails at that hop and the report names the service, the operation and the contract version; no further step is marked evidenced | None | TC-E7-014-01-ITG (ITG AC2) |
| X2 | The partner read returns a score and no target of the named rule version to compare it with | The run fails on AC2 and the report names the partner, the rule version and the missing target; a miss is never declared from a target held in the code | None | TC-E7-014-01-ITG (ITG AC2) |
| X3 | The notice write answers 201 and the notice read-back returns a different notice | The run fails on AC2 and the report names the two answers field by field and the contract version of each hop | None | TC-E7-014-01-ITG (ITG AC2) |
| X4 | The cure period start is recorded with a length that is not the versioned reference value | The run fails on AC2 and the report names the length recorded, the length in force and its version; the length is never a value in the harness | None | TC-E7-014-01-ITG (ITG AC2) |
| X5 | A notice event is published twice, or consumed twice, or a replay changes state | The run fails on AC3 and the report names the event, the publication count and the consumer effect before and after the replay | None | TC-E7-014-01-ITG (ITG AC3) |
| X6 | The decision record fails and the notice still goes out, or a decision entry is written without the ledger confirmation | The run fails on AC4 and the report names the notice state, the notice read-back and the decision log before and after; nothing changes is asserted, not assumed | MSG-P7-003 (expected) | TC-E7-014-02-ITG and TC-E7-014-04-ITG (ITG AC4) |
| X7 | A caller holding Partner portal R and not C is allowed to issue a notice | The run fails on AC5 and the report names the caller's rights, the operation and the answer; a 201 is a failure even when no business data changed | MSG-P4-002 (expected, and missing) | TC-E7-014-03-ITG (ITG AC5) |

The report text is for the wave entry check and is not part of the message standard. The business messages the run touches are in section 14 and are asserted by ID and by their substituted values.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs against the published contracts and the stubs from Day 1; the only wait is RWB-S9-E7014-APP, and its fixture answers until it lands |
| Negotiable | The fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the stub answer shapes, the evidence shape, the report shape and the gate are configuration agreed at the wave entry check, not business values in code |
| Valuable | The notice is proved to be issued on a miss with the rule version in the record, the cure period is proved to start from versioned reference data, and a notice that cannot be recorded is proved to change nothing |
| Estimable | One runner, one stub set, one partner probe, one target probe, one notice driver, one decision read-back, one event observer and one report |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its five criteria and four tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against the stubs and again against RWB-S9-E7014-APP as it lands |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Issue a notice on a missed target - wave 4 integration harness

  Scenario: AC1 Issue a notice on a missed target (legacy RWB-E7-014 AC1)
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When the user acts on the screen
    Then sends the contractual notice when a partner misses its targets, and starts the cure period
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 The notice is issued on a missed target and the cure period starts (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the partner read returns the partner with partner_code, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end and score
    And the score and the contractual target of the named rule version show the miss
    When the notice is issued through POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices
    Then the answer is 201 and the notice carries notice_type and sent_date
    And GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId} returns the same notice
    And the cure period start is recorded and read back
    And the length of the cure period is taken from versioned reference data and never from code

  Scenario: AC3 One decision record and each event once (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the notice has been issued for the case
    When the decision record and the events are read back
    Then one decision record carries decision_code, rule_id and rule_version
    And "rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1" is published once and confirmed by the central ledger
    And "rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1" is published once and consumed once
    And "rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1" is published once and consumed once
    And a replay of each event changes nothing

  Scenario: AC4 A forced local decision-record failure stops the notice (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the local decision-record library is forced to fail for the notice
    When the notice is issued through POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices
    Then the notice write stops with "MSG-P7-003"
    And no notice and no decision entry are written
    And the partner and the instruction are unchanged when they are read again

  Scenario: AC5 A caller holding Partner portal R and not C is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a caller whose right set holds Partner portal R and not Partner portal C
    When the caller issues a notice through POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices
    Then the answer is 403 with "MSG-P4-002"
    And nothing changes
```

Legacy AC2 (the decision log cannot be written) is built and tested in RWB-S9-E7014-APP, and this story asserts the same failure at the notice write through AC4.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every partner type is managed on the same six points: selection, contract and fees, targets and incentives, data exchange, performance reviews, notice and exit; the notice on a missed target is the notice and exit point of that set | REQ-S9-001 |
| BR2 | A partner that misses its service level is chased once and then has the work recalled | REQ-S9-005 |
| BR3 | When the partner misses the service level on the portal, the work is chased once, then recalled and re-selected on the scorecard, to PARTNER_RECALLED | R-UNI-25 |
| BR4 | When a conduct or complaint breach is upheld, allocation is suspended, the affected cases are recalled and the breach is reported to the partner review, to PARTNER_RECALLED | R-UNI-29 |
| BR5 | When the time in the current state exceeds the service level, the breach is raised to the named escalation point and the case does not move, to ESCALATED | R-UNI-30 |
| BR6 | When a new rule version reaches its effective date, it applies to decisions taken from that date, and open cases keep the version they were decided under, so the notice carries the rule version in force on its sent date | R-UNI-38 |
| BR7 | When the decision log entry cannot be written, the action is blocked and no action proceeds unlogged, which is MSG-P7-003 on the notice write | R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | Partner performance, conduct and complaint data are reported to the partner review forum, and the notice is one of the facts reported | REQ-S9-007 |
| BR9 | Every call is one hop on the owner's base with a 2 s budget, and the decision record is written through the local decision-record library on the shared topic and confirmed by the central ledger | DP-11, DP-13, DP-03; ADR-020, ADR-022 |

The harness asserts these rules and changes none of them; the rules themselves are evaluated in RWB-S9-E7014-APP and P6 rwb-comms, and the contractual target and the length of the cure period are the versioned reference data of FEAT-PRM-02 that the run reads and never writes.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| No notice | `NoticeGenerated` on `rwb.comms.events.v1` | the notice is issued on a missed target and the cure period starts | Notice record raised, cure period running |
| Notice raised | `NoticeDispatched` on `rwb.comms.events.v1` | the notice leaves by its channel | Notice dispatched |
| Notice dispatched | `NoticeDelivered` on `rwb.comms.events.v1` | the channel confirms delivery | Notice delivered |
| SENT | PARTNER_NO_RESPONSE | the service level is missed and the chase has run once (R-UNI-25) | RECALLED |
| ANY_ACTIVE | PARTNER_CONDUCT_BREACH | a conduct or complaint breach is upheld (R-UNI-29) | RECALLED |
| ANY_ACTIVE | SLA_BREACHED | time in the current state exceeds the service level (R-UNI-30) | ESCALATED |

`NoticeGenerated`, `NoticeDispatched` and `NoticeDelivered` are the events of Arch v5 slide 42 rows 13 to 15; SENT and RECALLED are instruction status values of DF-PRT-014, and PARTNER_NO_RESPONSE, PARTNER_CONDUCT_BREACH and SLA_BREACHED are the event codes of R-UNI-25, R-UNI-29 and R-UNI-30, whose to_state is PARTNER_RECALLED and ESCALATED. No source names a notice status list for the record P6 holds, so the run asserts the notice through its facts — notice_type, sent_date, the template, the dispatch and the delivery events — and asserts no status value for it that the source does not name (GAP-0475; ASM-0667). The cure period is a date fact, not a state the harness sets: the start is recorded by the owning service and the end is counted from the versioned reference length. The harness changes no state at all: P6 rwb-comms owns the notice and NoticeDispatchWorkflow, S9 rwb-partner owns the instruction and the partner, and P3 rwb-case holds the case state the run reads. A state the harness had set by hand would prove nothing, so the report names the owner and the operation behind every value it asserts.

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| RW-NPAMGR, partner and agency manager | Holds Partner portal C and R; is the role the notice is written for and the role that issues it |
| RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-SALEOFF, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-GUARANT, RW-AGENCYMG | Hold Partner portal C per the legacy section; issue the same notice where their scope allows |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-LEGAL, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE and the 21 further roles of the legacy R list | Read the partner and the instructions where their rights allow; the R list of the legacy section names them |
| QA lead | Owns the harness configuration, the fixtures, the report shape and the pass or fail gate |
| Integration lead | Owns the harness code, the stub set and the swap from a stub to the real service |
| The owning services' identities | P6 issues the notice, answers the notice read, publishes NoticeGenerated and NoticeDispatched and runs NoticeDispatchWorkflow; S9 answers the partner and instruction reads and writes the decision record; P7 holds the central ledger; P3 holds the case; P4 answers the session; they make every change the harness asserts |
| No delegation of authority level applies | The harness takes no business decision; the notice is the manager's, and authorisation is answered by rwb-access and the DoA table of P4 |

Field IDs are those the legacy section names and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 holds. The notice is P6's, the partner and its instructions are S9's, the decision log and the rule rows are P7's, and the case behind the instruction is P3's; the harness reads them only through those contracts and never from a schema. The contractual target and the length of the cure period are the versioned reference data of FEAT-PRM-02, read as data and never written by the harness. The harness owns no table and writes no row.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` | S9 rwb-partner | The partner, with partner_code, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end and score (AC1, AC2, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions` | S9 rwb-partner | The instructions on the case, with their case, type, due time and status (AC1, AC2, AC4) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices` | P6 rwb-comms | Issues the notice from the approved template the fixture names (AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` | P6 rwb-comms | Reads the notice back with its notice_type and sent_date (AC2, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | P7 rwb-decision | The decision record of the notice, with its decision code and rule version (AC1, AC3, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case before and after the notice, and the consumer effect of the events (AC3, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The caller's roles and rights before a read or a write (AC5) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13). No operation is invented in this story: each path is the owner's published operation, and where a screen would compose them the path would be the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The Ownership Map publishes no notice-on-a-missed-target operation and no cure-period read of its own, so the notice is not called through an operation of its own here: it is asserted through the P6 notice write and read-back, the partner and instruction reads, and the decision log, which is what the manager's screen would read after the action.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it writes its report to the wave record.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use in the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 rwb-comms | Counts one publication per notice and proves the notice is generated from the approved template before it is dispatched (AC2, AC3) |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 rwb-comms | Counts one publication per notice and asserts the consumer effect once, with the replay proving one processed row per consumer (AC3) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | The owning service through the local decision-record library (DP-03) | Proves the decision record of the notice was published with its rule version and confirmed by the central ledger, and stays one record after a replay (AC3, AC4) |

The harness subscribes to both topics under one consumer group of its own, counts publications and replays each event once. `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` is consumed by rwb-decision and `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` by rwb-reporting, per the event catalogue of Arch v5 slide 42 rows 13 and 14, so those are the consumer effects the run counts; `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` is consumed by rwb-decision and rwb-reporting per slide 42 row 08. The consumer effect that has a published operation in this story is the case through the rwb-case read of §12.2; where a consumer exposes no operation here, its inbox row count comes from the consumer evidence in the run fixture. `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` is out of the harness's scope: delivery happens after the notice leaves the service, and the harness asserts the notice to the dispatch and no further.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness observes two workflows and builds neither. NoticeDispatchWorkflow, P6's kit-template workflow on the task queue `rwb-comms` in the `rwb-recovery` namespace, takes the generated notice, generates the letter through rwb-document, takes the approval child on rwb-decision and hands the file to rwb-integration; the activities it observes are that document and integration hand-off as named on Arch v5 slide 17. InstructionWorkflow, S9's workflow on the task queue `rwb-partner`, holds the SLA timer per partner type that turns a missed service level into a chase and then a recall, with the activities `issueInstruction` and `recordResult`; the harness observes it because the notice is about a partner whose instruction is on that clock. No workflow, activity or Schedule is created, changed or owned by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added. NoticeDispatchWorkflow is started by the notice event and InstructionWorkflow is started by the instruction and held by its own SLA timer, so the harness starts nothing by cron and sets no overlap policy or catch-up window. JOB-10, the 16:00 WIN notices run owned by rwb-comms with rwb-integration, is the owner's schedule and not this story's.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-01); notice and template are P6's, partner and partner_instruction are S9's, decision_log_entry and rule_row are P7's, the reference data rows are P3's under the default ruling, and recovery_case is P3's.

| Fake | Contract | Stubbed answer in the run |
|---|---|---|
| Stub for rwb-partner (partner read) | `GET /partners` | The synthetic partner with partner_code, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end and the score the fixture names (GAP-0475; ASM-0667) |
| Stub for rwb-partner (instruction read) | `GET /partner/instructions` | The one synthetic instruction on the case, with its case_id, partner_id, instruction_type, instructed_at, due_at and status; the keys are the fixture's (GAP-0475; ASM-0667) |
| Stub for rwb-comms (notice write) | `POST /cases/{caseId}/notices` | Accepts the notice for the notice type and template the fixture names, answers 201 with the notice carrying notice_type and sent_date, and answers 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a caller holding R and not C (GAP-0475; ASM-0667) |
| Stub for rwb-comms (notice read) | `GET /notices/{noticeId}` | Returns the same notice the write answered, field for field, including the cure period start (GAP-0475; ASM-0667) |
| Stub for rwb-decision | `GET /decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | One record for the notice with its decision_code, rule_id, rule_version and the central ledger confirmation (GAP-0475; ASM-0667) |
| Stub for rwb-case | `GET /cases/{caseId}` | The case with its state unchanged across the notice and the forced failure (GAP-0475; ASM-0667) |
| Stub for rwb-access | `GET /me/session` | Allows RW-NPAMGR with Partner portal C and R; refuses a caller holding R and not C with 403 and MSG-P4-002 (GAP-0475; ASM-0667) |
| Fixture for the missed target and the cure period | The named rule version, its contractual target, the score and the versioned cure period length | The partner score, the contractual target of the named rule version, the notice type, the approved template and the cure period length with its version, held as fixture data (GAP-0475; ASM-0667) |

Each stub is generated from the published contract and its version is pinned in the run report, so a contract change shows up as a run failure and not as a silent pass. The harness environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic partner, instruction, case and notice keys, the stub answer shapes, the conduct of the missed-target comparison against the named rule version, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0475; ASM-0667).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 7 consumed, one hop each on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H dependencies the table adds, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for DP-03 and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for DP-19, are platform contract stories delivered in the platform wave, are recorded here and are not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays None; DP-13 adds none. The only blocking dependency is the I story RWB-S9-E7014-APP, which replaces its stub as it lands and never blocks the lane.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| NoticeRunner | Job | Runs the five owned criteria in order for a case and partner and holds the run lock |
| PartnerProbe | Service | Reads the partner with partner_code, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end and score from S9 |
| TargetProbe | Service | Compares the score with the contractual target of the rule version the fixture names and records the miss with the version beside it |
| NoticeDriver | Service | Issues the notice through P6 from the approved template, reads it back through P6, and reads the cure period start and its versioned length |
| DecisionReadBack | Service | Reads the decision log through P7 and asserts one record with its decision code, rule id and rule version, and the ledger confirmation |
| EventObserver | Service | Subscribes to `rwb.comms.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`, counts publications and consumptions, and replays each event once |
| StubSet | Fake | The eight stubs and the fixture of §12.8, generated from the published contracts with the version pinned |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes one report per case and partner keyed by story, caseId and partner_code, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the stubs from Day 1 and the real services as RWB-S9-E7014-APP lands, on the synthetic partner, instruction, case and notice keys held as fixture data, with the rule version, the contractual target, the score, the notice type and the cure period length named by the fixture and never by the code. The harness seeds nothing by hand and never writes a schema row. The environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the stub answer shapes, the conduct of the missed-target comparison, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0475; ASM-0667).

**Build steps**

1. Generate the eight stubs and the missed-target fixture from the published contracts, pin each contract version in the run report, and fail the run on a mismatch (X1).
2. Build the PartnerProbe and prove the partner read answers partner_code, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end and score, and the instruction read answers the instruction on the case (AC2).
3. Build the TargetProbe: compare the score with the contractual target of the named rule version, record the miss with the version, and fail the run where the target is missing or taken from the code (AC2, X2).
4. Build the NoticeDriver for the write and the read-back, and prove 201 with notice_type and sent_date and the same notice returned, field for field (AC2, X3).
5. Prove the cure period start is recorded and read back with the length of the versioned reference data and its version, and fail the run where the length differs (AC2, X4).
6. Add the DecisionReadBack for AC1 and AC3: one record with decision_code, rule_id and rule_version, and the ledger confirmation before the notice is reported as recorded.
7. Add the EventObserver for AC3: one publication and one consumption of each notice event, one `DecisionRecorded` confirmed by the ledger, the case effect once, and a replay of each event that changes nothing (X5).
8. Add the forced decision-record failure for AC4 through the notice read-back, the decision log, the partner read and the instruction read before and after, so nothing changes is asserted and not assumed (X6).
9. Add the session read and the refused notice write for AC5, then the EvidenceReport and the gate, and swap a stub for the real owner as RWB-S9-E7014-APP lands (X7).

**Feature switch.** None. The harness has no production flag and runs in the test environment only.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass against the fakes and again against RWB-S9-E7014-APP when it lands, and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story, caseId and partner_code, with the rule version, the target, the notice and the cure period cited from the fixture and the data.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values on the answer it reads, and owns no message text. The legacy section carries these three messages for the feature and no P6-specific or S9-specific message, so none is invented here: MSG-GEN-001 with the missing field when the notice write is made short of a required value such as the notice type or the template, MSG-P4-002 with the refused action on the notice write, and MSG-P7-003 when the decision record cannot be written and the notice does not go out.

##### 15. Screens and states

The harness renders no screen: it observes the owners' operations and writes a report. The legacy section names SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation, which belong to S9 and its CON story; the harness neither builds nor reads them, and it asserts their data through the partner read, the instruction read and the notice read-back.

| State | Read through | What the run asserts |
|---|---|---|
| ACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED, EXITED (panel status) | rwb-partner partner read | The panel classification of the partner at the time of the notice (DF-PRT-005) |
| SENT, ACCEPTED, IN_PROGRESS, DONE, DECLINED, RECALLED (instruction status) | rwb-partner instruction read | The status of the instruction before and after the notice, and that a refused or failed notice leaves it unchanged (DF-PRT-014) |
| The notice record | rwb-comms notice read | The same notice the write answered, with its notice_type, sent_date and barcode, and no status value the source does not name (DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023) |
| The cure period | rwb-comms notice read and the versioned reference data | The start is recorded and read back, and its length is the versioned reference value with its version (FEAT-PRM-02) |
| The decision record of the notice | rwb-decision decision log | One record with its decision code, rule id and rule version, confirmed by the central ledger |
| The case state | rwb-case case read | The case is unchanged by the notice and by the forced failure |
| PARTNER_RECALLED, ESCALATED | the rule rows and the instruction read | The recall and conduct context the notice sits in, recorded by S9 and never set by the harness |

The environment, layout and retention of the run report are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0475; ASM-0667).

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |

| TC-E7-014-02-ITG | Legacy AC2 not recorded stays with RWB-S9-E7014-APP; ITG AC4 | Integration | The decision-record library forced to fail on the notice write |

The Covers column names the legacy AC the copy derives from and the ITG AC it asserts, and the full legacy test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx under the same legacy test case ID. Legacy AC2, the forced decision-log failure, stays with RWB-S9-E7014-APP and is asserted here at the notice write through AC4.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the rule version, the contractual target, the score, the notice type, the approved template, the cure period length and its version, the synthetic keys and the report layout are data.
- No personal data in logs, events or reports: every key is synthetic, and the events carry IDs and facts only.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this run reads no ACE data at all, and the partner, instruction, notice, decision and case rows are read only through their owners' contracts (DP-01).
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would (DP-11, DP-13).
- A stub pass is never reported as a real pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner.
- The notice is asserted from the owner's answer and never from a narrative, and no status value is asserted for it that no source names.
- The cure period length is read from versioned reference data and never counted in the harness, and a new rule version is never applied to a case decided under an earlier one (R-UNI-38).
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and it never writes a row by hand or sets a state it then asserts.
- A failing criterion is fixed in the owning service or raised as a gap; it is never waived in the script.
