Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. The legacy section names partner with DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007, decision_log_entry with DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 and rule_row with DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015, and those ranges are copied unchanged; the instruction row is cited where the S9 field catalog and the dictionary give it, and no field ID is invented. The partner and its instructions are S9's, the decision log and the rule rows are P7's, and the case behind the instruction and the sample is P3's; the harness reads them only through those contracts and never from a schema. The harness owns no table and writes no row.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` | S9 rwb-partner | The partner, its type and its panel status before and after the breach, with the optional `type` and `status` filters (AC1, AC2, AC3) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions` | S9 rwb-partner | The instructions placed with the partner, with their case, type and status, and the instruction each sampled contact or complaint belongs to (AC2, AC3) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results` | S9 rwb-partner | Builds the sample population of partner results for the period, and proves the refusal after the breach (AC2, AC3, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?ruleId={ruleId}&from={from}` | P7 rwb-decision | The breach records of the run, with their decision code and the rule version in force (AC1, AC3, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case state before and after the check and the forced failure, and the consumer effect of the partner events (AC3, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The caller's roles and rights before a read or a write (AC5) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13). No operation is invented in this story: each path is the owner's published operation, and where a screen would compose them the path would be the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The conduct check itself has no published operation and starts on its own trigger inside S9, so the harness fires the trigger through the S9 fixture hook of section 12.8, reports that hop as a stub pass until RWB-S9-E7016-APP lands, and proves the effect through the reads: the panel status on the partner read, the statuses on the instruction read, the case on the case read and the breach on the decision log.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it writes its report to the wave record.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use in the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1` | S9 rwb-partner | Counts the results that make up the sample population, asserts the case effect once, and proves the replay leaves the case and the instruction unchanged (AC3) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | S9 rwb-partner through the local decision-record library (DP-03) | Proves the breach record was published with its rule version and confirmed by the central ledger, and stays one entry after a replay (AC3, AC4) |
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | Pins the rule package version in force for the run, published by JOB-20 at 00:01, so the breach is read against the version that was in force and not the latest one (AC1, AC3) |

`rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` is Arch v5 slide 43 row 21, with rwb-litigation, rwb-asset and rwb-case as consumers; `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` is slide 42 row 08, produced by all 19 services into rwb-decision's central ledger; `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` is slide 43 row 30, produced by rwb-decision on `rwb.decision.events.v1`, and its publication is the promote step JOB-20 of slide 44 and the publish step of slide 27. The harness subscribes to the topics under one consumer group of its own, counts publications and replays each event once. The consumer effect it reads is the case through the rwb-case operation of section 12.2; the inbox row counts of rwb-litigation and rwb-asset, the other consumers of `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1`, come from the consumer evidence in the run fixture, because neither consumer exposes an operation in this story.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness exercises InstructionWorkflow, S9's workflow on the task queue `rwb-partner` in the `rwb-recovery` namespace, and observes what it does: the SLA timer per partner type that turns a missed service level into a chase and then a recall, and the activities `issueInstruction` and `recordResult`, which carries the result that becomes a sample. They are stated here as observed and not built here; no workflow, activity or Schedule is created, changed or owned by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added. The conduct check runs on its own trigger, so the harness sets no cron, no overlap policy and no catch-up window. JOB-20, the rule promote at 00:01, is rwb-decision's Schedule and is observed through its event, never started here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-01); partner and partner_instruction are S9's, decision_log_entry and rule_row are P7's, and recovery_case is P3's.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Contract | Stubbed answer in the run |
|---|---|---|
| Stub for rwb-partner (partner read) | `GET /partners` | Partner `PTR-SYN-0008` with partner_code, partner_type AGENCY, panel_status ACTIVE, contract_end 2027-12-31 before the breach and SUSPENDED after it, filtered by the `type` and `status` parameters it is given |
| Stub for rwb-partner (instruction read) | `GET /partner/instructions` | Instructions `INS-SYN-000801` and `INS-SYN-000802` on case `RW-2027-000801`, each with its instruction_type, instructed_at, due_at, status and result; RECALLED after the breach, the status they held before it after a forced failure |
| Stub for rwb-partner (result write) | `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results` | Accepts the result once per instruction and returns the instruction with its new status; returns 409 on a second submission of the same result; refuses the write for a caller holding R and not U with 403 and MSG-P4-002 |
| Stub for rwb-decision | `GET /decision-log?ruleId={ruleId}&from={from}` | One breach record for the run with its decision_code, rule_id, rule_version and inputs_ref, and the central ledger confirmation; no entry after the forced failure |
| Stub for rwb-case | `GET /cases/{caseId}` | Case `RW-2027-000801` with its state unchanged across the conduct check and the forced failure |
| Stub for rwb-access | `GET /me/session` | Answers the session for a caller holding Partner portal R and U, and for a caller holding R and not U |
| S9 conduct-trigger fixture hook | The conduct check, which publishes no operation | Fires the check for `PTR-SYN-0008` as data: the population period, the sampled contacts and complaints, the breach and the rule package version, at the point where S9's own trigger would fire; the hook is fixture configuration and no production operation |

Each stub is generated from the published contract and its version is pinned in the run report, so a contract change shows up as a run failure and not as a silent pass. The harness environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic partner and instruction keys, the stub answer shapes, the sample size and sampling method, the source of the contacts and complaints the sample reads, the fixture hook for the unpublished conduct trigger, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0476; ASM-0668).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 6 consumed, one hop each on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13) |
| Kafka | None published; three consumed, `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1`, `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` and `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1`, counted and replayed once |
| Temporal | None added; InstructionWorkflow on `rwb-partner` observed, with its SLA timer and the `issueInstruction` and `recordResult` activities |
| File | None. The result write accepts documents on the S9 contract, and the run holds no file of its own |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H dependencies the table adds, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, are platform stories delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays None; DP-13 adds none. The only blocking dependency is the I story RWB-S9-E7016-APP, which replaces its stub; until it is live the run uses the stub and reports a stub pass as a stub pass, and the story is Day 1.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ConductRunner | Job | Runs the five owned criteria in order for a partner and holds the run lock |
| SampleBuilder | Service | Builds the sample population of partner results for the period through the result write, and proves one result per instruction |
| ConductDriver | Service | Fires the conduct check through the S9 fixture hook and records the hop as a stub pass until RWB-S9-E7016-APP lands |
| PartnerProbe | Service | Reads the partner and its panel status, and the instructions and their statuses, before and after the breach and after the forced failure |
| DecisionReadBack | Service | Reads the decision log by rule and by period, and asserts one breach record with its rule version and the ledger confirmation |
| EventObserver | Service | Subscribes to `rwb.partner.events.v1`, `rwb.decision-record.v1` and `rwb.decision.events.v1`, counts publications and replays each event once |
| CaseProbe | Service | Reads the case before and after each step and asserts it is unchanged where the run says nothing changes |
| StubSet | Fake | The six stubs and the conduct-trigger fixture hook of section 12.8, generated from the published contracts with the version pinned |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes one report per partner keyed by story and partner_code, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the stubs from Day 1 and the real services as RWB-S9-E7016-APP lands, on the synthetic partner `PTR-SYN-0008`, instructions `INS-SYN-000801` and `INS-SYN-000802`, case `RW-2027-000801` and contract end 2027-12-31, with the sampled contacts and complaints held in the fixture as data. The harness seeds nothing by hand and never writes a schema row. The environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the sample size and method, the source of the contacts and complaints, the fixture hook for the unpublished trigger, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0476; ASM-0668).

**Build steps**

1. Generate the six stubs and the conduct-trigger fixture hook from the published contracts and the fixture, and pin each contract version in the run report; fail the run on a mismatch (X1).
2. Build the SampleBuilder and the PartnerProbe, and prove the sample population is built once through the result write with a 409 on a repeated submission (AC2, X5).
3. Name the sample size, the population period, the partner and each sampled contact with its instruction in the evidence, and fail the run where a sample has no record behind it (AC2, X2).
4. Build the ConductDriver and prove the trigger fires through the hook, with the hop reported as a stub pass until the APP story lands (AC1).
5. Add the DecisionReadBack for AC1 and AC3: one breach record with its decision code and rule version, the version that was in force, and the ledger confirmation before the breach is reported as upheld (X3, X4).
6. Prove the effect of the breach through the reads: SUSPENDED on the partner, RECALLED on the affected instructions, and the case unchanged where the rule does not move it (AC3, X5).
7. Add the EventObserver for AC3: one publication of the decision record, the partner topic events counted, the case effect once, and a replay that changes nothing (AC3).
8. Add the forced decision-record failure for AC4 through the partner, instruction and case reads before and after, so nothing changes is asserted and not assumed (X6).
9. Add the session read and the refused result write for AC5, then the EvidenceReport and the gate, and swap a stub for the real owner as RWB-S9-E7016-APP lands (X7).

**Feature switch.** None. The harness has no production flag and runs in the test environment only.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass against the fakes and again against RWB-S9-E7016-APP when it lands, and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story and partner_code.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values on the answer it reads, and owns no message text. The legacy section carries these three messages for the feature and no S9-specific message, so none is invented here: MSG-GEN-001 with the missing field when a read is made short of a required parameter, MSG-P4-002 with the refused action on the result write, and MSG-P7-003 when the decision record cannot be written and the breach and the recall stop.

##### 15. Screens and states

The harness renders no screen: it observes the owners' operations and writes a report. The legacy section names SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation, which belong to S9 and its CON story; the harness neither builds nor reads them, and it asserts their data through the partner read and the instruction read.

| State | Read through | What the run asserts |
|---|---|---|
| ACTIVE, ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED, EXITED (panel status) | rwb-partner partner read | The panel classification before the breach and SUSPENDED after it (DF-PRT-005) |
| SENT, ACCEPTED, IN_PROGRESS, DONE, DECLINED, RECALLED (instruction status) | rwb-partner instruction read | The status of each instruction before the breach, RECALLED after it, and unchanged after the forced failure (DF-PRT-014) |
| The sample of contacts and complaints | rwb-partner partner and instruction reads, and the result write | Each sampled contact or complaint is named with the instruction it belongs to, or reported as a gap in the evidence |
| The breach record | rwb-decision decision log, by rule and by period | One entry with its decision code, rule version and inputs reference, confirmed by the central ledger |
| The case state | rwb-case case read | The case is unchanged by the conduct check where the rule does not move it, and unchanged by the forced failure |
| PARTNER_RECALLED, NOTICE_BLOCKED, PLACEMENT_RECALLED, EXCEPTION_QUEUE | the rule rows and the owners' reads | The conduct, notice, placement and unlogged-action context the run reads at its edges, recorded by the owning services and never set by the harness |

The environment, layout and retention of the run report are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0476; ASM-0668).

##### 16. Test cases

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-E7-016-01-ITG | AC1 (legacy); ITG AC1 | End to end | One partner on the panel with two instructions and a sampled result on each, the conduct check and the decision record live |
| TC-E7-016-02-ITG | Legacy AC2 not recorded stays with RWB-S9-E7016-APP; ITG AC4 | Integration | The decision-record library forced to fail on the conduct check |
| TC-E7-016-03-ITG | Access; ITG AC5 | Component | A caller holding Partner portal R and not U |

The Covers column names the legacy AC the copy derives from and the ITG AC it asserts, and the full legacy test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx under the same legacy test case ID. Legacy AC2, the forced decision-log failure, stays with RWB-S9-E7016-APP and is asserted here at the conduct check through AC4.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the partner, its type, its panel status, the contract end, the rule package version, the sample size and method, the sampled contacts and complaints and the report layout are data.
- No personal data in logs, events or reports: every key is synthetic, and the events carry IDs and facts only.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this run reads no ACE data at all, and the partner, instruction, decision and case rows are read only through their owners' contracts (DP-01).
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would (DP-11, DP-13).
- A stub pass is never reported as a real pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner, and the conduct trigger hop is named as a stub until the APP story lands.
- A sampled contact or complaint is evidenced or reported as a gap; it is never written up from a narrative.
- The breach is read against the rule version that was in force, never against the latest version, so R-UNI-38 is asserted and not assumed.
- No action proceeds unlogged: the forced failure of R-UNI-39 must leave the partner, its instructions and its case unchanged.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and it never writes a row by hand or sets a state it then asserts.
- A failing criterion is fixed in the owning service or raised as a gap; it is never waived in the script.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract baseline of the additional-cost claim on a held asset, split from RWB-E7-017. It fixes the three partner operations the claim is made and read by on `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13), the claim and invoice elements over DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016, the rights of TSD S9 T6.1, the error sets of T-A.2, the one event of the pair that announces a claim, the tables of `rwb_partner` and the fakes. No source publishes the fields of `InvoiceRequest` or `Invoice`, a cost line of its own, the value set of `result_code`, an operation that approves a claim, or an event that announces an invoice or an approval (GAP-3134; ASM-5483, ASM-5484, ASM-5488). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract of the additional-cost claim of rwb-partner - the three operations, the claim and invoice elements, the rights, the error set, the event, the tables and the fakes**, so that **the app story, SCR-35, the partner gateway and the wave 4 harness build against one fixed, testable contract on Day 1, and a field, a right or an answer shape of a cost claim can never drift between rwb-partner, rwb-access and rwb-asset without a failing build**.

This baseline declares shapes and moves nothing. It writes no code, no migration and no table, and changes no instruction, no firm and no claim. What it publishes is one OpenAPI 3.1 fragment for three operations, nine contract tables, four fakes and the one event schema the claim is announced by.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy story named two endpoints on the monolith base; TSD S9 T-A.1 publishes six operations for the module and the ownership rows confirm six provided and none consumed. The extra cost of a held asset is a partner result and a fee invoice, so two mutations and one read of those six are this key's surface.

- **The base moves and nothing else.** DP-13 moves the result and instruction paths to `/api/recovery/partner/v1`; the paths, the requests, the answers and the error sets are TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2 unchanged.
- **The claim is a result, and the money is an invoice.** `PartnerInstruction` covers DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 and API-S9-005 records the claim with its files; API-S9-006 takes `InvoiceRequest` and answers `Invoice`. No source publishes a cost line of its own, so the baseline fixes the element names, the flags and the absence, and nothing more (GAP-3134; ASM-5483).
- **The rights are the matrix.** TSD S9 T6.1 gives 29 identities the partner-portal rights R, C, U and A; the claim is U on the result write, C on the invoice write and R on the instruction read, and the baseline widens nothing.
- **One event and no approval announcement.** EV-21 `PartnerResultSubmitted` is TSD S9 T5.3's published fact and a claim is a result, so its schema is published and no invoice or approval event exists to publish (GAP-3134; ASM-5488).
- **The edge is one hop and the asset is not declared.** The composite route serves SCR-35 and PRT-02 to PRT-04 and the partner gateway terminates the partner's token (DP-19; INT-24); the asset record and `v_ace_npa_asset` are rwb-asset's and P1's, and no property of them is declared (DP-05; ASM-5486).

The naming is fixed here: schema and login `rwb_partner`, base `/api/recovery/partner/v1`, topic `rwb.partner.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner` (Template and Rules §R4; context pack).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the queue and the event name follow the platform rule.
- The platform error envelope, the pagination and filter convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline; where this document narrows them it says so.
- Ownership comes from the context pack and the Ownership Map only: `partner`, `partner_instruction` and `partner_user` are S9's, `recovery_case` is P3's, `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` are P7's, `document` is P5's, `payment` is P8's, and the asset record with `v_ace_npa_asset` is S5's and P1's. No other service's table or operation is declared here.
- TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2 publish the six operations with their requests, answers, rights and error sets, and the API Specification publishes `PartnerInstruction` and `Invoice`; FSD S9 A2.14 and the legacy story give the business meaning of the extra cost.
- RWB-S9-AD022-CON publishes the firm element, the partner read, the issue and the accept operations and shares this service's schema and topic; this baseline re-publishes none of them and names the boundary in 12.1.
- The partner gateway's FAPI 2.0 token profile and the partner-portal rights of rwb-access are named but not yet published for this key, and the placeholder is recorded (GAP-3134; ASM-5487).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 and sits in contract group `CG-W4` by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7), and no approval is needed to tag a Draft baseline.

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 fragment: `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results` (API-S9-005), `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/invoices` (API-S9-006) and `GET /partner/instructions` (API-S9-003), each with its request, its answer, its right and its errors.
2. Fix the claim on the `PartnerInstruction` element over DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 and mark the three fields it writes: `resultCode`, `feeAmount` and `status`.
3. Fix `InvoiceRequest` and `Invoice` with the fields the API Specification gives them and record that no source publishes the rest (GAP-3134; ASM-5483).
4. Record that the additional cost has no table and no element of its own in S9: it rides on `partner_instruction` and on the result file of rwb-document (AC3).
5. Fix the rights from TSD S9 T-A.1 and T6.1: U on the result write, C on the invoice write, R on the read, each with the scope applied (AC4).
6. Publish one event schema: EV-21 `PartnerResultSubmitted`, with its envelope, its payload and the rule that a payload carries identifiers and no personal data (AC5).
7. Publish the fakes of 12.8, the error envelope of section 14 and the naming baseline of 12.9 (AC6).
8. Record the boundary: no consumed operation, no `v_ace_*` read, no asset element, no approval route and no second topic (AC7).
9. Add the contract tests and tag the baseline, then hand it to RWB-S9-E7017-APP, SCR-35, PRT-02 to PRT-04, RWB-PLT-N001-CON and RWB-ITG-E7017-ITG.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A request or a response fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 400 or 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC2 |
| X2 | A field is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC2 |
| X3 | A fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X4 | A field of the invoice element carries a value no source gives | The review fails and the element test fails the build | None | AC2, AC3 |
| X5 | A right differs from TSD S9 T6.1 or T-A.1 | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC4 |
| X6 | A consumed operation, a second topic, an approval route or an asset element is declared | The absence test fails the build | None | AC5, AC7 |
| X7 | The document names another service's base, table or topic as its own | The boundary test fails the review | None | AC7 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the context pack, FSD S9, TSD S9 and the ownership rows only |
| Negotiable | The example values and the internal record shape are settled in the baseline review; the base, the operations, the rights, the element names, the topic, the queue and the schema are fixed |
| Valuable | Unblocks RWB-S9-E7017-APP, SCR-35, PRT-02 to PRT-04 and RWB-ITG-E7017-ITG on Day 1 |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI fragment, one event schema, nine contract tables, four fakes and seven contract tests |
| Small | One sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 The three claim operations are declared on the partner base with their errors (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then it validates with no error

    Then POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/invoices (API-S9-006) declares InvoiceRequest in, Invoice out, the Idempotency-Key header and the errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503

    Then feeAmount is numeric(18,2), status is required over LOV-INSTR-STATUS, resultCode is varchar(40) and optional, and the lists are LOV-INSTRUCTION, LOV-INSTR-STATUS, LOV-PANEL and LOV-PARTNER-TYPE copied from TSD S9 T3.2
    Then the value set of resultCode is reference data and no member is invented

    Then the decision-record stub answers a healthy chain and a stopped chain

    Then the drift test compares every fake with the document and fails the build on any difference

    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner, with None where the element is empty
    Then the schema is rwb_partner, the login is rwb_partner, the base is /api/recovery/partner/v1, the topic is rwb.partner.events.v1 with its retry and .dlt topics, the queue is rwb-partner in namespace rwb-recovery and the Java package is th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner
    Then the tables named as owned are partner, partner_user and partner_instruction, and the asset record, every v_ace_* view, recovery_case, decision_log_entry, document and payment are named as other owners'
    Then the document declares no consumed operation, no v_ace_* read and no asset, case, document or payment element of its own
    Then the absence test fails a build that adds a consumed operation, a second topic, an approval route, a cost table, a Schedule or a v_ace_* path
```

These seven criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only. They restate no business outcome owned by RWB-S9-E7017-APP, whose one legacy criterion stays with it word for word, and they copy no criterion of the legacy story.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The claim and its invoice are rwb-partner's, and the contract declares the claim on the instruction element and the money on the invoice pair only | TSD S9 T3.1, T-A.2; ownership rows |
| BR2 | Every path sits under `/api/recovery/partner/v1` and no monolith path is kept | DP-13; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR3 | The event name is `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on `rwb.partner.events.v1`, with the retry and `.dlt` topics | DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR4 | No value a business person may change is an enumeration member taken from no source: the lists are TSD S9 T3.2's and the codes of `resultCode` are reference data | BR-S9-014; FSD S9 A2.14.3.1 |
| BR5 | The rights are the matrix of TSD S9 T6.1 and T-A.1; the contract widens none and declares no approval right | TSD S9 T6.1, T-A.1 |
| BR6 | The additional cost has no table of its own: the claim rides on `partner_instruction` and the evidence on rwb-document | GAP-3134; ASM-5483 |
| BR7 | The payload of EV-21 carries identifiers, a code and a date and no personal data | Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17); TSD S9 T6.2 |
| BR8 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version | Platform API rule (ADR-020) |
| BR9 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-partner and re-publishes no other baseline's operations | DP-01, DP-11; ownership rows (6 provided, 0 consumed) |
| BR10 | No read of ACE and no read of the asset: no `v_ace_*` path, view or property and no asset element is declared | DP-05; ASM-5486 |
| BR11 | The `Idempotency-Key` header is declared on the two mutations and on neither read | TSD S9 T-A.2 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The operations, the elements, the rights, the event and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, the screens, the edge contract and the wave 4 harness accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1 | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or a list member changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake, or a forbidden element | A contract test or an absence test fails | In review |

The state machine the document serves is the claim's: the instruction moves on `status` from `SENT` and `ACCEPTED` to `IN_PROGRESS`, then to `DONE` on approval, and a recall moves it to `RECALLED` (TSD S9 T3.2). This baseline publishes the vocabulary and moves nothing, and it declares no approval status because the list has none (ASM-5485).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-partner (S9); base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results` (API-S9-005) | Multipart `result` and `files` in, `PartnerInstruction` out | Partner portal, right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` |
| POST | `/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/invoices` (API-S9-006) | `InvoiceRequest` in, `Invoice` out | Partner portal, right C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` |
| GET | `/partner/instructions` (API-S9-003) | Query `status`, `page`, `size`; `InstructionPage` out for the caller's firm | Partner portal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

API-S9-003 answers 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002 and 503. API-S9-005 answers 401, 403, 404, 409, 415, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503. API-S9-006 answers 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503. Each carries the error envelope and one message ID of section 14. The paths, requests, answers and error sets are TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2's; the fields of the two invoice elements are not published there and that absence is recorded (GAP-3134; ASM-5483). The other three operations of the module — API-S9-001, API-S9-002 and API-S9-004 — are RWB-S9-AD022-CON's and are not restated here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The right is enforced by the platform guard and the assets the claim refers to arrive as identifiers, so no consumed operation and no read of another service is declared. The plan's contract-dependency row is empty and DP-08 is not in its pattern set, so the guard is not a contract row of this key (ASM-5487).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Name | Payload | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| EV-21 `PartnerResultSubmitted` | `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` | `caseId`, `instructionId`, `resultCode`, `resultedAt` | The case-owning service, rwb-litigation, rwb-asset and rwb-reporting |
| `DecisionRecorded` (library, DP-03) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | The record reference, the decision code, the rule id and its version | rwb-decision, which seals it in the central ledger |

Both go through the outbox, the CloudEvents envelope and the retry and `.dlt` topics (DP-09). The pair of the service is EV-20 `InstructionIssued` and EV-21, and only EV-21 is the claim's; EV-20 is named and not declared. No invoice and no approval event exists in the pair, so none is declared (GAP-3134; ASM-5488). The app story builds the events; this baseline publishes the schema.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The service places and receives work through REST on its own base and reads no other service's topic in the ownership rows. A consumer group, a subscription or an inbox row added here fails the absence test of AC5.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `InstructionWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per instruction | `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the instruction, the case reference and the firm; signals: accept, result, costApproval, recall, contract end; outcome: the instruction status |

`InstructionWorkflow` is the one workflow in the ownership rows; this baseline declares the workflow and its signal surface only and registers no activity and no Schedule. The `costApproval` signal is the claim's approval step and has no REST operation behind it (GAP-3134; ASM-5484).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. This baseline declares no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row and no shared job table; the service's job list is empty in the ownership rows (Jobs: None).

No cost table exists and none is declared (BR6).

##### 13. Solution plan

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is a prohibition: the document declares no `v_ace_*` path or property and the service holds no grant, so the asset of a claim is an identifier and the asset record is S5's (ASM-5486). DP-13 moves the two legacy paths and gives the three operations their home, and DP-19 sits behind SCR-35 and PRT-02 to PRT-04. DP-09, which the outbox carries, DP-14, which the topic name carries, and DP-08, which the rights carry, are not in the pattern set, so their absence is recorded (GAP-3134; ASM-5487, ASM-5488).

1. Write the three operations and the additive rule of AC1 into the pipeline.
2. Fix the claim element with its nine fields and the flags of AC2, and the two invoice elements with the fields their owner publishes.
3. Record the absence of a cost table and a cost line, and name the evidence file of rwb-document (AC3).
4. Publish the rights (AC4), the one event schema (AC5), the four fakes with the drift test (AC6) and the naming baseline, the tables and the boundary (AC7).
5. Tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off.

The deliverables are `openapi/rwb-partner-cost-v1.yaml`, the EV-21 schema, the contract README row of the absence, and the four fakes of 12.8. **Done when** the fragment validates in the pipeline, the seven contract tests pass, the fakes answer every path and the drift test is green, and the app story, the screens, the edge contract and the wave 4 harness have accepted the baseline.

The contract serves SCR-35 Placement and allocation for the claim and the approval, SCR-34 Partner list for the firm, PRT-02 Instruction and PRT-03 Upload result for the partner, and PRT-04 Invoice for the fee; all arrive through the gateway-bff composite route and, outside the bank, the partner gateway of FAPI 2.0 (FSD S9 Screens; Arch v5 slide 8; INT-24). The legacy screen table gives SCR-34 and SCR-35 "Loading; list"; PRT-02 to PRT-04 are named by the FSD and carry no legacy state, and the composite route specification and the screen field lists belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

No source publishes a screen for the approval or the refusal, so the place and the wording of the approval state are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3134; ASM-5485). The refusal, duplicate, invalid-answer and not-recorded states read the messages of section 14 on the same route.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the states, the types, the rights, the cost codes and the amount stay reference data and rule rows, never a schema default.
- No personal data in a schema, an event, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, dates, amounts and list values only, and every example is synthetic.
- The claim, the invoice and the firm stay with rwb-partner: the document declares no case, asset, document, payment or ACE property (DP-01).
- ACE data and the asset only through their owners: no `v_ace_*` path, no view property and no asset element is declared (DP-05, BR10).
- One base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The document lists only operations owned by rwb-partner and re-publishes no other baseline's operations (BR9).
- No approval route is invented: where no operation exists, the contract says so and the signal is declared in 12.5.
- The error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule and the outbox library come from the platform; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the extra-cost slice of RWB-E7-017 in rwb-partner. AC2 is kept word for word with its origin tag added. The additional partner cost on a held asset is recorded as the partner's result on `partner_instruction` (`result_code`, `fee_amount`) through API-S9-005 and its fee invoice through API-S9-006, checked against the fee schedule version and the recorded result, then approved or refused on `InstructionWorkflow` with the decision record written first. The held asset and its holding cost stay with rwb-asset (S5, FEAT-AST-07). No source gives the claim a field catalogue, a cost type list, an approval limit or a table of its own, names an operation that approves it, or gives the event pair an invoice event (GAP-3133; ASM-5483, ASM-5484, ASM-5488). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **partner and agency manager**, I want **the extra costs and services a partner claims on a held asset to be recorded against its instruction and approved or refused with the decision record written first**, so that **partners are placed, paid and measured by rule, and a cost that cannot be recorded changes nothing**.

This story owns: the one legacy criterion the plan gives it, AC2; the recording of the claim and its evidence on `partner_instruction` through API-S9-005 and the fee invoice through API-S9-006; the check against the fee schedule version and the recorded result; the approval or refusal with the decision record written first (DP-03) and one EV-21 publication per recorded claim; and SCR-35 with the SCR-34 read, through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) on base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13).

It does not own: the published shapes, rights, error set and fakes, which are RWB-S9-E7017-CON; AC1, the end-to-end proof, which is RWB-ITG-E7017-ITG's; the held asset, its holding cost, the work order and the provision step, which are rwb-asset's (S5, FEAT-AST-07); the panel and the fee schedule as reference data (FEAT-PRM-02); issuing, accepting and closing an instruction; the recall and notice rules R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-30; the case, which is rwb-case; the rights as code, which is rwb-access; and the deployment, which is the operations story of this key.

##### 2. Business rationale

The objective, the problem and the metric are unchanged from the legacy story and the module FSD: partners were instructed and paid by email and spreadsheet, and the cost of holding an asset is one of the six points every partner type is managed on (FSD S9 A1.3, A2.14.1; REQ-S9-001, REQ-S9-004). The target records the claim on the instruction, approves it against the contracted schedule and the recorded result, and writes one decision record, measured on the decision log at the monthly target of A2.14.1. What D-RCV-60 changes is who owns the claim, the approval, the record and the asset facts.

- **The claim is a result on the instruction, not a new object.** The ownership rows give S9 three tables and `partner_instruction` carries `result_code`, `fee_amount` and `status` (DF-PRT-014 to DF-PRT-016); the evidence lands in rwb-document, so no cost table and no migration is added (GAP-3133; ASM-5483).
- **The fee is checked, not computed here.** REQ-S9-004 pays fees from the contracted schedule against a recorded result; the schedule is a versioned reference-data row of the panel and the result is the instruction's own row (ASM-5489).
- **The extra cost is a work order on a held asset.** Storage, property tax, insurance, security and eviction are raised as work to a vendor; its invoice is released when the work is accepted and blocked when it is refused (R-DIS-10, R-DIS-11, R-DIS-12). The stage that raises the work order is rwb-asset's and this story owns the partner side of it.
- **The record is a condition of the act.** R-UNI-39 blocks an action whose log entry cannot be written; AC2 is that rule at this claim.
- **The asset keeps its owner.** The legacy data section reads `v_ace_npa_asset` (DF-ACE-208 to DF-ACE-219); after the split the asset record and that view are rwb-asset's and rwb-source-data's, and this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-05; ASM-5486).
- **Two facts have no source.** No published operation approves a claim, and the event pair has no invoice or approval event (GAP-3133; ASM-5484, ASM-5488).

No business value moves: the cost type, the fee schedule, the approval limit, the instruction states and the right are reference data and rule values, read with their version and never written in code.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S9-E7017-CON is published: the results and invoice writes on `/api/recovery/partner/v1`, the claim and invoice elements, the rights, the error set and the fakes.
- `partner_instruction` exists in `rwb_partner` from the DB story of this service with DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 and the standard columns of TSD S9 T3.0; `partner` carries DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the decision-record library creates `decision_record` and `outbox_event` in `rwb_partner` and publishes on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-34 and SCR-35 reach this service through the composite route (DP-19), and a partner outside the bank arrives on the partner gateway of FAPI 2.0 (INT-24).
- A partner holds a live instruction of a type from LOV-INSTRUCTION against a held asset, and the asset reference on it is an identifier of rwb-asset's record.
- The fee schedule version in force is a reference-data row of the panel (ASM-5489).
- The service runs as its own login on `rwb_partner`, holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant.
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline.

##### 4. Flow

1. The partner reads its own firm's work through `GET /partner/instructions` and picks the instruction the extra cost belongs to (DF-PRT-011 to DF-PRT-014).
2. It records the cost claim with its evidence through `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results` (API-S9-005, right U, `Idempotency-Key`): result code, the service performed, the amount claimed and the files.
3. The service validates the claim and answers 422 with MSG-GEN-001 on a missing field, 415 on a disallowed file type, 409 on a repeat (X3, X5, X6).
4. `CostDecisionRecordWriter` writes one local record before any row moves: the instruction, the firm, the case reference, the amount, the schedule version, the rule version in force and the trigger (DP-03; R-UNI-39). A failed write leaves the row as it was and answers MSG-P7-003 (AC2, X1).
5. `recordCostClaim` writes in one transaction: `result_code`, `fee_amount`, and `status` from `SENT` or `ACCEPTED` to `IN_PROGRESS`; no other column moves and no row is deleted.
6. The outbox publishes EV-21 `PartnerResultSubmitted` with `caseId`, `instructionId`, `resultCode` and `resultedAt`, once per recorded claim (DP-09).
7. The partner submits the fee invoice through `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/invoices` (API-S9-006, right C): `InvoiceRequest` in, `Invoice` out, the same record-first rule.
8. The manager opens SCR-35, sees the claim against the instruction with its amount, its evidence and the schedule version in force, and checks it against the schedule and the recorded result (REQ-S9-004).
9. On approval the `costApproval` signal reaches `InstructionWorkflow`: the approval is recorded, `approveCostInvoice` releases the invoice for payment against `fee_amount`, and `status` moves to `DONE`. On refusal the claim is recorded as refused, the invoice stays blocked and the status stays `IN_PROGRESS`, with the coded reason from reference data (R-DIS-11, R-DIS-12; §9).
10. The asset, its holding cost and the work order are shown on SCR-35 through rwb-asset's own fragment; this service writes no asset row and announces nothing about the asset (ASM-5486).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The decision record cannot be written before the claim or the approval | Nothing changes: no column, no release, no outbox row | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, TC-E7-017-02 |
| X2 | The caller lacks the partner-portal right of the operation | 403 before any read or write | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E7-017-03 |
| X3 | The same claim is submitted twice, or the instruction already carries it | 409; one claim and one EV-21 remain | None | TC-S9-E7017-APP-02 |
| X4 | The instruction belongs to a partner of another firm | 404; the scope comes from the caller's firm, never from a parameter | None | BR8 |
| X5 | A result file is outside the allowed set | 415; nothing is recorded | None | TC-S9-E7017-APP-02 |
| X6 | The claim reaches an instruction already `DONE` or `RECALLED` | 409; the status is not moved backwards | None | §9, BR5 |
| X7 | The claim is refused | The refusal is recorded, the invoice stays blocked, the status stays `IN_PROGRESS` | None | TC-S9-E7017-APP-01 |
| X8 | An approval arrives for an instruction with no recorded claim | 422; no record is written | MSG-GEN-001 | TC-S9-E7017-APP-01 |
| X9 | A statement reaches a `v_ace_*` view, an `rwb_asset` row or another schema | The grant refuses it and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | TC-S9-E7017-APP-03, BR6 |

X1 and X2 are the legacy exception flows of FSD S9 A2.14.4.3; X3 to X9 are the paths the portal writes, the workflow approval and the schema boundary add.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Day 1 against RWB-S9-E7017-CON, the record library and the composite-route fake, on its own schema, with no live S5 or P4 |
| Negotiable | The activity names, the claim's internal shape and the screen fragment are this story's design; the criterion, the base, the rights, the element flags and the screens are fixed |
| Valuable | An extra cost on a held asset is recorded once and approved or refused with a record that can be defended |
| Estimable | Two writes, one transaction, one check, one approval step, one event and two screen fragments |
| Small | Two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each path runs on a synthetic instruction, with the record library forced to fail and to pass |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Manage extra costs and services on an asset

  Scenario: AC2 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E7-017 AC2)
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns a stopped decision record
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

AC2 is the legacy criterion word for word, with its origin tag added and nothing else changed: "the decision log cannot be written", "the action is taken", "nothing changes" and MSG-P7-003 all stand. Its cross-service part is the decision record, so AC2 carries the one `Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns a stopped decision record` line and that is the only addition. AC1, the recording and approval of the additional cost, is owned by RWB-ITG-E7017-ITG; the component behaviour behind it is proved by TC-E7-017-01, so no criterion is restated.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The claim is a result on `partner_instruction`: `result_code` and `fee_amount` hold it, the evidence goes to rwb-document, and no cost table and no column is added | DF-PRT-015, DF-PRT-016; GAP-3133; ASM-5483 |
| BR2 | The decision record is written before any row moves; a failed write leaves claim, status and invoice as they were and answers MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; R-UNI-39; AC2 |
| BR3 | A claim is recorded once per instruction: the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the 409 on a repeat and one EV-21 publication per claim | TSD S9 T-A.2; X3, X6 |
| BR4 | The fee is checked against the fee schedule version in force and the recorded result; both are read with their version and neither is computed here | REQ-S9-004; BR-S9-014; ASM-5489 |
| BR5 | The approval and the refusal move only `status` within LOV-INSTR-STATUS: `DONE` on approval, `IN_PROGRESS` on refusal; no new state and no new list value | TSD S9 T3.2; ASM-5485 |
| BR6 | The asset, its holding cost and the work order stay with rwb-asset; no `v_ace_*` view, no `rwb_asset` row and no foreign key leaves `rwb_partner` | DP-01, DP-05; ASM-5486 |
| BR7 | No value a business person may change is written in code: the cost type, the schedule, the approval limit and the coded refusal reason are reference data or rule rows read with their version | BR-S9-014; FSD S9 A2.14.3.1 |
| BR8 | The scope of every read and write is the firm of the caller's `partner_user` row; a parameter never widens it | TSD S9 T6.2; X4 |
| BR9 | No personal data in a row, a file, a log or a workflow input: an instruction, a case reference, a code, an amount and a date | Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17); TSD S9 T6.2 |
| BR10 | One base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service, and the claim announces on the service's own pair only | DP-13, DP-14; Template and Rules §R4; ASM-5488 |

Lists this story reads, copied from TSD S9 T3.2 and published unchanged:

| List | Values | Use here |
|---|---|---|
| LOV-INSTR-STATUS | `SENT`, `ACCEPTED`, `DECLINED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `DONE`, `RECALLED` | The status a claim and an approval move, and the one it refuses (X6) |
| LOV-INSTRUCTION | `COLLECT`, `FILE_SUIT`, `ENFORCE`, `APPRAISE`, `REPOSSESS`, `LIST`, `SELL` | The type of the instruction the cost is claimed against |
| LOV-PANEL | `ACTIVE`, `ON_NOTICE`, `SUSPENDED`, `EXITED` | Read to refuse a claim from a firm that has left the panel |
| LOV-PARTNER-TYPE | `AGENCY`, `LAW_FIRM`, `VALUER`, `AUCTION_VENDOR`, `BROKER`, `DEBT_BUYER`, `AMC`, `RAMC` | Read only, to show the firm that claims the cost |

##### 9. State transitions

| From (`status`) | Event | Condition | To | Written by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SENT`, `ACCEPTED` | A cost claim recorded | The claim and its evidence are valid and the record is written | `IN_PROGRESS` | rwb-partner, this story |
| `IN_PROGRESS` | The approval | The claim is inside the fee schedule version and the result is recorded | `DONE`, invoice released | rwb-partner, this story |
| `IN_PROGRESS` | The refusal | The claim is outside the schedule or the result is missing | `IN_PROGRESS`, invoice blocked | rwb-partner, this story |
| `DONE`, `RECALLED` | A further claim | Any | Unchanged; 409 | none (X6) |
| `SENT`, `ACCEPTED`, `IN_PROGRESS` | A recall of the partner | R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-30 | `RECALLED` | the recall stories of the module |

| Invoice | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Submitted | The approval of its claim | The claim is approved | Released for payment against `fee_amount` |
| Submitted | The refusal of its claim | The claim is refused | Blocked; the refusal stands on the record |
| Submitted | A forced record failure | The record cannot be written | Submitted, unchanged (X1) |

The states are the lists of TSD S9 T3.2 and this story adds none; a claim whose status no source names sits at `IN_PROGRESS`, which is the only value the list offers (ASM-5485).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-AGENCYMG, partner and agency manager | CRUDA: the primary role of FSD S9 A2.14.3.3, approving and refusing a claim |
| RW-NPAMGR, NPA and asset manager | CRU: the also-uses role of FSD S9 A2.14.3.3, reading the claim against the asset |
| RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-SALEOFF, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-GUARANT | CRU: record and approve where their rights allow; they are among the holders of U in the legacy table |
| RW-HEADLIT, RW-HEADNPA, RW-HEADASL | RA: read the claim and the record |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-LEGAL, RW-CONDUCT, RW-CAPACITY, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE | R: read only, refused the approval |
| PT-AGENCY, PT-LAWFIRM, PT-VALUER, PT-AUCTION, PT-BUYER, PT-RAMC | RU: partner users, scoped to their firm, recording the claim and refused the approval |
| rwb-partner service identity | Writes the claim row, the record and the outbox row, serves the operations and sends the approval signal; no grant on another schema and no `v_ace_*` grant |

The rights are the rows of TSD S9 T6.1 and nothing wider: the legacy table names eight roles and "21 more", and T6.1 resolves them to the 23 `RW-*` and 6 `PT-*` identities above, which are 29 and agree with the legacy count. DP-08 is not in the pattern set: the right is enforced by the platform guard (ASM-5487).

| BR Field ID | Entity (owner) | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-PRT-008, DF-PRT-009, DF-PRT-010 | partner_instruction (S9, `rwb_partner`) | id, case_id, partner_id | Read; `case_id` is a reference carried into EV-21, never a foreign key across schemas |
| DF-PRT-011 to DF-PRT-013 | partner_instruction (S9, `rwb_partner`) | instruction_type, instructed_at, due_at | Read only, shown on SCR-35 |
| DF-PRT-014 | partner_instruction (S9, `rwb_partner`) | status | Write, `IN_PROGRESS` and `DONE` over LOV-INSTR-STATUS |
| DF-PRT-015 | partner_instruction (S9, `rwb_partner`) | result_code | Write, the code of the claim or of the refusal |
| DF-PRT-016 | partner_instruction (S9, `rwb_partner`) | fee_amount | Write, the amount claimed and released |
| DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | id, partner_code, partner_name, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end, score | Read only, to scope the claim and refuse a firm at `EXITED` |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (PLT library, in `rwb_partner`) | decision code, rule id, rule version, inputs, from and to state, decided at | Write through the library, before the row moves |

**No new table, no new column and no migration** is declared: the claim rides on `partner_instruction`, the record, the key and the outbox are library objects created in `rwb_partner` by the library's migration (DP-03), and the evidence file is rwb-document's.

**No personal data.** The claim carries an instruction, a case reference, a code, an amount, a date and a file reference. No customer name, contact value or identity number is read into a row, an answer, a log or a workflow input, and every fixture is synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-partner (S9); base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the two writes the claim is made and paid by.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results` (API-S9-005) | Multipart `result` and `files` in, `PartnerInstruction` out with `resultCode`, `feeAmount`, `status` | Partner portal, right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` |
| POST | `/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/invoices` (API-S9-006) | `InvoiceRequest` in, `Invoice` out | Partner portal, right C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` |

API-S9-005 answers 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409, 415, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503; API-S9-006 answers 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503. Both sets are TSD S9 T-A.2's and neither is widened. No operation approves or refuses a claim: the service has six and none does, so the approval is a signal on `InstructionWorkflow` (§12.5) and not a route (GAP-3133; ASM-5484).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The right is enforced by the platform guard and the asset reaches SCR-35 through rwb-asset's own fragment, so no consumed operation, no read of `rwb-asset` and no read of `rwb-source-data` is declared; the plan's contract-dependency row is empty (ASM-5486, ASM-5487).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Name | Payload | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| EV-21 `PartnerResultSubmitted` | `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` | `caseId`, `instructionId`, `resultCode`, `resultedAt` | The case-owning service, rwb-litigation, rwb-asset and rwb-reporting |
| `DecisionRecorded` (library) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | The record reference, the decision code, the rule id and its version | rwb-decision, which seals it in the central ledger |

Both go through the outbox, the CloudEvents envelope and the retry and `.dlt` topics (DP-09). EV-21 is published once per recorded claim; the decision record is the library's publication (DP-03). EV-20 `InstructionIssued` is not on this path, and nothing announces an approval, a refusal or an invoice (GAP-3133; ASM-5488).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The claim is made by a person or a partner on the portal and the approval is a signal on this service's own workflow, so the story holds no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox row. FSD S9 A2.14.4.4 declares no background event for the feature.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `InstructionWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per instruction | `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Signal `costApproval` (approve or refuse, the claim reference, the reason) |
| `recordCostClaim` | Activity | `rwb-partner` | The claim in; the instruction with `resultCode`, `feeAmount` and `status` out, record first |
| `writeCostDecisionRecord` | Activity | `rwb-partner` | The claim and the rule version in; the record reference out |
| `approveCostInvoice` | Activity | `rwb-partner` | The instruction and the approval in; the invoice released or blocked, and the status out |

`InstructionWorkflow` is the one workflow in the ownership rows; this story adds the `costApproval` signal and its activities and creates no second workflow, no Schedule and no child of `CaseWorkflow`, which stays with rwb-case (ASM-5484).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The service's job list is empty in the ownership rows (Jobs: None) and the claim is event-driven on the workflow, so no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row and no shared job table is declared (ADR-016).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| partner_instruction | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The claim and its approval; this story writes `result_code`, `fee_amount` and `status` |
| partner | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The firm and its panel status; read only here |
| partner_user | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The caller's firm and period; read only here, to scope the claim |
| decision_record | PLT library, in `rwb_partner` | The local hash-linked record of the claim and the approval (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, in `rwb_partner` | The key and the stored answer of the two writes |
| outbox_event | PLT library, in `rwb_partner` | The relay row of EV-21, one per recorded claim |

Not owned and never read as a table: the asset record and `v_ace_npa_asset` (S5, P1), `recovery_case` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `payment` (P8). No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01), and the claim has no table of its own (GAP-3133; ASM-5483).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Decision-record library stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and outbox, and a stopped chain | AC2, X1 |
| Partner-portal right and identity fake | Right R, C and U per operation, and a caller of one firm | X2, X4 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake (SCR-35, SCR-34) | The claim, the instruction and the asset fragment of the caller's firm, before and after an approval | §15, TC-S9-E7017-APP-01 |
| Instruction and cost fixture | One instruction of a type from LOV-INSTRUCTION with a claim, its amount and its evidence | TC-E7-017-01 |
| rwb-document upload stub (P5) | A stored document reference, and a 415 for a type outside the allowed set | X5 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT; RWB-ITG-E7017-ITG swaps them for the owners and asserts the same paths end to end.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 0 consumed | API-S9-005 and API-S9-006 on `/api/recovery/partner/v1`; the guard and the asset fragment are not contract rows of this key |
| Kafka | 1 published + the library's record event, 0 consumed | `rwb.partner.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, and `rwb.decision-record.v1` from the library |
| Temporal | 1 workflow signal, 3 activities, 0 Schedules | `InstructionWorkflow` with `costApproval`, `recordCostClaim`, `writeCostDecisionRecord`, `approveCostInvoice` |
| File | The result file and the invoice attachment | Uploaded to rwb-document through its owner; the service keeps the reference, never the bytes |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner`, module `cost`; front end `src/modules/recovery/partner/PlacementAllocation.tsx`.

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is applied as a prohibition: the legacy data section reads `v_ace_npa_asset`, and after the split that view and the asset record are rwb-asset's, so this service holds no `AceSourceQuery` and no grant and the asset reference arrives as an identifier (ASM-5486). DP-13 gives the two writes their base and DP-19 is how SCR-35 and SCR-34 reach this service. DP-09, which the outbox carries, DP-04, which a fee rule would need, and DP-08, which the rights carry, are not in the pattern set: the outbox follows the platform library, the fee is a reference-data comparison and not a Drools decision, and the right is enforced by the guard (GAP-3133; ASM-5487, ASM-5489).

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `CostClaimController` | Controller | Serves API-S9-005 and API-S9-006, maps the error envelope, enforces the `Idempotency-Key` |
| `CostClaimService` | Service | Validates the claim, checks it against the schedule version and the result, decides the approval path |
| `CostDecisionRecordWriter` | Service | Writes the record before a row moves, through the library (DP-03) |
| `CostClaimRepository` | Repository | The two transactions on `partner_instruction` and the read of the caller's firm |
| `CostApprovalSignal` | Workflow client | Sends `costApproval` to `InstructionWorkflow` and reports the outcome |
| `PlacementAllocation` | React component | SCR-35 with the claim, its evidence, the schedule version and the asset fragment |

**Database and migrations.** No Flyway file: the columns are those of `partner_instruction` and `partner`, and the record, the key and the outbox are library objects created in `rwb_partner` (DP-03).

**Configuration.** The cost type, the fee schedule, the approval limit and the coded refusal reason are reference data with their version (BR7); the capability area "Partner portal" and its rights are access rows; the retry and timeout of the two writes are platform configuration.

**Build steps**

1. `CostClaimController` and the two writes against the fakes, record first, with the error envelope (AC2, X1).
2. `recordCostClaim` as one transaction over `result_code`, `fee_amount` and `status`, with the repeat refused at 409 (X3, X6).
3. The fee check against the schedule version and the recorded result, and the approval and refusal paths (TC-S9-E7017-APP-01, X7, X8).
4. The `costApproval` signal with its idempotent repeat, and `approveCostInvoice` releasing or blocking the invoice.
5. The outbox publication of EV-21 once per claim, with its envelope and its `.dlt` path (BR3).
6. `PlacementAllocation` through the composite route fake, with the asset fragment and the states of §15.
7. The boundary test: no statement outside `rwb_partner`, no `v_ace_*` read, no asset row, no case write, no approval route (X9, BR6).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.partner.cost-claim-v1`; off means the two writes answer 503, the approvals wait and no row moves.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, a claim is recorded once with one EV-21, an approved claim releases its invoice at `DONE` and a refused one keeps it blocked, a forced record failure leaves the row unchanged with MSG-P7-003, a caller of another firm sees 404, no `v_ace_*` read and no asset write exists, and SCR-35 answers through the composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of the claim is absent or invalid, or an approval arrives with no claim (VR-S9-014-1; X8) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the partner-portal right of the operation (X2) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the claim or the approval moves a row (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The three IDs are those of the legacy and FSD sets; the text is copied unchanged, no message is reworded and no new one is added. MSG-GEN-001 is VR-S9-014-1, MSG-P4-002 is the legacy refusal, and MSG-P7-003 is AC-EXC-S9-014-02 of FSD S9 A2.14.4.3 and the text of AC2.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-35 Placement and allocation is where the cost is recorded and approved and SCR-34 Partner list is where the firm and its panel status are read (FSD S9 Screens; legacy table: both "Loading; list"). Both arrive through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and a partner outside the bank arrives on the partner gateway of FAPI 2.0 (Arch v5 slide 8; INT-24).

| State on SCR-35 | What it shows | Act available |
|---|---|---|
| Loading | The instruction, its claim and the asset fragment being composed | None |
| Claim recorded | The amount, the evidence, the schedule version and an `IN_PROGRESS` instruction | Approve, refuse |
| Approved | The instruction at `DONE` and the invoice released | Read the record |
| Refused | The instruction at `IN_PROGRESS`, the invoice blocked, the coded reason | Re-claim once the cause is fixed |
| Not recorded | The claim unchanged, MSG-P7-003 shown (AC2) | Retry |

The screen field lists and the asset fragment belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and to rwb-asset's screens; the legacy table gives both screens "Loading; list" and no further state, so the refusal reason is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3133; ASM-5485).

| TC-E7-017-02 | AC2 | Component | The record stub stopped; the claim unchanged, no outbox row, MSG-P7-003 |

The four legacy cases are those of RWB-E7-017 in their legacy order, with the Level column added: every case runs on the fakes and against this service's own rows, so every case is `Component`. TC-E7-017-01 exercises AC1, which RWB-ITG-E7017-ITG owns and proves end to end; its `-ITG` copy stays with that story and is not repeated here. The three cases `TC-S9-E7017-APP-01` to `-03` are new. The full test is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the cost type, the fee schedule, the approval limit, the refusal reason, the states and the right stay reference data and rule rows.
- No personal data in a row, a file, a workflow input or a log: an instruction, a case reference, a code, an amount and a date only.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views, and this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant at all (DP-05).
- The asset stays with rwb-asset and the case with rwb-case: no asset row and no case row is written here (BR6).
- The record is written before the rows and before the release; a build that answers outside its transaction fails the review (BR2).
- One base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service (DP-13, DP-14).
- A claim is a fact announced once; a second publication or a new approval event fails the absence test (BR3, BR10).
