**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E4-042 for rwb-comms. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **compliance and PDPA officer (RW-COMPLY)**, I want **the Workbench to check, when a case of rwb-comms closes, that every notice document of that case carries a retention class on the contract of the document hub, to record the coverage as a decision under the rule version in force, and, where a class is missing, to hold the closure and ask for the Document Hub task**, so that **a case never closes with a notice that has no retention class, and the class, its period and the disposal of the record stay the reference data of their owner and are never set by the communications service**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A case that closes with a document that has no retention class cannot be disposed of or extended on the record, and a disposal that is not a recorded decision is the defect that REQ-DCM-019 and NFR-074 exist to prevent. The closure rules already state the gate: R-WO-47 closes the case when the retention timer expires and every document carries a retention class, and R-WO-48 holds the closure and raises a Document Hub task with five working days for a document with no class. The retention classes themselves are defined per document type with the periods not set (NFR-028, DL26), and the class, its period, the disposal or extension decision and the JOB-17 retention run all belong to rwb-document (Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 44; Ownership Map: `retention_rule`, `retention_action`, `document`, `document_type`, `case_document_check` all P5).

The communications service is therefore not the owner of retention: it is the owner of the notice, and the notice is what points at a document (`notice.document_id`, DF-LEG-017). This story is that slice. On the closure fact it reads the retention class of every notice document through the P5 contract, records the coverage through the local decision-record library with decision code D9 and rule R-WO-47 or R-WO-48 and the rule version in force, asks rwb-case for the hold and the Document Hub task where a class is absent, and serves the coverage on its own read so that the officer and the auditor can see it. It sets no class, holds no period, disposes of nothing and schedules nothing.

The legacy story is a thin auto-generated entry: module P6, FEAT-COM-08, depends FEAT-DCM-17, screen SCR-33, two criteria and four test cases. The decoupling of the target is the one this story applies: the notice rows are `rwb_comms` rows (DP-01); the coverage decision goes through the local library and the shared topic (DP-03); the base is `/api/recovery/comms/v1` (DP-13); and the coverage reaches the case record through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). DP-10 is deliberately absent: the trigger is the consumed `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` event and not a Temporal Schedule, and the only retention run in the catalogue is JOB-17, a Schedule of rwb-document. It serves REQ-DCM-010 and the closure gate portion of REQ-DCM-019, and it gives the FSD P6 A2.21 measure "notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent" its compliance-side evidence at closure.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P6-E4042-CON is published: the coverage read on base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, the consumed event element, the class-present vocabulary, the case-hold fact, the nine contract tables and the fakes, so this story builds against a fixed contract on Day 1.
- The `rwb_comms` baseline is in place from RWB-P6-E1046-APP and RWB-P6-E1052-APP: `notice`, `template`, `merge_field` and the per-service Flyway sequence exist, and `notice` carries `id`, `case_id`, `document_id` and `notice_type` (DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-018).
- The decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` are live with RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (DP-03), and a failed write blocks the step (Principle 5, R-UNI-39).
- The gateway-bff composite route is live with RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19) for the case record documents panel that shows the coverage.
- The rwb-document contract publishes a read of the retention class of a document. No such operation is named in any source and the plan declares no C row on a P5 contract for this key: the class, its list and the per-type mapping are P5 reference data and the read is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1141; ASM-2088). The story is built against the rwb-document fake until that row exists.
- The rwb-case contract accepts the closing fact, the hold of the closure and the Document Hub task with the reason code RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING of R-WO-48. The operation, its body and the message a missing class shows are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1143; ASM-2090).
- The closing state of a case is `CASE_CLOSED` as R-WO-47 names it; the other states that mean a case closes are the vocabulary of rwb-case and are read as data of their owner (GAP-1145; ASM-2092).
- The retention class list, the class per document type and the periods are unset in the sources (NFR-028, DL26) and are not this service's data; this story only needs presence or absence of a class per notice document (GAP-1144; ASM-2091).
- No build dependency outside rwb-comms and the platform contracts: the H rows of the metadata table are the contract baseline of this key and two platform contract stories, and the story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-case closes a case under R-WO-47 and publishes `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` with `caseId`, `fromState`, `toState` `CASE_CLOSED` and `changedAt`.
2. The event listener of this service dedupes the delivery by the CloudEvents id and starts the coverage check for the case.
3. The check reads the notice rows of the case (`id`, `case_id`, `document_id`, `notice_type`) from `rwb_comms`, and for each notice with a `document_id` it reads the retention class of that document on the rwb-document contract, one hop, one document at a time, with no table read of `rwb_document`.
4. If every notice document answers a class, the check records one decision through the local decision-record library: decision code D9, rule R-WO-47, the rule version in force, the case, the number of notice documents checked, and the result COVERED. The case is not held and needs nothing from this service.
5. If at least one notice document answers no class, the check records the decision with decision code D9, rule R-WO-48 and the same rule version, naming the notice and the document with no class, and sends one fact to rwb-case with the reason code RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING: closure is held and the Document Hub task with its five working days is raised by rwb-case, which owns the task and the timer (R-WO-48).
6. If the decision record cannot be written, nothing proceeds: no hold is asked, the case fact is not sent, the check is failed and an incident is raised under R-UNI-39, and the answer to the officer and the run record show MSG-P7-003.
7. An officer or an auditor reads the coverage with `GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/retention-coverage` and the case record documents panel shows, for every notice document of the case, its notice type, its document reference and whether a class is present. The read computes the coverage on the contract of the owner at the moment it is called; it never returns a class value it did not receive from rwb-document.
8. When a later `CaseStateChanged` for the same case arrives and every notice document now answers a class, the check records the covered decision under R-WO-47 again; the earlier missing-class decision and its hold remain in the decision history, and no decision is overwritten.
9. A read of a case outside the caller's scope answers 404, and a read by a role without the Documents right answers 403 with MSG-P4-002.
10. A delivery of the same event with the same CloudEvents id is ignored, and a second run for the same case and the same closing state writes no second decision for the same document set.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A notice document of the closing case answers no retention class | Closure held; one decision under R-WO-48; the case fact with RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING is sent and rwb-case raises the Document Hub task | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1143; ASM-2090) | AC1 |
| X2 | The rwb-document contract does not answer inside its budget, or answers an error | No class is assumed present and no covered decision is written; the check fails and is retried on the next delivery and the next closure event | None | AC1 |
| X3 | The decision record cannot be written | Nothing changes: no hold is asked, the fact is not sent, the incident is raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC2 |
| X4 | The closing case has no notice document | The coverage is an empty list and the decision records the case with no notice document; no hold is asked | None | AC1 |
| X5 | The same event is delivered twice, or the same case and closing state are checked twice | The second delivery is ignored by the CloudEvents id and no second decision is written for the same document set | None | AC1 |
| X6 | The caller holds no Documents right | Refused, nothing is returned | MSG-P4-002 | AC1 |
| X7 | The case is outside the caller's scope | Not found | The scope refusal envelope of the gateway-bff route | AC1 |

X2, X6 and X7 are the refusals of the read and of the check; they carry no new business rule. X1 is the only outcome of this story that asks another service to act.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P6-E4042-CON and the two platform contracts only; the document class read, the case fact and the decision library are fakes from the first run |
| Negotiable | The closing state, the class list, the class per document type and the five working days of the task are data of their owners; the story fixes the order of the check, the decision code D9 and the class-present vocabulary |
| Valuable | A case cannot close with a notice document that has no retention class, and the coverage is a recorded decision with its rule version |
| Estimable | One read, one event listener, one coverage service, two adapters and one decision path |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests, as the app slice of a thin legacy key |
| Testable | Each criterion of section 7 runs against the fakes; the coverage read is asserted field by field |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Apply retention on case closure — the rwb-comms slice

  Background:
    Given the closing state of a case is "CASE_CLOSED"
    Given case "RC-2026-000412" has notice "N-0101" with document "DOC-0101" and notice "N-0102" with document "DOC-0102"

  Scenario: AC1 Apply retention on case closure (legacy RWB-E4-042 AC1)
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns case "RC-2026-000412" closing with toState "CASE_CLOSED" and accepts the fact with reason "RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING"
    Given the rwb-document contract mock returns a retention class for document "DOC-0101" and a retention class for document "DOC-0102"
    When its trigger arrives
    Then applies the retention class to every document on the case when the case closes
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E4-042 AC2)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The two criteria above are the criteria of RWB-E4-042 copied line for line, with the origin tag on each scenario line and one mock line for each fact of another owner that the criterion names: the closure and the case fact on the rwb-case contract, and the retention class on the rwb-document contract. No legacy line and no legacy value is dropped. The target reading of "applies the retention class" is the one section 8 fixes in BR1 to BR5: the class and its period are P5 reference data, so this service checks that the class is present on every notice document and records the coverage; it never sets, changes or holds a class. The legacy gherkin uses no path, so no path of the legacy story is carried here and the base of this service is `/api/recovery/comms/v1` (DP-13).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A case closes when the retention timer expires and no placement, sale or exception is open and a retention class is on every document; the closing state is `CASE_CLOSED` | R-WO-47 |
| BR2 | A document on the case with no retention class holds the closure and raises a Document Hub task with five working days | R-WO-48 |
| BR3 | Every document carries a retention class, and the class sets how long the document is kept; the classes are defined per document type and the periods are not set | REQ-DCM-010; NFR-028; DL26 |
| BR4 | Retention runs by class, and a document at the end of its period is disposed of or extended by a recorded decision and never silently; the disposal or extension decision is P5's | REQ-DCM-019; NFR-074 |
| BR5 | The retention class, its list, the class per document type and the period are reference data of rwb-document; this service reads the class and never sets, defaults, maps or validates it | NFR-028; Ownership Map (`retention_rule`, `retention_action` P5); Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR6 | A legal hold overrides the retention class and stops every automated decision; a case under a hold is not presented for closure by rwb-case, and this service reads no hold of its own | REQ-DCM-016; R-UNI-20 |
| BR7 | The coverage is recorded through the local decision-record library with decision code D9, rule R-WO-47 or R-WO-48 and the rule version in force; a write that fails blocks the step and raises an incident | Principle 5; DP-03; R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | The notice rows are `rwb_comms` rows; `retention_rule`, `retention_action`, `document`, `document_type` and `case_document_check` are P5's and are read on the owner's contract, never as tables | DP-01; Ownership Map |
| BR9 | The trigger is the consumed `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1`; this story declares no workflow and no Schedule, and the only retention run is JOB-17 of rwb-document | Architecture v5 slides 42 and 44; Template and Rules §R5.5 (DP-10 not applied) |
| BR10 | The hold of the closure and the Document Hub task are rwb-case's; this service sends the fact with the reason code `RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING` and owns neither the task nor its timer | R-WO-48; Ownership Map (`task`, `timer` P3) |
| BR11 | The coverage reaches the case record documents panel through the gateway-bff composite route; this service serves the read and the panel belongs to its owner | DP-19; Template and Rules §R7.2 s15 |
| BR12 | No value a business person may change is written in code: the closing state, the class list and the task timer are data of their owners, read with the version in force | FSD P6 A2.21 BR-P6-021 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not checked | `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` with `toState` `CASE_CLOSED` for the case | The event is new and the case has notice rows | Checking |
| Checking | The rwb-document contract answers a class for every notice document | At least one notice document, or none to check | Covered: one decision under R-WO-47, no hold |
| Checking | The rwb-document contract answers no class for at least one notice document | R-WO-48 | Class missing: one decision under R-WO-48, the hold and the Document Hub task are asked of rwb-case |
| Checking | The decision record cannot be written | R-UNI-39 | Not checked: nothing is held and the incident is raised |
| Class missing | A later closure event for the case arrives and every notice document now answers a class | P5 applied the class | Covered: a new decision under R-WO-47; the earlier decision stays in the history |

The case state (RETENTION_RUNNING to CASE_CLOSED) is rwb-case's under R-WO-47 and is not state of this service; the four states above are states of the coverage check of one case and are recorded in the decision history, not in a table of the service. A notice with no `document_id` has no document to check and enters the coverage list as absent with no class, so that the panel never hides a notice.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-COMPLY, Compliance and PDPA officer | Documents RU in the matrix of TSD P6 T6.1: reads the coverage of a case and its decisions |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Documents CRUA in TSD P6 T6.1: reads the coverage of the notices he owns |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Documents CRUA in TSD P6 T6.1: reads the coverage for a legal or an audit answer |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Documents R in TSD P6 T6.1: reads the coverage and its decisions |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Documents R in TSD P6 T6.1: reads the coverage and operates the check through the run records |
| rwb-comms service identity | Consumes the event, reads its own `notice` rows, calls the two consumed rows and writes the local decision record (DP-02) |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the coverage decision and relays it on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) |

The FSD A2.21 names the primary actor as "None; runs unattended" and the Compliance and PDPA officer as the second actor; the matrix above is the only source used for the rights, and the capability area of the read is fixed by RWB-P6-E4042-CON (GAP-1142; ASM-2089). The authorise contract of rwb-access (DP-08) is not in this story's pattern set: the capability area and the right of the read are declared in the contract story and enforced at gateway-bff.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-LEG-015 | `notice` in `rwb_comms` | id | Read, as the entry key of the coverage |
| DF-LEG-016 | `notice` in `rwb_comms` | case_id | Read, as the selection of the case |
| DF-LEG-017 | `notice` in `rwb_comms` | document_id | Read, as the document whose class is checked |
| DF-LEG-018 | `notice` in `rwb_comms` | notice_type | Read, for the coverage entry |
| DF-LEG-021, DF-LEG-022 | `notice` in `rwb_comms` | callback_date, delivery_status | Read only, to show a delivered notice beside its coverage; never written here |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local, through the library) | decision code D9, rule R-WO-47 or R-WO-48, rule version, case, notice, decided at, hash chain | Write |
| DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-011 | `document`, through the rwb-document contract | id, document_type, the retention class and its presence | Read through the contract, never a table |
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | `recovery_case`, through the rwb-case contract | id, status and the closing state | Read through the contract, never a table |
| The retention class and its period | `retention_rule`, `retention_action`, owned by P5 rwb-document | class code and period | Not read and not written: the class fact arrives on the owner's contract and this service stores neither |

No column is added to `rwb_comms` by this story and no table is created: the coverage of a case is a projection of its `notice` rows and of the class fact of the owner's contract at the moment of the read, and its result is the decision record. The read uses the index `ix_notice_case_id` on `notice (case_id)` of RWB-P6-E2021-APP, so no migration is needed (DP-15, ADR-021). No personal data is written or returned: the coverage carries notice IDs, a case ID, document IDs, a notice type and a boolean, and no name, address, identity number or account number. Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-comms (P6); base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`. The shape is the one fixed in RWB-P6-E4042-CON; this story implements it and adds no path.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/retention-coverage` | Read the retention coverage of the notice documents of a case: one entry per notice document with `noticeId`, `caseId`, `documentId`, `noticeType` and `classPresent`, 200 | Documents, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The operation is fixed by this baseline because no source names a retention operation of this service: the TSD P6 endpoint inventory stops at API-P6-011 and carries no retention path, and the legacy story names only the notice request and the notice read (GAP-1142; ASM-2089). Errors: 401 no session; 403 the role lacks the Documents right (MSG-P4-002); 404 the case is absent or out of scope; 503 the class read of the owner is unavailable. The exact field types and the page shape are fixed in the contract story and are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1142; ASM-2089).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | the retention class read of a document on the rwb-document contract | P5 rwb-document | The class present or absent for each notice document of the case; faked. The plan declares no C row for this contract and no P5 operation names the class read, so the path is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1141; ASM-2088) |
| POST | the case fact that holds the closure and asks for the Document Hub task with reason `RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING` | P3 rwb-case | The hold and the task of R-WO-48, which rwb-case owns; faked. The operation, its body and the message of a missing class are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1143; ASM-2090) |

Each row is one hop on the owner's published contract, read or written inside the same step that writes the decision, and a missing or late answer never counts as a class present. No row reads a table and no row reads a view of another service (DP-01).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The event catalogue carries no retention event and this service announces no retention action of its own; the decision record is relayed on the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1` by the local library (DP-03), and JOB-17 and any retention outcome remain rwb-document's (Architecture v5 slide 44).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | What this story does with it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (EV-05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | The trigger of the check: `caseId`, `fromState`, `toState`, `changedAt`; a `toState` equal to the closing state `CASE_CLOSED` starts the coverage check of that case. Deduped by the CloudEvents id. The event catalogue names rwb-comms as a consumer of EV-05 |

The event carries IDs, state codes and a timestamp only. This story reads no other event and no event of this story is published to keep the local picture current: the coverage is computed from the live answers of its owners at the moment it is asked.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The trigger is the consumed event and the check is one listener step in this service; no workflow, no activity and no Temporal element is declared, because DP-10 is not in the pattern set of this legacy key and the only retention run of the catalogue is JOB-17, a Schedule of rwb-document.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The retention run is JOB-17 of rwb-document on its own Schedule (Architecture v5 slides 16 and 44; Ownership Map: JOB-17 owner P5), and this story neither registers a Schedule nor reads a job table.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| notice | P6 (rwb_comms) | Read for the notice documents of the case; written by RWB-P6-E1052-APP and RWB-P6-E2021-APP |
| template, merge_field | P6 (rwb_comms) | Read only, for the notice type and the template provenance of a coverage entry |
| decision record (local) | P6 rows in `rwb_comms`, written through the P7 library | The coverage decisions of this story (DP-03) |

Not owned and never read: `retention_rule`, `retention_action`, `document`, `document_type` and `case_document_check` (P5), `recovery_case`, `task` and `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry` (P7), `interaction` (P1), `outbound_item` and `interface_config` (P2). No table of this service carries a retention class, a period or a disposal, and no foreign key crosses a service boundary (DP-01, BR5).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Documented answers used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-document fake | The retention class read | A class for `DOC-0101` and `DOC-0102`; no class for `DOC-0102`; a document absent; an answer beyond the budget; the answer is derived from the published document and carries the placeholder of the class list (GAP-1141; ASM-2088) |
| rwb-case fake | The closing event and the hold with the Document Hub task | `CaseStateChanged` with `toState` `CASE_CLOSED` for `RC-2026-000412`; a repeat delivery with the same CloudEvents id; an accepted fact with reason `RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING`; a refused fact; a case with no notice document |
| Decision-record library stub | The coverage decision | A healthy chain and outbox; a stopped chain for AC2 and TC-E4-042-02 |

The fakes are derived from RWB-P6-E4042-CON, and the drift test of that story fails a build in which a fake and the document disagree.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 provided, 2 consumed | The coverage read provided; the class read of P5 and the case fact of P3 consumed; one hop each |
| Kafka | None published, 1 consumed | `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` consumed as the trigger |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity, no Schedule: the trigger is the event |
| File | None | This story reads and writes no file |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms`, module `retention`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms.retention`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 is applied as a prohibition and adds no dependency: this service reads no `rwb_document` table, and the class arrives on the owner's contract (BR8). DP-10 is not applied: the trigger is the consumed event, there is no Schedule and no Quartz row, and JOB-17 stays rwb-document's.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RetentionCoverageController | Controller | `GET /cases/{caseId}/retention-coverage` with the Documents right, the scope test and the problem mapping for 401, 403, 404 and 503 |
| CaseStateListener | Listener | Consumes `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1`, dedupes by the CloudEvents id, filters on the closing state and starts the check |
| RetentionCoverageService | Service | Builds the coverage of a case from its `notice` rows plus the class fact of the owner, one document at a time, and answers present or absent per entry |
| ClosureCheck | Service | The ordered step of section 4: coverage, decision, case fact; fails closed on any missing answer |
| DocumentRetentionClient | Adapter | The retention class read on the rwb-document contract, one hop, with a breaker and no default class |
| CaseFactClient | Adapter | The hold of the closure and the Document Hub task with reason `RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING` on the rwb-case contract |
| CoverageDecision | Service | Writes the local decision record with decision code D9, the rule and its version through the library |

**Database and migrations**

- Reads `notice`, `template` and `merge_field`; writes the local decision record; all in schema `rwb_comms`. No table and no column is added and no migration is needed; the read uses `ix_notice_case_id` of RWB-P6-E2021-APP.
- No retention class, period or disposal is stored in `rwb_comms`, and no copy of `retention_rule` or `retention_action` is created (BR5).

**Configuration and reference data**

- The closing state of a case is `CASE_CLOSED` as R-WO-47 names it, held as a parameter and never in code; the other closing states are the vocabulary of rwb-case and are read as data of their owner (GAP-1145; ASM-2092).
- The reason code of the missing class is `RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING` of R-WO-48, and the five working days of the Document Hub task are the timer of rwb-case, not a value of this service.
- The retention classes and the periods are not configured here at all: they are P5 reference data and unset in the sources (NFR-028, DL26; GAP-1144; ASM-2091).
- The feature switch `rwb.comms.retention-closure-check`, read as a parameter: when it is off the check writes no decision and holds the closure, because a class is never assumed present.

**Build steps**

1. RetentionCoverageController and CaseStateListener over the one read and the one consumed event, with the dedupe and the closing-state filter; tests for the empty case and the repeat delivery.
2. DocumentRetentionClient and the coverage service: one document at a time, no default class, a failed or late answer fails the step; tests for presence, absence and an absent document.
3. CoverageDecision and the fail-closed path: a failed write leaves nothing held and raises the incident; test for AC2 and TC-E4-042-02.
4. CaseFactClient and the missing-class path with reason `RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING`, behind the fake until the rwb-case row is published.
5. The closure step of section 4 end to end against the three fakes, and the covered decision under R-WO-47 for the all-present case; test for AC1 and TC-E4-042-01.
6. The contract-fake run of the whole check before the real services are live, and the drift test of RWB-P6-E4042-CON in the pipeline.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.comms.retention-closure-check`, read as a parameter; off writes no decision and holds the closure.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P6-E4042-CON stay green, and a SIT week shows every closing case of the service with one coverage decision and its rule version, every missing class with a hold and a Document Hub task under R-WO-48, no case held without a missing class, and no retention class, period or disposal value written by this service.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record could not be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the Documents right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The message a missing class shows to the officer and the message a refused case fact returns are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1143; ASM-2090), because R-WO-48 names the hold and the task and no source names a message ID for either.

MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P4-002 are copied unchanged from the legacy story. The legacy table also carries MSG-P6-003, MSG-P6-004, MSG-P6-001 and MSG-GEN-001: those belong to the notice and dispatch capabilities of the same module (RWB-P6-E1052-APP, RWB-P6-E2021-APP) and are not used by this story. The check runs unattended, so the missing-class outcome is shown to a person only through the coverage read and through the Document Hub task of rwb-case, and both texts are fixed in the RWB-P6-E4042-CON review.

##### 15. Screens and states

The legacy story names SCR-33 Template approval, which is the template screen of the same module and does not fit an unattended retention check (GAP-1145; ASM-2092). The coverage is shown on the case record documents panel of the case record view, served through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), where each notice document of the case shows:

| Coverage state | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| Class present | The notice type, the document reference and the class the owner returned |
| Class absent | The notice type, the document reference and the fact that no class is present, with the Document Hub task of the case |
| Not checked | The case has no coverage decision yet, or the check failed; MSG-P7-003 where the decision could not be written |
| Covered after a missing class | The newer decision under R-WO-47 beside the earlier R-WO-48 decision in the case timeline |

The panel, its field list and its masking belong to the story that owns the case record view and to RWB-PLT-N001-CON; this story serves only the coverage read. SCR-44 Batch and job monitor shows nothing for this story because there is no run of this service.

##### 16. Test cases

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-E4-042-01 | AC1 | End to end | Case `RC-2026-000412` closing with `N-0101`/`DOC-0101` and `N-0102`/`DOC-0102`; the rwb-document fake answers a class for both; the decision carries D9 and R-WO-47 with its version |
| TC-E4-042-02 | AC2 | End to end | The decision chain is forced to fail; no hold is asked, no fact is sent, MSG-P7-003 and the incident of R-UNI-39 |
| TC-E4-042-03 | Access | Component | RW-COMPLY reads the coverage of a case in scope; a role without the Documents right is refused with MSG-P4-002 |

The four cases keep their legacy order, their legacy coverage and their legacy test intent; the legacy story states no level, so the levels above follow the mapping of the run (System to End to end, Access to Component, Resilience to NFR) and the Data column carries the synthetic values the tests need. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the closing state, the reason code, the task timer, the class list and the periods are data of their owners, read with the version in force; this service writes none of them in code and none of them in its schema.
- This service sets no retention class, no period and no disposal: the class, its list, the per-type mapping, `retention_rule`, `retention_action` and JOB-17 are P5 rwb-document's (BR5).
- No personal data in events, logs, workflow inputs, tests or prompts: notice IDs, case IDs, document IDs, notice types, rule IDs and timestamps only.
- No read of another service's tables and no view of this service: the class and the case state arrive on the owner's contract (DP-01).
- A class is never assumed present: a missing, refused or late answer of the owner fails the step and never produces a covered decision.
- A decision that cannot be written stops the check, holds nothing and raises the incident (Principle 5, R-UNI-39).
- The consumed event is deduped and the check is idempotent for one case and one closing state, so a repeated delivery writes no second decision for the same document set.
- One base, one topic, one queue: `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, `rwb.comms.events.v1` and `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; no other base, topic or queue is declared as this service's own (DP-13, DP-14).
- No Quartz row, no shared job table, no batch table and no second Schedule: the trigger is the event and the only retention run is JOB-17 of rwb-document.

##### 19. Out of scope

- The retention class, its list, the class per document type, the periods and the disposal or extension decision: P5 rwb-document (`retention_rule`, `retention_action`, `document_type`). This story reads the class and sets nothing.
- The retention run JOB-17 and its Schedule: rwb-document (P5), per Architecture v5 slides 16 and 44 and the Ownership Map.
- The case status, the closing state, the hold of the closure, the Document Hub task and its five working-day timer: rwb-case (P3). This story sends the fact with reason `RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING`.
- A legal hold and its block on outbound action and automated decision (R-UNI-20, REQ-DCM-016): rwb-case with rwb-document. A case under a hold is not presented for closure.

- The central decision ledger: rwb-decision (P7). This story writes the local record through the library (DP-03).

- The contract document, the coverage answer shape and the fakes as published artefacts: RWB-P6-E4042-CON.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead of rwb-payment**, I want **the published contract baseline of the settlement match — the OpenAPI 3.1 document of `/api/recovery/payment/v1` with `GET /proceeds` and `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match`, the `Proceeds`, `ProceedsPage` and `MatchRequest` elements over DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 and the lists `LOV-MATCH` and `LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC`, the three event schemas `TreatmentBooked`, `PaymentMissed` and `ProceedsMatched` on `rwb.payment.events.v1` with the CloudEvents envelope, the `proceeds` table of `rwb_payment` and its versioned baseline, the error envelope, the rights, the compatibility rule and the fakes**, so that **the app story, SCR-28 Proceeds matching and the wave 3 harness build against one fixed contract on Day 1, and a path, a field, a list value, a match state or an event name can never drift between rwb-payment, rwb-treatment, rwb-case and the screens without a failing build**.

This is the contract slice of legacy RWB-E4-043 (FEAT-PAY-03, module P8 Payments and posting). It owns the published surface only: the two operations, the three event schemas, the table baseline, the error set, the rights, the compatibility rule and the fakes. It owns no behaviour and copies no legacy criterion: the two legacy acceptance criteria of the story stay word for word with RWB-P8-E4043-APP (GAP-2510; ASM-4159).

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). In the monolith, the settlement match read `v_ace_payment`, the `treatment` row, the `recovery_case` row and the `decision_log_entry` row in one process on `/api/recovery/v1`, so no boundary existed that another team could build against; every reader of the match was also a reader of four other modules' tables. In the target each boundary is a contract: the receipt facts are rwb-source-data's, the settlement treatment is rwb-treatment's, the case is rwb-case's, the rule package is rwb-decision's and the money is rwb-payment's.

Two teams depend on this baseline on Day 1. RWB-P8-E4043-APP builds the settlement arm of JOB-07 and cannot start until the elements, the match value, the event names and the fakes are fixed. The rwb-case, rwb-asset, rwb-debtsale, rwb-writeoff and rwb-guarantee teams consume `ProceedsMatched` (Architecture v5 slide 43, row 25) and must pin a schema while their own stages are still being written. SCR-28 reaches the two operations through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), so the screen contract, the error envelope and the pagination have to be settled before the screen work starts.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_payment`, base `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, topic `rwb.payment.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt` topics, event names `rwb.payment.<Event>.v1`, task queue `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.payment` (Architecture v5 slide 41; Template and Rules §R4). It records that this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and no grant on another `rwb_*` schema (Architecture v5 slide 29), so DP-05 is declared as a prohibition: the payment facts of ACE arrive on rwb-source-data's contract and never through a view of this service.

Two points are carried as gaps rather than decided quietly. The TSD names `MatchRequest` and `ProceedsPage` without a field list, and the request's element list has to be derived from the nine columns of `proceeds` and the query parameters of API-P8-001 (GAP-2514; ASM-4163). The payloads of `TreatmentBooked` and `ProceedsMatched` are not published anywhere, while `PaymentMissed` appears with a full example on Architecture v5 slide 22, so the three schemas are written from that envelope and the modelled columns (GAP-2515; ASM-4164). The settlement money side itself is R-SET-14 of the Settlement route set, but the package code and the rule IDs of the matching mechanism appear in no source, so the contract names the PAYMENT_MATCH package without fixing a rule ID (GAP-2516; ASM-4165).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service naming rule of the platform library is in force: base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`, topic `rwb.<short>.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt`, event names `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1`, queue `rwb-<short>`, login and schema `rwb_<short>` (Architecture v5 slide 41 notes; Template and Rules §R4).
- The platform error envelope, the pagination and filter convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline (Architecture v5 slide 11); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The ownership of the objects is taken from the Ownership Map only: `proceeds` and the two operations are P8's, `treatment` and `GET /treatments/{treatmentId}` are S2's, `recovery_case` is P3's, the `v_ace_*` views are P1's, `rule_row`, `rule_package_version` and `decision_log_entry` are P7's. This document never declares another service's operation or table as provided.
- The two operations and their shapes are the ones of TSD P8 T-A.1 and T-A.2: API-P8-001 `GET /proceeds` with `ProceedsPage` out and errors 401, 403 and 503, and API-P8-002 `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` with `MatchRequest` in, `Proceeds` out, errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, and the `Idempotency-Key` header.
- The columns and the lists are the ones of TSD P8 T3.1 and T3.2: DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 and the values `INSTALLMENT`, `SETTLEMENT`, `FEE`, `SALE_PROCEEDS` and `UNMATCHED` of `LOV-MATCH`, and `CUSTOMER`, `LED`, `AUCTION`, `BUYER`, `AGENCY`, `INSURER` and `GUARANTOR` of `LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC`.
- The three events are the ones of Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43: `TreatmentBooked` (11) and `PaymentMissed` (12) with consumers rwb-case, rwb-treatment and, for `PaymentMissed`, rwb-comms, and `ProceedsMatched` (25) with consumers rwb-case, rwb-asset, rwb-debtsale, rwb-writeoff and rwb-guarantee; the envelope is CloudEvents 1.0 in binary mode with key `caseId`, 12 partitions, replication factor 3 and 7-day retention (slide 22).
- The schema registry is in BACKWARD mode and the AsyncAPI document per service is the contract, so every event is registered against it (Architecture v5 slide 42 notes).
- The `proceeds` table arrives with the DB story of this service; this baseline declares its name, its schema, its columns and its baseline version, and creates nothing.
- RWB-P8-E4043-APP, SCR-28 and the wave 3 harness are named as the consumers of this baseline but are not build dependencies: this story has none and is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).
- No approval is needed to publish a Draft baseline in this run, and no human verification stop is part of it.

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-payment for this surface: the two operations with their request and answer elements, the query parameters, the pagination, the rights and the seven error responses.
2. Fix the `Proceeds` element on DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009, the `ProceedsPage` element on the pagination convention, and the `MatchRequest` element with the fields the match needs, marking the fields no source gives with the placeholder.
3. Publish `LOV-MATCH`, `LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC` and the match state `SETTLEMENT` as enumerated values of the document, and fix the rule that no list value is a constant of the code.
4. Draft the AsyncAPI fragment and the three JSON schemas `TreatmentBooked`, `PaymentMissed` and `ProceedsMatched` with the CloudEvents envelope, `ce_type` `rwb.payment.<Event>.v1`, `ce_source` `/rwb-payment`, `ce_subject` `case/<caseId>`, key `caseId` and no personal data.
5. Fix the `rwb_payment.proceeds` table baseline: the columns, the standard record columns, the baseline version and the rule that no foreign key leaves the schema.
6. Record the consumed surface as consumed and faked: the settlement treatment of rwb-treatment, the case read and answer of rwb-case, the receipt read of rwb-source-data and the package read of rwb-decision.
7. Fix the error envelope and one message ID per condition, the rights of the capability area "Write-off and posting", and the `Idempotency-Key` rule with its stored answer.
8. Publish the five contract fakes and the drift test that compares each with the document.
9. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the additive rule, the vocabulary, the pagination, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the error envelope, the absence of a `v_ace_*` read and of another service's property, and the compatibility of the three event schemas.
10. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P8-E4043-APP, SCR-28 and the wave 3 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body or a request body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 400 or 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC3 |
| X2 | A path, a property or a list value is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version and a new event type | None | AC7 |
| X3 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC6, AC7 |
| X4 | A field of `MatchRequest`, `ProceedsPage` or an event payload has no source value | The row carries the placeholder, the gap and the assumption, and the fake is derived from the published document | None | AC3, AC4 |
| X5 | A value outside `LOV-MATCH` or `LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC` appears in the document, an example or a fake | The vocabulary test fails the build | None | AC3 |
| X6 | The document declares another service's operation as provided, a `v_ace_*` view, or a `treatment`, `recovery_case` or `rule_row` property | The review fails the baseline and the boundary test fails the build | None | AC7 |
| X7 | A POST is repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key` | The stored answer is returned and no second effect is described | None | AC2 |
| X8 | The rights of an operation are not the ones TSD P8 T6.1 and T-A.2 declare | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the Ownership Map, TSD P8 and the published owner documents of rwb-treatment, rwb-case, rwb-source-data and rwb-decision only |
| Negotiable | The element names beyond the ones the sources give, the example values and the fake fixtures are settled in the baseline review; the paths, the columns, the lists, the base, the topic, the queue and the event names are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks RWB-P8-E4043-APP, SCR-28 and the wave 3 harness on Day 1, and the five `ProceedsMatched` consumers on the same day |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, one AsyncAPI fragment with three schemas, nine contract tables, five fakes and five new contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The receipt and its match are P8's: `proceeds` in `rwb_payment` carries the case, the treatment, the account payment, the source, the amount, the received date, `matched_to` and the posting reference, and the contract declares their shapes only | Architecture v5 slide 41; Ownership Map (`proceeds` owner P8); TSD P8 T3.1 |
| BR2 | The vocabulary is closed: `source` is one value of `LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC`, `matched_to` is one value of `LOV-MATCH`, and the settlement match writes `SETTLEMENT`; no list value is a constant of the code | TSD P8 T3.2; FSD P8 A2.3.3.1 (BR-P8-003) |
| BR3 | The decision record is declared as an element written before the proceeds row changes, through the local library on the shared topic, and a failed write is MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; legacy RWB-E4-043 AC1 and AC2, owned by the app story |
| BR4 | No ACE view and no ACE table is read: the receipt facts are consumed on rwb-source-data's contract and the service holds no `v_ace_*` grant | DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR5 | The treatment, the case and the rule package stay with their owners: the contract declares the treatment read as consumed, the case read and answer as consumed, and the package read as consumed, and declares no property of them | Ownership Map (treatment S2, recovery_case P3, rule_row and rule_package_version P7); DP-01 |
| BR6 | A POST declares the `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer; a GET declares none | Architecture v5 slide 11; TSD P8 T-A.2 |
| BR7 | One REST base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; the document never declares another service's base or topic as its own | DP-13, DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR8 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version with a new event type | Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR9 | The events carry IDs and facts only: caseId, treatmentId, dueDate, amountDue, daysLate, the proceeds reference, the amount, the value date, the match value and a rule version, and no personal data | Architecture v5 slide 22 notes and slide 42 notes; Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17) |
| BR10 | The settlement money side is the transition R-SET-14 of the Settlement route set (AWAITING_PAYMENT to PAYMENT_CLEARED, amount_received = settlement_amount), governed in rwb-decision; the package code, the rule IDs of the matching mechanism and its tolerance and window rows appear in no source, so the contract names the PAYMENT_MATCH package of the Temporal and Drools design, fixes no rule ID and carries the placeholder (GAP-2516; ASM-4165) | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-SET-14); Temporal and Drools Design slide 18 (PAYMENT_MATCH replaces payment_match_rule); GAP-2516 |
| BR11 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-payment; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | Ownership Map; DP-11 |

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of this document, not of a receipt:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The two operations, the elements, the three event schemas, the table baseline and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, SCR-28, the wave 3 harness and the rwb-treatment, rwb-case, rwb-source-data and rwb-decision owners accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example an optional request field | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A path, a property or a list value is removed, renamed or retyped, or a match value changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | The absence test of AC7 fails: a `v_ace_*` view, another service's property, a second topic or a Schedule | In review |

The match state of the receipt that the document describes is the app story's: `matched_to` is one value of `LOV-MATCH` of TSD P8 T3.2 and the settlement arm writes `SETTLEMENT`; this baseline fixes the vocabulary and moves no receipt.

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-payment | Owns the OpenAPI document, the AsyncAPI fragment and the contract tables; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version, and the correction of the Ownership Map rows the baseline consumes |
| Consuming teams (the app story, SCR-28, the wave 3 harness and the owners of rwb-treatment, rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-decision and rwb-access) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |

The per-service login behind the security scheme of the document is named "the rwb-payment login" and is not part of this baseline.

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |

| Proceeds element | The columns of DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009: `id`, `case_id`, `treatment_id`, `account_payment_id`, `source`, `amount`, `received_date`, `matched_to` and `posting_ref` |
| Standard record columns | `is_active`, `state`, `version`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at` and `updated_by` of TSD P8 T3.0 |
| Lists | `LOV-MATCH` and `LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC` of TSD P8 T3.2, published as enumerated values |
| MatchRequest element | The fields the match needs, carried with the placeholder where no source gives them: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2514; ASM-4163) |
| PaymentMissed payload | The published example fields `caseId`, `treatmentId`, `dueDate`, `amountDue` and `daysLate` of Architecture v5 slide 22 |
| TreatmentBooked and ProceedsMatched payloads | The identifiers and facts of the modelled rows, with the fields that no source gives carried as Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2515; ASM-4164) |
| Decision record | DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 through the local library, written before the row changes (DP-03) |
| Not declared here | `treatment` (S2), `recovery_case` (P3), `v_ace_*` (P1), `rule_row`, `rule_package_version` and `decision_log_entry` (P7): each is named as an answer or a rule version of its owner and none is a property of this document |

The field-level types, lengths and required flags of the added elements are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the element names, the vocabulary of AC3 and the optionality rule of BR8. **No new table, no new column and no migration** is created by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-payment (P8); base `/api/recovery/payment/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/proceeds` | `ProceedsPage` out, filtered by `matched`, `from` and `to`, paginated by `page` and `size` (API-P8-001) | Write-off and posting, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` | `MatchRequest` in, `Proceeds` out (API-P8-002) | Write-off and posting, right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header required; the answer is stored |

The two operations answer 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, each with the error envelope and one message ID of section 14. The operation IDs are those of TSD P8 T-A.1 and T-A.2; the paths are those of the target base and not the monolith form. `GET /cases/{id}/payments` and the manual `POST /proceeds/{id}/allocate` of Architecture v5 slide 17 are read as the case-scoped view and the manual form of this family, and neither is declared as a third operation: their operation names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2514; ASM-4163).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /treatments/{treatmentId}` | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` | S2 rwb-treatment | The settlement treatment of the case: its type, its terms and its status; faked |
| The case read and the money-side answer (operation names Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2514; ASM-4163)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference, its product group and its route state, and the answer that carries the rule ID and the version that closed the money side; faked |
| The receipt read of the ACE batch (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2514; ASM-4163)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The receipts of the business date for source `ALS`, with the freshness stamp of the data product; faked |
| The rule-package read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2516; ASM-4165)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The PAYMENT_MATCH package at the version in force; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The four rows are contract dependencies of class C that the plan's C row for this story does not carry, because it is None, so the app story builds against these documents and fakes on Day 1 (GAP-2514; ASM-4163).

###### 12.3 Events published

Topic `rwb.payment.events.v1`, with the `.retry` and `.dlt` topics, 12 partitions, replication factor 3 and 7-day retention, key `caseId` (Architecture v5 slide 22).

| Event | Schema name | Consumers | Payload element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TreatmentBooked` (EV-11) | `rwb.payment.TreatmentBooked.v1` | rwb-case, rwb-treatment | The case and treatment references with the booking facts; the field list is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2515; ASM-4164) |
| `PaymentMissed` (EV-12) | `rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1` | rwb-case, rwb-treatment, rwb-comms | `caseId`, `treatmentId`, `dueDate`, `amountDue` and `daysLate`, as the published example of Architecture v5 slide 22 |
| `ProceedsMatched` (EV-25) | `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` | rwb-case, rwb-asset, rwb-debtsale, rwb-writeoff, rwb-guarantee | The case, proceeds and treatment references, the amount, the value date, the match value and the rule ID with its version; the remaining field list is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2515; ASM-4164) |

Each message declares the CloudEvents 1.0 binary envelope with `ce_specversion`, `ce_type`, `ce_source` `/rwb-payment`, `ce_id`, `ce_subject` `case/<caseId>` and a W3C `traceparent` header, and the body is validated against the registry in BACKWARD mode. `ProceedsMatched` is published by the settlement, auction and enforcement matching steps of this service, and this baseline declares its schema once for all of them; the publishing story is RWB-P8-E4043-APP for the settlement arm.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Consumer group | Payload used | When |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AceDataReady` (EV-26) | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | `rwb-payment.match-run.v1` | The business date and the source of the completed batch | Declared as consumed by the matching stories; starts the JOB-07 workflow |
| `TreatmentApproved` (EV-10) | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | `rwb-payment.match-run.v1` | The case, the treatment reference and the treatment type | Declared as consumed by the matching stories |
| `RulePackageInForce` (EV-30) | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | `rwb-payment.match-run.v1` | The package code and the version in force | Declared as consumed by the matching stories |

`DecisionRecorded` (EV-08) is written by all nineteen services through the local library on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and its consumers are rwb-decision and rwb-reporting (Architecture v5 slide 42, row 08). rwb-payment is a **producer** of that topic and not a consumer: the baseline declares the record through the library of DP-03 and adds no consumer group, subscription or inbox row for it.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| The JOB-07 event-started workflow (`PaymentMatchingWorkflow` in the app story; the name is a target design choice) | Workflow, one execution per business date and source, started by `AceDataReady` | `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | The workflow boundary the baseline serves: the input record, the three signals and the outcome; not built here |
| `matchPayments` | Activity, the matching step (Architecture v5 slide 17) | `rwb-payment` | The activity contract the baseline serves: the receipts, the case and the treatment in; the rule ID with its version, the match outcome, the record, the row and the outbox event out |
| `postProceeds` | Activity, the saga step (Architecture v5 slide 17; Temporal and Drools Design, `Payment.postProceeds`) | `rwb-payment` | Another story's activity on the same queue; its answer is one hop in a saga and is not declared by this baseline |

No child workflow for the money and no Nexus operation is declared here. The baseline fixes the input and the answer of the matching boundary only, and the workflow name is the app story's choice because no source document names it.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-07 and JOB-08 are event-triggered workflows in the owning service and not Temporal Schedules (Architecture v5 slide 44), so the baseline declares no Schedule, no Quartz row and no shared job table, and no Job of slide 44 is moved here.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| proceeds | P8 (`rwb_payment`) | The receipt and its match; the table the two operations read and the match writes |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_payment` | The local hash-linked decision record of the rule outcome (DP-03) |
| outbox_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_payment` | The three events of 12.3 and the relay (DP-09) |
| processed_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_payment` | The inbox row of each consumed event (DP-09) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_payment` | The key of the repeated POST and the answer it holds |

The baseline declares the `proceeds` table and its versioned baseline in `rwb_payment`; the migration itself is the DB story of this service. `treatment` (S2), `recovery_case` (P3), the `v_ace_*` views (P1), and `rule_row`, `rule_package_version` and `decision_log_entry` (P7) are other owners'; the baseline names them only as answers, rule versions or a later story's table, and no foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-source-data receipt fake | A receipt of source `CUSTOMER` for case `RC-2026-000431` with its business date; a stale product with its date; no answer beyond 2 s | AC1, AC3, AC6 |
| rwb-treatment settlement fake | The settlement treatment `TR-2026-000431` of the case; a case without a treatment | AC1, AC2, AC6 |
| rwb-case fake | The case reference with its route state; an accepted and a refused money-side answer | AC1, AC2, AC6 |
| rwb-decision package fake | The PAYMENT_MATCH package at its version in force | AC1, AC6 |
| Local decision-record library stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and outbox, and a stopped chain with MSG-P7-003 | AC2, AC6 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The operation names of the rwb-case answer, the rwb-source-data receipt read and the rwb-decision package read are derived from the published documents and carry the placeholder until their owners confirm them (GAP-2514, GAP-2516; ASM-4163, ASM-4165).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 4 consumed | The two operations on `/api/recovery/payment/v1`; the treatment, case, receipt and package rows; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 3 published, 3 consumed | `TreatmentBooked`, `PaymentMissed` and `ProceedsMatched` on `rwb.payment.events.v1`; `AceDataReady`, `TreatmentApproved` and `RulePackageInForce` in group `rwb-payment.match-run.v1` |
| Temporal | 1 workflow boundary and 2 activities declared, 0 registered | JOB-07 on `rwb-payment` with `matchPayments`; `postProceeds` is another story's; no Schedule |
| File | None | No file is read, built or delivered here; the posting file is the posting story's |

##### 13. Solution plan

**The CON declares shapes and moves nothing.** It writes no code, no migration and no table, and it changes no receipt, no treatment, no case and no rule package. What it publishes is one OpenAPI 3.1 document, one AsyncAPI fragment with three schemas, nine contract tables and five fakes.

**Deliverables.** The additive document `openapi/rwb-payment-v1.yaml` for this surface, the `Proceeds`, `ProceedsPage` and `MatchRequest` elements, `LOV-MATCH` and `LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC` as published enumerations, the three JSON schemas with the CloudEvents envelope, the contract README rows for the four consumed rows and their placeholders, and the five WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is declared as a prohibition: only rwb-source-data holds SELECT on the `recovery.v_ace_*` views (Architecture v5 slide 29), so the document declares no `v_ace_*` read and no grant on another `rwb_*` schema, and the legacy `v_ace_payment` read of DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054 is consumed on the owner's contract instead. DP-03 fixes the record element that is written before the match; DP-13 moves the base and nothing else; DP-19 is behind SCR-28 Proceeds matching, whose screen model is the edge contract's. DP-09 is not in the pattern set of this key, so the outbox and inbox rows are declared as library objects and not as a pattern of this baseline.

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds the two H rows `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` for DP-03 and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` for DP-19, while the plan's build list for this story is None, so the baseline builds against their fakes until those platform contract stories publish; the four consumed rows are class C dependencies in fact that the plan's C row does not carry, and they are built against their documents and fakes until their owners publish (GAP-2514; ASM-4163).

**Build steps**

1. Write the two operations and validate the surface of AC1 in the pipeline.
2. Write the `Proceeds` and `ProceedsPage` elements of AC3 from DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 and the pagination convention, with the placeholder on the fields the sources do not give.
3. Write the `MatchRequest` element of AC3 against the match the app story describes, with the placeholder and the note on its unstated fields.
4. Publish `LOV-MATCH` and `LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC` as enumerations and add the vocabulary test of AC3.
5. Write the AsyncAPI fragment and the three schemas of AC4 with the CloudEvents envelope and the no-personal-data rule.
6. Record the table baseline of AC5 and the versioned file naming, with the no-cross-schema-key test.
7. Record the error envelope, the rights and the `Idempotency-Key` rule of AC2.
8. Publish the five fakes of AC6 and the drift test.
9. Record the compatibility and boundary of AC7, then tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI document validates in the pipeline, the seven contract tests pass, the five fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, the three event schemas register in BACKWARD mode, and the app story, SCR-28 and the wave 3 harness have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of the `MatchRequest` is absent or invalid, or a body fails schema validation | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the Write-off and posting right the operation declares | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the proceeds row changes | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The data product of the source is stale after a late or failed ACE batch, which is VR-P8-003-1 of the FSD | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The four message IDs are contract elements and the text is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new one is added. MSG-P1-001 is carried because it is in the message set of this feature, and it is raised by the receipt read of the app story and not by this baseline.

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves SCR-28 Proceeds matching in its loading, matched and unmatched states through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The route calls rwb-payment for `GET /proceeds` and `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match`, rwb-case for the case and its route state and rwb-treatment for the settlement treatment; this baseline fixes the rwb-payment answers only, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The refusal and failure states the screen shows — refused with MSG-P4-002, not recorded with MSG-P7-003, stale data with MSG-P1-001 — read the messages of section 14 on the same route.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the match thresholds, the tolerance, the window, the percentages, the amounts and the rule IDs stay data, reference data or the rule package, never a schema default, an example constant or an enumeration member of the code.
- No personal data in a schema, an example, an event payload or a fake: identifiers, amounts, dates, list values and a rule version only, and every example is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or a `v_ace_*` view the service holds: it holds none, so the document declares no ACE view and no ACE table and the receipt is consumed on rwb-source-data's contract (DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 29).
- The treatment stays with rwb-treatment, the case with rwb-case and the rule package with rwb-decision: the document declares no `treatment`, `recovery_case`, `rule_row` or `rule_package_version` property and no write of their rows (DP-01).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service: `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, `rwb.payment.events.v1`, `rwb-payment` and the `rwb_payment` login, and a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The document lists only operations owned by rwb-payment; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided (DP-11).
- No retired element is reintroduced: the absence test fails a build that declares a `v_ace_*` read, a second topic, a Schedule, a Quartz row or a shared job table.
- The error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule and the decision-record library come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.
