| Element | Type | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proceeds.id` | uuid | Workbench | DF-FIN-001 |
| `case_id` | uuid | rwb-case reference | DF-FIN-002 |
| `treatment_id` | uuid, optional | rwb-treatment reference | DF-FIN-003 |
| `account_payment_id` | uuid, optional | ACE payment reference | DF-FIN-004; GAP-2521 |
| `source` | `LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC` | Workbench | DF-FIN-005: CUSTOMER, LED, AUCTION, BUYER, AGENCY, INSURER, GUARANTOR |

| `received_date` | date | ACE payment fact | DF-FIN-007 |

Reads are `recovery.v_ace_payment` (DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054, SELECT only) and `recovery.v_ace_batch_status` for freshness; the case reference is read on rwb-case's contract. The table carries the seven standard record columns. No ACE payment is copied, no account or payment master is held, and no table of another owner is read: `recovery_case` (P3), `treatment` (S2), `asset` and `sale` (S5), `debt_sale_lot` (S6), `write_off` (S7) and `rule_row`, `rule_package_version` and `decision_log_entry` (P7) are named by their owners only.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-payment (P8); base `/api/recovery/payment/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the behaviour behind the two operations whose shapes are declared by RWB-P8-E4044-CON.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/proceeds` | `ProceedsPage` out, query `matched`, `from`, `to`, `page`, `size`, paginated (API-P8-001) | Write-off and posting, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` | `MatchRequest` in, `Proceeds` out (API-P8-002) | Write-off and posting, right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header; the answer is stored and returned on a repeat |

The answers: 400 for a malformed request, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope proceeds reference, 409 on an already matched receipt under a new key, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for an invalid element, 503 when the decision library or a consumed read does not answer.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The case read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2518; ASM-4168)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The open case of the account or the case named by the remittance: its reference and stage; faked |
| The rule-package read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2518; ASM-4168)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The proceeds arm of the match package at the version in force, with its rule IDs; faked |

Each row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, one retry on a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The plan gives this slice no C dependency, so the two rows are built against the fakes and their owners confirm the names before the contract tag.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Envelope | Key |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ProceedsMatched` (`rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1`, EV-25) — payload `proceedsId`, `caseId`, `amount` | `rwb.payment.events.v1`, with `.retry` and `.dlt` | CloudEvents 1.0, event id and subject | The case reference |

`TreatmentBooked` (EV-11) and `PaymentMissed` (EV-12) sit on the same topic and are published by the sibling stories of this service; the schema is declared once in RWB-P8-E4044-CON, and this story publishes only `ProceedsMatched`. The event is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the row; there is no event without the row and no row without the event (DP-09; Event and Messaging Design rule Transactions).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Read or topic | Payload used | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AceDataReady` (EV-26) | `recovery.v_ace_batch_status`, the ACE batch record of source ALS (read, not delivered on a topic) | `source_system`, `business_date`, `status`, `completed_at` | Starts the run of a business date when the batch is COMPLETED |

The receipt facts themselves are read on the service's view of `v_ace_payment` rather than on an event, so the story subscribes to no topic. A repeat of the same business date is deduped on (source, business date) in `inbox_event` of `rwb_payment` (DP-09; R-UNI-40).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| The JOB-07 payment-matching workflow (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2520; ASM-4170)) | Workflow, one execution per business date | `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the business date. Signals: none in this slice |
| The matching activity, name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2520; ASM-4170) | Activity | `rwb-payment` | In: business date. Out: the row, record and outbox references, in one transaction |

Drools is called only inside an activity, so a replay reuses the recorded answer; the record and the change are one transaction (DP-03; the slide 14 pattern of the Temporal and Drools design). Retry: 1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The run starts on the ACE batch completion of source ALS for a business date (FSD P8 A2.4 AC-BG-P8-004-01; EV-26); no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz row is declared for it (DP-10 is not applied by this story).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `proceeds` | P8, schema `rwb_payment` | The table of TSD P8 T3.1 with the standard record columns |
| `outbox_event` | Platform library, created in `rwb_payment` | The `ProceedsMatched` row (DP-09) |
| `inbox_event` | Platform library, created in `rwb_payment` | The (source, business date) replay guard (DP-09) |
| `decision_record` | Platform library, created in `rwb_payment` | The local decision record of DP-03 |
| `idempotency_key` | Platform library, created in `rwb_payment` | The `Idempotency-Key` of the manual match |

The Flyway baseline of the service is a `V0001` sequence in `rwb_payment`, owned by the DB story of this service (DP-15 is not applied by this story). No table of another owner is declared.

Each fake answers only what its owner documents; a fake that answers more than the document fails the review. The two operation names that are not published carry the placeholder of GAP-2518 until their owners confirm them.

##### 13. Solution plan

| Step | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The matching activity: read the receipts of the business date, resolve the case, evaluate the rules, write the row, the record and the outbox row in one transaction | A receipt of source `AUCTION` produces a `proceeds` row with SALE_PROCEEDS and one `ProceedsMatched` |
| 2 | The unmatched path: a receipt with no case reference produces an UNMATCHED row and the daily exception | The daily exception lists the receipt; no case is touched |
| 3 | The two operations on the contract of RWB-P8-E4044-CON: filter, page, match, error map | The documented 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 answers |
| 4 | The idempotency rule: an `Idempotency-Key` stores the answer; a repeat returns it, a second key answers 409 | A repeated POST returns the stored answer |
| 5 | The outbox relay and the topic declaration | One event per committed row, with the case as the key |
| 6 | SCR-28 through the composite route: loading, matched and unmatched | The three states render from the merged answer |

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. | A required element of the match is missing or invalid (422) |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | A caller without the right (403) |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | The decision record cannot be written (AC2) |
| MSG-P1-001 | Error | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. | The payment data product is stale (VR-P8-004-1) |

The four rows are the legacy message set of the key plus the stale-data row of the module; no other message is added. Every refusal is one problem document with a code, the message ID and a correlation reference, and no message text is assembled in code (BR-P8-004).

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-28 Proceeds matching | Loading | The receipts of the business date are being read; a skeleton, no partial totals |
| SCR-28 Proceeds matching | Matched | One row per receipt with its case, its source, its amount, `matched_to` and its posting reference when known |
| SCR-28 Proceeds matching | Unmatched | The receipts with `matched_to` UNMATCHED and the daily exception, with the manual match action for right U |

The screen is a gateway-bff composite route: the receipt rows come from this service, the case label from rwb-case, and the two are merged one hop each, in parallel (DP-19). The screen declares no business value of its own; every list it shows is a reference-data list of rwb-case.

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |

| TC-E4-044-01 | AC1 | Component | The receipts of business date `2026-11-22` for case `RC-2026-000611`: one of source `AUCTION` with amount 820,000.00 THB, resolved to the case, matched to SALE_PROCEEDS, with one record and one `ProceedsMatched` |

The four cases keep their legacy IDs and their legacy intent; the data column states the synthetic set of ASM-4167 and no business threshold. A wave 3 harness copy, where one is made, takes the `-ITG` suffix.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the tolerance, the window, the grace, the priority and the rule IDs are rule rows read at run time; a constant that changes an answer fails review (BR-P8-004).
- No personal data in an event, a workflow input, a log or a test: `ProceedsMatched` carries `proceedsId`, `caseId` and `amount` only, and every example is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the service's own `v_ace_*` read: the payment facts are read on `recovery.v_ace_payment`, SELECT only, and never copied.
- No read of another service's table: the case comes from rwb-case's contract, the rules from rwb-decision's, and the schema `rwb_payment` is the only one written.
- The record precedes the change, and both or neither: the activity writes the decision record, the row and the outbox row in one transaction (R-UNI-39).
- One hop, 2 s, breaker per downstream, one retry on a GET, and the manual match idempotent on its key (ADR-020).
- The service holds one base, one topic, one queue and one login: `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, `rwb.payment.events.v1`, `rwb-payment` and the `rwb_payment` login.

##### 1. Story

As a **finance and CFO delegate**, I want **the Workbench to work out partner fees, court fees and charges from the fee tables held as data**, so that **every payment and booking is matched to its case**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E4-045, feature FEAT-PAY-05 of module P8 Payments and posting (FSD P8 A2.5; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3). It owns:

- the one legacy acceptance criterion this slice keeps, AC2, copied word for word with its origin tag; AC1 of the key is owned by RWB-ITG-E4045-ITG;
- the fee-and-charge step of the payment run in rwb-payment: it takes a fee fact of a case — a partner fee, a court fee or a charge — works the amount out of the fee rows in force, read at their version, and records the answer before anything uses it (DP-03; FSD P8 A2.5; TSD P8 T3.1);
- the account fee facts read on `recovery.v_ace_account` (`collections_fee` DF-ACE-024, `fees_outstanding` DF-ACC-011) and the receipt facts read on `recovery.v_ace_payment`, SELECT only, no copy (DP-05);
- the money side of the fee: a receipt that settles a fee is carried on the `proceeds` row of schema `rwb_payment` with `matched_to` FEE, one of the values of `LOV-MATCH`, so the fee is tied to its case, its treatment and its posting reference (DF-FIN-005 to DF-FIN-009);
- the record of every calculation — fee row identity, its version, the inputs and the answer, hash-linked to the previous record of the case — written before the row, both or neither (DP-03; R-UNI-39);
- SCR-28 Proceeds matching in its loading, matched and unmatched states with the fee rows in place, reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

It does not own: AC1 of the legacy key, the end-to-end evidence of the fee across the services, which is RWB-ITG-E4045-ITG; the published shapes of the service's two operations, its three event schemas and the fakes, which are the baseline of RWB-P8-E2008-CON; the other P8 features, the matching of FEAT-PAY-01 above all, and the sibling stories of RWB-E4-043 to RWB-E4-049; the case, its stages and its tasks (P3); the legal-spend approval and its limit (S4); the work order and the sale behind a vendor or broker fee (S5); the partner (S9); the fee package, the rule rows and the central ledger (P7); and the ACE fee and payment facts (P1).

##### 2. Business rationale

Fee arithmetic is where recovery money leaks and where an audit finding starts. A court fee, a panel law firm's fee, a property vendor's charge and a broker fee are worked out today by hand against a table nobody versions, and the FSD states the module's problem in one line: payments are matched to plans and settlements by hand, and broken plans are found late (FSD P8 A1.3, repeated in A2.5.1). The measure is the module's own: receipts matched the same day, rising each month, read from the decision log and the Workbench records (FSD P8 A2.5.1).

The routing logic says exactly when a fee falls due, in four different routes: a court fee or legal expense (R-LIT-41, event FEE_DUE, routed to the approver at D7.4), a work order at the vendor's fee schedule (R-DIS-10), a broker fee at acceptance (R-DIS-64) and an agency fee on a post-charge-off recovery (R-WO-37). Under D-RCV-60 each of those owners knows that a fee is due; none of them may hold the arithmetic, because the fee values are data rows of the Workbench and the money side is this service's. The calculation therefore sits in rwb-payment, reads the ACE fee facts on the service's own read path (DP-05) and records every answer locally (DP-03), so that a route owner, an approver and an auditor can see the fee that was raised, from which row and at which version — which is what the legacy criterion asserts when it says the result is written to the decision log with the rule version.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service runs unattended as primary; the Finance and CFO delegate uses the result (FSD P8 A2.5.3.3). A person reading the fee rows on SCR-28 holds right R in the capability area Write-off and posting (TSD P8 T6.1, T6.2); the legacy permission table of the key gives the same intent as right R on Case record.
- The ACE batch of the source that carries the fee's money side is COMPLETED in `recovery.v_ace_batch_status` for the business date; a late or failed batch leaves the product stale and no amount is raised on it (FSD P8 A2.5.3.1 VR-P8-005-1; FSD P8 A1.4).
- The case and workflow capability the feature depends on is in place (legacy Depends on FEAT-CWC-23; FSD P8 A2.5 Prerequisites): the case, its product group and its stage are read on rwb-case's contract, never from its tables.
- The fee rows of the fee type are readable at a version, and no rate, flat amount, cap or validity is written in code (FSD P8 A2.5.3.1 BR-P8-005; GAP-2543; ASM-4202).
- The build dependencies are tagged: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for the local decision record, RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the composite route of SCR-28.
- The fakes of the consumed reads answer the documented shapes, so the build never waits for another service (ADR-020; GAP-2543; ASM-4202).

##### 4. Flow

1. Trigger. A fee fact arrives for a case: a court fee or legal expense falls due (R-LIT-41, FEE_DUE), a work order is raised on a held asset (R-DIS-10), a broker sale is agreed (R-DIS-64), or a post-charge-off recovery is placed with an agency (R-WO-37). The fact is consumed into the inbox of `rwb_payment` and deduped on its key (R-UNI-40).
2. The step reads the case on rwb-case's contract — product group, stage, amount basis — one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker (ADR-020).
3. It reads the fee rows of that fee type in force on the fee date, with the rate or flat amount, the cap, the validity and the version, and keeps the row identity (GAP-2543; ASM-4202).
4. It reads the account fee facts of the case's account on `recovery.v_ace_account` — `collections_fee` (DF-ACE-024) and `fees_outstanding` (DF-ACC-011) — and, where the fee is settled by a receipt, the receipt on `recovery.v_ace_payment` (DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054). SELECT only, no copy, no other service's table (DP-05).
5. It computes the amount from the fee row and the read facts alone. Every threshold, rate, cap and tolerance is a row read at run time; a constant that changes an answer fails review (BR-P8-005).
6. It writes the decision record first — fee row identity, version, inputs, answer, hash-linked to the previous record of the case — and the `proceeds` row in the same transaction. A failure of either leaves neither, and the fact stays on the inbox for the next attempt (DP-03; R-UNI-39).
7. The row carries `matched_to` FEE, with `case_id`, `treatment_id` when the fee belongs to a treatment, `source` from `LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC`, `amount`, `received_date` and `posting_ref` when the ACE record carries one (DF-FIN-002 to DF-FIN-009).
8. No amount is raised that an approver has not cleared: where the court fee or legal expense needs approval inside the D7.4 limit, the approved fact is read on the route owner's contract and the calculation uses it (R-LIT-41, R-LIT-42). Where the answer needs a person, a task is raised on rwb-case's contract (FSD P8 A2.5.2 step 3).
9. SCR-28 shows the fee rows of the case with their match status, merged by gateway-bff from this service and the case label of rwb-case (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| Condition | What happens | Message or reference |
|---|---|---|
| The decision record cannot be written | Nothing changes; no fee row and no amount; an incident is raised | MSG-P7-003; R-UNI-39; AC2 |
| No fee row is in force for the fee type on the fee date | No amount and no row; the fact is held for the fee owner with the date it needs | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2544; ASM-4203) |
| The ACE batch of the source is late or failed | The step does not compute; the product is shown with its date | MSG-P1-001 {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. (VR-P8-005-1) |
| The same fee fact arrives twice | The second one is ignored and the idempotency hit is recorded | R-UNI-40 |
| The partner is recalled for insolvency | Fee payments to that partner stop and no new amount is raised against its work | R-UNI-28 |
| A person without the right opens the fee rows | Refused, nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 |
| The case of the fee is unknown or out of the caller's scope | One problem document, no change | HTTP 404 |
| A required fact of the amount basis is missing | Refused, nothing changes | MSG-GEN-001 |
| A consumed read does not answer inside 2 s | The step stops for that fact and retries; the breaker opens per downstream | HTTP 503; ADR-020 |
| The fee row version is replaced between the read and the record | The row is recorded at the version read; the next fact is computed at the new version | BR-P8-005 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Letter | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Independent | Yes. It builds against two platform contract stories; no other service's build blocks it. |
| Negotiable | The fee values, their version and the approval limits stay with their owners; the story fixes only the step, the record and the row. |
| Valuable | Yes. A fee is worked out from data, recorded with the row and version that produced it, and tied to its case. |
| Estimable | Yes. One step, one activity, one record, one row and one screen state set. |
| Small | Yes. One calculation, one write path, no new operation and no new event. |
| Testable | Yes. The legacy criterion, the four legacy cases and the documented refusals. |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Calculate fees and charges

  Scenario: AC2 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E4-045 AC2)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The criterion is the legacy AC2 of the key, word for word, and is the only criterion this slice owns. AC1 of the same key — "Then works out partner fees, court fees and charges from the fee tables held as data / Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version" — is owned by RWB-ITG-E4045-ITG, which carries the cross-service journey of the key in wave 3; the calculation behind it is built here and stated in sections 4, 8 and 16. The fee facts both criteria are exercised on are the synthetic set of ASM-4201 and are used in section 16 only.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Message |
|---|---|---|
| BR-P8-005 | No value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version | None |
| VR-P8-005-1 | Data product stale after a late or failed ACE batch for its source (`v_ace_batch_status`) | MSG-P1-001 {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| R-LIT-41 | A court fee or legal expense falls due: route the fee to the approver inside the D7.4 limit | None |
| R-LIT-42 | Inside the limit, or approved above it: raise the fee and post it against the case | None |
| R-DIS-10 | Storage, property tax, insurance, security or eviction required: raise the work order on the portal at the vendor's fee schedule | None |
| R-DIS-54 | On proceeds posted: apply the proceeds to the case and the loan account, and match the vendor fee | None |
| R-DIS-64 | Sale price at or above the approved floor: complete the sale and pay the broker fee on acceptance | None |
| R-WO-37 | A payment is matched after charge-off: post it as post charge-off income and calculate the agency fee | None |
| R-UNI-28 | The partner enters insolvency: recall the work, secure cash held and stop fee payments | None |
| R-UNI-39 | The decision log entry cannot be written: block the action and raise an incident; no action proceeds unlogged | MSG-P7-003 |
| R-UNI-40 | The same event arrives twice with the same key: ignore the second, record the idempotency hit | None |

The four route rules are the rows whose events carry a fee, and they are the four triggers of section 4: the fee amount this story works out is their input, and the approval and the case move stay with the route owners (Business Rules and Routing Logic v4). BR-P8-005 and VR-P8-005-1 are the two rows of FSD P8 A2.5.3.1.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Trigger | To | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| No `proceeds` row | A fee fact is computed from the fee row in force | `proceeds` row with `matched_to` FEE, and one decision record | R-LIT-42; R-DIS-10 |
| No `proceeds` row | No fee row is in force for the fee type and date | No row; the fact is held for the fee owner | GAP-2544 |
| FEE row | A receipt of the same case settles the fee | The same row, its `posting_ref` written by the posting story | DF-FIN-008, DF-FIN-009 |
| FEE row | The partner is recalled for insolvency | No further fee payment to that partner | R-UNI-28 |
| Any | The decision record or the row write fails | No change; nothing is published and the fact stays on the inbox | R-UNI-39 |

The case state, its route stage, its tasks and its timers are not moved here: this story writes one row of its own schema and one local record, and rwb-case decides what the case does with the fee.

##### 10. Authority

The step runs unattended as primary; the Finance and CFO delegate is the role that uses its result (FSD P8 A2.5.3.3). The person-facing part is the read of the fee rows on SCR-28, under capability area **Write-off and posting**, right R (TSD P8 T6.1, T6.2).

| Right | Roles that hold it (TSD P8 T6.1) |
|---|---|
| R (read) | RW-FRAUD, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-WRITEOFF, RW-CREDITAD, RW-CONDUCT, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-WOCOMM, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-FINANCE, RW-AUDIT, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE, SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-DATALOAD, SY-AGENT |
| No write right on this path | The step writes with the service identity of the run, under the same role checks as a person (NFR-051) |

The legacy permission table of the key gives right R on **Case record** with an open role list; the module matrix is the authority for the list and the legacy line for the intent. The right is checked on the object: a caller scoped away from the case gets 404, not 403.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-payment (P8); base `/api/recovery/payment/v1` (DP-13). The service declares no fee operation: the two operations of the service are the only ones, and their shapes are the frozen baseline of RWB-P8-E2008-CON. This story supplies the behaviour behind them for a fee row.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/proceeds` | `ProceedsPage` out, query `matched`, `from`, `to`, `page`, `size`, paginated (API-P8-001); the FEE rows of a case are read with the case scope applied | Write-off and posting, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` | `MatchRequest` in, `Proceeds` out (API-P8-002); a fee receipt matched by hand carries the same answer block | Write-off and posting, right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header; the stored answer is returned on a repeat |

The answers: 400 for a malformed request, 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 for an unknown or out-of-scope proceeds reference, 409 on an already matched receipt under a new key, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for an invalid element, 503 when the decision library or a consumed read does not answer. The service plan gives this story no build dependency on that baseline: it is Day 1 work of the same service and this story builds against its shapes.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The case read (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2543; ASM-4202)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The product group, the stage and the amount basis of the case; faked |
| The reference-data and fee-row read (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2543; ASM-4202)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case, as the owner of parameters and reference data | The fee rows of the fee type in force on the fee date, with their version; faked |
| The partner read (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2543; ASM-4202)) | `/api/recovery/partner/v1` | S9 rwb-partner | The partner of a partner fee, its type, its panel status and its contract end; faked |
| The approved legal-spend fact (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2543; ASM-4202)) | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2543; ASM-4202) | the litigation route (S4) as R-LIT-42 scopes it | That a court fee or legal expense is approved, and inside which limit; faked |
| `recovery.v_ace_account`, `recovery.v_ace_payment`, `recovery.v_ace_batch_status` | read-only views, no REST operation | P1 rwb-source-data | The account fee facts, the receipt and the freshness of the product (DP-05) |

Each row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, one retry on a GET and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The plan gives this slice no C dependency, so every row is built against its fake and the owner confirms the name before the contract tag.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service owns three events — `TreatmentBooked` (EV-11), `PaymentMissed` (EV-12) and `ProceedsMatched` (EV-25) — and no source declares a fee event for it, so this story publishes nothing and adds no topic, no event name and no outbox row (GAP-2545; ASM-4204). The answer of the calculation is the local decision record of DP-03 plus the `proceeds` row with `matched_to` FEE, which the posting and matching stories of the service read on their own paths.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Read or topic | Payload used | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| The fee-due fact of the litigation route (FEE_DUE, R-LIT-41) | topic of the owner, name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2543; ASM-4202) | the case, the fee type and the fee date | A court fee or legal expense falls due |
| The work-order fact of the asset route (WORK_ORDER_RAISED, R-DIS-10) | topic of the owner, name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2543; ASM-4202) | the case, the work type and the fee schedule in force | A work order is raised on a held asset |
| The sale-agreed fact of the asset and debt-sale routes (BROKER_SOLD, R-DIS-64) | topic of the owner, name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2543; ASM-4202) | the case, the sale reference and the agreed price basis | A broker sale is agreed at or above its floor |
| The matched-payment fact after charge-off (PAYMENT_RECEIVED_AFTER_CHARGEOFF, R-WO-37) | topic of the owner, name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2543; ASM-4202) | the case, the placement and the amount matched | A recovery is matched on a placed case |
| `AceDataReady` (EV-26) | `recovery.v_ace_batch_status`, the ACE batch record of the source (read, not delivered on a topic) | `source_system`, `business_date`, `status`, `completed_at` | Decides whether the run may compute for a business date |

A duplicate is deduped in `inbox_event` of `rwb_payment` on the key of the fact (R-UNI-40; DP-09 library). No other subscription is added, and the fee values themselves are read on the reference-data contract rather than on an event.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| The fee-calculation run (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2546; ASM-4205)) | Workflow, event-started per fee fact | `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the fee fact and its business date. Signals: none in this slice |
| The calculation activity (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2546; ASM-4205)) | Activity | `rwb-payment` | In: the fee fact. Out: the record and row references, in one transaction |

Drools is not called: the fee values are data rows read at their version, not a rule package, so no rule answer has to be replayed (DP-04 is not applied by this story). The retry policy is 1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts; a fee row missing in force is a non-retryable answer.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The run starts on a fee fact of a route, and the JOB-07 and JOB-08 runs of this service are event-started (FSD P8 A2.5.4.4 AC-BG-P8-005-01 gives the ACE batch of source ALS as the daily cadence), so no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row and no shared job table is declared here (DP-10 is not applied by this story).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `proceeds` | P8, schema `rwb_payment` | The table of TSD P8 T3.1 with the standard record columns; the FEE row of a fee |
| `decision_record` | Platform library, created in `rwb_payment` | The local decision record of DP-03, one per calculation |
| `inbox_event` | Platform library, created in `rwb_payment` | The dedup of a fee fact (R-UNI-40) |

No fee table is declared in `rwb_payment`: the ownership map gives this service one table, `proceeds`, and the fee rows live with their owner (GAP-2543; ASM-4202). The Flyway baseline of the service is a `V0001` sequence in `rwb_payment`, owned by the DB story of the service (DP-15 is not applied by this story).

Each fake answers only what its owner documents; a fake that answers more than the document fails the review. Every name that is not published carries the placeholder of GAP-2543 until its owner confirms it.

##### 13. Solution plan

| Step | Work | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The calculation activity: read the case, the fee rows and the ACE fee facts; compute the amount from the rows alone | A fee fact produces one amount, with the fee row identity and version in the record |
| 2 | The record-then-row transaction: decision record first, `proceeds` row with `matched_to` FEE second, both or neither | A stopped record leaves no row and the fact on the inbox |
| 3 | The freshness guard on `recovery.v_ace_batch_status` and the stale answer | A late batch produces MSG-P1-001 and no amount |
| 4 | The dedup of a repeated fee fact on the key of the fact | A repeated fact writes no second row and records the hit |
| 5 | The partner guard: a recalled partner raises no new fee | A recalled partner blocks the amount under R-UNI-28 |
| 6 | SCR-28 through the composite route, with the fee rows in loading, matched and unmatched | The three states render from the merged answer |

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. | A required fact of the amount basis is missing (422) |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | A caller without right R on the fee rows (403) |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | The decision record cannot be written (AC2) |
| MSG-P1-001 | Error | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. | The product of the source is stale (VR-P8-005-1) |

These are the three legacy messages of the key plus the stale-data row of the module. No source publishes a message for a fee type with no row in force, so that condition is carried as the placeholder of GAP-2544 rather than invented. Every refusal is one problem document with a code, the message ID and a correlation reference, and no message text is assembled in code (BR-P8-005).

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-28 Proceeds matching | Loading | The fee rows of the case are being read; a skeleton, no partial total |
| SCR-28 Proceeds matching | Matched | One row per fee with its fee type, amount, case, `matched_to` and posting reference when known |
| SCR-28 Proceeds matching | Unmatched | The fee facts that produced no amount, with the reason and the date they need |

The screen is a gateway-bff composite route: the fee rows come from this service, the case label from rwb-case, and the two are merged one hop each, in parallel (DP-19). The screen declares no business value of its own; every list it shows is a reference-data list of its owner.

| TC-E4-045-03 | Access | Component | A caller without right R on the fee rows is refused with MSG-P4-002, and nothing changes |
| TC-E4-045-04 | Principle 5 | Component | A forced decision-record failure stops the action with MSG-P7-003 and raises one incident under R-UNI-39 |

The four cases keep their legacy IDs and their legacy intent; the data column states the synthetic set of ASM-4201 and no business threshold. TC-E4-045-01 is exercised end to end by RWB-ITG-E4045-ITG, whose copy of it takes the `-ITG` suffix.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the rate, the flat amount, the cap, the validity and the fee type are fee rows read at run time; a constant that changes an amount fails review (BR-P8-005).
- No personal data in an event, a workflow input, a log or a test: the calculation carries the case reference, the fee type, the fee row and the amount, and every example is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the service's own `v_ace_*` read: `collections_fee`, `fees_outstanding` and the receipt are read on the views, SELECT only, and never copied.
- No read of another service's table: the case and the fee rows come from rwb-case's contract, the partner from rwb-partner's, and `rwb_payment` is the only schema written.
- The record precedes the change, and both or neither: the activity writes the decision record and the row in one transaction (R-UNI-39).
- A recalled partner raises no new fee (R-UNI-28), and a repeated fact never raises a second one (R-UNI-40).
- One hop, 2 s, breaker per downstream, and one retry on a GET (ADR-020).
- The service holds one base, one topic, one queue and one login: `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, `rwb.payment.events.v1`, `rwb-payment` and the `rwb_payment` login.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E4-045 for the wave 3 integration harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a member of the integration and QA team, I want **one repeatable cross-service harness that takes a seeded case with a payment on its account and a partner on its contracted fee terms, drives the fee step through rwb-payment, and proves that partner fees, court fees and charges are worked out from the fee tables held as data and written to the decision record with the rule version, against the owning services' published contracts and their fakes**, so that **every fee raised on a payment or a booking is shown to come from data a business person may change and to be on record before it is raised, and no fee reaches a partner, a court or the ledger on a value that lives in code**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A fee worked out from a number in code cannot be defended when the contracted schedule moves, and it cannot be changed without a release. A court fee or a legal expense raised without its approval is spend beyond the delegation of authority, which the bank has to unwind. A partner fee paid without a recorded result is money it cannot recover. All three sit on one chain: the payment and its fee step in P8 rwb-payment, which owns payment and proceeds matching, fees and bookings in `rwb_payment`; the partner and its contracted fee terms in S9 rwb-partner, which owns the panel, partner users, instructions, results, fees and scorecards in `rwb_partner`; the payment row in `v_ace_payment`, which is ACE's and is read through P1 rwb-source-data's data product; the approver inside the D7.4 limit, whose DoA table is P4 rwb-access's; and the record that cites the rule and its version, which is written with the change in one transaction and reaches the ledger through `rwb.decision-record.v1` (REQ-DRI-001; R-UNI-39). Where the payment on the account is the settlement payment, the posting that raises it is R-SET-14's, and it belongs to the treatment and payment stories and not to this one.

This story owns the harness that proves that chain as the legacy key describes it, carrying AC1 of RWB-E4-045 into evidence. The fee tables are data, so the run asserts the outcome against the terms the owners publish and not against a figure written here. The three states the same loop touches are the owner's: PAYMENT_MATCHED when the payment matches (R-WO-37), PROCEEDS_APPLIED when the proceeds and the vendor fee are applied (R-DIS-54), and FEE_APPROVED when a court fee passes its approval (R-LIT-42). It serves REQ-S9-004, REQ-CHO-009 and REQ-DRI-001, and it carries FEAT-PAY-05 into evidence, with REQ-S9-004 read against the contracted schedule and against recorded results (R-DIS-11; R-WO-37).

The harness is decoupled the same way the services are. It owns no schema and reads no other service's table (DP-01): the fee step, the matched proceeds and the fees on the case come from rwb-payment, the partner and its contracted fee terms from rwb-partner, the payment row from rwb-source-data's product, the record from rwb-decision and the authority from rwb-access. It reads `v_ace_payment` through rwb-source-data's contract and never through a view of its own (DP-05). The record is read from rwb-decision's contract and the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1` topic rather than from a local log table (DP-03). It calls each owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`, one hop per call with a 2 s timeout and a circuit breaker per downstream, and it calls the gateway-bff composite route where a screen would (DP-19).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The published contracts of rwb-payment, rwb-partner, rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access are in the contract registry, and a stub set is generated from each published OpenAPI or AsyncAPI document with its version pinned.
- A case, a payment on its account and a partner on its contracted fee terms are seeded through the owning services' published operations only. The seeding set, the harness environment specification and the fixture contents are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607).
- The fee tables, the court fee and charge schedules and the partner's contracted fee terms are read from their owners only, and the harness holds no copy of any of them. Who owns and stores the fee tables and the two schedules, and their table and field names, are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607).
- The operation and field names in rwb-payment that carry the calculated fee amounts, and which field or child record of `partner` carries the contracted fee terms, are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607).
- The data product code that serves the `v_ace_payment` row through the source-data products operation is not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607).
- The rule package in force carries R-LIT-41, R-LIT-42, R-DIS-11, R-DIS-54 and R-WO-37, and the version of each rule is readable on the decision record that cites it.
- An approver inside the D7.4 limit exists on the DoA data that rwb-access holds, and the approval it gives is the one the record cites before a court fee or a legal expense is raised (R-LIT-41; R-LIT-42).
- An authorisation path exists through `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` for the roles that hold the case record R and for a caller whose role does not include the right.
- No build dependency and no contract dependency. Day 1, with the fakes of section 12.8 in place from the first run, and the rwb-payment fake replaced by the real service when RWB-P8-E4045-APP lands.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: seeds the case, the payment on its account and the partner on its contracted fee terms through the owning services' published operations only; the seeding set and its environment are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607).
2. Harness: reads the partner and its contracted fee terms through `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` and pins the terms the run is keyed by, so that every fee assertion is made against the owner's data and not against a figure in the script (REQ-S9-004).
3. Harness: reads the payment row from `v_ace_payment` through `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/{productCode}/records` and asserts `payment_code`, the amount, the account and the payment date the run was seeded with (DP-05, REQ-CHO-009). The product code is not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607).
4. Harness: drives the fee step with `POST /api/recovery/payment/v1/proceeds/{proceedsId}/match`, so the fees are worked out by the service that owns them and not by the harness. In production the same step is the `matchPayments` activity on queue rwb-payment (JOB-07), which updates `rwb_payment` and writes `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` to its outbox in one transaction.
5. Harness: reads the matched proceeds and the fee amounts recorded against them through `GET /api/recovery/payment/v1/proceeds`, and the payments and the fees on the case through `GET /api/recovery/payment/v1/cases/{caseId}/payments`, which Architecture v5 slide 17 gives to rwb-payment. The field names that carry the fee amounts are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607).
6. Harness: asserts the partner fee against the contracted schedule read in step 2 and against the recorded result it is paid on, so the fee follows the schedule and the result and is not a percentage in the script (REQ-S9-004; R-DIS-11; R-WO-37).
7. Harness: asserts, for a court fee or a legal expense, that it was checked against its schedule and routed for approval inside the D7.4 limit before it was raised, and that the decision record names R-LIT-41 and R-LIT-42 with their versions (R-LIT-41; R-LIT-42).
8. Harness: asserts that where proceeds are applied, the vendor fee is matched on them, and that the proceeds and the fee read back from step 5 agree (R-DIS-54).
9. Harness: asserts that no fee amount is hard-coded: the same step is run for a second seeded partner on a different contracted schedule, and the fee must follow that partner's terms with no change to the harness. Who owns and stores the schedules is not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607).
10. Harness: subscribes to `rwb.payment.events.v1` and asserts `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` for the case, once for the run, with no personal data on it, and asserts `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the record, reaching the ledger within 5 minutes (DP-03).
11. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` and asserts exactly one record for the fee step, carrying the rule ID and the rule version the owner recorded, and the fee amounts it was based on (REQ-DRI-001).
12. Harness: repeats the run with the decision record forced to fail and asserts that nothing moves: no fee amount, no proceeds match, no approval and no case change, and the message the owner returns. This is the negative path of AC2, whose criterion belongs to RWB-P8-E4045-APP.
13. Harness: authorises each call through `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` and records the refusal path for a role that does not include the right.
14. Harness: publishes one evidence report per story and business date, naming the criterion, the assertions, the contract versions and whether each hop was a stub or the owner. The evidence format and its retention are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A fake answers a shape the published contract does not allow | The run fails at that hop; the report names the service, the operation and the contract version | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The partner read from rwb-partner carries no contracted fee terms for the run's business date | The run fails on AC1 and the report names the partner and the terms it found | None | AC1 |
| X3 | The payment row read from `v_ace_payment` does not carry the `payment_code` the case was seeded with | The run fails on AC1 and the report names the payment row and the code it found | None | AC1 |
| X4 | The fee step returns or records a fee amount that does not follow the schedule read from the owner | The run fails on AC1 and the report names the schedule term, the expected amount and the amount recorded | None | AC1 |
| X5 | A court fee or a legal expense is raised with no approval inside the D7.4 limit | The run fails on AC1 and the report names the fee and the approval it looked for | None | AC1 |
| X6 | The proceeds are applied but no vendor fee is matched on them | The run fails on the R-DIS-54 assertion and the report names the proceeds | None | AC1 |
| X7 | The fee amount does not follow the second partner's contracted schedule, or it stays fixed when the terms differ | The run fails on the data-not-code assertion and the report names both partners and both schedules | None | AC1 |
| X8 | More than one record exists for the fee step, or its rule ID or rule version is missing | The run fails on AC1 and the report names the records it found | None | AC1 |
| X9 | The record does not reach `rwb.decision-record.v1` inside 5 minutes | The run fails on AC1 and the report names the record and its arrival time | None | AC1 |
| X10 | The decision record is forced to fail but a fee amount, a proceeds match or an approval still moves | The run fails on the negative path and the report names what moved | MSG-P7-003 | AC2 path, BR7 |
| X11 | A role that does not include the right is authorised, or a caller outside the case scope passes | The run fails on the access check and the report names the operation | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E4-045-03-ITG |
| X12 | A real service is reachable but its contract version differs from the registry | The run fails before any assertion and the report names the service and both versions | None | AC1 |

The report text is for the wave entry check and is not part of the message standard. R-LIT-41, R-LIT-42, R-DIS-11, R-DIS-54 and R-WO-37 carry no message ID in the rule set, so the harness asserts the state, the data, the proceeds and the decision record, and names a message ID only where an owning service returns one of the three in section 14.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs against published contracts and fakes from Day 1; the only wait is one I story, RWB-P8-E4045-APP |
| Negotiable | The seeding set, the schedule fixture, the report shape and the composite route are configuration agreed at the wave entry check, not business values in code |
| Valuable | The fee amounts, their schedule basis and their record are proven end to end before wave 3 opens |
| Estimable | One harness runner, one stub set, one event probe, one report |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | The criterion runs against its fakes and again against the real owner as RWB-P8-E4045-APP lands |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Calculate fees and charges

  Background:
    Given the seeded case carries a payment on its account and a partner on its contracted fee terms
    And the contract fakes of section 12.8 are published with their versions pinned

  Scenario: AC1 Calculate fees and charges (legacy RWB-E4-045 AC1)
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When its trigger arrives
    Then works out partner fees, court fees and charges from the fee tables held as data
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version
```

AC2 of the legacy key ("Not recorded") is owned by RWB-P8-E4045-APP and is not restated here; the harness exercises it only as the negative path of the same loop, in step 12 of section 4 and in TC-E4-045-02-ITG.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Partner fees, court fees and charges are worked out from the fee tables held as data, never from a value in code | Legacy RWB-E4-045 AC1; REQ-S9-004 |
| BR2 | A partner fee follows the contracted schedule and is paid against recorded results | REQ-S9-004; R-DIS-11; R-WO-37 |
| BR3 | A court fee or legal expense is checked against its schedule and routed for approval inside the D7.4 limit before it is raised | R-LIT-41; R-LIT-42 |
| BR4 | Payments are matched to the plan, the settlement or the fee they belong to by the ACE `payment_code`, and anything unmatched goes to the exception list | REQ-CHO-009 |
| BR5 | A vendor fee is matched when proceeds are applied | R-DIS-54 |
| BR6 | The fee amounts and the rule version are written to the decision record with the change in one transaction | REQ-DRI-001; R-UNI-39 |
| BR7 | No fee action proceeds if its record cannot be written | REQ-DRI-005; R-UNI-39 |

The fee tables' owner and storage are not named by any source read, and the harness reads the fee terms through the owning contracts and holds no copy.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLACED_WITH_AGENCY | PAYMENT_RECEIVED_AFTER_CHARGEOFF | the payment matches the case and the placement | PAYMENT_MATCHED (R-WO-37) |
| ASSET_SOLD | PROCEEDS_POSTED | any | PROCEEDS_APPLIED (R-DIS-54), with the vendor fee matched on the proceeds |
| LEGAL_SPEND_APPROVAL | FEE_APPROVED | inside the D7.4 limit, or the committee approves above it | IN_HEARING (R-LIT-42), with the fee raised and posted against the case |

These are the owner's states: rwb-payment raises PAYMENT_MATCHED and PROCEEDS_APPLIED in its own schema, and the approval inside the D7.4 limit is rwb-access's and rwb-decision's. The harness changes none of them itself. It seeds through the owning services' published operations, drives the fee step through the rwb-payment contract, and then asserts the state the owner reached, naming the owner and the operation behind each move in the report. A state the harness set by hand would prove nothing.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL and the roles that hold Treatment and offer C | Drive the fee step for their case and read the fees, the proceeds and the record through the owning contracts |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-PHONECOL, RW-FIELDCOL, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD and the further roles that hold the case record R | Read the same run evidence, including the partner's fee terms, the payment row and the decision record |
| QA lead | Owns the harness configuration, the seeding set, the report shape and the pass or fail gate |
| Integration lead | Owns the harness code, the stub set and the swap from a fake to the real service |
| The owning services' identities | rwb-payment, rwb-partner, rwb-source-data, rwb-decision and rwb-access make every change the harness asserts |
| No approval level from the delegation of authority applies to the harness | The harness takes no business decision; the approval inside the D7.4 limit belongs to the fee story and to the approver |

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |

| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case | id, case_no, product_group, primary_person_key, status, stage_code | Read, through the rwb-case contract |
| DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054 | v_ace_payment | payment_code, account_key, payment_date, payment_amount, payment_channel, capital_amount | Read, through the rwb-source-data data product (DP-05) |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary, taken from the legacy key. Which field or child record of `partner` carries the contracted fee terms, and which `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` fields carry the calculated fee amounts, are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607). The harness owns no table and writes no row directly: every read and every seed goes through the API of the owning service (DP-01, DP-05), and the payment row is ACE's, so the Workbench holds no payment copy (legacy RWB-E4-045; D-RCV-35 U1 and U4).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/payment/v1/proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` | P8 rwb-payment | Drive the fee step as part of the payment and proceeds match (AC1) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/payment/v1/proceeds` | P8 rwb-payment | The matched proceeds and the fee amounts recorded against them (AC1) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/payment/v1/cases/{caseId}/payments` | P8 rwb-payment | The payments and the fees on the case; Architecture v5 slide 17 gives this path to rwb-payment (AC1) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case state and identity the fee is recorded against (AC1) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` | S9 rwb-partner | The partner record and its contracted fee terms (AC1) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/{productCode}/records` | P1 rwb-source-data | The payment row from `v_ace_payment` (AC1, DP-05) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | The record with the rule ID and the rule version (AC1) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Role and scope, including the refusal path (AC1) |

Every operation is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`, with a 2 s timeout and a circuit breaker per downstream. Where a screen would compose them, the harness calls the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The `{productCode}` that carries the `v_ace_payment` row, the operation and field names that carry the calculated fee amounts in rwb-payment, and the field that carries the contracted fee terms in rwb-partner are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607). No operation is invented in this story.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it drives the fee step through the rwb-payment contract and consumes the owners' events.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` (EV-25) | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | P8 rwb-payment | The fact that the fee step follows, once for the run (AC1) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | every service, through its own local decision-record library | The record written with the fee change reaches the ledger within 5 minutes (AC1, DP-03) |

Both carry IDs and business facts only, keyed by caseId and proceedsId, and the harness asserts that no personal data is present.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness exercises the `matchPayments` and `postProceeds` activities on queue rwb-payment, which carry the fee step and the proceeds posting, and the treatment and settlement path that raises them, and it asserts their effects through the services' contracts and the owner's topic. No workflow, activity or Schedule is created, changed or owned by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added. The fee step is triggered by the payment and the proceeds match and not by a Schedule, and this story sets no cron, overlap policy or catch-up window.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-01); the fees, the proceeds and the payments are rwb-payment's, the partner and its fee terms are rwb-partner's, the record and the rule rows are rwb-decision's, the role, scope and DoA data are rwb-access's, and the payment row is ACE's, read through rwb-source-data's contract (DP-05).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Contract | Use in the run |
|---|---|---|
| Stub for rwb-payment | `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match`, `GET /proceeds`, `GET /cases/{caseId}/payments`, `rwb.payment.events.v1` | Day-1 run of AC1 and of the negative path before RWB-P8-E4045-APP is live |
| Stub for rwb-partner | `GET /partners` | Day-1 assertion of the partner and its contracted fee terms |
| Stub for rwb-source-data | `GET /data-products/{productCode}/records` | Day-1 assertion of the `v_ace_payment` row |
| Stub for rwb-case | `GET /cases/{caseId}` | Day-1 assertion of the case state and identity the fee is recorded against |
| Stub for rwb-decision | `GET /decision-log` | Day-1 assertion of one record for the fee step with its rule version |
| Stub for rwb-access | `POST /authorise` | Day-1 authorisation and refusal path |
| ProceedsMatched event stub | `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` | The fact that the fee step follows, where the environment does not run the payment match |

Each fake is generated from the published OpenAPI or AsyncAPI document of its service, and its version is pinned in the run report, so a contract change shows up as a run failure and not as a silent pass. The fee tables and the court fee and charge schedules, the fee operation and its field names in rwb-payment, the data product code, the harness environment, the seeding set and the evidence format are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 8 consumed, one hop each on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s timeout and a circuit breaker per downstream, composed through gateway-bff where a screen would (DP-19) |
| Kafka | None published; `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` consumed (DP-03) |

| File | None |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform H dependencies in the table above (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H row of this story, which stays None. The blocking dependency is the one I story, RWB-P8-E4045-APP: until it is live the run uses the rwb-payment stub, and a stub pass is reported as a stub pass.

The decoupling is also the story's reading of the legacy behaviour. The legacy key states no endpoint and says the work runs inside the recovery module, so the fee step is the owner's activity and not something the harness computes. The harness owns no schema (DP-01) and reads the fees, the proceeds, the partner, the record and the payment row from their owners only. The payment row is read through rwb-source-data's data product, which owns the ACE view contract, and not through a view of the harness's own (DP-05). The record is read from rwb-decision's contract and the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1` topic rather than from a local log table (DP-03). The composed reads a screen would make are exercised through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| FeeCalculationRunner | Job | Runs the owned criterion and the negative path in order for a business date and holds the run lock |
| StubSet | Fake | The six service stubs and the ProceedsMatched event stub of section 12.8, each generated from the published contract with the version pinned |
| FeeScheduleProbe | Service | Reads the partner's contracted fee terms and the court fee and charge schedules from their owners, and asserts the fee amounts against them rather than against a figure in the script |
| ProceedsProbe | Service | Reads the matched proceeds, the fees on the case and the payment row, and asserts them for the case and the payment |
| EventProbe | Service | Consumes `rwb.payment.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` and asserts the facts for the case |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes the report keyed by story and business date and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the fakes from Day 1 and the real services as they land, with one case carrying a payment on its account and one partner on its contracted fee terms, and one case whose proceeds are applied for the vendor fee path. The environment, the seeding set, the fee tables and the schedules behind it, and the evidence retention are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607). Seeding uses only the owning services' published operations, never a schema write.

**Build steps**

1. Generate the six service stubs and the ProceedsMatched event stub from the published contracts, pin each version in the report and fail the run on a version mismatch (X1, X12).
2. Build the FeeScheduleProbe to read the partner's contracted fee terms and the court fee and charge schedules from their owners, and to fail where the owner publishes none for the business date (X2).
3. Build the ProceedsProbe to read the payment row from `v_ace_payment` and the fees from rwb-payment (X3).
4. Build the FeeCalculationRunner for AC1: drive the fee step, read the matched proceeds and the fees on the case, assert the partner fee against the schedule and the recorded result, and assert the court fee against its schedule and its approval (X4, X5).
5. Add the vendor fee assertion on the R-DIS-54 path: apply the proceeds and assert the vendor fee matched on them (X6).
6. Add the data-not-code assertion: change the schedule held by the owner for the business date and assert the fee follows it, with no change to the harness (X7).
7. Assert one record for the fee step through the rwb-decision contract, naming the rule ID and version and the fee amounts it was based on, and fail where either is absent (X8).
8. Add the EventProbe for `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`, and assert the key, the 5-minute arrival and the absence of personal data (X9).
9. Add the negative path: force the decision record to fail, assert that nothing moves and record the message the owner returns (X10).
10. Add the access path through `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise`, including the refusal for a role that does not include the right (X11).
11. Add the EvidenceReport and the gate, then swap the rwb-payment stub for the real service when RWB-P8-E4045-APP lands and rerun the criterion.

**Feature switch.** The legacy key names no feature switch for this behaviour. The harness runs behind the platform feature-flag library as the wave releases it; the flag key is not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607).

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass; the criterion passes against the fakes on Day 1 and again against rwb-payment when RWB-P8-E4045-APP lands; and the wave entry check holds a report keyed by story and business date with the contract, schedule and fixture versions named.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record for the fee step cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's role does not include the right, or the case is outside their scope | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required value is missing from the request | Enter {field}. |

R-LIT-41, R-LIT-42, R-DIS-11, R-DIS-54 and R-WO-37 carry no message ID in the rule set, so the harness asserts the state, the data and the decision record, and names a message ID only where an owning service returns one of the three above. The harness produces none of these messages itself.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-28 Proceeds matching is the screen the legacy key names for this behaviour:

| State | What the user sees and does |
|---|---|
| Loading | The payment match and the fee step are running for the business date |
| matched | The payment, the proceeds and the fee are aligned to the case and to the partner's schedule |
| unmatched | The payment, a fee or a vendor fee does not align to the case, and an officer has to resolve it on the exception list |

The harness renders no screen. It reads these states through the rwb-payment, rwb-partner, rwb-source-data and rwb-decision contracts, so a passed run means the screen has the right data behind it. What the wave entry check looks at instead is the evidence report, whose format and retention are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0431; ASM-0607).

##### 16. Test cases

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-E4-045-01-ITG | AC1, BR1, BR2, BR3, BR4, BR6 | Integration | Seeded case with a payment and a partner on a contracted fee schedule |
| TC-E4-045-02-ITG | AC2 (owned by RWB-P8-E4045-APP), BR7 | Integration | Decision log forced to fail; MSG-P7-003 |
| TC-E4-045-03-ITG | Access | Component | A role without the right; MSG-P4-002 |
| TC-E4-045-04-ITG | Principle 5 | NFR | Forced decision-log write failure; nothing moves |

These are the ITG copies of TC-E4-045-01 to TC-E4-045-04 and carry the legacy data unchanged, with the component and NFR copies keeping the legacy levels. The full legacy tests, with their Given, When and Then, are in `Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx`, tab Story test cases, under those IDs.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the fee tables, the court fee and charge schedules, the partner's contracted fee terms, the rule versions, the seeding set and the result mappings are data, and the harness holds no copy of any of them.
- No personal data in logs, fixtures, reports, tests or prompts: the events carry IDs and business facts only, and the harness asserts the absence of personal data.
- No read of another service's tables: every read and every seed goes through the owning contract (DP-01), and the payment row is ACE's, read through rwb-source-data's data product (DP-05).
- The Workbench holds no payment copy and writes no fee row outside the owning service; the fee amounts are the owner's and are read back through its contract (legacy RWB-E4-045; D-RCV-35 U1 and U4).
- One hop and a 2 s timeout per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would.
- A stub pass is never reported as a real-service pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and it never sets a fee, a proceeds match, an approval or a decision state by hand.
- A failing assertion is fixed in the service that owns it or reported as a gap; it is never waived in the script.

| REQ-DRI-001 | Every decision writes one record holding case and decision, the rule, model, agent and prompt versions, an inputs snapshot, the recommendation, the approval, the actions taken and the outcome | Business Requirements Program v4, section 5.7 | FEAT-PAY-05 | D6.4 settlement; D7.4 legal spend | R-LIT-41, R-LIT-42, R-DIS-54 | TC-E4-045-01-ITG, TC-E4-045-02-ITG, TC-E4-045-04-ITG |

##### 19. Out of scope

- AC2 of the legacy key, the refusal when the decision log cannot be written, which is owned by RWB-P8-E4045-APP; this story exercises it only as a negative path.
- The production payment endpoint and the fee step inside rwb-payment, which are RWB-P8-E4045-APP: the fee calculation, the proceed and fee records and the posting file.
- The fee tables themselves and the court fee and charge schedules, their owner, their storage, their table and field names and the business values they hold.
- The contract baselines of rwb-payment, rwb-partner, rwb-source-data, rwb-decision and rwb-access, which are their CON stories and are consumed here through the published documents and their fakes.
- The platform configuration: the decision-record library, the gateway-bff composite route, the feature-flag library and the observability set.
- The partner portal and the partner gateway: the panel, the partner users and how a partner submits a result, which belong to rwb-partner.
- The approval itself inside the D7.4 limit and the DoA table behind it, which belong to the fee story, to rwb-access and to rwb-decision.
- Any production screen, event, workflow, Schedule or table: this story builds a test harness and its evidence only.
- The fixture contents, the harness environment, the evidence format and its retention, and the feature flag key: carried as a gap and an assumption, not decided here.
