##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead of rwb-payment**, I want **the published rental profile of the payment contract - the two operations `GET /proceeds` and `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` on `/api/recovery/payment/v1` with the rental fields of `MatchRequest` and `Proceeds`, the rental element of the `payment_match_rule` row, the `PaymentMissed` and `ProceedsMatched` schemas with their rental facts on `rwb.payment.events.v1`, the `proceeds` table template, the error envelope, the rights, the compatibility rule and the fakes**, so that **RWB-P8-E4048-APP, SCR-28 and the wave 3 harness build against one fixed rental contract on Day 1, and the rental amount, the debit day, the match state or the arrears event can never drift between rwb-payment, rwb-treatment, rwb-case and the screens without a failing build**.

This is the contract slice of legacy RWB-E4-048 (FEAT-PAY-09, module P8 Payments and posting). It owns the published surface of the rental arm only. It owns no behaviour and copies no legacy criterion: the two legacy acceptance criteria of the key stay word for word with RWB-P8-E4048-APP (GAP-2527; ASM-4177).

The base surface of `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, the `proceeds` element group and the three payment event schemas are declared once by RWB-P8-E4043-CON. This profile declares the rental additions to that surface and the rental fakes, and it never redefines a member it does not own (GAP-2527; ASM-4177).

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (ADR-020), and the rental arm is the clearest case of it in this service. In the monolith the rental was a treatment row, an auto-debit instruction, a `v_ace_payment` read, a `proceeds` row and a task in one process: no boundary existed that rwb-treatment, rwb-case or the screens could build against, so every reader of the rental was also a reader of four other modules' tables.

In the target the rental has two owners and one seam. rwb-treatment owns the rental record, its amount, its debit day and the arrears limit (FEAT-TRT-16, R-DIL-32, R-DIL-34). rwb-payment owns the receipt, its match, the arrears announcement and the posting (TSD P8 T3.1; Ownership Map, `proceeds` owner P8). The seam is this document: the rental read as a consumed answer, the receipt as a published element, and `PaymentMissed` as the announcement that lets rwb-treatment apply the arrears rule without reading a payment table.

Three teams need it on Day 1. RWB-P8-E4048-APP builds the rental arm of JOB-07 and cannot start until the request element, the match value, the event names and the fakes are fixed. rwb-treatment consumes `PaymentMissed` and must pin a schema while its own rental record is being written. SCR-28 reaches both operations through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), so the screen answer, the pagination and the error envelope have to be settled before the screen work starts.

The profile also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_payment`, base `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, topic `rwb.payment.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt` topics, event names `rwb.payment.<Event>.v1`, queue `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.payment` (Template and Rules R4). It records that this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant, so DP-05 is a prohibition: the receipt arrives on rwb-source-data's contract and never through a view of this service.

Two points are carried as gaps rather than decided quietly. `LOV-MATCH` holds no value that names a rental, so the rental receipt is matched to INSTALLMENT and the assumption is recorded (GAP-2528; ASM-4172). The payloads of `PaymentMissed` and `ProceedsMatched` are published in part only - `PaymentMissed` has a full example on Architecture v5 slide 22 and `ProceedsMatched` has a consumer list and no payload - so the rental fields beyond the example are marked with the placeholder (GAP-2526; ASM-4178).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service naming rule is in force: base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`, topic `rwb.<short>.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt`, event names `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1`, queue `rwb-<short>`, login and schema `rwb_<short>` (Template and Rules R4; Architecture v5 slide 41 notes).
- RWB-P8-E4043-CON has published the base surface: the two operations, the `Proceeds`, `ProceedsPage` and `MatchRequest` elements, the `proceeds` table template and the three payment event schemas. This profile is additive on it and declares no member of it a second time.
- The platform error envelope, the pagination convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline (Architecture v5 slide 11); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The ownership of the objects is taken from the Ownership Map only: `proceeds`, `payment_match_rule` and the two operations are P8's, the treatment and the rental record are S2's, `recovery_case` is P3's, the `v_ace_*` views and the ACE batch are P1's, `rule_row` and `rule_package_version` are P7's. No other service's operation or table is declared as provided.
- The operations and their base shapes are those of TSD P8 T-A.1 and T-A.2: API-P8-001 `GET /proceeds` with `ProceedsPage` out and errors 401, 403 and 503, and API-P8-002 `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` with `MatchRequest` in, `Proceeds` out, errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, and the `Idempotency-Key` header.
- The columns and the lists are those of TSD P8 T3.1 and T3.2: DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 for `proceeds`, DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 for `payment_match_rule`, LOV-MATCH, LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC and LOV-MATCH-TYPE.
- The events are those of Architecture v5 slides 22, 42 and 43: `PaymentMissed` (12) with the published example `caseId`, `treatmentId`, `dueDate`, `amountDue` and `daysLate`, and consumers rwb-case, rwb-treatment and rwb-comms; `ProceedsMatched` (25) with consumers rwb-case, rwb-asset, rwb-debtsale, rwb-writeoff and rwb-guarantee. `TreatmentBooked` (11) belongs to the booking profile and is not declared here.
- The schema registry is in BACKWARD mode and an AsyncAPI document per service is the contract, so every event is registered against it (Architecture v5 slide 42 notes).
- The `proceeds` table arrives with the DB story of this service; this profile declares its rental constraints and creates nothing.
- RWB-P8-E4048-APP, SCR-28 and the wave 3 harness are the consumers of this profile but are not build dependencies: this story has none and is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules R5.7).
- No approval is needed to publish a Draft baseline in this run, and no human verification stop is part of it (ASM-4180).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the additive profile of the rwb-payment OpenAPI document for the rental arm: the request fields of the match that the rental needs, the answer fields the rental shows, the rights and the errors.
2. Fix the rental values of `MatchRequest`: the case reference, the treatment reference, the receipt reference, the amount, the received date and the match value INSTALLMENT; mark every field no source gives with the placeholder.
3. Fix the rental group of `Proceeds`: the treatment reference of DF-FIN-003, the receipt reference of DF-FIN-004, the source of DF-FIN-005, the amount of DF-FIN-006, the received date of DF-FIN-007, the match value of DF-FIN-008 and the posting reference of DF-FIN-009.
4. Publish the `payment_match_rule` element of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 as read-only reference data of the service, with its lists, and fix the rule that no window, grace, tolerance, floor or priority is a constant of the code.
5. Draft the AsyncAPI fragment for `PaymentMissed` and `ProceedsMatched` with the CloudEvents envelope, `ce_source` `/rwb-payment`, key `caseId` and no personal data.
6. Fix the rental constraints of the `proceeds` template: the unique key of a receipt, the index of the match state, and the rule that no foreign key leaves `rwb_payment`.
7. Record the consumed rental read, the receipt read, the case answer and the package read as consumed and faked.
8. Fix the error envelope, one message ID per condition, the rights of the capability area Write-off and posting, and the `Idempotency-Key` rule with its stored answer.
9. Publish the five fakes and the drift test that compares each with the document.
10. Add the contract tests and tag the baseline for RWB-P8-E4048-APP, SCR-28 and the wave 3 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A body fails schema validation | The pipeline schema lint fails; a deployed service answers 400 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | A path, a property or a list value is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC7 |
| X3 | A fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC6, AC7 |
| X4 | A field of `MatchRequest` or of an event payload has no source value | The row carries the placeholder, the gap and the assumption, and the fake derives from the document | None | AC3, AC4 |
| X5 | A value outside LOV-MATCH, LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC or LOV-MATCH-TYPE appears in the document, an example or a fake | The vocabulary test fails the build | None | AC3 |
| X6 | The profile declares another service's operation as provided, a `v_ace_*` view, or a `treatment`, `recovery_case` or `rule_row` property | The review fails the baseline and the boundary test fails the build | None | AC7 |
| X7 | A POST is repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key` | The stored answer is returned and no second effect is described | None | AC2 |
| X8 | The rights of an operation are not the ones TSD P8 T6.1 declares | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |
| X9 | The profile restates a member of the base surface of RWB-P8-E4043-CON | The review fails the profile as a duplicate and the drift test names the owner | None | AC7 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the Ownership Map, TSD P8 and the base surface of RWB-P8-E4043-CON only |
| Negotiable | The added element names, the example values and the fixtures are settled in the review; the paths, the columns, the lists, the base, the topic and the event names are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks the rental arm, SCR-28 and the wave 3 harness on Day 1, and pins `PaymentMissed` for rwb-treatment |
| Estimable | One additive profile, one AsyncAPI fragment with two schemas, nine contract tables and five fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

These seven criteria are new for the contract profile and test the artefact only. They restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P8-E4048-APP and they copy no criterion of the legacy story, whose two criteria stay with the app story word for word (GAP-2527; ASM-4177).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The receipt and its match are P8's: `proceeds` in `rwb_payment` carries the case, the treatment, the account payment, the source, the amount, the received date, `matched_to` and the posting reference, and the profile declares their shapes only | TSD P8 T3.1; Ownership Map (`proceeds` owner P8) |
| BR2 | The vocabulary is closed: `source` is one value of LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC, `matched_to` is one value of LOV-MATCH, `match_type` is one value of LOV-MATCH-TYPE, and the rental receipt closes to INSTALLMENT because no list value names a rental | TSD P8 T3.2; GAP-2528; ASM-4172 |
| BR3 | The decision record is declared as an element written in the transaction of the row, through the local library on the shared topic, and a failed write is MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; legacy RWB-E4-048 AC2, owned by the app story; ADR-022 |
| BR4 | No ACE view and no ACE table is read: the receipt and the account are consumed on rwb-source-data's contract and the service holds no `v_ace_*` grant | DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR5 | The rental, its amount, its debit day and its arrears limit stay with rwb-treatment; the profile declares the rental read as consumed and declares no property of it | Ownership Map (treatment S2); FSD P8 A2.9 (prerequisite FEAT-TRT-16) |
| BR6 | The case stays with rwb-case and the package with rwb-decision: the profile declares the case answer and the package read as consumed and no property of them | DP-01; Ownership Map (recovery_case P3, rule_row P7) |
| BR7 | A POST declares the `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer; a GET declares none | TSD P8 T-A.2; Architecture v5 slide 11 |
| BR8 | One REST base, one topic, one queue and one login per service, and the profile declares no member of another service's base or topic as its own | DP-13, DP-14; Template and Rules R4 |
| BR9 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version with a new event type | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD) |
| BR10 | The events carry identifiers, amounts, dates and a rule version only, never a name, an address, a contact value or an identity number | Template and Rules R7.2 (s17); Architecture v5 slide 22 notes |
| BR11 | The base surface, the `Proceeds` element group and `TreatmentBooked` are RWB-P8-E4043-CON's; this profile adds the rental members and restates none | GAP-2527; ASM-4177 |
| BR12 | The rental arm is a step of the JOB-07 run started by `AceDataReady`; the profile declares no Schedule and no new workflow | Architecture v5 slide 44; GAP-2524; ASM-4174 |

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of this profile, not of a receipt:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The two operations, the rental elements, the two event schemas and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | RWB-P8-E4048-APP, SCR-28, the wave 3 harness and the rwb-treatment, rwb-source-data, rwb-case and rwb-decision owners accept the profile and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1 | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A path, a property or a list value is removed, renamed or retyped | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A duplicate of the base surface appears | X9 fires and the review names the owner document | In review |

The receipt state the profile describes is the app story's: `matched_to` is one value of LOV-MATCH, the rental receipt is INSTALLMENT, and a rental with no receipt has no row at all. This baseline fixes the vocabulary and moves no receipt.

The per-service login behind the security scheme is named "the rwb-payment login" and is not part of this profile.

The profile declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Proceeds rental fields | DF-FIN-003 `treatment_id`, DF-FIN-004 `account_payment_id`, DF-FIN-005 `source`, DF-FIN-006 `amount`, DF-FIN-007 `received_date`, DF-FIN-008 `matched_to`, DF-FIN-009 `posting_ref` |
| standard record columns | `is_active`, `state`, `version`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at` and `updated_by` of TSD P8 T3.0 |
| Lists | LOV-MATCH (INSTALLMENT, SETTLEMENT, FEE, SALE_PROCEEDS, UNMATCHED), LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC (CUSTOMER, LED, AUCTION, BUYER, AGENCY, INSURER, GUARANTOR) and LOV-MATCH-TYPE (EXACT, WINDOW, PARTIAL) of TSD P8 T3.2 |
| `payment_match_rule` element | DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273, read-only reference data of the service |
| MatchRequest rental fields | The fields the rental match needs, with the placeholder where no source gives them: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2526; ASM-4178) |
| PaymentMissed payload | The published example fields `caseId`, `treatmentId`, `dueDate`, `amountDue` and `daysLate` of Architecture v5 slide 22 |
| ProceedsMatched payload | The identifiers and facts of the modelled row, with the fields no source gives carried as Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2526; ASM-4178) |
| Decision record | DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 through the local library, written in the transaction of the row (DP-03) |
| Not declared here | `treatment` and the rental record (S2), `recovery_case` (P3), the `v_ace_*` views (P1) and `rule_row`, `rule_package_version` and `decision_log_entry` (P7): each is named as an answer or a rule version of its owner |

The field types, lengths and required flags of the added members are settled in the review; this story fixes the member names, the vocabulary of AC3 and the optionality rule of BR9. **No new table, no new column and no migration** is created by this story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-payment (P8); base `/api/recovery/payment/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/proceeds` | `ProceedsPage` out, filtered by `matched`, `from` and `to`, paginated by `page` and `size`, each item carrying the rental fields of DF-FIN-003 to DF-FIN-009 (API-P8-001) | Write-off and posting, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` | `MatchRequest` in with the rental fields, `Proceeds` out (API-P8-002) | Write-off and posting, right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header required; the answer is stored |

The two operations answer 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, each with the error envelope and one message ID of section 14. The operation IDs, the base surface and the element groups are RWB-P8-E4043-CON's; this profile adds the rental members of AC3 and declares no third operation (GAP-2527; ASM-4177).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the profile |
|---|---|---|---|
| The rental read of the business date (name and fields Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2523; ASM-4173)) | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` | S2 rwb-treatment | The rentals due on the business date: rental, treatment, case, rental amount, debit day and due date; faked |
| The receipt read of the ACE batch (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2524; ASM-4175)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The receipts of the business date for source `ALS`, the batch status and the freshness stamp; faked |
| The case read and money-side answer (name Not specified) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference, its route state and the answer that applies the money side; faked |
| The rule-package read (name Not specified) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The package at its version in force for the business date; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The four rows are contract dependencies of class C in fact and the plan's C row for this story is None, so the app story builds against these documents and fakes from Day 1 (GAP-2524; ASM-4175).

###### 12.3 Events published

Topic `rwb.payment.events.v1` with the `.retry` and `.dlt` topics, key `caseId`, CloudEvents 1.0 binary.

| Event | Schema name | Consumers | Payload element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PaymentMissed` (EV-12) | `rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1` | rwb-case, rwb-treatment, rwb-comms | `caseId`, `treatmentId`, `dueDate`, `amountDue` and `daysLate`, as the published example of Architecture v5 slide 22; any further field is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2526; ASM-4178) |
| `ProceedsMatched` (EV-25) | `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` | rwb-case, rwb-asset, rwb-debtsale, rwb-writeoff, rwb-guarantee | The case, proceeds and treatment references, the amount, the value date, the match value and the rule identity with its version; the remaining field list is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2526; ASM-4178) |

Each message declares the CloudEvents 1.0 binary envelope with `ce_specversion`, `ce_type`, `ce_source` `/rwb-payment`, `ce_id`, `ce_subject` `case/<caseId>` and a W3C `traceparent` header, and the body is validated against the registry in BACKWARD mode. `TreatmentBooked` (EV-11) is RWB-P8-E4043-CON's and is not restated here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Consumer group | Payload used | When |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AceDataReady` (EV-26) | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | `rwb-payment.match-run.v1` | The business date and the source of the completed batch | Starts the JOB-07 run the rental arm is a step of |
| `TreatmentApproved` (EV-10) | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | `rwb-payment.match-run.v1` | The case, the treatment reference and the treatment type | Declared as consumed by the matching stories |
| `RulePackageInForce` (EV-30) | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | `rwb-payment.match-run.v1` | The package code and the version in force | Declared as consumed by the matching stories |

`DecisionRecorded` (EV-08) is written by all nineteen services through the local library on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; rwb-payment is a producer of that topic and not a consumer, so the profile declares no subscription or inbox row for it (DP-03).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| The JOB-07 event-started run (`PaymentMatchingWorkflow` in the matching story; the name is a target design choice) | Workflow, one execution per business date and source, started by `AceDataReady` | `rwb-payment` in `rwb-recovery` | The boundary the rental arm runs inside; not built here |
| `matchPayments` | Activity, the matching step | `rwb-payment` | The activity contract the profile serves: the rentals and the receipts in; the rule identity with its version, the match outcome, the record, the row and the outbox event out |
| The rental arm (a step of `matchPayments`; the name is a target design choice) | Activity step | `rwb-payment` | Declared only as a step of the run, with no workflow, child workflow or Nexus operation of its own |

The profile registers no workflow. The ownership rows of P8 hold no workflow of the service, and the rental arm is a step of the run that already exists (GAP-2524; ASM-4174).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-07 and JOB-08 are event-triggered runs and not Temporal Schedules (Architecture v5 slide 44), the rental due date is a fact of the rental read, and the profile declares no Schedule, Quartz row or shared job table.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| `proceeds` | P8 (`rwb_payment`) | The receipt and its match; the table the two operations read and the match writes; the rental constraints of AC5 |
| `payment_match_rule` | P8 (`rwb_payment`) | The match rules read in force; declared read-only here, written by the matching-rule story |
| `decision_record` | PLT library, created in `rwb_payment` | The local record of the step (DP-03) |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_payment` | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects (the library's, not a pattern of this key) |

`treatment` and the rental record are S2's, `recovery_case` is P3's, the `v_ace_*` views are P1's and `rule_row` and `rule_package_version` are P7's; the profile names them only as answers and rule versions, and no foreign key leaves `rwb_payment` (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-treatment rental fake | Rental `RT-2026-000701` of treatment `DIL-2026-000701` on case `RC-2026-000701` with its amount and due date 2026-12-15; a treatment with no rental; no answer beyond 2 s | AC1, AC3, AC6 |
| rwb-source-data receipt fake | Receipt `PAY-90701` of the business date 2026-12-15; a receipt 3 days after the due date; no receipt; a batch that is not complete with MSG-P1-001 | AC1, AC4, AC6 |
| rwb-case fake | The case reference with its route state; an accepted and a refused money-side answer | AC1, AC2, AC6 |
| rwb-decision package fake | The package at its version in force for 2026-12-15 | AC1, AC6 |
| Local record library stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy write and a refused write with MSG-P7-003 | AC2, AC6 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT. The operation names of the rental read, the receipt read, the case answer and the package read are derived from their owners' published documents and carry the placeholder until the owners confirm them (GAP-2523, GAP-2524; ASM-4173, ASM-4175).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 4 consumed | The two operations on `/api/recovery/payment/v1`; the rental, receipt, case and package rows; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 2 published, 3 consumed | `PaymentMissed` and `ProceedsMatched` on `rwb.payment.events.v1`; `AceDataReady`, `TreatmentApproved` and `RulePackageInForce` in group `rwb-payment.match-run.v1` |
| Temporal | 1 run boundary and 1 activity declared, 0 registered | The JOB-07 run on `rwb-payment` with `matchPayments`; the rental arm is a step; no Schedule |
| File | None | No file is read, built or delivered by this profile |

##### 13. Solution plan

**The profile declares shapes and moves nothing.** It writes no code, no migration and no table, and changes no receipt, no rental, no case and no package. What it publishes is one additive profile of the OpenAPI document, one AsyncAPI fragment with two schemas, nine contract tables and five fakes.

**Deliverables.** The additive profile of `openapi/rwb-payment-v1.yaml` for the rental arm, the rental members of `Proceeds` and `MatchRequest`, the read-only `payment_match_rule` element, the two JSON schemas with the CloudEvents envelope, the contract README rows for the four consumed rows and their placeholders, and the five WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is declared as a prohibition: only rwb-source-data holds SELECT on the `recovery.v_ace_*` views (Architecture v5 slide 29), so the profile declares no ACE view and the `v_ace_payment` receipt of DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054 is consumed on the owner's contract instead. DP-03 fixes the record element written in the transaction of the row; DP-13 keeps the base and adds nothing; DP-19 is behind SCR-28, whose screen model is the edge contract's. The outbox and inbox objects are library objects of the service template and are not a pattern of this key.

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** This is a CON story with no build dependency: it is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules R5.7). The two H rows of DP-03 and DP-19 are the platform contracts it builds against, and the four consumed rows are class C in fact and are declared as consumed and faked (GAP-2524; ASM-4175).

**Build steps.** (1) The rental members of the two operations, AC1. (2) The error envelope, the rights and the `Idempotency-Key` rule, AC2. (3) The `Proceeds` and `MatchRequest` rental fields, the three lists and the read-only rule element, AC3. (4) The two event schemas with the envelope and the no-personal-data rule, AC4. (5) The rental constraints of the `proceeds` template and the no-cross-schema-key test, AC5. (6) The five fakes and the drift test, AC6. (7) The compatibility rule, the boundary to the base surface and the absence test, AC7.

**Done when.** The profile validates in the pipeline, the seven contract tests pass, the five fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, the two event schemas register in BACKWARD mode, and the app story, SCR-28 and the wave 3 harness have accepted the profile.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of `MatchRequest` is absent or invalid, or a body fails schema validation | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the Write-off and posting right the operation declares | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written in the transaction of the row | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The data product of the source is stale after a late or failed ACE batch | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-P8-002 | No `payment_match_rule` row is in force on the business date | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2522; ASM-4179) |

The message IDs are contract elements and the text is the legacy and FSD wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and no new identifier is invented. MSG-P1-001 and MSG-P8-002 are carried because they are in the message set of this feature and are raised by the app story, not by this baseline.

##### 15. Screens and states

The profile serves SCR-28 Proceeds matching in its Loading, matched and unmatched states through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The route calls rwb-payment for `GET /proceeds` and `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match`, rwb-case for the case and its route state and rwb-treatment for the rental; this profile fixes the rwb-payment answers only, and the composite route, the field list and the merge order belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The refusal and failure states the screen shows - refused with MSG-P4-002, not recorded with MSG-P7-003, stale data with MSG-P1-001 - read the messages of section 14 on the same route.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the rental amount, the debit day, the arrears limit, the window, the grace, the tolerance, the floor, the priority and the rule IDs stay rows of the rental read or of `payment_match_rule`, never a schema default, an example constant or an enumeration member of the code.
- No personal data in a schema, an example, an event payload or a fake: identifiers, amounts, dates, list values and a rule version only, and every example is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the service holds no `v_ace_*` grant, so the profile declares no ACE view and no ACE table (DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 29).
- The rental stays with rwb-treatment, the case with rwb-case, the package with rwb-decision and the rights with rwb-access: the profile declares none of their properties and writes none of their rows (DP-01).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service: `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, `rwb.payment.events.v1`, `rwb-payment` and the `rwb_payment` login, and a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13).
- The profile lists only operations owned by rwb-payment, and every member of the base surface stays RWB-P8-E4043-CON's; a duplicate fails X9 and the drift test (BR11).
- No Schedule, Quartz row or shared job table is declared, and the rental arm is a step of the event-started run (BR12).
- The error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the naming rule and the record library come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

##### 1. Story

As a **sale officer**, I want **the Workbench to take the rental of a deed in lieu buy-back by auto-debit, issue the receipt as a `proceeds` row of `rwb_payment`, and follow up the arrears as `PaymentMissed` on the payment topic - with the rental terms read from the rwb-treatment contract, the debit facts read from rwb-source-data, the run started by the ACE batch event and the local decision record written with the rule version in the same transaction**, so that **every rental of a buy-back is matched to its case without a person, and a rental that falls behind is found the next morning instead of at month end**.

Inside `rwb-payment`, schema `rwb_payment`, base `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, topic `rwb.payment.events.v1`, queue `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.payment`:

- The rental arm of the JOB-07 payment matching run: it reads the rentals due on the business date, reads the receipts of that date, matches them with the `payment_match_rule` rows in force and writes the result (DP-13 keeps the base, DP-05 keeps the ACE facts with their owner).
- The receipt: one `proceeds` row of `rwb_payment` with `source` CUSTOMER and `matched_to` INSTALLMENT, from DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009, written by the rental arm and by the manual `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match`.
- The announcement: `ProceedsMatched` (EV-25) on a matched rental and `PaymentMissed` (EV-12) when the rental is not received inside the window in force, both through the outbox in the transaction that writes the row.
- The record: the local decision record of the step, written through the RWB-PLT-E1027-CON library inside the caller's transaction, with the rule identity and version of the `payment_match_rule` row that decided the match (DP-03).
- The service side of SCR-28 Proceeds matching, reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

It does not own: the deed in lieu rental record, its amount, its debit day and its arrears limit, which are rwb-treatment's (S2, FEAT-TRT-16, rules R-DIL-32 and R-DIL-34); the ACE receipt, batch and freshness facts, which are rwb-source-data's (P1); the case, the owner's task and the route state, which are rwb-case's (P3); the rule packages, which are rwb-decision's (P7); the rights and scope data, which are rwb-access's (P4); the published shapes, the event schemas, the error envelope and the fakes, which are RWB-P8-E4048-CON; the receipt notice, which is rwb-comms' (P6); the deployment of this build, which is the operations story of this key.

##### 2. Business rationale

A deed in lieu ends with the asset on the bank's books and the customer renting it back. The business objective of the feature is fixed and unchanged: take the rental by auto-debit, issue the receipt and follow up the arrears without a person for a standard arrangement (FSD P8 A2.9; FEAT-PAY-09; legacy RWB-E4-048). The legacy story ran that loop as one service method against one `recovery` schema, and the same arrangement was written one epic ahead as FEAT-TRT-16 in rwb-treatment (FSD S2, rule R-DIL-32).

What D-RCV-60 changes is where each half lives. The rental record, its terms, the auto-debit instruction and the arrears limit stay with rwb-treatment, which owns treatments, deed in lieu agreements and plan timers. The money side - the receipt, its match to the case and the treatment, the arrears follow-up and the posting - is rwb-payment's, which owns payment and proceeds matching and the `proceeds` row (TSD P8 T3.1; Ownership Map, `proceeds` owner P8; Architecture v5 slide 4, P8 Payments and posting). The two halves meet at one read and one event: the rental read of rwb-treatment, and `PaymentMissed`, which rwb-treatment consumes to apply R-DIL-34 when the arrears exceed the limit.

The loop reports itself in the open. Instead of a private arrears table, the receipt is a `proceeds` row with `matched_to` INSTALLMENT and the arrears follow-up is `PaymentMissed` with `caseId`, `treatmentId`, `dueDate`, `amountDue` and `daysLate` (Architecture v5 slide 22). That is what lets rwb-case raise the owner's task, rwb-treatment hand the asset to the disposal route under R-DIL-34, rwb-comms notify and the reporting read model count the rental, without one service reading another's table.

The record moves with the write: the local decision record is written in the same transaction as the `proceeds` row, so a rental that cannot be recorded changes nothing (DP-03; ADR-022). AC2 is exactly that rule.

No business value is invented. The rental amount, the debit day and the arrears limit that the legacy text does not state stay unstated here, with the placeholder and the recorded gap, and every list value, field type and message is the value the FSD, the TSD and the legacy story already carry, read in force.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P8-E4048-CON is published: base `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, `GET /proceeds` with `ProceedsPage`, `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` with `MatchRequest` in and `Proceeds` out, the error set with the problem body, the `Idempotency-Key` header, the `proceeds` DDL template, the `PaymentMissed` and `ProceedsMatched` schemas and the fakes. This story builds against that contract and its fake.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: `DecisionRecordWriter.record(DecisionRecord)` declared with `@Transactional(propagation = MANDATORY)`, failing with MSG-P7-003, and the `decision_record` template applied in this service's own schema (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-28 from the proceeds read, the case read of rwb-case and the treatment read of rwb-treatment, one hop each, read only (DP-19).
- The `rwb_payment` baseline exists from the service template: schema, login, outbox, inbox and idempotency objects, and the per-service Flyway sequence (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON). This story adds no table of its own and never edits an applied migration.
- rwb-source-data publishes the receipt read of the business date for source `ALS`, the batch status of that source and the freshness stamp of the data product, one hop with a 2 s timeout (DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 29). This service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and reads no ACE table.
- rwb-treatment publishes the read of the buy-back rentals due on a business date: the rental reference, the treatment reference, the case reference, the rental amount, the debit day and the due date. The field names of that answer are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2523; ASM-4173) and are settled with rwb-treatment before the build.
- The `payment_match_rule` rows in force for the business date carry `rule_code`, `rule_version`, `match_type`, `amount_tolerance_pct`, `window_days_before`, `window_days_after`, `grace_days`, `partial_floor_pct` and `priority`, with the match types EXACT, WINDOW and PARTIAL (TSD P8 T3.1, T3.2). The rule code of the rental arm is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2524; ASM-4181).
- The lists LOV-MATCH, LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC and LOV-MATCH-TYPE are read as data with their version; no member of any of them is written in code (BR-P8-009; TSD P8 T3.2).
- The workflow kit is provisioned on queue `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and the JOB-07 run of a business date is started by the `AceDataReady` event through the inbox of the outbox library, so a redelivered event starts no second run.
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline, and a story with only CON build dependencies is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-source-data publishes `AceDataReady` (EV-26) on `rwb.source-data.events.v1` for source `ALS` and the business date 2026-12-15; the inbox of this service records the event id, so a redelivery starts no second run.
2. The JOB-07 run of that date starts on queue `rwb-payment` and checks the batch status and freshness of the source. A batch that is not complete stops the run before matching, and the plan view shows MSG-P1-001 with the date the product carries.
3. The run loads the `payment_match_rule` rows in force for the date and stops before matching if none is in force (MSG-P8-002).
4. The rental arm reads the rentals due on 2026-12-15 from rwb-treatment: rental `RT-2026-000701` of treatment `DIL-2026-000701` on case `RC-2026-000701` and account `A-0701`, with its rental amount and its due date.
5. It reads the receipts of 2026-12-15 from rwb-source-data: `payment_code`, `account_key`, `payment_date`, `payment_amount`, `payment_channel` and the capital columns of the account payment.
6. It matches each rental to a receipt in priority order: EXACT on the amount and the due date, then WINDOW inside `window_days_before`, `window_days_after` and `grace_days`, then PARTIAL above `partial_floor_pct` inside `amount_tolerance_pct`.
7. A rental that matched: in one `rwb_payment` transaction the run writes one `proceeds` row with `case_id`, `treatment_id`, `account_payment_id`, `source` CUSTOMER, `amount`, `received_date`, `matched_to` INSTALLMENT and `posting_ref`, its local decision record with the rule identity and version of the row that decided the match, the outbox row of `ProceedsMatched` (EV-25) and the idempotency row of the step.
8. The receipt is issued: `ProceedsMatched` names the case, the treatment and the receipt, rwb-case applies the money side, rwb-comms issues the notice and SCR-28 shows the rental matched.
9. A rental with no receipt inside the window: no `proceeds` row is written, because no money arrived. The run writes the local decision record and the outbox row of `PaymentMissed` (EV-12) with `caseId`, `treatmentId`, `dueDate` 2026-12-15, the `amountDue` the terms carry and `daysLate`.
10. The arrears follow-up: rwb-case raises the owner's task, rwb-treatment applies R-DIL-34 when the arrears exceed the limit, and rwb-comms notifies. One missed event is published per rental due date, never one per run.
11. The manual path: a sale officer or a Credit Administration officer matches an unmatched rental receipt with `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` and an `Idempotency-Key`; the same record, row change and event follow, once.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The ACE batch of source `ALS` is not complete for the business date | The run stops before matching; no `proceeds` row and no event is written | MSG-P1-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | No `payment_match_rule` row is in force on the business date | The run stops before matching; the job monitor shows the run failed and Credit Administration is alerted | MSG-P8-002 | AC1 |
| X3 | A rental has no receipt inside the window in force | No `proceeds` row; one decision record and one `PaymentMissed` for the due date; the arrears task is rwb-case's | MSG-P8-001 | AC1 |
| X4 | A receipt matches no rental | It is left for the unmatched exception list of the exception-list story; this arm writes no row for it | MSG-P8-001 | AC1 |
| X5 | The same business date, the same receipt or the same event arrives twice | One `proceeds` row, one record and one event; the repeat is counted and the first id answered | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X6 | The decision record cannot be written | The transaction rolls back: no `proceeds` row, no event, and the caller sees MSG-P7-003 | MSG-P7-003 | AC2 |
| X7 | The rwb-treatment or rwb-source-data answer does not arrive inside 2 s | The rental of that answer is left unmatched for the run; the breaker opens and the next run retries | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1 |
| X8 | A role without the Write-off and posting right, or a case outside scope | Refused with MSG-P4-002 or 404, and nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | AC1 |

The rental-side exceptions of the legacy story - a customer who never debited, an auto-debit refused by the bank and a rental whose arrangement was withdrawn - are decided in rwb-treatment under R-DIL-32 and R-DIL-34 and are proved by that service's stories. This story neither evaluates them nor writes their state.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P8-E4048-CON, the record library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and the composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the rental, receipt, case and package answers are consumed from their owners' published contracts and fakes |
| Negotiable | Nothing business is fixed: the rental amount, the debit day, the arrears limit, the window, the tolerance, the grace and the match priority are rows of the rental read or of `payment_match_rule` |
| Valuable | Every rental of a buy-back is matched to its case without a person, and a rental that falls behind is visible the next morning |
| Estimable | One rental read, one receipt read, one matcher, one writer, one record and two events |
| Small | One sprint with its tests, as the payment slice of a legacy key that rwb-treatment also serves |
| Testable | Both criteria of section 7 are automated on the synthetic rental and receipt fixtures |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Run the deed in lieu rental auto-debit

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-000701" carries deed in lieu treatment "DIL-2026-000701" with buy-back rental "RT-2026-000701" on account "A-0701", due on 2026-12-15
    Given the business date is 2026-12-15 and the ACE batch for source ALS of that date is COMPLETE in the batch status of rwb-source-data
    Given the payment_match_rule rows in force for 2026-12-15 carry their rule_code, rule_version, match types, windows, grace, tolerance and priority
    Given the lists LOV-MATCH, LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC and LOV-MATCH-TYPE are read with their version

  Scenario: AC1 Run the deed in lieu rental auto-debit (legacy RWB-E4-048 AC1)
    Given the rwb-treatment contract mock returns the buy-back rental "RT-2026-000701" of treatment "DIL-2026-000701" with its rental amount, its debit day and due date 2026-12-15
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns receipt "PAY-90701" of the rental amount on account "A-0701" dated 2026-12-15, and a rental with no receipt at all
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When its trigger arrives
    Then takes the rental by auto-debit, issues the receipt and follows up arrears
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E4-048 AC2)
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns a failed decision-log write with MSG-P7-003
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003
```

The two criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E4-048 word for word, with their origin tag added and nothing else changed: the legacy wording of `its trigger arrives`, `the action is taken` and `the decision log cannot be written` all stand. One leading `Given` group is added to each, and those lines are the only additions: AC1 needs the rental read of rwb-treatment and the receipt read of rwb-source-data, which are other services' facts, and AC2 needs the failed write of the record library. What the legacy lines describe happens in five places in the target: rwb-source-data answers the receipts and the batch status, rwb-treatment answers the rental and applies R-DIL-34 on the arrears, this story matches the rental, writes the `proceeds` row, records the decision and publishes `ProceedsMatched` or `PaymentMissed`, rwb-case raises the owner's task, and rwb-comms issues the notice. Because the legacy criteria are generic, the rental detail behind them is filled from FSD P8 A2.9, TSD P8 and the R-DIL rules and is recorded as GAP-2522 with ASM-4172, and every value no source carries is held as GAP-2523 with ASM-4173.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| VR-P8-009-1 | Data product stale after a late or failed ACE batch for its source (`v_ace_batch_status`) raises MSG-P1-001 `{product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived.` | FSD P8 A2.9.3.1, copied character for character |
| BR-P8-009 | No value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version | FSD P8 A2.9.3.1, copied character for character |
| BR1 | The receipt and its match are this service's: `proceeds` in `rwb_payment` carries the case, the treatment, the account payment, the source, the amount, the received date, `matched_to` and the posting reference, and no other service writes them | TSD P8 T3.1; Ownership Map (`proceeds` owner P8); Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | A rental receipt is one value of LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC and closes to INSTALLMENT of LOV-MATCH; the rental arm writes no other match value, and a rental with no receipt writes no row | TSD P8 T3.2; FSD P8 A2.9; GAP-2528 (no RENTAL value in LOV-MATCH); ASM-4172 |
| BR3 | The match uses only the `payment_match_rule` rows in force for the business date, in `priority` order, with their window, grace, tolerance and floor; a run with no row in force stops before matching | TSD P8 T3.1, T3.2; FSD P8 AC-P8-001-05 (the same stop for the plan arm) |
| BR4 | The decision is recorded in the transaction that writes the row, one record per rule outcome, with the rule identity and version of the row that decided it; a failed write changes nothing and the caller sees MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; legacy RWB-E4-048 AC2; ADR-022 |
| BR5 | The ACE receipt, batch and freshness facts stay with rwb-source-data: this story reads no `v_ace_*` view and no ACE table and takes the receipt on the owner's contract only | DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 29; GAP-2524 |
| BR6 | The rental, its amount, its debit day, the auto-debit instruction and the arrears limit stay with rwb-treatment; R-DIL-32 sets the rental and the debit, R-DIL-34 hands the asset to the disposal route when the arrears exceed the limit, and this story evaluates neither | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIL-32, R-DIL-34); FSD P8 A2.9 (prerequisite FEAT-TRT-16) |
| BR7 | The case, the owner's task and the route state stay with rwb-case, and the notice with rwb-comms; this story raises no task and sends no notice | Ownership Map (recovery_case P3); Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR8 | The money side is announced once: `ProceedsMatched` on a matched rental and `PaymentMissed` on a rental due date with no receipt, each written to the outbox in the transaction of the row and relayed with key `caseId`; one missed event per due date, never one per run | Architecture v5 slides 22, 42 and 43; DP-09 is the platform library's |
| BR9 | The same fact twice, or the same `Idempotency-Key` twice, writes once, records once and publishes once, and the repeat is counted | Architecture v5 slide 11; TSD P8 T-A.2 |
| BR10 | No cross-schema join and no foreign key leaves `rwb_payment`; `case_id`, `treatment_id` and `account_payment_id` are identifiers of other services' facts | DP-01; TSD P8 T3.3 |
| BR11 | The auto-debit instruction itself is not this story's: FSD P8 A2.9 names ATS and AMIS as integration points while TSD P8 T5.1 names only ALS and GL, so the instruction is placed with FEAT-TRT-16 in rwb-treatment and this story collects, matches and follows up | FSD P8 A2.9.2; TSD P8 T5.1; GAP-2525; ASM-4176 |

BR2, BR3 and BR10 run in the loader and the matcher. BR4 runs in the writer, where the record, the row and the outbox are one transaction. BR5, BR6 and BR7 run at the boundary, before any row is written. BR8 runs in the outbox and the relay. BR9 runs in the idempotency table and the inbox.

##### 9. State transitions

The lifecycle of a rental receipt, not of the case:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | the run of the business date | No receipt for the rental due date | No row; one `PaymentMissed` for the due date |
| None | the run of the business date | A receipt inside the window in force and the record written | One `proceeds` row with `matched_to` INSTALLMENT; `ProceedsMatched` |
| INSTALLMENT | the same receipt or the same event again | The idempotency key repeats | No change; the first id is answered and the repeat counted |
| UNMATCHED | `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` with a valid `Idempotency-Key` | The officer matches the receipt to the rental | INSTALLMENT; one record and one `ProceedsMatched` |
| Pending | the record cannot be written | MSG-P7-003 | None; the row, the record and the event are all absent |
| INSTALLMENT | the run of a later date | The same receipt appears again in the source | No change; no second row and no second event |

The case state machine is not this service's (TSD P8 T4): rwb-treatment moves `RENTAL_RUNNING` by R-DIL-32 and hands the asset to `HANDED_TO_DISPOSAL` by R-DIL-34, rwb-case holds the case status, the task and the timer, and this service only writes the receipt and announces the miss.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-payment service identity, schema `rwb_payment`, own login (DP-02) | Reads the rental and the receipts on their owners' contracts, writes `proceeds`, the decision record and the outbox rows; the login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2524; ASM-4175) |
| SY-DATALOAD, data load identity | Holds right U on the match operation, which is how the ACE-driven path posts a receipt (TSD P8 T6.1) |
| RW-WRITEOFF, RW-CREDITAD | Hold right U on the match operation and right R on the receipts of the cases in scope |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-CREDITAD and the other holders of right R | Read the receipts and their match state for the cases in scope (TSD P8 T6.1) |
| Sale officer (FSD P8 A2.9.3.3) | Uses the rental result on the case; the run itself is unattended and holds the primary use |
| rwb-access (P4) | Owns the rights, the roles and the scope data; this story calls no guard of its own and holds no role row |
| rwb-treatment (S2), rwb-source-data (P1), rwb-case (P3), rwb-decision (P7) | Own the rental, the receipts, the case and the rule packages; this service reads their answers and writes none of their rows |

Refusals are 403 with MSG-P4-002 and 503 with MSG-P7-003; a case outside scope answers 404.

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and TSD P8 T3.1. `proceeds` is the only table this story writes that holds business facts, and no column, key, join or view leaves `rwb_payment` (DP-01). The rental terms of DF-FIN-003 travel inside the receipt as identifiers and are never copied as columns; the rental amount is the amount of the receipt, read from the source, and is not a column of this schema.

##### 12. Contract

Base `/api/recovery/payment/v1` (DP-13), topic `rwb.payment.events.v1` (DP-14 is the naming library's), queue `rwb-payment`, schema `rwb_payment`, Java package as section 1.

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Method | Path | Purpose | Authorization |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/proceeds` | The receipts of a case or a date range with their match state: query `matched`, `from`, `to`, `page`, `size`; `ProceedsPage` out | Write-off and posting, right R, scope applied |
| POST | `/proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` | Match an unmatched rental receipt to its case and treatment; `MatchRequest` in, `Proceeds` out; `Idempotency-Key` required | Write-off and posting, right U, scope applied |

The two operations are API-P8-001 and API-P8-002 of TSD P8 T-A.1 and T-A.2, and their shapes are RWB-P8-E4048-CON's. This story implements the rental arm behind them and declares no third operation; the exception list of a receipt that matches no rental is FEAT-PAY-02's story.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The rental read of the business date (path and field names Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2523; ASM-4173)) | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` | rwb-treatment (S2) | The rentals due on the business date: rental, treatment, case, rental amount, debit day and due date | One hop, 2 s (DP-11 is the pattern; the row itself is class C in fact, GAP-2524) |
| The receipt read of the ACE batch (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2524; ASM-4175)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | rwb-source-data (P1) | The receipts of the business date for source `ALS`, the batch status and the freshness stamp | One hop, 2 s |
| The case read and money-side answer (name Not specified) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | rwb-case (P3) | The case reference and the answer that applies the money side | One hop, 2 s |
| The rule-package read (name Not specified) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | rwb-decision (P7) | The version in force for the business date, the same one the record names | One hop, 2 s |

The four rows are contract dependencies of class C in fact, and the plan's C row for this story is None, so they are built against the owners' published documents and fakes from Day 1 (GAP-2524; ASM-4175). Each is a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream.

###### 12.3 Events published

Topic `rwb.payment.events.v1` with the `.retry` and `.dlt` topics, key `caseId`, CloudEvents 1.0 binary, `ce_source` `/rwb-payment`.

| Event | Schema name | Consumers | Payload used here |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ProceedsMatched` (EV-25) | `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` | rwb-case, rwb-asset, rwb-debtsale, rwb-writeoff, rwb-guarantee | The case, the proceeds and the treatment references, the amount, the value date, the match value INSTALLMENT and the rule identity with its version |
| `PaymentMissed` (EV-12) | `rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1` | rwb-case, rwb-treatment, rwb-comms | `caseId`, `treatmentId`, `dueDate`, `amountDue` and `daysLate`, as the published example of Architecture v5 slide 22 |

Both are written to the outbox in the transaction of the write and relayed after the commit, and the record on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is the library's (DP-03). `TreatmentBooked` (EV-11) is the booking story's and is not published by the rental arm.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `AceDataReady` (EV-26) | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | Starts the JOB-07 run of the business date and source; the inbox deduplicates on the event id |
| `TreatmentApproved` (EV-10) | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | Names the deed in lieu treatment that carries the buy-back rental, so the rental read of the date has an arrangement to match |
| `RulePackageInForce` (EV-30) | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | The package and version in force for the business date |

Consumed through the inbox with the retry and dead-letter topics. `DecisionRecorded` (EV-08) is the record this service writes through the library on the shared topic, so this story is a producer of it and adds no consumer group.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Kind | Queue | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| The JOB-07 event-started run (`PaymentMatchingWorkflow` in the matching story; the name is a target design choice) | Workflow | `rwb-payment` in `rwb-recovery` | RWB-P8-E2008-APP |
| `matchPayments` | Activity | `rwb-payment` | RWB-P8-E2008-APP |
| The rental arm of the run (a step of `matchPayments` in the app design of this story) | Activity step | `rwb-payment` | This story |

This story registers no workflow, no child workflow and no Nexus operation: the ownership rows of P8 hold no workflow of its own, and the rental arm is a step of the run that already exists.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-07 and JOB-08 are event-triggered runs in the owning service and not Temporal Schedules (Architecture v5 slide 44), and the rental due date is a fact of the rental read, not a timer of this service. The legacy Quartz marker of the key becomes the `AceDataReady` start, and no Schedule, Quartz row or shared job table is added.

| `proceeds` | P8 (`rwb_payment`) | The receipt and its match; the only business table this story writes |
| `payment_match_rule` | P8 (`rwb_payment`) | The match rules read in force; written by the matching-rule story of this service |
| `decision_record` | PLT library, created in `rwb_payment` | The local record of the step (DP-03) |

`treatment` and the rental record are S2's, `recovery_case`, `task` and `timer` are P3's, the `v_ace_*` views and the ACE batch are P1's and `rule_row` is P7's. This story creates no table and no column.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.payment`, module `rental`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RentalDueReader | Service | The rentals due on the business date, from the rwb-treatment contract, with their amount and due date |
| ReceiptReader | Service | The receipts of the business date and the batch freshness, from the rwb-source-data contract |
| RentalMatcher | Service | The `payment_match_rule` rows in force, in priority order, and the EXACT, WINDOW and PARTIAL comparison |
| ProceedsWritingStep | Service | The one transaction: the `proceeds` row, the local decision record, the outbox row and the idempotency row |
| RentalArrearsStep | Service | The `PaymentMissed` of a due date with no receipt, once per due date |
| ProceedsMatchResource | Controller | The two operations of section 12.1, their rights, their `Idempotency-Key` and their errors |

**Database and migrations.** Writes `proceeds` and the library objects and reads `payment_match_rule`; index `(case_id, received_date)` and `(matched_to, received_date)`, and a unique key on the idempotency key of business date, treatment and due date. Per-service Flyway in `rwb_payment`: the table is RWB-P8-E4048-CON's template and the migration is the DB story of this service, so this story adds no migration and no row.

**Configuration.** No business value: the window, the grace, the tolerance, the floor, the priority and the rule version are rows of `payment_match_rule` read in force, and every list value comes from the lists (BR-P8-009). Two settings only, the page size of the read and the retry count of the run, neither fixed by a source in the read set (GAP-2524; ASM-4175).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is applied as the owner's contract: the service holds no `v_ace_*` grant, so the receipt and the account of DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-054 are read on rwb-source-data's contract. DP-03 fixes the record written in the transaction of the row. DP-13 moves the base and nothing else. DP-19 is behind SCR-28. The outbox and inbox objects and the Flyway sequence come with the service template and are named as library objects, not as a pattern of this key (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON and RWB-PLT-E1044-CON are the platform stories that own them).

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The two H rows of DP-03 and DP-19 are the ones the metadata carries, with this key's CON; the four consumed reads are class C in fact and are built against their owners' documents and fakes from Day 1 (GAP-2524; ASM-4175).

**Build steps.** (1) The readers against the two contract fakes, AC1. (2) The matcher over the `payment_match_rule` fixtures, AC1. (3) The writing step with the record, the row, the outbox and the idempotency row in one transaction, AC1 and AC2. (4) The arrears step, one `PaymentMissed` per due date, AC1. (5) The manual `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match`, AC1. (6) The absence assertions: no `v_ace_*` grant, no cross-schema key, no Schedule.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P8-E4048-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON stay green, and a SIT week shows the rental of 2026-12-15 matched once with a receipt and an INSTALLMENT row, a rental with no receipt leaving one `PaymentMissed` for its due date and no row, a repeat writing nothing, and a stopped record leaving the row and the event absent with MSG-P7-003.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of `MatchRequest` is absent or invalid | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the Write-off and posting right the operation declares | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written, or the ledger refuses it | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE batch of the source is late or failed, which is VR-P8-009-1 | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-P8-001 | The run summary of a date with an unmatched receipt | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2522; ASM-4179) |
| MSG-P8-002 | No `payment_match_rule` row is in force on the business date | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2522; ASM-4179) |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A consumed answer does not arrive inside 2 s | The service is not available. Try again in a few minutes. |

MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P1-001 are copied unchanged from the legacy story and the FSD, and MSG-GEN-006 is the platform timeout message. An error is the problem body of the platform envelope; the reads and the match answer 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 as the contract declares.

##### 15. Screens and states

No new screen. The rental result shows on SCR-28 Proceeds matching: the receipts of the case in Loading, matched and unmatched states, each row with the amount, the received date, the treatment, the match state and the rule identity of the record. An unmatched rental receipt shows in the unmatched list with the manual match action; a rental with no receipt shows on the case as the `PaymentMissed` of rwb-case, not here. The screen is one gateway answer through the composite route, which calls this service for the receipts and rwb-case and rwb-treatment for the header (DP-19); its field list, its path and its merge order are RWB-PLT-N001-CON's, and the screen writes only through the match operation.

##### 16. Test cases

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-E4-048-01 | Legacy AC1 (BR1, BR2, BR3, BR4, BR8); the rental read and the receipt read are the owners'; the rental is matched once, the row and the record name the rule version, and a due date with no receipt leaves one `PaymentMissed` | End to end | Synthetic rental RT-2026-000701 on case RC-2026-000701, receipt PAY-90701 dated 2026-12-15, and a rental with no receipt |
| TC-E4-048-02 | Legacy AC2 (BR4); the record cannot be written and the caller sees MSG-P7-003 | Component | The record library stub refuses the write |
| TC-E4-048-03 | Legacy Access criterion; the right is P4's; a role without right U is refused with MSG-P4-002 on the match operation | Component | A role without Write-off and posting U calls POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match |
| TC-E4-048-04 | Legacy Principle 5 (BR4); a forced record failure stops the action with MSG-P7-003 and leaves no row and no event | NFR | The record store stopped during the run of 2026-12-15 |

Every legacy test case of RWB-E4-048 appears once. System maps to End to end, Access to Component and Resilience to NFR. The rental and receipt values are synthetic, built on the pattern of the FSD case RC-2026-000555, treatment T-0701 and payment PAY-90001, and the `-ITG` copies belong to the wave 3 harness.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the rental amount, the debit day, the arrears limit, the window, the grace, the tolerance, the floor, the priority and the rule version are rows of the rental read or of `payment_match_rule`, and every list value comes from LOV-MATCH, LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC and LOV-MATCH-TYPE.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, logs or tests: an event carries a case identifier, a treatment identifier, a due date, an amount and a day count, never a name, an address, a contact value or an identity number. Test data is synthetic.
- No cross-schema read (DP-01): no `rwb_treatment`, `rwb_case` or other service's table is read and no foreign key points into one.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the receipt and the account come from the rwb-source-data operations; no `v_ace_*` view and no ACE table is read by this service.
- The rental, the auto-debit instruction and the arrears limit are rwb-treatment's, and no rule of that service is evaluated here.
- No Quartz job, no Schedule and no shared job table: the run is event-started, and the due date is a fact of the rental read.
- No topic or event name is typed in code, and no message is reworded.

##### 18. Traceability
