**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract baseline of RWB-E6-037 for rwb-reporting — the additive change to `GET /reports/measures` that carries the benefit-realisation comparison, the variance rule, the freshness header and the nine contract tables — is split from the behaviour (RWB-P9-E6037-APP). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract of the benefit-realisation view as rwb-reporting serves it — `GET /api/recovery/reporting/v1/reports/measures` with its period, its `baselineDate` and its filters, the measure row with `value`, `baselineValue`, `variance`, `variancePercent`, `definitionVersion`, `isBaseline` and `frozen`, the `X-Data-As-Of` header and the stale flag, the variance rule, the error envelope with its message codes, the right each answer requires, the consumed readiness answer, the nine contract tables and the contract fakes**, so that **the app story of this legacy key builds against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1, and a baseline value, a variance or a definition version can never be computed one way in the service and read another way on the screen**.

The legacy key is moved with no business change: the measures, the baseline, the monthly cadence, the record with the rule version and the refusal when the record cannot be written are the ones RWB-E6-037 fixes. What this story adds is the contract form of them: one document owner, one shape per answer, one variance rule, one order, one error envelope and one fake per consumed answer.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The measure answer is the most-consumed read surface of rwb-reporting: the steering dashboard SCR-37, the benefit section of the same screen, the Power BI refresh through the extract hand-over and the audit sample all read the same rows. Three things drift silently if no contract holds them: which baseline a value is compared with, how the variance and its percentage are computed, and which definition version a month was produced under. A baseline date that a consumer chooses for itself turns one benefit number into two; a variance computed at the edge rather than in the owner means the screen and the report disagree.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_reporting`, REST base `/api/recovery/reporting/v1`, topic `rwb.reporting.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-reporting` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.reporting`. It records that this read path writes nothing and publishes no event type, that the local decision record of a tracked month is the only write of the capability (DP-03), and that the ACE data products behind a measure are reached through rwb-source-data's answer and never through a view of this service (DP-05).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL), so the document, topic and event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope and the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope are the platform baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- RWB-P9-E1013-CON is published, so `measure_definition` and `measure_snapshot` and the six baseline measures of definition version "MD-2026.11" have one owner document and the fields this story extends are an additive change to it.
- RWB-P9-E2009-CON is published, so `GET /reports/measures`, its `dimension` and `baselineValue` fields and the `X-Data-As-Of` header already have an owner document and the fields this story adds are declared against it.
- The decision-record library RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published, so the record of a tracked month has one contract and this document declares it as consumed (DP-03).
- The gateway-bff composite route RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published, so the consumer of the answer composes SCR-37 at the edge (DP-19).
- The Ownership Map gives `GET /reports/measures` to P9 rwb-reporting; this document declares no other service's operation as provided and names no operation the map does not already give P9.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7) and sits in contract group `CG-W4`.

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the additive change to the rwb-reporting OpenAPI 3.1 document for the one read operation: the `baselineDate` parameter, the four added row properties and the stale flag.
2. Fix the variance rule in the document — value less baseline value, and the percentage over a non-zero baseline value — so no consumer computes its own (GAP-2580; ASM-4256).
3. Fix the period rule: `from` and `to` name the first and last day of the month asked for, `baselineDate` names the frozen baseline and defaults to the baseline of the definition version in force, and the period of the answer is stated once (GAP-2580; ASM-4259).
4. Fix the row order and state that the answer is one bounded array with no paging in major version 1, the ceiling being a platform parameter (GAP-2580; ASM-4257).
5. Declare that the document publishes no event type and subscribes to none, and name the local decision record as the one write of the capability (GAP-2580; ASM-4258).
6. Record the consumed readiness element with its owner, its use and its failure mapping; record that no REST operation is consumed.
7. Map every failure to the error envelope and a message ID, with the legacy texts unchanged.
8. Publish the nine contract tables of section 12 and the contract fakes; every fake answers the document and fails the build when it drifts.
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P9-E6037-APP, to the dashboard and to the audit consumers of the answer.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 500 with the platform error envelope | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A field is renamed, retyped or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC9 |
| X4 | `from` is after `to` | 422 with MSG-GEN-003 naming the two fields | MSG-GEN-003 | AC5 |
| X5 | A required parameter is empty | 422 with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X6 | `baselineDate` names a date with no frozen baseline | 200 with the rows of the month and no variance, the row flagged as having no baseline; never an error and never a guess | None | AC4 |
| X7 | A caller reads a month outside its scope | 200 with the rows of its scope only; a scope that excludes every row answers an empty array, not an error | None | AC6 |
| X8 | The readiness answer does not arrive inside the budget | The stale flag and the header are omitted, no row is dropped and no value changes | None | AC8 |
| X9 | An operation of another service is written into this document as provided | The review fails: the document lists only rwb-reporting's own operation | None | AC1 |
| X10 | The document declares an event type of this view | The review fails: the capability publishes only the local record of DP-03 | None | AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the two same-service contracts it extends and the Ownership Map only |
| Negotiable | Property names and lengths are settled with the consumers; the operation, the variance rule, the period rule and the order are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story of this legacy key on Day 1 and every consumer of the measure answer, the dashboard and the audit sample |
| Estimable | One document, one additive change, one consumed element, nine contract tables and three fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin

  Background:

  Scenario: AC1 The read operation is declared with its owner and the change is additive (new, D-RCV-60)

  Scenario: AC2 The period and the baseline date are parameters of the answer (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then baselineDate names the frozen baseline the values are compared with and defaults to the baseline of the definition version in force, 2026-11-27 for "MD-2026.11" (GAP-2580; ASM-4259)

  Scenario: AC3 The measure row fixes the value and its comparison (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then the document states that value is the measure of the period, baselineValue is the frozen value of the same measure, product and dimension, and isBaseline and frozen are read from measure_snapshot and never recomputed by a consumer
    Then the document states that the rows are ordered by measureCode, then productGroup, then dimensionCode, and that the answer is one bounded array with no paging in major version 1 (GAP-2580; ASM-4257)

    When the rule of their computation is reviewed

    Then a measure with no frozen baseline row answers baselineValue null, variance null and variancePercent null with no error
    Then the document states that no consumer computes, rounds or re-bases a variance, and that the baseline rows are never rewritten

  Scenario: AC5 The error envelope and the message codes (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error responses declared on the operation
    When each condition is mapped to its status and its message ID
    Then 401 no session, 403 a missing right, 422 an inverted period or an empty required parameter, and 503 a store failure are declared with the platform envelope
    Then 422 an inverted period maps to MSG-GEN-003 and an empty required parameter to MSG-GEN-001, 403 to MSG-P4-002 and 503 to MSG-P7-003
    Then MSG-P1-001 is declared as the stale flag of a measure and not as an error
    Then every text is the legacy text of RWB-E6-037 unchanged and the envelope is the platform envelope, never a local one

  Scenario: AC6 The right and the scope the answer requires (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the security and scope statements of the operation
    When they are compared with the roles and the right names of the target

    Then the scope filters every row before any value, count or percentage is computed, so a value never includes a case the caller may not read
    Then RW-FINANCE holds Reporting R, and a role without the right is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002 and never with an empty answer
    Then the contract declares the right and the scope only: the guard that applies them belongs to the platform library and is not redefined here

  Scenario: AC7 The freshness stamp and the stale flag (new, D-RCV-60)

  Scenario: AC8 The consumed element, the one write of the capability and the 2 s budget (new, D-RCV-60)

These nine criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P9-E6037-APP, which keeps the two legacy criteria with their own tags.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/reporting/v1`; the document never declares another service's path as provided | DP-13; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR2 | Event names are `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on the topic `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, with retry and `.dlt` topics, and this view carries no event type | DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR3 | A read declares no Idempotency-Key and writes nothing; a command declares it and stores its response | ADR-020; DP-09 |
| BR4 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; the business texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR5 | A schema change is additive within a major version; a breaking change is a new major version | Template and Rules §R7.2 s12 |
| BR6 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-reporting; a consumed element is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | Ownership Map v1 |
| BR7 | The variance is computed by the owner and declared in the contract, so no consumer can compute a second version of the same number | Legacy AC1; GAP-2580; ASM-4256 |
| BR8 | The baseline is the frozen baseline of the definition version in force and is never rewritten, re-based or recomputed | RWB-E1-013 baseline of 2026-11-27 |
| BR9 | No business value is fixed in the contract: measure codes, formulas, units, dimensions and the publish state stay data rows | Principle 1; FSD P9 BR-P9-006 |
| BR10 | No personal data is declared in an answer: rows carry measure codes, codes, counts, amounts, days, percentages, dates and a definition version only | DP-19; TSD P9 T6.2 |
| BR11 | The order and the period of the answer are part of the contract: a consumer that sorts or re-bases differently from the document has a defect | TSD P9 T-A.2 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The operation, the variance rule, the period rule and the order are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, the dashboard and the audit consumers accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example a new dimension | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or the variance rule changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | An event type of the view appears in the document | The review of AC8 fails | In review |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-reporting | Owns the OpenAPI document and the fakes of the operation; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change and a new major version |
| Consuming teams (the app story, the dashboard, the extract hand-over and the audit sample) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| rwb-source-data owner | Signs off the readiness row, its budget and the stale rule |
| Platform library owner | Owns the error envelope, the naming rule and the guard this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in the answer |

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Measure row | `measureCode`, `definitionVersion`, `period`, `productGroup`, `dimensionCode`, `dimensionValue`, `unit`, `value`, `baselineValue`, `variance`, `variancePercent`, `isBaseline`, `frozen`, `staleDate` from `measure_snapshot` DF-RPT-042 to DF-RPT-051 and `measure_definition` DF-RPT-032, DF-RPT-036 and DF-RPT-037 |
| Period | `from` and `to` naming the first and last day; `period` in the row is the month the rows belong to (GAP-2580; ASM-4259) |
| Baseline | `baselineDate` and the frozen rows of 2026-11-27 read beside the period; never rewritten |
| Variance | `variance` and `variancePercent`, computed by the owner (GAP-2580; ASM-4256) |
| Lists | LOV-MEASURE-UNIT COUNT, THB, DAYS, PERCENT; LOV-MEASURE-DIM ROUTE, AGE_BAND, QUEUE, STAGE, AGENT; LOV-PRODUCT MORTGAGE, HIRE_PURCHASE, SSME, UNSECURED; LOV-DATA-PRODUCT DP01 to DP14, from TSD P9 T3.2 |
| Freshness | The `X-Data-As-Of` header and `staleDate`, from the readiness answer of rwb-source-data |
| Error envelope | The platform envelope with one message ID per condition; the texts of section 14 |

The field-level types, lengths and required flags of the added properties are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the names, the optionality rule of AC1, the variance rule of AC4, the period rule of AC2 and the order of AC3.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-reporting (P9); base `/api/recovery/reporting/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/reports/measures` | Measure array: filters `measure`, `product`, `route`, `from`, `to`, `baselineDate`; rows with `measureCode`, `definitionVersion`, `period`, `productGroup`, `dimensionCode`, `dimensionValue`, `unit`, `value`, `baselineValue`, `variance`, `variancePercent`, `isBaseline`, `frozen`, `staleDate`; header `X-Data-As-Of` | Reporting R, scope applied |

The operation answers 401, 403, 422 and 503; it takes no Idempotency-Key and writes nothing. The answer is one bounded array with no paging in major version 1, ordered by `measureCode`, then `productGroup`, then `dimensionCode`. `baselineDate` defaults to the baseline of the definition version in force, and a baseline date with no frozen row answers null variance and is never an error.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The data-product readiness of the month is consumed as an activity on the queue of P1 rwb-source-data, and the local decision record is written through the library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; neither is a REST operation of another service, so no hop and no breaker is declared here.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The contract publishes no event type. `rwb.reporting.events.v1` exists with its `.retry` and `.dlt` topics, and the publish marker of a measure run belongs to the Epic 1 measure story; this view publishes nothing of it (GAP-2580; ASM-4258). The one write of the capability — the local decision record of a tracked month — is relayed on `rwb.decision-record.v1` by the library of DP-03 and is declared as consumed, not as published here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None as a subscription of this contract. The facts of a month are replayed by the run of RWB-P9-E6037-APP from the events of P3, S2, S6, S7, P6 and P2 and from `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; their types are owned and published by those services, and this document declares their consumer groups once so that the owner of each type can see who reads it. The read path of this contract subscribes to nothing.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reportingMeasuresDaily` (JOB-15, owned by RWB-P9-E2009-APP) | Workflow, one execution per business date | `rwb-reporting` | Carries the month step whose rows this contract publishes; owned by the measure story, named here as the writer |
| The data-product readiness of a month | Activity, on the owner's queue | `rwb-source-data` | The consumed element of 12.2 and AC8; faked |

No workflow, activity or child workflow is registered by this story; the rows fix what a consumer of the answer may assume about the writer.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The 01:30 daily Schedule `reportingMeasuresDaily` (JOB-15) is RWB-P9-E2009-APP's; this baseline registers no Schedule, no cron entry and no job name, and the monthly view is a period of the same rows rather than a second job.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The additive change to `openapi/rwb-reporting-v1.yaml` for `GET /reports/measures`, the `Measure` row component shared with RWB-P9-E2009-CON and RWB-P9-E1013-CON, the contract README rows for the variance rule, the period rule, the order and the stale rule, and the four WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`: the record of a tracked month is declared as the one write of the capability | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | The data products of a month are read through rwb-source-data's readiness and snapshot answer; this document declares no view and no cross-schema join | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/reporting/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for SCR-37 | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

No pattern is claimed outside this list: the baseline registers no Schedule, so DP-10 is not applied, and the answer carries no personal data, so no masking pattern is added.

**Build steps**

1. Add the `baselineDate` parameter, the four row properties and the stale flag to the document; validate the additive rule of AC1 in the pipeline.
2. Write the variance rule of AC4 and the period rule of AC2 into the document and the README, so a consumer cannot compute a second version of a benefit number.
3. Fix the order and the absence of paging of AC3, with the platform parameter as the only ceiling.
4. Record the consumed readiness row and the one write of the capability; state the absence of events of AC8.
5. Map every failure code of AC5 and compare each text with the legacy text.
6. Publish the four fakes and the nine contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
7. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note, including the rwb-source-data owner and the consumers of the answer.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI artefact validates in the pipeline, the nine contract tests pass, the four fakes answer every path and the drift test is green, and RWB-P9-E6037-APP and the consumers of the answer have accepted the baseline.

The message IDs are contract elements and the texts are the agreed legacy and FSD P9 texts unchanged. Which data product fills the `{product}` of MSG-P1-001 for a given measure is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2580; ASM-4258); the row of `measure_definition` names it.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: measure codes, formulas, units, dimensions and the definition version are data rows, and the baseline date is a parameter, never a constant.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: measure codes, codes, counts, amounts, days, percentages, dates and a definition version only.
- The contract names only rwb-reporting's tables and only the operation owned by rwb-reporting; the readiness element is consumed and faked, never declared as provided (DP-01, DP-05).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The variance is computed once, by the owner; a consumer that re-bases or re-rounds it has a defect, not a preference.
- No retired element is reintroduced: a build that declares a data-lake target, a second extract or a benefit Schedule fails the absence test of AC9 (DP-17).
- Every example in the document is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope, the guard and the naming rule come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the benefit-realisation slice of RWB-E6-037 for rwb-reporting — the monthly comparison of every measure of the benefit model against the frozen baseline, computed from the decision log and the event-derived read model, the monthly step of the existing JOB-15 run, one local decision record per month, and `GET /reports/measures` with the baseline comparison — is split from the published shapes (RWB-P9-E6037-CON). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **finance and CFO delegate (RW-FINANCE)**, I want **each measure of the benefit model shown for a closed calendar month beside its frozen baseline, computed from the decision log and the events of the month and recorded with the definition version and the rule version in force**, so that **the benefit the programme claims is read from the same record the teams work on, and not counted by hand from spreadsheets at month end**.

Inside rwb-reporting this is the benefit half of RWB-E6-037:

- service `rwb-reporting`, schema `rwb_reporting`, REST base `/api/recovery/reporting/v1`, topic `rwb.reporting.events.v1` with event names `rwb.reporting.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-reporting` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.reporting` (DP-13);
- the read model of the month built from events and from the decision record of every decision (`DecisionRecorded`, EV-08, on `rwb.decision-record.v1`), with no data lake and no ACE view read by this service (DP-17, DP-05);
- one local decision record per closed month — the tracking record with the measure set, the baseline date and the definition version — written before the month's rows are published and relayed on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03);
- the month's rows written to `measure_snapshot` in `rwb_reporting`, beside the frozen baseline rows of 2026-11-27, which are never rewritten (DP-01);
- `GET /reports/measures` on the per-service base, each value beside its `baselineValue` with `variance` and `variancePercent`, served to SCR-37 through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-13, DP-19).

Not here: the published shapes, the error model and the fakes (RWB-P9-E6037-CON); the baseline measure set, `measure_definition` and the frozen baseline of 2026-11-27 (RWB-P9-E1013-APP and RWB-P9-E1013-CON); the steering measures and the daily publish or hold of JOB-15 (RWB-P9-E2009-APP and RWB-P9-E2009-CON); the deployment, the topics and the runbook (RWB-P9-E2009-OPS); regulatory returns of FEAT-RPT-07 (RWB-E8-001) and the classification and re-ageing of FEAT-RPT-10 (RWB-E8-002).

##### 2. Business rationale

The benefits of the programme are measured today by hand from spreadsheets at month end, after the month has closed and after the numbers have been argued over. FEAT-RPT-06 asks for the opposite: the measures of the benefit model tracked against the baseline, monthly, from the decision log. The baseline exists from Epic 1 — six measures under definition version "MD-2026.11", frozen on business date 2026-11-27 (RWB-P9-E1013-APP) — and the daily measures exist from Epic 2 (RWB-P9-E2009-APP). What no story owns is the comparison: a month's value, the baseline value, the variance, and the record that says which definition version and which rule version produced them.

RWB-E6-037 is three lines of behaviour and three facts. The behaviour is: track the measures against the baseline monthly, record the result with the rule version, and stop if the record cannot be written. The facts are the decision log entry, the score rows and the rule rows it reaches in the monolith through `DecisionLogApi`, `v_ace_score` and the rule table. Under D-RCV-60 all four things move, and they move for one reason: a benefit number that cannot be reproduced is not a benefit number.

- **the facts become events.** The month's facts arrive on the events of the services that own them and on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; rwb-reporting reads no `v_ace_score` row and calls no Java interface of another module (DP-17, DP-05).
- **the baseline is data.** The baseline is not recomputed and not typed in: it is the frozen `measure_snapshot` rows of 2026-11-27 read beside the month, so a benefit number cannot drift because a spreadsheet was refreshed (DP-01).
- **the record is written first.** The tracking record is a local decision record committed in the same transaction as the month's rows, so a month that cannot be recorded is a month that is not published (DP-03).
- **the screen is one route.** The Finance delegate reads the benefit view on SCR-37 through the gateway-bff composite route, which merges the reporting answer with the case-side and decision-side answers of the same screen (DP-19).

That is why the story is small and the risk is not: every failure here looks like a number, not an error.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P9-E6037-CON is published: the additive change to `GET /reports/measures` — the `baselineDate` parameter, the `baselineValue`, `variance` and `variancePercent` row fields and the `X-Data-As-Of` header — its error model and its contract fakes. The field names of the three added properties are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2580; ASM-4256).
- RWB-P9-E1013-APP is done: `measure_definition` holds definition version "MD-2026.11" with the six measures "CASES_BY_ROUTE", "CASES_BY_AGE", "CASES_BY_QUEUE", "REALIZED_RECOVERY", "TIME_IN_STAGE" and "TAT_BY_ROUTE", and the baseline rows of business date 2026-11-27 are written and frozen.
- The JOB-15 run of RWB-P9-E2009-APP exists as the Schedule `reportingMeasuresDaily` at 01:30 on queue `rwb-reporting`, with its workflow, its activities and its read-model loader; this story adds one step to it and no workflow, no activity of its own task queue registration and no Schedule.
- The decision-record library RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published, so the month's tracking record is written in the caller's transaction and relayed on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03).
- The gateway-bff composite route RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published, so the benefit section of SCR-37 is composed at the edge and the browser calls one route (DP-19).
- Which measures belong to the benefit model is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2579; ASM-4251): the assumed rule is the measures of the definition version in force that hold a frozen baseline row, membership being data and never code.
- Which business day of the new month runs the monthly step, and how a month is keyed in `measure_snapshot`, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2579; ASM-4252; ASM-4253).
- The service runs as login `rwb_reporting` on schema `rwb_reporting`, holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema, reads no `v_ace_*` view and writes no other service's table (DP-01, DP-05).
- No build dependency outside the three contract stories; Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7), because every H dependency is a contract.

##### 4. Flow

1. The Schedule `reportingMeasuresDaily` opens the JOB-15 execution of business date D, with the execution id derived from D so a rerun joins the run (RWB-P9-E2009-APP, DP-10 inherited).
2. D is the first business date of a new calendar month, so the run opens the benefit step for the closed month M (the assumed timing; GAP-2579; ASM-4252).
3. `loadBenefitModel` reads the measures of the definition version in force that hold a frozen `measure_snapshot` row, with their data product, unit and dimension, from `measure_definition` and the baseline rows (GAP-2579; ASM-4251).
4. `loadBenefitReadModel` replays the events of M — `CaseCreated` and `CaseStateChanged` on `rwb.case.events.v1`, `TreatmentApproved` on `rwb.treatment.events.v1`, `LotAwarded` on `rwb.debtsale.events.v1`, `WriteOffApproved` on `rwb.writeoff.events.v1`, `NoticeDispatched` on `rwb.comms.events.v1`, `FileDelivered` on `rwb.integration.events.v1` — and `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, deduplicated on the event id and ordered per case by the sequence of the outbox (DP-17).
5. The data-product date of each source of M is read on the rwb-source-data readiness answer; a source whose last complete day is before the end of M marks the affected measure with that date instead of the month's, and raises MSG-P1-001 (DP-05).
6. `computeBenefit` computes each measure of M from the facts by the formula of its definition row — counts, amounts, days or percentages — and pairs it with the baseline value of the same measure, product and dimension.
7. `variance` is the month value less the baseline value and `variancePercent` is the variance over the baseline value when the baseline value is not zero; both are computed and never stored (GAP-2579; ASM-4256).
8. In one `rwb_reporting` transaction the step writes the month's `measure_snapshot` rows under the dimension of each measure, keyed by the last business date of M, with the definition version in force, and writes one local decision record naming the measure set, the baseline date 2026-11-27, the definition version and the rule version in force (DP-03, DP-01; GAP-2579; ASM-4253).
9. A measure with no frozen baseline row writes no variance, is flagged as having no baseline and never blocks the month (AC4).
10. `GET /reports/measures?from=<first day of M>&to=<last day of M>&baselineDate=2026-11-27` answers the month's rows on `/api/recovery/reporting/v1`, filtered by measure, product and route, with the scope of the role applied and the business date in `X-Data-As-Of` (DP-13).
11. A rerun of the same month replaces the month's rows with the same values, writes no second decision record and leaves the frozen baseline untouched (AC5).
12. SCR-37 shows the benefit section through the gateway-bff composite route, which calls rwb-reporting once for the measures and merges them with the rest of the screen (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The local decision record cannot be written | The transaction writes nothing: no month row and no record; the read answers nothing for the month and the run is retried | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, AC5 |
| X2 | A source of M is stale | The affected measure carries the stale data-product date, the stale flag and its date, and the rest of the month publishes | MSG-P1-001 | AC3 |
| X3 | A measure of the definition version has no frozen baseline row | No variance and no percentage is written for it; the row is flagged as having no baseline | None | AC4 |
| X4 | The period sent to the read is inverted | Refused before any read, naming the two fields | MSG-GEN-003 | AC6 |
| X5 | A required query field is empty | Refused before any read, naming the field | MSG-GEN-001 | AC6 |
| X6 | The role lacks Reporting R | The read is refused and nothing is returned | MSG-P4-002 | AC6, TC-E6-037-03 |
| X7 | The month holds no fact — no case, no decision, no treatment and no notice moved in M | The month writes its rows with zero counts and no rate rows, and publishes | None | AC3 |
| X8 | A rerun of a month already published | The rows are replaced with the same values and no second record is written | None | AC5 |
| X9 | The read model loader reaches another service's schema, a `v_ace_*` view or the data lake | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | Section 17 |
| X10 | A measure code, a formula, a unit or the baseline date is written as a constant | The definition-rows test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | Section 17 |

X1 to X3 are the exception paths that RWB-E6-037 fixes in AC2 and in the data of the feature; X4 to X10 are the paths the microservice adds. No path publishes a month whose record could not be written, and no path writes a measure code, a formula, a unit or a baseline date as a constant.

| Independent | Day 1 against RWB-P9-E6037-CON, the decision-record library and the composite route; the events of the month are replayed from fixtures, with no live neighbour |
| Negotiable | The step, activity and calculator names, the read-model shape and the run summary are this story's choice; the measures, the baseline, the messages and the recorded facts are fixed |
| Valuable | The benefit the programme claims is read from the decision log and reproduced from the frozen baseline |

| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against a synthetic month built from event fixtures and the baseline rows of 2026-11-27 |

    When the benefit step runs again for the same month
    Then the month rows hold the same values and the same business date
    Then no second decision record is written and the existing record keeps its rule version and definition version
    Given the local decision-record store is unavailable
    When the benefit step runs for the month of 2027-01
    Then no measure_snapshot row is written for 2027-01 and nothing is published
    Then the run record carries MSG-P7-003 and the next run publishes the month

  Scenario: AC6 The Finance delegate reads the month beside the baseline (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given user "U-9001" holds RW-FINANCE, whose Reporting letter is "R"
    Given the month of 2026-12 is published
    When "U-9001" calls GET /api/recovery/reporting/v1/reports/measures?from=2026-12-01&to=2026-12-31&baselineDate=2026-11-27
    Then the answer holds one row per measure of "MD-2026.11" with value, baselineValue, variance and variancePercent for the period "2026-12"
    Then the header X-Data-As-Of carries 2026-12-31
    Given a user holding a role without the Reporting right
    When the same operation is called
    Then the call is refused with status 403 and MSG-P4-002 and no row is returned

  Scenario: AC7 SCR-37 shows the benefit section read only (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the gateway-bff composite route serves SCR-37 for the period 2026-12
    Given the month of 2026-12 is published
    When the Finance and CFO delegate opens SCR-37
    Then the benefit section shows the month, the six measures, each value beside the baseline of 2026-11-27 and the variance
    Then the stale flag and its date appear for a measure whose source is stale
    Then the screen builds no number of its own and offers no action that changes a measure, a baseline or a record
    And the browser calls one composite route and no owner service directly
```

AC1 and AC2 are the legacy criteria of RWB-E6-037, copied word for word with the origin tag added to the `Scenario` line: the repeated `Then` of AC1, the words "the data", "the rule version", "the screen" and "the decision log" all stand, and the cross-service part of each `Given` is expressed by the contract mock it runs against — `rwb-source-data` for the data and `rwb-decision` for the rule version and the decision log. AC3 to AC7 are new for the rwb-reporting slice and test only the deliverable of the title: the month's computation, the variance against the frozen baseline, the one record per month, the read and the screen section. The month, the case count, the amounts and the test user are synthetic fixtures of the same kind as the FSD examples, and no measure value of a real month is fixed here.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A benefit measure is computed from Workbench records and the decision log, never from a separate count and never by hand | NFR-065; FSD P9 A2.6; FEAT-RPT-06 |
| BR2 | The measures of the benefit model are the measures of the definition version in force that hold a frozen baseline row; membership is data, never code | Principle 1; FSD P9 BR-P9-006 |
| BR3 | Each month is shown beside the frozen baseline of the same measure, product and dimension, and the baseline rows are never rewritten | RWB-E1-013 baseline 2026-11-27; FSD P9 BR-P9-006 |
| BR4 | Variance is the month value less the baseline value; variance percent is the variance over the baseline value and is written only when the baseline value is not zero | Derived from BR3; GAP-2579; ASM-4256 |
| BR5 | The month, the baseline date, the definition version and the rule version in force are recorded in one local decision record before the month is published | Legacy AC1; DP-03; Principle 5 |
| BR6 | A month that cannot be recorded is not published: no row and no record | Legacy AC2; MSG-P7-003 |
| BR7 | A source that is stale marks its measure with the stale data-product date; the measure is never silently computed from an older month | FSD P9 VR-P9-006-1; MSG-P1-001 |
| BR8 | A measure with no baseline row is shown without a variance and never blocks the month | Derived from BR2; FSD P9 A2.6 |
| BR9 | The same month twice writes the same rows once and one record; the month key and the definition version carry the rule | Legacy AC1; BR5 |
| BR10 | Every read applies the role's scope and the Reporting right, and a read writes nothing | TSD P9 T6.1, T6.2 |
| BR11 | No measure code, formula, unit, age band, data product or baseline date is a constant; each is a data row or a request value | Principle 1; FSD P9 BR-P9-006; VR-P9-006-1 |
| BR12 | The month's facts arrive on events; rwb-reporting reads no other service's table and no `v_ace_*` view | DP-01; DP-05; DP-17 |
| BR13 | The month's rows and the baseline rows are the same `measure_snapshot` table of this service, so the comparison cannot read two different stores | DP-01; FSD P9 A2.6 |

##### 9. State transitions

None of a case: RWB-E6-037 says so and this slice keeps it. The states here are the tracking state of a month and the execution state of the run.

| From (month state) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not existing | The benefit step completes and the record commits | BR5 holds and every measure of BR2 is computed | Published, with the month rows and one record |
| Not existing | The record cannot be written | BR6 fails | Not published; the month is retried by the next run |
| Published | A rerun of the same month | BR9 | Published with the same values and the same record |
| Published | A measure added to the definition version later | BR2 does not apply to a closed month | Unchanged; the new measure starts with the next month |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The recovery service identity of rwb-reporting (`rwb_reporting`) | Runs the benefit step, loads the month's facts, computes the measures and writes the month rows and the record; holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema |
| The local decision-record library (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON) | Writes the month's tracking record in the caller's transaction and publishes `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) |
| RW-FINANCE, Finance and CFO delegate | Reads the benefit section of SCR-37 and the measures of a month (Reporting R) |
| RW-BIANAL, Reporting and BI analyst | Reads the measures, the definition versions and the variance, and receives the stale alert (Reporting CRUD) |
| RW-TRIBE, Tribe lead and squad members | Reads a month beside the baseline (Reporting R) |
| RW-PRODHEAD, product head | Reads a month for the products in scope (Reporting R) |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Receives the stale alert and reads the data-product date behind a measure (Reporting CRU) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the record of a month and its variance (Reporting R) |
| A role holding no Reporting right | Refused on the read with MSG-P4-002 |

The rights are the rows of TSD P9 T6.1 and of the legacy permission table, and nothing wider. No person is named: every duty is a role.

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 and of TSD P9 T3.1. `measure_publish` is not written by this story: the daily publish or hold of a business date stays RWB-P9-E2009-APP's. No table is added and no migration is needed, because `measure_snapshot` already carries the definition version, the baseline flag and the frozen flag; how a month is keyed when no month column exists is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2579; ASM-4253). No personal data is written: measure codes, codes, counts, amounts, days, percentages, dates and a definition version only.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None added by this story. It supplies the behaviour behind `GET /api/recovery/reporting/v1/reports/measures` — the operation the Ownership Map gives P9 rwb-reporting — whose published shape is RWB-P9-E6037-CON and whose first build is RWB-P9-E2009-APP.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/reports/measures` | API-P9-001: a list of `Measure` — measure, product, route, period, value, dimension, `baselineValue`, `variance`, `variancePercent` — filtered by `measure`, `product`, `route`, `from`, `to` and `baselineDate`, with `X-Data-As-Of` | Reporting, right R, scope applied | Not applicable; a read writes nothing |

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The month's facts arrive on events and the data-product dates on the readiness answer of rwb-source-data, which runs as an activity on the owner's queue and returns its answer to the workflow (DP-05, DP-17). No REST call of another service is made by this story, so the two-second one-hop budget of ADR-020 is not exercised and no breaker is configured.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Trigger | Payload used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DecisionRecorded` (EV-08), the local record of a tracked month | `rwb.decision-record.v1`, owned by rwb-decision | The month's transaction commits | the record id, the month, the baseline date, the definition version, the rule version and the outcome; no measure value |

The service topic `rwb.reporting.events.v1` carries no event type of this view (GAP-2580; ASM-4258); the publish marker of a measure run belongs to the Epic 1 measure story and is not published here. `DecisionRecorded` is written by the local library to this service's outbox on the shared topic (DP-03).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Consumer group | Payload used | When |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CaseCreated` (EV-01), `CaseStateChanged` (EV-05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.case.v1` | the case id, product group, stage, route and entry date; CASES_BY_ROUTE, CASES_BY_AGE, CASES_BY_QUEUE, TIME_IN_STAGE | replayed for the month of the run |
| `DecisionRecorded` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | `rwb-reporting.decision.v1` | the decision code, the time and the rule version; the decision measures and BR1 | as above |
| `TreatmentApproved` (EV-10) | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.treatment.v1` | the treatment id, case and outcome | as above |
| `LotAwarded`, `AccountsTransferred` | `rwb.debtsale.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.debtsale.v1` | the lot, the case and the amount realised | as above |
| `WriteOffApproved` | `rwb.writeoff.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.writeoff.v1` | the write-off id, the case and the amount | as above |
| `NoticeDispatched` (EV-14) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.notice.v1` | the notice id, case, type and sent date | as above |
| `FileDelivered` | `rwb.integration.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.integration.v1` | the interface, the business date and the delivery result | as above |

The consumer groups are declared once by RWB-P9-E6037-CON and registered by RWB-P9-E2009-OPS. The run replays a bounded window — the month and the look-back of the age measures — rather than consuming continuously, so no read-model table is added and a repeat is deduplicated on the event id. The money facts of the month arrive on the debt-sale and write-off events of S6 and S7, the services the connection matrix gives this row of P9.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reportingMeasuresDaily` (JOB-15, owned by RWB-P9-E2009-APP) | Workflow, one execution per business date | `rwb-reporting`, namespace `rwb-recovery` | This story adds one step to it; it adds no workflow and changes no input |
| `loadBenefitModel` | Activity | `rwb-reporting` | the measures of the definition version in force with a frozen baseline row in; the measure set with its formulas out |
| `loadBenefitReadModel` | Activity | `rwb-reporting` | the events of the month in; the run-scoped month fact view out, deduplicated on the event id |
| `computeBenefit` | Activity | `rwb-reporting` | the month fact view and the baseline rows in; the month rows with value, baselineValue, variance and variancePercent out |
| `recordAndPublishBenefit` | Activity | `rwb-reporting` | the one transaction: the local decision record and the month rows |

The step and activity names are this story's design choice: no source names the step that tracks benefit realisation, and JOB-15 is the one job the ownership row of the service carries (GAP-2579; ASM-4252).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added. The 01:30 daily Schedule `reportingMeasuresDaily` is RWB-P9-E2009-APP's and this story only opens the benefit step inside its first execution of a new month; no cron entry, no second Schedule and no Quartz row is created. The bank's Airflow may trigger the same workflow by its start signal and calls no schema.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.reporting`, module `benefit`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.reporting.benefit`; front end `src/modules/recovery/reporting/BenefitSection.tsx`, the fragment SCR-37 embeds.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`: one record per month, written before the month rows | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract — the readiness answer on its queue — or, for a monitoring measure, the service's own projection; rwb-reporting reads no `v_ace_*` view | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/reporting/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for the benefit section of SCR-37 | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

No pattern is claimed outside this list: the month runs on the Schedule that already exists, so DP-10 is not applied here, and the story writes no decision-log entry of another service, so the shared ledger stays P7's.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `BenefitStep` | Step of the existing workflow | Opens the month, sequences the two loaders and the calculator, and commits the month |
| `BenefitModelLoader` | Service | Reads the measures of the definition version in force with a frozen baseline row and their formulas |
| `BenefitReadModel` | Service | Replays the month's events into a run-scoped fact view, deduplicated on the event id |
| `BenefitCalculator` | Service | One calculator per measure driven by the definition rows; value, baselineValue, variance and variancePercent |
| `MonthWriter` | Repository | Writes the month rows to `measure_snapshot` in schema `rwb_reporting` only |
| `BenefitRecordWriter` | Library adapter | Writes the month's local decision record with the definition version and the rule version, in the same transaction (DP-03) |
| `MeasureController` | Controller | `GET /reports/measures` with the period, the baseline date, the scope and `X-Data-As-Of` |
| `BenefitSection` | React component | The benefit section of SCR-37: month, measures, baseline, variance and stale flag, read only |

**Build steps**

1. Take RWB-P9-E6037-CON tagged, and add the `baselineDate` parameter, the three row fields and the header to the query of `MeasureController`; test the shape of AC6.
2. Build the month fixtures of the seven event types and `BenefitReadModel`; test the replay and the deduplication of AC3.
3. Build `BenefitModelLoader` and `BenefitCalculator`; test the six measures of AC3 and the calculated variance of AC4.
4. Build `MonthWriter` and `BenefitRecordWriter` in one transaction; test AC5 and the failed-record path of X1.
5. Build the stale flag and the date from the readiness answer; test X2.
6. Build the read with the period check, the scope and the header; test AC6 and the refusal of X6.
7. Build the `BenefitSection` of SCR-37 and the composite-route contract test; test AC7.
8. Replay one month twice and compare the rows byte for byte; test BR9.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.p9.benefit-tracking`, a service configuration value read as a parameter. Off: the step records the month as not tracked and publishes nothing; on: the step computes and publishes the month.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, one SIT month is published with its record, the baseline rows of 2026-11-27 are unchanged, and a rerun of the same month writes the same values and no second record.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required query field is empty | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | The period sent is inverted | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the Reporting right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The month's record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | A source of the month is stale | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The first four texts are the legacy texts of RWB-E6-037 section 14, unchanged; MSG-GEN-003 and MSG-P1-001 are the FSD P9 texts of A2.6 and the platform texts the split adds. A message names a measure code, a product, a count and a date, and never a case, an account or a customer value.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-37 Steering dashboard (capability area Reporting) carries the benefit section; the legacy story says "No screen in this story", and the screen the FSD A2.6 names for the Finance and CFO delegate is assumed to be this section of SCR-37 rather than a new screen (GAP-2579; ASM-4254).

| State | What the user sees and does |
|---|---|
| Loading | Skeleton rows while `GET /reports/measures` returns |
| Published month | The month, the six measures, each value beside the baseline of 2026-11-27 and the variance, with the business date |
| Stale | The measure, its stale date and MSG-P1-001 for the source that has not arrived |
| No baseline | A measure without a frozen baseline row, shown with no variance and the reason |
| No tracking | The month not tracked yet, with no value and no action |
| Error | MSG-P4-002, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-003 or MSG-P7-003 with its field names and no partial value |

The section builds no number of its own: it renders the published rows and their stamps. The screen field order, the masking and the merge order belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the editable states of SCR-37 stay with the stories that own them.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: measure codes, formulas, units, data products, dimensions and the baseline date are data rows or request values, and the definition version is read, never written.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history, events or prompts: measures carry counts, amounts, days, percentages, codes and a definition version only.
- No read of another service's tables and no ACE view: every fact arrives on an event or on its owner's contract (DP-01, DP-05, DP-17).
- The month's rows and the record are one transaction: a month that cannot be recorded is never published (DP-03).
- The baseline rows of 2026-11-27 are frozen: no path rewrites, unfreezes or recomputes them.
- A measure of a closed month is never silently recomputed from a partial source; the stale date stands beside the value.
- Every example is synthetic and every measure value of a real month comes from the run, never from a fixture promoted to production.
- No data lake and no Power BI target is written by this story; the extract hand-over stays RWB-P9-E2009-APP's (DP-17).

##### 19. Out of scope

- The published shapes, the error model and the fakes of the read (RWB-P9-E6037-CON).
- The baseline measure set, `measure_definition`, the frozen baseline of 2026-11-27 and JOB-15's first build (RWB-P9-E1013-APP and RWB-P9-E1013-CON).
- The steering measures, the daily publish or hold and the extract hand-over (RWB-P9-E2009-APP and RWB-P9-E2009-CON), and the deployment, topics, alerts and runbook (RWB-P9-E2009-OPS).
- The decision log itself, its hash chain and the central ledger (rwb-decision, P7); this story writes a local record only.
- The event types of the month: they are owned and published by P3, S2, S6, S7, P6, P2 and P7.
- The regulatory returns of FEAT-RPT-07 (RWB-E8-001) and the classification and re-ageing of FEAT-RPT-10 (RWB-E8-002).
- The editable states of SCR-37 and the screen field list (RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the stories that own the screen).
- The cross-service journey harness and its evidence, when a wave 4 journey story is raised for this legacy key.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the regulatory returns of rwb-reporting — the single provided read fixed under `/api/recovery/reporting/v1` with its closed answer, its definition version and its frozen flag, the consumed decision-log read of rwb-decision, the six consumed topics of the read model, the returns decision element on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the negative declarations of the lake, the file and the event, the three owned tables and the three fakes**, so that **the app story of this legacy key builds against one fixed, testable contract on Day 1 and a return can never be published from a shape, a version or a source that nobody agreed**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop is the decoupling decision (DP-13, ADR-020). The Ownership Map gives rwb-reporting one provided operation, GET `/reports/measures`, and three tables; the TSD P9 endpoint inventory has the same single row, API-P9-001. The baseline therefore fixes that one operation and nothing else: no second path is invented for a return, because a second path would be a second owner of the same measure and the same answer.

What the baseline must fix for the return is narrower and sharper than a path. A measure is only defensible if the answer says which definition produced it, so the answer carries `definition_version`, `business_date`, the product group, the dimension and the `frozen` flag; the returns decision on the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1` carries the rule version in force (DP-03), which is what the legacy AC1 records. The baseline also fixes, in the negative, what the return must never be again: no data lake copy, no INT-19 extract file, no event of this service and no second Schedule, because Architecture v5 removes the lake (DP-17, ADR-018) and the pattern set of this key carries neither DP-09 nor DP-10.

The contested points are carried as gaps and assumptions rather than settled quietly: the return layout and the field types beyond the TSD P9 T3.1 definitions are unset, the query parameters beyond the five of T-A.2 are additive guesses, the consumed event names beyond `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` are catalogue work, the decision code is unnamed, the texts of MSG-P9-002 and MSG-P9-003 do not exist, the data lake removal conflicts with the FSD A2.7.2 and TSD P9 T5.1 as written, and the plan declares no C row for the decision-log read.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are in force, so the base, the schema, the topic and the queue follow the platform rule and not a local choice (RWB-PLT-TPL).
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the retry and `.dlt` topic convention are the platform baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); this document narrows them and never redefines them.
- The decision-record library of DP-03 and its topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` are available as a platform contract (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON).
- The operations and tables of section 12 are taken from the Ownership Map only: `measure_definition`, `measure_snapshot` and `measure_publish` are rwb-reporting's, the decision ledger is rwb-decision's, the case is rwb-case's and the documents are rwb-document's.
- The decision-log read of rwb-decision has no C row in the plan of this key; it is declared as consumed and faked (GAP-2583; ASM-4272).
- No build dependency: a CON story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the additive change to the rwb-reporting OpenAPI 3.1 document: the measure read of API-P9-001, its five query parameters, its 200 answer, its four error responses and its access right.
2. Fix the answer as a closed set: `measureCode`, `name`, `definitionVersion`, `businessDate`, `productGroup`, `dimensionCode`, `dimensionValue`, `value`, `caseCount`, `unit` and `frozen`, with no definition text, no formula and no free-text label.
3. Fix the fact that the return set is read through this one operation, and record that no second path is declared because the Ownership Map gives rwb-reporting one provided operation.
4. Record the consumed decision-log read of rwb-decision as consumed, one hop and faked, with the members the return needs.
5. Record the six consumed owner topics and the dedupe rule, and stress that event names beyond `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` are catalogue work.
6. Record the decision element: decision reference FEAT-RPT-07, the rule version in force, the business date, the definition version, the result PUBLISHED or HELD, through the local library on the shared topic.
7. Record the negative declarations: no event of this service, no domain workflow, no file, no data lake copy, no second base, no second Schedule.
8. Record the three owned tables as shapes: measure definition, frozen snapshot, publish row, with the unique keys of TSD P9 T3.1.
9. Publish the three fakes, the eight contract tests, the baseline tag and the sign-off note to RWB-P9-E8001-APP.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 500 with the envelope | The platform schema message | AC1 |
| X2 | A member is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC2 |
| X3 | The answer carries a formula, a definition text or a personal field | The closed-set test fails the build | None | AC2 |
| X4 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC7 |
| X5 | An event of rwb-reporting is declared, or the document declares a lake path | The absence test fails the build | None | AC6 |
| X6 | The document declares another service's operation as provided | The review fails the baseline; the operation is described as consumed and faked | None | AC5 |
| X7 | The answer quotes a rule version as a constant | The decision-element test fails; the version is a value of the record | None | AC3 |
| X8 | The Schedule of JOB-15 is restated with a name no source gives | The row carries the placeholder and the platform owns the registration | None | AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the ownership rows and the naming rule only |
| Negotiable | The member names beyond the TSD fields, the paging and the decision code are settled with the rwb-decision, gateway-bff and reporting owners; the base and the topic are fixed by the target |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story on Day 1 and stops the return from ever being published from an unversioned or unspecified shape |
| Estimable | One document change, one event element, one decision element, nine contract tables, three fakes and eight contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact and not against a business outcome |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/reporting/v1`; the document never declares another service's path as provided | DP-13; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR2 | The topic is `rwb.reporting.events.v1` and an event name would be `rwb.reporting.<Event>.v1`; this service owns no event | DP-14; Ownership Map |
| BR3 | Every consumed event carries the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, is keyed by caseId and carries no personal data | Architecture v5 event notes |
| BR4 | A read declares no Idempotency-Key and no request body; this baseline has no POST of its own | Platform baseline |
| BR5 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; the legacy texts stay unchanged | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR6 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a breaking change is a new major version | Architecture v5 API notes |
| BR7 | The document lists only operations and tables owned by rwb-reporting | Ownership Map |
| BR8 | No value a business person may change is a contract constant: measures, formulas, units, data products, dimensions and definition versions are data rows | BR-P9-007 |
| BR9 | The decision record is the local library's entry on the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1`, never an event of this service | DP-03 |
| BR10 | The data lake and Power BI copy is removed; the return is read from the frozen snapshots of this schema | DP-17; ADR-018 (GAP-2584) |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The operation, the closed answer, the decision element, the negatives and the tables are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story and the rwb-decision, gateway-bff and platform owners accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A member is added within major version 1, for example a data product filter | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A member is removed, renamed or retyped | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A lake path, a file or a published event appears | The absence test of AC6 fails | In review |

The snapshot and publish states of section 9 of the app story are the app story's; this baseline fixes the shapes and moves nothing.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-reporting | Owns the OpenAPI document and the fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version, the lake removal and the correction of the ownership rows the baseline consumes |
| Consuming teams (app story, rwb-decision, gateway-bff, platform library) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| Platform library owner | Owns the CloudEvents envelope, the error envelope, the naming rule and the decision library |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field and no formula is declared in the answer or in an event |

The per-service login name behind the security scheme is not part of this baseline; the document names the scheme "the rwb-reporting login (DP-02)".

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Measure answer | `measureCode` DF-RPT-032, `name` DF-RPT-033, `definitionVersion` DF-RPT-037, `businessDate` DF-RPT-044, `productGroup` DF-RPT-045, `dimensionCode` DF-RPT-046, `dimensionValue` DF-RPT-047, `value` DF-RPT-048, `caseCount` DF-RPT-049, `unit` DF-RPT-036, `frozen` DF-RPT-051 |
| Publish element | `businessDate` DF-RPT-054, `status` DF-RPT-055 with PUBLISHED or HELD, `caseListCount` DF-RPT-056, `dashboardCount` DF-RPT-057, `heldReason` DF-RPT-058 |
| Decision element | FEAT-RPT-07 as the decision reference, the rule version in force, the business date, the definition version, the result PUBLISHED or HELD, decided at; DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 |
| Consumed facts | `caseId` and the decision facts of a date, from the rwb-decision read and the six topics; codes, dates, amounts and counts only |
| Not declared | Any formula, definition text, approved by, personal field, lake path or file (GAP-2583; ASM-4271) |

The field types and required flags of the answer beyond TSD P9 T3.1, the page limits and the optional dimension filter are settled in the baseline review (GAP-2583; ASM-4274).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-reporting (P9); base `/api/recovery/reporting/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/reports/measures` | Measure[] of status 200 out: the members of section 11 for the frozen rows of a period, filtered by measure, product, route, from and to | Reporting, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The operation answers 401, 403 and 503 with the error envelope and one message ID of section 14; TSD P9 T-A.2 fixes the request, the answer and the three errors. It is the only provided operation of the baseline, because the Ownership Map gives rwb-reporting one (GAP-2583; ASM-4270).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | the decision-log read of `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The decision facts and the rule version of a business date, faked. The plan declares no C row for it (GAP-2583; ASM-4272) |

One row, one hop, on the owner's published contract; no row reads a table or a view of another service, and the document declares no other consumed operation.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The Ownership Map gives rwb-reporting no event; the returns record is relayed on the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1` by the local library of DP-03 and never as an event of this service.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Consumer contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (event 05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | caseId, fromState, toState, changedAt, behind the count measures; dedupe by the CloudEvents id |
| The notice and contact facts | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 rwb-comms | The notice and contact measures |
| The treatment outcome facts | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | S2 rwb-treatment | The settlement and restructuring measures |
| The debt-sale lot facts | `rwb.debtsale.events.v1` | S6 rwb-debtsale | The sale measures |
| The write-off and recovery facts | `rwb.writeoff.events.v1` | S7 rwb-writeoff | The write-off and recovery measures |
| The payment facts | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | P8 rwb-payment | The cash and recovery measures |

The connection matrix names rwb-reporting as a listener on exactly these six owners, so the rows are not a new claim. The event names beyond the first are Not specified in the sources read for this WP and are pinned by the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog (GAP-2583; ASM-4273).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The Ownership Map gives rwb-reporting no workflow; the return runs as the step of JOB-15 of section 12.6 inside the service's own run, and the baseline declares no child workflow, no activity contract and no Nexus call.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Job | Queue | When | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| JOB-15, the daily reporting run of rwb-reporting | `rwb-reporting` | Daily at 01:30 | The returns step of the app story; the baseline declares no second Schedule, no Quartz row and no shared job table |

The Schedule name and the registration detail are the platform's and are Not specified in the sources read for this WP (GAP-2583; ASM-4276).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| measure_definition | P9 (rwb_reporting) | The definition in force: measure code, name, formula as data, data product, unit, definition version, valid from |
| measure_snapshot | P9 (rwb_reporting) | The value per measure, definition version, business date, product group, dimension and the frozen flag |
| measure_publish | P9 (rwb_reporting) | The PUBLISHED or HELD status of a business date with the two counts and the held reason |

`decision_log_entry` is P7 rwb-decision's, `recovery_case` is P3 rwb-case's, `document` is P5 rwb-document's and the ACE views are P1's; the document names them only as consumed answers (DP-01). No table of `rwb_reporting` carries a formula string as a contract constant, a definition text or a personal field (AC2).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-decision WireMock | The decision facts of a date, an empty day, a refused write and an answer beyond the budget; the path and the members are fixed with the P7 owner (GAP-2583; ASM-4272) | App story, contract tests |
| decision-record library stub | An accepted record carrying the rule version and a stopped chain | App story, contract tests |
| event harness | One synthetic business date across the six topics, a repeat delivery with the same CloudEvents id and a stale product | App story, contract tests |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 provided, 1 consumed | The measure read provided; the decision-log read of P7 consumed; one hop each |
| Kafka | None declared as published, 6 topics declared as consumed | The read model of the day; the decision record is the library's on the shared topic |
| Temporal | The job's own run | JOB-15 on `rwb-reporting`; no workflow of this key |
| File | None | No file and no lake path is declared (GAP-2584; ASM-4275) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The additive change to `openapi/rwb-reporting-v1.yaml` for the measure read and its closed answer, the AsyncAPI note naming the six consumed topics and no published event, the contract README rows for the decision element and the negatives, and the three WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/reporting/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 is applied as a prohibition and adds no dependency: the decision facts arrive on the owner's contract. DP-17 is not in the pattern set of this key and adds no dependency; the lake removal it states is recorded once as a conflict and an assumption.

**Build steps**

1. Add the measure read and the closed answer of AC2 to the OpenAPI document and validate the closed-set rule in the pipeline.
2. Record the decision-log read of AC5 and the six consumed topics of AC4, and validate the AsyncAPI note against the registry.
3. Record the decision element of AC3 with the placeholder on the decision code and the rule version.
4. Record the negatives of AC6 and write the absence test for a lake path, a file, an event and a second base.
5. Record the three tables of AC8 with the unique keys of TSD P9 T3.1.
6. Publish the three fakes and the eight contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
7. Baseline tag and the sign-off note, including the app story and the rwb-decision, gateway-bff and platform owners.

**Done when** the OpenAPI and AsyncAPI artefacts validate in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the three fakes answer every consumed path, the drift test is green and the app story has accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the Reporting right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The returns decision record could not be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P1-001 | A data product is stale at the read boundary | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A downstream does not answer within the budget | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P9-002 | The counts behind a publish do not match | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2583; ASM-4266) |
| MSG-P9-003 | A measure has no definition in force | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2583; ASM-4266) |

The schema-validation message of a failed body and the message of a consumed call that does not answer in time are the platform's own and are not redefined here. MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P4-002 are copied unchanged from the legacy story, which is the source of both texts.

##### 15. Screens and states

The baseline serves the frozen measure set to SCR-37 Steering dashboard and to the reporting screens of the module through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); the screens, their states and their field masks belong to the story that owns each view and to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The legacy story says there is no screen of its own, and none is declared here.

##### 16. Test cases

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-E8-001-01 | AC1 | Component | A synthetic business date whose read answers the frozen set; the contract half answers the answer of AC2 and the decision of AC3 |
| TC-E8-001-02 | AC2 | Component | The decision record forced to refuse; the contract half answers the stopped chain of AC7 |
| TC-E8-001-03 | Access | Contract | RW-BIANAL reads in scope and a role without Reporting R is refused with MSG-P4-002; the contract half answers the 403 of AC1 |

The four legacy cases keep their legacy order and their legacy intent as the evidence the contract serves; the eight contract cases test the artefact and are new. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the measures, formulas, units, data products, dimensions, definition versions and the rule version stay data rows of their owners.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: case IDs, measure codes, codes, dates, amounts and counts only.
- The contract names only rwb-reporting tables and only the one operation owned by rwb-reporting; the decision-log read is consumed and faked, never declared as provided (DP-01).
- One base, one topic and one queue per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- No retired element is introduced: the absence test fails a build that declares a lake path, an INT-19 file, a Quartz row or a published event.
- Every example in the document is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope, the CloudEvents envelope and the naming rule come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.
