##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One version shape for the load, the approval, the read and the run; the version is `agent_policy` or `agent_prompt` and its label is unique for the agent and the kind | TSD P10 v2 T3.1; ASM-0995 |
| BR2 | The autonomy mode is one of the values of LOV-AUTONOMY and the status one of the values of LOV-CONFIG-STATUS; the contract accepts no other value and maps none | TSD P10 v2 T3.2; ASM-0992 |
| BR3 | A version takes effect only after approval and only from its valid-from date; a LOADED version is never in force | FSD P10 v3 A2.1 AC-ALT-P10-001-01; TSD P10 v2 DF-AGT-021 to DF-AGT-023 |
| BR4 | The loader may not approve their own version | FSD P10 v3 A2.1 AC-EXC-P10-001-03 |
| BR5 | The version row, the local decision record and the outbox row are one transaction; a refused record write leaves the version LOADED | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; DP-03 |
| BR6 | The configuration version travels in the rule-version element of the record, and no rule row and no package version is named, because no Drools package decides a configuration change | Legacy RWB-E3-030 AC1; ASM-0998 |
| BR7 | One REST base per service and one topic per service: this document declares `/api/recovery/agent/v1` and consumes the shared record topic; it never declares another service's path as provided | DP-13; DP-01; Ownership Map v1 |
| BR8 | The rights are rwb-access's: the contract names the capability area and the right of each operation and never restates role membership | DP-01; FSD P10 v3 A2.12.3.3; ASM-0994 |
| BR9 | Both admin operations carry the Idempotency-Key rule, and a repeat with the same key writes nothing new | TSD P10 v2 T-A.2; R-UNI-40 |
| BR10 | No business value in the contract: the level, the label, the dates, the thresholds and the review date are rows of the loaded version and never literals of this document | BR-P10-012; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | LOAD accepted | the file follows the version shape, the lists and the identity rule | LOADED |
| None | LOAD refused | a required field is empty, a value is outside its list, or the label exists for the agent and the kind | None, and nothing is written |
| LOADED | APPROVE | the approver is not the loader and the record is written in the same transaction | APPROVED |
| LOADED | SELF_APPROVAL refused | the approver is the loader | LOADED, unchanged |
| LOADED | RECORD refused | the local decision record cannot be written | LOADED, because the transaction rolls back |
| APPROVED | IN FORCE | the business date is at or after `valid_from` and before `valid_to` | APPROVED, in force for the date |
| APPROVED | RETIRE | `valid_to` is passed or a later version is approved for the same agent | RETIRED, and the row stays readable |

The status column carries the three values of LOV-CONFIG-STATUS (TSD P10 v2 DF-AGT-021); "in force for a date" is read from the status with the two date columns and is not a fourth value, so the contract adds no status and no state to the table. The contract document itself moves Draft → In review → Baselined as the app and test stories accept it, and a breaking change to a consumed element returns it to In review.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-agent | Owns the version shape, the three operations, the record payload, the ordering rule, the message map and the fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change to the version shape or to the record payload, and any change to the ordering rule |
| The rwb-decision owner | Owns the record library and the shared topic, and signs off the payload and the transaction rule taken from its document |
| The rwb-access owner | Owns the capability areas, the rights and the role matrix, and signs off the right named on each operation |
| The rwb-case owner | Owns the lists and the parameters, and confirms that this contract re-declares neither |
| The rwb-agent app and test stories of this key | Review and accept the parts they consume |
| Center of excellence analyst (RW-COE) and risk and model risk officer (RW-RISK) | Named as the actors of the load and of the approval; the roles stay rows of rwb-access |

The deployment identity that serves the three operations is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0637; ASM-1009); the document names it "the rwb-agent login (DP-02)" and leaves the name to the platform set-up story.

##### 11. Data

The contract declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Version element | agent code over LOV-AGENT, kind POLICY or PROMPT, version label inside varchar(20), autonomy mode over LOV-AUTONOMY, status over LOV-CONFIG-STATUS, valid-from date, optional valid-to date, loader reference, approver reference |
| Policy fields of the version | model code, model version, output schema reference, allowed tools, confidence floor, timeout in seconds, daily cost cap, price per 1k tokens, alert role, review date, promotion conditions, watched measures, fallback rule, segment product group, segment region (DF-AGT-004 to DF-AGT-020) |
| Prompt fields of the version | body text and its SHA-256 hash in `body_hash`, with the same status, date and loader elements (DF-AGT-026 to DF-AGT-035) |
| Standard record columns | state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by (TSD P10 v2 T3.0); the approval instant is `updated_at` at the APPROVED transition |
| Load request | multipart file, kind, agent, validFrom, and the Idempotency-Key header (TSD P10 v2 API-P10-003) |
| Record payload | agent code, kind, configuration version, autonomy mode, the version in force before the change, approver role, valid-from date, record reference |
| Event envelope | the CloudEvents 1.0 attributes and the record reference; identifiers and facts only, no personal data |

The element names of the record payload are those of the record shape of the Temporal and Drools design (slide 16), read into this contract as the shell of the record, with the configuration version travelling in the rule-version element (ASM-1005); how the library names each member in JSON is its own and is not restated. The kind takes the two values POLICY and PROMPT, from the two resource names of TSD P10 v2 T3.1, because T3.2 carries no list for it (GAP-0637; ASM-1006). The column set and the column order of the loaded file are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0637; ASM-1007), and this document fixes the element set from the FSD field catalog and TSD P10 v2 T3.1 and leaves the physical layout to the contract freeze. `agent_policy` carries `approved_by` and no `approved_at`, so the approval instant is a derived element and not a column (GAP-0637; ASM-0996).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Method | Path | Purpose | Right | Errors | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-P10-002 | GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs` | List the policy and prompt versions per agent with status and dates; query agent, kind, status | Rules and parameters R | 401, 403, 503 | Not applicable |
| API-P10-003 | POST | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs` | Load a new policy or prompt version from a checked file; multipart file, kind, agent, validFrom | Rules and parameters C | 401, 403, 409, 422, 503 | Idempotency-Key header |
| API-P10-004 | POST | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve` | Approve a loaded version; no request body | Rules and parameters A | 401, 403, 404, 409, 503 | Idempotency-Key header |

The three operations are rwb-agent's and are declared once, by this contract. The service summary line of Arch v5 slide 16 names `GET/POST /agent-policies (admin)`; that line is a summary of the admin surface and not an operation inventory, and the paths above are the ones the operation inventory of TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 carries (GAP-0637; ASM-1004). The monitor read `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-runs` (API-P10-001) is the monitor stories' and is not declared here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. This contract consumes the record library and the access guard as platform elements and declares no REST operation of another service; a call of rwb-decision or rwb-access from the change path would be a separate C dependency and is not claimed (ASM-0999).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 owns the type and the central ledger; every service writes its own record | the record reference | record reference, agent code, kind, configuration version, autonomy mode, the version in force before the change, approver role, valid-from date |

The payload is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the version row and relayed with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope by the record library (DP-03). No agent event is published by a change: the P10 OUT line of Arch v5 slide 16 names AgentRunCompleted only, the agent event `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) on the service topic `rwb.agent.events.v1` is the run path's, and a configuration change publishes none.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The change path reads no topic and this contract declares no inbox handler.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The load and the approval are synchronous operations of the request path and the record is written in the request transaction; this contract declares no workflow, no activity and no task queue. AgentRunWorkflow on the queue `rwb-agent` reads the version in force at run time and belongs to the run contract.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule creates, promotes or retires a configuration version: the effective date is `valid_from` of the row, and the Arch v5 job map names no job for an agent configuration change.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| agent_policy | P10 (rwb_agent) | The policy version and its autonomy mode, status, dates, loader and approver (DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-025) |
| agent_prompt | P10 (rwb_agent) | The prompt version on the same version element (DF-AGT-026 to DF-AGT-035) |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_agent | The outbox, inbox and idempotency envelope of the record write and the two admin operations |

No other table is declared. `decision_log_entry` and `approval` are rwb-decision's and `role` and `permission` are rwb-access's; `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value`, `reference_row` and `lov_value` are rwb-case's, and the contract declares none of them (DP-01; Ownership Map v1).

| Fake | Serves | Documented answer |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-decision record stub | The record library contract and `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) | A committed record with its reference; a forced write failure; the outbox row and its relay with the CloudEvents attributes |
| rwb-access guard stub | The rights of the three operations (P4) | Rules and parameters R granted to RW-AUDIT, C to RW-COE and A to RW-RISK; a role without the right refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002 |
| gateway-bff route stub | The DP-19 route of SCR-46 | The merged screen answer carrying the version in force, its autonomy mode and its state; the refusal path of a role without the right; the degraded answer when the agent read is unreachable |

A drift between any fake and this document fails the contract test. The list rows of TSD P10 v2 T3.2 are not faked here; they arrive through the reference-data wiring of the platform set-up story and this contract adds no list dependency (ASM-0997).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `contract/agent-config-version.yaml` (the version shape of `agent_policy` and `agent_prompt`, with the lists of TSD P10 v2 T3.2), `contract/agent-config-operations.yaml` (the three operations with rights, errors and the Idempotency-Key rule), `contract/agent-config-record.md` (the record payload, the transaction rule and the event), `contract/agent-config-ordering.md` (LOADED, APPROVED, RETIRED, the in-force rule and the four-eyes refusal), `contract/agent-config-messages.md` (the message map) and the three WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/agent/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

Both dependencies are platform contract stories and neither is a build dependency of this story, which is Day 1 by rule. DP-13 adds no dependency because it is a naming rule.

**Build steps**

1. Write the version shape and the list references; add a schema lint that refuses a field outside the shape and a value outside its list.
2. Write the three operations with their rights, errors and the Idempotency-Key rule, and the note that resolves the Arch v5 summary label against the operation inventory.
3. Write the record payload and the transaction rule from the record library contract, with the version in the rule-version element.
4. Write the ordering rule: the three statuses, the in-force test, the four-eyes refusal and the 404 case.
5. Write the message map with the three legacy texts character for character and the two further IDs named only.
6. Build the three fakes and their fixtures.
7. Add the six contract tests, including the drift test between each fake and this document.
8. Tag the baseline and collect the sign-off of the app and test stories of this key and of the integration story of the wave.

**Done when.** The five contract files validate in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the three fakes answer every path and payload this document declares, and the app and test stories of this key have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required value of a version is empty, or a value is outside its list | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A caller without the right of the operation calls the read, the load or the approve | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written on the approval | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The three texts are the legacy texts of RWB-E3-030 and keep their wording character for character; this contract adds no message. Two further messages are named by the specifications and are recorded by ID only, because their wording is in neither the legacy message set nor the extracts: MSG-P7-002 for an approver who is also the loader (FSD P10 v3 A2.1 AC-EXC-P10-001-03) and MSG-P10-001 for a configuration file that fails a check (FSD P10 v3 A2.1 AC-EXC-P10-001-02). The `{field}` value names a field of the version shape only, and no text is invented for the two IDs.

##### 15. Screens and states

None in this story. The contract serves SCR-46 Agent monitor, states Shadow; live; paused, through the gateway-bff composite route only (DP-19), and the screen, its fields and its masking belong to the monitoring stories (RWB-P10-E1063-APP and RWB-P10-E2031-APP). The states are named here because the route answers them: the contract fixes the elements the route may carry — the version in force, its autonomy mode and its status — and fixes no panel and no layout. How a state of the screen maps to a value of LOV-AUTONOMY is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0637; ASM-1008) and is settled with the monitor stories.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the level, the label, the dates, the thresholds, the review date and the alert role are rows of the loaded version and never literals of this document (BR-P10-012).
- No personal data in an event, a fake or an example: the record carries agent codes, list values, dates and role names, and the loader and approver are references and not identities.
- The contract names only `rwb_agent` tables as owned and only rwb-agent's operations as provided; the record library, the access guard and the lists are consumed and never restated as this service's (DP-01, DP-03, DP-13).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base as provided, or a topic outside `rwb.agent.events.v1` and the shared record topic, fails the review (DP-13).
- The version shape accepts no value outside its list and maps none, so a level the source does not name cannot enter through a file.
- Every example and fixture is synthetic; no production file, record or payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The envelope, the record shape and the access guard come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.
- The wording of every message that this contract names is the legacy wording; where a source gives no text, the ID is recorded and no text is written.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E3-030 for rwb-agent. The autonomy level stops being a row of the shared configuration service and becomes `autonomy_mode` of a versioned `agent_policy` row in `rwb_agent` (DP-01; TSD P10 v2 T3.1, DF-AGT-008); the version is loaded and approved on the rwb-agent configuration operations published under `/api/recovery/agent/v1` (DP-13; TSD P10 v2 API-P10-002 to API-P10-004) and reached through the gateway-bff composite route for SCR-46 (DP-19); the change is recorded through the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` in the transaction that writes the version (DP-03). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **risk and model risk officer (RW-RISK)**, I want **to change the autonomy level of one agent as a versioned configuration row of the service that runs the agent — loaded by the center of excellence as a checked file, approved by me, recorded with the version that is now in force, and read by the run step at run time**, so that **an agent prepares the work and people decide where they must, and no change to what an agent may do unattended takes effect without a dated version, an approver and a decision record behind it**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story RWB-E3-030 gave the risk and model risk officer one administrative step: change the autonomy level for one agent and one decision as a versioned configuration row, and write the result to the decision log with the rule version, with nothing changed when the log cannot be written (FEAT-AGT-12; FSD P10 v3 A2.12; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row E3 · P10 · FEAT-AGT-12). It is an Admin feature of Epic 3, priority Should, read on SCR-46 Agent monitor in the states Shadow, live and paused, and its only operation in the legacy story is the monitor read `GET /admin/agent-runs` under Platform administration R. The BOT AI Risk Management Guidelines of 12 Sep 2025 put lifecycle risk management and a human decision on material actions behind every agent, which is what an autonomy level written and approved as data makes provable (Arch v5 slide 35 and the guideline row of the extract).

In the target the configuration row lives where the agent lives. rwb-agent owns the agent policies, the prompts, the runs, the guardrails and the evaluations in schema `rwb_agent` (Arch v5 slide 41), and the level is the `autonomy_mode` column of `agent_policy`, whose list is LOV-AUTONOMY — OFF, SHADOW and L1 — with the version status in LOV-CONFIG-STATUS, LOADED, APPROVED and RETIRED (TSD P10 v2 T3.1 DF-AGT-008 and DF-AGT-021, T3.2). A prompt version is the same shape in `agent_prompt` (DF-AGT-026 to DF-AGT-035), and the load carries a `kind` that selects one of the two (TSD P10 v2 API-P10-002). The legacy prerequisite FEAT-CWC-22 — the parameter catalog and configuration service of P3 — is therefore not read for this row: the parameter catalog keeps the parameters that are not agent configuration, and `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` stay with rwb-case under the §R3 default ruling (DP-01). That is the first realignment: the autonomy level is no longer a shared parameter row but a version of the owning service's own table. The unit of change is one agent's version, and the finer key that makes a level apply to one decision step belongs to the per-decision story, because `agent_policy` carries no decision column (GAP-0636; ASM-0993).

The second is the record. The legacy step wrote the decision log in process; the target writes the version row, the local decision record and the outbox row in one transaction, and the relay publishes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` for rwb-decision to seal (Temporal and Drools design slide 11 and slide 16; R-UNI-39; DP-03). That is what turns legacy AC2 from a promise into a property: if the record cannot be written, the version row is not written either, so nothing changes. The record names the configuration version in its rule-version element, because no Drools package is evaluated on a configuration change and `rule_row` stays with rwb-decision (DP-04 is not a pattern of this story; ASM-0998).

The third is the seam. The load and the approval are the two admin operations the service already publishes — `POST /admin/agent-configs` and `POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve`, with the read `GET /admin/agent-configs` — under the per-service base `/api/recovery/agent/v1` (DP-13; TSD P10 v2 API-P10-002 to API-P10-004; Ownership Map v1). The screen that shows the change is SCR-46 Agent monitor, served by the gateway-bff composite route, so the browser calls no owner service directly (DP-19; Arch v5 slides 8, 10 and 20). The gate on the loader approving their own version is the four-eyes rule the platform already states with MSG-P7-002 (FSD P10 v3 A2.1 AC-EXC-P10-001-03).

The step-up and step-down of a level on measured evidence is FEAT-AGT-15 and the Epic 8 key RWB-E8-004; the autonomy level per decision step is FEAT-ADM-01 and the Administration key RWB-AD-020. This story owns the plain change of one agent's version and nothing else. It owns both legacy criteria of RWB-E3-030 — AC1 and AC2 — and copies them verbatim in section 7; AC3 to AC9 are new and test the microservice deliverable of the title only. The legacy story carries no requirement ID and no BRD in the extracts carries FEAT-AGT-12, which section 18 records (GAP-0636).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P10-E3030-CON is published: the shape of a configuration version, the three operations with their rights, errors and Idempotency-Key rule, the decision-record payload written on a change, the ordering rule that a version takes effect only after approval, the message set and the contract fakes (GAP-0637).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library, the record shape and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` with its CloudEvents envelope. This story writes its record through the library and never writes the shared topic directly (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route contract for SCR-46 and its stub, so the exposure of the change is built and tested before the screen story lands (DP-19).
- The `rwb_agent` schema exists with the agent runtime baseline migration that carries `agent_policy` (DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-025) and `agent_prompt` (DF-AGT-026 to DF-AGT-035). RWB-P10-E1058-APP owns the schema and the baseline; this story issues no migration of its own and adds no table and no column (ASM-1001).
- A policy version is in force for the agent before the change: its `status` is APPROVED and the business date falls within `valid_from` and `valid_to`; the change is a new version and never an edit of the one in force (FSD P10 v3 A2.1 AC-ALT-P10-001-01).
- The lists used by the load are those of TSD P10 v2 T3.2: LOV-AGENT (INTAKE, SCREENING, LEGAL_DOC, EXTRACT, TDR_OFFER), LOV-AUTONOMY (OFF, SHADOW, L1), LOV-CONFIG-STATUS (LOADED, APPROVED, RETIRED), LOV-PRODUCT (MORTGAGE, HIRE_PURCHASE, SSME, UNSECURED) and LOV-REGION. The list rows are reference data of rwb-case under the §R3 default ruling; the wiring of the reference-data contract is the platform set-up story's (DP-07 with H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON there), and this story adds no list of its own and holds no copy of a list in code (ASM-0997).
- The version label is free text inside `policy_version` and `prompt_version`, both varchar(20). The labels P1 and PR1 of the FSD examples are illustrative and no format rule is stated (GAP-0636; ASM-0996).
- The approver is a person other than the loader, as the four-eyes rule requires; the approval instant is read from `updated_at` of the row at the APPROVED transition, because `agent_policy` carries `approved_by` and no `approved_at` column (GAP-0636; ASM-0996).
- The login is the rwb-agent login (DP-02): its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0636; ASM-1003).

##### 4. Flow

1. The center of excellence analyst (RW-COE) prepares one checked file for one agent and one kind, POLICY or PROMPT. The file carries the fields of the FSD field catalog and of the policy table: the agent code, the version label, the autonomy mode, the model code and version, the output schema reference, the allowed tools and the segment product group and region (FSD P10 v3 A2.12.3.2; TSD P10 v2 T3.1), together with the remaining policy fields of the version — the confidence floor, the timeout, the daily cost cap, the price per 1k tokens, the alert role, the review date, the promotion conditions, the watched measures, the fallback rule and the valid-from date.
2. The analyst calls `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs` with the file, the kind, the agent and the valid-from date, and an `Idempotency-Key` header (TSD P10 v2 API-P10-003 and T-A.2).
3. AgentConfigValidator checks the file against the field catalog and against the lists. A required value that is empty is refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-001 naming the field; a value outside its list is refused with 422 naming the field; a file that fails a further check is refused with 422 and no version row is written, and the version in force stays in force (FSD P10 v3 A2.1 AC-EXC-P10-001-02; VR-P10-012-1).
4. The version is written as one `agent_policy` row, or one `agent_prompt` row when the kind is PROMPT, with status LOADED, `loaded_by` the caller and `valid_from` the date of the file. No other schema is written: no `parameter_catalog` and no `parameter_value` row of rwb-case, and no `rule_row` of rwb-decision (DP-01).
5. The risk and model risk officer (RW-RISK) approves the version with `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve` and an `Idempotency-Key` header (TSD P10 v2 API-P10-004 and T-A.2). The operation is refused with 409 and MSG-P7-002 when the caller loaded the version (FSD P10 v3 A2.1 AC-EXC-P10-001-03); it is refused with 404 when the version does not exist.
6. RecordAndApply runs in one `rwb_agent` transaction: it moves the version to APPROVED with `approved_by`, it writes the local decision record that names the agent, the kind, the configuration version, the autonomy level, the version that was in force before, the approver role and the valid-from date, and it inserts the DecisionRecorded row in the outbox. A failed record write rolls the whole transaction back, so the version keeps status LOADED and no outbox row exists (DP-03; R-UNI-39; legacy AC2).
7. The DecisionRecorded row is relayed from the outbox to `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and rwb-decision seals it into the central ledger. The request waits for no confirmation: an autonomy change is not a point of no return.
8. A version is in force for a business date when its status is APPROVED and the date falls within `valid_from` and `valid_to`. The run step reads `autonomy_mode` from the row in force at run time and writes the value it used into `agent_run.autonomy_mode`; it reads no cache and no copy of the level is held anywhere (DP-01; TSD P10 v2 DF-AGT-043).
9. A repeat of the load or of the approval with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the first answer and writes nothing: no second version row, no second record and no second outbox row (TSD P10 v2 T-A.2; R-UNI-40).
10. The analyst and the risk officer read the version and its state on SCR-46 Agent monitor. The screen is served by the gateway-bff composite route, which calls the config read on `/api/recovery/agent/v1` and merges the answers; the browser calls no owner service directly (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A required field of the file is empty | The load is refused with 422 before any row is written, and the field is named | MSG-GEN-001 | AC3 |
| X2 | The autonomy mode of the file is not a value of LOV-AUTONOMY | The load is refused with 422 and the field is named; no version row exists and no value is mapped to a nearby level | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4 |
| X3 | The same agent and version label are loaded a second time | The load is refused with 409 and no second row exists; the version in force is unchanged | None | AC9 |
| X4 | The local decision record cannot be written on the approval | The transaction rolls back: the version keeps status LOADED, no outbox row exists and no notification is sent | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, AC5 |
| X5 | The approver is the loader of the version | The approval is refused with 409 and the version keeps status LOADED | MSG-P7-002 | AC6 |
| X6 | A caller without the right of the operation calls the load or the approve | The call is refused with 403, nothing is written and nothing is returned | MSG-P4-002 | AC7 |
| X7 | The version is LOADED and its valid-from date has arrived | It is not in force: the run step keeps the previous APPROVED version, because a version takes effect only after approval | None | AC6 |
| X8 | The same request arrives again with the same Idempotency-Key | No second version row, no second record and no second outbox row; the first answer is returned and the repeat is counted | None | AC9 |
| X9 | The gateway-bff route cannot reach the agent read | The screen shows the route's own degraded answer and no business value is defaulted; no version row is written by the screen | None | AC7 |

The step writes no case field and raises no case task on any path, so none of these exceptions moves a case. X4 is the behaviour legacy AC2 and FSD A2.12 AC-EXC-P10-012-02 describe, and X6 is FSD A2.12 AC-EXC-P10-012-01.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on Day 1 against RWB-P10-E3030-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, the agent runtime baseline and the three contract fakes; it waits for no other in-lane story and its metadata "Depends on (build)" holds no non-CON story of this service |
| Negotiable | The version label, the file format of the load and the granularity of "one decision" are agreed at the contract freeze and recorded as assumptions; the values themselves are always rows of the version |
| Valuable | The level an agent may act at is a dated, approved and recorded version of the owning service, and a failed record leaves nothing changed |
| Estimable | One controller, one validator, one repository, one record writer, one route and its contract test |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each of the nine criteria of section 7 is one automated test against the decision-record, access and route fakes; no criterion needs a production file |

AC1 and AC2 are the legacy criteria of RWB-E3-030, copied verbatim, and AC3 to AC9 are new for this service change.

**Target reading.** AC1 and AC2 each gained one Given line and lost nothing. AC1 gained `Given the rwb-decision contract mock records the decision log entry with the rule version` as its first Given, because the write that the legacy criterion asserts is now a cross-service act — the local record through the RWB-PLT-E1027-CON library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` that rwb-decision seals — and the criterion cannot be proved without the contract fake that stands in for that write (DP-03). AC2 gained `Given the rwb-decision contract mock refuses the decision log write` as its first Given for the same reason: the legacy line "the decision log cannot be written" now has one concrete, testable cause, the refusal of the record library, and the fake is the only way to force it. Every other legacy line and value is unchanged, including "the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place", "the user acts on the screen", both Then lines and MSG-P7-003.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The autonomy level of an agent is `autonomy_mode` of a versioned configuration row and not a value in code; a change of the level is a new version | BR-P10-012; FEAT-AGT-12; TSD P10 v2 DF-AGT-008 |
| BR2 | A version is never edited in place: a change writes a new version with a new label, and the version in force stays readable with its own fields and dates | FSD P10 v3 A2.1 AC-ALT-P10-001-01; TSD P10 v2 DF-AGT-022 and DF-AGT-023 |
| BR3 | A version takes effect only after approval and only from its valid-from date; a version in status LOADED is not in force | FSD P10 v3 A2.1 AC-ALT-P10-001-01; TSD P10 v2 DF-AGT-021 |
| BR4 | The version row, the local decision record and the outbox row are one `rwb_agent` transaction; a failed record write leaves the version LOADED and writes nothing else | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; DP-03; legacy RWB-E3-030 AC2 |
| BR5 | The version on the decision record is the configuration version label, and the record names the agent and the kind in its rule-identity element; no Drools package is evaluated and no rule row is read on a configuration change | Legacy RWB-E3-030 AC1; ASM-0998; DP-04 not applied |
| BR6 | The load needs Rules and parameters C, the approve A and the read R; a caller without the right is refused with MSG-P4-002 and nothing changes | TSD P10 v2 API-P10-002 to API-P10-004 and T6.1; FSD P10 v3 A2.12.3.3; ASM-0994 |
| BR7 | The loader may not approve their own version; the approval is refused with 409 and MSG-P7-002 | FSD P10 v3 A2.1 AC-EXC-P10-001-03 |
| BR8 | Only the values of LOV-AUTONOMY are accepted, and a value outside the list is refused rather than mapped or created | TSD P10 v2 T3.2; ASM-0992 |
| BR9 | The run step reads the level from the row in force at run time and records the value it used on the run; no cache and no second copy of the level is held | DP-01; FSD P10 v3 A2.12; TSD P10 v2 DF-AGT-043 |
| BR10 | The configuration row is `rwb_agent`'s and no foreign key crosses a schema: `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` stay with rwb-case and `rule_row` stays with rwb-decision | DP-01; Template and Rules §R3 default ruling; Ownership Map v1 |
| BR11 | One load and one approval per Idempotency-Key: a repeat returns the first answer and writes no second row, no second record and no second outbox row | TSD P10 v2 T-A.2; R-UNI-40 |
| BR12 | No personal data is written by the change: the version holds agent codes, list values, numbers, dates and a user reference for the loader and the approver, and the record carries no personal data | TSD P10 v2 T3.1 and T6.2; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | LOAD | the checked file passes the field catalog and the lists | LOADED |
| None | LOAD_REFUSED | a required value is empty, a value is outside its list, or the label already exists for the agent | None, and nothing is written |
| LOADED | APPROVE | the approver is not the loader and the record is written in the same transaction | APPROVED |
| LOADED | SELF_APPROVAL_REFUSED | the approver is the loader | LOADED, unchanged |
| LOADED | RECORD_WRITE_FAILED | the local decision record cannot be written | LOADED, because the transaction rolls back |
| APPROVED | IN_FORCE | the business date is at or after `valid_from` and before `valid_to` | APPROVED, in force for the date |
| APPROVED | RETIRE | `valid_to` is passed or a later version is approved for the same agent | RETIRED, and the row stays readable |

These are the states of a configuration version and not a case state machine. The status column carries the three values of LOV-CONFIG-STATUS (TSD P10 v2 DF-AGT-021); "in force for a date" is read from the status together with the two date columns and is not a fourth value. **This story moves no case status**: `recovery_case` is neither read nor written, no task and no assignment row is written, and no run is started, retried or ended.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Risk and model risk officer (RW-RISK) | Primary actor of the change: approves a loaded version under Rules and parameters A, reads the version and its record, and reads the state on SCR-46 |
| Center of excellence analyst (RW-COE) | Loads a version under Rules and parameters C, reads the version list, and may not approve what they loaded |
| Platform administrator (RW-PLATADM) | Holds CRUD on Platform administration in TSD P10 v2 T6.1 and R in the legacy permission list; reads the versions and the run evidence, and may re-drive a refused approval |
| Internal audit (RW-AUDIT), Compliance and PDPA officer (RW-COMPLY), Security administrator (RW-SECADM) | Read the version list and its records, as the legacy permission list allows under Platform administration R |
| Data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW) | Reads the versions and the lists the change uses |
| rwb-agent service identity (the rwb-agent login, DP-02) | Writes the version row, the local record and the outbox row, and serves the three operations |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the local decision record and its outbox row (Decision log C) |
| SY-RULES rules identity | Not used by this story: no Drools package is evaluated on a configuration change |
| RW-REFADM | Holds neither Rules and parameters C nor A; refused on the load and on the approve with MSG-P4-002 |

The legacy permission list of RWB-E3-030 gives Platform administration R to RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM and RW-SECADM, while the configuration operations of TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 are governed by Rules and parameters with rights R, C and A and FSD P10 v3 A2.12.3.3 names the risk and model risk officer as the primary user. The right under which a change is made is therefore Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0636; ASM-0994), and this story reads the legacy row as the read on the monitor while the change is made under Rules and parameters, reconciled by rwb-access. The per-service login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0636; ASM-1003); the story names it "the rwb-agent login (DP-02)" until it is agreed.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity in rwb_agent | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-025 | agent_policy | id, agent_code, policy_version, model_code, model_version, output_schema_ref, allowed_tools, autonomy_mode, segment_product_group, segment_region_code, confidence_floor, timeout_seconds, daily_cost_cap_thb, price_per_1k_tokens_thb, alert_role, review_date, evaluation_run_id, promotion_conditions, watch_measures, fallback_rule, status, valid_from, valid_to, loaded_by, approved_by | Write on a POLICY load and approve; read on the list |
| DF-AGT-026 to DF-AGT-035 | agent_prompt | id, agent_code, prompt_version, body_text, body_hash, status, valid_from, valid_to, loaded_by, approved_by | Write on a PROMPT load and approve; read on the list |
| DF-AGT-043 | agent_run | autonomy_mode | Read only here: written by the run step with the value in force at run time, not by this story |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local library) and decision_log_entry (rwb_decision, owner P7) | all fields, written through P7's library and sealed by rwb-decision | Write locally |
| TSD P10 v2 T3.0 | standard record columns of `agent_policy` and `agent_prompt` | state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by | Write; `updated_at` is the approval instant (ASM-0996) |

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 and TSD P10 v2 T3.1. No foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01). Three tables that the legacy step touched are no longer read or written by this slice: `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` stay with rwb-case under the §R3 default ruling, because the autonomy level is no longer a shared parameter row, and `rule_row` stays with rwb-decision, because no Drools package decides a configuration change. The `body_text` and `body_hash` of a prompt version are stored as the file supplies them and the hash is computed on the text; the file format of the load and its column order are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0636; ASM-0995). The version label has no format rule (GAP-0636; ASM-0996). No personal data is written: the loader and the approver appear as user references and the record carries no personal data.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Method | Path | Purpose | Right |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs` | List policy and prompt versions per agent with status and dates; query agent, kind, status (API-P10-002) | Rules and parameters R |
| POST | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs` | Load a new policy or prompt version from a checked file; multipart file, kind, agent, validFrom; `Idempotency-Key` (API-P10-003) | Rules and parameters C |
| POST | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve` | Approve a loaded version; no request body; `Idempotency-Key` (API-P10-004) | Rules and parameters A |

The three operations are the service's own and are declared once; their shape, their error codes, the Idempotency-Key rule and the checks of the file are the contract of RWB-P10-E3030-CON, which this story implements. The legacy monitor read on the shared base under DP-13 becomes `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-runs` (API-P10-001, Platform administration R); it belongs to the monitor stories and is not changed here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The decision record is written through a library and not over REST, and the rights of the three operations are resolved by the access guard that the service template and the gateway-bff route install, so this story calls no rwb-access operation of its own and claims no contract dependency (ASM-0999). No reference-data operation is called by this story either: the list rows are wired by the platform set-up story (ASM-0997).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 owns the type and the central ledger; every service writes its own record | the record reference | record reference, agent code, kind POLICY or PROMPT, configuration version, autonomy level, the version in force before the change, approver role, valid-from date |

The row is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the version row and relayed with the CloudEvents envelope (DP-03). No agent event is published for the change: the P10 OUT line of Arch v5 slide 16 names AgentRunCompleted only, and the agent event `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) on the service topic `rwb.agent.events.v1` is published by the run path of RWB-P10-E1058-APP and not here, while the version is read from the table through the config read. No personal data is carried.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The change is a request path and reads no topic; this story has no inbox handler of its own.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The load and the approval are synchronous admin operations of the request path, and the record is written in the request transaction; no Temporal workflow, no activity and no task queue is added by this story. The run that reads the level belongs to AgentRunWorkflow on the queue `rwb-agent` and to the run story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule creates, changes, promotes or retires a configuration version; the effective date is `valid_from` of the row and needs no job (ASM-1000).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| agent_policy | P10 (rwb_agent) | The policy version: DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-025, including `autonomy_mode`; created by the agent runtime baseline migration, not by this story |
| agent_prompt | P10 (rwb_agent) | The prompt version: DF-AGT-026 to DF-AGT-035; created by the same baseline |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_agent | The outbox, inbox and idempotency envelope of the record write and of the two admin operations (DP-09 library elements, not a pattern of this story) |

`decision_log_entry` is a rwb-decision table and is written only through the P7 decision-record library (DP-01, DP-03). `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` are rwb-case tables and `rule_row` is a rwb-decision table; this story reads and writes none of them.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-decision decision-record library stub | The P7 record contract and `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) | A committed record with its reference; a forced write failure on the approve; the outbox row and its relay |
| rwb-access guard stub | The rights of the three operations (P4) | Rules and parameters C and A granted to RW-COE and RW-RISK; a role without the right refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002 |
| gateway-bff composite route stub | The DP-19 route of SCR-46 | The merged screen answer with the version in force and its state; the degraded answer of X9 |

The list values of TSD P10 v2 T3.2 are not faked here: they arrive through the baseline wiring of the platform set-up story and this story adds no list dependency (ASM-0997).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 3 provided, 0 consumed | The config read, the load and the approve on `/api/recovery/agent/v1`; the rights are resolved by the access guard; no operation of another service is called |
| Kafka | 1 published, 0 consumed | `rwb.decision-record.v1` published through the outbox; nothing consumed |
| Temporal | 0 workflows, 0 activities | The change is synchronous and the run that reads the level is the run story's |
| File | 1 per load | The checked file of a policy or prompt version is the input of the load and is stored as rows; no run-time file exchange |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.agent`, module `config`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.agent.config`. No front-end module: the change is called from the Workbench through the gateway-bff route, and the screen is the monitor story's.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/agent/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The two platform contract stories are build dependencies of the metadata rows, and the third build dependency is RWB-P10-E3030-CON, the contract story of this key. DP-13 adds no dependency because it is a naming rule.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AgentConfigController | REST controller | The three operations, the multipart load, the Idempotency-Key header, validation errors as problem responses |
| AgentConfigValidator | Service | Checks the file against the field catalog and the lists, and returns the field and the check that failed |
| AgentConfigService | Service | Loads, approves and retires a version; applies the four-eyes rule; resolves the version in force for a business date |
| AgentConfigRepository | Repository | Reads and writes `agent_policy` and `agent_prompt` only, in `rwb_agent` |
| DecisionRecordWriter | Library adapter | Writes the local decision record with the configuration version, the level and the approver role, hash-linked, in the same transaction (DP-03) |
| ConfigView | Read model | The version list and the one version in force, for the read operation and the route |
| Screen adapter | None | SCR-46 is served by the gateway-bff composite route and belongs to the monitor stories |

**Database and migrations**

- No new table and no new column. `agent_policy` and `agent_prompt` come from the agent runtime baseline migration of `rwb_agent` that RWB-P10-E1058-APP owns, and this story adds only what TSD P10 v2 T3.1 already lists (ASM-1001).
- If the baseline does not carry the table when the story is picked up, the script that adds it takes its number from the rwb-agent Flyway sequence; that number is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0636; ASM-1001) and no number is claimed here.
- One index for the read of the version in force: `agent_policy (agent_code, status, valid_from)` and the same on `agent_prompt`, so the in-force lookup and the duplicate-label check are key lookups and not scans. The index name is a naming-library value and not a business value.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The values the load accepts are the list values of TSD P10 v2 T3.2 and none is written in code: LOV-AGENT, LOV-AUTONOMY (OFF, SHADOW, L1), LOV-CONFIG-STATUS (LOADED, APPROVED, RETIRED), LOV-PRODUCT and LOV-REGION.
- The kind of a version is POLICY or PROMPT and is carried by the resource, `agent_policy` or `agent_prompt`; the list name of the kind is not in TSD P10 v2 T3.2, and only the two resource names are used (GAP-0636; ASM-0995).
- The version label is free text and its format is not fixed by any source (GAP-0636; ASM-0996).
- The file format of the load is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0636; ASM-0995); the contract of RWB-P10-E3030-CON fixes the column set from the field catalog of FSD P10 v3 A2.12.3.2 and TSD P10 v2 T3.1, and the two are one document.

**Build steps**

1. AgentConfigRepository and the in-force resolver over `agent_policy` and `agent_prompt`, with the duplicate-label check; tests for AC3 and AC6.
2. AgentConfigValidator against the field catalog and LOV-AUTONOMY, with the field and the check named in the refusal; tests for AC3, AC4 and X1.
3. The load operation with the multipart file and the Idempotency-Key; tests for AC3, AC9 and X3.
4. The approve operation with the four-eyes rule and the version transition; tests for AC6 and X5.
5. DecisionRecordWriter and the one-transaction write of the version, the record and the outbox row, with the rollback path; tests for AC2 and AC5.
6. The read operation and the route contract with the refusal path and the degraded answer; tests for AC7 and X9.
7. The run-time read of `autonomy_mode` and its hand-over to the run step, including the value on `agent_run`; test for AC8.
8. The list wiring check against the baseline of RWB-P10-E1058-APP and the full scenario run over synthetic rows for a business date; tests for AC6 and AC8.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, no version row exists without its decision record, every record names the configuration version and the approver role, a version in status LOADED never takes effect, the decision-record and route contract tests stay green, and the SIT week showed no change of a level without an approved version behind it.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required value of the file is empty, or a value is outside its list | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A caller without the right of the operation calls the load or the approve | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written on the approval | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The three messages are the legacy messages of RWB-E3-030 and keep their wording. Two further messages are named by the specifications and are not restated here because their wording is not in the legacy message set: MSG-P7-002 for an approver who is also the loader (FSD P10 v3 A2.1 AC-EXC-P10-001-03) and MSG-P10-001 for a configuration file that fails a check (FSD P10 v3 A2.1 AC-EXC-P10-001-02). This story names them by ID, tests the code and the ID, and invents no text for them. No other message is added.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-46 Agent monitor, states Shadow; live; paused, is the legacy screen of RWB-E3-030 and shows the version in force and its autonomy level. The screen and its read belong to the agent monitoring stories (RWB-P10-E1063-APP and RWB-P10-E2031-APP), and this story changes no panel, no field order and no masking; what it adds is the data: the agent, the kind, the version label, the autonomy level, the status, the valid-from date, the approver role and the approval instant, read from `agent_policy` or `agent_prompt` and the record through the config read and the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The mapping from the level to the screen state — shadow for SHADOW, live for L1 and paused for OFF — is a reading of the three states the legacy story names against the three values of LOV-AUTONOMY, and it is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0636; ASM-1002); it is shown for the user's orientation and changes no value. The screen fields, their order and their masking are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0636; ASM-1002) and stay with the monitor stories.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the autonomy levels are the values of LOV-AUTONOMY, the statuses those of LOV-CONFIG-STATUS, and every other value of a version is a row of the loaded file (BR-P10-012).
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts: the version holds agent codes, list values, numbers, dates and user references for the loader and the approver, and the record carries no personal data.
- No read or write of another service's tables: the version lives in `rwb_agent`, the record is written through the P7 library, and `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value` and `rule_row` are never touched (DP-01).
- The record is written in the same transaction as the version, before the version can take effect; a failed write rolls the whole transaction back (R-UNI-39).
- A version in status LOADED never takes effect, and no date, level or status is defaulted to make one take effect.
- The change starts no agent run, retries no run and changes no run status; the value a run used is written by the run step and not by this story.
- The change moves no case status and raises no task or assignment row; the case side of an autonomy decision belongs to rwb-case.
- Only the version row, the record and the outbox row are new data; no copy of a list, of a parameter or of the level is written outside `rwb_agent`.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E3-031 for rwb-agent. The drift check stays with the service that owns the agent rows: the facts are built per agent and segment from `agent_run` and `agent_evaluation`, the calibration figure is read from the ACE score facts through rwb-source-data's contract (DP-05), the thresholds and the review date are rows of the policy version in force, a breach writes `agent_alert` with type DRIFT together with the local decision record that names the owner role and the review date (DP-03), and the result is read on SCR-46 through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **risk and model risk officer (RW-RISK)**, I want **the Workbench to watch the calibration and the drift of each agent and segment on the rows its own runs and evaluations leave, to raise a drift alert that carries the measured value against the threshold of the policy version in force, and to record a decision with an owner role and a review date on a breach**, so that **an agent whose answers are drifting is caught on evidence rather than on a complaint, a person owns the correction with a date on it, and no alert is raised for a segment whose sample is too small to prove anything**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story RWB-E3-031 gave one unattended check to the risk and model risk officer: it watched calibration and drift, it raised a decision with an owner and a date on a breach, and it wrote the result to the decision log with the rule version (FEAT-AGT-13; FSD P10 v3 A2.13). It depends on FEAT-AGT-06, the agent monitor that gathers the runs, the fallbacks and the evaluation scores in one place. Without the check an agent that starts answering outside its reviewed behaviour keeps preparing work for officers, and nobody holds a dated decision to fix it. The BOT AI Risk Management Guidelines of 12 Sep 2025 name lifecycle risk management and accuracy as a condition of running the agents at all, and Arch v5 keeps the AI inside rwb-agent where it can be switched off (slide 35).

In the target the evidence and the check are in the same service. rwb-agent owns the agent policies, the prompts, the runs, the guardrails and the evaluations (Arch v5 slide 41), so the drift step reads `agent_run` for the run outcomes of the window — the LOV-AGENT-RUN statuses, the fallback flag and the confidences — and `agent_evaluation` with `agent_evaluation_run` for the latest DONE evaluation of the agent version: its agreement rate, its precision, its recall and its sample size. The calibration figure is the one fact of another service: it comes from the ACE score facts, read through rwb-source-data's contract and never from a table (DP-05; DP-01). The thresholds, the minimum sample, the alert role and the review date are rows of the `agent_policy` version in force, so no value a business person may change is written in code (BR-P10-013).

On a breach the step writes `agent_alert` with `alert_type` DRIFT, the segment, the business date, the measured value, the threshold value and the role that holds the alert, and it writes the local decision record in the same transaction, which is what makes the owner role and the review date part of the decision and not part of a screen (DP-03; R-UNI-39). The notification leaves through the ACE notification path and the row keeps `sent_at` empty until it succeeds, so a notification outage loses no alert (R-UNI-33, R-UNI-35; FSD A2.6 AC-EXC-P10-006-03). The officer then reads the alert and the decision on SCR-46 Agent monitor through the gateway-bff composite route, which composes the agent read with the other services the screen needs (DP-19).

The realignment work is what leaves the slice. The legacy read of `rule_row` for the rule version goes, because no Drools package decides a drift breach: the version on the record is the policy version of `agent_policy`, and `rule_row` stays with rwb-decision. The legacy `assignment` row goes, because a breach raises a decision with an owner role rather than a case task, and `assignment` and `task` stay with rwb-case. The direct read of the score view becomes the rwb-source-data contract, the decision-log write becomes the local decision-record library plus the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the screen stops being served by the monolith and comes from the gateway-bff composite route.

This story owns both legacy criteria of RWB-E3-031 — AC1 and AC2 — and copies them verbatim in section 7. AC3 to AC10 are new and test the microservice deliverable of the title only. The legacy story carries no requirement ID; section 18 records that and traces the feature instead.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library, the record shape and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` with its CloudEvents envelope. This story writes its record through the library and never writes the shared topic directly.
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route contract for SCR-46 and its stub, so the exposure of the result is built and tested before the screen story lands.
- The `rwb_agent` schema exists with the agent runtime baseline migration — `agent_policy`, `agent_prompt`, `agent_run`, `agent_sample`, `agent_evaluation_run`, `agent_evaluation`, `agent_feedback` and `agent_alert` (TSD P10 v2 T3.1; RWB-P10-E1058-APP owns the schema and the baseline). This story issues no migration of its own (ASM-1065).
- At least one agent has run and one evaluation has finished for the business date, because the facts are built from rows and not from a calculation of this story (FEAT-AGT-01, FEAT-AGT-05, FEAT-AGT-06).
- Policy versions are in force for the business date with `agent_code`, `policy_version`, `model_code`, `model_version`, `autonomy_mode`, `segment_product_group`, `segment_region_code`, `confidence_floor`, `alert_role`, `review_date` and `watch_measures`. The threshold of each watched measure, the minimum sample and the review date are rows of the version in force, and their literal values are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0646; ASM-1060).
- The list values used by the step are those of TSD P10 v2 T3.2: LOV-AGENT (INTAKE, SCREENING, LEGAL_DOC, EXTRACT, TDR_OFFER), LOV-AGENT-ALERT (COST_CAP, DRIFT), LOV-AGENT-RUN (ANSWERED, TIMED_OUT, GUARDRAIL_FAILED, BELOW_FLOOR, TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, MODEL_ERROR, DISABLED), LOV-PRODUCT (MORTGAGE, HIRE_PURCHASE, SSME, UNSECURED) and LOV-REGION. The lists are reference data owned by rwb-case under the §R3 default ruling, and the step holds no copy of a list in code.
- The ACE score facts of the model code and model version in force are reachable through rwb-source-data's contract: `score_key`, `account_key`, `model_code`, `model_version`, `score_value`, `estimate_value` and the four remaining fields of DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279. The exact operation and its product path are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0646; ASM-1063).
- The drift window is the week to the business date, and the cadence belongs to the agent monitor run that starts the step (ASM-1061).
- The login is the rwb-agent login (DP-02): its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0646; ASM-1069).

##### 4. Flow

1. The agent monitor run for the business date has finished and has left the runs and the evaluation results of the date in `rwb_agent`. The DriftCheck step is registered at the end of that run on task queue `rwb-agent`; it is also startable for a business date on its own, so it is built and tested on Day 1 and the wiring into the monitor run belongs to the monitor story (FEAT-AGT-06; ASM-1061).
2. The step reads the policy versions in force on the business date from `agent_policy` — a version whose `valid_from` is after the date, or whose `valid_to` is before it, is not in force — and takes the agent, the model code and version, the segment product group and region, the `alert_role`, the `review_date` and the `watch_measures` of each.
3. For each agent and segment in force, DriftFacts builds one fact set from three sources. From `agent_run` it counts the runs of the window by `status` over LOV-AGENT-RUN, the runs whose `fallback` is true, and the confidence values. From `agent_evaluation_run` and `agent_evaluation` it takes the latest run in status DONE for the agent version with its `sample_size`, `agreement_rate`, `precision_value` and `recall_value`. From the rwb-source-data contract it takes the score facts of the model code and version and computes the calibration figure as the mean absolute difference between `score_value` and `estimate_value`.
4. A score row with an empty `estimate_value` counts as not scored: it is listed in the fact set and it is never counted as a zero difference. The number of scored and unscored rows is part of the facts, so the officer can see what the figure rests on.
5. A run whose `status` is not in LOV-AGENT-RUN is not mapped to a bucket: it is listed as a data error with the value it carried and it is excluded from the counts, and the step continues.
6. DriftDetector compares each watched measure of the policy version with its threshold. A measure whose sample is below the minimum sample of the policy version is not compared at all: the segment is reported as "not enough feedback" and raises no alert (FSD A2.6 AC-EXC-P10-006-04; legacy RWB-E2-031).
7. RecordAndApply runs in one `rwb_agent` transaction: it writes the `agent_alert` row with `alert_type` DRIFT, the `agent_code`, the `segment`, the `business_date`, the `measured_value`, the `threshold_value` and `sent_to_role` from `alert_role`, with `sent_at` empty; it writes the local decision record with the owner role and the review date; and it inserts the DecisionRecorded row in the outbox. A failed record write rolls the whole transaction back, so no alert row and no outbox row exist (DP-03; R-UNI-39).
8. The notification of the alert leaves through the ACE notification path to the holders of the role in `sent_to_role`. `sent_at` is written when the notification succeeds; where the path is unavailable the row keeps `sent_at` empty and it is sent when the sender succeeds, so no alert is lost (R-UNI-33, R-UNI-35; FSD A2.6 AC-EXC-P10-006-03).
9. The DecisionRecorded row is relayed from the outbox to `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and rwb-decision seals it into the central ledger. The step waits for no confirmation: the drift decision is not a point of no return.
10. A rerun for the same business date recomputes the same facts, finds the alert of the key and writes nothing: no second alert row, no second record and no second notification. The repeat is counted once in the step summary (R-UNI-40).
11. The officer reads the alert and the decision on SCR-46 Agent monitor. The screen is served by the gateway-bff composite route, which calls the agent read on `/api/recovery/agent/v1` and merges the answers; the browser calls no owner service directly (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The sample of an agent and segment is below the minimum sample of the policy version | No measure is compared, no alert row and no record exist, and the monitor shows "not enough feedback" for the segment | None | AC7 |
| X2 | The rwb-source-data contract returns an error, or the score facts are older than the business date | The calibration measure is recorded as not available for that agent and segment; no alert and no record are written for it; the measure built from the agent's own rows is still written | None | AC10 |
| X3 | The local decision record cannot be written | The transaction rolls back: no alert row, no outbox row and no notification; the step fails and is retried | MSG-P7-003 | AC2 |
| X4 | The notification path is unavailable | The alert row is kept with `sent_at` empty and sent when the sender succeeds | None | AC4 |
| X5 | A run carries a status outside LOV-AGENT-RUN | The value is listed as a data error and excluded from the counts; no bucket is invented and the step continues | None | AC3 |
| X6 | The policy version in force has no `review_date` | No record and no notification are written for that version; the version is named as a configuration exception, because a decision without a date is not raised and no date is defaulted | None | AC5 |
| X7 | The step runs twice for the same business date | No second alert row, no second record and no second notification | None | AC6 |
| X8 | An agent version has a policy in force and no run in the window | No alert is raised and the segment shows "not enough feedback" (FSD A2.6 AC-EXC-P10-006-02) | None | AC7 |
| X9 | A caller without the Platform administration right opens the monitor route | Refused; nothing is returned and nothing is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC8 |

The step writes no case field and raises no case task on any path, so none of these exceptions moves a case. The rollback of X3 and the retry of X4 are the behaviours FSD A2.13 AC-EXC-P10-013-02 and FSD A2.6 AC-EXC-P10-006-03 describe.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on Day 1 against the platform contracts RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, the agent runtime baseline and the rwb-source-data fake; it waits for no in-lane story and starts itself for a business date |
| Negotiable | The thresholds, the minimum sample, the watched measure, the alert role and the review date are rows of the policy version in force; the segment composition and the window are agreed defaults, recorded as assumptions |
| Valuable | A drifting agent is caught on its own run and evaluation evidence, and a named role owns a dated decision to correct it |
| Estimable | One step, one facts builder, one detector, one alert writer, one decision-record writer, one client, no controller |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each of the ten criteria of section 7 is one automated test against the rwb-source-data and decision-record fakes; no criterion needs a screen |

```gherkin

    Given the latest evaluation run of "SCREENING" in status DONE holds sample size 200, agreement rate 0.9100, precision 0.9444 and recall 0.8947 on the same segment

    Then the agent_alert row, the decision record and the outbox row commit in one rwb_agent transaction
```
