##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A publication puts a configuration version in force from an effective date: the rows of the version take `valid_from` = that date, the rows of the version in force take `valid_to` = the day before, and the two windows never overlap | RWB-E8-012 AC1; FSD P4 v3 A2.23; REQ-DRI-011 |
| BR2 | Exactly one configuration version is in force on any date, and it is resolved from the rows' dates and not from the act of publication | FSD P4 v3 A2.23.1; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; ASM-1584 |
| BR3 | A publication needs Rules and parameters A; a caller without it is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002 and nothing is read for a decision, written or published | TSD P4 v3 T6.1; legacy RWB-E8-012 permission checks |
| BR4 | Only a version in state `APPROVED` is published; any other state is refused with 409 and MSG-GEN-004 and nothing is written | FSD P4 v3 A2.23.4.3; TSD P4 v3 T3.2; ASM-1583 |
| BR5 | A configuration version is the triple of `matrix_version`, `masking_version` and `limit_version` over rows this service owns; no table, column or copy is created for it | TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-044, DF-REF-202, DF-REF-055; ownership map; GAP-0872 |
| BR6 | `effectiveFrom` is checked against the earliest and the latest date the parameters contract answers, and a date outside them is refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-001; no bound is a constant in code | DP-06; FSD P4 v3 A2.23.3.1 VR-P4-023-1; GAP-0872 |
| BR7 | Every publication appends exactly one entry to the local decision-record chain of DP-03 in the transaction that writes the dates; an act that cannot be recorded is not taken and is withheld with 503 and MSG-P7-003 | R-UNI-39; RWB-E8-012 AC2; DP-03 |
| BR8 | The entry carries the three labels, the `versionId`, the effective date, the reason, the note, the publishing role code and the time, and no name, no e-mail address and no personal field | NFR-040; Principle 5; ASM-1585 |
| BR9 | The publication publishes exactly one `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1`, keyed by `versionId`, so the authorise caches refresh; the payload carries no person and no personal data | Architecture v5 slide 14, slide 41 and slide 43; ASM-1585 |
| BR10 | The answer names the version, its three labels, the state it takes from `effectiveFrom`, its window, the time and role of the publication and the version it supersedes | TSD P4 v3 T3.2; section 12.1 |
| BR11 | Every field is validated before any row is read for a decision: an empty or malformed value is 422 with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field, and nothing is written | FSD P4 v3 A2.23.3.1 VR-P4-023-1 |
| BR12 | One `Idempotency-Key` answers one publication: a replay answers the first answer, writes no second window, appends no second entry and publishes no second event | Architecture v5 slide 42; DP-09 |
| BR13 | The list read answers the versions this service holds with the state each is in on the day of the read, ordered by window, filtered by `status` and paged from the parameters contract | FSD P4 v3 A2.23.2; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 |
| BR14 | The state of a version is `IN_FORCE` inside its window and `SUPERSEDED` after it, both derived from the rows' dates; the five states that are not derived are read from the record because the tables carry no state column | TSD P4 v3 T3.2; GAP-0872; ASM-1583 |
| BR15 | The partner panel, the partner firm, the partner users, the fee schedule and the partner service levels are S9's and are neither read nor written; FEAT-PRM-02 is not a prerequisite of this story | Ownership map (`partner`, `partner_user`, `partner_instruction` = S9); Architecture v5 slide 41; GAP-0872 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-access`:

- BR1 and BR2 are one update statement per table inside one transaction: `valid_from` on the rows of the version and `valid_to` on the rows of the version it replaces, so no reader ever sees two windows open on the same date or none.
- BR3 is one call to the own authorise operation with A, made before the version is read for a decision; the refusal returns before the repository is reached, which is why AC3 can assert that no row changed.
- BR4 is the recorded state read from the chain, not a column read: the gate compares the version's last recorded state with `APPROVED` and refuses anything else, including a version that was rolled back.
- BR5 is the absence of a table: the module has no `config_version` table, no view and no join for one, and the version is the label triple the contract names.
- BR6 is the parameters reader at request time with the version in force; a changed bound is data and needs no build.
- BR7, BR8 and BR9 are one transaction: the two date updates, the entry, the outbox row and the idempotency row commit together, and the relay sends the event after the commit.
- BR10 is the answer shape of the contract: the version item plus the id of the version superseded, and no field of another service.
- BR11 is the validation of the controller before any read, so a malformed request cannot even be counted as an attempt on a version.
- BR12 is the `idempotency_key` row of the platform library in `rwb_access`, written with the answer.
- BR13 and BR14 are the read: a projection over the three tables and the chain, with the derived state computed for the day of the read and the paging from DP-06.
- BR15 is a negative rule: the module has no repository, no client and no join for `partner`, `partner_user` or `partner_instruction`, and the tests assert that no partner fake is called.

##### 9. State transitions

This story holds no state of its own. The state it reads and moves is the state of a configuration version, and the two states it writes are written as dates on the rows.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| `APPROVED` | A publication is submitted | A held, the version is `APPROVED`, the date is inside the bounds | `IN_FORCE` from `effectiveFrom`; the version in force `SUPERSEDED` from the day before |
| `APPROVED` | A publication is submitted | No A letter | Refused 403 with MSG-P4-002; no write, no entry, no event |
| `APPROVED` | A publication is submitted | The date is outside the bounds | Refused 422 with MSG-GEN-001; no write, no entry, no event |
| `APPROVED` | A publication is submitted | The entry or a date cannot be written | Refused 503 with MSG-P7-003; nothing changed |
| `LOADED`, `VALIDATED`, `ROLLED_BACK`, `REFUSED` | A publication is submitted | The recorded state is not `APPROVED` | Refused 409 with MSG-GEN-004; no write |
| `IN_FORCE` | A publication of the same version with a new key | The window is already open | Refused 409 with MSG-GEN-004; the window is never moved twice |
| `IN_FORCE` | The same `Idempotency-Key` is sent again | None | The first answer is replayed; no second write, entry or event |
| `IN_FORCE` | The window closes | `valid_to` has passed | `SUPERSEDED`, derived from the dates and written by no process |

| Chain | Event | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Append-only local chain | A publication, or a refusal that is recorded at the service edge | One entry appended with its `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`; no entry is ever updated or deleted |
| `rwb.access.events.v1` | A publication | Exactly one `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1`, from the outbox of the publishing transaction |
| `rwb.decision-record.v1` | A publication | Exactly one `DecisionRecorded` for the entry, from the same outbox |

The two shapes of the state must not be confused, and the contract says so once: the answer of the publication names the state the version takes on its effective date, `IN_FORCE`, while the list read derives the state of each version from its window and the day of the read, so the same version is `APPROVED` in the list on the day before its date, `IN_FORCE` inside its window and `SUPERSEDED` after it. No process moves a version from one state to the other: the calendar does, which is why no Schedule and no Temporal job is added for it (ASM-1584).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Risk and model risk officer (RW-RISK) | Publish a configuration version with Rules and parameters A; the publisher of the target, and the role code recorded on the entry (TSD P4 v3 T6.1) |
| Center of excellence analyst (RW-COE) | Prepares and loads a version with `CRUD` in Rules and parameters and cannot publish it, because `CRUD` carries no A; the maker half of the separation |
| Security administrator (RW-SECADM) | Holds `CRUDA` in Platform administration and `R` in Rules and parameters; this story gives no write path to that right, and the role administration is RWB-P4-E1037-APP's |
| Reference data administrator (RW-REFADM) | Prepares a load with `CRUD` in Reference data as the FSD A2.23.3.3 role table states; holds `R` in Rules and parameters and cannot publish |
| Internal audit (RW-AUDIT) | Reads the list with Rules and parameters R and reads the entries; publishes nothing |
| A case role without Rules and parameters A (RW-CASEOWN, RW-PHONECOL) | Refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002; nothing is read for a decision, written or published |
| The gateway-bff route | Calls the two operations on behalf of the signed-in user, one hop each, and passes the `Idempotency-Key` unchanged |
| `rwb-access` itself | Reads and writes `permission`, `masking_rule` and `delegation_limit` in its own schema, reads `role` and `permission`, and writes only its own chain and outbox |
| `rwb-partner` (S9) | Owns the partner panel, the partner firm, the partner users, the fee schedule and the partner service levels; this story calls it not at all |
| `rwb-decision` (P7) | Owns the central ledger and the rule package registry; this story calls it not at all |

The maker-checker separation is achieved through the letters and needs no named-person four-eyes message: RW-COE prepares with C and U, RW-RISK publishes with A, and no single role holds both in Rules and parameters. A caller without A is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002, which is the same refusal the legacy story carried for an action outside the role's permission. The other refusal shapes are 401 with MSG-P4-001 for no session, 409 with MSG-GEN-004 for a version that is not `APPROVED` or is already in force, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for a field or a date, and 503 with MSG-P7-003 for a record that cannot be written. The database login is the per-service login of the service baseline (DP-02), which belongs to RWB-P4-E1037-CON.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Table in `rwb_access` | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 | `permission` | id, role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version | Read: the rows of the version and the matrix label. Write: none — the table carries no date column, and the matrix label is in force for the window the version takes |
| DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204 | `masking_rule` | id, role_code, field_id, unmasked, masking_version, valid_from, valid_to | Read: the rows of the version and of the version in force. Write: `valid_from` on the rows of the version, `valid_to` on the rows of the version it supersedes |
| DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026, DF-REF-055 to DF-REF-062 | `delegation_limit` | id, decision_code, approval_level, product_group, the four amounts, valid_from, valid_to, limit_version and the other conditions | Read: the rows of the version and of the version in force. Write: `valid_from` on the rows of the version, `valid_to` on the rows of the version it supersedes. No amount, level or product group is changed |
| DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039 | `role` | id, role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope, entra_group | Read: the caller's role and its class, and the role code recorded as the publisher |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local library, DP-03) | the publication entry: `decision_code` DF-DEC-003, `case_id` DF-DEC-002 empty, `inputs_ref` DF-DEC-008 with the three labels, the `versionId`, the effective date, the reason, the note, the publishing role code, the version superseded and the grant id, `decided_at` DF-DEC-016, `prev_hash` DF-DEC-017 and `entry_hash` DF-DEC-018 | Write; and read for the state of a version and for the list |
| (idempotency) | `idempotency_key` (platform library table in `rwb_access`) | the request and the stored answer of a publication | Write and read (DP-09; ASM-0074) |
| (outbox) | `outbox_event` | the `AccessPolicyChanged` row and the record row of the publication entry | Write |
| (inbox) | `processed_event` | none: this story consumes no event | None |
| DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 | `partner` of `rwb_partner` | none | Not read and not written: the partner panel is S9's |
| DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217 | `partner_user` of `rwb_partner` | none | Not read and not written: the partner users are S9's |

No row of `partner`, `partner_user` or `partner_instruction` is read or written: they are `rwb-partner`'s (S9) under the ownership map, the legacy story's `partner` rows travel with the partner capability and not with the access panel, and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01, BR15). No row of `decision_log_entry` is read or written either: the central ledger is P7's and this story writes only its own local chain on `rwb.decision-record.v1`. No row of `rule_row`, `rule_package_version` or `lov_value` is read: the rule registry is P7's, the list values are P3 reference data, and the version labels are read from the rows themselves. Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 and of TSD P4 v3 T3.1.

The configuration version and its `versionId`, the exact field set of the two operations, the scheme that builds `versionId` from the three labels, and the date columns of the matrix label are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0872; ASM-1583): no source defines a configuration-version object, the two paths appear in no endpoint inventory, and `permission` carries no date column. The schema of RWB-P4-E8012-CON fixes them and this story reads and writes them as that contract publishes them.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Path | Owner | Request | Response | Errors | Authorization | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/config-versions/{versionId}/publish` | P4 `rwb-access` | Path: `versionId`. Body: `effectiveFrom` (a date), `reason`, `note` (optional) | `versionId`, `matrixVersion`, `maskingVersion`, `limitVersion`, `state` `IN_FORCE` from `effectiveFrom`, `validFrom`, `validTo`, `publishedAt`, `publishedByRole`, `supersedesVersionId` | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 (MSG-P4-002); 409 (MSG-GEN-004); 422 (MSG-GEN-001); 503 (MSG-P7-003) | Rules and parameters A, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` required; a replay answers the first answer and publishes no second event |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/config-versions` | P4 `rwb-access` | Query: `status`, `page`, `size` | `items[]` of `versionId`, `matrixVersion`, `maskingVersion`, `limitVersion`, `state`, `validFrom`, `validTo`, `publishedAt`, `publishedByRole`, plus `page`, `size`, `total` | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 (MSG-P4-002); 422 (MSG-GEN-001); 503 (MSG-P7-003) | Rules and parameters R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |

Both operations sit on the base `/api/recovery/access/v1` of DP-13. The publication answer names the state the version takes from its effective date, and the list derives the state of each version from its window and the day of the read (section 9). `status` filters on the state set of BR14, `page` defaults to the value of its parameter row and `size` is capped by it, both read through DP-06 and never from code (BR6, BR13). Neither operation appears in the endpoint inventory of TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A, which declares no configuration-version operation at all, so both paths are fixed by RWB-P4-E8012-CON and raised in the key's gap (GAP-0872; ASM-1583).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 `rwb-access` (own service) | The Rules and parameters A check behind the publication and the R check behind the list, cached for the session; MSG-P4-002 on a refusal |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 `rwb-case` | The earliest and the latest effective date and the page bounds, with the version in force (DP-06) |

One hop per call, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11); the parameters read and the authorise answer are cached for the request or the session. The own authorise operation is the one Architecture v5 slide 14 names as the first path of `rwb-access`, and this story declares it as consumed and never defines it. No other operation of `rwb-case`, `rwb-decision`, `rwb-partner` or `rwb-document` is called.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | P4 | `versionId` | `versionId`, `matrixVersion`, `maskingVersion`, `limitVersion`, `effectiveFrom`, `supersedesVersionId`, `publishedByRole`, `reason` |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library; consumed by P7 | entryId | the hash-chained entry of a publication: the three labels, the effective date, the reason, the note, the publishing role code and the time |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, from the outbox of the transaction that writes the dates. `AccessPolicyChanged` is one of the two events of `rwb-access` in Architecture v5 slide 14 and slide 41, and slide 43 gives it every service as a consumer with the note "cache refresh". Its payload carries labels, a date, a role code and a reason and no name, no e-mail address, no user reference and no personal field (BR9). `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` belongs to RWB-P4-E8008-APP and is not published here, even though a limit label travels in the payload.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `rwb-access` is a reference-data owner in Architecture v5 slide 14 with no inbound event for this capability, and a publication of its own tables needs no subscription. No `processed_event` row is written and the contract declares no consumer group.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The publication is synchronous and the maker-checker separation is a pair of letters, not a state: this story starts no workflow, signals no workflow and registers no activity on the `rwb-access` queue. `ApprovalWorkflow` of the workflow kit belongs to `rwb-decision` (P7) and is not used for an administration change of this service.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None, and the absence is deliberate. The effective date of a version is resolved at read time by `POST /authorise` as the version whose `valid_from` ≤ today < `valid_to`, so no promotion job has to run at 00:01 and no Temporal Schedule or workflow is added for it (ASM-1584). The six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) is the only Schedule of `rwb-access` and belongs to RWB-P4-AD008-APP. The rule-promotion Schedule of `rwb-decision` is P7's and promotes rule packages, not an access panel.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `permission` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Read only: the rows of the version, the matrix label and the letters of the caller. Created by RWB-P4-E1037-APP |
| `masking_rule` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Read and write: `valid_from` on the rows of the version, `valid_to` on the rows it supersedes. Created by RWB-P4-AD004-APP |
| `delegation_limit` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Read and write: `valid_from` on the rows of the version, `valid_to` on the rows it supersedes; no amount is changed. Created by RWB-P4-E1038-APP |
| `role` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Read only: the role code recorded as the publisher |
| the local decision-record table of the DP-03 library | P4, in `rwb_access` | Write: the entry of a publication. Read: the recorded state of a version and the list |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_access` | The two outbox rows of a publication and its idempotency row; no inbox row, because no event is consumed (DP-09; ASM-0074) |
| `partner`, `partner_user`, `partner_instruction` | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | Not read and not written: the partner panel is S9's (BR15) |
| `decision_log_entry` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | Not read and not written: the central ledger is P7's and the local record goes on `rwb.decision-record.v1` |
| `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | Not read and not written: the rule registry is P7's and the "rule version" of the legacy criterion is read here as the version of the panel (section 11) |
| `lov_value`, `reference_version`, `reference_row` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | Not read: reference data of P3 under the ownership ruling; this story's pattern list carries no DP-07 and its contract-dependency list no `RWB-P3-E1043-CON` |

No table is created by this story: the configuration version is a label over three tables that already exist, and a `config_version` table would be a second writer of a window that the rows themselves carry (BR5). No table of another service is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`, module `access/configversion`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.configversion`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The legacy markers this slice replaces are the in-module rule-version load and approve of the monolith, addressed on the monolith's own base (DP-13: the service's own base and its own tables), and the ace-web screens that published in process (DP-19: a gateway-bff composite route). DP-01, DP-02, DP-09 and DP-11 govern the service baseline and the one-hop budget of section 12.2; they add no dependency of their own, they are not in the pattern list the Work Package fixes for this story, and they are not claimed as patterns of it. The reference-data list check of the version labels would need DP-07 and `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`, neither of which this story's metadata carries, so the labels are read from the rows and the point is raised in the key's gap (GAP-0872; ASM-1583).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ConfigVersionPublicationController | Controller | `POST /admin/config-versions/{versionId}/publish`: validation, the `Idempotency-Key` lookup, the RFC 9457 problem responses |
| ConfigVersionQueryController | Controller | `GET /admin/config-versions`: the `status` filter, the paging from DP-06 and the state of each version on the day of the read |
| PublicationGate | Service | The ordered gate of BR3, BR4 and BR6: right, recorded state, bounds; a refusal returns before the next step |
| ConfigVersionPublisher | Service | BR1 and BR2: the two date updates in one transaction, the version superseded, the answer of BR10 |
| ConfigVersionRepository | Repository | The triple and its rows in `permission`, `masking_rule` and `delegation_limit`, the version in force for a date, the two updates; no delete method and no write to `permission` |
| ConfigVersionStateService | Service | BR14: the derived state of a version and the recorded state read from the chain, and the list projection |
| PermissionReader | Service | The `role` and `permission` rows of the caller, the A and R letters and the role code that carries A |
| ParameterReader | Service | The effective-date bounds and the page bounds through the parameters contract of DP-06, with the version in force |
| AccessPolicyEventPublisher | Service | The `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` row in the outbox of the publishing transaction, with the payload of section 12.3 |
| DecisionRecordAppender | Service | The publication entry with its outbox row, in the transaction that writes the dates (DP-03, DP-09) |
| IdempotencyStore | Service | The `Idempotency-Key` lookup and store of the platform library, written with the answer |

**Database and migrations**

- This story creates no table and adds no column. `permission`, `masking_rule` and `delegation_limit` are created by RWB-P4-E1037-APP, RWB-P4-AD004-APP and RWB-P4-E1038-APP in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15, the local decision-record table by RWB-P4-E1039-APP and the platform library tables by the service's own DB story; this story reads and writes rows of them.
- The two date updates are guarded so that two windows cannot overlap: the update of the version in force is conditional on its rows having no `valid_to` after the new `valid_from`, and the update of the new version is conditional on its rows having no window of their own. If SIT needs an index for the version-in-force window, it is added to the owning story's migration with the agreement of its owner.
- No write statement touches an amount, a level, a product group, a letter or a role: the publisher writes two dates per row, which is what makes a publication unable to change a business value by accident.
- The two date updates, the entry, the two outbox rows and the idempotency row commit in one transaction; a failure rolls all of them back and the answer is withheld with MSG-P7-003 (BR7).

**Configuration and reference data**

- The earliest and the latest effective date and the page default and maximum are parameter rows of `rwb-case` read through DP-06 with the version in force; no bound is a constant in code (BR6). Their names are fixed by RWB-P4-E8012-CON.
- The version labels are values of the rows the administration stories loaded; this story copies and compares them and validates nothing against a list of its own (section 12.7).
- The publishing role code is read from `role` through the `permission` row that carries the A letter; no role code and no capability area is a constant in code (BR3, BR8).
- The state names are those of LOV-VERSION-STATUS of TSD P4 v3 T3.2 and are the contract's enumeration, not a local list.

**Build steps**

1. `ConfigVersionRepository` and the triple resolution; test that a `versionId` with an incomplete triple is refused with 422 and that the repository has no delete and no write to `permission`.
2. `ConfigVersionPublicationController` and its validation; tests for X1 and X2 with no read for a decision and no write.
3. `PermissionReader` and the authorise call; test the AC3 refusal of a caller with R only, with no date changed, no entry and no event, and the list still answering `APPROVED`.
4. `ConfigVersionStateService` over the chain and the fixture; test that "CFG-2026.11" is `IN_FORCE`, "CFG-2027.02" is `VALIDATED` and an old version is `SUPERSEDED`, all from the same read.
5. `PublicationGate` with the state and the bounds; test AC4, including the proof that neither refusal writes a date and that the parameters fake is the only source of the bounds.
6. `ConfigVersionPublisher` with the two guarded updates; test the window of AC5 on a fixed clock, including the day before, the effective day and the day after.
7. `DecisionRecordAppender`, `AccessPolicyEventPublisher` and `IdempotencyStore` in one transaction; test the replay of AC5 with one entry and one event, and the forced failure of AC2 with nothing changed.
8. `ParameterReader` over the parameters fake, so the story builds before `rwb-case` is in the environment; test that a changed bound is data and needs no build.
9. The contract-fake run of both operations through the gateway-bff fake, so SCR-43 can be demonstrated while the route and the panel stories are being built.

**Feature switch.** The two operations are switched by the service baseline of RWB-P4-E1037-CON, not by a flag of their own. A publication that is switched off would leave an approved version undated and visible as such in the list, which is the state the gate is meant to resolve, so this story adds no flag and removes nothing.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; "CFG-2027.01" is published for 2027-01-01 by RW-RISK and answered with its labels, its window and the version it supersedes; the rows of "CFG-2026.11" carry `valid_to` 2026-12-31 and the list answers it `SUPERSEDED` on 2 January 2027; a caller with R only is refused with MSG-P4-002 with no row changed; a version in `VALIDATED` is refused with MSG-GEN-004 and a date outside the bounds with MSG-GEN-001, neither writing anything; one entry is appended and one `AccessPolicyChanged` is published per publication; the same `Idempotency-Key` replays one answer; and a forced failure of the record leaves every date as it was with MSG-P7-003.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The caller has no session | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | This story, on both operations |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller holds no Rules and parameters A on the publication, or no R on the list | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, on both operations |
| MSG-P4-004 | A break-glass grant is active for the caller | Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded. | This story, as a warning on the publication answer, with the grant id recorded in the entry |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is empty, `effectiveFrom` is not a date, `versionId` names no complete triple, or `effectiveFrom` is outside the bounds in force | Enter {field}. | This story, on both operations |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The version is not in state `APPROVED`, or it is already in force and its window cannot be moved again | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. | This story, on the publication |
| MSG-P7-003 | The dates, the entry, the outbox row or the idempotency row cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on both operations |

Every error from this service is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled and `instance` naming the request. The business texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story where the message already existed: MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-004, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P7-003 are the legacy texts, and MSG-GEN-004 is the platform text of the record that someone else changed, carried unchanged and added here as a platform value and not as a new business text. No named-person four-eyes message is produced, because the separation of the preparer and the publisher is held by the C and A letters of TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and not by a comparison of two people on one act.

The delegation-of-authority panel of the screen shows the limit label of a version, and the masking panel shows its masking label, both read through the operations of the stories that own those panels; this story renders no screen surface of its own.

| SCR-43 Roles and access | Versions, in force | The version whose window contains today, marked `IN_FORCE`, and the versions before it marked `SUPERSEDED` with their `valid_to` |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Publication, form | One `APPROVED` version opened for publication with `effectiveFrom`, `reason` and `note`; the bounds come from the parameters read |

The legacy story named SCR-39 Rules and parameters and SCR-41 Delegation of authority in its screen table, and neither name fits the access panel of the target: the panel a publication puts in force is the role, permission, scope, masking and limit panel, which the target screen SCR-43 Roles and access carries with the delegation-of-authority and masking panels. ##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the effective-date bounds and the page bounds are parameter rows (BR6), the publishing role is read from `role` and `permission` (BR8), and the state names are the contract's enumeration of LOV-VERSION-STATUS.
- No personal data anywhere: the request, the answer, the list and the entry carry version labels, a date, a role code, a reason and a time; no name, no e-mail address and no user reference appears in the answer, the entry, the event or a test (BR8, BR9, NFR-040).
- No read of another service's tables (DP-01): `partner`, `partner_user` and `partner_instruction` are S9's, `decision_log_entry` and the rule registry are P7's, and no join crosses a schema.
- One writer for the panel window: only this operation writes `valid_from` and `valid_to` of a configuration version, and it writes nothing else of a row; the rows themselves are loaded by the administration stories.
- No publication without its record: the two date updates, the entry and the outbox rows commit together, and the answer is withheld with MSG-P7-003 when the entry cannot be written (BR7, R-UNI-39).
- Maker and publisher are different letters: `CRUD` prepares and `A` publishes, so no single role can load a version and put it in force, and the refusal is the ordinary MSG-P4-002.
- No clock of its own: the effective date is resolved at read time from the rows' dates, so the story adds no Schedule, no workflow and no promotion job (ASM-1584).
- One key, one publication: the `Idempotency-Key` is stored with the answer, so a retry after a timeout cannot write a second window, a second entry or a second event (BR12).
- The partner panel is out of reach: the module has no repository and no client for it, and a test asserts that no partner fake is called (BR15).
- Every example, fixture and test payload is synthetic; no production panel row is copied into a schema, a fake or a test.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E8-012 as the wave 4 integration proof of the panel change, driven through the versioned reference load of rwb-case, the rule version and its four-eyes approval in rwb-decision and the panel read of rwb-partner, with the decision record read back and the effective date asserted on both sides of the date; the build of the change, its effective dating and the reference data is RWB-P4-E8012-APP with RWB-S9-E8012-APP and its CON story. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **partner and agency manager**, I want **a partner panel change to be published with its effective date, through the versioned reference row of rwb-case and the approved rule version of rwb-decision, with the partner read returning the old panel status before the date and the new one from the date, proved end to end against the owners' real contracts**, so that **access, limits and rules change without a code release, and no change takes effect unapproved or unrecorded**.

This story builds the wave 4 integration harness and its evidence for this feature, and nothing else. The panel change, its effective dating, the approval and the versioned reference data are built by P4 rwb-access and S9 rwb-partner in RWB-S9-E8012-APP and its CON story; the app story of the same legacy key that this harness swaps in is RWB-P4-E8012-APP, and that is the integration dependency in the metadata above. The versioned reference data is carried by P3 rwb-case under the default ruling that puts parameters and reference data with rwb-case, and the rule versions are carried by P7 rwb-decision under the default ruling that puts the rule package registry with rwb-decision. The harness owns no production endpoint, no table, no workflow, no activity, no schedule and no screen, and it writes no code in any service.

##### 2. Business rationale

A panel change is the one administrative act that moves access, limits and rules at once. The legacy story is written against the release: the panel status of a partner, its fee schedule and the rule version that reads them must be changed without a code release (FEAT-ADM-07). If the effective date is not carried by the data, every service reads the change the moment the row is written, cases that were decided under the old panel are re-read under the new one, and nobody can say which version was in force on which date.

The thin sources put four obligations on the change. Every versioned table carries its valid from and valid to dates, its author and its approver (REQ-DRI-011). Roles, teams, queues, queue membership and capacity are held as versioned reference data and change without a code release (REQ-CWC-006). The limit, the rule version and the approver are written to the decision log with every approval (REQ-APD-009). A new rule version applies to decisions taken from its effective date, while open cases keep the version they were decided under (R-UNI-38). A partner panel exit recalls every open case held by that partner (R-UNI-26, REQ-S9-006), which is why the panel status the change publishes is asserted through the partner read and never through the screen that wrote it, and no action proceeds when its decision record cannot be written (R-UNI-39). Every partner type is managed on the same six points, selection and contract and fees among them (REQ-S9-001), so a panel change is a change to a contract record and not to a display.

What is not proved today is the join between the three owners: the reference row is loaded in rwb-case, the rule version is created and approved in rwb-decision, and the effect is visible in rwb-partner. This harness proves that join on one date: the row and the version are loaded and approved through the owners' own operations, one decision record carries the code, the rule id, the rule version and the approver, and the partner read answers the old panel status before the effective date and the new one from it, with the date taken from the fixture and never from code.

Every call is one hop on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13). The reference data is rwb-case's and the rule version is rwb-decision's, so the harness writes nothing itself: it drives the owners' operations and reads the effect back. The decision record is written by the service that takes the decision, through the local decision-record library on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), and confirmed by the central ledger in rwb-decision. Where a screen would compose these calls the path is the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which is P4's screen path and not this harness.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The published contracts of P7 rwb-decision (rule versions, the approval, the decision log, the rule package event), P3 rwb-case (the versioned reference load and the list read), S9 rwb-partner (the panel read) and P4 rwb-access (the session) are in the contract registry, and a stub set is generated from each one.
- The rights are in force for the run: Rules and parameters C to create the rule version and load the reference row, Rules and parameters A to approve it. The legacy section names RW-COE as the holder of C and RW-RISK as the holder of A, and the author cannot approve; the harness holds no business right of its own and drives the run as synthetic callers with those right sets.
- The panel and fee schedule reference row, its valid from and valid to dates, its author and approver, the rule version key, the effective date the run uses and the synthetic panel and partner keys are held in the fixture as data. No business date, decision code or panel status value is written in code.
- RWB-P4-E8012-APP owns the panel change, its effective dating and the versioned reference data on the P4 side, and RWB-S9-E8012-APP with its CON story owns the panel and the partner side; until they land, the stub set of §12.8 stands in for their effect and the run is reported as a stub pass.
- The panel and fee schedule as data is FEAT-PRM-02, held as versioned reference data by S9 and loaded through P3's reference contract; this story asserts the load and the read-back and builds none of it.
- The harness environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the stub answer shapes, the effective date the run uses, the shape of the panel reference row, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0478; ASM-0670).
- No build dependency. Day 1, with the stubs in place from the first run; the one wait is RWB-P4-E8012-APP, which replaces its stub and never blocks the lane.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: loads the fixture: the synthetic panel and partner keys, the panel and fee schedule reference row with its valid from and valid to dates, its author and approver, the rule version key, and the effective date the run uses. The date and every key come from the fixture; on Day 1 the stubs of §12.8 return the same records.
2. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` as the caller that will create the change and asserts Rules and parameters C and not A, then as the approver and asserts Rules and parameters A, then as a caller with no Recovery Workbench role.
3. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` and asserts the panel status the partner carries before the change, together with partner_code, partner_type and contract_end (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007).
4. Harness: loads the versioned panel and fee schedule reference row through `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads` with the fixture file and the load key, and asserts the answer carries the row, its valid from and valid to dates, its author and its approver.
5. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` and asserts the loaded row with its effective dates, so the version is proved to exist in rwb-case and not only in the load answer.
6. Harness: creates the rule version through `POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-versions` as the caller holding Rules and parameters C, and asserts the answer carries the version id and its state.
7. Harness: approves the rule version through `POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve` as the approver holding Rules and parameters A, and asserts one approved version with its approver.
8. Harness: submits the same approval a second time and asserts the answer is refused and one approved version remains, so a repeated click is never a second approval.
9. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?ruleId={ruleId}&from={from}` and asserts one record for the change with its decision_code, rule_id, rule_version and approver (DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018, DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015).
10. Harness: counts one `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, asserts the central ledger in rwb-decision confirmed it, replays the event and asserts the decision log still holds one record for the change.
11. Harness: observes `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` on `rwb.decision.events.v1` and records the version it names against the version id approved in step 7.
12. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` before the effective date and asserts the old panel status, then at and after the effective date and asserts the panel status the change carries, on both sides of the date the fixture names.
13. Harness: forces the local decision-record library to fail for the change and asserts the publish stops with MSG-P7-003, the reference version stays unapproved and the partner read still returns the old panel status.
14. Harness: calls the approve operation as a caller holding Rules and parameters C and not A and asserts 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no state change, then as a caller with no Recovery Workbench role and asserts MSG-P4-001.
15. Harness: writes one run report keyed by story and by the reference load key, naming the contract version of each hop, whether the hop was a stub or the owner, the reference row and its effective dates, the rule version and its approver, the decision record, the panel status on both sides of the effective date, and the pass or fail gate.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A stub answers a shape the published contract does not allow, or a contract version moves under the run | The run fails at that hop and the report names the service, the operation and the contract version; no criterion is marked passed | None | TC-E8-012-01-ITG (ITG AC1) |
| X2 | The reference load answers without a valid from or valid to date, an author or an approver | The run fails on AC2 and the report names the load key and the missing field; the harness never supplies an effective date or an approver of its own | None | TC-E8-012-01-ITG (ITG AC2) |
| X3 | The partner read returns the new panel status before the effective date, or the old one from it | The run fails on AC2 and the report names the date read, the status answered and the status expected; the date is taken from the fixture, never from the clock of the machine | None | TC-E8-012-01-ITG (ITG AC2) |
| X4 | The rule version is approved and no decision record carries its version, or the central ledger has not confirmed the record | The run fails on AC3 and the report names the version, the record and the missing confirmation; confirmation is never assumed | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E8-012-01-ITG (ITG AC3) |
| X5 | The same approval is submitted twice and a second approved version is created | The run fails on AC3 and the report names the two submissions and the version; a repeated click is never a second approval | None | TC-E8-012-01-ITG (ITG AC3) |
| X6 | The decision record fails and the reference version is approved, or the partner read moves to the new status | The run fails on AC4 and the report names the approval state and the panel status before and after; nothing changes is asserted, not assumed | MSG-P7-003 (expected) | TC-E8-012-02-ITG and TC-E8-012-04-ITG (ITG AC4) |
| X7 | A caller holding Rules and parameters C and not A is allowed to approve, or a caller with no Recovery Workbench role is allowed to act | The run fails on AC5 and the report names the caller's rights, the operation and the answer; a 200 is a failure even when no business data changed | MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-001 (expected, and missing) | TC-E8-012-03-ITG (ITG AC5) |

The report text is for the wave entry check and is not part of the message standard. The business messages the run touches are in section 14 and are asserted by ID and by their substituted values.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs against the published contracts and the stubs from Day 1; the only wait is RWB-P4-E8012-APP, and its fixture answers until it lands |
| Negotiable | The fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the effective date the run uses, the shape of the panel reference row, the report shape and the gate are configuration agreed at the wave entry check, not business values in code |
| Valuable | The reference row and the rule version are proved to be loaded and approved by their owners, the approval is proved to be recorded once, and the change is proved to take effect on its date and nowhere else |
| Estimable | One runner, one stub set, one reference load, one list read-back, one rule version create, one approve, one partner probe, one decision read-back, one event observer and one report |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its five criteria and four tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against the stubs and again against RWB-P4-E8012-APP as it lands |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Publish a panel change - wave 4 integration harness

  Background:
    Given the synthetic panel and partner keys and the panel and fee schedule reference row are held in the fixture as data, with its valid from and valid to dates, its author and its approver
    Given the rule version of the change is held in the fixture with its author and approver
    Given the effective date the run uses is taken from the fixture and never from code

  Scenario: AC1 Publish a panel change (legacy RWB-E8-012 AC1)
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place
    When the user acts on the screen
    Then puts a partner panel change in force with an effective date
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 The change is published with its effective date (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the versioned reference row for the panel and the fee schedule is loaded and approved through the owner's operations with valid from and valid to dates, author and approver
    And the rule version of the change is in force for the effective date the fixture names
    When the partner read is made before the effective date and again from it
    Then the partner read shows the panel status the change carries, the old value before the effective date and the new value from it
    And the effective date used is the one the fixture names, never a date written in code
    And the list read returns the loaded reference row with its effective dates
    And a run whose partner read answers the new status before the date fails, and is never written up as a pass

  Scenario: AC3 The approval and the record (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a caller holding Rules and parameters C creates the rule version of the change
    When the version is approved through the decision service's approval operation by a caller holding Rules and parameters A
    Then one approved version exists, and the author is not the approver
    And one decision record carries decision_code, rule_id and rule_version with the approver
    And "rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1" is published once on "rwb.decision-record.v1" and confirmed by the central ledger
    And the same approval submitted twice is refused and leaves one approved version
    And a replay of the event changes nothing

  Scenario: AC4 A forced local decision-record failure stops the publish (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the local decision-record library is forced to fail for the change
    When the change is published through the rule-version approval
    Then the publish stops with "MSG-P7-003"
    And the reference version stays unapproved
    And the partner read still returns the old panel status
    And the reference row and the rule version are unchanged when they are read again

  Scenario: AC5 A caller without the approval right is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a synthetic caller holding Rules and parameters C and not A
    When the caller approves the rule version through POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve
    Then the answer is 403 with "MSG-P4-002"
    And no approved version and no decision record are written
    And a caller holding no Recovery Workbench role is refused with "MSG-P4-001"
```

Legacy AC2 (the decision log cannot be written) is built and tested in RWB-P4-E8012-APP, and this story asserts the same failure at the publish through AC4.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A partner panel change is put in force with an effective date, and access, limits and rules change without a code release | FEAT-ADM-07; legacy RWB-E8-012 |
| BR2 | Every versioned table carries its valid from and valid to dates, its author and its approver | REQ-DRI-011 |
| BR3 | Roles, teams, queues, queue membership and capacity are held as versioned reference data and change without a code release | REQ-CWC-006 |
| BR4 | The limit, the rule version and the approver are written to the decision log with every approval | REQ-APD-009 |
| BR5 | A new rule version applies to decisions taken from its effective date; open cases keep the version they were decided under | R-UNI-38 |
| BR6 | A partner panel exit recalls every open case held by that partner and re-selects | R-UNI-26; REQ-S9-006 |
| BR7 | When the decision log entry cannot be written, the action is blocked and no action proceeds unlogged | R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | Every partner type is managed on the same six points, selection and contract and fees among them | REQ-S9-001 |
| BR9 | Every call is one hop on the owner's base with a 2 s budget, the reference data and the rule registry stay with their owners, and the decision record is written through the local decision-record library on the shared topic and confirmed by the central ledger | DP-03, DP-06, DP-11, DP-13; ADR-020, ADR-022 |

The harness asserts these rules and changes none of them; the rules themselves are evaluated in the owning services, and BR5 to BR7 are the effective-dating, recall and no-unlogged-action context the change is proved against, not states the harness sets.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| LOADED | the approver approves the version | a different person from the author approves (four-eyes) | APPROVED |
| APPROVED | its effective date arrives | the version reaches the valid from date it carries | IN_FORCE |
| IN_FORCE | a later version is approved | the newer version reaches its effective date | SUPERSEDED |
| IN_FORCE | a rollback call is made | the rollback is the owner's decision, read here and never made here | ROLLED_BACK |
| LOADED | the approver refuses the version | the author cannot approve, and a refusal is recorded | REFUSED |

LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK and REFUSED are the rule version states of the rule package registry (Temporal and Drools design slide 15), and they are read from the owners' answers and never set by the harness. The panel status the change carries is the classification of DF-PRT-005: the harness reads the old value before the effective date and the new value from it and never writes either. The reference row's own approval state is P3's and is asserted only through the load answer and the list read-back, because no source names that state vocabulary. A state the harness had set by hand would prove nothing, so the report names the owner and the operation behind every value it asserts.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Holds Rules and parameters C: creates the rule version of the change and loads the versioned reference row |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Holds Rules and parameters A: approves the rule version, and the author cannot approve |
| Partner and agency manager | The role the legacy story is written for, and the role that decides the panel change; the harness reads the effect of that decision on the partner side |
| QA lead | Owns the harness configuration, the fixtures, the report shape and the pass or fail gate |
| Integration lead | Owns the harness code, the stub set and the swap from a stub to the real service |
| The owning services' identities | P3 answers the reference load and the list read-back, P7 creates and approves the rule version, holds the ledger and publishes the rule package event, S9 answers the panel read, P4 answers the session; they make every change the harness asserts |
| No delegation of authority level applies | The harness takes no business decision; the approval is RW-RISK's under four-eyes, and authorisation is answered by rwb-access |

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 | partner | id, partner_code, partner_name, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end | Read through the rwb-partner contract, before and after the effective date |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | decision_code, rule_id, rule_version, model_version | Read through the rwb-decision contract |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015 | rule_row | rule_id, rule_version | Read through the rwb-decision contract |
| DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-038 | role | role_code, role_class | Read through the rwb-access session answer, for the caller's rights |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8, and the legacy section names these four entities with these ranges. The reference row and the reference version of the panel and fee schedule are P3's, in rwb-case; the legacy section names no field ID for them, so none is cited here. The partner and its panel status are S9's, the decision log and the rule rows are P7's, and the role behind a right is P4's; the harness reads them only through those contracts and never from a schema. The harness owns no table and writes no row.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-versions` | P7 rwb-decision | Creates the rule version the change is published under; the path is the one the legacy section names, re-based on the owner's base (AC1, AC3) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve` | P7 rwb-decision | The four-eyes approval of that version, and the refusal on a second submission (AC3, AC4, AC5) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads` | P3 rwb-case | Loads the versioned panel and fee schedule reference row with its valid from date, author and approver (AC1, AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | Reads the panel list back with its effective dates (AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` | S9 rwb-partner | The panel status the change carries, before the effective date and from it (AC2, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?ruleId={ruleId}&from={from}` | P7 rwb-decision | The change records of the run, with decision_code, rule_id and rule_version (AC3, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The caller's rights before a create, an approve or a refusal (AC5) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13). No operation is invented in this story: each path is the owner's published operation, and where a screen would compose them the path would be the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The Ownership Map publishes no panel-change operation of its own, so the harness publishes the change through the versioned reference row and the rule version, and proves the effect through the partner read; a hop that has no owner in the map is never invented. The two rule-version paths are owned by P7 and the two reference paths by P3 under the default ruling that puts reference data with rwb-case (ASM-0040, ASM-0041); the panel read is S9's and the session is P4's.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it writes its report to the wave record.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use in the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | The service that takes the decision, through the local decision-record library (DP-03) | Proves the change was recorded with its rule version and confirmed by the central ledger, and stays one record after a replay (AC3, AC4) |
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | Records the version the rule registry put in force against the version id approved in the run (AC3) |

Both events are cited from the Arch v5 extract: `DecisionRecorded` is row 08 of slide 42 on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and `RulePackageInForce` is row 30 of slide 43 on `rwb.decision.events.v1` with P7 as producer, which is why the second is kept and not left out. The harness subscribes to both topics under one consumer group of its own, counts publications and replays each event once; its consumers of record are rwb-decision and rwb-reporting for the first, and rwb-case, rwb-valuation, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment for the second, and their effect is observed by count because no consumer exposes an operation this story consumes.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness observes ApprovalWorkflow, the workflow-kit template that runs on the task queue `rwb-decision` in the `rwb-recovery` namespace and carries the four-eyes approval of the rule version; it is stated here as observed and not built. No workflow, activity or Schedule is created, changed or owned by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added. JOB-20, rule promotion at 00:01, is a Schedule of rwb-decision (Arch v5 slide 44) and is observed only; the harness sets no overlap policy and no catch-up window, and it starts nothing by cron.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-01); partner and partner_user are S9's, reference row and reference version are P3's, and rule_package, rule_package_version and decision_log_entry are P7's.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Contract | Stubbed answer in the run |
|---|---|---|
| Stub for rwb-decision (rule version create) | `POST /admin/rule-versions` | Creates a version with the id and state the contract allows and returns it with the version id the run then approves |
| Stub for rwb-decision (rule version approve) | `POST /admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve` | Approves the version once with its approver, refuses a second submission of the same approval, and answers 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a caller without Rules and parameters A |
| Stub for rwb-case (reference load) | `POST /admin/reference-loads` | Accepts the fixture file and returns the row with its valid from and valid to dates, author and approver; a load without one of them answers the empty field for X2 |
| Stub for rwb-case (list read) | `GET /admin/lists/{listCode}` | Returns the loaded panel list with its effective dates, and the rejection state after a forced decision-record failure |
| Stub for rwb-partner | `GET /partners` | Returns the synthetic partner with partner_code, partner_type, contract_end and the old panel status before the effective date and the new one from it, with the date taken from the fixture |
| Stub for rwb-decision (decision log) | `GET /decision-log?ruleId={ruleId}&from={from}` | One record for the change with decision_code, rule_id, rule_version and approver, and the central ledger confirmation; none after a forced failure |
| Stub for rwb-access | `GET /me/session` | Allows Rules and parameters C and not A for the creator, A for the approver, and refuses a caller holding C and not A on the approve with 403 and MSG-P4-002, and a caller with no Recovery Workbench role with MSG-P4-001 |
| Panel-change fixture | The reference row, the rule version key and the effective date | The panel and fee schedule row with its valid from and valid to dates, author and approver, the rule version key, the synthetic panel and partner keys and the effective date, all as data |

Each stub is generated from the published contract and its version is pinned in the run report, so a contract change shows up as a run failure and not as a silent pass. The harness environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the stub answer shapes, the effective date the run uses, the shape of the panel reference row, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0478; ASM-0670).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 7 consumed, one hop each on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13) |
| Kafka | None published; two consumed, `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` and `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1`, counted and replayed once |
| Temporal | None added; ApprovalWorkflow on `rwb-decision` observed, and JOB-20 observed as its Schedule |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H dependencies the table adds, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, are platform contract stories delivered in the platform wave and are recorded here and not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays None; DP-13 adds none. The C dependency RWB-P3-E1042-CON is built against its published contract and its fake and never blocks. The only blocking dependency is the I story RWB-P4-E8012-APP, which replaces its stub, so the story is Day 1; until it is live the run uses the stub, and a stub pass is reported as a stub pass.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ChangeRunner | Job | Runs the five owned criteria in order for one change and holds the run lock |
| SessionProbe | Service | Reads the caller's rights, and names the right each operation needs |
| ReferenceLoadDriver | Service | Posts the fixture file to the reference load, reads the panel list back and asserts the effective dates, the author and the approver |
| RuleVersionDriver | Service | Creates the rule version, drives the four-eyes approval, retries the same approval and asserts the refusal |
| PanelProbe | Service | Reads the partner and asserts the panel status before the effective date and from it, on the date the fixture names |
| DecisionReadBack | Service | Reads the decision log and asserts one record with its code, rule id, rule version and approver, with the ledger confirmation |
| EventObserver | Service | Subscribes to `rwb.decision-record.v1` and `rwb.decision.events.v1`, counts publications and replays each event once |
| StubSet | Fake | The seven stubs and the panel-change fixture of §12.8, generated from the published contracts with the version pinned |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes one report keyed by story and by the reference load key, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the stubs from Day 1 and the real services as RWB-P4-E8012-APP lands, on the synthetic panel and partner keys, the panel and fee schedule reference row with its valid from and valid to dates, author and approver, the rule version key and the effective date, all held in the fixture as data. The harness seeds nothing by hand and never writes a schema row. The environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic keys, the stub answer shapes, the effective date the run uses, the shape of the panel reference row, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0478; ASM-0670).

**Build steps**

1. Generate the seven stubs and the panel-change fixture from the published contracts and pin each contract version in the run report; fail the run on a mismatch (X1).
2. Build the SessionProbe and prove the three right sets of AC5: C and not A, A, and no Recovery Workbench role.
3. Build the ReferenceLoadDriver for AC2: post the fixture file, read the panel list back, and fail the run where a valid from date, a valid to date, an author or an approver is missing (X2).
4. Build the RuleVersionDriver for AC3 against both operations, and prove one approved version with the author not the approver, and a refusal on the same approval submitted twice (X5).
5. Add the DecisionReadBack for AC3: one record with its code, rule id, rule version and approver, and the ledger confirmation before the publish is reported as recorded (X4).
6. Add the EventObserver for AC3: one publication of the decision record, one of the rule package in force, a replay that changes nothing, and one record after the replay.
7. Add the PanelProbe and the effective-date assertion for AC2, with the date read from the fixture, and fail a run whose partner read answers the new status before the date (X3).
8. Add the forced decision-record failure for AC4 through the load answer, the rule version state and the partner read, so nothing changes is asserted and not assumed (X6), then the refused approve and the no-role refusal for AC5 (X7), then the EvidenceReport and the gate, and swap a stub for the real owner as RWB-P4-E8012-APP lands.

**Feature switch.** None. The harness has no production flag and runs in the test environment only.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass against the fakes and again against RWB-P4-E8012-APP when it lands, and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story and by the reference load key.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-004 | Warning | Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-001 | Error | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values on the answer it reads, and owns no message text. The legacy section carries these five messages for the feature, so none is invented here: MSG-GEN-001 with the missing field when a load or a create is made short of a required value, MSG-P4-002 with the refused approve for a caller holding C and not A, MSG-P4-001 for a caller with no Recovery Workbench role, MSG-P7-003 when the decision record cannot be written and nothing changes, and MSG-P4-004 as the warning that every action is recorded while emergency access is on, which the run reads and does not assert as a state.

##### 15. Screens and states

The harness renders no screen: it observes the owners' operations and writes a report. The legacy section names SCR-39 Rules and parameters and SCR-41 Delegation of authority, which belong to P4 and its CON story; the harness neither builds nor reads them, and it asserts their data through the reference load, the rule version and the partner read.

| State | Read through | What the run asserts |
|---|---|---|
| The panel status of DF-PRT-005 | rwb-partner partner read | The old value before the effective date and the new value the change carries from it, with the date taken from the fixture |
| LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED (rule version state) | rwb-decision rule version operations and the decision log | One approved version with its approver, a refusal on a repeated approval, and the version the rule package event puts in force |
| The approval state of the reference version | rwb-case reference load answer and list read-back | The version is loaded and approved before the publish, and stays unapproved after a forced decision-record failure |
| The decision record of the change | rwb-decision decision log | One record with its decision code, rule id, rule version and approver, confirmed by the central ledger |
| The caller's rights | rwb-access session answer | Rules and parameters C for the creator, A for the approver, and the refusal of C without A and of no Recovery Workbench role |

The environment, layout and retention of the run report are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0478; ASM-0670).

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-E8-012-01-ITG | AC1 (legacy); ITG AC1 | End to end | One synthetic panel, one versioned panel and fee schedule reference row and one rule version, with the effective date from the fixture |
| TC-E8-012-02-ITG | Legacy AC2 not recorded stays with RWB-P4-E8012-APP; ITG AC4 | Integration | The decision-record library forced to fail on the publish, with the reference version and the partner read before and after |

The Covers column names the legacy test case the copy derives from and the ITG criterion it asserts, and the full legacy test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx under the same legacy test case ID. Legacy AC2, the forced decision-log failure, stays with RWB-P4-E8012-APP and is asserted here at the publish through AC4.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the panel and fee schedule row, its effective dates, the author and approver, the synthetic keys, the rule version key, the effective date, the panel status values and the report layout are data.
- No personal data in logs, events or reports: every key is synthetic, and the events carry IDs and facts only.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this run reads no ACE data at all, and the partner, reference, decision and session values are read only through their owners' contracts (DP-01).
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would (DP-11, DP-13).
- A stub pass is never reported as a real pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner.
- The effective date is read from the fixture and never from the clock or from code, and the partner read is asserted on both sides of it.
- The harness never approves on behalf of the author, and it never supplies an approver, an effective date or a panel status of its own.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and it never writes a row by hand or sets a state it then asserts.
- A failing criterion is fixed in the owning service or raised as a gap; it is never waived in the script.
