
AC1 and AC2 are the two criteria of RWB-E8-013, copied with their text unchanged and their values kept; AC1 carries one added line at the top of its scenario, the decision mock, so the sample is provable while the `rwb-decision` contract is still a fake. AC3 to AC5 are new under D-RCV-60 and test only what this story adds: the right, the three consistency failures and the bounded, recorded and replayable run.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A sample of closed decisions is tested against the rule version that was recorded on each of them, and the result of the run is recorded with the rule version | RWB-E8-013 AC1; FSD P4 v3 A2.24; REQ-DRI-001 |
| BR2 | A decision record carries the rule id and the rule version that decided it, so the record alone is enough to test the decision afterwards | REQ-DRI-001, REQ-CWC-016; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 |
| BR3 | The run needs Rules and parameters R; a caller without it is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002 and nothing is read, computed or recorded | TSD P4 v3 T6.1; FSD P4 v3 A2.24.4.3 |
| BR4 | The decision log and the rule registry are P7's: this story reads them through the P7 contract and holds no decision row, no rule row, no package source and no copy of a version state | Ownership Map v1 (`decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` = P7; ASM-0069); Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; DP-01 |
| BR5 | The test is a consistency test and never a re-evaluation: no rule package is evaluated, no KieBase is built and no rule evaluator is called, because evaluation is the owning service's and the registry is P7's | Temporal and Drools Design slide 15 T6; ASM-1586 |
| BR6 | The sample is drawn by the rule and the size held as parameter rows, in a stable order, so the same request over the same data draws the same decisions in the same order | ASM-1587; FSD P4 v3 A2.24.3.1 BR-P4-024 |
| BR7 | Each drawn decision is checked in order: the recorded rule version's `valid_from` and `valid_to` cover the decision's `decided_at`; the recorded rule id is present in that version's `rule_row` set; the recorded answer agrees with that row's `action_text` and `outputs`. The first failure decides the item | REQ-CWC-016; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015, DF-REF-296 to DF-REF-298; ASM-1586 |
| BR8 | Every run appends exactly one entry to the local decision-record chain of DP-03 in the transaction that stores the answer; an answer that cannot be recorded is withheld with 503 and MSG-P7-003 | R-UNI-39; RWB-E8-013 AC2; DP-03 |
| BR9 | The entry and the answer carry the run id, the period, the requested and drawn sizes, the passed and failed counts, the window, the state, the time and the reason code of each failure | REQ-DRI-012; ASM-1588 |
| BR10 | The verdict is PASS or FAIL and each FAIL carries exactly one reason code, taken from a parameter row set and never from a constant in code | FSD P4 v3 A2.24.3.1 BR-P4-024; ASM-1587 |
| BR11 | The default sample size, the maximum sample size, the period bounds and the page bounds are parameter rows read through DP-06 with the version in force; a changed cap is data and needs no build | DP-06; BR-P4-024; ASM-1587 |
| BR12 | One `Idempotency-Key` answers one run: a replay answers the first answer, appends no second entry and makes no second read | Architecture v5 slide 42; DP-09 |
| BR13 | A run is answered from what this service stored: the same `qaSampleId` answers the same items in the same order, and the item set is never re-drawn on a read | REQ-DRI-012; ASM-1588 |
| BR14 | A FAIL verdict is an observation and changes nothing: no case is reopened, no task is raised, no rule version is moved and no decision is rewritten | REQ-DRI-002; DP-03; ASM-1588 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-access`:

- BR1, BR3 and BR7 are one ordered run in `QaSampleService`: authorise, read the parameters, read the period, draw, read each version, check, record. Each step that refuses returns before the next one is reached, so a refused run can never have read a decision.
- BR2 is not a rule of this service but the reason for it: the record of a decision carries `ruleId` and `ruleVersion` (Temporal and Drools Design slide 16), and a QA run that had to guess the version would be testing a re-evaluation and not the record.
- BR4 is the absence of a ledger and registry repository: the module has no table, no view and no join for `decision_log_entry`, `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` or `rule_test_case`, and every decision field and rule field arrives in a P7 answer.
- BR5 is the absence of a rule evaluator: the module has no KieBase, no DRL parser, no agenda listener and no DP-04 dependency, and the checker compares three values it was handed.
- BR6 and BR11 are the parameter reader at request time with the version in force: the size, the bounds and the order rule are rows, so a changed cap is data.
- BR7 and BR10 are the checker and the reason resolver: the checker returns which of the three checks failed, and the resolver maps that to the code the parameter rows hold.
- BR8, BR9 and BR13 are the record appender of DP-03 and its read: the entry and the stored items commit with the idempotency row, and the read is a read over that stored run with no write method.
- BR12 is the `idempotency_key` row of the platform library in `rwb_access`, written with the answer.
- BR14 is the absence of a side effect: the run writes no case, no task and no rule version, and a FAIL is answered and recorded only.

##### 9. State transitions

This story holds no rule version state and no case state. The states it reads are `rwb-decision`'s, and the one state it records is the state of its own run.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| No run | A sample is requested | R held, the fields valid, the period inside its bounds, P7 answers the period and the versions | One run recorded, answer 201 with its counts and its items |
| No run | A sample is requested | No R letter | Refused 403 with MSG-P4-002; no read, no entry |
| No run | A sample is requested | A field invalid, the period outside its bounds, or the size above the maximum | Refused 422 with MSG-GEN-001; no read, no entry |
| No run | A sample is requested | The period holds no closed decision | One run recorded with draws 0 and an empty item set |
| No run | A sample is requested | `rwb-decision` cannot be reached | Refused 503 with MSG-P7-003; no entry |
| No run | A sample is requested | The entry cannot be written | Refused 503 with MSG-P7-003; nothing recorded |
| Recorded | The same `Idempotency-Key` is sent again | None | The first answer is replayed; no second entry, no second read |
| Recorded | The run is read by its id | None | The same items in the same order, paged |

| Chain | Event | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Append-only local chain | A run, or a refusal that is recorded at the service edge | One entry appended with its `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`; no entry is ever updated or deleted |
| `rwb-decision` | A rule version is promoted or superseded | Its `valid_from`, its `valid_to` and its `rule_row` set change as P7 writes them; a run already recorded keeps the verdicts it reached |

A run recorded before a rule version is superseded keeps its verdicts: the entry is append-only, the comparison it made is stated in its items, and a later promotion at `rwb-decision` is P7's and not a correction of this run (BR4, BR13).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Conduct and QA officer (RW-CONDUCT) | Runs a sample and reads it: the primary user of the FSD P4 v3 A2.24.3.3 role table, holding `R` in Rules and parameters in the T6.1 matrix |
| Center of excellence analyst (RW-COE) | Also uses the feature per the FSD role table and holds `CRUD` in Rules and parameters; runs a sample and reads it, and authors no rule version here (that is P7's) |
| Internal audit (RW-AUDIT) | Also uses the feature and holds `R`; reads a run and its verdicts and runs a sample of a period |
| A role without Rules and parameters R (RW-PHONECOL, RW-FIELDCOL) | Refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002; nothing is read, computed or recorded |
| The gateway-bff route | Calls the two operations on behalf of the signed-in user, one hop each, and passes the `Idempotency-Key` unchanged |
| `rwb-access` itself | Reads `role` and `permission` in its own schema and writes only its own chain and the platform library rows of the request |
| `rwb-decision` (P7) | Owns the decision log, the rule packages, their versions, their rows and their test cases; answers the period read and the rule-model read, and promotes a version at 00:01 |
| The owning service of a model | Evaluates its own package locally and writes the decision with the rule id and the rule version; this story never evaluates it |

The refusal shapes are 403 with an RFC 9457 problem response and `messageId` set to MSG-P4-002 for an absent right, 401 with MSG-P4-001 for no session, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for a field, a period or a size, and 503 with MSG-P7-003 for a read or a record that cannot be completed. The database login is the per-service login of the service baseline (DP-02), which belongs to RWB-P4-E8013-CON.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Table in `rwb_access` | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039 | `role` | id, role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope, entra_group | Read: the role code of the caller who ran the sample |
| DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 | `permission` | id, role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version | Read: the Rules and parameters R letter and the role it is held through |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local library, DP-03) | the run entry: `decision_code` DF-DEC-003, `case_id` DF-DEC-002 empty, `inputs_ref` DF-DEC-008 with the qaSampleId, the period, the sizes, the counts, the window and the reason code of each failure, `decided_at` DF-DEC-016, `prev_hash` DF-DEC-017 and `entry_hash` DF-DEC-018 | Write; and read for the run read |
| (run items) | the stored item set of a run in `rwb_access` | per item: `decisionEntryId`, `caseId`, `decidedAt`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion`, `verdict`, `reasonCode`, and the draw order | Write and read |
| (idempotency) | `idempotency_key` (platform library table in `rwb_access`) | the request and the stored answer of a run | Write and read (DP-09; ASM-0074) |
| (outbox) | `outbox_event` | the record row of the run entry | Write |
| (inbox) | `processed_event` | none: this story consumes no event | None |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | `decision_log_entry` of `rwb_decision` | id, case_id, decision_code, rule_id, rule_version, model_version and the rest of the record | Returned through the P7 contract; not read |
| DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015, DF-REF-052 to DF-REF-054, DF-REF-296 to DF-REF-298 | `rule_row` of `rwb_decision` | rule_id, rule_version, route_set, from_state, event_code, action_text, owner_role, timer_spec, valid_from, valid_to, rule_table, row_order, target_queue_code, package_version_id, drools_rule_name, outputs | Returned through the P7 contract; not read |
| DF-REF-274 to DF-REF-278, DF-REF-279 to DF-REF-295 | `rule_package`, `rule_package_version` of `rwb_decision` | package_code, version_label, status, valid_from, valid_to and the rest of the version | Returned through the P7 contract; not read |
| DF-REF-185 to DF-REF-197, DF-REF-299 | `rule_test_case` of `rwb_decision` | none | Not read |

No row of `decision_log_entry`, `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` or `rule_test_case` is read or written: they are `rwb-decision`'s (P7) under the ownership map and the ruling ASM-0069, and their fields arrive in the contract, not by a schema read (DP-01). No row of `case` or `task` is read either: a QA sample addresses a period and not a case, and the `caseId` it answers is the one P7 returned on the entry. No row of `delegation_limit` is read, because the sample tests rule versions and not approval limits. Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 and of TSD P4 v3 T3.1.

The name and the shape of a run id, the ordered field set of the run answer and of an item, the run state set, the reason-code set, the draw rule, and the record code of a QA sample are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0873; ASM-1586): FSD P4 v3 A2.24 names the journey and one validation rule (VR-P4-024-1) and one business rule (BR-P4-024) and no operation and no field. The schema of RWB-P4-E8013-CON fixes them and this story reads and writes them as that contract publishes them.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Path | Owner | Request | Response | Errors | Authorization | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/qa-samples` | P4 `rwb-access` | Body: `from`, `to`, `sampleSize`, `reason` | `qaSampleId`, `from`, `to`, `sampleSize`, `draws`, `passed`, `failed`, `state`, `recordedAt`, with `Location` of the read | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 (MSG-P4-002); 422 (MSG-GEN-001); 503 (MSG-P7-003) | Rules and parameters R | `Idempotency-Key` required; a replay answers the first answer and makes no second read |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/qa-samples/{qaSampleId}` | P4 `rwb-access` | Path: `qaSampleId`. Query: `page`, `size` | `QaSampleRun`: `qaSampleId`, `from`, `to`, `sampleSize`, `draws`, `passed`, `failed`, `state`, `recordedAt`, `items[]` of `decisionEntryId`, `caseId`, `decidedAt`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion`, `verdict`, `reasonCode`, and `page`, `size`, `total` | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 (MSG-P4-002); 422 (MSG-GEN-001); 503 (MSG-P7-003) | Rules and parameters R | Not applicable, read only |

Both operations sit on the base `/api/recovery/access/v1` of DP-13. The read answers only what this service recorded, so its items and their order are the ones the run stored, and a later promotion of a rule version at `rwb-decision` is P7's answer and not this read's. `page` defaults to the value of its parameter row and `size` is capped by it, both read through DP-06 and never from code (BR11). A `qaSampleId` this service issued but has no run for cannot arise, because ids are issued by this service and a run is never deleted, so the read has no 404 branch; a malformed id is a 422 with MSG-GEN-001.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 `rwb-access` (own service) | The Rules and parameters R check behind both operations, cached for the session; MSG-P4-002 on a refusal |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 `rwb-case` | The default sample size, the maximum sample size, the period bounds, the page bounds and the reason-code set, with the version in force (DP-06) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?from=&to=&page=` | P7 `rwb-decision` | The closed decisions of the period: each entry's id, case id, `decidedAt`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion` and recorded answer, from which the sample is drawn. Declared as consumed, never as provided, and named as the missing C dependency of the key (GAP-0873; ASM-1586) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{versionLabel}` | P7 `rwb-decision` | One rule-model version with its `valid_from`, its `valid_to` and its `rule_row` set, read once per drawn version and cached for the run. Declared as consumed, never as provided, and part of the same missing C dependency |

One hop per call, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11); the authorise answer and the parameters read are cached for the session or the request, and a rule-model version is read once per run and reused across the decisions that name it. The two P7 operations are the decision-log query and the rule-model read of the P7 contract (Architecture v5 slide 14: `GET /decisions?caseId=` and `GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}`); this story declares them as consumed and never defines them, and its metadata carries no P7 contract dependency, which is the missing dependency raised in the key's gap row and not added to the metadata. No other operation of `rwb-decision`, `rwb-case`, `rwb-document` or `rwb-comms` is called, and no rule-version operation of the legacy endpoint table is called either: under the ruling ASM-0040 the rule-version paths belong to P7 and this story only reads a version.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library; consumed by P7 | entryId | the hash-chained entry of a QA sample: the run id, the period, the requested and drawn sizes, the passed and failed counts, the window and the reason code of each failure |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, from the outbox of the transaction that stores the answer. The payload carries ids, counts, codes and times and no name, no e-mail address, no case narrative and no personal field. This story publishes no `rwb.access.<Event>.v1` message: the two events of `rwb-access` are `AccessPolicyChanged` (RWB-P4-E1037-APP) and `DoaLimitChanged` (RWB-P4-E8008-APP), and a QA verdict changes no policy and no limit, so neither fits (Architecture v5 slide 14).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `rwb-access` is a reference-data owner in Architecture v5 slide 14 with no inbound event for this capability, and the run answers from the P7 contract and its own chain. No `processed_event` row is written, and `RulePackageInForce` (EV-30) is not subscribed to: a run reads the version it needs at the time it runs.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The run is synchronous: this story starts no workflow, signals no workflow and registers no activity on the `rwb-access` queue. The daily chain check at 02:00 (JOB-14) is P7's Schedule and not a workflow of this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The run is request-driven; the six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) is the only Schedule of `rwb-access` and belongs to RWB-P4-AD008-APP. A monthly conduct check is a person's act on the screen and not a Schedule of this story.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Read only: the role code of the caller who ran the sample |
| `permission` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Read only: the Rules and parameters R letter and the role it is held through |
| the local decision-record table of the DP-03 library | P4, in `rwb_access` | Write: the entry of a run. Read: the run read |
| the stored item set of a run | P4, in `rwb_access` | Write: the items of a run with their draw order. Read: the run read |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_access` | The outbox row of the entry and the idempotency row of the request; no inbox row, because no event is consumed (DP-09; ASM-0074) |
| `decision_log_entry` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | Not read and not written: the central ledger is P7's and is read through its contract |
| `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row`, `rule_test_case` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | Not read and not written: the registry is P7's under ASM-0069 and is read through its contract |

No rule or ledger table is named as this service's and none is created here. `lov_value`, `reference_version` and `reference_row` are reference data of P3 under the ownership ruling; this story's pattern list carries no DP-07 and its contract-dependency list no `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`, so a verdict or a reason code is taken from the parameter rows and validated against no list of this service (GAP-0873; ASM-1587). No table of another service is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| decision fake | the `rwb-decision` contract (GAP-0873; ASM-1586) | `GET /decision-log?from=&to=&page=` answering the closed decisions of a period with their entry id, case id, `decidedAt`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion` and recorded answer; an empty period; a 503 for X8 |
| rule-model fake | the `rwb-decision` contract (GAP-0873; ASM-1586) | `GET /rule-models/{packageCode}/{versionLabel}` answering "ALLOCATION" version "ALLOC-2026.09" with `valid_from` 2026-10-15 and `valid_to` 2026-11-14, version "ALLOC-2026.10" with `valid_from` 2026-10-01 and `valid_to` 2026-10-31 and its `rule_row` set, and a 404 for a version P7 does not hold |
| authorise fake | RWB-P4-E8013-CON, RWB-P4-E1037-CON | A granted answer for RW-CONDUCT, RW-COE and RW-AUDIT with R in Rules and parameters, and a refused answer with MSG-P4-002 for RW-PHONECOL with no letter |
| parameters fake | RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The default sample size, the maximum sample size, the period bounds, the page bounds and the reason-code set, with the version in force |

| Call type | Count in this story | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | Provided 2 (the run and the read); consumed 4 | Base `/api/recovery/access/v1`; two `rwb-decision` operations, the own authorise operation and the `rwb-case` parameters read, one hop and 2 s each |
| Kafka | Published 1 event type; consumed 0 | `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the DP-03 library |
| Temporal | 0 workflows, 0 activities | The `rwb-access` queue carries the access review Schedule of RWB-P4-AD008-APP only |
| File | None | No file input and no file output: the run is a request, and a report export is not part of this capability |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`, module `access/qasample`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.qasample`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-13 | the monolith REST base | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The legacy markers this slice replaces are the in-module decision-log read and the in-module rule-row read of the monolith (DP-01 and DP-13: the ledger and the registry owned by P7 and addressed on this service's own base through the P7 contract), and the ace-web screen that read a rule version in process (DP-19: a gateway-bff composite route). DP-01, DP-02, DP-09 and DP-11 govern the service baseline and the one-hop budget of section 12.2; they add no dependency of their own, they are not in the pattern list the Work Package fixes for this story, and they are not claimed as patterns of it. **DP-04 is not applied**: this story evaluates no rule package, so it needs no embedded Drools kit, no `RWB-PLT-E1072-CON` and no `RWB-P7-E1073-CON`; the consistency test reads the recorded version and its row and never runs the engine (BR5). DP-08 is not applied either: the right is checked through the own authorise operation, which is the service baseline, and this story calls no guard library. The two `rwb-decision` operations are consumed through the P7 contract and its fake, and the missing C dependency is raised in the key's gap row and not added to the metadata.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| QaSampleController | Controller | The two operations: validation, the `Idempotency-Key` lookup, the RFC 9457 problem responses, `Location` on a created run |
| QaSampleService | Service | The ordered run of BR1, BR3 and BR7: right, parameters, period, draw, version reads, checks, record; a refusal returns before the next step |
| QaSampleDrawer | Service | The sample of BR6: the population from the P7 answer, the size from the parameter rows, the stable draw order |
| RuleVersionConsistencyChecker | Service | The three checks of BR7 in order, stopping at the first failure, and the verdict |
| VerdictReasonResolver | Service | The reason code of a failed check, read from the parameter rows and never held as a literal (BR10) |
| QaSampleRunService | Service | The answer of BR9: the counts, the state, the `recordedAt` and the entry payload |
| QaSampleRunRepository | Repository | The stored run and its item set in `rwb_access`: write on the run, read on the read, with no re-draw |
| DecisionLogClient | Client | The `rwb-decision` decision-log query, one hop, 2 s timeout and a breaker; maps a timeout to 503 |
| RuleModelClient | Client | The `rwb-decision` rule-model read by package code and version label, one hop, 2 s timeout, a breaker and a per-run cache; maps a 404 to the absent-version check |
| PermissionReader | Service | The `role` and `permission` rows of the caller and the Rules and parameters R letter |
| ParameterReader | Service | The default size, the maximum size, the period bounds, the page bounds and the reason-code set through DP-06, with the version in force |
| DecisionRecordAppender | Service | The run entry with its outbox row, in the transaction that stores the answer (DP-03, DP-09) |
| IdempotencyStore | Service | The `Idempotency-Key` lookup and store of the platform library, written with the answer |

**Database and migrations**

- This story creates no table of its own. `role` and `permission` are created by RWB-P4-E1037-APP, the local decision-record table by RWB-P4-E1039-APP and the platform library tables by the service's own DB story, in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15; this story reads and uses them.
- The stored item set of a run is a table of this service in `rwb_access`, created by the same DB story; it holds the run id, the draw order and the seven item fields, and it is written once per run and never updated (BR13).
- No decision-log or rule table is created in `rwb_access` and no column of one is copied: a copy would be a second writer of a ledger entry and would drift from `rwb-decision` on the first correction (BR4).
- No write statement touches `role`, `permission` or `delegation_limit`: the readers are read-only, so a run can never grant itself a right or move a limit.
- The entry, the stored items, the idempotency row and the outbox row commit in one transaction; a failure rolls all four back and the answer is withheld with MSG-P7-003 (BR8).

**Configuration and reference data**

- The default sample size, the maximum sample size, the period bounds and the page bounds are parameter rows of `rwb-case` read through DP-06 with the version in force; no bound is a constant in code (BR11). Their names are fixed by RWB-P4-E8013-CON.
- The reason-code set is a parameter row set of the same contract: PASS, FAIL, RULE_VERSION_NOT_IN_FORCE, RULE_ROW_ABSENT and ANSWER_MISMATCH at the version in force, and a code that is not in the set is a configuration error and not a silent pass (BR10).
- The draw rule — the ordering key of the population and the rounding of the drawn size — is a parameter row too, so a change of sampling policy is data (BR6, ASM-1587).
- The role codes are read from `role` through the `permission` row that carries the R letter; no role code and no capability area is a constant in code (BR3).

**Build steps**

1. `QaSampleController` and its validation; tests for X1, X2 and X3 with no decision read.
2. `PermissionReader` and the authorise call of step 5; test the AC3 refusal of a caller with no letter, with no P7 read and no entry afterwards.
3. `DecisionLogClient` and `QaSampleDrawer` over the decision fake: the period read of AC1, the empty period of X6, the stable order and the draw size.
4. `RuleModelClient` over the rule-model fake: the two versions of AC4, the absent version of X7 and the 503 of X8.
5. `RuleVersionConsistencyChecker` with the three checks in order; tests for AC4, one per failure, and the proof that a decision that passes all three is PASS with no code.
6. `VerdictReasonResolver` over the parameters fake; test that a changed code set is data and that a code outside the set fails the run rather than passing it.
7. `QaSampleRunService`, `QaSampleRunRepository`, `DecisionRecordAppender` and `IdempotencyStore` in one transaction; test the replay of AC5 with one entry and one read, and the forced failure of AC2 with no record.
8. The run read over a seeded run of twenty items; test the order, the paging, the same answer on every call and the absence of a re-draw.
9. The contract-fake run of both operations through the gateway-bff fake, so SCR-39 can be demonstrated while the route and the P7 platform are being built.

**Feature switch.** The two operations are switched by the service baseline of RWB-P4-E1037-CON, not by a flag of their own. A run that is switched off would leave a period untested and invisible as such, which is the state the sample is meant to resolve, so this story adds no flag and removes nothing.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; a sample of twenty closed decisions is run by RW-CONDUCT and answered with its counts and its items; a caller with no letter is refused with MSG-P4-002 and no decision is read; the three seeded decisions of AC4 are FAIL with RULE_VERSION_NOT_IN_FORCE, RULE_ROW_ABSENT and ANSWER_MISMATCH and nothing changes for any of them; a size above the maximum is refused with MSG-GEN-001; the same run id answers the same items in the same order; the same `Idempotency-Key` replays one answer with one entry and one read; and a forced record failure withholds the answer with MSG-P7-003.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The caller has no session | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | This story, on both operations |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller holds no Rules and parameters R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, on both operations |
| MSG-P4-004 | A break-glass grant is active for the caller | Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded. | This story, as a warning on the run answer, with the grant id recorded in the entry |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is empty, `from` or `to` is not a date, `to` is earlier than `from`, `sampleSize` is not a whole number, the period is outside its bounds, or the size is above the maximum | Enter {field}. | This story, on both operations |
| MSG-P7-003 | `rwb-decision` cannot be reached, or the entry, the stored items, the idempotency row or the outbox row cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on both operations |

Every error from this service is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled and `instance` naming the request. The business texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story where the message already existed: MSG-P4-004, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-001, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P7-003 are the legacy texts, and VR-P4-024-1 of the FSD is the rule behind MSG-GEN-001. The four-eyes message of a rule package approval is not produced here: this story approves no rule version and its failure codes are the three of BR7, not a message. MSG-P3-022, the missing checklist item, is not produced here either, because this story approves no package version.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-39 Rules and parameters is the screen, served through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 (H RWB-PLT-N001-CON), which shows the rule version in force and its evidence as `rwb-decision` answers them and calls the two operations of this story, one hop each. This story renders no screen surface of its own.

| Screen | State | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Rule version in force | The version in force and its evidence as `rwb-decision` answers them, with the run panel of this service beside it |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Sample, form | The period, the sample size and the reason, with the size and the bounds shown from the parameter rows in force |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Sample, recorded | The 201 answer with `qaSampleId`, `from`, `to`, `sampleSize`, `draws`, `passed`, `failed`, `state` and `recordedAt` |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Sample, items | One row per drawn decision with its decision entry, case, decided time, rule id, rule version, verdict and reason code, paged |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Sample, all passed | A run with `failed` 0 and every item PASS, so a clean period is visible as a clean period |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Sample, failures | A run with its FAIL items and their reason codes, with no action offered on the case they belong to |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Sample, refused | The 403 of X4 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without the R letter |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Sample, out of bounds | The 422 of X2 or X3 with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field and the bound in force |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Not recorded | The 503 of X9 or X8 with MSG-P7-003 and a retry action that reuses the same `Idempotency-Key` |

The legacy story named SCR-39 Rules and parameters and SCR-41 Delegation of authority in its screen table although a QA sample sits on neither of them as a panel of its own; the target screen is SCR-39 Rules and parameters, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON. The FSD P4 screen list names no QA-sample screen — it lists SCR-39, SCR-40, SCR-41, SCR-42, SCR-43 and SCR-47 and no sample screen — so this story claims no screen id of its own and the absence is carried in the key's gap row rather than filled with an invented id (GAP-0873; ASM-1586).

##### 16. Test cases

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is added to the next version of Recovery Workbench Test Cases, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID. The four legacy rows are kept: TC-E8-013-01 for AC1, TC-E8-013-02 for AC2, TC-E8-013-03 for the access refusal and TC-E8-013-04 for the forced record failure; two rows are added for the new criteria of this story. The legacy test table carries a Covers column and no Level column: `Access` is read as Component and `Principle 5` as NFR, and the Level of each row is this template's assignment under §R7.2 s16. No ITG story is split from this legacy key, so no `-ITG` copy of these test cases is written here and no `-ITG` id appears in this table.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the default and maximum sample size, the period bounds, the page bounds, the draw rule and the reason codes are parameter rows (BR6, BR10, BR11), and a test proves that a changed cap needs no build.
- No personal data anywhere: the request, the answer, the items and the entry carry ids, dates, rule ids, rule versions, verdicts, reason codes and counts; no name, no e-mail address and no case narrative appears in the answer, the entry or a test (BR9, NFR-040).
- No read of another service's tables (DP-01): `decision_log_entry`, `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` are P7's, and no join crosses a schema. The decision fields and the rule fields arrive in the P7 answer.
- No second opinion on a decision: the run never evaluates a package, never builds a KieBase and never rewrites a decision, so a FAIL is an observation and not a re-decision (BR5, BR14).
- No record without its answer: the entry, the stored items and the outbox row commit with the answer, and the answer is withheld with MSG-P7-003 when they cannot be written (BR8, R-UNI-39).
- One key, one run: the `Idempotency-Key` is stored with the answer, so a retry after a timeout cannot create a second run or a second entry (BR12).
- A run cannot be re-drawn: the items are stored with the run, so the same id answers the same items in the same order and a later rule promotion cannot change a past verdict (BR13).
- A run reads what it needs and no more: the decision query answers six fields per entry and the rule-model read one version at a time, so the sample never pulls a case narrative or a package source into this service.
- Every example, fixture and test payload is synthetic; no ledger entry, rule package or production payload is copied into a schema, a fake or a test.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E8-014 for rwb-access. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the pack check and return gate of `rwb-access`: an OpenAPI 3.1 document for the check and the read, the `PackCheck`, `PackRow`, `DefectItem`, `PackCheckAnswer` and `PackCheckSummary` schemas with the three check codes PC-ENT, PC-SCP and PC-MSK and the two verdicts, one RFC 9457 error envelope with its message IDs, the consumed authorise and parameters operations with their owners and the 2 s budget, the contract tables of section 12 and the four contract fakes**, so that **the app story, the SCR-39 route and the integration harness can build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1 without waiting for `rwb-access`, `rwb-case` or the matrix stories of this service to be built**.

This contract carries no legacy acceptance criterion: AC1 and AC2 of RWB-E8-014 belong to RWB-P4-E8014-APP, and the six criteria of section 7 test the document, the schemas and the check codes, the verdict set, the envelope, the consumed declarations and the fakes.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST and one hop with a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy story checked a pack inside a screen of the monolith, where the rows it read and the decision log it wrote were tables of one schema and no other consumer existed. In the target the rows are this service's and the record is a shared topic, and the screen is a route of the gateway that no longer shares a process with the check.

Two things must therefore be fixed once. The first is the vocabulary of a verdict: what a defect is, what a check code names, and which field of which table a rule reference points at — because the app story, the screen and the harness all have to agree on it, and a defect that is named differently in two places is a defect an owner cannot act on. The second is the boundary: the check answers a verdict and applies nothing, and the load of a matrix version stays with the administration stories of this service (BR9).

Fixing the field-level contract once, with faked consumers, lets the app story build in parallel with the parameters contract of `rwb-case` and the local decision-record library, and it catches a drift between a fake and the document in a contract test rather than in an integration window. The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_access`, REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1` for the service, the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.

The baseline also states the one thing it is not: it defines no matrix version, no masking profile, no role and no pack content. Those rows are other stories' of this service, and this document only names them in a rule reference.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the document, the base path and the topic follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) that calls the two operations behind SCR-39 Rules and parameters, and it is a consumer of this baseline.
- The rows the document names are described by TSD P4 v3 T3.1: `role` DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039, `permission` DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 (`capability_area` DF-REF-042, `letters` DF-REF-043, `matrix_version` DF-REF-044) and `masking_rule` DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204 (`role_code`, `field_id`, `unmasked`, `masking_version`). This document names those fields in a rule reference and defines none of them.
- The platform error envelope and the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope are the platform baseline; where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The verdict entry is a decision-record entry of the DP-03 library (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON); this document describes the fields the entry carries and no field of another service.
- The operations and their owners are taken from the ownership map only: the two operations of this document are P4's, the authorise operation is P4's and the parameters read is P3's. The three check codes and the two verdicts are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2288; ASM-3789) and are fixed here.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the check and the read with the shared components used across the `rwb-access` operations: the security scheme, the problem envelope, the paging parameters and the five schemas.
2. Fix the `PackCheck` request: `packVersion`, `ownerRole`, `capabilityArea` and `rows[]` of `PackRow`, with `rowType` one of `PERMISSION`, `SCOPE` and `MASKING`, `rowNo`, `roleCode` and the fields the row type carries — `capabilityArea` and `letters` for a permission row, `scope` for a scope row, `fieldId` and `unmasked` for a masking row.
3. Fix the `PackCheckAnswer`: `packCheckId`, `packVersion`, `ownerRole`, `capabilityArea`, `state`, `ruleVersion`, `defectCount`, `defects[]` of `DefectItem`, `decidedAt`, and the warning of a break-glass grant where one is active.
4. Fix the `DefectItem`: `checkCode` one of PC-ENT, PC-SCP and PC-MSK, `rowRef` with the row type, the row number and the role code, `field` and `ruleRef` — the reference of the row in force or of the parameter row the defect breaks — and no message ID, because a defect is not a catalogue message (GAP-2288; ASM-3789).
5. Fix the `PackCheckSummary` and the query of the read, with the page default and maximum held as parameter rows behind the contract.
6. Fix the verdict set: `ACCEPTED` and `RETURNED`, and state in the document that a check applies nothing, that a `RETURNED` pack is not stored as a version, and that a decided `packVersion` of an owner role is never decided twice.
7. Agree the error envelope and the message-ID mapping for 401, 403, 409, 422 and 503, with the business texts taken from the legacy story where the message already existed and MSG-GEN-002 and MSG-GEN-004 carried as message IDs only.
8. Declare the consumed own authorise operation and the `rwb-case` parameters read as consumed, each with its owner, one hop and the 2 s client budget, and declare that no matrix, masking, role or rule-package operation is provided or consumed here.
9. Publish the contract tables of section 12 (nine sub-tables) and the four contract fakes.
10. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the five schemas and their required fields, the three check codes and the two verdicts, the envelope and message IDs, the consumed declarations and drift detection between a fake and the document.
11. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P4-E8014-APP, the SCR-39 route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the harness of the wave 4 administration journey.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The document fails OpenAPI 3.1 validation | The pipeline fails and no baseline is tagged | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A declared operation names another service's base, path or owner, or declares a matrix, masking or role operation as provided here | The review refuses the document; the operation is declared as neither provided nor consumed | None | AC1, AC5 |
| X3 | A response of 401, 403, 409, 422 or 503 is declared without the envelope or without a message ID | The contract test fails | None | AC4 |
| X4 | A schema carries a name, an e-mail address or a user reference in a defect, a row or an answer | The contract test fails; the review refuses the document | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X5 | A check code outside PC-ENT, PC-SCP and PC-MSK, or a verdict outside `ACCEPTED` and `RETURNED`, is declared | The review refuses the document | None | AC3 |
| X6 | The document declares a matrix version, a masking profile or a role as written by the check, or declares a pack as stored | The review refuses the document | None | AC3, AC5 |
| X7 | A fake answers a path, a status or a payload the document does not declare | The drift test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X8 | A consumed operation is declared without an owner, without the one-hop rule or without the 2 s budget | The contract test fails | None | AC5 |
| X9 | A field of the answer has no source definition | The field is marked with the placeholder and the gap is carried | None | AC2 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the ownership map, the platform envelopes, the TSD P4 field set and the P3 and P4 contracts only |
| Negotiable | The pack version label shape, the personal-area parameter and the page bounds are parameter rows behind the document; the base, the paths, the check codes and the envelope are fixed |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story, the SCR-39 route and the harness on Day 1, and fixes what a named defect is before two teams name it differently |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, one error envelope, nine contract tables, four fakes and six contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Return a defective pack contract baseline for rwb-access

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the access model is held by rwb-access and the pack check applies nothing

  Scenario: AC1 The OpenAPI 3.1 document describes the check and the read (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the pack check and return gate is published
    When it is validated against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares the base /api/recovery/access/v1
    Then it declares POST /admin/pack-checks and GET /admin/pack-checks with the owner rwb-access
    Then the check names Rules and parameters C, the read names Rules and parameters R, and both name their error responses 401, 403, 409, 422 and 503
    Then the check requires an Idempotency-Key and the read is a read that carries none
    Then no operation of another service is declared as provided by rwb-access

  Scenario: AC2 The five schemas are fixed and carry no person (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the PackCheck, PackRow, DefectItem, PackCheckAnswer and PackCheckSummary schemas of the document
    Then the request carries packVersion, ownerRole, capabilityArea and rows, all required, and each row carries rowType, rowNo and roleCode
    Then a PERMISSION row carries capabilityArea and letters, a SCOPE row carries scope, and a MASKING row carries fieldId and unmasked
    Then the answer carries packCheckId, packVersion, ownerRole, capabilityArea, state, ruleVersion, defectCount, defects, decidedAt
    Then a DefectItem carries checkCode, rowRef of row type, row number and role code, field and ruleRef, and no message ID
    Then the summary carries the same verdict fields and page, size and total
    Then no schema declares a name, an e-mail address or a user reference, and page and size are read from the parameters contract and never from code

  Scenario: AC3 The check codes and the verdict set are fixed and the check applies nothing (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the check codes and the verdict set of the document
    Then checkCode is one of PC-ENT, PC-SCP and PC-MSK
    Then state is one of ACCEPTED and RETURNED
    Then the three codes are defined in the document as: an entitlement defect, a scope defect and a masking-coverage defect
    Then the document states that a check writes no permission, role or masking_rule row and stores no pack
    Then the document states that a decided packVersion of an owner role answers 409 and is never decided twice
    Then the document names no capability area, no role code, no letter, no scope and no personal-area value
    Then no workflow and no Schedule is declared for the capability

  Scenario: AC4 Every failure is one envelope with one message (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error envelope component of the document
    When a 401, 403, 409, 422 or 503 response is produced by either operation
    Then the body is one RFC 9457 problem response carrying type, title, status, detail, instance, messageId and traceId
    Then 401 carries MSG-P4-001 and 403 carries MSG-P4-002
    Then 409 carries MSG-GEN-004, 422 carries MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-GEN-002, and 503 carries MSG-P7-003
    Then no operation declares a second error shape and no message ID outside this list is declared

  Scenario: AC5 The consumed operations are declared as consumed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the authorise operation and the parameters read this service calls
    Then POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise is declared as consumed with the owner P4 rwb-access
    Then GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters is declared as consumed with the owner P3 rwb-case
    Then each carries one hop and the 2 s client budget with a breaker
    Then no matrix, masking, reference-data, delegation, rule-package or case operation appears as provided or consumed
    Then no operation owned by rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-document or rwb-litigation is declared as provided by rwb-access

  Scenario: AC6 The fakes match the document and carry no personal data (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the four contract fakes of the baseline
    When they are run against the document
    Then every fake answers only paths, statuses and payloads the document declares
    Then a fake that drifts from the document fails the build
    Then the decision-record fake answers an appended verdict, a replayed key and a forced failure
    Then no schema, example or fake carries a name, an e-mail address or a user reference
```

These six criteria test the artefact only. No criterion restates a legacy acceptance criterion; AC1 and AC2 of RWB-E8-014 belong to RWB-P4-E8014-APP.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/access/v1`; a document never declares another service's path | DP-13; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | A consumed operation is described as consumed, never as provided; its owner comes from the ownership map | DP-11; Ownership Map v1 |
| BR3 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; the business texts are taken from the legacy story where the message already existed | Architecture v5 slide 11; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR4 | The schemas carry the fields of this gate and no field of another service: no case, no document, no rule package and no delegation limit | DP-01; Ownership Map v1 |
| BR5 | A defect names a check code, a row, a field and the rule it breaks, and never a person and never a message | RWB-E8-014 AC1; ASM-3789 |
| BR6 | The verdict set is `ACCEPTED` and `RETURNED`; a check applies nothing and stores no pack | FSD P4 v3 A2.25; ASM-3789 |
| BR7 | A decided pack version of an owner role is never decided twice; the repeat is a 409 and the corrected pack is a new version | ASM-3789 |
| BR8 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a removed, renamed or retyped field is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 |
| BR9 | A write requires an `Idempotency-Key`; a replay answers the first answer and appends no second entry | Architecture v5 slide 42; DP-09 |
| BR10 | The contract declares no workflow, no activity and no Schedule for the capability | Architecture v5 slide 14; TSD P4 v3 T5.3 |
| BR11 | The role codes, capability areas, letters and scopes a row names are values of the model tables and left to the app story; this document declares their shape and no value | TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and T3.2; ASM-3791 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The two operations, the five schemas, the three check codes and the consumed operations are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, the SCR-39 route and the harness accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A field is added within major version 1 | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A field is removed, renamed or retyped, or a check code or a verdict is removed | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A consumed operation changes | The parameters read or the authorise answer changes | Baselined, with the client budget and the stub restated |

The verdict set the document fixes is `ACCEPTED` and `RETURNED`, written once per pack version. The lifecycle of a pack before its check and the lifecycle of a matrix version after it — including the load, the approval and the rollback — are other stories' of this service and are not declared here.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-access | Owns the document, the five schemas, the check codes and the fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change and a new major version |
| Security administrator | Reviews the two rights, the three check codes and the verdict set as the owner of the matrix |
| Compliance and PDPA officer | Reviews the masking-coverage check code and the absence of a person in a defect |
| Tech lead of rwb-case (P3) | Reviews the parameters read as `rwb-access` uses it; owns its definition |
| Internal audit | Reviews the verdict fields, the rule version and the stable order of the read |
| Data steward | Confirms that no name, e-mail address or user reference is declared in a schema, an example or a fake |

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| `PackCheck` request | `packVersion` (a label of the shape in force), `ownerRole` (a role code), `capabilityArea` (an area code of the matrix), `rows[]` of `PackRow`; all required |
| `PackRow` | `rowType` (`PERMISSION`, `SCOPE` or `MASKING`), `rowNo` (a whole number), `roleCode`; and `capabilityArea` and `letters` for a permission row, `scope` for a scope row, `fieldId` and `unmasked` for a masking row |
| `DefectItem` | `checkCode` (`PC-ENT`, `PC-SCP` or `PC-MSK`), `rowRef` of row type, row number and role code, `field`, `ruleRef` |
| `PackCheckAnswer` | `packCheckId`, `packVersion`, `ownerRole`, `capabilityArea`, `state` (`ACCEPTED` or `RETURNED`), `ruleVersion`, `defectCount`, `defects[]`, `decidedAt` |
| `PackCheckSummary` | `items[]` of the verdict fields above with `defects[]`, `page`, `size`, `total` |
| Rows as consumed by a rule reference | `role` DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039, `permission` DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044, `masking_rule` DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204 |
| Record event | `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` with the entry of a verdict, from the DP-03 library |
| Refusal | `messageId` MSG-P4-001 on a 401, MSG-P4-002 on a 403, MSG-GEN-004 on a 409, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-GEN-002 on a 422 and MSG-P7-003 on a 503 |

The exact field set of `ruleRef`, the shape of the pack version label, the three check codes and the record code of a verdict are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2288; ASM-3789): FSD P4 v3 A2.25 names the intent and two rules (VR-P4-025-1, BR-P4-025) and no operation and no field, the legacy story names the rule-version endpoints of other keys, and TSD P4 v3 T-A declares no pack operation. The personal capability areas the masking-coverage check needs are a parameter row and are named in no source either (GAP-2288; ASM-3791): the document declares the parameter and not its value.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-access (P4); base `/api/recovery/access/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/admin/pack-checks` | `PackCheck` in; `PackCheckAnswer` out in state `ACCEPTED` or `RETURNED` with `packCheckId`, `ruleVersion`, `defectCount`, `defects` and the `Location` of the read | Rules and parameters C; `Idempotency-Key` required |
| GET | `/admin/pack-checks` | `PackCheckSummary` out: `items` of one owner role with `packVersion`, `capabilityArea`, `state`, `ruleVersion`, `decidedAt`, `defectCount` and `defects`, paged, filtered by `ownerRole` and `state` | Rules and parameters R, scope applied |

Errors for both: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001), 403 no right (MSG-P4-002), 409 the pack version of the owner role is already decided (MSG-GEN-004), 422 a required field empty, a label of the wrong shape or `rows` above the pack row limit (MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002), 503 the parameters read fails or the verdict entry cannot be written (MSG-P7-003). The check is a write of a verdict and not of a row of the model, so every request carries an `Idempotency-Key` and a replay answers the first answer with no second entry (BR9); the read carries none. Major version 1 sits in the path; an additive field within version 1 is a compatible change, and a removed, renamed or retyped field is a new major version tested against the registry with BACKWARD compatibility (BR8).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11).

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The C check behind the submit and the R check behind the read, cached for the session |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | The personal capability areas, the pack row limit, the page bounds and the check rule-set label, with the version in force (DP-06) |

Neither is declared as provided by rwb-access. No matrix, masking, reference-data, delegation, rule-package or case operation appears in this document as provided or consumed.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library; consumed by P7 | The entry of a verdict with its pack version, owner role, capability area, verdict, rule version and defect list, with its `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`, in the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope |

This document declares the record message only. `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` is RWB-P4-E1037-APP's and `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` is RWB-P4-E8008-APP's, and a pack check publishes neither: a check changes no row of the model, so there is nothing for the service to announce.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `rwb-access` is a reference-data owner in Architecture v5 slide 14, and the two operations of this contract need no subscription. The document declares no inbox and no consumer group, and no case, document or rule-package event is consumed.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. No workflow, no activity and no signal is part of this contract: the check is synchronous and short, and the returned-packs list of the screen is not a workflow task (BR10).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. Both operations are request-driven, and the access review Schedule of `rwb-access` (JOB-18) belongs to RWB-P4-AD008-APP and not to this document.

| `role` | P4 (rwb_access) | The role code, class and default scope a rule reference names |
| `permission` | P4 (rwb_access) | The capability area, letters and `matrix_version` a rule reference names |
| `masking_rule` | P4 (rwb_access) | The masking profile a rule reference names |
| the local decision-record table of the DP-03 library | P4, in rwb_access | The verdict entry the record event carries and the list the read answers |

No table of another service is named in the contract (DP-01): `lov_value`, `reference_version` and `reference_row` are P3 rwb_case's; `delegation_limit` and `role_conflict` are this service's but belong to RWB-P4-AD016-APP and RWB-P4-AD005-APP and are named on no path of this document; `case`, `document` and `rule_package_version` are named nowhere (BR4).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the personal capability areas, the pack row limit and the page bounds stay parameter rows behind the document, and the role codes, capability areas, letters and scopes stay rows of the model tables (BR11).
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: role codes, row references, check codes, field ids, labels and times only, and no user reference in any answer (BR5).
- The contract names only `rwb-access` tables and only operations owned by `rwb-access`; a case, a document, a rule package and the delegation table are absent, never named as this service's (BR4).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic fails the review (DP-13).
- A check applies nothing: the document states that no permission, role or masking row is written and that no pack is stored (BR6).
- A decided pack version is never decided twice, and the repeat is a declared 409 rather than an undeclared second verdict (BR7).
- Every example in the document is synthetic; no matrix version, no pack and no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope and the CloudEvents envelope come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.
- A write without its `Idempotency-Key` is refused by the contract, and a replay never appends a second entry.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer whose role owns a pack**, I want **every candidate access pack to be checked before it is released, and a pack that fails to be sent back to the role that owns it with each defect named — the row, the field and the rule it breaks — and the verdict recorded against the pack version and the rule version in force**, so that **an access change that would break the matrix, the scope or the masking is corrected by its owner before it can reach the service, and a code release is not needed to change a role, a letter or a masking profile**.

Inside `rwb-access` this is the pack check and return gate of the legacy story RWB-E8-014:

- Service `rwb-access`, schema `rwb_access`, REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.
- A **pack** is a candidate version of this service's own access model: an ordered set of `PERMISSION`, `SCOPE` and `MASKING` rows that a centre of excellence analyst prepares for a role set, with its `packVersion`, its `ownerRole` and the `capabilityArea` it covers. It is a document of rows, not a file and not a set of documents.
- Two deliverables: the write `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/pack-checks`, which authorises, checks every row, decides the verdict and records it; and the read `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/pack-checks`, which answers the checks of one owner role with their verdicts and defect lists.
- The checks are this service's, because the rows they read are its own: `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule` (DP-01). No row of another service is read, and the pack's own content is nothing but rows of these three tables.
- The verdict is one of `ACCEPTED` and `RETURNED`. A `RETURNED` pack is not applied, is not stored as a version, and is answered with its defect list; the owner role corrects it and submits a new `packVersion`. The load and the approval of the version that follows are the matrix and reference-data stories of this service, and are not part of this one.
- The result is recorded as one entry of the local decision-record chain of the DP-03 library, in the transaction that answers the verdict, with the pack version, the owner role, the capability area, the verdict, the rule version in force and the defect list (AC1, AC2).
- The screen is SCR-39 Rules and parameters through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19, which shows the returned packs of the caller's owner role and their defects; this story renders no screen of its own.
- This story starts no workflow, owns no Schedule and publishes no message on `rwb.access.events.v1`: the check is request-driven, and the only message it produces is `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on the shared decision-record topic.
- The separation-of-duty check at sign-in (RWB-P4-AD005-APP), the load of a permission matrix version (RWB-P4-AD002-APP), the scope table (RWB-P4-AD003-APP), the masking profile load (RWB-P4-AD004-APP) and the delegation of authority table (RWB-P4-AD016-APP) are other stories of this service; this story reads their rows and writes none of them.

##### 2. Business rationale

REQ-ACA-003 makes the role to permission matrix the only source of what a role may see and do, REQ-ACA-005 requires personal data to be masked by role on every screen, REQ-ACA-007 requires access requested outside the authority matrix to be refused **and the refusal recorded**, and REQ-ACA-009 requires a user to see only what the role and scope allow. All four are Must and all four are E1. The legacy story carried them as one administration journey (FEAT-ADM-09, RWB-E8-014): the pack, the check and the decision log were rows of one schema and the check was a step of a screen.

The target splits the act in two. The owner of an access change prepares a pack; the service that owns the matrix checks it and either accepts it or returns it with the defects named. Nothing is applied by the check, and nothing is applied without it. That is what makes REQ-ACA-007 provable: a refusal is a recorded verdict with a defect list, not a message on a screen, and the record names the rule version it was decided under.

The gate exists because the three ways an access pack goes wrong are all silent if nobody looks. A row that names a capability area the matrix does not hold quietly widens the authority of a role. A row that names a role twice quietly leaves two scopes in force for one role. A `PERMISSION` row that gives a role access to a personal area with no masking row quietly exports personal data to a screen that has no profile. Each is cheap to detect at submission and expensive to detect in production, and each is detectable only where the rows live — here.

Fixing the verdict and its defect list once, in a published contract and a faked consumer set, is what lets the screen story, the gateway route and the matrix work build in parallel, and lets a drift between the fake and the document fail a build rather than an integration window.

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| RWB-P4-E8014-CON (same service, its own contract story) | The OpenAPI 3.1 document of the two operations, the `PackCheck`, `PackRow`, `DefectItem`, `PackCheckAnswer` and `PackCheckSummary` schemas, the three check codes, the verdict set, the error envelope, the consumed-operation list and the contract fakes. This story implements that document and adds no path |
| RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03): the entry of a verdict, hash-linked, written in the transaction that answers it |
| RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The parameters client library and the `rwb-case` parameters contract (DP-06): the personal capability areas of PC-MSK, the pack row limit and the page bounds, as rows and not as code |
| RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) that serves SCR-39 and calls the two operations, one hop each |
| The `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule` rows of the service | Created and loaded by RWB-P4-AD002-APP, RWB-P4-AD003-APP and RWB-P4-AD004-APP; this story reads them and writes none of them |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E8-014, from the feature specification and from the technical specification:

- The rights in force are those of TSD P4 v3 T6.1: RW-COE holds `CRUD` in Rules and parameters, RW-LITOFF holds `R`, RW-PHONECOL holds a dash, RW-AUDIT holds `R` and RW-SECADM holds `R`. The submit authorises Rules and parameters C; the read authorises Rules and parameters R (BR3).
- The FSD P4 v3 A2.25.3.3 role table names the litigation officer as a user of the feature and the check itself as unattended; in the target the pack is submitted by the role that prepares it and read by the role that owns it, and the difference is carried as a conflict row of the key (GAP-2290; ASM-3792).
- The three letters of the permission model are those of TSD P4 v3 T3.1 `permission.letters` (DF-REF-043, `varchar(5)`): C, R, U, D and A. A row that names a letter outside that set is a defect of PC-ENT.
- A role's default scope is TSD P4 v3 T3.1 `role.default_scope` (DF-REF-038, list LOV-SCOPE: OWN, TEAM, REGION, ALL) and its class is DF-REF-037. The role code and the scope are read; neither the role nor the scope is changed here.
- The masking profile of a role and field is a `masking_rule` row, DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204, with `unmasked` and `masking_version`. A `PERMISSION` row for a personal capability area of a role that holds no masking row in the pack is a defect of PC-MSK.
- The personal capability areas, the pack row limit and the page bounds are parameter rows of `rwb-case` read through DP-06 with the version in force; no value is a constant in code (BR-P4-025, BR10). Their names and their values are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2288; ASM-3791).
- The rule version a verdict is recorded under is the version label the parameters contract answers plus the `matrix_version` of the `permission` rows in force (DF-REF-044), read at the moment of the check (BR8).

##### 4. Flow

1. The owner role opens SCR-39 Rules and parameters through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which shows the packs of that owner role in state `RETURNED` with their defect lists and calls this service for the read.
2. The centre of excellence analyst prepares a pack and submits it for check: `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/pack-checks` with `packVersion`, `ownerRole`, `capabilityArea`, `rows[]` of `PERMISSION`, `SCOPE` and `MASKING` rows, and an `Idempotency-Key` header.
3. `PackCheckController` validates the request: every field is required; `packVersion` matches the label shape in force; `ownerRole` is an existing `role.role_code`; `rows` is not empty and not above the pack row limit. An empty field or a value outside its range is refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-001 or MSG-GEN-002 naming the field, and no row is checked and nothing is recorded (BR11).
4. The controller looks the `Idempotency-Key` up in the idempotency table of the platform library in `rwb_access`. A key already answered replays that first answer and checks nothing and records nothing (BR12, AC6).
5. The controller calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` on its own service, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a cached answer, for Rules and parameters C. A caller without the C letter is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002, and no row is read and nothing is recorded (BR3, AC3).
6. `RuleVersionReader` reads the parameters contract for the personal capability areas, the pack row limit and the page bounds, and takes the `matrix_version` of the `permission` rows in force; the pair is the rule version the verdict is recorded under (BR8).
7. `PackChecker` runs the three checks over every row, in the fixed order PC-ENT, PC-SCP, PC-MSK, and does not stop at the first defect:
   - PC-ENT: the row names a `role_code` of `role` and a `capability_area` that the `permission` rows in force hold; a letter outside C, R, U, D and A, or an area the matrix does not hold, is a defect (BR4, REQ-ACA-003, REQ-ACA-007).
   - PC-SCP: the pack holds at most one `SCOPE` row per role, and every scope row names a role of `role`; a second row for one role, or a role that does not exist, is a defect (BR5, REQ-ACA-009).
   - PC-MSK: every `PERMISSION` row for a capability area named in the personal-area parameter row has at least one `MASKING` row for the same role in the pack; a personal area with no masking row for that role is a defect (BR6, REQ-ACA-005).
8. Each failing row appends one `DefectItem` with its `checkCode`, its `rowRef` (row type, row number and role code), its `field` and its `ruleRef` (the row in force or the parameter row the defect breaks), in the order the checks run and then in the order of the rows (BR7, AC5).
9. `PackCheckService` decides the verdict: no defect is `ACCEPTED`; one defect or more is `RETURNED`. A returned pack is not applied, no version is written to `permission`, `role` or `masking_rule`, and the pack itself is not stored as a row (BR9, AC1, AC4).
10. In one local transaction the service appends one entry to the decision-record chain of DP-03 with the record code of a pack check, the pack version, the owner role, the capability area, the verdict, the rule version, the defect count and the defect list; writes the idempotency row; and stages the outbox row of the entry (BR8, BR10, BR12).
11. The answer is 201 with `packCheckId`, `packVersion`, `ownerRole`, `capabilityArea`, `state`, `ruleVersion`, `defectCount`, `defects[]`, `decidedAt` and the `Location` of the read (BR1).
12. Where the entry, the idempotency row or the outbox row cannot be written, the verdict is withheld with 503 and MSG-P7-003: nothing is answered, nothing is applied and the pack stays undecided, so a check that cannot be recorded is not a check (BR10, AC2).
13. Where the same `packVersion` of the same owner role has already been decided, the call answers 409 with MSG-GEN-004 and no second entry; the owner corrects the pack and submits a new `packVersion`, which is a new check and leaves the earlier verdict in the chain (BR13, AC7).
14. `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/pack-checks?ownerRole=&state=&page=&size=` answers the checks of one owner role with their `packVersion`, `capabilityArea`, `state`, `ruleVersion`, `decidedAt`, `defectCount` and `defects[]`, newest first and then by entry id, with the page bounds read through DP-06; an owner role with no check answers 200 with an empty `items` and total 0, never a 404 (BR14).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A required field is empty, or `rows` is empty | 422 naming the field; no row checked, no entry | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | `packVersion` does not match the label shape in force | 422 naming `packVersion`; no row checked, no entry | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X3 | `rows` exceeds the pack row limit of the parameter row in force | 422 naming `rows` with its bounds; no row checked, no entry | MSG-GEN-002 | AC1 |
| X4 | The caller holds no Rules and parameters C | 403; no row read, no verdict, no entry | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X5 | The caller's session has ended | 401; no row read, no verdict, no entry | MSG-P4-001 | AC3 |
| X6 | The same `packVersion` of the same owner role is already decided | 409 and no second entry; the earlier verdict stands | MSG-GEN-004 | AC7 |
| X7 | The parameters contract does not answer inside 2 s | 503 and no verdict; a check without the rule version in force is not decided | MSG-P7-003 | AC4 |
| X8 | The decision-record entry, the idempotency row or the outbox row cannot be written | 503 and no verdict; nothing is applied and the pack stays undecided | MSG-P7-003 | AC2 |
| X9 | The same request arrives twice with the same `Idempotency-Key` | The first answer is replayed; one entry, no second check | None | AC6 |
| X10 | A break-glass grant is active for the caller | The check proceeds and the answer carries the warning with the end time of the grant; the entry carries the grant id | MSG-P4-004 | AC3 |
| X11 | A row names a role code that no `role` row holds | One `DefectItem` with check code PC-ENT, the row and the field; the verdict is `RETURNED` | None | AC5 |

No exception path of this story writes a `role`, a `permission`, a `masking_rule` or a `delegation_limit` row, and none changes a case, a task or a pack's content: the only row this story writes of its own is the entry of its own chain plus the platform library rows of the request.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P4-E8014-CON and its fakes; reads only its own three tables and one parameter read, so no other service blocks it |
| Negotiable | The personal-area parameter, the pack row limit, the page bounds and the label shape are rows; the three check codes and the verdict set are fixed by the target architecture and reviewed with the security administrator |
| Valuable | A pack that would break the matrix, the scope or the masking is returned with its defects named, and the refusal is recorded with the rule version — REQ-ACA-003, 005, 007 and 009 |
| Estimable | One controller, one checker, one rule-version reader, one query service, one record appender, one idempotency store, four fakes and nine test cases |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests; no new table, no workflow, no Schedule, no screen and no event of its own |
| Testable | Each criterion has a test case in section 16; a defect list is provable against a seeded pack, and the record-before-answer rule is provable with a forced failure |
