AC1 and AC2 are the two criteria of RWB-E8-014, copied with their text unchanged and their values kept: "the data and the rule version this feature needs", "its trigger arrives" and "the defects named" read in this story as the pack check and its defect list. AC1 carries one added line at the top of its scenario, the parameters mock, so the rule version is provable while `rwb-case` is still a fake. AC3 to AC7 are new under D-RCV-60 and test only what this story adds: the right, an accepted pack, the complete defect list, the record and the replay, and the version rule.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One verdict per pack version: `ACCEPTED` when no row fails a check, `RETURNED` when one row or more does, and the answer names the pack version, the owner role, the capability area and the rule version | RWB-E8-014 AC1; FSD P4 v3 A2.25; ASM-3789 |
| BR2 | The pack is checked against this service's own rows only: `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule`; no row of another service is read and the pack's content is stored nowhere | DP-01; Ownership Map v1; REQ-ACA-003 |
| BR3 | The submit needs Rules and parameters C and the read needs Rules and parameters R; a caller without the letter is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002 and nothing is read and nothing is recorded | TSD P4 v3 T6.1; legacy RWB-E8-014 permission checks |
| BR4 | PC-ENT: every `PERMISSION` row names a role of `role`, a capability area the `permission` rows in force hold, and letters drawn from C, R, U, D and A; anything else is a defect and is refused rather than applied | REQ-ACA-003, REQ-ACA-007; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-042 and DF-REF-043 |
| BR5 | PC-SCP: the pack holds at most one `SCOPE` row per role and every scope row names a role of `role`; a duplicate row for one role or an unknown role is a defect | REQ-ACA-009; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-038; ASM-3790 |
| BR6 | PC-MSK: a `PERMISSION` row for a capability area named in the personal-area parameter row needs at least one `MASKING` row for the same role in the pack; a personal area with no masking row is a defect | REQ-ACA-005; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204; ASM-3791 |
| BR7 | The defect list is complete and ordered: one item per failing row and check with its check code, its row reference, its field and the rule it breaks; the checker never stops at the first defect | FSD P4 v3 A2.25.2; RWB-E8-014 AC1 |
| BR8 | The verdict is recorded in one entry of the local chain with the pack version, the owner role, the capability area, the verdict, the rule version in force, the defect count and the defect list | RWB-E8-014 AC1; R-UNI-39; DP-03 |
| BR9 | A check applies nothing: no `permission`, `role` or `masking_rule` row is written, and a returned pack is not a version of the matrix | FSD P4 v3 A2.25; ASM-3789 |
| BR10 | An answer that cannot be recorded is withheld with 503 and MSG-P7-003, so no verdict exists without its record | RWB-E8-014 AC2; DP-03 |
| BR11 | The pack version label, the personal areas, the pack row limit and the page bounds are parameter rows read through DP-06 with the version in force; no value is a constant in code | BR-P4-025; DP-06; ASM-3791 |
| BR12 | One `Idempotency-Key` answers one check: a replay answers the first answer, appends no second entry and checks nothing again | Architecture v5 slide 42; DP-09 |
| BR13 | A decided `packVersion` of an owner role is never decided twice: a repeat answers 409 with MSG-GEN-004, and a corrected pack is submitted under a new version whose verdict sits beside the earlier one | RWB-E8-014 AC1; ASM-3789 |
| BR14 | The read answers the checks of one owner role, newest first and then by entry id, and an owner role with no check answers an empty list with total 0; it never answers a 404 | DP-03; ASM-3794 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-access`:

- BR1, BR4, BR5 and BR6 are one ordered pass in `PackChecker`: entitlement, scope, masking, over every row, collecting defects instead of returning at the first one.
- BR2 is the absence of a repository for anything else: the module has no table, view or join for a case, a document, a rule package or a delegation limit, and the pack's rows are the three tables it reads.
- BR3 is the authorise call of the service's own contract, cached for the session; the read is filtered by the owner role the caller may see.
- BR7 and BR8 are one payload: the defect list is part of the entry, so the read is a projection of the chain and not a second store.
- BR9 is a rule about what is missing: the service has no write method on `permission`, `role` or `masking_rule`, so a check cannot apply even by mistake.
- BR10 is the transaction order: entry, idempotency row and outbox row commit together, and a failure rolls all three back.
- BR11 is the parameter reader at request time; a changed limit or a changed personal area is data and needs no build.
- BR12 and BR13 are the `idempotency_key` row of the platform library and the decided-version lookup in front of the checker.
- BR14 is the read: it filters by the owner role, orders on `decidedAt` then entry id, and has no 404 branch.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| No check | A pack is submitted | C held, the pack is valid, no row fails a check | `ACCEPTED`, one entry, answer 201 |
| No check | A pack is submitted | C held, the pack is valid, one row or more fails | `RETURNED`, one entry with the defect list, answer 201 |
| No check | A pack is submitted | No C letter | Refused 403 with MSG-P4-002; nothing read, no entry |
| No check | A pack is submitted | The session has ended | Refused 401 with MSG-P4-001; no entry |
| No check | A pack is submitted | A field is empty, outside its range, or `rows` is above the limit | Refused 422 with MSG-GEN-001 or MSG-GEN-002; no check, no entry |
| No check | A pack is submitted | The parameters contract does not answer | Refused 503 with MSG-P7-003; no verdict |
| No check | A pack is submitted | The entry cannot be written | Refused 503 with MSG-P7-003; nothing answered, nothing applied |
| `RETURNED` | The owner submits a corrected pack | A new `packVersion` for the same owner role | A new check, `ACCEPTED` or `RETURNED`; the earlier entry stays |
| `RETURNED` or `ACCEPTED` | The same `packVersion` is submitted again | None | Refused 409 with MSG-GEN-004; one verdict per version |
| `RETURNED` or `ACCEPTED` | The same request is sent again with its key | The key is stored | The first answer is replayed; no second entry |

| Chain | Event | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Append-only local chain of DP-03 | A check is decided | One entry appended with the pack version, the verdict, the rule version and the defect list, with its `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`; no entry is updated or deleted |
| `permission`, `role`, `masking_rule` | A check is decided | No change: the check applies nothing (BR9) |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Center of excellence analyst (RW-COE, `CRUD` in Rules and parameters) | Submit a pack for check with Rules and parameters C; receives the verdict and the defect list (TSD P4 v3 T6.1) |
| Litigation officer (RW-LITOFF, `R` in Rules and parameters) | The owner role a pack is returned to: reads the returned packs and their defects with Rules and parameters R |
| Internal audit (RW-AUDIT, `R`) | Reads the verdicts of the owner roles in scope; checks nothing and applies nothing |
| Security administrator (RW-SECADM, `R`) | Reads the verdicts and the defect lists; the load and approval of a matrix version are other stories of this service |
| A role with a dash in Rules and parameters (RW-PHONECOL) | Refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002; nothing is read and nothing is recorded |
| The gateway-bff route | Calls the two operations on behalf of the signed-in user, one hop each, and passes the `Idempotency-Key` unchanged |
| `rwb-access` itself | Reads `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule` in its own schema and writes only its own chain and the platform library rows of the request |
| `rwb-case` (P3) | Owns the parameters and reference data under the default ruling; answers the one parameters read of DP-06 |
| `rwb-decision` (P7) | Owns the central ledger; this story calls it not at all |

The refusal shapes are 403 with an RFC 9457 problem response and `messageId` MSG-P4-002 for an absent right, 401 with MSG-P4-001 for no session, 409 with MSG-GEN-004 for a decided pack version, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 or MSG-GEN-002 for a pack that cannot be read, and 503 with MSG-P7-003 for a parameters read or a record that cannot be completed. The database login is the per-service login of the service baseline (DP-02), which belongs to RWB-P4-E8014-CON.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Table in `rwb_access` | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039 | `role` | `id`, `role_code`, `role_name`, `role_class`, `default_scope`, `entra_group` | Read: the role code of every row, its class and its default scope |
| DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 | `permission` | `id`, `role_id`, `capability_area`, `letters`, `matrix_version` | Read: the areas and letters in force and the `matrix_version` of the verdict |
| DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204 | `masking_rule` | `id`, `role_code`, `field_id`, `unmasked`, `masking_version`, `valid_from`, `valid_to` | Read: the masking profile in force per role and field |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local library, DP-03) | the verdict entry: `decision_code` DF-DEC-003, `case_id` DF-DEC-002 empty, `inputs_ref` DF-DEC-008 with the pack version, the owner role, the capability area, the verdict, the rule version and the defect list, `decided_at` DF-DEC-016, `prev_hash` DF-DEC-017 and `entry_hash` DF-DEC-018 | Write; and read for the list |
| (idempotency) | `idempotency_key` (platform library table in `rwb_access`) | the request and the stored answer of a check | Write and read (DP-09; ASM-0074) |
| (outbox) | `outbox_event` | the record row of the verdict entry | Write |
| (inbox) | `processed_event` | none: this story consumes no event | None |
| DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026, DF-REF-055 to DF-REF-062 | `delegation_limit` | none | Not read: the delegation table is RWB-P4-AD016-APP's |
| DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211 | `role_conflict` | none | Not read: the sign-in conflict check is RWB-P4-AD005-APP's |

No row of another service is read: a pack names no case, no document and no rule package, and the parameters the check needs arrive in the one contract answer of section 12.2 (DP-01). The name and the shape of the pack version label, the personal capability areas and the pack row limit are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2288; ASM-3791): they are parameter rows, their names are fixed by RWB-P4-E8014-CON, and the check fails closed without them (BR11).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Path | Owner | Request | Response | Errors | Authorization | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/pack-checks` | P4 `rwb-access` | Body: `packVersion`, `ownerRole`, `capabilityArea`, `rows` of `rowType`, `rowNo`, `roleCode`, `capabilityArea`, `letters`, `scope`, `fieldId`, `unmasked` | `packCheckId`, `packVersion`, `ownerRole`, `capabilityArea`, `state` `ACCEPTED` or `RETURNED`, `ruleVersion`, `defectCount`, `defects` of `checkCode`, `rowRef`, `field`, `ruleRef`, `decidedAt`, with `Location` of the read | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 (MSG-P4-002); 409 (MSG-GEN-004); 422 (MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002); 503 (MSG-P7-003) | Rules and parameters C | `Idempotency-Key` required; a replay answers the first answer and appends no second entry |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/pack-checks` | P4 `rwb-access` | Query: `ownerRole`, `state`, `page`, `size` | `PackCheckSummary`: `items` of `packCheckId`, `packVersion`, `capabilityArea`, `state`, `ruleVersion`, `decidedAt`, `defectCount`, `defects`, and `page`, `size`, `total` | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 (MSG-P4-002); 422 (MSG-GEN-001); 503 (MSG-P7-003) | Rules and parameters R, filtered by the owner role the caller may see | Not applicable, read only |

Both operations sit on the base `/api/recovery/access/v1` of DP-13. `page` defaults to the value of its parameter row and `size` is capped by it, both read through DP-06 and never from code (BR11).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 `rwb-access` (own service) | The Rules and parameters C check behind the submit and the R check behind the read, cached for the session; MSG-P4-002 on a refusal |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 `rwb-case` | The personal capability areas of PC-MSK, the pack row limit, the page bounds and the check rule-set label, with the version in force (DP-06) |

One hop per call, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11). No operation of `rwb-comms`, `rwb-decision`, `rwb-document`, `rwb-litigation` or `rwb-integration` is called by this story.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library; consumed by P7 | entryId | the hash-chained entry of a verdict: the pack version, the owner role, the capability area, the verdict, the rule version and the defect list |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, from the outbox of the transaction that answers the verdict. The payload carries codes, a version label and row references and no name, no e-mail address and no personal field. This story publishes no message on `rwb.access.events.v1`: the ownership row of `rwb-access` carries no event of its own for this capability, and the two events of the service named in Architecture v5 slide 14 belong to RWB-P4-E1037-APP and RWB-P4-E8008-APP.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The check is request-driven and reads its own rows and one parameters answer; no inbox row is written and no consumer group is declared.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The check is synchronous and short; it starts no workflow, signals none and registers no activity on the `rwb-access` queue. The raising of a task where a person is needed, which FSD P4 v3 A2.25.2 names, is the returned-packs list of the screen and not a workflow task (GAP-2289; ASM-3793).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The check runs when a pack is submitted; the six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) is the only Schedule of `rwb-access` and belongs to RWB-P4-AD008-APP.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Read only: the role code, the role class and the default scope of every row the pack names |
| `permission` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Read only: the capability areas and letters in force, and the `matrix_version` the verdict is recorded under |
| `masking_rule` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Read only: the masking profile in force per role and field |
| the local decision-record table of the DP-03 library | P4, in `rwb_access` | Write: the verdict entry. Read: the list of checks |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_access` | The outbox row of the entry and the idempotency row of the request; no inbox row, because no event is consumed (DP-09; ASM-0074) |
| `delegation_limit`, `role_conflict` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Not read: the delegation table is RWB-P4-AD016-APP's and the conflict table is RWB-P4-AD005-APP's |

No table of another service is named as this service's and none is created here (DP-01). `lov_value`, `reference_version` and `reference_row` are reference data of P3 under the ownership ruling; this story's pattern list carries no DP-07 and its contract-dependency list no `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`, so the check reads no list of values and the letter set of BR4 is the model constant of the `permission.letters` column, not a reference row (GAP-2288; ASM-3791).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| authorise fake | RWB-P4-E8014-CON, RWB-P4-E1037-CON | A granted answer for RW-COE with C and for RW-AUDIT and RW-LITOFF with R in Rules and parameters, and a refused answer with MSG-P4-002 for RW-PHONECOL with a dash |
| parameters fake | RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The personal capability areas, the pack row limit, the page bounds and the check rule-set label, with the version in force, and a 503 for X7 |
| decision-record fake | RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The append of a verdict, the hash-link check, a seeded chain of packs "AP-2027.03" and "AP-2027.06", the replay of a stored key and the forced failure AC2 needs |
| gateway-bff fake | RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The composite route of SCR-39 with the returned packs of the owner role, the pack form and the defect panel |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count in this story | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | Provided 2 (the check and the list); consumed 2 | Base `/api/recovery/access/v1`; the own authorise operation and the `rwb-case` parameters read, one hop and 2 s each |
| Kafka | Published 1 event type; consumed 0 | `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the DP-03 library |
| Temporal | 0 workflows, 0 activities | The `rwb-access` queue carries the access review Schedule of RWB-P4-AD008-APP only |
| File | None | A pack is a JSON body of rows; no file is uploaded and no file is produced |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`, module `access/packcheck`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.packcheck`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The legacy markers this slice replaces are the in-module check and the in-module decision-log write of the monolith (DP-03 and DP-13: the record on the shared topic and the operations on this service's own base), and the ace-web screen that checked a pack in process (DP-19: a gateway-bff composite route on SCR-39). DP-01, DP-02, DP-09 and DP-11 govern the service baseline and the one-hop budget of section 12.2; they add no dependency of their own and are not claimed as patterns of this story.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| PackCheckController | Controller | The two operations: validation, the `Idempotency-Key` lookup, the RFC 9457 problem responses, `Location` on a decided check |
| PackCheckService | Service | The verdict of BR1 and BR9, the answer and the record call of BR8; applies nothing |
| PackChecker | Service | The three checks of BR4, BR5 and BR6 over every row, collecting defects in the order of BR7 |
| RuleVersionReader | Service | The parameters read of DP-06 and the `matrix_version` of the rows in force; the rule version of BR8 |
| PackCheckQueryService | Service | The read of BR14: the checks of one owner role, the order, the paging and the empty answer |
| PackCheckRepository | Repository | Read-only queries over `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule` and the local chain; no write method on any of the three tables |
| PermissionReader | Service | The caller's letters from its own `permission` and `role` rows, and the authorise call |
| DecisionRecordAppender | Service | The verdict entry with its outbox row, in the transaction that answers the check (DP-03, DP-09) |
| IdempotencyStore | Service | The `Idempotency-Key` lookup and store of the platform library, written with the answer |

**Database and migrations**

- This story creates no table of its own. `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule` are created by RWB-P4-AD002-APP, RWB-P4-AD003-APP and RWB-P4-AD004-APP, the local decision-record table by RWB-P4-E1039-APP and the platform library tables by the service's own DB story, all in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15; this story reads them.
- No write statement touches `role`, `permission` or `masking_rule`, so a check can never apply itself even if the verdict is wrong (BR9).
- The entry, the idempotency row and the outbox row commit in one transaction; a failure rolls all three back and the verdict is withheld with MSG-P7-003 (BR10).

**Configuration and reference data**

- The personal capability areas, the pack row limit, the page default and maximum and the pack version label shape are parameter rows of `rwb-case` read through DP-06 with the version in force; no value is a constant in code (BR11). Their names are fixed by RWB-P4-E8014-CON.
- The letter set C, R, U, D and A is the domain of the `permission.letters` column and is a model constant of the contract, not a reference list of this service (section 12.7).
- The scope codes the pack may name are read from the matrix and not fixed here; the check of PC-SCP is the one-row-per-role rule and the role code, and no scope code is a constant of this story (BR5).

**Build steps**

1. `PackCheckController` and its validation; tests for X1, X2 and X3 with no row read.
2. `PermissionReader` and the authorise call; test the AC3 refusal of a caller with a dash, with no row read and an empty list afterwards.
3. `RuleVersionReader` over the parameters fake; test that a changed limit or area is data and needs no build, and the 503 of X7.
4. `PackChecker` and PC-ENT; tests for an unknown capability area, an unknown role code and a letter outside C, R, U, D and A.
5. `PackChecker` and PC-SCP and PC-MSK; tests for a duplicate scope row and for a personal area with no masking row, including the ordering of the defect list of AC5.
6. `DecisionRecordAppender` and `IdempotencyStore` in one transaction; tests for the replay of AC6 and the forced failure of AC2 with no verdict.
7. The decided-version lookup of BR13; tests for the 409 of AC7 and for the corrected version that leaves the earlier entry in place.
8. `PackCheckQueryService` over a seeded chain of packs "AP-2027.03" and "AP-2027.06"; tests for the order, the paging, the state filter and the empty answer of BR14.
9. The contract-fake run of both operations through the gateway-bff fake, so SCR-39 can be demonstrated while the route and the matrix stories are being built.

**Feature switch.** The two operations are switched by the service baseline of RWB-P4-E1037-CON, not by a flag of their own. A pack check that is switched off would let an unchecked pack be loaded by the matrix story, which is the state the gate exists to prevent, so this story adds no flag and removes nothing.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; a pack with a row outside the matrix, a duplicate scope row and a personal area with no masking row is answered `RETURNED` with four ordered defects and one entry that carries the rule version; a clean pack is answered `ACCEPTED` with no defect and writes no access row; a caller with a dash is refused with MSG-P4-002 and nothing is read; a forced record failure withholds the verdict with MSG-P7-003; the same key replays one answer with one entry; and a decided pack version is refused with MSG-GEN-004 while a corrected version is decided beside it.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The caller has no session | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | This story, on both operations |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller holds no Rules and parameters C on the submit, or no R on the read | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, on both operations |
| MSG-P4-004 | A break-glass grant is active for the caller | Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded. | This story, as a warning on the answer |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is empty, or `packVersion` is not of the shape in force | Enter {field}. | This story, on the submit and on the read query |
| MSG-GEN-002 | `rows` is above the pack row limit, or `size` is above the page maximum | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2291; ASM-3795) | This story, on the submit and on the read query |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The pack version of the owner role is already decided | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2291; ASM-3795) | This story, on the submit |
| MSG-P7-003 | The parameters read fails, or the verdict entry cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on the submit |

The message IDs are contract elements; the text is the agreed text taken from the legacy story where the message already existed. MSG-GEN-002 and MSG-GEN-004 carry an identifier and no text here, because no source read for this work package gives their wording; the message catalogue supplies it before the operations are frozen. The defect items of section 12.1 are not catalogue messages: each names a check code, a row, a field and the rule it breaks, and its wording is not specified either (GAP-2288; ASM-3789).

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | What the screen consumes |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Returned packs, list | The read of `state=RETURNED` for the caller's owner role, with the pack version and the defect count |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Returned pack, defects | The `defects` of one check: check code, row reference, field and rule |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Accepted pack, list | The read of `state=ACCEPTED`, with the verdict and the rule version |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Pack, form | `PackCheck` with `packVersion`, `ownerRole`, `capabilityArea` and the three row types |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Pack, refused | The 403 of the envelope with MSG-P4-002, the pack unchanged |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Pack, malformed | The 422 of the envelope with MSG-GEN-001 or MSG-GEN-002 naming the field |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Pack, already decided | The 409 of the envelope with MSG-GEN-004 and a reload action |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | Not recorded | The 503 of the envelope with MSG-P7-003 and a retry that reuses the same `Idempotency-Key` |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters | List, empty | An empty `items` with total 0 and no error |

The screens are served by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which shows the returned packs of the caller's owner role and calls the two operations of this story, one hop each. The route specification, the panel split and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the load, the approval and the rollback of a matrix version are the administration stories of this service and are not part of this document.

The legacy level System maps to Contract, Access to Component and Principle 5 to NFR. ##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the personal capability areas, the pack row limit, the page bounds and the version label shape stay parameter rows behind DP-06, and the role codes stay rows of `role` (BR11).
- No personal data: a pack row, a defect item, an entry and a log line carry role codes, capability areas, letters, scopes, field ids and references only — never a name, an e-mail address or a user reference (BR7, NFR-040).
- The service names only its own tables and only operations it owns; `lov_value`, `case`, `document`, `rule_package_version` and `delegation_limit` are named as other stories' and are never read here (BR2).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a change that names another service's base or topic fails the review (DP-13).
- A check applies nothing: there is no write method on `role`, `permission` or `masking_rule`, so a verdict can never become a change by accident (BR9).
- The verdict is written before it is answered, and an answer that cannot be recorded is withheld (BR10).
- Every example is synthetic; no pack, no matrix version and no production row is copied into a test, a fixture or a log.
- The error envelope and the CloudEvents envelope come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.
- A submit without its `Idempotency-Key` is refused, and a replay never decides a second time.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract slice of RWB-E8-015 for rwb-access: the chain-check document, its run and report schemas, the outcome set, the Schedule and workflow declarations and the five fakes. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the chain check of `rwb-access`: an OpenAPI 3.1 document for the on-demand run and the run report, the `ChainCheckRun` and `ChainCheckPage` schemas with their outcome set, the error envelope with its message IDs, the consumed authorise and parameters operations with their owners and their one-hop budget, the declared `chain-check-daily` Schedule, the declared `AccessChainCheckWorkflow` with its three activities, the declared `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` message, the contract tables of section 12 and the five contract fakes**, so that **the app story, the gateway-bff composite route and the audit harness can build against one fixed shape on Day 1 without waiting for the library, the parameters contract or the platform workflow kit to be finished**.

This contract carries no legacy acceptance criterion: AC1 and AC2 of RWB-E8-015 belong to RWB-P4-E8015-APP, and the six criteria of section 7 test the document, the schemas, the outcome set, the declared workflow and Schedule, the envelope, the consumed declarations and the fakes.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy story drew the chain check in process, inside the module that held the decision log; in the target the check belongs to the service that wrote the entries, and three other parties build against its answer at the same time: the app story that implements the walk, the composite route that shows the breach on SCR-43 Roles and access, and the harness that records the evidence for REQ-DRI-003 and NFR-035.

Without a fixed shape each of them would invent one. The route would read an outcome field the service does not answer, the harness would assert a count the app story does not compute, and the first disagreement would appear in an integration window instead of in a contract test. The baseline fixes the four things all of them need: what a run is (window, counts, outcome, first broken entry, trigger and time), what a breach is (outcome `BROKEN` with the first entry that failed), what a refusal is (one envelope with MSG-P4-002 or MSG-P7-003), and what the service does not answer at all (no case id, no person, no chain entry of another service).

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_access`, REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1` for the service and `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the record, task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`. Two of its elements are not ownership-map rows — the two paths and the Schedule name — and both are carried in GAP-2293 and GAP-2296 with ASM-3799 and ASM-3804.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the document, the base path, the topic and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) that consumes this answer on SCR-43 Roles and access and merges it with the access log of RWB-P4-AD007-APP, one hop each.
- The platform error envelope and the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope are the platform baseline; where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The run entry is an entry of the DP-03 library (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON); this document describes the entry as that library publishes it and adds no field.
- The owners of the consumed operations are taken from the ownership map: the authorise operation is P4 `rwb-access`'s own path, declared as consumed with the fake of RWB-P4-E1037-CON, and the parameters operation is P3 `rwb-case`'s under DP-06. The two chain-check paths are not ownership-map rows: no source names a chain-check endpoint, so this contract fixes them on the DP-13 base and the point is carried in GAP-2293 and ASM-3799. `GET /admin/roles` (API-P4-007), `GET /me/session` (API-P4-012) and `GET /admin/access-log` (API-P4-008) are other P4 stories' and are neither provided nor consumed here. No table of another service is named (DP-01).
- The workflow kit and the Schedule API are the platform's (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON); the document declares the Schedule and the workflow by name and adds no element of its own (GAP-2296; ASM-3804).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document with the shared components used across the `rwb-access` operations: the security scheme, the problem envelope and the version fields.
2. Fix the two operations on the base `/api/recovery/access/v1`: `POST /admin/chain-checks` with no body and a required `Idempotency-Key`, and `GET /admin/chain-checks` with `outcome`, `page` and `size`.
3. Fix the `ChainCheckRun` schema: `checkId`, `outcome`, `entriesChecked`, `verifiedThrough`, `firstBrokenEntryId`, `windowFrom`, `windowTo`, `trigger`, `checkedAt` and `entryId`, and the `ChainCheckPage` schema with its `items`, `checkpointEntryId`, `page`, `size` and `total`.
4. Fix the outcome set as a closed enumeration of `CLEAN` and `BROKEN`, and state that `firstBrokenEntryId` is present when and only when the outcome is `BROKEN`, and that `verifiedThrough` is the last entry that verified.
5. Declare the `chain-check-daily` Schedule on the `rwb-access` queue with its cadence as a parameter row, and declare `AccessChainCheckWorkflow` with its three activities and their inputs and outputs.
6. Declare the `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` message of a run on `rwb.decision-record.v1` with its key and its payload, and declare no `rwb.access.<Event>.v1` message.
7. Agree the error envelope and the message mapping for 401, 403, 422 and 503, with the business texts copied unchanged from the legacy story where the message already existed.
8. Declare the consumed authorise and parameters operations as consumed, each with its owner, one hop and the 2 s client budget.
9. Publish the contract tables of section 12 (nine sub-tables) and the five contract fakes, with the seeded chain fixture of any length and one variant with a broken link.
10. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the two schemas, the outcome set, the workflow and Schedule declarations, the message declaration, the envelope, the consumed declarations and drift detection between a fake and the document.
11. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P4-E8015-APP, the composite route work of RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the wave 4 audit journey harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The document fails OpenAPI 3.1 validation | The pipeline fails and no baseline is tagged | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A declared operation names another service's base, path or owner | The review refuses the document; the operation is declared as consumed instead | None | AC1, AC5 |
| X3 | A response of 401, 403, 422 or 503 is declared without the envelope or without a message ID | The contract test fails | None | AC4 |
| X4 | A run field is declared without a source in the library entry or in the run store | The contract test fails and the field is carried as a gap instead of a value | None | AC2 |
| X5 | The outcome set carries a third value, or `firstBrokenEntryId` is declared as always present | The contract test fails | None | AC2 |
| X6 | The document declares a Schedule or an activity the platform kit does not provide, or a cadence as a constant | The review refuses the document | None | AC3 |
| X7 | A fake answers a path, a status or a payload the document does not declare | The drift test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X8 | An example, a fake or a schema carries a name, an e-mail address, a case id or a personal field | The review and the pipeline refuse the document | None | AC6 |
| X9 | A consumed operation is declared without an owner, without the one-hop rule or without the 2 s budget | The contract test fails | None | AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the ownership map, the platform envelopes, the DP-03 entry schema and the P4 and P3 contracts only |
| Negotiable | The field names of the run row and the filter name are settled with the app story and the screen route; the base, the outcome set and the envelopes are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story, the composite route and the audit harness on Day 1, and keeps the central ledger and the chain of every other service out of this contract |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, two schemas, one outcome set, one Schedule declaration, one workflow declaration, one declared message, nine contract tables, five fakes and six contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

```gherkin

  Background:

    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares the base /api/recovery/access/v1
    Then it declares POST /admin/chain-checks and GET /admin/chain-checks with the owner rwb-access
    Then each operation names its security right, Platform administration R, and its error responses 401, 403 and 503, with 422 on the read

  Scenario: AC2 The run and report schemas and the outcome set are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
```

These six criteria test the artefact only. No criterion restates a legacy acceptance criterion; AC1 and AC2 of RWB-E8-015 belong to RWB-P4-E8015-APP.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/access/v1`; a document never declares another service's path | DP-13; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | A consumed operation is described as consumed, never as provided; its owner comes from the ownership map | DP-11; Ownership Map v1 |
| BR3 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; the business texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story | Architecture v5 slide 11; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR4 | The run entry is the decision-record entry of DP-03: the contract describes it and adds no field | DP-03; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| BR5 | The contract declares no table of another service and no central ledger; the chain of every other service and `decision_log_entry` are P7's | DP-01; ASM-3798 |
| BR6 | The outcome set is closed: `CLEAN` and `BROKEN`, with `firstBrokenEntryId` only on a breach and `verifiedThrough` the last entry that verified | RWB-E8-015 AC1; DP-03 |
| BR7 | The cadence, the start time, the batch size and the page bounds are parameter rows behind the contract, never values in the document or in code | DP-06; BR-P4-026 |
| BR8 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a removed, renamed or retyped field is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 |
| BR9 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: entry ids, counts, outcome codes, role codes, versions and times only | NFR-040 |

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Run row | `checkId`, `outcome` (`CLEAN` or `BROKEN`), `entriesChecked` (whole number), `verifiedThrough` (entry id), `firstBrokenEntryId` (entry id, on a breach), `windowFrom` and `windowTo` (entry ids), `trigger` (`SCHEDULED` or `ON_DEMAND`), `checkedAt` (timestamp), `entryId` (the decision-record entry of the run) |
| Report page | `items[]` of the run row, `checkpointEntryId`, `page`, `size`, `total` |
| Record entry | The decision-record entry of DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018: `decision_code` DF-DEC-003 with the library's chain-check code, `case_id` DF-DEC-002 empty, `inputs_ref` DF-DEC-008 with the run row, the parameter version and the library's algorithm version, `decided_at` DF-DEC-016, `prev_hash` DF-DEC-017 and `entry_hash` DF-DEC-018 |
| Refusal | `messageId` MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-GEN-001 or MSG-P7-003 with the detail text and the instance |

The record code of a chain check, the order and batch of the walk, the start time of the Schedule and the same-day channel to Compliance are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2294; ASM-3801); the schema of this contract fixes the run-row field names and the outcome set before the paths are frozen, and the app story reads and writes them as the document publishes them. The two paths themselves are not ownership-map rows (GAP-2293; ASM-3799).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-access (P4); base `/api/recovery/access/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/admin/chain-checks` | No body; `Idempotency-Key` required. Answer: the run row of section 11 with `trigger` `ON_DEMAND`, and the `Location` of the report | Platform administration R |
| GET | `/admin/chain-checks` | Query `outcome` (`CLEAN` or `BROKEN`), `page`, `size`. Answer: the report page of section 11 | Platform administration R, scope applied |

The full paths are `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/chain-checks` for both operations, on the base of DP-13. Errors: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001), 403 no right (MSG-P4-002), 422 a page bound (MSG-GEN-001, read only) and 503 the run cannot be recorded or a parameters row is missing (MSG-P7-003). The write answers 201 and never 202; the read carries no `Idempotency-Key` and the document states it so that no consumer sends the header. Major version 1 sits in the path; an additive field within version 1 is a compatible change, and a removed, renamed or retyped field is a new major version tested against the registry with BACKWARD compatibility (BR8).

The provided set of this document is two operations on one path. `GET /admin/roles` is API-P4-007 of RWB-P4-E1019-APP, `GET /me/session` is API-P4-012 and `GET /admin/access-log` is API-P4-008 of RWB-P4-AD007-APP; none of them appears as provided here, and the legacy `POST /admin/rule-versions` and its approve path are not declared at all because the rule registry is `rwb-decision`'s (GAP-2295).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11).

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The Platform administration R check behind both operations, cached for the session |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | The cadence, the start time, the batch size and the page bounds, with the version in force (DP-06) |

Neither is declared as provided by rwb-access, and no operation of `rwb-decision`, `rwb-comms` or `rwb-document` appears in the document at all: the central ledger and its chain check are P7's and the chain walked is this service's own.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library; consumed by P7 | The entry of a run with the window, the counts, the outcome, the first broken entry, the trigger, the parameter version and the algorithm version, with its `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`, in the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope |

This document declares the record message only. `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` belongs to RWB-P4-E1037-APP and `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` to RWB-P4-E8008-APP; neither is declared here, and the service publishes no other event of the chain check.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `rwb-access` subscribes to no topic for this capability: the run is started by its own Schedule or by its own request, and the document declares no subscription.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Element | Kind | Queue | Declared use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AccessChainCheckWorkflow` | Workflow | `rwb-access` | One run: window, walk, result, checkpoint |
| `readCheckWindow` | Activity | `rwb-access` | Input: the business date; output: the window, the checkpoint and the chain head |
| `recomputeChainRange` | Activity | `rwb-access` | Input: the window and the batch size; output: the entries checked, `verifiedThrough` and optionally `firstBrokenEntryId` |
| `recordCheckResult` | Activity | `rwb-access` | Input: the run row; output: the entry id and the moved checkpoint |

Namespace `rwb-recovery`. The document declares the three activities and their inputs and outputs so that the app story and the harness agree on the evidence, and it declares no retry policy of its own: the retry is the kit's.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Queue | Cadence | Declared use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain-check-daily` | `rwb-access` | Daily, from the parameter row in force with its version; the start time is a parameter row | The daily check of REQ-DRI-003 and NFR-035 |

The cadence is declared as a reference to the parameter row and never as a value (BR7); the same Schedule starts an on-demand run only through the request of section 12.1, which uses the same workflow definition.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| the local decision-record table of the DP-03 library | P4 (rwb_access) | The entry the document describes and the report reads |
| the checkpoint row of this service | P4 (rwb_access) | The `checkpointEntryId` the report answers |
| `idempotency_key` | Platform library, in `rwb_access` | The on-demand request row |
| `outbox_event` | Platform library, in `rwb_access` | The record row of the entry |

No table of another service is named in the contract (DP-01): `decision_log_entry` is P7 `rwb_decision`'s, the parameters and lists are P3's, and no view of `case`, `task` or `rule_row` is named.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| authorise fake | `POST /authorise` with a granted answer for RW-AUDIT, RW-PLATADM, RW-SECADM, RW-DATASTEW, RW-COE and RW-COMPLY with Platform administration R, and a refused answer with MSG-P4-002 for RW-PHONECOL | App story, contract tests, harness |
| parameters fake | `GET /admin/parameters` with the cadence, the start time, the batch size and the page bounds as rows and the version in force | App story, contract tests |
| decision-record fake | The append of a run entry with its `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`, the hash-link check, the canonical form and a forced failure | App story, contract tests |
| chain fixture | A seeded chain of any length, one variant with a broken link at a named entry and one clean variant | App story, contract tests, harness |
| gateway-bff fake | The SCR-43 Roles and access route: the breach list of this answer merged with the access log of RWB-P4-AD007-APP, one hop each | Screen route, harness |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 2 consumed | The run and the report provided; the authorise and the parameters reads consumed; one hop, 2 s timeout |
| Kafka | 1 published, 0 consumed | `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` through the DP-03 outbox |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 3 activities, 1 Schedule | Declared on queue `rwb-access`; `chain-check-daily` |
| File | 0 | No file input and no file answer |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `openapi/rwb-access-chain-checks-v1.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1) with the two operations and the shared components, `contract/error-envelope.yaml`, the `ChainCheckRun` and `ChainCheckPage` schemas with their examples, the `CLEAN` and `BROKEN` examples, the AsyncAPI fragment that declares `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` for a run, the Schedule and workflow declaration fragment, the versioning rules and the five WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/access/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story; this story is Day 1 by rule and carries no H and no C of its own. The workflow kit and its Schedule API are a platform prerequisite of the declared Schedule and are not in this story's metadata list (GAP-2296; ASM-3804).

**Build steps**

1. OpenAPI 3.1 skeleton with the base path, the security scheme, the problem responses and the shared components; schema lint in the pipeline.
2. The two operations with the shape of section 11; the run row, the report page and the filter.
3. The outcome set and the two conditional fields: `firstBrokenEntryId` on a breach only, `verifiedThrough` always.
4. The Schedule and workflow declarations with the three activities, their inputs and outputs.
5. The message declaration of `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` with its key, its payload and the library's chain-check code.
6. The consumed operations with their owners, the one-hop rule and the 2 s client budget.
7. The error envelope and the message mapping, with the business texts copied unchanged from the legacy story.
8. The five fakes and the chain fixture of section 12.8.
9. The six contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
10. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note from the app story, the screen route and the harness.

**Feature switch.** The run is switched by the service baseline of this contract and by the cadence parameter row; the document declares no 404 branch of its own and adds no flag.

**Done when.** The document validates in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the five fakes answer every declared path, the Schedule and workflow declarations match the kit, and the app story, the screen route and the harness have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | No session | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Platform administration R calls either operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field or page bound has no valid value in the rows in force | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The entry of the run cannot be written, or a version the run needs is missing | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-004 | A break-glass grant is active for the caller | Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded. |

The message IDs are contract elements; the text is the agreed text taken from the legacy story RWB-E8-015, where all five messages already exist. The document declares the 401, the 403, the 422 and the 503 of these operations and no other error shape; MSG-P4-004 is declared as the warning header of the session, not as an error.

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | Contract element the screen consumes |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-43 Roles and access, audit panel | Day clean | The latest run row with outcome `CLEAN`, `entriesChecked`, `verifiedThrough` and `checkedAt` |
| SCR-43 Roles and access, audit panel | Breach | The run row with outcome `BROKEN`, `firstBrokenEntryId` and `verifiedThrough`, and the report filtered to `outcome=BROKEN` |
| SCR-43 Roles and access, audit panel | Running | The run in flight with `trigger` `ON_DEMAND` and the `checkpointEntryId` it started from |
| SCR-43 Roles and access, audit panel | Refused | The 403 of the envelope with MSG-P4-002 and no row |
| SCR-43 Roles and access, audit panel | Not recorded | The 503 of the envelope with MSG-P7-003 and no row |
| SCR-43 Roles and access, audit panel | Break-glass warning | The warning of the session read, shown as the MSG-P4-004 banner over the panel |

The panel is served by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls this read and the access log of RWB-P4-AD007-APP in parallel, one hop each, and merges the answers. The composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and to the Epic 8 screen work; the document fixes the chain-check side of the merge only. The legacy screens SCR-39 Rules and parameters and SCR-41 Delegation of authority are not part of this feature (GAP-2295).

No `-ITG` id appears in this table, because no integration slice is split from this key.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the cadence, the start time, the batch size and the page bounds are parameter rows behind the document, and the record code is the library's (BR7).
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: entry ids, counts, outcome codes, role codes, versions and times only (BR9).
- The contract names only `rwb-access` tables and only operations owned by `rwb-access`; the central ledger, the chain of every other service and the parameters are consumed or absent, never named as this service's (DP-01, BR5).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic fails the review (DP-13).
- Every example in the document is synthetic; no production entry, no production hash and no personal payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The document declares one path, two operations and no chain of another service, so no consumer can read a verdict the service did not reach (BR6).
- The error envelope and the CloudEvents envelope come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

##### 18. Traceability

| Requirement ID | Requirement (short) | Contract element | Test cases |
|---|---|---|---|

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: app slice of RWB-E8-015 for rwb-access: the daily chain check of this service's own decision-record chain, the on-demand run of internal audit, the breach record and the two reads. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As an **internal audit (RW-AUDIT)**, I want **the Workbench to walk the hash chain of its own decision-record entries every day, to stop at the first entry that does not verify, to record the run with its outcome and the version in force, and to answer the runs and their breaches**, so that **a changed, missing or reordered record is found by the control itself instead of by a reader, and the finding reaches Compliance on the same business day**.

Inside `rwb-access` this is the control half of the legacy story RWB-E8-015:

- Service `rwb-access`, schema `rwb_access`, REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.
- The chain this story walks is **this service's own** local decision-record chain in `rwb_access`, written through the library of DP-03. Each of the 19 services writes its local record where the decision is taken, and the one central chain over `rwb.decision-record.v1` is `rwb-decision`'s. The archive therefore carries two controls, not one: the owner verifies what it wrote, and P7 verifies the ledger (ADR-022; ASM-3798).
- Three deliverables and nothing else: the Schedule `chain-check-daily` on the `rwb-access` queue, which runs `AccessChainCheckWorkflow`; the write `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/chain-checks`, which is the same workflow started by internal audit outside the schedule; and the read `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/chain-checks`, which answers the runs this service recorded and filters to the breaches.
- The run row is not a new table. The result is one append to the local chain, and the read is a projection over the entries that carry the check's record code, so the record of a run is as untouchable as the record of an approval (BR2, BR8).
- The check is read-only on the chain it walks: it writes one entry of its own and moves a checkpoint, and it never repairs, rewrites, deletes or re-sequences an entry it found or did not find.
- The two paths are not ownership-map rows: no source names a chain-check endpoint. They are fixed on the DP-13 base by the contract of RWB-P4-E8015-CON and the point is carried in GAP-2293 and ASM-3799.
- A daily unattended run needs the workflow kit and a Schedule (the platform story RWB-PLT-E1071-CON). That dependency is not in this story's metadata build list, so the Schedule is built against the platform Schedule API and the missing H is raised at D1 (GAP-2296; ASM-3804). The metadata is not changed here.
- This story publishes no `rwb.access.<Event>.v1` message: the only message is `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, from the outbox of the run that records the result.

The legacy story's two endpoints (`/admin/rule-versions` and its approve path) and its data table (`decision_log_entry`, `rule_row`, `role`) belong to other keys and other services; they are read as the legacy copy of the generic administration template and are carried in GAP-2295, not implemented here.

##### 2. Business rationale

REQ-DRI-002 (Must) says the decision log is append only, and REQ-DRI-003 (Must) says it is hash chained **and the chain integrity is checked every day, with a break reported to Compliance the same day**; NFR-035 repeats the target as a daily check with a same-day report. A chain that is never walked proves nothing: the hash link only becomes evidence when a control recomputes it on a schedule and records that it did.

The legacy story carried the feature inside the monolith (FEAT-ADM-10, RWB-E8-015), where the decision log was a table of the one recovery schema and one administration module could read it end to end. In the target there is no single table an administration module may read: every service writes its record into its own schema and P7 keeps the central ledger (Architecture v5 slides 20 and 28; DP-01; ADR-022). The control therefore splits by owner. `rwb-access` is the service that already holds the access log, the break-glass grants and the audit surface, and it holds the check for the entries it wrote; the central ledger and its 02:00 Schedule belong to RWB-P7-E1008-APP, which this story neither calls nor duplicates.

The split is what makes the control finishable in wave 4: no cross-service read, no C dependency on `rwb-decision`, and a check that runs on its own queue over its own rows. The evidence a reader needs is unchanged from the legacy intent: which window was checked, how many entries verified, where the walk stopped, when, and under which parameter and algorithm version. The three questions behind an audit finding, in order, are answered by one row and one written record, and a breach cannot be quietened because the next run walks the same window again until the chain verifies.

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| RWB-P4-E8015-CON (same service, its own contract story) | The OpenAPI 3.1 document of the two operations, the `ChainCheck` and `ChainCheckPage` schemas, the outcome set, the error envelope, the consumed-operation list, the Schedule and workflow declarations and the five fakes. This story implements that document and adds no path |
| RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03): the entry shape, the canonical form of a hash, the append, the hash-link check and the record codes |
| RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The parameters client library and the `rwb-case` parameters contract (DP-06): the cadence, the start time, the batch size and the page bounds, as rows and not as code |
| RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) that serves SCR-43 Roles and access and calls the two operations, one hop each |
| The platform workflow kit and Schedule API | The daily run and the on-demand run are one workflow started from a Schedule and from a request. The kit's own contract story is RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, which this story's metadata does **not** carry (GAP-2296; ASM-3804) |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E8-015, from the feature specification and from the technical specification:

- The cadence is daily and the report to Compliance is same-day (REQ-DRI-003; NFR-035). The cadence itself is a parameter row read through DP-06, with the version in force written on the run; no interval is a constant in code (BR4).
- The rights in force are those of TSD P4 v3 T6.1: RW-AUDIT holds `R` in Platform administration, RW-PLATADM holds `CRUD`, RW-SECADM holds `CRUDA`, and the case roles hold a dash. Both operations authorise Platform administration R (BR3, ASM-3802). The legacy permission table's Rules and parameters `C` and `A` describes the rule-version feature of RWB-E8-007 and is carried in GAP-2295.
- The FSD P4 v3 A2.26.3.3 role table names the feature as one that runs unattended, with internal audit as the role that also uses it; that is the reading this story implements.
- The chain this service may walk is the one its own login owns: the local decision-record table of the DP-03 library in `rwb_access`. `decision_log_entry` is P7's and is not read (DP-01).
- The entry a run appends is the library's entry, not a new shape: `decision_code`, `case_id` empty, `inputs_ref`, the version, `decided_at`, `prev_hash` and `entry_hash` (DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018).
- The record code, the order and batch of the walk, the start time of the Schedule and the same-day channel to Compliance are library codes and parameter rows; where a value is missing, section 11 carries the placeholder and its citation (GAP-2294; ASM-3801).

##### 4. Flow

1. The Schedule `chain-check-daily` on the `rwb-access` queue starts `AccessChainCheckWorkflow` with the business date as its input and no personal data in it. The cadence and the start time are parameter rows read through DP-06 with the version in force (REQ-DRI-003).
2. `readCheckWindow` reads the checkpoint from the run store of the service (the `verifiedThrough` entry id of the last `CLEAN` run) and the head of the local chain from the DP-03 library, and fixes the window: the entries after the checkpoint up to the head, or none when the checkpoint is the head (BR5).
3. `recomputeChainRange` walks the window in the library's chain order in batches whose size is a parameter row. For each entry it recomputes the entry hash from the canonical form the library publishes and compares the `prev_hash` of the entry with the `entry_hash` of the entry before it (BR6).
4. A link that verifies moves the position on and counts one entry checked.
5. The first link that does not verify ends the walk: `outcome` is `BROKEN`, `firstBrokenEntryId` is that entry, `verifiedThrough` is the entry before it, and no entry after it is checked (BR6, AC4).
6. A walk that reaches the head with every link verified answers `outcome` `CLEAN`, `verifiedThrough` the head and `firstBrokenEntryId` null (BR6, AC1).
7. `recordCheckResult` appends exactly one entry to the local chain of DP-03 with the library's record code for a chain check, `case_id` empty, `inputs_ref` carrying the run row (window, counts, outcome, first broken entry, trigger, parameter version and the library's algorithm version), `decided_at` and the `prev_hash` and `entry_hash` the library computes (BR2, BR7, AC1).
8. The same transaction stages the outbox row, so `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` is published from the outbox and never from the workflow (BR8).
9. A `CLEAN` run moves the checkpoint to `verifiedThrough`. A `BROKEN` run leaves the checkpoint where it was, so the next run walks the same window and re-raises the breach until the chain verifies or the owning team takes the incident path (BR7, BR9).
10. A `BROKEN` outcome **is** the control breach: the result entry plus the run row answered with `outcome` `BROKEN`, readable on SCR-43 Roles and access and on the read of step 12 on the same business day by the Compliance and PDPA officer and internal audit (REQ-DRI-003; ASM-3803).
11. Where the result entry, the checkpoint row or the outbox row cannot be written the transaction rolls back: no outcome is answered, no checkpoint moves and the Schedule's failure is alerted by the platform; the retry walks the same window and records one result (BR10, AC2).
12. `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/chain-checks` answers the runs this service recorded: one item per run in `checkedAt` order then entry id, with `outcome`, `entriesChecked`, `verifiedThrough`, `firstBrokenEntryId`, `windowFrom`, `windowTo`, `trigger`, `checkedAt`, `entryId`, and `page`, `size`, `total` and the checkpoint entry id; `outcome=BROKEN` filters to the breaches, and page and size come from parameter rows (BR11, AC5).
13. `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/chain-checks` starts the same workflow with `trigger` `ON_DEMAND` under an `Idempotency-Key`, under the same checkpoint rule, and answers 201 with the run row and the `Location` of the read (BR12, AC3).
14. Both operations authorise first: Platform administration R through the authorise operation of this service, one hop and cached for the session. A caller without it is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002, no run is started, nothing is appended and no parameters row is read (BR3, AC3).
15. The service reads no row of `decision_log_entry`, no `rule_row` and no `case`: the central ledger and its own check are P7's, the rule registry is P7's, and a chain check addresses no case (BR5, DP-01).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The caller holds no Platform administration R | 403, no run started, no entry, no parameters read | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X2 | The caller's session has ended | 401, no run started and nothing appended | MSG-P4-001 | AC3 |
| X3 | The parameters read answers no cadence, no batch size or no page bound | The run is not started and the read answers 503; nothing is appended | MSG-P7-003 | AC2 |
| X4 | The checkpoint names an entry that no longer exists in the local chain | The walk starts from the chain head instead, the run row states the window it actually walked, and the finding is carried as a breach of type `WINDOW_RESET` | None | AC4 |
| X5 | The first link that does not verify is found | The walk stops, `outcome` `BROKEN`, `firstBrokenEntryId` set, `verifiedThrough` the entry before it, one entry appended | None | AC4 |
| X6 | The window is empty because the checkpoint is the chain head | The run answers `CLEAN` with `entriesChecked` 0 and `verifiedThrough` the checkpoint; one entry is appended so the control still shows a run | None | AC1 |
| X7 | The result entry, the checkpoint row or the outbox row cannot be written | The transaction rolls back, no outcome is answered, no checkpoint moves; the platform alerts the failed Schedule | MSG-P7-003 | AC2 |
| X8 | A second `POST` arrives with the same `Idempotency-Key` | The first result is replayed; one entry, one walk | None | AC3 |
| X9 | `page` or `size` is outside the bounds in force | 422 naming the field, no run row answered | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X10 | A break-glass grant is active for the caller | The run proceeds and the answer carries the warning with the end time of the grant and the grant id in the entry | MSG-P4-004 | AC3 |

No exception path of this story changes a chain entry, a case, a task, a role, a permission or a rule: the walk is read-only on everything it inspects, and the only row it writes of its own is the entry of its own chain plus the platform library rows of the run.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P4-E8015-CON and its fakes; walks only its own chain, so no `rwb-decision` dependency and no cross-service read |
| Negotiable | The record code, the batch size, the start time and the page bounds are parameter rows and library codes; the outcome field names are settled with the contract story and with Internal audit |
| Valuable | Makes REQ-DRI-003 and NFR-035 provable for the entries this service wrote, and leaves a record that a changed record was found and when |
| Estimable | One workflow with three activities, one Schedule, two controllers, one chain walker, one result appender, one read projection, five fakes and six test cases |
| Small | Fits one sprint; no new table, no screen of its own and no event of its own |
| Testable | Each owned criterion has a test case in section 16; a break is provable against a seeded chain and the record failure against the library fake |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Detect a broken hash chain in the decision log

  Background:
    Given the environment is SIT
    Given the chain walked is the local decision-record chain of rwb-access in schema rwb_access, and decision_log_entry of rwb_decision is not read
    Given test user "U-8101" holds RW-AUDIT, whose Platform administration letter is "R" in the SIT matrix
    Given test user "U-8110" holds RW-PHONECOL, whose Platform administration letter is a dash in the SIT matrix

  Scenario: AC1 Detect a broken hash chain in the decision log (legacy RWB-E8-015 AC1)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the chain-check cadence, the start time, the batch size and their version in force
    Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place

    Then tests the log chain and raises a control breach if a record does not verify
    Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version

  Scenario: AC2 Not recorded (legacy RWB-E8-015 AC2)
    Given the decision log cannot be written
    When the action is taken
    Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003

  Scenario: AC3 A caller without Platform administration R is refused (new, D-RCV-60)

    When "U-8110" calls POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/chain-checks with Idempotency-Key "k-015-3"

  Scenario: AC4 The walk stops at the first entry that does not verify (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the local chain holds 5 entries and the entry_hash of entry "E-4" was changed after it was written, so its prev_hash no longer matches the entry_hash of entry "E-3"
    When the daily run walks the window from the checkpoint to the chain head
    Then the run answers outcome "BROKEN", firstBrokenEntryId "E-4", verifiedThrough "E-3" and entriesChecked 3
    Then entries "E-4" and "E-5" are not checked and no entry of the chain is repaired, rewritten or re-sequenced
    Then exactly one chain-check entry is appended with the run row and the parameter version in force
    When the next daily run starts
    Then it walks the same window again and answers outcome "BROKEN" with firstBrokenEntryId "E-4", because the checkpoint did not move

  Scenario: AC5 The run report answers one row per run and role codes only (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a "CLEAN" run verified through entry "E-9" and a later "BROKEN" run stopped at entry "E-11"
    When "U-8101" calls GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/chain-checks
    Then the answer carries one item per run, each with outcome, entriesChecked, verifiedThrough, firstBrokenEntryId, windowFrom, windowTo, trigger, checkedAt and entryId
    Then the answer carries the checkpoint entry id "E-9" and the page, size and total it answered with
    Then no item carries a name, an e-mail address, a user reference or a case id
```
