
AC1 and AC2 are the two criteria of RWB-E8-015, copied with their text unchanged; AC1 carries one added line at the top of its scenario, the parameters mock, so the run is provable while the `rwb-case` contract is still a fake. AC3 to AC5 are new under D-RCV-60 and test only what this service adds: the right, the stop at the first break and the run report.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The chain is walked every day and a break is reported the same business day; the daily check is the Schedule `chain-check-daily` of this service | REQ-DRI-003; NFR-035 |
| BR2 | The chain walked is this service's own local decision-record chain, and the record of a run is one append to it with the library's record code; a run is never a new table | ADR-022; DP-03; ASM-3798 |
| BR3 | Both operations need Platform administration R, authorised through the authorise operation of this service; a caller without it is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002 and nothing is walked or written | TSD P4 v3 T6.1; FSD P4 v3 A2.26.3.3; ASM-3802 |
| BR4 | The cadence, the start time, the batch size and the page bounds are parameter rows read through DP-06 with the version in force, and the version is written on the run; no interval and no batch size is a constant in code | DP-06; BR-P4-026 |
| BR5 | The service walks only the rows its own login owns; `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` and `case` are other services' and are never read | DP-01; Ownership Map v1 |
| BR6 | The walk recomputes the entry hash from the library's canonical form and compares each `prev_hash` with the `entry_hash` before it, in chain order, in batches; it stops at the first link that does not verify and checks no entry after it | RWB-E8-015 AC1; DP-03 |
| BR7 | Exactly one result entry is appended per run, inside the transaction that moves the checkpoint; a `CLEAN` run moves the checkpoint and a `BROKEN` run does not, so a break is re-raised until it is resolved | R-UNI-39; DP-03; ASM-3800 |
| BR8 | `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` is published from the outbox of that transaction, with references, counts, versions and times and no case id and no personal field | DP-09; EV-08; NFR-040 |
| BR9 | The walk is read-only on the chain it inspects: no entry is repaired, rewritten, deleted or re-sequenced, and a break is a finding and not a write | REQ-DRI-002; DP-03 |
| BR10 | An answer that cannot be recorded is withheld: the transaction rolls back, no checkpoint moves, no outcome is answered and the failed Schedule is alerted | RWB-E8-015 AC2; REQ-DRI-005; DP-03 |
| BR11 | The read answers this service's own runs only, in `checkedAt` order then entry id, with `outcome=BROKEN` as its filter, and it never answers a name, an e-mail address, a user reference or a case id | DP-01; NFR-040; ASM-3800 |
| BR12 | An on-demand run and a scheduled run are one workflow under one checkpoint rule, and one `Idempotency-Key` answers one run and makes no second walk | Architecture v5 slide 42; DP-09 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-access`:

- BR1 and BR12 are one Schedule and one request path onto the same workflow definition; the only difference is the `trigger` value on the run row.
- BR2 is the absence of a run table: the projection of section 12.7 reads the entries whose record code is the library's chain-check code, so the report inherits the append-only guarantee of the chain.
- BR5 is the absence of a foreign repository: the module has no view, no join and no synonym for `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` or `case`.
- BR6 is the walker: the canonical form and the hash come from the library, and this service supplies the order, the batch and the comparison, never a second hash algorithm.
- BR7 is the checkpoint: `verifiedThrough` and the checkpoint row commit with the entry, and the two are never written apart.
- BR9 is the absence of a repair path: there is no update, no delete and no re-chain method on the chain, and a break is answered only by the incident path of the owning team.
- BR10 is the rollback and the alert on the failed Schedule; the retry is the platform's and it walks the same window.
- BR11 is the page shape of the read and the filter, with role codes and entry ids only.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Idle | The Schedule fires, or internal audit posts a run | The right is held and the parameters are in force | Window fixed |
| Window fixed | The walk starts | The checkpoint is before the chain head | Walking |
| Walking | A link verifies | `prev_hash` equals the `entry_hash` before it | Walking, one entry further |
| Walking | A link does not verify | `prev_hash` differs, or an entry hash cannot be recomputed | Stopped, outcome `BROKEN` |
| Walking | The head is reached | Every link verified | Stopped, outcome `CLEAN` |
| Stopped | The result is appended | The entry, the checkpoint and the outbox row commit | Recorded |
| Stopped | The result cannot be appended | The transaction fails | Idle, nothing recorded, the Schedule alerted |
| Recorded | `CLEAN` | None | Checkpoint moves to `verifiedThrough` |
| Recorded | `BROKEN` | None | Checkpoint unchanged; the breach stays open |

| Chain | Event | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Local decision-record chain | A run is recorded, a decision is taken, an approval is given | One entry appended with its `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`; no entry is ever updated or deleted |
| Checkpoint | `CLEAN` and `BROKEN` runs | One row per service, moved only by a `CLEAN` run |
| Central ledger | None | Not touched by this story; P7's chain is verified by RWB-P7-E1008-APP |

A breach is closed by a decision of the owning team, recorded as its own entry; this story neither closes nor annotates a breach, and the next run states whether the chain verifies again (BR7, BR9).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Internal audit (RW-AUDIT) | Reads the runs and the breaches, and starts an on-demand run: Platform administration `R` in TSD P4 v3 T6.1 |
| Compliance and PDPA officer (RW-COMPLY) | Reads the breach list on the same business day; starts no run unless a Platform administration right is granted |
| Platform administrator (RW-PLATADM) | Holds Platform administration `CRUD`; may start a run and operate the Schedule |
| Security administrator (RW-SECADM) | Holds Platform administration `CRUDA`; may start a run |
| A case role without a Platform administration letter (RW-CASEOWN, RW-PHONECOL) | Refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002; nothing is walked and nothing is recorded |
| The gateway-bff route | Calls the two operations on behalf of the signed-in user, one hop each, and passes the `Idempotency-Key` unchanged |
| The platform workflow kit | Starts the workflow from the Schedule and from the request, and records the failed run as an alert |
| `rwb-access` itself | Reads its own chain and its own checkpoint, appends one entry, and writes only its own rows |
| `rwb-decision` (P7) | Owns the central ledger, its chain and its 02:00 check; this story calls it not at all |
| `rwb-case` (P3) | Owns the parameters read; consumed one hop, never a table read |

The refusal shapes are 403 with an RFC 9457 problem response and `messageId` MSG-P4-002 for an absent right, 401 with MSG-P4-001 for no session, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for a page bound, and 503 with MSG-P7-003 for a record or a parameters read that cannot be completed. The database login is the per-service login of the service baseline (DP-02), which belongs to RWB-P4-E8015-CON.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Table in `rwb_access` | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local library, DP-03) | the run entry: `decision_code` DF-DEC-003 with the library's chain-check code, `case_id` DF-DEC-002 empty, `inputs_ref` DF-DEC-008 with the window, the counts, the outcome, the first broken entry, the trigger, the parameter version and the algorithm version, `decided_at` DF-DEC-016, `prev_hash` DF-DEC-017 and `entry_hash` DF-DEC-018 | Write; and read for the walk and the report |
| DF-DEC-017, DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local library, DP-03) | `prev_hash` and `entry_hash` of every entry in the window | Read: the two values the walk compares |
| DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 | `permission` | id, role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version | Read by the authorise operation of this service only, for Platform administration R |
| DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039 | `role` | id, role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope, entra_group | Read by the authorise operation only; the answer carries role codes |
| (idempotency) | `idempotency_key` (platform library table in `rwb_access`) | the request and the stored answer of an on-demand run | Write and read (DP-09) |
| (outbox) | `outbox_event` | the record row of the run entry | Write |
| (checkpoint) | the service checkpoint row | the last verified entry id and the time it was set | Write on a `CLEAN` run; read at the start of every run |
| (inbox) | `processed_event` | none: this story consumes no event | None |
| parameters | `rwb_case` parameters | the cadence, the start time, the batch size and the page bounds, with the version in force | Returned through the P3 contract; not read |

No row of `decision_log_entry` is read or written: the central ledger is P7's, and this story writes and walks only its own chain in `rwb_access` (DP-01, BR5). No row of `case`, `task` or `rule_row` is read: a chain check addresses no case and evaluates no rule. The placeholder for a field the sources do not fix is carried where it is used: the record code of a chain check, the order and batch of the walk, the start time of the Schedule and the same-day channel to Compliance are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2294; ASM-3801), and the name and shape of the checkpoint and the run-row fields are fixed by RWB-P4-E8015-CON (GAP-2293; ASM-3800). Field ids are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 and of TSD P4 v3 T3.1.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Path | Owner | Request | Response | Errors | Authorization | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/chain-checks` | P4 `rwb-access` | No body; header `Idempotency-Key` required | `checkId`, `outcome` (`CLEAN` or `BROKEN`), `entriesChecked`, `verifiedThrough`, `firstBrokenEntryId`, `windowFrom`, `windowTo`, `trigger` `ON_DEMAND`, `checkedAt`, `entryId`, with `Location` of the read | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 (MSG-P4-002); 503 (MSG-P7-003) | Platform administration R | Required; a replay answers the first result and makes no second walk |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/chain-checks` | P4 `rwb-access` | Query `outcome`, `page`, `size` | `ChainCheckPage`: `items[]` of the run row, `checkpointEntryId`, `page`, `size`, `total` | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 (MSG-P4-002); 422 (MSG-GEN-001); 503 (MSG-P7-003) | Platform administration R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |

Both operations sit on the base `/api/recovery/access/v1` of DP-13. Asynchronous work never answers 202: the on-demand run completes inside the request budget and answers the run row, or it answers 503 and records nothing (BR10). `page` defaults to its parameter row and `size` is capped by it, both read through DP-06 and never from code (BR4). `GET /admin/chain-checks` is not an ownership-map row; the path, the outcome set and the field names are fixed by RWB-P4-E8015-CON (GAP-2293; ASM-3799).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 `rwb-access` (own service) | The Platform administration R check behind both operations, cached for the session; MSG-P4-002 on a refusal |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 `rwb-case` | The cadence, the start time, the batch size and the page bounds, with the version in force (DP-06) |

One hop per call, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11). No operation of `rwb-decision`, `rwb-case` (other than the parameters read) or any other service is called: the central ledger and its check are P7's and the chain walked is this service's own.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library; consumed by P7 | entryId | the hash-chained entry of a chain check: the window, the counts, the outcome, the first broken entry, the trigger, the parameter version and the algorithm version |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, from the outbox of the transaction that appends the entry and moves the checkpoint. The payload carries identifiers, counts, versions and times, and no case id, no name, no e-mail address and no personal field. This story publishes no `rwb.access.<Event>.v1` message: the administration events of `rwb-access` belong to RWB-P4-E1037-APP and RWB-P4-E8008-APP, and a chain check adds neither.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `rwb-access` subscribes to no topic for this capability; the run is started by its own Schedule or by its own request, and no `processed_event` row is written.

| Element | Kind | Queue | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AccessChainCheckWorkflow` | Workflow | `rwb-access` | One run: window, walk, result, checkpoint |
| `readCheckWindow` | Activity | `rwb-access` | Reads the checkpoint and the chain head through the DP-03 library and fixes the window |
| `recomputeChainRange` | Activity | `rwb-access` | Recomputes the hashes and compares the links in batches, stopping at the first break |
| `recordCheckResult` | Activity | `rwb-access` | Appends the result entry, moves the checkpoint on a `CLEAN` run and stages the outbox row |

Namespace `rwb-recovery`; one workflow and three activities with no personal data in any input or output (NFR-040). The workflow is started by the Schedule of section 12.6 and by the on-demand operation of section 12.1.

No other Schedule belongs to this story. The access review Schedule (JOB-18) is RWB-P4-AD008-APP's.

No table of another service is named (DP-01): `decision_log_entry` is P7 `rwb_decision`'s, the parameters are P3's, and `case`, `task` and `rule_row` are not touched.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `ChainCheckController` (POST and GET), `ChainCheckService`, `ChainCheckpointRepository`, `ChainWalker` (canonical form, hash comparison, first-break stop), `ChainCheckResultAppender` (the DP-03 append, the checkpoint and the outbox in one transaction), `AccessChainCheckWorkflow` with its three activities, the `chain-check-daily` Schedule, the authorise and parameters clients, the read projection with its filter and paging, and the six test cases of section 16.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/access/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story. The workflow kit and its Schedule API are a platform prerequisite of the daily run and are not in this story's metadata list (GAP-2296; ASM-3804).

**Build steps**

1. The controller pair on the DP-13 base with the contract's schema, the problem responses and the `Idempotency-Key`.
2. The parameters reader and the authorise client, with the session cache and the 2 s budget.
3. `readCheckWindow`: the checkpoint, the head, the window rule and the empty-window case.
4. `recomputeChainRange`: the library's canonical form, the batch loop, the comparison per link and the first-break stop.
5. `recordCheckResult`: one transaction for the entry, the checkpoint and the outbox row, and the rollback that withholds the answer.
6. The workflow and its three activities on queue `rwb-access`, and the `chain-check-daily` Schedule started from the parameter rows.
7. The read projection with the `outcome` filter, the ordering, the paging and the checkpoint entry id.
8. The five fakes and the two chain fixtures.
9. The six test cases; a break is proved against the seeded chain and the withheld answer against the forced failure.

**Feature switch.** The run is switched by the service baseline of RWB-P4-E8015-CON and by the cadence parameter row; the document of the contract declares no 404 branch and this story adds no flag of its own.

**Done when.** The daily Schedule records one `CLEAN` or `BROKEN` run per day on a seeded chain, an on-demand run answers one row, the report answers the runs and the breaches without personal data, a forced record failure leaves no outcome and no checkpoint move, and the harness of the wave 4 audit journey has accepted the evidence.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | No session | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A caller without Platform administration R calls either operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | `page` or `size` is outside the bounds in force | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The result entry, the checkpoint or the outbox row cannot be written, or a parameters row the run needs is missing | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-004 | A break-glass grant is active for the caller | Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded. |

The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story RWB-E8-015; MSG-GEN-001 is the general field message of the FSD. The message IDs are contract elements of RWB-P4-E8015-CON, and this story answers no sixth message and no business text of its own.

No `-ITG` copy appears in this table, because no integration slice is split from this key in this Work Package.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the cadence, the start time, the batch size, the page bounds and the record code are parameter rows or library codes (BR4).
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, logs or the report: entry ids, counts, versions, outcome codes, role codes and times only (BR8, BR11, NFR-040).
- The chain walked is this service's own; `decision_log_entry`, `rule_row` and `case` are never read, joined or viewed (DP-01, BR5).
- The walk is read-only: no entry is repaired, rewritten, deleted or re-sequenced, and a break is a finding that only the owning team's decision can close (REQ-DRI-002, BR9).
- One REST base and one topic per service; the paths of this story sit on `/api/recovery/access/v1` and it declares no `rwb.access.<Event>.v1` message (DP-13).
- Every fixture is synthetic: no production entry, no production hash and no personal field is copied into a test or a fake.
- The error and CloudEvents envelopes come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E8-016 for rwb-access. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the data subject request register of `rwb-access`: an OpenAPI 3.1 document for the open, the decision, the read and the list, the `DataSubjectRequest`, `DataSubjectRequestDecision` and `DataSubjectRequestList` schemas with the state set and the evidence block and no person, one RFC 9457 error envelope with its message IDs, the consumed authorise, access-log and parameters operations with their owners and the 2 s budget, the contract tables of section 12 and the five contract fakes**, so that **the app story, the SCR-47 route, the access-log owner, the parameters owner and the integration harness can build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1 without waiting for `rwb-access`, `rwb-case` or the access-log capability to be built**.

This contract carries no legacy acceptance criterion: AC1 and AC2 of RWB-E8-016 belong to RWB-P4-E8016-APP, and the six criteria of section 7 test the document, the schemas and the state set, the envelope, the consumed declarations and the fakes.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST and one hop with a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy story worked a data subject request inside a screen of the monolith, where the request, the masking rows and the decision log were rows of one schema and no other service had to agree on what "answered inside the statutory period" meant. In the target the period is a parameter of `rwb-case`, the case and its hold are `rwb-case`'s and `rwb-deviation`'s, the masking policy and the access entries are `rwb-access`'s, and the record of who decided what is the decision record (ADR-022).

Three things must therefore be fixed once. The first is the boundary: which service owns the register (this one), which owns the period (P3 through DP-06) and which owns the access evidence (the access-log capability of this service). The second is the state set: a request moves from open to in progress to answered or refused, and no consumer should have to infer that from dates. The third is what the register says: a person reference, case ids, field ids, a decision code, a role code and times, and never a personal value, because the answer of a request is read by audit and copied into a topic that every consumer of the decision record reads.

Fixing the field-level contract once, with faked consumers, lets the app story build in parallel with the parameters contract of `rwb-case`, the local decision-record library and the access-log read, and it catches a drift between a fake and the document in a contract test rather than in an integration window. The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_access`, REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1` for the service, the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.

The baseline also states the one thing it is not: it defines no retention class, no masking policy, no access entry and no case state, and it names no table of `rwb-case`, `rwb-decision` or `rwb-source-data` as this service's. The consumed operations appear in the document as consumed, which is what makes the split real.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the document, the base path, the topic and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) that calls the four operations behind SCR-47 Personal data, and it is a consumer of this baseline.
- The access-log read is described by TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A as API-P4-008 `GET /admin/access-log` with the query `user`, `from`, `to`, `event`, `page` and `size` and the response `AccessLogPage`; the case-id filter this story needs is not in that list, so the filter is fixed here and raised with the access-log owner (GAP-0877; ASM-1592).
- The parameters read is DP-06 and the `rwb-case` parameters contract (RWB-P3-E1042-CON): the statutory period, the person-reference shape and the page bounds are rows and not fields of this document's code.
- The platform error envelope and the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope are the platform baseline; where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The register is a set of entries of the DP-03 library (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON); this document describes the fields a step records and no field of another service.
- The operations and their owners are taken from the ownership map only: the four operations of this document are P4's, the authorise operation and the access-log read are P4's, and the parameters read is P3's. No table of another service is named as this service's (DP-01).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the four operations with the shared components used across the `rwb-access` operations: the security scheme, the problem envelope, the paging parameters and the three schemas.
2. Fix the `DataSubjectRequest` request and answer schemas with the fields of section 11: `dataSubjectRef`, `requestType`, `caseIds`, `fieldIds`, `receivedAt` and `reason` in, and `requestId`, `requestType`, `state`, `openedAt`, `dueDate`, `version`, `steps` and `evidence` out, with no person field of any kind.
3. Fix the `DataSubjectRequestDecision` schema behind the `PATCH`, with `decision`, `fieldIds`, `effectiveFrom`, `refusalReason`, `answerSummary` and `reason` in, `requestId`, `state`, `decision`, `version`, `updatedAt`, `maskingVersion` and `maskingRowCount` out, and the `If-Match` header declared as required.
4. Fix the state set: `OPEN`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `ANSWERED` and `REFUSED`, with the transition each operation may cause, the terminal pair and the overdue flag as a computed answer field and not a state.
5. Fix the evidence block of a read: one item per access entry with its case id, decision code, decided time, field ids and mask flag, and the statement that no actor name and no personal value is part of it.
6. Agree the error envelope and the message-ID mapping for 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, with the business texts taken from the legacy story where the message already existed and MSG-GEN-004 used for the stale version and the terminal state.
7. Declare the consumed own authorise operation, the own access-log read and the `rwb-case` parameters read as consumed, each with its owner, one hop and the 2 s client budget; declare the case, task, retention, masking-policy and ledger operations as neither provided nor consumed here.
8. Publish the contract tables of section 12 (nine sub-tables) and the five contract fakes.
9. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the three schemas and their required fields, the state set, the envelope and message IDs, the consumed declarations and drift detection between a fake and the document.
10. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P4-E8016-APP, the SCR-47 route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON, the access-log owner, the `rwb-case` parameters owner and the harness of the wave 4 access journey.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The document fails OpenAPI 3.1 validation | The pipeline fails and no baseline is tagged | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A declared operation names another service's base, path or owner, or declares a case, retention, masking-policy or ledger operation as provided here | The review refuses the document; the operation is declared as consumed instead | None | AC1, AC5 |
| X3 | A response of 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 or 503 is declared without the envelope or without a message ID | The contract test fails | None | AC4 |
| X4 | A schema carries a name, an e-mail address, a national identity number, a phone number, an address, a date of birth or a user reference of the person or of the officer | The contract test fails; the review refuses the document | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X5 | A state outside `OPEN`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `ANSWERED` and `REFUSED` is declared, or an operation is declared to move a state it may not move | The review refuses the document | None | AC3 |
| X6 | The document declares a `case`, `task`, `decision_log_entry`, retention or masking-policy table as this service's, or declares a case state as written here | The review refuses the document | None | AC3, AC5 |
| X7 | A fake answers a path, a status or a payload the document does not declare | The drift test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X8 | A consumed operation is declared without an owner, without the one-hop rule or without the 2 s budget | The contract test fails | None | AC5 |
| X9 | A field of the answer has no source definition | The field is marked with the placeholder and the gap is carried | None | AC2 |
| X10 | The `If-Match` header is declared optional, or the evidence block is declared to carry an actor name | The review refuses the document | None | AC2, AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the ownership map, the platform envelopes, the DP-03 entry schema, the P4 appendix T-A and the P3 and P4 contracts only |
| Negotiable | The statutory period, the reference shape and the page bounds are parameter rows behind the document; the base, the paths, the state set and the envelope are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story, the SCR-47 route, the access-log owner and the harness on Day 1, and keeps the person out of the register and out of the evidence |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, one error envelope, nine contract tables, five fakes and six contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Handle a data subject request contract baseline for rwb-access

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the data subject request register is held by rwb-access and the case, its hold and the statutory period are held by rwb-case

  Scenario: AC1 The OpenAPI 3.1 document describes the four operations (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the data subject request register is published
    When it is validated against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares the base /api/recovery/access/v1
    Then it declares POST /admin/data-subject-requests, PATCH /admin/data-subject-requests/{requestId}, GET /admin/data-subject-requests/{requestId} and GET /admin/data-subject-requests with the owner rwb-access
    Then the open names Rules and parameters C, the decision and the answer name A, the two reads name R, and every operation names its error responses 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503
    Then the open requires an Idempotency-Key and the decision requires an If-Match
    Then no operation of rwb-case, rwb-decision or the access log is declared as provided by rwb-access

  Scenario: AC2 The schemas are fixed and carry no person (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the DataSubjectRequest, DataSubjectRequestDecision and DataSubjectRequestList schemas of the document
    Then the open request carries dataSubjectRef, requestType, caseIds, fieldIds, receivedAt and reason, with dataSubjectRef, requestType, caseIds and receivedAt required
    Then the answer carries requestId, requestType, state, openedAt, dueDate, version, steps and evidence
    Then the decision carries decision, fieldIds, effectiveFrom, refusalReason, answerSummary and reason, with decision and reason required
    Then the list carries items of requestId, requestType, state, openedAt, dueDate, overdue, page, size and total
    Then dataSubjectRef is a reference and no schema declares a name, an e-mail address, a national identity number, a phone number, an address, a date of birth or a user reference
    Then the evidence item carries the case id, the decision code, the decided time, the field ids and the mask flag, and no actor name
    Then the statutory period, the reference shape and the page bounds are read from the parameters contract and never from code

  Scenario: AC3 The state set is fixed and one operation moves each state (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the state set of a data subject request in the document
    Then state is one of OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, ANSWERED and REFUSED
    Then the open moves a request to OPEN, the first correction or erasure decision moves it to IN_PROGRESS, and the answer or the refusal moves it to ANSWERED or REFUSED
    Then ANSWERED and REFUSED are terminal and any further decision is a 409
    Then the overdue flag is a computed answer field and not a state, and no workflow and no Schedule escalates it
    Then the document states that no case state, no hold and no task is written by this service

  Scenario: AC4 Every failure is one envelope with one message (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error envelope component of the document
    When a 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 or 503 response is produced by any operation
    Then the body is one RFC 9457 problem response carrying type, title, status, detail, instance, messageId and traceId
    Then 401 carries MSG-P4-001, 403 carries MSG-P4-002, 409 carries MSG-GEN-004 and 422 carries MSG-GEN-001
    Then 503 carries MSG-P7-003 and 404 carries MSG-GEN-004 with no personal value in the detail
    Then no operation declares a second error shape, and a break-glass grant adds a warning block with its end time to the answer and not a new error

  Scenario: AC5 The consumed operations are declared as consumed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the authorise operation, the access-log read and the parameters read this service calls
    Then POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise is declared as consumed with the owner P4 rwb-access
    Then GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log is declared as consumed with the owner P4 rwb-access and the case-id filter this document fixes
    Then GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters is declared as consumed with the owner P3 rwb-case
    Then each carries one hop and the 2 s client budget with a breaker
    Then the case, task, retention, masking-policy and decision-ledger operations appear as neither provided nor consumed here
    Then no operation owned by rwb-case, rwb-decision or rwb-source-data is declared as provided by rwb-access

  Scenario: AC6 The fakes match the document and carry no personal data (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the five contract fakes of the baseline
    When they are run against the document
    Then every fake answers only paths, statuses and payloads the document declares
    Then a fake that drifts from the document fails the build
    Then the access-log fake answers an entry with its case id, decision code, time, field ids and mask flag only, and no actor name
    Then no schema, example or fake carries a name, an e-mail address or a personal value, and no answer of this service carries a user reference
```

These six criteria test the artefact only. No criterion restates a legacy acceptance criterion; AC1 and AC2 of RWB-E8-016 belong to RWB-P4-E8016-APP.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/access/v1`; a document never declares another service's path | DP-13; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | A consumed operation is described as consumed, never as provided; its owner comes from the ownership map | DP-11; Ownership Map v1 |
| BR3 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; the business texts are taken from the legacy story where the message already existed | Architecture v5 slide 11; Template and Rules R7.2 s14 |
| BR4 | The schemas carry the fields of this register and no field of another service: no case state, no retention class, no access entry and no ledger row | DP-01; Ownership Map v1 (`case` = P3, `decision_log_entry` = P7) |
| BR5 | The person is a reference: no schema, example, fake or entry of this contract carries a name, an e-mail address, a national identity number, a phone number, an address, a date of birth or a user reference | NFR-040; ASM-1589 |
| BR6 | The state set is `OPEN`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `ANSWERED` and `REFUSED`, one operation moves each state, and the last two are terminal | FSD P4 v3 A2.27.4.1; ASM-1589 |
| BR7 | The statutory period, the person-reference shape and the page bounds are parameter rows behind the document and never fields of the code | DP-06; NFR-043; ASM-1590 |
| BR8 | The access-log read is consumed with its case-id filter, its owner, one hop and the 2 s budget, and the missing filter in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A is carried in the gap and not added to the metadata | GAP-0877; ASM-1592 |
| BR9 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a removed, renamed or retyped field is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 |
| BR10 | A write requires an `Idempotency-Key` or an `If-Match`, and a replay answers the first answer | Architecture v5 slide 42; DP-09 |
| BR11 | The contract declares no workflow, no activity and no Schedule for the capability, and no timer for the due date | Architecture v5 slide 14; TSD P4 v3 T5.3 |
| BR12 | The contract names no retention class, no masking policy row and no case hold: those are P5's, RWB-P4-E1037-APP's and `rwb-case`'s | Ownership Map v1; FSD P4 v3 screen list |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The four operations, the three schemas, the state set and the consumed operations are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story, the SCR-47 route, the access-log owner, the parameters owner and the harness accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A field is added within major version 1 | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A field is removed, renamed or retyped, or a state is removed | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A consumed operation changes | The access-log read or the parameters read changes | Baselined, with the client budget and the stub restated |

The state set the document fixes for a data subject request is `OPEN`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `ANSWERED` and `REFUSED`, with the register of this service as its only writer and no case state among them. A case state such as the `HELD_LEGAL` of R-UNI-11 is `rwb-case`'s and `rwb-deviation`'s and is not declared here.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| `DataSubjectRequest` open request | `dataSubjectRef` (a reference, validated against a parameter row), `requestType` (`ACCESS`, `CORRECTION`, `ERASURE`), `caseIds`, `fieldIds`, `receivedAt` (a date), `reason`; `dataSubjectRef`, `requestType`, `caseIds` and `receivedAt` required, `fieldIds` required for a correction and for an erasure |
| `DataSubjectRequest` answer | `requestId`, `requestType`, `state`, `openedAt`, `dueDate`, `version`, `steps[]` in entry order, `evidence[]` for an access request |
| `DataSubjectRequestDecision` request | `decision` (`CORRECTION`, `ERASURE`, `ANSWER`, `REFUSAL`), `fieldIds`, `effectiveFrom`, `refusalReason`, `answerSummary`, `reason`, under an `If-Match`; `decision` and `reason` required, `fieldIds` required for a correction and for an erasure, `effectiveFrom` required for an erasure, `refusalReason` required for a refusal |
| `DataSubjectRequestDecision` answer | `requestId`, `state`, `decision`, `version`, `updatedAt`, and for an erasure `maskingVersion` and `maskingRowCount` |
| `DataSubjectRequestList` | `items[]` of `requestId`, `requestType`, `state`, `openedAt`, `dueDate`, `overdue`, `page`, `size`, `total` |
| Evidence item | `caseId`, `decisionCode`, `decidedAt`, `fieldIds[]`, `masked`; no actor, no name, no value |
| Roles and letters | The role code of the caller and of the erasure, and the capability areas of `role` DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039 and `permission` DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044, read behind the authorise answer |
| Masking rows, as consumed by the story | `masking_rule` DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204: `role_code`, `field_id`, `unmasked`, `masking_version`, `valid_from`, `valid_to` |
| Record event | `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` with the entry of a step, from the DP-03 library |
| Refusal | `messageId` MSG-P4-001 on a 401, MSG-P4-002 on a 403, MSG-GEN-004 on a 404 and a 409, MSG-GEN-001 on a 422 and MSG-P7-003 on a 503 |

The exact field set of the three schemas, the type and length of each field, the shape of `dataSubjectRef`, the record code of a data subject request and the case-id filter of the access-log read are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0874; ASM-1589) and (GAP-0877; ASM-1592): FSD P4 v3 A2.27 names the journey, two validation rules and BR-P4-027 and no operation and no field, and the P4 appendix T-A declares neither a data subject request operation nor a case filter on the access log. The statutory period is Not specified either: NFR-043 states the target as "Statutory period, Not set as a working service level" and marks it "Open, DL26" (GAP-0875; ASM-1590). Where a corrected value is applied and where an erased field is removed are Not specified (GAP-0876; ASM-1591); this document records the decision and declares no value field.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-access (P4); base `/api/recovery/access/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/admin/data-subject-requests` | `DataSubjectRequest` in; `DataSubjectRequest` out in state `OPEN` with `requestId`, `openedAt`, `dueDate`, `version` and the `Location` of the read by id | Rules and parameters C; `Idempotency-Key` required |
| PATCH | `/admin/data-subject-requests/{requestId}` | `DataSubjectRequestDecision` in; the decision out with `state`, `version`, `updatedAt` and, for an erasure, `maskingVersion` and `maskingRowCount` | Rules and parameters A; `If-Match` required |
| GET | `/admin/data-subject-requests/{requestId}` | `DataSubjectRequest` out with its `steps` and its `evidence` block | Rules and parameters R, scope applied |
| GET | `/admin/data-subject-requests` | `DataSubjectRequestList` out, paged, ordered by `openedAt` then request id | Rules and parameters R, scope applied |

Errors for all four: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001), 403 no right (MSG-P4-002), 404 no request with that id (MSG-GEN-004), 409 a stale `If-Match` or a state that does not accept the decision (MSG-GEN-004), 422 a required field empty or a value of the wrong shape (MSG-GEN-001), 503 a read or a record that cannot be completed (MSG-P7-003). The open is a write and carries an `Idempotency-Key`; the decision is a write and carries an `If-Match`; both reads carry neither and are a read only. Major version 1 sits in the path; an additive field within version 1 is a compatible change, and a removed, renamed or retyped field is a new major version tested against the registry with BACKWARD compatibility (BR9).

The four paths are fixed here (GAP-0874; ASM-1589). No case, retention, masking-policy or ledger operation is declared as provided in this document.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11).

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The C check behind the open, the A check behind the decision and the R check behind the reads, cached for the session |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` | P4 rwb-access | The access entries of the case ids of a request, with the case-id filter this document fixes, for the evidence block (API-P4-008; BR8) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | The statutory period, the person-reference shape and the page bounds, with the version in force (DP-06) |

None of the three is declared as provided by rwb-access in this document, although two are owned by this service: the authorise operation is RWB-P4-E1037-CON's and the access-log read is RWB-P4-E1039-CON's, so both appear here as consumed and are stubbed by their fakes. The case-id filter is not in the T-A list of API-P4-008, which declares `user`, `from`, `to`, `event`, `page` and `size`; it is fixed here and raised with the access-log owner (GAP-0877; ASM-1592), and the gap is not added to this story's metadata. The case read, the task operations, the retention operations, the masking-policy operations and `GET /decision-log` appear nowhere in this document as provided or consumed.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library; consumed by P7 | The entry of a step with its request id, type, person reference, case ids, field ids, decision code, role code, received date, due date and time, with its `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`, in the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope |

This document declares the record message only. `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` is RWB-P4-E1037-APP's and `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` is RWB-P4-E8008-APP's, and a data subject request publishes neither (Architecture v5 slide 14); a request announces no change on `rwb.access.events.v1`, because the caching consumers of that topic have nothing to refresh for a register.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `rwb-access` is a reference-data owner in Architecture v5 slide 14, and the four operations of this contract need no subscription. The document declares no inbox and no consumer group, and no case, retention or ledger event is consumed.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. No workflow, no activity and no signal is part of this contract: the open, the decision and the answer are synchronous, and the statutory due date is data and not a timer (BR11). The `rwb-access` queue carries the access review Schedule of RWB-P4-AD008-APP only.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. All four operations are request-driven, and the due date of a request is computed from its received date and the parameter row in force; no Schedule reminds, escalates or closes a request in this contract.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | P4 (rwb_access) | The role code of the caller and the role codes an erasure covers |
| `permission` | P4 (rwb_access) | The C, A and R letters of Rules and parameters and the role they are held through |
| `masking_rule` | P4 (rwb_access), created by RWB-P4-E1037-APP | The rows an erasure writes: `role_code`, `field_id`, `unmasked`, `masking_version`, `valid_from` |
| the local decision-record table of the DP-03 library | P4, in rwb_access | The step entries the register is built from and the record event carries |
| `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in rwb_access | The stored request and answer of an open, so one key answers one request (DP-09; ASM-0074) |
| `case`, `task`, `parameter_catalog`, `lov_value` | P3 (rwb_case) | Not named as this service's: the period arrives in the consumed answer and no case row is read (DP-01, DP-06, DP-07) |
| `decision_log_entry` | P7 (rwb_decision) | Not named as this service's: the ledger consumes the topic and answers its own query |
| retention, consent and the case hold | P5 and the P3 and S8 work | Declared nowhere in this document (BR12) |

No table of another service is named in the contract (DP-01): `template`, `notice` and `merge_field` are not part of this capability, `decision_log_entry` and the rule registry are P7 rwb_decision's, and `case`, `task`, `parameter_catalog` and `lov_value` are P3 rwb_case's. The register is a chain of entries and not a table, so the document names no request table and no column of one (BR1 of the app story).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| parameters fake | `GET /admin/parameters` with the statutory-period row at "2027.1" (45 days) and at "2027.2" (60 days), the person-reference shape, the page bounds, a version not in force and a 503 | App story, contract tests, harness |
| authorise fake | `POST /authorise` with a granted answer for RW-COE with C, RW-RISK with A and RW-AUDIT with R in Rules and parameters, and a refused answer with MSG-P4-002 for RW-CASEOWN with R only and for a C holder without A | App story, contract tests, harness |
| access-log fake | `GET /admin/access-log?caseId=...` answering two `AC-READ` entries and one `AC-EXPT` entry for "RW-2026-000123", each with its field ids and mask flag, an empty page for a case with no entry and a 503 | App story, contract tests, harness |
| decision-record fake | The append of a step, the hash-link check, a seeded register of "DSR-2027-000118" with its opening, its erasure decision and its answer, and a forced failure | App story, contract tests |
| gateway-bff fake | The composite route of SCR-47 with the register list, the request form, the decision form and the evidence panel | Screen route, harness |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 4 provided, 3 consumed | The open, the decision, the read and the list provided; the authorise, the access-log read and the parameters read consumed; one hop, 2 s timeout |
| Kafka | 1 event type published, 0 consumed | `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` through the DP-03 library |
| Temporal | 0 workflows, 0 activities | None in this contract |
| File | None | No file input and no file output; the evidence is an answer block and not a document |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `openapi/rwb-access-data-subject-request-v1.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1) with the four operations and the shared components, `contract/error-envelope.yaml`, the `DataSubjectRequest`, `DataSubjectRequestDecision` and `DataSubjectRequestList` schemas with their examples, the state-set rule and the versioning rules in the contract README, and the five WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story; this story is Day 1 by rule and carries no H and no C of its own. The access-log read is consumed and faked, and its missing case-id filter is carried in the gap row of the key and not added to this story's metadata (GAP-0877; ASM-1592).

**Build steps**

1. OpenAPI 3.1 skeleton with the base path, the security scheme, the problem responses and the shared components; schema lint in the pipeline.
2. The four operations with the shapes of section 11: the open, the decision with its `If-Match`, the read with its steps and its evidence, and the list with its paging.
3. The state set of BR6, stated in the document and in the contract README, with the operation that may move each state and the terminal pair named.
4. The evidence block of a read, with the five fields of an item and the explicit statement that no actor name and no personal value is part of it.
5. The consumed operations with their owners, the one-hop rule and the 2 s client budget, the case-id filter of the access-log read, and the explicit statement that no case, retention, masking-policy or ledger operation is provided here.
6. The error envelope and the message-ID mapping for 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, with the texts of the legacy messages and MSG-GEN-004 for the conflict and the absent request.
7. The five fakes and the stub fixtures of section 12.8, including the two versions of the statutory-period row and the seeded register of "DSR-2027-000118".
8. The six contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
9. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note from the app story, the SCR-47 route, the access-log owner, the parameters owner and the harness.

**Feature switch.** The four operations are switched by the service baseline of RWB-P4-E1037-CON, not by a flag of this contract; the document declares no 404 branch of its own beyond the absent request and adds no parameter.

**Consumer sign-off**

| Consumer | What it accepts |
|---|---|
| RWB-P4-E8016-APP | The four provided operations, the three schemas, the state set, the evidence block and the five fakes |
| RWB-PLT-N001-CON (gateway-bff and SCR-47) | The register list, the request form, the decision form with its `If-Match` and the evidence panel |
| The access-log owner (RWB-P4-E1039-CON) | The read as consumed, with the case-id filter this document fixes |
| The `rwb-case` parameters owner (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) | The statutory-period row, the reference shape and the page bounds as consumed |
| The harness of the wave 4 access journey | The due date, the state path and the evidence as the facts it records |

The shape of `dataSubjectRef`, the record code of a data subject request and the case-id filter of the access-log read are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0874; ASM-1589) and (GAP-0877; ASM-1592); the reference is validated against a parameter row, the record code is the library's data subject request code, and both are confirmed with Compliance and with the decision-record library owner before the operations are frozen.

**Done when.** The document validates in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the five fakes answer every declared path, the access-log owner has accepted the case-id filter, and the app story, the screen route and the harness have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | No session | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Rules and parameters C opens, without A decides, or without R reads | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-004 | A break-glass grant is active for the caller | Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is empty, `requestType` is not one of the three, `caseIds` is empty, `fieldIds` is missing for a correction or an erasure, `receivedAt` is not a date, or `dataSubjectRef` is not of the shape in force | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The `If-Match` is stale, the state does not accept the decision, or no request has that id | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The parameters read or the access-log read cannot be completed, or a step cannot be recorded | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The message IDs are contract elements; the text is the agreed text taken from the legacy story where the message already existed. MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-004, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P7-003 are the five texts of RWB-E8-016, copied unchanged; MSG-GEN-004 is the platform conflict text, declared here for the stale version, the terminal state and the absent request. MSG-P4-003, the legacy scope message of another key, is declared on no response of this document, because a request is scoped by role and by the person reference and not by a case in the caller's scope.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the statutory period, the reference shape and the page bounds stay parameter rows behind the document, and the role codes stay rows of `role` and `permission`.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: person references, case ids, field ids, decision codes, role codes and times only, and no user reference of the officer or of the person (BR5).
- The contract names only `rwb-access` tables and only operations owned by `rwb-access` and by its parameters owner; `case`, `task`, `decision_log_entry`, the retention classes and the masking policy are not named as fields of this register (BR4, BR12).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic fails the review (DP-13).
- One writer of a request state: the document states that the register of this service moves `OPEN`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `ANSWERED` and `REFUSED`, and that no case state is written here (BR6).
- The access-log read is consumed and faked, and its missing case-id filter is carried in the gap rather than added to the metadata (BR8).
- Every example in the document is synthetic; no production personal value is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope and the CloudEvents envelope come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.
- A write without its `Idempotency-Key` or its `If-Match` is refused by the contract, and a replay never makes a second step (BR10).
- The due date is declared as an answer field computed from the parameter row, never as a constant and never as a timer (BR7, BR11).

##### 1. Story

As a **compliance and PDPA officer**, I want **a PDPA access, correction or erasure request opened, worked and answered from one register that checks the right, holds the statutory due date as a parameter of the platform, records the correction and the erasure as decisions of this service, writes the masking rows an erasure needs, and answers the access evidence from the access entries of this service**, so that **every data subject request is answered inside the statutory period and the answer, its decisions and its evidence can be shown afterwards without asking another team**.

Inside `rwb-access` this is the data subject request of the legacy story RWB-E8-016:

- Service `rwb-access`, schema `rwb_access`, REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1` with event names `rwb.access.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.
- Four operations, and nothing else: the open `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/data-subject-requests`; the decision `PATCH /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/data-subject-requests/{requestId}`, which records the correction or the erasure decision and the answer under an `If-Match`; the read `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/data-subject-requests/{requestId}`; and the list `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/data-subject-requests`, paged.
- The register is the local decision-record chain of DP-03, not a table of its own: one entry per step of a request, written with the record code of a data subject request, hash-linked and published as `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`. The service creates no new table for the register and copies no row of it.
- The statutory due date is a parameter row of `rwb-case` read through DP-06 at its version in force, and it is never a constant in code. The row's name, its value and its unit are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0875; ASM-1590); NFR-043 states the target as "Statutory period, Not set as a working service level" and marks it "Open, DL26".
- An erasure writes `masking_rule` rows (DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204) for **every** role with `unmasked` false from a `valid_from` and moves `masking_version` on by one, in the transaction that records the decision. The masking policy itself, which field a role may see, belongs to RWB-P4-E1037-APP; this story only executes the erasure against it.
- A correction records the field ids corrected and **no value**: the decision carries the case ids, the field ids, the person reference, the time and the role code, and the value is not read, not copied and not written here (NFR-040).
- The access evidence of an access request is answered from this service's own access entries, the `AC-READ`, `AC-EXPT` and `AC-DENY` entries of the local chain written by RWB-P4-E1039-APP, read through that capability's own read `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` (API-P4-008) filtered by the case ids of the request. The workbench-wide answer across the other eighteen services is the central ledger's query and is not this story's (GAP-0877; ASM-1592).
- The request is reached from SCR-47 Personal data through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19, which shows the register and calls the four operations; this story renders no screen of its own.
- This story starts no workflow, owns no Schedule and publishes no event of its own: opening, deciding and answering are synchronous, the due date is data and not a timer, and the only message it produces is `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) on `rwb.decision-record.v1`.
- The legacy story's two endpoints (a rule-version load and a rule-version approval) and two of its three data rows are not this capability's; the split keeps the capability, the criteria, the messages and the test ids and drops the copied rule-change apparatus (GAP-0878; ASM-1593).

##### 2. Business rationale

A data subject request is a statutory obligation with a clock on it. NFR-043 asks that an access, correction or erasure request be answered inside the statutory period, and REQ-S8-007 (Must) asks that the request hold automated processing on the case and route to Compliance inside the same period; R-UNI-11 is the routing rule behind it, a universal rule that moves a case to `HELD_LEGAL` when a PDPA access, correction or erasure request is received. The legacy story carried the capability as one administration journey of the monolith (FEAT-ADM-11, RWB-E8-016), where the request, the masking rows and the decision log were rows of one schema and the request was worked on a screen of the same module. In the target the masking policy is a table of `rwb-access` (P4, slide 41), the case and its hold are `rwb-case`'s and `rwb-deviation`'s, the parameters are `rwb-case`'s under DP-06, and the record of who decided what is the decision record (ADR-022). So a data subject request is no longer a single screen: it is a decision that needs an authority, a register, a due date that lives as data, and a masking write that is the erasure.

This story is that register. It meets NFR-043 on the side this service can hold: the request exists with a due date computed from the parameter row in force, every step is a recorded decision, and the answer names the evidence. It supports REQ-S8-007 on the Compliance side, while the hold on the case stays with `rwb-case` and `rwb-deviation`, which own the case state and the rule that moves it. It carries the FSD target measure of the administration features: rule and limit changes made without a code release, 100 percent, measured monthly from the decision record (FSD P4 v3 A2.27.1). The statutory period is a row, the field set of a correction is data, and neither needs a release.

The control that makes the answer worth anything is the evidence. The FSD A2.7 writes every read of the case store to the access log, and A2.5 masks a personal field by role, so "who read this person's data, and was it masked" is answerable from two tables this service already owns. An access request answered without that evidence is a letter; with it, it is a statement the bank can defend. Answering it here also keeps the request inside the service that holds the masking rules and the access entries, so no personal value has to travel to answer a question about personal data.

Keeping the register off a table is the deliberate choice of the target. A request has states, steps and a clock, and a new table would give the service a second lifecycle to migrate and a second place where a step could be lost; the decision record is append-only, hash-chained and already published to the ledger, so the register is provable and the steps cannot be rewritten. The cost is that a request is a chain of entries and not one row, and the split pays it once, in the read of section 12.1.

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| RWB-P4-E8016-CON (same service, its own contract story) | The OpenAPI 3.1 document of the four operations, the `DataSubjectRequest`, `DataSubjectRequestList` and `DataSubjectRequestDecision` schemas, the state set, the error envelope, the consumed-operation list and the five contract fakes. This story implements that document and adds no path |
| RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03): the entry of a step, hash-linked, written in the transaction that stores the answer |
| RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The parameters client library and the `rwb-case` parameters contract (DP-06): the statutory period, the page bounds and the reference shape, as rows and not as code |
| RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) that serves SCR-47 Personal data and calls the four operations, one hop each |
| The access-log read of RWB-P4-E1039-CON | `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` (API-P4-008) over the entries of this service's own chain, filtered by case id; the filter is fixed by the contract (GAP-0877; ASM-1592) |
| RWB-P4-E1037-APP's masking table | The `masking_rule` rows (DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204) the erasure writes and the `masking_version` it moves on; this story writes no policy and adds no column |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E8-016, from the feature specification and from the technical specification:

- The rights in force are those of TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and of the legacy permission table: a request is opened with Rules and parameters C (RW-COE holds `CRUD`), its decision and its answer are recorded with A (RW-RISK holds `RA`), and it is read with R. A caller without the letter is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002 (BR3).
- The FSD P4 v3 A2.27.3.3 role table names the Compliance and PDPA officer as the primary user and the Security administrator as the second. The matrix of T6.1 gives RW-COMPLY `R` only in Rules and parameters and gives RW-SECADM `CRUDA` in Platform administration, not in Rules and parameters, so the primary role of the FSD cannot open or decide a request unless a permission row carries the letter; the difference is carried as an assumption and changes no metadata value (ASM-1592).
- The legacy permission table fixes the capability area as Rules and parameters, and the legacy validation rules VR-P4-027-1 and VR-P4-027-2 fix the sign-in message and the break-glass warning of a request.
- A case hold is the case's: R-UNI-11 moves a case to `HELD_LEGAL` and routes it to Compliance, and this story neither holds nor releases a case and writes no case state (BR13).
- The statutory period, its unit and its working-day rule are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0875; ASM-1590): the due date is computed from the parameter row in force and the calculation this story applies is calendar days from `openedAt` (ASM-1590).
- Where a corrected value is applied and where an erased field is removed are Not specified (GAP-0876; ASM-1591): this story records the decision, names the field ids and writes the masking rows of an erasure, and the execution in the owning services is out of scope.

##### 4. Flow

1. The compliance and PDPA officer opens SCR-47 Personal data through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The route shows the register as this service answers it and calls the four operations.
2. The officer records a request. The route calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/data-subject-requests` on `rwb-access` with `dataSubjectRef`, `requestType` (`ACCESS`, `CORRECTION` or `ERASURE`), `caseIds`, `fieldIds` (required for `CORRECTION` and `ERASURE`), `receivedAt` and `reason`, and an `Idempotency-Key` header.
3. `DataSubjectRequestController` validates the request: every required field is present, `requestType` is one of the three, `caseIds` holds at least one case id, `fieldIds` is present for a correction and for an erasure and empty for an access request, `receivedAt` is a date, and `dataSubjectRef` matches the reference shape in force read through DP-06. An empty field or a value of the wrong shape is refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-001 naming the field, and nothing is read and nothing is written (BR4).
4. The controller looks the `Idempotency-Key` up in the idempotency table of the platform library in `rwb_access`. A key already answered replays that first answer, stores nothing and appends no entry (BR11, AC4).
5. The controller resolves the caller's session and calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` on its own service, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a cached answer, for Rules and parameters C. A caller without the C letter is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002, and nothing is recorded (BR3, AC3).
6. `ParameterReader` reads the statutory-period row through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` of `rwb-case` with the version in force and computes `dueDate` as the received date plus the period the row gives. No period, unit or working-day rule is a constant in code (BR8, AC7).
7. In one local transaction the service appends one entry to the decision-record chain of DP-03 with the record code of a data subject request, the request id, the type, the person reference, the case ids, the field ids, the received date, the due date, the opening role code, no case state and no personal value; sets the idempotency row to the answer; and stages the outbox row of the entry (BR1, BR7, BR11).
8. The answer is 201 with `requestId`, `requestType`, state `OPEN`, `openedAt`, `dueDate`, `version` and the `Location` of the register read (BR6).
9. The officer works the request. Where a correction is decided, the route calls `PATCH /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/data-subject-requests/{requestId}` with `decision` `CORRECTION`, the `fieldIds`, `reason` and the `If-Match` of the version the screen holds.
10. `DataSubjectRequestService` authorises Rules and parameters A (403 with MSG-P4-002 otherwise), compares the `If-Match` with the version of the latest entry (409 with MSG-GEN-004 otherwise, the register unchanged), and refuses a decision the state does not accept (409 with MSG-GEN-004) (BR3, BR5, BR6).
11. `CorrectionRecorder` appends the decision with the field ids and no value, moves the request to `IN_PROGRESS`, and returns 200 with the new `version`; the corrected value is not read and not written here (BR7, NFR-040).
12. Where an erasure is decided, `ErasureWriterService` writes one `masking_rule` row for every role in force with `unmasked` false from the `effectiveFrom` of the decision, moves `masking_version` on by one, and appends the same decision, all in one transaction; a failure writes no masking row and appends no entry (BR7, AC5).
13. The answer to the request is recorded with `decision` `ANSWER` (or `REFUSAL` with a reason); the state moves to `ANSWERED` (or `REFUSED`) and the answer carries `answeredAt`, the number of calendar days from `openedAt`, and whether the due date was met (BR6, BR9).
14. Where the request is of type `ACCESS`, the read of step 15 answers the evidence: `AccessEvidenceReader` calls `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` on its own service with the case ids of the request, one hop with a 2 s timeout, and takes the decision code, the decided time, the field ids and the mask flag of each entry. No entry of another service is read and no ledger query is made (BR9, AC6).
15. `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/data-subject-requests/{requestId}` answers the request with its `steps` in entry order and its `evidence` block, and `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/data-subject-requests` answers the page of requests with their state, their dates and their version, ordered by `openedAt` then by request id so the paging is stable (BR10, BR12).
16. A request with no entry answers 404 on the read by id and an empty `items` with total 0 on the list; no message carries a personal value, and no answer names a person (BR12, BR14).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A required field is empty, `requestType` is not one of the three, `caseIds` is empty, `fieldIds` is missing for a correction or an erasure, or `receivedAt` is not a date | 422 naming the field; nothing is read and nothing is written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | `dataSubjectRef` does not match the reference shape in force | 422 naming `dataSubjectRef`; no entry | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X3 | The caller holds no Rules and parameters C on the open, or no A on the decision | 403, no entry, no masking row | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X4 | The caller's session has ended | 401, no entry and no masking row | MSG-P4-001 | AC3 |
| X5 | The `If-Match` of a decision is older than the request's version | 409 and the register unchanged; the screen reloads the request | MSG-GEN-004 | AC4 |
| X6 | A decision arrives for a request in `ANSWERED` or `REFUSED` | 409 and the register unchanged | MSG-GEN-004 | AC4 |
| X7 | The `rwb-case` parameters read does not answer inside 2 s, or the statutory-period row is not in force | 503 and no request opened; a retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` opens exactly one | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X8 | The access-log read does not answer inside 2 s | 503 on the read by id, the request itself unchanged and readable again later | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X9 | The decision-record entry, the masking rows, the idempotency row or the outbox row cannot be written | 503 and no answer; nothing is recorded and the retry completes one step | MSG-P7-003 | AC2 |
| X10 | The same request arrives twice with the same `Idempotency-Key` | The first answer is replayed; one entry, one masking write | None | AC4 |
| X11 | A break-glass grant is active for the caller | The step proceeds and the answer carries the warning with the end time of the grant, and the entry carries the grant id | MSG-P4-004 | AC3 |
| X12 | The request's due date has passed and the request is still open | The answer carries the overdue flag and the list shows it; no state changes and no message is produced by a timer | None | AC7 |

No exception path of this story changes a case, a task, a role, a permission or a rule: the case and its hold belong to `rwb-case` and `rwb-deviation`, the masking policy to RWB-P4-E1037-APP, and the only rows this story writes of its own are its chain entries, the masking rows of an erasure and the platform library rows of the request.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P4-E8016-CON and its fakes; the period and the page bounds are parameter rows, the access entries are read through their owner's operation, and the masking policy is another story's table |
| Negotiable | The reference shape, the page bounds and the statutory period are parameter rows; the approving letters and the state set are reviewed with Compliance and with the access-log owner |
| Valuable | One register answers whether a data subject request was worked and answered inside the statutory period, and the erasure leaves the masking rows that make it true |
| Estimable | One controller, one register service, one erasure writer, one evidence reader, one record appender, one idempotency store, five fakes and ten test cases |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests; no new table, no workflow, no schedule, no screen and no event of its own |
| Testable | Each owned criterion has a test case in section 16; the due date is provable with two versions of the parameter row, and the erasure is provable against a seeded matrix |
